translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ ba Abimelek ṅõ nyōṅ ye̱ lamõ mli, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, obagbo ye̱ yō le̱ ní oṅõ le̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ nū ṅã dšile̱.

english_verse: Abimelech said to the Lord, “Don't kill me! I haven't slept with Sarah. Didn't they say they were brother and sister? I am completely innocent.”
translation_verse: Ani dšee le̱ ekē̱mi ake̱: Minyemiyō dšile̱? ni yō le̱ dientše̱ hũ kē̱ ake̱: Minyeminū dšile̱? Mitšui mū ke̱ mideṅ tšemo̱ mike̱-fe ene̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Then God continued: I know you are innocent. That's why I kept you from sleeping with Sarah and doing anything wrong.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ kē̱le̱ ye̱ lamõ le̱ mli ake̱: Mi hũ mile ake̱ otšui mū oke̱-fe ene̱; ni mi hũ mitšĩ onā, ní okafe eša ošimi; nohewo̱ ni mihāão hegbe̱ ake̱ ota ehe le̱.

english_verse: Her husband is a prophet. Let her go back to him, and his prayers will save you from death. But if you don't return her, you and all your people will die.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ṅõ nū le̱ ṅã le̱ ohãle̱ ekoṅ, ši *gbalo̱ dšile̱, ni eekpa fai ehão, ni oyi anã wala; ši ke̱dši oke̱le̱ hāāle̱ le̱, no le̱ ná ole ake̱ gbo oogbo, bo ke̱ mei fẽ ni dši onõ le̱! *Lal.

english_verse: Early the next morning Abimelech sent for his officials, and when he told them what had happened, they were frightened.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni etšé̱ etšũdši le̱ fẽ, ni ewie wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ ewo ame̱toiiaṅ; ni hĩĩ le̱ še gbeyei naakpa.

english_verse: Abimelech then called in Abraham and said: Look what you've done to us! What have I ever done to you? Why did you make me and my nation guilty of such a terrible sin?
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek tšé̱ Abraham, ni eké̱le̱ ake̱: Meni ofewo̱ ne̱? Ni meni eša mifeo, ni oke̱ eša kpeteṅkple ebami ke̱ mimaṅtše̱yeli le̱ no̱ ne̱? Noni afee ofemi ne̱!

english_verse: What were you thinking when you did this?
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek sã kē̱ Abraham ake̱: Meni ona, ni oye ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱?

english_verse: Abraham answered: I did it because I didn't think any of you respected God, and I was sure that someone would kill me to get my wife.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham kē̱: Edšake̱ miyasusu ake̱, ekole̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyeišemo̱ be̱ bie̱, ni ame̱abagbemi ye̱ miṅã le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Besides, she is my half sister. We have the same father, but different mothers.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ eye̱ mli le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ minyemiyō ni; mitše̱bi ni, ši dšee minyebiṅ; ni etšṍ miṅã.

english_verse: When God made us leave my father's home and start wandering, I told her, “If you really love me, then tell everyone that I am your brother.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Nyoṅmo̱ hã midše mitše̱ we ni miyatšomlo le̱, mikē̱le̱ ake̱: Edšũrõ ni ofemi ne̱: hefẽhe ni wo̱o̱te le̱, kē̱mo̱ ye̱ mihe ake̱: Minyeminū ni.

english_verse: After Abimelech had given Abraham some sheep, cattle, and slaves, he sent Sarah back
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek ṅõ tōi ke̱ tšinai ke̱ wehĩĩ ke̱ weyei eyabã Abraham, ni eṅõ eṅã Sara ebãle̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: and told Abraham he could settle anywhere in his country.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek kē̱: Na, mišikpoṅ le̱ kã ohĩe ne̱; hĩ heni osumoo̱.

english_verse: Meanwhile, God had kept Abimelech's wife and slaves from having children. But Abraham prayed, and God let them start having children again.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa etšĩmo̱ yei fẽ ni yo̱ Abimelek we le̱ amũsũi anā ye̱ Abraham ṅã Sara sane le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: The Lord was good to Sarah and kept his promise.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa basra Sara, take̱ bo̱ni ekē̱ le̱, ni Iehowa fe ehã Sara, take̱ bo̱ni ewie le̱.

english_verse: Although Abraham was very old, Sarah had a son exactly at the time God had said.
translation_verse: Ni Sara ná mũsũ, ni eke̱ Abraham fo̱ binū ye̱ egbo̱le̱ mli, ye̱ be ni Nyoṅmo̱ ekē̱le̱ le̱ mli. Heb.

english_verse: and Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. And now everyone will laugh with me.
translation_verse: Ni Sara kē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ewo *ṅmlõkpã ehãmi; mofẽmo ni aanu le̱ aaṅmõ eko ahãmi. *

english_verse: One day, Sarah noticed Hagar's son Ishmael playing, and she said to Abraham, “Get rid of that Egyptian slave woman and her son! I don't want him to inherit anything. It should all go to my son.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Abraham ake̱: *ſiemo̱ tšũlo̱yō ne̱ ke̱ ebi le̱; ši tšũlo̱yõ ne̱ bi le̱ ke̱ mibi Isak akaye gbošinii le̱. *Gal.

english_verse: but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱yō le̱ bi le̱ hũ, *mahã etšṍ dšeṅmaṅ, edšake̱ oseši dšile̱. *

english_verse: Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away. They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba,
translation_verse: Ni Abraham te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni eko̱ abolo ke̱ nu ke̱ woloto̱ ehã Hagar, ni eṅõ-tſa ekõṅ, ke̱ gbekẽ le̱ hũ, ni ewole̱ gbe̱. Ni eyiṅ ete ni eyatšomlo ye̱ Beer-šeba ṅã le̱ṅ.

english_verse: When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ nu oblanyo le̱ gbē, ni Nyoṅmo̱ bo̱fo le̱ tšé̱ Hagar ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei, ni eké̱le̱ ake̱: Meni feo̱o, Hagar? Kāše gbeyei; ši Nyoṅmo̱ enu oblanyo le̱ gbē ye̱ heni eyo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ gble ehĩṅme̱ii, ni ena nubu ko; ni eyiṅ ete, ni eyaye̱ nu ewo woloto̱ le̱ obõ, ni eṅõ-hã oblanyo le̱ enu.

english_verse: About this time Abimelech and his army commander Phicol said to Abraham, “God blesses everything you do!
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli ake̱ Abimelek ke̱ etatše̱ Fikol bakē̱ Abraham ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱o ye̱ ye̱ nibii fẽ ní ofeo̱ le̱ mli.

english_verse: Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ kã Nyoṅmo̱ kitã otšõmi ye̱ bie̱ ne̱, ake̱ oyeṅmi lo mibii ke̱ miho̱i akũtũmpo̱o; ši edšũrõ bo̱ni *mifeo le̱, nakai ooṅō-femi ke̱ šikpoṅ ni obato gbo̱ ye̱ no̱ ne̱. *

english_verse: And so, Abraham promised he would.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham kē̱: Makã kitã le̱.

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Ni Abraham kã Abimelek hĩe ye̱ nubu ko ni Abimelek tšũdši le̱ šõ ekā̃ nā le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abraham ṅõ tōi ke̱ tšinai ebã Abimelek, ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ ame̱kpãṅ.

english_verse: and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek kē̱ Abraham ake̱: Ne̱ke̱ gwanteṅbiyei kpawo ni odšie oto afã ne̱, té ešišiṅ.

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Gwanteṅbiyei kpawo ne̱ oṅõ ye̱ mideṅ, koni aṅō-ye odase ahãmi, ake̱ mi midše ne̱ke̱ nubu ne̱.

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ etšé̱ dše̱i *Beeršeba, edšake̱ dše̱i ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ ame̱kãmo̱ kitã ye̱. *

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kpãṅ ye̱ Beeršeba; ni Abimelek ke̱ etatše̱ Fikol te ši, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham te̱o tamarisketšo ye̱ Beeršeba, ni *etšé̱ Iehowa, †nāno̱ Mawu le̱, gbe̱i ye̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham to gbo̱ ye̱ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩĩ pī.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ Abraham hole ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱, ni ena dše̱i ye̱ šoṅṅ.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ba heni Nyoṅmo̱ etšõle̱ le̱; ni Abraham mã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni eto lai le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱, ni efĩ ebi Isak le̱, ni eṅõle̱ eṅmẽ lai le̱ no̱ ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham kpã enine mli eko̱ kakla le̱, koni eke̱-gbe ebi le̱. Iak.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Ni Abraham wo dše̱i gbe̱i: Iehowa aakwe̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ ake̱o̱ ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱ fẽ ake̱: Iehowa goṅ le̱ no̱ aakwe̱ ye̱.

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: bewo̱ le̱ dšō̱mo̱ madšō̱o, ni fá mahā *oseši afá tamo̱ ṅwei ṅulamii ke̱ ṅšo̱ nā šia, ni oseši le̱ †aaye ehenye̱lo̱i agbói le̱ ano̱;

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: ni oseši le̱ mli aadše̱ adšō̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšeṅmãdši fẽ, edšake̱ obo migbẽ toi.

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abraham kũ ese̱ ke̱-ba eblahĩĩ le̱ aṅõ; ni ame̱te ši, ni ame̱fẽ ame̱ṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-te Beeršeba. Ni Abraham hĩ ši ye̱ Beeršeba.

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Ni eye̱ ṅã kroko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Reuma, le̱ hũ efo̱ Teba ke̱ Gaham ke̱ Tahaš ke̱ Maaka.

english_verse: he went to the Hittites and said,
translation_verse: Ni Abraham te ši ke̱-dše̱ egbonyo le̱ he, ni eke̱ Hetbii le̱ yawie ake̱:

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: *Gbo̱ dšimi, ni nye mibato; nyehãami fũhe ko ye̱ nyeteṅ, koni mato migbonyo ni kã mihīe ne̱.

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: Bowo̱ toi, minuṅtšo̱! Nyoṅmo̱ lumo̱ dšio ye̱ wo̱teṅ; wo̱fū̃hei le̱ ateṅ noni hĩ fè fẽ le̱, fũ ogbonyo le̱ ye̱ mli; wo̱teṅ mokomoko etšīṅo gbe̱ ake̱ okafũ ogbonyo le̱ ye̱ efū̃he le̱.

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: ni eke̱ame̱ wie ekē̱: Ke̱dši nyeye̱ he tšui ake̱ mifũ migbonyo ni kã mihĩe ne̱, nyeboami toi, ni nyekpaä Zohar bi Efron le̱ fai nyehãami,

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: Dahi, minuṅtšo̱, bomi toi! Šikpoṅ le̱ mike̱-mīhão, ni te̱kplo le̱ ni yo̱ mli le̱ hũ mike̱-mīhão; mimaṅbii le̱ ahĩe mike̱-hãao ye̱ ne̱. Fū ogbonyo le̱!

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: ni mahã okã Iehowa, ṅwei Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ šikpoṅ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kitã ake̱ *ow̌e̱ṅ Kanaanbii ni miyo̱ ame̱teṅ ne̱ abiyei le̱ eko ohãṅ mibi le̱; *

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: ši moṅ oote mišikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ miweku le̱ mli ni oyaw̌e̱ yō abahã mibi Isak.

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ekole̱ yō le̱ ebakplẽṅ mise̱ nyiemo̱ ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ bã, bĕle̱ mike̱ obi le̱ akũ se̱ aya šikpoṅ no̱ heni odše̱ oba le̱ lo?

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Ni Abraham kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kwe̱ ohe ni ahĩ ní oke̱ mibi le̱ akakũ se̱ ke̱-mīya dše̱i doṅṅ!

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši yö le̱ sumo̱o̱ ake̱ eenyie ose̱ le̱, no le̱ obe edše mikitã ne̱ mli; mibi le̱ ke̱ke̱ ni oke̱le̱ akaya dše̱i doṅṅ.

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ le̱ ṅõ enine eho̱ enuṅtšo̱ Abraham ſuo̱ šiši, ni ekãle̱ kitã ye̱ sane le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ le̱ ṅõ enuṅtšo̱ yomai le̱ ateṅ nyoṅma, ni eṅõ enuṅtšo̱ nibii kpakpai le̱ fẽ eko ehĩe edẽ, ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ke̱-te *Nahor mã le̱ṅ ye̱ Mesopotamia. *

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Iehowa, minuṅtšo̱ Abraham Nyoṅmo̱! Mĩkpao fai ni ohã mihe aba nii ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, ni omli ahĩ ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ Abraham no̱.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: Na, midamo̱ nubu ne̱ he, ni mã le̱ṅ bii abiyei le̱ mīdše kpo mība nuyē̱:

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nu, minuṅtšo̱! Ni ehe fe oyá ni eto egbé̱ le̱ ehĩe edẽ ni ehã enu.

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: Ni ehe fe oyá ni etšṍ egbé̱ le̱ mli nu le̱ ewo nunumo̱nõ le̱ mli, ni eša foi ete bu le̱ṅ ekoṅ eyaye nu le ehã eyomai le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ nā ni kpe̱ ehe ye̱ ehe hewo̱ le̱ efe diṅṅ, koni eṅõ-le ake̱ Iehowa ehã ehe eba nii ye̱ egbe̱fā̃ le̱ mli lo.

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Milka bi Betuel ni eke̱ Nahor fo̱ le̱ bi dšimi.

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ mã eyi ši ni edšá Iehowa,

english_verse: “I thank you, Lord God of my master Abraham! You have led me to his relatives and kept your promise to him.”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Aadšie Iehowa, minuṅtšo̱ Abraham Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, yi ake̱ ehãko emlihĩle̱ ke̱ eno̱kwayeli se̱ afo ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ no̱; ni mi hũ, Iehowa ebatšõmi minuṅtšo̱ nyemimei awe gbe̱!

english_verse: Rebekah ran straight home and told her family everything.
translation_verse: Ni oblayō le̱ ša foi ke̱-te ni eyagba mei ní yo̱ enye we le̱ ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱.

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni ena ga le̱ ke̱ ninešigai le̱ ye̱ enyemiyõ le̱ nine ši, ni enu enyemiyō Rebeka wiemo̱i ni ewie ake̱: Bo̱ni nū le̱ kē̱mi ne̱ le̱, eba nū le̱ ṅõ, ni na, edamo̱ yomai le̱ amase̱i ye̱ nubu le̱ he.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: Ni eke̱: Ba šĩa, bo moni Iehowa edšō̱o! mẽhewo̱ odamo̱ ṅmaṅmaša? Ši midientše̱ misā šĩa le̱ ke̱ gbe̱ hũ mihã yomai le̱.

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ ba šĩa le̱. Ni edšie yomai le̱ ano̱nii le̱, ni ehã yomai le̱ adſe̱i ke̱ niyenii, ni ebãle̱ ke̱ mei ni eke̱-nyie le̱ nu ni ame̱ke̱-fo̱ ame̱nãdši ahe.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ nii ba mã ehĩe ni eye; ši eke̱ ake̱: Miyeṅ nii, ake̱ dša midšadše nõ sane ní mihĩe ke̱-ba le̱ dã. Ni ekē̱: Wiemo̱!

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Abraham tšũlo̱ dšimi.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa edšō̱ minuṅtšo̱ naakpa, ni etšṍ gbomo agbo; ni ehãle̱ tōi ke̱ tšinai, ke̱ dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika, ke̱ wehĩĩ ke̱ weyei, ke̱ yomai ke̱ tedšii.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: Ni minuṅtšo̱ ṅã Sara le̱ ke̱ minuṅtšo̱ efo̱ binū ye̱ egbo̱le̱ se̱ ne̱; ni le̱ eṅõ enii fẽ ni eyo̱ le̱ ehã.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Ni minuṅtšo̱ hã mikã kitã ake̱: Kaw̌e̱ Kanaanbii, mei ašikpoṅ no̱ ni miyo̱ ne̱ abiyei le̱ ateṅ moko obã mibi le̱,

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: ši ya mitše̱ we le̱ ke̱ midšaku le̱ moṅ oyawe̱ yō obahã mibi le̱.

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Ni mikē̱ minuṅtšo̱ akē̱: Ekole̱ yō le̱ ebanyieṅ mise̱.

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱mi akē̱: Iehowa, *mo hĩe ní minyie ne̱, aatšũ ebo̱fo afata ohe ke̱-ya, ni eehã ogbe̱ le̱ adša, ni oyaw̌e̱ yō ye̱ midšaku ke̱ mitše̱ we lē̱ obahã mibi le̱. *

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: No dãni obe aadše mikitã lē̱ mli; kē̱ ote midšaku le̱, ni ame̱hãāo le̱, bẽle̱ ohe edše mikitã le̱ mli.

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: Ni ṅme̱ne̱ miba nubu le̱ he, ni mikē̱: Iehowa, minuṅtšo̱ Abraham Nyoṅmo̱! ke̱dši oobã migbe̱ ni minyie ne̱ adša le̱,

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: no le̱ na, midamo̱ nubu ne̱ he, ni hã aba mli ake̱ oblayō ni aadše kpo aba nuyē̱, ni makē̱le̱ ake̱: Mikpao fai ni ohãmi ogbé̱ le̱ mli nu le̱ fiō manu,

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: ni eekē̱mi ake̱: Bodientše̱ nu, ni masã maye̱ eko mahã oyomai le̱ hũ le̱, hã le̱ noṅṅ efe yō̱ moni Iehowa edšie ebã minuṅtšo̱ bi le̱.

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Ni beni mikē̱ miwieo̱ migbeo̱ nā ye̱ mitšui mli pe̱ le̱, na, Rebeka pue, ni egbé̱ tſa ekõṅ ke̱-mība, ni ekpleke ši ke̱-te bu le̱ mli eyaye̱ nu; ni mikē̱le̱ ake̱: Mīkpao fai ni ohã manu eko!

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Ni ehe fe oyá, ni eto egbé̱ le̱ ehĩe edẽ, ni eké̱: Nu! ni mahã oyomai le̱ hũ eko ame̱nu. Ni minu, ni yomai le̱ hũ ehãame̱ eko ame̱nu.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Ni mibile̱ ake̱: Namo bi dšio? Ni ekē̱: Betuel, Nahor bi ni eke̱ Milka fo̱ le̱, bi dšimi. Ni miṅõ ga le̱ miwo egugõṅ, ni miṅõ ninešigai le̱ miwo enine;

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: ni mimã miyi ši, ni midšá Iehowa, ni midšie Iehowa, minuṅtšo̱ Abraham Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, yi ake̱ etšõmi gbe̱ kpakpa, ní mike̱-yaṅõ minuṅtšo̱ nyemibi mihã ebi le̱.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Ni agbē̱ne̱, ke̱dši nyeke̱ minuṅtšo̱ aaye ye̱ mlihìle̱ ke̱ ano̱kwayeli mli le̱, no le̱ nyekē̱ mi; ni ke̱-dšee nakai hũ, nyekē̱ami, koni mawo ninedšũrõ lo abe̱kuiaṅ tšṍmo̱.

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Laban ke̱ Betuel here no̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Iehowa ṅõ sane nē̱ dše̱; wo̱nyẽṅ wo̱ke̱o awie efõṅ lo ekpakpa.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: Na, Rebeka le̱ ne̱, ṅõle̱ ni oke̱le̱ aya, ni eyatšṍ onuntše̱ bi le̱ ṅã, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ekē̱ lē̱.

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ le̱ dšie dſie̱te̱i nibii ke̱ šika nibii ke̱ mamai ke̱-ba, ni eke̱-bahã Rebeka; ni esā ehã enyeminũ le̱ ke̱ enye hū nibii ní dšra wa.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eke̱ mei ni fata ehe le̱ ye nii ni ame̱nu noko, ni ame̱wo̱ dše̱i nakai nyō le̱ṅ; ni beni ame̱te ši lebi le̱, ekē̱: Nyewoami gbe̱, ni maya minuṅtšo̱ ṅõ!

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Ni enyeminũ le̱ ke̱ enye kē̱: Hā oblayō le̱ ke̱wo̱ ahĩ ši gbĩĩ fiō ake̱ gbĩĩ nyoṅma ne̱ke̱, no se̱ koni oke̱le̱ aya.

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekatšĩa minā, edšake̱ Iehowa ehã migbe̱ le̱ edša; nyewoami gbe̱, ní maya minuṅtšo̱ ṅõ!

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱tšé̱ oblayō le̱, ni wo̱bi edāṅ gbē.

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšē̱ Rebeka ni ame̱bile̱ ake̱: Oke̱ nū ne̱ aate lo? Ni ekē̱: Mate.

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wo ame̱nyemiyō Rebeka ke̱ efufo̱hālo̱ le̱ ke̱ Abraham tšũlo̱ le̱ ke̱ emei ni fata ehe le̱ agbe̱.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Niame̱dšō̱ Rebeka, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱nyemiyō, tšṍ mei akpei huhā anye, ni oseši aye ehenye̱lo̱i agbói le̱ ano̱!

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ni Rebeka te ši ke̱ eblayei le̱, ni ame̱ho ame̱trá yomai le̱ ano̱ ke̱-nyie nū le̱ se̱; ni tšũlo̱ le̱ ṅõ Rebeka ni eṅõſie no̱.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ni Isak dše̱ hĩekãlo̱ ní naämi le̱ *nubu le̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ẽba; ši wuoyigbe̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ehĩo̱; *

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ le̱ gba Isak sãdši fẽ ní eyaye le̱.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Ni Isak ke̱le̱ ba enye Sara bū le̱ mli; ni eṅõ Rebeka ni ebatšṍ eṅã, ni esumo̱le̱. Ni Isak tšé̱ etšui eṅmẽ emli ye̱ *enye gbĕle le̱ se̱. *

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱le̱ fo̱ Zimran ke̱ Iokšan ke̱ Medān ke̱ Midian ke̱ Išbak ke̱ Šua.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Ni Iokšon fe̱ Šeba ke̱ Dedan. Ni Dedan bii le̱ dši Ašurbii ke̱ Letušbii ke̱ Leumbii.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Ni Midian bii dši Efa ke̱ Efer ke̱ Hanok ke̱ Abida ke̱ Eldaa. Mene̱mei fẽ le̱ Ketura bii ni.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Ni Abraham gbẽle se̱ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ dšō̱ ebi Isak; ni Isak hĩ ši ye̱ hĩekãlo̱ ni naämi le̱ *nubu le̱ hewo̱. *

english_verse: Ishmael had twelve sons, in this order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
translation_verse: Išmaelbii le̱ agbe̱ii ni aṅõ-tšē̱o̱ ame̱-sešibii le̱ ne̱: Išmael kromo̱bi le̱ Nebaiot, ke̱ Kedar ke̱ Adbeel ke̱ Mibsam,

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: ke̱ Mišma ke̱ Duma ke̱ Masa,

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: ke̱ Hadad ke̱ Tema ke̱ Ietur ke̱ Nafiš ke̱ Kedema.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: Ni ame̱he ši ke̱-dše̱ Havila ke̱-yaši Šur ni ye̱ Mizraim hĩe, ke̱-yaä Ašur gbe̱ le̱. *Enyemimei le̱ fẽ hĩegbe̱ ehe ši ye̱. *

english_verse: Isaac was the son of Abraham,
translation_verse: Abraham bi Isak le̱ sešibii ne̱: Abraham fo̱ Isak.

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Ni Isak kpa Iehowa fai ehã eṅã le̱, edšake̱ efe kene; ni Iehowa bo efai-kpamo̱ le̱ toi, ni eṅã Rebeka ná mũsũ.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Ni gbekẽbii le̱ šimo̱šimō̱ ame̱he ye̱ emũsũṅ. Ni ekē̱: Kē̱dši nakai le̱, mẽha hũ ni mife ne̱ke̱ ne̱? Ni ete eyabi Iehowa,

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dšeṅmãdši enyo̱ yo̱ omũsũṅ, ni mãdši enyo̱ aadše̱ omūsūṅ bẽbe agbla ame̱mli; ni maṅ kome he aawa ſè maṅ ko le̱, ni *onukpa le̱ aasúmo̱ gbekẽ le̱. *

english_verse: the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau.
translation_verse: Kleṅkleṅmo ni ba le̱, etšuo̱ fö̱, ke̱ ehe fẽ sulaṅṅ tamo̱ bò ni ake̱ tšo̱i lò, ni ame̱wole̱ Esau.

english_verse: The second baby grabbed on to his brother's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ le̱ enyemi le̱ hũ ha, ni enine hĩe Esau nanetšitši mli, ni awole̱ Iakob. Ni beni afo̱ame̱ le̱ Isak eye afii nyoṅmai-ekpa.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Ni Isak sumoo̱ Esau, edšake̱ mĩle̱lo ṅõ enā; ši Rebeka sumoo̱ Iakob.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ho niyenii ko. Ni Esau dše̱ ṅãṅ eba ni eto̱le̱.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Ni Esau kē̱ Iakob ake̱: Mīkpao fai, hãmi pe̱ke̱ nitšuru ne̱ eko maye, ši eto̱mi! Nohewo̱ le̱ awole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Edom.

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ši Iakob kē̱: Hõmo̱ okromo̱bi-gbe̱nā le̱ ohãmi dãl

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Ni Esau kē̱: Na, gbo mibagbo sa, ni meni kromo̱bi-gbe̱nā nē̱ bafe ahãmi?

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ ake̱: Kãmi no̱ kitã dã! Ni ekãle̱ no̱ kitã, ni *ehõ ekromo̱bi-gbe̱nā le̱ ebã Iakob. *

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iakob bã Esau abolo ke̱ abo̱bo̱i ní eho le̱ eko; ni eye ni enu noko eſie no̱, ni ete ši, ni eyiṅ ete. Ne̱ke̱ Esau gbe ekromo̱bi-gbe̱nã le̱ he guo̱.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Ni hõmo̱ ha šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, sōro *kleṅkleṅ hõmo̱ ni ba ye̱ Abraham yino̱ le̱; ni Isak yiṅ ete Filistibii amaṅtše̱ †Abimelek ṅõ ye̱ Gerar. *

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Ni mahã oseši *afá tamo̱ ṅwei ṅulamii, ni maṅõ ne̱ke̱ šikpõdši ne̱ fẽ mahã oseši le̱, ni oseši le̱ †mli aadše̱ adšō̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšeṅmādši le̱ fẽ; *

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: Ni Isak hĩ ši ye̱ Gerar.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Ni dše̱ibii le̱ bi eṅã le̱ ši; ni ekē̱ akē̱: Minyemiyō ni; edšakē̱ ēše gbeyei ake̱ eekē̱ ake̱: Miṅã ni, ekē̱: Beni afe ni dše̱ibii le̱ akabagbemi ye̱ Rebeka hewo̱, edšake̱ ebe ye̱ fe̱o.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek tšē̱ Isak ni ekē̱ ake̱: Ei, yō le̱ oṅã ni kwá; ni té fe tēṅ ni okē̱ akē̱: Minyemiyõ dšile̱ le̱? Ni Isak kē̱le̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ mikē̱: Beni afe ní akabagbemi ye̱ ehewo̱.

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek wo maṅ le̱ fẽ kitã ake̱: Moni aata nū ne̱ lo eṅã le̱ he le̱, gbe aagbele̱!

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ tšṍ gbomo agbo, ni ehle ſeremo̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni etšṍ agbo kpanã.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: Eye̱ tōkui ke̱ tšinakui ke̱ webii pī; ni Filistibii le̱ ahĩe kõ eno̱.

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: Ni *nubui fẽ ni etše̱ Abraham tšũdši le̱ dše ye̱ etše̱ yino̱ le̱, Filistibii le̱ etšĩmo̱, ni amelō sũ ame̱wo mli totō̱to̱. *

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek kē̱ Isak ake̱: Dše wo̱mase̱i, ši ohe wa babaō fèwo̱!

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Ni Isak sā edše nubui le̱ ni adše ye̱ etše̱ Abraham yino̱ le̱, edšake̱ Abraham gbẽle se̱ le̱ Filistibii le̱ tšĩmo̱; ni eṅõ gbe̱ii ni etše̱ ṅõ-woame̱ le̱ noṅṅ ewoame̱.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Ni Isak tšũdši le̱ tša dšō̱ le̱ mli, ni ame̱ná nubu ni baä nu ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Ni Gerar kolokwe̱le̱i ke̱ Isak kolokwe̱lo̱i le̱ bé ni ame̱kē̱: Nu le̱ wo̱nõṅ! ni ewo nubu le̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Esek, edšake̱ ame̱ke̱le̱ blo̱ ye̱ he.

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Ni edše dše̱i ete Beeršeba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa dšie ehe kpo etšõle̱ nakai nyõ le̱ṅ noṅṅ, ni eké̱: Midši otše̱ Abraham Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; kãše gbeyei, ši mike̱o ye̱, ni madšō̱o, ni mahã oseši afá ye̱ mitšũlo̱ Abraham hewo̱.

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Ni emã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni etšé̱ Iehowa gbe̱i, ni eši ebū le̱ ye̱ dše̱i; ni Isak tšũdši le̱ dše nubu ye̱ dše̱i hũ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek ke̱ enanyo Ahuzat ke̱ etatše̱ Fikol dše Gerar ba Isak ṅõ.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Ni Isak kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Meni bewo̱ nyebaä miṅõ, nye ni nyenye̱o̱mi, ni nyeſiemi ye̱ nyemase̱i le̱?

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Na wo̱na ake̱ Iehowa ke̱o ye̱; ni wo̱kē̱: Hã kitã ahĩ wo̱teṅ, wo̱ke̱o fẽ teṅ, ni ohã wo̱ke̱o akpãṅ,

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: ake̱ ofeṅwo̱ efõṅ ko; edšake̱ wo̱tako ohe, ni wo̱fekoö nokonoko, ake̱ dša ekpakpa ke̱ke̱, ni wosā wo̱woö gbe̱ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli. Ni agbe̱ne̱ bo Iehowa edšō̱ ne̱!

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ni eṅmẽame̱ okplõ, ni ame̱ye nii, ni ame̱nu noko.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ ake̱ Isak tšũdši le̱ ha ni ame̱bagbale̱ nubu ni ame̱dše le̱ he sane ake̱: Wo̱yanina nu.

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Ni ewole̱ *Šeba; nohewo̱ ni atšé̱o̱ maṅ le̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Beeršeba ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱ṅme̱ne̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Isak egbo̱, ni ebĩṅme̱ii ano̱ eha ni enaa nii dšogbāṅ le̱, etšé̱ ebi nukpa Esau le̱, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mibi! Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nami!

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: ni obafele̱ niyenii ke̱ ṅõmo̱, take̱ bo̱ni misumoo̱ le̱, ni oke̱-bahãmi, koni maye, beni afe ni misusuma adšō̱o, dãni magbo. Heb.

english_verse: Rebekah had been listening, and as soon as Esau left to go hunting,
translation_verse: Ni Rebeka nu, beni Isak ke̱ ebi Esau wieo̱ le̱. Ni Esau yiṅ ete ṅã le̱ṅ eyatao mĩle̱lo ke̱-ba.

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Ni Rebeka yakē̱ ebi Iakob ake̱: Na, minu ake̱ otše̱ ke̱ onyemi Esau miwie ake̱:

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: Yatao mĩle̱lo, ni ofele̱ niyenii ke̱ ṅõmo̱ obahãmi, koni maye, ni madšō̱o ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, dãni magbo.

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Ya tōi le̱ ateṅ ní oyamõmo̱ tōbii kpakpai enyo̱ ye̱ abotiai le̱ ateṅ obahãmi, ni maṅõ-fe niyenii ke̱ ṅõmo̱ mahã otše̱, take̱ bo̱ni esumoo̱ le̱,

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ enye Rebeka ake̱: Na, minyemi *Esau le̱, tšo̱iatše̱ dšile̱, ni mi le̱, mihe ye̱ trotro. *

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Ni enye kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mi ne̱ olōmo̱ le̱ aba, mibi, bo migbẽ toi ke̱ke̱, ni oyamõmo̱ obahãmi!

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ete, ni eyamõmo̱ ni eke̱bahã enye; ni enye ṅõ-fe niyenii ke̱ ṅõmo̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni etše̱ sumoo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: Ni Rebeka kō̱lo̱ ebi nukpa Esau atadei fe̱fe̱dši ní yo̱ eṅõ ye̱ šĩa le̱, ni eṅṍ-wo Iakob, ebi gbekẽ le̱;

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: ni eṅõ tōbii le̱ ahe wodši le̱ ewo enidši ke̱ ekue̱, hei ní ye̱ trotro le̱;

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Ni eba etše̱ ṅõ ni ebakē̱: Mitše̱! Ni ekē̱: Nami! Bo namoṅ, mibi?

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Mi, Esau, okromo̱bi le̱ṅ; mife be̱ni okē̱mi le̱. Ofai ne̱, te ši otá ši, ni oye mimĩle̱lo le̱ eko, koni osusuma adšō̱mi!

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Ni Isak kē̱ Iakob ake̱: Tši oba, mibi, ni matăra ohe makwe̱ ake̱ mibi Esau dientše̱ dšio lo dšee le̱ ni.

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Ni Iakob tši ebe̱ṅke̱ etše̱ Isak, ni etāra ebe, ni ekē̱: Gbē le̱ Iakob gbē ni, Ši nidši le̱ Esau nidši ni.

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Ni etši eba ni ebaſo̱ enā; ni enu etadei le̱ amli ṅma le̱, ni edšō̱le̱ ni ekē̱: Kwē̱, mibi lē̱ he ṅma tamo̱ ṅã ko ni Iehowa edšō̱ le̱ ṅma!

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ ahão ṅwei hō̱ ke̱ šikpoṅ fo̱ le̱ eko ke̱ ṅmā̃ ke̱ wein babaō hũ.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Mãdši asúmo̱o, ni dšeṅmãdši akotóö. Ye onyemimei le̱ ano̱ *nuṅtšo̱, ni onye bihĩĩ akotoö. Mofẽmo ni †lomoo̱o le̱, aalomo̱le̱; ni mofẽmo ní dšō̱o̱o le̱, aadšō̱le̱! *

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Isak egbe Iakob dšō̱mo̱ le̱ nā, ni Iakob kē̱ edšeo̱ etše̱ Isak hĩe pe̱ le̱, enyemi Esau hũ dše̱ emĩle̱ le̱ eba;

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: ni le̱ hũ efe niyenii ke̱ ṅõmo̱ ni eke̱-bahã etše̱, ni ekē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Hã mitše̱ ate ši, ni eye ehi mĩle̱lo le̱ eko, koni osusuma adšō̱mi.

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ni etše̱ Isak kē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo namoṅ? Ni ekē̱: Mi, obi, okromo̱bi Esau ni.

english_verse: Esau cried out in great distress, “Father, give me a blessing too!”
translation_verse: Ni beni Esau nu etše̱ wiemo̱i le̱, ebo wā dientše̱ ke̱ aw̌ere̱hō babaō, ni ekē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Mi hũ, dšō̱mo̱mi eko, mitše̱! Heb.

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Egbe̱i *Iakob ni awole̱ le̱ edi ehe. Šii enyo̱ so̱ṅṅ ní etõtṍo̱ minane ne̱: †mikromo̱bi-gbe̱nā le̱ ešõ, ni na, agbe̱ne̱ ebaṅõ midšō̱mo̱ le̱ bũ! Ni ekē̱: Ani oſe̱e̱ dšō̱mo̱ le̱ eko ohããmi? *

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Ni Isak to be ni ekē̱ Esau ake̱: Na, miwole̱ ono̱ nuṅtšo̱, ni miṅṍ enyemimei le̱ fẽ mife etšũdši, ni miṅṍ ṅmā̃ ke̱ wein mihãle̱; ni bo le̱, meni mafe mahão mo̱, mibi?

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Ni Esau kē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Ani no kome pe̱ dši dšō̱mo̱ ni oyo̱, mitše̱? Mi hũ dšō̱mo̱mi eko, mitše̱! Ni Esau wó egbẽ ni efó.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Ni etše̱ Isak to he, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, heni šikpoṅ fo̱ be̱ oohĩ ke̱ heni ṅwei bō̱ hũ be̱;

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: ni oklante nā oyi aaná wala ye̱, ni onyemi le̱ oosúmo̱. Ši aaba mli ake̱, ké̱ ople ohe le̱, oohwãnyã epã le̱ ke̱-dše okue̱.

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ni Esau nye̱ Iakob ye̱ dšō̱mo̱ ni etše̱ dšō̱le̱ le̱ hewo̱. Ni Esau kē̱ ye̱ etšui mli ake̱: Gbĩĩ ní ake̱-bafó mitše̱ le̱ eše̱ etã, ni magbe minyemi Iakob.

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Ni abagba Rebeka ebi nukpa Esau wiemo̱i ne̱; ni etšũ ayatšé̱ Iakob, ebi gbekẽ le̱, ke̱-ba, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, onyemi Esau bato̱ ehe owele ye̱ ono̱ ni egbeo.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, mibi, bo migbē toi, ni ote ši ni odšo foi ke̱-ya minyemi Laban ṅõ ye̱ *Haran, *

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: ni oke̱le̱ ayaht ši gbĩĩ flō ko ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni onyemi le̱ mlila le̱ aadše emli,

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni onyemi le̱ mlifũ ní enáo le̱ aadše emli, ni ehĩe aakpa noni ofele̱ le̱ no̱, koni matšũ ni abaṅõo ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i ke̱-ba; mẽba nyeyi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ nyeaṅmẽmi gbī kome?

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Ni Rebeka kē̱ Isak ake̱: Midšeṅhĩle̱ edše mitšine ye̱ Hetbiyei le̱ ahewo̱. Ke̱-dši Iakob w̌e̱ Hetbiyei ni tame̱ mene̱mei ni dši šikpoṅ ne̱, no̱ biyei le̱ eko le̱, té mahĩ dšeṅ make̱ tẽṅ?

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: ni eṅõ *Abraham dšō̱mo̱ le̱ ehão ke̱ oseši fẽ, koni ofe ogbo̱tō šikpoṅ ne̱ ni Nyóṅmo̱ ṅõ-bã Abraham le̱ yelo̱; *

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Ni beni Esau na ake̱ Isak edšō̱ Iakob, ni ewole̱ gbe̱ ke̱-te Mesopotamia, ni eyaw̌e̱ yō ye̱ dše̱i, ni asaṅ beni edšō̱le̱ le̱, ewole̱ kitã ake̱: Kāw̌e̱ yō ye̱ Kanaan biyei le̱ ateṅ,

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: ni Esau sā na ake̱ etše̱ Isak nyã́ã́ Kanaan biyei le̱ ahe le̱:

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: Esau yiṅ ete Abraham bi Išmael ṅõ, ni eyaw̌e̱ ebiyō Mahalat, *Nebaiot nyemiyõ le̱, †efata eṅãmei ni eyo̱ le̱ ahe. *

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob dše̱ Beeršeba ēya Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Ni eše̱ heko ni eto dše̱i, edšake̱ hũlũ enyõ ši; ni eko̱ dše̱i te̱i le̱ eko etšo̱le, ni ekā dše̱i ewo̱.

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Ni Iakob hĩe tšẽ kē̱-dše̱ ewo̱ le̱ mli ni ekē̱: Iehowa ye̱ bie̱ kwá, ni mi le̱ milee ne̱!

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Ni eše gbeyei ni ekē̱: Bie̱ ne̱ ye̱ *gbeyei pi! Bie̱ ne̱ dšee hekoheko ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we ne̱, ni ṅwei agbó ne̱! *

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni etē te̱ le̱ ni etšo̱le le̱ ši emã ši eṅõ-to okadi, ni efo̱se mũ eſie yiteṅ;

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: ni ewo dše̱i *Betel; ši sá le̱ nakai maṅ le̱ gbe̱i dši Luz. *

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Ni Iakob wo ši ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱mi hĩ ši, ni ebu mihe ye̱ gbe̱ ni miyanyie ne̱ mli, ni ehãmi ṅmā̃ miye ke̱ atade miwo,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ni mikũ mise̱ miba mitše̱ we le̱ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli le̱, no le̱ Iehowa aatšṍ mi-Nyoṅmo̱;

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: ni ne̱ke̱ te̱ ni miṅṍ-mã ši mito okadi ne̱ *aatšṍ Nyoṅmo̱ we; ni nibii fẽ ni oohãmi le̱, maṅõ mlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekome mahão. *

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iakob wó enane no̱ ni eba bokãgbe̱bii ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Ni ekwe̱, ni na, nubu ko ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni na, tōkui etẽ dſehe he ye̱ dše̱i; edšake̱ nakai bu le̱ mli nu le̱ aye̱e̱ ahãa tōi le̱ nuo̱; ni te̱ kpeteṅkple kã bu le̱ nā

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Minyemimei, nẽgbe̱ nyedše̱? Ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱dšē̱ Haran.

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ni ebiame̱ ake̱: Ani nyele Nahor bi Laban le̱? Ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱lelē̱.

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Ni ebiame̱ ake̱: Ani eye̱ dšogbāṅ lo? Ni ame̱kē̱: Eye̱ dšogbãṅ; ni na, ebiyō Rahel ke̱ tōi baä ne̱!

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Ni eké̱: Na, dše nako kwrā, ni eše̱ko koloi awo̱be; nyehãa tōi le̱ anua nu, ni nyeyahãaame̱ nii!

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ké̱: Wo̱nyẽṅ, dša abna tō-kuikui le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱koklo te̱ le̱ ke̱-dše bu le̱ nā, dãni wo̱o̱hã tōi le̱ anu.

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Ni beni eke̱ame̱ wieo̱ lolo le̱, Rahel ke̱ etše̱ tōi le̱ ba, edšake̱ le̱ ekwe̱o̱ame̱.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ſo̱ Rahel nā, ewó egbẽ no̱ ni efó.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ Rahel ake̱ etše̱ nyemi dšile̱, ni Rebeka bi dšile̱; ke̱ke̱ ni eša foi ete ni eyakē̱ etše̱.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Laban nu enyemibi Iakob sane le̱ he le̱, eša foi etele̱ kpẽmo̱, ni elōle̱ atū ni eſo̱ enā, ni eke̱le̱ ba ewe le̱; ni egba Laban sãdši ne̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱le̱ ake̱: Asano̱kwa, miwú ke̱ mihelo dšio! Ni eke̱le̱ hĩ ši nyõṅ kome.

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱ Iakob ake̱: Ake̱-ní oyafe minyemi hewo̱ le̱, oosúmo̱mi yaka lo? Tšõmo̱ bo̱ni oohemi.

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Ni Lea hĩṅme̱ii ye̱ sukusuku, ši Rahel he ye̱ fe̱o ni ehĩe hũ ye̱ fe̱o.

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱: Ehĩ ake̱ mike̱le̱ hãao fè noni mike̱le̱ aahã nū kroko; oke̱mi ahĩ ši!

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob súmo̱ afii kpawo ye̱ Rahel hewo̱, ni suomo̱ ní esumoo̱le̱ hewo̱ le̱, efele̱ tamo̱ gbĩ komekome ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ Laban ake̱: Oke̱ miṅã le̱ ahãmi, koni ebawo̱ miṅō, edšake̱ mi-gbĩĩ le̱ eše̱.

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ni Laban bua dše̱i bii le̱ fẽ nā, ni eṅmẽ okplõ.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Ni gbe̱ke̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ eṅõ ebiyō Lea ni eke̱le̱ bahãle̱; ni ebawo̱ eṅõ.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Ni Laban ṅõ eweyō Zilpa ehã ebi Lea, ni efe eweyõ.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni dše tše̱re le̱, na, Lea ni. Ni ekē̱ Laban ake̱: Meni ofemi ne̱? Ani dšee Rahel hewo̱ ni misúmo̱o le̱? Mẽhewo̱ mo̱ ni ošišiumi ne̱?

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱: Wo̱bie̱ ne̱ afee nakai, ahãã gbekẽ gblã dāni ahã kromo̱bi.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Gbe mone̱ otši le̱ nā, ni wo̱ke̱ mokroko le̱ hũ aahão ye̱ súomo̱ ní oosúmo̱mi afii kpawo kroko hũ hewo̱.

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iehowa na ake̱ asumo̱o̱ Lea le̱, egble emũsũ nā, ši Rahel fe kene.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Ni Lea ná mũsũ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Ruben, ni eke̱: Edšake̱ Iehowa ekwe̱ mimanehũlũ le̱; ni agbe̱ne̱ miwù basumo̱mi!

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ni ená mũsũ ekoṅ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ekē̱: Edšakē̱ Iehowa enu ake̱ asumo̱o̱-mi, hewo̱ le̱ ehāmi bi ne̱ bũ, ni ewole̱ Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Ni esā ená mũsũ, ni efo̱ binù, ni ekē̱: Ene̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ miwù ke̱ ehe aakpe̱te̱ mihe, edšake̱ mike̱le̱ efo̱ bihĩĩ etẽ; nohewo̱ le̱ ewole̱ Levi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ni ená mũsũ ekoṅ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ekē̱: Ene̱ le̱ madšie Iehowa yi; nohe-wo̱ le̱ ewole̱ Iuda. Ni efo fo̱mo̱ dã.

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Na, miweyō Bilha; hã ebawo̱ oṅõ, *ni efo̱ eſie miſuo̱ no̱, koni mi hū matšṍ eno̱ maná bii. *

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Ni Rahel ké̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ekodšo ehã-mi, ni enu migbē hũ, ni ehãmi binū; nohewo̱ lo̱ ewole̱ Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Ni Bilha, Rahel weyō le̱, ná mũsũ ekoṅ, ni eke̱ Iakob fo̱ binū ni dši enyo̱.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ni Rahel ké̱: Mike̱ minyemiyō le̱ eši Nyoṅmo̱ mple, ni minyẽle̱! Ni ewole̱ Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Ni beni Lea na ake̱ efo fo̱mo̱ le̱, le̱ hũ eṅõ eweyō Zilpa le̱ ehã Iakob gblā.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Ni Lea weyō Zilpa le̱ ke̱ Iakob fo̱ binū.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Ni Lea kē̱: Asafo eba! ni ewole̱ Gad.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Ni Lea kē̱: Midšō̱mo̱ mli nē̱! edšake̱ biyei badšō̱mi; ni ewole̱ Ašer.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Ni ṅmā̃kū̃ be mli le̱ Ruben yana suomo̱yibii ko ye̱ ṅãno̱, ni eke̱-bahã enye Lea. Ke̱ke̱ ni Rahel kē̱ Lea akē̱: Mīkpao fai ni ohãmi obi lē̱ suomo̱yibii le̱ eko!

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Aso ni ošõ miwù le̱, no fáá, ši obašõ mibi le̱ suomo̱yibii le̱ hũ? Ni Rahel kē̱: Nohewo̱ le̱ yawo̱ eṅõ ṅme̱no̱ nyõ ne̱ṅ ye̱ obi le̱ suomo̱yibii le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ bo Lea toi, ni ená mũsũ, ni eke̱ Iakob fo̱ binū ni dši enumo̱.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Ni Lea kē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ehãmi mipābō̱nii, edšake̱ mike̱ miweyō le̱ ehã miwù gblã; ni ewole̱ Isakar.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ le̱ efo̱ biyō, ni ewole̱ Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Ni ená mũsũ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ekē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ edšie *mihĩegbĕle le̱; Ies.

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: ni ewole̱ Iosef, ni ekē̱: Iehowa aaṅõ bi kroko afata he ahãmi!

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake, beni Rahel efo̱ Iosef se̱ le̱, Iakob kē̱ Laban akē̱: Womi gbe̱, koni maya midientše̱ midšē̱he ke̱ mišikpoṅ no̱.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Oke̱ miṅãmei ke̱ mibii ni *misúmo̱o ye̱ ame̱hewo̱ le̱ ahāmi, ni maya; ši bo-dientše̱ ole bo̱ni misúmo̱o mihã. *

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bodientše̱ ole, bo̱ni misúmo̱o mihá, ke̱ bo̱ hũ ni okoloi le̱ ht miṅõ hã.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Ši fiõ ko oyo̱ beni miba le̱, ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱ ame̱ſere babaõ, ni Iehowa etšṍ minine no̱ edšō̱o, ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, té gbĩ ni makwe̱ midientše̱ miwe hũ?

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Meni mahão? Ni Iakob kē̱: Kāhãmi nokonoko; kē̱dši oofe ene̱ ohãmi le̱, no le̱ masã malè̱ okoloi le̱, ni ma-kwe̱ame̱ ekoṅ:

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Nme̱ne̱ makpa otoi le̱ fẽ mli, ni mahala tõbi-fẽ-tõbi ni he yo̱ truntrãi ke̱ damdam, ke̱ tōbi-fẽ-tōbi ni dĩo̱ ye̱ tō-gwanteṅi le̱ amli, ke̱ abotiai le̱ ateṅ nii ni he yo̱ damdam ke̱ nii ni be yo̱ truntrãi le̱; ni nomei aatšṍ minyṍmo̱wo,

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: koni wō̱ lo wō̱se̱, beni oobakwe̱ minyõmo̱wo le̱, midšale̱ le̱ adšie minã ye̱ ohĩe; abotiai le̱ ateṅ nii ní be be̱ truntrãi ke̱ damdam, ke̱ gwanteṅi le̱ amli nii ni be dĩĩ le̱, dšũnii dši no ye̱ mideṅ.

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱: Na, bã afe be̱ni okē̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ eyahala tōkpakpoi ni he ye̱ sãmãisãmãi ke̱ damdam, kē̱ abotiai le̱ ateṅ nii ni he yo̱ truntrãi ke̱ damdam le̱ fẽ, nofẽno ní eye̱ṅ ta ehe ke̱ nii fẽ ni he dĩo̱ ye̱ gwanteṅi le̱ ateṅ, ni etuame̱ ewo ebihĩĩ le̱ adeṅ.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ gbĩĩ etẽ gbe̱ eto ame̱ ke̱ le̱ Iakob le̱ teṅ. Ni Iakob yalè̱ Laban tōi ní ſe̱ le̱.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kō̱le̱ libne-tšei ṅmõdši ke̱ luz-tšei ke̱ harmon-tšei, ni eye ame̱he sāmãi ye̱dši, ni ebã tšei le̱ amli eye̱dši le̱ dše ši.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ tšei ni eye ame̱he sãmãi le̱ eſie nunumo̱ ahĩmai le̱ ni tōi le̱ banuo̱ nu ye̱ṅ le̱ amli, ye̱ tōi le̱ ahĩe, ní ké̱ amē̱ba nunumo̱ lē̱, ame̱náa mũsũ.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob tšere̱ tōgwanteṅbii le̱ eto afã, ni etšṍmo̱ tōi le̱ ahle ehã Laban tōi le̱ ateṅ nii ní he yo̱ sãmãisãmãi le̱ ke̱ nii ní dĩo̱ le̱ fë; ni eṅõ le̱dientše̱ etōku le̱ eto afã, ni eke̱ame̱ futuu Laban tōi le̱.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ dāne̱ ké̱ tōi ni be wa le̱ ná mũsũ le̱, Iakob ṅõo̱ tšei le̱ eſieo̱ tōi le̱ ahĩe ye̱ ahĩmai le̱ amli, koni ame̱ná mũsũ ye̱ tšei le̱ ahe.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ tōi le̱ ye̱ wudo̱wudo̱ le̱, no le̱ eṅṍ-ſiee mli; nohewo̱ le̱ wudo̱wudo̱i le̱ tšṍmoo̱ Laban nii, ni nii ní be wa le̱ tšṍmoo̱ Iakob nii.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ni gbomo le̱ ſere naakpa dientše̱, ni ená tōi pī ke̱ weyei ke̱ wehĩĩ ke̱ yomai ke̱ tedšii.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Ni enu ni Laban *bihĩĩ le̱ mīwiewie ake̱: Iakob ešõ wo̱tše̱ nii fẽ, ni we̱tše̱ nii le̱ eke̱-ná ehe ne̱. *

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob tšũ ayatšē̱ Rahel ke̱ Lea ke̱-ba ṅã le̱ no̱ heni etōi le̱ yo̱ le̱,

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mina nyetše̱ hĩe, ake̱ etšee ehĩe ehããmi tamo̱ sá le̱; ši *mitše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱mi ye̱.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ekē̱: Nii ni be yo̱ *truntrãi le̱ atšṍ onyõmo̱wo le̱, bĕle̱ tōi le̱ fẽ efo̱ truntrãi; ni ke̱dši ekē̱: Nii ni he yo̱ sãmãisãmãi le̱ atšṍ onyõmo̱wo le̱, bẽle̱ tōi le̱ fẽ efo̱ nii ni he yo̱ sãmãisãmãi. *

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ fe ešõ ṅyetše̱ koloi le̱ ehãmi.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: Ni eba mii ake̱ tōi le̱ amũsũnámo̱ be mli le̱ mihole mihĩṅme̱ii ano̱, ni mina ye̱ lamõ mli, ake̱ tōkpakpoi ní kwo̱ō̱ tōi le̱ ahe ye̱ sãmãisãmãi ke̱ truntrãi ke̱ ṅwãtãṅwãtã.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Midši *Betel, heni ofo̱ okadite̱ le̱ mũ ni owomi ši ye̱ le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ le̱. Aghe̱ne̱ te ši, dše šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱, ni okũ ose̱ oya owekumei ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ani dšee meikpõdši ebuo̱wo̱? edšake̱ *ehõwe̱, ni eye wo̱yinii le̱ hũ.

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iakob te ši ni eṅõ ebii ke̱ eṅãmei le̱ etrá yomai ano̱,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: ni ekpla ekoloi le̱ fẽ, ke̱ enii fẽ ni ená le̱, koloi ni elē̱ ni ená ye̱ Mesopotamia le̱, koni eya etše̱ Isak ṅõ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eke̱ nii ni eyo̱ le̱ fẽ dšo foi; ni ete ši ni eyafo fã le̱, ni eṅõ ehĩe eka Gilead goṅ le̱.

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Laban yanina Iakob; ni Iakob eši ebū ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱, ni Laban hũ ke̱ enyemimei le̱ baši ame̱būi le̱ ye̱ Gilead goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱ Iakob ake̱: Meni ofe ne̱, ake̱ odšu mitšui ni olō mibiyei le̱ ke̱-mĩya take̱ mei ní aṅõame̱ nom ye̱ klante nā ne̱?

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Ši mofẽmo dẽ ní oona onyoṅmo̱i le̱ ye̱ le̱, kāhã ehĩ dšeṅl Wo̱nyemimei ne̱ ahĩe ne̱, taomo̱ noni dši onõ ní yo̱ miṅõ, ni oko̱ onii ke̱-ya. Ši Iakob lee ake̱ Rahel edšu. K.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Laban te Iakob bū le̱ mli ke̱ Lea bū le̱ mli ke̱ weyei enyo̱ le̱ abūi le̱ hũ mli, ši enaa; ni edše Lea bū le̱ mli ete Rahel bū le̱ mli.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Ši Rahel ekō̱lo̱ amãgãi le̱, ni eṅõwo yoma le̱ no̱nii le̱ mli, ni eho etá no̱; ni Laban nyẽmo̱nyẽmo̱ ši ye̱ bū le̱ṅ fẽ, ši enaa.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Akafe minuṅtšo̱ mlifũ ake̱ minyẽẽ ši mate ye̱ ohĩe le̱; ši mife yeianii. Ni ekpa ši etao amāgãi le̱ āhũ, ši enaa.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Ni Iakob mli wo la, ni eke̱ Laban bé. Ni Iakob here no̱ ni ekē̱ Laban ake̱: Mẽ tõ mitõ, ni mẽ eša hũ mife, ni ohĩe edo̱ ke̱-nyie mise̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Kole̱ ni otãratăra minibii fẽ he ne̱, meni ona ní dši ošĩa nibii le̱ eko? Nõ sane ne̱ oṅmẽ minyemimei ke̱ bo hũ onyemimei ne̱ ahĩe ye̱ bie̱, ni ame̱kodšo wo̱yi enyo̱ le̱ wo̱teṅ.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Noni koloi ye hū mike̱-bahãão, mi mitoo̱ nãdšiaṅ, ké̱ ſane adšu eko dšio, nyōṅ adšu eko dšio, *mideṅ oheo̱ ye̱. *

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Noni mina ne̱: latšā tšaämi ſane, ni fẽi yeo̱mi nyōṅ, ni miwo̱ hũ tšere̱o̱ ye̱ mihĩe.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Ni Laban here no̱ ni ekē̱ Iakob akē̱: Biyei nē̱ mibiyei ni, ni bii ne̱ hũ mibii ni, tōi ne̱ hũ mitōi ni, ni nibii ní onaä ne̱ fē le̱ minii ni; ši meni mawo mibiyei ne̱ ke̱ ame̱bii ni ame̱fo̱fo̱i le̱ afemo̱ ṅme̱ne̱?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ba, ni wo̱kpãṅ, mi ke̱ bo, ní atšŏ odase ye̱ mike̱o teṅ.

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob wó te̱ emā ši eṅõ-to *okadi.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ enyemimei le̱ ake̱: Nyebuaä te̱i anā! Ni ame̱kö̱lo̱ te̱i ni ame̱tole̱ ku; ni ame̱ye nii ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ ku le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Ni Laban wole̱ Iegar-Sahaduta; ši Iakob le̱ ewole̱ Galed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Ni Laban kē̱: Ne̱kē̱ ku ne̱ mĩye *odase ye̱ mike̱o teṅ ṅme̱ne̱; nohewo̱ atšé̱o̱ egbe̱i Galed, *Ios.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Ke̱dši oowa mibiyei le̱ ayi, alo oow̌e̱ yei krokomei ofata mibiyei le̱ ahe le̱, no le̱ gbomo ko fataa wo̱he moṅ, ši na, Nyoṅmo̱ dši odasefonyo ye̱ mike̱o teṅ!

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ ku ne̱ dši odase, ni ne̱ke̱ okadite̱ ne̱ hũ dši odase, ake̱ mi le̱ mihoṅ ku ne̱ he mibaṅ oṅõ, ni bo hũ ohoṅ ku ne̱ ke̱ okadite̱ ne̱ he obaṅ miṅõ ye̱ efõṅ-femo̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Abraham Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ Nahor Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ ame̱tše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ afe *ko-dšolo̱ ye̱ wo̱teṅ. Ni Iakob kã etše̱ Isak †gbeyeišeme̱ le̱ kitã. *

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iakob šã afo̱le ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱, ni etšé̱ enyemimei le̱ niyeli; ni ame̱ye nii, ni ame̱hi ši nyõ le̱ṅ fẽ ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ni lebi mā̃ṅkpa le̱ Laban te ši ni eſo̱ſō̱ ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ anã ni edšō̱ame̱. Ni Laban ṅõ-tšere̱ mli ke̱-kũ ese̱ ke̱-te emaṅ.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-tšṍ ehĩe ke̱-te enyemi Esau ṅõ ye̱ *Seir šikpoṅ ni dši Edom ṅã le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ni ewoame̱ kitã ake̱: Nyeyakē̱a minuṅtšo̱ Esau akē̱: Bo̱ni otšũlo̱ Iakob kē̱ ne̱: Miyato gbo̱ ye̱ Laban ṅõ, ni mitše̱ ye̱ dše̱i āhũ ke̱-baši bene̱,

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: ni miná tšinai ke̱ tedšii ke̱ tōi ke̱ tšūdšihĩĩ ke̱ tšũdšiyei; ni mitšũ ni abakē̱ minuṅtšo̱, koni mihĩe aba nyam ye̱ ohĩe.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Esau ba asafoku kome ne̱ no̱ ni ebatſiaame̱ nii le̱, koni ku kome ní eſe̱ le̱ aná gbe̱ adšo foi.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: omo̱bo̱nale̱i ke̱ onokwayeli fẽ ni odšie otšõ otšũlo̱ le̱, ekomeflo ne̱ke̱ *esaami; ši tšo mihĩe ke̱-fo Iordan ne̱, ni agbe̱ne̱ mitšṍ asafokui enyo. *

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob bile̱ ake̱: Mīkpao fai ni *otšõmi ogbe̱i! Ni ekē̱: Meni hewo̱ ni obio̱ migbe̱i ne̱? Ni edšō̱le̱ ye̱ dše̱i. *Kodš.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: no le̱ okē̱ ake̱: Otšũlo̱ Iakob nikẽnii ní etšũ ake̱ ake̱-bake minuṅtšo̱ Esau ni; ni na, le̱ hũ enyie wo̱se̱.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: ni nyesā nyekē̱ale̱ ake̱: Na, otšũlo̱ Iakob nyie wo̱se̱. Edšake̱ ekē̱: Mike̱ nikēnii ni nyie mihĩe ne̱ yakpãtãle̱, ni no se̱ dãni mayana ehĩe, ekole̱ eekwe̱ mihĩe.

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Ni ete ši nakai nyō le̱ṅ, ni eṅõ eṅãmei enyo̱ le̱ ke̱ eweyei enyo̱ le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ nyoṅma ke̱ ekome le̱ ni eyafo Iabok fōhe le̱;

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Ni ebaſe̱ Iakob kome. Ni nū ko ke̱le̱ banõ ke̱-yaši dšetše̱remo̱. Hos.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Ni beni ena ake̱ enyẽẽle̱ le̱, eta egboṅ talo̱ le̱ he, ni Iakob gboṅ talo̱ le̱ hwãṅ beni eke̱le̱ nõo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Hã maya, ši dše mītše̱re! Ši ekē̱: *Mihãṅ oya, dša odšō̱mi dã! *Mat.

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ ake̱: *Atšē̱ṅ ogbe̱i Iakob doṅṅ, ši Israel aatšē̱o; edšake̱ oke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ gbomei eši mple ni oye kũnim. *

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob wo dše̱i Peniel; edšake̱ ekē̱: *Mina Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe kē̱ hĩe, ši migboo. *

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Ni beni efoṅ ye̱ Peniel le̱, hũlũ dše ye̱ eno̱, ni etšutšo̱ ye̱ egboṅ le̱ mli.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ni lebi mā̃ṅkpa le̱ Laban te ši ni eſo̱ſō̱ ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ anã ni edšō̱ame̱. Ni Laban ṅõ-tšere̱ mli ke̱-kũ ese̱ ke̱-te emaṅ.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-tšṍ ehĩe ke̱-te enyemi Esau ṅõ ye̱ *Seir šikpoṅ ni dši Edom ṅã le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ni ewoame̱ kitã ake̱: Nyeyakē̱a minuṅtšo̱ Esau akē̱: Bo̱ni otšũlo̱ Iakob kē̱ ne̱: Miyato gbo̱ ye̱ Laban ṅõ, ni mitše̱ ye̱ dše̱i āhũ ke̱-baši bene̱,

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: ni miná tšinai ke̱ tedšii ke̱ tōi ke̱ tšūdšihĩĩ ke̱ tšũdšiyei; ni mitšũ ni abakē̱ minuṅtšo̱, koni mihĩe aba nyam ye̱ ohĩe.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Esau ba asafoku kome ne̱ no̱ ni ebatſiaame̱ nii le̱, koni ku kome ní eſe̱ le̱ aná gbe̱ adšo foi.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: omo̱bo̱nale̱i ke̱ onokwayeli fẽ ni odšie otšõ otšũlo̱ le̱, ekomeflo ne̱ke̱ *esaami; ši tšo mihĩe ke̱-fo Iordan ne̱, ni agbe̱ne̱ mitšṍ asafokui enyo. *

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob bile̱ ake̱: Mīkpao fai ni *otšõmi ogbe̱i! Ni ekē̱: Meni hewo̱ ni obio̱ migbe̱i ne̱? Ni edšō̱le̱ ye̱ dše̱i. *Kodš.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: no le̱ okē̱ ake̱: Otšũlo̱ Iakob nikẽnii ní etšũ ake̱ ake̱-bake minuṅtšo̱ Esau ni; ni na, le̱ hũ enyie wo̱se̱.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: ni nyesā nyekē̱ale̱ ake̱: Na, otšũlo̱ Iakob nyie wo̱se̱. Edšake̱ ekē̱: Mike̱ nikēnii ni nyie mihĩe ne̱ yakpãtãle̱, ni no se̱ dãni mayana ehĩe, ekole̱ eekwe̱ mihĩe.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Ni Esau ša foi eke̱le̱ bakpe, ni elōle̱ atū, ni eke̱ eyitšo fõ ekue̱ no̱, ni eſo̱ enā, ni ame̱fó.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
