translation_verse: Ni ehole ehīṅme̱ii ano̱, ni ena yei le̱ ke̱ gbekẽbii le̱, ni ekē̱: Namei dši mei ní fata ohe ne̱? Ni ekē̱: Bii *ní Nyoṅmo̱ edro otšũlo̱ le̱ ni. *Lal.

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni weyei le̱ tši ba, ame̱ke̱ ame̱bii le̱, ni ame̱bakoto ši.

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Ni Esau kē̱: Bo̱ni miyo̱ le̱ fá, minyemi, hã onõ le̱ ahĩ ši ahão!

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱: Dabida, mĩkpao fai, ni ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe le̱, no le̱ hemo̱ mideṅ nikēnii le̱; ši ni mina ohĩe ne̱, tamo̱ noni mina *Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, ni oná mihe tšui hũ. *

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Mīkpao fai ni ohe *minikẽnii ni ake̱-bahão ne̱; edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ edromi, ni misã miye̱ nofēno hũ. Ni ehĩele̱ āhũ, ni ehe. *

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱ le ake̱ gbekẽbii le̱ ahĩe esako, ni tōi ke̱ tšinai ni bãa fufo̱ fata mihe; ni ke̱dši atšire̱ ame̱yise̱ gbĩ kome dšenamo̱ le̱, koloi le̱ fẽ aabagboi.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ hã ni minuṅtšo̱ atšṍ etšũlo̱ hĩe, ni mi le̱ manyie ble̱ōble̱ō, bo̱ni koloi le̱ ni nyie mihĩe le̱ ke̱ gbekẽbii le̱ aanyẽ, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní maba minuṅtšo̱ ṅõ ye̱ Seir.

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Ni Esau kē̱: Hã mašĩ mei ni ke̱mi nyie lē̱ eko mato ohe. Ni ekē̱: Mēba ehia? Hã ni mihĩe aba nyam ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ hĩe ke̱ke̱!

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-te Sukot, ni eyamã etšũ ye̱ dše̱i, ni efe asesei ehã ekoloi le̱; nohewo̱ le̱ awo dše̱i Sukot.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob še̱ šekem maṅ le̱ ni yo̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ſeſēſe, beni edše̱ Mesopotamia ebaä le̱, ni ebašišĩ ebūi ye̱ maṅ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Ni ebā dſie̱te̱i kukudši oba *eke̱he šikpoṅ le̱ ni eši ebū le̱ ye̱ no̱ le̱, ye̱ Šekem tše̱ Hamor bii le̱ adeṅ. *Ios.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni emã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni ewole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Israel Nyoṅmo̱ Mawu le nõ.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Ni Dina, Lea hiyõ le̱ *ní eke̱ Iakob fo̱ le̱, dše kpo ete šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ biyei le̱ akwe̱mo̱. *

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Ni etšui mõ Iakob biyō Dina le̱, ni ešumo̱ oblayō le̱ sane, ni ehã oblayō le̱ tšui.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Ni Šekem kē̱ etše̱ Hamor ake̱: Yaw̌e̱ ne̱ke̱ oblayō ne̱ ohãmi.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Ni Hamor ke̱ame̱ wie ekē̱: Mibi Šekem tšui emõ nyebiyō le̱; mĩkpanye fai ni nyeṅõle̱ nyehãle̱ gblã.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Nyeke̱wo̱ ayea yōw̌ē̱; nyeṅōa nyebiyei nyehãawo̱ gblã, ni nye hũ nyew̌e̱ wo̱biyei,

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: ni nyeke̱wo̱ ahĩa ši. Šikpoṅ le̱ nā kã hãnye; nyehĩa no̱, ni nyetšu no̱ nii, ni nyenáa nii ye̱ no̱.

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Ni Šekem kē̱ etše̱ ke̱ enyemimei le̱ ake̱: Nyehãa mihĩe abaä nyam ye̱ nyebleaṅ, ši nofẽno ni nyeabimi le̱, mahã.

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Nyebiami gblãnii ke̱ kẽnii bo̱fẽbo̱, ni bo̱ni nyeabimi le̱ mahãnye, koni nyeṅõ oblayō le̱ nye̱bãmi.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob bii le̱ wie ni ame̱ke̱ hĩelakamo̱ hã Šekem ke̱ etše̱ Hamor hetō, edšake̱ ebule ame̱nyemiyō Dina le̱,

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Wo̱nyẽṅ ne̱ke̱ sane wo̱ye, ni wo̱ṅõ wo̱nyemiyõ le̱ wo̱hã moko ní dši fōlo̱, edšake̱ no le̱ wo̱to kpa.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Ši gbe̱ no̱ ni wo̱o̱kplẽnye ke̱ke̱ ne̱: ke̱dši nyeatšṍmo̱ tamo̱wo̱, ni aaflo̱ nyeteṅ hĩĩ fẽ ketia le̱.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: No le̱ wo̱o̱ṅõ wo̱biyei wo̱hãnye gblã, ni wo̱ hũ wo̱o̱ṅõ nyebiyei, ni wo̱ke̱nye aabī ši, ni woo̱tšṍ maṅ kome.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeboowo̱ toi ní nyehã aflo̱nye ketia le̱, no le̱ wo̱o̱ṅõ wo̱biyō le̱ ní wo̱ya

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wiemo̱i le̱ sa Hamor ke̱ Hamor bi Šekem hĩe.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Ni oblanyo le̱ eṅõõ nakai nii le̱ femo̱ le̱ ešašaoo ši, edšake̱ eye̱ Iakob biyō le̱ be tšui. Ni abuo̱le̱ fè etše̱ we le̱ bii fẽ.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Ni Hamor ke̱ebi Šekem le̱ ba ame̱mā le̱ṅ agbó le̱ nā, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱mã le̱ṅ hĩĩ le̱ wie ní ame̱kē̱:

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Ši kē̱ aflo̱ wo̱teṅ hĩĩ fẽ ketia, tamo̱ bo̱ni aflo̱ame̱ le̱, dša no, dãni gbomei le̱ aakplẽ wo̱ke̱ šihĩle̱, ni ame̱ke̱wo̱ aafe maṅ kome.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Ame̱kolokui ke̱ ame̱nii ní ame̱yo̱ ke̱ ame̱šĩa koloi fẽ le̱, dšee wo̱nii ebatšṍmo̱ṅ? Nyehãa wo̱kplẽa wo̱hãa-ame̱ ke̱ke̱, ni ame̱ke̱wo̱ ahī ši.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱, beni ame̱fadši le̱ ewo wu le̱, Iakob bihĩĩ enyo̱ *ni dši Simeon ke̱ Levi, Dina nyemimei le̱, kŏ̱lo̱ ame̱klantei ni amebatua maṅ le trukã, ni amegbe hĩĩ le̱ fē; *

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: ni ame̱gbe Hamor ke̱ ebi Šekem hũ ye̱ klante nā, ni ame̱yaṅõ Dina ye̱ Šekem we le̱, ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob bihĩĩ le̱ banina mei ni enyõnyõi Ie̱, ni ame̱ha maṅ le̱, edšake̱ ame̱bule ame̱nyemiyō le̱.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Ame̱tōi ke̱ ame̱tšinai ke̱ ame̱tedšii ke̱ nii ní yo̱ mã le̱ṅ ke̱ nii ni yo̱ ṅãno̱ le̱, ome̱lō ke̱-te.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ ame̱henii fẽ ke̱ ame̱bii bibii fẽ ke̱ ame̱ṅãmei nom, ni ame̱ha ame̱we nibii fẽ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ Simeon kē̱ Levi ake̱: Nyewomi amane mli, ni nyebã mihe *edše fũ ewo šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii ní dši Kanaanbii ke̱ Perizbii le̱; ni mi hũ ni miyikule̱ dši fiõ ne̱, ame̱abua ame̱he nä amebatuami ni ame̱agbemi; ni aakpãtã mihĩe, mike̱ miwe le̱. *

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱: Aso edša ake̱ afe wo̱nyemiyō le̱ tamo̱ afeo̱ adſamaṅ ko?

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ ewe lē̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ le̱ ake̱: *Nyedšiea maṅse̱ nyoṅmo̱i ni yo̱ nyeteṅ le̱ nyeſiea, ni nyetšūa nyehe, ni nyetšakea nyetadei. *

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Ni emã *afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni etšē̱ dše̱i El-Betel, edšake̱ dše̱i Nyoṅmo̱ dšie ebe ši etšõle̱ ye̱, beni edšo foi ye̱ enyemi le̱ hĩe le̱. *

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: ni šikpoṅ le̱ ni miṅõ-hã Abraham ke̱ Isak le̱, bo maṅõ-hã, ni oseši ni aaba ye̱ ose̱ le̱ maṅõ šikpoṅ ne̱ mahã.

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ṅõ te̱ eto okadi ye̱ heni eke̱le̱ wie ye̱ le̱, ni efo̱se wein ke̱ mũ eſie no. *

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Ni Iakob wo heni Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱le̱ wie ye̱ le̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Betel.

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Betel, ni eſe̱ gbe̱ kukuō ko ni ame̱še̱o̱ Efrat, ke̱ke̱ ni Rahel bõi kõmo̱, ni efo̱mo̱ le̱ he yawa hãle̱.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni efo̱mo̱ le̱ mli wa le̱, yōfo̱yō le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāše gbeyei, ši obafo̱ nū ekoṅ.

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni esusnma beo̱ emli adše ni ebu enā le̱, ewole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Benoni; ši etše̱ wole̱ Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ni Rahel gbo, ni afùle̱ ye̱ Efrat ni dši Betlehem le̱ gbe̱ le̱ mase̱i. Mika

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ke̱ te̱ to okadi ye̱ esãṅ le̱ no̱; no dši Rahel sãṅ no̱ te̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Ni Israel ṅõ-ſie no̱ ni eyaši ebū le̱ ye̱ *Eder mõ le̱ se̱ghe̱. *Mika

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, heni Israel yo̱ nakai šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, *Ruben yiṅ ete ni eke̱ etše̱ ṅã Bilha le̱ yawo̱; ni Israel nu. Agbe̱ne̱ Iakob bihĩĩ le̱, ame̱yi nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱: *

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob ba etše̱ Isak ṅõ ye̱ Mamre, ye̱ Kiriat-Arba ni dši Hebron le̱, heni Abraham ke̱ Isak hato gbo̱ ye̱ le̱.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Esau *moni atšé̱o̱le̱ Edom le̱ sešibii ne̱: *

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: ke̱ Išmael biyō Basemat ni dši Nebaiot nyemiyō le̱.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱nii ni ame̱ná le̱ fá tšõ, bo̱ni ame̱anyẽ ši ame̱hĩ ye̱ hekome, ni ame̱lē̱koloi le̱ ahewo̱ le̱ ame̱boo šikpoṅ ni ame̱bato gbo̱ ye̱ no̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Ki Esau yahĩ Seir goṅ le̱ no̱. Esau noṅṅ dši Edom le̱.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Ni Esau bii le̱ ateṅ lume̱i ne̱: Esau kromo̱bi Elifaz bii dši: Lumo Teman, lumo̱ Omar, lumo̱ Zefo, lumo̱ Kenaz,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: lumo̱ Kora, lumo̱ Gatam, lumo̱ Amalek. Mene̱mei dši Elifaz lume̱i ye̱ Edom šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱dši Ada bii.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Ni Esau bi Reuel le̱ bii ne̱: Lnmo Nahat, lumo̱ Zera, lumo̱ Šama, lumo̱ Miza. Mene̱mei dši Reuel lume̱i ye̱ Edom šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱dši Esau ṅã Basemat bii.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Ni Esau ṅã Obolibama hii ne̱: Lumo Ieuš, lumo̱ Ialam, lumo̱ Kora. Mene̱mei dši Ana biyō Oholibama ni dši Esau ṅã le̱ lume̱i le̱.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Esau bii ni mene̱mei dši ame̱lumei. Le̱ noṅṅ dši Edom le̱.

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: *Hornyo Seir bii ní yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ne̱: Lotan ke̱ Šobal ke̱ Zibeon ke̱ Ana, *

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Ni Lotan bii dši Hori ke̱ Hemam; ni Lotan nyemiyō dši Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Ni Šobal bii ne̱: Alvan ke̱ Manahat ke̱ Ebal, Šefo ke̱ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Ni Zibeon bii ne̱: Aia ke̱ Ana. Mone̱ dši Ana le̱ ni yana nula-nubui ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, beni elè̱o̱ etše̱ Zibeon tedšii le̱.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ni Ana bii ne̱: Dišon ke̱ Ana biyō Oholibama.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Ni Dišon bii ne̱: Hemdan ke̱ Ešban ke̱ Itran ke̱ Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezer bii ne̱: Bilhan ke̱ Zaavan ke̱ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Ni Dišan bii ne̱: Uz ke̱ Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Horbii alumei ne̱: Lumo Lotan, lumo̱ Šobal, lumo̱ Zibeon, lumo̱ Ana,

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: lumo̱ Dišon, lumo̱ Ezer, lumo̱ Dišan. Mene̱mei dši Horbii le̱ alumei ni ye lume̱i ye̱ Seir šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Ni Esau lume̱i ye̱ ame̱wekui ke̱ ame̱dšé̱hei ke̱ ame̱gbe̱ii anā le̱ agbe̱ii ne̱: Lumo Timna, lumo̱ Alva, lumo̱ Ietet,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: lumo̱ Oholibama, lumo̱ Ela, lumo̱ Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: lumo̱ Kenaz, lumo̱ Teman, lumo̱ Mibzar,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: lumo̱ Magdiel, lumo̱ Iram. Mene̱mei dši Edom lume̱i le̱ ye̱ ame̱šihĩle̱hei le̱ anà ye̱ šikpoṅ ni ame̱ná le̱ no̱. Le̱ dši Esau ni dši Edombii atše̱ le̱.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ kē̱: Ame̱dše biē̱; ši minu ake̱ ame̱kē̱: Nyehãa wo̱yaä Dotan. Ni Iosef tiu enyemimei le̱, ni eyanaame̱ ye̱ Dotan.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Ni beni enyemimei le̱ na ake̱ le̱ ame̱tše̱ sumoo̱ fẽ enyemimei le̱ fẽ le̱, ame̱nye̱le̱, ni ame̱nyẽẽ ame̱ke̱le̱ awie ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef la lamõ ko, ni edšadše etšõ enyemimei le̱, ni ame̱sā ame̱nye̱le̱ fè tšutšu le̱.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Ši na, wo̱mĩfĩmo̱ ṅmā̃kei ye̱ ṅmõši, ni na, mike le̱ te ši damo̱ ši, ni na, nyekei le̱ babo̱le mike le̱ ni ame̱kotole̱.

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Ni enyemimei le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Aso maṅtše̱ po okē̱ ooye ye̱ wo̱no̱ ne̱? alo ye obaye wo̱no̱ ne̱? Ni ame̱nye̱le̱ fè tšutšu le̱ ye̱ elamõi le̱ ke̱ ewiemo̱i le̱ ahewo̱.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Ni esā ela lamõ kroko hũ, ni egba enyemimei le̱, ni ekē̱: Na, mila lamõ ko ekoṅ, ni na, hũlũ ke̱ nyoṅtšẽre ke̱ ṅulamii myoṅma ke̱ ekome hakotomi.

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Ni beni egba etše̱ ke̱ enyemimei le̱, etše̱ kã ehĩe, ni eké̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽ lamõ ola ne̱? Bĕle̱ kotomo̱ mike̱ onye ke̱ enyemimei le̱ aabakotoö ye̱ šikpoṅ?

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Ni enyemimei le̱ yiṅ ame̱te ame̱tše̱ tōi le̱ lè̱ *ye̱ Šekem. *

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya ni oyakwe̱ ake̱ onyemimei le̱ ke̱ tōi le̱ ye̱ dšogbāṅ lo, ni obakē̱mi. Ke̱ke̱ ni etšũle̱ ke̱-dše̱ *Hebron dšō̱ le̱ mli, ni eba Šekem. *

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Ni nū ko nale̱, ni na, ētšomlo ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱; ni nū le̱ bile̱ ake̱: Meni otaoo̱?

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mītao minyemimei lē̱; mīkpao fai, tšõmo̱mi heni ame̱lè̱o̱ ame̱tōi le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱nale̱ ye̱ šoṅṅ ní enáko ebe̱ṅke̱ame̱ le̱, ame̱kpãṅ eyi no̱ ake̱ ame̱agbele̱.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱kē̱ ame̱be ake̱: Na, lamõi atše̱ le̱ baä.

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyebaä ni wo̱gbeale̱, ni wo̱še̱ale̱ we̱fõa bui le̱ eko mli, ni wo̱kē̱: Kolo fõṅ ko eyele̱; ni wo̱kwe̱ bo̱ni elamõi le̱ aate ahã.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Ni Ruben nu, *ni ẽtao ni edšiele̱ ye̱ amedeṅ, ni ekẽ: Nyekahãa wogbeale! *

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Ni Ruben sā kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekaſiea lá ši, ši nyeṅõale̱ nyeyawoa bu ni yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ne̱ mli, ni nyekataä ehe! beni afe ni edšiele̱ ye̱ ame̱deṅ, koni eke̱le̱ ayahã etše̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Iosef še̱ enyemimei le̱ aṅõ le̱, ame̱kplo̱ etade ni dši atade wuyã fe̱fe̱o ni ewo le̱ ye̱ ehe, K.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ho ame̱trá ši ni ame̱baye nii. Ni ame̱hole ame̱hĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ame̱kwe̱ ni na, Išmaelbii gbe̱nyielo̱i asafo ko dše̱ Gilead miba ke̱ ame̱yomai ni tĕre tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai ke̱ gbonyowō tšofã ke̱ ohe̱ ni dšeo̱ ṅma ke̱-mĩya Mizraim.

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Nyebaä ni nyehãa wo̱hõale̱ wo̱hãa Išmaelbii le̱, ši nyekahāa wo̱ke̱ wo̱niné mïsa ehe; edšake̱ wo̱nyemi ke̱ wo̱belo dšilo̱. Ni enyemimei le̱ kplẽ.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Ni *Midianbii ni dši guo̱yelo̱i le̱ baho; ni ame̱yagbla Iosef ni ame̱dšiele̱ ye̱ bu le̱ mli, ni ame̱yahõ Iosef ame̱hã Išmaelbii le̱ ame̱he dſie̱te̱i kukudši nyoṅmai-enyo. Ni ameke Iosef te Mizraim. *

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ko̱ Iosef atade le̱, ni ame̱gbe tõkpakpo ko, ni ame̱ṅõ atade le̱ ame̱tšo̱ lá le̱ mli,

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱tšũ ake̱ atade wuyā fe̱fe̱o le̱ yahã ame̱tše̱ akē̱: Noni wo̱na ne̱; kwe̱mo̱ ake̱ obi le̱ atade le̱ ni lo dšee noṅ,

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ni eyo, ni ekē̱: Mibi le̱ atade le̱ ni! *kolo fõṅ ko eyele̱, tšere̱mo̱ etšere̱ Iosef mli ne̱! *K.

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ni Iakob *gbla ehe atade le̱, hi eke̱ kpekpe emĩa ehe̱, ni eye ebi le̱ he ṅko̱mo̱ gbĩĩ pī. *K.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Ni ebihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ fẽ te ši, koni ame̱baše̱dše emī, ši ekplẽẽ mīše̱dšemo̱, ni ekē̱: Nko̱mo̱yeli mike-akpleke ši ke̱yanina mibi le ye gbohīĩadše. Ni etše̱ fóle̱.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ni Midianbii le̱ yahõle̱ ye̱ Mizraim ame̱hã Potifar ni dši Farao piafonyo ke̱ eblafoi atše̱ le̱.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Ni Iuda na Kanaannyo ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Šua le̱ biyō ko ye̱ dše̱i; ni eṅōle̱, ni ebawo̱ eṅõ.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Ni ená mũsũ ekoṅ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Onan.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda w̌e̱ yō ko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Tamar ehã ekromo̱bi Er le̱.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda kromo̱bi Er fe ehe gbomo fõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni Iehowa gbele̱.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Ni Iuda ké̱ Onan ake̱: Ya onyemi le̱ ṅã le̱ ṅõ, ni oṅõle̱ ake̱ gbošiṅã, koni oke̱le̱ afo̱ ato onyemi le̱ se̱.

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Ši Onan le ake̱ bii le̱ ebatšṍṅ enõ, ṅi eba mli ake̱, ké̱ ete enyemi le̱ ṅã le̱ ṅõ le̱, eṅõ-ſieo̱ ši ye̱ šikpoṅ efiteo̱, koni ekahã enyemi le̱ mīná sešibii.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Ni noni efe le̱, efõṅ dši ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; nohewo̱ le̱ egbele̱ hũ.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda kē̱ ešāyō Tamar ake̱: Yahĩ ši ake̱ okũlafo ye̱ otše̱ we le̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni mibi Šela lē̱ aada. Edšake̱ ekē̱: Koni le̱ hũ ekabagbo tamo̱ enyemimei le̱. Ni Tamar te eyahĩ etše̱ we le̱.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Ni ye̱ mli āhũ le̱, Šua biyō le̱ ni dši Iuda ṅã le̱ bagbo. Ni beni Iuda tšé̱ etšui eṅmẽ emli le̱, eke̱ enanyo Hira, Adulamnyo le̱, yiṅ te etōiahetšo̱i kulo̱i le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Timna.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ni ayakē̱ Tamar akē̱: Na, ošānũ le̱ miya Timna ní eyaku etōi le̱ ahetšo̱i.

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Ni edšie ekũlafemo̱ atade le̱ ye̱ ehe efõ ši, ni eṅõ hĩehānõ eha ehĩe, ni eṅõbla ehe, ni eyatá ši ye̱ Enaim klotia ye̱ Timna gbe̱ le̱ toi; edšake̱ ena ake̱ Šela eda ni aṅõõle̱ ahããle̱ gblã.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Ni beni Iuda nale̱ le̱, ebule̱ ake̱ yō adſamaṅ ko; edšake̱ eha ehĩe.

english_verse: and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
translation_verse: Ni egba ke̱-te eṅõ ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ toi, ni ekē̱: Kwe̱, hã ni maba oṅõ; edšake̱ *elee ake̱ ešāyõ le̱ ni. Ni ekē̱: Meni oohãmi, koni oba miṅõ? *

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mahã amõ tõkpakpobi ko ye̱ tōi le̱ ateṅ abahão. Ni ekē̱: Ké̱ ootomi awaba ko ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni oohã ake̱-ba le̱.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mẽ awaba matoõ? Ni ekē̱: Owolonāso̱omo̱nõ ke̱ ehe kpã ke̱ odẽhĩemo̱tšo le̱. Ni eṅõ-hãle̱, ní eba eṅõ, ni eke̱le̱ ná mũsũ.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Ni ete ši ete, ni eyadšie ehĩehānõ le̱ efõ ši, ni eko̱ ekūlafemo̱ atade le̱ ewo.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda ṅõ tōkpakpobi le̱ ehã enanyo Adulamnyo le̱ ke̱-te, koni eyahe ewabatōnii le ye̱ yō le̱ deṅ; ši enaa yō le̱.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eli dše̱ibii ke̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ yō adſamaṅ ní tá Enaim gbe̱ le̱ toi le̱ yo̱? Ni ame̱ke: Yō adſamaṅ ko be̱ bie̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Ni eku ese̱ eba Iuda nõ ekoṅ, ni ekē̱: Minaale̱; ni asaṅ dše̱ibii le kē̱: Yō adſamaṅ ko be̱ bie̱ ne̱.

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Ni Iuda kē̱: Hã ni eke̱-ya, koni wo̱hĩe akabagboi; na, mihã oke̱ tōkpakpobi ne̱ te, ni onaale̱.

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ aafe nyõdši etẽ le̱ eba mli ake̱ adekē̱ Iuda eke̱: Ošāyō Tamar eyabo̱ adſamaṅ, ni asaṅ na, ená mũsũ ye̱ adſamaṅbō̱ le mli. Ni Iuda kē̱: Ake̱le̱ adše kpo ke-ba, koni abašãle̱.

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Ni beni ake̱le̱ dše kpo ba le̱, etšũ ate ešānū le ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Nū mo nõ ní dši nii ne̱ le, le̱ mike̱-nà mũsũ le̱. Ni esā ekē̱: Kwe̱mo̱ ake̱e ooyo mo nõ ni dši wolonāso̱omo̱nõ ne̱ ke̱ ehe kpã ne̱ ke̱ tšo ne̱ lo?

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda yo ni ekē̱: Dšalo̱ dšile̱ fèmi, ake̱ noni miṅõõle̱ midãã mibi Šela le̱. Ni ehi esaa ebe doṅṅ.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni efo̱ö̱ le̱, mokome dšie enine. Ni yōfo̱yō lo mō mli, ni eke̱ kpã tšuru fĩ enine le̱, ni ekē̱: Mone̱ tšutšu ba.

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni esu enine le̱ ekoṅ le̱, na, enyemi le̱ ba; ni ekē̱: Mẽba otšere̱ mll ke̱-ba ne̱? Ni awole̱ Perez. Mat.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ le̱ enyemi le ni kpã tšuru le yo̱ enineši le hũ ba; ni awole̱ Zera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ Iosef *te Mizraim, ni Farao piafonyo ke̱ eblafoi atše̱ Potifar ní dši Mizraimnyo le̱ hele̱ ye̱ Išmaelbii le̱ ní ke̱le̱ ba dše̱i le̱ adeṅ. *

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef hĩe de nyam ye̱ ehĩe, ni esúmoo̱le̱, ni ewole̱ onukpa ye̱ ewe le̱ no̱, ni nofẽ̱no ní eyo̱ le̱ etu ewo edeṅ.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ etu enibii fẽ ní eyo̱ le̱ ewo Iosef deṅ, ni ekwe̱e̱ enokonoko ake̱ dša nii ní eyeo̱ ke̱ke̱. Ni Iosef he ye̱ fe̱o ni ehĩe hũ ye̱ fe̱o.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Ni nii ne̱ ase̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ enuṅtšo̱ ṅã le̱ dšie ehĩe eka Iosef ekē̱: Oke̱mi abawo̱! Abe̱i

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Ši ekplẽẽ, ni ekē̱ enuṅtšo̱ ṅã le̱ ake̱: Na, minuṅtšo̱ kwe̱e̱ noni yo̱ mideṅ ye̱ šĩa ne̱, ni etu nii ni eyo̱ fẽ ewo mideṅ;

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: mokomoko be̱ ni fèmi ye̱ šĩa ne̱, ni ekãmããmi nokonoko, ake̱ dša bo ke̱ke̱, edšake̱ bo le̱ eṅã dšio. Té aafe tẽṅ ni mafe efõṅ kpeteṅkple ni tamo̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱, ni mafe eša maši Nyoṅmo̱ṅ?

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ehĩe Iosef ke̱ wiemo̱ dāne̱, ši eboole̱ toi nó eke̱le̱ awo̱ lo ebe̱ṅke̱le̱.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli gbĩ le̱ eko ake̱ Iosef te šĩa le̱ eyatšu enii, ni šĩa le̱ bii le̱ eko-eko be̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Ni emõ etade le̱ mli, ni ekē̱: Oke̱mi abawo̱! Ši ešĩ etade le̱ ye̱ edeṅ, ni edšo foi ke̱-dše kpo.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: etšé̱ ešiabii le̱, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyebakwe̱a noko, eyaṅõ Hebrinyo ne̱ ke̱-ba wo̱ṅõ, koni ebaye wo̱he fe̱o. Ebe miṅõ, ni eke̱mi abawo̱, ni mibo ke̱ gbē wā;

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: ni eba mli ake̱, beni enu ake̱ miwó migbē no̱ ni mibo le̱, eši etade le ye̱ miṅõ, ni edšo foi ke̱-dše kpo.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ etade le̱ efò emase̱i ke-yeši beyino̱ ni enuṅtšo̱ le̱ ba šĩa.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: Ni edšadše ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ noṅṅ etšõle̱ ake̱: Nyṍṅnū Hebrinyo le̱ ni ba wo̱ṅõ le̱ ba ní ebaye mihe fe̱o.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni miwó migbē no̱ ni mibo le̱, ešĩ etade le̱ ye̱ miṅõ, ni edšo foi.

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef nuṅtšo̱ le̱ mõle̱ ni eyawole̱ tšũṅ ye̱ beni awoo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ gbokle̱foi atšũṅ ye̱ le̱, ni gbokle̱foi atšũ le̱ṅ eyo̱.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa ke̱ Iosef ye̱, ni enale̱ mo̱bo̱, ni ewo ehĩe nyam ye̱ gbokle̱foi akwe̱lo̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Ni gbokle̱foi akwe̱lo̱ le̱ tu gbokle̱foi le̱ ni yo̱ tšũ le̱ṅ le̱ fẽ ewo Iosef deṅ, ni nofẽno ni afeo̱ ye̱ dše̱i le̱, le̱ efeo̱.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Gbokle̱foi akwe̱lo̱ le̱ kwe̱e̱ nokonoko ni yo̱ edeṅ le̱; edšake̱ Iehowa ke̱le̱ ye̱, ni nofẽno ni efeo̱ le̱, Iehowa hãa eſereo̱.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: ni eyawoame̱ tšũṅ ye̱ oblafoi atše̱ le̱ šĩa le̱, ye̱ gbokle̱foi atšũ le̱ṅ, heni aṅõ *Iosef awo le̱. *

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Ni oblafoi atše̱ le̱ tuame̱ ewo Iosef deṅ, ni esṅmoo̱ame̱, ni ame̱tše̱ kplaṅ ye̱ tšũ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef ba ame̱sramo̱ lebi, ni ekwe̱amē̱, ni na, ame̱fe mo̱bo̱mo̱bo̱.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱la lamõ ko, ni moko be̱ ni aatšõ šiši. Ni Iosef kē̱-ame̱ ake̱: Ani *šišitšõmo̱ le̱ dšee Nyoṅmo̱ nõṅ? mīkpanye fai, nyegbaämi! *

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Ni dā̃wolo̱i anukpa le̱ gba Iosef elamõ le̱, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Milamõ le̱ mli le̱, na, weintšo ko mã mihĩe,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: ni egbla nidši etẽ, ni efĩmo̱ afofrokpo̱i, ni egba ni ewo yibii šabii ni etšu;

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: ni mihĩe Farao kpulu le̱; nimitšere̱ weinyibii le̱, ni miṅã miwo Farao kpulu le̱ mli, ni miṅõ kpulu le̱ miwo Farao deṅ.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ešišitšõmo̱ ne̱; nidši etẽ le̱ gbĩĩ etẽ ni;

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: biē̱ gbĩĩ etẽ le̱ Farao aawó oyitšo no̱ ni eke̱o aayato ogbe̱he le̱ ekoṅ, ni ooṅõ Farao kpala le̱ owo edeṅ, take̱ bo̱ni ofeo̱ sá, beni odši edā̃wolo̱ le̱.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Ši *dšu adšumi ye̱ Hebrimei ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni bie̱ ne̱ hũ mifeko noko ni sa ake ameaṅõmi amewo bu neṅ. *

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Ni beni abološãlo̱i anukpa le̱ na ake̱ šišitšõmo̱ le̱ hĩ dšogbāṅ le̱, ekē̱ Iosef akē̱: Mi hũ milamõ le̱ mli le̱, na, mitēre akpānõ kpãnyãi etẽ ye̱ miyiteṅ;

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: ni kpãnyã ni mã yiteṅ le̱, niyenii sro̱toi fẽ ní dši abološãlo̱ nitšumo̱ ni etšuo̱ ehãa Farao le̱ ye̱ mli; ni lofõdši ye ye̱ kpãnyã le̱ mli ye̱ miyiteṅ.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef here no̱ ni ekē̱: Ešišitšõmo̱ nē̱: kpãnyãi etẽ le̱ gbĩĩ etẽ ni;

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: bie̱ gbĩĩ etẽ le̱ Farao aawó oyitšo no̱, ni eese̱ṅo ye̱ tšo no̱; ni lofõdši aaye ohelo ye̱ ohe.

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ ní dši Farao fo̱mo̱gbĩ le̱, eṅmẽ etšũdši le̱ fē okplõ; ni ehole dā̃wolo̱i anukpa le̱ ke̱ abološãlo̱i anukpa le̱ ayitšei ano̱ ye̱ etšũdši le̱ ateṅ;

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: ni ehã dā̃wolo̱i anukpa le̱ yaye enukpa le̱ ekoṅ, ni eṅõ kpulu le̱ ewo Farao deṅ;

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: ši abološãlo̱i anukpa le̱, ese̱ṅle̱, take̱ be̱ni Iosef tšõame̱ šiši le̱.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Ši dā̃wolo̱i anukpa le̱ *eyakaii Iosef, ši ehĩe kpa eno̱. *K.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ afii nãkplo̱i enyo̱ se̱ le̱ Farao la lamõ ko, ni na, edamo̱ fā le̱ nā.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ni na, abletšei kpawo ni noko be̱ yi ni bokã kō̱yo̱ egbĩame̱ keklẽ bakwẽ ye̱ ame̱se̱.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Ke̱kē̱ ni dā̃woio̱i anukpa le̱ ke̱ Farao wie ake̱: Mikai mitõmo̱ ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: ni wo̱la lamõi komei nyōṅ kome mli, mi ke̱ le̱, wo̱la, mo ke̱ elamõ ke̱ ešiši.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, bo̱ni edšadše šiši etšõwo̱ le̱, nakai eba mli; mi le̱ aṅõmi ato migbe̱he ekoṅ, ni le̱ le̱ ase̱ṅle̱.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Mila lamõ ko, ni mokomoko be̱ ni nyẽ šiši tšõ; ni minu ni akē̱ ye̱ ohe ake̱ ke̱dši onu lamõ ko le̱, onyẽo̱ šiši otšõo̱.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosef here Farao no̱ ake̱: *No he̱ mimli; Nyoṅmo̱ aahã Farao hedšo̱le̱ hetō. *

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ni Farao dšadše etšõ Iosef ake̱ Milamõ le̱ mli le̱, na, midamo̱ fā le̱ nā,

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: ni na, tšinai kpawo ni eſiſī ni he yo̱ fe̱o fã kpo ke̱-dše̱ fā le̱ mli, ni ame̱yaye nii ye̱ dſe̱iaṅ.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni na, tšinai krokomei kpawo hũ nyie ame̱se̱ ba, ame̱nii ye̱ mo̱bo̱ ni ame̱he ye̱ nyãṅemo̱ ni ame̱trãtrā̃ lō hũ, ni minako ame̱no̱ pẽṅ ke̱ tãṅ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no fẽ.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱bote ame̱mũsũṅ le̱, anaa ake̱ ame̱yeame̱; ši moṅ ame̱be ye̱ nyãṅemo̱ lolo tamo̱ tšutšu le̱ noṅṅ. Ke̱ke̱ ni mihĩe tšẽ.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Ni misā mikwe̱ ye̱ milamõ le̱ mli, ni na, abletšei kpawo ba tšo kome yi, eba kpokplō.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ni na, abletšei kpawo ni nii be̱ yi, ní yo̱ legelege, ní bokã kō̱yo̱ egbĩame̱ keklē bakwẽ ye̱ ame̱se̱.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Ni abletšei legelegei le̱ mĩ abletšei kpakpai kpawo le̱. Ni midšadše ene̱ mitšõ woloṅlelo̱i le̱, ši mokomoko enaa he eko ekē̱ē̱mi.

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ Farao akē̱: Farao lamõ lē̱ ekomeṅ. Nyoṅmo̱ etšõ Farao noni ebafe.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Tšinai kpakpai kpawo le̱ afii kpawoṅ, ni abletšei kpakpai kpawo le̱ hũ afii kpawo ni; lamõ lē̱ ekomeṅ.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Ni tšinai kpawo ní etrã lõ, ni he yo̱ nyãṅemo̱, ni nyie ame̱se̱ ba le̱, afii kpawoṅ, ni abletšei kpawo ni noko be̱ yi ni bokã kō̱yo egbĩame̱ keklē le̱, hõmo̱yeli afii kpawo ni.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Ene̱ dši noni mikē̱ Farao akē̱ noni Nyoṅmo̱ bafe le̱, no edšie etšò Farao ne̱ le̱.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ni hõmo̱ ni banyie se̱ aba le̱ hãṅ ale nifále̱ le̱ doṅṅ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no; edšake̱ enā bawa naakpa.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ni noni akũ lamõ le̱ abo̱ he toi enyo̱ ahã Farao le̱, ešiši dši ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ bafe nakai le̱le̱ṅ, ni Nyoṅmo̱ bafe le̱ oyá.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ hã Farao atao moko ni dši hĩešikãlo̱ ke̱ nilelo̱, ni eṅõle̱ eto Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Hã Farao afe ene̱, ni eto no̱kwe̱lo̱i ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni eṅõ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ niyenii le̱ amlidšā enumo̱ mli ekome ye̱ nifále̱ afii kpawo le̱ mli.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: ni aṅõ nakai niyenii le̱ ato se̱ ahã šikpoṅ le̱ ye̱ hõmo̱ afii kpawo le̱ ni baba Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ hewo̱, koni šikpoṅ le̱ akafite ye̱ hõmo̱ le̱ mli.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: *Ani wo̱o̱nyẽ wo̱ná moko ni Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ yo̱ emli tamo̱ mone̱? *Abe̱i

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef akē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni Nyoṅmo̱ eṅõ ene̱ fẽ etšõo ne̱, mokomoko be̱ ni dši hĩešikãlo̱ ke̱ nilelo̱ tamo̱ bo.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Bo ooye miwe le̱ no̱, ni odāṅ gbẽ toi mimaṅbii le̱ fē aabo; sẽi le̱ gbe̱fãṅ pe̱ mafèo ye̱. Dsads.

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Na, miṅõo mito Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱. Bo̱f.

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Ni Farao *dšie ewolonāso̱omo̱ga le̱ ye̱ enine ni eṅõ-wo Iosef nine, ni ewole̱ klala fe̱fe̱o atadei, ni eṅõ †šika kõsõṅ-kõsõ ewo ekue̱; *Est.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: ni ehã etá eſīli ni dši enyo̱ le̱ mli, ni ame̱ble̱ ke̱-nyie ehĩe ake̱: Nyekũlaä ši! Ni ewole̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱ onukpa.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef akē̱: Mi, midši Farao le̱; ni moko edšeṅ ose̱ ewóṅ enine lo enane no̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱.

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni Farao wo Iosef gbe̱i ake̱ Zafenat-Panea; ni eṅõ On oso̱fo Potifera biyō Asenat le̱ ehãle̱ gblã. Ni Iosef dše kpo eyakpa Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Ni nifále̱ afii kpawo le̱ mli le̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ba nii babaō ke̱-teke no̱.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ni ebua afii kpawo le̱ mli niyenii le̱ fẽ ni ba ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ nā, ni eto niyenii le̱ ye̱ mãdši le̱ amli; ṅmõši niyenii ni yo̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ be le̱ eṅõ-to no noṅṅ mli.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iosef bua able nā eto babaō dientše̱ take̱ ṅšo̱ nā šia, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni efõ kanemo̱; edšake̱ ebe̱ yikule̱.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef fo̱ bibĩĩ enyo̱, dãni hõmo̱ afii le̱ ba, mei ní eke̱ Asenat, On oso̱fo Potifera biyō le̱, fo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosef wo ekromo̱bi le̱ Manase, ni ekē̱: Edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ehã mihĩe ekpa mihaomo̱ le̱ fẽ ke̱ mitše̱ we le̱ fẽ no̱.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ni ewo moni dši enyo̱ le̱ Efraim, ni ekē̱: Edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ehã miwo ſĩei ye̱ mimanehũlũ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Ni afii kpawo ní niyenii ba babaō ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ se̱ fo;

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: ni hõmo̱yeli afii kpawo le̱ bõi bā, take̱ bo̱ni Iosef kē̱ lē̱. Ni hõmo̱ ba šikpõdši fẽ no̱; ši Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ le̱ niyenii ye̱.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Mizraim šikpoṅ mũ le̱ fē bõi hõmo̱yeli le̱, maṅ le̱ fó tšē̱ Farao ake̱ ehãame̱ niyenii; ni Farao kē̱ Mizraimbii le̱ fẽ ake̱: Nyeyaä Iosef ṅõ, ni noni eekē̱nye le̱, nyefea.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ni beni hõmo̱ le̱ eba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ le̱, Iosef gble fiasei le̱ fẽ nā, ni ehõ able ehã Mizraimbii le̱; edšake̱ hõmo̱ le̱ nā wa naakpa ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Ni mãdšimãdši fẽ bahe able ye̱ Iosef ṅõ ye̱ Mizraim; edšake̱ hõmo̱ le̱ nā ewa naakpa ye̱ šikpõdši le̱ fë no̱.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Ni beni Iakob na ake̱ able ye̱ Mizraim le̱, ekē̱ ebibĩĩ le̱ ake̱: Mẽba nye-kwe̱kwe̱o̱ nyehe ne̱?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Na, minn akē̱ able ye̱ Mizraim; nyeyaä dše̱i ní nyeyahea eko ke̱-baä, koni wo̱yi anã wala, ni wo̱kagboi.

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef nyemimei nyoṅma le̱ yiṅ ke̱-te able hemo̱ ye̱ Mizraim.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Ši Iosef nyemi Benyamin le̱, Iakob hãã eke̱ enyemimei le̱ aya; edšake̱ ekē̱: Koni aleenõ ošrã ko akayašrãle̱.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef dši lumo̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni le̱ ehõo̱ able ehãa šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii fẽ. Ni Iosef nyemimei le̱ ba, ni ame̱ba-kotole̱, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱hĩe bumo̱ ši.

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dabi, minuṅtšo̱, ši niyenii hemo̱ otšũdši ba.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Wo̱fẽ nū kome bii dšiwo̱; ano̱kwafoi dšiwo̱, dšee sralo̱i dši otšũdši.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Dabi, ši šikpoṅ ne̱ yayaiaṅ kwe̱mo̱ nyeba.

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Otšũdši le̱ nyemimei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ni, nū kome bii dšiwo̱ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ni na, gbekẽ le̱ ye̱ wo̱tše̱ ṅõ amrõ ne̱, ni mokome be̱.

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ene̱ mina mi mikē̱nye akē̱: Sralo̱i dšinye lē̱!

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Noni akē̱-akpanye ši nē̱: Mina Farao ake̱ nyedšeṅ bie̱ nyeyaṅ, dša nyenyemi gbekẽ le̱ eba bie̱ dã.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Nyetšũa nyeteṅ mokome, ni eyaṅõ nyenyemi le̱ ke̱-ba; ni nye le̱ aawonye tšũṅ, koni aṅõ-kpa nyewiemo̱i le̱ aši akwe̱ akē̱ ano̱kwale ye̱ nyemli lo; ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, mina Farao ake̱, sralo̱i dšinye!

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Ni ewoame̱ tšũṅ gbĩĩ etẽ.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ Iosef kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyefea ene̱, ní nyeyi aná wala; ši mi le̱ mīše Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ké̱ ano̱kwafoi dšinye le̱, nyehãa afĩa nyenyemimei le̱ ateṅ mokome awoa heni awonye tšũṅ ye̱ le̱; ši nye le̱, hõmo̱ ní yo̱ nyešĩai le̱ hewo̱ le̱, nyeyaṅõa able le̱ ke̱-yaā;

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: ni nyeke̱ nyenyemi gbekẽ le̱ abaä miṅõ, no ake̱-ana nyewiemo̱i le̱ ano̱kwale, koni nyekagboi. Ni ame̱fe nakai.

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱ le̱ ame̱lee ake̱ Iosef enu noni ame̱ke̱ le̱; edšake̱ nādšielo̱ dšieo̱ ame̱nā.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Ni etšṍ ehe ke̱-dše ame̱ṅõ ni eyafó; ni ekũ ese̱ eba ame̱ṅõ ekoṅ ni ekeame̱ bawie; ni edšie Simeon ye̱ ame̱teṅ, ni efĩle ye̱ ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Ni Iosef fá ake̱ awo ame̱nibii le̱ amli ahle obõbõ, ni ake̱ mofẽmo šika akũ se̱ awo ekotoku mli ekoṅ, ní ahãame̱ ghe̱no̱ niyenii. Ni afe nakai ahãame̱.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ ame̱ble le̱ ame̱tẽre ame̱tedšii le̱, ni ame̱dše dše̱i ame̱te.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Ni heni ame̱teṅ moko fẽne ekotoku nā ní ebahã etedši niyenii ye̱ tōhe le̱, ena ešika le̱, ni na, ekā no̱ ye̱ ekotoku le̱ mli.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ enyemimei le̱ ake̱: Ake̱ mišika le̱ ekũ se̱ ehãmi, ni na, eye̱ mikotoku le̱ mli po. Ni ame̱tšui fã ni ame̱kwe̱kwē̱ amē̱he ke̱ hekpokpomo̱, ni ame̱kē̱: Meni Nyoṅmo̱ fewo̱ ne̱?

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ba ame̱tše̱ Iakob ṅõ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱, ni ame̱bagbale̱ nii ni afeame̱ le̱ fē ake̱:

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: Nū le̱ ni dši šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nuṅtšo̱ lē̱ tutu ehĩe ewowo̱, ni ebuwo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ sralo̱i.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Ni wo̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ano̱kwafoi dšiwo̱, wo̱dšee sralo̱i;

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: nyemimei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ dši wo̱tše̱ bii le̱; mokome be̱, ni gbekẽ le̱ ye̱ wo̱tše̱ ṅõ amrõ ne̱ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ ni dši šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kē̱wo̱ akē̱: Ene̱ maṅõ-le ake̱ anokwafoi dšinye: nyešĩa nyenyemimei le̱ ateṅ mokome nyehãami, ni hõmo̱ ní yo̱ nyešĩai le̱ hewo̱ le̱ nyeṅõa niyenii ke̱-yaã,

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: ni nyeyaṅõa nyenyemi gbekẽ le̱ ke̱-ba, no dāni male ake̱ dšee sralo̱i dšinye, ši ano̱kwafoi dšinye, koni madšie nyenyemi le̱ mahãnye, ni nyeye dšra ye̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱.

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Ni eha mli ake̱, beni ame̱dšie ame̱kotokui le̱ amli nii le̱, na, mofẽmo šika ni afĩ le̱ ye̱ ekotoku le̱ mli. Ni beni ame̱na ame̱sika ni afĩmo̱fĩmo̱i le̱, ame̱ke̱ ame̱tše̱ fẽ še gbeyei.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tše̱ Iakob kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekpakpā mibii ye̱ mihe: Iosef be̱, ni Simeon be̱, ni nyebaṅõ Benyamin hũ ke̱-ya; ene̱mei ne̱ fẽ le̱ mino̱ kã!

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ni Ruben kē̱ etšē̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši mike̱le̱ ekũũ se̱ ebabãão le̱, no le̱ gbe mibihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱; tule̱ owo mideṅ, ni mike̱le̱ aakũ se̱ ababão.

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mibi le̱ ke̱nye eyaa; edšake̱ enyemi le̱ egbo, ni le̱ ekome eſe̱; ke̱dši ošrã ko yašrãle̱ ye̱ gbe̱ ni nyeyanyie le̱ no̱ le̱, no le̱ nyebaṅõ miwadši le̱ ke̱-ya gbohïĩadše ke̱ aw̌ere̱hō.

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: ši ke̱dši ohãṅ eya le̱, no le̱ wo̱woṅ yā; edšake̱ nū le̱ kē̱wo̱ ake̱: Nyenaṅ mihĩe, akē̱ dša nyenyemi le̱ fata nyehe.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ši dšee šõ wo̱fe kũle̱, bene̱ wo̱te wo̱ba šii enyo̱.

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tše̱ Israel kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši nakai le̱, no le̱ bo̱ni nyefe ne̱: nyeṅõa šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ yibii kpakpai le̱ eko nyewoa nyenibii amli, ni *nyeke̱-yakea nū le̱, gbonyowō tšofã fiō ke̱ wò fiō ke̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ke̱ ohe̱ ni dšeo̱ ṅma, ke̱ amitšro̱bii ke̱ ṅme̱i; *Abe̱i

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: ni nyeṅõa šika kroko nyehĩea nyedeṅ, ni šikai le̱ ni akũ se̱ ake̱-ſie no̱ ye̱ nyekotokui amli le̱ nyeṅõa no hũ nyehĩea nyedeṅ ke̱-yaä ekoṅ, ekole̱ hene̱ hĩe dše no̱.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Ši Mawu Ofe le̱ ahã nū le̱ mũsũṅ atšõle̱ ye̱ nyehe, koni eṅmë nyenyemi mokome le̱ ke̱ Benyamin he ehãnye. *Ši mi le̱, ké̱ akpakpā mibii ye̱ mihe dšiṅṅ, akpakpā. *

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Ni hĩĩ le̱ ṅõ nakai nikēnii le̱, ni ame̱kũ šika le̱ ame̱bo̱ he ame̱hĩe ame̱deṅ, ke̱ Benyamin, ni ame̱te ši ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te Mizraim, ni ame̱yadamo̱ Iosef hĩe.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Iosef na ake̱ Benyamin fata ame̱he le̱, ekē̱ ešĩa le̱ no̱ onukpa le̱ ake̱: Oke̱ ne̱kē̱ hĩĩ ne aya šĩa ni ogbe koloi oke̱-fe niyenii oto; ši hĩĩ ne̱ ke̱mi baye nii ſane ne̱.

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ fe take̱ bo̱ni Iosef kē̱le̱ le̱, ni eke̱ hĩĩ le̱ te Iosef we le̱.

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tši ame̱be̱ṅke̱ Iosef šĩa le̱ no̱ onukpa le̱, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ wie ye̱ šĩa le̱ šinā le̱ ši,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱: Ofai ne̱, wo̱nuṅtšo̱! Kleṅkleṅ ní wo̱ba niyenii hemo̱ le̱,

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: eba mli ake, beni wo̱še̱ tōhe le̱, ní wo̱fẽne wo̱kotokui le̱ anã le̱, na, mofẽmo šika kã no̱ ye̱ ekotoku lē̱ mli, wo̱šika le̱ ye̱ ho̱ni aṅmē le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱; ni wo̱ke̱-hĩe wo̱dẽ ke̱-ha ekoṅ;

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: ni šika kroko hũ wo̱ke̱-hĩe wo̱dẽ ke̱-ba niyenii heme̱ ne̱; wo̱lee moni ṅõ wo̱šika le̱ ewo wo̱kotokui le̱ amli.

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Hedšo̱le̱ abãnye; nyekašea gbeyei! Nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ nyetše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ehã nyeto ahṹ ye̱ nyekotokui le̱ amli; nyešika le̱ eše̱ midẽ. Ni edšie *Simeon ebahãame̱. *

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ ke̱ hĩĩ le̱ ba Iosef we le̱, ni ebahãame̱ nu, ni *ame̱fo̱ ame̱nãdši ahe, ni ehã ame̱tedšii le̱ anii. *

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱sā nikēnii le̱ ame̱to Iosef se̱, dãni eba ſane le̱, edšake̱ ame̱nu ake̱ ame̱baye nii ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Ni ebiame̱ bo̱ni ame̱yo̱, ni ekē̱: Ani nyetše̱ nūmo le̱ *ni nyetšĩ etā le̱ ye̱ dšogbāṅ lo? Ani eye̱ dšeṅ lolo? *

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Otšũlo̱, wo̱tšē̱ le̱, eye̱ dšogbāṅ, eye̱ dšeṅ lolo. Ni *ame̱mãmo̱ ame̱yitšo ši, ni ame̱kotole̱. *

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Ni ehole ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ni ena enyemi Benyamin, enye mũsũṅ bi le̱, ni ekē̱: Nyenyemi gbekẽ le̱ ni nyetšĩ etã nyetšõmi le̱ ne̱? Ni ekē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ adšō̱o, mibi!

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef he fe oyá, edšakē̱ emũsũṅ tšōle̱ ye̱ enyemi le̱ hewo̱, ni ẽtao heko eyafó ye̱, ni eyabote ese̱tšũṅ, ni eyafó ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Ni efo̱ ehĩe ni edše kpo, ni emĩa ehĩe, ni ekē̱: Nyeke̱ niyenii abamãmo̱a ši!

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ enõ bamã ši eyimū ke̱ ame̱ bũ ame̱nõ yimūyimū, ke̱ Mizraimbii ni ke̱le̱ yeo̱ nii le̱ hũ anõ yimūyimū; edšake̱ Mizraimbii ke̱ Hebribii kaa nine yee nii, edšake̱ Mizraimbii *mīhĩ nõ. *

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ame̱ batrá ehĩe, kromo̱bi le̱ ye̱ enukpa gbe̱nã, ni gbekẽ hũ ye̱ egbekẽ gbe̱nã; ni hĩĩ le̱ anā kpe̱ ame̱he ni ame̱kwe̱kwē̱ ame̱hĩeaṅ ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Ni edšieo̱ nii ke̱-dše̱o̱ ehĩe ehãa-ame̱; ši Benyamin nõ le̱ ſè ame̱teṅ mofẽmo nõ šii enumo̱. Ni ame̱nu noko ni ame̱ke̱le̱ *ná mīše̱. *Hag.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: ni mikpuln ni dši midſie̱te̱i kpulu le̱ oke̱-fata able šika le̱ he ofõ no̱ ye̱ gbekẽ le̱ kotoku le̱ mli. Ni efe bo̱ni Iosef kē̱ le̱.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Beni ame̱dše kpo ye̱ mã le̱ṅ ni ame̱še̱ko šoṅṅ heko le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni Iosef kē̱ ešĩa le̱ no̱ onukpa le̱ ake̱: Te ši, ni otiu gbomei le̱, ni ké̱ oninaame̱ le̱, kē̱mo̱ame̱ ake̱: Menihewo̱ nyeke̱ efõṅ to ekpakpa nãdšiaṅ ne̱?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Té ene̱ mli minuṅtšo̱ nuo̱ dā̃ ye̱, ni esā ekē̱-klaä? Nyefe efõṅ ake̱ nyefe nakai le̱!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Na, šika le̱ ni wo̱na dſere no̱ ye̱ wo̱kotokui le̱ amli le̱ wo̱ke̱-dše̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ tõ *wo̱bahão; té aafe tẽṅ mo̱ ni wo̱o̱dšu dſie̱te̱i lo šika ye̱ onuṅtšo̱ we̱ṅ? *

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nyehãa afea bo̱ni nyekē̱ lē̱. Mofẽmo deṅ ni aana ye̱ le̱, eetšṍ minyṍṅ, ni nye le̱ sõ ko wulaṅnye.

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱he fe oyá ni ame̱totō ame̱kotokui le̱ ame̱māmo̱ ši, ni ame̱fẽnefẽnē ame̱kotokui le̱ anā.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Ni ebṍi taomo̱ ke̱-dše̱ onukpa le̱ no̱ ni eyagbe nā ye̱ gbekẽ le̱ no̱; ni ayana kpulu le̱ ye̱ Benyamin kotoku le̱ mli.

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Ni Iuda kē̱: Meni wo̱bakē̱ minuṅtšo̱? Mẽ wiemo̱ wo̱bawie? Alo té wo̱badšie wo̱nā tẽṅ? *Nyoṅmo̱ ena otšũdši anõša le̱. Na, wo̱tšṍmo̱ minnntšo̱ nyṍdši, wo̱ ke̱ mo dẽ ni ana kpulu le̱ ye̱ le̱ fẽ. *

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: Kpaõ, minyẽṅ nakai mafe; mo deṅ ni ana kpulu le̱ ye̱ le̱, le̱ eetšṍ minyṍṅ, ni nye le̱ nyeyaä nyetše̱ ṅõ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda tši be̱ṅke̱le̱ ni ekē̱: Ofai ne̱, minuṅtšo̱! Hã ní otšũlo̱ awie wiemo̱ ko ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ toiiaṅ; ni kãhã omli mīwo otšũlo̱ la, ši otamo̱ Farao noṅṅ!

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Minuṅtšo̱ bi etšũdši ake̱: *Ani nyeye̱ tše̱ lo nyeminū ko? *

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Ni wo̱kē̱ minuṅtšo̱ ake̱: Wo̱ye̱ tše̱ nūmo ke̱ enakutšoṅbi fiō ko; ni enyemi le̱ egbo, ni enye bi kome ní eſe̱ dšile̱, ni etše̱ sumoo̱le̱.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Ni okē̱ otšũdši ake̱: Nyeyaṅōale̱ ke̱-baä, koni manale̱ ke̱ mihiṅme̱ii.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Ni wo̱kē̱ minuṅtšo̱ akē̱: Gbekẽ le̱ nyēṅ ašĩ etše̱, edšake̱ ke̱dši ešĩ etše̱ le̱, etše̱ aagbo.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Ni *okē̱ otšũdši ake̱: Ke̱dši nyenyemi gbekẽ le̱ ke̱nye baa le̱, nyenaṅ mihĩe doṅṅ. *

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni wo̱ba otšũlo̱, mitše̱, ṅõ le̱, wo̱kē̱le̱ minuṅtšo̱ wiemo̱i le̱.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱tše̱ kē̱ ake̱: Nyeyaä ekoṅ ni nyeyabea niyenii fiō ko nyebahãawo̱ le̱,

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: wo̱kē̱: Wo̱nyẽṅ wo̱ya; ke̱dši wo̱nyemi gbekẽ le̱ fata wo̱be le̱, no dãni wo̱o̱te; ši wo̱nyẽṅ nū le̱ hĩe wo̱na, dša wo̱nyemi gbekẽ le̱ fata wo̱he.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ni otšũlo̱, mitše̱, kē̱wo̱ akē̱: Nyedientše̱ nyele ake̱ miṅã le̱, bii enyo̱ mike̱le̱ fo̱;

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: ni mokome dše mihe, ni *mikē̱: Tšere̱mo̱ kẽ atšere̱ emli ne̱! ni minakole̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱; *

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: ni ke̱dši *nyeṅõ mone̱ hũ ke̱-dše̱ mibe ke̱-te ni ošrã ko yašrãle̱ le̱, no le̱ nyebaṅṍ miwadši le̱ ke̱-ya gbohĩĩadše ke̱ aw̌rere̱hō. *

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ke̱dši mite otšũlo̱, mitše̱, ṅõ ni gbekẽ le̱ fataa wo̱he le̱, ake̱ noni gbekẽ ne̱ susuma he esusuma kpe̱te̱ hewo̱ le̱,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ otšũlo̱ *damo̱ mli ye̱ gbekẽ ne̱ hewo̱ ye̱ mitše̱ ṅõ, ni mikē̱: Ke̱dši mike̱le̱ ekũũ se̱ ebahãão le̱, no le̱ maye mitše̱ yi sõ ke̱-ate nãno̱. *

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱no̱ mĩkpao fai ni ohã otšũlo̱ ahĩ bie̱ ake̱ minuṅtšo̱ ayṍṅ ye̱ gbekẽ le̱ nãdšiaṅ, ni ohã gbekẽ le̱ ke̱ enyemimei le̱ aya.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ši té aafe tẽṅ ni mate mitše̱ ṅõ ni gbekẽ le̱ fataa miheṅ? No le̱ mayana efõṅ ní aba mitše̱ no̱!

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Iosef nyẽẽ ehĩe emĩa doṅṅ ye̱ mei ní damo̱ emase̱i le̱ fẽ hĩe, ni ebo ake̱: Nyehãa mofẽmo adšea kpo ke̱-dšea mimase̱i! Ni mokomoko ke̱ Iosef damo̱o̱ ši, beni edšie ehe ši etšõ enyemimei le̱.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ni ewó egbē ni efó, ni Mizraimbii ke̱ Farao webii le̱ tete nu.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ enyemimei le̱ ake̱: Mi Iosef ni. Ani mitše̱ ye̱ dšeṅ lolo? Ni enyemimei le̱ nyẽẽle̱ hetõ ahã, edšake̱ ame̱dšidšā ye̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ enyemimei le ake̱: Nyetšia nyebe̱ṅke̱ami kol Ni ame̱tši ame̱ba. Ni ekē̱: Midši nyenyemi Iosef, moni nyehõ *ke̱-ba Mizraim le̱! *

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ nyekahãa mĩdo̱anye ni nyemli akawowoa nyehe la, ye̱ hõmo̱ ní nyehõmi ke̱-ba bie̱ le hewo̱; edšake̱ *mei ayiwalaheremo̱ hewo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ tšũmi ke̱-tšṍ nyehĩe. *

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Ši afii enyo̱ ne̱ ní hõmo̱ ba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni eſe̱ afii enumo̱ hũ lolo ni hũmo̱ lo kpamo̱ be̱ mli.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ tšũmi ke̱-tšṍ nyehĩe, koni mahā nyeteṅ meikomei kẽ aſe̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni mahere nyeyiwala ke̱ dšiemo̱ kpeteṅkple.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ dšee nye nyehã miba bie̱, ši Nyoṅmo̱ moṅ ni; ni le̱ noṅṅ ebaṅõmi efe take̱ Farao tše̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ no̱ nuṅtšo̱ ke̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱ lumo̱.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Nyebe afea oyá ni nyeyaä mitše̱ ṅõ, ni nyekē̱ale̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni obi Iosef kē̱ ne̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ewomi Mizraim fẽ no̱ nuṅtšo̱; ba miṅõ, kātše̱!

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Ni obahĩ Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni obe̱ṅke̱mi, ho ke̱ obii ke̱ onãbii ke̱ otōi ke̱ otšinai ke̱ nibii fẽ ni oye̱;

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: ni malè̱o ye̱ dše̱i; edšake̱ eſe̱ hõmo̱ afii le̱ enumo̱ lolo, koni okaye ohĩa, bo ke̱ owe ke̱ mei fẽ ni oyo̱.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Ni na, nyehĩe tua, ni minyemi Benyamin hũ hĩe tua ake̱ midientše̱ mike̱nye wieo̱ ke̱ minābu ne̱.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Ni nyeyagbaä mitše̱ minumnyam fẽ ni miyo̱ ye̱ Mizraim ke̱ nibii fẽ ni nyena le̱, ni nyehe afea oyá ni nyeke̱ mitše̱ abaã bie̱.

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Ni eho egbē enyemi Benyamin kue̱ no̱ ni efó, ni Benyamin hũ fó ſie ekue̱ no̱.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ni esā eſo̱ſō̱ enyemimei le̱ fẽ nā, ni efó eſie ame̱no̱; ni no se̱ le̱ enyemimei le̱ ke̱le̱ wie.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Ni anu sane ne̱ ye̱ Farao we le̱ ake̱: Iosef nyemimei eba! Ni Farao ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ná be mīše̱.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Kē̱mo̱ onyemimei le̱ ake̱: Noni nyefe ne̱: nyetẽrea nyekoloi le̱ adšatšui, ni nyeyiaṅ ke̱-yaä Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱,

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
