translation_verse: ni nyeyaṅõa nyetše̱ ke̱ nyebii ke̱ ho̱i, ni nyebaä miṅõ, ni mahãnye Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nikpakpai, ni nyeaye šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ni bo le̱ afā̃o ake̱: Noni nyefe ne̱: nyeṅõa ſīlii ke̱-dše̱a Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ nyebāa nyebii ke̱ nyeṅãmei, ni nyeyaṅõa nyetše̱ ke̱-baä.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ nyekadia nyenibii ase̱; ši Mizraim šikpoṅ mū le̱, fẽ no̱ nikpakpai le̱ nyenõṅ.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Ni Israel bihĩĩ le̱ fe nakai. Ni Iosef hāame̱ ſīlii; take̱ boni Farao fále̱ le̱, ni ehãame̱ gbe̱no̱ niyenii.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Ni etše̱ le̱, nii ni emādšele̱ ne̱: Tedšii nyoṅma ni tĕre Mizraim nibii kpakpai, ke̱ tedšiyei nyoṅma ni tẽre able ke̱ abolo ke̱ niyenii, ni ake̱-yahã etše̱, ni eke̱-nyie gbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ewo enyemimei le̱ agbe̱ ni ame̱ṅõ-ſie no̱; ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: *Nyekayabéa ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ ne̱! *

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱dše Mizraim, ni ome̱ba ame̱tše̱ Iakob ṅõ ye̱ Kanaan sikpoṅ le̱ no̱,

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: ni ame̱bakē̱le̱ ake̱: Iosef ye̱ dšeṅ lolo, ni le̱ eyee̱ lumo̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱. Ni eyiṅ fele̱ ko̱šiko̱ši, edšake̱ eheeame̱ eyee.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ Iosef wiemo̱i fẽ ni eke̱ame̱ wie le̱. Ni beni ena ſīlii le̱ ni Iosef hã ake̱-bale̱ ṅõ le̱, ame̱tše̱ Iakob he tšele̱.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Ni Israel kē̱: Efá; mibi Iosef ye̱ dšeṅ lolo! Mate mayakwe̱ ehĩe däni magbo.

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Lea bihĩĩ ni eke̱ Iakob fo̱ ye̱ Mesopotamia le̱, ke̱ ebiyō Dina le̱. Ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ fẽ dši susumai nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ etẽ,

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Ni kē̱ aaba mii akē̱ Farao aabatšé̱nye, ni eebinye ake̱: Meni dši nye-nitšumo̱? le̱,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Zilpa, moni Laban ṅõ-hā ebiyō Lea le̱, bii; ni mene̱mei eke̱ Iakob fo̱, susumai nyoṅma ke̱ ekpa.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Bilha, moni Laban ṅõ-bã ebiyō Rahel le̱, bii ní eke̱ Iakob fo̱ le̱, snsumai le̱ fẽ dši kpawo.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Susumai fē ni ke̱ Iakob ba Mizraim ni dše̱ ehe̱ mli ne̱, sõro ebii le̱ aṅãmei le̱, *susumai le̱ fẽ dši nyoṅmai-ekpa ke̱ ekpa.

english_verse: Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of
translation_verse: Ni Iosef bii ni efo̱ ye̱ Mizraim le̱ dši susumai enyo̱. Iakob we le̱ fẽ ni ba Mizraim le̱ nā šio̱ *susumai nyoṅmai-kpawo. *

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef sã eſīli ni eyiṅ ete etše̱ Israel kpēmo̱ ye̱ Gošen. Ni beni enale̱ le̱ ebo egbẽ ekue̱ no̱, ni efó eſie ekue̱ no̱ āhũ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Ni Israel kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ ni mina ohĩe ake̱ oye̱ dšeṅ lolo ne̱, hã magbo.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ enyemimei le̱ kē̱ etše̱ we le̱ ake̱: Miya ni miyagba Farao ake̱: Minyemimei ke̱ mitše̱ we le̱ ni yo̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ eba miṅõ;

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: nyekē̱ale̱ ake̱: Otšũdši lè̱o̱ koloi kē̱-dše̱ wo̱blahĩaṅ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, wo̱ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ fẽ; koni ehã nyehĩ Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ no̱. Edšake̱ Mizraimbii *nyãṅeo̱ mofẽmo ní dši kolokwe̱lo̱ *

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱sā ame̱kē̱ Farao akē̱: Gbo̱tō wo̱ba ye̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱, edšake̱ otšũdši le̱ akoloi le̱ náá niyelihe; edšake̱ hõmo̱ le̱ nā ewa ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ wo̱mīkpao fai ni ohā otšũdši ahĩ Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ Iosef akē̱: Otše̱ ke̱ onyemimei le̱ eba oṅõ ne̱;

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ kã ohĩe; šikpoṅ le̱, beni hĩ fè fẽ ni dši Gošen šikpoṅ le̱, hã otše̱ ke̱ onyemimei le̱ ahĩ dše̱i; ni ke̱dši ole ame̱teṅ meikomei ṅí dši gbomei ni sa le̱, no le̱ ṅõame̱ ofe oṅukpai ye̱ mikoloi le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Ni Farao bi Iakob ake̱: Afii enyie oye?

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Ši niyenii be̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ hekoheko; edšake̱ hõmo̱ le̱ nā ewa naakpa, ni Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ mīgboi ke̱ hõmo̱.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef bua šika fẽ ni ana ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ni ame̱ke̱-bahe ṅmā̃ le̱ nā, ni Iosef ke̱ šika le̱ ba Farao we le̱.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ni heni šika tã ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱; Mizraimbii fẽ ba Iosef ṅõ ni ame̱hakē̱: Hãwo̱ nii wo̱ye! ši mẽhewo̱ ni ookwé̱ ni wo̱o̱gboi, ake̱-ní we̱šika etã hewo̱ le̱?

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosef ké̱: Ni nyešika etã ne̱, nyeṅõa nyekoloi nyehãa, ni mahãnye ye̱ nyekoloi le̱ anā.

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Beni nakai afi le̱ ho le̱, ame̱ba eṅṍ ye̱ afi ni dši enyo̱ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱bakē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱ṅõ-tēṅ wo̱nuṅtšo̱ ake̱ wo̱šika ke̱ koloi kui le̱ fẽ etã, ni ake̱-ba wo̱nuṅtšo̱ ṅõ; eſe̱ko nokonoko ye̱ wo̱nuṅtšo̱ hĩe doṅṅ, ake̱ dša wo̱gbomotšei ke̱ wo̱šikpõdši.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Mẽhewo̱ ookwe̱ ni wo̱o̱gboi, wo̱ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ? Nõ niyenii ohewo̱ ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ le̱, koni wo̱ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ le̱ atšṍmo̱ Farao nyṍdši, ni ohãwo̱ dũmo̱nii, koni wo̱yi aná wala, ni wo̱kagboi, ni wo̱šikpoṅ le̱ mīhatšṍ amaṅfõ.

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Ni Iosef he Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ ehã Farao; edšake̱ Mizraimnyo-fẽ-Mizraimnyo hõ ešikpoṅ, edšake̱ hõmo̱ le̱ efèame̱; bo̱ni fe ni šikpoṅ le̱ tšṍ Farao nõ ne̱.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Dša oso̱foi le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ke̱ ni ehee; edšake̱ oso̱foi le̱ ye̱ gbe̱nä ko ni Farao hãa-ame̱, ni ame̱gbe̱nã ni Farao hãa-ame̱ le̱ ame̱yeo̱; nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱hõõ ame̱šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iosef kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Na, mihenye ke̱ nyešikpoṅ le̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ mihã Farao; na, nyedũmo̱nii ne̱, ní nyedũ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Ni Iosef ṅõ ene̱ efe akpo̱ efõ ši ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ake̱ Farao aṅõ mlidšãi enumo̱ mli ekome, dša oso̱foi le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ke̱ tšṍṍ Farao nõ.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Ni Israel hĩ Mizraim, ye̱ Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱náná šikpṍdši ye̱ no̱, ni ame̱fo̱fo̱i, ni *ame̱yi fá babaō. *

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: ši ké̱ mike̱ mitše̱mei le̱ yawo̱ le̱, owómi ke̱-dše Mizraim, ni oyafũmi ye̱ *amefũhe le̱. Ni eké̱: Mafe bo̱ni okē̱ le̱.

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Ni eké̱: Kãmi kitã! Ni ekále̱ kitã. Ni Israel mã eyi ši ye̱ sātšo le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Ni ayakē̱ Iakob akē̱: Na, obi Iosef mība oṅõ. Ni Israel wadše ehe ete ši etá sātšo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Ni Iakob kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Mawu Ofe le̱ dšie ehe kpo etšṍmi ye̱ *Luz ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni edšō̱mi, *

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱, beni midše̱ Mesopotamia mihaä le̱, *Rahel gbo ye̱ mihe ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ye̱ gbe̱ teṅ, beni eſe̱ gbe̱ kukuō ko ni aše̱o̱ Efrat le̱, ni mifũle̱ ye̱ Efrat ni dši Betlehem le̱ gbe̱ le̱ mase̱i. *

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef dšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ enakutšei ateṅ ke̱-ba, ni eho ekoto ši, eṅõ ehĩe ebu ši.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ši Israel kpã eninedšūrõ mli ni eṅõṅmẽ Efraim ni dši gbekẽ le̱ yiteṅ, ni eṅõ ebe̱ku eṅmẽ Manase yiteṅ, ni ehĩe kã he ni eto enidši le̱ nakai; ši Manase dši kromo̱bi.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Ni edšō̱ Iosef ni eke̱: Nyoṅmo̱, mo hĩe ni *mitše̱mei, Abraham ke̱ Isak, nyie le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ ní dši †mikwe̱lo̱ ke̱-dše̱ be-yino ni miyo̱ ke-baši ṅmene̱ ne̱, *

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: *bo̱fo le̱ ni kpõmi ke̱-dše efõṅ fẽ mli le̱, adšō̱ ghekẽbii ne̱, ni ehã aṅõ migbe̱i ke̱ mitše̱mei, Abraham ke̱ Isak, gbe̱ii atšé̱ame̱, ni ame̱yi afá ni ame̱tšṍme̱ mei babaō ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosef kē̱ etšē̱ ake̱: Dšee nakai ni, atā; ši mone̱ dši kromo̱bi; ṅõ oninedšũrõ oṅmẽ eyiteṅ.

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Ni etše ekplẽẽ ni ekē̱: Mile, mibi, mile; le̱ hũ ehatšṍ maṅ, ebatšṍ kpeteṅkple moṅ; ši kẽle̱ enyemi gbekẽ le̱ batšṍ kpeteṅkple fèle̱, ni eseši aatšṍ mãdši babaō.

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ni edšō̱ame̱ nakai gbĩ le̱, ni ekē̱: Bo, Israel aaṅõ-dšō̱ akē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ ahã otšṍ tamo̱ Efraim ke̱ Manasel Ni eṅõ Efraim eto Manase hĩe. Heb.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Ni Israel kē̱ Iosef ake̱: Na, mi le̱ mīgbo, ši Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱nye ahì ši, ní eke̱nye akũ se̱ aya nyetše̱mei ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Eefĩ etedšibi eṅmõ weintšo ke̱ etedšiyō bi hũ eṅmõ weintšonine; eke̱ wein aafo̱ etade he, ni ehebo le̱ eke̱ weinyibii amli lá aafo̱ he. Ioel

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Ehĩṅme̱ii tšuo̱ fō̱ ke̱ wein, ni enyã-nyõdši ye̱o̱ futā ke̱ fufo̱.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isakar le̱, tedši ni wuiaṅ esa dšile̱, ni ebuo̱ ši ye̱ koloi atšũi ateṅ;

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: ni ena ake̱ hedšō̱mo̱ ṅõ, ni Šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bũ ye̱ fe̱o̱; ni eba ekõṅ ši etẽre, ni etšṍ tšũlo̱ ni tšuo̱ onia.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Ni Dan aatšṍ onũfũ ni ble gbe̱ no̱, onãṅkã ni kã tempõṅ no̱, ni kõo̱ okpo̱ṅo̱ nanetšitši, ni eno̱tálo̱ le̱ kpaä gbēo̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: Iehowa, owalaheremo̱ le̱ gbe̱ mikwe̱o̱ ne̱! Lal.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftali le̱, ofrote ni he yo̱ oyá ni, ni ewieo̱ wiemo̱i ke̱ ṅõmo̱i. Kods.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Iosef le̱, tšo ni woo̱ yibii ni, nu ni baä he tšo ni woo̱ yibii ni, ni enidši le̱ kwō̱lo̱ö̱ gbogbo. Hos.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Ši egãi le̱ emli wa kpẽṅṅ, ni eni-dši ke̱ ekõdši ahe ye̱ oyá, edše̱ Iakob kãkãlo̱ le̱ deṅ, edše̱ tōkwe̱lo̱ ní dši Israel te̱sā le̱ gbe̱i amli,

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Otše̱ dšō̱mo̱i le̱ teke miblemabii adšō̱mo̱i le̱, ke̱-yaši nāno̱ goṅkpo̱i le̱ ahũsũi ano̱ tõ; ame̱aba Iosef yiteṅ, ke̱ le̱ ni dši enyemimei le̱ ateṅ le̱ *Nazirnyo le̱ yiteṅ pampamso! *

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benyamin le̱, klaṅ ni yo̱ hahāha ni; eeye emĩle̱lo lebi, ni gbe̱ke̱ le̱ eedša nomṅõnii le̱ amli. Kods.

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Mene̱mei fẽ dši Israel akutšei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱, ni noni ame̱tše̱ ke̱ame̱ wie ni eṅõ-dšō̱ame̱ ne̱; dšō̱mo̱ ni sa mofẽmo le̱, no eke̱-dšō̱le̱.

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Abō̱ le̱ ke̱ te̱kplo ni yo̱ mli le̱ ahe ye̱ Hetbii le̱ adeṅ.

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iakob ewo ebii le̱ akitã egbe nā le̱, ebua enãdši anā eſïe sā le̱ no̱, ni eṅõ emumo̱ ehã, ni abua enā aši emei le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef ho bu etše̱ hĩe, ni efó *eſĩe eno̱, ni eſo̱ enā. *

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Ni beni efómo̱ gbĩĩ le̱ ebo le̱, Iosef ke̱ Farao we le̱ bii le̱ wie ni ekē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ nyehĩe le̱, mīkpanye fai, nyewoa Farao toi no̱ ake.

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱: Ya ni oyafũ otše̱, take̱ bo̱ni ehā okã kitã le̱.

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱še̱ Atad ablešāhe le̱ ni yo̱ Iordan se̱ le̱, ame̱fe yăra kpeteṅkple ni nā wa hũ ye̱ dše̱i; ni eye etše̱ be ṅko̱mo̱ gbĩĩ kpawo.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Ni ebii le̱ fe bo̱ni *ewoame kitã le̱ amghãle̱; *

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Ni beni Iosef efũ etše̱ se̱ le̱, eke̱ enyemimei le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ni ke̱le̱ te etše̱ fũ le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Mizraim ekoṅ.

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Ni beni Iosef nyemimei le̱ na ake̱ ame̱tše̱ egbo le̱, ame̱kē̱: Ekole̱ Iosef ebè̱wo̱ ewo emli, ni eebawowo̱ efõṅ fẽ ni wo̱fele̱ le̱ he nyõmo̱.

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱hã ayakē̱ Iosef ake̱: Otše̱ wo kitã dãni egbo ake̱:

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni nyekē̱ Iosef ne̱: Mīkpao fai ni oke̱ onyemimei le̱ ano̱tõmo̱ ke̱ ame̱be eša le̱ afaame̱; ši ame̱feo efõṅ. Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ wo̱ṅkpao fai ní oṅõ otše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ tšũdši le̱ ano̱tõmo̱ le̱ ofaame̱! Ni beni ame̱ke̱ Iosef wie nakai le̱, efó.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Ni enyemimei le̱ hũ te ame̱yabumo̱ ši ye̱ ehĩe ni ame̱kē̱: Na, otšũdši dšiwo̱!

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Nye le̱, nyesusumi efõṅ; ši *Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, esusule̱ ekpakpa, beni afe ni ahere mei babaõ yiwala take̱ bo̱ni eba mli ùmene ne.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyekašea gbeyei! malè̱nye ke̱ nyebii le̱. Ni eše̱dše ame̱mĩ, ni eke̱ame̱ wie tšuidšũrõ nā.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Ni Iosef na Efraim nãnãkãnsowai; ni Manase bi Makir bii le̱ hũ afo̱ame̱ *aſie Iosef ſuo̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosef hã Israelbii le̱ kãle̱ kitã ni ekē̱: Sramo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ aabasranye kẽ, ni nyeṅõ miwui le̱ ke-dše bie̱.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Ni *Iosef ke̱ enyemimei le̱ fẽ ke̱ nakai yino̱bii le̱ fẽ gboi. *

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Agbene maṅtše̱ hẽ ko bate ši ye̱ Mizraim ní lee Iosef.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Ni eke emaṅbii le̱ ake: Nyekwe̱a, Israelbii amaṅ le̱ yi efá ni ame̱ná hewale̱ hũ fèwo̱.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyebaä, nyehãa woke̱ame̱ ayea ṅā mli, koni ame̱yi akafá ní ebaba mli ake, ké̱ ta ko bate ši le̱, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱yafata wo̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ ahe ní ame̱ke̱wo̱ ṅwu ní ame̱mīfã ke̱-ṅdše šikpoṅ le̱ no̱!

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Ši babaō ní ame̱waäame̱ yi le̱, babaō ní ame̱yi fáa ní ame̱ſereo̱ dši no, ni ame̱tšui suo̱ Israelbii le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Ni Mizraimbii le̱ hĩe Israelbii le̱ nyṍdšiahĩemo̱ še̱ī,

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: ni nyṍdšiahĩemo̱ še̱ī ní ame̱ke̱-hĩe-ame̱ ye̱ sũ ke̱ ntaya femo̱ ke̱ ṅmõši ni-tšumo̱ sro̱toi fẽ mli le̱, ha ame̱dšeṅhĩle̱ dše ame̱tšine.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Ni Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Hebriyei-fo̱yei, ní ame̱teṅ mokome gbe̱i dši Šifra ní mokome hũ gbei dši Pua le̱,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: ake: Ké̱ nyete Hebriyei le̱ afo̱me̱ ní nyena ye̱ fomo-sẽi le̱ no̱ ake binūṅ le̱, nyegbeale̱, ši ke̱dši biyōṅ le̱, ehĩ ši.

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Ši yeifo̱yei le̱ yaše Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei, ni ame̱fee boni Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ame̱ le̱, ši ame̱here gbekẽbiihĩĩ le̱ ayiwala.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ni Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ tšé̱ yeife̱yei le̱ ni ekē̱ame̱ ake: Mẽhewo̱ nyefe nakai ni nyehere gbekẽbiihĩĩ le̱ ayiwala le̱?

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Ni yeife̱yei le̱ kē̱ Farao ake̱: Edšake̱ Hebriyei le̱ tamo̱o̱ Mizraimyei, ši ame̱ le̱, ame̱ye̱ kamkam, ni beni yōfo̱yō le̱ kē̱ eše̱o̱ ame̱ṅõ le̱, ame̱fo̱ momo.

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ní yeife̱yei le̱ še Nyoṅme̱ gbeyei hewo le̱, ehã ame̱ſere.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao wo emaṅbii le̱ fẽ akpo ake̱: Binū-fẽ-binū ní aafo̱ le̱, nyeya-še̱ale̱ nyefoa fā le̱ mli, ši biyō-fe-biyō le̱, nyehãa eyi anaa wala!

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ ná mũsũ, ni efo̱ binū; ni beni ena ake̱ *ehe ye̱ fe̱o le̱, eṅole̱ etē nyõdši etẽ. *Bo̱f.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Ni *enyemiyō damo̱ se̱ fle̱ṅṅ ēkwe̱ noni aafele̱. *

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Ni Farao biyō le̱ ba ebedšū ye̱ fā le̱ nā, ni eweyei le̱ mīšĕra ši ye̱ fā le̱ toi; ni ena adeka le̱ ye̱ gălãi le̱ amli, ni etšũ eweyō yawó ke̱-ba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ni beni egble nā le̱, ena gbekẽ le̱, ni na, gbekẽnū le̱ mīfo. Ni emũsũṅ tšõle ye̱ ehewo̱ ni ekē̱: Hebribii le̱ abihĩĩ le̱ eko ne̱.

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Ni Farao biyō le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya! Ni oblayō le̱ te eyatšé̱ gbekẽ le̱ nye ke̱-ba.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ni Farao biyō le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ gbekẽ ne̱ ke̱-ya, ni oyahãle̱ fufo̱ ohãmi, ni mawoö nyõmo. Ni yō le̱ ṅõ gbekẽ le̱ ni eyahãle̱ fufo̱.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ni etšṍ ehe ekwe̱ bie̱ ke̱ bie̱, ni beni ena ake̱ moko be̱ dše̱i le, etſa Mizraimnyo le̱ nõ, ni eṅõle̱ etē šia mli. Bo̱f.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Agbene *Midian oso̱fo le̱ ye̱ biyei kpawo; ni ameba amebagbla nu ame̱wo nunumo̱-ahĩmai le̱ obõbõ, ní ame̱tše̱ tōi le̱ anu. *

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ši tōkwe̱lo̱i le̱ ba baſieame̱; ni Mose te ši, ni efã amehe, ni *ehã ametōi le̱ anu. *

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Mizraimnyo ko dšiewo̱ ye̱ tōkwe̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ, ni esā egbla nu le̱ tete ehãwo̱, ni ehã tōi le̱ anu.

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ ebiyei le̱ ake̱: Ni nẽgbe̱ eyo? Mẽhewo̱ ni nyešĩ nū le̱? Nyeya-tšé̱ale̱ ke̱-baä, koni ebaye nii!

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kplẽ nū le̱ ke̱ šihĩle̱; ni eno ebiyō Zipora ehã Mose.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Ni efo̱ binū, ni Mose wole̱ Geršom; edšake̱ ekē̱: Mibato gbo̱ ye̱ maṅse̱ šikpoṅ no̱.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ nakai gbĩĩ pī le̱ amli le̱ Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ bagbo, ni Israelbii le̱ dõmo̱ ntšo̱i ye̱ nyṍṅyeli le̱ hewo, ni ame̱fó ame̱tšé̱ Nyoṅmo̱; ni ame-nyṍṅyeli le̱ mli fómo̱-ke̱-tšémo̱ le̱ *yase̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ. *

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ nu ame̱ṅke̱mo̱yeli blo̱mo̱ le̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ kai *ekpãṅmo̱ ní eke̱ Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Iakob kpãṅ le̱; *

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: ni Nyoṅmo̱ kwe̱ Israelbii le̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ ame̱yi te̱.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: *Ni Iehowa kē̱: Na mina amanehũlũ ní mimaṅ ní yo̱ Mizraim le̱ naä le̱, ni *ame̱blo̱mo̱ ní ame̱blo̱ö̱ ye̱ ame̱kplalo̱i le̱ ahĩe le̱ minu, edšake̱ mile ame̱nidō̱nii le̱. *

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Ni agbene, na, Israelbii le̱ ablo̱mo̱ le̱ eše̱ miṅõ, ni misā mina haomo̱ ní Mizraimbii haoo̱ame̱ le̱;

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ake̱: Na, mi le̱, kē̱ mite Israelbii le̱ aṅõ, ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyetše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ tšũmi nyeṅõ ne̱, ni ame̱abimi ake̱: Té egbe̱iṅ? le̱, té mikē̱amē̱ tẽṅ?

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Ya ní oyabua Israel onukpai le̱ anā, ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iehowa, nyetše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ní dši Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Iakob Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, edšie ehe kpo etšõmi, ni ekē̱: Sramo̱ mibasranye, ni mina noni afeo̱nye ye̱ Mizraim le̱;

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: ni mikē̱ ake̱: Madšienye ke̱-dše Mizraim amanehũlũ le̱ mli ke-ya Kanaanbii ke̱ Hitbii ke̱ Amorbii ke̱ Perizbii ke̱ Hivbii ke̱ Iebusbii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, šikpoṅ ní fufo̱ ke̱ wò hoo ye̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱abo ogbē toi, ni oke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ aya Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, ni nyeyakē̱le̱ ake̱: *Iehowa, Hebribii a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱wo̱ ebakpe; nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱mīkpao fai, hã wo̱nyie gbĩĩ etẽ gbe̱ ke-ya ṅã le̱ no̱, koni wo̱yašã afo̱le we̱hã Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱. *

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱ mile ake̱ Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ eṅmẽṅnye gbe̱ ní nyeya, dša ninešiwale̱ nā.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Ni makpã minine mli, ni mike̱ minākpe̱nii fẽ ní mafe ye̱ dše̱i le̱ atſia Mizraim nii, ni no se̱ dãni eehã nyeya.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ke̱ okũ ose̱ ote Mizraim le̱, kwe̱ ní ofe nākpe̱-nii le̱ fẽ ní miṅõ-wo odeṅ le̱ ye̱ Farao hĩe; ši *mi le̱ mawadše etsui, ni ehãṅ maṅ le aya. *

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Ni okē̱ Farao ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱; *Mibi, mikromo̱bi dši Israel; *Ier.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: ni mīkē̱o ake̱: Hã mibi le̱ aya, ni eyasúmo̱mi; ši ke̱dši okplẽẽ ní eya le̱, no le, na, *magbe obi, okromo̱bi le̱! *

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ye̱ šitōhe le̱ ake̱ Iehowa bahẽṅle̱, ni ētaole̱ egbe.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Zipora ko̱ *te̱ ní nā ba, ni eṅõ-fo ebi le̱ ketia, ni eše̱ efõ enãdši anā ni ekē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ lá ayemforowu dšio hãmi. *Ios.

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eṅmē̃ ehe. Ketiafo le̱ hewo le̱ ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Lá ayemforowu dšio le̱.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Aaron ake̱: Ya ní oke̱ Mose ayakpe ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱. Ni ete ní eke̱le̱ yakpe ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ goṅ le̱ he, ni eſo̱ enā.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Ni Mose dšadse Iehowa wiemo̱i fẽ ní eke̱-tšũle̱ le̱ ke̱ okadii fẽ ní efã́le̱ ake̱ efe le̱ etšõ Aaron.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ Aaron te, ni ame̱yabua Israelbii anukpai le̱ fẽ nā.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Ni Aaron dšadše wiemo̱i fẽ ní Iehowa ke̱ Mose ewie le̱, ni efe okadii le̱ yẽ maṅ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ he ye. Ni heni ame̱nu ake̱ Iehowa *ebasra Israelbii le̱ ni ena ame̱manehũlũ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱mãme̱ ame̱yitšei aši ni ame̱so̱le. *

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ ake̱: Namo *dši Iehowa le̱ ni mabo egbē toi ní mahã Israel aya? Milee Iehowa, ni Israel hũ mihãã ame̱ya. *Dan.

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Hebribii a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱wo̱ ebakpe; nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱mīkpao fai ní ohã wo̱ya ni wo̱yanyie gbĩĩ etẽ gbe̱ ke̱-ya ṅã le̱ no̱, ni wo̱yašã afole wo̱hã Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅme̱ le̱, koni ekabatuawo̱ ke̱ gbĕle-hela la klante.

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Ni Farao sā kē̱: Na, agbe̱ne̱ maṅ le̱ *yi efa momo ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni nyehã ame̱dšo̱ö̱ amehe noṅṅ ne̱! *

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ le̱ Farao wo maṅ le̱ kplalo̱i ke̱ ame̱no̱kwe̱lo̱i le̱ akitã ake̱:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: Nyekahãa maṅ le̱ dſe̱i ame̱ṅõ-fe ntayāi le̱ doṅṅ tamo̱ tšutšu le̱; ame̱dientše̱ ameya ní ame̱yabuabua dſe̱i anā ame̱hã amehe;

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: ši ntayāi le̱ ayikule̱ ní amefe tšutšu le̱, nyehãa ame̱fea nakai noṅṅ, nyekatšea no̱; ši ame̱mīfe anihao, nohewo̱ ni ame̱blo̱ö̱ ake̱: Hã wo̱ya ní wo̱yašã afole wo̱hã wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱!

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Ahã nitšumo̱ le̱ anyẽ gbomei le̱, koni ato̱ame̱ ní ame̱kabo yakawiemo̱i atoi!

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ kplalo̱i le̱ ke̱ ame̱ne̱kwe̱loi le̱ dše kpo ni ame̱yakē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Farao kē̱ ne̱: Mihããnye dſe̱i doṅṅ;

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: nyedientše̱ nyeyaä nyeyataoa dſe̱i ye̱ hefẽhe ní nyeana eko ye̱ nyehãa nyehe; ši kẽle̱ atšeṅ nyenitšumo̱ le̱ ne̱ nokonoko.

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ gbe̱ ſã Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ, ni ame̱buabua gbetšelii anā ame̱ṅõ-fe dſe̱i.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Ši kplalo̱i le̱ tšire̱ ame̱yise̱ ame̱kē̱: Nyegbea nyedāgbĩ nitšumo̱i le̱ anā tamo̱ be mli ní dſe̱i yo̱ le̱!

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ni ayi Israelbii le̱ ano̱kwe̱lo̱i ní Farao kplalo̱i le̱ ṅõ-to ame̱no̱ le̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni nyè ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱ fẽ nyegbee nyentayāi ní atonye le̱ anā tamo̱ sá le̱?

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israelbii le̱ ano̱kwe̱lo̱i le̱ ba ni ame̱bablo̱ ame̱wo Farao ame̱kē̱: Mẽhewo̱ oke̱ otšũdši yeo̱ ne̱ke̱?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Ahãã otšũdši adſe̱i, ši ntayāi le̱, ame̱kē̱ wo̱fe dō kẽ; ni na, āyi otšũdši le̱, tše̱ tõmo̱ le̱ dše̱ omaṅ le̱.

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: Hedšõlo̱i dšinye, hedšõlo̱i! nohewo̱ nyekē̱ ake̱: Hã wo̱ya ní wo̱yašã afole wohã Iehowa le̱.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nyeyaä ní nyeyatšua nii; ni dſe̱i le̱ ahããnye, ši kẽle̱ ntayāi le̱ ayikule̱ nyefea nakai noṅṅ!

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israelbii le̱ ano̱kwe̱lo̱i le̱ na ake̱ sane fõṅ eyeame̱, edšake̱ akē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekatšea nyentayāi le̱ ní dši nyedāgbĩ nitšumo̱ le̱ no̱ gbĩkogbĩko.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱dše̱ Farao ṅõ ame̱baä le̱, ame̱banina Mose ke̱ Aaron ní ame̱damo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱,

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iehowa aakwe̱ ní ekodšo, edšake̱ nyehã wohe *edše fũ ewo Farao ke̱ etšũdši le̱, ni nyeṅõ klante nyewo ame̱dẽ ní ame̱ke̱-gbewo̱. *

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Ši Mose kũ ese̱ ke̱-te Iehowa ṅõ ni ekē̱: Nuṅtšo̱, mẽba ofe maṅ le̱ efõṅ ne̱ke̱? Mẽba otšũmi ke̱-ba bie̱ mo̱?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ši ke̱-dše̱ beyino ní miba Farao ṅõ ní mike̱le̱ bawie ye̱ ogbe̱i amli ne̱, efõṅ moṅ efeo̱ maṅ ne̱, ni dšiemo̱ hũ odšieko omaṅ le̱!

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: ni mike̱nye aate šikpoṅ ni *miwó minine no̱ ake̱ mike̱-ahã Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Iakob le̱ no̱, ni mike̱-ahãnye ní nyeye no, midši Iehowa le̱! *

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron wie, ni efã́ame̱ ake̱ ameya Israelbii le̱ ke̱ Mizraim maṅtše̱ Farao le̱ ṅõ, ní ame̱ya-dšie Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši onukpai ye̱ ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱: Israel kromo̱bi Ruben le̱ bii ne̱: Hanok ke̱ Palu, Hezron ke̱ Karmi; mene̱mei dši Ruben wekui le̱.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Ni Simeon bii ne̱: Iemuel ke̱ Iamin ke̱ Ohad ke̱ Iakin ke̱ Zohar ke̱ Saul, Kanaanyō le̱ bi le̱; mene̱mei dši Simeon wekui le̱.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Geršon bii ne̱: Libni ke̱ Šimei ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ni Merari bii ne̱: Maheli ke̱ Muši. Mene̱mei dši Levi wekui le̱ ye̱ ame̱fo̱mo̱i le̱ anā.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Ni Izehar bii ne̱: *Kora ke̱ Nefeg ke̱ Zikri. *

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Ni Uziel bii ne̱: Mišael ke̱ Elzafan ke̱ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron we̱ Aminadab biyō Eli-šeba ní dši Nahašon nyemiyō le̱, ni eke̱le̱ fo̱ *Nadab ke̱ Abihu, Eleazar ke̱ Itamar. *

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Ni Kora bii ne̱: Asir ke̱ Elkana ke̱ Abiasaf. Mene̱mei dši Korabii wekui le̱.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Aaron ke̱ Mose ni Iehowa kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeyadšiea Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ ame̱tai le̱ anā le̱.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Ame̱dši mei ní ke̱ Farao, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, wie, koni adšie Israelbii le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim le̱; nakai Mose ke̱ Aaron le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ye̱ gbĩ no̱ ní Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ake̱ Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Midši Iehowa le̱; kē̱mo̱ Farao, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, nii fẽ ní mike̱o wieo̱ le̱.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ake̱: Na, minā tšee; té aafe tēṅ ní Farao aabomi toiṅ? K.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ Aaron te Farao ṅõ, ni amefe bo̱ni Iehowa efã́ame̱ le̱; ni Aaron ṅõ etšo le̱ efõ ši ye̱ Farao ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ahĩe, ni etšṍ šikpã.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo ṅõ etšo efõ ši, ní ame̱tšã́mo̱ šikpãi; ši Aaron tšo le̱ mī̃ ame̱tšei le̱.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Ni awadše Farao tšui, ni ebooame̱ toi, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa *ewie le̱. *

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Farao tšui wa, ekplẽẽ ní maṅ le̱ aya.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Ya Farao ṅõ lebi; na, ēdše kpo eya fā le̱ nā, ni oyadamo̱ fā le̱ nā omẽle̱, ni tšo le̱ ní tšṍ onũfũ le̱ ko̱ ohĩe odẽ,

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: ni okē̱le̱ ake̱: Iehowa, Hebribii le̱ a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, tšũmi oṅõ ake̱ mibakē̱o ake̱: *Hã ní mimaṅ le̱ aya ní ame̱ya-súmo̱mi ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱; ni na, okplẽko ke̱-baši bene̱. *

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Boni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ene̱ oke̱-ale ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱: na, mike̱ tšo ní mihĩe ye̱ midẽ ne̱ batſa fā le̱ mli nu le̱, ni *eetšṍ lá. *

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Ni lōi ni yo̱ fā le̱ mli le̱ aagboi, ni fá le̱ aaša, ni Mizraimbii le̱ aanyãṅe fā le̱ mli nu le̱ numo̱.

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Kē̱mo̱ Aaron ake̱: Ko̱ otšo le̱, ni okpã onine mli ye̱ Mizraim *nui le̱ ke̱ ame̱nudšō̱i le̱ ke̱ ame̱fāi le̱ ke̱ ame̱kpākpoi le̱ ke̱ ame̱nui ní bua ši le̱ fẽ no̱ ní ame̱tšṍmo̱ lá; ní nu ní yo̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ, ye̱ tšonibii ke̱ te̱nibii amli le̱, aatšo lá. *Kpods.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ Aaron fe bo̱ni Iehowa fã́ame̱ le̱, ni ewó etšo le̱ no̱, ni eke̱-tſa nu ní yo̱ fā le̱ mli le̱ ye̱ Farao ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ahĩe, ni fā le̱ mli nu le̱ fè tšṍ lá.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni lōi ní yo̱ fā le̱ mli le̱ gboi, ni fā le̱ ša, ni Mizraimbii le̱ nyẽẽ fā le̱ mli nu le̱ anu; ni lá so̱ṅṅ yo̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ni *Mizraim ṅkũnyāyelo̱i le̱ ke̱ ame̱ṅkũnyāyeli-ṅāi le̱ fe nakai noṅṅ. Ni awadše Farao tšui ni ebooame̱ toi, take̱ boni Iehowa ewie le̱. *K.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Ni Farao kũ ese̱ ete ewe, ni ehãã ene̱ hũ ata etšui mli.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ni Mizraimbii le̱ fẽ dšedšē nubui ye̱ fā le̱ hewo̱hewo̱ ní ame̱na nu ame̱nu, edšake̱ fā le̱ mli nu le̱ ame̱nyẽẽ amenu.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Ni beni Iehowa tſa fā le̱ nõ se̱ le gbĩĩ kpawo bafoṅ.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši okplẽẽ ní ameya le̱, na, mike̱ ko̱ko̱denei bahao okpokpai le̱ fẽ;

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Wó̱. Ni ekē̱: Afe bo̱ni okē̱ le̱ koni oná ole ake̱ *mokomoko be̱ ní tamo̱ Iehowa wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa fe boni Mose kē̱ le̱, ni ko̱ko̱denei le̱ gboi ye̱ šĩai ke̱ kpoi ano̱ ke̱ dſe̱iaṅ.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Ši beni Farao na ake̱ ená hedšo̱le̱ le̱, ewadše etsui, ni ebooame̱ toi, take̱ boni Iehowa ewie le̱.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ke̱mo̱ Aaron ake̱: Kpã otšo le̱ mli ní oke̱-tſa šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ mlu le̱, koni etšṍ tõntõṅi ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Ni amefe nakai; ši Aaron kpã enine mli ke̱ etšo le̱ ni eke̱-tſa šikpoṅ mlu le̱, ni etšṍ tõntõṅi ye̱ gbomei ke̱ koloi ahe, šikpoṅ mlu fẽ tšṍ tõntõṅi ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ṅkũnyāyelo̱i le̱ kē̱ Farao ake̱: *Ene̱ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ wao ne̱! Ši †awadše Farao tšui, ni ebooame̱ toi, boni Iehowa ewie le̱. *

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ní oyadamo̱ Farao hĩe, na, ēba fā le̱ nā; ni okē̱le̱ ake̱: Boni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: *Hã mimaṅ le̱ aya, ní ame̱yasúmo̱mi. *

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa fe nakai, ni ofo̱ii babaō ba. Farao we ke̱ etšũdši awei ke̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ; ni šikpoṅ le̱ hĩe kpãtã ye̱ ofo̱ii le̱ ahewo̱.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao tšé̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron ni ekē̱: Nyeyaä nyeyašãa afole nyehãa nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱.

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Esaa ake̱ afeo nakai; edšake̱ Mizraimbii anihĩnii woke̱bašã afole wo̱hã Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; na, ke̱dši wo̱ke̱ *Mizraimbii anihĩnii le̱ šã afole ye̱ amehĩe ne̱, ani ametſiaṅwo tei? *

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Wo̱o̱nyie gbĩĩ etẽ gbe ke̱-ya ṅã le̱ no̱, ní wo̱yasã afole wohã Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, *take̱ boni ekē̱wo̱ le̱, *

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱ ake̱: Mibaṅmẽnye gbe̱ ní nyeya, koni nyeyašã afole nyehã Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ye̱ ṅã le̱ ne̱; ši šoṅṅ ke̱ke̱ ni nyekayaä; *nyekpaä fai nyehãami! *K.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Na, mibadše oṅõ maya ní mayakpa Iehowa fai, koni ofo̱ii le̱ adše Farao ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ke̱ emaṅbii le̱ ano̱ wó̱; ši šišiumo̱ sane ke̱ke̱ ni Farao akaye doṅṅ ake̱ ehãṅ maṅ le̱ aya ayašã afole ahã Iehowa.

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ni Mose dše Farao hĩe ni ete ni *eyakpa Iehowa fai. *K.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa fe boni Mose kē̱ le̱, ni edšie ofo̱ii le̱ ye̱ Farao ke̱ etšũdši ke̱ emaṅbii le̱ ane̱, eſe̱e̱ ekomeflo.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Ši Farao *wadše etšui ekoṅ, ni ehãã maṅ le̱ aya. *

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ Iehowa fe nakai, ni Mizraimbii akoloi le̱ fẽ gboi; ši Israelbii akoloi le̱ ateṅ ekomeflo gboo.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ni ṅkũnyāyelo̱i le̱ nyẽẽ Mose hĩe adamo̱ ye̱ asane le̱ hewo, edšake̱ asanei le etšĕrẽ ṅkũnyãyeloi le ke̱ Mizraimbii le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa wadše Farao tšui, ni ebooame̱ toi, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose ewie le̱.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ní oyadamo̱ Farao hĩe, ni okē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Hebribii a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Hã mimaṅ le̱ aya, koni ame̱yasúmomi.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ kũle̱ bene̱ mikpã minine mli mike̱ gbẽle-hela etſao ke̱ omaṅ le̱ nõ, ni afoö ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ aše̱ afõ momo.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Okã he ōwó ohe no̱ ye̱ mimaṅ le̱ no̱ kẽ ake̱ ohãã ameya.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Na, wó aafe bene̱ yino̱ le̱ mahã *nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i ní nā wa naakpa dientše̱ ane̱ ní anako no̱ dã ye̱ Mizraim ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ ní atole̱ le̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. *Hiob

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ tšũ ní ayabua okoloi le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní oyo̱ ye̱ ṅãno̱ le̱ anā ke̱-ba šĩa; ši gbomo-fẽ-gbomo ke̱ kolo-fẽ-kolo ní aana ye̱ ṅãne̱ ní akele baa šĩa le̱, nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ aayiame̱ ni ame̱agboi.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Ni Farao tšũdši le̱ ateṅ moni yaše Iehowa wiemo le̱ gbeyei le̱, ehã etšũdši ke̱ ekoloi dšo foi ke̱-ba šĩa;

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Kpã onine mli ke̱-ya ṅwei, koni nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i aba Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ, ye̱ gbomei ano̱ ke̱ koloi ano̱ ke̱ ṅãno̱ bāi fẽ no̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ ne̱ ke̱ la ní tšoo̱ plamplam ye̱ nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ ateṅ, ni ena wa naakpa dientše̱, boni anako no̱ dã ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ ke̱-dše̱ be mli ní etšṍ maṅ ne̱.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Dša Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱, heni Israelbii le̱ yo̱ le̱ ke̱ke̱ ni nyoṅme̱ṅte̱i le̱ ene̱e̱ ye̱.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao tšũ ayatšē̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron ke̱-ba, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: *Ene̱ le̱ mife eša; Iehowa le̱ dšalo̱ dšile̱, ši mi le̱ mike̱ mimaṅ le̱ meifõdši dšiwo. *

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: *Nyekpaä Iehowa fai ní nyoṅmo̱šimo̱i ke̱ nyoṅme̱ṅte̱i le̱ akpa, ši efá, ni mahã nyeya ni nyehĩṅ ši doṅṅ.

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱le̱ ake̱: Amrõ pe̱ ni madše kpo ye̱ mã le̱ṅ le̱, magbe minidši amli ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni nyoṅme̱šimo̱i le̱ ase̱ aafo, ni nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ eko baṅ doṅṅ, koni oná ole ake̱ dšeṅ le̱ Iehowa nõ ni.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ši mile ake̱ bo ke̱ otšũdši le̱, nyenáko nyeše Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbeyei.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Ši odonti ke̱ akoko le̱ hĩe akpãtã le̱; edšake̱ akoko le̱ ewo, ni odonti le̱ hũ egba.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ši ṅmā̃ ke̱ able hĩe kpãtãã; edšake̱ ekwẽko.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Ni Mose dše Farao ṅõ ni edše mã le̱ṅ, ni eyagbe enidšiaṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni nyoṅme̱šimo̱i ke̱ nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ se̱ fo, ni nyoṅmo̱ le̱ kpa ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Ši beni Farao na ake̱ nyoṅmo̱ne̱mo̱ ke̱ nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i ke̱ nyoṅmo̱šimo̱i le̱ ase̱ efo le̱, esā efe eša ekoṅ, ni ewadše etšui, le̱ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Ni Farao tšui bawa, ni ehãã Israelbii le̱ aya, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ewie ye̱ Mose nā le̱.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ayimo̱ ošĩai ke̱ otšũdši fẽ ašĩai ke̱ Mizraimbii fẽ ašĩai, bo̱ni otše̱mei le̱ ke̱ otše̱mei atše̱mei le̱ enako no̱ pẽṅ ke̱-dše̱ beyino ní ame̱ba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱. Ni etšṍ ehe, ni edše Farao ṅõ.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao tšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽ beyino noṅṅ ni nū ne̱ aahaowo̱ ke̱-yaši? Hã gbomei le̱ aya ní ame̱yasúmo̱ Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱! Ani oleko ake̱ Mizraim mifite?

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Ni Mose kpã etšo le̱ mli ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni Iehowa hã bokã kō̱yo̱ batſa ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ fẽ; ni beni dše tše̱reo̱ le̱, bokã kō̱yo̱ le̱ ke̱ bālabii le̱ eba.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Ni bālabii le̱ ba Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱, ni ame̱baſie Mizraim kpokpai le̱ fẽ no̱ nyẽṅẽnyẽṅẽ, bālabii le̱ eko bako dã ní tame̱ame̱, ni ame̱se̱ ne̱ hũ eko baṅ nakai doṅṅ.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱ha šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ hĩe ni šikpon le̱ ne̱ wo duṅ, ni ame̱ye šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bāi fẽ ke̱ tšei ní nyoṅmo̱ṅte̱i le̱ šĩ le̱ no̱ yibii fẽ, ni nokonoko eſe̱e̱ ní dši efo̱ ye̱ tšei lo bāi ano̱ ye̱ ṅãno̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao tšũ ayatšé̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron ke̱-ba oya mli ni ekē̱: *Mife Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ke̱ nye hũ eša; *

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: ši agbe̱ne̱ ṅõ mihe eša le̱ ofami šikome ne̱ hũ, ni *nyekpaä Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, fai, koni edšie ne̱ke̱ gbĕle ne̱ ke̱ke̱ ke̱-dše̱ mino̱. *

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Ni edše Farao ṅõ ete *eyakpa Iehowa fai. *

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hã anai kō̱yo̱ ní nā wa naakpa batſa, ni elō bālabii le̱ ke̱-te, ni eke̱ame̱ yaſie Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ mli; bālabii le̱ ateṅ ekomeflo eſe̱e̱ ye̱ Mizraim kpokpai le̱ fẽ no̱.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa wadše Farao tšui, ni ehãã Israelbii le aya.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kpã enine mli ke̱-te ṅwei, ni duṅ kpī wo ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no fẽ gbĩĩ etẽ;

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: mokomoko enaa enanyo, ni mokomoko etee ši ye̱ egbe̱he gbĩĩ etẽ; ši dšeṅ tše hã Israelbii le̱ fẽ ye̱ ame̱hĩle̱hei le̱.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao tšé̱ Mose ni ekē̱. Nyeyaä ní nyeyasúme̱a Iehowa; nyetoi ke̱ nyetšinai le̱ ke̱ke̱ nyešĩa ye̱ bie̱; *nyebii le̱ hũ kenye aya. *K.

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Dša bo hũ ohãwo̱ gbē-afo̱lei ke̱ šā̃-afo̱lei wo̱hĩe wo̱dẽ, ní woyašã we̱hã Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Ni wo̱koloi akui le̱ hũ wo̱ke̱-mīya, ni ašĩṅ kokloto tete ye̱ se̱; ši nomei eko wo̱ke̱-yasúmo̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; ši wo̱dientše̱ wo̱lee noni wo̱ke̱-yasúmo̱ Iehowa, ake̱ dša wo̱še̱ dše̱i fẽdã.

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa wadše Farao tšui, ni ekplẽẽ ake̱ ameya.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dšee mino̱ ní oya! Kwe̱ ohe ní ahĩ, ní okaba mihĩe doṅṅ; ši gbĩ ne̱ ní oona mihĩe le̱, oogbo.

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Odšogbāṅ; mibaṅ ohĩe doṅṅ!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Eſe̱ amanehũlũ kome ni mike̱-baba Farao ke̱ Mizraim no̱, ni no se̱ le̱ eehã nyedše bie̱ nyeya; beni eehã nyefẽ nyeya kwrā le̱, no le̱ ſiemo̱ tete ebaſienye ke̱-dše̱ bie̱.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Agbene kpã owo maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ ake̱ *nū-fẽ-nũ ke̱ yō-fẽ-yō abăla dſieteinii ke̱ šikanii ye̱ enanyo deṅ. *

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hã maṅ le̱ hĩe ba nyam ye̱ Mizraimbii le̱ ahĩe; ni asaṅ Mose hũ, gbomo wulu dientše̱ dšile̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Farao tšũdši le̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: ni Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ *krome̱bii fẽ aagboi, ke̱-dše̱ Farao kromo̱bi le̱ ní táa esẽi le̱ no̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši nyṍṅyō ní yo̱ w̌ie̱ se̱ le̱ kromo̱bi le̱ tete no̱, ke̱ koloi akromo̱bii fẽ. *

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ni yāfó babaō aaba Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ, bo̱ni eno̱ bako dã ni asaṅ eno̱ baṅ doṅṅ;

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: ši Israelbii le̱, šiflo tete tšiṅ elile̱i ye̱ ame̱teṅ moko no̱ ke̱-dše̱ gbomo no̱ ke̱-yaši kolo no̱, koni nyena nyele ake̱ Iehowa *mīgbla Mizraim ke̱ Israel teṅ. *

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni otšũdši ne̱ fẽ aakpleke ši aba minõ, ni ame̱abakotomi ame̱akē̱: Dše kpo ní oya, bo ke̱ maṅ le̱ fẽ ní ye̱ ošiši le̱! ni no se̱ le̱ mate. Ni eke mlila dše Farao ṅõ ke̱-te.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Farao ebaboṅnye toi, koni minākpe̱nii le̱ afá ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ Aaron fe ne̱ke nākpe̱nii ne̱ fẽ ye̱ Farao hĩe; ši Iehowa *wadše Farao tšui, ni ehãã Israelbii le̱ adše ešikpoṅ le̱ no̱ aya. *

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ye lō le̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ noṅṅ, ašã ye̱ la mli, ni ake̱ abolo akpĩtĩ ke̱ ſie ní dšōo̱ aye.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Nyekayeale̱ eṅmõṅ, ni nyeke̱ nu akahoa, ši moṅ nyešãa ye̱ la mli, eyitšo ke̱ eſũo̱dši ke̱ emlinii le̱.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Edšake̱, makpa Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ, ni magbe Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ kromo̱bii fẽ, ke̱-dše̱ gbomo no̱ ke̱-yaši kolo no̱; ni Mizraim nyoṅmo̱i le̱ *makodšo ame̱fẽ, midsi Iehowa le̱! *

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ gbĩ ne̱ atšṍ kaimo̱-gbĩ ahãnye, ni nyeyele̱ gbĩdšŭrõ nyehã Iehowa *nyeke̱ nyesešibii fẽ, ni etšṍ nāno̱ akpo ehãnye.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Ni kleṅkleṅ gbĩ le̱ akpe kpē kroṅkroṅ, ni gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ hũ akpe kpē kroṅkroṅ ye̱ nyeteṅ; akatšu nitšumo̱ ko nitšumo̱ ko ye̱ mli, dša noni mofẽmo aaye ke̱ke̱ he nii nyetšu.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Ni nyeyea nakai akpĩtĩ gbĩdšŭrõ le̱; edšake̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ midšie nyetai le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; nohewo̱ le̱ nyeyea nakai gbĩ le̱ nye ke̱ nyesešibii fẽ, ní etšṍ nāno̱ akpo ehãnye.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱ nyeše̱ šikpoṅ ní Iehowa ke̱-bahãnye le̱ no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni ewo ši le̱, nyehĩea ne̱ke̱ dšámo̱ ne̱ mli.

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: nyekē̱a ake̱: Iehowa Hehō le̱ afole ni, edšake̱ beni etſia Mizraimbii anii le̱, eho Israelbii le̱ ašĩai le̱ ahe ye̱ Mizraim, ni edšie wo̱šĩai le̱. Ni maṅ le̱ mãmo̱ ame̱yi ši, ni ame̱so̱le.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ yiṅ ame̱te, ni ame̱-yafe bo̱ni Iehowa ewo Mose ke̱ Aaron kitã le̱, nakai amefe.

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ nyōṅ teṅ le̱ Iehowa tſia Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ kromo̱bii fẽ nii, ke̱-dše̱ Farao kromo̱bi ní táa esẽi le̱ no̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši moni aṅõle̱ nom ní awole̱ tšũṅ le̱ kromo̱bi no̱ ke̱ šĩa koloi akromo̱bii fẽ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Farao te ši nakai nyõ le̱ṅ noṅṅ, le̱ ke̱ etšũdši fẽ ke̱ Mizraimbii fẽ, ni yāfó babaō te ši ye̱ Mizraim; edšake̱ šĩa ko šĩa ko be̱ ní gbonyo be̱ mli.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Ni ehã ayatšé̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron nyō le̱ṅ ni ekē̱: Nyetea ši nyedšea mimaṅbii le̱ ateṅ nyeyaä, nye ke̱ Israelbii le̱, ni nyeyasúmo̱a Iehowa, take̱ bo̱ni nyekē̱ le̱.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ nyeṅõa nyetōi ke̱ nyetšinai le̱ hũ ke̱-yaä, *take̱ bo̱ni nyekē̱ le̱; ni nyedšo̱ami hũ. *

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ni Mizraimbii le̱ *tšire̱ maṅ le̱ yi se̱, koni ame̱he afe oyã́ ní ame̱dše šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Wo̱fẽ wo̱mīgboi! *

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fe bo̱ni Mose ekē̱ame̱ le̱, ni *ame̱băla dſie̱te̱inii ke̱ šikanii ke̱ mamai ye̱ Mizraimbii le̱ adeṅ; *

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ yiṅ ke̱-dše̱ Rameses ke̱-te Sukot, hĩĩ naneno̱nyielo̱i aafe mei akpei-ohai-ekpa, sõro gbekẽbii hũ.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Ni futufutugbomei babaō hũ fata ame̱he ke̱-te, ke̱ tōi ke̱ tšinai babaō dientše̱.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ mã le̱ ní ame̱ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim le̱ ame̱šã akpĩtĩ kakai; edšake̱ ešako, edšake̱ Mizraimbii le̱ ſieame̱ ni ame̱woo mẽ, ni ame̱sāko niyenii ame̱toko gbe̱nyiemo̱ le̱ hũ.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Nohewo ní ayeo ne̱ke̱ nyōṅ ne̱ ake̱ Iehowa gbĩdšŭrõ le̱, dši dšiemo̱ ní edšie-ame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱; ene̱ dši nyōṅ ní sa ake̱ ayeo̱le̱ gbĩdšũrõ ahãa Iehowa ye̱ Israelbii le̱ fẽ ateṅ, ye̱ ame̱seši fẽ mli.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron ake̱: Hehō le̱ he akpo̱ ne̱: Mokpõṅ ko mokpõṅ ko akaye eko.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Ši mofẽmo nyṍṅ ní ake̱ šika hele̱ le̱, ofole̱ ketia dãni eye eko.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Moni bahĩ nyeṅõ ke̱ apāfonyo hũ akaye eko.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Sĩa-fẽ-šìa aye enõ; ake̱ lō le̱ eko akadše kpo ye̱ šĩa le̱, *ni asaṅ nyekadſaä ewui le̱ eko. *Ioh.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel asafo le̱ fẽ afe nakai.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ moko ebatoö gbo̱ ni ētao ake̱ eyeo̱ Hehō le̱ ehãa Iehowa le̱, hã aflo̱ ehĩĩ le̱ fẽ ketia, fẽdã ní eba ní ebaye, ni eetsṍ tamo̱ moko ní afo̱le̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ši fōlo̱ ko fōlo̱ ko akaye eko.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mla kome akã ši ahã moni dši maṅ-nyo ke̱ moni batonye gbo̱.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fẽ fe nakai, bo̱ni Iehowa wo Mose ke̱ Aaron kitã le̱, nakai amefe.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ le̱ Iehowa dšie Israelbii le̱ ke̱-dše Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ ame̱tai le̱ anā.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Gbĩĩ kpawo le̱ fẽ le̱ aye akpĩtĩ, ni akana mãša abolo ko ye̱ oṅõ lo mãša ko ye̱ okpokpai ano̱ hekoheko.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, beni Iehowa ke̱o eba Kanaanbii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, bo̱ni ekã kitã etšõo ke̱ otše̱mei le̱, ake̱ eeṅõhão le̱,

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Ši tedšibi-fẽ-tedšibi ní afo kleṅkleṅ le̱, oke̱ tō akpõle̱; ši ke̱dši okpõõle̱ le̱, no le̱ kũ ekue̱ṅ. Ši gbomo kromo̱bi-fẽ-kromo̱bi ní yo̱ obihĩĩ ateṅ le̱, kpõle̱.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱, ke̱dši wó̱ lo wó̱se̱ ni obi bio ake̱: Meni dši ene̱? le̱, okē̱le̱ ake̱: Ninešiwale̱ nā Iehowa dšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim, ye̱ nyodši awe le̱.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Ni eetšṍ okadi ye̱ odẽ ke̱ kaimo̱-bõṅ ye̱ ohĩṅme̱ii ateṅ, edšake̱ ninešiwale̱ nā Iehowa dšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim.

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Farao ehã maṅ le̱ gbe le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ kplaa-ame̱ ke̱-tšṍṍ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ gbe̱ le̱, tše̱ no dšeke̱e̱, edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ kē̱: Koni maṅ le̱ akayana ta ko, ní ame̱ſa amehe, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Mizraim ekoṅ.

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Nohewo le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱ lo̱go̱ ši ke̱-tšṍ Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ he ṅã le̱ ne̱ gbe̱. Ni Israelbii le̱ fã tamo̱ ta ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose ṅõ Iosef wui le̱ ke̱-te; edšake̱ Iosef ehã Israelbii le̱ ekãle̱ kitã ni ekē̱: Sramo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ aabasranye kẽ, ní nyeṅõ miwui le̱ ke̱-dše bie̱.

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yiṅ ke̱-dše̱ Sukot, ni ame-yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Etam ye̱ ṅã le̱ nā.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ši Farao aakē̱ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ahewo̱ ake̱: Ame̱dũ gbe̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ṅã le̱ esa ame̱yi.

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Ni esā eſīli, ni elō emaṅ le̱ efata ehe;

english_verse: He commanded his officers in charge of his
translation_verse: ni eṅõ ſĩlii ní ahala ohai-ekpa ke̱ Mizraim ſĩlii le̱ fẽ, ke̱ ame̱fẽ ame̱no̱ tatše̱mei.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa wadše Mizraim maṅtše̱ Farao tšui ni etiu Israelbii le̱. Ši Israelbii le̱ dše kpo *ke̱ nine ní tšī. *

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ani dšee wiemo̱ ní wo̱ke̱o wie ye̱ Mizraim le̱ ne̱ ake̱: Fõmo̱ ní ohã wo̱súmo̱ Mizraimbii le̱? Ši fãṅ nõ moṅ ní wo̱súmo̱ Mizraimbii le̱ fè noni wo̱o̱bagboi ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱!
