english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni ke̱ miwo mihĩe nyam ye̱ Farao ke̱ eſīlii ke̱ ekpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ ano̱ le̱, Mizraimbii le̱ aana ale ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kpã enine mli ye̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ no̱; ni Iehowa hã bokã kō̱yo̱ ní nā wa batſa nakai nyõ le̱ṅ fẽ, ni ṅšo̱ le̱ ho ke̱-te, ni eha ṅšo̱ le̱ tšo šikpoṅ gbĩṅ, ni nu le̱ mli gba.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ lebi būbe le̱ mli le̱ Iehowa tšṍ la ke̱ atatu kutū le̱ mli *ekwe̱ Mizraim ta le̱, ni ehao Mizraim ta le; *Lal.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: ni efãmo̱ ame̱ſīlii le̱ anãdši, ni ewo-ame̱ hedšramo̱; ni Mizraimbii le̱ kē̱: Nye-hãa wo̱dšoa foi ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ahĩe; edšake̱ *Iehowa ke̱ Mizraim mīwu mīhãame̱! *K.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Kpã onine mli ye̱ nšo̱ le̱ no̱, koni nui le̱ akũ se̱ aba Mizraimbii le̱ ke̱ ame̱ſīlii ke̱ ame̱kpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ ano̱!

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kpã enine mli ye̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ no̱, ni beni dše tše̱re lebi le̱, ṅšo̱ le̱ kũ se̱ ke̱-baho ekoṅ, ni Mizraimbii le̱ dšo foi ame̱ke̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ bakpe; ni Iehowa še̱re̱ame̱ eſie ṅšo̱ le̱ teṅ.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Ni nui le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ba, ni ame̱-baha Farao ſīlii ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei ke̱ eta mū le̱ fẽ ní tiuame̱ ke̱-ba ṅšo̱ le̱ mli le̱ no̱; eſe̱e̱ ame̱teṅ mokome tete po.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ši Israelbii le̱ nyie sikpoṅ gbĩṅ no̱ ke̱-tsṍ ṅšo̱ le̱ teṅ, ni *nui le̱ tšṍ gbogbo ye̱ ame̱ninedšŭrõ ke̱ ame̱be̱kuiaṅ. *K.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ Iehowa fe ehere Israel yiwala nakai gbĩ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraimbii le̱ adeṅ; ni Israel na Mizraimbii le̱ ní ame̱gboi ame̱dſere ṅšo̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Ni Israel na nine wulu ní Iehowa ṅõ-tšõ Mizraim le̱; ni maṅ le̱ še Iehowa gbeyei, ni amehe Iehowa ke̱ *etšũle̱ Mose ame̱ye. *

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Farao ſīlii le̱ ke̱ eta le̱ elō ewo ṅšo̱ṅ; eſīliiatše̱mei ní ahala le̱ hũ ašiuame̱ ye̱ Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ṅ;

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: Iehowa, oninedšŭrõ le̱ hĩe eba nyam ye̱ hewale̱ na; Iehowa, oninedšŭrõ le̱ etšere̱ henye̱lo̱ le̱ mli.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Ogũgõ mli mumo̱ le̱ ake̱-bua nui le̱ anā; ṅšo̱kei le̱ mãmo̱ ši keikei ni bui le̱ hũ fĩmo̱ ye̱ ṅšo̱ le tšuiṅ.

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Otfa okō̱yo̱ le̱ hū, ṅšo̱ le̱ tšĩmo̱ ame̱no̱; ame̱šiu take̱ sumui ye̱ nui ní yo̱ hãmãhãmã le̱ mli.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Omlihĩle̱ nā okpla ne̱ke̱ maṅ ní okpõ ne̱, oke ohewale̱ le̱ tšoame̱ gbe̱ ke̱-te ošihĩle̱he kroṅkroṅ le̱.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ha gbeyei ke̱ ṅmiṅmi alōame̱; onine dale̱ nā so̱ṅṅ le̱ ame̱sẽ ši mũī tamo̱ te̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní omaṅ le̱ aaho, Iehowa, omaṅ ní ohe ne̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eeho eya.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Oke̱ame̱ aya ni oyate̱oame̱ ye̱ ono̱yeli goṅ le̱ no̱, heni oṅõ-fe ošihĩle̱he le̱, Iehowa, ní dši hekroṅkroṅ le̱, Nuṅtšo̱, ní onidši esā eto le̱.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Iehowa aaye maṅtše̱ ke̱-ate nāno̱i anāno̱! Lal.

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Farao okpe̱ṅo̱i le̱ ke̱ eſīlii le̱ ke̱ ekpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ te ṅšo̱ le̱ṅ, ni Iehowa hã ṅšo̱ le̱ mli nu le̱ kũ se̱ baha ame̱no̱; ši Israelbii le̱ nyie šikpoṅ gbĩṅ no̱ ke̱-tšṍ ṅšo̱ le̱ teṅ ke̱-te.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Ni gbalo̱yō Miriam ní dši Aaron nyemiyō le̱ ke̱ *fao hĩe edeṅ, ni yei le̱ fẽ nyie ese̱ ni ame̱ša fabii, ni ame̱dšodšoi. *Lal.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Ni Miriam here no̱ ehãame̱ ake̱: Nyelaä nyehãa Iehowa; edšake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam, okpo̱ṅo̱ ke̱ eno̱tálo le etšire̱ame̱ eſie ṅšo̱ṅ. K.

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mose hã Israelbii le̱ fã ke̱-dše̱ Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ nā ke̱-te Šur ṅã le̱ no̱; ní ame̱nyie gbĩĩ etẽ gbe̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni ame̱naa nu.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱ba Mara le̱, ame̱nyẽẽ Mara nu le̱ ame̱nu, edšake̱ ẽdšō; nohewo̱ le awo dše̱i Mara.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ wie hũhū̃hũ ame̱ši Mose ame̱kē̱: Meni wo̱nu?

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ni ebo etšé̱ Iehowa, ni Iehowa tšõle̱ tšo ko, ni beni eše̱ efõ nu le̱ mli le̱, nu le̱ baṅõ. Dše̱i ewoame̱ akpo ke̱ kitã ye̱, ni dše̱i hũ ekaame̱ ye̱,

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši oobo Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbē toi, ni oofe noni dša gbe̱ ye̱ ehĩe, ni oobo ekitãi le̱ atoi, ni ooye ekpoi le̱ fẽ no̱ le̱, no le̱ *helai le̱ ní mike̱ba Mizraimbii ano̱ le̱, mike̱ ekomeflo baṅ ono̱; edšake̱ midši Iehowa †otšalo̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ba Elim, heni nubui nyoṅma ke̱ enyo ke̱ amitšrobitšei nyoṅmai-kpawo yo̱ le̱; ni ame̱babo̱ nsra ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ nu le̱ he.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: ni lebi le̱ nyeana Iehowa anumnyam le̱, edšake̱ enu nyehũhū̃hũwiemo̱i ní nyewieo̱ nyešio̱ Iehowa le̱; ši wo̱ le̱, namei dši wo̱ ni nyewieo̱ hũhū̃hũ nyešio̱ wo̱?

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbe̱ke̱ mli le̱ *trako̱ko̱i ba, ni ame̱baha nsra le̱ṅ, ni lebi le̱ bó̱ nyõ nsra le̱ hewo̱ ke̱-kpe. *

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Ni beni bó̱ le̱ ní nyõ le̱ ekpla le̱, nokomei kokrobii bibii dſere ṅã le̱ no̱, bibiibibii tamo bó̱ ní efĩ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱, no̱.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Kitã ní Iehowa wo ye̱ he ne̱: Mofẽmo abua boni eeye nā, mofẽmo le̱ gomer kome ye̱ nyesusumai le̱ ayibo̱ nā; nyeteṅ mofẽmo akŏ̱lo̱ ahã mei ní yo̱ ebū le̱ mli le̱.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fe nakai; ni ame̱bua nā, meikomei kŏ̱lo̱ pī, meikomei hũ kē̱le̱ fiō.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Moko akaſe̱ eko ní dše mĩtše̱re no̱. Mat.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱buaä nā dā lebi, mofẽmo boni eeye; ši ké̱ hũlũ nā wa le̱, esẽreo.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ ekpa le̱ ame̱bua abolo le̱ nā nakai bo̱ toi enyo, mokome nõ gomeri enyo̱; ni asafo le̱ mli onukpai le̱ fẽ ba ame̱bakē̱ Mose.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ene̱ dši noni Iehowa kē̱ le̱ ake̱: Wó̱ dši hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ, Iehowa hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ kroṅkroṅ le̱; nyešãa noni nyeyo̱ šã, ni nyehoa noni nyeyo̱ hõmo̱; ni noni aaſe̱ ye̱ se̱ le̱ nyeṅõ-toa ke̱-yašia lebi.

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ-to ke̱-yaši lebi, take̱ boni Mose wo kitã le̱; ni ešaa le̱, asaṅ ewoo gõgõmi.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ ake̱: Nyeyea no ṅme̱ne̱, edšake̱ Iehowa hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ dši ṅme̱ne̱; ṅme̱ne̱ nyenaṅ eko ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyeabua nā gbĩĩ ekpa; ši gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ ni, no no̱ le̱ eko baṅ.

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ maṅ le̱ mli meikomei dše kpo te eko nābuamo̱, ši ame̱naa eko.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Mẽ beyino̱ ni nyeakwa mikitãi ke̱ mimlai le̱ ano̱yeli ke̱-yaši?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyekwe̱a, ní Iehowa hãnye hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱, nohewo ni ehãanye gbĩĩ enyo abolo ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ ekpa le̱ no̱ le̱; nyeteṅ mofẽmo ahĩ ši ye̱ ewe; moko akadše egbe̱he ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ dšō̱ ame̱he ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Ni Israel we le̱ tšē̱ egbe̱i mána; ni etamo̱ gbo̱w̌ei, ni eye̱o̱ futafuta, ni eṅõmo̱ tamo̱ akpānõ ke̱ wò.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Kitã ní Iehowa ewo ne̱: Nyeṅõa eko nyewoa gomer obõ ní aṅõ-to ahã nyesešibii le̱, koni ame̱na abolo ní miṅõ-lè̱nye ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, beni midšienye ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Aaron ake̱: Wó *kpulu, ni owo mli mána gomer kome, ni oṅõmã Iehowa hĩe, ní aṅõ-to ahã nyesešibii le̱. *Heb.

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa fã́ Mose le̱, nakai Aaron ṅo-mã odasenõ le̱ hĩe, ni aṅõ-to.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ gomer feo efa mlidšā nyoṅma mli ekome.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Na, mibadamo̱ ohĩe ye̱ te̱sā le̱ no̱ ye̱ Horeb; ni otſa te̱sā le̱, ni nu aadše̱ mli aba, koni maṅ le̱ anu. Ni Mose fe nakai ye Israel onukpai le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Ni ewo *dše̱i gbei ake̱ Masa ke̱ Meriba, ye̱ Israelbii le̱ abéi ke̱ kā ní ame̱ka Iehowa ame̱kē̱: Ani Iehowa ye̱ woteṅ lo ebe̱? le̱ hewo̱. *Lal.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ *Iošua ake̱: Halamo̱ hĩĩ ohãwo̱, ni ame̱ya ame̱ke̱ Amalek ayawu; mi le̱ wó̱ le̱ mibadamo̱ goṅkpo̱ le̱ yiteṅ ni mahĩe Nyoṅmo tšo le̱ ye̱ midẽ. *

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua fe bo̱ni Mose kē̱le̱ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱ Amalek yawu; ni Mose ke̱ Aaron ke̱ Hur kwo̱ goṅkpo̱ le̱ te yiteṅ.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, kē̱ Mose wó enine no̱ pe̱ le̱, bĕle̱ Israel eye kũnim, ni ké̱ ehã enine ba ši pe̱ le̱, bĕle̱ Amalek eye kũnim.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Ši Mose nidši tšī; ni ame̱wó te̱, ni ame̱ṅõ-to ešiši, ni eho etá no̱; ni Aaron ke̱ Hur hĩe enidši amli, mokome ye̱ bie̱ ne̱, ni mokome hũ ye̱ bie̱ ne̱; ni enidši le̱ damo ši šiṅṅ ke̱-yaši hũlũ šinyō̃ mli.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ſie Amalek ke̱ emaṅ le̱ ye̱ klante nā.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ṅmã ene̱ owo wolo mli oṅo-fe kaime̱nõ, ni okpã owo Iošua toiiaṅ; ši mibagbe *Amalek kaimo̱ kwrā ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei šiši. *

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose mã afo̱lešãlate̱, ni ewole̱ gbei ake̱: Iehowa-Nisi .

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Iehowa ekã kitã ake̱: Iehowa ke̱ Amalek bawu ke̱-dše̱ yino̱ ke̱-yaši yino̱.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: ni ehã ayakē̱ Mose ake̱: Mi, ošānũ Ietro, mibaä oṅõ ke̱ oṅã ke̱ obihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Ni Mose dše kpo eke̱ ešānū le̱ yakpe, ni ekotole̱ ni eſo̱ enā; ni ame̱flaflā amehe, ni ameba bū le̱ mli.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Ni Mose gba ešānū le̱ nibii fẽ ni Iehowa efe Farao ke̱ Mizraimbii le̱ ye̱ Israel hewo̱ le̱, ke̱ haome̱i fẽ ní eba ame̱no̱ ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, ke̱ bo̱ni fe ní Iehowa dšieame̱ le̱.

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ni Ietro, Mose šānū le̱, ṅõ šā̃-afo̱lei ke̱ gbē-afo̱lei ebahã Nyoṅmo̱; ni Aaron ke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ fẽ ba, koni ame̱ke̱ Mose šānū le̱ abaye nii ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe.

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ebato̱o, bo ke̱ maṅ ní fata ohe ne̱; ši nii ne̱ tšī tšṍ hão, okometõ onyeṅ ofe.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ lebi le̱ eba mli ake̱ Mose ho tá ši, ní ekodšo maṅ le̱; ni maṅ le̱ damo̱ Mose no̱ ke̱-dše̱ lebilebi ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱.

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ ešānū le̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ maṅ le̱ baä miṅõ ame̱babio̱ Nyoṅmo̱ dāṅ gbē.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Ké̱ ame̱ná sane ko le̱, ame̱ke̱-baä miṅõ, ni mikodšoo̱ mo ke̱ enanyo teṅ, ni mitšõoame̱ Nyoṅmo̱ akpoi le̱ ke̱ emlai le̱.

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Ni Mose šānū le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Noni ofeo̱ ne̱ ehĩĩ.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ bo migbē toi; mawoö ṅā, ni Nyoṅmo̱ afata ohe: Bo le̱ damo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe ohã maṅ le̱, koni oko̱ ame̱sãdši le̱ aba Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ,

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: ni otšõame̱ akpoi ke̱ mlai le̱, ni ohã ame̱le nõ gbe̱ ne̱ ní sa ake̱ amenyie kē̱ nitšumo̱ ni sa ake̱ ame̱tšu.

english_verse: You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ fãmo maṅ le̱ fẽ mli hĩĩ ní yo̱ hewale̱ ní šeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei, ní ame̱dši ano̱kwafoi, ní hĩe̱ hïedšōmo̱; ni owoame̱ akpei-atše̱mei, ohahai-atše̱mei, nyonmai-enumo̱enumo̱-tše̱mei, ke̱ nyoṅmanyoṅmai-atše̱mei ye̱ ame̱no̱,

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: ni ohã ame̱kodšo maṅ le̱ befẽbe; ni aba mli ake̱ sane wulu-fẽ-sane wulu le̱ ame̱ke̱-ba ohĩe, ši sãdši bibii fẽ le̱ ame̱ye, beni afe ní amemõ se̱ ame̱hão, ní efo tšó̱ ehão.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ofe nakai le̱, no le̱ oonyẽ ši odamo̱, ní ofe noni Nyoṅmo̱ aafã́o le̱, ni maṅ ne̱ fẽ hũ ayaše̱ ame̱šē̱he ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
translation_verse: Ni Mose hala Israelbii fẽ mli hĩĩ ní yo̱ hewale̱, ni ewoame̱ onukpai ye̱ maṅ le̱ no̱, akpekpei-atše̱mei, ohaha-atše̱-mei, nyoṅmai-enume̱enumo̱-tše̱mei ke̱ nyoṅmanyoṅmai-atše̱mei.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Ni ame ame̱kodšoo̱ maṅ le̱ beſëbe; sãdši ní wa le̱ ame̱ke̱baä Mose ṅõ, ši sãdši bibii fẽ le̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱yeo̱.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Ni Mose yadšie ešānū le̱ gbe̱, ni eyiṅ ete le̱dientše̱ ešikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: Nyedientše̱ nyena noni mife Mizraimbii le̱, ke̱ bo̱ni *mitĕrenye ye̱ okropoṅi afĩdši ano̱, ni mike̱nye ba miṅõ ne̱. *

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ fẽ here no̱ šikōme ni ame̱kē̱: Nibii fẽ ní Iehowa ewie le̱ wo̱o̱fe. Ni Mose yatšĩ maṅ le̱ gbē le̱ ehã Iehowa.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Na, mi le̱ mibaba oṅõ ye̱ atatu kpī mli, koni ke̱ mike̱o mīwie le̱ ní maṅ le̱ anu, ni bo hũ ame̱heo ame̱ye ke̱-ya nāno̱. Ni Mose dšadše maṅ le̱ wiemo̱i le̱ etšõ Iehowa.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ya maṅ le̱ ṅõ, ni otšū ame̱he ṅme̱ne̱ ke̱ wó̱, ni ohã ame̱fo̱ ametadei ahe,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: ni ame̱sā ame̱he ame̱to gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱; edšake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ Iehowa bakpleke ši ye̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ hĩe ke̱-ba Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Mokomoko nine akata ehe, ši tſiamo̱ atſiale̱ tei, lo atšẽle̱ gai; kolo ni dsio, gbomo ni dsio, akahã eyi ná wala. Kē̱ akpã te̱tre̱mantre̱ le̱ ni ese̱ tše̱ āhũ le̱, ameba goṅ le̱ he. Heb.

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ goṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba maṅ le̱ ṅõ, ni etšū maṅ le̱ he, ni amefo̱fō̱ ametadei ahe.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Nyesāa nyehe nyetoa gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱; nyekayaä nyeṅãmei aṅõ.

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ no̱ lebi le̱, nyoṅmo̱šimo̱i ke̱ srawagblamo̱i ke̱ atatu kpī ba goṅ le̱ no̱, ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱ gbē ní nā wa naakpa; ni maṅ le̱ fẽ ní yo̱ nsra le̱ṅ le̱ he kpokpo. Heb.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ maṅ le̱ dše kpo ke̱-dše̱ nsra le̱ṅ ní ame̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ayakpe; ni ame̱yadamo̱ goṅ le̱ šiši.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Ni Sinai goṅ mū le̱ fẽ mīdše lasũ, edšake̱ Iehowa ekpleke ši ke̱-ba ne̱ ye̱ la mli; ni elasũ le̱ fãa ke̱-yaä ṅwei ta-mo̱ flõnõ mli lasũ, ni goṅ mū le̱ fẽ mihoso naakpa.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Ni beni te̱tre̱mantre̱ le̱ gbē̱o̱ wā ke̱-yaä ne̱ le̱, Mose wie ni Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ gbẽ herele̱ no̱. Bo̱f.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iehowa kpleke ši ke̱-ba Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ goṅ le̱ yiteṅ le̱, etšé̱ Mose ake̱ eba goṅ le̱ yiteṅ, ni Mose te.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Kplekemo̱ ši, ni oyakpã owo maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ, koni ame̱katšere̱ mli ke̱-mība Iehowa ṅõ ame̱bakwe̱, ni ame̱teṅ mei pī mīplenē.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ oso̱foi le̱ ní be̱ṅke̱o̱ Iehowa le̱, hã ní ame̱tšū ame̱he, koni Iehowa akabatšere̱ ame̱mli.

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Iehowa ake̱: Maṅ le̱ nyẽṅ aba Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ bodientše̱ okpã owo wo̱toiiaṅ ake̱: Nyefoa akrabatša nyewoa goṅ le̱ he, ni nyefeale̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya, kplekeme̱ ši ni oya, ni oke̱ Aaron akwo̱ ke̱-ba; ši kāhã oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱ ntšere̱ mli mīkwo̱ ke̱-mība Iehowa ṅõ, ní ebatšere̱ ame̱mli.

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mose kpleke ši ke̱-ba maṅ le̱ ṅõ, ni ebakē̱ame̱.

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ *damo̱ se̱ fle̱ṅṅ, ši Mose tši be̱ṅke̱ duṅ kpī le̱ ní Nyoṅmo̱ yo̱ mli le̱. *Heb.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: Kābo̱ adſamaṅ.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: Kāye amale odase ye̱ onanyo hewo̱.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ohĩe akakõ onanyo šĩa no̱. Ohĩe akakõ onanyo ṅã, lo ewenū, lo eweyō, lo etšina, lo etedši, alo noko ní dši onanyo nõ no̱. Rom.

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Nyekafea mino̱ dſietei nyoṅmo̱i lo šika nyoṅmo̱i; nyekafea eko nyehãa nyehe.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱ Mose ake̱: Bo moṅ oke̱wo̱ awie, ni wo̱o̱bo toi; ši kāhã Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱wo̱ mīwie ní wo̱bagboi.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Nyekašea gbeyei; edšake̱ ka Nyoṅmo̱ banye kā, koni ehe gbeyei ahĩ nyehĩe, ní nyekafe eša.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Bo̱ni okē̱ Israelbii le̱ ne̱: Nyedientše̱ nyena ake̱ ṅwei midše̱ mike̱nye wie ne̱.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: *Sũ-afo̱lešãlate̱ ofe ohãmi, ni ošā̃-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ ošidā-afo̱lei le̱, ogwanteṅi le̱ ke̱ otšinai le̱ ošã ye̱ no̱; hefẽhe ní mahã akai migbe̱i le̱ ye̱ le̱, †maba oṅõ; ni madšō̱o. *

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši obafe te̱-afo̱lešãlate̱ ohãmi le̱, oke̱ te̱ ní ako akamã; ši ke̱dši owó oṅānii ano̱ otſa no̱ pe̱ le̱, obulele̱.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Ni okakwo̱ atrakpoi hũ ke̱-mīya mifo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, koni oyayaiaṅ aka-dše kpo ye̱ no̱.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for murder.
translation_verse: Moni aatſa gbomo ko nõ ní eegbo le̱, gbe aagbele̱.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši hĩĩ mīnõ, ni moko tſa enanyo te̱, lo emãle̱ atſe̱le̱, ni egboo, ši efele̱ šikãmo̱ le̱:

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši esaa enuṅtšo̱ le̱ hĩe ake̱ eekpele̱ le̱, no le̱ ehã abakpõle̱; ké̱ ka le̱ hõmo̱ ke̱ maṅse̱bii ahãmo̱ le̱, ebo̱ no hegbe̱, edšake̱ eye ehe fe̱o.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši efee nii etẽ ne̱ ehããle̱ le̱, no le̱ eyaye ehe yaka, ni akahe šika ko.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši moko dše gbe̱ batua enanyo, ni egbele̱ ye̱ ṅā mli le̱, mifolešãlate̱ le̱ he po odšiele̱ ye̱, ní ayagbele̱.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: Ni moni aalomo̱ etše̱ lo enye le̱, gbe aagbele̱.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši hĩĩ mīnõ, ni ame̱yatši yōho̱lo̱, ni eho̱ le̱ dše, ni efõṅ ko baa ye̱ se̱ le̱, dša ahele̱ nii bo̱ni yō le̱ wù le̱ aaṅõ-fõ eno̱; ni ehã boni saneyelo̱i le̱ aatšo.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši sane fõṅ ko ba ye̱ se̱ le̱, no le̱ oṅõ susuma oto susuma nãdšiaṅ,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: hĩṅme̱i ye̱ hĩṅme̱i nãdšiaṅ, nyãnyõṅ ye̱ nyãnyõṅ nãdšiaṅ, nine ye̱ nine nãdšiaṅ, nane ye̱ nane nãdšiaṅ,

english_verse: burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
translation_verse: šã ye̱ šã nãdšiaṅ, pilamo̱ ye̱ pilamo̱ nãdšiaṅ, fla ye̱ fla nãdšiaṅ.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši moko tſa ewenū lo eweyō hĩṅme̱i nõ, ni efite le̱, ehã eyaye ehe ye̱ ehĩṅme̱i le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši efa ewenū lo eweyō nyãnyõṅ le̱, eha eyaye ehe ye enyãnyoṅ le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši tšina ši nū lo yō, ni egbo le̱, no le̱ atſia tšina le̱ tei, ni akaye elō le̱; ši tšina le̱ nuṅtšo̱ le̱ aye ehe.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši tšina le̱ fo̱ö̱ šimo̱ ke̱-dše̱ sasāsa, ni ahã enuṅtšo̱ le̱ ná le ni esraale̱, ni eyagbe nū lo yō le̱, atſia tšina le̱ tei, ni enuṅtšo̱ le̱ hũ agbele̱.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši āhele̱ kpãtãmo̱nii le̱, no le̱ ehã bo̱fẽbo̱ ní aheo̱le̱ le̱, ní eke̱-kpõ esusuma.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Binū eši dšio, biyō eši dsio, ne̱ke̱ kodšomo̱ ne̱ aṅõ-kodšole̱.

english_verse: If the bull kills a slave, you must pay the slave owner
translation_verse: Ke̱dši tšina le̱ ši tšũlo̱nū lo tšũlo̱yō le̱, ehã enuṅtšo̱ le̱ dſie̱te̱i šekeli nyoṅmai-etẽ, ni atſia tšina le̱ te̱i.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši moko yagble bu nā, lo moko yadše bu, ni etšĩĩ no̱, ni tšina lo tedši yagbe mli le̱,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: bu le̱ tše̱ le̱ ato nãdšiaṅ, ni ehã enuṅtšo̱ le̱ šika, ni kolo gbonyo le̱ atšṍ enõ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši moko tšina pila enanyo nõ ni egbo le̱, no le̱ ame̱hõ tšina hĩekãlo̱ le̱, ni ame̱dša eyinii le̱ mli, ni gbonyo le̱ hũ ame̱dša.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Alo ke̱dši ale ake̱ tšina le̱ fo̱ö̱ šimo̱ ke̱-dše̱ sasāsa, ni enuṅtšo̱ le̱ esraale̱ le̱, no le̱ eṅõ tšina eto tšina le̱ nãdšiaṅ, ni gbonyo le̱ atšṍ enõ.

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši nū ko yalaka oblayō ní atše̱ko ehe bā, ni eke̱le̱ wo̱ le̱, hã ehãle̱ w̌ē̱nii ní etšṍ eṅã.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ofa mimaṅbĩi le̱ ateṅ ohĩafo ko ní ke̱o yo̱ šika le̱, kāšile̱ akaple, ni kāhele̱ hekpa hũ.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Ke̱dši he po oohe onanyo hebo awaba le̱, oke̱-kũ se̱ ohãle̱ dãni hũlũ ayanyõ ši;

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: *Kodšolo̱i le̱, kādše̱ame̱; ni †omaṅ-onukpa hũ, kālomole̱. *

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: *Onikpame̱nii ke̱ owein mli kleṅ-kleṅnõ hãmo le̱, kāṅo-šašao ši. Obihĩĩ ateṅ †kromo̱bi le̱, ṅõ-hãmi. *

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Nakai noṅṅ ofe otšinai ke̱ otoi le̱: gbĩĩ kpawo eke̱ enye ahĩ ši; gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpānyo le̱ oṅõle̱ ohãmi.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: Ké̱ oke̱ ehenye̱lo̱ tšina lo etedši kpe ní edũ gbe̱ le̱, kplamo̱le̱ obahãle̱ ekoṅ. Luk

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: Kātšṍ ohĩafo sane hĩe obu ši ye̱ ekodšomo̱ mli.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Ni nibii fẽ ní mikē̱nye le̱, nyeyea no̱. Ni nyekatšïa *nyoṅmo̱i krokomei agbe̱i atã, ni asaṅ nyekahãa anua ye̱ nyenā. *Ios.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Šrãkelo̱ lo kene ehĩṅ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱; mahã otše̱ ye̱ dšeṅ.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Afi mli le̱ šii etẽ ohĩĩ le̱ fẽ abapue ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
translation_verse: Kwe̱mo̱ ohe ní ahĩ ye̱ ehĩe, ni obo egbē toi; kāwo emli la; eṅõṅ nyeno̱tõmo̱i le̱ efaṅ-nye; edšake̱ migbe̱i ye̱ emli. Ies.

english_verse: If you faithfully obey him, I will be a fierce enemy of your enemies.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši oobo egbē toi, ni oofe nii ní mikē̱o le̱ fẽ le̱, no le̱ matsṍ ohenye̱lo̱i ahenye̱lo̱, ke̱ ohetšẽlo̱i ahetšẽlo̱.

english_verse: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
translation_verse: Ni mibo̱fo le̱ aanyie ohĩe, ni eke̱o aaba Amorbii ke̱ Hitbii ke̱ Perizbii ke̱ Kanaanbii ke̱ Hivbii ke̱ Iebusbii le̱ aṅõ, ni mafio̱ame̱ maše̱re̱ maſie.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: Ši nyesúmo̱a Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni eedšō̱ obolo ke̱ onu no̱; ni mako̱ *hela ye̱ oteṅ maše̱ mafõ. *

english_verse: I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you.
translation_verse: Mahã miheṅmiṅmi anyie ohĩe, ni mahã maṅ-fẽ-maṅ ni ooše̱ no̱ le̱ adšidšā, ni mahã ohenye̱lo̱i fẽ atšṍmo̱ ame̱se̱ ame̱-hão.

english_verse: I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach.
translation_verse: Ni matšŭ *sosomotii ke̱-atšṍ ohĩe, ní ame̱ſie Hivbii ke̱ Kanaanbii ke̱ Hitbii le̱ ye̱ ohĩe. *

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: Ši miſieṅame̱ ye̱ ohĩe ye̱ afi kome no̱, koni šikpoṅ le̱ akabatšṍ amaṅfõ, ní ṅãṅ koloi ayi mībafá mīwoö.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: Fiofio maſieame̱ ye̱ ohĩe, ke̱-yaši beyino ní oofá, ní oohe šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: Ni mafo *hũsũ mahão ke̱-dše̱ Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ nā ke̱-yaši Filistifoi le̱ aṅšo̱ le̱ nā, ni asaṅ ke̱-dše̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši fā le̱ nā; ši madšie šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ mawo nyedeṅ, ni oſieame̱ ye̱ ohĩe. *

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: Oke̱ame̱ lo ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ akakpãṅ kpãṅmo̱ ko.

english_verse: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_verse: Kāhã ame̱hĩ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ní amemīhã obafe eša ošimi; edšake̱ ke̱dši osúmo ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱, befẽbe ní fe le̱ eetšṍ tsõne ehão. Kods.

english_verse: but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kome atši abe̱ṅke̱ Iehowa; ši ame̱ le̱ ame̱katši ame̱be̱ṅke̱, ni maṅ le̱, hũ ke̱le̱ akakwo̱ ke̱-mība.

english_verse: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ṅõ lá le̱ fã ewo lalakãi amli, ni lá le̱ fã ní ſe̱ le̱ eṅõ-ſã afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
translation_verse: Ni eko̱ kpãṅmo̱ le̱ *wolo le̱, ni ekane ewo maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ; ni ame̱kē̱: Nii fiā ní Iehowa ewie le̱, wo̱o̱fe ni wo̱o̱-bo toi. *K

english_verse: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose wó lá le̱ ni *eṅo-ſã maṅ le̱ no̱, ni ekē̱: Na, kpãṅmo̱ ní Iehowa kenye ekpãṅ ye̱ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ no̱ le̱ no̱ lá ne̱. *Heb.

english_verse: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ ateṅ abladei ne̱, ekpãã *enine mli etaa ame̱he; ni ame̱na Nyoṅmo̱, ni ame̱ye nii ni amenu noko. *

english_verse: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
translation_verse: Ni Mose te ši ke̱ etšũlo̱ Iošua; ni Mose kwo̱ ke̱-te Nyoṅmo̱ goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ onukpai le̱ ake̱: Nye le̱ nyehĩa bie̱ nyemẽawo̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní wo̱o̱ba nyeṅõ ekoṅ; ni na, Aaron ke̱ Hur ke̱nye ye̱; ke̱dši moko ye̱ sane ko yeli le̱, nyehãa ebaä ame̱ṅõ.

english_verse: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kwo̱ ke̱-te goṅ le̱ ne̱, ni atatu le̱ baha goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you.
translation_verse: Oke̱ Israelbii le̱ awie, ni ame̱bahãmi no̱wómo̱-nikēnii; mofẽmo ní yo̱ he tšui ake̱ eehã le̱, le̱ edeṅ nyehea mino̱wómo̱-nikēnii le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
translation_verse: Ni oke̱ šika ṅmīṅmi aha he, emli ke̱ ehewo̱ fẽ oha, ni ofe šika kakra obo̱le eno̱ kpŭla.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: Ni oſie šika gai edſe̱ owo he, ni oṅõ-to ekodši edſe̱ le̱ ano̱; ni gai enyo̱ aye efã kome, ni gai enyo̱ aye efã kome ne̱ hũ.

english_verse: Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold
translation_verse: Ni oke̱ yō̱itšo agbo̱ tšei, ni oke̱ šika aha he;

english_verse: and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles.
translation_verse: ni oke̱ tšei le̱ aho̱lo̱ gai le̱ amli ye̱ adeka le̱ mase̱ii le̱, koni ake̱-wó adeka le̱.

english_verse: Don't ever remove the poles from the rings.
translation_verse: Tšei le̱ aho̱lo̱ adeka le̱ he gai le̱ amli; akadšie ye̱ mli.

english_verse: Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest.
translation_verse: Mi ofe kerub kome ye̱ nāgbēhe kome ne̱, ke̱ ekome hũ ye̱ nāgbēhe kome ne̱; kerubim le̱ atša kpãtãmo̱ sẽi le̱ no̱ noṅṅ ye̱ enāgbēhei enyo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ kpãtãmo̱ sẽi le̱ obu adeka le̱ nā; ni adeka le̱ oṅõ *odaseyelinõ ní mibahão le̱ owo mli. *

english_verse: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Ni *dše̱i mike̱o aakpe ye̱, ni madše̱ kpãtãmo̱ sẽi le̱ ne̱, ke̱ kerubim enyo̱ le̱ ní ye̱ odaseyeli adeka le̱ ne̱ le̱ teṅ mike̱o aawie nibii fẽ ní mafã́o ake̱ okē̱ Israelbii le̱. *

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Ni ogbo tšo bloblo ní elē̱mo̱ tamo̱ dẽ ke̱-bo̱le he kpŭla, ni ofe šika kakra ke̱-bo̱le tšo bloblo le̱ he kpŭla.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Ni oke̱ yō̱itšo agbo̱ tšei le̱, ni oke̱ šika aha he, koni ake̱-wó okplõ le̱.

english_verse: Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold
translation_verse: Ni oke šika ṅmīṅmi afe kanetšo; tſiamo̱ nitšumo̱ oke̱-fe kanetšo le̱, etšo le̱ ke̱ ehe nidši le̱ fẽ; ehe to̱i le̱ ke̱ ehe kpo̱bii le̱, ke̱ ehe fo̱fo̱ii le̱ fẽ atša.

english_verse: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
translation_verse: Ame̱he kpo̱bii ke̱ ame̱he nidši le̱ fẽ atšăra no̱; ake̱ šika ṅmīṅmi afe fẽ tſiamo̱ nitšumo̱ kome.

english_verse: The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold.
translation_verse: Ni ehe abe̱lei, ke̱ ehe lagbēnii le̱ hũ ake̱ šika ṅmīṅmi afe.

english_verse: The lampstand and its equipment will require
translation_verse: Šika ṅmīṅmi talenta kome ake̱-fe, ke̱ ehe nibii ne̱ fẽ.

english_verse: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_verse: Ni kwe̱mo̱ ní ofeame̱ tamo̱ *nii ní aṅõ-tšoo ye̱ goṅ le̱ no le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱. *

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Ni bū le̱ nā šĩnā le̱ oke̱ mama, ní ake̱ kpã blū ke̱ afaseo ke̱ etšuru ke̱ eye̱ṅ futā nī anyẽne elò abuinānitšumo̱ ewo mli, afe.

english_verse: As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth
translation_verse: Mama kome ke̱le̱ dši ninetalo̱i nyoṅmai-etẽ, ni elē̱mo̱ dši ninetalo̱i edſe̱; ni mamai nyoṅma ke̱ ekome le̱ fẽ ahĩe susumo̱ kome.

english_verse: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: Ni šihìle̱he le̱ oke mamai nyoṅma, ní ake̱ kpa ye̱ṅ futā ní anyẽne ke̱ blū ke̱ afaseo ke̱ etšuru elò kerubim ní dši nii-aṅlòlo nitšumo̱ ewo mli, afe.

english_verse: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ tōagbo wodši ní awoame̱ etšuru ofe bū le̱ no̱hānõ, ni oke̱ nuṅgbé wodši hũ aha yiteṅ. (

english_verse: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ kpãtãmo̱ sẽi le̱ obu odaseyeli adeka le̱ nā ye̱ hekroṅkroṅ fè fẽ le̱.

english_verse: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ yō̱itšo ofe mplãṅi ní damo̱ ši ohã šihĩle̱he le̱.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Ni aṅõame̱ abo̱ he ye̱ šišigbe̱ ke̱ yiteṅgbe̱ ye̱ ga kome yi; ne̱ke̱ afe enyo̱ le̱ fẽ, ye̱ kodši enyo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Ni mlibe̱nõ le̱ ní ble̱ mplãṅi le̱ ateṅ le̱ aho̱ mli ke̱-dše̱ šišidšē ke̱-yaši nāgbē.

english_verse: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through.
translation_verse: Ni oke̱ šika aha mplãṅi le̱ ahe, ni oke̱ šika afe ame̱he gai le̱ ní ake̱ mlible̱mo̱nii le̱ aho̱lo̱ mli, ni mlible̱mo̱nii le̱ hũ oke̱ šika aha he.

english_verse: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ni omã šihĩle̱he le̱ tamo̱ noni *adšie atšõo ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ noṅṅ. *

english_verse: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ *okplõ le̱ omã muhō̱ le̱ kpono̱gbe̱, ni kanetšo le̱ aye okplõ le̱ ṅe̱le̱no̱ ye̱ šihĩle̱he le̱ heni ye ke̱-yaä wuoyigbe̱ le̱; ni oke̱ okplõ le̱ amã heni ye ke̱-yaä kōyigbe̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ muhē̱ le̱ otšotšŏro ši ye̱ *kpodši le̱ anā, koni oke̱ odaseyeli adeka le̱ abamã muhō̱ le̱ se̱; ni muhō̱ le̱ afo hekroṅkroṅ le̱ ke̱ †hekroṅkroṅ fè fẽ le̱ teṅ ahãnye. *K.

english_verse: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ yō̱itšo ofe akulašĩṅi enumo̱ ní damo ši ohã mama le̱, ni oke̱ šika aha he, ke̱ ame̱he šika kpodši; ni oſie akō̱ble no̱damo̱nii enumo̱ ohãame̱.

english_verse: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ tšei le̱ aho̱lo̱ gai le̱ amli, ni tšei le̱ aye afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ mase̱ii enyo̱ le̱, ni aṅõ-wó.

english_verse: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Femo̱le̱ ke̱ ṅmoṅmlo ni gbe̱ akã mli; bo̱ni *atšõo ye̱ goṅ le̱ ne̱ le̱, nakai ame̱fele̱. *

english_verse: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
translation_verse: Ni bo le̱ ofã́ Israelbii le̱, ni ame̱bahão mũtšo mũ ní aši ni mli tše kroṅṅ, ní aṅõ-su kane le̱, koni ahã kane le̱ amã no dā;

english_verse: for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain
translation_verse: ke̱ ehe akulašĩṅi nyoṅmai-enyo̱, ni ame̱no̱damo̱nii nyoṅmai-enyo̱ le̱ ake̱ akō̱ble afe; akulašĩṅi le̱ ahe kpodši le̱ ke̱ ame̱mlible̱mo̱nii le̱ ake dſietei afe.

english_verse: Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
translation_verse: Ni kpo le̱ no̱ agbó le̱ nā mama ní lē̱mo̱ hĩe ninetalo̱i nyoṅmai-enyo̱ le̱ ake̱ mama, ní ake̱ kpã blū ke̱ afaseo ke̱ etšuru ke̱ eye̱ṅ futā ní anyẽne elò abuinā-nitšumo̱ ewo mli, afe; ame̱kulašĩṅi edſe̱ ke̱ ame̱no̱damo̱nii hũ edſe̱.

english_verse: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
translation_verse: Šihĩle̱he le̱ mli súomo̱ le̱ he nibii le̱ fẽ, ke̱ ehe šiṅmlitšei le̱ fẽ, ke̱ kpo le̱ he šiṅmlitšei le̱ fẽ le̱ ake̱ akō̱ble afe.

english_verse: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_verse: Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ asa, ní etšo ke̱-dše̱ gbe̱ke̱ ke̱-yaši lebi ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ mli ye̱ muhō̱ le̱ ní ha odase-yelinõ le̱ hĩe le̱ hĩegbe̱. Ene̱ atšó nāno̱ akpo ni kã ši hã Israelbii le̱ ayino̱bii fẽ.

english_verse: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: ke̱ šika ṅmīṅmi kõsõṅkõsõi enyo̱ ní aṅõ-tša ní agbo̱le̱ tamo̱ kpã, ni oṅõ kõsõṅkõsõi ní agbo̱ le̱ olala hebo̱lemo̱nii le̱ amli.

english_verse: From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do.
translation_verse: Ni oke̱ ṅā afe kodšomo̱ tšitšino̱nii le̱; bo̱ni afe efod le̱, nakai ofele̱: šika ke̱ mama blū ke̱ afaseo ke̱ etšuru ke̱ klala kpakpa oṅõ-fe.

english_verse: with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ te̱i omãmo̱ mli, te̱i klempẽi edſe̱; klempẽ kome le̱ sardio, ke̱ topasion, ke̱ smaragdo; ene̱ dši kleṅkleṅ klempẽ le̱.

english_verse: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
translation_verse: Ni klempẽ ní dši enyo̱ le̱ karfuṅkle, ke̱ safiro, ke̱ sardoniki.

english_verse: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
translation_verse: Ni klempẽ ní dši etẽ le̱ hiakinto, ke̱ agate, ke̱ ametisto.

english_verse: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings
translation_verse: Ni klempẽ ní dši edſe̱ le̱ krisolito, ke̱ šoham, ke̱ yaspi; aṅõ-ho̱lo̱ šika mli ye̱ ame̱fo̱dší le̱ amli.

english_verse: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: Ni kõsõṅkõsõi enyo̱ ní agbo̱ tamo̱ kpã le̱ anãbui enyo̱ le̱ ní eſe̱ le̱ hũ oṅõ-lala hebo̱lemo̱nii enyo̱ le̱ mli, ni oṅõ-ſie efod le̱ kõdši le̱ ano̱ ye̱ hĩegbe̱.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Ni flo̱ akã yiteṅ; ake̱ bõṅ ní alò abãṅ flo̱ le̱ nā ke̱-kpe, tamo̱ dama nā flo̱, koni ekagba.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them.
translation_verse: šika ṅmle̱ kome ke̱ kpo̱ kokrō kome, šika ṅmle̱ kome ke̱ kpo̱ kokrō kome ke̱-bo̱le atade yū le̱ nāmū le̱ ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron awo ní eke̱-súmo̱, ni ke̱ ēbote hekroṅkroṅ le̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni asaṅ ke̱ ẽdše kpo le̱, ní anu ame̱gbē̱mo̱, *koni ebagbo. *

english_verse: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni otſia šika ṅmīṅmi fe̱te̱fe̱te̱, ni oṅmã ye̱ no̱ tamo̱ welonāso̱omo̱nõ no̱ niṅmã ake: Kroṅkroṅ hã Iehowa.

english_verse: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
translation_verse: Ni oṅo-kpe̱te̱ boṅ blū no̱, koni ahĩ fai le̱ he; eta fai le̱ hĩenā.

english_verse: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
translation_verse: Ni ahĩ Aaron hĩenā, ni Aaron atĕre Israelbii ano̱tõmo̱i ní yo̱ ame̱nikēnii fẽ ni ame̱ke̱-baä le̱ he le̱; ni ahĩ ehĩenā dāne̱, koni ame̱sa Iehowa hĩe. (

english_verse: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron bihĩĩ le̱ okpe̱ flakai ohãame̱ hũ, ni ofe mliteṅfĩnii oto he, ni ofe fai ní yo̱ nyam ke̱ fe̱o ohãame̱.

english_verse: Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ-wo onyemi Aaron ke̱ ebihìĩ le̱ hũ ofata ehe; ni *ofe̱ame̱ mũ, ni oke̱ oso̱foyeli †awo ame̱deṅ, ni ofeame̱ kroṅkroṅ, koni ame̱ye oso̱foi ame̱hãmi. *

english_verse: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
translation_verse: Ni ofe klala tſakoto ohãame̱ ni ame̱ke̱-ke ame̱yayaiaṅ, ke̱-dše̱ he̱ ke̱-yaši ſuo̱.

english_verse: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ awo, ke̱ ame̱ miba kpē-bū le̱ mli le̱, lo ke̱ ame̱ba-be̱ṅke̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱, ní ame̱basúmo̱ ye̱ hekroṅkroṅ le̱, koni ame̱kalō musu, ni ame̱gboi. Ene̱ atšṍ akpo̱ ní kã ši ke̱-yaä nāno̱ ahãle̱ ke̱ esešibii ní baba ye̱ ese̱ le̱.

english_verse: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ le̱ oṅõ tšina kome ošã eša-aſo̱le ni ake̱-kpãtã, ni oke̱ kpãtãmo̱ ní okpãtãa ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ akpla ehe eša, ni ofo̱le̱ mũ, ní oke̱-fele̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash.
translation_verse: Ni okŏ̱lo̱ atadei le̱, ni oṅõ-wo Aaron: Aaka le̱, ke̱ efod le̱ šiši atade yū le̱, ke̱ efod le̱, ke̱ tšitšino̱nii le̱, ni oke̱ efod le̱ mliteṅfĩnii le̱ afĩ emli;

english_verse: and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
translation_verse: Koni owo mũ ní ake̱-foö̱ mo le̱, ni ofo̱se oſĩe eyi teṅ, ni oṅo-fo̱le̱.

english_verse: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Ni ohã ake̱ tšinanū le̱ aba kpē-bū le̱ hĩe, ni Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ aṅõ ame̱nidši aſie tšina le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
translation_verse: Ši tšina le̱ lō ke̱ ewolo ke̱ efei le̱ oke̱ la ašã ye̱ nsra le̱ se̱; eša-afo̱le ni.

english_verse: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Asaṅ oṅo tōagbo le̱ ekome, ni Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ aṅo ame̱nidši aſie tōagbo le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ni ogbe tōagbo le̱, ni oṅõ elá le̱, ni oṅõ-ſã afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ fẽ ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
translation_verse: Ni oflo̱ tōagbo le̱ mli kukudši, ni ofó̱ emlinii le̱ ke̱ eſŭo̱dši le̱ ahe, ni oṅõ-ſie kukudši le̱ ke̱ eyitšo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Ni oṅo tōagbo kroko le̱ hũ, ni Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ aṅõ ame̱nidši aſie tōagbo le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ lá le̱ ní yo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ eko ke̱ mũ ní ake̱-fo̱ö̱ mo le̱ eko, ni oṅo-ſã Aaron ke̱ etadei le̱, ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ atadei le̱ hũ ano̱; ni ake-fe le̱ ke̱ etadei le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ atadei le̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ oṅo tōagbo le̱ *fo̱ le̱ ke̱ elei le̱ ke̱ fo̱ ní ha emlinii ahe le̱ ke̱ noni tšotšŏro mle̱bo le̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱ sabai enyo̱ le̱ ke̱ fo̱ ní yo̱ ne̱ le̱ ke̱ ninedšŭrõ kõṅ le̱ , *

english_verse: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ni ohe ye̱ ame̱dẽ, ni omã nā la ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ ye̱ šā̃-afo̱le le̱ ne̱, ní edše ṅma ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; afo̱le ní ake̱ la šãa ahãa Iehowa ni.

english_verse: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ Aaron oso̱fowō-afo̱le tōagbo le̱ tšitši, ni ofõ oṅõ-fe fō̃-afo̱le ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ni atšṍ ogbe̱fãṅnõ.

english_verse: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
translation_verse: Ni ebihĩĩ le̱ ateṅ moni baye oso̱fo ye̱ enãdšiaṅ le̱ awo gbĩĩ kpawo, ke̱ eba kpē-bū le̱ṅ ebasúmo̱ ye̱ hekroṅkroṅ le̱.

english_verse: Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place,
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ oso̱fowō-afo̱le tōagbo le̱, ni oho elō le̱ ye̱ heni yo̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ aye tōagbo le̱ lō le̱ ke̱ abolo le̱ ni yo̱ kafũ le̱ mli le̱ ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ šĩnā le̱ nā.

english_verse: At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ye nibii ní ake̱-kpãtãa le̱ ni ake̱-woame̱ oso̱fo, ni asaṅ aṅõ-feame̱ kroṅkroṅ; ši gbo ni akaye eko, edšake̱ nii kroṅkroṅi ni.

english_verse: If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši dše tše̱re oso̱fowō-afo̱le lō le̱ ke̱ abolo le̱ eko no̱ lebi le̱, no le̱ oke̱ la ašã noni aaſe̱ le̱; akaye, edšake̱ eye̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ ofe Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱, take̱ boni miwoö kitã le̱ fẽ; gbĩĩ kpawo dši ame̱-osofowō gbĩĩ le̱.

english_verse: Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy. Daily Sacrifices (Leviticus
translation_verse: Gbĩĩ kpawo okpãtã ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, ni ofele̱ kroṅkroṅ, ni etšṍ afo̱le-šãlate̱ ní yo̱ kroṅkroṅ fè fẽ; nofẽno ní aasa afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he le̱, afe kroṅkroṅ. (

english_verse: Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ ene̱ dši noni ofe ye̱ afo̱le-šãlate̱ le̱ no̱: tōbii enyo̱ ní eye afifi ošã ye̱ ne̱ gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ.

english_verse: one in the morning and one in the evening.
translation_verse: Oke̱ tōbi le̱ ekome ašã afole lebi, ni oke̱ ekome hũ ašã afo̱le gbe̱ke̱; Lal.

english_verse: With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Ni tōbi kroko le̱ oṅõ-šã afole gbe̱ke̱, ni ofele̱ tamo̱ lebi niyenii-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ ehe dā̃-afo̱le le̱, ní ahã adše ṅma, etšṍ afo̱le ní ake̱ la šãa ahãa Iehowa.

english_verse: Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: Ni mahã kpē-bū le̱ ke̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ afe kroṅkroṅ; ni asaṅ mahã Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ fẽ afe kroṅkroṅ, ní ame̱ye oso̱foi ame̱hãmi.

english_verse: I will live among you as your God,
translation_verse: Ni mahĩ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ, ni matšṍ ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱;

english_verse: and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_verse: ni ame̱aná ame̱le ake̱ midsi Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo le̱, ní dšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ní mahĩ ame̱teṅ le̱, mi Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves.
translation_verse: Ni tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ní obafe ne̱, nyekakwe̱a ne̱ bo̱ni afutule̱ ahã le̱ nyemīfe eko nyemīhã nyehe; atšṍ kroṅkroṅ ye̱ ohĩe aha Iehowa.

english_verse: the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand.
translation_verse: ke̱ šā̃-afo̱lelate̱ le̱ ke̱ ehenii le̱ fẽ, ke̱ lalakã le̱ ke̱ ekăla le̱.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Ni ofe šika gai enyo̱ owo he ye̱ ehe kakra le̱ šiši, ye̱ ekodši enyo̱ le̱ nā, eṅmãwui enyo̱ le̱ no̱ ofe ye̱, ni ake̱ tšei aho̱lo̱ mli ní aṅõ-wó.

english_verse: Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings.
translation_verse: Nyekašãa tšofã-ke̱-ṅma *kroko ye̱ no̱, alo šā̃-afo̱le alo niyenii-afo̱le; ni nye-kafo̱sea dã-afo̱le nyeſiea no̱. *

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱:

english_verse: Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ okane Israelbii le̱ ni ona ame̱-yikule̱ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo aṅõ esusuma kpõmo̱nii ahã Iehowa, koni ke̱ okaneame̱ ní gbĕlehela ko akaba ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: , whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: koni Aaron ke̱ ebii le̱ ke̱-fo̱flo̱ ame̱nidši ke̱ ame̱nãdši ahe.

english_verse: This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: Ni ohe kpãtãmo̱ šika le̱ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ adeṅ, ni oṅõ-to ohã kpē-bū le̱ṅ súomo̱ le̱, koni atšṍ Israelbii le̱ akaimo̱nõ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni aṅõ-kpãtã ahã nyesusumai.

english_verse: If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_verse: Mofẽmo ní aafe eko tamo̱ no, ní eešã le̱, aafole̱ ye̱ emã le̱ṅ aše̱ afõ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ekē̱:

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ekē̱:

english_verse: for dedicating the tent and chest,
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ-fo̱ kpē-bū le̱, ke̱ odaseyeli adeka le̱,

english_verse: the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils,
translation_verse: ke̱ okplõ le̱ ke̱ ehenii le̱ fẽ, ke̱ kanetšo le̱ ke̱ ehenii le̱, ke̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma-šãlate̱ le̱,

english_verse: When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil,
translation_verse: Ni ofo̱ Aaron ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ amũ, ni ofeame̱ kroṅkroṅ, koni ame̱ye oso̱foi ame̱hãmi.

english_verse: So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves.
translation_verse: Gbomo hewolo no̱ ni akafo aſie, ni nyekafea eko hũ ní tamo̱ no, bo̱ni atsõ afutule̱ le̱: eye̱ kroṅkroṅ, ni ahĩ kroṅkroṅ ahãnye.

english_verse: If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.” The Sweet-Smelling Incense
translation_verse: Mofẽmo ní aafutu eko tamo̱ no, lo ní aaṅõ eko asa gbo̱ he le̱, aafole̱ ye̱ emã le̱ṅ aše̱ afõ.

english_verse: Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy.
translation_verse: ni oṅõ-fe tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ní ašãa, ní afutule̱ ye̱ tšofãfutulo̱ ṅã le̱ nā, ní afutule̱ dšogbāṅ, ni emli atše, ní efe kroṅkroṅ,

english_verse: Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy.
translation_verse: ni oši eko bo̱dobo̱do̱ dientše̱, ni oṅõ eko omã odaseyelinõ le̱ hĩe ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ṅ, *heni mike̱o aakpe ye̱ le̱; atšṍ kroṅkroṅ fè fẽ ahãnye. *K.

english_verse: This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
translation_verse: Mike̱ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ okadi dši no ke̱-yaä nāno̱; edšake̱ gbĩĩ *ekpa Iehowa ṅõ-fe ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ, ni gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ edšō̱ ehe, ni ewo etšui. *

english_verse: When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_verse: Ni beni eke Mose ewie egbe nā ye̱ Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, eṅõ odaseyeli te̱i enyo̱, ní dši *te̱i te̱tre̱bii ní Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ ewao ṅmã no̱ le̱, ehãle̱. *

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ya, kplekemo̱ ši ní oya, ši omaṅ le̱ ní oke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba le̱ efite ame̱he;

english_verse: Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
translation_verse: Kaimo̱ Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Israel, otšũdši le̱, *ní oṅõ bodientše̱ okitã okã-ame̱, ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mahã nyesešibii afá tamo̱ ṅwei ṅulamii, ni šikpoṅ ne̱ fẽ ní miwie he le̱ maṅõ-hã nyesešibii le̱, ni ame̱aye no̱ ke̱-ya nāno̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
translation_verse: Ni te̱i te̱tre̱bii le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ninenā nitšumo̱ ni, ni niṅmã ni aṅmlã ye̱ te̱i le̱ ano̱ le̱ hũ Nyoṅmo̱ niṅmã ni.

english_verse: When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Iošua nu maṅ le̱ blo̱mo̱ le̱, beni ame̱bo̱ö̱ oše le̱, ekē̱ Mose ake̱: Ta blo̱mo̱ ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Dšee kũnimyeli he ošebo̱ ni, ni dšee tagbe he blo̱mo̱ hũ ni, ši lala no̱heremo̱ moṅ minuo̱ ne̱.

english_verse: As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ amrõ pe̱ ní ebe̱ṅke̱ nsra le̱, ena tšinabi le̱ ke̱ dšō le̱; ni Mose mli wo la, ni eṅõ te̱i te̱tre̱bii le̱ etſia ši, ni edſăraame̱ ye̱ goṅ le̱ šiši.

english_verse: Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Aaron ake̱: Meni po maṅ ne̱ feo, ni oke̱ eša kpeteṅkple ní tamo̱ ne̱ke̱ eba ame̱no̱ ne̱?

english_verse: Aaron answered: Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron kē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ mli akawo la; bodientše̱ ole maṅ ne̱ he, ake̱ efõṅ yo̱ ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱kē̱mi ake̱: Femo̱ nyoṅmo̱i ohãwo̱, ní amenyie wo̱hĩe; ši ne̱ke̱ Mose ne̱, ní dši nū le̱ ní yadšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba ne̱, wo̱lee nõ kōme ní efele̱.

english_verse: Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
translation_verse: Ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mofẽmo ní yo̱ šika ko le̱, hã ní ame̱kple̱ ke̱-ba! Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ṅõ-hãmi; ni miše̱re̱ miſie la mli, ni etšo tšinabi ne̱.

english_verse: So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!” Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses,
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni Mose badamo̱ nsra le̱ agbó le̱ nā, ni ekē̱: Namo yo̱ Iehowa gbe̱fãṅ? mo le̱ aba miṅõ! Ni Levibii le̱ fẽ bua amehe nā ke̱-ba eṅõ.

english_verse: and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Boni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Nū-fẽ-nū aṅmõ eklante ye̱ ehe̱, ni nyefoa mli ke̱-yaä, ni nyekũ se̱ ke̱-ba ke̱-dše̱ agbó kome mli ke̱-ya agbó kome mli, ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ, ni mofẽmo agbe enyemi, ni mofẽmo agbe enanyo, ni mofẽmo agbe ehegbomo.

english_verse: The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ lebi le̱ eba mli ake̱ Mose kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Nyefe eša kpeteṅkple; ši agbe̱ne̱ makwe̱ ke̱-ya Iehowa ṅõ; ekole̱ makpãtã ye̱ nyehe eša le̱ hewo.

english_verse: Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kũ ese̱ ke̱-te Iehowa ṅõ, ni ekē̱: Ao, maṅ ne̱ efe eša kpeteṅkple, ni amefe šika nyoṅmo̱i ame̱hã ame̱he.

english_verse: But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ agbe̱ne̱ ke̱dši ooṅõ ame̱he eša le̱ ofaame̱ le̱, ṅõ-fa! ni ke̱-dšee nakai hũ le̱, ofai ne̱, ní ogbe mi moṅ migbe̱i ye̱ wolo le̱ ní oṅmã le̱ mli. Lal.

english_verse: Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ya, ní oyakpla maṅ le̱ ke̱-ya heni mike̱o ewie he le̱; na, *mibo̱fo le̱ aanyie ohĩe; ši kẽle̱ gbĩ no̱ ní mabasraame̱ le̱, masra ame̱he eša le̱ hũ ye̱ ame̱no̱. *

english_verse: So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa tſia maṅ le̱ nii, edšake̱ amefe tšinabi le̱ ní Aaron fe le̱.

english_verse: The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ ake̱: Mihĩe ke̱o aate, ni mahão hedšo̱le̱.

english_verse: But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
translation_verse: Ši meni aaṅõ-le ye̱ bie̱ ake̱ mike̱ omaṅ ne̱ hĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe, ake̱ dša te ní oke̱wo̱ aate le̱? *beni afe ní mãdši fẽ ní yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ akafo mi ke̱ omaṅ ne̱! *

english_verse: So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake: Noni okē̱ ne̱ hũ mafe; edšake̱ ohìe eba nyam ye̱ mihĩe, ni *mileo ke̱ ogbe̱i. *K.

english_verse: but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ ekē̱: Onyẽṅ mihĩe ona; *ši mokomoko enaṅmi, ní eyi aaná wala. *

english_verse: There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱: Na, gbe̱ ye̱ mimase̱i ne̱, ni odamo̱ te̱sā le̱ no̱;

english_verse: and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by.
translation_verse: ni aaba mli ake̱, beni minumnyam le̱ *hoo̱ le̱, maṅõo mawo te̱kplo le̱ mli, ni mike̱ †minine atšĩ ono ni maho dã; *

english_verse: Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_verse: ni madšie minine, ni oona mikotose̱ gbe; ši mihĩe ni anaa.

english_verse: The Lord said: I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Na, mi le̱ mikpãṅ kpãṅmo̱ ko: omaṅ le̱ fẽ hĩe mibafe nākpe̱nii ní afeko eko ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ, lo maṅ ko maṅ ko mli dã, ni maṅ le̱ fẽ ni oyo ame̱teṅ le̱ aana Iehowa nitšumo̱ le̱; ši gbeyei noko dši noni mibafeo le̱.

english_verse: Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Dā afi le̱ šii etẽ nyeteṅ hĩĩ fẽ abapue ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa ní dši Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
translation_verse: Nofẽno ní gbleo̱ mũsũ nā le̱, minõṅ; ke̱ okoloi ateṅ kleṅkleṅnõ ní dši nū le̱, tšina dšio, tō dšio.

english_verse: Don't make metal images of gods.
translation_verse: Kāfe nyoṅmo̱i ní aſie ohã ohe.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals.
translation_verse: koni oke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ akakpãṅ, ní ame̱yanyie ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ase̱ ame̱bo̱ adſamaṅ, ní ame̱šã afo̱le ame̱hã ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱, ni moko mībatšé̱o ní oyaye efo̱le le̱ eko;

english_verse: You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son. Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
translation_verse: Ši tedši kromo̱bi le̱ oko̱ tōbi akpõle̱, ni ke̱dši okpõõle̱ le̱, no le̱ okũ ekue̱ṅ. Obihĩĩ ateṅ kromo̱bii fẽ le̱ okpõ-ame̱. Ni mokomoko akabapue ke̱ edẽ flo ye̱ mihĩe!

english_verse: Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting.
translation_verse: Gbĩĩ ekpa otšu nii, ši gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱ odšō̱ ohe, hũmo̱ be mli dšio, kpamo̱ be mli dšio.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Ni oye otšii agbĩdšŭrõ le̱ be mli ní akũo̱ ṅmā̃ kpokploku le̱; ni ke̱ afi le̱ gbo le̱, oye yibii anābuamo̱ gbĩdšŭrõ le̱.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
translation_verse: Kāṅõ mãša ofata mifo̱le lá le̱ he ošã, ni dše hũ akatše̱re Hehō gbĩdšũrõ afole le̱ no̱.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
translation_verse: Ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱ kleṅkleṅnii ní aaba le̱ mli kleṅkleṅnõ le̱ oke̱-ba Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, we le̱. Kāho tōbi ní tšeko fufo̱.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: *Ṅmã ne̱ke̱ wiemoi ne̱; ši ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ anā mike̱o ke̱ Israel kpãṅ ye̱. *

english_verse: Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Mose dše̱ Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱ ekpleke ši le̱, ehĩe odaseyeli te̱i enyo̱ le̱ ye̱ edeṅ; ši Mose lee ake̱-ni eke̱le̱ wie hewo̱ le̱ ehã ehĩe ekpe̱.

english_verse: When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him.
translation_verse: Ni beni Aaron ke̱ Israelbii le̱ fẽ na Mose le̱, na, ehĩe mīkpe̱; ni ame̱še gbeyei ake̱ ame̱abe̱ṅke̱le̱.

english_verse: Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them.
translation_verse: Ni Mose tšé̱ame̱; ni Aaron ke̱ asafo le̱ mli onukpai le̱ fẽ kũ ame̱se̱ ameba eṅõ; ni Mose ke̱ame̱ wie.

english_verse: Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Ni fe se̱ le̱ Israelbii le̱ fẽ tši ba; ni ewoame̱ kitãi fẽ ni Iehowa ke̱-hãle̱ ye̱ Sinai goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱ Mose *mīya Iehowa hĩe ní eke̱le̱ ayawie le̱, edšieo̱ hĩehānõ le̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni eedše kpo. Ni edšeo̱ kpo, ni ebadšadšeo̱ kitãi ni awole̱ le̱ etšõo̱ Israelbii le̱. *

english_verse: They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ naä Mose hĩe ake̱ ehĩe mīkpe̱; ni Mose sā eke̱ hĩehānõ le̱ haä ehĩe ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eete ekoṅ ní eke̱le̱ ayawie ekoṅ.

english_verse: The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made.
translation_verse: Ni yei fẽ ní le ṅā ye̱ ame̱tšuiiaṅ le̱ ke̱ ame̱nidši tšẽ kpã, ni ame̱ke̱ nii ní ame̱tšẽ le̱ ba nī dši kpã blū ke̱ afaseo ke̱ etšuru ke̱ eye̱ṅ futā.
