translation_verse: Ši Iošua, Nun bi le̱, ke̱ Kaleb, Iefune bi le̱, dši mei ní yi ná wala ye̱ hĩĩ ní te yasra šikpoṅ le̱ ateṅ. K.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Mẽba nyetaoo̱ ake̱ nyekũ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ mli ne̱? Ši ene̱ ebahoṅ.

english_verse: The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Amalekbii ke̱ Kanaanbii ní yo̱ nakai goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ kpleke ši, ni ame̱bagbeame̱ ni ame̱ſieame̱ ke̱-te *Horma tõ. *

english_verse: The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message.
translation_verse: Ni Mose dšadše ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ etšõ Israelbii le̱ fẽ; ni maṅ le̱ ye ṅko̱mo̱ babaō;

english_verse: so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
translation_verse: edšake̱ Amalekbii le̱ ke̱ Kanaanbii le̱ ke̱nye aakpe ye̱ dše̱i, ni nyeanyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā; edšake̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ní nyekpale ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa se̱ le̱, Iehowa hũ fĩṅ nyese̱.

english_verse: But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱ši ame̱tšitši ni ame̱kwo̱ goṅ le̱ ke̱-te eyiteṅ; ši Iehowa kpãṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ke̱ Mose tšii amehe ke̱-dšee nsra le̱ṅ.

english_verse: you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil.
translation_verse: no le̱ niyenii-afo̱le ní oke̱-fata tšina-oblanyo le̱ he ke̱-ba ne̱: ṅmā̃ mã [efa] mlidšāi nyoṅma mli etẽ ní awo mli mũ hin fã;

english_verse: All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
translation_verse: Nyeke̱ nyekleṅkleṅ mã le̱ eko ahãa Iehowa ake̱ no̱wómo̱-afo̱le ye̱ nyeyino̱i fẽ mli.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: kitãi fẽ ní Iehowa tšṍ Mose nine no̱ ewonye ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ ní Iehowa ha mla le̱ no̱ ke̱-baši nyeyino̱i fẽ mli le̱,

english_verse: Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices,
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo le̱ akpãtã ahã Israelbii asafo mū le̱ fẽ, ni aaṅo-faame̱; edšake̱ gbe̱dū̃ ni. Ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱nikēnii ní dši afo̱lei ní ašãa ahãa Iehowa le̱ ke̱ ame̱he eša-afo̱le le̱ eba Iehowa hĩe ye̱ ame̱tõmo̱ le̱ hewo̱;

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Mla kome akã ši ahã mofẽmo ní dšee kwa ekwa efe eša le̱, Israel šīafo̱mo̱bi dšio, mokpõṅ ní too̱ gbo̱ ye̱ nyeteṅ dšio.

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ni beni Israelbii le̱ yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, ame̱yana nū ko mīle̱ lai ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Ni mei ní nale̱ ake̱ ēle̱ lai le̱ kplale̱ ke̱-ba Mose ke̱ Aaron ke̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ hĩe.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wole̱ tšũṅ; edšake̱ anáko atšõ noni sa ake̱ afele̱.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Gbe ágbe nū le̱; asafo mū le̱ fẽ atſiale̱ te̱i ye̱ nsra le̱ se̱!

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ kplale̱ ke̱-te nsra le̱ se̱, ni ame̱yatſiale̱ te̱i ni egbo, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa wo Mose kitã le̱.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel.
translation_verse: Oke̱ Israelbii le̱ awie ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱ amefe amãnyãi ame̱wo ametadei anā ye̱ ame̱yino̱i fẽ mli, ni ame̱ke̱ kpã blū aſimo amãnyãi le̱ ano̱,

english_verse: These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires.
translation_verse: beni afe ní nyekai ní nyeye mikitãi le̱ fẽ no̱, ni nyetšṍmo̱ mei kroṅkroṅi nyehã nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Midši Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni dšienye ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, koni matšṍ nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, midši Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱!

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Aso efáá hããnye, ake̱ Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ *etšenye ke̱-dše̱ Israel asafo le̱ he, ni ehã nyebe̱ṅke̱le̱, koni nyetšu Ie-howa šihĩle̱he le̱ he nii, ni asaṅ nyedamo̱ asafo le̱ hĩe ni nyesúmoame̱ le̱? *

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Ke̱dši obakplawo̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ ní fufo̱ ke̱ wò hoo̱ ye̱ no̱ le̱ no̱, ni obagbegbēwo̱ ye̱ ṅã ne̱ no̱ le̱, no fáá, ši no se̱ hũ le̱ otao ake̱ oyeo̱ wo̱no̱ lumo̱?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mose mli wo la naakpa, ni ekē̱ Iehowa ake̱: Kāhe ame̱fo̱lei le̱! Miheko *tedsi kome tete ye̱ ame̱deṅ, ni asaṅ miyeko ame̱teṅ moko afõṅfõṅ sane ko! *

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Kora ake̱: Wó̱ le̱ bo ke̱ osafo le̱ fẽ aba Iehowa hĩe, bo ke̱ ame̱ ke̱ Aaron fẽ;

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Ni Kora kpē asafo mū le̱ fẽ ewoame̱, ni ame̱bo̱ gwa ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ šìnā le̱ ši. Ni *Iehowa anumnyam le̱ pue ye̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ hĩe. *

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron wie ni ekē̱:

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: Nyetšia nyehe ke̱-dše̱a ne̱ke̱ asafo ne̱ he, ni makpãtã ame̱hĩe hĩṅme̱itſā!

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱hĩe bumo̱ ši ni ame̱kē̱: Bo Mawu ní dši *helo fẽ mumo̱i a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱! Aso †mokome aafe eša ni oogri owo asafo mū le̱ fẽ lo? *Hiob

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ni ekē̱:

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: Kē̱mo̱ asafo le̱ ake: Nyewoa nyehe no̱ ke̱-dše̱a Kora, Datan ke̱ Abiram šihĩle̱hei le̱ ahewo̱!

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Ni Mose te ši ni eyiṅ ke̱-te Datan ke̱ Abiram ṅõ, ni Israel onukpai le̱ nyie ese̱ ke̱-te.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ asafo le̱ wie ake̱: Nyetšia nyehe oyá ke̱-dše̱a ne̱ke̱ gbomei fõdši ne̱ abūi le̱ ahe, ni nyekataä ame̱nokonoko he, koni akakpãtã nyehĩe ye̱ ame̱he ešai le̱ ſẽ ahewo!

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱: Ene̱ nyeke̱-ale ake̱ Iehowa tšũmi ake̱ mibatšu ne̱ke̱ nii ne̱ fẽ, ši dšee midientše̱ mito miyiṅ mife:

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši mene̱mei aagboi tamo̱ bo̱ni gbomei fẽ gboio̱, ni ošrã ní šrãa mei fẽ aašrãame̱ le̱, bĕle̱ dšee Iehowa tšũmi.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši Iehowa fe noko ní bako dã, ni šikpoṅ gble enābu ni emī̃ame̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ní ame̱yo̱, ni ame̱kpleke ši ke̱-te gbohĩĩadše hĩekãlo̱i le̱, no le̱ nyeale ake̱ ne̱ke̱ hĩĩ ne̱ eye Iehowa he fe̱o!

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ewie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ egbe nā le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni šikpoṅ gba ye̱ ame̱šiši,

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ ke̱ ame̱nii fẽ te gbohĩĩadše hĩekãlo̱i, ni šikpoṅ le̱ mũa enā ewo ame̱yi, ni ame̱hĩe kpãtã ke̱-dše̱ gwabō̱ le̱ teṅ.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Ni Israel mū le̱ fẽ ní bo̱leame̱ ke̱-kpe le̱ dšo ame̱blo̱mo̱ le̱ nā foi, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Kũle̱ šikpoṅ le̱ bamī̃wo̱ hũ!

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the
translation_verse: Ni *la dše̱ Iehowa ṅõ ni ebašã hĩĩ ohai-enyo̱ ke̱ nyoṅmai-enumo̱ le̱ ni ke̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ba le̱. *

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Ni eyadamo̱ gbohĩĩ le̱ ke̱ hĩekãlo̱i le̱ ateṅ; ni gbĕle-hela le̱ se̱ fo.

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱lō le̱ atšṍ onõ, take̱ boni fō̃-tšitši le̱ ke̱ nine dsŭrõ le̱ dši onõ le̱.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Ni onõ hũ ne̱: ame̱nikẽnii le̱ amli no̱wómo̱-afo̱le ní yo̱ Israelbii le̱ afō̃-afo̱lei fẽ amli le̱, mike̱-hão ke̱ obihĩĩ ke̱ obiyei le̱ fẽ ake̱ gbe̱nā ní kã ši dā; mofẽmo ní he tše ye̱ owe le̱ aye eko.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Helo-ſẽ-helo ní gbleo̱ mũsũ nā ní ake̱-bahãa Iehowa le̱, gbomo dšio, šĩa kolo dšio, atšṍ onõ; ši gbomo kromo̱bi le̱ ohã akpõle̱, ni šĩa koloi ní be tšee le̱ akromo̱bii le̱ hũ ohã akpõ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Ni nii ní akpõo̱ le̱, ke̱ ame̱ye nyõṅ kome lo nõ le̱, hã akpõame̱ ye̱ dšra ní oowole̱ nā ke̱ dſie̱te̱i šekeli enumo̱ ye̱ hekroṅkroṅ šekel ní nā šio̱ gerai nyoṅmai-enyo̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ši tšina kromo̱bi lo tōgwanteṅ kromo̱bi lo tōabotia kromo̱bi ke̱ke̱ ni okahã akpõ: ame̱ le̱ amehe tše; ame̱lá le̱ oke̱-ſã afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱fo̱ le̱ ošã, ní efe afole ní ake̱ la šãa ní dšeo̱ ṅma woo̱ Iehowa.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Nii kroṅkroṅi ní Israelbii le̱ ke̱bahãa Iehowa le̱ mli no̱wómo̱-afo̱lei le̱ fẽ miṅõ-hão ke̱ obihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ obiyei le̱ fẽ ake̱ gbe̱nā ní kã ši dā; nāno̱ ṅō kpãṅmo̱ dši no ye̱ Iehowa hĩe hão ke̱ oseši le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Aaron ake̱: Ame-šikpoṅ le̱ onáṅ eko ake̱ onõ, ni asaṅ onáṅ *gbe̱fãṅ ko hũ ye̱ ame̱teṅ; midši ogbe̱fãṅnõ ke̱ ogbošinii ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ. *

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ši Levibii le̱, na, miṅõ Israel *nibii amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ fẽ mihãame̱ ake̱ ame̱gbošinii, ye̱ nii ní ame̱tšuo̱ ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ he nitšumo̱ le̱ mli le̱ hewo̱; *

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Ši Levibii le̱ atšu kpē-bū le̱ he nii, ni ame̱tĕre ame̱no̱tõmo̱; edši akpo̱ ní kã ši dā hã nyesešibii fẽ; ši ame̱kaná gbošinii ko ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ;

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: edšake̱ Israelbii anii mlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome, ní ame̱ke̱-feo̱ nowómo-afo̱le ame̱hãa Iehowa le̱, miṅõ-hã Levibii le̱ ake̱ ame̱gbošinii; nohewo̱ le̱ mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: ame̱náṅ gbošinii ko ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ le̱.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ni ekē̱:

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: Oke̱ Levibii le̱ hũ awie ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ké̱ nyehe Israelbii le̱ anibii le̱ amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome ní miheo̱ ye̱ ame̱deṅ mihãanye ake̱ nyegbe̱fãṅnõ le̱, no le̱ nyeṅõa mlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekome ne̱ hũ mlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekome nyešãa no̱wómo̱-afo̱le nyehãa Iehowa.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Ni abu nyenowóme̱-afole ne̱ tamo̱ nyedientše̱ nyeṅmā̃-šāhe ṅmã ke̱ nyeweinbu mli wein ní fá.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ kē̱mo̱ame̱ ake̱: Ké̱ nyeke̱ emli noni hĩ fè fẽ le̱ šã no̱wómo̱-afo̱le le̱, no le̱ abule tamo̱ Levibii aṅmā̃-šāhe nibānii ke̱ ame̱weinbu mli nibānii.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni nyeaye ye̱ hefẽhe, nyeke̱ nyešïabii ſẽ; edšake̱ *nyenii ní nyetšuo̱ ye̱ kpē-bū le̱ mli le̱ he nyõmo̱wo ni. *Mat.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni ké̱ nyeke̱ emli noni hĩ fè fẽ le̱ šã no̱wómo̱-afo̱le, bẽle̱ eša ko kãã nyeno̱, ni nyebulee Israelbii le̱ anii kroṅkroṅi le̱ hũ, ni nyebagboi.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: Mla le̱ mli akpo̱ ní Iehowa wo ne̱: Kē̱mo̱ Israelbii le̱ ake̱ ame̱ke̱ *tšinayō tšuru ní yo̱ mliṅṅ ní †kpa ko kpa ko be̱ ehe ní ake̱ apã ko efoko eno̱ dã abahão; *Heb.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Ni ašã tšinayō le̱ ye̱ ehĩe, ehewolo le̱ ke̱ elō le̱ ke̱ lá le̱ ke̱ efei le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱fo le̱ *afo̱ etadei le̱ ahe, ni eke̱ nu adšu ehe, ni no se̱ fẽdã ní eba nsra le̱ṅ, ni oso̱fo le̱ he tšeṅ ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱. *

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ni moni šãle̱ le̱ ke̱ nu afo̱ etadei ahe, ni eke̱ nu adšu ehe, ni ehe tšeṅ ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Ni moko ní he tše alō tšinayō le̱ lamlu le̱, ni eke̱-yaſie nsra le̱ se̱ ye̱ heko ní tše, ni ake̱-to ní ake̱-fe hetšūmo̱nu ahã Israelbii asafo le̱; eša-afo̱le ni.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ni moni lō tšinayō le̱ lamlu le̱ afo̱ etadei le̱ ahe, ni ehe tšeṅ ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱. Ni atšṍ akpo̱ ní kã ši dā ahã Israelbii le̱ ke̱ mokpõṅ ní batoo̱ gbo̱ ye̱ ame̱teṅ le̱.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Moni aata gbomo ko gbonyo he le̱, ehe tšee gbĩĩ kpawo;

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: mo le̱ ke̱ ene̱ atšũ ehe ke̱-dše̱ ehe eša le̱ mli ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ no̱ ke̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱ ní ehe atše, ši ké̱ eke̱-tšūū ehe ke̱-dše̱e̱ ehe eša le̱ mli ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ no̱ ke̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱, no le̱ ehe tšeṅ.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Mofẽmo ní aata gbomo ko gbonyo he ni etšūū ehe ke̱-dše̱e̱ ehe eša le̱ mli le̱, *ebule Iehowa šihĩle̱he le̱, ni aafo nakai mo le̱ ye̱ Israel aše̱ afõ; edšake̱ atšẽṅeko hetšūmo̱nu le̱ aſãko ene̱ hewo̱ le̱, ehe tšee; ehe mũdši le̱ ye̱ ehe lolo. *

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Ké̱ gbomo gbo ye̱ ebū mli le̱, ehe mla ní kã ši ne̱: Mofẽmo ní aate bū le̱ mli le̱ ke̱ nofẽno ní yo̱ bū le̱ mli le̱ he tšee gbĩĩ kpawo.

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: Ni nõ-fẽ-nõ ní nā kã ni ebe̱ nānõ ní ake̱-fĩo̱ nā le̱, ehe tšee.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ni mofẽmo ní aata moni enyõ ye̱ klante nā lo gbonyo ko lo gbonyowu ko lo gbonyobu ko he ye̱ dſe̱iaṅ le̱, ehe tšee gbĩĩ kpawo.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Ni moko ní he tše aṅõ hisopo atšo̱ nu le̱ mli, ni eke̱-ſã bũ le̱ ke̱ emli nii le̱ fẽ ke̱ gbomei fẽ ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ ano̱, ke̱ moni eyata gbonyowu ko lo moni enyõ lo gbonyo ko lo gbonyobu ko he le̱ no̱.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Ni moni he tše le̱ aṅõ-ſã moni he tšee le̱ no̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ ke̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱, ni etšū ehe ke̱-dše̱ ehe le̱ mli ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱, ni efo̱ etadei le̱ ahe, ni eke̱ nu adšu ehe, ni gbe̱ke̱ le ehe aatše.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ši moni he tšee ni etšūū ehe ke̱-dše̱e̱ ehe eša le̱ mli le̱, aafo nakai mo le̱ ke̱-adše̱ asafo le̱ mli aše̱ afõ; edšake̱ ebule Iehowa hekroṅkroṅ le̱; atšẽṅee hetšūmo̱nu le̱ eko afãã ene̱, hewo̱ le̱ ehe tšee.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ atšṍ akpo̱ ní kã ši dā ahãame. Ni moni tšẽṅe hetšūmo̱nu le̱ eſã le̱ hũ afo̱ etadei ahe; ni moni taä hetšūmo̱nu le̱ he le̱ hũ he tšee ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ni nofẽno ní moni he tšee aata he le̱ he tšee; ni moni aata nõ le̱ he le̱, ehe tšee ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱.

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ tšo le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa hĩe, take̱ bo̱ni efã́le̱ le̱.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ke̱ Aaron ake̱: Ake̱-ni nyehee mino̱ nyeyee, ní nyefemi kroṅkroṅ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ahĩe hewo̱ le̱, nyeke̱ ne̱ke̱ asafo ne̱ eyaṅ šikpoṅ ní mike̱-hãame̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Ni Mose tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-dše̱ Kadeš *ke̱-te Edom maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ake̱: Bo̱ni †onyemi Israel kē̱ ne̱: Bodientše̱ ole amanehũlũi fẽ ní wo̱na, *

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: bo̱ni wo̱tše̱mei le̱ te Mizraim, ni wo̱hĩ ši ye̱ Mizraim āhũ, ni Mizraimbii le̱ fe wo̱ ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ efõṅ;

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: ni beni wo̱blo̱ wo̱tšé̱ Iehowa le̱, enu wo̱gbē, ni etšũ *bo̱fo ni ebadšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim; ni na, wo̱še̱ Kadeš, maṅ ní yo̱ okpokpai le̱ anā kpākpa ne̱. *

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Ofai ne̱, hã *wo̱tšṍ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱! Wo̱tšṍṅ ṅmõdšiaṅ lo weintromiaṅ, ni asaṅ wo̱nuṅ nubui le̱ amli nu le̱ eko; maṅtše̱ gbe̱dšēgbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱ke̱ wo̱banyie, wo̱gbaṅ ninedšŭro lo abe̱ku ke̱-yaši wo̱o̱-foṅ ye̱ okpokpai le̱ ano̱. *

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Ši Edom kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kābatšṍ mišikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ke̱-dšee nakai le̱ mike̱ klante aadše kpo ke̱o aabakpe!

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱ke̱ wo̱batšṍ, ni ke̱dši mi ke̱ mikoloi le̱ aanu onui le̱ eko po le̱, wo̱o̱wo nyõmo̱; sane ko be̱ se̱, minane no̱ ke̱ke̱ mibanyie ke̱-foṅ!

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: Kābatšṍ bie̱! Ni Edom ke̱ ta babaō ke̱ ninešiwale̱ dše kpo eke̱le̱ bakpe.

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii asafo mū le̱ fẽ fã ke̱-dše̱ Kadeš, ni ame̱ba Hor goṅ le̱ he.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ababua Aaron nā afata emei le̱ ahe; edšake̱ enãdši enyo̱ yiṅ šikpoṅ ní miṅõ-hã Israelbii le̱ no̱, edšake̱ nyeboo midāṅ wiemo̱ le̱ toi ye̱ Meriba nu le̱ he.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ṅõ Aaron ke̱ ebinū Eleazar, ni okeame̱ aya Hor goṅ le̱ no̱,

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: ni odšie Aaron atadei le̱ ye̱ ehe, ni *oke̱-wo ebinū Eleazar. Ni aabua Aaron nā [aafata emei le̱ ahe], ni eegbo ye̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ni Mose fe bo̱ni Iehowa fã́le̱ le̱, ni ame̱kwo̱ Hor goṅ le̱ ye̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ hĩe.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Ni Mose dšie Aaron atadei le̱ ye̱ ehe, ni eke̱-wo ebinū Eleazar; ni Aaron *gbo ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ goṅ le̱ yiteṅ. Ni Mose ke̱ Eleazar kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ goṅ le̱ no. *

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ na ake̱ Aaron edše dšeṅ, ni Israel we le̱ fẽ fó Aaron gbĩĩ nyoṅmai-etẽ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Hor goṅ le̱ he ke̱-tšṍ Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ nā gbe, koni ame̱bo̱le Edom šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱-lo̱go̱ ke̱-ya. Ni *edše maṅ le̱ tsine ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa hã onũfũi ní nä dšraä babote maṅ le̱ teṅ, ni ame̱kõmo̱ mei le̱, ni Israelbii ateṅ mei pī gboi.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Femo̱ onũfũ ko ní nā dšraã, ni oke̱-tšotšŏro aflaṅātšo no̱, ni aaba mli ake̱ mofẽmo ni eko ekõle̱ le̱, ké̱ ekwe̱le̱, eyi aana wala. Ioh.

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ni Mose fe akō̱ble onũfũ, ni eke̱-tšotšõro aflaṅātšo no̱, ni eba mli ake̱, ke̱dši onũfũ kõ moko le̱, ekwe̱o̱ akō̱ble onũfũ le̱, ni eyi náa wala.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ye̱ dše̱i le̱ ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Zered dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ye̱ dše̱i hũ le̱ ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Arnon ní hoo̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ní edše̱o̱ Amorbii le̱ ahũsũ le̱ no̱ le̱ se̱gbe̱; edšake̱ Arnon dši Moab hũsũ, ni ekã Moab-bii ke̱ Amorbii le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ akē̱ ye̱ Iehowa tai *awolo le̱ mli ake̱: “Matšṍ mihe ye̱ Sufa, ke̱ Arnon he nudšō̱i le̱ anā, *Ios.

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ke̱ nudšō̱i le̱ ašikplekemo̱ he ní mãa eyi ši ke̱-yaä Ar šikãmo̱ he le̱, ni ekã Moab kpokpai le̱ ano̱ le̱?”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ye̱ dše̱i ke̱-te Beer; no dši nubu ní Iehowa kē̱ Mose ye̱ hewo̱ ake̱: Buamo̱ maṅ le̱ nā, ni mahãame̱ nu ame̱nu le̱.

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Nubu ní lume̱i le̱ tša le̱, ni mã le̱ṅ abladei le̱ lō mli ke̱ maṅtše̱tšo le̱, ke̱ ame̱dẽhĩemo̱tšei le̱!” Ni ame̱dše̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱te Matana;

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: ni ame̱dše̱ Matana ke̱-te Nahaliel, ni ame̱dše̱ Nahaliel ke̱-te Bamot,

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: edšake̱ Hešbon dši Amorbii amaṅtše̱ Sihon le̱ maṅ, ni le̱ eke̱ tšutšu Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ wu, ni eṅõ ešikpoṅ le̱ fẽ ye̱ edeṅ ke̱-baši Arnon nā.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Sihon, Amorbii amaṅtše̱ le̱, ṅõ ayakē̱:

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ši Sihon ekplẽẽ Israel ní etšṍ ekpokpai le̱ ano̱; ni Sihon bua emaṅ le̱ fẽ nā, ni efa eke̱ Israel bakpe ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni beni eše̱ Iahaz le̱, eke̱ Israel wu.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Ni Israel ṅõ mãdši ne̱ fẽ, ni Israel hĩ Amorbii amãdši le̱ fẽ mli, ye̱ Hešbon ke̱ ehe akrowai le̱ amli;

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ ni abe̱bulo̱i le̱ kē̱o̱ ake̱: “Nyebaä Hešbon! Hã ní atſa Sihon maṅ le̱ ní asā!

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ la ko dše̱ Hešbon, lalile̱i hũ dše̱ Sihon maṅ wulu le̱ṅ; ešã Moab maṅ le̱ ke̱ Arnon goṅkpoi le̱ ano̱ bii le̱.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Kpóo hão, Moab! Ohĩe ekpãtã, *Kemoš maṅ! Ehã ebihĩĩ le̱ etšṍmo̱ kobo̱foi, ni ebiyei le̱ ehã ame̱tšṍmo̱ Amorbii amaṅtše̱ Sihon le̱ nomi. *Kodš.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Ši wo̱tſiaame̱ nii, Hešbon hĩe ekpãtã ke̱-yaſie Dibon tō̃; wo̱kpãtã ame̱hĩe ke̱-te Nofa āhũ ke̱-yaši Medeba.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Bo̱ni fe ní Israelbii le̱ hĩ Amorbii ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ni Mose tšũ ayasra Iazer, ni ame̱ṅõ ehe mãdši le̱, ni ame̱ſie Amorbii ni yo̱ dše̱i le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšṍ ame̱he ni ame̱ko̱ Bašan gbe̱. Ni Bašan maṅtše̱ Og fã ke̱ emaṅ le̱ fẽ eke̱ame̱ bakpe, koni eke̱ame̱ abawu ye̱ Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Kāšele̱ gbeyei; edšake̱ miṅõle̱ ke̱ emaṅbii le̱ fẽ ke̱ ešikpoṅ le̱ miwo odeṅ, ní ofele̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni ofe Amorbii amaṅtše̱ Sihon ní yo̱ Hešbon le̱. Lal.

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱gbele̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ emaṅbii le̱ fẽ ní mokomeflo eſe̱e̱ hããle̱, ni ame̱ṅõ ešikpoṅ le̱ ame̱hĩ no̱.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Ni Moab kē̱ Midian onukpai le̱ ake̱: Ene̱ le̱ ta ne̱ balē̱mo̱ nii fẽ ní bo̱lewo̱ le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni tšina lé̱moo̱ ṅãno̱ dſe̱i le̱. Ši Balak, Zipor bi le̱, dši Moab maṅtše̱ ye̱ no be le̱ mli.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, ofai ne̱, ba ní obalomo̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ ohãmi, edšake̱ minyẽṅame̱, ake̱ aleenõ minine aabó ame̱no̱, ni maſie-ame̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ lo; edšake̱ mile ake̱ moni odšō̱o̱ le̱, adšō̱o̱le̱, ni moni olomoo̱ le̱, alomoo̱le̱.

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ni Moab onukpai le̱ ke̱ Midian onukpai le̱ yiṅ ame̱te, ni ame̱hĩe klamo̱ *nyõmo̱wo le̱ ke̱-te; ni ame̱ba Bileam ṅõ, ni ame̱tšĩ Balak gbẽ le̱ ame̱hãle. *

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ ba Bileam ṅõ ni ebakē̱: Mẽ hĩĩ yo̱ oṅõ ne̱?

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ake̱: Balak, Zipor bi ní dši Moab maṅtše̱ le̱, tšũame̱ miṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: Na, maṅ ní dše̱ Mizraim ba le̱, eha šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ba ni obalomo̱ame̱ ohãmi, ake̱ aleenõ manyẽ mike̱ame̱ awu, ni maſieame̱ lo.

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Oke̱-ame̱ akaya, kālomo̱ maṅ le̱ hũ, edšake̱ adšō̱le̱!

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ni Moab lume̱i le̱ te ši, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Balak ṅõ, ni ame̱kē̱: Bileam ekplẽẽ ake̱ eke̱wo̱ aba.

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Ni Balak sā tšũ bo̱foi ní yi fá ni ame̱hĩe yo̱ nyam fè tšutšubii le̱.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mawo ohĩe nyam babaō, ni nofẽno ní ookē̱mi le̱, mafe; hewo̱ le̱ ba ke̱ke̱ ni obalomo̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ ohãmi!

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Ni Bileam here no̱ ni ekē̱ Balak tšũdši le̱ ake̱: *Ke̱dši Balak ṅõ ewe le̱ dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika obõ ehãmi tete le̱, minyẽṅ mateke Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, wiemo̱ le̱, ní mafe noko bibiō lo noko wulu ko. *

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ nye hũ nyewo̱a bie̱ nyō ne̱ṅ, koni makwe̱ noni Iehowa aakē̱mi ekoṅ.

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ ba Bileam ṅō nyōṅ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši kpēmo̱ hĩĩ ne̱ bao kpēmo̱ le̱, te ši ni oke̱ame̱ aya; ši kẽle̱ noni makē̱o le̱, no noṅṅ oſe.

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Bileam te ši lebi, ni ewo etedšiyō no̱ nii, ni eke̱ Moab lume̱i le̱ yiṅ ete.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ mli wo la ake̱ ēya, ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ badamo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱, koni ebafole̱; ši le̱ le̱ etá etedšiyō le̱ no̱ ke̱-mba, ni eblahĩĩ enyo̱ le̱ ke̱le̱ nyie.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ yadamo̱ gbe̱ vō ko ní kã weintromi ateṅ ní gbogbo yo̱ bie̱ ke̱ bie̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Ni beni tedšiyō le̱ na Iehowa bo̱fo le̱, eke̱ ehe yakpe̱te̱ gbogbo le̱, ni emĩa Bileam nane ekpe̱te̱ gbogbo le̱; ni eyile̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ sã tši ke̱-te ehĩe, ni eyadamo̱ nifĩfĩaṅ heko, heni gbe̱ be̱ ní ake̱-tšṍo̱ he ke̱-yaä ninedšŭrõ lo abe̱ku.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Ni beni tedšiyō le̱ na Iehowa bo̱fo le̱, eho ekũla ši ye̱ Bileam šiši; ke̱ke̱ ni Bileam mli wo la, ni eṅõ tšo le̱ etſa tedšiyō le̱.

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ tedšiyō le̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ ofemi kolo! Edši mihĩe klante kũle̱, be ne̱ migbeo momo!

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Ni tedšiyō le̱ kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Ani dšee otedšiyō dšimi ni otáa mino̱ dãne̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱? Ani mifeo ne̱ke̱ dã lo? Ni ekē̱: Dabi.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa gble Bileam hĩṅme̱ii, ni ena Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ damo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱, ní egbla eklante ehĩe edeṅ; ni emã eyi ši ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši fe̱tē̱.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ oyi otedšiyō le̱ šii etẽ so̱ṅṅ ne̱? Na, mi le̱ miba mibafoö; edšake̱ ogbe̱ le̱ edšaa ye̱ mihĩe.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Ni tedšiyō le̱ nami, ni ew̌i ehe ke̱-dše̱ mihĩe šii etẽ so̱ṅṅ; edši ew̌ii ehe ke̱-dše̱e̱ mihĩe kũle̱, be ne̱ migbeo momo, ni le̱ le̱ mihere eyi wala.

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ ake̱: Mife eša; edšake̱ milee ake̱ bo obafomi ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱; nohewo le̱ agbe̱ne̱, ke̱dši esaa ohĩe le̱, makũ mise̱ mo̱!

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Oke̱ hĩĩ le̱ aya ke̱ke̱; ši wiemo̱ ní mike̱o aawie le̱, no noṅṅ owie! Ke̱ke̱ ni Bileam ke̱ Balak lume̱i le̱ yiṅ te.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Ni beni Balak nu ake̱ Bileam mība le̱, eyiṅ ke̱-tele̱ kpēmo̱ ye̱ Moab maṅ ní kã Arnon kpokpai le̱ ana ye̱ kpokpai le̱ anāgbēhe le̱ tō̃.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Ni Balak kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Ani dšee tšũ mitšũ kpẽkpē̃kpẽ ake̱ abakpēo ke̱-ba? Mẽba obaa le̱? Ani osusuo̱ ake̱ minyẽṅ ohĩe nyam mawo?

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ Balak ake̱: Na, miba oṅõ moṅ; ši ani manyẽ wiemo̱ ko mawie lo? Wiemo̱ ní Nyoṅmo̱ aaṅõ-wo minā le̱, no noṅṅ mibawie!

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ni Bileam ke̱ Balak te, ni ame̱ba Kiriat-Huzot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Ni Balak ṅõ tšinai ke̱ tōi ešã afole, ni emãdše Bileam ke̱ lume̱i ní ke̱le̱ yo̱ le̱ eko.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ ake̱ Balak ṅõ Bileam ni eke̱le̱ te *Baal gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni dše̱i edše̱ ena heni maṅ le̱ nā yakpa. *

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Ni Balak fe boni Bileam kē̱ le̱; ni Balak ke̱ Bileam šã tšinanũ kome ke̱ tōagbo kome ye̱ afe̱lešãlate̱-fẽ-afo̱lešãlate̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ Balak ake̱: Yadamo̱ ošā̃-afo̱le le̱ he; ni maya, ake̱ aleenõ Iehowa ke̱mi aakpe lo; ni wiemo̱-fẽ-wiemo̱ ní eekē̱mi le̱, matšĩ tã makē̱o. Ni eyiṅ ke̱-te goṅ kpatā ko no̱.

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ṅõ wiemo̱ ewo Bileam nā ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Kũ ose̱ ke̱-ya Balak ṅõ, ni bo̱ni owie ne̱!

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Ni ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te eṅõ, ni na, edamo ešã-afo̱le le̱ he, le̱ ke̱ Moab lume̱i le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Ni ewó ebe̱bua le̱ no̱ ni ekē̱: Aram tō̃ Balak yaṅõmi ke̱-dše̱, Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ yaṅõmi ke̱-dše̱ bokã gõdši le̱ ano̱ ake̱: Ba, ní obalomo̱ Iakob ohãmi, ni obakpa musu oſie Israel no̱!

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Namo aanyẽ Iakob *mlu le̱ akane, lo Israel mlidšāi edſe̱ mli ekome le̱ yikule̱? Hã †magbo dšalo̱i agbĕle, ni mināgbē atamo̱ ame̱no! *

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Balak kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Té oke̱mi yeo̱ tēṅ ne̱? Mihenye̱lo̱i alōmo̱ hewo̱ miyaṅõo ke̱-ba, ni na, dšō̱mo̱ so̱ṅṅ odšō̱ame̱ ne̱!

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Ni Balak kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, ba ní wo̱te hekroko, heni oonaame̱ ye̱; ame̱fã ke̱ke̱ oona, ši onaṅ ame̱fẽ; ni olomo̱ame̱ ye̱ dše̱i ohãmi!

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Ni eṅole̱ ke̱-te Zofim ṅã le̱ no̱ ye̱ Pisga goṅ le̱ yiteṅ, ni emãmo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱i kpawo, ni ešã tšinanā kome ke̱ tōagbo kome ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱-fẽ-afo̱lešãlate̱ no̱.

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Bileam kpe, ni eke̱ wiemo̱ wo enā ni ekē̱: Kũ ose̱ ke̱-ya Balak ṅõ, ni bo̱ni owie ne̱!

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Ni eba eṅõ, ni na, edamo̱ ešā̃-afo̱le le̱ he, ni Moab lume̱i le̱ ke̱le̱ damo̱ ši; ni Balak kē̱le̱ ake̱: Meni Iehowa kē̱?

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Dšee gbomo dši Mawu ní eemale, alo gbomo bi ní eeſa ehe. Aso eekē̱ noko ni efeṅ? Alo eewo ši ni eyeṅ no̱?

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Na, dšō̱mo̱ afã́mi ake̱ midšō̱; ni edšō̱, ni minyẽṅ hĩe matšake.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Enako ošrã ko ye̱ Iakob he, ni asaṅ enako hedšramo̱ ko ye̱ Israel he. Iehowa, e-Nyoṅme̱ le̱, ke̱le̱ ye̱, ni maṅtše̱ he nyã́mo̱ ye̱ ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Mawu edšieame̱ ye̱ Mizraim, ehewale̱ tamo̱ wuo nõ.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ṅkũnyā ko nyẽṅ Iakob, ni okomfoi agbale̱ ko hũ mōṅ Israel. Ke̱ še̱ be le̱ aagba nii ní Mawu etšu ye̱ Iakob ke̱ Israel he le̱.

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Ni Bileam here no̱ ni ekē̱ Balak ake̱: Ani mikē̱ē̱o ake̱: Nofẽno ni Iehowa aakē̱ le̱, no mibafe lo? K.

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Ni Balak kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ hã wo̱ya hekroko; ekole̱ aasa Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, ni olomo̱ame̱ kẽ ye̱ dše̱i ohãmi!

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ni Balak ṅõ Bileam ke̱-te *Peor goṅ le̱ ní kwe̱o̱ ṅã kplenẽ le̱ no̱ le̱ yiteṅ. *

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Ni Bileam kē̱ Balak akē̱: Mãmo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱i kpawo ye̱ bie̱ ohãmi, ni oba-hãmi tšinahĩĩ kpawo ke̱ tōagboi kpawo ye̱ bie̱! K.

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Ni Balak fe bo̱ni Bileam kē̱le̱ le̱, ni ešã tšinanū kome ke̱ tōagbo kome ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱-fẽ-afo̱lešãlate̱ no̱.

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Balak mli wo Bileam la, ni etſa edẽ. Ni Balak kē̱ Bileam ake̱: Miyakpēo ní obalomo̱ mihenye̱lo̱i, ni na, dšō̱mo̱ so̱ṅṅ odšō̱o̱ame̱ šii etẽ ne̱ fẽ!

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši Balak ṅõ ewe le̱ dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika obõ ehãmi tete le̱, minyẽṅ mateke Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱, ní mato miyiṅ mafe ekpakpa lo efõṅ ko, ake̱ dša noni Iehowa aakē̱ le̱ noṅṅ makē̱ lo?

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Ni *eeye Edom no̱, ni eeye Seir, ehenye̱lo̱ le̱, no̱; ši Israel le̱, efeo ekà. *

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Ni moko aadše̱ Iakob mli *aye no̱, ni eekpãtã mei ní aaſe̱ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ le̱ ahĩe. *Mika

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ni beni ekwe̱ Amalekbii le̱, ewó ebe̱bua le̱ no̱ ni ekē̱: Dšeṅmãdši ateṅ kleṅkleṅ maṅ dši Amalek; ši *enāgbē dši hĩekpãtãmo̱! *

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Ni beni ekwe̱ *Kenbii le̱, ewó ebe̱bua le̱ no̱ ni ekē̱: Ošihĩle̱he le̱ mã ši šiṅṅ, ni †oṅõ otšũ le̱ omã te̱sā no̱. *

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ Kenbii le̱ ahĩe aakpãtã, ni etše̱ṅ ni Ašur aaṅõame̱ nom.

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Ši le̱dši aadše̱ Kitim ṅšo̱nā aba, ni ame̱abahao Ašur, ni ame̱abahao Heber; ni le̱dientše̱ hũ, eete hĩekpãtãmo̱ mli!

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Bileam *te ši ni eyiṅ ete, ni ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te emaṅ; ni Balak hũ ko egbe. *

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: Ṅõ maṅ le̱ no̱ onukpai le̱ fẽ ní *ose̱ṅame̱ ohã Iehowa ye̱ hũlũ ne̱ hĩe, koni Iehowa mlifũ ní nā wa le̱ adše Israel no̱! *

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Israel kodšolo̱i le̱ ake: Nyeteṅ mofẽmo agbe emei ní ke̱ ame̱he yakpe̱te̱ Baal-Peor he le̱!

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Ni na, Israelbii le̱ ateṅ nū ko yakpla Midianyō ko ke̱-ba enyemimei le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Mose ke̱ Israelbii asafo mũ le̱ fẽ hĩe, beni ame̱ le̱ ame̱fóo̱ ye̱ kpē-bē le̱ šĩnä le̱ nā le̱.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Ši beni oso̱fo Aaron bi Eleazar bi Pinehas na ene̱ le̱, ete ši ye̱ asafo le̱ teṅ, ni eyako̱ akplo̱ ehĩe edeṅ,

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: Oso̱fo Aaron bi Eleazar bi Pinehas ekũ mimli ni ewo Israelbii le̱ ala le̱ nā, edšake̱ eye awuṅã ehãmi ye̱ ame̱teṅ, ni ehãã maplenē Israelbii le̱ ye̱ miwuṅãyeli le̱ mli.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Ni le̱ ke̱ eseši ní aaba ye̱ ese̱ le̱ anõ nāno̱ oso̱foyeli kpãṅmo̱ le̱ aatšṍ, edšake̱ eye awuṅã ehã e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni ekpãtã ehã Israelbii le̱! Lal.

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Ni Israelnyo, ní agbele̱ ke̱ Midianyō, le̱ gbe̱i dši Zimri, Salu bi le̱, ní dši Simeonbii le̱ atše̱ we le̱ no̱ onukpa le̱.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Ni Midianyō ní agbele̱ gbe̱i dši Kozbi; etše̱ dši *Zur ní dši Midianbii le̱ aweku le̱ eko no̱ onukpa le̱. *

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ni ekē̱:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱ hũ ame̱ke̱ ame̱lakamo̱ le̱ wonye haomo̱ mli, beni ame̱lakanye ye̱ Baal-Peor sane le̱ mli ke̱ ame̱nyemiyō Kozbi, ní dši Midian onukpa ko biyō le̱, sane le̱ mli le̱; le̱ dši moni agbele̱ ye̱ Peor hewo̱ ye̱ gbĕle-hela gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ši Iuda bii le̱ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ ana ne̱: Šela ke̱ Šelabii aweku le̱; Perez ke̱ Perezbii aweku le̱; Zera ke̱ Zerabii aweku le̱.

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Ni Palu bi dši Eliab;

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: ni Eliab bii dši Nemuel ke̱ Datan ke̱ Abiram. Mene̱mei dši *Datan ke̱ Abiram, akuašoṅbii ní futu Kora asafo le̱ mli ní tē béi ši ame̱wo Mose ke̱ Aaron, beni ame̱tē béi ši ame̱wo Iehowa, *Yi.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Ši Kora bihĩī le̱ gboii.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Ši mei ní Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Aaron kane, beni ame̱kane Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Sinai ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, ateṅ mokomeflo be̱ mene̱mei ateṅ.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron fo̱ Nadab ke̱ Abihu, Eleazar ke̱ Itamar.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: Adša šikpoṅ le̱ mli ahã mene̱mei ye̱ ame̱gbe̱ii le̱ ayibo̱ nā, ní etšṍ ame̱nõ.

english_verse: The total number of Israelite men listed was
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ ateṅ mei ní akane le̱ ayibo̱ dši akpei-ohai-ekpa-ke̱-ekome ke̱ ohai-kpawo ke̱ nyoṅmai-etẽ.

translation_verse: Ni ké̱ etše̱ be̱ nyemimeihĩĩ hũ le̱, no le̱ nyeke̱ egbošinii le̱ ahãa ewekunyo ní be̱ṅke̱le̱ ye̱ eweku le̱ mli, ní eye egbošinii le̱. Ni ene̱ atsṍ mla ní ake̱-kodšo ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa wo Mose kitã le̱.

translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱: *Ṅõ Iošua, Nun bi le̱, moni dši nū ko ní Mumo̱ le̱ yo̱ emli le̱, ni oṅõ onine ofõ eno, *

translation_verse: Ni ebadamo̱ oso̱fo Eleazar hĩe, koni etšṍ *urim gbale̱ le̱ no̱ ebi nii ehãle̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ni ewiemo̱ nā ame̱dše kpo ye̱, ni ewiemo̱ nā ame̱ba ye̱, le̱ ke̱ Israelbii le̱ fẽ ke̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ. *

translation_verse: Ni ye̱ nyenyõdši le̱ adšē kleṅkleṅ gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ nyebašãa šā̃-afo̱le nyehãa Iehowa: tšina-oblahĩĩ enyo̱, tōagbo kome, gwanteṅbihĩĩ kpawo ní eye afifi ní kpa ko be̱ ame̱he;

translation_verse: sŏro nyõṅ hē no̱ šā̃-afo̱le ke̱ ehe niyenii-afo̱le le̱, ni sŏro dā šā̃-afo̱le ke̱ ehe niyenii-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ ame̱he dā̃-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱ ame̱gbe̱nāgbe̱nā, ni eefe afo̱le ní ake̱ la šãa ní dšeo̱ ṅmã woo̱ Iehowa.

translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši yō ko wo Iehowa ši ni eke̱-gu ehe noko ye̱ etše̱ we ye̱ eblayeiaṅ,

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: ni etše̱ banu ešiwō le̱ ke̱ nõ femo̱ ní eguo̱ ehe le̱, ni ekē̱ē̱ noko le̱, no le̱ ešiwōi le̱ fẽ mà heni mã, ni nõ femo̱ ní egu ehe le̱ hũ mã heni mã.

english_verse: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ be mli ní ešiwōi le̱ kã eno̱ lolo lo eša ehe ewie wiemo̱ ko eke̱-gu ehe noko le̱ ni eyagbã,

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: ni ewù le̱ banu ni gbĩ ní enu le̱ ekē̱ē̱ noko le̱, no le̱ ešiwōi le̱ mã heni mã, ni nõ femo̱ ní egu ehe le̱ hũ mã heni mã.

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.

translation_verse: ni ewṅ le̱ nu ni ekē̱ē̱ noko ni ekplẽle̱ le̱, no le̱ ešiwōi le̱ fẽ mã heni mã, ni nofẽno ní egu ehe femo̱ le̱ hũ mã heni mã.

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: Ni Mose wo akutšo-fẽ-akutšo mli mei akpekpe le̱ gbe̱ ke̱-te ta le̱, ni oso̱fo Eleazar bi *Pinehas ke̱ame̱ te; ni ehĩe nibii kroṅkroṅi le̱ ke̱ †ošèbō̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱. *

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ Midianbii le̱ wu, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa wo Mose kitã le̱, ni *amegbe nū-fẽ-nū. *

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ ṅõ Midian yei ke̱ bii le̱ anom, ni ame̱ha ame̱dšatšutẽremo̱ koloi ke̱ ame̱lẽ̱̀-koloi ke̱ ame̱henibii fẽ.

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱mãdši ní ame̱hĩo̱ mli ke̱ ame̱nsrai le̱ fẽ ame̱ke̱ la šã.

english_verse: Then they returned to their own camp in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, where Moses, Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders met the troops outside camp.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Eleazar ke̱ asafo le̱ mli onukpai le̱ fẽ dše kpo yakpeame̱ ye̱ nsra le̱ se̱.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: ni Mose kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mẽba nyehã yei le̱ fẽ hĩe kãmo̱?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyegbea gbekẽ-bii le̱ ateṅ *nū-fẽ-nū, ni asaṅ nyegbea yō-fẽ-yō ní ele nu; *Kodš.

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: ši gbekẽbiiyei fẽ ni leko nū le̱, nyešiaame̱ nyehãa nyehe.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Ni mama-fẽ-mama ke̱ wolonõ-fẽ-wolonõ ke̱ nofẽno ní aṅõ tōabotia hetšo̱i afe ke̱ tšonõ-fẽ-tšonõ hũ nyetšūa he.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose ake̱:

english_verse: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
translation_verse: Fã ní dši ame̱nõ le̱ mli odšie ye̱, ni oṅõ-hã oso̱fo Eleazar, ní ake̱-fe no̱wómo̱-afo̱le ahã Iehowa.

english_verse: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
translation_verse: nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱ke̱ Iehowa nikēnii eba, mofẽmo noni ená, šika dſinei, nanešinii, ninešigai, niianāso̱omo̱gai, toiaṅnii ke̱ kue̱nii, koni ake̱-kpãtã ahã wo̱susumai ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Eleazar fe bo̱ni Iehowa wo Mose kitã le̱.

english_verse: women and gave them to Eleazar to be dedicated to the Lord. Then from the half that belonged to the people, Moses set aside one out of every
translation_verse: Ni ta mli nii ní tabiloi le̱ ha le̱ amli noni ſe̱ ní ame̱ke̱-ba dši tōi, akpei-ohai-ekpa ke̱ akpei-nyoṅmai-kpawo-ke̱-enumo̱,

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: ke̱ gbomei ní dši yei ní leko nū le̱ akpei-nyoṅmai-etẽ-ke̱-enyo̱.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: ni ame̱bakē̱ Mose ake̱: Otšũdši ekane tabilo̱i ní wo̱hĩe le̱, ni ame̱teṅ mokomoko ekaa;

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Eleazar he šika dſinei le̱ fẽ ye̱ ame̱deṅ.

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Ši tabilo̱-fẽ-tabilo̱ ha nii hã ehe hũ.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Eleazar he šika le̱ ye̱ mei akpekpei atše̱mei ke̱ mei ohahai atše̱mei le̱ adeṅ, ni ame̱ke̱-ba kpē-bū le̱ mli, ní ake̱-fe kaimo̱nõ ahã Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
translation_verse: ni aaye šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni no se̱ fẽdã ni nyeakũ nyese̱ le̱, no le̱ nyeaye bem ye̱ Iehowa ke̱ Israel hĩe, ni ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ aatšṍ nyegbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: Ni Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Rubenbii le̱ ba ame̱bakē̱ Mose ke̱ oso̱fo Eleazar ke̱ asafo le̱ no̱ lume̱i le̱ ake̱:

english_verse: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Rubenbii le̱ ake̱: Aso nyenyemimei le̱ aya ní ameya wu, ni nye le̱ nyetrá ši ye̱ bie̱ ne̱?

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Ni mẽba nyefãa Israelbii le̱ atšui, koni ame̱kafoṅ ke̱-mīya šikpoṅ ní Iehowa ke̱-hãame̱ le̱ no̱?

english_verse: They went as far as Eshcol Valley, then returned and told the people that we should not enter it.
translation_verse: ni beni ame̱baše̱ Eškol dšō̱ le̱ṅ, ni ame̱na šikpoṅ le̱, ame̱báfã Israelbii le̱ atšui, koni ame̱kaya šikpoṅ ní Iehowa eṅõ-hãame̱ le̱ no̱;

english_verse: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši nyeafe ne̱ke̱, ake̱ *nyeasā nyehe ní nyenyie Iehowa hĩe ke̱-ya ta le̱, *Ios.

english_verse: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
translation_verse: Ni Mose ṅõ Gilead ehã Manase bi Makir le̱, ní ehĩ dše̱i.

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad replied: Let us build places to keep our sheep and goats, and towns for our wives and children,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱tši ame̱be̱ṅke̱le̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Koloi atšũi ke̱ke̱ wo̱bamãmo̱ ye̱ bie̱ wo̱hã wo̱koloi, ke̱ mãdši wo̱hã wo̱bii abifabii;

english_verse: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
translation_verse: Wo̱kũṅ wo̱se̱ ke̱-baṅ wo̱šĩai ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní Israelbii le̱ ateṅ mofẽmo nine aaše̱ egbe̱fãṅnõ no̱.

english_verse: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱ke̱ame̱ eṅõṅ no̱yelinii ye̱ Iordan se̱gbe̱ ke̱-yaä le̱, edšake̱ wo̱-no̱yelinii le̱ ebadše Iordan bie̱gbe̱ ye̱ bokãgbe̱.

english_verse: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
translation_verse: ni nyeteṅ tabilo̱-fẽ-tabilo̱ aafo Iordan ke̱-nyie Iehowa hĩe ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eeſie ehenye̱lo̱i le̱ ye̱ ehĩe,

english_verse: But if you don't keep your promise, you will sin against the Lord and be punished.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyefee nakai le̱, na, nyemīfe Iehowa šiši eša, ni befẽbe ní fe le̱ nyeaná nyehe eša le̱ he nyõmo̱wo.

english_verse: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
translation_verse: Nyetoa mãdši nyehãa nyebii abifabii le̱, ni nyemãmo̱a koloi atšŭi nyehãa nyekoloi le̱, ni noni nyeke̱ nyenābu ekē̱ le̱ nyefea!

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
translation_verse: Ni Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Rubenbii le̱ kē̱ Mose ake̱: Otšũdši aafe bo̱ni minuṅtšo̱ kē̱o̱ le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
translation_verse: Wo̱bii abifabii ke̱ wo̱ṅãmei ke̱ wo̱lē̱-koloi ke̱ wo̱dšatšutĕremo̱-koloi le̱ fẽ ahĩ Gilead mãdši le̱ amli;

english_verse: But those of us who are prepared for battle will cross the Jordan and fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: ši wo̱, otšũdši le̱, wo̱o̱sã wo̱he ke̱-nyie Iehowa hĩe ke̱-ya ta le̱, take̱ bo̱ni minuṅtšo̱ kē̱ le̱.

english_verse: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kē̱ame̱ ake̱: *Ke̱dši Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Rubenbii le̱ kenye aafo Iordan, ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo aasã ehe ahã ta ke̱-nyie Iehowa hĩe, ni nyeaaye šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, no le̱ nyeṅõa Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ nyehãa-ame̱ ake̱ ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ; *Ios.

english_verse: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
translation_verse: ši ke̱dši ame̱sāā ame̱he ní ame̱ke̱nye afo mli ke̱-ya le̱, no le̱ ame̱ná ame̱gbe̱-fãṅnõ ye̱ nyeteṅ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
translation_verse: Wo̱ le̱ wo̱o̱sã wo̱he ní wo̱fo mli ke̱-nyie Iehowa hĩe ke̱-ya Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, koni wo̱gbe̱fãṅnõ ní wo̱ná ye̱ Iordan bie̱gbe̱ le̱ ahĩ ši ahãwo̱.

english_verse: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mose ṅõ Amorbii amaṅtše̱ Sihon maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ke̱ Bašan maṅtše̱ Og maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ke̱ mãdši ní yo̱ ehũsũi le̱ amli, ní dši šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ mãdši le̱ fẽ ke̱-kpe le̱, ehã Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Iosef bi Manase akutšo le̱ fã. Ios.

english_verse: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
translation_verse: Ni Gadbii le̱ sā to Dibon ke̱ Atarot ke̱ Aroer

english_verse: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
translation_verse: ke̱ Atrot-Šofan ke̱ Iazer ke̱ Iogbeha

english_verse: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ke̱ Bet-Nimra ke̱ Bet-Haran, ní dši màdši ní atſa gbogbo awo he le̱, ekoṅ, ni ame̱mãmo̱ koloi atšũi.

english_verse: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
translation_verse: Ni Rubenbii le̱ sā to Hešbon ke̱ Eleale ke̱ Kiriataim

english_verse: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
translation_verse: ke̱ Nebo ke̱ Baal-Meon, ni ame̱tšake ame̱gbe̱i, ke̱ Šibma; ni ame̱wo mãdši ní ame̱totoi le̱ agbe̱ii hēi.

english_verse: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ni Manase bi Makir bii le̱ yiṅ ke̱-te Gilead ni ame̱yamō dše̱i, ni ame̱-ſie Amorbii le̱ ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱.

english_verse: Jair from the Manasseh tribe captured villages and renamed them “Villages of Jair.”
translation_verse: Ni Manase bi Iair le̱ yiṅ ete eyamõmo̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱, ni etšé̱ame̱ ake̱ Iair akrowai.

english_verse: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
translation_verse: Ni Noba yiṅ ete eyamõ Kenat ke̱ ehe akrowai le̱, ni eṅõ egbe̱i Noba le̱ ewole̱.

english_verse: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ *Hahirot hĩe ke̱-tšṍ ṅšo̱ le̱ mli ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱, ni ame̱nyie gbĩĩ etẽ gbe̱ ye̱ Etam ṅã le̱ no̱ ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ †Mara. *

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Aluš ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Refidim; ni dše̱i le̱ maṅ le̱ náá nu anu.

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Refidim ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Sinai ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Kadeš ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Hor goṅ le̱ he ye̱ Edom šikpoṅ le̱ hũsũ no̱.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Aaron kwo̱ ke̱-te Hor goṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā, ni eyagbo ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ Israelbii le̱ a-Mizraim-dšē le̱ se̱ afi ní dši nyoṅmai-edſe̱ le̱ mli nyõṅ ní dši enumo̱ le̱ no̱ kleṅkleṅ gbĩ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Ni Arad maṅtše̱ ni dši Kanaannyo ní yo̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱ nu ake̱ Israelbii le̱ miba.

english_verse: and finally in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Abarim gõdši le̱ ano̱ ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Moab ṅã kplenē le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iordan se̱ ye̱ Ieriko ṅe̱le̱no̱.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bo̱ nsra ye̱ Iordan nā ke̱-dše̱ Bet-Iešimot ke̱-yaši Abel-Šitim ye̱ Moab ṅã kplenẽ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ye̱ Moab ṅã kplenē le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iordan se̱ ye̱ Ieriko ṅe̱le̱no̱ ni ekē̱:

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: Oke Israelbii le̱ awie ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši nyefo Iordan ke̱-te Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱,

english_verse: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
translation_verse: no le̱ nyeſiea šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ ke̱-dše̱a nyehĩe, ni nyekpãtãa ame̱te̱-mfonirii le̱ fẽ hĩe, ni ame̱mãgãi ní aſie le̱ hũ nyekpãtãa fẽ hĩe, ni nyefitea ame̱hei groṅṅi le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Ni nyeṅõ šikpoṅ le̱ ni nyehĩ no̱; edšake̱ miṅõ šikpoṅ le̱ mihãnye, koni nyeye no̱.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Ni *nyefõ ošiki nyeke̱-dša šikpoṅ le̱ nyehã nyekutšei le̱: mei ní yi fá le̱ nyehãa ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ afáa, ni mei ní yi fáá le̱ nyehãa ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ afea fiō; heni mo ošiki aayagbe le̱, dše̱i atšṍ onõ; nyetše̱mei akutšei le̱ anā nyená nyegbe̱ſãṅnii le̱ ye̱. *

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeſiee šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ ke̱-dše̱e̱ nyehĩe le̱, no le̱ ame̱teṅ mei ni nyeašĩ le̱ aatšṍmo̱ tamo̱ aklatii ye̱ nyehĩṅme̱iaṅ ke̱ ṅmeii ye̱ nyeṅmãwuiaṅ, ni ame̱ahaonye ye̱ šikpoṅ ní nyeyo̱ no̱ le̱ no̱. Ios.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱, bo̱ni misusu ake̱ mafeame̱ le̱, nakai mafenye.

english_verse: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: No le̱ nye wuoyigbe̱ koṅ le̱ adše̱ *Zin ṅã le̱ no̱ ke̱-nyie Edom mase̱i, ni nyewuoyigbe̱ hũsũ le̱ adše̱ Ṅō-ṅšo̱ le̱ nā ye̱ bokãgbe̱; *Ios.

english_verse: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
translation_verse: ni nyehũsũ le̱ alo̱go̱ ke̱-tšṍ Akrabim ṅmeṅme le̱ wuoyigbe̱, ni efoṅ ke̱-tšṍ Zin, ni etšṍ ke̱-yadše Kadeš-Barnea wuoyigbe̱, ni ešrã Hazar-Adar ke̱-ya Azmon;

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ afe nyekōyigbe̱ hũsũ le̱: nyedšea ṅšo̱ wulu le̱ nā nyekadia Hor goṅ le̱ nyehãa nyehe;

english_verse: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
translation_verse: ni nyedšea Hor goṅ le̱ he nyekadia ke̱-yašia Hamat, ni hũsũ le̱ nā ayaſie Zedad.

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
translation_verse: Ni hũsũ le̱ ayaše̱ Zifron, ni enyie no̱ ke̱-yaši Hazar-Enan. Ene̱ afe nyekōyigbe̱ hũsũ.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin at Hazar-Enan in the north, then run south to Shepham,
translation_verse: Ni nyekadia nyebokãgbe̱ hũsũ le̱ ke̱-dše̱a Hazar-Enan ke̱-yaši Šefam;

english_verse: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
translation_verse: ni hũsũ le̱ adše̱ Šefam akpleke ši ke̱-ya Ribla ye̱ Ain bokãgbe̱, ni hũsũ le̱ akpleke ši ke̱-yamõ *Kineret-ṅšo̱ le̱ nā ye̱ bokãgbe̱, *Luk.

english_verse: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
translation_verse: ni hũsũ le̱ akpleke ši ke̱-yamõ Iordan, ni enā ayaši Ṅō-ṅšo̱ le̱ nā? Ene̱ dši nyešikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ehũsũi le̱ ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
translation_verse: Akutšei enyo̱ ke̱ fã le̱ ena ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ Iordan se̱ ye̱ Ieriko ṅe̱le̱no̱ ye̱ bokãgbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Mose wie ni ekē̱:

english_verse: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Hĩĩ ní adša šikpoṅ le̱ ahãnye le̱ agbe̱ii ne̱: Oso̱fo Eleazar ke̱ Iošua, Nun bi le̱. Ios.

english_verse: One leader from each tribe will help them,
translation_verse: Ni nyefãa lumo̱ kome ye̱ akutšo-fẽ-akutšo mli, koni ame̱dša šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši mei ni Iehowa fã́ ake̱ ame̱dša Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ mli ame̱hã Israelbii le̱.

english_verse: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ši mãdši ní nyeaṅõ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ano̱yelinii le̱ amli nyehã le̱, mei ní ame̱nō fã le̱ adeṅ nyehea mãdši pī ye̱, ni mei ní ame̱nõ fáá le̱ nyehea fiō ye̱ ame̱deṅ; mofẽmo le̱ bo̱ni eno̱yelinõ le̱ fále̱ yo̱ le̱, nakai mãdši abo̱ eke̱-hã Levibii le̱.

english_verse: There are to be six of these Safe Towns,
translation_verse: Ni mãdši ní nyeaṅõ-hã ní afe abobāhei le̱ afe mãdši ekpa.

english_verse: choose Safe Towns, where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection.
translation_verse: no le̱ nyehalaä mãdši ní sa ní atšṍmo̱ abobā-mãdši ahãnye, koni gbomogbelo̱ ní nine kpa ye̱ moko no̱ le̱ adšo foi ke̱-ya dše̱i.

english_verse: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ abobā-mãdši ame̱hãnye ke̱-dše̱ oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ deṅ, koni gbomogbelo̱ le̱ akagbo ake̱ dša ebadamo̱ asafo le̱ hĩe ni akodšole̱ dã.

english_verse: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
translation_verse: Alo ke̱dši moko hĩe tšo ní aagbe gbomo ye̱ edeṅ ni eke̱-tſa moko, ni egbo le̱, awuyelo̱ dšile̱; dša agbe awuyelo̱ le̱.

english_verse: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
translation_verse: no le̱ asafo le̱ akodšo moni tſa mo nõ le̱ ke̱ lá he oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ teṅ ye̱ ne̱ke̱ mlai ne̱ anā;

english_verse: If they decide that you are innocent, you will be protected from the victim's relative and sent to stay in one of the Safe Towns until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: ni asafo le̱ ahere gbomogbelo̱ le̱ yiwala ke̱-dše̱ lá he oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ deṅ, ni asafo le̱ ke̱le̱ akũ se̱ ke̱-ya abobā-maṅ heni edšo foi ete le̱, ni eyahĩ dše̱i ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní oso̱fonukpa ní ake̱ *mũ kroṅkroṅ le̱ efo̱le̱ le̱ aagbo. *

english_verse: But if you ever leave the Safe Town
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši aleenõ gbomogbelo̱ le̱ dše kpo ke̱-teke abobā-maṅ, heni edšo foi ete le̱, hũsũ le̱,

english_verse: and are killed by the victim's relative, he cannot be punished for killing you.
translation_verse: ni lá he oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ baninale̱ ye̱ abobā-maṅ le̱ hũsũ le̱ se̱, ni lá oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ gbe gbomogbelo̱ le̱, eyee elá yi sõ.

english_verse: You must stay inside the town until the high priest dies; only then can you go back home.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ kũle̱ sa ake̱ ehĩ ebobā-maṅ le̱ mli ke̱-yaši oso̱fonukpa le̱ aagbo; ši oso̱fonukpa le̱ gbĕle se̱ le̱ gbomogbelo̱ ye̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ ekũ ese̱ ke̱-ya eno̱yeli šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
translation_verse: Awuyelo̱-fẽ-awuyelo̱ ní egbe moko le̱, odasefoi adāṅ wiemo̱ no̱ adamo̱ agbele̱; ši akagbe moko ye̱ odasefonyo kometō odaseyeli nā.

english_verse: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
translation_verse: Asaṅ gbomogbelo̱ ní eye fo̱ ni sa gbĕle le̱, nyekahea eyitšo heremo̱nii; ši dša agbele̱.

english_verse: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ nyekahea yitšo heremo̱nii ye̱ moni edšo foi ke̱-te abobā-maṅ le̱ deṅ, koni ekũ ese̱ ebahĩ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, beni oso̱fo le̱ náko agbo le̱.

english_verse: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
translation_verse: Ni Manase bi Makir bi Gilead bii le̱ aweku le̱ mli tše̱mei onukpai ni dše̱ Iosef bii le̱ akutšei le̱ amli le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱ ni ame̱bawie ye̱ Mose ke̱ Israelbii le̱ atše̱mei onukpai ni dši lume̱i le̱ ahĩe,

english_verse: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱: Iehowa fã́ minuṅtšo̱ ake̱ edša šikpoṅ le̱ mli *ye̱ ošikifõ nā ehã Israelbii, ni Iehowa †fã́ minuṅtšo̱ ake̱ eṅõ wo̱nyemi Zelofehad gbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ ehã ebiyei le̱. *
