english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kē̱ Akan ake̱: Mibi, ṅõ anumnyam ohã Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ní owole̱, ní odšadše otšõmi ko: meni ofe? kãšiumi no̱!

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Akan to he ehã Iošua ni ekē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, mife eša miši Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ mife:

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱dšie ke̱-dše̱ bū le̱ teṅ, ni ame̱ke̱-ba Iošua ke̱ Israelbii le̱ fõ ṅō, ni ame̱ke̱-baſie Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ṅõ Akan, Zera bi le̱, ke̱ dſie̱te̱i le̱ ke̱ bò le̱ ke̱ šika ante̱le le̱, ke̱ ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei, ke̱ etšinai ke̱ ete-dšii ke̱ etōi ke̱ ebū ke̱ nofẽno ni eyo̱, ni Israel mū le̱ fẽ fata ehe, ni ame̱ke̱-ame̱ te Akor dšē̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱to te̱i ame̱ſie eno̱ kú agbo ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. Ni Iehowa kpale ke̱-dše̱ emlifũ ní nā wa le̱ mli. Nohewo̱ le̱ awo dše̱i gbe̱i ake̱ Akor dšō̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. Ies.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: ni ame̱batiuwo̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní wo̱o̱gblaame̱ ke̱-dše̱ maṅ le̱ he; edšake̱ ame̱bakē̱ ake̱: Na, foi ame̱dseo̱ ye̱ wo̱hĩe *tamo̱ tšutšu le̱! ni wo̱o̱dšo foi ye̱ ame̱hĩe hũ. *

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Ši nye le̱ nyetea ši ke̱-dše̱a káwō le̱ṅ ní nyebahe maṅ le̱; edšake̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, aaṅõle̱ awo nyedeṅ.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa kē̱ Iošua ake̱: Kpã akplo̱ ní ohĩe le̱ mli otsṍ Ai gbe̱; edšake̱ madšiele̱ mawo odeṅ! Ni Iošua kpã akplo̱ ni ehĩe le̱ mli etšṍ maṅ le̱ no̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni káwolo̱i le̱ te ši oyá ke̱-dše̱ heni ame̱yo̱ le̱, ni amrõ ní Iošua kpã enine mli le̱, ame̱wo foi ni ame̱babote mã le̱ṅ, ni ame̱ṅõle̱, ni ame̱he fe oyá ni ame̱mã maṅ le̱ nā la.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Israel egbe Aibii fẽ ní yo̱ ṅmõdšiaṅ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ heni ame̱tiuame̱ ke̱-te le̱ etã, ni ame̱fẽ ame̱nyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā etã le̱, Israel mū le̱ fẽ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Ai, ni ame̱gbe-ame̱ ye̱ klante nā.

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Ši beni Gibeonbii le̱ hũ nu noni Iošua fe *Ieriko ke̱ †Ai le̱, *

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te Iošua ṅõ ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ ye̱ Gilgal, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ke̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ ake̱: Wo̱dše̱ maṅse̱ šoṅṅ, hewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeke̱wo̱ akpãṅa!

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Maṅse̱ šoṅṅ otšũdsi dše̱ ni ame̱ba ye̱ Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbe̱i ahewo̱; edšake̱ wo̱nu ehe sane le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ni efe ye̱ Mizraim,

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱nukpai ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ kē̱wo̱ ake̱: Nyeṅõa gbe̱no̱ niyenii ni nyeyaä ní nyeke̱ame̱ ayakpea, ni nyekē̱aame̱ ake̱: Nyetšũdši dšiwo̱, hewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeke̱wo̱ aakpãṅa!

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Wo̱boloi ne̱, gbĩ ni wo̱yiṅ ake̱ wo̱miba nyeṅõ le̱, klakla wo̱ṅõ ke̱-dše̱ wo̱šĩai, koni wo̱baye ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱, ni agbe̱ne̱, na, egbĩ ni efufūi.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ woloto̱i ne̱ ni wo̱woame̱ mli wein obõbõ le̱ ehēi ni, ni na, ame̱gblagblai; ni wo̱tadei ke̱ wo̱tokotai ne̱ esū ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ ni dšeke̱ tšṍ le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱here hĩĩ le̱ ye̱ ame̱gbe̱no̱ niyenii le̱ anā, ši ame̱bii *Iehowa dāṅgbē. *

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ke̱ame̱ ye omanye sane, ni eke̱ame̱ kpãṅ ake̱ agbeṅame̱. Ni asafo le̱ no̱ lume̱i le̱ kãmo̱ame̱ kitãi. K.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fã, ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ ame̱yanina ame̱mãdši le̱; ni ame̱mãdši le̱ dši Gibeon ke̱ Kefira ke̱ Beerot ke̱ Kiriat-Yearim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ egbeeame̱; edšake̱ asafo le̱ no̱ lume̱i le̱ ena Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱kãmo̱ame̱ kitãi; ši asafo mū le̱ fẽ wie hũhū̃hũ ame̱ši lume̱i le̱.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Ni Iošua tšé̱ame̱ ke̱-ba, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake: Meni hewo̱ nyelakawo̱ ake: Wo̱ke̱nye teṅ dšeke̱ naakpa; ani moaṅ le̱ wo̱teṅ nyeyo̱?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ alomo̱nye, ni nyṍdši ni aate lai ke̱ mei ni aate fāṅ ke̱-ba mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ ase̱ efoṅ ye̱ nyeteṅ?

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱to he ame̱hã Iošua ake̱: Edšake̱ agba otšũdši, bo̱ni Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ etšũlo̱ Mose ake̱ eeṅõ šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ ehãnye, ni eefite šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii fẽ ye̱ nyehĩe, ni wo̱še gbeyei naakpa ake̱ nyebagbewo̱, ni no hã wo̱ye ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, nawo̱, wo̱ye̱ odeṅ; bo̱fẽbo̱ hĩ ní edša ye̱ ohĩe ake̱ oofewo̱ le̱, femo̱.

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Ni efeame̱ nakai, ni edšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Israelbii le̱ adeṅ, ni ame̱kagbeame̱.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Ierusalem maṅtše̱ Adonizedek tšũ ke̱-te Hebron maṅtše̱ Hoham ke̱ Iarmut maṅtše̱ Piram ke̱ Lakiš maṅtše̱ Iafia ke̱ Eglon maṅtše̱ Debir ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ ta le̱ fẽ ke̱ tabilo̱i agboi le̱ fẽ fã ke̱-dše̱ Gilgal ke̱-te.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hã ame̱dšidšā ye̱ Israel hĩe, ni ame̱gbeame̱ babaō ye̱ Gibeon, ni ame̱tiuame̱ ke̱-tšṍ Bet-Horon kwē̱he le̱, ni ame̱gbegbẽame̱ ke̱-yaši Azeka ke̱ Makeda tō̃.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Ni *hũlũ wa, ni nyoṅtšẽre hũ damo̱ ši, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní maṅ le̱ to̱ ame̱he owele ye̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ ano̱. Ani aṅmãko ene̱ ye̱ †Iašar wolo le̱ mli? Ni hũlũ damo̱ ši ye̱ ṅwei teṅ, ni eyee oyai ní eyanyõ ši aafe gbĩ mū. *Hab.

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱mei enumo̱ ne̱ dšo foi, ni ame̱yatē ame̱he ye̱ te̱kplo ni yo̱ Makeda le̱ mli.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Ni abatſa Iošua adafi ake̱: Ana maṅtše̱mei enumo̱ le̱ ní ame̱yatẽ ame̱he ye̱ te̱kplo ní yo̱ Makeda le̱ mli.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Ši nye le̱ nyekadamo̱a ši; nyetiua nyehenye̱lo̱i le̱, ni nyetſia mei ní ekpe se̱ le̱ anii; nyekahãa ame̱yabotea ame̱mãdši le̱ amli; edšake̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, etuame̱ ewo nyedeṅ.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua kē̱: Nyegblea te̱kplo le̱ nā, ni nyedšiea nakai maṅtše̱mei enumo̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱a te̱kplo le̱ṅ nyebahãami!

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ake̱ nakai maṅtše̱mei le̱ dše kpo ke̱-ba Iošua ṅõ le̱, Iošua tšé̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱-ba, ni ekē̱ tabilo̱i ní ke̱le̱ te le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ake̱: Nyetšia nyebaä ni nyeke̱ nyenãdši abamãmo̱a ne̱ke̱ maṅtše̱mei ne̱ akue̱i ano̱! Ni ame̱tši ame̱ba, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱nãdši bamãmo̱ ame̱kue̱i ano̱.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekašea gbeyei, ni nyetšui hũ akafãã! nyehe awaä ni nyefea ekã; edšake̱ ne̱ke̱ Iehowa bafe nyehenye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ ní nyeke̱wuo̱ le̱!

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ le̱ Iošua tſiaame̱ nii ni egbeame̱, ni ese̱ṅame̱ ye̱ tšei enumo̱ no̱; ni ame̱tšotšõro tšei le̱ ano̱ ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Ši beni *hũlũ yanyõ ši le̱, Iošua fã́ ní adšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ tšei le̱ ano̱, ni aše̱re̱ame̱ aſie te̱kplo ni ame̱yatẽ ye̱ mli le̱ noṅṅ mli, ni ame̱hole te̱i kplei ame̱tšĩ te̱kplo le̱ nā, ni eye̱ ke̱-baši ṅmene̱. *

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ṅõ Makeda hũ ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni eke̱ klante gbeame̱, ni efe emli maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ susumai ní yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ musu, eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo ni dše mli; ni efe Makeda maṅtše̱ le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni *efe Ieriko maṅtše̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ Israel fẽ tšẽre̱ mli ke̱-dše̱ Makeda ke̱-te Libna, ni eke̱ Libna wu.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ṅõ no hũ ewo Israel deṅ ke̱ emli maṅtše̱ le̱ fẽ; ni eke̱ klante gbele̱ ke̱ susumai ni yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ, eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo ni dše mli; ni efe emli maṅtše̱ le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni efe Ieriko maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ Israel fẽ tšẽre̱ mli ke̱-dše̱ Libna ke̱-te Lakiš, ni ebo̱ nsra ewo ehe, ni eke̱le̱ wu.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ṅõ Lakiš ewo Israel deṅ, ni ame̱ṅõle̱ ye̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ enyo̱ le̱ no̱, nī ame̱ke̱ klante gbele̱ ke̱ susumai ní yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ, tamo̱ bo̱ni efe Libna le̱,

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: No be le̱ mli le̱ Geser maṅtše̱ Horam fã ke̱-ba ni ebaye ebua Lakiš: ni Iošua gbele̱ ke̱ emaṅ le̱ fẽ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo ni dše mli.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ Israel fẽ tšẽre̱ mli ke̱-dše̱ Lakiš ke̱-te Eglon; ni ame̱bo̱ nsra ame̱wo ehe, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ wu;

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ Israel fẽ fã ke̱-dše̱ Eglon ke̱-te Hebron, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ wu;

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: ni ame̱ṅõle̱, ni ame̱ke̱ klante gbeame̱ ke̱ emli maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ ehe akrowai le̱ fẽ ke̱ susumai ní yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ; eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo ni dše mli, tamo̱ bo̱ni efe Eglon le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱, ni efele̱ ke̱ susumai ni yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ musu.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua ke̱ Israel fẽ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Debir, ni eke̱le̱ yawu;

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: ni eṅõle̱ ke̱ emli maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ ehe akrowai le̱ fẽ, ni ame̱ke̱ klante gbeame̱, ni ame̱fe susumai ní yo̱ mli le̱ fẽ musu; eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo ní dše mli; bo̱ni efe Hebron le̱, ke̱ bo̱ni efe Libna ke̱ emli maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ le̱, nakai noṅṅ efe Debir ke̱ emli maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kpãtã šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ hĩe: gõdši ašikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ wuoyigbe̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ṅãno̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ gõdši ahĩe ši le̱ ke̱ ame̱mli maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ, ni eſe̱e̱ moko ni dše mli; ni nofẽno ni mũo̱ le̱ *efele̱ musu, tamo̱ bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ewo kitã le̱.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kpãtã ame̱hīe ke̱-dše̱ Kadeš-Barnea ke̱-te Gaza tõ, ke̱ *Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ ke̱-yaši Gibeon tõ. *

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: ke̱ Kanaanbii ní yo̱ bokãgbe̱ ke̱ anaigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ Amorbii le̱ ke̱ Hitbii le̱ ke̱ Perizbii le̱ ke̱ Iebusbii ní yo̱ goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱ Hivbii ní yo̱ Hermon goṅ le̱ šiši ye̱ Mizpa šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ṅõ nakai šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ, gõdšì ašikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱ fẽ ke̱ *Gošen šikpoṅ le̱ fã ke̱ ṅãno̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ṅã kpatã le̱ ke̱ Israel gõdši ašikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ehe ṅã kplanā le̱; *

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua fã ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli ni *eyabule Anakbii le̱ aseši ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱, ye̱ Hebron ke̱ Debir ke̱ Anab ke̱ Iuda gõdši le̱ fẽ no̱ ke̱ Israel godši le̱ fẽ no̱; ni Iošua feame̱ ke̱ ame̱mãdši le̱ fẽ musu. *

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anakbii le̱ ateṅ mokomeflo eſe̱e̱ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ake̱ dša Gaza ke̱ *Gat ke̱ Ašdod pe̱ meikomei ſe̱ ye̱. *

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ṅõ šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ, tamo̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ Mose le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱; ni Iošua dša mli hã Israel ye̱ ame̱mlidšāi anā ke̱ ame̱kutšei le̱ anā, ni etšṍ ame̱gbošinii. Ni *šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšo̱ ni tawū se̱ fo. *

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iošua egbo ní eye afii pī le̱, Iehowa kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ogbo̱ ni oye afii pī, ni šikpoṅ ní eſe̱ ní abaṅõ le̱ fá babaō lolo.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: ke̱-dše̱ Aroer ni kã Arnon fā le̱ nā ke̱ maṅ ní kã dšē̱ le̱ teṅ le̱ he, ke̱ Medeba ṅã kplanā le̱ fẽ ke̱-yaši Dibon,

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Ši Israelbii le̱ eſiee Gešurbii ke̱ Maakatbii le̱, nohewo̱ le̱ Gešurbii ke̱ Maakatbii le̱ hĩ ši ye̱ Israel teṅ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: *Levi akutšo le̱ ke̱ke̱ ni ehããle̱ gbe̱fãṅnõ ko; Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, afo̱lei ní ake̱ la šãa le̱ dši egbe̱fãṅnõ, take̱ bo̱ni ewole̱ ši le̱. *K.

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Noni Mose ṅõ-hã Rubenbii le̱ akutšo le̱ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anä ne̱:

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Ame̱hũsũ le̱ dše̱ Aroer ni kã Arnon fā le̱ nā ke̱ maṅ ni kã dšē̱ le̱ teṅ le̱, ke̱ Medeba ṅã kplanä le̱ fẽ he,

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Ni Rubenbii le̱ ahũsũ dši Iordan ke̱ etoitoii le̱. Ene̱ dši Rubenbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā, mãdši le̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱.

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Noni Mose ṅõ-hã Gad akutšo le̱ ni dši Gadbii le̱ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā ne̱:

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: ni ke̱-dše̱ Hešbon ke̱-yaši Ramat-Mizpe ke̱ Betonim, ni ke̱-dše̱ Mahanaim ke̱-yaši Debir hũsũ le̱ nā;

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: ke̱ dšē̱ le̱ mli: Bet-Haram ke̱ Bet-Nimra ke̱ Sukot ke̱ Zafon, noni ſe̱ ye̱ Hešbon maṅtše̱ Sihon maṅtše̱yelihe le̱, Iordan ke̱ etoitoii le̱ ke̱-yaši Kineret-ṅšo̱ le̱ nāgbẽ, ye̱ Iordan se̱, ye̱ bokãgbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Ene̱ dši Gadbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā, mãdši le̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱.

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Noni Mose ṅõ-hã Manase akutšo fã le̱ hũ, ni etšṍ Manasebii le̱ akutšo fã le̱ nõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā ne̱:

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: ke̱ Gilead fã ke̱ Aštarot ke̱ Edrei, Og ní yo̱ Bašan le̱ maṅtše̱yelihe le̱ mli mãdši le̱, Manase bi Makir bii le̱, ni dši Makir bii le̱ aſã le̱ nõ etšṍ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši mei ní Mose hãame̱ ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ, ye̱ Moab ṅã kplanā le̱ no̱, ye̱ Iordan se̱, ye̱ Ieriko ṅe̱le̱no̱ ye̱ bokãgbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Ši *Levi akutšo le̱, Mose hããle̱ gbe̱fãṅnõ ko; Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, dši egbe̱fãṅnõ, take̱ bo̱ni ewole̱ ši le̱. *

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Ni Iudabii le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱ Iošua ye̱ Gilgal, ni Iefune bi Kaleb, Keniznyo le̱, kē̱le̱ ake̱: Bodientše̱ ole wiemo̱ ni *Iehowa ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo Mose le̱ wie ye̱ mihewo̱ ke̱ ohewo̱ ye̱ Kadeš-Barnea le̱. *

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ši minyemimei ní ke̱mi te le̱ hã maṅ le̱ tšui fã; ši mi le̱ miho Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, toi ke̱-wula ši.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose kã kitã ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ ake̱: Šikpoṅ ní onane eyanyie no̱ le̱, ke̱-dšee bo ke̱ obii agbe̱fãṅnõ eetšṍ ke̱-ya näno̱, fĩ! edšake̱ obo Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, toi ke̱-wula ši!

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Hebron tšo Kaleb, Iefune bi Keniznyo le̱, gbe̱fãṅnõ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, edšake̱ ebo Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, toi ke̱-wula ši.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ni sá le̱ Hebron gbe̱i dši Kiriat-Arba; ni le̱ dši gbomo agbo ye̱ Anakbii le̱ ateṅ. Ni *šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšo̱ ni tawū se̱ fo. *

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: ni etšṍ Akrabim ṅmeṅme le̱ wuoyigbe̱, ni eſoṅ ke̱-tšṍ Zin, ni etšṍ ke̱-yadše Kadeš-Barnea wuoyigbe̱, ni ešrã Hezron ke̱-te Adar, ni elo̱go̱ ke̱-te Karka,

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Ni hũsũ le̱ dše̱ Akor dšō̱ le̱ṅ ewó enā no̱ ke̱-ba Debir, ni edo̱ eyi ke̱-tšṍ kōyigbe̱ ke̱-te Gilgal ye̱ Adumim ṅmeṅme le̱ ní yo̱ fā le̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱ ṅe̱le̱no̱; ni hũsũ le̱ šrã En-Šemeš nui le̱, ni eke̱ enā yawó *Rogel nubu le̱ mli; *

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: Ni hũsũ le̱ nyie Ekron mase̱i ye̱ kōyigbe̱ le̱, ni agba ke̱-yaši Šikeron, ni etšṍ Baala goṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yadše Iabneel, ni enā yamõ ṅšo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ni edše dše̱i ete Debir bii le̱ aṅõ. Ni sá le̱ Debir gbe̱i dši Kiriat-Sefer.

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Ene̱ dši Iudabii le̱ akutšo le̱ gbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: ke̱ Lebaot ke̱ Šilhim ke̱ Ain ke̱ Rimon: fẽ dši mãdši nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ ne̱hũ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ke̱ Šaaraim ke̱ Aditaim ke̱ Gedera ke̱ Gederotaim: mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ke̱ Gederot, Bet-Dagon ke̱ Naama ke̱ Makeda: mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ ekpa ke̱ ame̱he akrowai.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Si Iebusbii le̱ hĩ ši ye̱ Ierusalem, Iudabii le̱ nyẽẽame̱ ame̱ſie, *nohewo̱ le̱ Iebusbii le̱ ke̱ Iudabii le̱ hĩ Ierusalem ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. *

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Ni Efraimbii le̱ ahũsũi ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā ne̱: ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ bokãgbe̱ hũsũ dši Atarot-Adar ke̱-yaši Bet-Horon ni yo̱ yiteṅgbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱ſiee Kanaanbii ni yo̱ Gezer le̱, nohewo̱ le̱ Kanaanbii le̱ hĩ Efraim teṅ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ni ame̱súmo̱ame̱.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tapua šikpoṅ le̱ tšṍ Manase nõ; ši Tapua [maṅ] ní yo̱ Manase hũsũ le̱ no̱ le̱ Efraimbii le̱ anõ ni.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Ni mãdši ni *Manase ná ye̱ Isakar ke̱ Ašer teṅ le̱ ne̱: Bet-Šean ke̱ ehe mã-dši le̱, Ibleam ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, Dorbii ke̱ ame̱mãdši le̱, †En-Dorbii ke̱ ame̱-mãdši le̱, Taanakbii ke̱ ame̱mãdši le̱ ke̱ Megidobii ke̱ ame̱mãdši le̱; šikpõdši sro̱toi etẽ. *Kodš.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Ši Manasebii le̱ *nyẽẽ ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ amli bii le̱ ame̱ſie, nohewo̱ le̱ Kanaanbii le̱ ná hegbe̱ hĩ nakai šikpoṅ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iosefbii le̱ bakē̱ Iošua ake̱: Mẽba ohãmi mlidšä kome ke̱ susumo̱ kpã kome pe̱ ake̱ migbe̱fãṅnõ? Ni ole ake̱ maṅ wulu dšimi ní Iehowa edšō̱mi ke̱-baši bene̱ le̱!

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši nyeyi fá tšṍ le̱, te ši ní oya kō le̱ mli, ni oyagba Perizbii le̱ ke̱ oblãṅi ašikpoṅ le̱ eko ohã ohe, edšake̱ ohoo Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱!

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Ni Iosefbii le̱ kē̱ ake̱: Gõdši le̱ ano̱ šikpoṅ le̱ fáá hããwo̱, ni asaṅ Kanaanbii ní yo̱ dšō̱ le̱ṅ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ fẽ ye̱ dade ſīlii, mei ni yo̱ Bet-Šean ke̱ ehe mãdši le amli le ke̱ mei ní yo̱ Iezreel dšō̱ le̱ṅ le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Ni Iošua kē̱ Iosef we le̱ ni dši Efraim ke̱ Manase le̱ ake̱: Maṅ wulu dšio ni oye̱ hewale̱ naakpa, dšee mlidša kome ke̱ke̱ aatšṍ onõ;

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: ši moṅ goṅ le̱ no̱ aatšṍ onõ, edšake̱ kō ye̱ no̱, ni ogba ohã ohe, ni etšṍ onõ ke̱ hei ní tšara no̱ le̱; edšake̱ kē̱ Kanaanbii le̱ ye̱ dade ſīlii ni ame̱he wa po le̱ ooſieame̱ kẽ.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Ni Iošua fõ ošiki ehãame̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ye̱ Šilo; ni Iošua dša šikpoṅ le̱ mli ye̱ dše̱i ehã Israelbii le̱ ye̱ ame̱mlidšäi le̱ anā.

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Ni ošiki le̱ kpe̱ hã Benyaminbii le̱ akutšo le̱ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā; ni ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ hũsũ kã Iudabii le̱ ke̱ Iosefbii le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: ni agba hũsũ le̱ ke̱-lo̱go̱ ši ke̱-tšṍ anaigbe̱ ke̱-te wuoyigbe̱, ke̱-dše̱ goṅ ní kã Bet-Horon hĩe le̱ wuoyigbe̱, ni enā yamõ Kiriat-Baal, ní dši Kiriat-Iearim, Iudabii le̱ amaṅ le̱. No dši anaigbe̱ nõ le̱.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Ni hũsũ le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-te goṅ ni kã Hinombi le̱ dšō̱ le̱ hīe le̱ nāgbē, ye̱ Refaim dšō̱ le̱ kōyigbe̱, ni ekpleke Hinom dšō̱ le̱ ke̱-te Iebusbii le̱ awuoyigbe̱, ni ekpleke ši ke̱-ba Rogel nubu le̱ nā;

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: ni agba ke̱-dše̱ kōyigbe̱ le̱, ni enā yamõ En-Šemeš, ni edše̱ Gelilot ní kã Adumim ṅmeṅme le̱ ṅe̱le̱no̱ le̱, ni ekpleke ši ke̱-te Rubenbi Bohan te̱ le̱ he;

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: ni ešrã he ke̱-te ṅã kplanā le̱ ṅe̱le̱no̱ ye̱ kōyigbe̱, ni ekpleke ši ke̱-te ṅã kplanā le̱ no̱;

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: ni hũsũ le̱ tšṍ ke̱-yadše Bet-Hogla mase̱i ye̱ kōyigbe̱, ni enā yamõ Ṅō-ṅšo̱ le̱ kōyigbe̱ ble le̱ ye̱ Iordan wuoyigbe̱ nāgbēhe le̱. Ene̱ dši wuoyigbe̱ hũsũ le̱.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Ni Iordan dši ebokägbe̱ hũsũ. Ene̱ dši Benyaminbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ehũsũi le̱ anā ke̱-kpe, ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: ke̱ Bet-Lebaot ke̱ Šaruhen: mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Ni edše̱ dše̱i etšṍ bokãgbe̱ heni hũlũ teo̱ ši ye̱ le̱ ke̱-te Gat-Hefer ke̱ Et-Kazin; ni etša no̱ ke̱-te Rimon ni edo̱ eyi ke̱-te Nea.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Ain, Rimon ke̱ Eter ke̱ Ašan: mãdši edſe̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai;

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Iudabii le̱ anõ le̱ eko aṅõ-hã Simeonbii le̱ ake̱ ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ; edšake̱ Iudabii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ fá tšṍ hãame̱, hewo̱ le̱ Simeonbii le̱ ná ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱nõ le̱ teṅ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱ dši Zebulonbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ awewekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱ dši Isakarbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anä.

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: ke̱ Ebron ke̱ Rehob ke̱ Hamon ke̱ Kana ke̱-yaši Zidon wulu le̱ he.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ ke̱ ame̱he akrowai le̱ dši Naftalibii le̱ akutšo le̱ gbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā.

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Ene̱mei dši gbe̱fãṅnii ni oso̱fo *Eleazar ke̱ Iošua, Nun bi le̱, ke̱ Israelbii le̱ akutšei ano̱ lume̱i le̱ dša mli ye̱ ošiki nā ye̱ †Šilo, ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ye̱ kpẽ-bū le̱ šĩnā le̱ nā le̱. Ni ame̱gbe šikpoṅ le̱ dšā nā. *

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Ene̱mei dši mãdši ni ahala ahã Israelbii le̱ fẽ ke̱ gbo̱ ní aabatoame̱ le̱, koni mofẽmo ní nine aakpa ye̱ moko no̱ le̱ adšo foi ke̱-ya dše̱i, ní lá he oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ akagbele̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni eeyadamo̱ asafo le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ Iošua wie ekē̱:

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: Kē̱mo̱ Israelbii le̱ ake̱: Nyehalaā ahobã-mãdši nyetoa, tamo̱ bo̱ni mitšṍ *Mose no̱ mike̱nye wie le̱, *

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Ši ehĩ ši ye̱ nakai mã le̱ṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni eeyadamo̱ asafo le̱ hĩe ní aako-dšole̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni nakai be le̱ mli oso̱fonukpa le̱ aagbo; no se̱ dãni gbomogbelo̱ le̱ akũ ese̱ ke̱-ya le̱dientše emaṅ ke̱ le̱dientše ewe ye̱ maṅ beni edšo foi ke̱-dše̱ le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱dšō̱ *Kedeš ye̱ Galilea ye̱ Naftali gõdši le̱ ano̱ ke̱ Šekem ye̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ ke̱ †Kiriat-Arba ní dši Hebron ní yo̱ Iuda gõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱ no̱ ame̱hã. *

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ni Iordan se̱ ye̱ Ieriko ṅe̱le̱no̱ ke̱-yaä bokãgbe̱ le̱ ame̱hala Bezer ye̱ šikpoṅ tre̱nē̱ le̱ no̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ke̱-dše̱ Ruben akutšo le̱ mli, ke̱ Ramot ní yo̱ Gilead le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Gad akutšo le̱ mli, ke̱ Golan ni yo̱ Bašan le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Manase akutšo le̱ mli.

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnii le̱ amli mãdši ke̱ ame̱he šikpõdši ni ame̱ṅo-hã Levibii le̱ ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā ne̱: (

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Ni ošiki le̱ kpe̱ hã Kahatbii le̱ awekui le̱; ni oso̱fo Aaron bii le̱ ní dše̱ Levibii le̱ ateṅ le̱ ná mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ ye̱ ošikifõ nā ye̱ Iuda akutšo le̱ ke̱ Simeon akutšo le̱ ke̱ Benyamin akutšo le̱ mli.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Mãdši fẽ ní Aaronbii ní dši oso̱foi le̱ ná dši mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ ke̱ ame̱he šikpõdši.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Geršonbii le̱ amãdši fẽ ní ame̱ná ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ anā dši mãdši nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ ke̱ ame̱he šikpõdši.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ amli maṅ-fẽ-maṅ ye̱ ehe šikpõdši ní bo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe; nakai mãdši ne̱ fẽ yo̱.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ ní *ekã he kitã ake̱ eeṅõ-hã ame̱tše̱mei le̱ hã Israel, ni ame̱ṅõ ni ame̱hĩ no̱. *

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hãame̱ hedšē̱mo̱ ke̱-kpe, take̱ bo̱ni ekã ame̱tše̱mei le̱ akitã le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱; ni ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ ateṅ mokomoko nyẽẽ ame̱hĩe adamo̱; ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ le̱, Iehowa tuame̱ ewo ame̱deṅ.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: *Nibii kpakpai fẽ ní Iehowa wo Israel we le̱ ši ye̱ he le̱, emli ekomeflo ekaa ši; fẽ kwa ba mli. *

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ nu ake̱: Na, Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Manase akutšo le̱ fã le̱ emã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iordan niiaṅ ye̱ Israelbii le̱ anõ le̱ mli.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Ni ame̱te Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Manase akutšo le̱ fã le̱ ṅõ ye̱ Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ yawie ame̱kē̱:

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Ani Peor *no̱tõmo̱ le̱, ni wo̱náko we̱tšū wo̱he ke̱-dše̱ mli ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, tše̱bele̱ Iehowa asafo le̱ na amanehũlũ ye̱ he le̱, fáá hããwo̱? *

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Hewo̱ ni nyekpaleo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa se̱; ni aaba mli ake̱, ké̱ nyetše Iehowa hĩe atũa ṅme̱ne̱ le̱, wó̱ le̱ emli aafũ awo Israel asafo mū le̱ fẽ!

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ nyesusuo̱ ake̱ šikpoṅ ní aṅõ-hãnye le̱ he tšee le̱, no le̱ nyefoa mli ke̱-baä Iehowa gbe̱fãṅ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, heni Iehowa sihĩle̱he le̱ yo̱ le̱, ni nyena nye-gbe̱fãṅnii ye̱ wo̱teṅ; ši nyekatšea Iehowa hĩe atũa, ni nyekatšea wo̱ hũ wo̱hĩe atũa, ní nyemã nyedientše̱ nyefo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ se̱!

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Nto Zera bi *Akan le̱ yato ye̱ musunii le̱ agbe̱fãṅ le̱, ni mlifũ bakã Israel asafo mū le̱ fẽ no̱, ni dšee ekome ke̱ke̱ ehĩe kpãtã ye̱ etomo̱ le̱ hewo̱? Yi.

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: Nānyoṅmo̱ Mawu Iehowa, Nānyoṅmo̱ Mawu Iehowa, le̱ dši moni le, ni Israel hũ aale: ke̱dši atũatšemo̱ mli, alo Iehowa no̱tõmo̱ mli wo̱fe ye̱ le̱, kãhere wo̱yiwala ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ké̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ wo̱mã wo̱hã wo̱-he, koni wo̱fõ Iehowa se̱ nyiemo̱ dšio, alo koni wo̱šã šã-afole lo niyenii-afo̱le ye̱ no̱, alo wo̱šã šidā-afo̱lei ye̱ no̱ dšio, no le̱ Iehowa dientše̱ abi ši!

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ ni wo̱kē̱ ake̱: Nyehãa wo̱sā wo̱he ní wo̱mã afo̱lešãlate̱ ko; dšee ake̱ wo̱bašã šã-afo̱le lo gbē-afo̱le ye̱ no̱,

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Ni Pinehas, oso̱fo Eleazar bi le̱, kē̱ Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ ke̱ Manasebii le̱ ake̱: Nme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ wo̱ná wo̱le ake̱ Iehowa ye̱ we̱teṅ, edšake̱ noni nyefe ne̱ nyeke̱-tõko Iehowa no̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ nyedšie Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Iehowa deṅ!

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Pinehas, oso̱fo Eleazar bi le̱, ke̱ lume̱i le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba Israelbii le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱bagbaame̱ sane le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Ni sane le̱ ṅõ Israelbii le̱ anā, ni Israelbii le̱ dšie Nyoṅmo̱ yi, ní ame̱kē̱ē̱ doṅṅ ake̱ ame̱mīfã ní ame̱ke̱ame̱ ayawu ní ame̱fite šikpoṅ le̱ ní Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ yo̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ni Rubenbii le̱ ke̱ Gadbii le̱ wo afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Ed, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Edši odase ye̱ wo̱teṅ ake̱ Iehowa dši Nyoṅmo̱!

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyefĩa ši dšogbäṅ, ní nyeye nii fẽ ní aṅmã ye̱ Mose mlawolo le̱ mli le̱ no̱ ni nyefe, ni *nyekagba ke̱-mīdše̱ he ke̱-mĩya ninedšũrõ lo abe̱ku, *

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa eſie mãdši wudši ní he wa ke̱-dše̱ nyehĩe; ši nye le̱, mokomoko damo̱ko nyehĩe ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Nyeteṅ mokome aaſie mei akpe; edšake̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, le̱ ewuo̱ ehãanye, take̱ bo̱ni ewonye ši le̱.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyelea nyehe no̱kwe̱mo̱, koni nyesumo̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱!

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: no le̱ nyenáa nyelea ake̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, eſieṅ ne̱ke̱ dšeṅmãdši ne̱ ke̱-dše̱ṅ nyehĩe doṅṅ, ši ame̱atšṍmo̱ *yā ke̱ tšõne ame̱bãnye, ke̱ kplebii ye̱ nyeṅmãwuiaṅ, ke̱ ṅmeii ye̱ nyehĩṅme̱iiaṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni nyehĩe aakpãtã ke̱-adše̱ šikpoṅ kpakpa ni Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, eṅõ-hãnye ne̱ no̱. *

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: Ši na, ṅme̱ne̱ mi le̱ mīya *dšeṅdšeṅ fẽ yahe le̱; ni nyele ye̱ nyetšui mli fẽ ke̱ nyesusuma mli ſẽ ake̱ †nibii kpakpai fẽ ni Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, wie ye̱ nyehewo̱ le̱, emli ekomeflo ekaa ši, fẽ eba mli ehãnye, emli ekomeflo ekaa ši. *

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Ni mike̱nye ba Amorbii ní yo̱ Iordan se̱ le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱ke̱nye wu, ni miṅõame̱ miwo nyedeṅ, ni nyeṅõ ame̱šikpoṅ le̱, ni mikpãtã ame̱hĩe ye̱ nyehĩe.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ni mitšũ *sosomo̱tii ke̱-tšṍ nyehĩe, ni ame̱ſieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ nyehĩe, Amorbii amaṅtše̱mei enyo̱ le̱, dšee oklante nā, ni dšee ogãi nā hũ ni. *

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyešea Iehowa gbeyei, ni nyedšie nyeyitšoṅ nyesúmo̱le̱ ye̱ ano̱kwale mli, ni nyekwa nyoṅmo̱i ni nyetše̱mei le̱ súmo̱ ye̱ fā le̱ se̱ ke̱ Mizraim le̱, ni nyesúmo̱a Iehowa. K.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši esaa nyehĩe ake̱ nyeasúmo̱ Iehowa le̱, no le̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbī ne̱ *nyekoa moni nyeasúmo̱, ke̱dši nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ni yo̱ fã le̱ se̱ ní nyetše̱mei le̱ súmo̱ le̱ dšio, lo Amorbii ní nyeyo̱ ame̱šikpoṅ no̱ ne̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ dšio; ši mi le̱, mike̱ miwe le̱, wo̱o̱súmo Iehowa! *Mat.

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ to he ni ame̱kē̱: Ene̱ akagbalewo fō̃ṅfõ ake̱ wo̱o̱šï Iehowa, ni wo̱yasúme̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa, wo-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, le̱ dši moni dšiewo̱ ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-dše̱ nyṍdši awe le̱, ke̱ moni fe nakai okadii wudši le̱ ye̱ wo̱hĩe, ni ebā wo̱yi ye̱ gbè̱i ní wo̱nyie no̱ le̱ fẽ no̱ ke̱ mãdši fẽ ni wo̱tšṍ ame̱teṅ ke̱-ho le̱ mli.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ſie mãdši le̱ fẽ ke̱ Amorbii ní yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ wo̱hĩe. Nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱ hũ wo̱o̱súmo̱ Iehowa; edšake̱ le̱ dši wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱!

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši nyekwa Iehowa ni nyeya-súmo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei le̱, no le̱ eekũ ese̱ efenye efõṅ ni eetã nyeyi, beni efenye edšũrõ se̱ le̱.

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ kē̱ Iošua ake̱: Dabi, ši Iehowa kẽ wo̱o̱súmo̱!

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ kē̱ Iošua ake̱: Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, wo̱o̱súmo̱, ni le̱ egbe toi wo̱o̱bo!

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Ni Iošua ṅmã ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ fẽ ewo Nyoṅmo̱ mlawolo le̱ mli; ni ewó te̱ kpeteṅkple ko emã dše̱i, ye̱ *tšo kple le̱ ni mã Iehowa hekroṅkroṅ le̱ šiši. *

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iošua wo maṅ le̱ gbe̱, ni mofẽmo te ešikpoṅ no̱.

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ ase̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ Iehowa tšũlo̱ Iošua, Nun bi le̱, gbo, beni eye afii oha ke̱ nyoṅma le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ le̱dientše̱ ešikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ye̱ *Timnat-Sera ní yo̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱, ye̱ Gaaš goṅ le̱ kōyigbe̱ le̱. *

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni Israel *súmo̱ Iehowa gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iošua yo̱ le̱ ke̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ni onukpai ní hĩ ši ye̱ Iošua gbẽle se̱ ni ame̱le Iehowa nitšumoi fẽ ní etšu ehã Israel le̱ yo̱ le̱. *Kodš.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Ni *Iosef wui le̱ ní Israelbii le̱ ṅo ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim le̱, ame̱fũ ye̱ Šekem ye̱ šikpoṅ kuku ni †Iakob he ye̱ Šekem tše̱ Hamor bii le̱ adeṅ ehã dſie̱te̱i kukudši oha le no̱, ni etšṍ Iosefbii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnõ. *

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron bi Eleazar hũ gbo, ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ ebi Pinehas maṅ Gibea ní aṅõ-hãle̱ ye̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱ mli.

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda kē̱ enyemi Simeon ake̱: Oke̱mi afã ke̱-ya migbe̱fãṅnõ le̱ no̱, ní wo̱ke̱ Kanaanbii le̱ ayawu, ni mi hũ mike̱o aate onõ le̱ no̱! Ni Simeon ke̱-le̱ te.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Ni Iudabii le̱ ke̱ Ierusalem bawu, ni ame̱ṅõle̱, ni ame̱ke̱ klante gbegbē emli bii le̱, ni ame̱mã maṅ le̱ nā la.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: No se̱ le̱ Iudabii le̱ fã ni ame̱ke̱ Kanaanbii ní yo̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱ ke̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ ṅãno̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ yawu Ios.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ni *ame̱ṅõ Hebron ame̱hã Kaleb, take̱ bo̱ni Mose kē̱ le̱, ni eſie Anak bihĩĩ etẽ le̱ ke̱-dše dše̱i. *Ios.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Ši Iebusbii ní yo̱ Ierusalem le̱, Benyaminbii le̱ eſieeame̱; ni Iebusbii le̱ ke̱ Benyaminbii le̱ hĩ Ierusalem ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. Ios.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Ni sralo̱i le̱ na nū ko ní dše̱ mã le̱ṅ, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Tšõmo̱wo̱ heni wo̱o̱tšṍ wo̱bote mã le̱ṅ, ni wo̱o̱feo edšũrõ!

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ yiṅ ete Hitbii ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni eyato maṅ, ni etšé̱ egbe̱i ake̱ Luz; no dši egbe̱i ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Ni Efraim eſiee Kanaanbii ní yo̱ Gezer le̱; ni Kanaanbii le̱ hĩ ame̱teṅ ye̱ Gezer. Ios.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naftali eſiee Bet-Šemešbii le̱ ke̱ Bet-Anatbii le̱, ši ebahĩ Kanaanbii ni yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ateṅ, *ni Bet-Šemešbii le̱ ke̱ Bet-Anatbii le̱ súmo̱ame̱. *Ios.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Ni Amorbii le̱ tši Danbii le̱ ke̱-te gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ame̱bãã ame̱kpleke ši ke̱-ba dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Ni Amorbii le̱ ná hegbe̱ hĩ Heres goṅ le̱ no̱, ye̱ *Ayalon ke̱ Šaalbim; ši beni Iosef we le̱ nine bó ame̱no̱ le̱, ame̱-súmo̱ame̱. *Ios.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Ni Amorbii le̱ ahũsũ le̱ dše̱ Akrabim ṅmeṅme le̱ he ke̱-dše̱ Sela ke̱-te yiteṅgbe̱.

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ le̱dientše̱ ešikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Timnat-Heres ye̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ ye̱ Gaaš goṅ le̱ kōyigbe̱. Ios.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Ni abua nakai yino̱bii le̱ hũ fẽ nā afata ame̱tše̱mei le̱ ahe; ni yino̱ kroko bate ši ye̱ ame̱se̱, mei ní lee Iehowa alo enitšumo̱i ní etšu eha Israel le̱.

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Hefẽhe ní ame̱afã ta ke̱-ate le̱, Iehowa nine kã ame̱no̱ wā, take̱ bo̱ni *Iehowa ewie le̱ ke̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ekãame̱ kitã le̱, ni efĩame̱ naakpa. *

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱kodšolo̱i le̱ hũ ame̱booame̱ toi, ši moṅ ame̱yabo̱ō̱ adſamaṅ ke̱-nyieo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei ase̱, ni ame̱dšáa-ame̱; etše̱e̱ ke̱ke̱ le̱ ame̱dše gbe̱ ní ame̱tše̱mei le̱ nyie no̱ ní ame̱bo Iehowa kitãi le̱ atoi le̱ no̱; ame̱ le̱ ame̱boo toi.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši Iehowa tē kodšolo̱i aši ehãame̱ le̱, no le̱ Iehowa fataä kodšolo̱ le̱ he, ni ehereo̱ ame̱yiwala ke̱-dše̱o̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ ní kodšolo̱ le̱ yo̱ le̱; edšake̱ ame̱ntšo̱ĩ ní ame̱dõmoo̱ ye̱ ame̱yiwalo̱i ke̱ ame̱haolo̱i le̱ ahewo̱ le̱ do̱ö̱ Iehowa.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, ké̱ kodšolo̱ le̱ gbo le̱, ame̱kũo̱ ame̱se̱ ekoṅ ni ame̱fiteo̱ fè ame̱tše̱mei le̱, ye̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei ase̱ ní ame̱yanyieo̱ ní ame̱súmoo̱ame̱ ní ame̱dšáa-ame̱ le̱ hewo̱; ame̱fõõ ame̱nifemo̱i le̱ ke̱ ame̱kue̱ṅtimo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱nyiemo̱.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ Iehowa mli woo̱ la woo̱ Israel, ni ekē̱o̱ ake̱: Ake̱ noni ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ etõ mikpãṅmo̱ le̱ ní miwo ame̱tše̱mei akitã ye̱ he le̱ no̱, ni ame̱boo migbē toi,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: hewo̱ le̱ mi hũ ke̱-dše̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ke̱-yaã ne̱ miſieṅ dšeṅmãdši ní ſe̱ beni Iošua gbo le̱ eko ye̱ ame̱hĩe doṅṅ,

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: koni mike̱ame̱ *aka Israel akwe̱ ake̱ ame̱dſẽṅ Iehowa gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ní ame̱nyie no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni ame̱tše̱mei le̱ dſẽṅ no̱ le̱, alo ame̱feṅ nakai. *

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ ni Iehowa ši nakai dšeṅmãdši le̱, ni eſieeame̱ mrã, ni asaṅ eṅõ̱õ-ame̱ ewoo Iošua deṅ hũ le̱.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: beni afe ke̱ke̱ ní Israelbii le̱ asešibii le̱ ale ni ake̱-tšõame̱ tawū, titri le̱ ame̱teṅ mei ní lee he eko sá le̱:

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ni ašĩame̱, beni afe ni ake̱ame̱ aka Israel akwe̱, ní aṅõ-le ake̱ ame̱abo Iehowa kitãi ní etšṍ Mose no̱ ewo ame̱tše̱mei le̱ atoi lo.

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni ame̱hĩe kpa Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱, ni ame̱yasúmo̱ Baalim ke̱ Ašerot.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Iehowa mli wo Israel la, ni ehõame̱ ehã Mesopotamia maṅtše̱ Kušan-Rišataim; ni Israelbii le̱ súmo̱ Kušan-Rišataim afii kpānyo̱.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ blo̱ tšé̱ Iehowa, ni Iehowa tē yiwalaherelo̱ ko ši ehãame̱, ni ehere ame̱yiwala, le̱ dši *Otniel, Kaleb nyemi gbekẽ Kenaz bi le̱. *

english_verse: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšo̱ afii nyoṅmai-edſe̱. Ni Otniel, Kenaz bi le̱, gbo.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fe efõṅ ekoṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ni Iehowa hã Moab maṅtše̱ Eglon le̱ ná Israel no̱ hewale̱, edšake̱ ame̱fe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Ni ebua Amonbii le̱ ke̱ Amalekbii le̱ anā eši eno̱, ni eba ebatſia Israel nii, ni eṅõ *tẽṅi amaṅ le̱. *

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni eke̱ nikēnii le̱ ehãle̱ egbe nā le̱, ewo mei ní tēre nikēnii le̱ agbe̱ ni ame̱te.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ehud kpã enine abe̱ku le̱ mli, ni efã klante le̱ ye̱ eninedšũrõgbe̱ le̱, ni eke̱-dũ emũsũṅ,

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Ni Ehud tšṍ asa le̱ no̱ ke̱-dše kpo, ni eṅã́mo̱ šĩnāi le̱ ewo eyi ni eṅmẽ mli.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Ni beni edše kpo ete le̱, tšũdši le̱ ba ame̱bakwe̱, ni na, aṅã́mo̱ šĩnāi le̱ ni aṅmẽ mli; ni ame̱kē̱: Bene̱ ēwá enane ye̱ kō̱yo̱heremo̱ tšũ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱mẽ āhũ ke̱-yaši beyine̱ ni ame̱hĩe gboi, ni na, egblee ṅwei-tšũ le̱ šĩnāi le̱; ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱yako̱ samfē ni ame̱bagble, ni na, ame̱nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kã šikpoṅ ni egbo.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱lilaä ši le̱, Ehud edšo foi ke̱-te momo, ni efoṅ ye̱ amãgãi le̱ ahe, ni edšo foi ke̱-te Seira.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyešaä foi ke̱-nyĩea mise̱; edšake̱ Iehowa eṅõ nyehenye̱lo̱i ní dši Moabbii le̱ ewo nyedeṅ. Ni ame̱kple-ke ši ke̱-nyie ese̱, ni ame̱he Iordan fõhei le̱ ní ake̱-yaä Moab le̱, ni ame̱ṅmẽẽ mokomoko gbe̱ ni efo.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Ni aba Moab ši ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ awo Israel nine šiši. Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšo̱ afii nyoṅmai-kpānyo̱.

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ni Šamgar, Anat bi le̱, baye ese̱, ni eke̱ tšina kplamo̱tšo gbe Filistibii le̱ ateṅ mei ohai-ekpa. Ni le̱ hũ ehere Israel yiwala.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hõame̱ ehã Iabin, Kanaan maṅtše̱ le̱, ní yeo̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Hazor le̱. Ni etatše̱ dši Sisera, ní yo̱ Harošet-Goyim le̱.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Damo̱ bū le̱ šĩnā le̱ ši, ni aba mli ake̱, ke̱dši moko ba ni ebio ake̱: Ani moko ye̱ bie̱ lo? le̱, koni okē̱ ake̱: Dabi!

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Ni ehī Debora tẽṅ le̱ šiši ye̱ Rama ke̱ Betel teṅ, ye̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱. Ni Israelbii le̱ baä eṅõ ní ekodšoo̱ame̱.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Ni etšū ayakpē Barak, Abinoam bi le̱, ke̱-dše̱ Kedeš-Naftali ke̱-ba, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani dšee fã́ ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, efã́o ake̱: Yafã ta ke̱-ya Tabor goṅ le̱ ne̱, ni oṅõ Naftalibii le̱ ke̱ Zebulonbii le̱ ateṅ hĩĩ akpei-nyoṅma ofata ohe?

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Ni makpla Sisera, Iabin tatše̱ le̱, ke̱ eſīlii le̱ ke̱ emei babaō le̱ ke̱-ba oṅõ ye̱ Kišon fā le̱ nā, ni maṅõle̱ mawo odeṅ.

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mike̱o aate; ši kẽle̱ gbe̱ ni oyaä ne̱ mli anumnyam le̱ efeṅ onõ; edšake̱ yō ko deṅ Iehowa baṅõ Sisera awo! Ni Debora te ši, ni eke̱ Barak te Kedeš.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Ši Heber, *Kennyo le̱, etše ehe ke̱-dše̱ Kainbii ni dši Mose šānū †Hobab bii le̱ ahe, ni ehĩe ebū le̱ ši āhũ ke̱-yaši tšo kple ní mã Zaananim ni yo̱ Kedeš mase̱i le̱ he. *

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ayatſa Sisera adafi ake̱ Barak, Abinoam bi le̱, efã ta ke̱-te Tabor goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Debora kē̱ Barak ake̱: Te ši, edšake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ Iehowa eṅõ Sisera ewo odeṅ! Ani dšee Iehowa efã ke̱-nyie ohĩe ne̱? Ke̱ke̱ ni Barak kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ Tabor goṅ le̱ no̱, ni mei akpei-nyoṅma le̱ nyie ese̱.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa hã Sisera ke̱ eſīlii le̱ fẽ ke̱ eta mū le̱ ſẽ dšidšā ye̱ klante nā ye̱ Barak hĩe, ni Sisera yi ši ke̱-dše̱ eſīli le̱ mli ni edšo foi ye̱ enane nā.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Ni Barak tiu ſīlii le̱ ke̱ ta le̱ ke̱-yaši Harošet-Goyim, ni Sisera ta le̱ fẽ nyõnyõ ye̱ klante nā, ni eſe̱e̱ mokomeflo.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Ši Sisera dšo foi ye̱ enane nā ke̱-te Iael, Kennyo Heber ṅã le̱ bū le̱ṅ. Edšake̱ hedšo̱le̱ ye̱ Iabin, Hazor maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ Heber, Kennyo le̱, we le̱ teṅ.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ni Iael dše kpo eke̱ Sisera yakpe, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱, ba, ba miṅõ; kāše gbeyei! Ni egbá ke̱-te eṅõ ye̱ bū le̱ṅ, ni eke̱ sāno̱ bò ko ha eno̱.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, hāmi nu fiō manu, edšake̱ kũmai mīyemi! Ni egble fufo̱nõ le̱ nā, ni ehãle̱ eko enu; ni eha eno̱.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iael, Heber ṅã le̱, fã bū le̱ he šiṅmlitšo le̱ eko, ni eko̱ hamle ehĩe edeṅ, ni ede̱ke ši ke̱-te eṅõ, ni eke̱ šiṅmlitšo le̱ yaka etoi ši, ni eyamõ šikpoṅ; edšake̱ ewo̱ vī, ni nõ nyõ eno̱, ni egbo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Ni na, beni Barak tiuo̱ Sisera le̱, Iael dše kpo eke̱le̱ yakpe, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ba, ni matšõo nū le̱ ní otaoo̱ le̱! Ni ete eṅõ; ni na, Sisera kã ši ní egbo, ni šiṅmlitšo le̱ tše̱ke̱ etoi ši.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ba Kanaan maṅtše̱ Iabin ši ye̱ Israelbii le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ enine hĩe Iabin, Kanaan maṅtše̱ le̱, no̱tšṍmo̱ ãhũ, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ame̱kpãtã Iabin, Kanaan maṅtše̱ le̱, hĩe.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Gõdši le̱ kpokpo ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ke̱ nakai Sinai le̱ hũ, ye̱ Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, hĩe. Lal.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Ye̱ Šamgar, Anat bi le̱, yino̱ ke̱ Iael yino̱ le̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱i le̱ ano̱ kãmo̱ eflo, ni gbe̱nyielo̱i le̱ dšuo̱ ši nyieo̱. *

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Asafoiatše̱mei ahe sẽ ye̱ Israel, ame̱he sẽ, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní mi, Debora, mite ši, ní mite ši ake̱ nye ye̱ Israel.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Miná Israel no̱yelo̱i le̱ ahe tšui; mei ní here ame̱he ye̱ suomo̱ nā ye̱ maṅ-bii le̱ ateṅ le̱, nyedšiea Iehowa yi!

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni abladei le̱ ke̱ maṅbii le̱ ateṅ mei ní eſe̱ le̱ kpleke ši, ni Iehowa kpleke ye̱ kãkãlo̱i le̱ ateṅ ye̱ mihewo̱.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Mẽba otá otōiatšũi le̱ ateṅ, ní oboo̱ be̱dši ni akpāa ake̱-tšé̱o̱ tōi le̱ atoi? Ruben nsutẽṅi le̱ anā le̱, ate adšinai ní he dšra ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead tá ši ye̱ Iordan se̱. Ni Dan hũ, mẽba elilaä Si ye̱ le̱dši amli? Ašer esẽ koni ke̱-tá ṅšo̱ nā, etá eṅšo̱-blei le̱ anā.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Zebulon dši maṅ ní še̱ ehe efõ ehã gbĕle, ke̱ Naftali hũ ye̱ ṅãno̱ goṅkpo̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Adše̱ ṅwei awu ta le̱, ṅulamii tete dše ame̱gbe̱hei ni ame̱ke̱ Sisera wu!

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kišon fā le̱ lōame̱ ke̱-te, blema fā le̱, Kišon fā le̱. Misusuma, fã nyiemo̱ ke̱ hewale̱.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: No mli le̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i le̱ ananekoklotoi le̱ šimo̱ ši ye̱ foidšē mli, ame̱hewalo̱i le̱ afoidšē mli.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱: Nyelomo̱a Meroz, nyelomo̱a emli bii le̱ kre̱dē̱! Edšake̱ ame̱bafataa Iehowa he, ame̱bafataa Iehowa he ye̱ kãkãlo̱i le̱ ateṅ!

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Aadšō̱ Iael ye̱ yei ateṅ, Heber, Kennyo le̱, ṅã le̱, aadšō̱le̱ fè yei ni yo̱ būi amli le̱ fẽ!

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Ebi nu, ni ehãle̱ fufo̱, tšene fe̱fe̱o mli eke̱ fufo̱-hĩe-fo̱ wó ebahãle̱.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ekpã enine mli eko̱ šiṅmlitšo le̱, ni eke̱ eninedšũrõ ko̱ nitšulo̱i ahamle le̱, ni eke̱ hamle le̱ tſa Sisera, edſa eyitšo, eke̱-gbule̱, ni eke̱-ka etoi ši.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sisera nye mīkwe̱ samfle̱ mli, ni ebo lelēle ye̱ samfle̱ ke̱ emli fo̱dši le̱ anā: Mẽhewo̱ ni eſīli le̱ bā le̱ etše̱ ne̱? Mẽhewo̱ ni eſīlii anãdši le̱ ekpe se̱ ne̱?

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Ehewo̱ yei le̱ ateṅ nilelo̱i le̱ to he hãle̱, ni le̱dientše̱ hũ eto he ehã ehe ake̱:

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: Ame̱ná hānii kẽ, ni ame̱mīdša; nū-fẽ-nū aaná oblayō kome lo enyo̱ tete, Sisera hũ he̱ aaná asāsā hānii, asāsā hānii ní alò mli, asāsā hānii kome lo enyo̱ ní alò mli ní ake̱-baha kue̱.

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
