translation_verse: Bo̱ noṅṅ ní ohenye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ ahĩe aakpãtã ne̱, Iehowa! Ši mei ní sumoo̱o le̱ aafe tamo̱ hũlũ beni eteo̱ ši yo̱ ehewale̱ mli le̱! Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšo̱ *afii nyoṅmai-edſo̱. *

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Israelbii le̱ blo̱ tšé̱ Iehowa ye̱ Midianbii le̱ ahewo̱ le̱,

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kwe̱ ehĩe ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: *Oke̱ ohewale̱ ne̱ aya, ní ohere Israel yiwala ye̱ Midianbii le̱ adeṅ! Ani dšee mi mĩtšũo? *

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱le̱ ake̱: *Mibafata ohe āhũ, ni oogbe Midianbii le̱ tamo̱ agbeo̱ mokome! *

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱, ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe le̱, no le̱ tšõmo̱mi okadi ko ake̱ bo oke̱mi wieo̱ ne̱!

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ni Gideon te ni eyasā tōabotiabi, ni eke̱ mã efa kome fe akpĩtĩ; lō le̱ eṅõ-wo kafũ mli, ni ehe-nu le̱ eṅõ-wo kukwe̱i mli, ni eke̱-dše kpo ke̱-ba eṅõ ye̱ tšo le̱ šiši, ni eke̱-bamã ehĩe.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ bo̱fo le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ lō le̱ ke̱ akpĩtĩ le̱ oſie te̱sā ne̱ no̱, ni ofo̱se ehe-nu le̱ oſie no̱! Ni efe nakai.

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Gideon mã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ dše̱i ehã Iehowa, ni etšē̱le̱ ake̱: Iehowa Šalom. Eye̱ Ofra ní dši Abiezerbii le̱ anõ le̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Ni omã afo̱lešãlate̱ ohã Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ye̱ ne̱ke̱ te̱sã ne̱ yiteṅ ni otole̱ hĩṅme̱i no̱; ni oṅõ tšinanū ní dši enyo̱ le ošã šã-afo̱le ni oke̱ akrabatša ní oflo̱ le̱ lai le̱ ašã.

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Gideon ṅõ etšũdši le̱ ateṅ mei nyoṅma, ni efe bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱le̱ le̱. Ši eba mli ake̱-ní ešeo̱ etše̱ we le̱ ke̱ maṅbii le̱ agbeyei hewo̱ le̱, enyẽẽ efe ſane, ši nyõṅ efe.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅbii le̱ te ši lebi mãṅkpa le̱, na, akũmo̱ Baal afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱, ni aflo̱ ehe akrabatša le̱, ni ašã tšinanũ ni dši enyo̱ le̱ ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ ní amã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioaš kē̱ mei fẽ ní ebabo̱le ehe ke̱-kpe le̱ ake̱: Ani nye nyebabé Baal he? Alo nye nyebahere eyiwala? Moni aabé ehe le̱ le̱, hã ní agbele̱ lebi ne̱ noṅṅ. *Ké̱ nyoṅmo̱ dšile̱ le̱, hã le̱dientše̱ ebé ehe ake̱ akũmo̱ efolešãlate̱ le. *

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ ewole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Ierubaal, ekē̱: Hã Baal ke̱le̱ abé, edšake̱ ekũmo̱ efo̱lešãlate̱ le̱.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Ni Midianbii ke̱ Amalekbii ke̱ bokãgbe̱bii le̱ fẽ bua ame̱he nā, ni ame̱fo mli ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Iezreel dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Ni *Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ bayi Gideon no̱, ni ekpã te̱tre̱mantre̱ eke̱-tšē̱ Abiezerbii le̱ ní ame̱banyie ese̱. *

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ni etšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Manase fẽ, ni ayakpẽame̱ hũ ni ame̱banyie ese̱. Ni etšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Ašer ke̱ Zebulon ke̱ Naftali, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱fã ame̱ke̱ame̱ bakpe.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: na, mike̱ tōgwanteṅ wolo baka ṅmā̃-šãhe le̱; ke̱dši bó̱ nyõ wolo le̱ kome ke̱ke̱ no̱ ni šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ gbĩ le̱, no le̱ maná male ake̱ minine no̱ obatšṍ ohere Israelbii le̱ ayiwala, take̱ bo̱ni okē̱ le̱.

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli nakai; ni beni dše tše̱re no̱ le̱, ete ši lebi mrã, ni eṅã tō wolo le̱ mli, ni bó̱ ní eṅã ye̱ tō wolo le̱ mli le̱ fe tšene obõ.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Ni Gideon kē̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ake̱: *Omli akafũmi ní mawie šikome ne̱ pe̱! mī-kpao fai, hã mike̱ wolo le̱ aka makwe̱ šikome hũ: hã ní wolo le̱ ke̱ke̱ agbĩ, ni bó̱ anyõ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ! *

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ hã ba mli nakai ye̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ, ni wolo le̱ ke̱ke̱ gbī, ši bó̱ nyō šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Gideon ake̱: Maṅ ni fata ohe le̱ fá tšṍ, bo̱ni maṅõ Midian mawo ame̱deṅ, koni Israel akabaſã etšõ-mi ake̱: Midientše̱ minine mike̱-here miyiwala!

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši ōše gbeyei ake̱ ookpleke ši le̱, oke̱ otšũlo̱ Pura akpleke ši ke̱-ya nsra le̱ṅ,

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ maṅ le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-te nu le̱ he. Ni Iehowa kē̱ Gideon ake̱: Mofẽmo ní ke̱ elile̱i aale̱mo̱ nu le̱ tamo̱ gbé le̱moo̱ le̱, oke̱le̱ adamo̱ afã; ši nakai noṅṅ ofe mofẽmo n í aakũla enakutšeĩ anā ni eenu le̱.

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Ni mei fẽ ni ke̱ ame̱nine to ame̱nā ní ame̱le̱mo̱ le̱ ayibo̱ dši mei ohai-etẽ, ši maṅ le̱ ní ſe̱ le̱ fẽ kũla ame̱nakutšei anā nu nu le̱.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Gideon ake̱: *Hĩĩ ohai-etẽ ní le̱mo̱ nu le̱ mike̱-ahere nyeyiwala, ni maṅõ Midian mawo odeṅ; ši maṅ le̱ fẽ aya, mofẽmo aya edšē̱he. *

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: ní oyabo nii ní ame̱wieo̱ le̱ toi, ni no se̱ dãni ohe aawao ke̱-kpleke ši ke̱-ya nsra le̱ṅ. Ke̱ke̱ ni eke̱ etšũlo̱ Pura kpleke ši ke̱-te tabilo̱i ní yo̱ nsra le̱ṅ le̱ amase̱i kpākpa.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Ši Midianbii ke̱ Amalekbii ke̱ bo-kãgbe̱bii le̱ fẽ bua dšō̱ le̱ṅ babaō tamo̱ bālabii, ni ame̱yomai le̱ alee ame̱yibo̱, ame̱yi fále̱ tamo̱ ṅšo̱ nā šia.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Gideon še̱ dše̱i le̱, na, moko *mīgba enanyo ko lamõ ní ela ake̱: Na, mila lamõ ko, ni abolo akwābo̱ ko koklo ke̱-ba Midianbii le̱ ansra le̱ṅ, ke̱-banina bū ko, ni ešile̱, ni etši egbē ši, ni ebutule̱ kwrā eſie ši. *

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ni enanyo le̱ to he ehãle̱ ake̱: Ene̱ dšee nokonoko ake̱ Ioaš bi Gideon, Israel-nyo le̱, klante le̱ ni. Nyoṅmo̱ eṅõ Midian ke̱ nsra le̱ ſẽ ewo edeṅ!

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Gideon nu lamõ le̱ ní agba le̱ ke̱ ešišitšõmo̱ le̱, ekũla ši eso̱le, ni ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te Israel nsra le̱ṅ ni ekē̱: Nyetea ši, ši Iehowa eṅõ *Midian nsra le̱ ewo nyedeṅ! *Ies.

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Ni ké̱ mike̱ mei fẽ ni fata mihe le̱ kpã te̱tre̱mantre̱ le̱, no le̱ nye hũ nyekpãa te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ ke̱-bolea nsra le̱ fẽ ni nyekē̱a ake̱: Iehowa ke̱ Gideon nõ ne̱!

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Gideon ke̱ hĩĩ oha ní fata ehe le̱ yaše̱ nsra le̱ nāgbē le̱ ye̱ nyōṅteṅ būbe le̱ šišidšē mli, beni ame̱tšake bulo̱i le̱ se̱ pe̱; ni ame̱kpãkpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ ni ame̱dſãradfãrā kpudši ní ame̱hĩe ye̱ ame̱deṅ le̱.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Ni koi etẽ le̱ fẽ kpãkpā̃ te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ ni ame̱dſăradſărā kpudši le̱, ni ame̱hĩe ko̱tii le̱ ye̱ ame̱be̱ku ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ ye̱ ame̱nine dšũrõ, ni ame̱-pã, ni ame̱bo̱ oše ake̱: Iehowa ke̱ Gideon klante!

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Ni mofẽmo damo̱ egbe̱he ke̱-bo̱le nsra le̱ kpũla; ni nsra mū le̱ fẽ bú ni ame̱dšo foi ke̱ blo̱mo̱.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱kpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i ohai-etẽ le̱, Iehowa hã mofẽmo do̱ eklante eto enanyo no̱ ye̱ nsra mū le̱ fẽ mli; ni ta mū le̱ fẽ dšo foi ke̱-yaši Bet-Šita ke̱ Zerera, ke̱-yaši Abel-Mehola fã le̱ nā ye̱ Tabat mase̱i.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ni ayakpē Israel hĩĩ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Naftali ke̱ Ašer ke̱ Manase fẽ, ni ame̱nyie Midian se̱.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Ni Gideon tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ fẽ ayakē̱: Nyekplekea ši nyeke̱ Midian abakpea, ni nyetšĩame̱ nui le̱ anā gbè̱ĩ le̱ ke̱-yaši Bet-Bara ke̱ Iordan nā! Ni ayakpē Efraim hĩĩ le̱ ſẽ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱tšĩame̱ nui le̱ anā gbè̱i le̱ ke̱-yaši Bet-Bara ke̱ Iordan nā.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱mõme̱ Oreb ke̱ Zeeb, Midian lume̱i enyo̱ le̱, ni ame̱gbe Oreb ye̱ Oreb te̱sã le̱ he, ni Zeeb hũ ame̱gbele̱ ye̱ Zeeb weinbu le̱ he; ni amenyie Midian se̱, ni ame̱ke̱ Oreb ke̱ Zeeb yitšei le̱ bahã Gideon ye̱ Iordan se̱.

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Ni Gideon kē̱: Odšogbāṅ, ke̱dši Iehowa ná ṅõ Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna ewo mideṅ le̱, no le̱ maṅõ ṅãno̱ ṅmeii ke̱ aklatii mayi nyegbomotšei!

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Ni efã ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i ke̱-te Penuel, ni eke̱ame̱ wie nakai noṅṅ. Ni Penuel hĩĩ le̱ to he hãle̱ tamo̱ bo̱ni Sukot hĩĩ le̱ to he hãle̱ le̱ noṅṅ.

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Ni ebanina Sukotbii le̱ ni ekē̱: Na, Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna ne̱, mei ahewo̱ ni nyesopami ake̱: Ani onine eše̱ Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna no̱ momo, hewo̱ ni wo̱ṅõo̱ abolo wo̱hãa ohĩĩ ni eto̱ame̱ le̱ lo le̱?

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Ni Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna dšo foi, ni etiuame̱, ni eyamõmo̱ Midian maṅtše̱mei enyo̱ Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna le̱, ni ēgbe̱ ta le̱ fẽ eſã.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Gideon, Ioaš bi le̱, kũ ese̱ ke̱-dše̱ ta le̱ṅ ni etšṍ Heres ṅmeṅme le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Ni emõmo̱ mã le̱ṅ onukpai le̱, ni eke̱ ṅãno̱ ṅmeii ke̱ aklatii yi Sukot hĩĩ le̱ wā.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna ake̱: Hĩĩ le̱ ní nyegbe ye̱ Tabor le̱, té ame̱subãṅ yo̱ tẽṅ? Ni ame̱kē̱: Ame̱tamo̱ bo pe̱, ame̱fẽ ame̱tamo̱ maṅtše̱mei abii.

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Ieter, ekromo̱bi le̱ ake̱: Te ši ní ogbeame̱! Ši oblanyo le̱ gblaa eklante; edšake̱ ēše gbeyei, edšake̱ edako.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Ni Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna kē̱: Bodĩentše̱ te ši ni otſiawo̱ nii; edšake̱ bo̱ni nū yo̱ le̱, nakai ehewale̱ yo̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni Gideon te ši ni egbe Zeba ke̱ Zalmuna, ni edšie nyoṅtšĕre-fãfãi ní yo̱ ame̱yomai le̱ akue̱i le̱.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israelbĩĩ le̱ kē̱ Gideon ake̱: Ye wo̱no̱, bo ke̱ obi ke̱ onãbi fẽ; edšake̱ ohere wo̱yiwala ke̱-dše̱ Midian deṅ!

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Ni Gideon kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Miyeṅ nyeno̱, ni mibi hũ yeṅ nyeno̱, Iehowa aaye nyeno̱!

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Ni Gideon kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mibabinye noko, no dši ake̱ nyeteṅ mofẽmo aṅõ dſinei ní eha le̱ ehãmi! Edšake̱ ake̱-ní Išmaelbii dšiame̱ hewo̱ le̱, ame̱hĩe šika dſinei.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ni ehemo ní yo̱ Šekem le̱, le̱ hũ eke̱le̱ fo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Abimelek.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Ni Gideon, Ioaš bi le̱, gbo̱ dšogbãṅ dãni egbo, ni afūle̱ ye̱ etše̱ Ioaš fū̃he le̱ ye̱ *Ofra ni dši Abiezerbii le̱ anõ le̱. *

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Gideon gbo le̱, Israelbii le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ni ame̱yabo̱ adſamaṅ ke̱-nyie Baalim se̱, ni ame̱ṅõ Baal-Berit ame̱fe ame̱nyoṅmo̱.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ kaii Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni dšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ adeṅ ye̱ hefẽhe le̱.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ *ame̱fee Ierubaal Gideon we le̱ edšũrõ ko, tamo̱ bo̱ni le̱ le̱ efe Israel edšũrõ le̱. *

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni enye nyemimei le̱ kpã ehe wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ wo Šekembii le̱ fẽ atoiiaṅ; ni ame̱yĩṅ tšṍ ke̱-yanyie Abimelek se̱, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Wo̱nyemi ni.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Šekembii le̱ fẽ ke̱ Milo we le̱ fẽ nā bakpe ši, ni ame̱te ame̱yawo Abimelek maṅtše̱ ye̱ kaimo̱ *tšo kpeteṅkple ní mã Šekem mase̱i le̱ šiši. *Ios.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Ni beni ayagba Iotam le̱, eyiṅ ete ni eyadamo̱ Gerizim goṅ le̱ yiteṅ, ni ewó egbē no̱ ni ebo ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeboami toi, nye Šekembii, koni Nyoṅmo̱ hũ abonye toi!

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ni tšei le̱ yakē̱ agbamitšo ake̱: Bo le̱ ba ní obaye we̱no̱ maṅtše̱!

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ni agbamitšo le̱ kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Aso mihã miṅõmo̱ ke̱ miyibii kpakpai le̱ abo̱mi, ni miyase̱ṅ kō̱yo̱ mli ye̱ tšei ano̱ lo?

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ni tšei le̱ yakē̱ weintšo ake̱: Bo le̱ ba obaye wo̱no̱ maṅtše̱!

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ni weintšo le̱ kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Aso mihã midã ní še̱dšeo̱ nyoṅmo̱i ko̱ gbomei amī le̱ abo̱mi, ní miyase̱ṅ kō̱yo̱ mli ye̱ tšei le̱ ano̱ lo?

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni tšei le̱ fẽ yakē̱ *ṅmeitšo ake̱: Bo le̱ ba ní obaye wo̱no̱ maṅtše̱ mo̱! *

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Ni ṅmeĩtšo le̱ kē̱ tšei le̱ ake̱: Ke̱-dši nyefo̱mi mũ nyewomi nyeno̱ maṅtše̱ ano̱kwale mli le̱, no le̱ nyebaä ni nye-babaä abo ye̱ mišiši hō̃ṅ le̱ mli, ši ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, no le̱ la adše̱ ṅmeitšo le̱ mli ni eyašã Lebanon tšenedrui le̱!

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: ni agbene̱ nyete ši nyewo mitše̱ we le̱ ṅme̱ne̱, ni nyegbe ebihĩĩ le̱, mei nyoṅmai-kpawo so̱ṅṅ, ye̱ te̱ kome no̱, ni nyewo Abimelek, eweyō bi le̱, maṅtše̱ ye̱ Šekembii le̱ ano̱, edšake̱ nyenyemi ni,)

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: bĕle̱ ke̱dši ano̱kwale ke̱ dšale̱ sane nyeke̱ Ierubaal ke̱ ewe le̱ ye ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, no le̱ nyenyã́a Abimelek he, ni le̱ hũ enyã́ nyehe!

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Ni Iotam dšo foi, ni egbla ehe ši ke̱-te Beer, ni eyahī dše̱i ye̱ gbeyei ní ešeo̱ enyemi Abimelek hewo̱.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek ye Israel no̱ afii etẽ.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Ni Šekembii le̱ to káwolo̱i ní ame̱yawole̱ ká ye̱ gõdši le̱ ayiteaṅ, ni ame̱ha mei fẽ ni batšṍ ame̱ṅõ ye̱ nakai gbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ anii; ni ayagba Abimelek.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ni Gaal, Ebed bi le̱, ke̱ enyemimei le̱ ba, ni ame̱bafoṅ ke̱-te Šekem; ni Šekembii le̱ ṅõ ame̱hĩe ame̱fõ eno̱.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱dše kpo ke̱-te ame̱ṅmõdši aši, ni ame̱kpa ame̱weintromi le̱ amli yibii, ni ame̱ṅã wein le̱, ni ame̱ye gbĩ-dšũrõ, ni ame̱te ame̱nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱, ni ame̱yeyē nii ni ame̱nunū dā̃i, ni ame̱lomo̱ Abimelek.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Ni Gaal, Ebed bi le̱, kē̱: Namo dši Abimelek, ni namo dši Šekem, ní we̱súmoo̱le̱? Ani dšee Ierubaal bi ni, ni esafoiatše̱ dši Zebul lo? Nyesúmo̱a Šekem tše̱ *Hamor webii le̱ moṅ! Ši mẽhewo̱ wo̱o̱súmo̱ mone̱? *

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Miná ni kũle̱ maṅ ne̱ ye̱ mideṅ, ní makpa Abimelek! Ni makē̱ Abimelek ake̱: Hã ota le̱ yi afá ni odše kpo ke̱-ba!

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Ni beni Zebul, mã le̱ṅ lumo̱ le̱, nu Ebed bi Gaal wiemo̱i le̱, emli wo la,

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbene̱ te ši nyōṅ, bo ke̱ mei ní fata ohe le̱, ni oyawo ká ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱;

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek ke̱ mei ní fata ehe le̱ te ši nyōṅ, ni ame̱gbla ame̱mii kui edſe̱ ame̱wo Šekem he ká.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Ni Gaal, Ebed bi le̱, dše kpo, ni eyadamo̱ maṅ le̱ agbó le̱ nā. Ni Abimelek ke̱ mei ní fata ehe le̱ te ši ke̱-dše̱ káwōhe le̱.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Gaal na mei le̱, ekē̱ Zebul ake̱: Na, gbomei mīdše̱ gõdši le̱ ayiteaṅ mīkpleke ši! Ni Zebul kē̱le̱ ake̱: Gõdši le̱ asusumai onaã tamo̱ gbomei le̱!

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ni Gaal wie ekoṅ ni ekē̱: Na, gbomei mīdše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ laṅmo̱ le̱ no̱ mīkpleke ši ke̱-mība, ni asafoku kome dše̱ Meonenim tšo kple le̱ he gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-mība!

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Ni Zebul kē̱le̱ ake̱: Agbene̱ nẽgbe̱ onābu le̱ ni oke̱-kē̱ ake̱: Namo dši Abimelek ni we̱súmoo̱le̱? le̱ ye̱? Ani dšee maṅ le̱ ni ogbe ame̱he guo̱ le̱ ne̱? Agbe̱ne̱ dše kpo ko ni oke̱ame̱ ayawu!

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ni Gaal dše kpo ke̱-nyie Šekembii le̱ ahĩe, ni eke̱ Abimelek bawu.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek ſiele̱, ni edšo foi, ni mei babaō nyõnyõi āhũ ke̱-yaši maṅ le̱ agbó le̱ nā tō̃.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Ši Abimelek hĩ ši ye̱ Aruma; ni Zebul ſĩe Gaal ke̱ enyemimei le̱ ake̱ ame̱kahĩ Šekem.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni dše tše̱re no̱ le̱, maṅbii le̱ dše kpo te ṅã le̱ no̱; ni ame̱yagba Abimelek.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ mei le̱ ni egbla ame̱mli asafokui etẽ, ni eyawo ká ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱; ni ekwe̱, ni na, maṅ le̱ mīdše kpo ke̱-mīdše̱ mã le̱ṅ, ni ete ši ewoame̱ ni etſia-ame̱ nii.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek ke̱ asafokui ni fata ehe le̱ tšẽ ke̱-te ame̱hĩe, ni ame̱yadamo̱ maṅ le̱ agbó le̱ nā, ni asafokui enyo̱ le̱ tšẽ ke̱-yanina mei fẽ ni yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ame̱gbegbẽame̱.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek ke̱ maṅ le̱ wu nakai gbĩ mū le̱ fẽ ni eṅõ maṅ le̱, ni egbe gbomei ní yo̱ mli le̱, ni edſa maṅ le̱, ni eṅõ ṅō eſã no̱.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Ni beni Šekem mō̃ le̱ṅ hĩĩ le̱ fẽ nu ene̱ le̱, ame̱yabote *El-Berit we le̱ mō̃ le̱ mli. *K.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Ni ayagba Abimelek ake̱ Šekem mō̃ le̱ṅ hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ebua ame̱he nā.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek kwo̱ ke̱-te Zalmon goṅ le̱ no, eke̱ mei fẽ ni fata ehe le̱, ni Abimelek ko̱ lema ehĩe edẽ, ni eyafo tšonine ko, ni ewó etſa ekõṅ, ni ekē̱ mei ní fata ehe le̱ ake̱: Noni nyena ní mife ne̱, nyehe afea oyá ní nyefe nakai.

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Ni mei le̱ ateṅ mofẽmo yafo etšonine, ni ame̱ke̱-nyie Abimelek se̱, ni ame̱ke̱-baſie mō̃ le̱ he, ni ame̱mã la ame̱wo mō̃ le̱ he ame̱woame̱. Ni gbomei fẽ ní yo̱ Šekem mō̃ le̱ mli le̱ hũ gboi, hĩĩ ke̱ yei aafe akpe.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abimelek yiṅ ete Tebez, ni eyabo̱ nsra ewo Tebez he, ni ehe dše̱i.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Ši mõ ni wa ko ye̱ maṅ le̱ teṅ, ni hĩĩ ke̱ yei le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅbii le̱ fẽ dšo foi ke̱-te dše̱i, ni ame̱ṅã́ ame̱yi, ni ame̱kwo̱ ke̱-te mō̃ le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek ba mō̃ le̱ he ni eke̱le̱ bawu, ni etši ebe̱ṅke̱ mō̃ le̱ šĩnā le̱, koni eše̱re la ewo he.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Ni yō ko fõ w̌ie̱bi eke̱-tſa Abimelek yitšo, ni edſãra eyitšoṅoṅo.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšē̱ oblanyo ní hĩe etawūnii le̱ oyá, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: *Gblamo̱ oklante ní ogbemi, koni akakē̱ ye̱ mihe ake̱: Yō po gbele̱! Ni oblanyo le̱ tšule̱ nõ ní egbo. *

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Ni beni Israel hĩĩ le̱ na ake̱ Abimelek enyõ le̱, ame̱teṅ mofẽmo te emaṅ.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Be̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ wo Abimelek efõṅ ni efe etše̱ ye̱ enyemimei nyoṅmai-kpawo le̱ agbē mli le̱ he nyōmo̱ ne̱. K.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Šekembii le̱ anõfõṅ ní ame̱fe le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ hã fẽ kpale ba ame̱ yiteaṅ, ni Iotam, Ierubaal bi le̱, *lōmo̱ le̱ ba ame̱no̱. *K.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Ni ese̱ le̱ *Iair, Gileadnyo le̱, te ši, ni ekodšo Israel afii nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ enyo̱. *

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa mli wo Israel la, ni ehõame̱ ehã Filistibii ke̱ Amonbii.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ni Gilead maṅbii ni dši lume̱i le̱ kē̱kē̱ ame̱he ake̱: Namo dši nū ni ke̱ Amonbii le̱ ababõi wū? Le̱ eeye *onukpa ye̱ Gileadbii le̱ fẽ no̱! *

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Amonbii le̱ bafo Iordan ni ame̱ke̱ Iuda hũ ke̱ Benyamin ke̱ Efraim we le̱ bawu; ni Israel fe yeyēye naakpa.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israelbii le̱ blo̱ tšé̱ Iehowa ame̱kē̱: Wo̱fe eša wo̱šio; edšake̱ wo̱kwa wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni wo̱yasúmo̱ Baalim!

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Nyeyaä ni nyeyablo̱a nyetšé̱a nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ní nyehala le̱; ame̱ ame̱here nyeyiwala ye̱ nyemanehũlũ be le̱ mli!

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ši Israelbii le̱ kē̱ Iehowa ake̱: Wo̱fe eša! bo le̱ feme̱wo̱ nofẽno ní sa ohĩe; ofai ne̱, dšiemo̱wo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ke̱ke̱!

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Ni *ame̱dšie nyoṅmo̱i krokomei le̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱teṅ ni ame̱súmo̱ Iehowa; ní Israelbii le̱ anii †fele̱ mo̱bo̱ ye̱ ame̱manehũlũ le̱ hewo̱. *

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Ni ayakpẽ Amonbii le̱ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱babo̱ nsra ye̱ Gilead. Ni Israelbii le̱ hũ bua ame̱he nā ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Mizpa.

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Ni Iefta kē̱ Gilead onukpai le̱ ake̱: Ani dšee nye nyehe tšẽmi, ni nyeſiemi ke̱-dše̱ mitše̱ we le̱? ni mẽhewo̱ ni kpāko ní nyeyo̱ amanehũlũ mli le̱ ni nyebaä miṅō?

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Ni Gilead onukpai le̱ kē̱ Iefta ake̱: Iehowa aaye wo̱teṅ odase ake̱ befẽbe ní fe le̱ wo̱o̱ye owiemo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta ke̱ Gilead onukpai le̱ yiṅ te, ni maṅ le̱ wole̱ onukpa ke̱ asafoiatše̱ ye̱ ame̱no̱; ni Iefta yawie ewiemo̱i le̱ fẽ *ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ye̱ Mizpa. *

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽ sane mike̱o yo̱, hewo̱ ni obaã mino̱ ní oke̱ mišikpoṅ le̱ abawu ne̱?

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Ni Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Iefta bo̱foi le̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ beni Israel dše̱ Mizraim baä le̱, eṅõ mĩšikpoṅ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Arnon he ke̱-yaši Iabok ke̱ Iordan he: nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ oke̱ minii akũ se̱ ahãmi kpō.

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Ni Iefta sā tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ekoṅ,

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: ši moṅ beni ame̱dše̱ Mizraim le̱, Israel tšṍ ṅã le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši Ṅšo̱-tšuru le̱ nā, ni ame̱ke̱-ba Kadeš.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ni Israel tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Edom maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, hã matšṍ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ho! Ši Edom maṅtše̱ le̱ boo toi. Ni etšũ Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ ṅõ, ši ekplẽẽ. Ni Israel hĩ ši ye̱ Kadeš;

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Amorbii amaṅtše̱ Sihon ni dši Hešbon maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ; ni Israel hã ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, hã wo̱tšṍ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ya heni miyaä le̱!

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Ši Sihon yiṅ etẽẽle̱ ye̱ Israel he bo̱ni eehã ame̱tšṍ ešikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ni Sihon bua emaṅ le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni eyabo̱ nsra ye̱ Iahaz, ni eke̱ Israel wu.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ Sihon ke̱ emaṅ le̱ ſẽ ewo Israel deṅ, ni ame̱tfſaame̱ nii; ni Israel ṅõ Amorbii ni yo̱ nakai šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ašikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ efe enõ.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ſie Amorbii le̱ ke̱-dše̱ emaṅ Israel le̱ hĩe le̱, ni bo le̱ otaoo̱ oṅõ no̱?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Ani noni onyoṅmo̱ *Kemoš le̱ ṅõ-hãao ake̱ onõ le̱, oṅõõ? Nakai noṅṅ wo̱ hũ, nofëno ní Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ-hãawo̱ ye̱ wohĩe le, wo̱o̱ṅõ ake wonõ! *

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ oye̱ hewale̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fè *Balak, Zipor bi le̱, ní dši Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ lo? Ani eke̱ Israel ebé pẽṅ, lo eke̱ame̱ ewu pẽṅ? *

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ mifekoö eša ko, ši bo moṅ ni ofeo̱mi efõṅ, ake̱-ni oke̱mi bawu ne̱. Iehowa ní dši kodšolo̱ le̱ ákodšo Israelbii le̱ ke̱ Amonbii le̱ ateṅ ṅme̱ne̱!

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱ boo Iefta wiemo̱i ni etšũ ayakē̱le̱ le̱ toi.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Ni *Iehowa Mumo̱ ba Iefta no̱, ni etšṍ Gilead ke̱ Manase, ni efoṅ ke̱-te Gilead-Mizpe, ni edše̱ Gilead-Mizpe efoṅ ke̱-yanina Amonbii le̱. *

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta fã ke̱-yanina Amonbii le̱, ni eke̱ame̱ wu; ni Iehowa ṅōame̱ wo edeṅ.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta ba ewe le̱ ye̱ Mizpa; ni na, ebiyō le̱ dše kpo bale̱ kpēmo̱ ke̱ fabii ke̱ dšōi, ni le̱ dši ebi kome pe̱; ese̱ le̱ ebe̱ binū lo biyō le̱ eko doṅṅ.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni enale̱ le̱, egbla etadei ni ekē̱: Ao, mibi! ohã mihe edšo̱ naakpa, bo pam ohã ošrã bašrãmi ne̱! Edšake̱ *migble minā mihã Iehowa, ni minyẽṅ minā makpale! *

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mitše̱, ogble onä okē̱ Iehowa; gbĩĩabo̱ kẽ ní Iehowa eto̱ ohe owele ye̱ ohenye̱lo̱i ní dši Amonbii le̱ ano̱ ne̱, femo̱mi bo̱ni dše onā le̱!

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Ni esā ekē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Femo̱ ene̱ ke̱ke̱ ohãmi: ṅmẽmi gbe̱ ke̱-yaši bie̱ nyõdši enyo̱, ní maya ni mayakpleke gõdši le̱, ni mĩke̱ minanemei ayafó miblayeiaṅ.

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Ya! ni ewole̱ gbe̱ eyaye nyõdši enyo̱; ni eke̱ enanemei le̱ te, ni eyafó eblayeiaṅ ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ nyõdši enyo̱ le̱ nā-gbē mli le̱ ekũ ese̱ eba etše̱ ṅõ ekoṅ, ni efele̱ tamo̱ bo̱ni ewo šĩ le̱ noṅṅ; ni egbãã nū ko nū ko. Ni etšṍ kusum ye̱ Israel,

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: ake̱ dā afi le̱ Israel oblayei le̱ yaä ame̱yakafoo̱ Iefta, Gileadnyo le̱, biyō le̱ gbĩĩ edſe̱ ye̱ afi mli.

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Ni Iefta kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mike̱ mimaṅ-bii le̱ wo̱ke̱ Amonbii le̱ ná sane kpeteṅkple, ni beni miblo̱ mitsé̱nye le̱, nyebahereemi ke̱-dše̱e̱ ame̱deṅ.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Ni beni mina ake̱ nyebahereemi le̱, *miši mitšitši, ni mifã ke̱-yanina Amonbii le̱, ni Iehowa dšieame̱ ewo mideṅ. Bĕle̱ mẽba nyefã ke̱-ba mino̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ni nyeke̱mi abawu? *

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta bua Gilead hĩĩ le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni eke̱ Efraim wu, ni Gilead hĩĩ le̱ tſia Efraim nii, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Nye Gileadbii le̱, Efraim mli kobo̱foi dšinye ye̱ Efraim ke̱ Manase teṅ!

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Ni Gileadbii le̱ yatšĩ Efraimbii le̱ agbe̱ ye̱ Iordan fōhei le̱; ni eba mli ake̱, ké̱ Efraimbii foidšelo̱i le̱ eko kē̱ ake̱: Hã mafo fā le̱, Gileadbii le̱ bio̱le̱ ake̱: Ani Efraimnyo dšio lo? ni ke̱dši ekē̱: Dabi! le̱,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: ame̱kē̱o̱le̱ akē̱: Bẽle̱ kē̱mo̱ “Šibolet!” ni kē̱ enyẽẽ ekē̱ dšogbãṅ, ni ekē̱ “Sibolet” le̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ ame̱mõo̱le̱, ni ame̱gbeo̱le̱ ye̱ Iordan fōhei le̱. Ni nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Efraimbii le̱ ateṅ mei akpei-nyoṅmai-edſe̱-ke̱-enyo̱ nyõnyõi.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Ni Iefta kodšo Israel afii ekpa. Ke̱ke̱ ni Iefta, Gileadnyo le̱, gbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ Gilead mãdši le̱ eko mli.

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ni ese̱ le̱ Ibzan ni dše̱ Betlehem le̱ kodšo Israel.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Ni ekodšo Israel afii kpawo. Ni Ibzan gbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ Betlehem:

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ni ese̱ le̱ Elon, Zebulonnyo le̱, bakodšo Israel; ni ekodšo Israel afii nyoṅma.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Ni Elon, Zebulonnyo le̱, gbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ Ayalon ye̱ Zebulon šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Ni Abdon, Hilel Piratonnyo le̱ bi le̱, gbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ Piraton ye̱ Efraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Amalekbii le̱ agoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱mi ake̱: Na, obaná mũsũ ni obafo̱ binū; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ le̱, kānu wein lo dā̃ ko ni wa, ni kāye noko ni he tšee; edšake̱ gbekẽ le̱ bafe Nyoṅmo̱ Nazirnyo ke̱-badše̱ mũsũṅ bēbe ke̱-yaši egbĕle gbĩ.

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Manoa kpa Iehowa fai ni ekē̱: O Nuṅtšo̱, mīkpao fai, hã Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ní otšũ le̱ eba wo̱ṅõ ekoṅ, ní ebatšõwo̱ bo̱ni wo̱tšṍ wo̱hĩe gbekẽ le̱ ni abafo̱ le̱ wo̱hã!

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ he fe oyá ni eša foi, ni oyagba ewù le̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, nū le̱ ní ba miṅõ nyese̱ le̱ ebadšie ehe kpo etšõmi!

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ni Manoa te ši, ni enyie eṅã le̱ se̱, ni eba nū le̱ ṅõ, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani bo dši nū le̱ ni ke̱ yō le̱ bawie le̱? Ni ekē̱: Miṅ!

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Ni Manoa kē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ kē̱ owiemo̱i le̱ ná ba mli le̱, meni dši gbekẽ le̱ gbe̱nā ni té wo̱o̱tšṍ wo̱hĩele̱ tēṅ?

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱ Manoa ake̱: Nibii fẽ ni mikē̱ yō le̱, ehĩe ahĩ ehe no̱ ye̱ he.

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱ Manoa ake̱: Ke̱dši otšĩ minā tete hũ, miyeṅ obolo ne̱ eko; ni ke̱dši šã-afo̱le obašã le̱, no le̱ šã ohã Iehowa. Edšake̱ Manoa lee ake̱ Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ ni.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Ni Manoa kē̱ Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ ake̱: *Té ogbe̱iṅ? koni ké̱ owiemo̱i le̱ ná ba mli le̱, ni wo̱dšie oyi. *

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba obio̱ migbe̱i ní yo̱ nākpe̱ le̱?

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni lalĩle̱i le̱ te ši ke̱-dše̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaã ṅwei le̱, Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ tšṍ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱ lalile̱i le̱ mli ekwo̱ ke̱-te ṅwei, ni beni Manoa ke̱ eṅã le̱ na le̱, ame̱ke̱ ame̱hĩe bumo̱ ši ye̱ šikpoṅ.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ ebadšiee ehe kpo etšõõ Manoa ke̱ eṅã le̱ doṅṅ. Ke̱ke̱ ni Manoa ná le ake̱ Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ ni.

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Ši eṅã le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Iehowa mītaowo̱ egbe dšikũle̱, eheṅ šã-afo̱le ke̱ niyenii-afo̱le le̱ ye̱ wo̱deṅ, ni kũle̱ etšõṅwo̱ ene̱mei fẽ, ni asaṅ kũle̱ ehãṅ wo̱na ne̱ke̱ sãdši ní wo̱nu ne̱ ye̱ be ne̱ mli.

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ fo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Samson. Ni gbekẽ le̱ bada, ni Iehowa dšō̱le̱.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Ni *Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ bōi ehe tā ye̱ Mahane-Dan, ye̱ Zora ke̱ Eštaol teṅ. *

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Ni Samson yiṅ ete Timna, ni eyana yō ko ye̱ Timna, ní dši Filistibii le̱ abiyei le̱ eko.

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ni etše̱ ke̱ enye kē̱le̱ ake̱: Aso yō ko yō ko be̱ onyemimei le̱ abiyei le̱ ke̱ midšakubii le̱ fẽ ateṅ, hewo̱ ni oyaã oyaṅõ yō *ye̱ Filistibii fōlo̱i le̱ ateṅ le̱? Ni Samson kē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Yaṅõ le̱ obahãmi, edšake̱ le̱ misumoo̱! *

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Ši etše̱ ke̱ enye lee ake̱ Iehowa deṅ dše̱, ni Filistibii le̱ ahe gbe̱ etaoo̱, edšake̱ nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Filistibii le̱ yeo̱ Israel no̱.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Ni Samson ke̱ etše̱ ke̱ enye yiṅ ke̱-te Timna. Ni beni ame̱še̱ Timna weintromi le̱ ahe le̱, na, dšata oblanyo ko hū ke̱-ba eno̱.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Ni *Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ bayi eno̱, ni etšere̱ emli, tamo̱ atšere̱o̱ abotiabi mli noṅṅ, tše̱ ehĩee nokonoko ye̱ edeṅ; ni egbaa etše̱ ke̱ enye noni efe le̱, *

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ete, ni eke̱ yō le̱ yawie, ni Samson sumo̱ esane.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ni yee gbĩ ko le̱ ekũ ese̱ ete le̱ ṅõ; ni egbá ke̱-te dšata gbonyo le̱ kwe̱mo̱, ni na, wòbii asafo eto wò ye̱ dšata le̱ mũsũṅ.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ni edšie eko ehĩe edẽ, ni ehĩe yeli ke̱-nyie, ni ebanina etše̱ ke̱ enye, ni ehã-ame̱ eko ame̱ye; ši ekē̱ē̱ame̱ ake̱ dšata le̱ mũsũṅ edšie wò le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etše̱ yiṅ ke̱-te yō le̱ ṅõ, ni Samson ṅmẽ okplõ ye̱ dše̱i, edšake̱ nakai oblahĩĩ le̱ fo̱ö̱ femo̱.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱nale̱ le̱, ame̱yaṅõ nanemei nyoṅmai-etẽ ame̱ba-fata ehe.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: ši ke̱dši nyenyẽẽ nyetšõmi šiši le̱, no le̱ nye hũ nyebahãmi mamai nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ hetšakemo̱ atadei nyoṅmai-etẽ. Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Bu obe̱ le̱, ní wo̱bo toi!

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Niyenii dše̱ nõyelo̱ le̱ mli, ni ṅõmo̱ dše̱ hewalo̱ le̱ mli. Ni ame̱nyẽẽ abe̱ le̱ šiši ame̱tšṍ ãhũ gbĩī etẽ so̱ṅṅ.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱, dãni hũlũ nyõ ši le̱, mã le̱ṅ hĩĩn le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Meni ṅõ fè wò, ni meni he wa fò dšata? Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeke̱ mitšina le̱ hũũ dšikũle̱, nyenaṅ mibe̱ le̱ šiši!

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Ši aṅõ Samson ṅã le̱ ahã *enanyo ní eke̱-bo̱ö̱ le̱. *

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Ni etše̱ kē̱: Mikē̱, bene̱ osumo̱o̱le̱ doṅṅ, nohewo̱ le̱ *miṅõle̱ mihā onanyo ko. Nto enyemi gbekẽ le̱ he ye̱ fe̱o fè-le̱? ṅõ le̱ ye̱ enãdšiaṅ. *

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Ni Samson kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ ke̱-dši mife Filistibii le̱ efõṅ ko le̱, ame̱sõ ko wulaa miyiteṅ!

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Ni beni emãmo̱ ko̱tii le̱ anã la le̱, eṅmē̃ ame̱he ewo Filistibii le̱ aṅmā̃ ni mãmo̱ ši le̱ mli, ni ešã ṅmā̃ kei le̱ ke̱ ṅmā̃ ni mãmo̱ ši ke̱ mũtšei atromi le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Filistibii le̱ kē̱: Namo po fe ene̱? Ni ame̱kē̱: Samson, Timnanyo le̱, šānū le̱ ni, edšake̱ eṅõ eṅã le̱ ehã enanyo ko. Ke̱ke̱ ni Filistibii le̱ yiṅ te, ni ame̱ke̱ la yašãle̱ ke̱ etše̱ fẽ.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Ni Samson kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni nye-tšṍ nyefe ne̱, dša mito̱ mihe owele ye̱ nyeno̱, dãni mafõ!

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Filistibii le̱ fã ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Iuda, ni ame̱ho ame̱lē̱ ši ye̱ Lehi.

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ni Iuda hĩĩ akpei-etẽ yiṅ ke̱-te Etam te̱sã flo̱ le̱ṅ, ni ame̱yakē̱ Samson ake̱: Ani olee ake̱ Filistibii le̱ yeo̱ wo̱no̱? Kole̱ meni dši noni ofewo̱ ne̱? Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni ame̱femi le̱, nakai mi hũ mifeame̱.

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Ni ena tedši kadā ṅmõṅ ko, ni ekpã enine mli ni eko̱ ni eke̱-gbe hĩĩ akpe.

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ewie egbe nā le̱, eṅmā̃ kadā le̱ he ye̱ edẽ eše̱ efõ, ni awo dše̱i ake̱: Ramat-Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Ni kũmai yele̱ naakpa, ni eblo̱ etšē̱ Iehowa ni ekē̱: Otšṍ otšũlo̱ nine no̱ otšu yiwalaheremo̱ nitšumo̱ kpeteṅkple ne̱, ni kpāko moṅ ni magbo ke̱ kũmai, ni ma-gbē fõlo̱i le̱ adeṅ!

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ gbá flo̱ kutruku ní yo̱ Lehi le̱ mli, ni nu tue ke̱-dše̱ mli, ni beni enu le̱, *emumo̱ kpale ba emli ni ehĩe tšere̱le̱, nohewo̱ le̱ awo dše̱i gbe̱i ake̱ En-Hakorē, ni eye Lehi ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. *

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni *ekodšo Israel afii nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ye̱ Filistibii le̱ ahe le̱ mli. *

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Ni no se̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ eyasume̱ yō ko sane ye̱ Sorek dšō̱ le̱ṅ, ni egbe̱i dši Delila.

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ni Samson kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši ame̱ke̱ kpãi hēi kãwekãwē kpawo fĩmi le̱, no dã-ni magbo̱dšo̱, ni matamo̱ gbomo-fẽ-gbomo.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Delila kē̱ Samson ake̱: Na, oye mihe fe̱o, ni olakami! Agbe̱ne̱ tšõmo̱mi noni ake̱-afĩo!

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dšĩ ame̱ke̱ tãṅkpēi hēi ní ake̱-tšuko noko dã fĩmi le̱, no dãni magbo̱dšo̱, ni matamo̱ gbomo-fẽ-gbomo.

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Delila ṅõ tãṅkpēi hēi ni eke̱-fĩle̱, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Filistibii le̱ eſie ono̱, Samson! Bĕle̱ ante̱owolo̱i le̱ trá pia le̱ṅ. Ni etšere̱ ye̱ enidši tamo̱ kpã legelege ko.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ni Delila kē̱ Samson ake̱: Dše̱eṅmõ ne̱ fẽ le̱ mihe fe̱o so̱ṅṅ oyeo̱ ni olakaãmi! Tšõmo̱mi noni ake̱-afĩo! Nĩ ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dšĩ oke̱ boṅ lò miyitšo̱i akuklui kpawo le̱ ofe ekome le̱.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni egbale̱ etšuiṅ sane fẽ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: *Asōyi nā esako miyiteṅ pẽṅ, edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ Nazirnyo dšimi ke̱-dše̱ minye mũsũṅ bēbe; ke̱dši aše̱ miyi le̱, no dãni mihewale̱ aadše mihe, ni magbo̱dšo̱ ni matamo̱ gbomo-fẽ-gbomo. *

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Ni ewo̱lele̱ ye̱ enakutšei anā, ni etšē̱ nū ko ni ehã ebaše̱ eyi akuklui kpawo le̱, ni ebõĩ ehe dšō̱mo̱, nĩ ehewale̱ le̱ dše eno̱.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ mõle̱ ni ame̱fãmo̱ ehĩṅme̱ii, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ te Gaza, ni ame̱ke̱ akō̱ble gbokle̱i enyo̱ wole̱, ni ame̱hãa ew̌ie̱o̱ ye̱ gbokle̱foi atšũ le̱ mli.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Ši beni aše̱ eyitšo̱i le̱ se̱ le̱, ebõĩ tšã ekoṅ.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ babua ame̱he nā, koni ame̱šã afo̱le kple ame̱hã ame̱nyoṅmo̱ *Dagon le̱, ni ame̱nyã́, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Wo̱nyoṅmo̱ le̱ edšie wo̱henye̱lo̱ Samson le̱ ewo wo̱deṅ! *

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Ni Samson kē̱ gbekẽ le̱ ni hĩe enineši le̱ ake̱: Ṅmẽmi gbe̱ ní matra akula-šĩṅi le̱ ni tšũ le̱ mã no̱ le̱ ahe makwe̱, ni makpasaame̱.

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Ni Samson tšē̱ Iehowa ni eke: Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa! mīkpao fai, kaimo̱mi agbe̱ne̱, ni owomi hewale̱ šikome ne̱ pe̱ ke̱ke̱, Nānyoṅmo̱, koni mato mihĩṅme̱ii enyo̱ ne̱ he owele šikome ye̱ Filistibii le̱ ano̱!

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Ni Samson mõmo̱ teṅ akulašĩṅi enyo̱ le̱ ni tšũ le̱ mã no̱ le̱ mli, eke̱ enine dšũrõ mõ ekome mli ni eke̱ ebe̱ku mõ ekome mli, ni eke̱ ehewale̱ fõ no̱.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Ni Samson kē̱: Hã mi ke̱ Filistibii le̱ agbo! Ni eba ši ke̱ ehewale̱ fẽ, ni šĩa le̱ wule gbē lume̱i le̱ ke̱ mei ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ fẽ no̱. Ni mei ní egbe ye̱ egbĕle mli le̱ agbohĩĩ le̱ fá fè mei ni egbe ye̱ ewalabe le̱ mli le̱.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni enyemimei le̱ ke̱ etše̱ we le̱ fē yiṅ ke̱-te, ni ame̱yawóle̱, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ ba ame̱bafũle̱ ye̱ *Zora ke̱ Eštaol teṅ, ye̱ etše̱ Manoa fū̃he le̱. Ni †ekodšo Israel afii nyoṅmai-enyo̱. *

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ dſie̱te̱i le̱ kũ se̱ hã enye. Ni enye ṅõ dſie̱te̱i kukudši ohai-enyo̱ ni eṅõ-hã *niſielo̱ le̱, ni eṅõ-fe amãgã ni akpe ke̱ noni aſie, ni ake̱-ba Mika we le̱. *Ies.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Ni nū Mika le̱ we le̱ tšṍ nyoṅmo̱i awe, ni efe *efod ke̱ wo̱dši, ni ewo ebi-hĩĩ le̱ ateṅ mokome oso̱fo, ni eye oso̱fo ehãle̱. *

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: No be le̱ mli le̱ *maṅtše̱ ko be̱ Israel; mofẽmo feo̱ noni dša ye̱ ledĩentše̱ ehĩe. *

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ fã ke̱-dše̱ Betlehem-Iuda mā le̱ṅ, koni eyahī hefẽhe ní eená; ni egbe̱nyiemo̱ le̱ mli le̱ ebaše̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ ye̱ Mika we le̱.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Ni Mika kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ odše̱ obaä ne̱? Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Levinyo ni dše Betlehem-Iuda dšimi, ni mīya miyahī hefẽhe ni miná.

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Ni Mika kē̱le̱ ake̱: Oke̱mi abahĩ ši, ni otšṍ mitše̱ ke̱ miso̱fo, ní dã afi kplo̱ le̱ mahāo dſie̱te̱i kukudši nyoṅma ke̱ atade bo̱ni aaše̱o wō, ke̱ oniyenii. Ni Levinyo le̱ te šĩa le̱.

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Ni Mika wo Levinyo le̱ oso̱fo, ni oblanyo le̱ ye oso̱fo ehãle̱, ni ehĩ Mika we le̱.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ni Mika kē̱: Kpāko miná mile ake̱ Iehowa bafemi edšũrõ, gbĩĩabo̱ ní miná Levinyo mife oso̱fo ne̱.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ni Danbii le̱ tšũ hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i enumo̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱weku le̱ fẽ mli ke̱-dše̱ *Zora ke̱ Eštaol, koni ame̱yasra šikpoṅ le̱ ní ame̱kpale̱ ši tſẽm, ni ame̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeyaä ni nyeyakpaä šikpoṅ le̱ ši! Ni ame̱ba Efraim gõdšĩ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Mika we le̱, ni ame̱bawo̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Beni ame̱be̱ṅke̱ Mika we le̱, ame̱na oblanyo *Levinyo le̱ wiemo̱; ni ame̱gbale dše̱i, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Oke̱ namo ba bie̱? ni meni ofeo̱ ye̱ bie̱? ni meni hũ oyo̱ ye̱ bie̱?

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱mīkpao fai, bi Nyoṅmo̱ ohãwo̱, koni wo̱ná wo̱le ake̱ wo̱gbe̱ ní wo̱nyie ne̱ aafe šade gbe̱ lo?

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni hĩĩ enumo̱ le̱ yiṅ ni ame̱te Laiš, ni ame̱yana dše̱ibii le̱, bo̱ni ame̱he edšo̱ame̱ tamo̱ Zidonbii le̱, ni ame̱yo̱ kpõ ke̱ ſeſēſe; ni moko be̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ni yeo̱ame̱ no̱ ní efeo̱ame̱ efõṅ ko, ni ame̱ke̱ Zidonbii le̱ ateṅ dšeke̱, ni ame̱ke̱ mokomoko be̱ nanyobō̱ ko.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba ame̱nyemi-mei le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Zora ke̱ Eštaol; ni ame̱-nyemimei le̱ biame̱ ake̱: Té nyeyana tẽṅ?

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Kē̱ nyete le̱, nyeayanina maṅ ko ni ame̱he edšo̱ame̱, ke̱ šikpoṅ ni da; edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ eṅõ-wo nyedeṅ; he ko ni šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ nihii fẽ mli eko eko he be̱ onã ye̱ le̱.

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ni Danbii aweku le̱ṅ hĩĩ ohai-ekpa ní emĩa ke̱ tawūnii fã ke̱-dše̱ Zora ke̱ Eštaol.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fo mli ye̱ dše̱i ke̱-te *Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ame̱yase Mika šĩa le̱ he. *

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yadše hĩĩ enumo̱ le̱ ni te yasra Laiš šikpoṅ le̱ nā le̱, ame̱kē̱ ame̱-nyemimei le̱ ake: Ani nyele ake̱ ne̱ke̱ šĩai ne̱, *efod ke̱ wo̱dši ke̱ amãgã ní akpe ke̱ noni aſie ye̱ mli lo? nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyekwe̱a bo̱ni nyeafe! *

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ oso̱fo le̱ nā, ní eṅõ efod le̱ ke̱ wo̱dši le̱ ke̱ amãgã ní akpe̱ le̱, ni eke̱-ha mei le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱tšṍ ame̱he ni ame̱ṅõ-ſie no̱, ni ame̱ṅõ gbekẽbii ke̱ šĩa koloi ke̱ nibii ni he dšraä le̱ ame̱to ame̱hĩegbe̱.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Beni ame̱ke̱ Mika we le̱ mli egbla kplaṅṅ le̱, šĩai ni be̱ṅke̱ Mika we le̱ amlibii le̱ bua ame̱he nā, ní ame̱tiu Danbii le̱.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱blo̱ ame̱tšē̱ Danbii le̱ ayise̱. Ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ ame̱hĩe ni ame̱kē̱ Mika ake̱: Meni feo̱o, ni oke̱ asafo ni tamo̱ ne̱ke̱ baã ne̱?

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Minyoṅmo̱i ni mife le̱ nyebalō, ke̱ oso̱fo le̱, ni nyeṅō-ſie no̱ ke̱-mīya, ni meni miyo̱ ye̱ se̱ doṅṅ? ni mẽba nyekē̱o̱mi ake̱: Meni feo̱o le̱?

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Ši Danbii le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāhã anu ogbē ye̱ wo̱teṅ, ní mlilatše̱mei akatšẽ ke̱-mība ono̱, ní ame̱bakpãtã bo ke̱ owebii le̱ asusuma hĩe!

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Ni Danbii le̱ yi ame̱gbe̱ no̱ ke̱-te; ni beni Mika na ake̱ ame̱he wa fèle̱ le̱, etšṍ ehe ni ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te ewe le̱.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Ni ehemo le̱ dše ese̱ eyabo̱ adſamaṅ, ni edšo foi ye̱ eṅõ ke̱-te etše̱ we ye̱ Betlehem-Iuda, ni eyaye nyõdši edſe̱ so̱ṅṅ ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Ni ewù le̱ te ši ni etiule̱ ke̱-te, koni eke̱le̱ ayawie tšuidšũrõ nā, ni ekpla-le̱ ke̱-ba ekoṅ, ni eke̱ etšũlo̱ ke̱ tedšii enyo̱ nyie. Ni yō le̱ ṅõle̱ ke̱-te etše̱ we le̱. Ni beni oblayō le̱ tše̱ le̱ nale̱ le̱, enyã́ ehe.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ enumo̱ le̱ ete ši lebi mãṅkpa ni ebaya; ni oblayō le̱ tše̱ le̱ kē̱: Wo onā noko dã, ni nyehĩ ši ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱nāšĩ! Ni ame̱yĩ enyo̱ le̱ fẽ ame̱ye nii.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ te ši ni ebaya, le̱ ke̱ ehemo le̱ ke̱ etšũlo̱ le̱; ni ešānū le̱ ní dši oblayō le̱ tše̱ le̱ kē̱: Na, agbe̱ne̱ dše mīna, nyewo̱a, na, hĩe ebu etã, wo̱ bie̱, ní omī aše̱ ohe, ni nyete ši mãṅkẽ mrã ni nyeyi mli, ní oya omaṅ.

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ši nū le̱ ekplẽẽ ní ehĩ ši nakai nyō le̱ṅ, ši ete ši ni eyi mli, ni eyaše̱ *Iebus ní dši Ierusalem le̱ ṅe̱le̱no̱, ni eke̱ tedšii enyo̱ ní awo ame̱no̱ nii le̱ ke̱ ehemo le̱ nyie. *

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ši enuṅtšo̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱katšṍ mei kpõdši amaṅ ko ní Israelbii le̱ eko be̱ dše̱i le̱ mli, ši moṅ wo̱foṅ ke̱-ya Gibea.

english_verse: or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ etšũlo̱ le̱ ake̱: Hã ní wo̱tši wo̱se̱ bie̱ heko, ni wo̱yawo̱ Gibea lo Rama!

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱foṅ ke̱-te, ni hũlũ nyõame̱ ši ye̱ Gibea ní dši Benyamin nõ le̱ mase̱i.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱gbá dše̱i, koni ame̱yawo̱ Gibea. Ni beni eše̱ dše̱i le̱, eho etá mã le̱ṅ blohũṅ; edšake̱ mokomoko eṅõõame̱ ke̱-yaa ewe ni ame̱yatole̱.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ni na, nūmo ko eyatšu nii ye̱ eṅmō mli eha ghe̱ke̱nāši, ni le̱ hũ edše̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ebato gbo̱ ye̱ Gibea; ši dše̱ibii le̱ Benyaminbii dšiame̱.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Ni beni eyawó ehĩe no̱ le̱, enanū gbe̱nyielo̱ le̱ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ blohũ le̱ mli, ni nūmo le̱ kē̱: Nẽgbe̱ oyaä, ni nẽgbe̱ hũ odše̱?

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱dše̱ Betlehem-Iuda wo̱mīſoṅ ke̱-ya Efraim goṅ le̱ se̱: dše̱i mi-dše̱; ni mite Betlehem-Iuda; ši Iehowa we le̱ miyaä ne̱, ni mokomoko eṅõõmi ní mayato ewe.

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ni nūmo le̱ kē̱: Oba ke̱ omanye! ši kẽle̱ nofẽno ní aahĩao le̱ mahão; blohũ le̱ṅ ke̱ke̱ ni okawo̱!

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõle̱ ke̱-te ewe le̱, ni ehã etedšii le̱ anii, ni ame̱fo̱fō̱ ame̱nãdši ahe, ni ame̱ye nii ni amenu noko.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
