translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ beni ame̱mī eše̱ ame̱be le̱, na, mã le̱ṅ bii komei ní dši hĩĩ yakagbomei le̱ babo̱le šĩa le̱ ke̱-kpe, ame̱ši-mo̱šimō̱ šĩnā le̱, ni ame̱kē̱ šīatše̱ ní dši nūmo le̱ ake̱: Oke̱ nū le̱ ni bato owe le̱ adše kpo ke̱-ba, ní wo̱lele̱!

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ ni dši šĩatše̱ le̱ dše kpo ba ame̱ṅõ, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Dabida, *minyemimei, nyekafea efõṅ ní tamo̱ ne̱ke̱, gbĩĩabo̱ ní ne̱ke̱ nū ne̱ ebato miwe ne̱, nyekafea ne̱ke̱ hĩegbedšianii! *

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Na, mibi oblayō fro ke̱ ehemo hũ ne̱, mike̱ame̱ moṅ badše kpo ke̱-ba, ni nye-flieame̱, ni nyefeame̱ nofẽno ní nyesumoo̱; ši nū ne̱, nyekafeale̱ hĩegbedšianii ni tamo̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Ši hĩĩ le̱ boole̱ toi; ke̱ke̱ ni nū le̱ ṅõ ehemo le̱ ni eke̱le̱ dše kpo ke̱-ba ame̱ṅõ ye̱ blohũ le̱ṅ; ni ame̱lele̱, ni ame̱-fele̱ niseniianii nyõṅnyõṅ ke̱ dšetše̱remo̱, ni beni dše bōi tše̱remo̱ le̱, ame̱ṅmē̃ ehe.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Ni hĩefute̱fute̱ mli le̱ yō le̱ ba, ni ebaho ebu ši ye̱ nū le̱ we heni enuṅtšo̱ le̱ yo̱ le̱ šĩnā le̱ ši ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní hĩe gble.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Ni beni enuṅtšo̱ le̱ te ši lebi ni egble šĩa le̱ šĩnā le̱ ni ebadše kpo ni eya le̱, na, yō le̱ ni dši ehemo le̱ bu ši ye̱ šĩa le̱ šĩnā le̱ ši, ni enidši dſere kpoku le̱ no̱.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Te ši ni wo̱te! Ši fẽ le̱ krãnã. Ke̱ke̱ ni nū le̱ wóle̱ ṅmẽ tedši le̱ no̱, ni eṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-te emaṅ.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Ši beni eše̱ ewe le̱, eko̱ kakla, ni emõ ehemo̱ le̱ mli ni eflo emli ye̱ etalo̱i ano̱ kukudši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱, ni ehã ake̱-te Israel šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ mofẽmo ni ná le̱ ekē̱o̱ ake̱: Ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ ni Israelbii le̱ dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ba āhũ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ afeko ne̱ke̱ noko dã ni asaṅ anako eno̱ hũ. Nyeſiea nyeyiṅ ye̱ ene̱ hewo̱, nyewoa he ṅā ni nyewiea!

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni nū Levinyo le̱ ní dši yō ní agbe le̱ wù le̱ to he ní ekē̱: Mike̱ mihemo le̱ fẽ yaše̱ *Gibea ní yo̱ Benyamin le̱, ni wo̱wo̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ni mimo mihemo le̱ mli, ni miflo̱ emli kukudši, ni mihã ake̱-te Israel no̱yeli šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ no̱; edšake̱ ame̱ho̱ musu ni ame̱tšu hĩegbedšianii ye̱ Israel!

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ni agbene̱, nye Israelbii le̱ fẽ ne̱, nyekodšoa ni nyewoa ṅā!

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ te ši damo̱ ši tamo̱ gbomo kome ame̱kē̱: Wo̱teṅ nū ko nü ko eyaṅ ebū mli, ni asaṅ wo̱teṅ nū ko nū ko gbaleṅ ewe;

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Ni Israel akutšei le̱ tšũ mei ke̱-te Benyaminbii akutšo le̱ fẽ ṅõ ayakē̱ ake̱: Mẽ musu pam abo̱ ye̱ nyeteṅ ne̱?

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: ši Benyaminbii le̱ bua ame̱he nā ke̱-dše̱ mãdšimãdši le̱ amli ke̱-ba Gibea, ni ame̱fã, koni ame̱ke̱ Israelbii le̱ ayawu.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Ni akane Israel hĩĩ le̱, ni aná hĩĩ akpei-ohai-edſe̱ ni gblaä klante: mei ni ese̱ tayā so̱ṅṅ ne̱, Benyaminbii le̱ be̱ mli.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ te ši lebi, ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ame̱wo Gibea,

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Ni Israel hĩĩ le̱ fã te ame̱ke̱ Benyamin yawu; ni Israel hĩĩ le̱ gbá ta le̱ woame̱ ye̱ Gibea.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: ni Pinehas, Aaron bi *Eleazar bi le̱, dši moni damoo̱ ehĩe ye̱ no gbĩĩ le̱ amli; ni ame̱kē̱: Ani mifã ekoṅ ní mi-ke̱ minyemi Benyaminbii le̱ ayawu lo mi-fõ? Ni Iehowa kē̱: Nyefãa ke̱-yaā; edšake̱ wó̱ le̱ matuame̱ mawo odeṅ. *Ios.

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel to káwolo̱i ke̱-bo̱le Gibea ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱tšṍ ame̱se̱ ame̱hã Israel hĩĩ le̱ ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱; ši ta le̱ nyie ame̱se̱ wā, ni mei ní dše̱ mãdšimãdši le̱ amli le̱ bū abo̱leame̱ ni akpãtã ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ame̱sá Benyaminbii le̱ ayi ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱ſieame̱ ke̱-yaši Menuha, ni ame̱nānã ame̱no̱ ke̱-yaši Gibea ṅe̱le̱no̱ ye̱ bokãgbe̱.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱tšṍ ame̱he ni ame̱dšo foi ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱, ke̱-yaã Rimon te̱sã le̱ be; ni ame̱yeame̱ atšo̱tšo̱ ke̱-gbe ame̱teṅ hĩĩ akpei-enumo̱ ye̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱i le̱ ano̱; ni ame̱nyie ame̱se̱ wā ke̱-yaši Gideom, ni ame̱saṅ ame̱gbe ame̱teṅ hĩĩ akpei-enyo̱.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Bẽle̱ mei fẽ ni nyõ ye̱ Benyaminbii le̱ ateṅ nakai gbī le̱ dši hĩĩ ní eše̱ klante gblamo̱ akpei-nyoṅmai-enyo̱-ke̱-enumo̱; mene̱mei fẽ le̱ hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i so̱ṅṅ ni.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Ši Israel hĩĩ le̱ tšṍ ame̱hīe ame̱wo Benyaminbii le̱ ekoṅ, ni ame̱ke̱ klante gbegbēame̱, gbomei ni yo̱ maṅ-fē-maṅ mli ke̱ koloi fẽ ke̱ nibii fẽ ni še̱ ame̱deṅ; ni asaṅ mãdši fẽ ni ame̱yanina le̱, ame̱-mãmo̱ nā la.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱: Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱, mẽba ene̱ ba ye̱ Israel ake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ aku-tšo kome mīlādše ye̱ Israel?

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ kē̱: Israel akutšei le̱ fẽ ateṅ le̱ namo dši moni ke̱ ãsafo le̱ *baa Iehowa ṅõ? Edšake̱ akã kitã wula afo moni baa Iehowa ṅõ ye̱ Mizpa le̱ no̱ ake̱: Gbe ágbele̱!

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Ni ame̱na oblayei froi ohai-edſe̱ ní leko nū ye̱ Iabeš-Gileadbii le̱ ateṅ, ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ ba nsra le̱ṅ ye̱ Šilo ni yo̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ tšũ ake̱ Benyaminbii ní yo̱ *Rimon te̱sā le̱ mli le̱ yawie, ni ake̱ame̱ yakpãtã. *

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Ni Benyaminbii le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli; ni ame̱ṅõ yei ní ame̱here ame̱yiwala ye̱ Iabeš-Gilead yei le̱ ateṅ le̱ ame̱hãame̱ gblã; ši no tete hũ le̱ eše̱e̱ame̱.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ ſa ame̱he ye̱ Benyamin hewo̱, edšake̱ Iehowa ehã mligblamo̱ eba Israel akutšei le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ni asafo le̱ mli onukpai le̱ kē̱: Té wo̱o̱fe tẽṅ wo̱ná ṅāmei wo̱hã mei ni eſe̱ le̱, ake̱-ni akpãtã Benyamin mli yei le̱ ahĩe ne̱?

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Ši wo̱ le̱ wo̱nyẽṅ wo̱ṅõ wo̱biyei le̱ eko wo̱hãame̱ gblã; edšake̱ Israelbii le̱ *ekãmo̱ kitãi ake̱: Alomo̱ moni aaṅõ yō ko ahã gblã ye̱ Benyamin! *K.

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Na, dă afi le̱ ayeo̱ Iehowa gbĩdšũrõ le̱ ye̱ Šilo ni kã Betel kōyigbe̱, ye̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱ ní kã ke̱-dše̱ Betel ke̱-yaã Šekem le̱ bokãgbe̱, ke̱ Lebona wuoyigbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fã́ Benyaminbii le̱ ake̱: Nyeyaã ní nyeyatea ye̱ weintromi le̱ amli,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: ni na, ke̱dši Šilo oblayei le̱ dše kpo ba ame̱badšò ye̱ dšòi le̱ amli le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni nyedše kpo ke̱-dše̱ weintromi le̱ amli ke̱-ba, ni nyeteṅ mofẽmo abamõ eṅã ye̱ Šilo oblayei le̱ ateṅ, ní nyeke̱-ame̱ aya Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱, kē̱ ame̱tše̱mei lo ame̱nyemimei ba wo̱ṅõ ke̱wo̱ babé le̱, wo̱o̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekwe̱a wo̱hewo̱ ní nyeke̱ame̱ ahãa-ame̱; edšake̱ wo̱náá ṅãmei wo̱hã ame̱fẽ ye̱ ta le̱ mli; ni asaṅ dšee nye nyeṅõame̱ nyehãame̱, ni kũle̱ nyeatẽre sõ ko!

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Ni Benyaminbii le̱ fe nakai, ni ame̱mõmo̱ ṅãmei ye̱ ame̱yikule̱ le̱ nā, ye̱ mei ni badšò le̱ ateṅ; ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ te ni ame̱-kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te ame̱šikpõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ame̱yasã mādši le̱, ni ame̱hĩ mli.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ hũ dše dše̱i ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli, mofẽmo te ekutšo ke̱ aweku mli, ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo te ešikpoṅ no̱.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Nakai *gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ maṅtše̱ ko be̱ Israel; mofẽmo feo̱ noni dša ye̱ le̱dientše̱ ehĩe. *

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱w̌e̱ Moab yei: mokome gbe̱i dši Orpa ni mokome hũ gbe̱i dši Rut. Ni ame̱hĩ dše̱i aafe afii nyoṅma.

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: Ni fe ee̱ le̱ Malon ke̱ Kilion hù gboi, ni ebaſe̱ yō le̱ ke̱ke̱ ye̱ ebihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱ ke̱ ewù le̱ se̱.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ke̱-dše̱ heni eyo̱ le̱, ni ešāyei enyo̱ le̱ fata ehe. Ni beni ame̱yi gbe̱ koni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱,

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Naomi kē̱ ešāyei enyo̱ le̱ ake̱: Nyekūa nyese̱ nyeyaā, nyeteṅ mofẽmo aya enye we; Iehowa afenye edšũrõ, take̱ bo̱ni nyefe gbohĩĩ le̱ ke̱ mi edšũrõ le̱!

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Iehowa ahí nyeteṅ mofẽmo aná *heko atá ye̱ ewù we le̱! Ni eſo̱ſō̱ ame̱nã. Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱bole ame̱gbēi ano̱ ni ame̱fó. *

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dabi, ši wo̱ke̱o aate omaṅbii le̱ aṅõ!

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kē̱: Nyekũa nyese̱, mibii! Mẽba nyeke̱mi aate? Ani bihĩĩ ye̱ mimũsũṅ lolo, ni ame̱batšṍmo̱ nyewùmei?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Mibii, nyekũa nyese̱ nyeyaä! edšake̱ migbo̱ tšṍ bo̱ni mayagbã. Ke̱ mikē̱ tete ake̱ miye̱ hĩeno̱kãmo̱, ni mayagbã nū ko nyō ne̱ṅ, ni mafo̱ bihĩĩ tete le̱,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: aso no hewo̱ ni nyeamẽ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ame̱adàra? Alo no hewo̱ ni nyeatšĩ nyehe nā ni nyegbãṅ? Dabi, mibii! Edšake̱ nyesane mīdo̱mi naakpa; edšake̱ *Iehowa nine ke̱mi eye! *Hiob

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱hole ame̱gbēi ano̱ ni ame̱dſa yāfó ekoṅ. Ni Orpa ſo̱ ešāyō le̱ nā; ši Rut le̱, le̱ le̱ ekpe̱te̱ ehe.

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ši Rut kē̱: Kāhĩemi dō ake̱ mišĩo ni mikũ mise̱ ni mifõ ose̱ nyiemo̱! *Ši hefẽhe ni oyaä le̱, mate; ni heni oyahĩ le̱, dše̱i mayahĩ. Omaṅ dši mimaṅ, ni o-Nyoṅmo̱ dši mi hũ mi-Nyoṅmo̱. *

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Heni oogbo ye̱ le̱, dše̱i magbo ye̱, ni dše̱i noṅṅ aafũmi ye̱; Iehowa ke̱mi aye ni eke̱mi aye ekoṅ, ke̱-dšee gbèle ke̱ke̱ aagblami ke̱ oteṅ fĩ!

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Ni beni ena ake̱ eṅmõ eyiṅ kpo̱ ake̱ eke̱le̱ aate le̱, efõle̱ ke̱ wiemo̱.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ame̱ṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ame̱še̱ Betlehem. Ni eba mli ake̱, heni ame̱še̱ Betlehem le̱, maṅ le̱ fẽ bú ye̱ ame̱hewo̱, ni ame̱kē̱: Naomi pam ne̱?

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekatšé̱ami Naomi doṅṅ, moṅ nyetšé̱ami *Mara; edšake̱ Ofe le̱ ke̱mi eye sane ke̱ dšōmo̱ tšṍ! *

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Mite obõ, ši Iehowa ke̱mi ekũ se̱ ke̱-ba eflo; mẽhewo̱ ni nyetšé̱o̱mi Naomi, mi ni Iehowa ke̱mi eye, ni Ofe le̱ eſiſiami ši le̱?

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Naomi ke̱ ešāyō Rut, Moabyō le̱, kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ Moab šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba ne̱; ni beni ame̱ba Betlehem le̱, abõi akoko fō.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Ni na, Boaz dše̱ Betlehem ba, ni ekē̱ nikpalo̱i le̱ ake̱: Iehowa afata nyehe! Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Iehowa adšō̱o!

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ni Boaz ke̱ etšũlo̱ ni eke̱-to enikpalo̱i le̱ ano̱ le̱ ake̱: Nẽ oblayō ne̱?

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ ni aṅõ-to nikpalo̱i le̱ ano̱ le̱ to he ake̱: Moab oblayō ni ke̱ Naomi dše̱ Moab šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ba le̱ ni.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ni ebakē̱: Mīkpao fai, hã ma-nyie nikpalo̱i le̱ ase̱ maye kpe̱kpe̱o ye̱ akoko kei le̱ ateṅ ni mabua nā. Ni eba ni ekã ehe ke̱-dše̱ lebi āhũ ke̱-baši be ne̱; etáá šĩa tũtu ko.

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Boaz kē̱ Rut ake̱: Mibi, ōbo toi? Kāya ni oyaye kpe̱kpe̱o ye̱ mokroko ṅmõši, ni osā okadše̱ bie̱ ne̱ hū, ši moṅ kpe̱te̱mo̱ miblayei le̱ ahe ye̱ bie̱ noṅṅ.

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Keke̱ ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši, ni eho ekũla šikpoṅ, ni eke̱le̱ ake̱: Mēhewo̱ ni mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe, ni otšeo̱ ohĩe ohãami, mi mokpõṅ ne̱?

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ni Boaz to he hãle̱ ake̱: Nii ni ofe ohã ošāyō le̱ ye̱ owù gbēle le̱ se̱ le̱, agbami ſẽ pe̱pēpe̱, bo̱ni *ošĩ otše̱ ke̱ onye ke̱ šikpoṅ ni afo̱o ye̱ no̱ le̱, ni oyiṅ ke̱-ba maṅ ko ní olee oto sá le̱ mli le̱. *

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Iehowa atoö onii ní otšu le̱ nã-dšiaṅ, ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mo fĩdši ašiši abo ni obaba ne̱, awoö nyõmo̱ šišīši!

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Hã mihĩe aba nyam ye̱ ohĩe, minuṅtšo̱! ake̱ nõ kẽ ni oše̱dše mimī, ni oke̱ oweyō ewie ye̱ mlihĩle̱ le̱ nā le̱, tše̱ mi ke̱ oweyei le̱ eko tete yee egbo̱.

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ni beni še̱ niyeli be le̱, Boaz kē̱le̱ ake̱: Tši oba bie̱, ni obaye abolo le̱ eko, ni oke̱ otrõma le̱ atšo̱ ašiṅ le̱ mli! Ni eba ebatá nikpalo̱i le̱ amase̱i; ni ame̱hãle̱ ablefo̱ ni ašĩ le̱ eko, ni ekpe ni eto̱, ni eſe̱ eko.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Ni beni ete ši eyaye kpe̱kpe̱o le̱, Boaz wo eblahĩĩ le̱ akitã ake̱: Nyehãa eyea kpe̱kpe̱o ye̱ kei ni afĩmo̱ le̱ ateṅ hũ, ni nyekanyãfĩale̱.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ nyefãmo̱a eko ye̱ nyamfĩĩ le̱ ahe nyefiea ši nyehãale̱, ni eye kpe̱kpe̱o, ni nyekadše̱ale̱!

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ni eye kpe̱kpe̱o ye̱ ṅmõ le̱ ši ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱nãši, ni egbẽ noni eye kpe̱kpe̱o le̱, ni efe akoko aafe efa kome.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ni ewó ke̱-te maṅ; ni ešãyō le̱ na noni eyakō̱lo̱ le̱. Ni edšie noni eye eto̱ ni ſe̱ le̱ ehãle̱.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ni ešāyō le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ ote oyaye kpe̱kpe̱o ye̱ ṅme̱ne̱, ni nẽghe̱ oya-tšu nii ye̱? Moni tše ehĩe ehão le̱, aadšō̱le̱! Ni egba ešāyō le̱ mo ṅõ ni eyatšu nii ye̱, ni ekē̱: Nū ni miyatšu nii ye̱ eṅõ ṅme̱ne̱ le̱ gbe̱i dši Boaz.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kē̱ ešāyō le̱ ake̱: Iehowa, moni ehãko emo̱bo̱nale̱ se̱ afo ye̱ hĩekãlo̱i ke̱ gbohĩĩ fē ano̱ le̱, aadšõle̱! Ni Naomi kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nū le̱ wo̱ mo ni, wo̱weku le̱ mli niyelo̱i le̱ eko dšile̱.

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ni Rut, Moabyō le̱, kē̱ ake̱: Bēle̱ nohewo̱ ni esā ekēmi ake̱: Kpe̱te̱mo̱ miblahĩĩ le̱ ahe ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ame̱agbe minikpamo̱ le̱ fē nā le̱.

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kē̱ ešāyō Rut ake̱: Ehĩ, mibi, ake̱ oke̱ eblayei le̱ anyie, ni aka-haoö ye̱ mokroko ṅmõši.

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ni ekpe̱te̱ Boaz oblayei le̱ ahe ke̱ kpe̱kpe̱o le̱ yeli āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni agbe akoko ke̱ ṅmã fẽ kpamo̱ nā; ni eke̱ ešāyō le̱ hĩ ši.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ dšu ohe, ni okpa mũ, ni owo otadei, ni okpleke ši ke̱-ya šāhe le̱; kāhã nū le̱ mīyoö ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eeye nii ni eenu noko dã.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Ni aba mli ake̱, ke̱ eyakã ši le̱, okadi ešikãmo̱he le̱, ni oya oyakpa mama le̱ ye̱ enane he, ni oho okã ši, ni le̱dientše̱ eetšõo noni ofe.

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ni ekpleke ši ete šāhe le̱, ni efe bo̱ni ešāyō le̱ kē̱le̱ le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Ni beni Boaz ye nii ni enu noko, ni emī še̱ ehe le̱, ete eyakã ši ye̱ akoko ku le̱ se̱; ni ede̱ke ši ke̱-ha, ni ebakpa mama le̱ ye̱ enane he, ni eho ekã ši.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Bo namoṅ? Ni ekē̱: Mi oweyō Rut ni; *lē̱mo̱ ofĩdši amli oha oweyō no̱; edšake̱ weku le̱ mli niyelo̱ dšio. *

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Iehowa adšōo, mihi! Edšũrõ ni ofe se̱kpē ne̱ fè *tšutšunõ le̱ tete, ake̱ onyiee oblahĩĩ ase̱, ohĩafoi dšio, niiatše̱mei dšio. *

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, mibi, kāše gbeyei! No-fēno ní okē̱o̱ le̱ mafe mahão; edšake̱ mi-maṅbii le̱ fẽ le ake̱ yō kpakpa dšio.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, eye̱ mli le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ weku le̱ mli niyelo̱ dšimi moṅ; ši kẽle̱ niyelo̱ le̱ eko ye̱ ni be̱ṅke̱ fèmi.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Hĩ ši nyõ ne̱ṅ, ni ke̱ dše tše̱re le̱, ke̱ eefe niyelo̱ gbe̱nãnii le̱ ehão le̱, dšo-gbāṅ, efe; ši ke̱dši esumo̱o̱ ake̱ efe le̱, no le̱ gbĩĩabo̱ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kí ne̱, mafe! Kã ši ní dše atše̱re!

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ni ekã ši ye̱ enãdšiaši ke̱-yaši dšetše̱remo̱, ni ete ši dãni abõi mo yōmo̱. Ni nū le̱ kē̱: Moko akale ake̱ yō le̱ eba šāhe le̱!

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Oke̱ mama ni oke̱-ha oyi no̱ le̱ aba ni omõ mli! Ni emõ mli. Ni eka akoko susumo̱ tšenei ekpa ewo mli, ni enõ-tẽrele̱, ni ete mã le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Naomi asked her what had happened, and Ruth told her everything.
translation_verse: Ni beni eba ešāyō le̱ ṅõ le̱, ekē̱: Té emli tamo̱ tēṅ, mibi? Ni egbale̱ noni nū le̱ ſe hãle̱ le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Ehãmi akoko tšenei ekpa ne̱; edšake̱ ekē̱: Oke̱ odē flo akaya ošāyō le̱ ṅõ!

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Hĩ ši diṅṅ, mibi, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni oona bo̱ni sane le̱ nā aayakpa; edšake̱ nū le̱ edšō̱ṅ ehe, dša egbe sane le̱ nā ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ niyelo̱ le̱ kē̱ Boaz ake̱: Hemo̱ ohã ohe! ni edšie etokota le̱.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: asaṅ Rut, Moabyō, ni dši Malon ṅã le̱ hũ mihe le̱, ni etšṍ miṅã, koni matē moni egbo le̱ gbe̱i ši ye̱ egboši šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, beni afe ni moni egbo le̱ gbe̱i akalādše ye̱ enyemimei ateṅ ke̱ emaṅ le̱ mli; nyedši odasefoi ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Ni Boaz ṅõ Rut ni etšṍ eṅã, ni eba eṅõ, *ni Iehowa hã ená mũsũ ni efo̱ binū. *Lal.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ni yei le̱ kē̱ Naomi ake̱: Yidšiemo̱ ahã Iehowa, moni hãã gbošiniyelo̱ abo̱o ṅme̱ne̱ le̱, ni ehí egbe̱i ahehe ye̱ Israel.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Ni ekūṅyei le̱ wole̱ gbe̱i ame̱kē̱: Afo̱ binū ahã Naomi; ni ame̱tšē̱ egbe̱i ake̱ Obed; le̱ dši David tše̱ Išai le̱ tše̱. Mat.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Ni dā afi le̱ ne̱ke̱ nū ne̱ dše̱o̱ emaṅ eyaä *Šilo eyaso̱leo̱ ni ešãa afo̱le ehã Iehowa Zebaot. Ni Hofni ke̱ Pinehas, Eli bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱, yeo̱ oso̱foi ye̱ dše̱i ame̱hãa Iehowa. *Ios.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: ši Hana le̱, ehãale̱ mei enyo̱ gbe̱nā, edšake̱ Hana esumoo̱; ši Iehowa eṅá emũsũ nā.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Ni nakai efeo̱ dā afi: ké̱ ame̱te Iehowa we le̱, no ewoo̱ emli la nakai; ke̱ke̱ le̱ efeo̱le̱ yāfó ni eyee nii.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Ni ewù Elkana kē̱o̱le̱ ake̱: Hana, mẽba ofóo̱? ni mẽba oyee nii? ni mẽba hũ oyeo̱ otšui? Ani mihĩĩ mihãão fè bihĩĩ nyoṅma?

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Ni eyakpa Iehowa fai, ni efó āhũ, edšake̱ ew̌ere̱ eho ehe.

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Hana le̱, etšui mli ewieo̱ ye̱, enābui ke̱ke̱ tšṍmoo̱, ši anua egbē; nohewo̱ le̱ Eli susu ake̱ eto̱ dā̃.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Ni Eli kē̱le̱ ake: Mẽ beyino̱ noṅṅ ni ooto̱ dā̃ ke̱-yaši? Hã owein le̱ atšere̱ ye̱ ohĩe!

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Hã oweyō hĩe aba nyam ye̱ ohĩe! Ke̱ke̱ ni yō le̱ yiṅ ete, ni eyaye nii, ni ehĩe efee to̱tō̱to̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Ni ame̱te ši lebi mãṅkpa, ni ame̱-yadšá ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱, ni ameba ame̱we ye̱ Rama. Ni Elkana le eṅã Hana, ni Iehowa *kaile̱. *

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ekē̱ eše̱o̱ afi nākplo̱ le̱, Hana ena mũsũ ni efo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Samuel; edšake̱ ekē̱: Iehowa ṅõ mibale̱ ye̱.

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni nū Elkana le̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ yiṅ te ni ame̱yašã dā afi afo̱le le̱ ke̱ ešiwō le̱ nō le̱ ame̱hã Iehowa.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Ši Hana le̱ eyaa; edšake̱ ekē̱ ewù le̱ ake̱: Dša atše gbekẽ le̱ fufo̱ dãni mi-ke̱le̱ aate, ní eyapue ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni ehĩ dše̱i kwrā.

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ni ewṅ Elkana kē̱le̱ ake: Femo̱ noni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe; hĩ ši ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní ootšele̱ fufo̱ dã; Iehowa ahã ewiemo̱ le̱ aba mli ke̱ke̱! Ni yō le̱ hĩ ši, ni ehã ebi le̱ fufo̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní etšele̱.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ kē̱: O, minuṅtšo̱, gbĩĩabo̱ ní osusuma hĩe kã ne̱, minuṅtšo̱, midši yō le̱ ni badamo̱ omase̱i ye̱ bĩe̱ ne̱, ni ekpa Iehowa fai le̱.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ gbekẽ ne̱ he fai mikpa le̱; ni Iehowa ehãmi *noni mibale̱ le̱. *K.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ mi hũ *mike̱le̱ eke Iehowa; ake̱le̱ eke Iehowa ewala gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ! Ni ame̱dšá Iehowa ye̱ dše̱i. *K.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Iehowa henye̱lo̱i le̱, aakũmo̱ame̱ dukuduku; eehã nyoṅmo̱ ašimo̱ ye̱ ṅwei awoame̱. Iehowa aakodšo šikpoṅ le̱ nā-gbēbei le̱; ni eke̱ hewale̱ aaha emaṅtše̱ le̱, ni *emo ní efo̱le̱ mù le̱, eewó eklonto le̱ no̱! *Lal.

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: lo oso̱foi le̱ agbe̱nānii ni sa ake̱ ame̱he ye̱ maṅ le̱ deṅ. Kē̱ nū ko ba afo̱lešã le̱, beni ahōo̱ lō le̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ oso̱fo le̱ tšũlo̱ eba ehĩe *lōkpoṅ ke̱ enā nyã-nyõdši etẽ, *

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: ni eke̱-bawoo̱ dadese̱ṅ le̱ lo gbē̱ le̱ lo ṅe̱sũ le̱ lo kukwe̱i le̱ mli; nofẽno ni lōkpoṅ le̱ tĩ ke̱-ba le̱, oso̱fo le̱ ṅõo̱. Nakai ame̱feo̱ Israelbii fẽ ní baä Šilo le̱.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Asaṅ beni anáko ašã *fo̱ le̱ tete le̱, oso̱fo le̱ tšũlo̱ le̱ baä ni ebakē̱o̱ moni šãa afo̱le le̱ ake̱: Hã lõ ní ayašĩ ahã oso̱fo lei edšake̱ ehee lō ní ahō ye̱ odeṅ, ši eṅmõṅ moṅ. *

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Ni kē̱ mo le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Abašã afo̱le amrõ ne̱ noṅṅ, koni obaṅõ bo̱fẽbo̱ ní osusuma taoo̱ le̱! ekē̱o̱le̱ ake̱: Dabi, ši hãmi nyoṅlo, ni ké̱ dšee nakai le̱, no le̱ mako̱ eka nā!

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ oblahĩĩ le̱ anõša le̱ da kple ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; edšake̱ ame̱buu Iehowa afo̱le le̱.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ enye kpe̱o̱ atade yū pe̱mpe̱ō ko ehãale̱, ni eke̱-bahãale̱ dā afi, ke̱ eke̱ ewù ba afi afo̱lešã le̱.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Si Iehowa basra Hana, ni ená mũsũ, ni efo̱ bihĩī etẽ ke̱ biyei enyo̱. Ni gbekẽ Samuel le̱ *da ye̱ Iehowa hĩe. *Luk.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Nyekafea nakai, mibii! ši dšee sane kpakpa ko minne̱ ne̱; nyemīhã Iehowa maṅ le̱ mītõ!

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Ši gbekẽ Samuel le̱ *hĩe dale̱, ni esa Iehowa ke̱ gbomei fẽ hĩe hũ. *Luk.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Eye̱ṅ moṅ ake̱ *mikē̱ ake̱ owe le̱ ke̱ otše̱ we le̱ aanyie mihĩe ke̱-ya nāno̱; ši agbe̱ne̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ene̱ akagbalemi fō̃ṅfõ! edšake̱ mei ní woo̱ mihĩe nyam le̱, mawo ame̱hĩe nyam; ši mei ní gbeo̱ mihe guo̱ le̱, abuname̱ ahãṅ nokonoko. *

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Na, *gbĩĩ mība, ni mafo onine ke̱ otše̱ we le̱ nine, ní nūmo ko akahĩ owe le̱; *

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: ni edšudši fẽ ni aafe Israel le̱ se̱ le̱ obana no amanehũlũ ni aaba šihīle̱hele̱ no̱; ni nūmo ko ehĩṅ owe le̱ gbĩkogbĩko.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ *mibuleṅ omei le̱ fẽ seši ke̱-dše̱ṅ mĩfo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he, koni ohĩṅme̱ii adſāra ní osusuma agbo̱dšo̱, ni bii ní afo̱ ye̱ owe le̱ fẽ aagboi ye̱ ame̱blahĩaṅ. *

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Ni noni baba obihĩī enyo̱ Hofni ke̱ Pinehas le̱ no̱ ne̱, no aafe okadi ahão: *ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ ame̱bagboi gbĩ kome! *

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Ni matē oso̱fo ano̱kwafo ko ši ma-hã mihe: noni yo̱ mitšui ke̱ midſēṅmo̱ mli le̱, no eefe; ni mamã šĩa ni mã ši šiṅṅ mahãle̱, ni eenyie ye̱ moni mafo̱le̱ mũ le̱ hĩe dā.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱ mofẽmo ni aaſe̱ ye̱ owe le̱ aaba abakotole̱ ye̱ dſie̱te̱i kuku ko lo abolo akwābo̱ ko hewo̱, ni eekē̱: Mīkpao fai ní oṅõmi owo oso̱foi anitšumo̱ le̱ eko mli, beni afe ní maná abolo atrõma ko maye!

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: ni Nyoṅmo̱ kane le̱ náko agbo, ni Samuel te eyakā ši ye̱ Iehowa so̱lemo̱tšũ le̱ṅ heni Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa tšé̱ Samuel, ni ehere no̱ ekē̱: Nami!

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Ni eša foi ke̱-te Eli ṅõ ni ekē̱: Nami, edšake̱ ōtšé̱mi! Ni ekē̱: Mitšé̱koö, kù ose̱ ni oyakã ši ekoṅ! Ni ekũ ese̱ eyakā ši.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa sā tšé̱le̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Samuel! Ni Samuel te ši ni eyiṅ ete Eli ṅõ ni ekē̱: Nami, edšake̱ ōtšé̱mi! Ni ekē̱: Mitšé̱koö, mibi; kù ose̱ ni oyakã ši ekoṅ.

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: No mli le̱ Samuel náko ale Iehowa, ni asaṅ anáko adšie Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ kpo atšõle̱.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa sā tšé̱ Samuel noni tĩa šii etẽ. Ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ete Eli ṅõ ni ekē̱: Nami, edšake̱ ōtšé̱mi! Ke̱ke̱ ni Eli bayo se̱ ake̱ Iehowa ni tšé̱o̱ gbekẽ le̱.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Eli kē̱ Samuel ake̱: Yakã ši, ni aaba mli ake̱, ke̱dši etšé̱o le̱, okē̱ ake̱: Wiemo̱, Iehowa! ši otšũlo̱ mībo toi! Ni Samuel te eyakã ši ye̱ ewō̱he le̱.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa ba ni ebadamo̱ ši, ni etšé̱le̱ tamo̱ tšutšu le̱ ake̱: Samuel, Samuel! Ni Samuel kē̱: Wiemo̱, ši otšũlo̱ mībo toi!

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Samuel ake̱: Na, mibafe noko ye̱ Israel pam, ni mofẽmo ní aanu he le̱, etoii enyo̱ le̱ fẽ mli aafele̱ heṅṅ.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩ le̱ mahã nibii fẽ ní miwie ye̱ Eli we le̱ he le̱ aba mli, ke̱-dše̱ šišidšē ke̱-yaši nāgbē.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mikē̱le̱ ake̱ makodšo ewe le̱ ke̱-ate nāno̱, ye̱ nōša ní ele le̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ edše ame̱he yakagbomei, ni etutuu ehĩe ewooame̱.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Ni nohewo̱ le̱ mikã Eli we le̱ yino̱ kitã ake̱: Ke̱dši ake̱ gbē-afo̱le lo niyenii-afo̱le ko aakpãtã ahā Eli we le̱ nõša le̱ ke̱-yaši nāno̱ fĩ!

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ni Eli tšē̱ Samuel ni ekē̱: Samuel, mibi! Ni ekē̱: Nami!

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mẽ wiemo̱ Iehowa ke̱o wie le̱? Kāšiumĩ no̱; ke̱dši ošiumi wiemo̱i fẽ ni eke̱o wie le̱ eko no̱ le̱, Nānyoṅmo̱ afeo ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel dšadše wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ etšõle̱, ni ešiuule̱ eko no̱. Ni ekē̱: Iehowa ni; *noni hĩ ye̱ ehĩe le̱, efe! *

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel bada, ni Iehowa ke̱le̱ ye̱, ni ehã ewiemo̱i le̱ ekomeflo afe yaka.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Ni Israel fẽ ní dše̱ Dan āhũ ke̱-yaſie Beeršeba le̱ ná le ake̱ Samuel le̱ Iehowa gbalo̱ ano̱kwafo ni.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kã he dšieo̱ ehe kpo ye̱ Šilo; edšake̱ Iehowa tšṍo̱ ewiemo̱ le̱ no̱ edšieo̱ ehe kpo etšõo̱ Samuel ye̱ Šilo.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ tšũ ate Šilo, ni ayawó Iehowa Zebaot ni táa *kerubim le̱ ano̱ le̱ kpăùmo̱ adeka le̱ ke̱-ba. Ni Hofni ke̱ Pinehas, Eli bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱, dši mei ni ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ kpãṅmo̱ adeka le̱ yo̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iehowa kpãṅmo̱ adeka le̱ baše̱ nsra le̱ mli le̱, Israel fẽ bo̱ oše wā, ni ehã šikpoṅ hoso.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ nu ošebō̱ le̱, ni ame̱kē̱: Té ošebō̱ ní gbē̱o̱ wa ye̱ Hebribii le̱ ansra le̱ mli ne̱ šišiṅ? Ni ame̱-baná ame̱le ake̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ eba nsra le̱ṅ.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Filistibii le̱ še gbeyei, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ eba nsra le̱ṅ! Ni ame̱sā ame̱kē̱: Wo̱na noko! edšake̱ ke̱-dše̱ kpla ne̱ afeko ne̱ke̱ noko da!

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Wo̱na noko! namo aadšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ ne̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱i kekenami ne̱ adeṅ? Mene̱mei dši Nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ní ke̱ haomo̱i sro̱toi hao Mizraimbii le̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ ne̱ le̱!

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Nyewadšea nyehe, ni nyefea hĩĩ, nye Filistibii, koni nyekasúmo̱ Hebribii le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni *ame̱súmo̱nye le̱! Nyefea hĩĩ, ni nyewua! *Kodš.

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ašõ, ni Hofni ke̱ Pinehas, Eli bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱, nyõ.

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni Benyaminnyo ko ša foi ke̱-dše̱ ta le̱ nā, ni eba Šilo nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ, ke̱ etade ní egbla, ke̱ eyiteṅ sũ.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Ni beni eba le̱, na, Eli tá sẽi no̱ ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ toi ēsra; edšake̱ etšui enyõõ emli ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ hewo̱. Ni nū le̱ ba mã le̱ṅ ni ebagba, ni maṅ le̱ fẽ wo yăra.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Ni nū le̱ kē̱ Eli ake̱: Midši moni dše̱ ta le̱ nā ba le̱, ni ṅme̱ne̱ noṅṅ midšo foi ke̱-dše̱ ta le̱ nā. Ni ekē̱: Mibi, tē emli tamo̱ tẽṅ?

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni etšĩ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ tã pe̱ le̱, ekpa ke̱-dše̱ esẽi le̱ no̱ eyagbē ese̱gbe̱ ye̱ agbó le̱ he, ni ekue̱ kũ, ni egbo; edšake̱ edši nūmo ni ehe tšī le̱. Ni ekodšo Israel afii nyoṅmai-edſe̱.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Ni ešāyō ní dši Pinehas ṅã le̱ hĩe mũsũ, ni eše̱ efo̱mo̱be etã; ni beni enu sane le̱, ake̱ ašõ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱, ni ešānū ke̱ ewù fẽ egboi le̱, eho esõ ši ni efo̱; edšake̱ kō̃mo̱ ta ehe.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Ni beni eheo̱ egbo le̱, yei ní da-mo̱ ehewo̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: *Kāše gbeyei, edšake̱ binū ofo̱ ne̱! Ši efoo mli, ni asaṅ eke̱ etsui eṅmẽẽ no̱. *

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ši Filistibii le̱ šõ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱, ni ame̱ke̱-dše̱ Eben-Ezer ke̱-te Ašdod.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ wó Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ke̱-te Dagon we le̱, ni ame̱ke̱-yamã *Dagon mase̱i. *Kodš.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ lebi mā̃ṅkpa, beni Ašdodbii le̱ te ši le̱, na, Dagon ekpa egbē ši, ni ehĩe bu šikpoṅ ye̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ hĩe. Ni ame̱wó Dagon no̱, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ mã emā̃he le̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ lebi mā̃ṅkpa, beni ame̱te ši ekoṅ le̱, na, Dagon ekpa egbe ši ekoṅ, ni ehĩe bu ši ye̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ hĩe, ni Dagon yitšo ke̱ enidši enyo̱ le̱ fẽ dſere kpoku le̱ no̱; Dagon kuku le̱ ke̱ke̱ eſe̱.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Dagon oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ni yaä Dagon we le̱ enāā Dagon kpoku le̱ no̱ ye̱ Ašdod ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa nine tši ye̱ Ašdodbii le̱ ano̱, ni ekpãtã ame̱hĩe, ni ehã *ame̱dšedšē gbuṅtuii, Ašdod ke̱ ehe kpokpai le̱. *Lal.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Ašdod hĩĩ le̱ na ake̱ bo̱ni tamo̱ ne̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱: Akahã Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ mīhĩ wo̱ṅõ, edšake̱ enineši wa tšṍ ye̱ wo̱ke̱ wo̱nyoṅmo̱ Dagon le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšũ ni ayabua Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-ba ame̱ṅõ ni ame̱kē̱: Té wo̱o̱fe Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ he tēṅ? Ni ame̱here no̱ ake̱: Áwó Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ ke̱-ya Gat. Ni awó Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ ke̱-te Gat.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ni ame̱hã ake Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ te Ekron. Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ se̱ Ekron le̱, Ekronbii le̱ blo̱ ame̱kē̱: Ame̱ke̱ Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ eba wo̱ṅõ, koni ame̱ke̱-bagbewo̱ ke̱ wo̱maṅbii le̱.

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱tšũ ayabua Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ fē nā ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱-kē̱: Nyehãa ake̱ Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ adeka le̱ ayaä, ní ake̱-kū se̱ ke̱-ya heni edše̱, koni ekabagbewo̱ ke̱ wo̱maṅbii le̱! Edšake̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ edšidšā ni ye̱ gbeyei; Nyoṅmo̱ nine etsī naakpa ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Ni mei ní gboii le̱, ahă ame̱dšedšē gbuṅtuii, ni maṅ le̱ blo̱mo̱ le̱ te ši ke̱-te ṅwei.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa adeka le̱ hĩ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nyõdši kpawo.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyefea nyegbuṅtuii le̱ ano̱ ke̱ nyekwakwei ní fiteo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ hũ ano̱, ni nyeke̱ anumnyam aha Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; ekole̱ eebagbo̱dšo̱ enine mli ye̱ nye ke̱ nyenyoṅmo̱i le̱ ke̱ nyešikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: ni nyewo Iehowa adeka le̱ ni nyeṅõ-mã ſīli le̱ no̱; ni nyeṅõ šika dſinei le̱ ní nyeke̱-bahãle̱ ake̱ sõ-afo̱le le̱ nyewo adeka fiō ko mli nyemã emase̱i, ni nyedšiele̱ gbe̱ ni eya.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Ni na, ke̱dši etšṍ ehũsũ le̱ no̱ gbe̱ ke̱-te Bet-Šemeš le̱, bēle̱ le̱ efewo̱ ne̱ke̱ efõṅ kpeteṅkple ne̱; ši ké̱ dšee nakai le̱, bĕle̱ wo̱ná wo̱le ake̱ dšee le̱ enine haowo̱ le̱, ši ošrã ko ke̱ke̱ bašrãwo̱.

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Ni gbomei le̱ fe nakai, ni ame̱ṅõ tšinayei enyo̱ ní hãa fufo̱, ni ame̱fīmo̱-ame̱ ame̱kpe̱te̱ ſīli le̱ nā, ni ame̱ṅã́mo̱ ame̱bii le̱ ayi ye̱ šĩa;

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: ni ame̱wó Iehowa adeka le̱ ame̱mã ſīli le̱ no̱ ke̱ adeka fiō le̱ ni šika kwakwei le̱ ke̱ ame̱gbuṅtuii le̱ aheno̱i le̱ yo̱ mli le̱.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Ni tšinai le̱ ko̱ gbe̱ trẽnē̃ ke̱-tšṍ Bet-Šemeš gbe̱ le̱, ni amenyie gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-te, ni beni ame̱yaä le̱ ame̱hĩe blo̱mo̱, ni ame̱gbáá ninedšũrõ lo abe̱ku; ni Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ nyie ame̱se̱ ke̱-haši Bet-Šemeš hũsũ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Ni Bet-Šemešbii le̱ mīkũ ame̱ṅmā̃ ni eba le̱ ye̱ dšō̱ le̱ṅ; ni beni ame̱yahole ame̱hĩṅme̱ii ano̱ le̱, ame̱na adeka le̱, ni ame̱nyá ake̱ ame̱na.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Ni beni Filistibii le̱ alumei enumo̱ le̱ na le̱, ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ame̱ba Ekron nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ni šika gbuṅtuii ní Filistibii le̱ ke̱-bahã ní aṅō-fe sõ-afo̱le ahã Iehowa le̱ ne̱: Ašdod nõ ekome, Gaza nõ ekome, Aškelon nõ ekome, Gat nõ ekome, Ekron nõ ekome;

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: ke̱ šika kwakwei le̱ ye̱ Filistibii le̱ amãdši le̱ fẽ ni dši lume̱i enumo̱ lo̱ anii le̱ ayikule̱ nā, mãdši ní atſa gbogbo awo ame̱he le̱ ke̱ kose̱ akrowai le̱ fẽ. Ni te̱ kpeteṅkple le̱ ní ake̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ mã no̱ ye̱ Iošua, Bet-Šemešnyo le̱, ṅmõ le̱ṅ le̱ yeo̱ odase ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Ni Bet-šemešbii le̱ kē̱: Namo po anyẽ Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱ kroṅkroṅ ne̱ hĩe adamo̱? ni namo ṅõ eedše wo̱ṅõ ke̱-ate?

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Kiriat-Iearimbii le̱ aṅõ ayakē̱: Filistibii le̱ ke̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ ekũ se̱ eba ekoṅ; nyebaä ni nyebawóa ke̱-yaä nyeṅõ!

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel kē̱ Israel we le̱ fẽ ake̱: Ke̱dši nyeke̱ nyetšui fẽ mīkũ nyese̱ ke̱-ba Iehowa ṅõ le̱, no le̱ *nyedšiea maṅse̱ nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ke̱ Aštarot le̱ ke̱-dšea nyeteṅ, ni nyesãa nyetšuii nye-hãa Iehowa, ní nyesúmo̱ale̱ kometō, ni eedšienye ke̱-adše̱ Filistibii le̱ adeṅ. *

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israelbii le̱ dšie *Baalim ke̱ Aštarot ame̱ſie, ni ame̱súmo̱ Iehowa kome. *Kodš.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Nyebuaä Israel fẽ nā ye̱ *Mizpa, ni makpa Iehowa fai mahãnye. *

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ni ame̱babua ame̱he nā ye̱ Mizpa, ni ame̱ye̱ nu ni ame̱fo̱se ame̱ſie ši ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni ame̱ye buada ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱kē̱ ye̱ dše̱i ake̱: Wo̱fe Iehowa šiši eša! Ni Samuel kodšo Israelbii le̱ ye̱ Mizpa.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Ni beni Filistibii le̱ nu ake̱ Israelbii le̱ ebabua ame̱he nā ye̱ Mizpa le̱, Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ fã ke̱-banina Israel. Ni beni Israelbii le̱ nu he le̱, ame̱še Filistibii le̱ agbeyei.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ kē̱ Samuel ake̱: *Kāfõ blo̱mo̱ ke̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, tšé̱mo̱ ke̱ wo̱ hãmo̱, koni ehere wo̱yiwala ye̱ Filistibii le̱ adeṅ! *

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Ni beni Samuel šãa šã-afo̱le le̱, Filistibii le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱ ni ame̱ke̱ Israelbii le̱ abawu. Ši Iehowa hã nyoṅmo̱ šimo̱ wā wo Filistibii le̱ ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni eſieame̱, ni agbeame̱ ye̱ Israel hĩe.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fã ke̱-dše Mizpa, ni ame̱nyie Filistibii le̱ ase̱, ni ame̱tſiaame̱ nii āhũ ke̱-yaši Bet-Kar šiši.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ mãdšimãdši le̱ ni Filistibii le̱ šõ ye̱ Israel deṅ le̱, akpale ahā Israel ekoṅ ke̱-dše̱ Ekron āhũ ke̱-yaſie Gat, ni ame̱he šikpõdši le̱ hũ Israel šõ ye̱ Filistibii le̱ adeṅ. Ni toiṅdšo̱le̱ ba Israel ke̱ Amorbii le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kodšo Israel ewala gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Ni dã afi le̱ eyakpaã ši ke̱-nyieo̱ Betel ke̱ Gilgal ke̱ Mizpa ni ekodšoo̱ Israel ye̱ dše̱mei fẽ.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Ni ekũo̱ ese̱ ke̱-baã Rama, edšake̱ dše̱i ewe yo̱, ni dše̱i noṅṅ ekodšoo̱ Israel ye̱; ni emã afo̱lešãlate̱ ehã Iehowa ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Ni ekromo̱bi le̱ gbe̱i dši Ioel, ni ebi ni dši enye̱ le̱ gbe̱i dši Abia; ame̱-dši kodšolo̱i ye̱ Beeršeba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Ši ebihĩĩ le̱ enyiee egbè̱i le̱ ano̱, ši moṅ ame̱yadi se̱námo̱ se̱, ni ame̱hehēo̱ nyōṅnii, ni ame̱tšṍo̱ kodšomo̱ hĩe ame̱-buo̱ ši.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel onukpai le̱ fẽ bua ame̱he nā, ni ame̱ba Samuel ṅõ ye̱ *Rama, *

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Ši sane le̱ eṅõõ Samuel nā, beni ame̱kē̱ ake̱: Hãwo̱ maṅtše̱ ní akodšowo̱ le̱. Ni Samuel so̱le etšé̱ Iehowa.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Bo̱ pe̱ ní ame̱fe ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ no̱ ni midšĩeame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim āhũ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ni ame̱ṅõ-kwami, ni ame̱yasúmo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei le̱, nakai noṅṅ ame̱-ṅõ-feo̱ bo hũ ne̱.

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Ni Samuel dšadše Iehowa wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ etšõ maṅ le̱ ni bio̱le̱ maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Maṅtše̱ ní baye nyeno̱ le̱ gbe̱nā ne̱: Eeṅõ nyebihĩĩ le̱ ehã ehe, ni eeṅõame̱ eto eſīlii ahe ni ame̱kwe̱ ekpo̱ṅo̱i le̱, ni ame̱dšodšō foi ke̱-nyie eſīlii le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Ni nyebiyei le̱ hũ eeṅô-fe tšofã-ke̱-ṅma futulo̱i ke̱ nihōlo̱i ke̱ abološãlo̱i.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Ni eeṅõ nyeṅmõdši ke̱ nyeweintromi ke̱ nyemũtromi ní hĩ fè fẽ le̱ ehã etšũdši.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Ni nyenidũmo̱nii le̱ ke̱ nyeweintromi amli nii le̱ amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ eeṅõ ni eke̱-ahã epiafoi ke̱ etšũ-dši le̱.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ni nyetšũdši ke̱ nyeweyei ke̱ nye-blahĩĩ fe̱fe̱dši ke̱ nyetedšii eeṅõ ni eke̱-atšu enii.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Eeṅõ nyetōi le̱ amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome; ni nyeatšṍmo̱ etšũdši.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ nyeablo̱ ye̱ nyemaṅtše̱ ní nyetao nyehã nyehe le̱ he-wo̱, ni Iehowa efoṅ nyedāṅ!

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: koni we̱ hũ wo̱tamo̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ fẽ, ní wo̱maṅtše̱ le̱ akodšowo̱, ni efã ke̱-nyie wo̱hĩe, ni ewu wo̱tai le̱!

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Ni beni Samuel nu maṅ le̱ wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ le̱, edšadše etšõ Iehowa.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ Samuel ake̱: *Bo ame̱gbẽ toi, ni owo maṅtše̱ ohãame̱! Ni Samuel kē̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ ake̱: Nyeteṅ mo-fẽmo aya le̱dientše̱ emaṅ! *K.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱ba Zuf šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, Saul kē̱ eblanyo ní ke̱le̱ nyie le̱ ake̱: Ba ni wo̱kũ wo̱se̱ wo̱ya; ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, *mitše̱ aafõ tedšiyei le̱ ase̱dī, ní etšui aabaye ye̱ wo̱ moṅ wo̱hewo̱! *

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo ko ye̱ ne̱ke̱ mã ne̱ṅ, ni edši nū ko ni hĩe yo̱ nyam; nofẽno ní ekē̱o̱ le̱, ebaă mli pe̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ hã wo̱te dše̱i; ekole̱ eetšõwo̱ gbe̱ ko ní wo̱tšṍ no̱.

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ eblanyo le̱ ake̱: Ši na, ke̱dši wo̱te le̱, meni ne̱ke̱ wo̱ke̱-ate ayahã nū le̱? edšake̱ abolo le̱ etã ye̱ wo̱nii le̱ amli, ni noko be̱ ní wo̱ke̱-ate ayake Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱; meni wo̱yo̱?

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ni oblanyo le̱ sā to he ehã Saul ake̱: Na, mihĩe dſie̱te̱i šekel mlidšāi edſe̱ mli ekome, mike̱ no ahã Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱, koni etšõwo̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ eblanyo le̱ ake̱: Owiemo̱ le̱ hĩ; ba ni wo̱te! Ni ame̱yiṅ ke̱-te mã le̱ṅ, heni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Beni ame̱hereo̱ ṅmeṅme le̱ ke̱-yaä mã le̱ṅ le̱, ame̱na oblayei mīdše kpo ame̱yaye̱ nu, ni ame̱biame̱ ake̱: Ninalo̱ le̱ ye̱ bie̱ lo?

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ni ame̱to he ame̱hãame̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Eye̱, na, le̱ eyaä ye̱ ohĩe le̱; ohe afe oyá agbe̱ne̱, edšake̱ eba mã le̱ṅ ṅme̱ne̱, edšake̱ mã le̱ṅ bii le̱ bašã afo̱le ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ he groṅṅ le̱.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Kè̱ nyebote mã le̱ṅ pe̱ le̱, nyeanale̱, dãni ekwo̱ ke-ya he groṅṅ le̱ eyaye nii. Ši dša ete dãni maṅ le̱ yeo̱ nii; edšake̱ le̱ ebadšō̱o̱ afo̱le le̱ no̱, dãni mei ní akpē le̱ yeo̱ nii le̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ nyeyaä, edšake̱ he mli noṅṅ ni nyeanale̱ ne̱.

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yiṅ ke̱-te mã le̱ṅ. Ni beni ame̱se̱ maṅ le̱ teṅ le̱, na, Samuel ke̱ame̱ bakpe ní ẽya he groṅṅ le̱.

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: Wó̱ aafe bene̱ yino̱ le̱ mibatšũ nū ko ní dše̱ Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba oṅõ, ni ofo̱le̱ mū owo mimaṅ Israel le̱ no̱ lumo̱, koni ehere mimaṅ le̱ yiwala ke̱-dše̱ Filistibii le̱ adeṅ; edšake̱ mikwe̱ mimaṅ le̱, ši ame̱blo̱mo̱ le̱ eše̱ miṅõ.

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul tši be̱ṅke̱ Samuel ye̱ agbó le̱ mli, ni ekē̱: Ofai ne̱, tšõmo̱mi heni ninalo̱ le̱ we yo̱.

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel here Saul no̱ ni ekē̱: Midši ninalo̱ le̱; tšṍ mihĩe ke̱-ya he groṅṅ le̱, ši nyeke̱mi baye nii ṅme̱ne̱; ni wó̱ lebi le̱ mawoö gbe̱ ní oya, ni magbao nofẽno ni yo̱ otšui mli.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Ni ke̱ ka otedšiyei le̱ ní lãdše ṅme̱ne̱ dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ ahewo̱ṅ le̱, kāye otšui; edšake̱ anaame̱. Ni namo nõ dší Israel nitaomo̱nii le̱ fẽ? Ani dšee bo ke̱ otše̱ we le̱ fẽ nõ ni?

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Ni Saul here ne̱ ni ekē̱: Ani dšee Benyaminnyo dšimi, ni Israel akutšei le̱ amli noni dši bibiō fè fẽ le̱ mli midše̱, ni miweku le̱ dši *bibiō fè Benyamin akutšo le̱ mli wekui le̱ fẽ? ni mẽhewo̱ oke̱mi wieo̱ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ne̱ mo̱? *

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Ni Samuel ṅõ Saul ke̱ eblanyo le̱, ni eke̱ame̱ te asa le̱ no̱, ni ehã ameyatrá mei ni akpēame̱ niyeli ni še̱o̱ gbomei nyoṅmai-etẽ le̱ ayitšo.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Ni nibōlo̱ te̱ ṅõ lõ ſuo̱ le̱ ke̱ noni tša no̱ le̱ ni eke̱-mā Saul hīe. Ní ekē̱: Noni aṅõ-to ahão ne̱; ṅõ mā ohĩe ni oye; edšake̱ bo ake̱-to ahā beni aké̱mi ake̱: Mikpẽ mei le̱. Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul ke̱ Samuel ye nii nakai gbĩ le̱.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱dše̱ he groṅṅ le̱ ame̱kpleke ši ke̱-ba mā le̱ṅ le̱, eke̱ Saul wie ye̱ tšũ le̱ yiteṅ.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Ni ame̱te ši mãṅkẽ mrã, ni eba mli ake̱, beni dše bõi tše̱remo̱ le̱, Samuel tšé̱ Saul ye̱ tšũ le̱ yiteṅ ni ekē̱: Te ši ní mawoõ gbe̱ ni oya! Ni Saul te ši, ni eke̱ Samuel fẽ dše kpo.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱kplekee̱ ši ke̱-yaã maṅ le̱ klotia le̱, Samuel kē̱ Saul ake̱: Kē̱-mo̱ oblanyo le̱ ni ebaho eyayi wo̱hĩe ni ekitē; Si bo le̱ damo̱ ši, koni mahã onu Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱i!

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Kē̱ odše̱ miṅõ ṅme̱ne̱ ni ōya le̱, ooyanina hĩĩ enye̱ ye̱ *Rahel fū̃he le̱ ye̱ Benyamin hũsũ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Zelza, ni ame̱akē̱o ake̱: Tedšiyei le̱ ní oteame̱ taomo̱ le̱, anaame̱; ni na, otše̱ efo te-dšiyei le̱ ahe dſẽṅmo̱, ni etsui miye ye̱ nyehewo̱, ekē̱: Té mafe tēṅ ye̱ mibi le̱ hewo̱ṅ? *

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ le̱ kē̱ odše dše̱i ni ōya ohĩe ni oyaše̱ Tabor tšo kple le̱ he le̱, oke hĩĩ etẽ ni yaä Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ ye̱ Betel aakpe; mokome tēre abotiabii etẽ, ni mokome hũ tēre abolo akwābo̱i etẽ, ni mokome hũ tẽre wein woloto̱ kome.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱aflao, ni ame̱ahão aboloi enyo̱, ní ohe ye̱ ame̱deṅ.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ aabayi ono̱, ni oke̱ame aagba, ni aatšṍo gbomo kroko. K.

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni etšṍ ehe ní edše Samuel ṅõ eyaã le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ hãle̱ tšuĩ kroko; ni nakai okadii le̱ fẽ ha mli nakai gbĩ le̱.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱še̱ dše̱i ye̱ goṅkpo̱ le̱ he le̱, na, gbalo̱i asafoku ke̱le̱ bakpe; ni *Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ bayi eno̱ ni egba ye̱ ame̱teṅ. *

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ni beni egba egbe nā le̱, eba he groṅṅ le̱.

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul tše̱kwẽ le̱ kē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ gbāmi noni Samuel kē̱nye!

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Israelbii le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Mikpla Israel ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim ke̱-ba, ni midšie-nye ke̱-dše̱ Mizraimbii adeṅ ke̱ maṅtše̱-yelii fẽ ni gba nyenā le̱ adeṅ;

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: ši nye le̱, ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ *nyekwa nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni le̱dientše̱ ehere nyeyiwala ke̱-dše̱ nyemanehũlũi ke̱ nye-fĩmo̱i fẽ amli le̱, ni nyekē̱le̱ ake̱: Dabi, ši wo maṅtše̱ ohãwe̱! Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyebadamo̱a Iehowa hĩe ye̱ nyekutšei ke̱ nyekpekpei le̱ anã! *

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ni beni eke̱ Benyamin akutšo le̱ be̱ṅke̱ ye̱ ewekui anā le̱, ako̱ Matribii aweku le̱, ni ako̱ Saul, Kiš bi le̱; ši beni ame̱taole̱ le̱, ame̱naale̱.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱sā ame̱yabi Iehowa ekoṅ ake̱: Ani nū le̱ eba bĩe̱ lo? Ni Iehowa kē̱: Na, eyatẽ ehe ye̱ nibii le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ša foi ni ame̱yaṅõle̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i. Ni heni eba ebadamo̱ mei le̱ ateṅ le̱, eke̱ fè mofẽmo ke̱-dše̱ ekõṅ no̱ āhũ ke̱-te ṅwei.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ake̱: Nyekwe̱a moni Iehowa ehala le̱; edšake̱ mokomoko tamo̱o̱le̱ ye̱ maṅbii le̱ fẽ ateṅ! Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ bo̱ oše ame̱kē̱: *Maṅtše̱ yi aná wala! *

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel gbaame̱ *maṅtăe̱-yeli le̱ gbe̱nānii le̱, ni eṅmã ewo wolo mli, ni eṅõ-ṅmẽ Iehowa hĩe. Ni Samuel dšie maṅ le̱ fẽ gbe̱, ni mofẽmo te ewe. *

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Ni Saul hũ yiṅ ete ewe ye̱ Gibea; ni kãkãlo̱i ní Nyoṅmo̱ etra ame̱tšuii amli le̱ ke̱le̱ te.
