english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Ši *yakagbomei komei kē̱: Té aafe tēṅ ní mone̱ aahere wo̱yiwalaṅ? Ni ame̱-gbe ehe guo̱, ni ame̱bakeele̱ noko. Ši efe tamo̱ noni enuu. *

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Nahaš, Amonnyo le̱, fã ke̱-ba, ni ebabo̱ nsra ewo *Iabeš-Gilead he. Ni Iabeš hĩĩ le̱ fẽ kē̱ Nahaš ake̱: Oke̱-wo̱ akpãṅ, koni wo̱súmo̱o. *

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Ni Nahaš, Amonnyo le̱, kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ké̱ nyeahã *mafãme̱ nyefẽ nyeninedšũrõ hĩṅme̱ii le̱, dša no dãni mike̱nye aakpãṅ, ni maṅõ-fe kpa mafõ ši mahã Israel mū le̱ fẽ. *Ier.

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iabeš onukpai le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nmẽwo̱ gbe̱ ke̱-yaši bie̱ gbĩĩ kpawo, koni wo̱tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-ya Israel mãdši le̱ fẽ no̱, ni ke̱dši anáá moko abaherewo̱ le̱, koni wo̱dše kpo wo̱ba oṅõ!

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni bo̱foi le̱ ba Saul maṅ Gibea le̱, ni ame̱badšadše sane le̱ ye̱ maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ; ni maṅ le̱ fẽ hole ame̱gbēi ano̱ ni ame̱fó.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Ni na, Saul nyie tšinai ase̱ ke̱-dše̱ ṅãno̱ ke̱-ba; ni Saul kē̱: Meni feo̱ maṅ le̱ ní ame̱fófṍo̱ ne̱? Ni ame̱gbale̱ Iabeš-bii le̱ asane le̱.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ni emõmo̱ tšinai enyo̱ eflo ame̱mli kukudši, ni eṅõ-hã bo̱foi le̱ ni ame̱ke̱-yakpa Israel mãdši le̱ fẽ no̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Mofẽmo ni baa ebanyiee Saul ke̱ Samuel se̱ le̱, bo̱ni abafe etšinai ne̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa he ṅmiṅmi mõ maṅ le̱, ni ame̱dše kpo ke̱-ba tamo̱ nū kome. Kodš.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱ bo̱foi le̱ ni ba le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni nyeyakē̱ Iabeš-Gileadbii le̱ ne̱: Wó̱, beni hũlũ kē̱ enā waä le̱, aahere nyeyiwala! Ni bo̱foi le̱ ba ame̱bakē̱ Iabeš hĩĩ le̱, ni ame̱tšui nyõ ame̱mli.

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ Saul dša maṅ le̱ mli kui etẽ, ni ame̱ba nsra le̱ teṅ ye̱ lebi būbe le̱ mli, ni ame̱tſia Amonbii le̱ anii ke̱-yaši ſane fintī̃; ni eba mli ake̱ mei ní ſe̱ le̱ gbe̱ ſã āhũ po ní ame̱teṅ mei enye̱ ſe̱e̱ ye̱ hekome.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ kē̱ Samuel ake̱: Namo dši moni kē̱ ake̱: Aso *Saul po baye we̱no̱ maṅtše̱ lo le̱? Oke̱ nakai gbomei le̱ aba ní wo̱gbeame̱! *

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Ši Saul kē̱: Akagbe gbomo ko ṅme̱ne̱; edšake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ *Iehowa etšu yiwalaheremo̱nĩĩ ye̱ Israel. *

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Nyebaä ni wo̱tea *Gilgal ní wo̱yafe maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ehẽ ye̱ dše̱i! *

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ fẽ te Gilgal, ni ame̱yawo Saul maṅtše̱ ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ye̱ Gilgal; ni ame̱šã šidā-afo̱lei ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ni Saul ke̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ fẽ nyã́ babaō dientše̱ ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱hĩe kpa Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱ le̱, ehõame̱ ehã *Sisera, Hazor ta le̱ no̱ asafoiatše̱ le̱, ke̱ †Filistibii le̱, ke̱ **Moab maṅtše̱ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ wu. *Kodš.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱sā ame̱blo̱ ame̱tšé̱ Iehowa ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱fe eša, edšake̱ wo̱kwa Iehowa, ni wo̱yasúmo̱ Baalim ke̱ Aštarot; ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ dšiemo̱wo̱ ke̱-dše̱ wo̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ, ni wo̱o̱súmo̱o!

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ši beni nyena ake̱ Nahaš, Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱, efã nyeyino̱ ta le̱, nyekē̱mi ake̱: *Dabi! ši maṅtše̱ aye wo̱no̱! tše̱ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, dši nye-maṅtše̱. *

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ na, maṅtše̱ le̱ ni nyetao ni nyebi le̱ ne̱; ni na, Iehowa ewo maṅtše̱ ehãnye.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ke̱dši nyeaše Iehowa gbeyei, ni nyeasúmo̱le̱, ni nyeabo egbē toi, ni nye-tšeṅ Iehowa kitã le̱ hĩe atũa le̱, no le̱ nye ke̱ maṅtše̱ ní yeo̱ nyeno̱ le̱ fẽ aanyie Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, se̱.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeboṅ Iehowa gbē toi, ši tše moṅ nyeatše Iehowa kitã le̱ hĩe atũa le̱, no le̱ Iehowa nine aakã nyeno̱ tamo̱ bo̱ni ekã nyetše̱mei le̱ ano̱ le̱.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyedamo̱a ši ni nyekwe̱a noko kpeteṅkple ni Iehowa bafe ye̱ nyehĩe ne̱.

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel tšē̱ Iehowa, ni Iehowa hã nyoṅmo̱ šimo̱ ni nyoṅmo̱ ne̱ nakai gbĩ le̱. Ni maṅ le̱ fẽ še Iehowa ke̱ Samuel gbeyei naakpa.

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Ši Samuel kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Nyekašea gbeyei! nyená nyefe ne̱ke̱ efõṅ ne̱ fẽ moṅ, ši kẽle̱ nyekakpalea ke̱-dšea Iehowa se̱, ši nyesúmo̱a Iehowa ke̱ nye-tšui fẽ!

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Ni nyekagbalea he kroko, ni nyeyanyie yakayakanii ni he be̱ se̱námo̱ ni *nyẽẽ mo adšie le̱ ase̱, edšake̱ yakayakanii ni. *

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa gbe̱i kpeteṅkple le̱ hewo̱ le̱ ekwaṅ emaṅ le̱; edšake̱ esa Iehowa hĩe ake̱ *eke̱nye aafe emaṅ. *

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Ni mi hũ, ene̱ akagbalemi fō̃ṅfõ ake̱ mafe eša maši Iehowa ni *mafõ fai-kpamo̱ ke̱ nye hãmo̱, ši moṅ matšõnye gbe̱ kpakpa ke̱ dšale̱ gbe̱. *

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Gbeyei ke̱ke̱ *nyešea Iehowa, ni nyesúmo̱ale̱ ye̱ ano̱kwale mli ke̱ nyetšui fẽ; ši nyekwe̱a nii wudši abo̱ ni efe ehãnye. *

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeakã he nyefe nifõdšianii le̱, no le̱ aakpãtã nye ke̱ nyemaṅtše̱ le̱ fẽ hĩe.

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Ni Israel mū le̱ fẽ nu ake̱: Saul eyatſia Filistibii le̱ asrafoi le̱ anii, ni Israel he edše fũ hũ ewo Filistibii le̱. Ni abua maṅ le̱ nā ke̱-kpe ni ame̱tiu Saul ke̱-te Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Ni beni Israel hĩĩ le̱ na ake̱ efīame̱, edšake̱ āhao maṅ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ yatētē ame̱he ye̱ bui amli ke̱ kow̌eii amli ke̱ te̱sāi amli ke̱ mõdši amli ke̱ fo̱dši amli.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Ni Hebribii le̱ ekomei efo Iordan ke̱-te Gad ke̱ Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ no̱. Ši Saul le̱ eye̱ Gilgal lolo, ni mei le̱ fẽ nyie ese̱ ni ame̱he mīkpokpo.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱: Nyeke̱ šã-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei le̱ abahãami ye̱ bie̱. Ni esă šã-afo̱le le̱.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli, beni egbe šã-afo̱le le̱ šã nā pe̱ le̱, na, Samuel ba; ni Saul dše kpo ke̱le̱ yakpe, koni eflale̱.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Meni ofe ne̱? Ni Saul kē̱: Edšake̱ mina ake̱ maṅ le̱ egbe̱ eſã ye̱ mihe, ni bo hũ obaa ye̱ gbĩ ni ato le̱ no̱, ni Filistibii le̱ ebua ame̱he nā ke̱-kpe ye̱ Mikmaš,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: nohewo̱ le̱ mikē̱: Agbene̱ Filistibii le̱ aakpleke ši abatuami ye̱ Gilgal, ni mikpako Iehowa fai; nohewo̱ ni mimla mihĩe, ni mišã šã-afo̱le le̱.

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱ Saul ake̱: Oye kwašiai asane; oyeko Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kitã ní ewoö le̱ no̱; edšake̱ kũle̱ kpako Iehowa bawadše omaṅtše̱yeli le̱ ye̱ Israel no̱ ke̱-ya nāno̱.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ omaṅtše̱yeli le̱ damo̱ṅ ši. Iehowa etao le̱dientše̱ *etšui nā nū ko ehã ehe, ni Iehowa ewole̱ emaṅ le̱ no̱ lumo̱; edšake̱ oyee kitã ni Iehowa woö le̱ no̱. *Bo̱f.

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Ni Samuel te ši ni edše̱ Gilgal ete Gibea ye̱ Benyamin. Ni Saul kane mei ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ dše̱i le̱, ame̱yi aafe hĩĩ ohai-ekpa.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Ni Saul ke̱ ebi Ionatan ke̱ mei ní fata ame̱he le̱ hĩ Geba ye̱ Benyamin; ši Filistibii le̱ bo̱ nsra ye̱ Mikmaš.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Ni ofõyelo̱i gbla ame̱mli asafokui etẽ ni ame̱fã ke̱-dše̱ Filistibii le̱ ansra le̱ṅ: asafoku kome tšṍ Ofra gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-te Šual šikpoṅ le̱ no̱,

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: ni ku kome hũ tšṍ Bet-Horon gbe̱ le̱ no̱, ni ku kroko le̱ tšṍ hũsũ ni kă ke̱-yaä Zeboim dšō̱ le̱ṅ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ *sõlo̱ ko sõlo̱ ko be̱ Israel šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ no̱; edšake̱ Filistibii le̱ kē̱o̱ ake̱: Ké̱ afe nakai le̱, no le̱ Hebribii le̱ aasõ klantei lo akplo̱i aha ame̱he. *Kodš.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ ame̱ye̱ kitai ni ake̱-dšo̱ō̱ tšinakō̱ii le̱ ke̱ adedai le̱ ke̱ ninēmo̱-dadei le̱ ke̱ lemai le̱ anā, ni ake̱-sãa tšina kplamo̱dadei le̱ hũ.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ tawū gbĩ le̱ no̱ le anaa klante lo akplo̱ ko ye̱ mei ní fata Saul ke̱ Ionatan he le̱ ateṅ mokomoko deṅ; ši Saul ke̱ ebi Ionatan deṅ pe̱ ana eko ye̱.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ asrafoi le̱ fã ke̱-te Mikmaš tšṍmo̱he le̱.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Ekome le̱ nā mã kōyigbe̱ ye̱ Mikmaš ṅe̱le̱no̱, ni ekome hũ nā mã wuoyigbe̱ ye̱ Geba ṅe̱le̱no̱.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan kē̱ oblanyo ni hĩe etawūnii le̱ ake̱: Ba ní wo̱te ne̱ke̱ fōlo̱i ne̱ asrafoi le̱ aṅõ! Ekole̱ Iehowa aatšu nii ahãwo̱; edšake̱ nokonoko etšĩĩ *Iehowa nā ake̱ eke̱ mei pī lo mei fiõ aahere yiwala! *Kodš.

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan nyie enidši ke̱ enãdši ano̱ ke̱-kwo̱, ni etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ hũ nyie ese̱. Ni *ame̱ſieſie ši ye̱ Ionatan hĩe; bĕle̱ etawūniihĩelo̱ mīgbegbẽame̱ ke̱-nyie ese̱. *

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Edši ake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ maṅ le̱ ye ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ anihānii ní ame̱na le̱ bo̱ni ame̱sumoo̱ kũle̱, ani agbeṅ Filistibii le̱ āhũ fè ne̱ke̱?

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ni ṅmiṅmi ba nsra le̱ṅ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ke̱ ta mū le̱ fẽ ne̱; asrafoi le̱ ke̱ nihalo̱i le̱, ame̱ hũ ṅmiṅmi mõme̱ame̱; ni šikpoṅ hoso, ni etšṍ Nyoṅmo̱ he ṅmiṅmi.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Ni Saul hebulo̱i ni yo̱ Gibea ye̱ Benyamin le̱ yakwe̱ le̱, na, asafo le̱ mli mītšere̱, ni ame̱mīgbe̱ ame̱mīſã.

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Hebribii ní ke̱ Filistibii le̱ yo̱ sá, ni ke̱ame̱ dše̱ šikpoṅ ní bo̱leame̱ ke̱-kpe le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba nsra le̱ṅ le̱, ame̱ hũ ame̱bafata Israelbii ni ke̱ Saul ke̱ Ionatan yo̱ le̱ ahe.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii fẽ ni eyatẽtē ame̱he ye̱ Efraim goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, beni amenu ake̱ Filistibii le̱ edšo foi le̱, ame̱ hũ ame̱ba-nyie ame̱se̱ wā ye̱ ta le̱ṅ.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ na nõ nakai gbĩ le̱; edšake̱ Saul ekã kitã efõ maṅ le̱ no̱ ake̱: Alomo̱ mofẽmo ní aaye noko dãni dše aana, koni ato̱ mihe owele ye̱ mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ ano̱! Nohewo̱ le̱ maṅ le̱ mli mokomoko esaa enā noko.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅ le̱ še̱ ko le̱ mli le̱, na, wò tšereo̱ ſieo̱ ši ne̱; ši mokomoko ke̱ enine woo edāṅ; edšake̱ maṅ le̱ mīše kitã le̱ gbeyei.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ši Ionatan nuu beni etše̱ kã kitã efõ maṅ le̱ no̱ le̱; nohewo̱ le̱ eṅõ tšo ni ehĩe le̱ nā etšo̱ wò-agbaku le̱ mli, ni eṅõ enine ewo edāṅ, ni ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ tšere̱le̱.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ tabilo̱i le̱ ateṅ moko here no̱ ake̱: Otše̱ ekã kitã efõ maṅ le̱ no̱ ake̱: Alomo̱ mofẽmo ní aaye noko ṅme̱ne̱! Ni maṅ le̱ mīto̱ biti.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan kē̱: Mitše̱ ewo šikpoṅ le̱ amane mli; nyekwe̱a, bo̱ni mihĩṅme̱ii ano̱ etšere̱mi, ní misa minā wó ne̱ fiō le̱.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ ame̱gbe Filistibii le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mikmaš ke̱-yaši Ayalon. Ni eto maṅ le̱ butū.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ tšẽ ke̱-te nihānii le̱ ane̱, ni ame̱mõme̱ tōi ke̱ tšinai ke̱ tšinabii ni ame̱gbeame̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ; ni maṅ le̱ ye ke̱ *lá le̱. *

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Ni ayagba Saul ake̱: Na, maṅ le̱ mife eša mīši Iehowa, ake̱-ni ame̱yeo̱ nii ke̱ lá le̱. Ni ekē̱: Nyetõ! Nyekokloa te̱ kpeteṅkple nyebahãami!

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Nyegbe̱a nyeſãa maṅ le̱ṅ, ni nyekē̱aame̱ ake̱: Mofẽmo ke̱ etšina aba ni mofẽmo ke̱ etō aba miṅõ ye̱ bie̱, ni nyebagbeaame̱ ye̱ bie̱ ni nyeye, ni nyekaye ke̱ lá le̱ ni nyeke̱-mīfe eša nyemīši Iehowa! Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ le̱, mofẽmo hĩe etšina ke̱-ba nakai nyō le̱ṅ, ni ame̱bagbe ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Ni Saul mã afo̱lešãlate̱ ehã Iehowa. Ene̱ dši kleṅkleṅ afo̱lešãlate̱ ni emã ehã Iehowa.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Nyehãa wo̱kplekea ši ke̱-nyiea Filistibii le̱ ase̱ nyōṅ, ni wo̱-haame̱ ke̱-yaši dšetše̱remo̱ we̱le̱ṅṅ, ni wo̱kašĩ ame̱teṅ mokomoko! Ni ame̱kē̱: Nofẽno ni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe le̱, femo̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱ſo le̱ kē̱: Nyehãa wo̱tšia wo̱be̱ṅke̱a bie̱ ke̱-yaä Nyoṅmo̱ ṅō!

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Ni Saul *bi Nyoṅmo̱ ake̱: Ani mikpleke ši ke̱-nyie Filistibii le̱ ase̱ lo? Ani oodšieame̱ owo Israel de̱ṅ lo? Ši ehããle̱ hetō nakai gbĩ le̱. *K.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱: Nyetšia nyebe̱ṅke̱a bie̱, nye maṅ le̱ mli onukpai le̱ fẽ; ni nyekwe̱a ake̱ nyeana nõ mli ni eša ne̱ yo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ lo!

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱ Israel fẽ ake̱: Nye le̱ nyeyea afã kome, ni mi ke̱ mibi Ionatan hũ aye afã kome. Ni maṅ le̱ kē̱ Saul ake̱: Noni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe le̱, femo̱!

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Nyefõa mi ke̱ mibi Ionatan hũ no̱ ošiki! Ni egbẽ Ionatan no̱.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ Ionatan ake̱: Tšõmo̱mi *noni ofe! Ni Ionatan tšõle̱ ni ekē̱: Sa ke̱ke̱ mike̱ tšo ni mihīe le̱ nā sa wŏ fiō misa minā; ni na, mibagbo! *Ios.

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Kē̱ dšee gbo oogbo fĩ, Ionatan, Nyoṅmo̱ afemi ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ši maṅ le̱ kē̱ Saul ake̱: Aso Ionatan ni etšu ne̱ke̱ yiwalaheremo̱ nitšumo̱ kpeteṅkple ne̱ ye̱ Israel le̱ agbo? Akaba mli nakai! Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, eyiteṅ tšo̱i kome akanyõ šikpoṅ; edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ eke̱-tšu nii ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱! Ni maṅ le̱ here Ionatan yiwala ní agbeele̱.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Ni Saul fõ Filistibii le̱ ase̱nyiemo̱ ṅi ekũ ese̱ ke̱-ba. Ni Filistibii le̱ yiṅ ke̱-te ame̱dientše̱ ame̱dšē̱hei.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ Filistibii le̱ wu ta ní nā wa naakpa ye̱ Saul yino̱ le̱ fẽ. Ni ké̱ Saul na nū hewalo̱ ko lo nū ekãlo̱ ko pe̱ le̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ eṅõle̱ ke̱-ba eṅõ.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ya ni oyatſia *Amalek nii, ni nyefeaame̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ni ame̱yo̱ le̱ musu, ni okabā ame̱yi, ši ogbe nū ke̱ yō, gbekẽ ke̱ fufo̱õ, tšina ke̱ tõ, yoma ke̱ tedši fẽ. *

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Samuel ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul ba Amalek maṅ le̱ he, ni ebawo ká ye̱ dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Ši meni dši tōi ablo̱mo̱ ní dſere mitoiṅ ne̱, ke̱ tšinai ablo̱mo̱ hũ ni minuo̱ ne̱ mo̱?

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Amalekbii le̱ aṅõ ame̱ke̱-dše̱, maṅ le̱ bã tōi ke̱ tšinai ni hĩ fè fẽ le̱ ayi, koni ame̱ke̱-basã afo̱le ame̱-hã Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; ši nii ní eſe̱ le̱ wo̱feame̱ musu.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa tšūo ni ekē̱: Ya ni oyafe Amalekbii ešafelo̱i le̱ amusu, ni oke̱ame̱ awu ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ookpãtã ame̱hĩe kwrakwra!

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Ši Saul kē̱ Samuel ake̱: Miho Iehowa gbē toi, ni mite hégbe̱ ni Iehowa tšũmi le̱, ni mike̱ Agag, Amalek maṅtše̱ le̱, eba, ni Amalekbii le̱ mifeame̱ musu.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ši maṅ le̱ ṅõ nihānii le̱ amli tōi ke̱ tšinai ní dši musunii le̱ amli ekpakpai le̱, koni ame̱ke̱-bašã afo̱le ame̱hã Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ye̱ Gilgal.

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Ši Samuel kē̱: Ani Iehowa náa šā̃-afo̱lei ke̱ gbē-afo̱lei ahe tšui tamo̱ Iehowa gbē toibō lo? Na, *toibō hĩ fè afo̱le, ni ninumo̱ hũ hĩ fè tōagboi afo̱. *Hos.

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱ Samuel ake̱: Mife eša, edšake̱ mitõ Iehowa kitã le̱ ke̱ bo hũ owiemo̱i le̱ ano̱; edšake̱ miše maṅ le̱ gbeyei ni miyabo ame̱gbẽ toi.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, oke̱ mihe eša afami, ni oke̱mi aku se̱ ke̱-ya, ni ma-yadšá Iehowa!

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Ši Samuel kē̱ Saul ake̱: Mike̱o ekũũ se̱ ke̱-yaa; edšake̱ okwa Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱, ni Iehowa hū ekwao maṅtše̱yeli ye̱ Israel no̱.

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Ni beni Samuel tšṍ ehe ni eyaã le̱, emō ebò le̱ nāmū le̱ mli, ni egbá.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ moni dši Israel hewale̱ le̱ maleṅ, ni eſaṅ ehe hũ; edšake̱ dšee gbomo dšile̱ ní eeſa ehe!

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Mife eša; ši kẽle̱ wo mihĩe nyam ye̱ mimaṅ onukpai le̱ ke̱ Israel hĩe, ni oke̱mi akũ se̱ ke̱-ya, ni mayadšá Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱!

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel kũ ese̱ ke̱-nyie Saul se̱; ni Saul yadšá Iehowa.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Nyeke̱ Agag, Amalekbii amaṅtše̱ le̱, abaä miṅõ! Ni Agag ba eṅõ ke̱ mīše̱. Ni Agag kē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, ake̱ gbĕle dšōmo̱ le̱ efoṅ ke̱-te!

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Bo̱ni oklante ehã yei etšṍmo̱ mei ní be̱ bii le̱, nakai onye hũ aatšṍ moni be̱ bi ye̱ yei ateṅ! Ni Samuel flo̱ Agag mli dukuduku ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ye̱ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel yiṅ ke̱-te Rama; ni Saul hũ yiṅ ke̱-te ewe ye̱ Saul Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel baa ebanaa Saul doṅṅ ke̱-yaši egbĕle gbĩ no̱; edšake̱ Samuel ye ṅko̱mo̱ ye̱ Saul hewo̱, ni Iehowa ſa ehe ake̱ ewo Saul maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel no̱.

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel fe noni Iehowa kē̱ le̱, ni eba Betlehem. Ni mã le̱ṅ onukpai le̱ ke̱le̱ bakpe ke̱ hekpokpomo̱, ni ame̱kē̱: *Toiṅdšo̱le̱ mli obaä ne̱ lo? *

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱ba ni ena Eliab le̱, ekē̱: Moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱ damo̱ ehĩe ne̱!

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Išai tšé̱ Abinadab, ni ehã ebaho ye̱ Samuel hĩe. Ni ekē̱: Mone̱ hũ Iehowa halakole̱!

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Ni Išai hã Šama baho. Ni ekē̱: Mone̱ hũ Iehowa halakole̱!

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱ Išai ake̱: Ani obla-ĩĩ le̱ fẽ ne̱? Ni ekē̱: Eſe̱ ame̱teṅ *gbekẽ le̱, ní na, ēkwe̱ tōi. Ni Samuel kē̱ Išai ake̱: Tšũ ni ayaṅõle̱ ke̱-ba; edšake̱ wo̱-woṅ šitrámo̱, ake̱ dša eba bie̱ dã. *

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Ni etšũ ni ayaṅõle̱ ke̱-ba. Ši etšuo̱õ ke̱ ehĩṅme̱ii fe̱o, ni kē̱ okwe̱le̱ hũ, ehe ye̱ fe̱o. Ni Iehowa kē̱: Te ši! ni ofo̱le̱ mũ; edšake̱ le̱ pi ne̱!

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel wó mũ ke̱ koṅ le̱, ni *eṅō-fo̱le̱ ye̱ enyemimei le̱ ateṅ. Ni Iehowa Mumo̱ yi David no̱ ke̱-dše̱ ne̱ke̱ gbĩ ne̱ no̱ ke̱-yaä ne̱ fē. Ke̱ke̱ ni Samuel te ši, ni eyiṅ ete Rama. *

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ edše Saul no̱, ni Iehowa hãa mumo̱ fõṅ ko bahaoo̱le̱.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Wo̱nuṅtšo̱ akē̱ etšũdši ní damo̱ ehĩe ne̱, ní ame̱yatao nū ko ni le saṅkũtſā mli kwāsoi le̱ fẽ; ni aaba mli ake̱ kē̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hã mumo̱ fõṅ le̱ ba ono̱ le̱, koni etſa, ní ahĩ ahão.

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Bĕle̱ nyeyataoa nū ko ni le saṅkũtſā dšogbāṅ nyehãami, ni nyeke̱le̱ abaä miṅõ.

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Ni oblahĩī le̱ ateṅ mokome here no̱ ni ekē̱: Na, mina Išai, Betlehemnyo le̱, binū ko ni le saṅkũtſā dšogbāṅ, ni nū kãkãlo̱ ke̱ tawulo̱ dšile̱, ele nii ni ehe hũ ye̱ fe̱o, ni Iehowa ke̱le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Išai ṅõ, ekē̱: Hã obi David ní ke̱ tōi le̱ yo̱ le̱ aba miṅõ!

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Ni Išai ṅõ tedši, ni eke̱ abolo ke̱ wein-ke̱-woloto̱ ke̱ abotiabi tĕrele̱, ni eke̱-tšṍ ebinū David nine no̱ amādše Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Ni David ba Saul ṅõ, ni ebasúmo̱le̱, ni esumo̱le̱ naakpa, ni etšṍ etawūniihĩelo̱.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšũ ate Išai ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Hã David asúmo̱mi, edšake̱ mīsumo̱ esane.

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Ni ebaã mli ake̱, ké̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hã *mumo̱ le̱ ba Saul no̱ le̱, David ko̱ō̱ saṅkũ ni etſaä: ni Saul he dšo̱ō̱le̱ ni ehĩo̱ ehãale̱, ni mumo̱ fõṅ le̱ dšeo̱ eno̱ eyaã. *K.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ dſere goṅ le̱ ekome hĩeši, ni Israelbii le̱ hũ dſere goṅ le̱ ekome hĩeši, ní dšō̱ kã ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Ni beni David eyagbe Filistinyo le̱ ni ekũ ese̱ eba le̱, Abner ṅõle̱, ni eke̱le̱ ba Saul hĩe, ni ehĩe Filistinyo le̱ yitšo le̱ ye̱ edẽ.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: ni ekplo̱ nā tšo tamo̱ mamalòlo̱ agbatšo, ni ekplo̱ le̱ yitšo ṅmẽo̱ dade šekeli ohai-ekpa; ni etše̱ṅhĩelo̱ nyie ehĩe.

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Ni Filistinyo le̱ kē̱: Mi le̱ *mībo̱ Israel tabilo̱i le̱ ahora ṅme̱ne̱: nyedšiea nū kome nyehãami, koni wo̱wu! *

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: ši David le̱ ké̱ fe le̱ edše̱o̱ Saul ṅõ le̱ eyaä ni eyakwe̱o̱ etše̱ tōi le̱ ye̱ Betlehem.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Ni eko̱ *edẽhĩeme̱tšo le̱ ehĩe, ni eyahala fo̱bite̱i enumo̱ ye̱ fā le̱ṅ, ni eṅõ-wo etōkwe̱lo̱i akotoku ni ehĩe le̱ mli, ni eke̱ ekromia le̱ ehĩe edẽ, ni etši ebe̱ṅke̱ Filistinyo le̱. *

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Išai kē̱ ebi David le̱ ake̱: Nõ mãmu efa kome ne̱ ke̱ abolo akwā-bo̱i nyoṅma ne̱, ni oša foi oya nsra le̱ṅ oke̱-yahã onyemimei le̱.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Ni oṅõ kēsui klatai nyoṅma ne̱ ohã akpetše̱ le̱, ni okwe̱ bo̱ni onyemimei le̱ yo̱, ni oke̱ ame̱he okadi ko aba.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: No mli le̱ Saul ke̱ ame̱ ke̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ye̱ Ela dšō̱ le̱ṅ, ame̱ke̱ Filistibii le̱ mīwu.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Ni David te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni etu tōi le̱ ewo no̱kwe̱lo̱ le̱ deṅ, ni ewó nii le̱ ni eṅō-ſie no̱ take̱ bo̱ni Išai fã́le̱ le̱, ni ebaše̱ ſīlii anābuame̱ he le̱; ši tabilo̱i le̱ edše kpo ame̱mībo̱ oše ke̱-ya ta le̱ nā.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Ši Israel ke̱ Filistibii le̱ fẽ egbá, ta mīkwe̱ ta hĩe.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David šī edšatsu le̱ ehã moni kwe̱o̱ dšatšui le̱ ano̱ le̱, ni eša foi ke̱-te ta le̱ṅ, ni eyaṅã enyemimei le̱.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Ši beni Israel hĩĩ le̱ na nū le̱, ame̱fẽ ame̱dšo foi ye̱ ehĩe, ni ame̱še gbeyei naakpa.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ ateṅ moko kē̱ ake̱: Nto nyemīna nū ni baã ne̱? Israel ahorabō̱ kẽ ebaä ne̱, ni aaba mli ake̱ moni aagbele̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ aafele̱ niiatše̱ agbo, ni eeṅõ ebiyō ehäle̱ gblã, ni eehã etše̱ we le̱ aye ame̱he ye̱ Israel!

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ hĩĩ le̱ ní eke̱-damo̱ ši le̱ ake̱: Meni aafe ahã moni aagbe Filistinyo ne̱, níi eedšie ahorabō̱ ne̱ ye̱ Israel no̱ le̱? Edšake̱ namo po dši ne̱ke̱ Filistinyo fõlo̱ ne̱, ni ebo̱ö̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩekãlo̱ le̱ tai le̱ ahora ne̱?

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ni mei le̱ herele̱ no̱ nakai noṅṅ ake̱: Ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ abafe ahã moni aagbele̱ le̱.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Ši enyemi nukpa Eliab nu beni eke̱ hĩĩ le̱ wieo̱ le̱; ni Eliab mli wo David la ni ekē̱: Mẽba oba bie̱? ni namo ošī tōi fiō ní yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ ohã? Mi le̱ mile olahō ke̱ otšuiṅ nifõdšianii le̱ momo, ake̱ ta le̱ kwe̱mo̱ hewo̱ kẽ oba ne̱!

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Ni etšṍ ehe ke̱-dše̱ emase̱i ehã mokroko, ni ewie bo̱ni ewie le̱ noṅṅ. Ni mei le̱ to he hãle̱ ekoṅ tamo̱ bo̱ni ame̱-kē̱le̱ tšutšu le̱.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Ni beni anu David wiemo̱i ni ewie le̱, ayatšĩ tã atšõ Saul, ni etšũ ayaṅõle̱.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Saul ake̱: Mokomoko tšuĩ akafã ye̱ ehewo̱: otšũlo̱ aate eke̱ ne̱ke̱ Filistinyo ne̱ ayawu.

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱ David ake̱: Onyẽṅ oke̱ ne̱ke̱ Filistinyo ne̱ ayakpe ni oke̱le̱ awu; edšake̱ bo le̱ gbekẽ dšio, ni le̱ le̱ nū tawulo̱ dšile̱ ke̱-dše̱ egbekẽbiiasi.

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Saul ake̱: Otšũlo̱ kwe̱o̱ etše̱ tōi, ni ké̱ dšata lo ošišibriši ba bamõ tōbi ko ke̱-dše̱ tōi le̱ ateṅ le̱,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: midšeo̱ kpo miyatiuo̱le̱, ni mitſaäle̱ nõ, ni midšieo̱le̱ ye̱ edãṅ; ni ké̱ ete ši ewomi le̱, mimõ etšëṅ, ni mĩtſiaäle̱ nii, ni migbeo̱le̱.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Dšata ke̱ ošĩšĩbriši po le̱ otšũlo̱ egbe, ni ne̱ke̱ Filistinyo fõlo̱ ne̱ aatšṍ tamo̱ ame̱teṅ mokome, ake̱ nõ kẽ ní ebo̱ö̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩekãlo̱ le̱ tai le̱ ahora ne̱!

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Ni David sā kē̱: Iehowa, moni dšiemi ke̱-dše̱ dšata ke̱ ošišibriši le̱ deṅ le̱, le̱ eedšiemi ke̱-adše̱ Filistinyo ne̱ deṅ! Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ David ake̱: Ya, ni Iehowa ke̱o aya!

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Ni Saul ke̱ etadei wo David, ni eṅõ akō̱ble fai ebule̱, ni esā eṅõ dama ewole̱.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Ni David ṅmõ eklante le̱ ye̱ etade le̱ no̱, ni eka nyiemo̱; edšake̱ ekako ekwe̱ko dã. Ni David kē̱ Saul ake̱: Minyẽṅ mike̱ ene̱mei aya, edšake̱ mikako mikwe̱ko dã! Ni David dšie ye̱ ehe.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Ni Filistinyo le̱ nyie ke̱-mība, ni ebabe̱ṅke̱ David; ni etše̱ṅhĩelo̱ le̱ nyie ehĩe.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Ni beni Filistinyo le̱ fõ ehĩe ni ena David le̱, ebuule̱; edšake̱ gbekẽ dši-le̱, *ni etšuo̱õ ke̱ ehĩe fe̱o. *

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Ni Filistinyo le̱ kē̱ David ake̱: Ani gbṍ dšimĩ ni obaä mino̱ ke̱ tšo lo? Ni Filistinyo le̱ tšé̱ enyoṅmo̱ eke̱-lomo̱ David.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Ni Filistinyo le̱ kē̱ David ake̱: Ba miṅõ, ni maṅō *ohelo mahã ṅwei lofõdši ke̱ ṅãṅ koloi! *Ezek.

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ Filistinyo le̱ ake̱: Bo le̱ ōba miṅõ ke̱ klante ke̱ akplo̱ ke̱ tše̱ṅ; ši mi le̱ miba oṅõ ye̱ Iehowa Zabaot ni dši Israel tai ní obo̱ö̱ame̱ ahora le̱ a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbe̱i amli!

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ Iehowa aadšieo awo mideṅ, ní magbeo, ni mafo oyi, ni maṅõ Filistibii ata le̱ mli gbohĩĩ le̱ mahã ṅwei lofõdši ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ koloi awuyelo̱i ṅme̱ne̱, koni šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ aana ale ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ko ye̱ Israel,

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: ni asafo ní ekpe ne̱ fẽ aaná ale ake̱ dšee klante lo akplo̱ Iehowa ke̱-hereo̱ mo yiwala; edšake̱ Iehowa nõ dši ta le̱, ni eeṅõnye ewo wo̱deṅ!

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ enine wo ekotoku le̱ mli ni eko̱ te̱ ye̱ mli, ni efõ akromia le̱, ni etſa Filistinyo le̱ hĩenā, ni te̱ le̱ bote ehĩeṅtšoṅ, ni egbē ši ni ehĩe yabu ši.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ša foi, ni eyaho edamo̱ Filistinyo le̱ no̱, ni emõ eklante le̱ egbla ke̱-dše̱ ehebo le̱ mli, ni egbele̱, ni eṅõ-fo eyi. Ni beni Filistibii le̱ na ake̱ ame̱tatše̱lo̱ le̱ egbo le̱, ame̱dšo foi.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel ke̱ Iuda hĩĩ le̱ te ši, ni ame̱bo̱ oše, ni ame̱yanyie Filistibii le̱ ase̱ ke̱-yaši dšō̱ le̱ mli ke̱ Ekron agbói le̱ anā. Ni Filistibii le̱ apilafoi le̱ nyõnyõi ye̱ Šaaraim gbe̱ le̱ no̱ āhū ke̱-yaſie Gat ke̱ Ekron tō̃.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ Filistibii le̱ ase̱nyiemo̱ le̱ mli, ni ame̱-baha ame̱nsrai le̱ amli nii.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Si David ko̱ Filistinyo le̱ yitšo le̱, ni eke̱-ba Ierusalem; ši etawūnii le̱ eke̱-yato ebū le̱ṅ.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Ši beni Saul na David yaā eke̱ Filistinyo le̱ ayakpe le̱, ekē̱ tatše̱ *Abner ake̱: Namo bi dši ne̱ke̱ oblanyo ne̱, Abner? Ni Abner kē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni osusuma hĩe kā ne̱, maṅtše̱, milee! *

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱le̱ ake̱: Namo bi dšio, oblanyo? Ni David kē̱: Otšũlo̱ Išai, Betlehemnyo le̱, bi dšimi.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Ni *Ionatan ke̱ David kpãṅ, edšake̱ ēsumo̱le̱ tamo̱ le̱dientše̱ ehe noṅṅ. *

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan dšie ebò ní yo̱ ehe le̱, ni eṅõ-hã David, ke̱ etadei le̱ āhũ ke̱-mõ eklante le̱ ke̱ egai le̱ ke̱ emlifĩnō le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Ni yei le̱ ní ſe̱o̱ le̱ woo̱ lala ni ame̱herehereo̱ no̱ ake̱: Saul egbe ekpei-kpei le̱, ši *David egbe ekpei-nyoṅma-nyoṅmai le̱! *

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul mli wo la naakpa, ni wiemo̱ ne̱ eṅõõ enā, ni ekē̱: Ame̱ṅõ akpei-nyoṅma-nyoṅmai ame̱ba David, ši mi le̱, ame̱ṅõ akpei-kpei ame̱hãmi: ni meni eſe̱le̱ doṅṅ ake̱ dša maṅtše̱yeli le̱!

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Ni Saul *fõ akplo̱ lo̱, ekē̱: Matšu David ke̱-mõ gbogbo le̱! Ni David w̌i ehe šii enyo̱ so̱ṅṅ. *

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Ši Israel ke̱ Iuda fẽ sumoo̱ David, edšake̱ le̱ enyieo̱ ame̱hĩe ke̱-yaä ke̱-baä.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱ David ake̱: Na mibiyō nukpa Merab le̱, mike̱le̱ bahão gblã; bo le̱ femo̱ ekã ohãmi ke̱ke̱, ni owu Iehowa tai le̱! Edšake̱ Saul kē̱: Mi le̱ minine akata ehe, ši Filistibii le̱ moṅ anine ágbele̱!

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Saul ake̱: Namo dši-mi, ni namei dši miwekumei alo mitše̱ weku le̱ ye̱ Israel, ni matšṍ maṅtše̱ šānū?

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni še̱ be ni kũle̱ aaṅõ Saul biyō Merab le̱ ahã David le̱, *akele hã Adriel, Meholatnyo le, gblã. *Kodš.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Ši Saul biyō Mikal le̱ mīsumo̱ David, ni beni atſa Saul adafi le̱, sane le̱ sa ehĩe.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Mike̱le̱ aahãle̱, ni etšṍ tšõne ehãle̱, ní Filistibii le̱ anine ágbele̱. Ni Saul kē̱ David ake̱: Ṅme̱ne̱ obatšṍ mĩšānū noni dši šii enyo̱!

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšũdši le̱ wie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ ame̱wo David toiĩaṅ; ši David kē̱: Ani efeo̱nye ake̱ maṅtše̱ šānū tšṍmo̱ le̱ ſe̱mo̱ sane ni? Ši mi le̱, ohĩafo dšimi, ni abuumi tūtu ko.

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšũdši le̱ yakē̱le̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Bo̱ni David kē̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Nyekē̱a David ne̱ke̱: Maṅtše̱ taoo w̌ē̱nii ko, ake̱ dša Filisti-bii le̱ afõnālõi oha ke̱ke̱, koni ake̱-to maṅtše̱ he owele ye̱ ehenye̱lo̱i le̱ ano̱. Ši Saul susu ake̱ eke̱-ahā enyõ ye̱ Filĩsti-bii le̱ anine nā.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Ni beni etšũdši le̱ yakē̱ David ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱, eṅṍ David nā ake̱ eke̱ ene̱ aatšṍ maṅtše̱ šānū; ni gbĩĩ le̱ še̱ko.

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Ni Saul na ni ekpá ši ake̱ Iehowa ke̱ David ye̱, ni ake̱ Saul biyō Mikal le̱ mīsumo̱le̱.

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Ni Saul sā *še David gbeyei babaō fè tšutšu le̱, ni Saul tšṍ David henye̱lo̱ egbĩĩ le̱ fẽ. *K.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ dšeo̱ kpo baã; ni ebaä mli ake̱ befẽbe ni ame̱fã ta le̱, David yeo̱ omanye fē Saul tšũdši le̱ fẽ, ni egbe̱i hehe naakpa.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱ mibadše kpo mayadamo̱ mitše̱ mase̱i ye̱ ṅã le̱ṅ heni oye̱ le̱, ni mike̱ mitše̱ bagba ohe sane, ni kē̱ mina noko le̱, makē̱o.

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ ewala ehīe edeṅ, ni *eyagbe Filistinyo le̱, ni Iehowa tšu yiwalaheremo̱ nitšumo̱ kpeteṅkple ehã Israel fẽ. Ona ni onyã́ he; mẽhewo̱ mo̱ ni oofe eša oši lá ni eye bem le̱, ni ogbe David yakatſā? *

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul bo Ionatan gbē toi; ni Saul kã kitã ekē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, agbeṅle̱!

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan yatšé̱ David, ni Ionatan dšadše nakai wieme̱i le̱ fẽ etšõle̱. Ni Ionatan ke̱ David ba Saul ṅõ ekoṅ, ni ebahī ši ye̱ ehĩe tamo̱ tšutšu le̱.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ši ta ba ekoṅ; ni David fã ni eke̱ Filistibii le̱ yawu, ni egbeame̱ butū, ni ame̱dšo foi ye̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni *Saul tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te David we le̱ ni ame̱yasrale̱ ní ame̱gbele̱ lebi. Ni Mikal, David ṅã le̱, kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši oheree osusuma yiwala nyō ne̱ṅ le̱, wó̱ le̱ abagbeo! *Lal.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mikal wó amãgã efõ sā le̱ no̱, ni eṅõ abotia wolo no̱hānõ eha eyitšogbe̱, ni eṅõ mama eha he.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Saul tšũ bo̱foi ake̱ ayamõ David ke̱-ba le̱, ekē̱: Ehe mīye.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšũ bo̱foi le̱ ekoṅ ake̱ ame̱yasra David ame̱kwe̱, ekē̱: Nyewóale̱ ke̱ sā le̱ fẽ nyebahãami ní agbele̱.

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Ni beni bo̱foi le̱ ba le̱, na, amãgã kã sā le̱ no̱ lo̱, ni abotia wolo no̱hānõ le̱ ha eyitšogbe̱.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ Mikal ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ po ni ošišiumi ne̱ke̱, ni odšie mihenye̱lo̱ le̱ gbe̱ ni ete ni edše mideṅ ne̱? Ni Mikal kē̱ Saul ake̱: Le̱ ekē̱mi ake̱: Dšiemo̱mi gbe̱ ní maya; mẽhewo̱ ni magbeo?

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ši David dšo foi ni edše edeṅ, ni eba Samuel ṅõ ye̱ Rama, ni ebagbale̱ nii fẽ ni Saul efele̱ le̱. Ni eke̱ Samuel fẽ te ame̱yahĩ ši ye̱ Naiot.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Ni ayatſa Saul adafi ake̱: Na, David ye̱ Naiot ye̱ Rama.

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšũ bo̱foi ake̱ ayamõ David ke̱-ba; ni beni ame̱na gbalo̱i asafoku ní gbaã le̱ ke̱ Samuel ní dši ame̱nukpa ní damo̱ Si le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ ba Saul bo̱foi le̱ ano̱, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱gbagbai.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ni beni ayagba Saul le̱, etšũ bo̱foi krokomei ke̱-te, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱gbagbai nakai noṅṅ. Ni Saul sā tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te ekoṅ noni dši šii etẽ, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱gbagbai.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni le̱dientše̱ hũ eyiṅ ke̱-te Rama, ni beni eše̱ nubu kpeteṅkple ni yo̱ Seku le̱ he le̱, ebi ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ Samuel ke̱ David yo̱? Ni akē̱: Na, ame̱ye̱ Naiot ye̱ Rama.

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ete Naiot ní yo̱ Rama le̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ yi le̱ hũ eno̱, ni ehĩe gbā āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eyaše̱ Naiot ye̱ Rama.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ni le̱ hũ ekplo̱ ehe atadei, ni le̱ hũ egba ye̱ Samuel hĩe, ni ekã ši ke̱ ehe flo nakai gbĩ le̱ ſaneſane ke̱ nyōṅnyōṅ fẽ. Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱kē̱: Ani Saul hũ ye̱ gbalo̱i le̱ ateṅ?

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Dabida! ogboṅ! na, mitše̱ efee noko wulu lo noko bibiō, ake̱ dša ewó mitoi no̱ dã; ni mẽhewo̱ mitše̱ aaṅõ sane ne̱ atēmi? Ebe̱ṅ!

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Ke̱dši otše̱ ná bi miši le̱, no le̱ kē̱mo̱ ake̱: David bimi gbe̱ kpẽkpē̃kpẽ ake̱ ēša foi ke̱-ya Betlehem, emã le̱ṅ; edšake̱ āšã afi afo̱le ye̱ dše̱i ahã weku le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ekē̱ ne̱ke̱ ake̱: Odšogbāṅ! le̱, bēle̱ otšũlo̱ baná hedšo̱le̱; ši ke̱dši emli fũ le̱, ná ole ake̱ emã efõṅ no̱ mĩ́ ye̱ emli.

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Ši Ionatan kē̱: Ene̱ akagbaleo fō̃ṅfõ! Ke̱dši male šrao ake̱ mĩtše̱ emã efõṅ no̱ mĩ́ yo̱ ohe le̱, ani mikē̱ṅo?

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan kē̱ David ake̱: Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, aaye odase, ké̱ mika mitše̱ mikwe̱ wó̱ lo wó̱se̱ be ne̱ yino̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱, ni mina ake̱ ekpakpa ko ye̱ hã David, ni mitšũũ abaa oṅõ abawóó otoi no̱ le̱:

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: no le̱ Iehowa afe Ionatan ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱! Ši ke̱dši mitše̱ mīsumo̱ ake̱ efeo efõṅ le̱, mabawó otoi no̱, ni madšieo gbe̱ ni oya ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli, ni Iehowa ke̱o ahĩ ši take̱ bo̱ni eke̱ mitše̱ hĩ ši le̱.

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan sā hã David kã kitã ekoṅ ye̱ *esuome̱ ní eke̱-sumeo̱le̱ le̱ he-wo̱; edšake̱ esumoo̱le̱ take̱ bo̱ni esumoo̱ le̱dientše̱ ehe. *

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱ oye gbĩĩ etẽ le̱, kplekemo̱ ši mrãmrã ke̱-ba hēgbe̱ ni oyatē ohe ye̱ ye̱ nitšumo̱ gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ohĩ Ezel te̱ le̱ mase̱i.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Ni mi le̱ mibatšẽrẽ gãimlibii etẽ ke̱-ya mase̱igbe̱, tamo̱ noni oti mitſaä.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Ni na, mibatšũ oblanyo le̱ ake̱: Yatao gãimlibii le̱! Ke̱dši mikē̱ oblanyo le̱ ake̱: Na, gãimlibii le̱ ye̱ ose̱gbe̱ ye̱ bie̱ ne̱, kŏ̱lo̱mo̱! le̱, no le̱ ba, edšake̱ hedšo̱le̱ ye̱ hão, ni sane ko be̱, gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa hĩe kã le̱!

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši mikē̱ gbekẽ le̱ ne̱ke̱ ake̱: Na, gãimlibii le̱ etekeo! le̱, no le̱ ya, edšake̱ Iehowa edšieo gbe̱.

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Ke̱ko̱ ni David yatē ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱. Ni eba mli ye̱ nyõṅ hẽ le̱ ne̱ ake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ho etá ši ni ebaye nii.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tá esẽi le̱ no̱ ye̱ hégbe̱ ni etáa dā le̱, ye̱ sẽi ni mã gbogbo he le̱ no̱; ši Ionatan te ši damo̱ ši, ni Abner tá Saul mase̱i, ši David gbe̱he le̱ kã eflo.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ Saul ekē̱ē̱ nokonoko nakai gbĩ le̱; edšake̱ esusu ake̱: Bene̱ noko efele̱, ni ehe tšee, le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ ehe tšee ši.

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ dšetše̱reno̱ ni dši nyõṅ hẽ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ enyo̱ le̱, David gbe̱he le̱ kã eflo ekoṅ, ni Saul kē̱ ebi Ionatan ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni Išai bi le̱ baa niyeli nyè ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱ fẽ ne̱?

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Ṅmẽmi gbe̱ ni maya, edšake̱ wo̱weku le̱ mīšã afo̱le ye̱ mā le̱ṅ, ni minyemi le̱ eše̱mi ake̱ miba; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe le̱, hã ni maya ni mayasra minyemimei le̱! Nohewo̱ ni ebaa maṅtše̱ okplõ le̱ he ne̱.

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul mli fũ wo Ionatan naakpa, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo yō fõṅ ke̱ atũatšelo̱ bi! Ani milee ake̱ oṅō Išai bi le̱ ofe onanyo ni oke̱-wo bodientše̱ ohe ke̱ onye yayaiaṅ hĩegbĕle?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ gbĩĩabo̱ fẽ ni Išai bi le̱ hĩe kã ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, bo ke̱ omaṅtše̱yeli le̱ fẽ damo̱ṅ ši. Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ tšũ ni ayaṅõle̱ abahãmi; edšake̱ gbĕle bi dšile̱!

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan here etše̱ Saul le̱ no̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba aagbele̱? meni efe?

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul *fõle̱ akplo̱ le̱ ni eke̱-gbele̱. Ni Ionatan ke̱-na ake̱ etše̱ emã no̱ mĩ́ ake̱ eegbe David. *

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan ke̱ mlifũ ní nā wa te ši ke̱-dše̱ okplõ le̱ he, ni eyee nii ye̱ nakai nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ enyo̱ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ David sane mīdo̱le̱, ake̱ etše̱ ewole̱ hĩegbĕle ne̱ke̱.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ dšetše̱reno̱ lebi le̱ Ionatan dše kpo ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱ ye̱ be ni eto David le̱ mli, ni eke̱ gbekẽ fiō ko nyie.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ egbekẽ le̱ ake̱: Ša foi ni oyatao gãimlibii le̱ ní mitšẽrẽ le̱! Ni beni gbekẽ le̱ ša foi pe̱ le̱, etšẽ gãimlibi le̱ ke̱-tekele̱.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Ni beni gbekẽ le̱ yaše̱ heni gãimlibi ní Ionatan tšẽ le̱ yo̱ le̱, Ionatan blo̱ gbekẽ le̱ yise̱ ni ekē̱: Ani dšee gãimlibi le̱ etekeo le̱ lo?

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Ši gbekẽ le̱ lee mli eko, Ionatan ke̱ David ke̱ke̱ le sane le̱.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ionatan ṅõ enibii le̱ ehã egbekẽ le̱, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Baho, ni oke̱-ya maṅ.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Beni oblanyo le̱ ete le̱, David te ši ke̱-dše̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱, ni eke̱ *ehĩe babu ši ni ekoto ši šii etẽ; ni ame̱ſo̱ſō̱ ame̱he nā, ni ame̱fófṍ ame̱ſie ame̱he ne̱ āhũ, ši David nõ teke no̱. *

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan kē̱ David ake̱: Ya ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli! gbĩĩabo̱ kẽ ni wo̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ wo̱kãmo̱ kitã ye̱ Iehowa gbe̱i ano̱ ake̱: Iehowa afe mike̱o ke̱ miseši ke̱ bo hũ oseši teṅ odase ke̱-ya nãno̱ le̱!

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: .] Ni oso̱fo le̱ here David no̱ ni ekē̱: Yaka abolo ko be̱ minine no̱, ši *abolo kroṅkroṅ le̱ eko yo̱; ke̱dši oblahĩĩ le̱ †etako yei ahe, ke̱ke̱ le̱ ehĩ. *

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: .] Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱fo le̱ ke̱ abolo kroṅkroṅ le̱ hāle̱, edšake̱ abolo ko abolo ko be̱ dše̱i, ake̱ dša hĩe-mã-abolo le̱ ni adšie ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, koni ake̱ abolo kla ayamã ši gbĩ no̱ ni adšie le̱ noṅṅ le̱. Mat.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: .] Ni David kē̱ Ahimelek ake̱: Ni kole̱ akplo̱ lo klante ko be̱ odeṅ ye̱ bie̱ ne̱? Edšake̱ miklante ke̱ minii tete mikō̱lo̱o̱ mihīee mideṅ ke̱-baa; edšake̱ ãye maṅtše̱ sane le̱ he oyái!

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: .] Ni oso̱fo le̱ kē̱: Goliat, Filistinyo le̱, ni *ogbele̱ ye̱ Ela dšō̱ le̱ṅ le̱ klante le̱, na, no aha he mama ni ekã efod le̱ se̱ le̱; ke̱dši osumo̱ ake̱ ooko̱ le̱, ko̱, edšake̱ ekroko ko be̱ bie̱. Ni David kē̱: Eko tamo̱o̱ no; ṅõhãmi!

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: .] Ke̱ke̱ ni David te ši ni edšo foi nakai gbĩ le̱ ye̱ Saul hĩe, ni eyiṅ ete Akiš, *Gat maṅtše̱ le̱, ṅõ. *Lal.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: .] Ni Akiš tšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani dšee David, šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ne̱? Ani dšee mone̱ be lala alaã ye̱ dšõ̀ mli akē̱o̱ ake̱: Saul egbe ekpeikpei le̱, ši David egbe ekpei-nyoṅmanyo-ṅmai le̱?

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: .] Ni David ṅõ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ eto etšui mli, ni eše Gat maṅtše̱ Akiš gbeyei naakpa.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: .] Ni etšake *enifemo̱ ye̱ ame̱hĩe, ni ekwa eye se̱ke̱ ye̱ ame̱deṅ, ni eṅmlā okadii ye̱ agbó le̱ šĩnāi le̱ ahe, ni ehã eladšõ wu etšẽṅiaṅ kpo̱tō̱. *Lal.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: .] Ke̱ke̱ ni Akiš kē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Na, nyena ake̱ nū le̱ miye se̱ke̱; mẽhewo̱ mo̱ ni nyeke̱le̱ ba miṅõ?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: .] Ani mītao se̱ke̱yelo̱i, hewo̱ ni nyekpla mone̱ ke̱-ba ní ebafe se̱ke̱yelo̱i anii ye̱ mihĩe ne̱? Aso esa ake̱ kũle̱ mone̱ aaba miwe po, be̱?

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõame̱ ke̱-te Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, nĩ ame̱ke̱le̱ hĩ ši gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ ni David yo̱ te̱kplo le̱ mli le̱.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Ši gbalo̱ Gad kē̱ David ake̱: Kāhĩ te̱kplo le̱ mli, ši dše dše̱i ni oya *Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱. Ni David yiṅ nĩ ete Heret kō le̱ mli. *

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Ni Saul banu ake̱ ayana David ke̱ mei ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ lo̱. Ni Saul tá ši ye̱ Gibea ye̱ tamarieke-tšo le̱ šišĩ ye̱ goṅkpo̱ le̱ no̱, ni ehĩe ekplo̱ ye̱ edeṅ, ni etšũdši le̱ fẽ damo̱ emase̱i.

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: hewo̱ ni nye fẽ tſẽm nyekpãṅ miyi no̱, nĩ mokomoko be̱ ni wóo̱ mitoi no̱, ake̱ *mibi le̱ ke̱ Išai bi le̱ ekpãṅ, ni mokomoko be̱ nyeteṅ ní misane do̱ō̱le̱, ni eewó mitoi no̱, ake̱ mibi le̱ etẽ mitšũlo̱ le̱ ši ewomi, koni ewomi ka, tamo̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱!

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul tšũ ayakpē oso̱ſo Ahimelek, Ahitub le̱ bi le̱, ke̱ etše̱ we le̱ ní dši oso̱foi ní yo̱ Nob le̱ fẽ ke̱-ba. Ni ame̱fẽ ame̱ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱: Bo toi, bo Ahitub bi! Ni ekē̱: Nami, minuṅtšo̱!

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mēba nyekpãṅ miyino̱, bo ke̱ Išai bi le̱, koni ohãle̱ niyenii ke̱ klante, ni obi nii ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ hũ ohãle̱, koni ete ši ewomi ni ewomi ká, tamo̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱?

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ni Ahimelek to he ehã maṅtše̱ le̱ ni ekē̱: Ši otšũdši le̱ fẽ ateṅ namo po dši ano̱kwafo tamo̱ David, ni edši *maṅtše̱ šānū, ni oke̱le̱ too̱ adšina, ni ehĩe yo̱ nyam ye̱ owe le̱?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Ani ṅme̱ne̱ dãni mibōi Nyoṅmo̱ nibimo̱ ke̱ le̱ hãmo̱? Ene̱ akagbalemi fṍṅfõ! Maṅtše̱ akaṅõ sane efõ etšũlo̱ no̱ lo mitše̱ we le̱ fẽ no̱; edšake̱ emli bibiō dšio, ewulu dšio, otšũlo̱ lee mli ekomeflo.

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ahimelek, dša agbeo, bo ke̱ otše̱ we le̱ fẽ!

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ hebulo̱i ní damo̱ emase̱i le̱ ake̱: Nyetšṍmo̱a nyehe ní nyegbea Iehowa oso̱foi le̱; edšake̱ ame̱ hũ ame̱nine fata David he, ni asaṅ ame̱le ake̱ foi edšeo̱ le̱, ni ame̱wóó mitoi no̱! Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũdši le̱ ekplẽẽ ake̱ ame̱-akpã ame̱nine mlĩ ye̱ Iehowa oso̱foi le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Ni *Nob ni dši oso̱foi le̱ amaṅ le̱, eke̱ klante gbe emli bii le̱, bii ke̱ yei, gbekẽbii ke̱ fufo̱bii, ke̱ tšinai ke̱ tedšii ke̱ tōi fẽ le̱ eke̱ klante gbe. *

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Ši Ahitub bi Ahimelek bihĩĩ le̱ ateṅ mokome ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Abiatar le̱ dše mli ni edšo foi ke̱-tiu David.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Ni Abiatar yagba David ake̱ Saul egbe Iehowa oso̱foi le̱.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Abiatar ake̱: Nakai gbĩ le̱ bēbe ni *Doeg, Edomnyo le̱, yo̱ dše̱i le̱ mile ake̱ kē̱mo̱ noṅṅ ebaya eyakē̱ Saul: mi mihã ene̱ ba otše̱ we le̱ susumai le̱ fẽ ano̱ ne̱! *K.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Oke̱mi ahĩ ši, kāše gbeyei! edšake̱ moni taoo̱ mi agbe, le̱ noṅṅ taoo̱ bo hũ agbe; ši ke̱ oye̱ miṅõ le̱, oofe ſeſēſe.

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Ši David webii le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, ye̱ Iuda bie̱ ne̱ po le̱ wo̱mīše gbeyei, ši mbasroo noni wo̱o̱te Keila ni wo̱ke̱ Filistibii atai le̱ ayawu?

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David sā yabi Iehowa ekoṅ. Ni Iehowa to he ehãle̱ ake̱: Te ši ni oya Keila; edšake̱ mibaṅõ Filistibii le̱ mawo odeṅ!

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ yiṅ ke̱-te Keila, ni eke̱ Filistibii le̱ yawu, ni elō ame̱koloi ke̱-te, ni *egbeame̱ butū. Ni David here Keilabii le̱ ayiwala. *

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ni beni David ná le ake̱ Saul eto ehe yiṅ fõṅ le̱, ekē̱ oso̱fo Abiatar ake̱: *Oke̱ efod le̱ aba bie̱! *

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱: Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱! otšũlo̱ enu ake̱ Saul mītao aba Keila, ni ebakpãtã maṅ le̱ hĩe ye̱ mihewo̱:

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
