translation_verse: ani Keilabii le̱ aadšiemi awo edeṅ lo? ani Saul aakpleke ši aba le̱le̱ṅ, ta-ke̱ bo̱ni otšũlo̱ enu le̱ lo? Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱, mīkpao fai, kē̱mo̱ otšũlo̱! Ni Iehowa kē̱: Hẽ, eeba.

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱: Ani Keilabii le̱ aadšiemi ke̱ miwebii le̱ ame̱wo Saul deṅ lo? Iehowa kē̱: Ame̱adšieo ame̱hã.

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Ši David yahĩ *ṅã le̱ no̱ ye̱ te̱-kploi le̱ amli, ni eyahĩ goṅ ko no̱ ye̱ Zif ṅã le̱ no̱. Ni gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ Saul mītao-le̱; ši Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱le̱ woo edeṅ. *K.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Ni David na ake̱ Saul efã ke̱-ba ebataole̱ egbe; ši David ye̱ Zif ṅã le̱ no̱ ye̱ kō le̱ mli.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Ni Saul bi Ionatan te ši ni eyiṅ ete David ṅõ ye̱ kō le̱ mli, ni eyawole̱ hewale̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāše gbeyei, edšake̱ mitše̱ Saul nine še̱ṅ ono̱, ší bo ooye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱, ni matšṍ ose̱mo; ni mitše̱ Saul dientše̱ *le nakai. *

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni *Zifbii le̱ yiṅ ke̱-ba Saul ṅõ ye̱ Gibea ame̱bakē̱: Ani dšee David ebatē ehe ye̱ wo̱ṅõ ye̱ kō le̱ṅ te̱kploi le̱ amli, ye̱ Hakila goṅkpo̱ le̱ ní yo̱ ṅã kpatā le̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱?

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nyeyaã ni nyeyataoa mli dšogbāṅ, ni nyekwe̱ ni nyele eſe̱mo̱he ke̱ moni nale̱ ye̱ dše̱i, edšake̱ akē̱mi ake̱ ele ṅã naakpa dientše̱.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyekwe̱a ní nyelea tē-mo̱hei hei ní eyatēo̱ ehe ye̱ le̱ fẽ, ni ké̱ nyele mli po̱tē̃ le̱, nyebaä miṅõ ekoṅ, ni mike̱nye aate. Ni aaba mli ake̱, ke̱-dši eye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, no le̱ mataole̱ fitšofitšo ke̱-akpa Iuda akpei abo̱ le̱ fẽ no̱!

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱te ši ni ame̱tšṍ Saul hĩe ke̱-te Zif. Ši David ke̱ ewebii le̱ ye̱ Maon ṅã le̱ no̱, ye̱ dšō̱-šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ ṅã kpatā le̱ wuoyigbe̱.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ni Saul ke̱ ewebii le̱ yiṅ ame̱te le̱ taomo̱. Ni ayagba David, ni ekpleke ši ke̱-te te̱sā le̱ mli, ni ehĩ ši ye̱ Maon ṅã le̱ no̱. Ni beni Saul nu le̱, eṅõ-ſie David se̱ ke̱-ba Maon ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Ni Saul nyie goṅ le̱ bie̱gbe̱, ni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ nyie goṅ le̱ se̱gbe̱; ni Saul he gbeyei nā le̱ David mīye oyái ní edše dše̱i, edšake̱ Saul ke̱ ewebii le̱ mīsá David ke̱ ewebii le̱ ayi, koni amemõmo̱ame̱.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Ši bo̱fo ko ba Saul ṅõ bakē̱le̱ ake̱: Ohe afe oyá ní oba, ši Filistibii le̱ eba ame̱baha šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Saul fõ David se̱nyiemo̱, ni eyiṅ ete eke̱ Filistibii le̱ yakpe; nohewo̱ le̱ atšé̱o̱ dše̱i ake̱ Sela-Hamahelekot.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul ṅõ hĩĩ akpei-etẽ ní ahalaame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Israel ſë mli, ni eyiṅ ete eyatao David ke̱ ewebii le̱ ye̱ dùdši ate̱sāi le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ tōiatšũi le̱ ahe ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱, heni te̱kplo ko yo̱ le̱, Saul te mli ní eyawa enane; ši *David ke̱ ewebii le̱ trá bu le̱ se̱gbe̱. *Lal.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ ewebii le̱ ake̱: Iehowa aka-hã ene̱ mīgbalemi fõṅfõ ake̱ mafe minuṅtšo̱, moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱, ne̱ke̱ noko, ake̱ *makpā minine mli ye̱ eno̱; edšake̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ dšile̱. *

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ wale ewebii le̱, ní ekplẽẽame̱ ní ame̱te ši ame̱wo Saul. Ni Saul te ši ke̱-dše̱ te̱kplo le̱ṅ ni eyi egbe̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni fe se̱ le̱ David hũ te ši ni edše kpo ke̱-dše̱ te̱kplo le̱ mli, ni eyablo̱ Saul yise̱ ekē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! Ni beni Saul kwe̱ ese̱ le̱, David ke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekotole̱.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Na, ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ ona ke̱ ohĩṅme̱ii, bo̱ni Iehowa dšieo ewo mideṅ ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ te̱kplo le̱ mli; ni meikomei kē̱mi ake̱ migbeo, ši kẽle̱ migbeeo, ni mikē̱: Mikpãṅ minine mli ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ no̱; edšake̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ dšile̱!

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Iehowa akodšo mike̱o teṅ, ni Iehowa noṅṅ ato̱ mihe owele ye̱ one̱; ši mi le̱ minine esaṅ ohe! Rom.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Take̱ bo̱ni blema abe̱ le̱ kē̱o̱ le̱: Meifõdši adeṅ nõfõṅ dše̱o̱; ši mi le̱ minine esaṅ ohe.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Namo se̱ po Israel maṅtše̱ efã kpo ke̱-nyie ne̱? namo po otiuo̱ ne̱? Gbé gbonyo ni, lo̱po ni!

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa aafe atẽṅbulo̱, ni eeko-dšo mike̱o teṅ, ni eekwe̱, ni eeye mi-sane ehãmi, ni eebumi bem ni edšiemi ye̱ odeṅ!

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ David ake̱: Odša fèmi; edšake̱ heni ofeo̱mi ekpakpa le̱, bēle̱ mi le̱ mifeo efõṅ.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Nme̱ne̱ otšõ faṅṅ, bo̱ni ofemi edšũrõ ohã, ake̱ nõ kẽ ní Iehowa tumi ewo odeṅ ni ogbeemi le̱.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ke̱ gbomo ko nine še̱ ehenye̱lo̱ no̱ le̱, aso eehã eke̱ ehe aya ſeſēſe? Nohewo̱ le̱ Iehowa aawoö nyõmo̱ kpakpa ye̱ noni ofe ohãmi ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, na, *miná mile ake̱ bo kẽ obaye maṅtše̱ le̱, ni Israel maṅtše̱yeli le̱ badamo̱ ši šiṅṅ ye̱ odeṅ. *

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ na Iehowa otšõmi ake̱ oflo̱ṅ misešibii ni aaba ye̱ mise̱ le̱ oše̱re̱ṅ oſieṅ, ni ogbeṅ migbe̱i ye̱ mitše̱ we le̱.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Ni David nu he ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ake̱ Nabal mīku etōi ahetšo̱i.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni nyekē̱ale̱ ne̱: Hã omanye aba! Hedšo̱le̱ ahão, ni hedšo̱le̱ ahã owe le̱, ni hedšo̱le̱ ahã nofẽno ní oyo̱!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ minu ake̱ oye̱ tōhetšo̱ikulo̱i; agbe̱ne̱ le̱ otōkwe̱lo̱i le̱ ke̱-wo̱ bahī ši le̱, wo̱feeame̱ efõṅ ko, ni asaṅ ame̱nokonoko elādšee gbĩĩabo̱ fẽ ni ame̱-yo̱ Karmel le̱.

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Ni beni David oblahĩĩ le̱ te le̱, ame̱tšĩ nakai gbẽ le̱ fẽ ame̱hã Nabal ye̱ David gbe̱i ano̱; ni ame̱sẽ koni.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Koni bēle̱ miṅõ mibolo ke̱ minu ke̱ milō ní migbe mihā mitõhetšo̱ikulo̱i le̱, ni miṅõ-hā hĩĩ ní milee heni ame̱-dše̱ le̱, be̱?

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David oblaĩĩ le̱ tšṍ ame̱he ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱, ni ame̱ba ame̱bagbale̱ nakai wieme̱i le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ ewebii le̱ ake̱: Nyeteṅ mofẽmo aṅmõ eklante! Ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo ṅmõ eklante, ni David hũ ṅmõ eklante, ni hĩĩ aafe ohai-edſe̱ nyie David se̱ ke̱-fã; ni hĩĩ ohai-enyo̱ hĩ nibii le̱ ahe.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ná ole ni odſẽṅ noni oofe; edšake̱ aſã wo̱nuṅtšo̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ yi no̱; ni le̱ le̱ yakagbomo dšile̱, ni ehĩĩ le̱ wiemo̱-ke̱-tšõmo̱ po.

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ eblahĩĩ le̱ ake̱: Nyetšṍa mihĩe; na, minyie nyese̱ ke̱-mība! Ši ewù Nabal le̱, ekē̱ē̱le̱ noko.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni etá tedši le̱ no̱ ke̱-kpleke Si ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱ kow̌ei le̱ mli ke̱-baã le̱, na, David ke̱ ewebii le̱ hũ kpleke ši ke̱le̱ bakpe.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ David ekē̱ ake̱: Yakatſā po miba nibii fẽ ní mone̱ ye̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ yi, ni enibii fẽ ní eyo̱ le̱ mli eko eko elādšee; ni eṅõ efõṅ etomi ekpakpa nãdšiaṅ ne̱.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ afe David, ke̱dši wō̱, beni dše aatše̱re le̱, mišĩ *nū ko nū ko ye̱ nii fẽ ní dši enõ le̱ ateṅ fĩ! *

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Ofai ne̱, minuṅtšo̱ akadi ne̱ke̱ nū yakagbomo ní dši Nabal ne̱ se̱, edšake̱ bo̱ni egbe̱i yo̱ le̱, nakai eyo̱: Nabal dši egbe̱i, ni bului asane eyeo̱; ši mi, oweyõ le̱, minaa minuṅtšo̱ oblahĩĩ le̱ ni otšũ le̱.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Ofai ne̱, ṅõ tõmo̱ ne̱ ofa oweyō; edšake̱ Iehowa bamã šĩa ní mã ši šiṅṅ ahã minuṅtšo̱; edšake̱ minuṅtšo̱ wuo̱ Iehowa tai le̱, ní akana nõfõṅ ko nõfõṅ ko hũ ye̱ ohe owala gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši gbomo ádesà aate ši ni eenyie ose̱ ake̱ etao bo egbe le̱, no le̱ aafī minuṅtšo̱ susuma afata mei ni yo̱ wala le̱ ahe ato Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅō; ši ohenye̱lo̱i le̱ asusuma le̱, le̱ le̱ eefõle̱ ye̱ akromia mli.

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: ene̱ akatšṍ pampĩ ke̱ tšõne mīhã minuṅtšo̱, ake̱ oſie lá ši yakatſā, alo ake̱ minuṅtšo̱ eto̱ le̱dientše̱ ehe owele. Ši kē̱ Iehowa ná fe minuṅtšo̱ edšũrõ le̱, no le̱ kaimo̱ oweyō!

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ Abigail ake̱: Aadšō̱ Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni tšũo ni oke̱mi bakpe ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱;

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: ni aadšē̱ onilẽ ne̱, ni aadšō̱ bodientše̱ ake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ otšĩ minā ní mikaye lá ko yi sõ, ni asaṅ mike̱ minine akato̱ midìentše̱ mihe owele!

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Ši ano̱kwa, gbĩĩabo̱ ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni tšĩ minā ní mikafeo efõṅ le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, edši ohe efee oyá ni oke̱mi abakpe kũle̱, wó̱, beni dše aatše̱re le̱, eſe̱ṅ nū ko nū ko hãṅ Nabal.

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David he noni eke̱-bahãle̱ le̱ ye̱ edeṅ, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya owe ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli; na, mibo ogbē toi, ni mikwe̱ ohĩe!

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Ni Abigail ba Nabal ṅõ, ni na, eṅmẽ okplõ ye̱ ewe le̱ tamo̱ maṅtše̱ ko, ni Nabal mī eše̱ ehe, ni eto̱ dã kpo̱tō̱; ni ekē̱ē̱le̱ noko ke̱-yaši dšetše̱reno̱ lebi.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ lebi, beni wein le̱ etšere̱ ye̱ Nabal hĩe le̱, eṅã le̱ gbale̱ sã-dši ne̱ fẽ. Ke̱ke̱ ni etšui gbo tum ye̱ emli, ni efe šikplikpī tamo̱ te̱.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ no se̱ aafe gbĩĩ nyoṅma le̱ Iehowa tſa Nabal nõ, ni egbo.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Ni ete ši ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekē̱: Na, oweyō dši tšũlo̱yō ní aafo̱ minuṅtšo̱ tšũdši le̱ anãdši ahe!

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Ni Abigail he fe oyá ni ete ši ni eho etá tedši no̱, ke̱ eblayeibii enumo̱ ní nyie ese̱, ni enyie David bo̱foi le̱ ase̱ ke̱-te, ni eyatšṍ *eṅã. *

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: David sā ṅõ Ahinoam ni dše̱ Iezreel le̱ hũ; ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ ame̱-tšṍmo̱ eṅãmei.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Ši Saul eṅõ ebiyō Mikal, David ṅã le̱, ehă *Palti ní dši Laiš bi ní dše̱ Galim le̱. *

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Ni Saul yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Hakila goṅkpo̱ le̱ ni yo̱ ṅã kpatā le̱ hĩe le̱ no̱, ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ he; ši David hĩ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni ena ake̱ Saul nyie ese̱ ke̱-mība ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: Ni David tšũ sralo̱i, ni ená ele ake̱ Saul ená eba le̱le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David te ši ni eba hégbe̱ ni Saul ebo̱ nsra ye̱ le̱; ni David na hégbe̱ ní Saul ke̱ *etatše̱ Abner, Ner bi le̱, kāmo̱; ni Saul kă ſīlii ateṅ, ni maṅ le̱ ebo̱ nsra ke̱-bo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe. *

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ le̱ yadše David nā le̱ ekē̱ Ahimelek, Hitnyo le̱, ke̱ Abišai, Zeruia bi ni dši Ioab nyemi le̱, ake̱: Namo ke̱-mi aakpleke ši ke̱-ate Saul ṅõ ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ? Ni Abišai kē̱: Mike̱o aakpleke ši ke̱-ate!

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ Abišai ba maṅ le̱ ṅõ nyōṅ, ni na, Saul kã ši ewo̱ ye̱ ſīlii le̱ ateṅ, ni ekplo̱ le̱ tše̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ye̱ eyiteṅgbe̱; ši Abner ke̱ maṅ le̱ kãmo̱ ehewo̱ ke̱-bo̱lelo̱ ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Ni Abišai kē̱ David ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ edšie ohenye̱lo̱ le̱ ewo odeṅ, nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ *hã matšule̱ akplo̱ ke̱-mõ ši-kpoṅ šikome nyoṅlo, ni mihãṅ atīale̱ šii enyo̱! *

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ši David kē̱ Abišai ake̱: Kākpãtã ehĩe; edšake̱ namo po aanyẽ akpã enine mli ye̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱ no̱, ni eeye ehe?

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Iehowa akahã ene̱ mīgbalemi fō̃ṅfō ake̱ makpã minine mli ye̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱ no̱! Ni agbe̱ne̱, ofai ne̱, ko̱ akplo̱ le̱ ni yo̱ eyiteṅgbe̱ le̱, ni owó nu-ke̱-kpulu le̱, ní wo̱te!

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ko̱ akplo̱ le̱ ni ewó nu-ke̱-kpulu le̱ ye̱ Saul yiteṅ, ni ame̱-dše dše̱i ame̱te, ni mokomoko enaa, ni mokomoko lee, ni asaṅ mokomoko hĩe etšẽẽ, ši ame̱fẽ ame̱wo̱wo̱i; edšake̱ Iehowa *ehã wō̱ ní tšī ko enyõ ame̱no. *

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David tše mli ke̱-te se̱ le̱, ni eyadamo̱ goṅ le̱ yiteṅ ye̱ se̱ fle̱ṅṅ, gbe̱ kplaṅṅ kã ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Ni David blo̱ tšé̱ maṅ le̱ ke̱ Abner, Ner bi le̱, ekē̱: Oheree no̱ lo? Abner! Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner here no̱ ni ekē̱: Bo namo oblo̱ō̱ owoo maṅtše̱ le̱?

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Abner ake̱: Ani dšee nū dšio? ni namo tamo̱o ye̱ Israel? kole̱ mẽba ni obuu onuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ he? Edšake̱ moko dše̱ mei le̱ ateṅ ba ní kũle̱ ebakpãtã onuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Noni ofe ne̱ ehīĩ po! Ake̱ nõ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kă ne̱, gbēle bii dšinye, edšake̱ nyebuu nyenuṅtšo̱ ni dši moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱ he! Ni agbe̱ne̱, kwe̱ heni maṅtše̱ akplo̱ le̱ ke̱ nu-ke̱-kpulu le̱ ní yo̱ eyiteṅgbe̱ le̱ yo̱.

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul yo David gbē, ni ekē̱: Mibi David, ogbē ne̱? Ni David kē̱: Migbē ni, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱!

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mẽba minuṅtšo̱ nyie etšũlo̱ se̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱? Ši meni mife? alo mẽ efõṅ po yo̱ mideṅ?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, hã minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ abo etšũlo̱ wiemo̱i atoi: Ke̱dši Iehowa ni tẽo ši womi le̱, hã ehere afo̱le ṅma; ši ke̱-dii ádesãi abii ni le̱, no le̱ alomo̱ame̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, edšake̱ ame̱ſiemi ṅme̱ne̱, ko-ni mikakpe̱te̱ Iehowa no̱yelihe le̱ he, ame̱-kē̱: Ya ni oyasúmo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei!

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ kāhã mila mīſie šikpoṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; edšake̱ Israel maṅtše̱ efã kpo eba lo̱po kome taomo̱, take̱ bo̱ni moko yagbo̱bio̱ afi ye̱ gõdši ano̱ le̱!

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱: Mife eša; kũ ose̱, mibi David; edšake̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ní misusuma dšra wa ye̱ ohĩe ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱, mifeṅo efõṅ ko doṅṅ; na, miye kwašiai asane, ni mitõ babaō dientše̱!

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Ni David here no̱ ni ekē̱: Na maṅtše̱ akplo̱ le̱! hã oblahĩĩbii le̱ ateṅ mokome aba ní ebaṅō!

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa aawo mofẽmo nyõmo̱ ye̱ edšale̱ ke̱ eno̱kwayeli hewo̱; edšake̱ Iehowa tuo ewo mideṅ ṅme̱ne̱, ši mi ni misumo̱o̱ ake̱ mikpāa minine mli ye̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Ni na, bo̱ni osusuma da kpeteṅkple ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ mihĩe le̱, nakai noṅṅ misusuma aada kpeteṅkple ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni eedšiemi ke̱-dše̱ amanehũlũi fẽ amli!

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Ni Saul kē̱ David ake̱: Aadšō̱o, mibi David! Ootšu nii wudši, ni ooye kũnim hũ! Ke̱ke̱ ni David yiṅ te, ni Saul kũ ese̱ ke̱-te edšé̱he.

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Ni ayagba Saul ake̱ David edšo foi ke̱-te Gat; ni eyaa no̱ etaoole̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Akiš ke̱ *Ziklag hãle̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ; nohewo̱ le̱ Ziklag etšṍ Iuda maṅtšemei le̱ anõ ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱. *Ios.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩĩ abo̱ ni David ye ye̱ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dši afi ke̱ nyõdši edſe̱.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ fă, ni ame̱-yatua Gešurbii ke̱ Girzibii ke̱ Amalekbii le̱; edšake̱ ame̱ ame̱yo̱ šikpoṅ ni kă ši ke̱-yaši Šur āhũ ke̱-yaſie Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-dše̱ tetēte.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Ni David yatua šikpoṅ le̱, ni ehãã nū ko lo yō ko yi aná wala, ni elō tōi ke̱ tšinai ke̱ tedšii ke̱ yomai ke̱ atadei, ni ekũ ese̱ ke̱-ba Akiš ṅõ.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Ni ké̱ Akiš bi ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ nyeyatua ṅme̱ne̱? le̱, David kē̱o̱ ake̱: Wo̱yatua Iuda wuoyigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ Ierameelbii le̱ awuoyigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ Kenbii le̱ awuoyigbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Ši David hãã nū ko lo yō ko yi aná wala ní eke̱ame̱ aba Gat, ekē̱: Koni ame̱kagba ye̱ wo̱hewo̱ ake̱: Ne̱ke̱ David fe! Ni gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ ni eyo̱ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ le̱, nakai efeo̱.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Ni Akiš he David eye ekē̱: Ehã emaṅ Israel yiṅ *edšele̱ fũ kwră po, nohewo le̱ eetšṍ mitšũlo ke̱-ate nāno̱! *

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Ni beni Filistibii bua ame̱he nā ni ame̱babo̱ nsra ye̱ Šunem le̱, Saul hũ bua Israel mū le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ní ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Ni beni Saul ná Filistibii le̱ ata le̱, eše gbeyei ni etšui fã naakpa.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Nyeyataoa yō *okõmfo ko nyehãami, ni maya eṅõ ní mayabi nii ye̱ eṅõ. Ni etšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake: Na, yō ekõmfo ko ye̱ Endor. *Bo̱f.

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Ni Saul tšake ehe ni ewo atade kroko, ni eyiṅ ete, ni hĩĩ enyo̱ fata ehe, ni ame̱ba yō le̱ ṅõ nyōṅ, ni ekē̱: Femo̱ nii ohãmi, ni ohã moni mawo egbe̱i atã matšõo le̱ aba.

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Ši yō le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, bodientše̱ ole noni Saul efe le̱, bo̱ni ekpãtã okõmfoi ke̱ klamo̱i ahĩe ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ni mẽba otšṍo̱ misusuma tšõne, koni ohã agbemi?

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul na Iehowa etšõle̱ ekē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, sō ko sō ko tēreṅo ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ hewo̱!

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yō le̱ kē̱: Namo mihã aba? Ni ekē̱: Hã Samuel aba!

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Ni beni yō le̱ na Samuel le̱, ebo ke̱ gbē wale̱; ni yō le̱ kē̱ Saul ake̱: Mẽba ni olakami ne̱ke̱? ši bo dši Saul!

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāše gbeyei! ši meni ona? Ni yō le̱ kē̱ Saul ake̱: Mina sisa ko mīfã kpo ke̱-mīdše̱ šikpoṅ šiši ke̱-mība.

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Té esu yo̱ tēṅ? Ni ekē̱: Nūmo ko mīfã ke̱-mība, ni ebu mama yū. Ni Saul yo ake̱ Samuel ni; ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekotole̱.

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Ni Samuel kē̱: Ni mẽba obio̱mi nii, ni ona ake̱ Iehowa edše ose̱ ni etšṍ ohenye̱lo̱ le̱?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa tšṍ mino̱ ewie le̱, efe nakai; edšake̱ Iehowa ešõ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ye̱ odeṅ, ni eke̱-hã onanyo ni dši David le̱;

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Iehowa aaṅõ bo ke̱ Israel fẽ awo Filistibii le̱ adeṅ; ni *wó̱ ni dši wó̱ le̱ bo ke̱ obihĩĩ le̱ ke̱mi aabahĩ ši; asaṅ Iehowa aato Israel ta le̱ awo Filistibii le̱ adeṅ. *

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni amrõ le̱ Saul fle̱o̱ ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei egbē ši, edšake̱ eše gbeyei naakpa ye̱ Samuel wiemo̱i le̱ ahewo̱; hewale̱ komeflo be̱ emli; edšake̱ eyeko nokonoko ſaneſane ke̱ nyōṅnyōṅ fẽ.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yō le̱ ba Saul ṅõ, ni ena ake̱ ehao naakpa, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, oweyō ebo ogbē toi, ni mike̱ miwala tete ehĩe mideṅ, ni miho owiemo̱i ni oke̱mi wie le̱ atoi.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, ofai ne̱, bo hũ bo oweyō gbē toi, ni ohã maṅō abolo atrõma ko mamã ohĩe ní oye, koni oná hewale̱, ke̱ oyi gbe̱ ni ōya le̱.

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Ši ekplẽẽ ni ekē̱: Miyee! Ši etšũ-dši le̱ ke̱ yō le̱ fẽ nyẽ eno̱; ni ebo ame̱-gbē toi, ni ete ši ye̱ šikpoṅ lo̱ ni eho etá sā le̱ no̱.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ ye̱ tšinabi ko ní ewo fo̱ ye̱ šĩa le̱, ni ehe fe oyá ni egbele̱, ni eṅõ mãmu ní ekpo̱to̱ ní eṅõ-šã abolo akpĩtĩ;

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: ni eke̱-mã Saul ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ahĩe, ni ame̱ye. Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱te ši ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te nakai nyō le̱ṅ.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Ši Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ amli fũ wole̱; ni Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Hã nū le̱ akũ ese̱, nĩ eya he ni oto ohale̱ le̱ ekoṅ, ni eke̱wo̱ akaya ta le̱, ní eyatšṍ ehĩe ewowo̱ ye̱ ta le̱ mli; ši meni mone̱ ke̱-ate ayakpãtã enuṅtšo̱ le̱? ani dšee ne̱ke̱ hĩĩ ne̱ ayitšei?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Ani dšee David ne̱ he *lala ame̱woo̱ ni ahereo̱ ne̱ ye̱ dšõ̀i amli ake̱: Saul egbe ekpeikpei le̱, ši David egbe ekpei-nyoṅmanyoṅmai le̱? *

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Akiš tšé̱ David ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, ano̱kwafo dšio, bo̱ni oke̱mi dšee̱ kpo ke̱-yaã ke̱-baä ye̱ nsra ne̱ mli le̱ esa mihĩe dšogbäṅ, edšake̱ minako noko efõṅ ko ye̱ ohe ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ ne̱ ni oba miṅõ ne̱ āhũ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱; ši lume̱i le̱ ni náá ohe mīše̱.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ kũ óse̱ ni oya ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli, koni okafe noko ni esaa Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ ahĩe!

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Ši David kē̱ Akiš ake̱: Ši meni po mife? ni meni hũ ona ye̱ otšũlo̱ he ke̱-dē̱e̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ni mibahĩ ši ye̱ ohĩe ne̱ āhũ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, hewe̱ ni mikaya ni mike̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ henye̱lo̱i le̱ mīyawu le̱?

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Ni Akiš here ne̱ ni ekē̱ David ake̱: Mile ake̱ ohĩ ye̱ mihīe tamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ *bo̱-fo; Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ ke̱ke̱ ni kē̱ ake̱: Eke̱wo̱ akaya ta le̱! *

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, oke̱ onuṅtšo̱ tšũdši le̱ ní ke̱o ba le̱, ni amrõ pe̱ ní nyeate ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni dšeṅ aatše ahãnye ke̱ke̱ le̱, nyeyia mli.

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ te ši mră, koni ame̱yiṅ lebi le̱ ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ya Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱. Ši Filistibii le̱ fã ke̱-te Iezreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ baše̱ Ziklag gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ no̱ le̱, Amalekbii le̱ ebatua wuoyigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ Ziklag, ni ame̱fite Ziklag, ni ame̱-ke̱ la ešãle̱;

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Ni beni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ ba mã le̱ṅ le̱, na, ašãle̱ ke̱ la, ni ame̱ṅãmei ke̱ ame̱bihĩĩ ke̱ ame̱biyei le̱, aṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Ni David *ṅãmei enyo̱ le̱, Ahinoam, Iezreelyō le̱, ke̱ Abigail ni dši Karmelnyo Nabal le̱ ṅã le̱, hũ aṅõame̱ nom. *

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Ni efĩ David naakpa dientše̱, edšake̱ maṅ le̱ kē̱ ame̱batſiale̱ tei; edšake̱ sane le̱ edo̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ, mofẽmo ye̱ ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei ahewo̱. Ši David wadše ehe ye̱ Iehowa, e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mli.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ oso̱fo Abiatar, Ahimelek bi le̱, ake̱: *Oke̱ efod le̱ abahãmi! Ni Abiatar ke̱ efod le̱ baha David. *

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱na Mizraimnyo ko ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni ame̱kplale̱ ke̱-ba David ṅō; ni ame̱hãle̱ abolo ni eye, ni ame̱hãle̱ nu hū enu,

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: ni ame̱hãle̱ agbãmi tatale kuku ke̱ weinyibii šabii enyo̱, ni eye, ni *ehĩe tšere̱le̱; edšake̱ eyeko abolo ko le̱, asaṅ enuko nu hũ dšetše̱remo̱ ke̱ dšenamo̱ gbĩĩ etẽ soṅṅ. *Kodš.

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani oke̱mi aakpleke ši ke̱-ya ta ne̱ ṅõ? Ni ekē̱: Na Nyoṅmo̱ otšõmi ake̱ ogbeṅmi ni osā odšieṅmi owoṅ minuṅtšo̱ deṅ, no le̱ mike̱o aakpleke ši ke̱-ya ta ne̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Ni beni eke̱le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-te le̱, na, ame̱buabna ši ye̱ dše̱i fẽ, ni ame̱mīyeyē nii ni ame̱mīnnnū dā̃i ni ame̱mīdšodšoi ye̱ hãnii babaō ní ame̱ha ke̱-dše̱ Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ahewo̱.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Ni David tſiaame̱ nii dšenamo̱ ke̱ dšetše̱remo̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱, ni ame̱-teṅ mokomoko edšeo mli, ake̱ dša oblahĩĩ ohai-edſe̱ ní ho trá yomai ano̱ ní ame̱dšo foi le̱.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Ni David šõ nibii fẽ ní Amalekbii le̱ balō ke̱-te le̱; ni David šõ eṅãmei enyo̱ le̱ hũ;

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: ni eſe̱e̱ ame̱nokonoko, bibiō dšio ewulu dšio, bihĩī dšio, biyei dšio, alo nihānii lo nibii ní ame̱ṅõ le̱ amli eko dšio: David šõ fẽ tſẽm ke̱-ba ekoṅ.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Ni David lō tōi ke̱ tšinai le fẽ, ni ame̱nyie koloi le̱ ahĩe, ni ame̱kē̱: Ene̱ le̱ David nomṅõnii ne̱!

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbomei fõdši ke̱ yakagbomei ni yo̱ mei ní ke̱ David te le̱ ateṅ le̱ here no̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní ame̱-ke̱wo̱ eyaa ne̱, akahãame̱ nihānii ní wo̱-yašõ ke̱-ba le̱ eko, ake̱ dša moſẽmo ṅã ke̱ ebii, ní ame̱kplaame̱ ni ame̱ya.

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Ši David kē̱: Minyemimei, nyeke̱ noni Iehowa ehãwo̱ le̱ akafea nakai, gbĩĩabo̱ ni eba wo̱he, ni edšie ta ni ba-tuawo̱ lo̱ ewo wo̱deṅ le̱.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ni namo po aabonye toi ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ mli? *Ši bo̱ni dši moni te ta le̱ nā le̱ gbe̱nã le̱, nakai noṅṅ dši moni hĩ nibii le̱ ahe le̱ gbe̱nã: ame̱dša mli pe̱pē̱pe̱! *

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ke̱-dše̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ āhũ ke̱-yaä ne̱, aṅõ ene̱ afe akpo ke̱ mla ahã Israel ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Ni beni David ba Ziklag le̱, etšũ ake̱ nomṅõnii le̱ eko yahã Iuda onukpai le̱ ni dši enanemei le̱, ekē̱: Na nikēnii ní dše̱ Iehowa henye̱lo̱i le̱ anomṅõnii le̱ amli ni ake̱-bahãnye!

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Ni beni ta le̱ mli wa hã Saul, ni gãitšẽlo̱i le̱ mīninale̱ le̱, etšui fã naakpa ye̱ ame̱hewo̱.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ ake̱: Gblamo̱ *oklante ní oke̱-dũmi, ko-ni ne̱ke̱ fõlo̱i ne̱ akaba ame̱badũmi, ní ame̱femĩ niseniianii. Ši etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ ekplẽẽ; edšake̱ ēše gbeyei naakpa dientše̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ Saul ko̱ eklante ni eho egbē no̱. *Kodš.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Ni beni etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ na ake̱ Saul egbo le̱, le̱ hũ eho egbē eklante no̱, ni eke̱le̱ gbo.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Saul ke̱ ebihĩĩ etẽ le̱ ke̱ etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ ke̱ ewebii le̱ fẽ gboi šikome ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ ne̱.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Ni beni Israelbii le̱ ni ye̱ dšō̱ le̱ se̱ ke̱ mei ni yo̱ Iordan se̱ le̱ na ake̱ Israel hĩĩ le̱ edšo foi, ni Saul ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ egboi le̱, ame̱šĩ mădši le̱ ni ame̱dšo foi. Ni Filistibii le̱ ba ni ame̱bahĩ mli.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ dšetše̱reno̱, beni Filistibii le̱ ba gbohĩĩ le̱ ahe nii kplo̱mo̱ le̱, ame̱na Saul ke̱ ebihĩĩ etẽ le̱ ni ame̱nyõnyõi ye̱ Gilboa goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ ame̱wuĩ le̱, ni ame̱bafũ ye̱ tamariske-tšo ni ye̱ Iabeš le̱ šĩši, ni *ame̱hĩ ṅmā̃ gbĩĩ kpawo.

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ oblanyo ní gbale̱ le̱ ake̱: Té ofe tēṅ ni ole ake̱ Saul ke̱ ebi Ionatan egboiṅ?

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ni ebimi ake̱: Namo dšio? Ni mihere no̱ ake̱: Amaleknyo dšimi.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱mi ake̱: Tši oba ni obagbemi; edšake̱ ṅmiṅmi emõmi, tše̱ misusuma ye̱ mimli ſēſe!

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David mõ ebe atadei le̱ ni *egbla, ni mei ni fata ebe le̱ fẽ fe nakai; *

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Ni David fó Saul ke̱ ebi Ionatan ke̱ ne̱ke̱ yāfó lala ne̱;

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: O Israel, onumnyam le̱ agbe ye̱ ogoṅkpo̱i le̱ ano̱! Té aye tēṅ ní kãkãlo̱i enyõnyõi ne̱!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: *Nyekayagbaä ye̱ Gat, nyekayatšĩa tã ye̱ Aškelon blohũi le̱aṅ, koni Filistibii le̱ abiyei le̱ akanyã́ ní †fōlo̱i le̱ abiyei le̱ mītũmo̱! Mika

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Nye Gilboa gōdši, bó̱ lo nu akane̱ nyeno̱, ni ṅmōdši ní baä nii akahĩ nyeno̱! Edšake̱ dše̱i aše̱ kākãlo̱i le̱ atše̱ṅ le̱ afõ ye̱, Saul tše̱ṅ le̱ po, tamo̱o̱ moni afo̱le̱ mũ nõ.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Mei ní enyõnyõi le̱ alá ke̱ kãkãlo̱i le̱ hũ afo̱ le̱, Ionatan gãi le̱ ekũũ ese̱ ke̱-dše̱e̱ he, ni Saul klante le̱ hũ kpalee eflo.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Saul ke̱ Ionatan, ame̱wala be mli le̱ asumo̱ame̱ ni ame̱be ye̱ fe̱o, ame̱gbēle mli hũ ame̱mli gblaa; ame̱he ye̱ oyá po fè okropoṅi, ni ame̱he wa hũ fè dšatai.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Nye Israel biyei, nyefóa Saul, le̱ ebumo̱nye mamai tšudši fe̱fe̱dši le̱, le̱ eṅõ šika dſinei eſie nyetadei ano̱ le̱!

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Té aye tēṅ ní kãkãlo̱i le̱ enyõnyõi ye̱ ta le̱ teṅ tū̃ntũ ne̱ṅ! Agbe Ionatan ye̱ ogoṅkpo̱i le̱ ano̱!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: Osane mīdo̱mĩ, minyemi Ionatan! Osane eṅõ minã ke̱-ho; osuomo̱ ní oke̱-sumo̱mi le̱ ye̱ nākpē̱, efè yei asuomo̱ po!

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Té aye tēṅ ní kãkãlo̱i le̱ enyõnyõi, ni tawūniĩ le̱ hũ ahĩe ekpãtã ne̱ṅ!

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda hĩĩ le̱ ba ni *ame̱bafo̱ David mũ ye̱ dše̱i, ame̱wole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Iuda we le̱ no̱. Ni ame̱gba David ake̱: †Iabeš-Gileadbii le̱ dši mei ní fũ Saul. *

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Iabeš-Gileadbii le̱ aṅō ayakē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iehowa adšō̱nye, ake̱ nyefe nyenuṅtšo̱ Saul ne̱ke̱ edšũrõ ne̱, ni nyefũle̱ le̱.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ Iehowa adšie mlihĩle̱ ke̱ ano̱kwale atšõnye; ni mi hũ mafenye edšũrõ mato nãdšiaṅ ye̱ noni nyefe ne̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyewadšea nyehe ni nyefea ekã; edšake̱ nyenuṅtšo̱ Saul egbo, ni agbe̱ne̱ Iuda we le̱ efo̱mi mũ ewomi ame̱no̱ maṅtše̱.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: ni eyawole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Gilead ke̱ Ašurbii le̱ ke̱ Iezreel ke̱ Efraim ke̱ Benyamin ke̱ Israel fẽ no̱.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Ni be ni David ke̱-ye maṅtše̱ ye̱ Hebron ye̱ Iuda we le̱ no̱ le̱ dši afii kpawo ke̱ nyõdši ekpa.

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ni Abner, Ner bi le̱, ke̱ Saul bi Išbošet tšũdši le̱ fã ke̱-dše̱ Mahanaim ni ame̱ba Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Ni Ioab, Zeruia bi le̱, ke̱ David tšũdši le̱ fā, ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ yakpe ye̱ Gibeon kpākpo le̱ he; mene̱mei bua kpākpo afã kome, ni mene̱mei hũ bua kpākpo le̱ afã kome ne̱.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Ni Abner kē̱ Ioab ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ hã oblahĩĩbii le̱ ate ši ni ame̱baſe̱ ye̱ wo̱hĩe! Ni Ioab kē̱: Ame̱te ši!

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱te ši ni ame̱kane amehe ni ame̱fo mli ke̱-te: Benyaminbii ni dše̱ Saul bi Išbošet nõ le̱ mli dši mei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱, ke̱ David tšũdši le̱ hũ ateṅ mei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni awu ta ní mli wa naakpa nakai gbĩ le̱; ni David tšũdši le̱ ſíe Abner ke̱ Israelbii le̱.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Ni *Zeruia bihĩĩ etẽ ye̱ dše̱i: Ioab ke̱ Abišai ke̱ Asahel; ni Asahel nane ye̱ oyá tamo̱ ṅãno̱ soṅāi. *

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner kwe̱ ese̱ ni ekē̱: Ani bo ni, Asahel? Ni ehere no̱ ni ekē̱: Mi ni.

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Ni Abner kē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbá oninedšũrõgbe̱ lo obe̱kugbe̱ ni omõ oblahĩĩbii le̱ eko ni ošõ etawūnii le̱ ye̱ edẽ! Ši Asahel ekplẽẽ ake̱ eekpale ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner sā ekē̱ Asahel ake̱: Kpalemo̱ ye̱ mise̱ ni oya! Mẽhewo̱ oohā matſao nõ ke̱-mõ ši? Ni té mafe tēṅ ni manyẽ mawó mihĩe no̱ makwe̱ onyemi Ioab hĩeṅ?

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ ekplẽẽ ni egbá afã; nohewo̱ le̱ Abner ke̱ akplo̱ le̱ tšṍ ese̱gbe̱ *tšu emũsũṅ ni eyafã kpo ye̱ ese̱; ni egbē ši ni egbo ye̱ dše̱i noṅṅ. Ni eba mlĩ ake̱ mofẽmo ní baše̱o̱ heni Asahel gbē ni egbo le̱, ewaä edamoo̱ ši. *

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Ši Ioab ke̱ Abišai nyie Abner se̱; ni beni ame̱še̱ Ama goṅkpo̱ le̱ ní kã Gia hĩe ye̱ Gibeon ṅã le̱ ne̱ gbe̱ le̱ he le̱, hũlũ enyõ ši;

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni Benyaminbii le̱ bua ame̱he nā ke̱-kpe ke̱-nyĩe Abner se̱, ni ame̱fe asafoku kome, ni ame̱yadamo̱ goṅkpo̱ ko yiteṅ.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner bo tšē̱ Ioab ni ekē̱: Aso klante aaye awui ne̱ke̱ dā? Ani olee ake̱ ke̱ fe se̱ le̱ dšōmo̱ baba? Mẽ beyino̱ noṅṅ omēo̱, dāni okē̱ maṅ le̱ ni ame̱fõ ame̱nyemimei le̱ ase̱nyieme̱?

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Ši Ioab kē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe kã ne̱, ke̱-dšee bo owie kũle̱, dša wó̱ lebi dãni maṅ le̱ mli mofẽmo aafō enyemi se̱nyiemo̱.

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab hã akpã te̱tre̱mantre̱, ni maṅ le̱ fẽ wá damo̱ ši, ni ame̱fõ Israel se̱nyiemo̱, asaṅ ame̱wuu doṅṅ.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ni Abner ke̱ ewebii le̱ nyie nakai nyō le̱ṅ fẽ ke̱-fo mli ye̱ ṅã kplenẽ le̱ ne̱, ni ame̱yafo Iordan, ni ame̱tšṍ Bitron, ni ame̱ke̱-ba Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Ni Ioab fõ Abner se̱nyiemo̱, ni beni ebua maṅ le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe le̱, eſe̱ David tšũdši le̱ ateṅ mei nyoṅma ke̱ ne̱hũ ke̱ Asahel.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wó Asahel ni ame̱yatole̱ ye̱ etše̱ fũhe le̱ ni yo̱ Betlehem le̱. Ni Ioab ke̱ emei le̱ nyie nyõṅnyõṅ fẽ, ni ame̱baše̱ Hebron ke̱ dšetše̱remo̱ we̱le̱ṅṅ.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Saul hemo ko ye̱ ni atšē̱o̱ egbe̱i ake̱ *Rizpa, Aia biyō le̱. Ni Išbošet kē̱ Abner ake̱: Mẽba ote mitše̱ hemo le̱ ṅõ? *

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner mli wo la naakpa ye̱ Išbošet wiemo̱i le̱ ahewo̱ ni ekē̱: Ani gbé yitšo dšimi, hewo̱ ni ṅmene̱ miteo̱ ši mĩwoo̱ Iuda, ni mike̱-feo̱ otše̱ Saul we le̱ ke̱ enyemimei ke̱ enanemei edšũrõ, ni midšiee bo mihãã David, ni bo le̱ ofoo̱ sane ofõo̱ mino̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ ne̱ke̱ yō ne̱ he ne̱?

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ afe Abner ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱, ke̱dši mifee mihãã David bo̱ni Iehowa ekãle̱ kitã le̱ fĩ!

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: ni mašõ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Saul we le̱, ni maṅõ David maṅtše̱sẽi le̱ mama ši ye̱ Israel ke̱ Iuda no̱ ke̱-dše̱ Dan āhũ ke̱-yaſie Beeršeba!

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ni enyẽẽ eto he wiemo̱ kome tete ehã Abner doṅṅ, edšake̱ ēšele̱ gbeyei.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Ni Abner tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te David ṅō ye̱ le̱dĩentše̱ egbëi ano̱ ake̱: Šikpoṅ le̱, namo nōṅ? Asaṅ ekē̱ ake̱: Oke̱mi akpãṅ, ni na, minine bafata ohe ke̱-gbla Israel fẽ ke̱-ba oṅō.

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Odšogbāṅ, mike̱o aakpãṅ; ši nõ kome pe̱ ní mitaoo̱ ye̱ odeṅ dši ake̱ okabana mihĩe, dša oke̱ Saul biyō Mikal le̱ ba dã, kē̱ ōba obana mihĩe le̱.

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Ni David sā tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te Saul bi Išbošet ṅõ ake̱: Ṅõ *miṅã Mikal, moni mĩke̱ Filistibii afōnālōi oha hã ese̱nii le̱, ohã abahãmi! *

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ni ewù le̱ ke̱le̱ nyie ke̱-te, ni ehĩe yāfó ke-nyie ese̱ ke̱-te Bahurim. Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kũ ose̱ ní oya! Ni ekũ ese̱ ete.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Ni Abner ke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ wie ni ekē̱: Nyèse̱ ne̱ kũle̱ nyemītao David ni eye nyeno̱ maṅtše̱:

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: agbe̱ne̱ nyefea nakai; edšake̱ Iehowa ewie ye̱ David hewo̱ ake̱: Mitšũlo̱ David nine no̱ matšṍ mahere mimaṅ Israel yiwala ke̱-dše̱ Filistibii le̱ ke̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ adeṅ.

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Ni Abner wie wo Benyamin hũ toiiaṅ, ni Abner le̱ noṅṅ yiṅ ete ni eyawie nii ní Israelbii le̱ ke̱ Benyaminbii le̱ taoo fẽ etšõ David ye̱ Hebron.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abner ba David ṅõ ye̱ Hebron, ni hĩĩ nyoṅmai-enyo̱ fata ehe. Ni David ṅmẽ Abner ke̱ hĩĩ ni fata ehe le̱ okplõ.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Ni Abner kē̱ David ake̱: Mi mate ši ni maya ni mayabua Israel fẽ nā ma-hã minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, koni ame̱ke̱o abakpãṅ, ni oye ame̱fẽ ame̱no̱ maṅtše̱, bo̱ni osusuma taoo̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni David dšie Abner gbe̱ ni ete ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Ni na, David tšũdši le̱ ke̱ Ioab dše̱ odšoyeli ba ni ame̱ke̱ nihãniĩ babaō ba. Ši Abner be̱ David ṅõ ye̱ Hebron doṅṅ, edšake̱ edšiele̱ gbe̱ ni ete ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Ni Ioab te maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ni ekē̱: Meni ofe ne̱? Na, Abner ba oṅō; mẽ-hewo̱ ni odšiele̱ gbe̱ ni ete?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Ole Abner, Ner bi le̱, ake̱ bo lakamo̱ ke̱ke̱ eba, koni ele oyā ke̱ obā mli, ni ele nofẽno ní ofeo̱!

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ni beni Ioab dše David ṅõ le̱, eyatšũ bo̱foi ní ame̱tiu Abner, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ kũ se̱ ke̱-dše̱ Sira nubu le̱ he ke̱-ba; ši David lee mli eko.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Ni beni Abner kũ ese̱ ke̱-ba Hebron le̱, Ioab ṅõle̱ ke̱-te afã ye̱ maṅ le̱ koi le̱ ši ake̱ eke̱le̱ yato adšina, ni *edũ emũsũṅ nõ ye̱ dše̱i ni egbo, ye̱ enyemi †Asahel lá le̱ hewo̱. *

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Hã ewula Ioab ke̱ etše̱ we le̱ fẽ yiteṅ; ni moni he hoo̱ nu ke̱ kpitiyelo̱ ke̱ moni hĩeo̱ tšo ke̱-nyieo̱ ke̱ moni nyõo̱ ye̱ klante nā ke̱ hõmo̱wo̱lo̱ akakpa ye̱ Ioab we le̱!

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Ši David kē̱ Ioab ke̱ maṅ le̱ fẽ ní fata ehe le̱ ake̱: Nyegblaä nyehe atadei ni nyemĩaä kpekpe ni nyewoa yãra ke̱-nyiea Abner hĩe! Ni maṅtše̱ David dientše̱ nyie adeka le̱ se̱.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱to Abner ye̱ Hebron; ni *maṅtše̱ le̱ wó egbẽ no̱ ni efó ye̱ Abner bu le̱ he, ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ fófói. *

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ fó Abner ke̱ ne̱ke̱ yāfó lala ne̱: Aso esa ake̱ Abner agbo tamo̱ yakagbomo ko gboo̱?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Onidši le̱, afĩmo̱koame̱ po, ni onãdši hũ, awokoame̱ gbokle̱i; bo̱ni anyõo̱ ye̱ gbomei fõdši ahĩe le̱, nakai pe̱ onyõ ne̱! Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ sā fó hãle̱ āhũ.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ni beni dše nako le̱, maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ba ake̱ ame̱bahã David aye nii, ši David kã kitã ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši misa minã abolo alo nokroko hũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni hũlũ aanyõ ši fī̃, Nyoṅmo̱ afemi ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ fẽ yo se̱ ni esa ame̱hĩe, tamo̱ bo̱ni nofẽno ni maṅtše̱ le̱ feo̱ le̱ sa maṅ le̱ fẽ hĩe le̱.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Ši maṅ le̱ fẽ ke̱ Israel fẽ ná le nakai gbĩ le̱ ake̱ dšee maṅtše̱ le̱ hã agbe Abner, Ner bi le̱.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Ani nyelee ake̱ *lumo̱ ke̱ gbomo agbo enyõ ši ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ Israel lo? *

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Ni mi le̱ afo̱mi mũ awomi maṅtše̱ moṅ, ši amrõmrõ ne̱ mibe̱ hewale̱, ni ne̱ke̱ hĩĩ ne̱ ní dši Zeruia bii le̱, ame̱sane wa fèmi. Iehowa awo efõṅfelo̱ nyõmo̱ ye̱ enōfõṅfemo̱ le̱ nā!

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ni Išbošet, Saul bi le̱, ye̱ hĩĩ enyo̱ ni dši asafoiatše̱mei: mokome gbe̱i dši Baana, ni mokome hũ gbe̱i dši Rekab, ni Beerotnyo Rimon ní dše̱ Benyaminbii le̱ ateṅ le̱ bii ni; (edšake̱ abuo̱ Beerot hũ ašio̱ Benyamin no̱;

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Ni Saul bi Ionatan ye̱ binū ko ní ye̱ enãdši enyo̱ le̱ fẽ edše kpa; eye afii enumo̱, beni Saul ke̱ Ionatan sane le̱ dše̱ Iezreel ba, ni ekwe̱lo̱ le̱ wóle̱ ni edšo foi, ni eba mli ake̱, beni eyeo̱ oyái ni edšo foi le̱, eyagbē ši ni edše kpa; ni egbe̱i dši Mefibošet.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Rekab ke̱ Baana, Beerotnyo Rimon le̱ bihĩĩ le̱, yiṅ ke̱-te Išbošet we le̱ ſane fintĩ, beni ekã ši ewe̱ö̱ ſane wō̱ le̱.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Beni ame̱baše̱ šĩa le̱, ekã esã no̱ ye̱ epiaṅ, ni ame̱tſiale̱ nii ni ame̱gbele̱, ni ame̱fo eyi; ni ame̱ko̱ eyitšo le̱ ni ame̱nyie ṅã kplenẽ le̱ no̱ nyõṅnyõṅ fẽ ke̱-te.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ Išbošet yitšo le̱ ba ame̱bahã David ye̱ Hebron, ni ame̱kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Na, ohenye̱lo̱ Saul, moni tao bo egbe le̱, bi Išbošet yitšo ne̱; ši Iehowa eto̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ he owele ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ Saul ke̱ esešibii le̱ ane̱!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: beni moko bagbamĩ ake̱: Na, Saul egbo! ni eyiṅ fẽ le̱, ená sane kpakpa ko ebagbami le̱, *mimõle̱ ni migbele̱ ye̱ Ziklag, ni mike̱-wole̱ esane ni ebagba le̱ he nyõmo̱, *

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: mbasroo noni gbomei fõdši eyagbe dšalo̱ ye̱ le̱dĩentše̱ ewe ye̱ esā no̱! no ni agbe̱ne̱ mibiṅ elá ši ye̱ nyedeṅ, ni makpãtã nyehĩe ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱?

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Ni David fã́ eblahĩĩ le̱ ni ame̱gbeame̱, ni ame̱flo̱ ame̱nidši ke̱ amenãdši ni ame̱ṅõ-tšotšŏro kpākpo ni yo̱ Hebron le̱ mase̱i. Ši Išbošet yitšo le̱ ame̱wó ni ame̱yafũ ye̱ Abner fũhe le̱ ye̱ Hebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Ni Hiram, Tiro maṅtše̱ le̱, tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-ba David ṅõ ke̱ tšenedrutšei ke̱ ṅmoṅmlogbo̱lo̱i ke̱ te̱gbogbotſalo̱i, ni ame̱bamã tšũ ame̱hã David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Eye Iuda no̱ maṅtše̱ afii kpawo ke̱ nyõdši ekpa ye̱ Hebron, ni eye Israel ke̱ Iuda fẽ no̱ maṅtše̱ afii nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ etẽ ye̱ Ierusalem.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Ni *David hewale̱ yaä no̱ ſereo̱, edšake̱ Iehowa, Zebaot Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, fĩ ese̱. *

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Ni David na ake̱ Iehowa ehã efĩ ši ake̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel no̱, ni emaṅ Israel hewo̱ le̱ ewó emaṅtše̱yelĩ le̱ no̱ godšō.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Ni beni David dše̱ Hebron ba le̱ se̱ le̱, esā efe hemei ni ekpēkpẽ yei ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem efata he, ni afo̱ bihĩĩ ke̱ biyei ehã David.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: ke̱ Ibhar ke̱ Elišua ke̱ Nefeg ke̱ Iafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: ke̱ Elišama ke̱ Eliada ke̱ Elifelet.

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Ši beni Filistibii le̱ nu ake̱ afo̱ David mũ awole̱ Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ le̱, Filistibii le̱ fẽ yiṅ ame̱ba David taomo̱. Ni beni David nu le̱, ete mō̃ le̱ mli.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ši Filistibii le̱ ba ni ame̱bagbá ye̱ Refaim dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David yabi Iehowa ake̱: Ani mifã ke̱-yanina Filistibii le̱ lo? ani oodšieame̱ owo mideṅ lo? Ni Iehowa kē̱ David ake̱: Fã ke̱-ya, edšake̱ befẽbe ni fe le̱ madšie Filistibii le̱ mawo odeṅ!

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ni David ba Baal-Perazim, ni David batſiaame̱ nii ye̱ dše̱i, ni ekē̱: Iehowa egbá ewo mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ ye̱ mihĩe, tamo̱ nu gbáa ke̱-dšeo̱ kpo le̱! Nohewo̱ le̱ etšé̱ dše̱i gbe̱i ake̱: Baal-Perazim.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱šĩ ame̱mãgãi le̱ ye̱ dše̱i; ni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ lō ke̱-te.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ši Filistibii le̱ fã ke̱-ba ekoṅ ni ame̱bagbá ye̱ Refaim dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Ni beni David yabi Iehowa le̱, ekē̱: Kāfá ke̱-mīya; ši yadše ame̱se̱gbe̱ obo̱leame̱, ni otšṍ Bakatšei le̱ aṅe̱le̱no̱ obatuaame̱.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Ni ké̱ onu nyiemo̱ gbē̱mo̱ ye̱ Bakatšei le̱ ano̱ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni owó ohe no̱; edšake̱ no mli le̱ Iehowa edše kpo ke̱-nyie ohĩe ni eyatſia Filistibii ata le̱ nii.

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ni David fe nakai, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa efã́le̱ le̱, ni etſia Filistibii le̱ anii ke̱-dše̱ Geba āhũ ke̱-yaſie Gezer.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Ni David dšó ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ke̱ ehewale̱ fẽ, ni David emĩa ke̱ klala efod.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ Israel we le fẽ yawó Iehowa adeka le̱ ke̱-ba ke̱ ošebō̱ ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱ kpãmo̱.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Iehowa adeka le̱ še̱ David mã le̱ṅ le̱, Mikal, Saul bi-yō le̱, yabu samfle̱ nā, ni ena maṅtše̱ David mīhũlu ni ēdšó ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni egbe ehe guo̱ ye̱ etšui mli. (

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wó Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ame̱mã ſīli hē ko no̱ ke̱-dše̱ *Abinadab we le̱ ye̱ Gibea, ni Uza ke̱ Ahio, Abinadab bihĩĩ le̱, kudo̱ö̱ ſīli hē le̱. *

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa mlila te ši wo Uza, ni Nyoṅmo̱ tſale̱ nõ ye̱ etõmo̱ le̱ hewo̱, ni *egbo ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ mase̱i. *

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Ni David še Iehowa gbeyei nakai gbĩ le̱, ni ekē̱: Té aafe tẽṅ ní Iehowa adeka le̱ aaba miṅõ hũ?

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ David sumo̱o̱ ake̱ eke̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ baä eṅõ ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ši David wó ke̱-tšṍ afã ke̱-te Obed-Edom, Gitinyo le̱, we le̱,

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ ba ni ame̱ke̱-bamã egbe̱he ye̱ bū ní David eši ehãle̱ le̱ teṅ. Ni David šā šã-afo̱lei ni egbe šidā-afo̱lei ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ni beni David šã šã-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei le̱ egbe nā le̱, eke̱ Iehowa Zebaot gbe̱i *dšŏ̱ maṅ le̱. *

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Ni edša maṅ le̱ fẽ ni dši Israel asafo mū le̱ fẽ nii, hĩĩ le̱ ke̱ yei le̱ fẽ, ehã mofẽmo abolo akwābo̱ kome ke̱ lō kukuli kome ke̱ weinyibii atatale kome. Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ fẽ ṅō-ſie no̱ mofẽmo ke̱-te ewe.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kũ ese̱ ke̱-ba ni ebadšō̱ ewe le̱. Ni Mikal, Saul biyō le̱, dše kpo eke̱ David bakpe ni ekē̱: Aso nyam pam Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ wo ehĩe ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱ ake̱ edšie ehebo ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ etšũdši le̱ aweyei le̱ ahĩe, tamo̱ yakagbomei le̱ eko dšieo̱ ehe ne̱!

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Ši David kē̱ Mikal ake̱: Iehowa ni dše otše̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ se̱ ni ehalami ewomi Iehowa maṅ Israel no̱ *lumo̱ le̱ hĩe midšò ye̱, hẽ, le̱ ehĩe madšó ye̱! *

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ mibafe mihe hũmi fè ne̱-ke̱ tete ni mibuṅ mihe ake̱ moko, ni weyei le̱ ni okē̱o̱ le̱, ame̱ moṅ ame̱awo mihĩe nyam!

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Ni Mikal, Saul biyō le̱, náá bi āhũ ke̱-yaši egbo.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ gbalo̱ Natan ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nto ōna, mi le̱ miye̱ tšenedru tšũ mli, ši Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ye̱ bū mli! Lal.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ mato he ko mahã mimaṅ Israel, ni mate̱oame̱, koni ame̱hĩ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱hĩle̱he, ni akatšire̱ame̱ doṅṅ, ni yiwalo̱i hũ akahaoame̱ doṅṅ tamo̱ sá le̱,

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: *Le̱ eemã tšũ ehã migbe̱i le̱, ni mahã emaṅtše̱yeli sẽi le̱ amã ši šiṅṅ ke̱-ya nāno̱. *

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: *Matšṍ etše̱, ni eetšṍ mibi. Ke̱dši etõ le̱, no le̱ mike̱ ádesãi atšo ke̱ gbomei akpãi aayile̱; *Lal.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, owó otšũlo̱ *toi no̱ okē̱: Mama šĩa mahão; nohewo̱ ni otšũlo̱ ná tšuĩ ake eso̱le ne̱ke̱ so̱lemo̱ ne̱ ehão. *Ies.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ David te ni eyatá ši ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ni ekē̱: Nuṅtšo̱ Ieho-wa, *namo dšimi, ni miwe le̱, meni edši po ni ohĩemi ke̱-baši bene̱ ne̱? *

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Ni meni yo̱ David nā ni ekē̱o doṅṅ? edšake̱ bo ole otšũlo̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa!

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Owiemo̱ ni owie le̱ hewo̱ ke̱ bodientše̱ otšui nā ni ofe nibii wudši ne̱ fẽ, koni oke̱-hã otšũlo̱ ale!
