english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱, oda kpeteṅkple! Edšake̱ mokomoko ke̱o yee egbo̱, ni asaṅ nii fẽ ní wo̱ke̱ wo̱toii enu le̱ anā le̱, nyoṅmo̱ ko nyoṅmo̱ ko be̱ ye̱ ose̱.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Ni mẽ *dšeṅmaṅ kome po yo̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ ni ke̱ omaṅ Israel ye gbo̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ yiṅ ete eyakpõ efe le̱dientše̱ emaṅ, ni eke̱-he gbe̱i, ni etšu nii wudši ehãnye ke̱ nii ni yo̱ gbeyei ehã ošikpoṅ le̱, ye̱ omaṅ ni okpo ohã ohe ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim, ke̱-dše̱ dšeṅmãdši ke̱ ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ adeṅ le̱, hĩe? *

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Ni omã omaṅ Israel no̱ mĩ́ ofe bodientše̱ omaṅ ke̱-mīya nāno̱, ni bo Iehowa otšṍ ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱, wiemo̱ ní owie ye̱ otšũlo̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ hewo̱ le̱, mã no̱ aduatšo̱ ke̱-ya nāno̱, ni ofe take̱ bo̱ni oke le̱!

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa, bo dši Nyoṅmo̱, ni owiemo̱i le̱ ano̱kwale ni, ni oke̱ ne̱ke̱ nõkpakpa ne̱ ewo otšũlo ši.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ná he tšui ni odšō̱ otšũlo̱ we le̱, koni ehĩ ši ke̱-ya nāno̱ ye̱ ohĩe; edšake̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa, bo õkē̱, ni odšō̱mo̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱ aadšō̱ otšũlo̱ we le̱ ke̱-ya nāno̱.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ David tſia Hadadezer, Rehob bi le̱, ni dši Zoba maṅtše̱ le̱, nii, beni eyiṅ ete ake̱ eyaple̱ ešikpoṅ ni ye̱ Eufrate fā le̱ nā le̱ he le̱.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ asrafoi to Damasko ní yo̱ Aram le̱, ni Arambii le̱ tšṍmo̱ David tšũdši ní tšuo̱ onĩa hãale̱. Ni Iehowa hãa David yeo̱ kũnim ye̱ hefẽhe ni eyaã.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni David šõ šika tše̱ṅi le̱ ní Hadadezer tšũdši le̱ hĩe le̱, ni eke̱-ba Ierusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ David lõ akō̱ble babaō dientše̱ ye̱ Beta ke̱ Berotai, Hadadezer mãdši le̱ amli.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni Toi tšũ ebi Ioram ke̱-te maṅtše̱ David ṅõ, ni eyahãle̱ ahekō ni edšō̱le̱, ake̱-ní eke̱ Hadadezer ewu ni etſiale̱ nii le̱, edšake̱ Hadadezer ke̱ Toi ewuwū tai āhũ; ni ehīe dſie̱te̱i nibii ke̱ šika nibii ke̱ akō̱ble nibii ke̱-ba.

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Ni tšũlo̱ ko ye̱ Saul we le̱ ni atšé̱o̱le̱ *Ziba. Ni ayatšé̱le̱ ke̱-ba David ṅõ, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ bile̱ ake̱: Ani bo dši Ziba le̱? Ni ekē̱: Otšũlo̱ ni. *

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ani moko be̱ Saul we le̱ lolo ní eſe̱ ní mafele̱ edšũrõ ye̱-Nyoṅmo̱ hewo̱ lo? Ni Ziba kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: *Ionatan binū ko ye̱ lolo, ni enãdši edše kpa. *

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ eyo̱? Ni Ziba kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Na, eye̱ Amiel bi *Makir we le̱ ye̱ Lo-Debar. *

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Mefibošet, Saul bi Ionatan bi le̱, ba David ṅõ le̱, eṅõ ehĩe ebu ši ni ekotole̱. Ni David tšé̱le̱ ake̱: Mefibošet! ni ehere no̱ ekē̱: Na otšũlo̱!

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāše gbeyei; ši edšũrõ mibafeo ye̱ otše̱ Ionatan hewo̱, ni madãi otše̱ Saul šikpõdši le̱ fẽ mahão ekoṅ, ní ooye nii ye̱ mikplõ he dāne̱.

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšé̱ Saul tšũlo̱ Ziba le̱ ke̱-ba ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nibii fẽ ni dši Saul ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ nõ le̱ miṅõ-hã onuṅtšo̱ bi le̱.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ní dši Hadadezer tšũdši le̱ na ake̱ Israel eye ame̱no̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱ Israel bakpãtã ni ame̱-súmo̱ame̱. Ni Arambii le̱ še gbeyei ake̱ ame̱aye ame̱bua Amonbii le̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ ake̱: Madšie mlihĩle̱ kpo matšõ Hanun, Nahaš bi le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni etše̱ mli hĩ hãmi le̱. Ni David tšũ etšũdši ake̱ ame̱yahãle̱ kpóo ye̱ etše̱ hewo̱. Ni David tšũdši le̱ ba Amonbii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ ne̱.

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Amonbii le̱ alumei le̱ kē̱ ame̱nuṅtšo̱ Hanun ake̱: Ani osusuo̱ ake̱ otše̱ hĩe nyamwō hewo̱ ni David tšũ kpóohãlo̱i ke̱-ba oṅõ ne̱? Ani dšee maṅ le̱ sramo̱ ke̱ šikpámo̱ ke̱ butumo̱ hewo̱ moṅ ni David tšũ etšũdšĩ le̱ ke̱-ba oṅō ne̱?

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Hanun mõmo̱ David tšũdši le̱ ni eše̱šē̱ ame̱tšēṅi afãfã ni efio̱ ame̱tadei le̱ ano̱ ye̱ teṅ tū̃ntũ ke̱-baše̱ ame̱dukuii ano̱, ni edšieame̱ gbe̱ ame̱te.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ni beni ayagba David le̱, etšũ ake̱ame̱ yakpe; edšake̱ abo̱ame̱ ahora naakpa. Nohewo̱ le̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Nyehĩa Ieriko ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní nyetšẽṅi le̱ aatša, dãni nyekũ nyese̱ nyeba.

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Ši beni Amonbii le̱ na ake̱ ame̱he e̱dše fũ ewo David le̱, Amonbii le̱ tšũ ni ayabo̱ Arambii ní yo̱ Bet-Rehob ke̱ Arambii ni yo̱ Zoba le̱ apā, nãdšiatše̱mei akpei-nyoṅmai-enyo̱, ke̱ Maaka maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ mei akpe, ke̱ Tob hĩĩ akpei-nyoṅma-ke̱-enyo̱.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Femo̱ ekã ni ohã wo̱damo̱ ši ake̱ hĩĩ wo̱hã wo̱maṅ ke̱ wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ mãdšĩ le̱; ni Iehowa afe noni sa ehĩe!

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Ni beni David nu le̱, etšũ Ioab ke̱ hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i le̱ ata le̱ fẽ ke̱-te.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Ni Amonbii le̱ dše kpo ni ame̱bagbá ta le̱ ye̱ agbó le̱ nā; ši Arambii ni dše̱ Zoba, ke̱ Rehob ke̱ Tob ke̱ Maaka hĩĩ le̱, ame̱tše ame̱he aṅklo ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Ši beni Ioab na ake̱ ta le̱ le̱ egbá ewole̱ ye̱ ese̱ ke̱ ehĩe le̱, ehala Israel mli kakabãi le̱ fẽ mli ekomei, ni ehã ame̱gbá ame̱wo Arambii le̱.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ le̱ mli mei ni eſe̱ le̱, etuame̱ ewo enyemi Abišai deṅ, koni ehã ame̱gbá ame̱wo Amonbii le̱.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Arambii le̱ anine mītšṍ mino̱ le̱, koni obaye obuami; ši ke̱dši Amonbii le̱ anine mītšṍ ono̱ le̱, koni mabaye mabuao.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Ni Ioab ke̱ ta ní fata ehe le̱ tšẽ ke̱-yanina Arambii le̱ ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ wu, ni ame̱dšo foi ye̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni beni Amonbii le̱ na ake̱ Arambii edšo foi le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ hũ ame̱dšo foi ye̱ Abišai hĩe ni ame̱yabote mã le̱ṅ. Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab kũ ese̱ ke̱-dše̱ Amonbii le̱ ase̱ ni eba Ierusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Ši beni Arambii le̱ na ake̱ Israelbii le̱ eye ame̱no̱, ame̱bua ame̱he nā ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Ni Hadadezer tšũ ni ayaṅõ Arambii ni yo̱ fā le̱ se̱ le̱ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱ba Helam; ni Hadadezer tatše̱ Šobak le̱ nyie ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Ni ebagba David, ni eyabua Israel mū le̱ fẽ nā, ni efo Iordan ni ete Helam. Ni Arambii le̱ gbá ta wo David ni ame̱ke̱le̱ wu.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: ni aleenõ maṅtše̱ le̱ mli fũ ni ekē̱o ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ nyebe̱ṅke̱ maṅ le̱ kpākpa nakai, beni nyewuo̱ le̱? Ani nyelee ake̱ ame̱adše̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ ame̱tſianye nii lo?

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ ṅō ho̱, ni etšũ ayakē̱ David ake̱: Miná mũsũ!

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Ni David tšũ ate Ioab ṅõ ake̱: Hã Uria, Hitnyo le̱, aba miṅõ. Ni Ioab hã Uria ba David ṅõ.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Ni beni Uria ba eṅõ le̱, David bile̱ bo̱ni Ioab ke̱ maṅ le̱ yo̱ ke̱ bo̱ni ta le̱ yaä no̱ hãa.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Uria ake̱: Kplekemo̱ ši ni oya owe le̱, ni oyafo̱flo̱ onãdši ahe. Ni beni Uria dše maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱, ake̱ niyenii dše kpo ke̱-nyie ese̱ ke̱-dše̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Ni beni ayagba David ake̱ Uria eyaa ewe le̱, David kē̱ Uria ake̱: Ani dšee gbe̱ odše̱ oba le̱? mẽba oyaa owe le̱?

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Ni Uria kē̱ David ake̱: *Adeka le̱ ke̱ Israel ke̱ Iuda fẽ ye̱ asesei amli, ni minuṅtšo̱ Ioab ke̱ minuṅtšo̱ tšũdši le̱ ebo̱ nsra ye̱ ṅãno̱, ni mi le̱ miya miwe ni miyaye nii ni minu ni mike̱ miṅã awo̱ lo? Gbĩĩabo̱ ní ohĩe kã ni osusuma hũ hĩe kã ne̱, miwoṅ ene̱ femo̱. *

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ Uria ake̱: Hĩ bĩe̱ ṅme̱ne̱ hũ, ni wo̱ le̱ mahã oya! Ke̱ke̱ ni Uria hĩ ši ye̱ Ierusalem nakai gbĩ le̱ ke̱ eno̱ dšetše̱remo̱.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Ni eṅmã ye̱ wolo le̱ mli ake̱: Nyeṅõa Uria nyetoa ta le̱ mli heni wa le̱ hĩe, ni nyegblaã nyehe ši ke̱-dšea ehe, koni atſiale̱ nii ní egbo.

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Ioab eyasra maṅ le̱ ekwe̱ le̱, eṅõ Uria eto heni ele ake̱ hĩĩ kakabãi yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Ni mã le̱ṅ hĩĩ le̱ dše kpo ni ame̱ke̱ Ioab bawu, ni mã le̱ṅ meikomei ni dši David tšũdši le̱ nyõnyõi, ni Uria, Hitnyo le̱, hũ nyõ.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab tšũ ayagba David ta le̱ mli sãdši fẽ tſẽm.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: Ni ewo bo̱fo le̱ kitã ekē̱: Ké̱ ogba maṅtše̱ le̱ ta le̱ṅ sãdši le̱ fẽ ogbe nā,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Namo tſa Abimelek, Ierubešet bi le̱, nõ le̱? *Ani dšee yō ko ṅō w̌ie̱bi etſa eyiteṅ ke̱-dše̱ gbogbo no̱ ni egbo ye̱ Tebez le̱? Mẽba mo̱ ni nyetši nyebe̱ṅke̱ gbogbo le̱ nakai le̱? ke̱ke̱ ni okē̱: Otšũlo̱ Uria, Hitnyo le̱, hũ enyõ! *Kodš.

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni bo̱fo le̱ yiṅ eba, ni ebagba David sãdši ſẽ ní Ioab tšũle̱ ye̱ he le̱.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Ni bo̱fo le̱ kē̱ David ake̱: Hĩĩ le̱ anine tšṍ wo̱no̱, ni beni ame̱baninawo̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, wo̱ṅõ-to ame̱no̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši agbó le̱ nā tõ.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ši gãitšẽlo̱i le̱ dše̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ tšẽre otšũdši agãii, ni maṅtše̱ tšũdši le̱ ekomei egboi, ni otšũlo̱ Uria, Hitnyo le̱, hũ egbo.

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Ni David kē̱ bo̱fo le̱ ake̱: Yakē̱ Ioab ne̱ke̱ ni oke̱-wole̱ hewale̱: Kāhã sane ne̱ mīdo̱o, edšake̱ klante yo̱ ne̱, ekpaa moni egbeo; hã ota le̱ mli awa ye̱ maṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ke̱, koni okũmo̱le̱!

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Ni beni Uria ṅã le̱ nu ake̱ ewù Uria egbo le̱, efó ewù le̱.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Ni beni eye ṅko̱mo̱ egbe nā le̱, David tšũ ayaṅõle̱ ke̱-ba ewe le̱, ni etšṍ eṅã ni efo̱ binū ehãle̱. Ši sane ni David ye ne̱ eṅõõ Iehowa nā.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Ši beni gbo̱ ko bato nū niiatše̱ le̱ ṅõ le̱, esumo̱o̱ ní emo le̱dientše̱ etōi ke̱ etšinai le̱ eko ni eho ehã gbo̱ ní batole̱ le̱; ši moṅ emõ ohĩafo le̱ gwanteṅbi le̱ ni eho ehã nū le̱ ni batole̱ le̱.

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Ni esã eto tōbi le̱ nãdšiaṅ toi edſe̱, ake̱ noni eye ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ ni enaale̱ mo̱bo̱ le̱!

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ni oke̱ noni ofe ne̱ ehã Iehowa henye̱lo̱i le̱ ená hegbe̱ pī ni ame̱ke̱-abo̱ musu hewo̱ le̱, *bi le̱ hũ ní afo̱ ahão le̱ gbo eegbo! *

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Ni Natan yiṅ ete ewe. Ši Iehowa tſa bi le̱ ni Uria ṅã le̱ ke̱ David fo̱ le̱ nõ, ni ehe ye naakpa.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ David kpa Nyoṅmo̱ fai ehã gbekẽ le̱, ni David hi ṅmā̃, ete tšũṅ ni eho ekã šikpoṅ nyõṅnyōṅ fẽ.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Ni ewe le̱ onukpai le̱ te ši ni ame̱te eṅõ ní ameyawó eno̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ; ši ekplẽẽ, ni asaṅ eke̱ame̱ yee nii.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ gbekẽ le̱ gbo. Ni David tšũdši le̱ mīše gbeyei ake̱ ame̱akē̱le̱ ake̱ gbekẽ le̱ egbo, edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Na, beni gbekẽ le̱ hĩe kã lolo po le̱, wo̱ke̱le̱ wie le̱ eboo wo̱gbẽ toi: kole̱ ke̱dši wo̱kē̱le̱ ake gbekẽ le̱ egbo le̱, no le̱ té eefe ehe efõṅ ehā tēṅ?

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ši beni David na ake̱ etšũdši le̱ miwie able̱bi le̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ David yo se̱ ake̱ gbekẽ le̱ egbo; nohewo̱ le̱ David bi etšũdšĩ le̱ ake̱: Ani gbekẽ le̱ egbo be̱? Ni ame̱kē̱: Egbo.

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽ sane oye ne̱? Beni gbekẽ le̱ hĩe kã le̱, ohĩ ṅmā̃ ni ofó ohãle̱; ši beni gbekẽ le̱ gbo moṅ le̱, kpãko ote ši oyeo̱ nii!

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Beni gbekẽ le̱ hĩe kã lolo le̱, mihĩ ṅmā̃ ni mifó; edšake̱ mikē̱: Aleenõ Iehowa aanami mo̱bo̱, ni gbekẽ le̱ yi aná wala.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱ ená egbo; kole̱ mẽba misā mihĩo̱ ṅmā̃? Ani manyẽ makpalele̱ ke̱-ba ekoṅ? Mi moṅ mibaye eṅõ, ši le̱ le̱ ekpaleṅ ebaṅ miṅõ doṅṅ.

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David še̱dše eṅã Batšeba mi, ni ete eṅõ ni eke̱le̱ yawo̱; ni efo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Salomo. Ni Iehowa sumo̱le̱,

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Ši Ioab ke̱ *Raba, Amonbii le̱ amaṅ le̱, wu, ni eṅõ maṅtše̱ maṅ le̱. *Ier.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Ni Ioab tšũ bo̱foi ke̱-ba David ṅō abakē̱le̱ ake̱: Mike̱ Raba ewu, ni asaṅ miṅõ nui anã maṅ le̱.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Nohewo le̱ agbe̱ne̱ buamo̱ maṅ le̱ mli mei ni eſe̱ le̱ anã, ni oke̱ame̱ ababo̱ nsra owo maṅ le̱ he, ni oṅõle̱, koni mi mikayaṅõle̱ ní ake̱-tšĩ migbei atã.

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David bua maṅ le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni eke̱ame̱ te Raba, ni eke̱le̱ yawu ni eṅõle̱.

english_verse: and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about
translation_verse: Ni edšie ame̱maṅtše̱ le̱ akekre le̱ ye̱ eyitšo, ni enā ṅmẽo̱ šika talenta kome, ke̱ ehe te̱i ní dšra wa, ni aṅõ-fĩ David yitšo; ni eṅõ mā le̱ṅ hānii le̱ babaō dientše̱ ke̱-ba.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Ni elō gbomei ni yo̱ mli le̱ ke̱-ba, ni eṅõame̱ eto akplalai ke̱ dade nigble̱mo̱nii ke̱ dade lemai ašiši, ni ehã ame̱tšṍtšṍ ntaya flõnõi amli. Ni ne̱ke̱ efe Amonbii le̱ amãdši le̱ fã. Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ maṅ mũ le̱ fẽ kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Ierusalem.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Ni no kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba bo, maṅtše̱-bi mū le̱, otãa lō gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ ne̱? Osumo̱o̱ ake̱ ogbami lo? Ni Amnon kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mīsumo̱ Tamar, minyemi Absalom nyemiyō le̱.

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Amnon yakã ši, ni eṅō-fe ake̱ ehe mīye; ni beni maṅtše̱ le̱ bale̱ sramo̱ le̱, Amnon kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Hã minyemi Tamar aba ni ebašĩ tatalei enyo̱ō ko ehãmi ye̱ mihĩe, ni ehĩe ye̱ edeṅ ní maye!

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David tšũ ate Tamar ṅõ ye̱ šĩa ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya onyemi Amnon we le̱ ni oyafe niyenii ohãle̱.

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Ni beni Tamar yiṅ ete enyemi Amnon we le̱, le̱ ekã ši ne̱; ni eṅõ mã ni ekpo̱to̱, ni efe tatalei ye̱ ehĩe, ni ešĩ tatalei le̱.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Ni Amnon kē̱ Tamar ake̱: Oke̱ niyenii lē̱ aba pia le̱ṅ, koni ohĩe ye̱ odeṅ ni maye. Ni Tamar ṅō tatalei le̱ ní ešĩ le̱ ni eke̱-te pia le̱ṅ eke̱-yahã enyemi Amnon.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Ni beni eke̱-bahãle̱ ni eye le̱, emõ emli ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: *Ba, oke̱mi abawo̱, minyemiyō! *

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Ni mi le̱, nẽgbe̱ po mike̱ ne̱ke̱ hĩegbĕle aate? ni bo le̱, ootšṍ tamo̱ Israel yakagbomei le̱ eko! Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, oke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ayawie, ši ekãmãṅ ake̱ eke̱mi aahão!

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Amnon he tšẽle̱ naakpa āhũ po ní ehe bo̱ni tšẽle̱ le̱ fá fè suomo̱ ni eke̱-sumo̱le̱ le̱. Ni Amnon kē̱le̱ ake̱: Te ši ni oya!

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ebe̱ nakai! ſiemo̱ ni oſieo̱mi ne̱ moṅ dši efõṅ kpeteṅkple fè tšutšunõ ní ofemi le̱? Ši eboole̱ toi;

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Ni ewo atade wuyā fe̱fe̱o ko, edšake̱ maṅtše̱mei abiyei oblayei froi le̱, nakai atadei ame̱woo̱. Ni etšũlo̱ le̱ ke̱le̱ dše kpo, ni ela šĩnā le̱ se̱ wole̱.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Tamar *lō lamlu eſie eyiteṅ, ni egbla atade wuyã fe̱fe̱o ní ewo le̱, ni ekŏ̱lo̱ enidšĩ eſie eyiteṅ, ni ehĩe yāfó gegēge ke̱-te. *Hiob

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Ši Absalom ke̱ Amnon ewĩee ekpakpa lo eſõṅ; edšake̱ Absalom enye̱ Amnon, ake̱-ni emõ enyemiyō Tamar le̱.

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ afii enyo̱ se̱ le̱ aku Absalom tōi ahetšo̱i ye̱ Baal-Hazor ni yo̱ Efraim mase̱i le̱, ni Absalom kpē maṅtše̱ bihĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱-te.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Ni Absalom ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅō ni ebakē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ na, āku otšũlo̱ tōi ahetšo̱i, hã maṅtše̱ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ke̱ otšũlo̱ aya!

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Absalom kē̱: Ke̱-dsee nakai dšiṅṅ, bĕle̱ hã minyemi Amnon ke̱-wo̱ aya mo̱. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ eke̱o aya?

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Ši Absalom hĩele̱ āhũ ni ehã Amnon ke̱ maṅtše̱ bihĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱le̱ te.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Absalom ewo etšũdšĩ le̱ akitã ake̱: Nyekwe̱a, nĩ ké̱ nyena ake̱ wein ehã Amnon mli eflile̱, ni mikē̱nye ake̱: Nyetſiaä Amnon nii! le̱, koni nyegbele̱; nyekašea gbeyei, edšake̱ mi mifã́nye; nyefea hĩĩ ni nyefea ekã!

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ni Absalom tšũdši le̱ fe Amnon bo̱ni Absalom fã́ame̱ le̱. Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱bĩĩ le̱ fẽ te ši, ni mofẽmo ho tá ete-dšiokpo̱ṅo̱ no̱ ni ame̱dšo foi.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱yo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ lolo le̱, abatſa David adafi ake̱: Absalom egbe maṅtše̱bii le̱ fẽ, ni ame̱teṅ mokomeflo eſe̱e̱.

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ te ši ni egbla etadei ni eho ekã šikpoṅ, ni etšũdši le̱ fẽ damo̱damō̱ emase̱i ke̱ ame̱tadei ni ame̱gblagblai.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ši Ionadab, David nyemi Šimea bi le̱, here no̱ ni ekē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ akasusu ake̱ agbe maṅtše̱bii oblahĩĩ le̱ fẽ; edšake̱ Amnon kome ke̱ke̱ egbo, edšake̱ Absalom ekpe̱ mli nakai eto momo ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ no̱ ní emõ enyemiyō Tamar le̱.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ akaye etsui ye̱ sane ne̱ hewo̱ ní esusu ake̱: Maṅtše̱bii le̱ fẽ egboi, edšake̱ Amnon kome ke̱ke̱ egbo.

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Ši Absalom dšo foi. Ni oblanyo le̱ ní buo̱ le̱ hole ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ni ekwe̱, ni na, mei babaō nyie goṅ le̱ he gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-mība.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ni Ionadab kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Na, maṅtše̱bii le̱ mība; bo̱ni otšũlo̱ kē̱ le̱, nakai kẽ ni.

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ amrõ pe̱ ni egbe wiemo̱ le̱ nā le̱, na, maṅtše̱bii le̱ ba, ni ame̱wó ame̱gbē no̱ ni ame̱fó; ni maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ fẽ fó āhũ.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ David mīſe Absalom; edšake̱ etšé̱ etšui eṅmẽ emli ye̱ Amnon gbĕle le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Ni beni Tekoayō le̱ yakē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱, eṅõ ehĩe ebu ši ni ekotole̱ ni ekē̱: Ye obuami, maṅtše̱!

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Ni oweyō ye̱ bihĩĩ enyo̱, ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ame̱yanõ ye̱ ṅãno̱, ni moko be̱ dše̱i ni aakpãtãame̱; ni mokome tſa mokome nõ ni egbele̱.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Ni na, weku mũ le̱ fẽ ete ši ewo oweyō, ni ame̱kē̱: Dšiemo̱ moni tſa enyemi nō le̱ ohã, *koni wo̱gbele̱ wo̱to enyemi ni egbe le̱ nãdšiaṅ, ni wo̱kpãtã nĩyelo̱ le̱ hũ hĩe! Ni bĕle̱ ame̱bagbe miṅãi ni eſe̱ le̱, koni akaſe̱ gbe̱i lo seši ko ahã miwù ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱! *

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ yō le̱ ake̱: Ya owe, ni mawo ohe akpoi!

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Ni Tekoayō le̱ kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! ne̱ke̱ tõmo̱ ne̱ akã mi ke̱ mitše̱ we le̱ no̱; ši maṅtše̱ ke̱ esẽi le̱ sõ ko sõ ko akawula eyiteṅ!

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Mofẽmo ni aakē̱o sane ko le̱, oke̱le̱ aba miṅõ, ni etaṅ ohe doṅṅ!

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Maṅtše̱ akai Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, koni lá he oweleto̱lo̱ le̱ aka-kpãtã hĩe doṅṅ, ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, ame̱-agbe mibi le̱! Ni ekē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, ke̱dši obi le̱ *yiteṅ tšo̱i kome dše nyõ ši fĩ! *

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yō le̱ kē̱: Ofai ne̱, hã ní oweyō akē̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ sane kome! Ni ekē̱: Wiemo̱!

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱bagboi kẽ, ni wo̱tamo̱ nu ni atši aſie šikpoṅ ni ehĩ! lōmo̱ doṅṅ; ši *Nyoṅmo̱ egbee mo, ši moṅ dſẽṅmo̱ edſẽṅo̱ bo̱ni aafe ni ekaſie moni aſiele̱ le̱ ke̱-mīdše̱ ehe kwrã. *Ezek.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nõ hewo̱ ni hã miba mike̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ bawie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ne̱ dši mihe gbeyei ní maṅ le̱ wo le̱; ni oweyō kē̱: Bĕle̱ miya ni mike̱ maṅtše̱ ayawie ake̱ aleenõ maṅtše̱ aafe noni etšũlo̱yō taoo̱ le̱ lo.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ maṅtše̱ aabo toi, ni eedšie etšũlo̱yō ye̱ nū ní taoo̱mi ke̱ mibi ſẽ hĩe akpãtã ke̱-dše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ no̱yelihe le̱ deṅ.

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱ yō le̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ kāṅõ noni mibabio ne̱ otēmi! Ni yō le̱ kē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ awie!

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ani Ioab nine fata ohe ye̱ ene̱ fẽ mli lo? Ni yō le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! gbĩĩabo̱ ni osusuma hĩe kã ne̱, mokomoko gbaleṅ ninedšũrõ lo abe̱ku ke̱-dšeṅ nokonoko ni minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ ewie le̱ he; edšake̱ otšũlo̱ Ioab le̱, le̱ efã́mi, ni le̱ noṅṅ eṅõ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ ewo oweyō nā.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Beni afe ni atšake sane le̱ hĩe hewo̱ otšũlo̱ Ioab fe ene̱: ši minuṅtšo̱ le nii *tamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ bo̱fo pe̱, hewo̱ le̱ ele nibii fẽ ni yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ le̱. *K.

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Ioab ake̱: Dšogbãṅ, mikplẽ, nohewo̱ le̱ ya ní oyaṅō oblanyo Absalom ke̱-ba.

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Ni Ioab ṅõ ehĩe ebu ši ni ekoto ši, ni edšō̱ maṅtše̱ le̱. Ni Ioab kē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! ṅme̱ne̱ otšũlo̱ ená ele ake̱ mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe, edšake̱ maṅtše̱ efe noni etšũlo̱ wie le̱.

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ni Ioab te ši ni eyiṅ ete *Gešur, ni eyaṅõ Absalom ke̱-ba Ierusalem. *

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Hã ni egbá ke̱-ya le̱dientše̱ ewe le̱, ši kāhã ebana mihĩe. Ke̱ke̱ ni Absalom gbá ke̱-te le̱dientše̱ ewe le̱, ni ebanaa maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱ eku eyi le̱, eyitšo̱i ṅmẽo̱ šekeli ohai-enyo̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ nsẽninte̱ le̱ nā,

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Ni afo̱ bihĩĩ etẽ ahã Absalom ke̱ biyō kome ni atšé̱o̱le̱ *Tamar; edši yō ko ni hĩe yo̱ fe̱o. *

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Absalom ye afii enyo̱ ye̱ Ierusalem, ni enaa maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Absalom tšũ ayatšé̱ Ioab, koni etšũle̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ; ši Ioab sumo̱o̱ ní eba. Ni etšũ ekoṅ noni dši šii enyo̱, ši esumo̱o̱ ní eba.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ekē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Nyekwe̱a, Ioab ṅmõ ye̱ minõ le̱ mase̱i, ni eye̱ akoko ye̱ dše̱i, nyeyaä ní nyeyamãa nā la. Ni Absalom tšũdši le̱ te ni ame̱yamã ṅmõ le̱ nā la.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab te ši ni eba Absalom ṅõ ye̱ šĩa ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba otšũdši le̱ yamã miṅmõ le̱ nā la?

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Ni Absalom kē̱ Ioab ake̱: Na, mitšũ aba oṅõ abakē̱o ake̱: Ba ni matšũo maṅtše̱ ṅõ ni oyabile̱ ohãmi ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ midše̱ Gešur miba? Miye dše̱i lolo kũle̱ ehĩ hãmi! nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ hã mana maṅtše̱ hĩe; ši ke̱dši tõmo̱ ko ye̱ mihe le̱, hã ní egbemi!

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ni ebakē̱le̱. Ni etšé̱ Absalom, ni eba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, ni eṅõ ehĩe ebu ši ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe ni ekotole̱, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ſo̱ Absalom nā.

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Asaṅ Absalom kē̱o̱ ake̱: Miná ní kũle̱ awomi kodšolo̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni mofẽmo ní hĩe sane ko lo kodšomo̱ ko le̱ eba miṅõ ni makodšole̱ ye̱ dšale̱ nā!

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši moko tši be̱ṅke̱ ni ebakotole̱ le̱, ekpãa enine mli ni emõo̱ emli ni eſo̱ö̱ enā.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ Absalom feo̱ Israelbii fẽ ni baä maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ saneyeli le̱, ne̱ke̱ Absalom fe edšu Israel hĩĩ le atšui.

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: *Ya ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli! Ke̱ke̱ ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ete Hebron. *

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni adafitſalo̱ ko ba David ṅõ ebakē̱le̱ ake̱: Israelbii le̱ atšui emõ Absalom!

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ etšūdši fẽ ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ Ierusalem le̱ ake̱: Nyetea ši, nyehãa *wo̱dšoa foi; ši ke̱-dšee nakai le̱ we̱dšeṅ Absalom deṅ! Nyefea mrãmrã ni wo̱tea ni ekabaninawo̱ trukā, ni ehã sane fõṅ bayewo̱, ni egbe maṅ le̱ ke̱ klante! *Lal.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ *Itai, Gatnyo le̱, ake̱: Mẽba ni bo hũ oke̱wo̱ yaä? Kũ ose̱ ní oke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ayahĩ ši; edšake̱ gbe̱ dšio ni afão ye̱ omaṅ.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Kole̱ nyè kpākpa nyè ní oba ne̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ ṅme̱ne̱ hũ misā mihã oke̱wo̱ ayatšomlo̱ lo? ši mi le̱ miya hefẽhe ni miná. Kũ ose̱ ní oke̱ onyemimei le̱ aya; Iehowa mo̱bo̱nale̱ ke̱ ano̱kwale ke̱o ahĩ ši!

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Ši Itai here maṅtše̱ le̱ no̱ ni ekē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ni minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ hũ hĩe kã ne̱, hefẽhe ni minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ aahĩ le̱, gbĕle mliō, wala mliõ, ke̱-dšee dše̱i otšũlo̱ aahĩ fĩ!

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David kē̱ Itai ake̱: Dšogbãṅ, ba ni obaho! Ni Itai, Gatnyo le̱, ke̱ ehĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱ gbekẽbii fẽ ni fata ehe le̱ baho.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ fó ke̱ gbē wale̱, ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ foṅ ke̱-ho, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ dientše̱ fo *Kidron fā le̱, ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ foṅ ke̱-ho ke̱-tšṍ ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ gbe̱. *Ioh.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ le̱ na, Zadok ke̱ Abiatar hũ ne̱, ni Levibii le̱ fẽ fata ehe, ni ame̱tẽre Nyoṅmo̱ kpāṅmo̱ adeka le̱; ni ame̱to Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ame̱mã ši ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni maṅ mŭ le̱ fẽ dše mã le̱ṅ ho tã.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Zadok ake̱: Oke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ aya mã le̱ṅ ekoṅ; ke̱dši mihĩe aaba nyam ye̱ Iehowa hĩe le̱, eke̱mi aaba ekoṅ ni eehã manale̱ ke̱ ešihĩle̱he le̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši ekē̱ ne̱ke̱ ake̱: Mibe̱ ohe tšui le̱, na mi ne̱, hã *efemi bo̱ni sa ehĩe! *

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Nyena, mibahĩ ṅã le̱ no̱ fāfōhe le̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní wiemo̱ ko aadše̱ nyeṅõ abatſami adafi.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Zadok ke̱ Abiatar wó Nyoṅmo̱ adeka le̱ ke̱-te Ierusalem ekoṅ, ni ame̱yahĩ dše̱i.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Ši David kwo̱ mũgoṅ le̱ ke̱-te, ni beni eyaã le̱, ehĩe yāfó, ni eha eyiteṅ, ni enyie enane flo; ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ní ke̱le̱ nyie le̱ ateṅ mofẽmo eha eyiteṅ, ni beni ame̱yaä le̱, ame̱hĩe yāfó.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ni moko bagba David ake̱: Ahitofel ye̱ mei ní ke̱ Absalom ekpãṅ le̱ ateṅ! Ni David kē̱: Iehowa, ofai ne̱, ní ohã Ahitofel ṅāwō le̱ atšṍ kwašiai asane!

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni David še̱ goṅ le̱ yiteṅ, heni adšáa Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ le̱, na, Hušai, Arkinyo le̱, ke̱le̱ bakpe ke̱ etade ní egbla, ke̱ eyiteṅ sũisũi.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: ši ke̱dši okũ ose̱ ke̱-te mã le̱ṅ ni oyakē̱ Absalom ake̱: Maṅtše̱, otšũlo̱ dšimi; tšutšu le̱ otše̱ tšũlo̱ dšimi, ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ matšṍ otšũlo̱ le̱: no moṅ *oofite Ahitofel ṅāwō le̱ ohãmi. *

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Ni Zadok ke̱ Abiatar, oso̱foi le̱, ani dšee oṅõ noṅṅ ame̱yo̱ ye̱ dše̱i? Nohewo̱ le̱ sane-fẽ-sane ní oonu ke̱-adše̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱, okē̱ Zadok ke̱ Abiatar, oso̱foi le̱.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Na, ame̱bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱ ke̱ame̱ ye̱ dše̱i: Zadok bi Ahimaaz ke̱ Abiatar bi Ionatan; ni ame̱nine no̱ nyetšṍ nyehã nofẽno ni nyeanu le̱ aše̱ mideṅ.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hušai, David *šientše̱ le̱, ba mã le̱ṅ. Ni Absalom hũ ba Ierusalem. *

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Ziba ake̱: Na, Mefibošet nii le̱ fẽ atšṍ onõ! Ni Ziba kē̱: Mīkotoö! Ha mihĩe aba nyam ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ hĩe!

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅtše̱ David baše̱ Bahurim le̱, na, nū ko ni dše̱ Saul we le̱ weku le̱ṅ ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Šimei, ní dši Gera bi le̱, dše kpo ke̱-ba, ni beni ebaä fẽ le̱, *ehĩe lōmo̱. *

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Ni etſia David ke̱ maṅtše̱ David tšũdši le̱ fẽ te̱i, tše̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ hĩĩ kakabãi le̱ ye̱ eninedšũrõ ke̱ ebe̱ku.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Ni bo̱ni Šimei kē̱o̱ beni elomoo̱ le̱ ne̱: Dše kpo, dše kpo, lá he gbomo ke̱ gbomo fõṅ!

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Abišai, Zeruia bi le̱, kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ po ni ne̱ke̱ gbè gbonyo ne̱ aalomo̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱? *Hã maya ni mayadšie eyitšo ye̱ eno̱! *

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Ni beni David ke̱ ewebii le̱ nyie gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaä le̱, bēle̱ Šimei mīšrãle̱ ke̱-nyie goṅ le̱ mase̱i ye̱ eṅe̱le̱no̱, ni be-ni eyaã fẽ le̱, ēlomo̱le̱ ni etſiale̱ te̱i ke̱ sūkukulii.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ mei le̱ fẽ ní fata ehe le̱ baše̱ [*Iordan nā], ni eto̱ame̱ kpo̱tō̱, ni ame̱bawo ame̱tšui ye̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ši Absalom kē̱ Hušai ake̱: Aso edšũrõ ni oná ofe onanyo le̱ ne̱? Mẽba ni oke̱ onanyo le̱ eyaa?

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Ni noni dši enyo̱ le̱, namo po esa ake̱ masúmo̱? Ani dšee ebi le̱ hĩe masúmo̱ ye̱? Bo̱ni misúmo̱ ye̱ otše̱ hĩe le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ mahĩ ši ye̱ ehĩe!

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Absalom kē̱ Ahitofel ake̱: Nyewoa ṅã ní wo̱kwe̱ noni wo̱o̱fe!

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ni Ahitofel kē̱ Absalom ake̱: Ya otše̱ hemei le̱ ní *ešĩ ake̱ ame̱kwe̱ šĩa le̱ aṅõ, koni Israel mū le̱ fẽ anu ake̱ ohã ohe edše fũ ewo otše̱, no aahã mei ní fata ohe le̱ fẽ awaame̱. *

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ši bū ame̱hã Absalom ye̱ tšũ le̱ yiteṅ, ni *Absalom te etše̱ hemei le̱ aṅõ ye̱ Israel fẽ hĩe. *

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Ši Ahitofel ṅã le̱ ni ewoo̱ ye̱ nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ tamo̱ noni ayabio̱ Nyoṅmo̱ dāṅ gbẽ; nakai David ke̱ Absalom fẽ buo̱ Ahitofel ṅāi fẽ ni ewoame le̱.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Koni wo̱yaninale̱ ye̱ hefẽhe ni aanale̱ ye̱, ni wo̱ſie eno̱ tamo̱ bō̱ nyõo̱ šikpoṅ, ni le̱ dšio, mei ní fata ehe le̱ dšio, we̱hãṅ ame̱teṅ mokomeflo aſe̱.

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: ni mike̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ aakū se̱ abahão: kē̱ hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ni otaoo̱ le̱ ekũ ame̱se̱ le̱, no koni maṅ mŭ le̱ ſë atoiiaṅ aadšō̱ame̱.

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Ni beni Hušai ba Absalom ṅõ le̱, Absalom kē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Ahitofel kē̱ ne̱: Ani wo̱ye ewiemo̱ le̱ no̱ lo? ké̱ dšee nakai le̱, bo hũ wiemo̱!

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ni Hušai kē̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Bodientše̱ ole otše̱ ke̱ ewebii le̱ ake̱ kakabãi dšiame̱, ni ame̱hĩe edo̱ tamo̱ ošišibriši ni ayalō ebii ye̱ dſe̱iaṅ; ni otše̱ le̱ nū tawulo̱ ni, ni eke̱ maṅ le̱ ehĩṅ šĩ nyō le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Ni no le̱ mo po ni dši ekãlo̱ ni etšui tame̱ dšata tšui le̱, etšui bafā; edšake̱ Israel fẽ le ake̱ otše̱ le̱ kakabã dšile̱, ni mei ní fata ehe le̱ hũ ekãlo̱i ni.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ṅā ni miwoo̱ dši ake̱: ohã abua Israel mū le̱ fẽ nā ahão ke̱-dše̱ Dan ke̱-yaſie Beeršeba, tamo̱ ṅšo̱ nā šia ye̱ fále̱ nā, koni bodientše̱ hũ oya ta le̱.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ ke̱dši maṅ ko mli eyabote le̱, no le̱ Israel fẽ aṅõ tāṅkpēi ke̱-ya nakai maṅ le̱ he, ni wo̱gblale̱ ke̱-ya fā le̱ṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní anaṅ te̱ bibiō kome ne̱ke̱ ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hušai yakē̱ Zadok ke̱ Abiatar, oso̱foi le̱, ake̱: Ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ Ahitofel wo Absalom ke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ aṅā, ni ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ mi hũ miwo ṅā.

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ Ionatan ke̱ Ahimaaz ye̱ *Rogel nubu le̱ mase̱i; ni tšũlo̱yō ko yakē̱o̱ame̱, koni ame̱ya ní ame̱yakē̱ maṅtše̱ David; ši beni afe ní akanaame̱ hewo̱ le̱, ame̱yaa mã le̱ṅ. *

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ oblanyo ko yanaame̱, ni eyakē̱ Absalom. Ši ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ame̱nyie oyáyá, ni ame̱se̱ Bahurim ni ame̱bote nū ko we, ni eye̱ nubu ko ye̱ ekpo le̱ no̱, ni ame̱yabote mli.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni beni Absalom tšũdši le̱ ba yō le̱ ṅõ ye̱ šĩa le̱, ame̱bile̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ Ahimaaz ke̱ Ionatan ye̱? Ni yō le̱ ke̱ame̱ ake̱: Ame̱fo fã bibiō le̱ ke̱-te. Ni beni ame̱yataoame̱ ni ame̱naa-ame̱ le̱, ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-baho Ierusalem ekoṅ.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱te se̱ le̱, ame̱dše kpo ke̱-dše̱ bu le̱ mli, ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te ame̱yagba maṅtše̱ David, ni ame̱kē̱ David ake̱: Nyetea ši ni nyeyafoa fā le̱ mrãmrã, bo̱ni Ahitofel ewo nyehe ṅā ne̱.

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ mei le̱ fẽ ní fata ehe le̱ te ši ni ame̱yafo Iordan; ni beni dše tše̱reo̱ le̱, eſe̱ko ame̱teṅ mokome flo ní efoko Iordan.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ni beni Ahitofel na ake̱ ayee eṅāwō le̱ no̱ le̱, ewo etedši no̱ nii, ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ete ewe ye̱ emaṅ, ni eto ewe le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱, ni *eyawo esẽ kpã ni egbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱ fū̃he le̱. *Mat.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Ši David eba Mahanaim. Ni beni Absalom ke̱ Israelbii le̱ fẽ yafo Iordan le̱, bĕle̱ David eše̱ Mahanaim momo.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Ni Absalom ṅõ Amasa ewo tatše̱ ye̱ Ioab nãdšiaṅ. Ni *Amasa le̱, Israelnyo ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Itra, ní te Ioab nye Zeruia nyemiyō Nahaš biyō Abigal ṅõ le̱, bi ni. *

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Ni Israel ke̱ Absalom yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni David še̱ Mahanaim le̱, Šobi ní dši Nahaš ní dše̱ Amonbii amaṅ Raba le̱ bi le̱, ke̱ *Makir, Amiel ni dše̱ Lo-Debar le̱ bi le̱, ke̱ †Barzilai, Gileadnyo ni dše̱ Rogelim le̱, *

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: ke̱ wò ke̱ butru ke̱ tōi ke̱ tšina kēsui ame̱bahā David ke̱ mei ní fata ehe le̱ ni ame̱ye; edšake̱ ame̱kē̱: Bene̱ hõmo̱ mīye mei le̱ ni *eto̱ame̱ ni kũmai hũ mīyeame̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Ni David dša ta le̱ mli etẽ, eke̱ mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome wo Ioab deṅ, ni eke̱ mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome hũ wo Abišai, Zeruia bi ni dši Ioab nyemi le̱, deṅ, ni eke̱ mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome hũ wo *Itai, Gatnyo le̱, deṅ. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ta le̱ ake̱: Midientše̱ hũ mike̱nye aate. *

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Ši maṅ le̱ kē̱: Kāya! Ši ke̱dši foi ni wo̱dše hũ, ame̱diṅ wo̱se̱; ni asaṅ kē̱ nyõ wo̱teṅ mei fã nyõ tete le̱, ame̱diṅ wo̱se̱; ši bo le̱ odšra wa tamo̱ wo̱yi akpei-nyoṅma; nohewo̱ le̱ ehĩ moṅ ake̱ odše̱ mā le̱ṅ oye obuawo̱.

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Ni nū ko yana, ni eyagba Ioab ake̱: Na, miyana Absalom tšotšõro ši ye̱ blo̱fo-yō̱itšo ko no̱.

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Ši ta le̱ gbe̱ ſã dše̱i šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ; ni mei ní kō ye nakai gbĩ le̱ fá fé mei ni klante ye.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Ni Absalom ke̱ David tšũdši le̱ yakpe. Ni Absalom tá tedšíokpo̱ṅo̱ no̱, ni tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱ le̱ ke̱le̱ yatšṍ blo̱fo-yō̱itšo kpeteṅkple ko nidší kusūi ašiši, ni eyitšo yaka tšo le̱ mli, ni etšotšŏro ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ teṅ, ni tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱ le̱ dše ešiši ete.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Ni Ioab kē̱ nū ní bagbale̱ le̱ ake̱: Ni beni onale̱ le̱, mẽba otſaale̱ nõ ke̱-mõõ ši ye̱ dše̱i? kũle̱ mahão dſie̱te̱i kukudši nyoṅma ke̱ mlifīnõ ko.

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Ke̱dši miši mitšitši mifele̱ efõṅ ko le̱, nto bodientše̱ hũ oote ši owomi!

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Ni Ioab kē̱: Ebe̱ ake̱ mašašao ši ne̱ke̱ ye̱ ohĩe! Ni ekō̱lo̱ akploi etẽ ehĩe edeṅ, ni eke̱-yatšuro̱ Absalom tšuiṅ. Ši ehĩe kā lolo ye̱ blo̱fo-yō̱itšo le̱ ne̱,

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: ni oblahĩĩ nyoṅma ní hĩe Ioab tawūnii le̱ babo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱tſia Absalom nii ni ame̱gbele̱.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Ši beni Absalom yo̱ dšeṅ le̱, emã kaimo̱šiu ní yo̱ maṅtše̱dšō̱ le̱ṅ le̱ ehã ehe, edšake̱ ekē̱: Mibe̱ binū ní aaṅõ-kai migbe̱i le̱; ni eṅõ le̱dientše̱ egbe̱i ewo kaimo̱šiu le̱, ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Absalom kaimo̱nõ ke̱ ṅmene̱.

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni *Ahimaaz, Zadok bi le̱, kē̱: Hã ní maša foi ni mayatſa maṅtše̱ adafi ake̱ Iehowa ekodšo ehenye̱lo̱i le̱ ehãle̱. *

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Ni Ioab kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dšee bo ooyatſa adafi ṅme̱ne̱; gbĩ kroko dšiṅṅ ooyatſa adafi, ši ṅme̱ne̱ le̱ oyatſaṅ adafi; edšake̱ maṅtše̱ bi le̱ egbo le̱.

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab kē̱ Kušnyo le̱ ake̱: Ya ni oyagba maṅtše̱ le̱ noni ona! Ni Kušnyo le̱ koto Ioab ni eša foi.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ši Ahimaaz, Zadok bi le̱, sā kē̱ Ioab ake̱: Nofẽno ni aaba le̱ aba! hã ni mi hũ maša foi ke̱-nyie Kušnyo le̱ se̱! Ni Ioab kē̱: Mẽba ni bo hũ ooša foi ke̱-ya, mibi? onáṅ nyõmo̱wo ko ye̱ adafi ní oyatſa ne̱ he!

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: Nofẽno ní aaba le̱ aba! maša foi ke̱-ya! Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ša foi ke̱-ya mo̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni Ahimaaz ša foi ke̱-tšṍ ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱ le̱ ni eho Kušnyo le̱ nā.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Ši David tá agbói enyo̱ le̱ teṅ. Ni bulo̱ le̱ kwo̱ ke̱-te agbó le̱ yiteṅ ye̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ewó ehĩe no̱ ekwe̱, ni na, nū ko hĩe foi ekometō ke̱-mība.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Ni bulo̱ le̱ bo ni ekē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ke̱dši ekometō ni le̱, bēle̱ sane ye̱ enā. Ni ehĩe bā āhũ ke̱-yaši ebe̱ṅke̱.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Ni bulo̱ le̱ na nū kroko hĩe foi ke̱-mība. Ni bulo̱ le̱ bo ekē̱ agbósralo̱ le̱ ake̱: Na, nū kroko hũ hĩe foi ekometō ke̱-mība! Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Le̱ hũ ehĩe sane ke̱-mība.

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ni bulo̱ le̱ kē̱: Efeo̱mi ake̱ moni nyie hĩe le̱ foidšē tamo̱ Ahimaaz, Zadok bi le̱, foidšē. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Gbomo kpakpa ni, ni ehĩeo̱ sane kpakpa ke̱-baä.

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ni Ahimaaz bo ni ekē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Omanye ni ēéi! Ni ebakoto ši ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekē̱: Aadšō̱ Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ní edšie gbomei ní wó ame̱nine no̱ ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ no̱ le̱ ewo odeṅ le̱!

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Oblanyo Absalom le̱ ye̱ dšogbãṅ lo? Ni Ahimaaz kē̱: Mina bumo̱ gidigidi ko, beni Ioab tšũo̱ maṅtše̱ tšũlo̱ le̱ ke̱ otšũlo̱ le̱, ši milee noni dši.

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Tši ohe oyadamo̱ bie̱! Ni etši ehe eyadamo̱ ši.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Ni na, Kušnyo le̱ ba; ni Kušnyo le̱ kē̱: Mihĩe Sane mibahã minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, edšake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ Iehowa ekodšo mei fẽ ni te ši woö le̱ ehão!

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Kušnyo le̱ ake̱: Ani oblanyo Absalom le̱ ye̱ dšogbãṅ lo? Ši Kušnyo le̱ kē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ henye̱lo̱i le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ni teo̱ ši woo̱o ní ame̱feo efõṅ le̱ atamo̱ oblanyo le̱!

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: .] Edšake̱ otšũlo̱ le ake̱ efe eša; nohewo̱ le̱ na, mi tšutšu midše̱ Iosef we le̱ fẽ teṅ miba ṅme̱ne̱, koni mike̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ abakpe ne̱.

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: .] Ni fāfõ-le̱le̱ le̱ fo ke̱-te se̱ le̱, koni aṅõ-fo maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱, ni afe noni sa ehĩe. Ni Šimei, Gera bi le̱, ho kũla ši ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe, beni efo Iordan ke̱-ba le̱,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: .] ni ekē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱ akabu nõša ehãmi, ni asaṅ kākai nibii fõdši ni otšũlo̱ fe gbĩ ni minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ dše kpo ye̱ Ierusalem le̱, ni maṅtše̱ ekaṅō-wo etšui he.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: .] Ši Abišai, Zeruia bi le̱, here no̱ ekē̱: Aso ene̱ hewo̱ le̱ akagbe Šimei, ake̱-ni elomo̱ moni Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ le̱?

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: .] Ši David kē̱: Nye Zeruia bii ne̱, tē mafe nyehe tēṅ, ní nyetšṍmo̱ satana nyehãmi ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱? Aso ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ agbe moko ye̱ Israel, be̱? ši aso milee ake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ mitšṍ Israel no̱ maṅtše̱, be̱?

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: .] Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Šimei ake̱: Agbeṅo! Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kãle̱ kitã.

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: .] Ni eba mli ake̱ beni eba Ierusalem ní eke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ bakpe le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mefibošet, mẽba ni oke̱mi eyaa le̱?

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: ]. Ni ekē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! mitšũlo̱ le̱ lakami; edšake̱ otšũlo̱ fã́le̱ ake̱: Wo tedši le̱ no̱ nii ohãmi ni matá no̱, ni mike̱ maṅtše̱ aya; edšake̱ akpake dši otšũlo̱.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: .] Ši fo *ebafo otšũlo̱ nā ehã minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱; ši minnntšo̱ maṅtše̱ †tamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ bo̱fo ko, nohewo̱ le̱ femo̱ noni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe! *

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: .] Edšake̱ mitše̱ we le̱ fẽ le̱, gbẽle pe̱ saame̱ ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ hĩe, ni kẽle̱ *oṅõ otšũlo̱ ofutu mei ni yeo̱ nii ye̱ okplõ le̱ he le̱ ateṅ, bĕle̱ mẽ hegbe̱ miyo̱ ake̱ mabi maṅtše̱ noko doṅṅ? *

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: .] Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba okã he odšadšeo̱ osane le̱ lolo? Noni *mikē̱o̱ dši ake̱: Bo ke̱ Ziba ayadša šikpoṅ le̱ mli! *

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: .] Ši Mefibošet kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Hã ni eṅõ fẽ tete, gbĩĩabo̱ ní minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ eba ewe ekoṅ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli le̱.

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: .] Ni *Barzilai, Gileadnyo le̱, kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ Rogelim ke̱-ba, ni eke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ba Iordan nā, koni ebawale̱ ke̱-fo Iordan. *

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: .] Nohewo̱ le̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Barzilai ake̱: Hã ní wo̱te, ni malè̱o ye̱ mimase̱i ye̱ Ierusalem.

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: .] Ši Barzilai kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Miwala mli afii le̱, gbĩĩ enyie po eſe̱, ni mike̱ maṅtše̱ yaä Ierusalem?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: .] Iordan ke̱ke̱ otšũlo̱ kē̱ eke̱ maṅtše̱ aafo eyawale̱; ni mẽba ni maṅtše̱ aatomi nãdšiaṅ ne̱ke̱?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: .] Hã ni otšũlo̱ akũ ese̱ aya, ni mayagbo ye̱ midientše̱ mimaṅ ye̱ mitše̱ ke̱ minye gbonyobu le̱ mase̱i. Ši na otšũlo̱ Kimham, hã ni eke̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ aya, ni ofe noni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe ohãle̱.

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: .] Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Mike̱ Kimham aate, ni mafe noni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe mabāle̱, ni noſēno ni oobimi le̱, mafe mahão.

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: .] Ni beni maṅ mŭ le̱ fē fo Iordan le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ fo; ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ſo̱ Barzilai nā ni edšō̱le̱, ní ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te edšē̱he le̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: .] Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ foṅ ke̱-te Gilgal, ni Kimham ke̱le̱ te. Ni Iuda maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ foṅ ke̱-te, ni Israel maṅ le̱ fā hũ fata ehe.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: .] Ni na, Israel hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅō, ni ame̱bakē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni wo̱nyemimei, Iuda hĩĩ le̱, dšuo ke̱-te, ni ame̱ke̱ maṅtše̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ ke̱ David hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ní fata ehe le̱ fo Iordan ke̱-ba le̱?

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: .] Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda hĩĩ le̱ fẽ here Israel hĩĩ le̱ ano̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Edšake̱ *maṅtše̱ le̱ wo̱wekunyo ni! ni mẽba ni nyemli ewo la ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ hewo̱ ne̱? Ani wo̱ye maṅtše̱ le̱ noko, alo ekewo̱ noko? *K.

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: .] Ni Israel hĩĩ le̱ here Iuda hĩĩ le̱ ano̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱ye̱ mlidšāi nyoṅma ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ mli, ni asaṅ wo̱ye̱ gbe̱nãi pī ye̱ David mli fènye; ni mi-he wo̱ mo̱ ni nyebuu wo̱, ni nyehãã wo̱ tšutšu wo̱wie ni ayaṅõ wo̱maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱-ba? Ši Iuda hĩĩ le̱ anā wa fē Israel hĩĩ le̱.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Amasa ake̱: Yakpē Iuda hĩĩ le̱ obahãmi ye̱ bie̱ gbĩĩ etẽ mli, ni bo hũ oba bie̱.

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Amasa yiṅ ete Iuda hĩĩ le̱ akpēmo̱; ši eyatše̱ fè be ni atole̱ le̱.

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab ke̱ ehĩĩ le̱ ke̱ Keretifoi ke̱ Peletifoi ke̱ hĩĩ kakabãi le̱ fẽ fã ke̱-nyie ese̱. Ni ame̱fã kpo ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem, koni ame̱yatiu Šeba, Bikri bi le̱.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ni Ioab kē̱ Amasa ake̱: *Minyemi, oye̱ dšogbāṅ lo? Ni Ioab ke̱ enine dšũrõ mõ Amasa tšẽṅ, koni eſo̱ enā. *Lal.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Ni *Amasa eyakwe̱e̱ klante le̱ ni Ioab hĩe ye̱ edeṅ le̱; ke̱ke̱ ni eke̱dũ emũsũṅ, ni emlinii tue eſie ši, ni etoo no̱ ehããle̱ doṅṅ, ni egbo. Ni Ioab ke̱ enyemi Abišai ṅõ-ſie Šeba, Bikri bi le̱, se̱. *

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Ni Ioab oblahĩĩ le̱ ateṅ mokome yadamo̱ emase̱i ni ekē̱: Moni tšui yo̱ Ioab he ní eyo̱ David gbe̱fãṅ le̱, enyie Ioab se̱!

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ni Amasa koklo ši ye̱ lá le̱ mli ye̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱ teṅ tũntũ. Ni heni na le̱ na ake̱ mei le̱ fẽ ewá edamo̱ ši le̱, ewó Amasa ke̱-dše̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱ no̱ eyaṅmẽ ṅã le̱ mli; ni beni ena ake̱ mofẽmo ní baše̱o̱ emase̱i le̱ ewáa edamoo̱ ši le̱, eke̱ mama ha eno̱.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ beni awóle̱ ke̱-dše̱ gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, mei le̱ fẽ ṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-nyie Ioab se̱ ke̱-yatiu Šeba, Bikri bi le̱.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Ni ekpa Israel akutšei le̱ fẽ no̱ ke̱-yaši Abel ke̱ Bet-Maaka ke̱ Berbii le̱ fẽ ano̱; ni abua ame̱na ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱ hũ ameba ame̱banyie ese̱.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ba ni ame̱basá eyi ame̱wo Abel-Bet-Maaka, ni ame̱tſa kpoku ame̱wo maṅ le̱ he, ni eše̱ mõ le̱ gbogbo ni wa le̱ he, ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ni fata Ioab he le̱ šimo̱šimō̱ gbogbo le̱ ni ame̱wulele̱ ame̱ſīe ši.

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Ni beni etši ebe̱ṅke̱le̱ le̱, yō le̱ kē̱: Ani bo dši Ioab le̱? Ni ekē̱: Miṅ. Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo oweyō wiemo̱i le̱ atoi! Ni ekē̱: Mībo toi!

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Midši hedšo̱le̱ ke̱ ano̱kwa mãdši ni yo̱ Israel le̱ ateṅ eko; bo le̱ ōtao okpãtã maṅ ke̱ bii anye hĩe ye̱ Israel: mẽba ooplenẽ Iehowa gbe̱fāṅnō le̱?

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioab here no̱ ni ekē̱: Kpaõ, ene̱ akagbalemi fõṅfõ ake̱ maplenē lo mafite noko!

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Dšee nakai dši sane le̱; ši moṅ nū ko ni dše̱ Efraim goṅ le̱ no̱ ni atšē̱o̱le̱ Šeba, Bikri bi le̱, ewó enine no̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ David no̱; nyedšieale̱ ke̱ke̱ nyehãa, ni madše maṅ le̱ he maya! Ni yō le̱ kē̱ Ioab ake̱: Na, ake̱ eyitšo batšṍ gbogbo le̱ no̱ aše̱ afōo.

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
