translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yō le̱ nyie enilē le̱ ne̱ ete maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ṅō, ni ehã ame̱fo Šeba, Bikri bi le̱, yitšo, ni ame̱še̱ ame̱fõ Ioab. Ke̱ke̱ ni ekpa te̱tre̱mantre̱, ni ame̱dše maṅ le̱ he ame̱gbe̱ ame̱ſā, mofẽmo te ebū mli. Ni Ioab kũ ese̱ ete maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅō ye̱ Ierusalem.

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ioab dši Israel ta le̱ fẽ tše̱, ni Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, dši Keretifoi ke̱ Peletifoi le̱ atše̱;

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: ni Adoram kwe̱o̱ onĩa le̱ no̱, ni Iehošafat, Ahilud bi le̱, dši sādšiaṅmãlo̱;

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: ni Šeia dši woloṅmãlo̱, ni Zadok ke̱ Abiatar dši oso̱foi,

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: ši Ira hũ ní dši Iairnyo le̱ dši oso̱fo hã David.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ David bi Gibeonbii le̱ ake̱: Meni mife mihãnye? ni meni hũ maṅõ-kpãtã, koni nyedšō̱ Iehowa gbe̱fāṅnō le̱?

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Nū le̱ ni plenēwo̱ ni esá etšṍ wohe ṅāi, beni afe ni akpãtã wo̱hĩe ni wo̱kaná šihīle̱he ye̱ Israel kpokpai le̱ ekomeflo no̱ le̱,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: hã ni aṅõ ebii le̱ ateṅ hĩĩ kpawo ahãwo̱ ní *wo̱se̱ṅame̱ wo̱hã Iehowa ye̱ Gibea ni dši Saul, moni Iehowa halale̱ le̱, maṅ le̱ mli. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Mahã. *

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David te ni eyaṅõ Saul wui ke̱ ebi Ionatan wui le̱ ye̱ Iabeš-Gileadbii le̱ adeṅ, edšake̱ gbĩ ni Filistibii le̱ gbe Saul ye̱ Gilboa le̱, ame̱ *ame̱yadšuame̱ ye̱ Bet-Šan blohũ le̱ṅ, heni Filistibii le̱ ke̱-batšotšŏro le̱. *

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: ni ame̱fũ Saul ke̱ ebi Ionatan wui le̱ ye̱ Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Zela, ye̱ etše̱ Kiš fũhe le̱; ni ame̱fe nibii fẽ ní maṅtše̱ le̱ wo he kitã le̱. *Ni no se̱ dãni akpãtã Nyoṅmo̱ ahã šikpoṅ le̱. *

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ ame̱wu ekoṅ ye̱ Gat; ni nū nyenyereṅṅ ko ye̱ dše̱i ke̱ eninewabii ekpa-ekpa ke̱ enanewabii ekpa-ekpa ni nā šio̱ nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ edſe̱, ni le̱ hũ oblãṅ le̱ bi ni.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ ke̱ Israel bawu ekoṅ; ni David ke̱ etšũdši le̱ fã ni ame̱-ke̱ Filistibii le̱ yawu; ni David to̱ biti.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Ni Išbi ní dše̱ Nob, ní dši oblãṅ le̱ bii le̱ eko, ní ekplo̱ tšīmo̱ ṅmẽo̱ akō̱ble šekeli ohai-etẽ, ní eṅmõ klante hē le̱, esusu ake̱ eegbe David.

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ se̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ ame̱ke̱ Filistibii le̱ wu ekoṅ ye̱ Gob. No mlĩ ni Sibekai, Hušanyo le̱, gbe Saf ní dši oblãṅ le̱ bii le̱ ateṅ mokome le̱.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ ame̱ke̱ Filistibii le̱ wu ekoṅ ye̱ Gob; ni Betlehemnyo Iaare-Oregim le̱ bi Elhanan le̱ gbe Goliat, Gatnyo le̱, moni *ekplo̱ nā tšo tamo̱ mamalólo̱ agbatšo le̱. *

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Ni beni etſa *Israel mpoa le̱, Ionatan, David nyemi Šimei bi le̱, tſale̱ nõ egbele̱. *

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱mei edſe̱ ne̱ oblãṅ le̱ ni yo̱ Gat le̱ bii ui; ni amenyõnyõi ye̱ David ke̱ etšũdši le̱ anine nā.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Edšiemi ke̱-dše̱ mihenye̱lo̱ ní he wa le̱ deṅ, ke̱-dše̱ mei ni he tšẽo̱mi le̱ adeṅ, edšake̱ ame̱he wa fèmi.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Ni David wie ne̱ke̱ lala ne̱ mli wiemo̱i le̱ etšõ Iehowa, gbĩ ni Iehowa dšiele̱ ye̱ ehenye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ adeṅ ke̱ Saul hũ deṅ le̱,

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ madšie oyi, Iehowa, ye̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ateṅ, ni mala madšie ogbe̱i le̱ yi,

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Iehowa dši mite̱sā ke̱ mimō̃ ke̱ miherelo̱.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ ni dši mite̱sā, eṅõ mibaä abo ye̱, mitše̱ṅ ke̱ miyiwalaheremo̱ aklonto, mimõ ní kwo̱ ke̱ mibobāhe hũ; miyiwala-herelo̱, bo ohereo̱ miyiwala ke̱-dše̱o̱ yiwale̱ mli.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Mabo matšé̱ Iehowa, moni sa yidšiemo̱ le̱, ni aahere miyiwala ye̱ mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ gbĕle ṅšo̱kei le̱ ebo̱lemi ke̱-kpe, ni fãi fõdši le̱ ewo mihe gbeyei;

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: gbohĩĩadše kpãi le̱ ebo̱lemi ke̱-kpe, gbẽle tšõnei le̱ hũ edũmi.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Beni efĩmi le̱, mibo mitšē̱ Iehowa, hē̃ mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ mitšé̱; ni enu migbē ke̱-dše̱ eso̱lemo̱we le̱, ni miblo̱mo̱ le̱ bote etoiiaṅ hũ.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni šikpoṅ le̱ hoso ni ekpokpo; ṅwei šišitōi le̱ tšire̱ ame̱he ni ame̱hoso, edšake̱ emli efũ.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Lasũ fã ke̱-dše̱ egugō mli ke̱-te ṅwei, ni la hũ dše̱ edãṅ šã nii, ehã ṅāi tãã ni ehere.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Ehã ṅwei kpo enā ši ni ebayi ši, ni duṅ kpĩ yo̱ enādšiaši.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Ni etá kerub no̱ ni efliki, ni anale̱ ye̱ kē̱yo̱ fīdši ano̱.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ duṅ eši bū ewo ehe, nyoṅmo̱ ni ewo ke̱ atatui kpīkpī.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Kpe̱mo̱ ni nyie ehīe le̱ hã ṅãi tšẽ ni ehere.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Šimo̱ Iehowa šimo̱ ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei, ni moni yo̱ ṅwei šoṅṅ le̱ wó egbē.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: Ni etšĕrẽ gãimlibii eke̱-gbe̱ame̱ eſã, srawa hũ eke̱-wo ame̱he gbeyei.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ṅšo̱ṅ nudšō̱i le̱ dše kpo, ni dše le̱ šišitōi le̱ bakãmo̱ ši faṅṅ ye̱ Iehowa dše̱mo̱ le̱ nā, ye̱ egugõṅ mumo̱ le̱ hũmo̱ nā.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Ekpã enine mli ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei eba-wómi, egblami ke̱-dše̱ nui babaō mli.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Ame̱batuami ye̱ mimanehũlũ gbĩ le̱ no̱, ši Iehowa dši mise̱tšo.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: Edšiemi ke̱-te heni lē̱ hũ, edšiemi, edšake̱ eye̱ mihe tšui.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Iehowa tomi nãdšiaṅ ye̱ midšale̱ le̱ nā, ewomi nyõmo̱ ye̱ mideṅ tšemo̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mible kã Iehowa gbe̱i le̱ ahe, ni nõša ko hāko mike̱ mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ teṅ agbla.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ emlai le̱ fẽ ye̱ mihĩe, ni ekpo̱i le̱, midšeko ame̱he.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Ni miye emū hũ mihāle̱, ni mitšĩ mihe ke̱-dše̱ minõša le̱ he.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Hewo̱ le̱ Iehowa ewomi nyõmo̱ ye̱ midšale̱ nā, ye̱ mihe ní tše ye̱ ehĩe le̱ nā.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Mo̱bo̱nalo̱ le̱, oke̱ ohe tšõo̱le̱ ake̱ moni naä mo mo̱bo̱; moni eye emū le̱, oke̱ ohe tšõo̱le̱ ake̱ moni eye emū;

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: hetšelo̱ le̱, oke ohe tšõo̱le̱ ake̱ moni he tše; ši moni be̱ eṅe̱le̱no̱ le̱, oke̱ ohe tšõo̱le̱ tamo̱ moni be̱ eṅe̱le̱no̱.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ ni naã amane le̱, ohereo̱ ame̱yi wala; ši hewolo̱i le̱, ohĩṅme̱ii kã ame̱he ni obaäame̱ ši.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo dši mikane, Iehowa, ni Iehowa aahã miduṅ le̱ mli atše.

english_verse: You help me defeat armies and capture cities.
translation_verse: Ši bo mike̱-tšẽo̱ ke̱-yaninaä ta, ni mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ mike̱-huluo̱ mitekeo̱ gbogbo.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Mawu le̱, egbe̱i le̱ hĩ pe̱pē̱pe̱l Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ mli tše; edši tše̱ṅ hã mei fẽ ni ṅōo̱ ame̱hĩe fõo̱ eno̱ le̱.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Ši namo dši Mawu, ake̱ dša Iehowa? ni namo dši te̱sā, ake̱ dša wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱?

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Mawu le̱, mimõ ni wa dšile̱, ni eetšõ mei ni eye emũ le̱ egbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ehãa minädši feo̱ tamo̱ ofrotei anõ, ni eṅōo̱mi edamoo̱ migoṅkpo̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Etšõo̱ minidši tawŭ, ni ehãa mi-nidši do̱ō̱ akō̱ble gãi.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Asaṅ oke̱ oyiwalaheremo̱ tše̱ṅ le̱ ehãmi, ni omlihĩle̱ le̱ ehā mitšṍ agbo.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Ohã minādšiſãmo̱i le̱ amli elē̱ ye̱ mišiši, ni minãdši šãnee.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Mitiu mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ ni mikpãtã ame̱hĩe, ni mikpalee ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní miplenẽame̱.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Ni miplenẽame̱, ni mitſiaame̱ nii, ni ame̱nyẽẽ ši ame̱te doṅṅ; ši ame̱nyõ-nyṍi ye̱ minādšiaši.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Ši oke̱ hewale̱ emīami ohã tawū, ohã mei ni tete ši womi le̱ ebakotomi.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Asaṅ ohã mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ etšṍmo̱ ame̱se̱ ame̱hāmi, beni afe ni makpãtã mei ni nye̱o̱mi le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ame̱kwe̱ gbe̱, ši yiwalaherelo̱ ko be̱; ame̱kwe̱ Iehowa gbe̱, ši efoo ame̱dāṅ.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Ni mišimo̱ame̱ mõnyõmõnyõ tamo̱ šikpoṅ mlu, minānā ame̱no̱ tamo̱ blohũiaṅ ṅmo̱to̱ ni migbe̱ame̱ miſã.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Osā odšiemi ke̱-dše̱ mimaṅ le̱ mansōi le̱ amli, obā miyi, koni matšṍ dšeṅmãdši le̱ atše̱; maṅ ní milee po asũmo̱mi.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Maṅse̱bii le̱ aagbĩ kekrē; ni ame̱-adše̱ ame̱kpokplobii le̱aṅ ame̱aba ke̱ hekpokpomo̱.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Iehowa hĩe kã, ni aadšie mite̱sā le̱ yi, ni aawo Nyoṅmo̱ ní dši miyiwala-heremo̱ te̱sā le̱ hīe nyam;

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Mawu ni te̱ō̱ mihe owele, ni ebaã mādši aši ewoo̱ mišiši le̱,

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: ni edšiee̱mi ke̱-dše̱o̱ mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ, hē̃, bo owóo̱ mino̱ ke̱-tekeo̱ mei ni teo̱ ši woo̱mi le̱; odšieo̱mi ke̱-dše̱o̱ nū yiwalo̱ le̱ deṅ.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: bo moni oke̱ yiwalaheremo̱ kple hãa omaṅtše̱ le̱, ni ofeo̱ moni ofo̱le̱ mũ ni dši David ke̱ eseši le̱ edšũrõ ke̱-yaã nāno̱ le̱!

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: eetamo̱ lebi la, beni hũlũ teo̱ ši le̱, lebi ni oblo̱tu be̱, beni dšeṅ etše ye̱ nune̱mo̱ se̱ le̱, ni dſe̱fo̱ kwẽo̱ ke̱-dše̱o̱ šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Ani dšee nakai miwe le̱ yo̱ ye̱ Mawu ṅõ lo? edšake̱ eke̱mi ekpãṅ nāno̱ kpãṅmo̱, ni atole̱ gbe̱dšiano̱ ye̱ nibii fẽ mli, ni emã ši šiṅṅ; miyiwalaheremo̱ fẽ ke̱ mitaomo̱ fẽ, ani ehãã akwẽ?

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Ši yakagbomei le̱, ame̱fẽ ame̱tamo̱ ṅmei ni aše̱re̱ aſie, ni anyẽẽ ake̱ nine akō̱lo̱;

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: ni moni aata ame̱he le̱, dša ehĩe dade ke̱ akplo̱tšo, ni ake̱ la aašãame̱ kwrā ye̱ heni ame̱yo̱ le̱ noṅṅ. (

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Mei etẽ le̱ ateṅ le̱, le̱ dši moni hīe yo̱ nyam fē fẽ; nohewo̱ le̱ awole̱ ame̱safoatše̱, ši kleṅkleṅ mei etẽ le̱ eninaa-ame̱.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Kākãlo̱i ni David yo̱ le̱ agbe̱i ne̱: Iošeb-Bašebet, Takemonnyo le̱, moni dši onukpa ye̱ mei etẽ le̱ ateṅ le̱, ewó ekplo̱ no̱ šikōme le̱, egbe mei ohai-kpānyo̱.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Ni onukpai nyoṅmai-etẽ le̱ ateṅ mei etẽ ne̱ kpleke ši ke̱-ba David ṅõ ye̱ nikpamo̱ be le̱ṅ ye̱ Adulam te̱kplo le̱ mli, ni Filistibii odšoyeli ta le̱ eba-bo̱ nsra ye̱ Refaim dšō̱ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Ni no mli le̱ David ye̱ te̱kplo le̱ mli, ni Filistibii asrafoi le̱ hũ ye̱ Betlehem.

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni hĩĩ kakabãi etẽ ne̱ ṅõtšere̱ mli ke̱-tšṍ Filistibii le̱ ansra le̱ mli, ni ame̱yaye̱ nu le̱ ye̱ Betlehem nubu le̱ ni yo̱ agbó le̱ mase̱i le̱ mli, ni ame̱wó ke̱-ba ame̱ke̱-bahā David, ši esumo̱o̱ ake̱ enu eko, ni eſo̱se eſie ši ehã Iehowa,

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia, nū ekãlo̱ ko ni tšu nibii wudši ni edše̱ *Kabzeel le̱ bi Iehoiada bi le̱, le̱ hũ egbe Ariel ní dše̱ Moab le̱ bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱, ni le̱ noṅṅ ekpleke ši ke̱-te ni eyagbe dšata ye̱ bu ko mli ye̱ snō be le̱ mli. *Ios.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Ni esā egbe Mizraimnyo kpanaku ko; ni Mizraimnyo le̱ hĩe akplo̱ ye̱ edeṅ, ši le̱ le̱ ehĩe dēhĩemo̱tšo ke̱kpleke ši ke̱-yaninale̱, ni ešõ akplo̱ le̱ ye̱ Mizraimnyo le̱ deṅ, ni eke̱ le̱dientše̱ ekple̱ le̱ gbele̱.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Eble ye̱ nyam fē mei nyoṅmai-etẽ le̱, ši kleṅkleṅ mei etẽ le̱ eninaa-ame̱. Ni David wole̱ onukpa ye̱ ehebuio̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱yaše̱ Gilead ke̱ šišigbe̱ Hodši šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱te Dan-Iaan ke̱-lo̱go̱ ke̱-te Zidon;

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Ioab, etatše̱ le̱ ni fata ehe le̱, ake̱: Yakpe Israel akutšei le̱ fẽ mli agbe̱ne̱, ke̱-dše̱ Dan āhũ ke̱-yaši Beeršeba, ni nyekana maṅ le̱, koni male maṅ le̱ yikule̱.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yafo Iordan, ni ame̱yabo̱ nsra ye̱ Aroer, maṅ ní kã Gad dšō̱ le̱ teṅ le̱ ninedšũrõgbe̱ ke̱-yaã Iazer gbe̱;

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Ni beni Arauna yakwe̱ le̱, ena maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ miba eṅõgbe̱, ni Arauna dše kpo ni eke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekoto maṅtše̱ le̱;

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Ni beni David na bo̱fo le̱ ni tſiaä maṅ le̱ nii le̱, eke̱ Iehowa wie ni ekē̱: Na, mi mife eša le̱, ni mi mitõ le̱; ši ne̱ke̱ tōi ne̱, meni ame̱fe? Kpã onine mli owo mi ke̱ mitše̱ we le̱ moṅ!

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Ni beni David te ši lebi le̱, Iehowa wiemo̱ ba gbalo̱ Gad ní dši David ninalo̱ le̱ ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Ni Gad ba David ṅõ, ni ebagbale̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani ōsumo̱ *ake̱ hõmo̱ aba oṅõ ye̱ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱ afii kpawo lo? alo oodšo foi ye̱ ohenye̱lo̱i ahĩe nyõdši etẽ, ni ame̱nyie ose̱? alo gbēle-hela aba ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩĩ etẽ? Agbe̱ne̱ susumo̱ he ni okwe̱ nõ hetō ní mĩke̱-yahã moni tšũmi le̱! *Ier.

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Ni Arauna kē̱ David ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, nofẽno ni hĩ ye̱ ohĩe le̱, ṅõ ni oke̱-šā afo̱le le̱: na, tšinai ni ake̱-šã šã-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ ṅmā̃gbēmo̱ſīlii le̱ ke̱ tšinai le̱ ahe nibii le̱ ni ake̱-fe lai.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Ene̱mei fẽ Arauna ṅõ-hã maṅtše̱ le̱; ni Arauna kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, aná ohe tšui!

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Arauna ake̱: Dabi, ši moṅ mahe ní mawoö nyõmo̱, beni afe ni mike̱ nibii ni miná yaka akašã šã-afo̱lei mīhã Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱! Ni David he ṅmā̃gbēmo̱he le̱ ke̱ tšinai le̱ ehā dſie̱te̱i šekeli nyoṅmai-enumo̱.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_verse: Ni David mã afo̱lešālate̱ le̱ ye̱ dše̱i ehã Iehowa, ni ešã šã-afo̱lei ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei; ni *akpãtã Iehowa ahã šikpoṅ le̱, ni gbĕle-hela le̱ se̱ fo ye̱ Israel no̱. *

english_verse: Adonijah himself was afraid of what Solomon might do to him, so he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Ni Adonia še Salomo gbeyei, ni ete ši eyiṅ ete ni eyamõmo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he aklontoi le̱ amli.

english_verse: You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ba ní mawoö ṅā, ní oke̱-here bodientše̱ oyiwala ke̱ obi Salomo hũ yiwala.

english_verse: While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
translation_verse: Na, beni oke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wieo̱ ye̱ dše̱i lolo le̱, mi hũ manyie ose̱ ke̱-ba ni mabamã owiemo̱i le̱ ano̱ aduatšo̱.

english_verse: Bathsheba answered: Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱le̱ ake̱: Minuṅtšo̱, bo okã Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kitã otšõ oweyō ake̱: obi Salomo baye maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ mise̱ ni le̱ ebatá misẽi le̱ no̱.

english_verse: But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ši na, agbe̱ne̱ Adonia yeo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ne̱, ni bo, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, olee mli eko.

english_verse: He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
translation_verse: Ni egbe tšinai ke̱ koloi ni ewo fo̱ ke̱ tōi babaō, ni ekpē maṅtše̱bii le̱ fẽ ke̱ oso̱fo Abiatar ke̱ tatše̱ Ioab, ši otšũlo̱ Salomo le̱, ekpēēle̱. K.

english_verse: Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king.
translation_verse: Ni bo, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, Israel fẽ mīkwe̱o gbe̱, ake̱ ootšõame̱ moni bata minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ sẽi le̱ no̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
translation_verse: Ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, aaba mli ake̱, beni minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ ete eke̱ etše̱mei eyawo̱ le̱, no le̱ ababu mi ke̱ mibi Salomo ake̱ efõṅfelo̱i!

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king?
translation_verse: Ni Natan kē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! ani bo okē̱ ake̱: Adonia aye maṅtše̱ ye̱ mise̱, ni etá misẽi le̱ no̱ lo?

english_verse: Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!”
translation_verse: Ši ṅme̱ne̱ eyiṅ ete, ni eyagbe tšinai ke̱ koloi ní ewo fo̱ ke̱ tōi babaō, ni ekpẽ maṅtše̱bii le̱ fẽ ke̱ ta le̱ no̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ oso̱fo Abiatar, ní na, ame̱mīyeyẽ nii ni ame̱mīnunū dā̃i ye̱ ehĩe ni ame̱kē̱o̱ ake̱: *Maṅtše̱ Adonia yi aná wala! *

english_verse: But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon.
translation_verse: Ši mi, otšũlo̱ le̱, ke̱ oso̱fo Zadok ke̱ Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, ke̱ otšũlo̱ Salomo le̱, ekpēēwo̱. K.

english_verse: Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
translation_verse: be̱ni mikã Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kitã mitšõo ake̱: obi Salomo baye maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ mise̱ ni le̱ ebatá misẽi le̱ no̱ ye̱ minãdšiaṅ le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ mafe ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ le̱le̱ṅ!

english_verse: Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Batšeba ke̱ ehĩe bu ši ni ekoto maṅtše̱ le̱ ni ekē̱: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ yi aná wala ke̱-ya nāno̱!

english_verse: Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.” When they arrived,
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ David kē̱: Nyetšē̱a oso̱fo Zadok ke̱ gbalo̱ Natan ke̱ Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, nyehãami! Ni ame̱ba maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: he told them: Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeṅõa nyenuṅtšo̱ tšũdši le̱ nyefataã nyehe, ni nyeke̱ Salomo atá midientše̱ mitedšiokpo̱ṅe̱ le̱ no̱ ni nyeke̱le̱ aya Gihon.

english_verse: When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Zadok ke̱ gbalo̱ Natan afo̱le̱ mũ ye̱ dše̱i awole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel no̱; ni nyekpãa te̱tre̱mantre̱ nyekē̱a ake̱: Maṅtše̱ Salomo yi aná wala!

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni nyenyie ese̱ ke̱-ba, ni kē̱ eba le̱, ebata misēi le̱ no̱, edšake̱ le̱ eeye maṅtše̱ ye̱ minãdšiaṅ, ni le̱ mito ni eye lumo̱ ye̱ Israel ke̱ Iuda fẽ no̱.

english_verse: The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
translation_verse: Be̱ni Iehowa ke̱ minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ hĩ ši le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ eke Salomo hũ aahĩ ši, ni ehã esẽi le̱ ada kple fē minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ David sẽi le̱!

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱fo Zadok ke̱ gbalo̱ Natan ko̱ Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, ke̱ Keretifoi ke̱ Peletifoi le̱ yiṅ te, ni ame̱hã Salomo ho tá maṅtše̱ David tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱ le̱ no̱ ni ame̱ke̱le̱ nyie ke̱-te Gihon.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Zadok yawó mũ ke̱ koṅ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ bū le̱ mli, ni eke̱-bafo̱ Salomo. Ni ame̱kpã te̱tre̱mantre̱, ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ kē̱: Maṅtše̱ Salomo yi aná wala!

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ nyie ese̱ ke̱-ba, ni maṅ le̱ kpãkpã be̱dši, ni ame̱nyã́ naakpa, ni šikpoṅ dšidše ke̱ ame̱nāwale̱ le̱.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Ni Adonia ke̱ mei fẽ ni ekpē ni yo̱ eṅõ le̱ nu he, beni ame̱ye nii le̱ eta le̱; ni beni Ioab nu te̱tre̱mantre̱ le̱ gbē̱mo̱ le̱, ekē̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni mã le̱ṅ le̱ efe hō ni ablo̱ō̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱?

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ni beni ewieo̱ lolo le̱, na, *Ionatan, oso̱fo Abiatar bi le̱, ba; ni Adonia kē̱: Ba, edšake̱ gbomo kpakpa dšio, ni sane kpakpa ohĩeo̱! *

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan here no̱ ni ekē̱ Adonia ake̱: Moṅ, wo̱nuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ David ewo Salomo maṅtše̱!

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: ni oso̱fo Zadok ke̱ gbalo̱ Natan efo̱le̱ mũ ame̱wole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Gihon, ni ame̱dše̱ dše̱i ame̱ba ke̱ nyã́mo̱, ni mã le̱ṅ ofe hō. No dši blo̱mo̱ ni nyenu le̱.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ Salomo tà maṅtše̱yeli sẽi le̱ no̱.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ maṅtše̱ tšũdši le̱ ba ame̱badšō̱ wo̱nuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ David ake̱: Onyoṅmo̱ le̱ ahã Salomo gbe̱i afẽ ogbe̱i le̱, ni ehã esẽi le̱ ada fè osẽi le̱! Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ mã eyi ši ye̱ esã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ bo̱ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ne̱: Aadšō̱ Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ake̱ ehã mo ní aatá misẽi le̱ ne̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, ni mihíṅme̱ii hũ ena ne̱!

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mei ní Adonia ekpẽ le̱ fẽ tšui fã, ni ame̱tetē ši, ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo yi egbe no̱.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ni ayagba Salomo ake̱: Na, Adonia mīše maṅtše̱ Salomo gbeyei, ni na, *eyamõmo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he aklontoi le̱ amli, ekē̱: Maṅtše̱ Salomo akã kitã atšõmi ṅme̱ne gbĩ ne̱ ake eke̱ klante egbeṅ etšũlo̱! *

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Ni Salomo kē̱: Kē̱ efe ehe gbomo kpakpa le̱, *eyitšo̱i kome po enyõṅ šikpoṅ, ši ke̱dši ana nõfõṅ ko ye̱ ehe le̱, no le̱ eegbo! *

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Salomo tšũ ayaṅõle̱ ke̱-dše̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he ke̱-ba; ni eba ebakoto maṅtše̱ Salomo; ni Salomo kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya owe!

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Ši bo le̱, kāhã eye ehe; edšake̱ nilelo̱ dšio, ni oole boni oofele̱, ni oha eke̱ eyiteṅ wadši le̱ anyie lá mli ke̱-ya gbohĩĩadše. K.

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni Šimei te ši ni ewo etedši no̱ nii, ni eyiṅ ete Akiš ṅō ye̱ Gat eyatao etšũdši le̱; ni Šimei te eyakpla etšũdši le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Gat ke̱-ba.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: koni ame̱lá le̱ akũ se̱ abua Ioab yiteṅ ke̱ esešibii le̱ ayiteṅ ke̱-ya nāno̱, ši David ke̱ esešibii le̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ ke̱ esẽi le̱, hedšo̱le̱ adše̱ Iehowa ṅō ahãame̱ ke̱-ya nāno̱!

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Salomo ho tá etše̱ David sẽi le̱ no̱, ni emaṅtše̱yeli le̱ damo̱ ši šiṅṅ dientše̱.

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Ši Adonia, Hagit bi le̱, ba Salomo nye Batšeba ṅõ. Ni ebile̱ ake̱: Ani obā le̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli lo? Ni ekē̱: Hedšo̱le̱ mli ni.

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Ni esā ekē̱: Miye sane ko ni miba-kē̱o. Ni ekē̱: Wiemo̱!

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Ofai ne̱, oke̱ maṅtše̱ Salomo ayawie, edšake̱ ekãmãṅo, koni eṅō *Abišag, Šunamyō le̱, ehãmi gblã. *

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Ni Batšeba kē̱: Odšogbāṅ, mike̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ bawie ahão.

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Batšeba te maṅtše̱ Salomo ṅõ ní eke̱le̱ ayawie ehã Adonia. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ te ši eke̱le̱ yakpe, ni ekotole̱, ni eho etá esẽi le̱ no̱; ni ehã ayawó sẽi abamã ši ahã maṅtše̱ nye le̱, ni eho etá eninedšũrõ no̱.

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Salomo kã Iehowa kitã ekē̱: Kē̱ wiemo̱ ní Adonia wie ne̱ dšee le̱dientše̱ esusuma ewie eši fī̃, Nyoṅmo̱ afemi ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa, moni hã midamo̱ ši šiṅṅ ni eṅõmi etá mitše̱ David sẽi le̱ no̱ ni esā emã šĩa ehãmi take̱ boni ewie le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, dša agbe Adonia ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ noṅṅ!

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Salomo tšũ Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, ke̱-te, ni eyatſiale̱ nii ni egbo.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ oso̱fo Abiatar ake̱: Ya *Anatot ye̱ bodientše̱ ošikpoṅ le̱ no̱; †kũle̱ osa gbĕle; ši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ migbeeo, edšake̱ bo **otĕre Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa adeka le̱ ke-nyie mitše̱ David hĩe, ni asaṅ amanehũlũ ni mitše na le̱ fẽ le̱ oke̱le̱ na. *Ier.

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ Salomo fe ſie Abiatar ní ekaye oso̱fo ehã Iehowa doṅṅ, beni afe ní Iehowa wiemo̱ ni ewie ye̱ Eli we le̱ he ye̱ Šilo le̱ aná aba mli.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni sane ne̱ baše̱ Ioab ṅõ; ši Ioab fĩ Adonia se̱, tše̱bele̱ eyafĩĩ Absalom se̱. Ni Ioab dšo foi ke̱-te Iehowa bū le̱ mli ni *eyamõmo̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he aklontoi le̱ amli. *

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Ni ayagba maṅtše̱ Salomo ake̱ Ioab edšo foi ke̱-te Iehowa bū le̱ mli, ni na, eye̱ *afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he. Ke̱ke̱ ni Salomo tšũ Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, ekē̱: Ya ni oyatſiale̱ nii! *

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia te Iehowa bū le̱ mli ni ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni maṅtše̱ kē̱ ne̱: Dše kpo ni oba! Ni ekē̱: Dabida, ši bie̱ ne̱ magbo ye̱! Ni Benaia bakē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Bo̱ni Ioab kē̱ ne̱ ni hetō ní ehãmi ne̱.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa ahã le̱dientše̱ elá akũ se̱ abua eyiteṅ, gbĩĩabo̱ ni etſia hĩĩ enyo̱ ni dši dšalo̱i ke̱ mei kpakpai fèle̱ le̱ anii, mei ni dši Abner, Ner bi le̱, ni dši Israel tatše̱ le̱, ke̱ Amasa, Ieter bi le̱, Iuda tatše̱ le̱ ní eke̱ klante gbeame̱, ni mitše̱ David lee mli eko le̱; K.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, yiṅ ete ni eyatſiale̱ nii ni egbele̱; ni afũle̱ ye̱ ewe le̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ *Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, eto enãdšiaṅ ye̱ ta le̱ no̱. Ni eṅõ oso̱fo Zadok eto Abiatar nādšiaṅ. *

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũ ayatšé̱ Šimei ke̱-ba ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Mã tšũ ohã ohe ye̱ Ierusalem, ni ohĩ dše̱i, ni okadše dše̱i ke̱-mīya hekoheko.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Ši gbĩ no̱ ni oodše kpo oyafo Kidron fā le̱, ná ole ake̱ gbo obagbo; olá aabua bodientše̱ oyiteṅ!

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Ši afii etẽ se̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ Šimei tšũdši le̱ ateṅ mei enyo̱ dšo foi ke̱-te Gat maṅtše̱ Akiš, Maaka bi le̱ ṅõ; ni ayatſa Šimei adafi ake̱: Na, otšũdši le̱ ye̱ Gat.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Ni ayatſa Salomo adafi ake̱ Šimei eyiṅ ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem ke̱-te Gat, ni ekũ ese̱ eba ekoṅ.

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũ ayatšé̱ Šimei ke̱-ba ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nto mikão Iehowa kitã ni migba mli kpō mikē̱o ake̱: Gbĩ no̱ ni oodše kpo ni oonyie ke̱-ate heko le̱, ná ole ake̱ gbo obagbo? ni okē̱mi ake̱: *Wiemo̱ le̱ hĩ, minu! *K.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mẽhewo̱ mo̱ ni oyee Iehowa kitã ke̱ akpo̱ ni miwoö le̱ no̱?

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Šimei ake̱: Bodientše̱ ple efõṅ ſẽ ní ohĩe kã he ni *ofe mitše̱ David le̱, nohewo̱ le̱ Iehowa ahã onõfõṅ ní ofe le̱ akũ se̱ abua bodientše̱ oyiteṅ. *K.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱ Salomo le̱, aadšō̱le̱, ni David sẽi le̱ aamã ši šiṅṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ke̱-ate nāno̱!

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ fá Benaia, Iehoiada bi le̱, ni edše kpo ni eyatſiale̱ nii ni egbo. Ni maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mã ši siṅṅ ye̱ Salomo deṅ.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱, owo otšũlo̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ mitše̱ David nãdšiaṅ; ni mi le̱ gbekē bibĩō ke̱ke̱ dšimi, mileko kpodšē lo mlibā.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Ni otšũlo̱ ye̱ omaṅ le̱ ni ohala le̱ teṅ, maṅ *kpeteṅkple ni anyẽṅame̱ akane lo ame̱nā abu ke̱ fále̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ hã otšũlo̱ *toibō tšui, ni mike̱-kodšo omaṅ le̱, koni mayo noni hĩ ke̱ noni ehĩĩ; edšake̱ namo po aanyẽ omaṅ kpeteṅkple ne̱ akodšo? *Lal.

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni obi ene̱ ni obii ni ahã owala se̱ atše̱, ni asaṅ obii ninámo̱ ohã ohe, ni osā obii ohenye̱lo̱ĩ asusuma, ši moṅ obi ni ahão dſẽṅmo̱ ni oke̱-na kodšomo̱ nā le̱ hewo̱ le̱,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši oonyie migbè̱i le̱ ano̱, ni oye mikpoi le̱ ke̱ mikitãi le̱ ano̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni otše̱ David nyie no̱ le̱, no le̱ ma-hõ otše̱ ye̱ dšeṅ!

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: No mli le̱ yei enyo̱ ní dši adſamaṅi ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, ni ame̱badamo̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ ekome kē̱: Taflatše̱, minuṅtšo̱, mi ke̱ ne̱ke̱ yō ne̱ fẽ yo̱ šĩa kome, ni mibafo̱ bi ye̱ emase̱i ye̱ šĩa le̱.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ yō ne̱ binū le̱ gbo nyõṅ, edšake̱ eyakã eno̱.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Ni nyõn teṅ, beni oweyō ewo̱ le̱, ete ši ni ebawó mibinū le̱ ye̱ mimase̱i, ni eṅõle̱ eyaho̱ emliši; ni ewó ebinū ni egbo le̱ ebaho̱ mimliši.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Ni beni mite ši lebi ni mibahã mibi le̱ fufo̱ le̱, na, egbo. Ši beni mikwe̱le̱ dšogbāṅ lebi le̱, na, dšee mibi ni mifo̱ le̱ ni.

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Ni yō kroko le̱ kē̱: Dabi, ši mibi dši hĩekãlo̱ le̱, ni obi dši moni egbo le̱! Ni mone̱ hũ kē̱: Dabi, ši moni egbo le̱ dši obi, ni hĩekãlo̱ le̱ dši mibi! Bo̱ni ame̱hĩe wiemo̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe ne̱.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Nyebahãami klante! Ni ake̱ klante ba maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Nyedšaä bi hĩekãlo̱ le̱ mli enyo̱, ní nyeṅõ fā nyehã mokome, ni nyeṅõ fã hũ nyehã mokome!

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni yō mo bi ni dši hĩekãlo̱ le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wie, edšake̱ *emũsũṅ mīšãle̱ ye̱ ebi le̱ hewo̱, ni ekē̱: Taflatše̱, minuṅtšo̱, ṅõ bi hĩekãlo̱ le̱ ohãle̱, ši akagbele̱ ko̱kō̱ko̱! Ši mokome le̱ kē̱: Ekatšṍ minõ le̱, ekatšṍ bo hũ onõ: ádša emli! *Ies.

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱: Nyeṅõa bi hĩekãlo̱ le̱ nyehãa mone̱, ši akagbele̱; edšake̱ le̱ dši enye!

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Ni Israel fẽ nu kodšomo̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kodšo le̱ he, ni ame̱še maṅtše̱ le̱ gbeyei; edšake̱ ame̱na ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ nilē ye̱ emli, ni eke̱kodšoo̱.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Ni Salomo ye̱ onĩabelo̱i nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ye̱ Israel fẽ no̱, ni ame̱bãa maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ niyenii; afi mli le̱ mofẽmo hãa niyenii nyõṅ kome.

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Deker bi le̱ ye̱ Makaz ke̱ Šaalbim ke̱ Bet-Šemeš ke̱ Elon-Bet-Hanan;

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: *Abinadab bi le̱ ye̱ Dor niiaṅ fẽ; ni eṅã dši Tafat, Salomo biyō le̱;

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Geber bi le̱ yo̱ Ramot-Gilead, enõ dši *Iair, Manase bi le̱, akrowai le̱ ni yo̱ Gilead le̱; le̱ noṅṅ enõ dši Argob šikpoṅ le̱ ni yo̱ Bašan ní hĩe mãdši wudši nyoṅmai-ekpa ke̱ amehe gbogboi ke̱ akō̱ble adabãṅi; *

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ahinadab, Ido bi le̱, yo̱ Mahanaim;

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Ahimaaz yo̱ Naftali; le̱ hũ ew̌e̱ Basemat, Salomo biyō le̱;

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Geber, Uri bi le̱, yo̱ Gilead šikpoṅ le̱ ní dši Sihon, Amorbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ Og, Bašan maṅtše̱ le̱, šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ni le̱ kometō dši onĩahelo̱ ni ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: .] Ni Hiram, Tiro maṅtše̱ le̱, tšũ etšũdši ke̱-ba Salomo ṅõ; edšake̱ enu ake̱ ame̱fo̱le̱ mũ ame̱wole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ etše̱ nãdšiaṅ. Edšake̱ Hiram *sumo̱ David sane ye̱ ewala gbĩĩ fẽ mli.

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: .] Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Hiram nu Salomo wiemo̱i le̱, ená mīše̱ babaō ni ekē̱: *Aadšō̱ Iehowa ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, ake̱ ehã David bi nilelo̱ ni baye ne̱ke̱ maṅ kpeteṅkple ne̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: .] Ni Hiram tšũ abakē̱ Salomo ake̱: Minu šē̱ ní oše̱mi le̱. Nofẽno ni otaoo̱ ye̱ tšenedrutšei ke̱ se̱se̱o gbe̱fãṅ le̱ mafe.

english_verse: and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of
translation_verse: ] Ni ehãa ame̱yaã Lebanon gbe̱dšiano̱ gbe̱dšiano̱: dā nyōṅ kome le̱ mei akpei-nyoṅma ya, ame̱yahĩo̱ Lebanon nyõṅ kome, ni ame̱bayeo̱ nyõdši enyo̱ ye̱ šĩa. Ni *Adoniram kwe̱o̱ maṅtše̱ nitšulo̱i ne̱ ano̱. *

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: .] Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ fã́ ake̱ ame̱gbla tei wudši kplei ke̱-ba, te̱i ni dšra wa, koni ake̱ te̱i ni ako le̱ ato šĩa le̱ šiši.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.

translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ Rehabeam he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ nii ſẽ ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Ni ta kã Rehabeam ke̱ Ierobeam teṅ dāne̱.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Ni Rehabeam ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ. Ni *enye gbe̱i dši Naama, Amonyō le̱. Ni ebi Abiam baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. *K.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Ni enye Maaka tete, ekpale̱ maṅnyeyeli, edšake̱ efe amãgã ko ní he yo̱ hĩegbẽle ehã Ašera; ni Asa fo emãgã le̱ ni eyašã ye̱ Kidron fā le̱ nā.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ Abiam he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli? Ni ta kã Abiam ke̱ Ierobeam teṅ.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Ni Abiam ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ni ebi Asa baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Ši Baeša, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, fã batua Iuda, ni ebamã Rama, koni mokomoko akaya Iuda maṅtše̱ Asa le̱ ṅõ lo edše̱ eṅõ ke̱-ba.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Asa ṅõ *dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika fẽ ní eſe̱ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ nitōhe le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ nitōhe le̱, ni etu ewo etšũdši le̱ adeṅ; ni maṅtše̱ Asa ke̱-tšũame̱ ke̱-te Ben-Hadad, Hezion bi Tabrimon bi le̱ ní dši Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ ní yo̱ Damasko le̱, ṅõ ake̱: *

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: Kpãṅmo̱ kã mike̱o teṅ ke̱ mitše̱ ke̱ bo hũ otše̱ teṅ. Na, mimadšeo dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika nikēnii; ya ni oyakũ oke̱ Baeša, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, kpãṅmo̱ le̱ mli, koni edše mino̱ eya.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Baeša nu he le̱, efõ Rama mā̃, ni eyahĩ Tirza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Asa he sãdši fẽ ni eſe̱ ke̱ eka fẽ ní efe ke̱ nii fẽ ní efe ke̱ *mãdši ní etotoi le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli? Ši egbe̱le̱ be le̱ mli le̱ eye hela ko ye̱ enãdši ahe. *

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Ni Nadab, Ierobeam bi le̱, baye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Asa yino̱ afi ní dši enyo̱ le̱ no̱, ni eye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ afii enyo̱.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ amrõ pe̱ ni ebaye maṅtše̱ le̱, etſia Ierobeam we le̱ fẽ nii, eſe̱e̱ mokomoko ni mũo̱ ehãã Ierobeam āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ekpatã ehĩe, take̱ bo̱ni *Iehowa tšṍ etšũlo̱ Ahia, Šilonyo le̱, nine no̱ ewie le̱, *

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: ye̱ Ierobeam he ešai ní efe ni esa eke̱-hã Israel hũ fe eša le̱ hewo̱, ke̱ Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mlila ní ewo le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Nadab he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ nii fã ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Ni ta kã Asa ke̱ Baeša, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, teṅ ame̱wala gbĩì fẽ. K.

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Asa, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, yino̱ afi ni dši etẽ le̱ no̱ Baeša, Ahia bi le̱, baye Israel fẽ no̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Tirza, ni eye maṅtše̱ le̱ afii nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ edſe̱. K.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni enyie Ierobeam gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱ ehe eša ni eke̱-hã Israel hũ fe eša le̱ mli. K.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: na, mibabē̱ Baeša ke̱ ewe le̱ maſie, ni mibafe owe le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni mife *Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, we le̱. *

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Asaṅ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ tšṍ gbalo̱ *Iehu, Hanani bi le̱, nine no̱ eba Baeša ke̱ ewe le̱ ṅõ ye̱ efõṅ fẽ ni efe ye̱ Ie-howa hĩe ni eke̱-wo emli la ye̱ enine nā nitšumo̱i le̱ amli ni etšṍ tamo̱ Ierobeam we le̱ pe̱ le̱ hewo̱, ke̱ gbē ní egbe-le̱ le̱ hũ hewo̱. *K.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ni Omri fe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni *efe efõṅ fè mei fẽ ní nyie ehĩe le̱. *Mika

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ebõi maṅtše̱ le̱ yeli lé̱, amrõ pe̱ ni eho etá esẽi le̱ no̱ le̱, egbe Baeša we le̱ fẽ, eſe̱e̱ nū ko nū ko ehããle̱, lo ewekumei ke̱ enanemei ateṅ moko tete.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ela he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ni efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅ le̱ ní eyabo̱ nsra le̱ nu ake̱ Zimri ete maṅtše̱ le̱ yi no̱ apãm ni egbele̱ le̱, Israel mū le̱ fẽ wo Omri, ní dši ta le̱ tše̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel ne̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ. K.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Ni Omri fã ke̱-dše̱ Gibeton ke̱-ba, ni Israel fẽ fata ehe, ni ame̱babo̱ nsra ame̱wo Tirza he.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Zimri na ake̱ ahe maṅ le̱, eyabote maṅtše̱ we le̱ mō̃ le̱ṅ ni ewo maṅtše̱ we le̱ la ni ešã eſie eno̱, ni egbo,

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: ye̱ ehe ešai ní efe ke̱ efõṅ ní efe ye̱ Iehowa hĩe ke̱ nyiemo̱ ní enyie Ierobeam gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱ eša ní efe ní eke̱-hã Israel hũ fe eša le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Ši Zimri he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ apãm ní ete le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Asa, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ ekome le̱ no̱ Omri baye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ afii nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱; eye maṅtše̱ le̱ afii ekpa ye̱ Tirza.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ enyie Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, gbe̱ le̱ fẽ no̱ ke̱ ehe ešai ni eke̱-hã Israel hũ fe eša ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱yakayakanii le̱ wo Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mli la le̱ mli.

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Ni Omri bi Ahab baye Israel ne̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Asa yino̱ afi ni dši nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ kpãnyo̱ le̱ no̱; ni Ahab, Omri bi le̱, ye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Samaria afii nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ enyo̱.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab, Omri bi le̱, fe noni dši efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe fè mei fẽ ni nyie ehĩe le̱.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱-ni Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, *he ešai le̱ ase̱ nyiemo̱ dšee fē̱ifē̱i ye̱ ehĩe hewo̱ le̱, eyaw̌e̱ Izebel, Zidonbii amaṅtše̱ Etbaal biyō le̱, ni ete eyasúmo̱ Baal ni edšále̱. *K.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Ni emã afo̱lešãlate̱ ehã Baal ye̱ Baal šĩa le̱ ni emã ye̱ Samaria le̱.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab fe akrabatša; ni Ahab te no̱ fe efõṅ ni eke̱-wo Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mli la fē Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ni nyie ehĩe le̱.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Eyino̱ ni Hiel, Betelnyo le̱, yasā Ieriko; eke̱ ekromo̱bi Abiram to šiši, ni eke̱ ebi se̱kpelo̱ Segub etăra enā agbói, tamo̱ bo̱ni Iehowa *tšṍ Iošua, Nun bi le̱, nine no̱ wie le̱. *Ios.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Ni Elia, Tišbinyo le̱, ni dše̱ Gileadbii le̱ ateṅ le̱, bakē̱ Ahab ake̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mo hĩe ni midamoo̱ le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, *ke̱dši bó̱ lo nyoṅmo̱ aane̱ ye̱ afii ne̱ amli fĩ, dša mi miwie! *Iak.

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Dše bie̱ ne̱ ni otšṍ bokãgbe̱, ni oyatē ohe ye̱ Kerit fā le̱ ni yo̱ Iordan hĩe le̱ nā.

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: Te ši ni oya Zarefat ní dši Zidonbii anõ, ni oyahĩ dše̱i; na, mifã́ yō okũlafo ko ye̱ dše̱i ni elè̱o̱! Luk.

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: *Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, mibe̱ kaka ko, ake dša mãmu dẽko̱ko̱ obŏ ye̱ gbe̱ mli ke̱ mũ fiō ye̱ to̱ mli: ni na, mīle̱ lai ṅme̱ṅmle̱bii enyo̱ō ko, koni maya mike̱ yašã kaka mahã mi ke̱ mibi le̱, ní wo̱ye ní wo̱gboi! *

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ši Elia kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kãše gbeyei! Ya ní oyafe bo̱ni okē̱ le̱; kẽle̱ ṅõ eko ofe kaka fiō ko ohãmi tšutšu dã, ni oke̱-bahãmi; no se̱ dãni ofe bo ke̱ obi le̱ nõ le̱.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Mãmu ke̱ gbé̱ le̱ etaṅ, ni *mũ ke̱ to̱ le̱ hũ se̱ efoṅ āhũ ke̱-yaši gbĩ no̱ ní Iehowa aahã nyoṅmo̱ abane̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no! *

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ete eyafe bo̱ni Elia kē̱ le̱; ni le̱ ke̱ yō le̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ ye gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ ase̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ yō le̱, ní dši šĩanye le̱, bi le̱ he baye, ni ehela le̱ mli wa āhũ po ní emũũ doṅṅ.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ kē̱ Elia ake̱: Mẽ sane mike̱o yo̱, bo Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo? Ani oba miṅõ ní ohã akai mihe eša le̱ ni agbe mibinū le̱? Luk.

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Hãmi obi le̱! Ni ehele̱ ye̱ eno̱ ni ewóle̱ ke̱-te ṅwei-tšũṅ heni eyo̱ le̱, ni eke̱le̱ yaṅmẽ le̱dientše̱ esā no̱.

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Ni ekpã emli ebu gbekẽ le̱ no̱ šii etẽ, ni eblo̱ etšé̱ Iehowa ni ekē̱: Iehowa, mi-Nyoṅmo̱! Mīkpao fai, ha gbekẽ ne̱ susuma akpale aba emli ekoṅ!

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo Elia gbẽ toi, ni gbe kẽ le̱ susuma kpale ba emli ekoṅ, ni ehĩe tšē.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Ni Elia wó gbekẽ le̱, ni eke̱le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei-tšũ le̱ṅ ke̱-ba šĩa le̱, ni *eke̱le̱ bahã enye; ni Elia kē̱: Kwe̱, obi le̱ yi ená wala! *Luk.

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni yō le̱ kē̱ Elia ake̱: Kpãko miná mile ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo dšio, ni ake̱ Iehowa wiemo ní yo̱ onā le ano̱kwale ni!

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱dša šikpoṅ le̱ ame̱hã ame̱he, koni ame̱kpa no̱ ke̱-ho; Ahab kome tšṍ afã, ni Obadia hũ kome tšṍ afã.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, bo noṅṅ okē̱o̱ ake̱: Yakē̱ onuṅtšo̱ ake̱: Na, Elia ye̱ bie̱!

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱ amrõ pe̱ ni mašĩo mate le̱, Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ aabawóo ke̱-ate heni milee, ni ké̱ mite miyakē̱ Ahab, ni ebanaao le̱, ebagbemi; ši otšũlo̱ *šeo̱ Iehowa gbeyei ke̱-dše̱ migbekẽbiiaši. *K.

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Obadia yiṅ ete ni eke̱ Ahab yakpe, ni egbale̱. Ni Ahab te ni eke̱ Elia yakpe.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Ahab bana Elia le̱, Ahab kē̱le̱ ake̱: *Bo Israel haolo̱ le̱, bo ne̱? *Amos

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab tšũ ate Israelbii le̱ fẽ ṅõ, ni ayabua gbalo̱i le̱ nā ke̱-bakpe ye̱ Karmel goṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Elia tši be̱ṅke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ, ni ekē̱: Mẽ beyino̱ noṅṅ nyedīdãa ye̱ sãdši enyo̱ teṅ ke̱-yaši? Ke̱dši Iehowa dši Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, nyenyiea ese̱; ši ke̱dši Baal ni le̱, no le̱ nyenyiea ese̱! Ši maṅ le̱ hããle̱ he-tõ komeflo. Ios.

english_verse: Then Elijah continued: I am the Lord's only prophet, but Baal has
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Elia kē̱ maṅ le̱ ake̱: Mi mikometō dši Iehowa gbalo̱ ni eſe̱, ši Baal gbalo̱i le̱ ayibo̱ dši hĩĩ ohai-edſe̱ ke̱ nyoṅmai-enumo̱.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ abahãwo̱ tšinahĩĩ enyo̱, ni hã ní ame̱mõ tšinanū le̱ ekome ame̱hã ame̱he, ni ame̱flo̱le̱ kukudši, ni ame̱ṅõ-ſie laii ano̱, ni ame̱kawo šiši la; ni mi hũ masã tšinanū kome le̱, ni mike̱-ṅmẽ laii ano̱, ni mi hũ miwoṅ šiši la;

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱mō tšinanū ni ahã ame̱bala le̱, ni ame̱sā, ni ame̱tšē̱ Baal gbe̱i ke̱-dše̱ lebilebi āhũ ke̱-yaši ſane ame̱kē̱: Baal, heremo̱wo̱ no̱! Ši gbẽ ko be̱ ni no̱herelo̱ ko hũ be̱. Ni ame̱tumo̱ ke̱-bo̱le afo̱lešãlate̱ ní ame̱fe le̱.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ſane mli le̱, Elia ye ame̱he fe̱o ni ekē̱: Nyeblo̱a ni awaä, edšake̱ nyoṅmo̱ dšile̱! ekole̱ bene̱ ēsusu eyiṅ, alo edše kpo, alo edom, alo ekole̱ bene̱ ēwo̱, koni ehĩe atšẽ!

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ní Elia kē̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ake̱: Nyetšia nyebe̱ṅke̱ami! Ni maṅ le̱ fẽ tši be̱ṅke̱le̱. Ni esā Iehowa afo̱lešãlate̱ ni ekũmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: ni eke̱ te̱i le̱ mã afo̱lešãlate̱ ye̱ Iehowa gbe̱i le̱ mli, ni etša bu ewo afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he, ni eda bo̱ni eenyẽ able seai enyo̱ eye.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni nu le̱ nyie afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ he ke̱-bo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe, ni ewo bu le̱ hũ mli nu obõ.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ niyenii-afo̱lešã be le̱ mli le̱, Elia, gbalo̱ le̱, tši eba ni ekē̱: Iehowa, Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Israel Nyoṅmo̱! ṅme̱ne̱ hã ní aná ale ake̱ bo dši Nyoṅmo̱ ní yo̱ Israel, ni ake̱ midši otšũlo̱, ni owiemo̱ le̱ nā mifeo̱ nii ne̱ fẽ ye̱!

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Heremo̱mi no̱, Iehowa, heremo̱mi no̱, koni ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ aná ale ake̱ bo Iehowa dši Nyoṅmo̱, ni ake̱ bo noṅṅ ohã ame̱tšui ekpale ke̱-ba ekoṅ!

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa *la le̱ bayi ši, ni ebašã šã-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ lai le̱ ke̱ te̱i le̱ ke̱ sũ le̱, ni nu le̱ ni yo̱ bu le̱ mli le̱ tete ele̱mo̱. *

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ na, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱-hĩeiaṅ bnmo̱ ši, ni ame̱kē̱: Iehowa le̱, le̱ dši Nyoṅmo̱! Iehowa le̱, le̱ dši Nyoṅmo̱!

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Ni Elia kē̱ame̱ ake̱: *Nyemõmo̱a Baal gbaloi le̱; nyekahãa ame̱teṅ mokomeflo mīdšoa foi! Ni ame̱mõmo̱ame̱; ni Elia ṅõame̱ ke̱kpleke ši ke̱-te Kišon fā le̱ nā, ni eyagbeame̱ ye̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Ni Elia kē̱ Ahab ake̱; Ya ni oyaye nii ni onu noko; edšake̱ nyoṅmo̱ne̱-mo̱ babaō mīgbē̱ ke̱-mība!

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ahab yiṅ ete ni eyaye nii ni enu noko; ši Elia kwo̱ ke̱-te Karmel yiteṅ, ni eyakoto ši ye̱ šikpoṅ, ni eṅõ ehĩe eho̱ enakutšei ateṅ; Iak.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱ etšũlo̱ le̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ kwo̱ ke̱-ya ni oyakwo̱ ṅšo̱ṅgbe̱! Ni ekwo̱ kete eyakwe̱, ni ekē̱: Nokonoko be̱! Ni ekē̱: Ya šii kpawo ekoṅ!

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ noni dši ši kpawo le̱ ebakē̱ ake̱: Na, atatu bibiō ko tamo̱ gbomo nine mite ši ke̱-mīdše̱ ṅšo̱ṅ! Ni ekē̱: Ya ni oyakē̱ Ahab ake̱: Sāmo̱ oſīli ni okpleke ši, koni nyoṅmo̱ne̱mo̱ akatšĩ onā!

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅhosomo̱ le̱ se̱ le̱ la ba; ši Iehowa be̱ la le̱ mli. Ni la le̱ se̱ le̱ kō̱yo̱ ni tſaã *nyãrãkē gbē̱mo̱ ba. *

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ni eké̱: *Miye Iehowa, Zebaot Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, he awuṅã; edšake̱ Israelbii le̱ ekwa okpãṅmo̱ le̱, ni ame̱wule ofo̱lešãlate̱i le̱, ni ame̱gbe ogbalo̱i le̱ ke̱ klante; ni mikometō pe̱ eſe̱, ni ame̱mītao misusuma hĩe ame̱kpãtã. *K.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: ni *Iehu, Nimši bi le̱, hũ ofo̱le̱ mũ ni eye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱; ni †Eliša, Šafat bi le̱ ní dše̱ Abel-Mehola le̱, ofo̱le̱ mũ owole̱ gbalo̱ ye̱ onãdšiaṅ. *

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱ moni aadše Hazael klante nā le̱, Iehu aagbele̱, ni moni aadše Iehu klante nā le̱, Eliša aagbele̱.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni edše dše̱i ni eyanina Eliša, Šafat bi le̱, ni ēhṹ ni tšinai ntataí nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ nyie ehĩe, ni le̱dientše̱ eke̱ noni dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱ nyie; ni beni Elia hoo̱ ehe le̱, eše̱ etade yū le̱ efõ eno̱.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Ni eši tšinai le̱, ní eša foi ke̱-nyie Elia se̱, ni ekē̱: *Hā ní mayaſo̱ mitše̱ ke̱ minye nā, dãni mabanyie ose̱! Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Kũ ose̱ ni oya, ši ohĩe ahĩ noni mifeo le̱ no̱! *Luk.

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Ni ekũ ese̱, ni eyamõmo̱ tšinai nta le̱ ni egbeame̱, ni eṅō tšinai le̱ ahenii le̱ eke̱-hō ame̱lõ le̱, ni eṅō-hã maṅ le̱ ni ame̱ye. Ke̱ke̱ ni ete ši ni eyanyie Elia se̱, ni esúmo̱le̱.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ke̱ kpekpei ṅmõlõ ame̱-he̱i, ni ame̱ke̱ tãṅkpẽi hũ fĩmo̱ ame̱yitšei, ni ame̱ba Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, ni ame̱bakē̱: Otšũlo̱ Ben-Hadad kē̱: Mĩkpao fai, hã miyi aná wala! Ni ekē̱: Ani ehĩe kã lolo? Minyemi dšile̱!

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱: Eye̱ mli tamo̱ bo̱ni okē̱ le̱, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! onõ dšimĩ ke̱ nofẽno ní miyo̱!

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: hewo̱ le̱ wó̱ aafe bene̱ yino̱ le̱ mibatšũ mitšũdši ke̱-ba oṅõ, ni ame̱bakpa owe le̱ ke̱ otšũdši le̱ awei le̱, ni aaba mli ake̱ nofẽno ni sa ohĩe le̱ ame̱alō ame̱hiĩ ame̱dẽ ke̱-ba!

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni onukpai le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kābo toi ni kākplẽ hũ!

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ Ben-Hadad bo̱foi le̱ ake̱: Nyeyakē̱a minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱ ake̱: Nibii fẽ ni otšũ otšũlo̱ ṅõ ye̱ hewo̱ tšutšu le̱, mafe; ši ene̱ le̱ minyẽṅ mafe! Ni bo̱foi le̱ yiṅ ame̱te ni ame̱yakē̱le̱.

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Ši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱: Nyeyakē̱ale̱ ake̱: Moni mīaã ní eyawu ta le̱ akaſã tamo̱ moni edšie tawūnii eſie ši!

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Ni eha mli ake̱, beni Ben-Hadad ke̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ nuo̱ dã ye̱ asesei le̱ amli ní enu ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ne̱, ekē̱ etšũdši le̱ ake̱: Nyegbáa! Ni ame̱gbá ame̱wo maṅ le̱ he.

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab kē̱: Namo nine no̱ ba-tšṍ? Ni ekē̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Akutšei atše̱mei le̱ ablahĩĩ le̱ anine no̱ batšṍ! Ni ekē̱: Namo atše̱ ta le̱? Ni ekē̱: Bo!

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Ni akutšei atše̱mei le̱ ablahĩĩ le̱ tšutšu fã. Ni Ben-Hadad tšũ, ni abagbale̱ ake̱: Hĩĩ komei dše̱ Samaria mība!

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Kē̱ hedšo̱le̱ hewo̱ ame̱baä dšio, ta hewo̱ ame̱baä dšio, nyemõmo̱a-ame̱ hīekālo̱i!
