english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: ame̱teṅ mofẽmo gbe moni eke̱kpe; ni Arambii le̱ dšo foi, ni Israel tiuame̱. Ni Ben-Hadad, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ trá okpo̱ṅo̱i ano̱ ke̱-dšo foi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Ši Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ gõdšiaṅ nyoṅmo̱i ni, nohewo̱ ni ame̱nine tšṍ wo̱no̱ le̱; ši hã wo̱ke̱ame̱ awu ye̱ ṅã kplenẽ no̱, ake̱ *wo̱nine tšṍṅ ame̱no̱ lo! *K.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: ni obua ta ko na ohã ohe tamo̱ ota ni hĩe kpãtã le̱, okpo̱ṅo̱i nakai bo̱ ke̱ ſīlii hũ nakai bo̱, ni wo̱ke̱ame̱ awu ye̱ ṅã kplenē no̱, ake̱ wo̱nine tšṍṅ ame̱no̱ lo! Ni ebo, ame̱gbē toi ni efe nakai.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli-ake̱, beni šé̱ afi nākplo̱ le̱, Ben-Hadad bua Arambii le̱ anā, ni efã ke̱-ba Afek, koni eke̱ Israel abawu.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Ni *Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ba ni eba-kē̱ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱ noni Arambii le̱ kē̱ ake̱: Gõdšiaṅ Nyoṅmo̱ dši Iehowa ni edšee dšō̱iaṅ Nyoṅmo̱ hewo̱ le̱, mibatu ne̱ke̱ asafo kpekpemkpekpem ne̱ fẽ mawo odeṅ, koni nyená nyele ake̱ midši Iehowa! *K.

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bo̱bō̱ nsrai gbĩĩ kpawo mene̱mei ye̱ mene̱mei aṅe̱le̱no̱. Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱ ake̱ ta le̱ yakũa nā, ni Israelbii le̱ gbe Arambii le̱ ateṅ naneno̱nyielo̱i akpei-oha gbĩ kome dšenamo̱.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: Ni etšũdši le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, wo̱nu ake̱ Israel we le̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ maṅtše̱mei mo̱bo̱nalo̱i dšiame̱; hã ni wo̱ke̱ kpekpei aṅmõlõ wo̱he̱i, ni wo̱ṅõ tãṅkpēi hũ wo̱fĩmo̱ wo̱yitšei, ni wo̱dše kpo ke̱-ya Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ; ekole̱ eehere oyiwala.

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Ši hĩĩ le̱ eká ame̱toi ame̱mībo enā toi ni ame̱he fe oyá ni ame̱so̱o ame̱kē̱: Onyemi dši Ben-Hadad! Ni ekē̱: Nyeyaṅõale̱ ke̱-baã! Ke̱ke̱ ni Ben-Hadad dše kpo ba eṅõ. Ni ehã ekwo̱ ſīli le̱ ke̱-ba eṅõ.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Ni Ben-Hadad kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mãdši le̱ ni mitše̱ šõ ye̱ otše̱ deṅ le̱, madãi mahã ekoṅ; ni ofe blohũi hũ ye̱ Damasko ohã ohe, tamo̱ bo̱ni mitše̱ fe ye̱ Samaria le̱. Ni [Ahab kē̱:] ni mi hũ madamo̱ ne̱ke̱ kpãṅmo̱ ne̱ no̱ maṅmē̃ ohe! Ke̱ke̱ ni eke̱le̱ kpãṅ ni edšiele̱ gbe̱ ete.

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Ni nū ko ní dši gbalo̱i abii le̱ ateṅ moko kē̱ enanyo ko ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā ake̱: Ofai ne̱, tſami nõ! Ni nū le̱ ekplẽẽ ní etſale̱ nõ le̱.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ake̱-ni oboo Iehowa gbē toi hewo̱ le̱, na, amrõ pe̱ ni oodše miṅõ oya, *dšata aagbeo! Ni beni edše eṅõ eyaã le̱, dšata ko yaninale̱ ni egbele̱. *

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ena nū kroko ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, tſami nõ! Ni nū le̱ tſale̱ nõ, ni epilale̱.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbalo̱ le̱ yiṅ ete, ni eyadamo̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ēmẽ maṅtše̱ le̱, ni eke̱ eyitšofĩnõ le̱ fĩ ehīese̱ eke̱-tšake ehe.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅtše̱ le̱ hoo̱ le̱, ebo etšé̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ni eke̱: Otšũlo̱ te ta le̱ṅ, ni na, nū ko gbá ni eke̱ moko bahãmi šitō ni ekē̱: Ṅõ ne̱ke̱ nū ne̱ oto; ke̱dši aleenõ ni elādše le̱, no le̱ aṅõ *osusuma ato esusuma nãdšiaṅ, lo ke̱-dšee nakai le̱, aaheo dſie̱te̱i talenta kome! *

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Ši beni otšũlo̱ hĩe edo̱ ni ehoo̱ bie̱ ni ehoo̱ bie̱ le̱, ete. Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Okodšomo̱ noṅṅ dši no; bodientše̱ obu atẽṅ!

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ehe fe oyá ni edšie yitšofĩnõ le̱ ye̱ ehīese̱, ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ yole̱ ake̱ gbalo̱i le̱ eko ni.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ni oṅmē̃ moni midšō̱ eno̱ mihã ni afele̱ musu le̱ he hewo̱ le̱, aaṅõ osusuma ato esusuma nãdšiaṅ, ke̱ omaṅ le̱ hũ ye̱ emaṅ le̱ nãdšiaṅ.

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Ši Nabot kē̱ Ahab ake̱: Iehowa akahã ene̱ mīgbalemi fõṅfõ ake̱ maṅõ mitše̱mei agbošinii le̱ mahão!

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ahab te ewe le̱ ni efe gblīnĩ ni emli ewo la ye wiemo̱ ni Nabot, Iezreelnyo le̱, wie le̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ ekē̱: Mike̱ mitše̱mei agbošinii le̱ hãão! Ni eho ekã esã no̱, ni etšṍ ehĩe eto afã, ni ekplēē niyeli.

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ mike̱ Nabot, Iezreelnyo le̱, wie ni mikē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ oweintrom le̱ ohãmi ni mahão šika, alo ke̱dši ōsumo̱ le̱, mike̱ weintrom kroko aatoö nãdšiaṅ; ni ekē̱: Mike̱ miweintrom le̱ hãão!

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Ni hĩĩ yakagbomei enyo̱ ba ni ame̱batrá emase̱i, ni hĩĩ yakagbomei le̱ ye odase ame̱ši le̱ Nabot le̱ ye̱ maṅ le̱ hĩe ame̱kē̱: Nabot lomo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱kplale̱ ke̱-dše̱ mã le̱ṅ, ni ame̱yatſiale̱ te̱i ni egbo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Elia, Tišbinyo le̱, ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Ni okē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ no̱: Ei! ogbe ni osā ōṅõ ni oke̱-fe onõ, be̱? Ni asaṅ kē̱mo̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Hégbe̱ ní gbēi le̱mo̱ Nabot lá ye̱ le̱, *dše̱i noṅṅ gbẽi aale̱mo̱ bo hũ olá ye̱! *

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab kē̱ Elia ake̱: Mõ obamẽ-mi ne̱, mihenye̱lo̱? Ši ehere no̱ ake̱: Mimõo; edšake̱ ohõ ohe ohã efõṅfemo̱ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe!

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Na, mahã efõṅ aha ono̱, ni mabē̱o maſie, ni maplenẽ *Ahab mei le̱ ateṅ nū-fẽ-nū ke̱ moni aṅã́ eyi ke̱ moni ašile̱ ye̱ Israel; *

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ni Izebel hũ Iehowa kē̱ ye̱ ehe ake̱: *Gbēi aaye Izebel ye̱ Iezreel gbogbo le̱ he. *

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Ké̱ Ahab moko *gbo ye̱ maṅ le̱, gbēi aayele̱, ni ké̱ emoko gbo ye̱ ṅãno̱ le̱, ṅwei lofõdši aayele̱! *

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: ni oyakē̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ne̱: Nyeṅõa mone̱ nyewoa tšũṅ, ni nyeke̱ amanehũlŭ abolo ke̱ amanehũlũ nu alè̱le̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní mate mayaye omanye ní maba.

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Ni esã ekē̱ Iehošafat ake̱: Ani oke̱-mi aate Ramot-Gilead ayawu lo? Ni Iehošafat kē̱ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: *Mi noṅṅ dši bo, mimaṅ le̱ noṅṅ dši omaṅ le̱, ni mikpo̱ṅo̱i le̱ noṅṅ dši okpo̱ṅo̱i le̱! *

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Ši Iehošafat kē̱: Ani Iehowa gbale̱ ko be̱ bie̱ ne̱ doṅṅ, ní wo̱o̱yabi nii ye̱ eṅõ?

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, trá ame̱maṅtše̱sẽii ano̱, ni ame̱wowō ametadei, ye̱ he ko kpatā ko ní yo̱ Samaria agbó le̱ nā le̱; ni gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ mīgbagbai ye̱ ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Ni bo̱fo le̱ ní te Mikaia tšé̱-mo̱ le̱, kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ nābu kome egba gbale̱ kpakpa ehã maṅtše̱ le̱; nohewo̱ le̱ hã owiemo̱i le̱ atame̱ ame̱ teṅ mokome nõ, ni owie ekpakpa!

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, na, Iehowa eṅõ amale mumo̱ ewo ogbalo̱i ne̱ fẽ nā, ši Iehowa ewie efõṅ ye̱ ohe!

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ṅõ Mikaia ni oke̱le̱ akũ se̱ ayahã Amon, mã le̱ṅ onukpa le̱, ke̱ Ioaš, maṅtše̱ bi le̱,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Ši nū ko gbla egãi ni elee be, ni etšẽ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ šišigbe̱ dama le̱ ke̱ ṅweigbe̱ dama le̱ kpēhe le̱. Ni ekē̱ eſīli kudo̱lo̱ le̱ ake̱: *Tsṍ onine ni oke̱mi adše ta le̱ nā, ši mipila! *

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-te Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ſīlii le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ na Iehošafat le̱, ame̱kē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ pi ne̱! ni ame̱gbá ke̱-ba ní ame̱ke̱le̱ abawu; ni Iehošafat bo.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Ni hũlũ šinyō̃ mli le̱ ašie̱ ye̱ nsra le̱ṅ fẽ ake̱: Mofẽmo aya emaṅ, ni mofẽmo aya ešikpoṅ no̱!

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ gbo ni ake̱le̱ ba Samaria; ni afũ maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ahab he sãdši ní eſe̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní efe ke̱ ſuo̱wu-tšũ ní emã ke̱ mãdši fẽ ní eto le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei ayino̱sădši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat, Asa bi le̱, baye Iuda no̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱ Ahab yino̱ afi ní dši edſe̱ le̱ mli.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Ni mei ni ke̱ ame̱he ehã adſamaṅbō̱ ni ſe̱ ni ašĩ ye̱ etše̱ Asa yino̱ le̱, eſie-ame̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ ko be̱ Edom, amralo ko yeo̱ maṅtše̱ nãdšiaṅ.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat fe Taršiš le̱dši, koni ake̱-ya *Ofir ayaṅõ šika ke̱-ba; ši ake̱-yaa, edšake̱ le̱dši le̱ dſăra ye̱ Ezion-Geber. *

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Ahazia, Ahab bi le̱, kē̱ Iehošafat ake̱: Hã ni mitšũdši le̱ ke̱ otšũdši le̱ anyie le̱dši amli ke̱-ya! Ši Iehošafat ekplẽẽ.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ afata etše̱mei le̱ ahe ye̱ etše̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ni ebi *Iehoram baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. *

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Ahazia, Ahab bi le̱, baye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Samaria ye̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ kpawo le̱ no̱, ni eye Israel no̱ maṅtše̱ afii enyo̱. K.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni enyie etše̱ gbe̱ le̱ ke̱ enye gbe̱ le̱ ke̱ *Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, moni hã Israel fe eša le̱, gbe̱ le̱ no̱; *

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Ni *Ahazia tšṍ eṅwei-asa ní yo̱ Samaria le̱ samfle̱ mli eyagbē ši, ni ehe mīye. Ni etšũ bo̱foi ni ekē̱ame̱ ake: Nyeyaä ni †nyeyabia Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ake̱ mihe aawami ke̱-adše̱ ne̱ke̱ hela ne̱ mli lo? *

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nū ko ke̱wo̱ bakpe, ni ekē̱wo̱ ake̱: Nyekũa nyese̱ ke̱-yaä maṅtše̱ ni tšũnye le̱ ṅõ, ni nyeyakē̱ale̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Aso Nyoṅmo̱ ko be̱ Israel, hewo̱ ni otšũo̱ ní ayabi nii ye̱ Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ ne̱? Nohewo̱ le̱ sātšo ni oyakã no̱ ne̱, odšeṅ no̱ oyiṅ ši doṅṅ, ši moṅ gbo obagbo!

english_verse: “What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nū ni ke̱nye bakpe ni ekē̱nye ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱, té esu yo̱ tẽṅ?

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nū le̱ *tšo̱iatše̱ dšile̱, ni wolo mlifĩnõ fĩ emliteṅ. Ni ekē̱: Elia, Tišbinyo le̱, ni. *Zak.

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Na, la dše̱ ṅwei bayi ši, ni ebašã kleṅkleṅ mei nyoṅmai-enumo̱ no̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ ame̱mei nyoṅmai-enumo̱-enumo̱i le̱ fẽ; ši agbe̱ne̱ hã misusuma dšra awa ye̱ ohĩe!

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ kē̱ Elia ake̱: Oke̱le̱ akpleke ši ke̱-ya, kãšele̱ gbeyei! Ni ete ši ni eke̱le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-te maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱ nõ kẽ *ní otšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te ni ame̱-yabi nii ye̱ Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ, tamo̱ ake̱ bĕle̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ko be̱ Israel ní aayabi edāṅgbē, hewo̱ le̱ sātšo ni oyakã no̱ ne̱, odšeṅ no̱ oyiṅ ši, ši moṅ gbo obagbo! *K.

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Ni egbo ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ ní Elia wie le̱ nā; ni *Iehoram baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoram ni dši Iehošafat bi le̱ yino̱ afi ni dši enyo̱ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ ebe bi. *

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ahazia he sãdši ni efe le̱ ke̱ nii ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Ni Elia kē̱le̱ ake̱: Eliša, hĩ ši ye̱ bie̱, edšake̱ Iehowa etšūmi Ieriko. Ši ekē̱: Ake̱ nõ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ni osusuma hũ hĩe kã ne̱, mišĩĩo! Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ba Ieriko.

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Ni Elia kē̱le̱ ake̱: Hĩ ši ye̱ bie̱, edšake̱ Iehowa etšũmi Iordan nā. Ni ekē̱: Ake̱ nõ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kā ni osusuma hũ hĩe kã ne̱, mišĩĩo! Ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ame̱te.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱fo mli ame̱te le̱, Elia kē̱ Eliša ake̱: Bimi noni mife mihão, dãni aṅõmi ke̱-dše oṅõ ke̱-ya! Ni Eliša kē̱: Mīkpao fai, hã ni omumo̱ le̱ *mlidšāi enyo̱ aba mino̱! *

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Obi noko ní wa; ši kēle̱ ke̱dši oonamĩ ni āṅõmi ke̱-dše oṅõ ke̱-ya le̱, aaba mli nakai ahão; ši ké̱ dšee nakai le̱, ebaṅ mli nakai.

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni amenyie ke̱-yaä ni ame̱wie lolo le̱, na, la ſīli ke̱ la okpo̱ṅo̱i ba, ni ame̱bagbla ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ame̱mli; ni Elia tšṍ lasũogbĕle mli ke̱-te ṅwei.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni Eliša na, ni ebo ake̱: *Mitše̱, mitše̱! Israel ſīlii le̱ ke̱ ekpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱! Ni enaale̱ doṅṅ. Ni emõ le̱dientše̱ etadei le̱ ni egbá mli enyo̱. *

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ni eko̱ *Elia atade le̱ ní dše ehe gbē ši le̱, ni ekũ ese̱ ni eyadamo̱ Iordan nā. *K.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: Ni eko̱ Elia atade ní dše ehe gbē ši le̱, ni eke̱-tſa nu le̱ mli, ni ekē̱: Nẽgbe̱ Iehowa, Elia Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, yo̱? Ni beni eke̱-tſa nu le̱ mli le̱, emli gba ke̱-te bie̱ ke̱ bie̱, ni Eliša tšṍ mli ke̱-foṅ.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Ni beni gbaloi abii le̱ ní yo̱ Ieriko *ye̱ eṅe̱le̱no̱ le̱ nale̱ le̱, ame̱kē̱: †Elia mumo̱ le̱ ye̱ Eliša no̱! Ni ame̱bakpele̱, ni ame̱koto ši ye̱ ehĩe. *K.

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱hĩele̱ āhũ ní fele̱ ahũntō le̱, ekē̱: Nyetšũa! Ni ame̱tšũ hĩĩ nyoṅmai-enumo̱, ni ame̱yataole̱gbĩĩ etẽ, ši ame̱naale̱.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba eṅõ ekoṅ; ši le̱ le̱ ehĩ ši ye̱ Ieriko, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ani mikē̱ē̱nye ake̱ nyekaya?

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Ni mã le̱ṅ bii le̱ kē̱ Eliša ake̱: Na, maṅ ne̱ kãmo̱he le̱ hĩ moṅ, take̱ bo̱ni minuṅtšo̱ naä ne̱; ši nu le̱ ehĩĩ, ni šikpoṅ le̱ hãa mo šrãkeo̱.

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nyebahãami kã hẽ, ni nyeke̱ ṅõ awoa mli! Ni ame̱babãle̱.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Ni edše kpo ke̱-te nubuhĩṅme̱i le̱ he, ni eyatši ṅõ le̱ ewo mli, ni ekē̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Mitšá nu ne̱; gbẽle lo šrãkemo̱ ko dše̱ṅ mli doṅṅ.

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Ni atšá nu le̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ ye̱ Eliša wiemo̱ ni ewie le̱ nā.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Ni edše̱ dše̱i ete Betel. Ni beni eyaã ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, gbekẽbiihĩĩ bibii dše̱ mã le̱ṅ ba, ni ame̱baye ehe fe̱o, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Yiteṅkpatātše̱, kwo̱ ke̱-ba! Yiteṅkpatātše̱, kwo̱ ke̱-ba!

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ni etšṍ ehe ni ekwe̱ame̱, ni etšé̱ Iehowa gbe̱i eke̱-lomo̱ame̱. Ni ošišibrišiyei enyo̱ dše̱ kō le̱ mli ba, ni ame̱ba-tše̱re̱ gbekẽbiihĩĩ le̱ ateṅ mei nyoṅmai-edſe̱ ke̱ enyo̱ mli.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni edše̱ dše̱i ete *Karmel goṅ le̱ no̱, ni edše̱ dše̱i ekũ ese̱ ke̱-te Samaria. *

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, ši kẽle̱ tamo̱o̱ etše̱ lo enye; edšake̱ edšie *Baal amãgã le̱ ní etše̱ fe le̱. *

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ ekpe̱te̱ *Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, he ešai ni eke̱-hã Israel fe eša le̱ he, ekpale̱e ke̱-dšee he.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni Ahab gbo le̱, Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ tše Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe atũa.

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nẽgbe̱ wo̱tšṍ ke̱-ya? Ni ekē̱: Edom ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Edom maṅtše̱ le̱ yiṅ ame̱te; ni ame̱yakpa ši gbĩĩ kpawo, ni anaa nu ahã tabilo̱i le̱ ke̱ koloi ní ame̱ke̱-nyie le̱.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ao! Iehowa etšé̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅtše̱mei etẽ ne̱ ke̱-bakpe, koni etuame̱ ewo Moabbii adeṅ!

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Ši *Iehošafat kē̱: Ani Iehowa gbalo̱ ko be̱ bie̱ ne̱, ní wo̱o̱te wo̱yabi Iehowa nii ye̱ eṅõ? Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũdši le̱ ateṅ mokome here no̱ ni ekē̱: †Eliša, Šafat bi le̱, ní fo̱se nu ſie Elia nidši ano̱ le̱, ye̱ bie̱. *

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat kē̱: Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ ke̱le̱ ye̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehošafat ke̱ Edom maṅtše le̱ yiṅ ke̱-te eṅõ.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Ši Eliša kē̱ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Mẽ sane mike̱o yo̱? ya otše̱ gbaloi le̱ ke̱ onye gbalo̱i le̱ aṅõ. Ši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dabida! edšake̱ Iehowa etšé̱ maṅtše̱mei etẽ ne̱ ke̱-bakpe, koni etuame̱ ewo Moabbii adeṅ!

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Ni Eliša kē̱: *Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa Zebaot, mo hĩe ní midamoo̱ le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, ké̱ dšee Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, hīeaṅ mihĩe ſieo̱, kũle̱ mikwe̱ṅo ni minaṅo hũ!

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ nyeyaṅõa saṅkũtſalo̱ ko nyebahãami! Ni eba mli ake̱, beni saṅkũtſalo̱ le̱ tſaã saṅkũ le̱, Iehowa nine ba eno̱.

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Nyetšaä bui ye̱ ne̱ke̱ dšō̱ ne̱ mli fẽ.

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Nyenaṅ kō̱yo̱ ni asaṅ nyenaṅ nyoṅmo̱ne̱mo̱; ši kẽle̱ ne̱ke̱ dšō̱ ne̱ bayi to̱ ke̱ nu, koni nye ke̱ nyelē̱-koloi ke̱ nyedšatšutëremo̱ koloi le̱ fẽ anu.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Ni uyeadſa maṅ-fẽ-maṅ ni atſa gbogbo awo he ke̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ ni yo̱ fe̱o, ni nyeatō tšo kpakpa-fẽ-tšo kpakpa, ni nyeatšīmo̱ nubui fẽ, ni nyeke̱ te̱i aafite abō̱ kpakpa-fẽ-abō̱ kpakpa!

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ lebi niyenii-afo̱lešã be mli le̱, na, nu dše̱ Edom gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ba, ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ yi to̱ ke̱ nu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Ni beni Moabbii le̱ fẽ nu ake̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ efã ke̱-mība ní ame̱ke̱ame̱ abawu le̱, ayakpe mei fẽ ní eše̱ tayā ke̱ mei ni efo mli le̱ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱badamo̱ hũsũ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱te ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa, ni hũlũ kpe̱ ye̱ nui le̱ ano̱ le̱, Moabbii le̱ na nui le̱ ní yo̱ ame̱hĩe le̱ ake̱ etšu fā tamo̱ lá;

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱: Lá ne̱! maṅtše̱mei le̱ dientše̱ ke̱ ame̱he ewuwui, ni ame̱tſiatſiā ame̱he nii; nohewe̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, Moabbii, nyeyahaä nii!

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱še̱ Israelbii le̱ ansra le̱ he le̱, Israelbii le̱ te ši ni ame̱tſia Moabbii le̱ anii, ni ame̱dšo foi ye̱ ame̱hĩe; ni ame̱bote šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ni ame̱gbegbē Moabbii le̱.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ni *ame̱dſāra mãdši le̱, ni mofẽmo še̱ ete̱ efō̱ abō̱ kpakpa-fẽ-abō̱ kpakpa mli, ni ame̱wowōame̱ obõbõ, ni ame̱tšĩmo̱ nubui fẽ, ni ame̱tō tšei kpakpai fẽ, dša Kir-Hareset gbogboi le̱ pe̱ ame̱šī; ši kẽle̱ akromiafõlo̱i le̱ yabo̱lele̱ ni ame̱tſiale̱ nii. *K.

english_verse: King Mesha of Moab saw that he was about to be defeated. So he took along
translation_verse: Ši beni Moab maṅtše̱ le̱ na ake̱ ta le̱ mli wa tšṍ hãle̱ le̱, eṅõ hĩĩ ohai-kpawo ni hĩe klante efata ehe, koni ame̱tšere̱ mli ke̱-ya Edom maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅō; ši ame̱nyēē.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eṅõ ebinū ní dši ekromo̱bi ní kũle̱ le̱ ebaye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱ le̱, ni eke̱le̱ šã šã-afo̱le ye̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱. Ni mlifũ kpeteṅkple ba Israel no̱. Ni ame̱šĩle̱, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba ame̱sikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Ya ni oyamãlã gbē̱i ye̱ okū le̱ṅ bii fẽ aṅõ, gbé̱i fodši, kā-mãlã fiō ko ke̱ke̱;

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni gbē̱i le̱ eyimo̱ le̱, ekē̱ ebinū le̱ ake̱: Wó gbé̱ le̱ eko hũ obahãmi! Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbé̱ le̱ eko be̱ doṅṅ! Ke̱ke̱ ni mũ le̱ se̱ fo.

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ko le̱ Eliša bafoṅ ke̱-te *Šunem, ni yō niianye ko ye̱ dše̱i, ni ehĩele̱ āhũ ake̱ ebaye nii. Nohewo̱ le̱ šii abo ní ebafoo̱ṅ fẽ le̱, egbaleo̱ dše̱i eyayeo̱ nii. *Ios.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Ni gbekẽ le̱ bada; ni gbĩ ko eba mli ake̱ ete etše̱ ṅõ ye̱ ṅmā̃kũlo̱i le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ etše̱ ake̱: Miyitšo, miyitšol Ni ekē̱ etšũlo̱ le̱ ake̱: Wóle̱ oyahã enye!

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Ni ewóle̱ ebahã enye. Ni etá eſuo̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši ſane, ni egbo.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: ni eyatšé̱ ewù ni ekē̱: Ofai ne̱, hãmi oblahĩĩ le̱ ateṅ mokome ke̱ tedšiyei le̱ eko, koni maša foi ke̱-ya Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ṅõ maba!

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Mēhewo̱ ni otaoo̱ oya eṅõ ṅme̱ne̱? dšee nyōṅ hē ne̱ ni asaṅ dšee hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ ne̱! Ekē̱: Dšogbāṅ!

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Ni ewo tedšiyō le̱ no̱ nii, ni ekē̱ etšũlo̱ le̱ ake̱: Wole̱ foi ni wo̱te kāgbo̱dšo̱ foidšē le̱ mli ohãmi, dša mi-kē̱o dã.

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ete ni eyaše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ṅõ *ye̱ Karmel goṅ le̱ no̱. Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ nale̱ ye̱ šoṅṅ le̱, ekē̱ etšũlo̱ Gehazi ake̱: Na, Šunamyō le̱ baä le̱! *

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ ša foi ni oke̱le̱ ayakpe, ni obile̱ ake̱: Oye dšogbāṅ lo? owù ye̱ dšogbāṅ lo? gbekẽ le̱ ye̱ dšogbāṅ lo? Ni ekē̱: Wo̱ye̱ dšogbăṅ!

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ṅõ ye̱ goṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, ebamõmo̱ enãdši amli; ši Gehazi tši ba ní kũle̱ ebatšire̱le̱. Ni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ kē̱: Ṅmēle̱ gbe̱, edšake̱ esusuma ehao ye̱ emli, ni Iehowa eṅõ-tẽmi ni edšieko etšõkomi.

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Ani mibaba binū ko ye̱ minuṅtšo̱ deṅ? ani *mikē̱ē̱o ake̱: Okalakami? *K.

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱ Gehazi ake̱: Mĩamo̱, ni oko̱ midẽhĩemo̱tšo le̱ ohĩe odē, ni oya; ke̱dši oke̱ moko kpe le̱, *kāṅãle̱, ni ke̱-dši moko hũ ni ṅão le̱, kāherele̱ no̱; ni oya ni oke̱ mitšo le̱ ayafõ gbekẽ le̱ hĩe! *Luk.

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Ši gbekẽ le̱ nye le̱ kē̱: Ake̱ nõ kẽ ni Iehowa hĩe kã ni osusuma hũ hĩe kã ne̱, mišĩĩo! Ke̱ke̱ ni ete ši ni enyie ese̱.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Ni Gehazi tšṍ ame̱hĩe ke̱-te, ni eke̱ tšo le̱ yafõ gbekẽ le̱ hĩe; ši gbē ko be̱, ninumo̱ hũ be̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ le̱ ekũ ese̱ ete ni eke̱le̱ yakpe, ni eyagbale̱ ake̱: Gbekẽ le̱ hĩe etšẽko.

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Ni beni Eliša še̱ šĩa le̱, na, gbekẽ le̱ egbo ekã esā le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Ni ekwo̱ eyabu gbekẽ le̱ no̱, ni eke̱ enābu bu enābu no̱, ni eke̱ ehĩṅme̱ii bumo̱ ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱, ni eke̱ enidši hũ ſie enidši ano̱, ni ekpã emli ebu gbekẽ lo̱ no̱; ni gbekẽ le̱ he do̱ la.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Ni etšé̱ Gehazi ke̱-ba ni ekē̱: Tšé̱ Šunamyō le̱ ke̱-ba! Ni etšé̱le̱, ni eba eṅõ; ni ekē̱: *Wó obi le̱! Luk.

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eba ni ebaho egbẽ enãdši anã, ni ekotole̱; ni ewó ebi le̱ ke̱-dše kpo.

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Ni Eliša kũ ese̱ ke̱-ba Gilgal ekoṅ; ni hõmo̱ eba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni gbalo̱i abii le̱ trá ehĩe. Ni ekē̱ etšũlo̱ le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ kukwe̱i wula le̱ omã no̱, ni ohō nii ohã gbalo̱i abii le̱.

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Ni moko dše kpo te ṅãno̱ eyatše ſie, ni eyana ṅãno̱ ba ko ni baã ši, ni etšere̱ ṅã mli sakribontei le̱ ewo emama nā obõ, ni eba ebaflo̱ mli ewo kukwe̱i ni niyenii yo̱ mli le̱ṅ; edšake̱ ame̱lee.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱fo̱se ame̱hã mei le̱ ní ame̱ye; ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱yeo̱ nii le̱, ame̱blo̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo! Gbĕle, ye̱ kukwe̱i le̱ mli! Ni ame̱nyẽẽ ame̱ye.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Bĕle̱ nyeke̱ mãmu abaä! Ni eṅõ-wo kukwe̱i le̱ mli, ni ekē̱: Fo̱semo̱ oha mei le̱ ní ame̱ye! Ni noko fõṅ ko be̱ kukwe̱i le̱ mli doṅṅ.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eṅõ-mã ame̱hĩe, ni ame̱-ye, ni eko ſe̱, ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā. Mat.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Ni Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Ya, ši mibamãdše Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ wolo. Ni eyiṅ, ni ehĩe dſie̱te̱i talentai nyoṅma ke̱ šika kukudši akpei-ekpa ke̱ wulamo̱ atadei nyoṅma ke̱-te.

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Ni Eliša tšũ bo̱fo ko ke̱-te eṅõ ekē̱: Ya ní oyadšu ohe šii kpawo ye̱ Iordan mli, ni ohewolo aahĩ ekoṅ, ni ohe aatše!

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Eliša, Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱, nu ake̱ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ egbla etadei le̱, etšũ ate maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽba ni ogbla otadei le̱? hã ní eba miṅõ ke̱ke̱, koni ená ele ake̱ gbalo̱ ko ye̱ Israel.

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Naeman ke̱ ekpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ eſīlii le̱ ba ni ebadamo̱ Eliša we le̱ agbó le̱ nā.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Naeman mli fũ, ni eyiṅ ke̱-miya, ni ekē̱: Na, miyiṅ fẽ le̱: Eedše kpo ke̱-ba miṅõ, ni ebadamo̱ ši, ni etšē̱ Iehowa, e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbei, ni eke̱ enine ahū dše̱i, ni etšá kpiti le̱!

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Ani Abana ke̱ Farfar, Damasko fai le̱, ehĩĩ fé Israel nui le̱ fẽ, ke̱ ka nakai le̱? kũle̱ midšuu ye̱ nomei amli ni mihe tše? Ni etšṍ ehe ni eyiṅ ke̱ mlila.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšũdši le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱le̱, ni ame̱wie ame̱tšõle̱ ni ame̱kē̱: Mitše̱! noko wulu ko ni gbalo̱ le̱ kē̱ ofe kũle̱, aso ofeṅ? āhũ moṅ ní ekē̱o ake̱: Yadšu ohe, ni ohe atše?

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekpleke ši, ni eke̱ ehe yatšo̱ Iordan mli šii kpawo ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ wiemo̱ le̱ nā; *ni ehewolo hĩ ekoṅ tamo gbekẽ fiõ hewolo, ni ehe tše. *Luk.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Ni ekũ ese̱ eba Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ ṅõ ekoṅ, le̱ ke̱ mei ní eke̱-nyie le̱ fẽ, ni ebadamo̱ ehĩe, ni ekē̱: Na, kpako dāni miná mile ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ko Nyoṅmo̱ ko be̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ fẽ, ake̱ dša Israel ke̱ke̱; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ hemo̱ otšũlo̱ deṅ *nikēnii ko! *K.

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni Iehowa, mo hĩe ní midamoo̱ le̱, hĩe kā ne̱: mihee noko! Ni enyẽ eno̱ ake̱ ehe kẽ, ši ekplẽẽ.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Naeman kē̱: Ké̱ hoo le̱, bĕle̱ ofai ne̱, hã ní ahã otšũlo̱ sũ tedši-okpo̱ṅo̱i enyo̱ yitĕremo̱; edšake̱ otšũlo̱ ešãṅ šã-afole lo afo̱le kroko ehãṅ nyoṅmo̱ ko nyoṅmo̱ ko doṅṅ, ake̱ dša Iehowa ke̱ke̱!

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ene̱ ke̱ke̱ Iehowa aṅõ-fa otšũlo̱, ake̱ ke̱dši minuṅtšo̱ miya Rimon we le̱ ayadšá ye̱ dše̱i, ní *ekpasaä minine, ni mi hũ mikotoo̱ ši ye̱ Rimon we le̱, ké̱ miyakoto ši ye̱ Rimon we le̱, no le̱ Iehowa aṅõ no afa otšũlo̱! *

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli! Ke̱ke̱ ni edše eṅõ ete ble fiō.

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Ši Gehazi, Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo Eliša tšũlo̱ le̱, kē̱: Na, minuṅtšo̱ eṅõ Naeman, Aramnyo ne̱, he ekele̱, ni ehee noni eke̱-ba le̱ ye̱ edẽ; gbĩĩabo̱ kẽ ní Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, maša foi ke̱-nyie ese̱, ni mayahe noko ye̱ edeṅ!

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Gehazi ṅõ-ſie Naeman se̱. Ni beni Naeman na ake̱ moko hĩe foi ke̱-nyie ese̱ le̱, edše̱ ſīli le̱ mli eyi ši, ni eke̱le̱ bakpe ni ekē̱: Mei le̱ fẽ ye̱ dšogbāṅ lo?

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Ame̱ye̱ dšogbāṅ! Minuṅtšo̱ tšũmi ake̱: Na, biane̱ tō̃ ne̱ gbalo̱i abii le̱ ateṅ oblahĩĩ enyo̱ edše̱ Efraim goṅ le̱ no̱ eba miṅõ; ofai ne̱, hãame̱ dſie̱te̱i talenta kome, ke̱ wulamo̱ atadei enyo̱!

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ni Naeman kē̱: Kplẽmo̱ ni ohe talentai enyo̱! Ni enyẽ eno̱, ni efĩmo̱ dſe̱te̱i talentai enyo̱ ewo kotokui enyo̱ mli, ke̱ wulamo̱ atadei enyo̱. Ni eṅõ-tĕre etšũdši le̱ ateṅ mei enyo̱, ni ame̱tẽre ke̱-nyie ehĩe.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱se̱ ṅmeṅme le̱ he le̱, ehe ye̱ ame̱dẽ, ni eṅõ-to šĩa le̱, ni ewo hĩĩ le̱ agbe, ni ame̱yĩṅ ame̱te.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Ni eba ebadamo̱ enuṅtšo̱ le̱ hĩe. Ni Eliša bile̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ odše̱, Gehazi? Ni ekē̱: Otšũlo̱ eyako hekoheko.

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nto mitšui ke̱o te, beni nū le̱ tšṍ ehe ke̱-dše̱ eſīli le̱ mli ni eke̱o bakpe le̱? Ani be ní ake̱-heo̱ dſie̱te̱i, ni asaṅ ake̱-heo̱ atadei ke̱ mũtšei ke̱ weintromi ke̱ tōi ke̱ tšinai ke̱ wehĩĩ ke̱ weyei ne̱?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Naeman kpiti le̱ aakpe̱te̱ ohe ke̱ osešibii ahe ke̱-ya nāno̱. Ni edše̱ eble edše kpo ke̱ ehe kpiti aakō tamo̱ snõ.

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ame̱ yiṅ te. Ni beni ame̱še̱ Iordan nā le̱, ame̱tōtō tšei le̱.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ etšũ Israel maṅtše le̱ ṅõ ayakē̱le̱ ake̱: Kwe̱mo̱ ní ahĩ ní okakũ ohĩe ofõ bie̱ ne̱ no̱; edšake̱ dše̱i Arambii le̱ batšṍ ke̱-ba.

english_verse: So the king would warn the Israelite troops in that place to be on guard.
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũo̱ ke̱-yaä he ni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ kē̱le̱ ni etſale̱ he adafi le̱, ni ebuo̱ dše̱i, dšee šikome ni asaṅ dšee šii enyo̱ ke̱ko̱.

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Ni etšũdši le̱ ateṅ mokome kē̱: Dšee nakai, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱, ši moṅ Eliša, gbalo̱ le̱ ní yo̱ Israel le̱, le̱ egbaã Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ wiemo̱i ní owieo̱ ye̱ ose̱tšũ mli tete!

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Nyeyaä ni ayeya-kwe̱a beni eyo̱, ni matší ní ayamōle̱ ke̱-ba! Ni akē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, eye̱ Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ etšũ okpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ ſīlii ke̱ ta babaō ke̱-te dše̱i; ni ame̱še̱ dše̱i nyōṅ, ni ame̱gbá ame̱bo̱le maṅ le̱.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Ni ehere no̱ ake̱: Kāše gbeyei; edšake̱ mei ní ke̱wo̱ yo̱ le̱ fá fè mei ní ke̱ame̱ yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Ni Eliša so̱le ni ekē̱: Iehowa, mīkpao fai, gblemo̱ ehĩṅme̱ii ni ena nii! Ni Iehowa gble oblanyo le̱ hĩṅme̱ii, ni ena nii: ni na, goṅ le̱ no̱ eyi to̱ ke̱ la okpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ ſīlii ke̱-bo̱le Eliša ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱kpleke ši ke̱-ba eṅõ; ni Eliša kpa Iehowa fai ni ekē̱: Mīkpao fai, ſilamo̱ ne̱ke̱ gbomei ne̱ ahĩṅme̱ii! Ni *eſila ame̱hĩṅme̱ii ye̱ Eliša wiemo̱ le̱ nā. *

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Eliša kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Dšee gbe̱ le̱ ne̱, ni asaṅ dšee maṅ le̱ hũ ne̱; nyenyiea mise̱, ni mike̱nye aya nū ní nyetaoe̱ le̱ ṅō! Ni eke̱ame̱ te Samaria tõ.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱še̱ Samaria le̱, Eliša kē̱: Iehowa, gbleme̱ gbomei ne̱ ahĩṅme̱ii, koni ame̱na nii! Ni Iehowa gble ame̱hĩṅme̱ii, ni ame̱na nii, ni na, Samaria teṅ ame̱yo̱ ne̱!

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Ni beni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ naame̱ le̱, ekē̱ Eliša ake̱: Mitše̱, mitſiaame̱ nii lo?

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Ni ehere no̱ ake̱: Kātſiaame̱ nii; ani mei po ní oke̱ oklante ke̱ ogãi yaṅõame̱ nom le̱ otſiaä-ame̱ nii lo? *Nõ abolo ke̱ nu omãmo̱ ame̱hĩe, koni ame̱ye ni amenu, ni ameya ame̱nuṅtšo̱ ṅõ! *Abe̱i

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni efe niyenii babaō ehãame̱; ni beni ame̱ye nii ni ame̱nu le̱, edšie̱ame̱ gbe̱, ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te ame̱nuṅtšo̱ ṅõ. Ke̱-dše̱ no se̱ le̱ Aram odšoyeli tai le̱ baa Israel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ se̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱ Ben-Hadad, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱, bua eta le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱fã ke̱-ba, ni ame̱babo̱ nsra ame̱wo Samaria he.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Ni hõmo̱ kpeteṅkple ba Samaria. Ši na, ame̱bo̱ nsra ame̱wo ehe āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní ahõ tedši yitšo ahe dſie̱te̱i kukudši nyoṅmai-kpānyo̱, ni okpo fei kab mlidšāi edſe̱ mli ekome hū he dſie̱te̱i kukudši enumo̱.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Ni beni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ hoo̱ ye̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ le̱, yō ko blo̱ tšē̱le̱ ekē̱: Ye obuami, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱!

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Iehowa yee buaao le̱, nẽgbe̱ maye mabuao ke̱-dše̱? ke̱-dše̱ aboṅo ši, lo ke̱-dše̱ weinbu mli?

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni wo̱hō mibi le̱, ni wo̱yele̱; ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ mikē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ obi le̱ ohã ni wo̱yele̱! ši le̱ le̱ eṅõ ebi le̱ etē.

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni maṅtše̱ le̱ nu yō le̱ wiemo̱i le̱, egbla etadei le̱; ni beni ehoo̱ ye̱ gbogbo no̱ le̱, maṅ le̱ yakwe̱ le̱, na, ewo kpekpe ye̱ ehewolo no̱ ye̱ etadei le̱ ašiši.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši Eliša, Šafat bi le̱, yitšo aamã eno̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ fĩ, Nyoṅmo̱ afemi ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱!

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Ši Eliša tá ešīa le̱, ni onukpai le̱ ke̱le̱ trá ši. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũ nū ko ke̱-tšṍ ehĩe. Ši dãni bo̱fo le̱ aaše̱ Eliša ṅõ le̱, ekē̱ onukpai le̱ ake̱: Nto nyemīna ake̱ ne̱ke̱ awuyelo̱ bi ne̱ etšũ ake̱ abafo miyi? Nyekwe̱a, ke̱dši bo̱fo le̱ ba le̱, nyeṅã́a šĩnā le̱ ni nyeke̱ šĩnā le̱ atšire̱a-le̱! Ani dšee enuṅtšo̱ naneši gbē̱o̱ ke̱-baä ye̱ ese̱ ne̱?

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Ni beni eke̱ame̱ wieo̱ lolo le̱, na, bo̱fo le̱ baše̱ eṅõ. Ni ekē̱: Na, ne̱ke̱ efõṅ ne̱ *dše̱ Iehowa ṅõ! meni mimëo̱ Iehowa miheo̱ doṅṅ? *Amos

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱kē̱kē̱ ame̱he ake̱: Bo̱ni wo̱feo̱ ne̱ edšaa! Ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ sane kpakpa gbĩ ni; ši ke̱dši wo̱fe diṅṅ ni wo̱mẽ ke̱-yaši dšetše̱re lebi le̱, sõ ko aaye wo̱yi; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyebaã ni wo̱tea wo̱yakē̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱!

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ba ni ame̱batšē̱ maṅ le̱ agbókwe̱lo̱i le̱, ni ame̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Wo̱te Aram nsra le̱ṅ, ni na, mokomoko be̱ dše̱i, ni anuu gbomo ko gbē hũ, ake̱ dša okpo̱ṅo̱i ní afĩmo̱ame̱ aṅmlō ši, ke̱ tedšii ni afĩmo̱ame̱ aṅmlō ši, ke̱ būĩ le̱ hũ ta-mo̱ bo̱ni ame̱yo̱ le̱ noṅṅ.

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni agbókwe̱lo̱i le̱ blo̱ tšé̱, ni ayakē̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ te ši nyō le̱ṅ, ni ekē̱ otšũdši le̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ matšõnye noni Aram fewo̱ ne̱. Ame̱le ake̱ hõmo̱ mīyewo̱; nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱dše nsra le̱ṅ ame̱te ame̱yatētē ame̱he ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ake̱: Kē̱ ame̱dše kpo ke̱-dše̱ mã le̱ṅ ke̱-ba le̱, wo̱mõmo̱ame̱ hĩekãlo̱i, ni wo̱yabote mã le̱ṅ.

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ni etšũdši le̱ ateṅ mokome here no̱ ni ekē̱: Bĕle̱ hã ni aṅõ okpo̱ṅo̱i ní eſe̱ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ le̱ enumo̱ ko, koni wo̱tšũ ni ayakwe̱.

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱ṅõ ſīlii enyo̱ ke̱ ame̱-nā okpo̱ṅo̱i, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũame̱ ni ame̱tin Aram ta le̱, ni ekē̱: Nyeyaä ni nyeyakwe̱a!

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tiuame̱ ke̱-yaši Iordan nā; ni na, gbe̱ le̱ no̱ fẽ eyi to̱ ke̱ atadei ke̱ nibiinibii ni Arambii le̱ eše̱re̱ eſie ye̱ ame̱yaiyeli le̱ mli. Ni bo̱foi le̱ kũ ame̱se̱ ame̱ba, ni ame̱bagba maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ dše kpo te, ni ame̱yaha Aram nsra le̱. Ni ahō ṅmā̃ māmu sea kome ahe šekel kome, ke̱ able seai enyo̱ hũ šekel kome *ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā. *K.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ asafoiatše̱ le̱ ni ekpasaä enine le̱ eto agbó le̱ nā; ni maṅ le̱ nānā eno̱ ye̱ agbó le̱ nā ni egbo, take̱ bo̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ kē̱, beni maṅtše̱ le̱ kpleke ši ke̱-ba eṅõ le̱. K.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli bo̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Wó̱ aafe bene̱ yi-no̱ le̱ able seai enyo̱ bahe šekel kome, ni ṅmā̃ māmu sea kome hũ bahe šekel kome ye̱ Samaria agbó nā,

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: ni nakai asafoiatše̱ le̱ here Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ no̱ ake̱: Na, ke̱dši Iehowa aafe samfe̱dši ye̱ ṅwei po le̱, aso wiemo̱ ne̱ aaba mli lo? ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, bodientše̱ oona ke̱ ohĩṅme̱ii, ši oyeṅ eko le̱!

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Nakai noṅṅ eba mli hãle̱, edšake̱ maṅ le̱ nānā eno̱ ye̱ agbó le̱ nā, ni egbo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Gehazi, Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱ tšũlo̱ le̱, miwie ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Gbami nibii wudši fẽ ní Eliša efe le̱.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Ni Hazael kē̱: Mẽhewo̱ minuṅtšo̱ fóo̱? Ni ehere no̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ mile efõṅ ni *obafe Israelbii le̱: ame̱mãdši ni he wa le̱ obamãmo̱ nā la, ni ame̱blahĩĩ le̱ oke̱ klante bagbeame̱, ni ame̱bii fufo̱bii le̱ ooṅõame̱ otſĩa ši, ni ame̱yeiho̱lo̱i le̱ oogblagbla ame̱mli! *

english_verse: Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.”
translation_verse: Ni eyiṅ ke̱-dše̱ Eliša ṅõ ete, ni eba enuṅtšo̱ le̱ ṅõ; ni no bile̱ ake̱: Meni Eliša kē̱o? Ni ehere no̱ ake̱: Ekē̱mi ake̱: Ohe bawao!

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Eyino̱ le̱ Edom tše Iuda hīe atũa, ni ame̱dientše̱ ame̱wo maṅtše̱ ame̱bã ame̱he.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ Iehowa sumo̱o̱ ake̱ ekpãtã Iuda hĩe, ye̱ etšũlo̱ David hewo̱, take̱ bo̱ni *ewole̱ ši ake̱ eehã le̱ ke̱ ebii le̱ kane dāne̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ši Iehoram he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ni efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Ni Iehoram ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei amase̱i ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ni ebi Ahazia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. (

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Ioram, Ahab bi, ní dši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱ no̱ Ahazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoram bi le̱, baye maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: Ni enyie Ahab we le̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱, ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe tamo̱ Ahab we le̱ noṅṅ; edšake̱ Ahab we le̱ bii le̱ ašānŭ dšile̱.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ Ioram, Ahab bi le̱, yiṅ ame̱te ni ame̱ke̱ Hazael, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱, yawu ye̱ Ramot-Gilead; ši Arambii le̱ pila Ioram.

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni owó mũ ke̱ to̱ le̱ ni ofo̱se oſie eyiteṅ, ni oke ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: *Miwoö Israel no̱ maṅtše̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni ogble šĩnā le̱, ni odšo foi, ni okatše̱. *

english_verse: The young prophet left for Ramoth.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oblanyo le̱ ni dši gbalo̱ oblanyo le̱, yiṅ ete Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said. “For which one of us?” Jehu asked. “You, sir,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ dše̱i le̱, na, ta le̱ no̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ trá ši; ni ekē̱: Mihĩe sane ko mihahão, asafoiatše̱! Ni Iehu kē̱: Wo̱fẽ wo̱teṅ namo? Ni ekē̱: Bo, asafoiatše̱!

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ete šĩa le̱, ni efo̱se mũ le̱ eſie eyiteṅ, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Mifo̱o mũ miwoö Iehowa maṅ ní dši Israel le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehu dše kpo ba enuṅtšo̱ tšũdši le̱ aṅõ; ni moko bile̱ ake̱: Hedšo̱le̱ sane ni lo? Mẽhewo̱ ni ne̱ke̱ se̱ke̱yelo̱ ne̱ ba oṅõ ne̱? Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyedientše̱ nyele gbomo le̱ ke̱ bo̱ni ewiemo̱i yo̱.

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ebe̱ mli! gbawo̱ moṅ! Ni ekē̱: Ne̱ke̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ ekē̱mi ake̱. Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Mifo̱o mũ miwoö Israel no̱ maṅtše̱!

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱he fe oyá, ni *ame̱teṅ mofẽmo dšie etade ni eṅõ-ha ši ehãle̱ ye̱ atrakpoi le̱ no̱, ni ame̱kpãkpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i ame̱kē̱: Iehu eye maṅtše̱! *Mat.

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Ni bulo̱ le̱ damo̱ mō̃ le̱ yiteṅ ye̱ Iezreel, ni ena Iehu asafoku le̱, beni ebaä le̱, ni ekē̱: Mīna asafoku ko! Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioram kē̱: Tšē̱ okpo̱ṅo̱no̱tálo̱ ko ni otšũle̱ ni eke̱ame̱ ayakpe, ni ebi ake̱: Hedšo̱le̱ sane ni lo?

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehu ko̱ egãi ni eṅõ-tšẽ Ioram kõdši ateṅ, ni gãimlibi le̱ tšṍ etsui mli ke̱-dše kpo, ni egbē eſīli le̱ mli.

english_verse: Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
translation_verse: Iehowa kē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ nyè le̱ mina Nabot lá le̱ ke̱ ebii le̱ alái, ni mawoö he nyõmo̱ ye̱ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ṅe̱ no̱ noṅṅ, Iehowa kei No̱hewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ wóle̱ ofõ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ ye̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ nā!

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.
translation_verse: Ši *beni Ahazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, na ene̱ le̱, edšo foi ke̱-tšṍ trom le̱ mli tšũ le̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱. Ni Iehu tiule̱ ni ekē̱: Le̱ hũ nyetſiaäle̱ nii ye̱ eſīli le̱ṅ! Ni ame̱tſiale̱ nii ye̱ Gur ṅmeṅme le̱ ní yo̱ Ibleam mase̱i le̱ he. Ni edšo foi ke̱-te Megido ni eyagbo ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni etšũdši le̱ *ke̱le̱ wo ſīli mli ni ame̱ke̱le̱ ha Ierusalem, ni ame̱bafũle̱ ye̱ efũhe le̱ ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ. *

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Ši Ahab bi Ioram yino̱ afi ni dši nyoṅma ke̱ ekome le̱ no̱ Ahazia babõi maṅtše̱yeli ye̱ Iuda no̱.

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Ni Iehu ba Iezreel. Ni beni Izebel nu le̱, ekpa ehĩṅme̱ii ase̱ tšofã, ni eho̱ eyi fe̱fe̱o, ni eyabu samfle̱ nā ēkwe̱.

english_verse: As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
translation_verse: Ni beni Iehu ba agbó le̱ nā le̱, no kē̱: *Ani Zimri ni gbe enuṅtšo̱ le̱ ná hedšo̱le̱ lo? *

english_verse: He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window,
translation_verse: Ni ewó ehĩe no̱ ekwe̱ samfle̱ le̱ nā ni ekē̱: Namo yo̱ migbe̱fãṅ, namo? Ni piafoi enyo̱ lo etẽ gbo ame̱yi nā kpo ame̱kwe̱le̱.

english_verse: and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nyetšiale̱ nyegbẽa ši! Ke̱-ke̱ ni ame̱tšile̱ ame̱gbē ši, ni elá le̱ eko tšẽṅe ſie gbogbo le̱ he ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i le̱ ahe, ni ame̱nānā eno̱.

english_verse: Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
translation_verse: Ni beni ete šĩa le̱ ni eyaye nii ni enu noko le̱, ekē̱: Nyeyaä nyeyakwe̱a ne̱ke̱ yō musumo ne̱, ni nyefũale̱; edšake̱ maṅtše̱ biyō ni.

english_verse: But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱tele̱ fũ; ši ame̱naa ehe nokonoko, ake̱ dša eyitšoṅoṅo ke̱ enãdši ke̱ enine ko̱ko̱i ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ame̱bakē̱le̱. Ni ekē̱: Iehowa *wieme̱ ni etšṍ etšũlo̱ Elia, Tišbinyo le̱, no̱ ewie le̱ ne̱, ēkē̱: Iezreel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ ni gbēí baye Izebel lō ye̱, *K.

english_verse: And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_verse: ni Izebel gbonyo batšṍ tamo̱ tumuno̱ noko ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iezreel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni akē̱ṅ ake̱: Izebel ne̱!

english_verse: The officials and leaders read the letters and were very frightened. They said to each other, “Jehu has already killed King Joram and King Ahaziah! We have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ši ame̱še gbeyei naakpa dientše̱, ni ame̱kē̱: Na, maṅtše̱mei enyo̱ le̱ po nyẽẽ ehĩe adamo̱, té wo̱o̱fe tẽṅ ni wo̱o̱nyẽ ši wo̱damo̱ṅ?

english_verse: The prime minister, the mayor of the city, as well as the other leaders and Ahab's supporters, sent this answer to Jehu, “We are your servants, Your Majesty, and we will do whatever you tell us. But it's not our place to choose someone to be king. You do what you think is best.”
translation_verse: Ni moni kwe̱o̱ šĩa le̱ ke̱ moni kwe̱o̱ maṅ le̱, ke̱ onukpai le̱ ke̱ biiatšo̱selo̱i le̱ hũ tšũ Iehu ṅõ ake̱: Otšũdši dšiwo̱, ni nofẽno ni ookē̱wo̱ le̱ wo̱o̱fe; wo̱ woo mokomoko maṅtše̱; femo̱ noni hĩ ye̱-ohĩe ke̱ke̱!

english_verse: The next morning, Jehu went out and stood where everyone could hear him, and he said, “You people are not guilty of anything. I'm the one who plotted against Joram and had him killed. But who killed all these men?
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ lebi le̱ edše kpo ebadamo̱ ši ni ekē̱ maṅ mũ le̱ fẽ ake̱: Dšalo̱i dšinye pe̱! Na, mi mite minuṅtšo̱ yi no̱ apãm, ni migbele̱; ši namo gbegbē mene̱mei fë ne̱?

english_verse: Listen to me. Everything the Lord's servant Elijah promised about Ahab's family will come true.”
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nyenáa nyelea ake̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ ni ewie ye̱ *Ahab we le̱ hewo̱ le̱ emli ekomeflo efeṅ yaka; edšake̱ Iehowa efe noni etšṍ etšũlo̱ Elia no̱ ewie le̱ *

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nyemõme̱aame̱ hĩekãlo̱i! Ni ame̱mõmo̱ame̱ hĩekãlo̱i, ni ame̱gbe-ame̱ ye̱ tōhetšo̱ikū tšũ le̱ bu le̱ he, hĩĩ nyoṅmai-edſe̱ ke̱ enyo̱, ni eſe̱e̱ ame̱teṅ mokomoko.

english_verse: As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?” “Yes, I am.” “Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot
translation_verse: Ni beni edše dše̱i eṅõ-ſie no̱ le̱, ena *Iehonadab, Rekab bi le̱, ní ēba eke̱le̱ abakpe; ni eṅãle̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake: Ani otšui dša, take̱ bo̱ni mitšui ke̱ otšui yo̱ le̱? Ni Iehonadab kē̱: Edša! — Ni ke̱dši edša le̱, ta midẽ! Ni eta edẽ; ni eṅõle̱ ke̱-ba eṅõ ye̱ ſīli le̱ mli. *Ier.

english_verse: to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah. Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ Samaria le̱, egbe Ahab mei fẽ ni eſe̱ ye̱ Samaria le̱ ke̱-yaši be-yino̱ ni ekpãtã ehĩe kwrā, tamo̱ boni *Iehowa kē̱ Elia le̱. *

english_verse: I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed. But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeyakpẽa Baal gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ edšálo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ eso̱foi le̱ fẽ nyebahãami, akaſe̱ mokomoko; edšake̱ miye̱ afo̱le wulu ko ní mibašã mahã Baal; mofēmo ni baa le̱ eyi náṅ wala! Ši ṅā Iehu tšõ̀o̱, beni afe ni ekpãtã Baal dšálo̱i le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced,
translation_verse: Ni Iehu kē̱: Nyetoa gbĩdšũrõ wulu ko nyehāa Baal!

english_verse: Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other.
translation_verse: Ni Iehu tšũ ate ayakpa Israel fẽ; ni Baal dšálo̱i le̱ fẽ ba, ni eſe̱e̱ mokomoko ni baa. Ni ame̱ba Baal we le̱, ni Baal we le̱ yi to̱ ke̱-dše̱ nāgbēhe kome ke̱-yaši nāgbēhe kroko le̱.

english_verse: Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ moni kwe̱o̱ atadei atšũ le̱ ake̱: Yadšie atadei ohã Baal dšálo̱i le̱ fẽ! Ni eyadšie atadei ebahãame̱.

english_verse: Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehu ke̱ *Iehonadab, Rekab bi le̱, te Baal we le̱, ni ekē̱ Baal dšálo̱i le̱ ake̱: Nyetaoa ni nyekwe̱a ni Iehowa dšálo̱i le̱ ateṅ mokomoko akabafutunye ye̱ bie̱, ake̱ dša Baal dšálo̱i le̱ ke̱ke̱. *K.

english_verse: As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ešã šã-afo̱le le̱ egbe nā le̱, Iehu kē̱ bulo̱i le̱ ke̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ake̱: Nyeyaã ni *nyeyagbeaame̱, nyekahãa mokomoko midšea kpo! Ni amo̱gbeame̱ ke̱ klante; ni bulo̱i le̱ ke̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ še̱re̱ame̱ ſie, ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te Baal we le̱ afãbaṅ le̱ mli; *
