translation_verse: Ši Amazia boo toi. Ke̱ke̱ ni Ioaš, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-ba eke̱ Amazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, bakwe̱kwē̱ ame̱hĩeaṅ ye̱ Bet-Šemeš ní dši Iuda nõ le̱.

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni elō šika ke̱ dſie̱te̱i fẽ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní ana ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ nitōhei le̱, ke̱ ta awabai hũ, ni eke̱-kũ ese̱ ke̱-te Samaria.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Ni Iuda maṅ mũ le̱ fẽ ṅõ Azaria ni eye afii nyoṅma ke̱ ekpa le̱, ni ame̱wole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ etše̱ Amazia se̱.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Le̱ etſa gbogbo ewo *Elat he, ni eke̱-kũ se̱ ehā Iuda ekoṅ, beni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ eyawo̱ se̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Iuda maṅtše̱ Amazia, Ioaš bi le̱, yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enumo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ *Ierobeam, Israel maṅtše̱ Ioaš bi le̱, bõi maṅtše̱yeli ye̱ Samaria, ni eye maṅtše̱ afii nyoṅmaĩ-edſe̱ ke̱ ekome. *K.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa na Israel amanehũlũ le̱ ake emli wa naakpa, ni moni aṅá eyi ke̱ moni ašĩle̱ tete be̱, ni bualo̱ ko be̱ hã Israel.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa ekē̱ko ake̱ eegbe Israel gbei ke̱-adše̱ ṅwei šiši, nohewo̱ le̱ etšṍ Ierobeam, Ioaš bi le̱, nine no̱ *ehere ame̱-yiwala. *

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ierobeam he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní efe ke̱ ekã ní efe ke̱ bo̱ni ewuwū tai ke̱ bo̱ni ešõ Damasko ke̱ Hamat ni dši Iuda nii le̱ ehã Israel le̱, ani aṅmāko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Iuda maṅtše̱ Azaria yino̱ afi ni dši nyoṅmai-enumo̱ le̱ no̱ Pekahia, Menahem bi le̱, bōi Israel no̱ maṅtše̱yeli, ni eye maṅtše̱ afii enyo̱ ye̱ Samaria.

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Iuda maṅtše̱ Azaria yino̱ afi ni dši nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ kpānyo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ Zakaria, Ierobeam bi le̱, baye Israel ne̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Samaria nyõdši ekpa.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Ene̱ dši Iehowa wiemo̱ ní *ekē̱ Iehu ake̱: Obii le̱ aatrá Israel sẽi le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši yino̱ ní dši edſe̱ no̱. Ni eba mli nakai. *

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ekpalee ke̱-dšee Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, he ešai ni eke̱-hã Israel fe esa le̱ ahe ye̱ ewala be fẽ. K.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Pul, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, batua šikpoṅ le̱; ni Menahem hā Pul dſie̱te̱i talentai akpe, koni efĩ ese̱ nĩ ehã emaṅtše̱yeli le̱ adamo̱.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Ni efe noni dša ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; bo̱ni etše̱ *Uzia fe le̱, nakai pe̱pē̱pe̱ efe. *

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Menahem he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Ni Menahem ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱; ni ebi Pekahia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ekpalee ke̱-dšee Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, he ešai ni eke̱-hã Israel fe eša le̱ ahe. K.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe; ekpalee ke̱-dšee Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, he ešai ni eke̱-hã Israel fe eša le̱ ahe. K.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Peka, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, yino̱ le̱ Tiglat-Pileser, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, ba ni ebaṅõ Iyon ke̱ Abel-Bet-Maaka ke̱ Ianoa ke̱ Kedeš ke̱ Hazor ke̱ Gilead fẽ, ke̱ Galilea ní dši Naftali šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ, ni eṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te Ašur.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni *Hošea, Ela bi le̱, †te Peka, Remalia bi le̱, yi no̱ apãm, ni etſale̱ nõ ni egbele̱, ni ebaye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱ ye̱ Iotam, Uzia bi le̱, yino̱ afi ni dši nyoṅmai-enyo̱ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Ni Peka he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní efe le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli. (

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Israel maṅtše̱ Peka, Remalia bi le̱, yino̱ afi ní dši enyo̱ le̱ no̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Uzia bi *Iotam baye maṅtše̱ le̱. *K.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ši adšiee hei groṅṅi le̱; maṅ le̱ mīšã afo̱lei ke̱ tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai ye̱ hei groṅṅi le̱ lolo. Le̱ etſa Iehowa we le̱ agbó ni kwo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ši Iotam he sãdši ni eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ni efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli Iehowa bõi *Rezin, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ Peka, Remalia bi le̱, tšũmo̱ ke̱ Iuda no̱ ſiemo̱. *

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Ni Iotam ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ etše̱ David mã le̱ṅ. Ni ebi Ahaz baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Ni Ahaz ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱, ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ. Ni ebi *Hezekia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. *

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Uria fe bo̱ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz wole̱ kitã le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ní ešãšã afo̱lei ke̱ tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai ye̱ hei groṅṅi le̱ ke̱ goṅkpo̱i le̱ ane̱ ke̱ tšo-fẽ-tšo ní ebu kusū šiši.

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Ni Ahaz *ṅõ dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika ní ana ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ nitōhei le̱, ni etšũ ni ake̱-yake Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱. *

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ bole̱ toi, ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ fã yatua Damasko ni eṅõle̱, ni eṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te Kir, ni egbe Rezin.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz yiṅ ke̱-te Damasko ni eke̱ Tiglat-Pileser, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, yakpe. Ni eyana afo̱lešãlate̱ ni yo̱ Damasko le̱; ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz ṅõ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ su ke̱ eheno̱ bo̱ni atšṍ afele̱ ahã le̱ fẽ emãdše oso̱fo Uria le̱.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱ſo Uria mã afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱; bo̱ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz ke̱-mãdšele̱ ke̱-dše̱ Damasko le̱, nakai pe̱pē̱pe̱ oso̱fo Uria fe eto be ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz aadše̱ Damasko aba le̱.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅtše̱ le̱ dše̱ Damasko eba le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ bana afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱; ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱, ni ešã afo̱le ye̱ no̱.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: Ni ešã ešã-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ eniyenii-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱ no̱, ni efo̱se edā̃-afolei le̱ eſie no̱, ni eṅõ ešidā-afo̱lei le̱ alá le̱ eſã afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ni akō̱ble afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ní mã Iehowa hĩe le̱, etši ke̱-dše̱ šĩa le̱ hĩegbe̱, ye̱ efo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehowa we le̱ teṅ, ke̱-hamã efo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ kõyigbe̱.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz wo oso̱fo Uria kitã ake̱: Afo̱lešãlate̱ wulu le̱ ne̱ ošã lebi šã-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ gbe̱ke̱ niyenii-afo̱le le̱, ke̱ maṅtše̱ šã-afo̱le ke̱ eniyenii-afo̱le le̱, ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ ašã-afo̱lei ke̱ ameniyenii-afo̱lei ke̱ ame̱dā̃-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱, ni oṅõ šā̃-afo̱lei le̱ alá le̱ ke̱ afo̱lei krokomei le̱ alá le̱ fẽ oſä no̱. Ši akō̱ble afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ahĩ ši ní masusu he.

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Ahaz flo̱ šiši-adekai le̱ adāmo̱nii le̱ ni edšie botokui le̱ ke̱-dše̱ no̱; ni ewó ṅšo̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ akō̱ble tšinai ni yo̱ šiši le̱ ano̱ ni eṅã-mã te̱i ni aṅõ-ka šikpoṅ le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Ahaz he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ní efe le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli nakai, edšake̱ Israelbii le̱ efe eša eši Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni dsieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ke̱-dše̱ Farao, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, deṅ le̱, ni ame̱yaše nyoṅmo̱i krokomei agbeyei,

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ to ame̱yiṅ ame̱fe nibii ní edšaa gbe̱ ame̱ši Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni ame̱mãmo̱ hei groṅṅi ame̱-hã ame̱he ye̱ ame̱mãdšimãdši le̱ fẽ mli ke̱-dše̱ bulo̱i amō̃ ní kwo̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši maṅ ni atſa gbogbo awo he le̱ no̱.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱mãmo̱ amãgãi ni ame̱fe wo̱ṅkōi ye̱ goṅkpo̱-fẽ-goṅkpo̱ ní kwo̱ no̱ ke̱ *tšo-fẽ-tšo ni ebu kusū šiši. *

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Ni dše̱i ame̱šãšã tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai ye̱, ye̱ hei groṅṅi le̱ fẽ, tamo̱ bo̱ni *dšeṅmãdšĩ ni Iehowa lōame̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱hĩe le̱ fe le̱; ni ame̱fe nibii fõdši nĩ ame̱ke̱wo Iehowa mlila. K.

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Tše̱ Iehowa tšṍ gbalo̱-fẽ-gbalo̱ ke̱ ninalo̱-fẽ̱-ninalo̱ no̱ eye odase etšṍ Israel ke̱ Iuda fẽ ake̱: Nyekpalea ke̱-dše̱a nyegbè̱i fõdši le̱ ano̱, ni nyeyea mikitãi le̱ ke̱ mikpo̱i le̱ ano̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni mla ni miwo nyetše̱mei le̱ fẽ ni mitšũ mitšũdši gbalo̱i le̱ ke̱-bahãnye le̱ yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ ame̱boo toi, šĩ ame̱fe ame̱he kue̱ṅtilo̱i tamo̱ ame̱tše̱mei ní hee Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ame̱yee le̱.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kwa ekpo̱i le̱ ke̱ ekpãṅmo̱ ní eke̱ ame̱tše̱mei le̱ kpãṅ le̱ ke̱ edasei ni eye etšõame̱ le̱, ni ame̱yanyie yakayakanii ase̱ ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ yakagbomei, ni ame̱nyie dseṅmãdši ni ebo̱leame̱ ke̱-kpe ni Iehowa *woame̱ kitã ye̱ ame̱he ake̱ ame̱kafe ame̱nĩi tamo̱ame̱ le̱ ase̱. *

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Iehowa mli fũ Israel naakpa, ni edšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ ehĩe; eſe̱e̱ mokomoko ake̱ dša Iuda aku tšo le̱ kome ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ etše *Israel ke̱-dše̱ David we le̱ he, ni ame̱wo Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, maṅtše̱, ni Ierobeam hã Israel kpale ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa se̱ ni ehã ame̱fe eša kpeteṅkple. *

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ yaṅõ mei ke̱-dše̱ Babel ke̱ Kuta ke̱ Ava ke̱ Hamat ke̱ Sefarvaim ke̱-ba, ni eke̱ame̱ bato Samaria mãdši le̱ amli ye̱ Israelbii le̱ anãdšiaṅ; ni ame̱ṅõ Samaria ame̱fe ame̱nō ni ame̱hĩ emãdši le̱ amli.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱bahĩ dše̱i kleṅkleṅ le̱, ame̱šee Iehowa gbeyei; no-hewo̱ le̱ Iehowa tšũo̱ dšatai ke̱-baã ame̱teṅ, ni ame̱gbegbēo̱ ame̱teṅ meikomei.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱yakē̱ Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Dšeṅmãdši le̱ ní oyalō obato Samaria mādši le̱ amli le̱ lee šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbe̱nanii; nohewo̱ le̱ etšũo̱ dšatai ke̱-baã ame̱teṅ, ni na, ame̱bagbegbēo̱ame̱, edšake̱ ame̱lee šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbe̱nānii.

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ fã́ ake̱: Nyehãa oso̱foi ní nyeyaṅõame̱ nom ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i ke̱-ba le̱ ateṅ mokome ayaä, ni ame̱-yahĩ dše̱i, koni etšõame̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbe̱nānii.

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱foi ni ame̱yaṅõame̱ nom ke̱-dše̱ Samaria ke̱-te le̱ ateṅ mokome ba ni ebahĩ Betel, ni etšõo̱ame̱ bo̱ni ame̱fe ame̱še Iehowa gbeyei.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ dšeṅmaṅ-fẽ-dšeṅmaṅ no̱ bii fe ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nyoṅmo̱i, ni ame̱ṅõame̱ ame̱totõ šĩai ni Samariabii le̱ efefē ye̱ hei groṅṅi le̱, maṅ-fẽ-maṅ no̱ bii ye̱ ame̱mãdši ni ame̱yo̱ mli le̱ amli.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Ni Babelbii le̱ fe Sukot-Benot, ni Kutbii le̱ fe Nergal, ni Hamatbii le̱ fe Ašima,

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: ni Avabii le̱ fe Nibhaz ke̱ Tartak, ni Sefarvaimbiĩ le̱ *šãšãa ame̱bii ye̱ la mli ame̱hãa Adramelek ke̱ Anamelek, Sefarvaimbiĩ anyoṅmo̱i le̱. *K.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Ame̱šeo̱ Iehowa gbeyei, ni asaṅ ame̱dšáa ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ hũ, take̱ bo̱ni dšeṅmãdši heni ayalōame̱ ke̱-dše̱ le̱ agbe̱nā yo̱ le̱.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: mei ni Iehowa ke̱ame̱ kpãṅ ni ewoame̱ kitã ake̱: *Nyekašea nyoṅmo̱i krokomei agbeyei ni nyekadšáa-ame̱, ni nyekasúmo̱a-ame̱ ni nyekašãa afo̱le nyehāa-ame̱ le̱; *

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ši moṅ Iehowa moni yadšienye ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba ke̱ he-wale̱ kpeteṅkple ke̱ nine ní akpā mli le̱, le̱ gbeyei nyešea, ni le̱ nyedšáa ni le̱ noṅṅ nyešãa afo̱le nyehãa!

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Ni kpãṅmo̱ ní mike̱nye kpãṅ le̱ nyehĩe akakpaä no̱, ni asaṅ nyekašea nyoṅmo̱i krokomei agbeyei;

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: ši moṅ Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbeyei nyešea, koni le̱ noṅṅ edšienye ke̱-dše̱ nyehenye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ adeṅ!

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱boo toi, ši ame̱sá gbe̱nãnii le̱ noṅṅ ame̱feo̱.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Nakai dšeṅmãdši ne̱ šeo̱ Iehowa gbeyei, ni ame̱sā ame̱súmoo̱ ame̱mãgãi le̱ hũ; ame̱bii ke̱ ame̱bii abii hũ, bo̱ni ame̱tše̱mei le̱ fe le̱, nakai ame̱ hũ ame̱-feo̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱.

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ne̱: Nyekahãa Hezekia mīlakaänye; edšake̱ enyẽṅnye edšie ye̱ mideṅ.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Nyekaboa Hezekia toi! Edšake̱ bo̱ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ne̱: Nyeke̱mi abakpãtãa ni nyedšea kpo nyebaä miṅõ, koni nyeteṅ mofẽmo aye *eweintšo ke̱ egbãmitšo yibii, ni nyeteṅ mofẽmo anu enubu mli nu, *

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Ši ani Iehowa se̱ midše mifã mibatua bie̱, ní mibakpãtã ehīe ne̱? Iehowa moṅ kē̱mi ake̱: Fã ni oyatua šikpoṅ le̱ ni okpãtã ehĩe!

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: *Le̱ edšie †hei groṅṅi le̱, ni ekũmo̱ amãgãi le̱, ni egbá wo̱ṅ-kõi le̱, ni edſăra akō̱ble onũfũ ní **Mose fe le̱; edšake̱ ke̱-bašĩ nakai gbĩĩ le̱ ano̱ le̱ Israelbii le̱ šãa tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ame̱hãale̱, ni atšé̱ole̱ Nehuštan. *

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Le̱ noṅṅ etſia Filistibii le̱ anii ke̱-yaſie Gaza ke̱ ekpokpai le̱ ano̱ tō̃, ke̱-dše̱ bulo̱i amō̃ ní kwo̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši maṅ ni atſa gbogbo awo he le̱ no̱.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Hezekia yino̱ afi ní dši edſe̱ ni dši Israel maṅtše̱ Hošea, Ela bi le̱, yino̱ afi ni dši kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱, eba mli ake̱ Šalmaneser, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, fã batua Samaria ni ebo̱ nsra ewo he.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni maba ni mabalōnye ke̱-ya šikpoṅ ní tamo̱ nyedientše̱ nyešikpoṅ le̱ no̱, able ke̱ wein šikpoṅ, abolo ke̱ weintromi ašikpoṅ, mũtšei ke̱ wò šikpoṅ no̱, ní nyeyi aná wala ni nyekagboi. Ni nyekaboa Hezekia toi, ké̱ ēlakanye ake̱: Iehowa bahere wo̱yiwala le̱!

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Ni Rabšake kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nyeyakē̱a Hezekia ake̱: Bo̱ni maṅtše̱ kpeteṅkple le̱ ní dši Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ ne̱: Meni no̱ po ohĩe kã ne̱?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeakē̱mi ake̱: Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱ moṅ wo̱hĩe kã le̱! ani dšee le̱ ehei groṅṅi ke̱ efo̱lešãlate̱i Hezekia dšie ni ekē̱ Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem ake̱: *Ne̱ke̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ ne̱ hĩe nyedšáa ye̱ ye̱ Ierusalem le̱? *

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Hezekia yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ Sanherib, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, fã batua Iuda mãdši ni atſa gbogboi awo be le̱ fẽ ni eṅõame̱.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hezekia ṅõ dſie̱te̱i fẽ ní ana ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ nitōhei le̱ ehã.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Hezekia kplo̱ Iehowa we le̱ šĩnāi ke̱ šĩnātšei le̱ ahe šika ni le̱ Hezekia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, dientše̱ eṅõ-ha he le̱, ni eṅõ-hã Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũ Tartan ke̱ Rabsaris ke̱ Rabšake ke̱-dše̱ Lakiš ke̱-ba maṅtše̱ Hezekia ṅõ ní ame̱ke̱ ta babaō ba Ierusalem. Ni ame̱fã ke̱-ba Ierusalem; ni beni ame̱še̱ le̱, ame̱bada-mo̱ ṅweigbe̱ kpākpo le̱ nudšō̱ le̱ mase̱i, ye̱ niiahefo̱lo̱i abō̱ le̱ tempõṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱tšé̱ maṅtše̱ le̱, Eliakim, Hilkia bi ní kwe̱o̱ maṅtše̱ šĩa le̱, ke̱ Šebna, woloṅmãlo̱ le̱, ke̱ Ioa, Asaf bi ni dši sãdšiaṅmãlo̱ le̱, dše kpo te ame̱ṅõ.

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ na, ohĩe kã ne̱ke̱ gãlã ni amĩa ní dši Mizraim ne̱ no̱, noni ke̱dši moko kpasa ni egbuo̱ edẽ ke̱-dšeo̱ kpo le̱. Nakai Farao, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, feo̱ mei fẽ ní ṅõo̱ ame̱hĩe ame̱fōo̱ eno̱ lo̱.

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ oke̱ minuṅtšo̱, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, ata abasa ko, ni madšie okpo̱ṅo̱i akpei-enyo̱ mahão, ake̱ ooná bodientše̱ omei otrá ameno̱ lo.

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Ni tá ooſe tẽṅ ni oonyi ohã minuṅtšo̱ tšũdši bibii le̱ ateṅ asafoiatše̱ kome atšṍ ese̱ ahão hũ? Ni ohĩe kã Mizraim no̱ ye̱ ſīlii ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei ahewo̱, be̱?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Eliakim, Hilkia bi le̱, ke̱ Šebna ke̱ Ioa kē̱ Rabšake ake̱: Ofai ne̱, oke̱ otšũdši awie Aram wiemo̱; edšake̱ wo̱nuo̱; ši oke̱wo̱ akawie Iuda wiemo̱ yo̱ maṅ ni dſere gbogbo le̱ no̱ lo̱ atoiiaṅ.

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Ši Rabšake kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ani onuṅtšo̱ ṅõ alo bo oṅõ minuṅtšo̱ tšũmi ake̱ mibawie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱? ani dšee hĩĩ le̱ ní trá gbogbo le̱ no̱ le̱ aṅõ etšūmi, koni ame̱ke̱nye fẽ aye ame̱dientše̱ ame̱wamo̱ ni ame̱nu ame̱dientše̱ ame̱šãme̱?

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Rabšake ho damo̱ šĩ ni ebo ke̱ gbē wāle̱ ye̱ Iuda wiemo̱ le̱ mli ni ekē̱: Nyeboa maṅtše̱ kpeteṅkple le̱ ní dši Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ gbē toi!

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ nyekahãa Hezekia mīhã nyeke̱ nyehĩe mīfō Iehowa no̱ ake̱: Iehowa bahere wo̱yiwala kẽ, ni atuṅ maṅ ne̱ awoṅ Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ deṅ!

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ani *dšeṅmãdši le̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ eko ehere ešikpoṅ yiwala ke̱-dše̱ Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ deṅ pẽṅ? Ies.

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Nẽgbe̱ Hamat ke̱ Arpad nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ye̱? Nẽgbe̱ Sefarvaim, Hena ke̱ Iva nyoṅmo̱i le̱ yo̱? ani ame̱here Samaria yiwala ke̱-dše̱ mideṅ?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Šikpõdši le̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ fẽ ateṅ namei ehere ame̱sikpoṅ yiwala ke̱-dše̱ mideṅ, hewo̱ ni Iehowa le̱, le̱ le̱ eehere Ierusalem yiwala ke̱-adše̱ mideṅ le̱?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Eliakim, Hilkia bi le̱, ní kwe̱o̱ maṅtše̱ šĩa le̱, ke̱ Šebna, woloṅmãlo̱ le̱, ke̱ Ioa, Asaf bi le̱, ní dši sãdšĩaṅmãlo̱ le̱, ba Hezekia ṅõ ke̱ ame̱tadei ní ame̱-gbla, ni ame̱bagbale̱ Rabšake wiemo̱i le̱.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni edšáa ye̱ e-nyoṅmo̱ Nisrok we le̱, Adramelek ke̱ Šarezer ní dši ebii le̱ *gbele̱ ke̱ klante, ni ame̱dšo foi ke̱-te Ararat šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; ni ebi Esar-Hadon baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. K.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Nẽgbe̱ Hamat maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Arpad maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Sefarvaim maṅ le̱ ke̱ Hena ke̱ Iva maṅtše̱ le̱ yo̱?

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yakē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Hezekia kē̱ ne̱: Haomo̱ ke̱ dše̱mo̱ ke̱ heguo̱gbē gbĩ dši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱; edšake̱ bii le̱ eše̱ asosodſā he, ši hewale̱ be̱ ní ake̱-fo̱ö̱.

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Hezekia tšũdši le̱ ba Iesaia ṅõ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Rabšake kū ese̱, ni eyanina Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱ ni eke̱ Libna mīwu; edšake̱ enu ake eſã ke̱-dše̱ Lakiš ke̱-te.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Na, bodientše̱ onu nii ni Ašur maṅtše̱mei le̱ fe šikpõdši le̱ fẽ ni ame̱feame̱ musu le̱, ni bo ni abahere oyiwala lo?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: *Dšeṅmãdši le̱ ni mitše̱mei le̱ kpãtã ame̱hĩe le̱, ani ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ here ame̱yiwala lo? tamo̱ Gozan ke̱ Haran ke̱ Rezef ke̱ Edenbii le̱ ni yo̱ Telasar le̱? *

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Ni beni Hezekia he wodši le̱ ye̱ bo̱foi le̱ adeṅ ni ekane le̱, eyiṅ ke̱-te Iehowa we le̱, ni Hezekia yagble mli efõ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: Ni Hezekia kpa fai ye̱ Iehowa hīe ni ekē̱: Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱, *bo ní ohĩo̱ kerubim ano̱, bo okometō dši Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱yelii le̱ fẽ no̱; bo ofe ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ! *

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Iehowa, eye̱ mli le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ Ašur maṅtše̱mei le̱ efite dšeṅmãdšimãdši le̱ ke̱ ame̱šikpõdši le̱ hũ,

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: ni ame̱še̱re̱ ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ame̱ſie la mli; edšake̱ dšee nyoṅmo̱i dšiame̱, ši moṅ gbomei anidši ana nitšumo̱ ni, tšei ke̱ te̱i ni, nohewo̱ ni ame̱fiteame̱ le̱,

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱, Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱, mīkpao fai, heremo̱ wo̱yiwala ke̱-dše̱ edeṅ, koni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱yelii fẽ aná ale ake̱ bo Iehowa okometō dši Nyoṅmo̱!

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Wiemo̱ ni Iehowa wie ye̱ ehe ne̱: Zion biyō oblayō fro le̱ mīgbe ohe guo̱, ni ēye ohe fe̱o, Ierusalem biyō le̱ mīhoso eyitšo ye̱ ose̱.

english_verse: That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ noṅṅ le̱ Iehowa bo̱fo le̱ dše kpo te ni eyagbe Ašur nsra le̱ṅ mei akpei-oha-ke̱-nyoṅmai-kpānyo̱-ke̱-enumo̱; ni beni ame̱-te ši lebi mãṅkpa le̱, na, ame̱fẽ-tſẽm ame̱tšṍmo̱ gbohĩĩ so̱ṅṅ.

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Namo ahora obo̱ ni owie musubō̱-wiemo̱i ošile̱ le̱? namo no̱ owó ogbē no̱ ye̱ ni ohole ohĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ke̱-te ṅwei ye̱ le̱? Israel mokroṅkroṅ le̱ ni!

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.

translation_verse: Ake̱-ni ogri owomi nĩ oſã le̱ ekwo̱ ke̱-baše̱ mitoiiaṅ hewo̱ le̱, mike̱ mikpoṅ aawo ogugõṅ, ni mike̱ mimanyofle̱ aawo odāṅ, ni makpaleo ke̱-kũ se̱ ke̱-tšṍ gbe̱ ni otšṍ no̱ ke̱-ba le̱ no̱!

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ aafe okadi ahão: Afi ne̱ mli le̱ nyeaye nii ni ame̱dientše̱ ame̱kwẽ, ni afi ni dši enyo̱ le̱ mli hũ nyeaye nii ni kwẽ ye̱ nomei ase̱ le̱; ši afi ni dši etẽ le̱ mli le̱ nyedũa nii ni nye-kpaä, ni nyefea weintromi hũ ni nyeyea emli yibii.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.

translation_verse: Edšake̱ *mabu ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ he, ni mahere eyiwala ye̱ midientše̱ mihewo̱ ke̱ mitšũlo̱ David hũ hewo̱! *

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: Kũ ose̱ ni oyakē̱ Hezekia, mimaṅ le̱ no̱ lumo̱ le̱, ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, otše̱ David Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Minn ofai-kpamo̱ le̱, ni mina ohĩeyāfónui le̱ hũ. Na, mibatšáo; ni bie̱ gbĩĩ etẽ le̱ oonyie ke̱-ate Iehowa we le̱.

english_verse: “What did you show them?” Isaiah asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Meni ame̱na ye̱ owe le̱? Ni Hezekia kē̱: Nibii fẽ ni yo̱ miwe le̱ ame̱na; nokonoko be̱ minitōhei le̱ ni mike̱-tšõkoame̱.

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Ni Iesaia kē̱ ake̱: Nyebahãami agbãmi-tatale! Ni ame̱ke̱-ba ni ame̱ke̱-bato asane le̱ no̱, ni ehe wale̱.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Ni Iesaia kē̱: Ene̱ aafe okadi ní dše̱ Iehowa deṅ ahão ake̱ Iehowa bafe nii ní ekē̱ le̱: Ani hũlũ ṅmle̱ le̱ no̱ susuma le̱ aya hĩegbe̱ mlidšãi nyoṅma alo ekũ ese̱ mlidšāi nyoṅma?

translation_verse: Ni Hezekia kē̱: Ewaa haã susuma le̱ ake̱ eete hĩegbe̱ mlidšāi nyoṅma; dabi, ši moṅ hã ní susuma le̱ akũ ese̱ mlidšāi nyoṅma!

translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbale̱ Iesaia blo̱ etšé̱ Iehowa, ni ehã susuma ní ete hĩegbe̱ momo ye̱ Ahaz hũlũ ṅmle̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ kũ ese̱ mlidšāi nyoṅma.

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Berodak-Baladan, Baladan bi le̱, ni dši Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, tšũ ake̱ wodši ke̱ nikēnii bahã Hezekia; edšake̱ enu ake̱ Hezekia he ye.

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iesaia kē̱ Hezekia ake̱: Bo Iehowa wiemo̱ toi:

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:

translation_verse: Ni magbla Samaria susumo̱ kpẽ le̱ mli mato Ierusalem he, ke̱ Ahab we le̱ kũlomũlo le̱ hũ, ni matšũmo̱ Ierusalem mli tamo̱ atšũmoo̱ kã mli, atšũmoo̱ mli ni atšṍo̱ abuo̱ ši!

english_verse: My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.

english_verse: At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said,

english_verse: she said: You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him:

translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mike̱ nõfõṅ baba bie̱ ne̱ ke̱ bie̱bii le̱ ano̱, ní dši wolo le̱ mli wiemo̱i fẽ ní Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱ ekane le̱;

english_verse: The people of Judah have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I cannot stand it any longer. I am furious.

english_verse: I noticed how sad you were when you read that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry.

translation_verse: Ni Iadai bii dši: Regem ke̱ Iotam ke̱ Gešan ke̱ Pelet ke̱ Efa ke̱ Šaaf.

english_verse: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
translation_verse: Kaleb hemo Maaka le̱ fo̱ Šeber ke̱ Tirhana.

english_verse: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
translation_verse: Ni esā efo̱ Šaaf, Madmana tše̱ le̱, ke̱ Ševa, Makbena tše̱ le̱ ke̱ Gibea tše̱ le̱; ni *Kaleb biyō dši Aksa. *Ios.

english_verse: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
translation_verse: Ni Šobal, Kiriat-Iearim tše̱ le̱, ye̱ bii: Haroe ke̱ Menuhot mei fã le̱.

english_verse: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
translation_verse: Ni Kiriat-Iearim sešibii dši: Itribii ke̱ Putbii ke̱ Šumatbii ke̱ Mišrabii le̱; mene̱mei amli *Zoratbii ke̱ Eštaolbii le̱ dše̱.

english_verse: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
translation_verse: Salma bii dši: Betlehem ke̱ *Netofatbii le̱, Atarot-Bet-Ioab, ke̱ Manahatbii le̱ fã ni dši Zoribii le̱.

english_verse: Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
translation_verse: Ni woloṅmãle̱i asešihii ni yo̱ Iabez le̱ dši Tiratbii, Šimeatbii, Sukatbii. Mene̱mei dši *Kenbii ni dše̱ †Rekab we le̱ tše̱ Hamat mli le̱. *Kodš.

english_verse: more sons. His wife Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel gave birth to Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
translation_verse: ni Iotam bi dši Ahaz, ni Ahaz bi dši Hezekia, ni Hezekia bi dši Manase,

english_verse: David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter. The Descendants of King Solomon
translation_verse: Mene̱mei fẽ le̱ David bii ni, sŏro ehemei abii. Ni *Tamar dši ame̱nyemiyō. *

english_verse: Solomon's descendants included the following kings: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah and his four sons, Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Ni Iosia bii ne̱: Ekromo̱bi dši Iohanan, moni dši enyo̱ dši Iehoiakim, moni dši etẽ dši Zedekia, moni dši edſe̱ dši Šalum.

english_verse: Jehoiakim was the father of Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: Ni Iehoiakim bii dši: Iekonia, ni Iekonia bi dši Zedekia.

english_verse: Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel,
translation_verse: Ni Iekonia, *moni aṅōle̱ nom le̱, bii dši: Šealtiel *

english_verse: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
translation_verse: ke̱ Malkiram ke̱ Pedaia ke̱ Šenazar ke̱ Iekamia ke̱ Hošama ke̱ Nedabia.

english_verse: Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
translation_verse: Ni Pedaia bii dši: *Zerubabel ke̱ Šimei. Ni Zerubabel bii dši: Mešulam ke̱ Hanania ke̱ ame̱nyemiyō Šelomit; Ezra

english_verse: He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.
translation_verse: ke̱ Hašuba ke̱ Ohel ke̱ Berekia ke̱ Hasadia ke̱ Iušab-Hesed, ame̱yi enumo̱.

english_verse: Hananiah's descendants were Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah,
translation_verse: Ni Hanania bii dši: Pelatia ke̱ Iesaia; Refaia bii le̱, Arnan bii le̱, Obadia bii le̱, Šekania bii le̱.

english_verse: the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
translation_verse: Ni Šekania bii dši: Šemaia; ni Šemaia bii dši: Hatuš ke̱ Igal ke̱ Baria ke̱ Nearia ke̱ Šabat, ame̱yi ekpa.

english_verse: Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
translation_verse: Ni Nearia bii dši: Elioenai ke̱ Hizkia ke̱ Azarkam, ame̱yi etẽ.

english_verse: Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
translation_verse: Ni Elioenai bii dši: Hodavia ke̱ Eliašib ke̱ Pelaia ke̱ Akub ke̱ Iohanan ke̱ Delaia ke̱ Anani, ame̱yi kpawo.

english_verse: daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Ni Naara ke̱le̱ ſo̱ Ahuzam ke̱ Hefer ke̱ Temeni ke̱ Haahaštari. Mene̱mei dši Naara bii le̱.

english_verse: Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family.
translation_verse: Ni Iabez hïe ye̱ nyam fè enyemimei le̱; ni enye wole̱ Iabez, edšake̱ ekē̱: Hedšramo̱ mli mifo̱le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton,
translation_verse: Ni Kelub, Šuha nyemi le̱, fo̱ Mehir, ni dši Ešton tše̱ le̱.

english_verse: whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
translation_verse: Ši Ešton fo̱ Bet-Rafa ke̱ Pasea ke̱ Tehina ni dši Ir-Nahaš tše̱ le̱; mene̱mei dši Reka mei le̱.

english_verse: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
translation_verse: Ni Šimon bii dši: Amnon ke̱ Rina ke̱ Ben-Hanan ke̱ Tilon. Ni Iši bii dši: Zohet ke̱ Ben-Zohet.

english_verse: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši gbē̱šõlo̱i ke̱ mei ní hĩo̱ ṅmõdši aši ke̱ abŏ̱i amli ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ mase̱i, ni ame̱tšuo̱ nii ame̱hãale̱.

english_verse: Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
translation_verse: Simeon bii dši: Nemuel ke̱ Iamin, Iarib, Zera, Saul;

english_verse: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
translation_verse: ni Saul bi dši Šalum, ni Šalum bi dši Mibsam, ni Mibsam bi dši Mišma,

english_verse: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
translation_verse: ni Mišma bi dši Hamuel, ni Hamuel bi dši Zakur, ni Zakur bi dši Šimei.

english_verse: Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim.
translation_verse: ke̱ Bet-Markabot ke̱ Hazar-Susim ke̱ Bet-Biri ke̱ Šaaraim. Ene̱mei dši ame̱mādši ke̱-yaši David maṅtše̱yeli be le̱ mli.

english_verse: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱krowai dši: Etam ke̱ Ain, Rimon ke̱ Token ke̱ Ašan: màdši ennmo̱;

english_verse: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
translation_verse: ke̱ ame̱krowai fẽ ni yo̱ ame̱mãdši ne̱ ahe ke̱-yaši Baal le̱. Ene̱mei dši ame̱-šihĩle̱hei ke̱ ame̱weku akontābū.

english_verse: As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei ni atšĩ ame̱gbe̱ii atā ne̱ dši lume̱i ye̱ ame̱wekui le̱ amli, ni ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱ ſere babaō.

english_verse: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yiṅ ame̱te heni atšṍo̱ ke̱-yaä Gedor ye̱ dšō̱ le̱ bokāgbe̱ le̱, koni ame̱yatao niyelihe ame̱hā ame̱koloi le̱.

english_verse: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ná niyelihe frõfrõ ní hĩ hũ, ni šikpoṅ le̱ le̱ ni *eno̱ dšo̱ ni hedšo̱le̱ ye̱ dše̱i; edšake̱ mei ní hĩ dše̱i sá le̱, Ham mli ame̱dše̱. *Kodš.

english_verse: but when Hezekiah was king of Judah, the descendants of Simeon attacked and forced the Hamites and Meunites off the land, then settled there.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mei ni aṅmã ame̱gbe̱ii ne̱ ba ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ *Hezekia yino̱, ni ame̱batſia nomei abũi ke̱ Meunbii ni ame̱na ye̱ dše̱i le̱ anii, ni ame̱feame̱ musu ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ni ame̱hĩ ši ye̱ ame̱nãdšiaṅ; edšake̱ niyelihe ye̱ dše̱i hi ame̱koloi. *

english_verse: They killed the last of the Amalekites and lived there from then on.
translation_verse: ni *ame̱yatſia Amalekbii le̱ ateṅ mei ní efe ní dšo foi le̱ anii; ni ame̱hĩ dše̱i ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. *

english_verse: Their relatives included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.
translation_verse: .] ni Šalum fo̱ *Hilkia, ni Hilkia fo̱ Azaria, *

english_verse: They were all descendants of Abihail, whose family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.
translation_verse: .] ni Azaria fo̱ *Seraia, ni Seraia fo̱ Iehozadak, *

english_verse: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
translation_verse: .] ni *beni Iehowa tšṍ Nebukadnezar nine no̱ ehã abalō Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem ke̱-te le̱, Iehozadak hū te nomṅṍ mli. *

english_verse: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers. The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
translation_verse: Ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai ne̱: Efer ke̱ Iši ke̱ Eliel ke̱ Azriel ke̱ Ieremia ke̱ Iodavia ke̱ Iadiel: hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i ni yo̱ gbe̱i ni dši ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai.

english_verse: These families received the following Safe Towns and the pastureland around them: Shechem in the hill country, Gezer, Jokmeam, Beth-Horon, Aijalon, and Gath-Rimmon.
translation_verse: .] ke̱ Ayalon ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Gat-Rimon ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱;

english_verse: The Gershonite clan received two towns from the tribe of East Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, including the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: .] Ni Geršom bii le̱, aṅõ Golan ni yo̱ Bašan le̱ ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Aštarot ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱ ahãame̱ ye̱ Manase akutšo le̱ fã le̱ weku le̱ mli,

english_verse: The Gershonites also received four towns from the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh, Daberath, Ramoth, and Anem, including the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: .] ke̱ Ramot ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Anem ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱;

english_verse: The Gershonites received four towns from the tribe of Asher: Mashal, Abdon, Hukok, and Rehob, including the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: .] ke̱ Hukok ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Rehob ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱;

english_verse: Finally, the Gershonites received three towns from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, including the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: .] ni Naftali akutšo le̱ṅ le̱: Kedeš ye̱ Galilea ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Hamon ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Kiriataim ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱.

english_verse: The rest of the Merari clan received the towns of Rimmono and Tabor and their pastureland from the tribe of Zebulun.
translation_verse: .] Ni Merari bii ni eſe̱ le̱, aṅō Rimono ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Tabor ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱ ahãame̱ ye̱ Zebulon akutšo le̱ mli;

english_verse: And from the tribe of Gad the Merarites received the towns of Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer, including the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: .] ke̱ Hešbon ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱, ke̱ Iazer ke̱ ehewo̱ šikpõdši le̱.

english_verse: Ephraim mourned for his sons a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tše̱ Efraim ye ame̱he ṅko̱mo̱ gbĩĩ pī, ni enyemimei le̱ ba ame̱baše̱dše emī.

english_verse: Uzzi was the father of Izrahiah and the grandfather of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, who were also family leaders.
translation_verse: Ni Uzi bii dši: Izrahia; ni Izrahia bii dši: Mikael ke̱ Obadia ke̱ Ioel ke̱ Išia, ame̱yi enumo̱ le̱ fẽ le̱ onukpai ni.

english_verse: Zophah was the father of Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
translation_verse: Zofa bii dši: Šua ke̱ Harnefer ke̱ Šual ke̱ Beri ke̱ Imra,

english_verse: Benjamin was the father of three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
translation_verse: *Benyaminbii dši: Bela ke̱ Beker ke̱ Iediael, ame̱yi etẽ.

english_verse: Bela was the father of Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their father's clan. The number of soldiers in their clan was
translation_verse: Ni Bela bii dši: Ezbon ke̱ Uzi ke̱ Uziel ke̱ Ierimot ke̱ Iri, ame̱yi enumo̱, onukpai ye̱ ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱, hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i so̱ṅṅ; ni beni akaneame̱ ye̱ fo̱mo̱ nā le̱, ame̱yibo̱ dši mei akpei-nyoṅmai-enyo̱-ke̱-enyo̱ ke̱ nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ edſe̱.

english_verse: Ephraim was the father of Shuthelah and the ancestor of Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath,
translation_verse: Ni Efraim bii dši: Šutela, Šutela bi dši Bered, ni Bered bi dši Tahat, ni Tahat bi dši Eleada, ni Eleada bi dši Tahat,

english_verse: Machir found a wife for Huppim and one for Shuppim. Machir had a sister named Maacah. Zelophehad was also a descendant of Manasseh, and he had five daughters.
translation_verse: Ni Makir w̌e̱ Hupim ke̱ Šupim nyemiyō ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Maaka le̱. Ni moni dši enyo le̱ gbe̱i dši Zelofehad; ni Zelofehad *fo̱ biyei. *

english_verse: Machir and his wife Maacah were the parents of Peresh and Sheresh. Peresh was the father of Ulam and Rekem.
translation_verse: Ni Makir ṅã Maaka le̱ fo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ gbe̱i ake̱ Pereš; ni enyemi le̱ gbei dši Šereš, ni ebii dši Ulam ke̱ Rakem.

english_verse: Gilead's sister Hammolecheth was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
translation_verse: Ni enyemiyō Hamoleket fo̱ Išhod ke̱ Abiezer ke̱ Mahela.

english_verse: Shemida, another descendant of Manasseh, was the father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam. The Descendants of Ephraim
translation_verse: Ni Šemida bii dši: Ahian ke̱ Šekem ke̱ Likhi ke̱ Aniam.

english_verse: Zabad, and Shuthelah. Ephraim had two other sons, Ezer and Elead. But they were killed when they tried to steal livestock from the people who lived in the territory of Gath.
translation_verse: ni Tahat bi dši Zabad, ni Zabad bi dši Šutela, ni Šutela bi dši Ezer ke̱ Elead. Ni Gatbii ni afo̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ gbeame̱, edšake̱ ame̱yiṅ ame̱te, koni ame̱yalō ame̱koloi le̱ ke̱-ya.

english_verse: Some time later his wife gave birth to another son, and Ephraim named him Beriah, because he was born during a time of misery.
translation_verse: Ni ete eṅă le̱ ṅõ, ni ená mũsũ, ni efo̱ binū, ni ewole̱ Beria, edšake̱ eba beni nõfõṅ yo̱ ewe le̱.

english_verse: Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah. She built the towns of Lower Beth-Horon, Upper Beth-Horon, and Uzzen-Sheerah.
translation_verse: Ni ebiyō dši Šeera; le̱ eto Bet-Horon ni yo̱ šišigbe̱ le̱ ke̱ noni yo̱ yiteṅgbe̱ le̱ ke̱ Uzen-Šeera.

english_verse: Ephraim also had a son named Rephah, and his descendants included Resheph, Telah, Tahan,
translation_verse: Ni ebi dši Refa ke̱ Rešef, ni Rešef bi dši Tela, ni Tela bi dši Tahan,

english_verse: The descendants of Ephraim took over the territory as far south as Bethel, as far east as Naaran, and as far west as Gezer. Their territory included all the villages around these towns, as well as Shechem, Ayyah, and the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱nii ke̱ ame̱šihĩle̱hei dši Betel ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ni bokãgbe̱ le̱ Naaran, ni anaigbe̱ le̱ Gezer ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱ Šekem ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱-yaši Aza ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱. Ios.

english_verse: The descendants of Manasseh settled in the territory that included Beth-Shan, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor, and the nearby villages. The descendants of Joseph lived in these towns and villages. The Descendants of Asher
translation_verse: Ni Manase bii le̱ amase̱i le̱ ame̱ye̱ Bet-Šean ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, Taanak ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, Megido ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, Dor ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱. Ne̱ke̱ mãdši ne̱ amli Israel bi Iosef bii le̱ hĩ. Ios.

english_verse: Asher had four sons, Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and one daughter, Serah.
translation_verse: Ašer bii dši: Imna ke̱ Išwa ke̱ Išwi ke̱ Beria ke̱ ame̱nyemiyō Sera.

english_verse: Beriah was the father of Heber and Malchiel the father of Birzaith.
translation_verse: Ni Beria bii dši: Heber ke̱ Malkiel, le̱ dši Birsavit tše̱ le̱.

english_verse: Heber was the father of three sons, Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and one daughter, Shua.
translation_verse: Ni Heber fo̱ Iaflet ke̱ Šomer ke̱ Hotam ke̱ ame̱nyemiyō Šua.

english_verse: Japhlet was the father of Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
translation_verse: Ni Iaflet bii dši: Pasak ke̱ Bimhal ke̱ Ašwat. Mene̱mei dši Iaflet bii le̱.

english_verse: Shomer was the father of Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
translation_verse: Ni Šomer bii dši: Ahi ke̱ Roga, Iehuba ke̱ Aram.

english_verse: And Japhlet's brother Hotham was the father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
translation_verse: Ni enyemi Helem bii dši: Zofa ke̱ Imna ke̱ Šeleš ke̱ Amal.

english_verse: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
translation_verse: Bezer ke̱ Hod ke̱ Šama ke̱ šilša ke̱ Itran ke̱ Beera.

english_verse: Jether was the father of Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
translation_verse: Ni Ieter bii dši: Iefune ke̱ Pispa ke̱ Ara.

english_verse: Ulla was the father of Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
translation_verse: Ni Ula bii dši; Ara ke̱ Haniel ke̱ Rizia.

english_verse: These were the descendants of Asher, and they were all respected family leaders and brave soldiers. The tribe of Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Mene̱mei fẽ dši Ašer bii, onukpai dšiame̱ ye̱ ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱, hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i ni ahalaame̱ ke̱ lume̱i le̱ ateṅ onukpai ni. Ni beni akaneame̱ ye̱ fo̱mo̱ nā le̱, ame̱yibo̱ dši mei akpei-nyoṅmai-enyo̱-ke-ekpa.

english_verse: Bela was the father of Addar, Gera, Abihud,
translation_verse: Ni Bela bii dšĩ: Adar ke̱ Gera ke̱ Abihud

english_verse: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
translation_verse: ke̱ Abišua ke̱ Naaman ke̱ Ahoa

english_verse: Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
translation_verse: ke̱ Gera ke̱ Sefuſan ke̱ Huram.

english_verse: Beriah and Shema were family leaders in the clan that lived in the town of Aijalon and that forced out the people of Gath.
translation_verse: Ni Beria ke̱ Šema dši tše̱mei le̱ ateṅ onukpai ye̱ Ayalonbii le̱ ateṅ; ame̱ ame̱ſie Gatbii le̱.

english_verse: Beriah's descendants included Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha.
translation_verse: ke̱ Mikael ke̱ Išpa ke̱ Ioha dši Beria bii.

english_verse: Elpaal's descendants included Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab.
translation_verse: ke̱ Išmerai ke̱ Izlia ke̱ Iobab dši Elpaal bii.

english_verse: Shimei's descendants included Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath.
translation_verse: ke̱ Adaia ke̱ Beraia ke̱ Šimrat dši šimei bii.

english_verse: Jeroham's descendants included Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri.
translation_verse: ke̱ Iaarešia ke̱ Elia ke̱ Zikri dši Ieroham bii.

english_verse: These were the family leaders in their ancestor's clan, and they and their descendants lived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši tše̱mei le̱ ateṅ onukpai ye̱ ame̱yĩno̱ĩ le̱ fẽ mli. Mene̱mei hĩ Ierusalem.

english_verse: Jeiel settled the town of Gibeon. He and his wife Maacah lived there
translation_verse: Ni Gibeon tše̱ le̱ hi Gibeon, ni eṅã gbe̱i dši Maaka.

english_verse: along with their sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
translation_verse: Ni ekromo̱bi dši Abdon, ke̱ Zur ke̱ Kiš ke̱ Baal ke̱ Nadab

english_verse: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
translation_verse: ke̱ Gedor ke̱ Ahio ke̱ Zeker.

english_verse: and Mikloth the father of Shimeah. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives. The Descendants of King Saul
translation_verse: Ši Miklot fo̱ Šimea; ni ame̱ hũ ame̱ke̱ ame̱nyemimei le̱ hi Ierusalem ye̱ ame̱nyemimei le̱ amase̱i.

english_verse: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
translation_verse: Ni Ner fo̱ Kiš, ni *Kiš fo̱ Saul, ni Saul fo̱ Ionatan ke̱ Malkišua ke̱ Abinadab ke̱ Ešbaal. *

english_verse: Jonathan was the father of Meribbaal, the grandfather of Micah,
translation_verse: Ni Ionatan bi dši Merib-Baal, ni Merib-Baal fo̱ Mika.

english_verse: and the great-grandfather of Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
translation_verse: Ni Mika bii dši: Piton ke̱ Melek ke̱ Tarea ke̱ Ahaz.

english_verse: Saul's other descendants were Jehoaddah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza,
translation_verse: Ni Ahaz fo̱ Iehoada, ni Iehoada fo̱ Alemet ke̱ Azmawet ke̱ Zimri, ni Zimri fo̱ Moza.

english_verse: as well as Azel's six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
translation_verse: Ni Azel fo̱ bihĩĩ ekpa, ni ame̱gbe̱ii dši: Azrikam, ekromo̱bi le̱, ke̱ Išmael ke̱ Šearia ke̱ Obadia ke̱ Hanan. Mene̱mei fẽ le̱ Azel bii ni.

english_verse: Azel's brother Eshek was the father of Ulam, Jeush, and Eliphelet.
translation_verse: Ni enyemi Ešek bii dši: Ulam, ekromo̱bi le̱, ke̱ Ieuš, moni dši enyo̱ le̱, ke̱ Elifelet, moni dši etẽ le̱.

english_verse: Ulam's sons were brave soldiers who were experts at using a bow and arrows. They had a total of
translation_verse: Ni Ulam bii le̱ dši hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i ke̱ *gãitšẽlo̱i, ni ame̱ye̱ bihĩĩ ke̱ bihĩĩ abii pī, oha ke̱ nyoṅmai-enumo̱. Mene̱mei fẽ dši Benyaminbii. *

english_verse: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives were the guards at the temple gates. Shallum was the leader of this clan,
translation_verse: Ni agbónākwe̱lo̱i dši: Šalum ke̱ Akub ke̱ Talmon ke̱ Ahiman ke̱ ame̱nyemimei le̱; Šalum dši onukpa.

english_verse: Shallum son of Kore, as well as the other men in the Korahite clan, guarded the entrance to the temple, just as their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ni Šalum, Kora bi Ebiasaf bi Kore bi le̱, ke̱ enyemimei ni dše̱ etše̱ we le̱ ni dši Korabii le̱, ame̱ ame̱kwe̱o̱ súomo̱ nitšumo̱ le̱ ní ame̱buo̱ bū le̱ šĩnāi le̱ anā; *ši ame̱tše̱mei dši mei ni bu Iehowa nsra le̱ nāgbe̱ le̱ he. *

english_verse: Phinehas son of Eleazar had supervised their work because the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: Ni Eleazar bi Pinehas dši moni ye ame̱no̱ lumo̱ sá le̱, ni Iehowa ke̱le̱ ye̱.

english_verse: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was also one of the guards at the temple.
translation_verse: Zakaria, Mešelemia bi le̱, dši agbónākwe̱lo̱ ni kwe̱o̱ kpēbū le̱ šĩnā le̱ nā.

english_verse: The four full-time guards were Levites, and they supervised the other guards and were responsible for the rooms in the temple and the supplies kept there.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ agbónākwe̱lo̱i onukpai edſe̱ ni dši Levibii le̱, dši mei ní atu nitšumo̱ le̱ awo ame̱deṅ, ni ame̱ ame̱kwe̱o̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ piai le̱ ke̱ fiasei le̱.

english_verse: They guarded the temple day and night and opened its doors every morning. The Duties of the Levites
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ mase̱i ame̱hĩo̱ nyōṅ fẽ; edšake̱ ame̱nitšumo̱ dši ake̱ ame̱bu dše̱i, ní ame̱gbleo̱ šĩnāi le̱ dā lebi.

english_verse: Some of the Levites were responsible for the equipment used in worship at the temple, and they had to count everything before and after it was used.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ ame̱teṅ meikomei kwe̱o̱ súomo̱ nibii le̱; ké̱ ake̱-mība abato le̱, akaneo̱, ni ké̱ ākō̱lo̱ ke̱-dse kpo hũ, akaneo̱.

english_verse: Mattithiah, Shallum's oldest son, was a member of the Levite clan of Korah, and he was in charge of baking the bread used for offerings.
translation_verse: Ni aṅõ Matitia ní dše̱ Levibii le̱ ateṅ, ni edši Koranyo Šalum kromo̱bi le̱, ato nibii ni ašĩo̱ ye̱ ṅe̱sũi amli le̱ ahe nitšumo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The Levites from the Kohath clan were in charge of baking the sacred loaves of bread for each Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ni Kahatbii ní dši ame̱nyemimei le̱ ateṅ meikomei kwe̱o̱ hĩe-mã-abolo le̱, ni ame̱sãa dā hedsōmogbĩ.

english_verse: The Levite family leaders who were the musicians also lived at the temple. They had no other responsibilities, because they were on duty day and night.
translation_verse: Ši *mene̱mei dši lalatše̱mei ni dši Levibii le̱ atše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai ni hĩo̱ piai le̱ amli, ni ame̱be̱ mli ni atšuo̱ nitšumo̱i krokomei le̱; edšake̱ ſane ke̱ nyõṅ fẽ le̱ ame̱kă ame̱nitšumo̱ le̱ he. *K.

english_verse: All of these men were family leaders in the Levi tribe and were listed that way in their family records. They lived in Jerusalem. King Saul's Family (
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dši Levibii le̱ atše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai ye̱ ame̱fo̱mo̱i le̱ anā. Mene̱mei hĩ Ierusalem.

english_verse: the father of Shimeam. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives.
translation_verse: Ni Miklot fo̱ Šimeam. Ní ame̱ hũ ame̱ke̱ ame̱nyemimei le̱ hĩ Ierusalem ye̱ ame̱nyemimei le̱ amase̱i.

english_verse: Jeiel had settled the town of Gibeon, where he and his wife Maacah lived.
translation_verse: Ni Gibeon tše̱ Ieiel hĩ Gibeon, ni eṅã gbe̱i dši Maaka.

english_verse: They had ten sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
translation_verse: Ni ekromo̱bi dši Abdon, ke̱ Zur ke̱ Kiš ke̱ Baal ke̱ Ner ke̱ Nadab

english_verse: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth
translation_verse: ke̱ Gedor ke̱ Ahio ke̱ Zakaria ke̱ Miklot.

english_verse: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
translation_verse: Ni Ner fo̱ Kiš, ni Kiš fo̱ Saul, ni Saul fo̱ Ionatan ke̱ Malkišua ke̱ Abinadab ke̱ Ešbaal.

english_verse: The descendants of Ahaz included Jarah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel and his six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
translation_verse: Ni Azel ye̱ bihĩĩ ekpa, ni ame̱gbe̱ii ne̱: Azrikam, Bokeru ke̱ Išmael ke̱ Šearia ke̱ Obadia ke̱ Hanan. Mene̱mei dši Azel bii le̱.

english_verse: Saul died because he was unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord. He even asked advice from a woman who talked to spirits of the dead,
translation_verse: Ni Saul gbo ye̱ tõ ni etõ Iehowa no̱ ke̱ Iehowa *wiemo̱ ní ebuu le̱ hewo̱, ni asaṅ eyafe nii †ye̱ sisatšé̱lo̱ ṅõ eke̱bi nii, *

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Ni beni ta le̱ mli wa hã Saul, ni gãitšẽlo̱i le̱ mīninale̱ le̱, etšui fã ye̱ ame̱hewo̱.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want those godless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Then Saul stuck himself in the stomach with his own sword and fell on the blade.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Saul kē̱ etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ ake̱: Gblamo̱ oklante ni oke̱-dũmi, koni ne̱ke̱ fõlo̱i ne̱ akaba ni ame̱bafemi niseniianii. Ši etawūniihĩelo̱ le̱ ekplẽẽ; edšake̱ ēše gbeyei naakpa dientše̱. Nohewo le̱ Saul ko̱ eklante ni eho egbẽ no̱.

english_verse: Saul, three of his sons, and all his male relatives were dead.
translation_verse: Boni Saul ke̱ ebihĩĩ etẽ le̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fẽ gboi šikome ne̱.

english_verse: The Israelites who lived in Jezreel Valley learned that their army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead. They ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites left behind.
translation_verse: Ni beni Israelbii le̱ ni yo̱ dšō̱ le̱ mli le̱ na ake̱ ame̱dšo foi, ni ake̱ Saul ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ egboi le̱, ame̱šī ame̱mădši le̱ ni ame̱dšo foi. Ni Filistibii le̱ ba ni ame̱bahĩ mli.

english_verse: they took Saul's weapons, pulled off his armor, and cut off his head. Then they sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the news among their people and to thank the idols of their gods.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kplo̱ ehe nii le̱, ni ame̱ṅõ eyitšo ke̱ etawūnii le̱, ni ame̱tšũ ayakpa Filistibii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ kpũla, koni ašie̱ atšõ ame̱dšemãwo̱dši le̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱.

english_verse: They put Saul's armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of their god Dagon.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõ etawūnii le̱ ame̱yato ame̱nyoṅmo̱i le̱ awe le̱; ši eyitšoṅoṅo le̱ ame̱ yaka ame̱kpe̱te̱ Dagon we le̱.

english_verse: some brave men went to get his body and the bodies of his three sons. The men brought the bodies back to Jabesh, where they buried them under an oak tree. Then for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: hĩĩ ekãlo̱i le̱ fẽ te ši ni *ameyadšie Saul gbonyo le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ agbohĩĩ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱-ba Iabeš, ni ame̱bafũ ame̱wui le̱ ye̱ blo̱fo-yō̱itšo ni yo̱ Iabeš le̱ šiši, ni ame̱ye buada gbĩĩ kpawo. *

english_verse: instead of asking the Lord. So the Lord had Saul killed and gave his kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
translation_verse: ši ebii Iehowa dāṅgbē hewo le̱ egbele̱, ni edãi maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ehã David, Išai bi le̱.

english_verse: Another time he killed an Egyptian who was over two meters tall and was armed with a spear. Benaiah only had a club, so he grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Ni esā egbe Mizraimnyo ko ní eke̱le̱ dši ninetalo̱i ennmo̱; ni Mizraimnyo le̱ hĩe akplo̱ ni *tamo̱ mamalòlo̱ agbatšo ye̱ edeṅ; ši le̱ le̱ ehĩe dẽhĩemo̱tšo ke̱kpleke ši ke̱-yaninale̱, ni ešõ akplo̱ le̱ ye̱ Mizraimnyo le̱ deṅ, ni eke̱ le̱dientše̱ ekplo̱ le̱ gbele̱. *

english_verse: Another one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite.
translation_verse: Ni eso̱ le̱ *Eleazar, Ahohinyo le̱, ní dši Dodo bi; edši hĩĩ kakabãi etẽ le̱ ateṅ mokome. *

english_verse: except Eleazar, who stayed with David. They took their positions in a nearby barley field and defeated the Philistines! The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ho ame̱damo̱ ši ye̱ šikpoṅ kukuō le̱ teṅ tūntu, ni ame̱fã he, ni ame̱gbe Filistibii le̱, ni Iehowa tšu kūnimyeli nitšumo̱ kpeteṅkple.

english_verse: One time the Three Warriors went to meet David among the rocks at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Ni onukpai nyoṅmai-etẽ le̱ ateṅ mei etẽ ne̱ kpleke ši ke̱-te te̱sā le̱ no̱ ye̱ David ṅõ ye̱ *Adulam te̱kplo le̱ mli; ni Filistibii ata le̱ ebo̱ nsra ye̱ Refaim dšō̱ le̱ṅ. *

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in a fortress,
translation_verse: Ni no mli le̱ David ye̱ te̱kplo le̱ mli, ni Filistibii asrafoi le̱ hũ ye̱ Betlehem;

english_verse: and said, “Drinking this water would be like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ akahã ene̱ mīgbalemi fō̃ṅfõ ake̱ mafe ene̱! aso manu ne̱ke̱ hĩĩ ní še̱re̱ amehe ame̱ſie ne̱ alá lo? edšake̱ ame̱he ame̱še̱re̱ ame̱ſie ni ame̱yaye̱ ke̱-ba ne̱! Nohewo le̱ esumo̱o̱ ake̱ enu. Nii ní hĩĩ kakabãi etẽ le̱ fe ne̱.

english_verse: Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed
translation_verse: Ni Abišai, Ioab nyemi le̱, dši mei etẽ le̱ ateṅ onukpa, le̱ hũ ewó ekplo̱ no̱ ye̱ mei ohai-etẽ no̱ ni egbeame̱, ni ená gbe̱i ye̱ mei etẽ le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: and was more famous than the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was their commander, but he never became one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Mei etẽ le̱ ateṅ le̱ le̱ dši moni hĩe yo̱ nyam fè mei enyo̱ le̱, nohewo le̱ awole̱ ame̱safoiatše̱; ši kleṅkleṅmei etẽ le̱ eninaa-ame̱.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. One time he killed two of Moab's best fighters, and one snowy day he went into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia, nū ekãlo̱ ko ni tšu nibii wudši ní edše̱ Kabzeel le̱ bi Iehoiada bi le̱, le̱ hũ egbe Ariel ni dše̱ Moab le̱ bihĩĩ enyo̱ le̱, ni le̱ noṅṅ ekpleke ši ke̱-te ni eyagbe dšata ye̱ bu ko mli ye̱ anõ be le̱ mli.

english_verse: Benaiah did things like that; he was just as brave as the Three Warriors,
translation_verse: Nii ni Iehoiada bi Benaia le̱ fe ne̱, ni ená gbe̱i ye̱ hĩĩ kakabãi etẽ le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: even though he never became one of them. And he was certainly as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. So David made him the leader of his own bodyguard.
translation_verse: Na, ehĩe ye̱ nyam fè mei nyoṅmai-etẽ le̱, ši kleṅkleṅmei etẽ le̱, enināa-ame̱. Ni David wole̱ onukpa ye̱ ehebulo̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Men from the tribe of Gad also joined David at his fortress in the desert and served as his warriors. They were also brave soldiers—fierce as lions and quick as gazelles. They were always prepared to fight with shields and spears.
translation_verse: Ni Gadbii le̱ ateṅ mei ni tše amehe ke̱-ba David ṅõ ye̱ te̱kplo ní yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ṅ, ní dši hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i ní le tawũ ní le tše̱ṅ ke̱ akplo̱ hĩemo̱, ni ame̱hĩe tamo̱ dšatai ahĩe, ní amehe ye̱ *oyá tamo̱ soṅăi ní yo̱ gõdši ano̱ le̱ ne̱: *

english_verse: All these men were army officers; some were high-ranking officers over a thousand troops, and others were officers over a hundred troops.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei dše̱ Gadbii le̱ ateṅ ni ame̱dši ta le̱ no̱ asafoiatše̱mei; moni dši bibiō ye̱ ame̱teṅ le̱ eyeo̱ mei oha no̱, ni moni dši agbo ye̱ ame̱teṅ le̱ eyeo̱ mei akpe no̱.

english_verse: One time a group of men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah went to the fortress where David was staying.
translation_verse: Asaṅ Benyamin ke̱ Iuda bii le̱ ateṅ meikomei hũ ba David ṅõ, ye̱ te̱kplo le̱ṅ.

english_verse: David met them outside and said, “If you are coming as friends to fight on my side, then stay and join us. But if you try to turn me over to my enemies, the God our ancestors worshiped will punish you, because I have done nothing wrong.”
translation_verse: Ni David dše kpo ke̱-ba ame̱hĩe, ni ehere no̱ ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši hedšo̱le̱-nyiemo̱ nyenyie ke̱-ba miṅõ, koni nyebaye nyebuami le̱, no le̱ miye̱ he tšui ake̱ mike̱nye aafe ekome; ši ke̱dši nyeba ni nyebatšõ mihenye̱lo̱i le̱ mise̱gbe̱ le̱, ake̱-ni sane fõṅ ko be̱ mideṅ hewo̱ le̱, wo̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le akwe̱ ní ekodšo!

english_verse: Some of the warriors who joined David were from the tribe of Manasseh. They had earlier gone with David when he agreed to fight on the side of the Philistines against King Saul. But as soon as the Philistine rulers realized that David might turn against them and rejoin Saul, they sent David away to the town of Ziklag.
translation_verse: Ni Manasebii le̱ hũ ateṅ meikomei tše ame̱he ke̱-badõmo̱ David, beni eke̱ Filistibii le̱ baã ní ame̱ke̱ Saul abawo le̱, ši ame̱náá ame̱fata ame̱he; edšake̱ *Filistibii le̱ alumei le̱ te adšina ni ame̱wole̱ gbe ame̱kē̱: Wo̱yitšei eke̱-batše ke̱-ya enuṅtšo̱ Saul ṅō. *

english_verse: and brave soldiers, and so David made them officers in his army. They fought on his side when enemy troops attacked.
translation_verse: Ni mene̱mei ye bua David ni eke̱ odšoyeli ta le̱ wu le̱; edšake̱ hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i dši ame̱fẽ-kwa, ni ame̱dši tatše̱mei hũ.

english_verse: Other Israelites from as far away as the territories of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought cattle and sheep to slaughter for food. They also brought donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen that were loaded down with flour, dried figs and raisins, wine, and olive oil. Everyone in Israel was very happy.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ mei ni be̱ṅke̱ame̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši Isakar ke̱ Zebulon ke̱ Naftali niiaṅ le̱ hã tedšii ke̱ yomai ke̱ tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ tšinai tšre abolo ke̱ niyenii sro̱toi ke̱-ba: mã ke̱ agbãmi-tatalei ke̱ weinyibii gbīdši ke̱ wein ke̱ mū ke̱ tšinai ke̱ toi babaō dientše̱; edšake̱ mīše̱ eba Israel.

english_verse: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
translation_verse: Mene̱mei fẽ ní dši hĩĩ tawulo̱i ni le tagbámo̱ le̱ ba Hebron ke̱ ame̱tšui fẽ, koni ame̱bawo David maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel mū le̱ fẽ no̱, ni Israelbii ni eſe̱ le̱ fẽ fe ekome ake̱ awo David maṅtše̱.

english_verse: The soldiers stayed in Hebron three days, eating and drinking what their relatives had prepared for them.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ David hĩ dše̱i gbĩĩ etẽ, ame̱yeyẽ nii ni ame̱nunū dãi; edšake̱ ame̱-nyemimei le̱ esra ame̱se̱.

english_verse: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
translation_verse: Ni David ke̱ Israel mū le̱ fẽ yiṅ ke̱-te *Baal ni dši Kiriat-Iearim ni yo̱ Iuda le̱, koni ame̱yawó Nyoṅmo̱ Iehowa ní hĩo̱ kerubim le̱ ateṅ le̱ adeka ní atšé̱o̱ egbe̱i ye̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i ke̱-ba. *Ios.

english_verse: Some time later, David talked with his army commanders,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni David ke̱ mei akpekpei ke̱ mei ohahai ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei ke̱ lume̱i le̱ fẽ te adšina;

english_verse: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
