english_verse: Solomon had one of the columns placed on the south side of the temple's entrance; it was called Jachin. The other one was placed on the north side of the entrance; it was called Boaz.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ akulašĩṅi le̱ mãmo̱ so̱lemo̱-tšũ le̱ hĩe, ekome ye̱ ninedšũrõgbe̱, ni ekome hũ ye̱ abe̱kugbe̱; ni etšé̱ ninedšũrõ nõ le̱ gbe̱i ake Iakin, ni abe̱ku nō le̱ hũ etšē̱ egbe̱i Boaz.

english_verse: Solomon had a bronze altar made that was nine meters square and four and a half meters high.
translation_verse: Asaṅ efe *akō̱ble afo̱lešãlate̱: eke̱le̱ dši ninetalo̱i nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ni elē̱mo̱ hũ ninetalo̱i nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ni ekwo̱le̱ ninetalo̱i nyoṅma. *

english_verse: Ten gold lampstands were also made according to the plans. Solomon placed these lampstands inside the temple, five on each side of the main room.
translation_verse: Ni esā efe šika kanetšei nyoṅma tamo̱ boni atšõ ake̱ afeame̱ le̱, ni eṅõ-mãmo̱ so̱lemo̱tšũ le̱ṅ, enumo̱ ye̱ nine-dšũrõgbe̱, ni enumo̱ hũ ye̱ abe̱kugbe̱.

english_verse: He also gave orders to make a large metal bowl called the Sea. It was
translation_verse: Ni efe ṅšo̱ ní aſie: ke̱-dše̱ nābu bie̱ ke̱-yaši nābu bie̱ le̱ efeo̱ ninetalo̱i nyoṅma, afele̱ kutruku, ni ekwo̱le̱ dši ninetalo̱i enumo̱, ni kpã ni hĩe ninetalo̱i nyoṅmai-etẽ aakpe he.

english_verse: The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls, with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions.
translation_verse: Emã tšinai nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ no̱, etẽ mīkwe̱ kōyigbe̱, ni etẽ mīkwe̱ anaigbe̱, ni etẽ mīkwe̱ wuoyigbe̱, ni etẽ mīkwe̱ bokãgbe̱; ni ṅšo̱ le̱ mã ameno̱ ye̱ ṅwei, ni ame̱se̱gbe̱i fẽ eyadše mligbe̱.

english_verse: Its outer edge was decorated with two rows of carvings of bulls, ten bulls to about every
translation_verse: Ni to̱ ke̱ ehe bāi bo̱le ekue̱ le̱ ke̱-kpe, ninetalo̱ kome ble nyoṅma ke̱-bo̱le ṅšo̱ le̱ kpũla; to̱ ke̱ ehe bāi le̱ srẽnẽi enyo̱ ni, ni aſieame̱ ke̱ le̱ fẽ šikome.

english_verse: He also made ten small bowls and put five on each side of the large bowl. The small bowls were used to wash the animals that were burned on the altar as sacrifices, and the priests used the water in the large bowl to wash their hands.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni efe botokui nyoṅma, ni eṅõ enumo̱ eto ninedšũrõgbe̱, ni eṅõ enumo̱ hũ eto abe̱kugbe̱, koni afo̱ nii ahe ye̱ mli, ni ame̱dšale šã-afo̱le le̱ he nibii le̱ ahe ye̱ mli; ši ṅšo̱ le̱ ye̱ hã oso̱foi le̱, ni ame̱fo̱flo̱ amehe ye̱ mli.

english_verse: He also made ten tables and placed them in the main room, five on each side. And he made
translation_verse: Asaṅ efe okplõi nyoṅma ni eṅõ-māmo̱ so̱lemo̱tšũ le̱ṅ, enumo̱ ye̱ ninedšũrõgbe̱, ni enumo̱ hũ ye̱ abe̱kugbe̱; ni efe šika lalakãi oha hũ.

english_verse: Solomon gave orders to build two courtyards: a smaller one that only priests could use and a larger one. The doors to these courtyards were covered with bronze.
translation_verse: Asaṅ efe oso̱foi le̱ akpo le̱ ke̱ kpo wulu le̱ ke̱ kpo le nā šĩnāi le̱, ni eke̱ akō̱ble ha ame̱nā šĩnāi le̱ ahe.

english_verse: The large bowl called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the temple.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ mã šĩa le̱ ninedšũrõgbe̱ ye̱ bokãgbe̱ ke̱-baä wuoyigbe̱.

english_verse: Huram made shovels, sprinkling bowls, and pans for hot ashes. Here is a list of the other furnishings he made for God's temple:
translation_verse: Ni Huram fe gbé̱i le̱ ke̱ nilōmo̱nii le̱ ke̱ lalakãi le̱ hũ. Ne̱ke̱ Huram gbe nitšumo̱ ní etšu ehã maṅtše̱ Salomo ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ he le̱ nā:

english_verse: two columns, two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of these columns, two chain designs on the caps,
translation_verse: akulašĩṅi enyo̱ lo̱ ke̱ kpo̱i kutrukui enyo̱ le̱ ni mãmo̱ akulašĩṅi le̱ ayiteaṅ le̱, ke̱ ntāṅi enyo̱ ni aṅõ-haä kpoi kutrukui enyo̱ le̱ ní mãmo̱ akulašĩṅi le̱ ayiteaṅ le̱ ahe le̱,

english_verse: the large bowl and the twelve bulls that held it up,
translation_verse: ke̱ ṅšo̱ kome ke̱ tšinai nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ni yo̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ šiši le̱,

english_verse: pans for hot ashes, as well as shovels and meat forks. Huram made all these things out of polished bronze
translation_verse: ke̱ kukwe̱ii le̱ ke̱ nilōmo̱nii le̱ ke̱ kpodši le̱ ke̱ nibii fẽ ní fata he le̱, Huram, etše̱ gbomo le̱, fe ehã maṅtše̱ Salomo hã Iehowa we le̱, ke̱ akō̱ble ni kple̱o̱ nyaramnyaram.

english_verse: by pouring melted bronze into the clay molds he had set up near the Jordan River, between Succoth and Zeredah.
translation_verse: Iordan ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hã aſie ye̱, ye̱ nišṍ sũ ni yo̱ Sukot ke̱ Zereda te le̱ṅ le̱ mli.

english_verse: There were so many bronze furnishings that no one ever knew how much bronze it took to make them.
translation_verse: Ní Salomo fe ne̱ke̱ nibii ne̱ fẽ, babaō dientše̱, āhū ní akō̱ble le̱ alee nā.

english_verse: Solomon also gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar, the tables that held the sacred loaves of bread,
translation_verse: Ni Salomo fe nibii fẽ ní yo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱, ke̱ šika afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ke̱ okplōi le̱ ni hĩe-mã-abolo le̱ mãa no̱ le̱,

english_verse: the lampstands and the lamps that burned in front of the most holy place,
translation_verse: ke̱ kanetšei le̱ ke̱ amehe kanei le̱ ni asu ye̱ se̱tšũ le̱ hĩe tamo̱ bo̱ni ato le̱, šika kro̱ṅṅ ake̱-fe,

english_verse: lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, ladles, fire pans, and the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_verse: ni kaklai le̱ ke̱ lalakăi le̱ ke̱ liko̱-liko̱i le̱ ke̱ ladšēṅe̱sũi le̱ hũ šika kro̱ṅṅ ake̱-fe; ni tšũ le̱ nă šĩnāi le̱, noni yo̱ mligbe̱ ní ake̱-yaä hekroṅkroṅ fè fẽ le̱, ke̱ šĩnāi ní yo̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱ tšũ le̱ nā le̱ hũ šika ake̱-fe.

english_verse: whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ kerubim le̱ elē̱ ame̱fĩdši amli eha adeka le̱ mãbe le̱, ni kerubim le̱ kete adeka le̱ ke̱ ehe tšei le̱ ano̱ ye̱ ṅweigbe̱.

english_verse: The priests of every group had gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable to the Lord. The Levite musicians, including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, were wearing robes of fine linen. They were standing on the east side of the altar, playing cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. One hundred and twenty priests were with these musicians, and they were blowing trumpets. They were praising the Lord by playing music and singing: “The Lord is good, and his love never ends.” Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the holy place.
translation_verse: ni beni te̱tre̱mantre̱kpãlo̱i le̱ ke̱ lalatše̱mei le̱ fe ekome ní anu gbē kome ni ake̱-mīdšie Iehowa yi ní ake̱-mīdale̱ ši le̱, beni ame̱wó ame̱gbē no̱ ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱i ke̱ ṅme̱dši ke̱ saṅkũi krokomei ni ame̱dšie Iehowa yi, *ake̱ ehĩ, edšake̱ nāno̱ emo̱bo̱nale̱ hĩo̱ ši ke̱-yaä le̱:) ke̱ke̱ ní atatu bayi šĩa le̱ ní dši Iehowa šĩa le̱ obo, *

english_verse: Then the priests and the Levites picked up the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship, and they carried them to the temple.
translation_verse: ni ame̱hole adeka le̱ ke̱ kpē-bū le̱ ke̱ nibii kroṅkroṅi le̱ fẽ ni yo̱ kpē-bū le̱ mli le̱ ke̱-ba, oso̱foi ke̱ Levibii le̱ dši mei ní hole ke̱-ba.

english_verse: Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Salomo ke̱ Israel asafo mū le̱ ſẽ ní nā ebakpe ši ye̱ eṅõ le̱ badamo̱ adeka le̱ hĩe ni ame̱gbegbē tōi ke̱ tšinai ni anyẽṅ akane lo abu ame̱fále̱ nā ame̱ke̱-šã afo̱lei.

english_verse: The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: *Nokonoko be̱ adeka le̱ mli, ake̱ dša te̱i te̱tre̱bii enyo̱ le̱ ní Mose ṅõ-to mli ye̱ Horeb heni Iehowa ke̱ Israel-bii le̱ kpãṅ ye̱, beni ame̱dše̱ Mizraim ame̱baä le̱. *Heb.

english_verse: The Lord's glory was in that cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work.
translation_verse: āhũ po ni atatu le̱ hewo̱ le̱ oso̱foi le̱ nyẽẽ ši adamo̱ ni ame̱súmo̱, edšake̱ Iehowa anumnyam le̱ eyi Nyoṅmo̱ šīa le̱ṅ obõ.

english_verse: and prayed: Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you! You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱! nyoṅmo̱ ko nyoṅmo̱ ko be̱ ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ní tamo̱ bo, ni otoo̱ kpãṅmo̱ ke̱ mo̱bo̱nale̱ ohãa otšũdši ní nyieo̱ ohĩe ke̱ ame̱tšui fẽ le̱,

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you, and so whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
translation_verse: Ni obo otšũlo̱ ke̱ omaṅ Israel fai ni ame̱abakpao ye̱ bie̱ ne̱ le̱ toi, ni onu ye̱ ṅwei ní dši ošihĩle̱he le̱, ni kē̱ onu le̱, ṅõ-fa!

english_verse: Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšṍ ehĩe ni edšō̱ Israel asafo mū le̱ fẽ; ni Israel asafo mū le̱ fẽ damo ši.

english_verse: My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
translation_verse: ni oye oši ni owo mitše̱ David, otšũlo̱ le̱, no̱; oke̱ onābu wie, ni oke̱ onine ehã eba mli, tamo̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱!

english_verse: You promised that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱! *ye oši ní owo mitše̱ David, otšũlo̱ le̱, no̱, noni oke: Nū ní aatá Israel maṅtše̱sẽi le̱ no̱ ebo̱ṅo ye̱ mihĩe, ke̱dši obii le̱ aale ame̱nane nā kwe̱mo̱ ke̱ke̱, koni amenyie mimla le̱ mli, take̱ bo̱ni onyie ye̱ mihīe le̱. *

english_verse: There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built?
translation_verse: Ši aso Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ gbomei aabahī ši ye̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ le̱le̱ṅ? Na, ṅwei ke̱ ṅweii amli ṅwei nyẽẽo ato, āhũ ní mbasroo šĩa ne̱ ni mimã ne̱!

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: no le̱ bo toi ye̱ ṅwei, ni oṅõ omaṅ Israel he eša le̱ ofaame̱, ni oṅõame̱ ke̱-ba šikpoṅ le̱ ni oṅõ-hãame̱ ke̱ ame̱tše̱mei le̱ no̱ ekoṅ.

english_verse: Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they stop sinning and turn toward this temple to pray in your name,
translation_verse: Ke̱dši *aṅã́ ṅwei nā ni nyoṅmo̱ ene̱e̱, ye̱ eša ko ní ame̱fe ame̱šio hewo, ni ame̱baso̱le ye̱ bie̱ ni ame̱bo ame̱tšé̱ ogbe̱i, ni ame̱kpale ke̱-dše̱ amehe eša le̱ he, ye̱ pĩmo̱ ní opīame̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱: *

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And send rain on the land you promised them forever.
translation_verse: no le̱ bo toi ye̱ ṅwei, ni oṅõ otšũdši ke̱ omaṅ Israel he eša le̱ ofaame̱, ni otšõame̱ gbe kpakpa ní amenyie no̱, ni ohã nyoṅmo̱ abane̱ aſie ošikpoṅ le̱ ni oṅō-hã omaṅ le̱ ake̱ ame̱nõ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši hõmo̱ ba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšio, gbẽle-hela ni ba dšio, latšā, niṅălãmo̱, bālabii, otukpe̱i ni ba dšio, ke̱dši ame̱henye̱lo̱i hũ basá ame̱yi wo ame̱mãdšiaṅ ye̱ ame̱šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dšio, nõ haomo̱-fẽ-haomo̱ ke̱ nõ hela-fẽ-hela ní dši le̱:

english_verse: Please listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple.
translation_verse: no le̱ so̱lemo̱-fẽ-so̱lemo̱ ke̱ faikpa-mo̱-fẽ-faikpamo̱ ní moko lo omaṅ Israel fẽ aakpa le̱, ke̱ ame̱teṅ mofẽmo le le̱dientše̱ ehaomo̱ ke̱ emanehũlũ ni ebagbe̱ enidšiaṅ etšṍ ne̱ke̱ šĩa ne̱ le̱:

english_verse: You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to what they do and what is in their hearts.
translation_verse: no le̱ bo toi ye̱ ṅwei ní dši ošihĩle̱he le̱, ni oṅõ-fa, ni owo mofẽmo nyõmo̱ ye̱ enifemo̱nii le̱ fẽ nā, bo̱ni ole etšuiṅ le̱; *

english_verse: Then your people will worship you and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: beni afe ni ame̱šeo gbeyei ní ame̱-nyie ogbē̱i le̱ ano̱ gbĩĩabo̱ fẽ ni ame̱yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ni oṅõ-hã wo̱tše̱mei le̱ no̱ le̱!

english_verse: Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple,
translation_verse: Ni gbo̱ tete ní dše̱e̱ omaṅ Israelbii le̱ ateṅ, ši moṅ ogbe̱i kpeteṅkple le̱ ke̱ oninešiwale̱ ke̱ onine ni akpã mli le̱ hewo̱ edše̱ maṅse̱ šoṅṅ eba le̱, ké̱ eba ni ebaso̱le ye̱ ne̱ke̱ šĩa ne̱ hĩe le̱:

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just as your own people Israel do, and they will know that I have built this temple in your honor.
translation_verse: no le̱ bo toi ye̱ ṅwei ni dši ošihĩle̱he le̱, ni ofe nofẽno ni gbo̱ le̱ boo̱ tšē̱o̱o ye̱ hewo̱ le̱, beni afe ní šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ màdšimădši fẽ ale ogbe̱i le̱, koni ame̱šeo gbeyei tamo̱ omaṅ Israel, ni ame̱-sā ame̱ná ame̱le ake̱ ogbe̱i aṅõ-wo ne̱ke̱ šĩa ni mimã ne̱.

english_verse: Sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši omaṅ le̱ fã ta ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i ayawu ye̱ hefẽhe ní otšũame̱, ni *ame̱tšṍ ame̱hĩe ame̱hã maṅ ni ohala le̱ ke̱ šĩa ni mimã mihã ogbe̱i le̱ ni ame̱kpa fai le̱: *Dan.

english_verse: Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
translation_verse: no le̱ bo ame̱so̱lemo̱ ke̱ ame̱faikpamo̱ le̱ toi ye̱ ṅwei, ni oye obuaame̱.

english_verse: Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ame̱fe esa ame̱šio, ni omli fũ-ame̱, ni otuame̱ owo ame̱henye̱lo̱i adeṅ, ni aṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te šikpoṅ ko no̱, edše-ke̱ dšio, edšeke̱e̱ dšio,

english_verse: Lord God, hear us when we pray in this temple.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱, mi-Nyoṅmo̱, mīkpao fai, hã ohĩṅme̱ii akãmo̱, ni oka otoi ohã so̱lemo̱ ni aso̱leo̱ ye̱ bie̱ ne̱ le̱!

english_verse: Come to your new home, where we have already placed the sacred chest, which is the symbol of your strength. I pray that when the priests announce your power to save people, those who are faithful to you will celebrate what you've done for them.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱, wó ohe no̱ ni oyabote ohedšō̱mo̱he le̱, bo ke̱ ohewale̱ adeka le̱! Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱, hã oso̱foi le̱ awo yiwalaheremo̱, ni ohã omei kroṅkroṅi le̱ anyã́ nõkpakpa le̱ he! Lal.

english_verse: Always remember the love you had for your servant David, so that you will not reject your chosen kings.
translation_verse: Iehowa Nyoṅmo̱, kãtšṍ moni ofo̱le̱ mũ le̱ hĩe ohã se̱; kaĩmo̱ *otšũlo̱ David mo̱bo̱nale̱i le! *

english_verse: When the crowd of people saw the fire and the Lord's glory, they knelt down and worshiped the Lord. They prayed: “The Lord is good, and his love never ends.”
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ fẽ mīkwe̱, beni la le̱ dše̱ ṅwei ba ni Iehowa anumnyam le̱ bayi šĩa le̱ no̱ lo̱, ni ame̱ko̱ ame̱hĩeiaṅ bumo̱ ši ye̱ beni aka dše̱i te̱ le̱, ni ame̱-dšá Iehowa ni ame̱dale̱ ši, edšake̱ *ehī, edšake̱ nāno̱ emo̱bo̱nale̱ hĩo ši ke-yaä! *

english_verse: Then they will answer, “It was because the people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
translation_verse: Ni aahere no̱ ake̱: Edšake̱ ame̱kwa Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, moni dšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱he yakpe̱te̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei ahe, ni ame̱dšáame̱ ni ame̱súmo̱-ame̱, nohewo̱ ni ehã ne̱ke̱ efõṅ ne̱ fẽ ba ame̱no̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Everybody stood up during the ceremony. The priests were in their assigned places, blowing their trumpets. And the Levites faced them, playing the musical instruments that David had made for them to use when they praised the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱foi le̱ damo̱ ame̱gbe̱hei le̱, ni Levibii le̱ hũ hĩe Iehowa lala he saṅkũi le̱ ní maṅtše̱ David fe ní aṅõ-da Iehowa ši, edšake̱ nāno̱ emo̱bo̱nale̱ hĩo̱ ši ke̱-yaä, beni David tšṍo̱ amenine no̱ dšieo̱ eyi le̱; ni oso̱foi le̱ kpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i ye̱ ame̱hĩe, ni Israel mū le̱ fẽ damo̱ ši.

english_verse: If my own people will humbly pray and turn back to me and stop sinning, then I will answer them from heaven. I will forgive them and make their land fertile once again.
translation_verse: ni mimaṅ ni aṅõ migbe̱i ewoame le̱ ba ame̱be ši, ni ame̱kpa fai, ni ame̱tao mihĩegbe̱, ni ame̱kpale ke̱-dše̱ ame̱-gbè̱i fõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱: no le̱ mi hũ madše̱ ṅwei mabo toi, ni maṅõ ame̱be ešai le̱ mafaame̱, ni matšá ame̱šikpoṅ le̱.

english_verse: Then on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left very happy because of all the good things the Lord had done for David and Solomon, and for his people Israel. The Lord Appears to Solomon Again (
translation_verse: Ši gbĩ ní dši gbĩ nyoṅmai-enyo̱ ke̱ etẽ le̱ no̱ ye̱ nyõṅ ní dši kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱ ewo maṅ le̱ gbe̱ ke̱-te ame̱būi amli, ni ame̱nyã́ ni ame̱ná tšuidšũrõ ye̱ edšũrõ ni Iehowa efe David ke̱ Salomo ke̱ emaṅ Israel le̱ hewo̱. (

english_verse: The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished. In fact, everything Solomon had planned to do was completed.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Salomo gbe Iehowa šĩa le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ šĩa le̱ nā, ni nibii fẽ ni ba Salomo tšui mli ake̱ eefe ye̱ Iehowa šĩa le̱ ke̱ le̱dientše̱ ešĩa le̱ hewo̱ le̱, efe ni ete no̱.

english_verse: Suppose I hold back the rain or send locusts to eat the crops or make my people suffer with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Na, kē̱ miṅã́ ṅwei nā ni nyoṅmo̱ ene̱e̱, alo mifã́ bālabii ni ame̱baye šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nii, alo mihã gbĕle-hela ba mimaṅbii le̱ ateṅ,

english_verse: I will hear the prayers made in this temple,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ magble mihĩṅme̱ii ni maka mitoi mahã so̱lemo̱ ní aso̱leo̱ ye̱ bie̱ ne̱ le̱.

english_verse: Your father David obeyed me, and now, Solomon, you must do the same. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Ni bo hũ, ke̱dši oonyie ye̱ mihĩe, tamo̱ bo̱ni otše̱ David nyie le̱, ni oofe nii fẽ ni miwoö he kitã le̱, ni ooye mi-kpo̱i ke̱ mimlai le̱ ano̱ le̱:

english_verse: and I will keep my solemn promise to him that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: no le̱ mahã omaṅtše̱yeli sẽi le̱ amã ši šiṅṅ, tamo̱ bo̱ni mike̱ otše̱ David kpãṅ *ake̱: Nū ni aaye Israel no̱ ebo̱ṅo le̱. *

english_verse: But if you or any of the people of Israel disobey my laws or start worshiping foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyekpale ni nyekwa mikpo̱i ke̱ mikitãi ní miṅõ-ſie nyehĩe ne̱, ni nyete nyeyasúmo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei ni nyedšáame̱ le̱:

english_verse: I will pull you out of this land I gave you. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped, so that people everywhere will think it is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: no le̱ mafãmo̱ame̱ ke̱ ame̱šišifãi ke̱-dše̱ mišikpoṅ ní miṅõ-hãame̱ le̱ no̱, ni ne̱ke̱ šĩa ne̱ ni mifele̱ kroṅkroṅ mihã migbe̱i le̱, maše̱le̱ mafō ke̱-adše mihĩe, ni maṅõle̱ mafe *abe̱būnõ ke̱ kpā-lamo̱-nõ ye̱ mãdšimãdši fẽ ateṅ. *

english_verse: This temple is now magnificent. But when these things happen, everyone who walks by it will be shocked and will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?”
translation_verse: Ni ne̱ke̱ šĩa ní kwo̱ godšō ne̱, mofẽmo ní aabaho ye̱ he le̱ he aadšõ ehe ni eekē̱: *Mẽhewo̱ po ni Iehowa fe šikpoṅ ne̱ ke̱ šĩa ne̱ ne̱ke̱? *

english_verse: He did the same thing to the town of Baalath and to the cities where he kept supplies, chariots, and horses. Solomon ordered his workers to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere else in his kingdom.
translation_verse: ke̱ Baalat ke̱ nitō-mãdši ní Salomo yo̱ le̱ fẽ, ke̱ ſīlii amãdši le̱ fẽ, ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei amãdši le̱, ke̱ nofẽno ni Salomo taoo amã ye̱ ehĩetšĕre̱dšiemo̱ hewo ye̱ Ierusalem ke̱ Lebanon ke̱ eno̱yeli šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: He followed the requirements that Moses had given for sacrifices offered on the Sabbath, on the first day of each month, the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters.
translation_verse: gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ ke̱ enõ, ni ešã afo̱lei le̱ bo̱ni *Mose wo kitã le̱, ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ ke̱ nyõdši hēi le̱ ke̱ gbĩĩ dšudši ni ato le̱ ano̱ šii etẽ ye̱ afi mli: ye̱ akpĩtĩ gbĩdšũrõ le̱ ke̱ otšii agbĩdšũrõ le̱ ke̱ asesei agbīdšũrõ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Solomon then assigned the priests and the Levites their duties at the temple, and he followed the instructions that his father, the man of God, had given him. Some of the Levites were to lead music and help the priests in their duties, and others were to guard the temple gates
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ *oso̱foi asafokui le̱ damo̱ ame̱súomo̱ le̱ nā, bo̱ni etše̱ David eto gbe̱dšiano̱ le̱, ke̱ Levibii le̱-hũ ye̱ ame̱nitšumo̱i le̱ anā, ní ame̱la yidšiemo̱lalai ni ame̱súmo̱ ye̱ oso̱foi le̱ ahĩe, gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ ke̱ enõ, ke̱ agbónākwe̱le̱i le̱ hũ ye̱ ame̱-safokui le̱ anā ye̱ agbṍ-fẽ-agbṍ he; edšake̱ nakai Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo David wo kitã. *

english_verse: Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
translation_verse: Ni Salomo nii ni etšu ke̱-dše̱ gbĩ ní ato Iehowa šĩa le̱ šiši le̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni egbe nā, ni Iehowa šĩa le̱ ye emū le̱, asā fẽ ato.

english_verse: Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: No be le̱ mli le̱ Salomo yiṅ ete Ezion-Geber ke̱ Elot ní yo̱ ṅšo̱ nā ye̱ Edom šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.

english_verse: Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than
translation_verse: Ni Huram tšṍ le̱dientše̱ etšũdši anine no̱ eyahãle̱ le̱dši ke̱ tšũdši ni le ṅšo̱ he nii, ni ame̱ke̱ Salomo tšũdši le̱ yiṅ te Ofir, ni ame̱yaṅõ šika talentai ohai-edſe̱ ke̱ nyoṅmai-enumo̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni ame̱ke̱-bahã maṅtše̱ Salomo.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Ni Salomo hãle̱ ewiemo̱i le̱ fẽ hetõ, emli eko eko be̱ ní Salomo enáá etšõõle̱.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told.
translation_verse: Tše̱bele̱ mihee ame̱wiemo̱i le̱ miyee, ke̱-yaši miba ní mibana ke̱ mihĩṅme̱ii ne̱. Ni na, dšee onilē le̱ dale̱ le̱ fã tete agbami le̱; oteke yidšiemo̱ ní minu le̱ tete.

english_verse: Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Adšō̱ owebii le̱, ni adšō̱ otšũdši ne̱ ní damoo̱ ohĩe dāne̱ ní ame̱boo̱ onilē le̱ toi le̱! Luk.

english_verse: I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
translation_verse: Aadšō̱ Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ake̱ ená ohe tšui ni eke̱o tá emaṅtše̱sẽi le̱ no̱, koni oye maṅtše̱ ohã Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; edšake̱ o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ mīsumo̱ Israel ni ehã edamo̱ ši ke̱-ya nāno̱, nohewo̱ ni ewoö ameno̱ maṅtše̱, koni okodšo ni oye dšale̱ sane!

english_verse: It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne,
translation_verse: Ni atrakpoi ekpa ye̱ sẽi le̱ he ke̱ šika māṅō hũ, ni akãlaame̱ akpe̱te̱ sẽi le̱ he; ni šitámo̱he le̱, nidši ye̱ ebie̱ ke̱ ebie̱, ni dšatai enyo̱ damo̱ nidši le̱ amase̱i.

english_verse: and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Ni dšatai nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ damo̱ atrakpoi ekpa le no̱ ye̱ bie̱ ke̱ bie̱. Afeko nakai no̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱yeli ko maṅtše̱-yeli ko mli dã.

english_verse: Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Salomo kpudši fẽ ní eke̱-nuo̱ nii le̱, šika so̱ṅṅ ni, ni nibii fẽ ni yo̱ Lebanon kō le̱ šĩa le̱, šika ṅmīṅmi ni, dſie̱te̱i be̱ mli, abuu no fē̱i-fē̱i ye̱ Salomo yino̱ le̱.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ le̱dši ni ke̱ Huram tšũdši le̱ yaä Taršĩš; dā afii etẽ le̱ Taršiš le̱dši le̱ baä šikome, ni ame̱-hĩe šika ke̱ dſie̱te̱i ke̱ ſuo̱wn ke̱ ofoi ke̱ me̱leōi.

english_verse: Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Salomo da kple fè šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱mei fẽ ye̱ nifále̱ ke̱ nilẽ gbe̱fãṅ.

english_verse: Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo ke̱ enikēnii ba: dſie̱te̱i nibii ke̱ šĩka nibii ke̱ atadei ke̱ tawūnii ke̱ tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai, ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱i, dā afi.

english_verse: He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni eye maṅtše̱mei fẽ no̱ ke̱-dše̱ fā le̱ nā ke̱-yaši Filistibii ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Mizraim hũsũi ano̱.

english_verse: While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ hã dſie̱te̱i tšṍmo̱ tamo̱ te̱i ye̱ Ierusalem, ni tšenedrutšei hũ ehã ame̱tšṍmo̱ tamo̱ sikamoretšei ní yo̱ dšō̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, ye̱ fále̱ nā.

english_verse: Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri. Solomon Dies (
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i dše̱o̱ Mizraim ke̱ šikpõdši fẽ no̱ abahāa Salomo. (

english_verse: he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Ni Salomo ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ni ebi Rehabeam baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Ierobeam, Nebat bi le̱, nu he le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni Ierobeam kũ ese̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim ke̱-ba. *

english_verse: The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšũ ayakpēle̱ ke̱-ba. Ni Ierobeam ke̱ Israel fẽ ba ni ame̱ke̱ Rehabeam bawie ake̱:

english_verse: “Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
translation_verse: Otše̱ hã wo̱kõṅtšo le̱ tšĩ tšṍ; nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ bo le̱, femo̱ otše̱ súomo̱ ni wa le̱ ke̱ ekõṅtšo ni tšī ní eṅṍ-fõ wo̱no̱ le̱ fle̱fle̱, ni wo̱súmo̱o!

english_verse: Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bie̱ gbĩĩ etẽ le̱ nyekũa nyese̱ nyebaä miṅõ ekoṅ! Ni maṅ le̱ yiṅ ame̱te.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Rehabeam ke̱ hĩĩ onukpai ní damoo̱ etše̱ Salomo hĩe, beni eyo̱ dšeṅ lolo le̱, te adšina ni ekē̱: Mẽ ṅā nyewoo̱mi ni mike̱-yahã maṅ ne̱ hetō?

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši omli hĩ hã ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ ni ofe noni sa ame̱hĩe ne̱ ni ohãame̱ gbè dšũrõ le̱, no le̱ ame̱atšṍmo̱ otšũdši dāne̱.

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Ši ekwa onukpai le̱ aṅā ni ame̱wole̱ le̱, ni eke̱ oblahĩī ní dši etipẽṅfoi ni damoo̱ ehĩe le̱ te adšina,

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mẽ ṅā nye hũ nyewoo̱ ni wo̱ṅō-hã maṅ ne̱ ní ke̱mi ebawie ake̱: Femo̱ kõṅtšo ní otše̱ ṅõ-fō wo̱no̱ le̱ fle̱fle̱ ohãwo̱ le̱! hetō?

english_verse: His younger advisors said: Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak.
translation_verse: Ni oblahĩĩ ní dši etipẽṅfoi le̱ kē̱-le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni okē̱ maṅ le̱ ní ke̱o bawie ake̱: Otše̱ hã wo̱kõṅtšo le̱ tšī, ši bo le̱, femo̱le̱ fle̱fle̱ ohãwo̱ le̱, — bo̱ni okē̱ame̱ ne̱: Miwao se̱kpelo̱ ti fè mitše̱ he̱!

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ hãame̱ hetō ní wa, ni maṅtše̱ Rehabeam kwa onukpai le̱ aṅā ní ame̱wole̱ le̱,

english_verse: and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: ni eke̱ame̱ wie ye̱ oblahĩĩ le̱ aṅã-wō le̱ nā ekē̱: Mitše̱ hã nyekõṅtšo le̱ tšī, ši mi le̱ maṅmẽ nyekõṅtšo le̱ no̱; mitše̱ ke̱ kplebii yinye, ši mi le̱ mike̱ nyoṅmo̱ṅkrakroi aayinye!

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ši Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Šemaia, Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo le̱, ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: “The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops. Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ no̱: Nyekayaä, ni asaṅ nyeke̱ nyenyemimei le̱ akawua; nyeteṅ mofẽmo akũ ese̱ ke̱-ya ewe; edšake̱ mideṅ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ dše! Ni ame̱bo Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ toi, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ame̱te ni ame̱yatuaa Ierobeam doṅṅ.

english_verse: Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included
translation_verse: Ni Rehabeam hĩ ši ye̱ Ierusalem, ni etſa gbogboi ewo mãdši le̱ ahe ye̱ Iuda;

english_verse: Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam,
translation_verse: ke̱ Bet-Zur ke̱ Soko ke̱ Adulam

english_verse: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
translation_verse: ke̱ Gat ke̱ Mareša ke̱ Zif

english_verse: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin,
translation_verse: ke̱ Zora ke̱ Ayalon ke̱ Hebron ní dši Iuda ke̱ Benyamin mãdši ní atſa gbogboi awo he le̱.

english_verse: he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine,
translation_verse: Ni etſa gbogboi ewo mãdši le̱ ahe, ni eke̱ asafoiatše̱mei to mli ke̱ niyenii ke̱ mū ke̱ wein ni abua nā ato.

english_verse: And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Levibii le̱ šĩ ame̱mãdši ahe šikpõdši le̱ ke̱ ame̱nibii ní ame̱yo̱ le̱ ni ame̱ba Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem; edšake̱ Ierobeam ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ *ſïeame̱, ní ame̱kaye oso̱foi ame̱hã Iehowa. *

english_verse: Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
translation_verse: Ni *ewo le̱dientše̱ eso̱foi ehã hei groṅṅi le̱ ke̱ wo̱dši le̱ ke̱ tšinabii le̱ ni efe le̱. *

english_verse: For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon. Rehoboam's Family
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wadše Iuda maṅtše̱yeli le̱, ni ame̱hã Rehabeam, Salomo bi le̱, ná hewale̱, afii etẽ so̱ṅṅ; edšako̱ amenyie David ke̱ Salomo gbe̱ le̱ no̱ afii etẽ.

english_verse: Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱le̱ fo̱ bihĩĩ: Ieuš ke̱ Šemaria ke̱ Zaham.

english_verse: Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
translation_verse: Ni ese̱ le̱ ew̌e̱ Maaka, Absalom biyō le̱; ni eke̱le̱ fo̱ Abia ke̱ Atai ke̱ Ziza ke̱ Šelomit.

english_verse: so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king.
translation_verse: Ni Rehabeam wo Abia, Maaka bi le̱, onukpa ke̱ lumo̱ ye̱ enyemimei le̱ ano̱; edšake̱ eto eyiṅ ake̱ eewole̱ maṅtše̱.

english_verse: Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_verse: Ni efe enii nilē mli, ni edša ebihĩĩ le̱ fẽ ewo Iuda ke̱ Benyamin šĩkpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱, ye̱ mãdši ni atſa gbogboi awo he le̱ fẽ mli, ni ehãame̱ niyenii babaō, ni ebibī yei babaō ši ehãame̱.

english_verse: but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni efe efõṅ, edšake̱ eke̱ etšui efõõ no̱ ake̱ etao Iehowa se̱gbe̱.

english_verse: So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ye̱ maṅtše̱ Rehabeam yino̱ afi ní dši enumo̱ le̱ no̱, ake̱ Šišak, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, fã batua Ierusalem, edšake̱ ame̱tõ Iehowa no̱.

english_verse: He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ *mãdši ní atſa gbogboi awo he ni yo̱ Iuda le̱, ni eba Ierusalem. *

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbalo̱ Šemaia ba Rehabeam ke̱ Iuda onukpai ní ebua ame̱he nā ke̱-ba Ierusalem ye̱ Sišak hewo̱ le̱ aṅõ, ni ebakē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱; Nyekwami, nohewo̱ le̱ mi hū miṅmē̃ nyehe miwo Šišak deṅ!

english_verse: When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah: The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry,
translation_verse: Ši beni Iehowa na ake̱ ame̱ba ame̱he ši le̱, Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Šemaia ṅõ ake̱: Ame̱ba ame̱he ši, nohewo̱ le̱ mikpãtãṅ ame̱hĩe, ši mahereame̱ fiō ko, koni mimlila le̱ akatšṍ Šišak nine no̱ mītue mīſie Ierusalem no̱.

english_verse: he will conquer and rule them. Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ ame̱atšṍmo̱ etšũdši, koni ame̱ná ame̱le bo̱ni misúomo̱ yo̱ ke̱ bo̱ni šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ maṅtše̱yelii le̱ hũ asúomo̱ yo̱.

english_verse: Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Šišak, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-ba Ierusalem, ni elō Iehowa we le̱ dſetrii le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ dſetrii le̱, elō fẽ-kwa ke̱-te; ni esā elō šika tše̱ṅi ni Salomo fe le̱.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Rehabeam hã afe akō̱ble tše̱ṅi eto nãdšiaṅ, ni etu ewo bulo̱i ni buo̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ agbó le̱ nā le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ adeṅ.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
translation_verse: Ni befẽbe ni maṅtše̱ le̱ yaä Iehowa we le̱, bulo̱i le̱ baä ni ame̱bahĩeo̱, ni ame̱ke̱-kũo̱ ame̱se̱ ame̱ke̱-yatoo̱ bulo̱i le̱ atšũ le̱ mli ekoṅ.

english_verse: Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again. Rehoboam's Rule in Judah (
translation_verse: Ni ake̱-ni eba ehe ši hewo̱ le̱, Iehowa mlifũ le̱ dše eno̱ ni ekpatãã ehĩe kwrakwra; ni asaṅ ana nii kpakpai komei ye̱ Iuda he.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Agbene̱ le̱ Rehabeam he sãdši le̱, kleṅkleṅnii ke̱ se̱kpēnii le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ gbalo̱ Šemaia ke̱ ninalo̱ *Ido sãdši le̱ ní ake̱-kane wekukpã le̱ mli? Ni ta kã Rehabeam ke̱ Ierobeam teṅ dāne̱. *

english_verse: When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_verse: Ni Rehabeam ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ; ni ebi Abia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army.
translation_verse: ni Iudabii le̱ bo̱ oše; ni eba mli ake̱, beni Iudabii le̱ bo̱ oše le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ tſia Ierobeam ke̱ Israel mū le̱ fẽ nii ye̱ Abia ke̱ Iuda hĩe.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family.
translation_verse: Ani nyelee ake̱ Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, eṅõ Israel no̱ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ehã David ke̱ ebii le̱ ke̱-mīya nāno̱ ye̱ *ṅō kpãṅmo̱ nā lo? *

english_verse: But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled.
translation_verse: Ši Ierobeam, Nebat bi ní dši David bi Salomo tšũlo̱ le̱, te ši ni etše enuṅtšo̱ le̱ hĩe atũa.

english_verse: Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
translation_verse: Ni hĩĩ fõdši ní dši yakagbomei yafata ehe, ni ame̱wadše amehe ame̱ši Rehabeam, Salomo bi le̱; ni Rehabeam edako ni etsui esako, hewo̱ le̱ enyẽēame̱.

english_verse: Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him!
translation_verse: ni *dā lebi ke̱ gbe̱ke̱ le̱ ame̱šãa šã-afo̱lei ke̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ame̱hāa Iehowa, ni asaṅ ame̱too̱ hĩe-mā-abolo le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱ ye̱ okplō ni he tše le̱ no̱, ni ame̱sāa šika kanetšo ke̱ ehe kanei ni asuo̱ dā gbe̱ke̱ le̱; edšake̱ wo̱ le̱ wo̱feo̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbe̱nānii le̱, ši nye le̱ nyekwale̱! *

english_verse: But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front.
translation_verse: Ši Ierobeam hã káwolo̱i lo̱go̱ame̱ ke̱-yadse ame̱se̱gbe̱; ni ame̱ye̱ Iuda hĩegbe̱, ši káwolo̱i le̱ ye̱ ame̱se̱gbe̱.

english_verse: Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni aba Israelbii le̱ aši ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli; ši Iudabii le̱ ná hewale̱, edšake̱ ame̱ṅõ ame̱hĩe ame̱fõ Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱.

english_verse: Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
translation_verse: Ši Abia tiu Ierobeam, ni eyašõ mãdši ye̱ edeṅ: Betel ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱ Iešana ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱ Efron ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱.

english_verse: Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
translation_verse: Ni Ierobeam náá hewale̱ ko doṅṅ ye̱ Abia gbĩĩ le̱ amli; ni Iehowa tſale̱ nõ ni egbo.

english_verse: Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_verse: Ni Abia he sãdši ni eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ enifemo̱nii ke̱ ewiemo̱i le̱, aṅmã ye̱ gbalo̱ Ido šišitsõmo̱wolo le̱ mli. *

english_verse: They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: .] Ni ame̱tua lẽ̱̀koloi abũi le̱ hũ, ni ame̱lō tōi babaō ke̱ yomai, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Ierusalem.

english_verse: At once, Azariah went to Asa and said: Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
translation_verse: ni edše kpo ni eke̱ Asa yakpe ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nyeboami toi, Asa ke̱ Iuda ke̱ Benyamin fẽ! Iehowa kenye ye̱ gbĩĩ-abo̱ ní nyeke̱le̱ yo̱ le̱; ni ke̱dši nyetao ese̱gbe̱ le̱, eehā nyenale̱, ši ké̱ nyekwale̱ le̱, le̱ hũ eekwanye!

english_verse: But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱fĩmo̱ le̱ mli le̱ ame̱akpale ke̱-aba Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ, ni ame̱ataole̱, ni eehã ame̱nale̱. Ier.

english_verse: As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Ni beni Asa nu ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ ke̱ Obed gbalo̱ le̱, gbale̱ le̱, ená ekã ni edšie nihīnii le̱ ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ fẽ ke̱ mãdši ni ešõ ye̱ Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱ amli hũ, ni esā Iehowa afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ni yo̱ Iehowa koi le̱ hĩe le̱ ehẽ.

english_verse: Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ebua Iuda ke̱ Benyamin fẽ ke̱ gbo̱i ní dše̱ Efraim ke̱ Manase ke̱ Simeon ba bafata ame̱he le̱ anā ke̱-kpe; edšake̱ mei babaō tše ke̱-dše̱ Israel he bafata ehe, beni ame̱na ake̱ Iehowa, e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ke̱le̱ ye̱ le̱.

english_verse: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱babua ame̱he nā ye̱ Ierusalem ye̱ nyõṅ ní dši etẽ le̱ no̱ ye̱ Asa maṅtše̱yeli afi ni dší nyoṅma ke̱ enumo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kpãṅ ake̱ ame̱atao Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, se̱gbe̱ ke̱ ame̱tšui mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ ame̱susuma mū le̱ fẽ; Ios.

english_verse: Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Asa nye Maaka tete, ekpale̱ maṅnyeyeli, edšake̱ efe amãgã ko ní he yo̱ hĩegbēle ehã Ašera; ni Asa fo emãgã le̱, ni ešile̱ bo̱do̱bo̱do̱, nī eyašã ye̱ Kidron fā le̱ nā.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel.
translation_verse: Ši hei groṅṅi le̱ adšiee ye̱ Israel; kẽle̱ Asa tšui hī ke̱-wula ši ewala gbĩĩ abo̱ fẽ.

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Ni eyaṅō nii ní etše̱ feame̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ ke̱ nii ni le̱dientše̱ efeame̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ ke̱-ba Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱: dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika ke̱ nibiinibii.

english_verse: There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_verse: Ni ta ko ta ko baa āhũ ke̱-yaši Asa maṅtše̱yeli afi ni dši nyoṅmai-etẽ ke̱ enumo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Asa dšie dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ nitōhei le̱, ni etšũ ake̱-yahã Benhadad, Aram maṅtše̱ ni yo̱ Damasko le̱, ake̱:

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept.
translation_verse: Ni Benhadad bo maṅtše̱ Asa toi, ni etšũ etatše̱mei ní ame̱yatua Israel mãdši le̱, ni ame̱tſía Iyon ke̱ Dan ke̱ Abel-Maim ke̱ Naftali nitō-mãdši le̱ fẽ anii.

english_verse: Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said: You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army.
translation_verse: Ni nakai be le̱ mli le̱ Hanani, ninalo̱ le̱, ba Iuda maṅtše̱ Asa ṅõ ni eba-kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ake̱ni *oke̱ ohĩe fõ Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ no̱, ši oke̱ ohĩe efõõ Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱ hewo̱ le̱, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ ta le̱ edše odeṅ. *Ier.

english_verse: Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them.
translation_verse: Nto Kušbii ke̱ Lubbii le̱ ata le̱ fá babaō, ni ame̱ſīlii ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ hũ fá babaō dientše̱? Ni kẽle̱ ake̱-ni oke̱ ohĩe fõ Iehowa no̱ hewo̱ le̱, atuame̱ awo odeṅ.

english_verse: The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Iehowa yo̱ ne̱, ehĩṅme̱ii kpaä šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ no̱, ni edšieo̱ ehewale̱ kpo ehãa mei ní ame̱tšui ehĩ ke̱-wula ši ye̱ egbe̱fãṅ le̱ le̱. Oye kwašiai asane ye̱ ene̱ mli; nohewo̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ ṅme̱ne̱ no̱ ke̱-yaã ne̱ tai aate ši awoö!

english_verse: Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Ni na, Asa he sãdši le̱, kleṅkleṅnii ke̱ se̱kpēnii le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ mli.

english_verse: In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help.

english_verse: Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fūle̱ ye̱ efũhe ni ekpe̱ ehã ehe ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ le̱ mli. Ni ame̱ke̱le̱ ṅmẽ sā ní no̱ eyi obõ ke̱ tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai sro̱toisro̱toi ní afutu ye̱ tšofã-futumo̱ ṅā nā le̱ no̱, ni *ame̱šã nii babaō dientše̱ ame̱hãle̱. *

english_verse: He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ ta eto Iuda mãdši ni atſa gbogboi awo he le̱ fẽ mli, ni eke̱ asrafoi to Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Efraim mãdši le̱ ni etše̱ Asa ešõ le̱ amli.

english_verse: he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱-ni eyo̱ Iehowa gbè̱i le̱ ahe tšui hewo̱ le̱, edšie hei groṅṅi le̱ ni egbá wo̱ṅ-kōi le̱ ye̱ Iuda.

english_verse: Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along.
translation_verse: ni Levibii Šemaia ke̱ Netania ke̱ Zebadia ke̱ Asahel ke̱ Šemiramot ke̱ Iehonatan ke̱ Adonia ke̱ Tobia ke̱ Tob-Adonia ni dši Levibii le̱ fata amehe; ni Elišama ke̱ Iehoram, oso̱foi le̱, hũ fata amehe.

translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat te no̱ ni eda babaō dientše̱, ni emãmo̱ mõdši ke̱ nitōhei ye̱ Iuda,

translation_verse: ni eye̱ niyenii babaō ye̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ amli, ke̱ tabiloi kākãlo̱i ye̱ Ierusalem.

english_verse: from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans. Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yibo̱ ni akane ye̱ ame̱tše̱mei awei le̱ anā ne̱: Iudabii le̱ ateṅ mei akpekpei ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei dši: asafoiatše̱ Adna, ni tabilo̱i kãkãlo̱i akpei-ohai-etẽ fata ehe;

translation_verse: ni ese̱ le̱ asafoiatše̱ Iehohanan, ni mei akpei-ohai-enyo̱-ke̱-nyoṅmai-kpānyo̱ fata ehe;

english_verse: Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with
translation_verse: ni ese̱ le̱ Amasia, Zikri bi le̱ ni ṅõ ehe ehã Iehowa tšuidšũrõ nā le̱, ni hĩĩ kãkãlo̱i akpei-ohai-enyo̱ fata ehe.

english_verse: Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had

english_verse: These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
