english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-te Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?” “Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command.
translation_verse: Ni Ahab, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, kē̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ake̱: Ani oke̱mi aate Ramot-Gilead lo? Ni eherele̱ no̱ ake̱: Mi noṅṅ dši bo, ni mimaṅ le̱ noṅṅ dši omaṅ le̱; wo̱ke̱o aate ta le̱!

english_verse: But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
translation_verse: Ši Iehošafat kē̱ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Ofai ne̱, yabi Iehowa dāṅgbē ṅme̱ne̱!

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Ši Iehošafat kē̱: Ani Iehowa gbalo̱ ko be̱ bie̱ ne̱ doṅṅ, ni wo̱o̱yabi nii ye̱ eṅõ?

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Iehošafat ake̱: Mokome ye̱, ni kũle̱ wo̱o̱yabi Iehowa dāṅgbē ye̱ eṅõ, le̱ dši Mikaia, Imla bi le̱; ši mi le̱ misumo̱o̱ esane, edšake̱ egbaa ekpakpa ko ye̱ mihe, ake̱ dša efõṅ egbaã dāne̱. Ši Iehošafat kē̱: Maṅtše̱ akakē̱ nakai!

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ tšé̱ piafonyo ko ni ekē̱: Hã Mikaia, Imla bi le̱, aše̱ bie̱ mrãmrã!

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, trá ame̱maṅtše̱sẽii ano̱, ni ame̱wowō ame̱tadei, ni ame̱trá he ko kpatā ko ni yo̱ Samaria agbó le̱ nā le̱; ni gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ mīgbagbai ye̱ ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ni gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ gba nakai ame̱kē̱: Ya Ramot-Gilead, ni oyaye omanye; ši Iehowa batule̱ awo maṅtše̱ deṅ!

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Ni bo̱fo le̱ ni te Mikaia tšē̱mo̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ nābu kome egba gbale̱ kpakpa ehã maṅtše̱ le̱; nohewo̱ le̱ hã owiemo̱i le̱ atamo̱ ame̱teṅ mokome nõ, ni owie ekpakpa!

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Ši Mikaia kē̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ni Iehowa hĩe kã ne̱, noni mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ aakē̱mi le̱, no mawie!

english_verse: Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mikaia, ani wo̱ya Ramot-Gilead wo̱yawu, alo wo̱kaya? Ni ekē̱: Nyeyaä ni nyeyayea omanye, ni aatuame̱ awo nyedeṅ!

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Šii enyie po makão kitã ake̱ okagbami sane ko sane ko, ake̱ dša ano̱kwale ke̱ke̱ ye̱ Iehowa gbe̱i amli?

english_verse: Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Iehošafat ake̱: Ani mikē̱ē̱o̱ ake̱ egbaṅ ekpakpa ko ye̱ mihe, ake̱ dša efõṅ?

english_verse: Micaiah replied: I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyeboa Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ toi: Mina Iehowa tá esẽi le̱ no̱, ni ṅwei ta le̱ fẽ damo̱ eninedšũrõ ke̱ ebe̱ku.

english_verse: The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?” They talked about it for a while,
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱: Namo aayalaka Ahab, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, koni eya ni eyanyõ ye̱ Ramot-Gilead? Ni moko mīkē̱ ne̱ke̱, moko hũ mikē̱ ne̱ke̱.

english_verse: then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.” “How?” the Lord asked.
translation_verse: Ni mumo̱ le̱ dše kpo ba ni ebadamo̱ Iehowa hĩe ni ekē̱: Mi mayalakale̱! Ni Iehowa kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱ meni?

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Madše kpo mate ni mayatšṍ amale mumo̱ ye̱ egbalo̱i le̱ fã nā! Ni ekē̱: Oolakale̱ ni onine aaše̱ eno̱ hũ; ya ni oyafe nakai!

english_verse: Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni *Zedekia, Kenaana bi le̱, tši ba ni ebagbá Mikaia hĩe māã ni ekē̱: Nẽgbe̱ Iehowa Mumo̱ le̱ tšṍ dše mino̱ ni eke̱o bawie? *K.

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
translation_verse: Ši Mikaia kē̱: Na, bodientše̱ obana ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱; beni oodše̱ pia mli ke̱-ya pia mli ní oyatē ohe le̱!

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Nyeṅõa Mikaia ni nyeke̱le̱ akũa se̱ ayahãa Amon, mā le̱ṅ onukpa le̱, ke̱ Ioaš, maṅtše̱ bi le̱,

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: ni nyeyakē̱a ake̱: Bo̱ni maṅtše̱ kē̱ ne̱: Nyeṅõa mone̱ *nyewoa tšũṅ, ni nyeke̱ amanehũlũ abolo ke̱ amanehũlũ nu alē̱le̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní mate mayaye omanye ni maba. *

english_verse: Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!” Ahab Dies at Ramoth (
translation_verse: Ni Mikaia kē̱: Ke̱dši ote oyaye omanye oba fĩ, bēle̱ dšee Iehowa tšṍ mino̱ wie le̱! Ni esā ekē̱: Nyeboa toi, nye mãdši le̱ fẽ!

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Iehošafat ake̱: Mibatšake mihe ni maya ta le̱ nā; ši bo le̱ wo otadei le̱! Ni Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ tšake ehe ni ete ta le̱ nā.

english_verse: The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab.
translation_verse: Ši Aram maṅtše̱ le̱ ewo eſīlii le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ akitã ake̱: Nyeke̱ mo bibiō alo mo wulu ko akawua, ake̱ dša Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ke̱!

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ſīlii le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ na Iehošafat le̱, ame̱kē̱ ake̱: Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ne̱! ni ame̱gbá ke̱-ba ní ame̱ke̱le̱ abawu. Ši Iehošafat bo, ni Iehowa ye buale̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ hã ame̱dše ehe.

english_verse: And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ſīlii le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ na ake̱ dšee Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ni le̱, ame̱kpale ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Ši nū ko gbla egāi ni elee be ni etšẽ Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ šišigbe̱ dama le̱ ke̱ ṅweigbe̱ dama le̱ kpēhe le̱, nohewo̱ le̱ ekē̱ eſīli kudo̱lo̱ le̱ ake̱: Tšṍ onine ni oke̱mi adše ta le̱ nā, ši mipila!

english_verse: The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_verse: Ni ta le̱ mli wa nakai gbĩ le̱, ni ahīe Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ mli ke̱-damo̱ eſīli le̱ mli ye̱ Arambii le̱ ahĩe ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱; ni aafe hũlũ šinyõ mli le̱ egbo.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, kũ ese̱ ke̱-ba ewe le̱ ye̱ Ierusalem ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehošafat hĩ ši ye̱ Ierusalem. Ni esa efã gbe ekoṅ ke̱-yanyie maṅbii le̱ ano̱, ke̱-dše̱ Beeršeba ke̱-yaši Efraim gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ekpaleamo̱ ke̱-ba Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ.

english_verse: and told them: Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱ kodšolo̱i le̱ ake̱: Nyekwe̱a dšogbāṅ ye̱ noni nyeafe le̱ hewo̱! Edšake̱ dšee gbomei nyekodšoo̱ nyehāa, ši moṅ Iehowa ni, ni efata nyehe ye̱ atẽṅ-bū le̱ mli.

english_verse: So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyehãa Iehowa gbeyeišemo̱ ahĩa nyemli! Nyekwe̱a dšogbāṅ ni nyefea; edšake̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kũtũmpo̱o ke̱ hĩeaṅkwe̱mo̱ ke̱ nyōṅnihemo̱ be̱ ehe!

english_verse: The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
translation_verse: Ni befẽbe ní ake̱ bēi sane ko aadše̱ nyenyemimei ni yo̱ ame̱mãdšiaṅ le̱ aṅõ abahãnye le̱, lá ke̱ lá teṅ sane ni dšio, mla ke̱ kitã lo akpo̱ ke̱ kodšomo̱ hewo̱ nõ ni dšio, nyetsõaame̱ nā, beni afe ni ame̱kaye sõ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, koni mlifũ akaba nye ke̱ nyenyemimei le̱ ano̱. Kē̱ nyefe nakai le̱, nyeyeṅ sō.

english_verse: Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_verse: Ni na, oso̱fonukpa Amaria le̱ dši nyeno̱ onukpa ye̱ Iehowa sane-fẽ-sane gbe̱fãṅ, ke̱ Išmael bi Zebadia ni dši Iuda we le̱ lumo̱ le̱ hũ, ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ sane-fẽ-sane gbe̱fãṅ, ni Levibii le̱ hũ afe no̱kwe̱lo̱i ahãnye. Nyewadšea nyehe ni nyefea, ni Iehowa ke̱ ekpakpafelo̱ aahĩ ši!

english_verse: Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni Iehošafat še gbeyei, ni eko̱ efō eno̱ ake̱ eetao Iehowa se̱gbe̱, ni ešie̱ ake̱ ahĩ ṅmã ye̱ Iuda fẽ.

english_verse: Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever.
translation_verse: Ani dšee bo ni dši wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, oſie ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ bii le̱ ke̱-dše̱ omaṅ Israel hĩe, ni oṅõ-hã ošientše̱ Abraham sešibii le̱ ke̱-mīya nāno̱?

english_verse: Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱hĩ no̱, ni ame̱mã hekroṅkroṅ ye̱ no̱ ame̱hã ogbe̱i le̱ ame̱kē̱:

english_verse: You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, na, Amonbii le̱ ke̱ Moabbii le̱ ke̱ Seir goṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ ni *oṅmẽẽ Israel gbe̱ ni ame̱tuaame̱, be mli ní ame̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ame̱baä le̱, ši moṅ ame̱tšṍ aſã ke̱-dše̱ ame̱he, ni ame̱-kpãtãã ame̱hĩe le̱; *

english_verse: Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us.
translation_verse: kwe̱ bo̱ni ame̱too̱wo̱ nãdšiaṅ ni ame̱-ba ame̱baſiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ ogbe̱fãṅnõ ni oke̱-hãwo̱ ake̱ wo̱nõ le̱ no̱!

english_verse: Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
translation_verse: Wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱! aso okodšoṅame̱? Edšake̱ wo̱ le̱ wo̱be̱ hewale̱ ye̱ ne̱ke̱ ta babaō ne̱ ni baã wo̱no̱ ne̱ hĩe; ni wo̱-lee bo̱ni wo̱o̱fe, ši moṅ bo ono̱ wo̱hĩṅme̱ii dſere!

english_verse: While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple,
translation_verse: Ni Iuda mū le̱ fẽ damo̱ Iehowa hĩe, ke̱ ame̱gbekẽbii ke̱ ame̱ṅãmei ke̱ ame̱bihĩĩ hũ.

english_verse: So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley.
translation_verse: Wó̱ ni dši wó̱ le̱ nyefāa nyeke̱ame̱ ayakpea; na, ame̱tšṍ Ziz ṅmeṅme le̱ no̱ ke̱-mība, ni nyeayaninaame̱ ye̱ dšō̱ le̱ nā ye̱ Ieruel ṅã le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
translation_verse: Dšee nye nyebawu ta ne̱; nyetoa ni nyedamo̱a ši diṅṅ ni nyekwe̱a nyeyiwala ni Iehowa bahere, Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem! Nyekašea gbeyei ni nyetšui akafãa! Wó̱ le̱ nyefãa ni nyeke̱ame̱ ayakpea, edšake̱ Iehowa ke̱nye ye̱!

english_verse: Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii ni dše̱ Kahatbii le̱ ke̱ Korabii le̱ ateṅ le̱ te ši, ni ame̱dšie Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, yi ke̱ gbẽ wale̱ dientše̱.

english_verse: so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
translation_verse: Ni Amonbii ke̱ Moabbii le̱ hũ te ši wo Seir goṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱, ni ame̱fe-ame̱ musu ni ame̱kpãtã ame̱hĩe; nĩ beni amegbe Seirbii le̱ butū le̱, ame̱teṅ mo-fẽmo *ye bua enanyo ni ame̱ke̱-kpãtã-kpãtã ame̱hĩe. *

english_verse: When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground.
translation_verse: Ši beni Iudabii le̱ baše̱ būhe ní yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ame̱kwe̱ ta babaō le̱, na, ame̱dši gbohĩĩ so̱ṅṅ ní dſere ši ne̱, ni moko edšee mli.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ní dši gbĩ edſe̱ le̱ ame̱babua ame̱he nā ye̱ yidšiemo̱-dšō̱ le̱ṅ; edšake̱ dše̱i ame̱dšie Iehowa yi ye̱, nohewo̱ le̱ yidšiemo̱-dšō̱ atšé̱o̱ dše̱i ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid
translation_verse: Ni Nyoṅmo̱ he ṅmiṅmi mõmo̱ šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ maṅtše̱yelii le̱ fẽ, beni amenu ake̱ Iehowa ke̱ Israel henye̱lo̱i le̱ ewu le̱.

english_verse: to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace. Jehoshaphat Dies (
translation_verse: Nĩ Iehošafat maṅtše̱yeli le̱ no̱ dšo̱, edšake̱ *e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ehã ehe edšo̱le̱ ye̱ hefẽhe ke̱-kpe. *

english_verse: While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ se̱ le̱ Iehošafat, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ *Ahazia, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, yafe ekome; ši Ahazia feo̱ nibii fõdši. *

english_verse: Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done,
translation_verse: Ni enyie etše̱ Asa gbe̱ le̱ no̱, ni edšee no̱ ke̱-tšṍṍ afã, ni efe noni dša ye̱ Iehowa hĩe.

english_verse: but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ hei groṅṅi le̱ adšiee; edšake̱ maṅ le̱ eṅõko ame̱tšui ame̱hãko ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Iehošafat he sãdši ni eſe̱ le̱, tšutšunii ke̱ se̱kpēnii le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Iehu, Hanani bi le̱, sãdši ní eṅmã ewo Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ṅ le̱ amli.

english_verse: They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱le̱ fe ekome ni ame̱kpe̱ le̱-dši ni ake̱-ya Taršiš, ni ame̱kpe̱ le̱dši le̱ ye̱ Ezion-Geber.

english_verse: But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_verse: Ši Eliezer, Dodawahu bi ní dše̱ Mareša le̱, gba eši Iehošafat ake̱: Ake̱-ní oke Ahazia eyafe ekome hewo̱ le̱, Iehowa efite onitšumo̱i le̱! Ni le̱dši le̱ dſãra, ni ame̱nyẽẽ Taršiš le̱ ame̱ya.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Eyino̱ le̱ Edom tše Iuda hĩe atũa, ni ame̱dientše̱ ame̱wo maṅtše̱ ame̱hã ame̱he.

english_verse: The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa te Filistibii ke̱ Arabiabii ni yo̱ Kušbii le̱ amase̱i le̱ amumo̱ ši ewo Iehoram;

english_verse: Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tše̱ le̱ keame̱ nikēnii pī: dſie̱te̱i ke̱ šika ke̱ nibii ni dšra wa ke̱ Iuda mli mãdši ni atſa gbogboi awo he le̱ ekomei; ši maṅtše̱yeli le̱ eṅõ-hã Iehoram, edšake̱ le̱ dši kromo̱bi.

english_verse: After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders.
translation_verse: Ši beni Iehoram bõi etše̱ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ no̱ yeli ni ená hewale̱ le̱, egbe enyemimeihĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱ klante ke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ ateṅ meikomei hũ.

english_verse: Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night,
translation_verse: Ni Iehoram ke̱ esafoiatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ ſīlii fẽ ní eyo̱ foṅ ke̱-te dše̱i; ni ete ši nyōṅ ni eyatſia Edombii ni ebo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe le̱ ke̱ ſīlii le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ anii.

english_verse: but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time. Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ni Edom tše Iuda hĩe atũa ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱. No be le̱ mli noṅṅ Libna hũ tše ehĩe atũa; edšake̱ ekwa Iehowa, etše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
translation_verse: Asaṅ efe hei groṅṅi ye̱ Iuda gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ehã Ierusalembii le̱ bo̱ adſamaṅ, ni ehã Iuda dū gbe̱.

english_verse: One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said: I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni wolo ko dše̱ gbalo̱ Elia deṅ ke̱-ba eṅõ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, otše̱ David Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní onyiee otše̱ Iehošafat gbe̱i le̱ ke̱ Asa, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, gbè̱i le̱ ano̱,

english_verse: Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
translation_verse: ši moṅ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ agbē̱i le̱ ano̱ onyie, ni ohã Iuda ke̱ Ierusalembii le̱ ebo̱ adſamaṅ, tamo̱ bo̱ni Ahab we le̱ bo̱ adſamaṅ le̱, ni asaṅ ogbe onyemimei ni dše̱ otše̱ we le̱ ní bi ſēo le̱ he-wo̱ le̱,

english_verse: They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
translation_verse: ni ame̱fã ame̱batua Iuda, ni ame̱dſa ame̱yi no̱, ni ame̱lō nii fẽ ní anaä ye̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ eṅãmei le̱ ke̱-te, ni ašĩĩ binū ko ahããle̱, ake̱ dša Iehoahaz, ebihĩĩ le̱ ateṅ gbekẽ le̱ pe̱.

english_verse: After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱mei fẽ se̱ le̱ Iehowa ke̱ mũsũṅ-hela ko ni ebĩĩ tšámo̱ pīle̱.

english_verse: About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni ene̱ kã he gbĩĩabo̱ ke̱-yaši afii enyo̱ se̱ le̱, hela le̱ so̱ṅṅ hã emlinii tue, ni egbo ke̱ hedšramo̱. Ni emaṅbĩi le̱ ešãã nokonoko hããle̱ *tamo̱ bo̱ni ašã ahā etše̱mei le̱. *

english_verse: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
translation_verse: Ni efe nõfõṅ ye̱ Iehowa hĩe tamo̱ Ahab we le̱; edšake̱ etše̱ gbẽle le̱ se̱ le̱ ame̱ noṅṅ ame̱woo̱le̱ ṅā ní aahã eble akpãtã.

english_verse: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Ame̱ṅāwõ no̱ noṅṅ enyie, ni eke̱ Iehoram, Ahab bi ni dši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, te ta ni ame̱ke̱ Hazael, Aram maṅtše̱ le̱, yawu ye̱ Ramot-Gilead; ni Arambii le̱ pila Ioram.

english_verse: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
translation_verse: Ši ošrã ní bašrã Ahazia, ake̱ ete Ioram ṅõ le̱, edše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ deṅ; edšake̱ beni ete le̱, eke̱ Iehoram fã ni ame̱ke̱ Iehu, Nimši bi *ní Iehowa efo̱le̱ mũ ní ekpãtã Ahab we le̱ hĩe le̱, yakpe. *

english_verse: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
translation_verse: Ši Iehošabeat, maṅtše̱ biyō le̱, ṅõ Ioaš, Ahazia bi le̱, ni edšule̱ ke̱-dše̱ maṅtše̱ bihĩĩ le̱ ni abagbeame̱ le̱ ateṅ, ni eke̱le̱ ke̱ efufo̱hãlo̱ le̱ fē yato sāi atšũ le̱ṅ. Ni Iehošabeat ní dši maṅtše̱ Iehoram biyō ke̱ oso̱fo Iehoiada ṅã le̱, ake̱-ní Ahazia nyemiyō dšile̱ hewo̱ le̱, eṅõle̱ etē Atalia, koni ekagbele̱.

english_verse: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
translation_verse: Ši beni Ahazia nye Atalia na ake̱ ebi le̱ egbo le̱, ete ši ni ekpãtã maṅtše̱ sešibii le̱ fẽ hĩe ye̱ Iuda we le̱.

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ame̱ yatē ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ afii ekpa. Ni Atalia ye maṅnye ye̱ šikpoṅ le no̱.

english_verse: These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yakpa Iuda, ni ame̱bua Levibii le̱ anã ke̱-dše̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ fē mli, ke̱ Israel tše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai le̱, ni ame̱bakpe ye̱ Ierusalem.

english_verse: Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱dšie maṅtše̱ bi le̱ ke̱-dše kpo, ni ame̱ke̱ maṅtše̱ akekre le̱ fīle̱, ni ame̱ṅõ odase le̱ hũ ame̱wo edeṅ, ni ame̱wole̱ maṅtše̱; ni Iehoiada ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ fo̱le̱ mũ, ní ame̱kē̱ ake̱: Maṅtše̱ yi aná wala!

english_verse: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
translation_verse: Bo̱ni nyefe ne̱: Nyeteṅ mei ni babõi ame̱nitšumo̱ ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱, ye̱ oso̱foi ke̱ Levibii le̱ ateṅ le̱, amlidšāi etẽ mli ekome atšṍmo̱ agbónākwe̱lo̱i;

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ nyã́, ni mã le̱ mli dšo̱; ši Atalia le̱, ame̱ke̱ klante gbele̱.

english_verse: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
translation_verse: Ši afi ni dši kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱ Iehoiada wadše ehe, ni eṅõ mei ohahai ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱, Azaria, Ieroham bi le̱, ke̱ Išmael, Iehohanan bi le̱, ke̱ Azariahu, Obed bi le̱, ke̱ Maaseia, Adaia bi le̱, ke̱ Elišafat, Zikri bi le̱, ni eke̱ame̱ kpãṅ.

english_verse: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
translation_verse: Ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ kpãṅ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱. Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Na, maṅtše̱ le̱ binū le̱ aye maṅtše̱, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ewie ye̱ David bihĩĩ le̱ ahe le̱.

english_verse: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
translation_verse: ni mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome ahĩ maṅtše̱ we le̱, ni mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome hũ abi šišitō agbó le̱ nā; ši maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ahĩ ši ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ kpoi le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Ni moko akaya Iehowa we le̱, ake̱ dša oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ mei ní súmoo̱ ye̱ Levibii le̱ ateṅ le̱ ke̱ke̱; ame̱ ame̱ya dše̱i, edšake̱ ame̱ye̱ kroṅkroṅ; ši maṅ mū le̱ fẽ aye Iehowa gbe̱nā le̱ no̱.

english_verse: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii le̱ abo̱le maṅtše̱ le̱ he ke̱-kpe, mofẽmo ahĩe etawūnii ye̱ edẽ; ni mofẽmo ni abote šĩa le̱, agbele̱. Ni kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ mīdše kpo dšio, ēba šĩa dšio, ame̱hī ehe.

english_verse: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii le̱ ke̱ Iuda fẽ fe bo̱ni oso̱fo Iehoiada woamo̱ kitã le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱, ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo ṅõ ewebii ní baã nitšumo̱ ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱ mei ni kpaã nítšumo̱ ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱; edšake̱ oso̱fo Iehoiada hãã asafokui le̱ agbe aſã.

english_verse: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Iehoiada ṅõ akploi ke̱ tše̱ṅi wudši ke̱ tše̱ṅi bibii ní dši maṅtše̱ David nii ní yo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ ehã mei ohahai ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱.

english_verse: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
translation_verse: Ni eto maṅ mū le̱ fẽ edamo̱ ši, ni mofẽmo hĩe etawūnii ye̱ edẽ, ke̱-dše̱ šĩa le̱ ninedšũrõ koṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši šĩa le̱ abe̱ku koṅ le̱ no̱ ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ ke̱ šĩa le̱ hĩe, ni ame̱bo̱le maṅtše̱ le̱ he ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple.
translation_verse: Ši beni Atalia nu maṅbii ni hĩe foi ke̱-ba ni ame̱dšĩeo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ yi le̱ ablo̱mo̱ le̱, eba maṅbii le̱ aṅō ye̱ Iehowa we le̱;

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: ni ebakwe̱, ni na, maṅtše̱ le̱ damo̱ ešidamo̱he le̱ ye̱ šĩnā le̱ ši, nĩ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱kpālo̱i le̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ mase̱i, ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ mīnyã́ nĩ ame̱mīkpãkpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i, ni lalatše̱mei le̱ hũ ke̱ saṅkũi woo̱ no̱ ni alaä yidšiemo̱ lalai. Ke̱ke̱ ni Atalia gbla ehe atadei ni ekē̱: Apām, apām!

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
translation_verse: Ši oso̱fo Iehoiada fã́ mei ohahai ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei ní aṅõ-to ta le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeke̱le̱ adšea klempẽi le̱ ateṅ, ni mofẽmo ni aanyie ese̱ le̱, ake̱ klante agbele̱! Edšake̱ oso̱fo le̱ ekē̱ eto ake̱: Nyekagbeale̱ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱!

english_verse: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehoiada ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ *kpãṅ ake̱ ame̱afe Iehowa maṅ. *

english_verse: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ yabote Baal we le̱, ni ame̱kũmo̱ ame̱ſĩe ši, ni efo̱lešãla-te̱i le̱ ke̱ emãgãi le̱ ame̱kũmo̱, ni Matan, Baal oso̱fo le̱, hũ ame̱gbele̱ ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱i le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
translation_verse: Nĩ Iehoiada to Iehowa we le̱ nitšumo̱i le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱ ewo oso̱foi ke̱ Levibii le̱ ní David edša ame̱mlĩ eto Iehowa we le̱ adeṅ, koni ame̱šā Iehowa šã-afo̱lei le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni aṅmã ye̱ Mose mla le̱ mli le̱, ni ame̱fe ke̱ nyã́mo̱ ke̱ *lala, tamo̱ bo̱ni David to le̱. *

english_verse: Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ eke̱ agbónākwe̱lo̱i le̱ to Iehowa we le̱ agbói le̱ anā, koni moko ni ebule ehe ye̱ sane ko hewo̱ akabote mli.

english_verse: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ mei ohahai ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ hīenāno̱bii le̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱ no̱yelo̱i le̱ ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ fẽ, ni ame̱yaṅõ maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa we le̱, ni ame̱tšṍ agbó ní kwo̱ le̱ mli ke̱-ba maṅtše̱ we le̱, ni ame̱ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ batá maṅtše̱yeli sẽi le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehoiada ṅõ-hã mei ni tšuo̱ Iehowa we le̱ súomo̱ nitšumo̱ le̱; ni ame̱ hũ ame̱ke̱-bo̱ te̱gbalo̱i ke̱ ṅālo̱i apā, koni ame̱sā Iehowa we le̱ ehẽ, ke̱ dade ke̱ akō̱ble ṅālo̱i hũ, koni ame̱-sā Iehowa we le̱.

english_verse: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yafūle̱ ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ, ye̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ amase̱i; edšake̱ etšu nii kpakpai ye̱ Israel ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ hũ he.

english_verse: And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Atalia, yō fōṅ le̱, *bii le̱ ekũmo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱, ní asaṅ Iehowa we le̱ nibii kroṅkroṅi le̱ hũ ame̱ke̱ fẽ ehã Baalim. *

english_verse: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
translation_verse: Ni ebua oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ anā ke̱-kpe ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeyaä Iuda mã-dši le̱ amli, ni nyeyatšũa šika ye̱ Israel fẽ deṅ, ni ake̱-sā nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ dã afi, ni nyehe afea oyá ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ mli! Ši kẽle̱ Levibii le̱ ahe efee oyá.

english_verse: Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ fã́ ni akpe adeka kome, ni ake̱-mã Iehowa we le̱ agbó le̱ nā;

english_verse: He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
translation_verse: ni ašie̱ ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem ake̱ ame̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ tšũlo̱ *Mose onĩa ní eto ehã Israel ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ aba ebahã Iehowa. *K.

english_verse: The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni onukpai le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ná mīše̱, ni ame̱ke̱-ba ame̱bawo adeka le̱ mli āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni eyi to̱.

english_verse: These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new.
translation_verse: Ni nitšulo̱i le̱ tšu nii, ni sāmo̱ nitšumo̱ le̱ te no̱ dšogbāṅ ye̱ ame̱deṅ, ni ame̱sā Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ ame̱mã ši bo̱ni eheo̱, ni ame̱hã ená hewale̱.

english_verse: They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple. Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived.
translation_verse: Ni beni amegbe nā le̱, ame̱ke̱ šika ní ſe̱ le̱ ba maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Iehoiada hĩe, ni aṅõ-fe nibii ahã Iehowa we le̱: súomo̱ ke̱ afo̱lešā̃ he nibii, ke̱ liko̱liko̱i, ke̱ ši-ka ke̱ dſie̱te̱i nibii. Ni ame̱sãa šã-afo̱le ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ dāne̱ ye̱ Iehoiada gbĩĩ le̱ fẽ mli.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted.
translation_verse: Ši Iehoiada gbĕle se̱ le̱ Iuda onukpai le̱ ba ni ame̱bakoto maṅtše̱ le̱; ke̱-ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ boame̱ toi.

english_verse: The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kwa Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, we le̱, ni ame̱yasúmo̱ Aše-rim ke̱ amãgãi le̱. Ni mlifũ ba Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem no̱ ye̱ ame̱no̱tõmo̱ ne̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ etšũ gbalo̱i ke̱-ba ame̱ṅõ ní ame̱kpaleame̱ ke̱-ba Iehowa ṅõ ekoṅ, ni ame̱ye odase ame̱šiame̱; ši ame̱boo toi.

english_verse: In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus.
translation_verse: Ni eba mii ake̱ afi nākplo̱ se̱ le̱ Arambii ata le̱ fã batuale̱, ni ame̱ba Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem, ni ame̱bakpãtã maṅ onukpai le̱ fẽ hĩe ye̱ maṅbii le̱ ateṅ, ni ame̱he nii ni ame̱ha le̱ fẽ ame̱ṅõ-mãdše Damasko maṅtše̱ le̱.

english_verse: The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
translation_verse: Ši mei fio ke̱ke̱ Aram ta le̱ hĩe ke̱-ba, ni kẽle̱ Iehowa ṅõ ta babaō le̱ ewo ame̱deṅ; edšake̱ ame̱kwa Iehowa, ame̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; ni ame̱ke̱ kodšomo̱ ba Ioaš no̱.

english_verse: The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_verse: Ši ebii le̱, ke̱ dšatšui kplei ni ake̱-ſie eno̱ le̱, ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ sāmo̱ le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ maṅtše̱mei awolo le̱ šišitšõmo̱ le̱ mli. Ni ebi Amazia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel,
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo ko ba eṅõ ni ebakē̱: Maṅtše̱! kāhã Israel ta le̱ ke̱o miya; edšake̱ Iehowa be̱ Israel ni dši Efraimbii le̱ fẽ ateṅ.

english_verse: After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed
translation_verse: Ši Amazia ná ekã ni ekpla emaṅ le̱ ke̱-te Ṅō-dšō̱ le̱ṅ, ni eyatſia Seirbii le̱ ateṅ mei akpei-nyoṅma nii.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home, raided the towns in Judah between Samaria and Beth-Horon. They killed
translation_verse: Ši tabiloi le̱, ni Amazia hã ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ake̱ ame̱ke̱le̱ akaya ta le̱, batua Iuda mãdši le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Samaria ke̱-yaši Bet-Horon, ni ame̱gbe ame̱teṅ mei akpei-etẽ, ni ame̱ha nii babaō.

english_verse: But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.” The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!” Israel Defeats Judah (
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni eke̱le̱ wieo̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani wo̱wo bo maṅtše̱ ṅāwolo̱ lo? Fõmo̱! mẽba oohã atſiao nii? Ni gbalo̱ le̱ fõ ni ekē̱: Ake̱-ni ofe ne̱ ni oboo miṅāwō le̱ toi ne̱, mile ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ eto eyiṅ ake̱ eekpãtã ohĩe!

english_verse: King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: No mli Amazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, te adšina, ni etšũ ayakē̱ Ioaš, Iehu hi Iehoahaz bi ni dši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Ba ní wo̱kwe̱kwē̱ wo̱hĩeaṅ!

english_verse: Jehoash sent back a reply that said: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Ši Ioaš, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, tšũ aya-kē̱ Amazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ake̱: *Ṅmei-tšo ni yo̱ Lebanon le̱ tšũ ayakē̱ tšenedrutšo ni yo̱ Lebanon le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ obiyō le̱ ohã mibinū le̱ gblã! Ši ṅãṅ kolo ko ni yo̱ Lebanon le̱, baho ni enãnā ṅmei-tšo le̱ no̱. *Kodš.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Okē̱ ake̱: Na, migbe Edom! Hewo̱ lo̱ otšui ewó ono̱ ake oſã. Agbe̱ne̱ tá owe le̱! Mẽba oſe̱o̱ ohĩekpãtãmo̱ he, ní bo ke̱ Iuda fẽ agbe ši?

english_verse: so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Ni Ioaš, Israel, maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-ba, ni eke̱ Amazia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ba-kwe̱kwē̱ ame̱hĩeaṅ ye̱ Bet-Šemeš ni dši Iuda nō le̱.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Ni atſia Iuda nii ye̱ Israel hĩe, ni mofẽmo dšo foi ke̱-te ebū mli.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Ši Iuda maṅtše̱ Amazia ni dši Iehoahaz bi Ioaš bi le̱, Israel maṅtše̱ Ioaš mõle̱ ye̱ Bet-Šemeš, ni eke̱le̱ ba Ierusalem. Ni ebakũmo̱ Ierusalem gbogbo le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Efraim agbó le̱ nā ke̱-yaši koṅ agbó le̱ nā, ninetalo̱i ohai-edſe̱.

english_verse: Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Ši Amazia he sādši ní eſe̱ le̱, kleṅkleṅnii le̱ ke̱ se̱kpẽnii le̱, ani aṅmãko ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ mli?

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱-dše̱ beyino̱ ni Amazia kpale ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa se̱ le̱, *ame̱te eyino̱ apām ye̱ Ierusalem. Ni edšo foi ke̱-te Lakiš; ši ame̱tšũ atiule̱ ke̱-te Lakiš; ni aya-gbele̱ ye̱ dše̱i. *

english_verse: His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱wóle̱ ame̱fõ okpo̱ṅo̱i ano̱, ni ame̱bafũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ Iuda mã le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging.
translation_verse: Ni Uzia fe tše̱ṅi ke̱ akploi ke̱ dadefaii ke̱ dadedamai ke̱ gãii ke̱ akromiate̱i tete ehãame̱, ni ame̱ṅõ-hã ta mū le̱ fē.

english_verse: Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Uzia ye kpiti ke̱-yaši egbẽle gbĩ, ni *ehĩ ši ye̱ helatše̱mei awe ke̱ ekpiti le̱; edšake̱ atšĩle̱ Iehowa we le̱ gbe̱. Ni ebi Iotam kwe̱o̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱, ni ekodšoo̱ šikpoṅ le no̱ bii le̱. *

english_verse: Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
translation_verse: Ši Uzia he sãdši ni eſe̱ le̱, kleṅkleṅnii ke̱ se̱kpēnii le̱, gbalo̱ *Iesaia, Amoz bi le̱, ṅmã. *Ies.

english_verse: Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall. God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world. Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
translation_verse: Ni ehã ake̱ ṅã fe tšõnei ye̱ Ierusalem ni aṅõ-to mõdši ní kwō̱lo̱ ke̱ gbogbokodši ano̱, koni ake̱tšẽrẽ gãii, ni ake̱-fō te̱i wudši. Ni egbe̱i dšidše ke̱-te šoṅṅ dientše̱; edšake̱ eye̱ nākpe̱ bo̱ni aye abuale̱ ni ená hewale̱ le̱.

english_verse: God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ ye buale̱ ye̱ Filistibii le̱ ke̱ Arabiabii le̱ ni yo̱ Gur-Baal le̱, ke̱ Meunbii le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Uzia eye afii nyoṅma ke̱ ekpa, beni ebabõi maṅtše̱yeli le̱, ni eye maṅtše̱ afii nyoṅmai-enumo̱ ke̱ enyo̱ ye̱ Ierusalem; ni enye gbe̱i dši Iekolia ni dše̱ Ierusalem le̱.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Ši beni ená hewale̱ le̱, etšui *wó ehe no̱ ni ehã ehãe kpãtã, ni eto Iehowa, e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱; edšake̱ ete Iehowa so̱lemo̱tšũ le̱ṅ, ní eyašã tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ye̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma-šãlate̱ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Ni Amonbii le̱ ke̱ nikēnii bahã Uzia, ni egbe̱i dšidše ke̱-te Mizraim kpokpai ano̱; edšake̱ edše agbo naakpa.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Ni Uzia mãmo̱ mõdši ni kwō̱lo̱ ye̱ Ierusalem, ye̱ koṅ agbó le̱ no̱ ke̱ dšō̱ le̱ṅ agbó le̱ no̱ ke̱ gbogbo le̱ lo̱go̱mo̱he le̱, ni etſa gbogboi ewo he.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ emãmo̱ mõdši ni kwō̱lo̱ ye̱ ṅā le̱ no̱ hũ, ni etša nubui pī; edšake̱ eye̱ koloi babaō ye̱ dšō̱ šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ni asaṅ eye̱ hũlo̱i ke̱ weintrom-sālo̱i ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱ ke̱ Karmel no̱; edšake̱ esumoo̱ hũmo̱.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Asaṅ Uzia ye̱ tabilo̱i ni fãa ta asafoiaṅ, ye̱ ame̱yibo̱ ní woloṅmālo̱ Ieiel ke̱ no̱kwe̱lo̱ Maaseia kane le̱ nā, ni Hanania ni dši maṅtše̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ ateṅ mokome le̱ šiši ame̱yo̱.

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Uzia mli fũ, ni ehĩe tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ṅe̱sũ ye̱ edeṅ ni eke̱-bašã tšofã-ke̱-ṅma; ni beni emli fũ wo oso̱foi le̱, kpiti ſie ehĩenā, ye̱ oso̱foi le̱ ahĩe, ye̱ Iehowa we le̱, ye̱ tšofã-ke̱-ṅma-šãlate̱ le̱ mase̱i.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Ni beni oso̱fonukpa Azaria le̱ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ fẽ kwe̱le̱ le̱, na, kpiti eſie ehĩenā. Ni ame̱tšire̱le̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i oyá, ni le̱dientše̱ hũ ehe fe oyá ke̱-dše kpo, edšake̱ Iehowa mīpĩle̱.

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Ni Uzia ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei le̱ amase̱i ye̱ maṅtše̱mei afũhe šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ ame̱-kē̱; Kpitiyelo̱ dšile̱! Ni ebi Iotam baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni efe noni dša ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, tamo̱ bo̱ni etše̱ Uzia fe le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱; *tše̱bele̱ ebotee Iehowa so̱lemo̱tšũ le̱ṅ. Ši maṅ le̱ kã ame̱fitemo̱ le̱ he lolo. *

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Ni Iotam tšṍ agbo; edšake̱ esā egbē̱i le̱ ye̱ Iehowa, e-Nyoṅme̱ le̱, hĩe.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Ši Iotam he sãdši ní eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ etai le̱ ke̱ enifemo̱nii le̱ fẽ le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Israel ke̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ mli.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Ni Iotam ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni afũle̱ ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ. Ni ebi Ahaz baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: Ni ešãšã afo̱lei ke̱ tšofãi-ke̱-ṅmai ye̱ hei groṅṅi le̱ ke̱ *goṅkpo̱i le̱ ano̱ ke̱ tšo-fẽ-tšo ni ebu kusū šiši. *

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ nyetſa fai ši ake̱ nyemīṅõ Iudabii ke̱ Ierusalembii nyefe nyenyṍ-dšihĩĩ ke̱ nyenyṍdšiyei. Aso bĕle̱ nye le̱ nyetõko Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, no̱ lo?

english_verse: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeboami toi, ni nyehãa nyenyemimei le̱ ni nyeyaṅõ-ame̱ nom le̱ akũa ame̱se̱ ayaä; edšake̱ Iehowa mlifũ ní nā wa kã nyeno̱!

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Efraimbii le̱ anukpai le̱ ateṅ meikomei ni dši Azaria, Iohanan bi le̱, ke̱ Berekia, Mešilemot bi le̱, ke̱ Iehizkia, Šalum bi le̱, ke̱ Amasa, Hadlai bi le̱, te ši wo mei ni dše̱ ta le̱ṅ baã le̱,

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: ni ame̱kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeke̱ nomi le̱ akabaã bie̱! Edšake̱ nyetſa fai ši ake̱ nyeaṅõ Iehowa no̱ tõmo̱ ko nyebafõ wo̱-no̱ nyeši wohe ešai ke̱ wo̱no̱tõmo̱i le̱ ano̱ le̱; ši wo̱tõmo̱ le̱ fá momo, ni mlifũ ní nā wa kã Israel no̱!

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni tabilo̱i le̱ šĩ nomi le̱ ke̱ hānii le̱ ye̱ lume̱i le̱ ke̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ hĩe.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help (
translation_verse: Ni hĩĩ ní atšĩ ame̱gbe̱ii atã le̱ te ši, ni ame̱he nomi le̱, ni ame̱teṅ *mei fẽ ní nyie yayai le̱, ame̱ṅõ hānii le̱ eko ame̱bumo̱ame̱ ni ame̱woame̱ atadei, ni ame̱woame̱ tokotai, ni ame̱hãame̱ nii ame̱ye, ni ame̱sā ame̱hãame̱ nu amenu, ni ame̱-kpaame̱ mũ, ni ame̱ṅõ ame̱teṅ mei fẽ ni nyẽẽ anyie le̱ ame̱trá tedšii ano̱, ni ame̱-ke̱ame̱ ba Ieriko, tẽṅi amã le̱ṅ, ye̱ ame̱-nyemimei le̱ aṅõ, ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Samaria. *Abe̱i

english_verse: Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places. Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help.
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii le̱ hũ ebatua mãdši ní yo̱ dšō̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ke̱ Iuda wuoyigbe̱ le̱, ni ame̱ṅõ Bet-Šemeš ke̱ Ayalon ke̱ Gederot ke̱ Soko ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱ Timna ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ke̱ Gimzo ke̱ ehe mãdši le̱, ni ame̱bahī dše̱i.

english_verse: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Israel maṅtše̱ Ahaz hewo̱ lo̱ Iehowa eba Iuda ši; edšake̱ ebo̱ nye-nyeṅtſi ye̱ Iuda, ni etõ Iehowa no̱ babaō.

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Ši efĩmo̱ be le̱ mli le̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅtše̱ Ahaz ne̱ noṅṅ kã he ētõ Iehowa no̱ lolo.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ešãa afo̱lei ehãa Damasko nyoṅmo̱i le̱ ni tſiale̱ nii le̱, ni ekē̱o̱ ake̱: Aram maṅtše̱mei le̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ yeo̱ buaä-ame̱ hewo̱ le̱ mašã afo̱le mahãame̱, ni ame̱ye ame̱buami hũ! Ši ame̱ moṅ ame̱-bã eke̱ Israel fẽ hĩe kpãtã.

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni Ahaz bua Nyoṅmo̱ we lo̱ nibii lo̱ anā, ni edſăra Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ nibii le̱, ni eṅã́mo̱ Iehowa we le̱ šĩnāi le̱, ni efe afo̱lešãlate̱i ehã ehe ye̱ Ierusalem koṅ-fẽ-koṅ.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: Ni efe hei groṅṅi ye̱ Iuda maṅ-fẽ-maṅ no̱, koni ašã tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ahã nyoṅmo̱i krokomei, ni ewo Iehowa, etše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mlila.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Ši ehe sãdši ni eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ enifemo̱-nii le̱, kleṅkleṅnii ke̱ se̱kpēnii le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ mli.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Ni Ahaz ke̱ etše̱mei le̱ yawo̱, ni ame̱fũle̱ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ, ye̱ Ierusalem; ši ame̱ke̱le̱ *eyaa Israel maṅtše̱mei afũhei le̱. Ni ebi Hezekia baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ ese̱. *

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: Ni efe noni dša ye̱ Iehowa hĩe, tamo̱ bo̱ni etše̱ David fe le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Ni ehã Levibii le̱ yadamo̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ ṅoṅoi ke̱ be̱dši ke̱ saṅkũi le̱ ye̱ *David ke̱ Gad, maṅtše̱ ninalo̱ le̱, ke̱ Natan, gbalo̱ le̱, kitã le̱ nā; edšake̱ Iehowa kitã ni etšṍ gbalo̱i le̱ ano̱ ewo ni. *

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni beni agbe šã-afo̱le le̱ nā le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní ke̱le̱ yo̱ dše̱i le̱ koto ši ni ame̱so̱le.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: Ni eṅõ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ke̱-te mli, ni ebua ame̱nā ye̱ he kpatā ko ni yo̱ bokãgbe̱ le̱,

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ etõ ni ame̱fe efõṅ ye̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, hĩe, ni ame̱-kwale̱; ni ame̱tšṍ ame̱hĩe ke̱-dše̱ Iehowa šihīle̱he le̱, ni ame̱tšṍ ame̱kotose̱ ame̱hãle̱;

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: Ši na, we̱tše̱mei le̱ enyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā, ni wo̱bihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ wo̱biyei le̱ ke̱ wo̱ṅãmei le̱, aṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te ye̱ ene̱ hewo̱

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Mibii! agbe̱ne̱ nyekafea hedšõ; edšake̱ Iehowa ehalanye ní nyedamo̱ ehĩe ni nyesúmo̱le̱ ni nyetšṍmo̱ esúolo̱i ke̱ tšo-fã-ke̱-ṅma šālo̱i.

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: ni nibii fẽ hũ ní maṅtše̱ Ahaz bule ye̱ etõmo̱ le̱ mli, beni eyeo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱, wo̱sā ni wo̱feame̱ kroṅkroṅ, ni na, ame̱ye̱ Iehowa afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ hĩe!

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Hezekia te ši lebi mãṅkpa, ni ebua mã le̱ṅ onukpai le̱ anā, ni eyiṅ ke̱-te Iehowa we le̱.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ tšinahĩĩ kpawo ke̱ tō-agboi kpawo ke̱ tōbii kpawo ke̱ tōkpakpoi hũ kpawo ba ni ake̱-šã eša-afo̱le ahã maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ke̱ hekroṅkroṅ le̱ ke̱ Iuda; ni efã́ Aaronbii ni dši oso̱foi le̱ ake̱ ame̱ke̱-šã afo̱lei ye̱ Iehowa afo̱lešã-late̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱foi le̱ gbeame̱, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱-lá le̱ fe eša-afo̱le ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, koni ame̱ke̱-kpãtã ame̱hã Israel fẽ; edšake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ fã́ ake̱ šã-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ eša-afo̱le le̱ ašã ahã Israel fẽ.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii le̱ hĩe David lala nibii le̱ ke̱-damo̱ ši, ni oso̱foi le̱ hũ hĩe te̱tre̱mantre̱i.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Ni Hezekia fã́ ake̱ ašã šã-afo̱le ye̱ afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱; ni beni abõi šã-afo̱le le̱ ši le̱, keke̱ ni abõi Iehowa lalai le̱ alamo̱ ke̱ te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ akpãmo̱ ye̱ Israel maṅtše̱ David lala nibii le̱ anā.

english_verse: and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
translation_verse: Ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ kũla ši; ni lalo̱i le̱ la ni akpã te̱tre̱mantre̱i le̱ hũ āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní agbe šã-afo̱le le̱ nā.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hezekia here no̱ ni ekē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nyefe nyehe kroṅkroṅ nyehā Iehowa; nyetšia nyebe̱ṅke̱a ní nyeke̱ afo̱lei ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei abaä Iehowa we le̱! Ni asafo le̱ ke̱ afo̱lei ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei ba, ni mofẽmo ni yo̱ he tšui le̱ eke̱ šã-afo̱lei ba.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Ši oso̱foi le̱ ayi fáá bo̱ni ame̱anyẽ šã-afo̱lei le̱ fẽ ahe wodši ame̱kplo̱; nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱nyemimei, Levibii le̱, waame̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni agbe nitšumo̱ le̱ nā ní oso̱foi le̱ fe ame̱he kroṅkroṅ; edšake̱ Levibii le̱ moṅ bo̱ mo̱deṅ ni ame̱fe amehe kroṅkroṅ fè oso̱foi le̱.

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ šã-afo̱le le̱ fá babaō ke̱ šidā-afo̱lei le̱ ahe *fo̱i le̱ ke̱ †dā̃-afo̱lei ní fata šā̃-afo̱le-fẽ-šā̃-afo̱le he le̱. Ni ato Iehowa we le̱ súomo̱ le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱. *

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: Ši Hezekia ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ná mīše̱ ye̱ sāmo̱ ní Nyoṅmo̱ esā maṅ le̱ eto le̱ hewo̱; edšake̱ afe nii ne̱ oyá.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱mã sane le̱ no̱ mĩ́ ake̱ ayašie̱ ye̱ Israel mŭ le̱ fẽ, ke̱-dše̱ Beer-šeba āhũ ke̱-yaſie Dan, koni ame̱ha ní ame̱baye Hehō le̱ ame̱hã Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ye̱ Ierusalem; edšake̱ ame̱yekole̱ ke̱ mei babaō nakai, tamo̱ bo̱ni aṅmã le̱, dã.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nyekafea nyehe kue̱ṅtilo̱i tamo̱ nyetše̱mei le̱; ši moṅ nyekpãa nyenine mli nyehãa Iehowa, ni nyebaä ehekroṅkroṅ le̱ ni efele̱ kroṅkroṅ ke̱-mīya nāno̱ le̱, ni nyesúmo̱a Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, koni emlifũ ni nā wa le̱ adše nyeno̱!

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Ni mei babaō babua ame̱he nā ye̱ Ierusalem, koni ame̱ye akpĩtĩ gbĩdšũrõ le̱ ye̱ nyõṅ ni dši enyo̱ le̱ no̱, asafo babaō dientše̱.

english_verse: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱te ši ni ame̱yadšie afo̱lešãlate̱i ni yo̱ Ierusalem le̱, ni tšofã-ke̱-ṅma šā̃nii le̱ hũ ame̱dšie fẽ, ní ame̱lō ame̱yawo Kidron fā le̱ mli.

english_verse: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa bo Hezekia toi, ni etšá maṅ le̱.

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii le̱ ní ba Ierusalem le̱ ye akpĩtĩ gbĩdšũrõ le̱ gbĩĩ kpawo so̱ṅṅ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ kpeteṅkple; ni Levibii le̱ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ dšie Iehowa yi gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ, ni ame̱ke̱ lala nibii ní nā wa la ame̱hã Iehowa.

english_verse: Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
translation_verse: Ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ te adšinã ake̱ ame̱aye gbĩĩ kpawo hũ ame̱fata he, ni ame̱ye gbĩĩ kpawo le̱ ke̱ nyã́mo̱.

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda asafo mū lo̱ fẽ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ná mīše̱, ke̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ ní dše̱ Israel ba le̱, ke̱ gboi ni dše̱ Israel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ba le̱, ke̱ gbo̱i ni yo̱ Iuda le̱ hũ.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Ni anyã babaō ye̱ Ierusalem; edšake̱ ke̱-dše̱ Salomo, David bi ni dši Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, yino̱ le̱, anako eko ni tamo̱ no ye̱ Ierusalem dã.

english_verse: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱foi Levibii le̱ te ši ni ame̱dšō̱ maṅ le̱, ni anu ame̱gbē, ni ame̱so̱lemo̱ le̱ yaše̱ ešihĩle̱he kroṅkroṅ le̱ ye̱ ṅwei.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: Asaṅ ame̱häa mei fẽ ni akane ye̱ ame̱weku le̱ mli, ní dši ame̱bii abifabii ke̱ ame̱ṅãmei ke̱ ame̱bihĩĩ ke̱ ame̱biyei fẽ anõ ye̱ asafo le̱ fẽ mli; edšake̱ ame̱ke̱ ano̱kwa ní ame̱yeo̱ ye̱ nii kroṅkroṅi le̱ ahe le̱ tšõo̱ ake̱ ame̱fe ame̱he kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Asaṅ efá maṅbii ni yo̱ Ierusalem le̱ ake̱ ame̱hã oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ agbe̱fãṅnō le̱, beni afe ni ame̱hĩe Iehowa mla le̱ mli ni awa.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii ke̱ Iudabii ni yo̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ amli le̱ hũ ke̱ tšinai ke̱ tôi amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome, ke̱ nii kroṅkroṅi ní ame̱dšō̱ no̱ ame̱ke Iehowa, ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome ba, ni ame̱batoame̱ kuikui.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Nyõṅ ní dši etẽ le̱ no̱ ame̱ke̱ kui le̱ bõi šiſiemo̱, ni nyõṅ ní dšĩ kpawo le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱gbe nā.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Ni beni Hezekia ke̱ onukpai le̱ ba ni ame̱bana kui le̱, ame̱dšie Iehowa ke̱ emaṅ Israel yi.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Ni Hezekia bi oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ asane ye̱ kui le̱ ahewo̱.

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fonukpa Azaria ni dše̱ Zadok we le̱ here no̱ ake̱: Ke̱-dše̱ beyino̱ ní ake̱ no̱wómo̱-afo̱lei le̱ bõi Iehowa we le̱ bā ne̱, wo̱yeo̱ nii ni wo̱tō̱ro̱ö̱ ni efeo babaō tete; edšake̱ Iehowa edšō̱ emaṅ le̱, ni noni ſe̱ le̱ dši ne̱ke̱ nii babaō ne̱.

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hezekia fã́ ake̱ asā tšũi ye̱ Iehowa we le̱; ni ame̱sā,

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: ni Iehiel ke̱ Azazia ke̱ Nahat ke̱ Asahel ke̱ Ierimot ke̱ Iozabat ke̱ Eliel ke̱ Ismakia ke̱ Mahat ke̱ Benaia dši no̱kwe̱lo̱i ni yo̱ Konania ke̱ enyemi Šimei šiši, bo̱ni maṅtše̱ Hezekia ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ no̱ lumo̱ Azaria toame̱ le̱.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Ni Kore, Imna bi ni dši Levinyo ni kwe̱o̱ bokãgbe̱ agbó le̱ nā le̱, dši moni kwe̱o̱ nikēnii ní abakeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ suomo̱ nā le̱, ni edšaä Iehowa no̱wómo̱-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ nii kroṅkroṅi fè fẽ le̱.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: sõro hĩĩ ní akane ye̱ ame̱wekukpã nā, ke̱-dše̱ mei ní eye afii etẽ no̱ ke̱-yaä le̱ ní dši mei fẽ ní baã Iehowa we le̱, ame̱baheo̱ ame̱gbe̱fãṅnõ dā gbĩ, ní ame̱-batšuo̱ ame̱gbe̱nānitšumo̱ ye̱ ame̱safokui le̱ anã le̱,

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Asaṅ Aaron bii, ni dši oso̱foi ni yo̱ ame̱mãdši le̱ ahewo̱ šikpõdši le̱ ano̱, ye̱ maṅ-ſẽ-maṅ mli le̱, ateṅ le̱ hĩĩ komei ye̱ ní atšī ame̱gbe̱ii atã, ni ame̱ṅõo̱ oso̱foi le̱ ateṅ hĩĩ fẽ ke̱ Levibii lo̱ ateṅ mei fẽ ní akane ye̱ wekukpã le̱ mli le̱ agbe̱fãṅnii ame̱hãa-ame̱.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: Ni nitšumo̱ fẽ ni ebõi ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we lo̱ súomo̱ le̱ ke̱ mla le̱ ke̱ kitã le̱ he, ni eke̱-tao e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ se̱gbe̱ le̱, etšui mũ lo̱ fẽ eke̱-fe, *ni eſere. *Lal.

english_verse: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱blo̱ ke̱ gbẽ wāle̱ ye̱ Iudafoi awiemo̱ le̱ mli ame̱tšé̱ Ierusalembii ní yo̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ le̱, koni ame̱wo ame̱he gbeyei ni ame̱hã ame̱dšidšā, beni afe ni ame̱ṅõ maṅ le̱.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: Ani nyelee noni mike̱ mitše̱mei le̱ fe šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ bii fẽ le̱? Ani šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ mãdši le̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ enyẽ ame̱šikpoṅ le̱ yiwala ehere ke̱-dše̱ mideṅ pẽṅ lo?

english_verse: The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa here Hezekia ke̱ Ierusalembii le̱ ayiwala ye̱ Sanherib, Ašur maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ mei krokomei fẽ adeṅ ne̱, ni ewaame̱ ye̱ hefẽhe ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mei babaō babua ame̱he nā, ni ame̱tšĩmo̱ nubui le̱ fẽ ke̱ fā ní hoo̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ teṅ le̱ ahĩṅme̱ii, ni ame̱kē̱: Mẽhewo̱ Ašur maṅtše̱mei le̱ aaba ni ame̱baná nu babaō?

english_verse: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
translation_verse: Ni ená ekã, ni esā gbogboi ní *ekũmo̱ le̱ fẽ, ni ehã kwo̱ ke̱-se̱ mõdši ni kwŏ̱lo̱ le̱ ahe, ni etſa gbogbo kroko, hũ ewo maṅ le̱ he, ni ewadše Milo ye̱ David mã le̱ṅ, ni efe tawūnii ke̱ tše̱ṅi babaō. *

english_verse: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
translation_verse: Ene̱ se̱ le̱ Ašur maṅtše̱ Sanherib tšũ etšũdši ke̱-ba Ierusalem, ni etšũame̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Hezekia ke̱ Iudabii fẽ ní yo̱ Ierusalem le̱ aṅõ ekē̱:

english_verse: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Ašur maṅtše̱ Sanherib kē̱ ne̱: Mẽ no̱ nyehĩe kã, hewo̱ ni nyetrá Ierusalem ni abo̱ nsra awo he le̱ lolo?

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyekahãa Hezekia mīšišiuanye ní elakaänye ne̱ke̱, ni asaṅ nyekaheale̱ nyeyea! Edšake̱ dšeṅmaṅ ko lo maṅtše̱yeli ko nyoṅmo̱ nyẽ-ko emaṅbii ayiwala ahere ke̱-dše̱ mideṅ lo mitše̱mei le̱ adeṅ, āhũ ní nye-Nyo-ṅmo̱ le̱ aanyẽ nyeyiwala ahere ke̱-dše̱ mideṅ!

english_verse: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
translation_verse: Ni esā eṅmlã wodši hũ eke̱-basopa Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ni ekē̱ ye̱ ehe wo̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ mãdši le̱ anyoṅmo̱i le̱ hereko ame̱maṅbii le̱ ye̱ mideṅ le̱, nakai noṅṅ Hezekia Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ hũ hereṅ emaṅ le̱ ye̱ mideṅ.

english_verse: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ Hezekia he miye ni ebagbo. Ni ekpa Iehowa fai, ni eke̱le̱ wie ni ehãle̱ nākpe̱ okadi ko.

english_verse: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

translation_verse: Ši etšũ bo̱foi ke̱-ba eṅõ abakē̱: Mẽ sane mike̱o yo̱, bo Iuda maṅtše̱? Dšee bo ono̱ miba ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱, ši moṅ šĩa ni mike̱-yo̱ ta le̱ ne̱ miba; ni Nyoṅmo̱ efã́-mi ake̱ mife oyá. Kākwe̱ ní obata Nyoṅmo̱ moni ke̱mi yo̱ le̱ he, ni ekpãtã ohĩe!

english_verse: Get ready to do the work that David and Solomon assigned to you, according to your clans.
translation_verse: ni nyesāa nyehe ye̱ nyetše̱mei awei le̱ anā ye̱ nyesafokui le̱ anā, take̱ bo̱ni David, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ ebi Salomo ṅmã le̱;

english_verse: When the people bring you their Passover lamb, you must kill it and prepare it to be sacrificed to the Lord. Make sure the people celebrate according to the instructions that the Lord gave Moses, and don't do anything to make yourselves unclean and unacceptable.
translation_verse: ni nyegbea Hehō tōbi le̱, ni nyefea nyehe kroṅkroṅ, ni nyesāa nyehãa nyenyemimei le̱, ni nyefe take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa tšṍ Mose no̱ ewie le̱.

english_verse: Josiah's officials also voluntarily gave some of their animals to the people, the priests, and the Levites as sacrifices. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were the officials in charge of the temple, gave the priests
translation_verse: Ni enukpai le̱ hũ hã maṅ le̱ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ eko ye̱ ame̱suo-mo̱ nā. Hilkia ke̱ Zakaria ke̱ Iehiel ni dši Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ lume̱i le̱ hã oso̱foi le̱ tōi akpei-enyo̱ ke̱ ohai-ekpa ke̱ tšinai ohai-etẽ ni ake̱-fe Hehō-afo̱lei.

english_verse: Conaniah, his two brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites, and they gave the other Levites
translation_verse: Ni Konania ke̱ Šemaia ke̱ Netanel, enyemimei le̱, ke̱ Hašabia ke̱ Ieiel ke̱ Iozabad ni dši Levibii le̱ anukpai le̱ hũ hã Levibii le̱ tōi akpei-enumo̱ ke̱ tšinai ohai-enumo̱ ni ake̱-fe Hehō-afo̱lei.

english_verse: The Levites set aside the parts of the animal that the worshipers needed for their sacrifices to please the Lord, just as the Law of Moses required. They also did the same thing with the bulls.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱dšie šã-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱ he, koni ame̱ṅõ-hã ye̱ maṅbii le̱ atše̱mei awei le̱ amlidšāi le̱ anā, ni ake̱-hã Iehowa, take̱ bo̱ni aṅmã ye̱ Mose wolo le̱ mli le̱; ni nakai noṅṅ ame̱fe tšinai le̱ hũ.

english_verse: They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱šã Hehō tōbii le̱ ye̱ la no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni ato le̱; ši nii kroṅkroṅi le̱ ame̱hõ ye̱ kukwe̱ii ke̱ dadeseṅi ke̱ kãi amli, ni ame̱ke̱-bahã maṅbii le̱ oyá.

english_verse: All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
translation_verse: No se̱ le̱ ame̱fe ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nõ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ hũ anõ; edšake̱ oso̱foi le̱ ní dši Aaron bii le̱ kã šã-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ fo̱i le̱ ašā̃ he ke̱-yaši dšenamo̱, nohewo̱ ni Levibii le̱ fe ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nõ ke̱ oso̱foi ni dši Aaron bii le̱ hũ anõ le̱.

english_verse: During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
translation_verse: Ni *lalatše̱mei ni dši Asaf bii le̱ hũ ye̱ ame̱šidamo̱he le̱, ye̱ David ke̱ Asaf ke̱ Heman ke̱ Iedutun, maṅtše̱ le̱ ninalo̱ le̱, kitã le̱ nā; ni †agbónākwe̱lo̱i le̱ ye̱ agbó-fẽ-agbó nā. Ame̱be̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ ame̱-dšeo̱ ame̱šidamo̱he le̱, hewo̱ le̱ ame̱nyemimei Levibii le̱ feo̱ ame̱nõ hãa-ame. *

english_verse: So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Ni ato Iehowa súomo̱ le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱ ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni aye Hehō le̱, ni asã šã-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱ Iehowa afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni maṅtše̱ Iosia wo kitã le̱.

english_verse: The worshipers then celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread for the next seven days.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii ni ba dše̱i le̱ ye Hehō le̱ ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli, ke̱ akpĩtĩ gbĩ-dšũrõ le̱ gbĩĩ kpawo.

english_verse: People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet. In fact, this was the greatest Passover celebration in Israel's history!
translation_verse: Ni ayeko *Hehō ko ni tamo̱ ene̱ pẽṅ ye̱ Israel ke̱-dše̱ gbalo̱ Samuel gbĩĩ le̱ ano̱; ni asaṅ Israel maṅtše̱mei le̱ eko eko yeko Hehō ko pẽṅ ní tamo̱ noni Iosia ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ke̱ Iuda mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ Israelbii ni ba dše̱i le̱ ke̱ Ierusalembii le̱ ye le̱. *

english_verse: All these things happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah. Josiah Dies in Battle (
translation_verse: Iosia maṅtše̱yeli afi ni dši nyoṅma ke̱ kpānyo̱ le̱ no̱ aye ne̱ke̱ Hehō ne̱.

english_verse: Some time later, King Neco of Egypt led his army to the city of Carchemish on the Euphrates River. And Josiah led his troops north to meet the Egyptians in battle.
translation_verse: Ene̱mei fẽ ase̱, beni Iosia esã so̱lemo̱we le̱, Mizraim maṅtše̱ Neko fã ke̱-ba ni eke̱ Karkemiš ni yo̱ Eufrate nā le̱ abawu. Ni Iosia yiṅ ete eke̱le̱ yakpe.

english_verse: They carried Josiah out of his chariot, then put him in the other chariot he had there and took him back to Jerusalem, where he soon died. He was buried beside his ancestors, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem mourned his death.
translation_verse: Ni etšũdši le̱ wóle̱ ye̱ ſīli le̱ mli ni ame̱ke̱le̱ wo ſïli kroko ni ehĩe le̱ mli, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ ba Ierusalem; ni ebagbo, ni afũle̱ ye̱ etše̱mei afũhei le̱. Ni Iuda ke̱ Ierusalem fẽ fó Iosia.

english_verse: Jeremiah the prophet wrote a funeral song in honor of Josiah. And since then, anyone in Judah who mourns the death of Josiah sings that song. It is included in the collection of funeral songs.
translation_verse: Ni *Ieremia fo Iosia he yāfólala, ni lalatše̱mei hĩĩ ke̱ yei fẽ tšĩo̱ Iosia tã ye̱ ame̱yāfólalai amli ke̱ ṅme̱ne̱; hi ame̱-ke̱-fe gbe̱nā ní kã ši ye̱ Israel, ni na, aṅmã ye̱ yāfólalai le̱ amli. *Ier.

english_verse: Everything else Josiah did while he was king, including how he faithfully obeyed the Lord,
translation_verse: Ši Iosia he sãdši ni eſe̱ ke̱ enii kpakpai ní efe take̱ bo̱ni aṅmã ye̱ Iehowa mla le̱ mli le̱,

english_verse: is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: ke̱ ekleṅkleṅ ke̱ se̱kpẽ sãdši le̱, na, aṅmã ye̱ Israel ke̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ awolo le̱ mli.

english_verse: The message said: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Koreš, Persia maṅtše̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Iehowa, ṅwei Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, etu šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱yelii le̱ fē ewo mideṅ, ni efámi ake̱ miyamã šĩa mihãle̱ ye̱ Ierusalem ye̱ Iuda. Emaṅbii le̱ ateṅ mofẽmo ní yo̱ nyeteṅ le̱, Iehowa, e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, afata ehe ní efã ke̱-ya!
