translation_verse: ni ake̱ ame̱dšadše ni ame̱šie̱ ye̱ ame̱mādši le̱ fẽ mli ke̱ Ierusalem hũ ake̱: Nyedšea kpo nyeyaä goṅ le̱ no̱, ni nyeyaṅõa mũtšei anidši ke̱ ṅkũtšei anidši ke̱ mirtotšei anidši ke̱ ble̱oi ke̱ tšei kusukusūi anidši, ni nyeke̱-bafe asesei, take̱ bo̱ni aṅmā le̱.

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ dše kpo ni ame̱yaṅõ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱ke̱-bafe asesei ame̱hã ame̱he, mofẽmo le̱ ye̱ etšũ yiteṅ, lo ame̱kpoi ano̱ ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ kpoi le̱ ano̱ ke̱ *nu agbó le̱ nā blohũ le̱ṅ ke̱ Efraim agbó le̱ nā blohũ le̱ṅ. *K.

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
translation_verse: Ni asafo mū le̱ fẽ ni kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ nomṅõ le̱ mli ke̱-ba le̱ fe asesei, ni ame̱hĩ asesei le̱ amli. Ni Israelbii le̱ efeko nakai dã ke̱-dše̱ Iešua, Nun bi le̱, yino̱ āhũ ke̱-baši nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱. Ni ame̱mī še̱ ame̱he naakpa.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Asaṅ ke̱-dše̱ kleṅkleṅ gbĩ le̱ no̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši nāgbē gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ akaneo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mla wolo le̱ gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ. Ni ame̱-ye gbĩdšũrõ le̱ gbĩĩ kpawo, ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ kpānyo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱kpe nāgbē kpē, take̱ bo̱ni ato le̱.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱ ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ fe hewõnii, ni *ame̱fe ame̱he kue̱ṅtĩlo̱i, ni ame̱-boo okitãi le̱ atoi. *

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: kēle̱ omo̱bo̱nale̱ babaō le̱ nā le̱ okwaa-ame̱ ye̱ ṅā le̱ no̱: ſane le̱ atatu kutū ní tšõo̱ame̱ gbe̱ le̱ edšee ame̱no̱, ni nyõṅ hũ la kutū ni hãa ame̱naä nii ye̱ gbe̱ ní amenyie no̱ le̱ ne̱ le̱ edšee ame̱no̱.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: Asaṅ *oṅō omumo̱ kpakpa le̱ ohā, koni etšõame̱ nii, ni o-mána le̱ hũ ohãã akpa ye̱ ame̱dāṅ, ni ame̱kũmai mli le̱ ohãame̱ nu kẽ. *

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Ni ohã ame̱bii le̱ hũ ayi fá tamo̱ ṅweĩ ṅulamii, ni oṅõame̱ ke̱-ba šikpoṅ le̱ ni okē̱ ame̱tše̱mei ake̱ ame̱ya ni ame̱ yaṅõ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni bii le̱ ba ni ame̱haṅõ šikpoṅ le̱, ni oba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii ni dši Kanaanbii le̱ ašĩ ye̱ ame̱hĩe, ni oṅõame̱ owo ame̱deṅ, ke̱ ame̱maṅtše̱mei ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ mädsimadši le̱, koni eme̱feame̱ bo̱ni ame̱sumoo̱. Ios.

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ otuame̱ owo ame̱haolo̱i le̱ adeṅ, ni ame̱haoame̱. Ni ame̱haomo̱ be le̱ mli le̱ ame̱blo̱ ame̱tšē̱o, ni odše̱ ṅwei oboame̱ toi, ni omo̱bo̱nale̱ babaō le̱ nā le̱ *ohãame̱ yiwalaherelo̱i, ni ame̱here ame̱yiwala ke̱-dše̱ ame̱haolo̱i le̱ adeṅ. *Kodš.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: Ši kē̱ ame̱ná hedšo̱le̱ pe̱ le̱, ame̱yafeo̱ efõṅ ye̱ ohĩe ekoṅ, ni oṅmē̃o̱ ame̱ he owoo ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ, ni ame̱yeo̱ ame̱no̱. Ši kẽle̱ ké̱ ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ni ame̱ bablo̱ ame̱tšē̱o le̱, odše̱o̱ ṅwei oboo̱ame̱ toi ni omo̱bo̱nale̱ babaō le̱ nā le̱ odšieame̱ šiiabo̱. Kodš.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ oto tšui ohãame̱ afii pī, ni otšṍ ogbalo̱i le̱ ano̱ oke̱ omumo̱ le̱ ye odase ošiame̱; ši ame̱boo toi. Nohewo̱ le̱ otuame̱ owo šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ bii le̱ adeṅ. Ier.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ omo̱bo̱nale̱ babaō le̱ nā le̱ oplenēēame̱ kwrakwra ni asaṅ okwaaame̱; edšake̱ Mawu odomfoo̱ ke̱ mo̱bo̱nalo̱ dšio! Yāfō

english_verse: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱, Mawu *kpeteṅkple ni he wa ní he yo̱ gbeyei ní too̱ kpaṅmo̱ ke̱ mo̱bo̱nale̱! kā-hã amanehũlũ fẽ ní eba wo̱ ke̱ wo̱maṅtše̱mei ke̱ wo̱nukpaĩ ke̱ wo̱so̱foi ke̱ wo̱gbalo̱i ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ ke̱ omaṅ le̱ fẽ no̱, ke̱-dše̱ Ašur maṅtše̱mei le̱ ayino̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ le̱, mife bibiō ye̱ ohĩe! *

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: Ši bo le̱, sãdši ni eba wo̱no̱ le̱ fẽ mli le̱ onõ dša; edšake̱ oye ano̱kwa, ši wo̱ le̱ wo̱fe efõṅ. Ezra

english_verse: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
translation_verse: Ni wo̱maṅtše̱mei le̱ hũ ke̱ wo̱nukpai le̱ ke̱ wo̱so̱foi le̱ ke̱ wo̱tše̱mei le̱ yeko omla le̱ no̱, ni asaṅ ame̱boko okitãi le̱ ke̱ odasei ni oke̱-ye odase ošiame̱ le̱ atoi.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ke̱ onii kpakpai babaō ni ohãame̱ le̱ ke̱ šikpoṅ kple̱lē̱ ní ewo fo̱ ní oṅõ-hā ye̱ ame̱hĩe le̱ mli le̱ ame̱súmo̱koö, ni ame̱kpaleko ke̱-dše̱ko eme̱nifõdíianii le̱ amli.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ni ebaä nii babaō ehãa maṅtše̱mei ni oṅõ-to wo̱no̱ ye̱ wohe ešai le̱ ahewo̱ le̱; ni ame̱yeo̱ wo̱gbomotšei ke̱ wo̱koloi ano̱, boni ame̱sumoo̱, ni wo̱ye̱ haomo̱ kpeteṅkple mli!

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: .] ame̱kpe̱te̱ ame̱nyemimei abladei le̱ ahe, ni ame̱lomo̱ ame̱he ni ame̱kãmo̱ kitãi ake̱ ame̱aye Nyoṅmo̱ mla le̱ ní atšṍ Nyoṅmo̱ tšũlo̱ Mose nine no̱ awo le̱ no̱, ni ame̱adſẽṅ no̱ ní ame̱ye Iehowa, wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ le̱, kitãi ke̱ emlai ke̱ ekpo̱i le̱ fẽ no̱;

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.

translation_verse: .] Wo̱sā wo̱wo wo̱he kitã ake̱ dā afi le̱ wo̱o̱hã šekel mlidšāi etẽ mli ekome ye̱ wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ súomo̱ le̱ hewo̱,

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: .] ye̱ hĩe-mã-abolo le̱ ke̱ dā niyenii-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ dā šā̃-afo̱le le̱ ke̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ ano̱ nii le̱ ke̱ nyõdši hēi le̱ ano̱ nii le̱ ke̱ gbĩĩ dšudši ní ato le̱ ano̱ nii le̱ ke̱ nii kroṅkroṅi le̱ ke̱ ešaafo̱lei le̱ ni ake̱-kpãtãa ahãa Israel le̱, ke̱ wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ nitšumo̱ le̱ fẽ hewo̱.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: .] Asaṅ wo̱, oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ke̱ maṅbii le̱, wo̱fõfṍ ošikii ye̱ lai hãmo̱ le̱ hewo̱, ní ake̱-ba wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ ye̱ wo̱tše̱mei awei le̱ anā, ye̱ bei ní ato le̱ amli dā afi, ní ašã ye̱ Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, afo̱lešãlate̱ le̱ no̱, take̱ bo̱ni *aṅmã ye̱ mla le̱ mli le̱. *

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: .] Ni asaṅ wo̱ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ kleṅkleṅ nibanii ke̱ tšo-fẽ-tšo no̱ kleṅkleṅ yibii aaba Iehowa we le̱ dā afi,

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: .] ni wo̱ke̱ wo̱kleṅkleṅ mi le̱ ke̱ wo̱no̱wómo̱-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ tšo-fẽ-tšo yibii le̱ ke̱ wein ke̱ mũ hū nō le̱ aaba abahã oso̱foi le̱ ni ake̱-wo wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ we le̱ fiasei le̱ amli; ni wo̱ke̱ wo̱šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nibii *amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ aaha Levibii le̱; ni ame̱, Levibii le̱ ame̱he nibii amlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ ye̱ mãdši ni wo̱hũo̱ ye̱ mli le̱ fẽ mli. *

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.

translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ onukpai ní hĩ Ierusalem le̱ ne̱. Ši Iuda mãdši le̱ amli le̱ mofẽmo hĩ le̱dientše̱ ešikpoṅ no̱ ye̱ ame̱mãdši le̱ amli: Israel, oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ke̱ so̱lemo̱we súolo̱i le̱ ke̱ *Salomo tšũdši abii le̱. *

english_verse: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
translation_verse: Hilkia nõ le̱ mli le̱, Hašabia; Iedaia nõ le̱ mli le̱, Netanel.

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Eliašib, Ioiada ke̱ Iohanan ke̱ Iadua *yino̱ le̱ aṅmä Levibii le̱ atše̱mei awei le̱ ano̱ onukpai le̱ ke̱ oso̱foi le̱ agbe̱ii ye̱ Dario, Persianyo le̱, maṅtše̱yeli be le̱ mli. *K.

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii le̱ anukpai ne̱: Hašabia, Šerebia ke̱ Iešua, Kadmiel bi le̱, ke̱ ame̱nyemimei ní yo̱ ame̱ṅe̱le̱no̱ le̱, ní ame̱dšie yi ni ame̱da ši ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo *David kitã le̱ nā, bulo̱i tša bulo̱i ano̱: *

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Ni beni ababule Ierusalem gbogbo le̱, ame̱yatao Levibii ye̱ hei ní ame̱yo̱ le̱ fẽ, ni ame̱ṅõame̱ ke̱-ba Ierusalem, ko-ni ame̱baye bulemo̱ gbīdšũrõ le̱ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ ke̱ šidāi ke̱ lalai ke̱ ṅoṅoi ke̱, be̱dši ke̱ saṅkũi.

english_verse: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
translation_verse: ke̱ mei ní dše̱ Bet-Gilgal ke̱ Geba kōi ase̱ ke̱ Azmawet; edšake̱ lalatše̱mei le̱ etotō ame̱krowai ke̱-bo̱le Ierusalem.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ tšū amehe, ni asaṅ ame̱tšū maṅ le̱ ke̱ agbói le̱ ke̱ gbogbo le̱ hũ he.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mihā Iuda onukpai le̱ kwo̱ ke̱-ba gbogbo le̱ no̱, ni mito asafokui kplei enyo̱ ni ame̱to ke̱-nyie ni ame̱la šidā lalai: ku kome tšṍ ninedäŭrõgbe̱ ye̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱ ke-mīya *tumu agbó le̱ ṅã gbe̱, *

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: ni Hošaia ke̱ Iuda onukpai le̱ amlĩdšā nyie ame̱se̱,

english_verse: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
translation_verse: ke̱ Azaria, Ezra, Mešulam,

english_verse: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Iuda, Benyamin ke̱ Šemaia ke̱ Ieremia,

english_verse: all of them blowing trumpets. Next, there was Zechariah of the Asaph clan
translation_verse: ke̱ oso̱foi abii le̱ ateṅ meikomei ní hĩe te̱tre̱mantre̱i: Zakaria, Ionatan bi, Šemaia bi, Matania bi, Mikaia bi, Zakur bi, Asaf bi le̱,

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: ke̱ enyemimei: Šemaia ke̱ Azarel ke̱ Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Netanel ke̱ Iuda ke̱ Hanani, ni ame̱hĩe Nyoṅmo̱ gbomo David lala nibii le̱; ni Ezra, woloṅmãlo̱ le̱, nyie ame̱hĩe;

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Ni lalo̱i asafoku ní dši enyo̱ le̱ tšṍ ne̱ke̱ gbe̱, ni mĩdientše̱ ke̱ maṅ le̱ fã le̱ nyie ame̱se̱ ye̱ gbogbo le̱ no̱, ke̱-tšṍ *flõnõĩ amō̃ ni kwo̱ le̱ ne̱, āhũ ke̱-yašĩ gbogbo le̱ke̱tē̱ le̱ no̱ *

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni lalo̱i asafokui enyo̱ le̱ yadamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱, ke̱ mi ke̱ no̱yelo̱i le̱ fã ní fata mihe le̱,

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: ke̱ oso̱foi: Eliakim, Maaseia, Miniamin, Mikaia, Elioenai, Zakaria ke̱ Hanania, ni ame̱hĩe te̱tre̱mantre̱i,

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: ke̱ Maaseia ke̱ Šemaia ke̱ Eleazar ke̱ Uzi ke̱ Iohanan ke̱ Malkia ke̱ Elam ke̱ Ezer. Ni lalo̱i le̱ la wā, ke̱ ame̱no̱-kwe̱lo̱ Iezrahia.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Ni ame̱šã šā̃-afolei babaō nakai gbĩ le̱, ni amenyã́nyã́i; edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ehã ame̱nyã́ nyã́mo̱ kpeteṅkple; ni yei le̱ ke̱ gbekẽbii le̱ hũ nyã́nyã́i, āhũ ní anu Ierusalem nyã́mo̱ le̱ ye̱ šoṅṅ po.

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ le̱ aṅõ hĩĩ komei ato fiasei *ní atoo̱ no̱wómo̱-afolei le̱ ke̱ kleṅkleṅ yibii le̱ ke̱ nibii amlidšãi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ ye̱ mli le̱ ano̱, koni ame̱bua mãdši le̱ ahewo̱ ṅmõdši le̱ amli nii le̱ amlidšāi ní mla le̱ to le̱ anã ame̱wo mli ame̱hã oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱; edšake̱ Iuda ená oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ ni damoo̱ ši súmoo̱ le̱ ahe mīše̱, *

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: ni ame̱ye ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ gbe̱nā le̱ no̱ ke̱ hetšūmo̱ le̱ gbe̱nā le̱ no̱, ni nakai nonṅ lalatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ agbónākwe̱lo̱i le̱ hũ fe ye̱ David ke̱ ebi Salomo kitã le̱ nā.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Ši *David ke̱ Asaf yino̱ bēbe ato lalatše̱mei ano̱ onukpai ke̱ yidšiemo̱ ke̱ šidā lalai aha Nyoṅmo̱. *

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Ni Zerubabel yino̱ ke̱ Nehemia yino̱ le̱ Israel mū le̱ fẽ hãa lalatše̱mei le̱ ke̱ agbónākwe̱lo̱i le̱ agbe̱nānii, gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ ke̱ enõ; ni asaṅ ame̱ke̱ nii ní afeame̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ hãa Levibii le̱, ni Levibii le̱ hũ ke̱ *nii ni afeame̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ eko hãa Aaron bii le̱. *

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Ni edo̱mi naakpa, ni midšie Tobia šĩa nibii fẽ ke̱-dše̱ tšũ le̱ṅ miſie.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mifã́ ake̱ ašā flasei le̱ amli, ni miṅõ *Nyoṅmo̱ we le̱ nibii le̱ ke̱-ba dše̱i ekoṅ, ke̱ niyenii-afo̱lei le̱ ke̱ kro̱bo̱o le̱ hũ. *

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ able ke̱ wein ke̱ mũ mlidšāi nyoṅma mli ekomekome le̱ ba ame̱bawo nitōhei le̱.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Ni mito nitōhei akwe̱lo̱i ye̱ nitōhei le̱ ano̱: Oso̱ſo šelemia ke̱ Zadok, woloṅmālo̱ le̱, ke̱ Pedaia, ni dše̱ Levibii le̱ ateṅ le̱; ni ame̱se̱mo dšĩ Hanan, Matania bi Zakur bi le̱; edšake̱ abuame̱ ano̱kwafoi, ni amenitšumo̱ dši ake̱ ame̱dša nibii le̱ ame̱hã ame̱nyemimei le̱.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ mina ye̱ Iuda, bo̱ni meikomei nāa weintšõne ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni ame̱ke̱ able dšatšui hũ baä, ame̱ke̱-tēreo̱ tedšii, ke̱ wein ke̱ weinyibii ke̱ agbãmii hũ ke̱ dšatšui sro̱toi fẽ, ni ame̱ke̱-baä Ierusalem ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱; ni mibo̱ame̱ ko̱ko̱ gbĩ ni *ame̱hõo̱ nii le̱. *

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ni Tirobii komei hũ ye̱ dše̱i, ni ame̱ke̱ lō ke̱ nihō̃mo̱nii sro̱toi fẽ baã, ni ame̱bahõo̱ ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱ ame̱hãa Iudabii le̱, ni ye̱ Ierusalem hũ.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni miblo̱ miwo Iuda abladei le̱, ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mẽ sane fõṅ nyeyeo̱ ni nyeke̱-buleo̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ ne̱?

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Nto ne̱ke̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ fe, ni wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ nõfõṅ ne̱ fẽ ba wo̱no̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ no̱ ne̱? ni kẽle̱ nyeke̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ bulemo̱ mītšé̱ mlifũ ke̱ba Israel no̱ nyefata he.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ dšrayelo̱i le̱ ke̱ guo̱yelo̱i ní hõo̱ nibii sro̱toi fẽ le̱ bawo̱ Ierusalem agbói le̱ ase̱ šikome lo šii enyo̱.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni mibo̱ame̱ ko̱ko̱, ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ nyeba wo̱ö̱ gbogbo le̱ se̱ le̱? Ke̱dši nyefe nakai ekoṅ le̱, mamõmo̱nye! Ke̱-dše̱ nakai be le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱baa ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli hũ le̱ mina Iudafoi ní ew̌e̱ Ašdodyei ke̱ Amonyei ke̱ Moabyei.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bii le̱ wieo̱ Ašdod wiemo̱ lo mofẽmo le̱ emaṅ wiemo̱ fã ke̱ fã, ni ame̱nyẽẽ Iuda wiemo̱ ame̱wie dšogbäṅ.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni miblo̱ miwoame̱, ni milomo̱ame̱, ni miyi ame̱teṅ meikomei, ni mifãmo̱ ame̱yĩtšo̱i, ni mihã ame̱kã Nyoṅmo̱ kitã mikē̱: Ke̱dši *nyeṅõ nyebiyei nyehã ame̱bihĩĩ agblã ni nyew̌e̱ ame̱biyei nyehã nyebihĩĩ lo nyedientše̱ nyehe fĩ! *

english_verse: God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin.
translation_verse: Ani dšee ene̱mei noṅṅ hã Israel maṅtše̱ Salomo fe eša le̱? tše̱ dšeṅmãdšĩ babaō mli maṅtše̱ ko maṅtše̱ ko be̱ ni tamo̱le̱, ni e-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ sumoo̱le̱, ni Nyoṅmo̱ wole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Israel mū le̱ fẽ no̱; kẽle̱ le̱ po *maṅse̱ yei le̱ hã efe eša. *

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Kole̱, aso wo̱bonye toi, ni wo̱fe ne̱ke̱ efõṅ kpeteṅkple ne̱ fẽ, ni wo̱w̌e̱ maṅse̱ yei ni wo̱ke̱-tõ wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ no̱?

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fonukpa Eliašib bi *Ioiada bii le̱ ateṅ mokome etšṍ †Sanbalat, Horonnyo le̱, šānū; nohewo̱ le̱ miſĩele̱ ke̱-dše̱ mihe. *

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mi-Nyoṅmo̱, kaimo̱ame̱; edšake̱ ame̱bule oso̱foyeli le̱ ke̱ oso̱foyeli kpãṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ anõ le̱ hũ!

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni mife mitšū ame̱he ke̱-dše̱ maṅse̱nii fẽ mli ne̱; ni mito oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ Levibii le̱ asúomo̱ le̱ gbe̱dšĩane̱, mofẽmo ye̱ enitšume̱ no̱,

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Ni beni ne̱ke̱ gbĩĩ ne̱ fo mli le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅmẽ maṅbii fẽ ni yo̱ Šušan mō̃ le̱ mli le̱, mei wudši ke̱ mei bibii fẽ, okplõ gbĩĩ kpawo, ye̱ maṅtše̱ mō̃ le̱ he trom le̱ kpo le̱ no̱;

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Ni ahãame̱ dã ye̱ šika kpudši amli, ni kpudši le̱ hũ sro̱toisro̱toi ni, ke̱ maṅtše̱ wein babaō, bo̱ni sa maṅtše̱.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ kpawo le̱ no̱, beni wein ehã maṅtše̱ le̱ mli efiile̱ le̱, efã́ Mehuman, Bizta, Harbona, Bigta ke̱ Abagta, Zeter ke̱ Karkas, ní dši piafoi kpawo ni súmoo̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš hĩe le̱,

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: ake̱ ame̱yaṅõ maṅuye Wašti ke̱-ba maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe ke̱ emaṅnye akekre le̱, koni ehã mãdši ano̱ bii le̱ ke̱ lume̱i le̱ ana ehefe̱o; edšake̱ ehe ye̱ fe̱o.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: ni mei ni be̱ṅke̱le̱ dši Karšena, Šetar, Admata, Taršiš, Meres, Marsena ke̱ Memukan, Persia ke̱ Media lume̱i kpawo ni ṅaã maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe, ni ame̱tráa yitšo ye̱ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mli le̱;)

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Memukan kē̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ lume̱i le̱ ahĩe ake̱: Dšee maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ke̱ no̱ ni maṅnye Wašti etõ, ši moṅ etõ lume̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ mãdšimšdši le̱ fẽ ni yo̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš šikpōdši sro̱toi le̱ fẽ no̱ le̱ hũ ano̱.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ maṅnye le̱ sane ne̱ bagbe̱ aſã yei fẽ ateṅ, ni eebã ame̱wumei ahe guo̱ agbo ye̱ ame̱hĩe, ke̱dši ayagba ake̱: Maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš fã́ ake̱ ayaṅõ maṅnye Wašti ke̱-ba ehĩe, ši ebaa le̱.

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ni ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ Persia ke̱ Media lumoyei le̱ ni enu maṅnye le̱ sane ne̱ aakē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ lume̱i le̱ fẽ nakai noṅṅ; ni heguo̱gbẽ ke̱ mlifū̃ babaō aate ši.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱, no le̱ maṅtše̱yeli kitã ko adše̱ edeṅ, ni aṅmã ye̱ Persia ke̱ Media mlai ni *atšakee le̱ amli: ake̱ Wašti akaba maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš hĩe doṅṅ, ni maṅtše̱ aṅõ emaṅnyeyeli le̱ ahã enanyo ko ní hĩ fèle̱. *Dan.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Ni hã ni ašĩe̱ maṅtše̱ akpo̱ ni ebawo ne̱ ye̱ emaṅtše̱yelihe le̱ fẽ, koni yeigbãyei fẽ ahĩe aso̱ ame̱wumei, mei wudši ke̱ mei bibii fẽ.

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Ni wiemo̱ le̱ sa maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ lume̱i le̱ ahĩe; ni maṅtše̱ le̱ fe bo̱ni Memukan kē̱ le̱.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšũ ake̱ wodši te maṅtše̱ le̱ šikpõdši sro̱toi le̱ fẽ ano̱, *šikpoṅ-fẽ-šikpoṅ le̱ aṅmã ke̱ le̱dientše̱ eniṅmã, ni maṅ-fẽ-maṅ hũ ye̱ le̱dientše̱ ewiemo̱ mli: ake̱ †nū-fẽ-nū le̱ eye ewe no̱; ni awie le̱dientše̱ emaṅ wiemo. *

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: ni maṅtše̱ ato no̱kwe̱lo̱i ye̱ emaṅtše̱yeli šikpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱, koni ame̱bua oblayei froi ní he yo̱ fe̱o le̱ fẽ nā ke̱ba Šušan mō̃ le̱ṅ ye̱ yei awe le̱, ni atuame̱ awo Hegai, maṅtše̱ piafonyo ni kwe̱o̱ yei le̱, deṅ, ni ahãame̱ ame̱hesāmo̱ nibii;

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: ni oblayō ní aasa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱ atšṍ maṅnye ye̱ Wašti nãdšiaṅ. Ni wiemo̱ le̱ sa maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe, ni efe nakai.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ Iudanyo ko ye̱ Šušan mō̃ le̱ṅ, ni egbe̱i dši Mordekai, ni Benyaminnyo *Kiš bi Šimei bi Iair bi dši le̱, *

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Ni le̱ dši moni kwe̱o̱ Hadasa, ní dši Ester, *etše̱kwẽ biyō le̱; edšake̱ ebe̱ tše̱ ebe̱ nye. Ni oblayō le̱ he ye̱ fe̱o, ni ehĩe hũ ye̱ fe̱o; ní beni etše̱ ke̱ enye gboi le̱, Mordekai ṅõle̱ fe le̱dientše̱ ebiyō. *K.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni eba mli ake̱, beni anu maṅtše̱ kitã ke̱ ekpo̱ le̱ ní abua oblayei pī anā ke̱-ba Šušan mō̃ le̱ṅ ni ake̱-ame̱ bawo Hegai deṅ le̱, aṅõ Ester hũ ke̱-ba maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱, ni ake̱le̱ bawo Hegai, yei akwe̱lo̱ le̱, deṅ.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Ni oblayō le̱ sa ehĩe, ni ehĩe ba nyam ye̱ ehĩe; ni oyá ke̱ke̱ ni ehãle̱ ehesāmo̱nii le̱ ke̱ egbe̱nānii le̱, ni esã eṅō oblayei kpawo ni ahala ke̱-dše̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ ehāle̱; ni edšiele̱ ke̱ eblayei le̱ eyato yei awe le̱ heni hĩ fé fẽ.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Ši dāne̱ Mordekai yašēraä ši ye̱ yei le̱ awe le̱ kpo le̱ hĩe, koni ele bo̱ni Ester yo̱ ke̱ noni abafele̱.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: ni ne̱ke̱ gbe̱ no̱ oblayō le̱ tšṍo̱ ke̱-yaä maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ, nofẽno ni ebio̱ le̱ ahãale̱ ke̱-dše̱o̱ yei awe le̱ ni eke̱-yaä maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Eyaä gbe̱ke̱, ni lebi le̱ ekũo̱ ese̱ ke̱-yaã yei awe kroko le̱, ni ake̱le̱ woo Šaašgaz, maṅtše̱ piaſonyo ni kwe̱o̱ ehemei le̱, deṅ; eyaa maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ doṅṅ, dša maṅtše̱ le̱ ná ehe tšui, ni awo egbe̱i atã atšé̱le̱.

english_verse: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
translation_verse: Ni aṅõ Ester ke̱-te maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš ṅõ ye̱ emaṅtše̱yeli šĩa le̱ ye̱ nyõṅ ni dši nyoṅma, ni dši Tebet nyõṅ le̱ no̱, ye̱ emaṅtše̱yeli afi ni dši kpawo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ sumo̱ Ester fè yei le̱ fẽ, ni ehĩe ba nyam ye̱ ehĩe ni ená ehe mīše̱ fè oblayei le̱ fẽ; ni eṅō maṅnyeyeli akekre efĩ eyitšo, ni ewole̱ maṅnye ye̱ Wašti nãdšiaṅ.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅmẽ elumei le̱ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ fẽ okplõ kpeteṅkple, Ester yino̱ okplõ ni, ni ehã šikpõdši wo ame̱tšui, ni ekekē nii bo̱ni sa maṅtše̱.

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ beni abua oblayei le̱ anā noni dši ši enyo̱ le̱, no mli le̱ Mordekai yatáa maṅtše̱ le̱ koi le̱ ši.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ Ester náko atšõ eweku ke̱ emaṅ, take̱ bo̱ni Mordekai ewole̱ kitã le̱; edšake̱ Ester yeo̱ Mordekai kitã no̱, tamo̱ be mli ni ekwe̱o̱le̱ le̱ noṅṅ. K.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli, beni Mordekai yatáa maṅtše̱ koi le̱ ši le̱, Bigtan ke̱ Tereš, maṅtše̱ piafoi enyo̱, ni dši mei ni buo̱ šĩnā le̱ nā le̱ ateṅ meikomei le̱, gri, ni ame̱mītao ni ame̱nine asa maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš he.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Ni Mordekai ná ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ le, ni eyakē̱ maṅnye Ester, ni Ester yakē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ye̱ Mordekai gbe̱i ano̱.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Ni beni atao sane le̱ mli le̱, ana ake̱ eye̱ mli nakai, ni ase̱ṅ ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ ye̱ tšo no̱; ni aṅmã ye̱ *yino̱sãdši awolo le̱ mli ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe. *

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ tšũdši ní ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ koi le̱ ši le̱ kē̱ Mordekai ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni bo le̱ otõo̱ maṅtše̱ kitã le̱?

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱kē̱o̱le̱ nakai dāne̱ ni ebooame̱ toi le̱, ame̱yagba Haman, koni ame̱kwe̱ ake̱ Mordekai wiemo̱i le̱ aadamo̱ ši lo; edšake̱ egbaame̱ ake̱ Iudanyo dšile̱.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Ni beni Haman na ake̱ Mordekai kũlaa ši ni ekotoole̱ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni Haman mli fũ naakpa.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Ši esaa ehīe ake̱ eke̱ enine aaṅmẽ Mordekai kometō ne̱; edšake̱ ame̱tšõle̱ Mordekai maṅ, nohewo̱ le̱ Haman mitao ake̱ ekpãtã Iudafoi fẽ ni yo̱ Ahašweroš maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mli ni dši Mordekai maṅbii le̱ ahĩe.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Kleṅkleṅ nyõṅ le̱, ni dši Nisan nyõṅ le̱, no̱ ye̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš yino̱ afi ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, ame̱fõ *Pur, no dši ošiki, ye̱ Haman hĩe ye̱ gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ hewo̱ ke̱ nyõṅ-fẽ-nyõṅ hewo̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši nyõṅ ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ni dši Adar nyõṅ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱, no le̱ ehã aṅmã ake̱ akpãtã ame̱hĩe; ni mahã maṅtše̱ tšũdši le̱ dſie̱te̱i talentai akpei-nyoṅma, ni ake̱-wo maṅtše̱ dſetritōhei le̱.

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ dšie *ewolonāso̱omo̱ga ye̱ enine, ni eṅõ-hã Hamedata bi Haman, Agagnyo le̱, ni dši Iudafoi ahenye̱lo̱ le̱. *

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Haman ake̱: Dſie̱te̱i le̱, ake̱-hão, ke̱ maṅbii le̱ hũ, ní ofe-ame̱ bo̱ni sa ohĩe.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni atšé̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ woloṅmãlo̱ĩ le̱ ke̱-ba ye̱ kleṅkleṅ nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ le̱ no̱; ni aṅmã bo̱ni Haman fã́ le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱, ni ake̱yahã maṅtše̱ le̱ amraloi ke̱ lume̱i ní yeo̱ šikpoṅ-fẽ-šikpoṅ no̱ le̱, ke̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ mli onukpai le̱, šikpoṅ-fẽ-šikpoṅ le̱ aṅmã ke̱ *le̱dientše̱ eniṅmã ni maṅ-fẽ-maṅ hũ ye̱ le̱dientše̱ ewiemo̱ mli; ni aṅmã ye̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš gbe̱i ano̱, ni ake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wolonāso̱omo̱ga le̱ se̱o nā. *

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱ wodši le̱ tšũ bo̱foi ni he yo̱ oyá ke̱-te maṅtše̱ le̱ šikpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱, koni akpãtã Iudafoi le̱ fẽ ahĩe, ni agbeame̱ ni aplenēame̱, oblahĩĩ ke̱ hĩĩmedši, gbekẽbii ke̱ yei fẽ, gbĩ kome dšenamo̱, ye̱ nyõṅ ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ni dši nyõṅ Adar le̱ no̱, gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ le̱ no̱, ni aha ame̱nii.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Amrõ pe̱ ni awo akpo̱ le̱ ye̱ Šušan mō̃ le̱ mli le̱ bo̱foi le̱ yi mli oyá ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ fã́mo̱ le̱ nā. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Haman ho trá ši ni ame̱banu dā̃; ši Šušan maṅ le̱ edšĩdšā.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hatak dše kpo ke̱-te Mordekai ṅõ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ blohũ ni ye̱ maṅtše̱ agbo le̱ nā le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hatak ba ni ebagba Ester Mordekai wiemo̱i le̱.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: Maṅtše̱ tšũdši le̱ fẽ ke̱ mei ní yo̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ hũ le ake̱ nū-fẽ-nū alo yō-fẽ-yō ni aaba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ ye̱ mligbe̱ kpo le̱ no̱, ní atšé̱kole̱ le̱, mla kome kã ši hāle̱ ake̱ aagbele̱, dia moni maṅtše̱ le̱ *aawó šika maṅtše̱tšo le̱ ne̱ atšõle̱ le̱ pe̱ yi náa wala; ši mi le̱ atšé̱-komi ake̱ miba maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ gbĩĩ nyoṅmai-etẽ so̱ṅṅ ne̱. *

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yagba Mordekai Ester wiemo̱i le̱.

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mordekai kē̱ ake̱ ayahã Ester hetõ ake̱: Kāsusu ake̱-ni oyo̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ hewo̱ le̱ bo le̱ ohe aadše mli ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ fẽ ateṅ.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ké̱ obu onā kwrā ye̱ ne̱ke̱ be ne̱ mli le̱, no le̱ mumo̱ ke̱ dšiemo̱ ke̱ walaheremo̱ aadše̱ he kroko ate ši ahã Iudafoi le̱; ši bo le̱ oke̱ otše̱ we le̱ hĩe aakpãtã. Ši ne̱ke̱ *be ne̱ hewo̱ noṅṅ onine še̱ maṅnyeyeli le̱ ne̱ ne̱ dšiṅ, namo le? *

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ester kē̱ame̱ ake̱ ame̱yahã Mordekai hetō ake̱:

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: Yabua Iudafoi ní yo̱ Šušan le̱ fẽ nā ke̱-kpe, ni nyehĩ ṅmä nyehãmi, ni nyekayea nii ni nyekanua nu hũ nyõṅ-nyōṅ ke̱ ſaneſane gbĩĩ etẽ; mi hũ ke̱ miblayei le̱ bahĩ ṅmā̃ nakai noṅṅ. Ke̱-ke̱ ni maya maṅtše̱ le̱ ṅõ tše̱ dšee mla le̱ nā ni; ni *ke̱dši milādše hũ, bĕle̱ milādše! *

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Mordekai yiṅ ete, ni eyafe bo̱ni Ester fã́le̱ le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni maṅtše̱ le̱ na maṅnye Ester damo̱ kpo le̱ no̱ le̱, ehīe ba nyam ye̱ ehĩe, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ *wó šika maṅtše̱tšo le̱ ní ehĩe le̱ ne̱ etšõ Ester. Ke̱ke̱ ni Ester tši be̱ṅke̱, ni eke̱ enine bata maṅtše̱tšo le̱ nābu. *

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Meni feo̱o, maṅnye Ester? ni meni hũ otaoo̱? Aahão āhũ ke̱-yaši maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mlidšā po.

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ni Ester kē̱: *Ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱, no le̱ maṅtše̱ ke̱ Haman aba okplõ ni miṅmẽo̱le̱ ṅme̱ne̱ le̱ he. *

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Nyeyatsē̱a Haman ke̱-baä mrãmrã, koni wo̱fe bo̱ni Ester kē̱ le̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Haman ba okplõ ní Ester eṅmẽ le̱ he.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Ester ye̱ wein okplõ le̱ he ake̱: *Meni obio̱? ni aahão; ni meni otaoo̱? Aafe ahão āhũ ke̱-yaši maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mlidšā po! *

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ maṅtše̱ hĩe, ni ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe ake̱ eehã noni mibio̱ le̱, ni eefe noni mitaoo̱ le̱, no le̱ maṅtše̱ ke̱ Haman aba okplõ ni mibaṅmẽame̱ le̱ he; ni wó̱ le̱ mafe bo̱ni maṅtše̱ kē̱ le̱.

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Haman dše kpo nakai gbĩ le̱ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ ke̱ mliflimo̱. Ši beni Haman na Mordekai ye̱ maṅtše̱ koi le̱ ši ake̱ etee ši ehããle̱, ni asaṅ etšii ehe tete, Haman mli wo Mordekai la naakpa.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ Haman ye ehe no̱, ni eyiṅ ete ewe le̱. Ke̱ke̱ ni etšũ ayatšé̱ enanemei ke̱ eṅã Zereš ke̱-ba.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Ni Haman gbaame̱ enii ni ená le̱ he nyam ke̱ ebii ayifále̱ ke̱ bo̱ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ewole̱ onukpa ke̱ boni ewó eno̱ fè lume̱i le̱ ke̱ maṅtše̱ tšũdši le̱.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Ni Haman sā kē̱ ake̱: Maṅnye Ester po hãã mokomoko ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ aba okplõ ni eṅmẽ le̱ he, ake̱ dša mi; ni wó̱ hũ ekpēmi ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱-mīya eṅõ.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ ene̱ fẽ efeemi šī, gbĩĩabo̱ ni minaä Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, tá maṅtše̱ koi le̱ ši ne̱.

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Nakai nyō le̱ṅ le̱ wo̱ tše ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe; ni efã́ ake̱ ayako̱ yino̱sãdši akaimo̱ wolo le̱ ke̱-ba, ni abakane ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Namo yo̱ kpo le̱ no̱ le̱? No mli le̱ Haman eba maṅtše̱ we le̱ agbónāgbe̱ kpo le̱ ne̱, eke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ba wie, ní ase̱ṅ *Mordekai ye̱ tšo ní emã ehāle̱ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Haman ba. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nū ní maṅtše̱ le̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam le̱, meni aafe ahãle̱? Ši Haman kē̱ ye̱ etsui mli ake̱: Namo po maṅtše̱ le̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam ake̱ dša mi?

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Haman kē̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ake̱: Nū ní maṅtše̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam le̱,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: hã ní ake̱ maṅtše̱ atade ní maṅtše̱ woo̱ le̱ aba, ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱ ní maṅtše̱ táa no̱ le̱, ke̱ maṅtše̱ akekre ní aṅõ-fĩo̱ eyi le̱;

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: ni hã ní atu ne̱ke̱ atade ne̱ ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱ ne̱ awo maṅtše̱ lume̱i agboi le̱ ateṅ mokome deṅ, koni ake̱-wo nū ní maṅtše̱ le̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam le̱, ni ahã etá okpo̱ṅo̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-fo mã le̱ṅ blohũ le̱ṅ, ni ašie̱ ke̱-nyie ebĩe ake̱: Bo̱ni aafe ahã nū ní maṅtše̱ le̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam le̱ ne̱!

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Haman ake̱: Ohe afe oyá, ni oṅõ atade ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱ le̱, take̱ bo̱ni okē̱ le̱, ni oyafe nakai ohã Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, ní táa maṅtše̱ koi le̱ ši le̱; kāšĩ nii ní otši tã le̱ fẽ mli ekomeflo!

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Haman ṅõ atade le̱ ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱ le̱, ni eke̱-yawo Mordekai, ni eke̱le̱ tá okpo̱ṅo̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-fo mã le̱ṅ blohũ le̱ṅ, ni ešie̱ ke̱-nyie ehīe ake̱: Bo̱ni aafe ahã nū ni maṅtše̱ le̱ sumoo̱ ake̱ ewo ehĩe nyam le̱ ne̱!

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Ni Mordekai kū ese̱ ke̱-ba maṅtše̱ koi le̱ ši ekoṅ; ši Haman he fe oyá ni eyiṅ ete ewe le̱ ke̱ ṅko̱mo̱yeli, ni eha eyi no̱.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Ni Haman gba eṅã Zereš ke̱ enanemei le̱ fẽ ošrã fẽ ní ešrãle̱ le̱. Ni enilelo̱i le̱ ke̱ eṅã Zereš kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši Mordekai ní obõi šigbēmo̱ ye̱ ehĩe ne̱ dše̱ Iudafoi aseši mli le̱, no le̱ onyẽṅ-le̱, ši moṅ ši noṅṅ obagbē kwrā ye̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Beni ame̱ke̱le̱ wieo̱ lolo le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ piafoi le̱ ba, ni ame̱mīye oyái ni ame̱ṅõ Haman ke̱-ya okplõ ní *Ester eṅmẽ le̱ be. *

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ Haman ba *ní ame̱ke̱ maṅnye Ester banu dā̃. *

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱ Ester ekoṅ gbĩ ní dši gbí enyo̱ le̱ ye̱ wein okplõ le̱ he ake̱: Maṅnye Ester, meni obio̱? ni aahão; ni meni otaoo̱? Aafe ahão āhũ ke̱-yaši maṅtše̱yeli le̱ mlidšā po!

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅnye Ester here no̱ ni ekē̱: Maṅtše̱, ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ ohĩe, ni ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱, hã ni aṅõ miwala akemi ye̱ mibimo̱ le̱ nā, ke̱ mimaṅbii le̱ anõ hũ ye̱ mitaomo̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ahõwo̱, mi ke̱ mimaṅ le̱, ní akpãtã wo̱hĩe, ní agbewo̱, ní aplenē-wo̱. Ni edši ahõwo̱ afe nyṍdšihĩĩ ke̱ nyṍdšiyei ke̱ke̱ dšiṅṅ, mikē̱ē̱ noko; ši henye̱lo̱ le̱ nyẽṅ maṅtše̱ nii ní bafite le̱ nãdšiaṅ ato!

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ester kē̱: Wo̱he ta ke̱ henye̱lo̱ le̱ dši ne̱ke̱ Haman gbomo fõṅ ne̱! Ke̱ke̱ ni ṅmiṅmi mõ Haman ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ maṅnye le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ te ši ke̱ mlifũ, ni edše wein okplõ le̱ he ete trom ní yo̱ mō̃ le̱ he le̱ mii. Ši Haman te ši damo̱ ši, koni ekpa maṅnye Ester fai ye̱ ewala hewo̱; edšake̱ ena ake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ emã efõṅ no̱ mĩ́ ye̱ ehewo̱.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kũ ese̱ ke̱-dše̱ mō̃ le̱ he trom le̱ mli ke̱-ba heni aṅmẽ wein okplõ le̱ ye̱ le̱; ni Haman eho ebu māṅō ní Ester tá no̱ le̱ no̱. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ kē̱: Aso ebatua maṅnye le̱ ye̱ mihĩe ye̱ šĩa ne̱? Beni wiemo̱ le̱ dše maṅtše̱ le̱ dāṅ pe̱, ke̱ke̱ ní ame̱ha Haman hĩe.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱yase̱ṅ Haman ye̱ tšo ni esā eto Mordekai le̱ no̱. Ni maṅtše̱ le̱ mli-la le̱ dšo̱.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ni Ester sā wie ekoṅ ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe, ni eho ekũla enãdší anā, ni eke̱ yāfó kpale̱ fai ni edšie Haman, Agagnyo le̱, nõfõṅ le̱ ke̱ eyiṅ ní eto ye̱ Iudafoĩ ahe le̱.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe, ni ke̱dši mihĩe eba nyam ye̱ maṅtše̱ hĩe, ni sane le̱ dša ye̱ maṅtše̱ hĩe, ni mi hũ misa ehĩe le̱, hã ní aṅmã wolo ní ake̱yakpale wodši ní Haman, Hamedata bi le̱ ni dši Agagnyo le̱, tšō ṅā eṅmã ni eke̱-kpãtã Iudafoi ni yo̱ maṅtše̱ šikpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱ le̱ ahĩe le̱.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ té mafe tẽṅ ni manyẽ makwe̱ efõṅ ní aaba mimaṅbii ano̱ le̱ hũ? ni té mafe tẽṅ ni manyẽ makwe̱ midšakubii le̱ ahĩekpãtãmo̱ le̱ hũ?

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš kē̱ maṅnye Ester ke̱ Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, ake̱: Na, Haman we le̱ miṅõ-hã Ester, ni le̱dientše̱ le̱ ase̱ṅle̱ ye̱ tšo no̱, edšake̱ ekpã enine mli ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Nyedientše̱ nyeṅmãa ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ ahewo̱, bo̱ni nyesumoo̱, ye̱ maṅtše̱ gbe̱i ano̱, ni nyeke̱ maṅtše̱ wolonāso̱omo̱ga le̱ aso̱o nā; edšake̱ wolo ni aṅmã ye̱ maṅtše̱ gbe̱i ano̱, ní ake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wolonāso̱omo̱ga le̱ eso̱o nā le̱, anyẽṅ akpale.

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Ni eṅmã ye̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš gbe̱i ano̱, ni eke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wolonāso̱omo̱ga le̱ so̱o nā, ni eke̱ wodši le̱ tšũtšũ bo̱foi ní he yo̱ oyá ni trá okpo̱ṅo̱ĩ ke̱ tedšiokpo̱ṅo̱i ní he yo̱ oyá ni dši okpo̱ṅo̱yei abii ano̱,

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Iudafoi le̱ ahe tšeame̱, ni ame̱nyã́, ni ame̱mli fliame̱, ni abuame̱.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅ-fẽ-šikpoṅ ke̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ no̱ ní maṅtše̱ le̱ kitã ke̱ ekpo̱ le̱ še̱ le̱, Iudafoi le̱ náa mīše̱ ni ame̱nyáa ni ame̱ṅmẽo̱ okplõ ni ame̱yeo̱ gbĩdšũrõ. Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ ateṅ mei pi tšṍmo̱ Iudafoi tete; *edšake̱ Iudafoi le̱ ahe ṅmiṅmi emōmo̱ame̱.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ ebaše̱ nyõṅ ní dši nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ ni dši Adar nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ le̱ no̱, ní abaye maṅtše̱ le̱ kitã ke̱ ekpo̱ le̱ no̱; ši nakai gbĩ le̱ ni Iudafoi le̱ ahenye̱lo̱i le̱ ahĩe kã no̱ ake̱ ame̱baye ame̱no̱ le̱, atšakele̱ ekroko, ni Iudafoi le̱ moṅ ná hewale̱ ye̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Mordekai etšṍ gbomo agbo ye̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱, ni egbe̱i ehehe ke̱-kpĕle šikpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱; edšake̱ ne̱ke̱ nū Mordekai ne̱ da ke̱ke̱ edaä ke̱-yaä no̱.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ noṅṅ le̱ mei ni agbe ye̱ Šušan mõ le̱ mli le̱ ayibo̱ baše̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ le̱, kē̱ maṅnye Ester ake̱: Šušan mõ le̱ mli le̱ Iudafoi le̱ egbegbẽ mei ni ame̱kpātã hĩĩ ohai-enumo̱ hīe ke̱ Haman bihĩĩ nyoṅma le̱ hũ; bĕle̱ maṅtše̱ šikpõdši ni eſe̱ le̱ ano̱ le̱ té ame̱fe tẽṅ mo̱! Kẽle̱ *meni obio̱? ni aahão; ni asaṅ meni otaoo̱ lolo? ni aafe. *

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ester kē̱: Ke̱dši esa maṅtše̱ hĩe le̱, hã ní aṅmi Iudafoi le̱ ní yo̱ Šušan le̱ gbe̱, ní wó̱ hũ ame̱fe tamo̱ bo̱ni afe ye̱ ṅme̱ne̱ mla le̱ nā le̱, ní ase̱ṅ Haman bihĩĩ nyoṅma le̱ hũ ye̱ tšo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Afe ene̱ ye̱ Adar nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ le̱ no̱, ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ le̱ ame̱dšō̱ ame̱he, ni ame̱ṅõ-fe okplõṅmõ ke̱ nyā̃mo̱ gbĩdšũrõ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Ši Iudafoi le̱ ni yo̱ Šušan le̱ bua ame̱he nā ye̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ etẽ le̱ ke̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ le̱ no̱, ni gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ enumo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱dšō̱ ame̱he, ni ame̱ṅõ-fe okplõṅmõ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ gbĩdšũrõ.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ Iudafoi ní dši akrowai amli bii ní yo̱ mãdši ní gbogboi be̱ he le̱ amli le̱ ṅõ Adar nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ le̱ ame̱fe okplõṅmē̃ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ gbĩdšũrõ ke̱ gbĩ kpakpa ke̱ henikē gbĩ.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Ni Mordekai ṅmã ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱, ni etšũ ake̱ wodši le̱ yahã Iudafoi fẽ ni yo̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš šikpõdši le̱ fẽ no̱ le̱, mei ní be̱ṅke̱ ke̱ mei ni yo̱ šoṅṅ le̱ fẽ,

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: ni eke̱-fo efõ ši ehãame̱ ake̱ ame̱ye Adar nyõṅ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ edſe̱ le̱ ke̱ gbĩ ni dši gbĩ nyoṅma ke̱ enumo̱ le̱ dā afi,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: ake̱ gbĩĩ ni Iudafoi le̱ ahe dšō̱ame̱ ye̱ no̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱henye̱lo̱i le̱ adeṅ, ke̱ nyõṅ ni ame̱w̌ere̱hō le̱ tšṍ mīše̱ ni ame̱ṅko̱mo̱yeli le̱ tšṍ gbĩdšũrõ hãame̱ ye̱ no̱, koni ame̱ṅõ nakai gbĩĩ le̱ ame̱fe okplõṅmõ ke̱ nyã́mo̱ ke̱ henikē ke̱ ohĩafoi anikē gbĩĩ.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ni Iudafoi le̱ ke̱ fõ ame̱no̱ ake̱ ame̱afe noni ame̱bõi femo̱ ne̱ ke̱ noni Mordekai ṅmã bahãame̱ le̱;

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: edšake̱ Hamedata bi Haman, Agagnyo le̱, ní dši Iudafoi le̱ fẽ ahenye̱lo̱ le̱ tšõ̀ ṅā ní ekpãtã Iudafoi le̱ ahĩe, ni efo *Pur ni dši ošiki le̱, koni eplenēame̱ ni ekpãtã ame̱hĩe; *

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: ši beni Ester ba maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe le̱, eṅmã wolo eke̱-fã́ ake̱ ahã eṅā fõṅ ní etšṍ ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ ahe le̱ akũ se̱ ababua le̱dientše̱ eyĩteṅ, ni *ase̱ṅ le̱ ke̱ ehihĩĩ le̱ ye̱ tšo le̱ no̱. *K.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱wo ne̱ke̱ gbĩĩ ne̱ agbe̱i ake̱ Purim ye̱ gbe̱i Pur le̱ hewo̱. Nohewo̱ hũ le̱ ne̱ke̱ wolo ne̱ mli wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱ noni ame̱dientše̱ ame̱na ye̱ ne̱-ke̱ sane ne̱ mli ke̱ noni ba ame̱nó̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱,

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: Iudafoi le̱ to, ni ame̱ke̱-fe gbe̱nã ni kã ši hãame̱ ke̱ ame̱sešibii ke̱ mei fẽ ni ke̱ ame̱he ebadõmo̱ame̱ le̱, ake̱ ame̱aye ne̱ke̱ gbĩĩ enyo̱ ne̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni aṅmã le̱ ye̱ ebe ni ato le̱ mli dã afi, ni ekaho ame̱yi;

english_verse: From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
translation_verse: ni ne̱ke̱ gbĩĩ ne̱ hĩe ahĩ no̱, ni aye ye̱ yino̱-fẽ-yino̱, weku-fẽ-weku, šikpoṅ-fẽ-šikpoṅ ke̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ mli; ni ne̱ke̱ Purim gbĩī ne̱ akaho Iudafoi le̱ ayi, ni ame̱kaimo̱ hũ se̱ akafo ye̱ ame̱sešibii ateṅ.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Ni maṅnye Ester ni dši Abihail biyō le̱, ke̱ Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, ke̱ ame̱hewale̱ ní ame̱ná le̱ fẽ ṅmã ni ame̱ke̱-mã ne̱ke̱ Purim he wolo ni dši enye̱ ne̱ no̱ aduatšo̱.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: koni ame̱ke̱-mã ne̱ke̱ Purim gbĩĩ ne̱ ano̱ mĩ́ ye̱ ame̱bei ni ato le̱ amli, take̱ bo̱ni Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, ke̱ maṅnye Ester efo efō ši ehãame̱ le̱, ke̱ bo̱ni ame̱dientše̱ ame̱to ne̱ke̱ ṅmā̃hĩle̱ ke̱ yāfó sãdši ne̱ ame̱fõ ši ame̱hã ame̱he ke̱ ame̱sešibii le̱.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Ni Ester kitã ni ewo le̱ mã ne̱ke̱ Purim sãdši ne̱ ano̱ aduatšo̱, ni aṅmã awo wolo mli.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš ke̱ onĩatšũmo̱ fõ šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ ṅšo̱kpo̱i le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Mordekai, Iudanyo le̱, dši moni yo̱ maṅtše̱ Ahašweroš se̱, ni edši gbomo agbo ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ, ni esane ṅõ enyemimei le̱ fẽ nā; etaoo̱ emaṅbii le̱ ekpakpa, ni ewieo̱ omanye wĩeme̱ ehãa esešibĩĩ le̱ fẽ.

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ni ebihĩĩ le̱ yaä ame̱yaṅmẽo̱ okplõ ye̱ mofẽmo we ké̱ še̱ egbĩ le̱, ni ame̱tšũo̱ ayatšé̱o̱ ame̱nyemimeiyei etẽ le̱ hũ ke̱-baã, ni ame̱ke̱ame̱ bayeo̱ nii ni ame̱ke̱-ame̱ nuo̱ dā̃.

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ko le̱, *Nyoṅmo̱ bii le̱ ba ame̱badamo̱ Iehowa hĩe, ni †satan hũ futuame̱ ke̱-ba. *

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ satan ake̱: Ani oṅõ otšui ofõ mitšũlo̱ Hiob bü no̱? Edšake̱ mokomoko be̱ ni tamo̱le̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, edši nū ni kpa ko be̱ ehe ni edša, ešeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei, ni eso̱leo̱ ehe ye̱ efõṅ he.

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ satan ake̱: Na, nofẽno ní eyo̱ le̱ eye̱ odeṅ, le̱dĩentše̱ ke̱-ke̱ ni onine akasa ehe! Ke̱ke̱ ni satan dše Iehowa hĩe ete.

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩ ko, beni ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ yeo̱ nii ni ame̱nuo̱ wein ye̱ ame̱nyemi nukpa le̱ we le̱,

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni *Šebabii batuawo̱, ni ame̱-mõmo̱ame̱ ke̱-te, ni tšũdši le̱ ame̱gbeame̱ ke̱ klante; ni mikometō pe̱ midše mli, ni mibatſao adafi ne̱. *

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Beni ewĩeo̱ lolo le̱, mokroko ba ni ebakē̱: Nyoṅmo̱ la le̱ dše̱ ṅwei bayi ši, ni ebašã toi le̱ ke̱ tšũdši le̱, ní eplenē̃-ame̱; ni mikometō pe̱ midše mli, ni mi-batſao adafi ne̱.

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Beni le̱ hũ ewieo̱ lolo le̱, mokroko hũ ba ni ebakē̱: *Kaldeabii le̱ gblá kui etẽ, ni ame̱tšẽ ke̱-banina yomai le̱ ni ame̱lõame̱ ke̱-te, ni amegbe tšũdši le̱ ke̱ klante; ni mikometō pe̱ midše mli, ni mibatſao adafi ne̱. *

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Beni le̱ hũ ewieo̱ lolo le̱, mokroko hũ ba ni ebakē̱ ake̱: Obihĩĩ le̱ ke̱ obiyei le̱ miye nii ni ame̱mīnu wein ye̱ ame̱nyemi nukpa le̱ we le̱;

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: ni na, ahum kple ko tſa ke̱-dše̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ gbe̱ ni ebalō šĩa le̱ kodši edſe̱ le̱, ni ewule eſie oblahĩĩ le̱ ano̱ ni ame̱-gboi; ni mikometō pe̱ midše mli, ni mi-batſao adafi ne̱.

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hiob te ši ni *egbla ehe atadei ni eku eyi, ni eho ebu šikpoṅ, ni eso̱le, *

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: *Yayai mike̱-dše̱ minye mũsũṅ miba, ni yayai mike̱-akũ mise̱ ke̱-ate. Iehowa ṅō-hã, ni Iehowa ebaṅõ ke̱-te; aadšie Iehowa gbei le̱ yi kẽ! Dsads.

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Ene̱ fẽ mli le̱ Hiob efee eša ko, ni asaṅ eke̱ sane gbonyo ko ſaa Nyoṅmo̱.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa kē̱ satan ake: Ani oṅõ otšui ofõ mitšũlo̱ Hiob hũ no̱ lo? Edšake̱ mokomoko be̱ ni tamo̱le̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, edši nū *ni kpa ko be̱ ehe ni edša, ešeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei, ni eso̱leo̱ ehe ye̱ efõṅ he; ni asaṅ ehĩe eno̱kwayeli le̱ mli kpẽṅṅ lolo, tše̱ ohã mite ši míwole̱ ní mikpãtã ehĩe yakatſā! *

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Ši satan to he hã Iehowa ake̱: Ake̱ hewolo hãa ye̱ hewolo nãdšiaṅ, ni nofẽno ni moko yo̱ le̱ eṅõ-hãa ye̱ ewala hewo̱!

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa kē̱ satan ake̱: Na, eye odeṅ; ši ewala yi ke̱ke̱ obā!

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni *eṅã kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ohĩe ono̱kwayeli ne̱ mli kpēṅṅ lolo lo? Kwa Nyoṅmo̱ ní ogbo! *

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Ši ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Owieo̱ tamo yei bului le̱ eko wieo̱. Ei, nõkpakpa le̱ wo̱-he ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ deṅ, ši nõfõṅ le̱, no le̱ wo̱kahe lo? *Ene̱ fẽ mli le̱ Hiob ke̱ enābu efee eša ko. *

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ beni Hiob nanemei etẽ le̱ nu amanehũlũ ni eba eno̱ ne̱ fẽ he-le̱, ame̱teṅ mofẽmo dše̱ heni eyo̱ eba, Elifaz, *Temannyo le̱, ke̱ Bildad, †Šuhinyo le̱, ke̱ Zofar, **Naamanyo le̱, ni ame̱nä fe ekome ake̱ ame̱ate ame̱yayele̱ ṅko̱mo̱ ni ame̱še̱dše emī. *

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱hole ame̱hĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ye̱šoṅṅ, ši ame̱yoole̱; ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱hole ame̱gbēi ano̱ ni ame̱fó, ni ame̱teṅ mofẽmo gbla ehe atadei, ni ame̱gbe̱ mlu ke̱-te ṅwei ame̱wo ame̱yiteaṅ.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bo ame̱trá ehe ye̱ šikpoṅ nyōṅnyōṅ ke̱ ſanefane gbĩĩ kpawo so̱ṅṅ, ni mokomoko ke̱le̱ ewiee wiemo ko; edšake̱ ame̱na ake̱ ēna nõ babaō dientše̱.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Ene̱ se̱ le̱ Hiob gble enā ni elomo̱ egbĩ.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Ni Hiob wó ena no̱ ni ekē̱:

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: Hã *gbĩ ní afo̱mi ye̱ no̱ le̱ alādše, ke̱ nyōṅ ní kē̱ ake̱: Aná binū mũsũ! le̱. *Ier.

english_verse: and send thick, gloomy shadows to fill it with dread.
translation_verse: Hã ní duṅ ke̱ gbĕlebō̃ṅ aṅõle̱; hã atatu kabitī ahĩ eno̱, noni hãa duṅ woo̱ ſane awo ehe gbeyei!

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Na, nakai nyōṅ le̱ afe kene, nyã́mo̱ lala akaba mli!

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: edšake̱ eṅã́ã́ minye mũsũ nā, ni eṅõõ haomo̱ etēē-mihĩṅme̱ii!

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Mẽhewo̱ ſuo̱ hemi fõ eno̱? Ni mẽba miná fufo̱ miye?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Kũle̱ bene̱ mikã ši kpō; kũle̱ mi-wo̱, ni mihe edšō̱mi,

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: mike̱ maṅtše̱meĩ ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ adšinafoi ní mãmoo̱ tšūi fodši ame̱hãa ame̱he le̱;

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: alo mike̱ lume̱i hũ ni yo̱ šika le̱, mei ni ke̱ dſie̱te̱i ewo ame̱šĩai obõbõ le̱;

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: lo mife tamo šrãkemo̱bi ni afũle̱ ni ebe̱, lo tamo̱ abifabii ni enaa la le̱.

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Dše̱i le̱ efõṅfelo̱i efõ mo haomo̱; ni dše̱i le̱ mei ní eto̱ame̱ le̱ ewo ame̱tšui.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: Mẽba aṅõ la abã moni ehao le̱, ni ahãa moni were̱ eho ehe le̱ hũ yi náa wala?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Mei ní ſeo̱ gbĕle, ní ebaa, ni ame̱-tšaä ši ame̱taoo̱ fè dſetrii ní aṅõ-tē le̱; Kpods.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: mei ṅi ame̱mī še̱o̱ ame̱he babaō, ni ame̱nyãa ké̱ ame̱na gbonyobu le̱,

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: ke̱ nū ni aṅõ egbe̱ atē, ni Nyoṅmo̱ *esá eyi le̱?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ké̱ mibaye nii pe̱ mikẽmo̱i le̱ eba, ṅi miblo̱mo̱i le̱ fo̱seo̱ ſieo̱ ši ta-mo̱ nu.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Mihe edšo̱komi, nī mináko miyitšo tōhe, ni mitšui enyõko mimli, ši kẽle̱ haomo̱ miba lolo!

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ mumo̱ ní emūo̱ le̱ nā le̱ ame̱hĩe kpãtãa, ni ame̱plenēo̱ ye̱ emliſũ kō̱yo̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Dšata hū̃mo̱ ke̱ olōwo̱ gbẽ ke̱ dšatabii atšodši fẽ ekũmoo̱.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Dšata ní he wa hĩe kpãtãa ye̱ ko-lo ní enáá emõ eye hewo, ni dšatayō bii gbe̱o̱ ſãa.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Ye̱ nyōṅ nināi ahe dſẽṅmo̱i amli, beni wo̱ ni tší nyōo̱ gbomei ano̱ le̱,

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Ewa edamo̱ ši, ši miyoo esu, subãṅ ko badamo̱ mihĩe; efe krãnã, ši kẽ-le̱ minu gbē ko:

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: Aso adesã ko aadša ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe? alo nū ko he aatše ye̱ moni fele̱ le̱ hĩe?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Na, etšũdši le̱ tete eke ehe efõõ ame̱no̱, ni ebo̱foi le̱ hũ, enaä tõmo̱ ye̱ amehe:

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: mbasroo mei ní hĩo̱ *sũtšūi amli, ní mlu mli ato ame̱šiši ye̱, ní ame̱fufluo̱ ye̱ omlẽgẽ hĩe! *

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Beni aadše̱ lebi ke̱-yaši gbe̱ke̱ le̱, akposaame̱; dãni moko aayo le̱, ame̱hĩe ekpãtã kwrakwra.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Ani dšee tšere̱mo̱ atšere̱o̱ ame̱bukpãi le̱ ye̱ ame̱he? Ame̱lee nii āhũ ni ame̱gboio̱.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: ši gbomo ádesã le̱ afo̱ö̱le̱ ahãa haomo̱, tamo bo̱ni lalile̱ii flikio̱ ke̱-yaä ṅwei gbe̱ le̱.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: Emõo̱ nilelo̱i ye̱ ame̱ṅā fõṅ le̱ mli, ni mei fõdši ayiṅtõ le̱ ebutuo̱.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Ame̱ke̱ duṅ kpeo̱ ſane fintĩ, ni ame̱-gbugbũo̱ ši ſane mlemle tamo nyōṅ. Ies.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Ehereo̱ ohĩafoi ayiwala ke̱-dše̱o̱ klante nā, ke̱-dše̱o̱ ame̱dāṅ ke̱ hewalo̱ le̱ deṅ hũ.

english_verse: Consider yourself fortunate if God All-Powerful chooses to correct you.
translation_verse: Na, adšō̱ ádesã ní Nyoṅmo̱ kãale̱ le̱! Nohewo̱ le̱ kãgbe Ofe le̱ tšo̱semo̱ le̱ he guo̱. Abei

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ epilaä mo, ni esā efĩo̱ no̱ hũ; etſaã mo nõ, ni enidšĩ noṅṅ tšáa.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Eedšieo ye̱ amanei ekpa mli, ni noni dši kpawo le̱ mli hũ nõfõṅ ko esaṅ ohe. Abe̱i

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Eehereo ke̱-adše̱ lile̱i kplebi nā, ni kē̱ hĩekpãtãmo̱ mība le̱, ošeṅ gbeyei.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Oonmõ hĩekpãtãmo̱ ke̱ hõmo̱ fẽ, ni asaṅ ošeṅ ṅāṅ koloi agbeyei;

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: edšake̱ oke̱ ṅãno̱ tei po aakpãṅ, ni ṅãṅ koloi hũ ke̱o aabo nanyo; Hos.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: ni ooná ole ake̱ obũ le̱ ye̱ ſeſēſe, ni ké̱ okwe̱ ošihĩle̱he le̱, oona ake̱ eſe̱-koö nokonoko;

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: ni ooná ole ake̱ osešibii le̱ bafá pī, ni oſĩei le̱ batamo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ dſe̱i.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Oogbo̱ kotokoto dãni oote ogbonyobu mli, tamo̱ boni ake̱ ṅmā̃kei baã ye̱ ebe mli le̱.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Na, wo̱tao ene̱ mli, ni nakai eyo̱! Bo toi, ni bo hũ ole ohã ohe!

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: Miná ni kũle̱ aṅmẽ miw̌ere̱hō le̱, ni mihedšramo̱ le̱ hũ aṅõ fẽ awo nsẽni mli!

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ Ofe le̱ gãimlibii le̱ tše̱ke̱ ši ye̱ mimli, ni mimumo̱ le̱ minu ame̱-nā ebō̱ le̱; Nānyoṅmo̱ he ṅmiṅmii hũ egbá ta ewomi. Lal.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Ani ṅāṅ tedši blo̱ö̱ kē̱ ená dſe̱i le̱? alo tšina blo̱ö̱ ye̱ eniyenii ahe?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Ani ayeo̱ nii mute̱ ni ṅō be̱ mli? alo ṅõmo̱ ko ye̱ wuo̱wŏ̱lo̱ mli eye̱ṅ le̱ mli?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Nii ní misusuma sumo̱o̱ ake̱ eeta he le̱, nomei noṅṅ etšṍ miniyenii ni yo̱ nyãṅemo̱.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
