english_verse: The second place I went was Egypt, where everyone had to drink from the cup, including the king and his officials, the other government workers, the rest of the Egyptians,
translation_verse: Farao, Mizraim maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ, ke̱ etšũdši le̱ ke̱ elumei le̱ ke̱ emaṅ mū le̱ fẽ,

english_verse: and all the foreigners who lived in the country. Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod.
translation_verse: ke̱ futufutugbomei le̱ fẽ, ke̱ Uz šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ, ke̱ Filistibii ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ Aškelon ke̱ Gaza ke̱ Ekron ke̱ Ašdod mei ní eſe̱ le̱,

english_verse: Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon,
translation_verse: ke̱ Edom ke̱ Moab ke̱ Amonbii le̱,

english_verse: and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea.
translation_verse: ke̱ Tiro maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ Zidon maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ ṅšo̱kpo̱ ni yo̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ se̱ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱,

english_verse: After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert,
translation_verse: ke̱ Arabia maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ futufutugbomei ní hĩo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ amaṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ,

english_verse: and the countries in the north, both near and far. I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
translation_verse: ke̱ kōyigbe̱ maṅtše̱mei le̱ fẽ, mei ní be̱ṅke̱ ke̱ mei ní yo̱ šoṅṅ le̱ fẽ, ke̱ ši-kpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅtše̱yelii fẽ ní yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, ni ame̱fẽ ame̱se̱ le̱ *Šešak maṅtše̱ le̱ aana! *

english_verse: The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
translation_verse: Ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Nyenua, ni nyetŏ̱ro̱a, ni nyeſea, ni nyegbēgbēa ši, ni nyekate ši doṅṅ ye̱ klante ní mibatšũ ke̱-ba nyeteṅ le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱, kē̱ ame̱kplẽẽ ake̱ ame̱ahe kpulu le̱ ye̱ odeṅ ame̱nu le̱, okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot kē̱ no̱: Nu kẽ nyeanu!

english_verse: Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ na, *midše šiši mife maṅ ní aṅõ migbe̱i awole̱ le̱ efõṅ, ni nye ni nyeaṅõ nyehe nyeye kwrā lo? Nyeṅõṅ nyehe nyeyeṅ, ši moṅ matšé̱ klante ke̱-aba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii fẽ no̱, Iehowa Zebaot kē̱. *

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: From my sacred temple I will roar like thunder, while I trample my people and everyone else as though they were grapes.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, gba ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ otšõame̱ ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iehowa aadše̱ ṅwei *ahũ, ni eewo egbē ke̱-adše̱ ešihĩle̱he kroṅkroṅ le̱, eehū̃ wā ewo ekoloi alẽ̱̀he le̱; eebo oše ewo šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii ſẽ tamo̱ weinṅã̀lo̱i anõ! *Ioel

english_verse: My voice will be heard everywhere on earth, accusing nations of their crimes and sentencing the guilty to death. Disaster Is Coming
translation_verse: Gbē̱mo̱ aayaše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ nēgbēhe tō̃; edšake̱ Iehowa ke̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ená, eke helo flā bakodšo: meifõdsi le̱, eeṅõ-ame̱ ehã klante! Iehowa kē̱.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says: You can see disaster spreading from far across the earth, from nation to nation like a horrible storm.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot kē̱ ne̱: Na, efõṅ aadše̱ dšeṅmaṅ no̱ aya dšeṅmaṅ no̱, ni ahum kpeteṅkple aate ši ke̱-adše̱ ši-kpoṅ le̱ nāgbēhe tō̃;

english_verse: The Lord's people are his flock, and you leaders were the shepherds. But now it's your turn to be butchered like sheep. You'll shatter like fine pottery dropped on the floor. So roll on the ground, crying and mourning.
translation_verse: Nyewo̱a lele ko, nye *tōkwe̱lo̱i, ni nyeblo̱a, ni nyekokloa ši ye̱ lamlu mli nye toi le̱ amli ekpakpai; edšake̱ nyegbē-gbĩĩ le̱ ese̱, ni madſăranye wo̱tšo̱wo̱tšo̱, ni nyeagbēgbē ši tamo̱ šō̃nõ ni dšra wa! *

english_verse: You have nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. *
translation_verse: Ni foidšē aalādse tōkwe̱lo̱i lo̱, ni toi le̱ amli ekpakpai le̱ náṅ gbe̱ adše mli.

english_verse: Listen to the cries of the shepherds, as the Lord's burning anger turns peaceful meadows into barren deserts.
translation_verse: ni hedšo̱le̱ šihĩle̱hei le̱ efite ye̱ Iehowa mliſũ ní nā wa le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Like a lion leaving its den, the Lord has abandoned his people to the destruction of war.
translation_verse: Ešĩ ebu le̱ efõ ši tamo̱ dšata, ni ame̱šikpoṅ le̱ etšṍ amaṅfõ ye̱ yiwale̱ klante le̱ hĩe, ke̱ emlifũ ní nā wa le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
translation_verse: le ke̱ke̱ nyelea ake̱, ke̱dši nyegbemi le̱, lá ní efeko noko nyebalō nyeſie nye ke̱ maṅ ne̱ ke̱ emli bii le̱ ano̱; edšake̱ eye̱ mli le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ Iehowa tšũmi nyeṅõ, koni mibawie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ ye̱ nye-toiiaṅ!

english_verse: Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once,
translation_verse: ní nyebo mitšũdši, gbalo̱i le̱, ní mitšũo̱ nyeṅõ, ni miteo̱ ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa mitšũo̱ame̱, ši nyeboo toi le̱, awiemo̱i le̱ atoi le̱:

english_verse: and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
translation_verse: Mẽhewo̱ ogba ye̱ Iehowa gbe̱i amli ake̱: Ne̱ke̱ šĩa ne̱ aatšṍ tamo̱ Šilo, ni ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ aatšṍ amaṅfõ ni moko ehĩṅ mli doṅṅ le̱? Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ nā bakpe ši ame̱wo Ieremia he ye̱ Iehowa we le̱.

english_verse: The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial.
translation_verse: Ni beni Iuda lume̱i le̱ nu ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ le̱, ame̱dše̱ maṅtše̱ we le̱ ke̱-ba Iehowa we le̱, ni ame̱batrá ši ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ agbó hē le̱ nā.

english_verse: While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ gbalo̱i le̱ kē̱ lume̱i le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ake̱: Nū ne̱ sa gbĕle; edšake̱ egba *eši maṅ ne̱, take̱ bo̱ni nyedientše̱ nyenu ke̱ nyetoii le̱! *Bo̱f.

english_verse: Then I told the judges and everyone else: The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyesāa nyegbè̱i ke̱ nyenifemo̱nii le̱, ni nyeboa Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbē toi, ni Iehowa aaſa ehe ye̱ nõfõṅ ní ewie ye̱ nyehe le̱ he-wo̱!

english_verse: You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right.
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱, na, miye̱ nyedeṅ: nyefeami bo̱ni hĩ ke̱ bo̱ni dša ye̱ nyehĩe;

english_verse: The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni lume̱i le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ kē̱ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ gbalo̱i le̱ ake̱: Nū ne̱ esaa gbĕle; edšake̱ Iehowa gbe̱i amli ewie etšõwo̱ ye̱.

english_verse: Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that
translation_verse: Ni šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ onukpai le̱ ateṅ meikomei te ši, ni ame̱kē̱ maṅ le̱ gwabō̱ mū le̱ fẽ ake̱:

english_verse: Then the leaders continued: No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would. People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
translation_verse: Ani gbe Iuda maṅtše̱ Hezekia ke̱ Iuda fẽ gbĕle̱? Ani dšee Iehowa gbeyei moṅ eše ni etao Iehowa hĩegbe̱, ni Iehowa hũ *ſa ehe ye̱ efõṅ ni ewie eši-ame̱ le̱ hewo̱? Ni wo̱ le̱ wo̱o̱fe efõṅ kple ne̱ wo̱ši wo̱susumai lo? *

english_verse: So have them tell their kings that I have said: I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel,
translation_verse: ni ofã́ame̱ ní ame̱yakē̱ ame̱nuṅtšo̱mei le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Nyeyakē̱a nyenuṅtšo̱mei le̱ ake̱:

english_verse: and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth,
translation_verse: Mi mife šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ gbomei ke̱ koloi ní yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ye̱ mihewale̱ kpeteṅkple le̱ ke̱ minine ní mikpã mli le̱ nā, ni miṅõ-hãa mofẽmo ní misumoo̱;

english_verse: This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱ dšeṅmaṅ lo maṅtše̱yeli ní súmo̱o̱ le̱ Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱kue̱ woo Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ apã le̱ šiši le̱, mike̱ klante ke̱ hõmo̱ ke̱ gbĕle-hela aawo nakai dšeṅmaṅ le̱ nyõmo̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní matšṍ enine no̱ maplenẽame̱, Iehowa kē̱.

english_verse: After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said: Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
translation_verse: Ni miwie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ mitšõ Zedekia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ni mikē̱: Nyeke̱ nyekue̱ awoa Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ apã le̱ šiši ni nyesúmo̱ale̱ ke̱ emaṅ le̱, ni nyeyi aná wala!

english_verse: But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned.
translation_verse: Mẽba ni oke̱ omaṅ le̱ aagboi ye̱ klante ke̱ hõmo̱ ke̱ gbĕle-hela nā, take̱ bo̱ni Iehowa ewie ye̱ dšeṅmaṅ ní súmo̱ṅ Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ he le̱?

english_verse: When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said: Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying!
translation_verse: Ni asaṅ miwie mitšõ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū ne̱ fẽ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Nyekaboa nyegbalo̱i ní gbaä hãanye ake̱: “Na, etše̱ṅ ni *aaṅõ Iehowa we le̱ nibii le̱ ke̱-adše̱ Babel ke̱-aba ekoṅ!” le̱ awiemo̱i le̱ atoi; edšake̱ amale gbale̱ ame̱gbaä ame̱hãanye le̱. *

english_verse: If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši gbalo̱i dšiame̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ye̱ ame̱mli le̱, hã ni ame̱kpa Iehowa Zebaot fai moṅ, koni nibii ní eſe̱ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ke̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱ ke̱ Ierusalem le̱ akaya Babel.

english_verse: Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ye̱ nakai afi le̱ no̱ noṅṅ, ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Zedekia maṅtše̱yeli le̱ šišidsē mli, ye̱ afi ní dši edſe̱ le̱ no̱ nyõṅ ní dši enumo̱ le̱ no̱, ake̱ Hanania, Ašur bi ní dši gbalo̱ ní dše̱ Gibeon le̱, kē̱mi ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ye̱ oso̱foi le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ hĩe ake̱:

english_verse: King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
translation_verse: ni asaṅ Iuda maṅtše̱ *Iekonia, Iehoiakim bi le̱, ke̱ Iuda nomi fẽ ni ete Babel le̱, maṅõame̱ ke̱-ba bie̱ ne̱ ekoṅ, Iehowa kē̱, edšake̱ mikũmo̱ Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ apã le̱. *

english_verse: Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home.
translation_verse: ni gbalo̱ Ieremia kē̱: Amen! Iehowa afe nakai! Iehowa ahã owiemo̱i ni ogba le̱ aba mli, ni eṅõ Iehowa we le̱ nibii le̱ ke̱ nomi le̱ fẽ ke̱-dše̱ Babel ke̱-ba bie̱ ne̱ ekoṅ!

english_verse: But let me remind you and everyone else
translation_verse: Kẽle̱ agbe̱ne̱ bo wiemo̱ ní miwieo̱ ye̱ otoiiaṅ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ toiiaṅ ne̱ toi:

english_verse: that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease.
translation_verse: Gbalo̱i ní tšṍ mike̱o fẽ hĩe ke̱-dše̱ tetēte le̱, ame̱gba ye̱ tai ke̱ nõſõṅ ke̱ gbĕle-hela hewo̱ ame̱ši šikpõdši babaō ko̱ maṅtše̱yeli wudši;

english_verse: Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
translation_verse: gbalo̱ ní gbaä hedšo̱le̱ le̱, ke̱dši gbalo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ná ba mli le̱, no dãni aleo̱ gbalo̱ le̱ ake̱ Iehowa tšũle̱ le̱le̱ṅ!

english_verse: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbalo̱ Hanania le̱ dšie kõṅtšo le̱ ke̱-dše̱ gbalo̱ Ieremia kue̱, ni ekũmo̱ mli;

english_verse: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
translation_verse: ni Hanania kē̱ ye̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ hĩe ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ne̱ke̱ pe̱ mibakũmo̱ Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, apã le̱ ke̱-dše̱ dšeṅmãdši fẽ akue̱ *bie̱ afii enyo̱! Ni Ieremia yiṅ ete. *K.

english_verse: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
translation_verse: ni Elasa, Šafan bi le̱, ke̱ Gemaria, Hilkia bi le̱, mei ní Iuda maṅtše̱ Zedekia tšũ ke̱-te Babel maṅtše̱ Nebukadnezar ṅõ ye̱ Babel le̱, anine no̱ etšṍ ke̱-mãdše:

english_verse: I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering.
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱ mile dſẽṅmo̱i ní midſẽṅo̱ ye̱ nyehe, Iehowa kē̱: hedšo̱le̱ dſẽṅmo̱i ni, ši dšee efõṅ nõ ni, koni mike̱ nāgbē ni nyehĩe kã no̱ le̱ ahãnye!

english_verse: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Ni nyeatšé̱mi, ni nyeate nyeakpami fai, ni mabonye toi;

english_verse: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
translation_verse: ni nyeataomi, ni nyeanami, ke̱-dši nyetao mise̱gbe̱ ke̱ nyetšui fẽ le̱;

english_verse: and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: ni mahã nyenami, Iehowa ke̱. Ni *makpale nyenomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱-ba ekoṅ, ni mabua nyenā ke̱-adše̱ dšeṅmãdši fiā no̱ ke̱ hei fiā ni miſienye ke̱-te le̱, Iehowa kē̱, ni mike̱nye aakũ se̱ ke̱-aba bie̱ ne̱ heni mihã aṅõnye nom ke̱-dše̱ ke̱-te le̱ ekoṅ! *Lal.

english_verse: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ši nyekē̱o̱ ake̱: Iehowa etē gbalo̱i aši ehãwo̱ ye̱ Babel!

english_verse: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
translation_verse: Ši nye le̱, nyeboa Iehowa wiemo̱ toi, nye *nomi fẽ ni mihã nyedše Ierusalem ke̱-te Babel le̱! *K.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
translation_verse: Iehowa ewoö oso̱fo ye̱ oso̱fo Iehoiada nãdšiaṅ, koni nyetšṍmo̱ no̱kwe̱lo̱i ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ nyehã mofẽmo ní *eye se̱ke̱ ni efeo̱ ehe gbalo̱, ni obo̱le̱ apã ni owole̱ gbokle̱ le̱: *Hos.

english_verse: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
translation_verse: mẽba okãã Ieremia, Anatotnyo le̱, ní feo ehe gbalo̱ ehãanye le̱?

english_verse: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
translation_verse: Ni oso̱fo Zefania kane ne̱ke̱ wolo ne̱ ye̱ gbalo̱ Ieremia toiiaṅ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Ieremia ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
translation_verse: Tšũ aya nomi le̱ fẽ ṅõ ayakē̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ye̱ Šemaia, Nehelamnyo le̱, he ne̱: Ake̱-ní Šemaia gba ehãnye, ni mitšũkole̱, ni ehã nyeṅõ nyehĩe nyefo amale no̱

english_verse: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: hewo le̱, bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mawo Šemaia, Nehelamnyo le̱, ke̱ eseši le̱ nyõmo̱; enáṅ nū ko ní aahĩ maṅ ne̱ teṅ, ni asaṅ enaṅ edšŭrõ ní mibafe mimaṅ le̱, Iehowa kē̱; edšake̱ *ewie atũatšemo̱ wiemo̱ eši Iehowa. *

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Wo̱nu hekpokpomo̱ gbē ke̱ gbeyeišemo̱ nõ, ni dšee hedšo̱le̱ nõ!

english_verse: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ye̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱, Iehowa Zebaot kē̱, ake̱ makũmo̱ *epã le̱ ke̱-adše̱ okue̱, ni matšere̱ okpãi le̱, ni meikpõdši yeṅo nyṍṅ doṅṅ; *

english_verse: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mike̱o ye̱, Iehowa kē̱, ko-ni mahere oyiwala. Edšake̱ mafite dšeṅ-mãdši ní migbe̱o miſã ame̱teṅ le̱ fẽ ke̱-mõ ši; ši bo le̱ mifiteṅo ke̱-mõṅ ši, ši moṅ magbla otoi *bo̱ni sa ke̱ke̱, ni mihãṅ oṅõ ohe oye kwrā. *

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: *Ohedšramo̱ le̱ ewo wu, ni opilame̱ le̱ wa. *

english_verse: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
translation_verse: Osuolo̱i le̱ fẽ ahĩe ekpa ono̱, ame̱-bii oši doṅṅ; edšake̱ mipilao tamo̱ henye̱lo̱ pilaä mo, tamo̱ yiwalo̱ gblaä mo toi, ye̱ onišaianii le̱ afále̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ ohe ešai le̱ dăra naakpa.

english_verse: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ mei fẽ ní yeo̱o le̱, aaye-ame̱, ni ohenye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ, ame̱fẽ-kwa, ame̱-ate nomṅō̃ mli, ni mei ni tſaä bo odšo le̱, aatſaame̱ odšo, ni mei fẽ ní haäo le̱, mike̱ame̱ aahã ní ahaame̱! Ies.

english_verse: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Ši mafĩmo̱ *ofadši le̱ ano̱, ni matšá opilamo̱i le̱, Iehowa kē̱; edšake̱ ame̱-tšé̱o̱o ake̱ moni aſiele̱, Zion ní moko bii eši! *

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
translation_verse: Boni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: *Na, makpale Iakob būi le̱ anomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱-aba ekoṅ, ni mimũsũṅ aatšõmi ye̱ ešihĩle̱hei le̱ ahewo̱, ni aato maṅ le̱ ye̱ egoṅkpo̱ le̱ no̱, ni mō̃ le̱ aamã emā̃he le̱! *K.

english_verse: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bii aatšṍmo̱ tamo̱ sá le̱, ni ame̱safo le̱ aamã ši šiṅṅ ye̱ mihĩe, ni mawo mei ní waäame̱ yi le̱ fẽ nyõmo̱.

english_verse: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
translation_verse: Ni *ame̱lumo le̱ aadše̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱teṅ, ni ame̱teṅ noṅṅ ame̱no̱yelo̱ le̱ aadše̱, ni mahã etši ebe̱ṅke̱mi; ši namo aaši etšitši ni ebe̱ṅke̱mi? Iehowa kē̱. *K.

english_verse: You will be my people, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱atšṍ mimaṅ, ni mi hũ matšṍ ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱.

english_verse: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
translation_verse: Iehowa mlifũ ní nā wa le̱ kpaleṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eefe egbe nā ni eehã etšui mli yiṅtōi le̱ aba mli, ni nāgbē gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ nyeana šiši!

english_verse: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
translation_verse: Masā mamāo ekoṅ, ni oomã ši, Israel oblayōl Ootšotšŏro omĩdši le̱ ekoṅ ni oodše kpo ye̱ mei ni mli efliame̱ le̱ adšõ̀ le̱ mli!

english_verse: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
translation_verse: Ame̱aba ke̱ yāfó ke̱ faikpamo̱, makplaame̱ ni mahã amenyie fāi atoi ye̱ gbe̱ trōmō̃ no̱, heni ame̱tĕ̱re̱ṅ ye̱, edšake̱ *mi-tšṍ Israel tše̱, ni mikromo̱bi dši Efraim! *

english_verse: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
translation_verse: Ši beni mikpale ke̱-dše̱ ohe le̱ se̱ le̱, miſa mihe, ni beni ahã miná mile se̱ le̱, migbla miſuo̱ he mãi: mihĩe gbo, ni mihĩe ſie ši; edšake̱ mitēre miblahīaṅ ahorabē̱ le̱.

english_verse: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Aso mibinū dšŭrõ dši Efraim, alo bi ní mimī še̱o̱ ehe ni? edšake̱ šiiabo̱ fẽ ni miwieo̱ mišio̱le̱ le̱ *mikaio̱le̱ kẽ; nohewo̱ le̱ †mimli nṍmoo̱mi ye̱ ehewo̱, mimũsũṅ tšõo̱mi ye̱ ehe kẽ! Iehowa kē̱. *Ies.

english_verse: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
translation_verse: Mãmo̱ gbe̱kadimo̱nii ohã ohe, ni omãmo̱ gbe̱tšõmo̱tšei hũ ohã ohe, hã odſẽṅmo̱ akã gbe̱dšegbe̱ le̱, gbe̱ ní onyie no̱ ke̱-te le̱ no̱; kpalemo̱ ke̱-ba ko, Israel oblayō, kpalemo̱ ke̱-ba omãdši ne̱ amli!

english_verse: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
translation_verse: Mẽ beyino̱ noṅṅ olilā ši ke̱-yaši, bo biyō ní okpale ke̱-te se̱? Ši Iehowa ebo̱ nõ hē ko ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱: yō aaba-bo̱le nū he!

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Kē̱ mikpale ame̱nomṅō̱̃ le̱ ke̱-ba le̱, ame̱awie ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ne̱ ye̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ emãdši le̱ amli ake̱: Iehowa adsō̱o, bo dšale̱ šihĩle̱he, bo goṅ kroṅkroṅ!

english_verse: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
translation_verse: Ni Iuda ke̱ emãdši fẽ-tſẽm aahĩ mli, okwāfoi hũ ke̱ mei ni ke̱ ame̱tōi-ku kpaä ši le̱.

english_verse: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
translation_verse: Ene̱ no̱ mihĩe tšẽ ye̱ ni mikwe̱, ni miwo le̱ ṅõ minā.

english_verse: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
translation_verse: Ni aaba mli ake̱, bo̱ni miši kpe ye̱ ame̱he, ní mafãmo̱, ní makũmo̱, ní mabutu, ní mafite, ní mafeame̱ efõṅ le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ maši kpe ye̱ ame̱he, ni mamãmo̱, ní mate̱oame̱, Iehowa kē̱.

english_verse: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ ano̱ le̱ ame̱kē̱ṅ doṅṅ ake̱: Tše̱mei le̱ eye weinyibii ṅmlikitii, ni bii le̱ moṅ anyãnyõdši eſã! Yāfó

english_verse: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Ši moṅ, mofẽmo aagbo ye̱ le̱dientše̱ enõša hewo̱, ni mofẽmo ní yeo̱ weinyibii ṅmlikitii le̱, le̱ noṅṅ enyãnyõdši aaſã.

english_verse: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
translation_verse: etamo̱o̱ kpãṅmo̱ ni mike̱ ame̱tše̱mei le̱ kpãṅ gbĩ ní mimõ amenine mli ni midšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱; nakai mikpãṅmo̱ le̱ ame̱kũ mli, tše̱ midši ame̱wù! Iehowa kē̱.

english_verse: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
translation_verse: Ni moko etšõṅ enanyo, ni asaṅ moko etšõṅ enyemi doṅṅ ake̱: Le Iehowa! edšake̱ ame̱fẽ-kwa ame̱ale-mi, ke̱-adše̱ ame̱teṅ mo bibiō no̱ ke̱-yaši ame̱teṅ mo wulu no̱. Iehowa kē̱; edšake̱ *maṅõ ame̱nišaianii le̱ mafa, ni ame̱he ešai le̱ mikaiṅdoṅṅ! *

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa, moni fe hũlũ ní ekpe ſane, ní ewo nyoṅtšĕre ke̱ ṅulamii akpoi ní ame̱kpe̱ nyōṅ, ní etaä ṅšo̱ mli ni emli ṅšo̱kei le̱ hũo̱, ní egbe̱i dši Iehowa Zebaot le̱, kē̱ ne̱:

english_verse: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ke̱dši ne̱ke̱ *akpo̱i ne̱ aalādše ye̱ mihĩe le̱, Iehowa kē̱, no †dãni Israel seši le̱ aatã, ni ame̱feṅ maṅ ye̱ mihĩe gbĩkogbĩko doṅṅ! *

english_verse: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ke̱dši aanyẽ ṅweii ní yo̱ yiteṅgbe̱ le̱ asusu, ni atao šikpoṅ le̱ šišitōi ni yo̱ šišigbe̱ le̱, no dãni mi hũ makwa Israel seši le̱ fiā ye̱ nibii fẽ ní ame̱fe le̱ hewo̱, Iehowa kē̱.

english_verse: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
translation_verse: Na, gbĩĩ mība, Iehowa kē̱, ní aato maṅ le̱ ahã Iehowa ke̱-adše̱ Hananel mō̃ ni kwo̱ le̱ he ke̱-yaši agbó ní yo̱ koṅ le̱ nā le̱ he; Zak.

english_verse: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
translation_verse: ni susumo̱ kpã le̱ aadše̱ dše̱i tē̃ ke̱-atšṍ Gareb goṅkpo̱ le̱ no̱, ni eedo̱ eyi ke̱-ba Goa;

english_verse: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_verse: ni gbohĩĩ ke̱ lamudši adšō̱ mū le̱ fẽ ke̱ ṅmõdsi le̱ fẽ ke̱-yaši Kidron fā le̱ nā, ke̱-yaši okpo̱ṅo̱i agbó le̱ koṅ ní ye bokãgbe̱ le̱ he le̱, aatšṍ kroṅkroṅ ahã Iehowa: akũmo̱ṅ ni awuleṅ aſieṅ ši doṅṅ ke̱-ate nāno̱!

english_verse: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Hanamel, mitše̱kwẽ le̱ bi le̱, ba miṅõ ye̱ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni Iehowa eke̱ le̱, ni ebake̱mi ake̱: He mišikpoṅ ní yo̱ Anatot ye̱ Benyamin šikpon le̱ no̱ le̱; edšake̱ bo oyo̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ oyeo̱ gbošinii, ni bo oyo̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ okpõo̱; be ohã ohe! Ke̱ke̱ ni mina ake̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ ni.

english_verse: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
translation_verse: ni miṅõ hemo̱-wolo le̱ mihã Baruk, Maeseia bi Neria bi le̱, ye̱ mitše̱kwẽ bi Hanamel ke̱ odasefoi ní eṅmã ame̱gbe̱i ye̱ hemo̱-wolo le̱ šiši le̱ ke̱ Iudafoi fẽ ní yo̱ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱ le̱ ahĩe;

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
translation_verse: Edšake̱ boni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Aahe šĩai ke̱ abō̱i ke̱ weintromi ye̱ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ ekoṅ!

english_verse: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: *onaä mei akpei abo mo̱bo̱, ni osā owoo tše̱mei anišaianii ahe nyõmo̱ ošãkãa ame̱bii ní baä ye̱ áme̱se̱ le̱ atšitši, bo Mawu kpeteṅkple ke̱ hewalo̱, Iehowa Zebaot dši ogbe̱i! *

english_verse: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
translation_verse: bo ní ofe okadii ke̱ nākpe̱nii ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱, ye̱ Israel ke̱ gbomei fẽ ateṅ, ni oke̱-he gbe̱i tamo̱ bo̱ni yo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱!

english_verse: But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster.
translation_verse: ni ame̱ba ni ame̱baṅõ-fe ame̱nõ, ši ame̱boo ogbe toi ni ame̱nyiee omlai le̱ amli hũ; nibii fẽ ni owoame̱ kitã ake̱ ame̱fe le̱, ame̱fee ekomeflo, nohewo̱ ni ohã ne̱ke̱ efõṅ ne̱ fẽ ba ame̱no̱ ne̱.

english_verse: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
translation_verse: ni kẽle̱ bo Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa noṅṅ oke̱mi ake̱: Oke̱ šika ahe šikpoṅ le̱, ni otšé̱ odasefoi abaye odase; tše̱bele̱ aṅõ maṅ le̱ awo Kaldeabii le̱ adeṅ!

english_verse: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, miṅõ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ miwo Kaldeabii le̱ adeṅ ke̱ Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, deṅ, ni eehaṅõle̱, K.

english_verse: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
translation_verse: Ši moṅ *ame̱ke̱ ame̱nihĩnii le̱ eto šĩa ní aṅõ migbe̱i awole̱ le̱, ni ame̱ke̱bulele̱; *

english_verse: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
translation_verse: ni ame̱mãmo̱ Baal hei groṅṅi le̱ ní yo̱ Hinom bi le̱ dšō̱ le̱ṅ le̱, koni ame̱hã ame̱bihĩī ke̱ ame̱biyei atšṍ la mli ahã Molek, noni mifã́ko ni esā ebako miyiṅ ake̱ ame̱fe ne̱ke̱ nihĩnii ne̱ ní ame̱ke̱-hã Iuda afe eša.

english_verse: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
translation_verse: Na, mi noṅṅ mabua ame̱nā ke̱-adše̱ šikpõdši fẽ ni miſieame̱ ke̱-te no̱ ye̱ mimlifũ ke̱ mlila ke̱ grimo̱ babaō nā le̱ ano̱, ni mike̱ame̱ aakũ se̱ ke̱-aba bie̱ ne̱ ekoṅ, ni mahã ame̱hĩ ší ſeſēſe.

english_verse: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱atšṍ mimaṅ, ni mi hũ matšṍ ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱;

english_verse: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Bo̱ni mike̱ ne̱ke̱ efõṅ kpeteṅkple ne̱ fẽ ba maṅ ne̱ no̱ le̱, nakai noṅṅ mike̱ ekpakpa fẽ ní miwoame̱ ši le̱ aaba ame̱no̱.

english_verse: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
translation_verse: Ni aahe abō̱i ye̱ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱, tše̱ nyekē̱o̱ ake̱ etšṍ amaṅfõ ní gbomo ke̱ kolo be̱ no̱ doṅṅ, ni aṅõ-wo Kaldeabii le̱ adeṅ.

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ake̱ šika aahehẽ abō̱i, ni aaṅmã no̱ wodši, ni aaso̱o nā, ni aatšé̱ odasefoi abaye odase, ye̱ Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Ierusalem niiaṅ ke̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ goṅ no̱ mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ ṅãno̱ mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ wuoyigbe̱ mãdši le̱ amli: edšake̱ *makpale ame̱nomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱-aba ekoṅ! Iehowa kē̱. *

english_verse: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
translation_verse: Ni matšũ ame̱he ke̱-adše̱ ame̱nišai anii fẽ ní ame̱ke̱-fe eša ame̱šimi le̱ mli; ni *maṅõ ame̱nišaianii fẽ ní ame̱ke̱-fe eša ame̱šimi ni ame̱ke̱-tõ mino̱ le̱ mafa-ame̱. *

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Boni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Bie̱ ne̱ ní nyekē̱o̱ ake̱ ehĩe ekpãtã ní gbomo lo kolo ehĩṅ mli doṅṅ le̱, ke̱ Iuda mãdši ke̱ Ierusalem blohũi ní etšṍmo̱ amaṅfõi ní gbomo be̱ mli ni moko be̱ ní hĩo̱ mli ni kolo ko be̱ mli le̱,

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: asaṅ *gõdši le̱ ano̱ mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ ṅãno̱ mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ wuoyigbe̱ mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Ierusalem niiaṅ ke̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ amli hũ, tōikui aatšṍ kanelo̱ nidši ašiši ke̱-ho ekoṅ, Iehowa kē̱. *

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Na, gbĩĩ mība, Iehowa kē̱, ní ma-hã wiemo̱ kpakpa ní miwie ye̱ Israel we le̱ ke̱ Iuda we le̱ he le̱ aba mli.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli ke̱ nakai be le̱ṅ le̱ mahã dšale̱ tšonine akwẽ ahã David, ni eekodšo ni eeye dšale̱ sane ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: Asaṅ oso̱foi, ní dši Levibii le̱ hũ, nū ní aašã šā̃-afo̱lei, ní eešã niyenii-afo̱lei, ní eegbe afo̱lei gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ ye̱ mi-hĩe, ebo̱ṅame̱.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba Ieremia ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: no le̱ aakũ mikpãṅmo̱ ni mike̱ mitšūlo̱ David ekpãṅ le̱ mli, ni enáṅ binū ni aatá esẽi le̱ no̱ aye maṅtše̱, ke̱ noni mike̱ Levibii, oso̱foi ní dši misúolo̱i le̱, ekpãṅ le̱ hũ!

english_verse: The Lord also said:
translation_verse: Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Ieremia ṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: Ani onako noni maṅ ne̱ wieo̱ ake̱: Wekui enyo̱ le̱, ní Iehowa hala le̱, ekwa-ame̱! ke̱ bo̱ni ame̱gbeo̱ mimaṅ le̱ he guo̱, ake amedšee dšeṅmaṅ doṅṅ ye̱ amehĩe le̱ lo?

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ke̱dši miſane ke̱ nyōṅ-he-kpãṅmo̱ le̱ emãã ši ni mitoko gbe̱nāi mihãko ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ le̱, K.

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: no le̱ makwa Iakob seši le̱, ke̱ mitšũlo̱ David nõ le̱ hũ, ni miṅõṅ esešibii le̱ ateṅ meikomei miwoṅame̱ Abraham ke̱ Isak ke̱ Iakob sešibii le̱ ano̱yelo̱i; edšake̱ *makpale ame̱nomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱-aba, ni mimũsũṅ aatšõmi ye̱ ame̱he! *

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: ni bodientše̱ hũ odšeṅ edeṅ, ši mõ kẽ aamõo, ni aaṅõo awo edeṅ, ni *oona Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe ke̱ hĩe, ni eke̱o aawie nābu ke̱ nābu, ni oote Babel! *

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbalo̱ Ieremia yadšadše wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ etšõ Zedekia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ye̱ Ierusalem,

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Ši fe se̱ le̱ ame̱hã ame̱wehĩĩ ke̱ ame̱weyei ní ame̱hã ame̱ye ame̱he le̱ kũ se̱ ke̱-ba ekoṅ, ni ame̱nyẽ ame̱no̱, koni ame̱tsṍmo̱ ame̱wehĩĩ ke̱ ame̱weyei ekoṅ.

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Mike̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ kpãṅ gbĩ ní miyadšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ke̱-dše̱ nyṍdši awe le̱, ake̱:

english_verse: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
translation_verse: Afii kpawo se̱ le̱ nyeteṅ mofẽmo ahã enyemi Hebrinyo ní ehõ ehe ehãle̱ le̱ aṅõ ehe ayaye, ni ké̱ esúmo̱o afii ekpa le̱, ke̱ke̱ le̱ ohã edše oṅõ, ni eṅõ ehe eyaye; ši nyetše̱mei le̱ boomi toi, ni asaṅ ame̱hãã ame̱toi aba no̱.

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Ši nyekũ nyese̱ ni nyeyabule migbe̱i le̱, ni mofẽmo ehã ewenū ke̱ eweyō ní nyehā ame̱ye ame̱he ye̱ ame̱tšui nā le̱ ekũ ese̱ eba ekoṅ, ni nyenyẽ ame̱-uo̱, ni ame̱tsṍmo̱ nyewehĩĩ ke̱ nyeweyei ekoṅ.

english_verse: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
translation_verse: Ni maṅõ hĩĩ le̱ ni eto mikpãṅmo̱ le̱, ni ame̱yee kpãṅmo̱ ni ame̱kpãṅ ye̱ mihĩe, beni ame̱gbá tšinabi mli enyo̱ ni *ame̱tsṍ efãfãi le̱ ateṅ le̱, wiemo̱i le̱ ano̱ le̱ mahã: *

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni miyaṅõ Iaazania, Habazinia bi Ieremia bi le̱, ke̱ enyemimei ke̱ ebihĩĩ le̱ fẽ ke̱ Rekab-bii le̱ awe le̱ bii fẽ,

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: ní miṅõ kpudši ni eyimo̱ obõbõ ke̱ wein ke̱ tšenei mimāmo̱ Rekab-bii le̱ awe le̱ bii le̱ ahĩe, ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyenua wein!

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Wo̱nuu wein! edšake̱ wo̱tše̱ *Ionadab, Rekab bi le̱, wowo̱ kitã ake̱: Nyekanua wein gbĩkogbĩko, nye ke̱ nyebii fẽ, *

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, fã ke̱-ba šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, wo̱kē̱ ake̱: Nyebaä ní wo̱dšea Kaldeabii ata le̱ ke̱ Arambii ata le̱ hĩe wo̱yaä Ierusalem! no dši Ierusalem ni wo̱yo̱ ne̱.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Aye Ionadab, Rekab bi le̱, wiemo̱i ní eke̱-wo ebii le̱ akitã ake̱ ame̱kanu wein le̱ no̱, ni ame̱nuu eko ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, edšake̱ ame̱bo ame̱tše̱ kitã le̱ toi: ši mi le̱ miwieo̱ mitsõo̱nye, miteo̱ ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa ni miwieo̱ mitšõo̱nye, ši nyeboomi toi.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: Ni mitšũo̱ mitšũdši ni dši gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱-baä nyeṅõ, miteo̱ ši lebi mā̃ṅkpa mitšũo̱ame̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nyeteṅ mofẽmo *akpale ke̱-dše̱ egbe̱ fõṅ le̱ no̱, ni nyesāa nyenifemo̱nii le̱, ni nyekanyiea ṅyoṅmo̱i krokomei ase̱, ní nyesúmo̱ame̱, ni nyeahĩ šikpoṅ ni miṅõ-hãnye ke̱ nye-tše̱mei le̱ ne̱! ši nyehãã nyetoi aba no̱ ni nyeboomi toi. *

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Ši Ionadab, Rekab bi le̱, bii le̱ eye ame̱tše̱ kitã ní ewoame̱ le̱ no̱; ši ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ boomi toi.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Iehowa, Zebaot Nyoṅmo̱, ní dši Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Na, mike̱ efõṅ fẽ ní miwie ye̱ Iuda ke̱ Ierusalembii le̱ fẽ he le̱ aaba ame̱no̱, edšake̱ *miwie mitšõame̱, ni ame̱boo toi, ni mitšé̱ame̱ ni ame̱heree no̱. *

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Ši Rekab-bii le̱ awe le̱, Ieremia kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ní nyebo nyetše̱ Ionadab kitã le̱ toi ni nyeye ekpoi le̱ fẽ no̱ ni nyefe bo̱ni ewonye kitã le̱ pe̱pē̱pe̱

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: hewo̱ le̱, bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Nū ní aadamo̱ mihĩe ebo̱ṅ Ionadab, Rekab bi le̱, gbĩkogbĩko.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Ni Ieremia fã́ Baruk ake̱: Mi le̱ atšĩmi gbe̱, minyẽṅ Iehowa we le̱ maya;

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: nohewo̱ le̱ bo le̱ ya ni oyakane Iehowa wiemo̱i ni oṅmã ke̱-dše̱ minā owo wolokpo le̱ṅ le̱ owo maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ye̱ ṅmā̃hĩle̱ gbĩ le̱ no̱, ni asaṅ okane owo Iuda fẽ ní dše̱o̱ ame̱mãdši amli baä le̱ atoiiaṅ;

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Baruk kane Ieremia wiemo̱i ní yo̱ wolo le̱ mli le̱ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ ye̱ woloṅmãlo̱ Šafan bi Gemaria le̱ pia le̱ mli ye̱ yiteṅgbe̱ kpo le̱ no̱ ye̱ Iehowa we le̱ agbó hẽ le̱ šĩnā le̱ nā ewo maṅ mū le̱ fẽ toiiaṅ.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Ni Mikaia gbaame̱ wiemo̱i fẽ ní enu, beni Baruk kane wolo le̱ ewo maṅ le̱ toiiaṅ le̱.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Tá ši agbe̱ne̱ ní okane owo wo̱toiiaṅ! Ke̱ke̱ ni Baruk kane ewo ame̱toiiaṅ.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni ame̱nu wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ le̱, ame̱ke̱ gbeyeišemo̱ kwe̱kwē̱ ame̱hīeaṅ, ni ame̱kē̱ Baruk ake̱: Dša wo̱yagba wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ wo̱tšõ maṅtše̱ le̱!

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱sā ame̱bi Baruk ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ kē̱mo̱wo̱, té ofe tēṅ ní oṅmã wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ ke̱-dše̱ enā hũ?

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Ni Baruk kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Le̱dientše̱ eke̱ enābu tšé̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ fẽ ehãmi, ni mike̱ ble̱gi ṅmã miwo wolo le̱ mli.

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Ni lume̱i le̱ kē̱ Baruk ake̱: Ya ni oyatē ohe, bo ke̱ Ieremia fẽ, koni mokomoko akale heni nyeyo̱!

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Ni beni maṅtše̱ le̱ ešã wolokpo le̱ ke̱ *wiemoi ni Baruk ṅmã ke̱-dše̱ Ieremia nā le̱ se̱ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Ieremia ṅõ ake̱: *K.

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: Ko̱ wolokpo kroko ni oṅmã tšutšu wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ ní yo̱ kleṅkleṅ wolokpo le̱ ní Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoiakim šã le̱ mli le̱ owo mli!

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Ši kē̱mo̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoiakim le̱ hewo̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Bo le̱ ošã ne̱ke̱ wolokpo ne̱, okē̱: Mẽhewo̱ ni oṅmã owo mli ake̱: “Ba kẽ *Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ aaba ní ebafite ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱, ní ehã ene̱ †gbomei ke̱ koloi fẽ ata”? *

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoiakim le̱ hewo̱ ne̱: Enáṅ mo-ko ní atá David maṅtše̱sẽi le̱ no̱, ni aaše̱ *egbonyo le̱ afõ ní latšā atšale̱ ſane ni fẽi ayele̱ nyōṅ. *

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: Ni mawo le̱ ke̱ esešibii le̱ ke̱ etšũdši le̱ nyõmo̱ ye̱ ame̱nišaianii le̱ ahewo̱, ni ame̱ ke̱ Ierusalembii le̱ ke̱ Iudahĩĩ le̱, mike̱ efõṅ fẽ ní miwie ye̱ ame̱he ní ame̱boo toi le̱ aaba ame̱no̱.

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ieremia ko̱ wolokpo kroko, ni eke̱-hã Baruk, Neria bi le̱, ní dši woloṅmãlo̱ le̱, ni eṅmã wiemoi fẽ ni yo̱ wolo ní Iuda maṅtše̱ Iehoiakim šã ye̱ la mli le̱ṅ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ Ieremia nā ewo mli; ni aṅõ wiemo̱i babaō ní tamo̱ nomei afata he tete.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Ni Zedekia, Iosia bi le̱, baye maṅtše̱ ye̱ Konia, Iehoiakim bi le̱, nãdšiaṅ, edšake̱ Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, ewole̱ maṅtše̱ ye̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Nyeyakē̱a Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱ ní tšũnye ke̱-ba miṅõ nyebabimi nii le̱ ake̱: Na, Farao ta ní fã ke̱-ba ni ebaye ebuanye le̱, aakũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ate ame̱šikpoṅ ní dši Mizraim le̱ no̱ ekoṅ;

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: ni Kaldeabii le̱ hũ aakũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-aba ni ame̱ke̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ aabawu ekoṅ, ni ame̱aṅõle̱ ni ame̱ke̱ la aašãle̱.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeagbe Kaldeabii ní ke̱-nye wuo̱ le̱ ata le̱ fẽ ni aaſe̱ ame̱teṅ pilafoi komei ke̱ke̱ tete le̱, ame̱teṅ mofẽmo aate ši ke̱-adše̱ ebū mli, ni ame̱ke̱ la aašã ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ kẽ.

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Kaldeabii le̱ ata le̱ efã ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem he ke̱-te ye̱ Farao ta le̱ hewo̱ le̱,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: ke̱ke̱ ni Ieremia dše kpo ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem, ake̱ ēya Benyamin šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱, eyaṅõ egbe̱fãṅnõ ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ ewekumei ateṅ.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ Benyamin agbó le̱ nā le̱, bulo̱i le̱ asafoiatše̱ ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Iiria, Hanania bi Šelemia bi le̱, ye̱ dše̱i, ni ebamõ gbalo̱ Ieremia le̱, ekē̱: Kaldeabii le̱ aṅõ otšeo̱ ke̱-ya ne̱!

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Ši Ieremia kē̱: Ebe̱ mli! dšee Kaldeabii le̱ aṅõ mitšeo̱ ke̱-ya! Ši eboole̱ toi. Ni Iiria mõ Ieremia ni eke̱le̱ ba lume̱i le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Zedekia tšũ ayaṅõle̱, ke̱-ba, ni maṅtše̱ le̱ bile̱ ye̱ ewe le̱ ye̱ tēmo̱ mli ake̱: Ani wiemo̱ ní dše̱ Iehowa ṅõ le̱ eko ye̱? Ni Ieremia kē̱: Eko ye̱! ni esā ekē̱: *Aaṅõo awo Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ deṅl *

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Ni Ieremia să kē̱ maṅtše̱ Zedekia ake̱: Mẽ eša mife bo ke̱ otšũdši le̱ ke̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱, hewo̱ ni nyewomi tšũṅ ne̱?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Ni nyegbalo̱i le̱ ni gba hãnye ake̱: “Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ baṅ nye ke̱ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱!” le̱, nẽgbe̱ ame̱yo̱?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱, bo toi, minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! Hã ní mifaikpamo̱ le̱ asa ohĩe, ni okahã ake̱mi mīkũ se̱ miya Ionatan, woloṅmãlo̱ le̱, we le̱ doṅṅ, koni mikayagbo ye̱ dše̱i!

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅtše̱ Zedekia fã́, ni ake̱ *Ieremia yato bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱, ni aṅõo̱ abolo subo̱o ke̱-dše̱o̱ abološãlo̱i le̱ ablohũ le̱ṅ abahãale̱ gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ āhũ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní abolo le̱ fẽ tã ye̱ mã le̱ṅ. Bo̱ni fe ní Ieremia hĩ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱, no̱ ne̱. *

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: Minuṅtšo̱ maṅtše̱! ne̱ke̱ hĩĩ ne̱ efe efõṅ ke̱ nii fẽ ní ame̱fe gbalo̱ Ieremia ní ame̱še̱le̱ ame̱fõ bu le̱ mli le̱, ní eegbo ke̱ hõmo̱ ye̱ heni eyo̱ le̱; edšake̱ abolo ko be̱ mã le̱ṅ doṅṅ,

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Ni Ebed-Melek ṅõ hĩĩ le̱ efata ebe, ni eyiṅ ete maṅtše̱ we le̱ ye̱ tšũ ní yo̱ nitōhe le̱ šiši le̱ mli ni eyakō̱lo̱ mama-ſe̱i ke̱ nii ní esū, ni ame̱ke̱ tãṅkpēi le̱ šiu ame̱hã Ieremia ye̱ bu le̱ṅ.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Ni Ebed-Melek, Kušnyo le̱, kē̱ Ieremia ake̱: Ṅõ mamaſe̱i ke̱ nii ni esū ne̱ owo oṅãšii ye̱ tãṅkpēi le̱ ašiši! Ni Ieremia fe nakai.

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ke̱ tãṅkpēi le̱ ša Ieremia ni ame̱dšiele̱ ke̱-dše̱ bu le̱ mli; ni Ieremia babĩ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱.

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ieremia kē̱ Zedekia ake̱: Ke̱dši migbao le̱, nto gbe obagbemi? ni asaṅ ké̱ miwoö ṅā hũ, oboṅmi toi!

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ Zedekia kã Ieremia kitã ye̱ tēmo̱ mli ake̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní Iehowa, moni fe ne̱ke̱ susuma ne̱ hãwo̱ le̱, hĩe kã ne̱, migbeṅo, ni asaṅ mike̱o woṅ *hĩĩ ní taoo̱ osusuma se̱gbe̱ ne̱ adeṅ! *K

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Ieremia kē̱ Zedekia ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Zebaot Nyoṅmo̱ ní dši Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Ke̱dši oodše kpo oya Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ lume̱i le̱ aṅō̃ le̱, oyi aaná wala, ni ašãṅ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ ke̱ la, ši bo ke̱ owe le̱ fẽ yi aaná wala.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši odšee kpo oyaa Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ lume̱i le̱ aṅõ le̱, aaṅō ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ awo Kaldeabii le̱ adeṅ, ni ame̱-ke̱ la aašã, ni bo hũ odšeṅ ame̱deṅ!

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Ši maṅtše̱ Zedekia kē̱ Ieremia ake̱: Mīše Iudafoi ní etše ke̱-te Kaldeabii le̱ aṅõ le̱ agbeyei, ake̱ aleenõ ame̱aṅõmi ame̱wo nomei adeṅ, ni ame̱aye mihe fe̱o!

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Ši Ieremia kē̱: Ake̱o woṅ ame̱deṅ! Bo Iehowa gbē toi, bo̱ni miwieo̱ mitšõo̱o ne̱, ni aahĩ ahão, ni oyi aaná wala!

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Na, yei fẽ ní eſe̱ ye̱ Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱ we le̱, aaṅõame̱ ke̱-adše kpo ke̱-ate Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ lume̱i le̱ aṅõ, ni ame̱-akē̱ ake̱: *“Onanemei le̱ ešišiu bo, ni ame̱ye ono̱! ni agbe̱ne̱ ní onãdši efũ ṅmo̱to̱ mli ne̱, ame̱tšṍmo̱ ame̱he ame̱te!” *

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Ni oṅãmei ke̱ obii fẽ hũ, aakplaame̱ ayahã Kaldeabii le̱, ni *bodientše̱ hũ odšeṅ ame̱deṅ, ši moṅ Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ enine aamõo, ni ake̱ la aašä ne̱-ke̱ maṅ ne̱. *

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Zedekia kē̱ Ieremia ake̱: Kāhã mokomoko mile ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱, ši ogboṅ!

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Ni ke̱dši lume̱i le̱ nu ake̱ mike̱o ewie, ni ame̱ba oṅõ ni ame̱bakē̱o ake̱: “Agbe̱ne̱ dšadsemo̱ wiemo̱ ni oke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ wie le̱ otšõwo̱, kāšíuwo̱ sane ko no̱, ši wo̱gbeṅo! ni té maṅtše̱ le̱ hũ ke̱o wie tēṅ?” le̱:

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: no le̱ kē̱mo̱ame̱ ake̱: Mike̱ mifaikpamo̱ ſie maṅtše̱ le̱ hĩe, koni ekahã ake̱mi miya Ionatan we le̱ doṅṅ, ni miyagbo ye̱ dše̱i!

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni lume̱i le̱ fẽ ba Ieremia ṅõ ame̱babile̱, ni edšadše wiemo̱i le̱ fẽ etsõ-ame̱ bo̱ni maṅtše̱ le̱ ewole̱ kitã le̱; ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱fõ enā gbamo̱, edšake̱ sane le̱ edšee kpo.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Ni Ieremia hĩ ši ye̱ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱ ke̱-yaši gbĩ ní aṅõ Ierusalem.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Zedekia, Iuda maṅtše̱ le̱, ke̱ tabiloi le̱ fẽ naame̱ le̱, ame̱dšo foi ni ame̱dše kpo ke̱-dše̱ mã le̱ṅ nyōṅ ke̱-tšṍ maṅtše̱ trom le̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ye̱ agbó ni yo̱ gbogboi enyo̱ le̱ teṅ le̱ mli. Ni edše kpo ke̱-tšṍ ṅã kplanā le̱ no̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: Ya ni oyakē̱ *Ebed-Melek, Kušnyo le̱, ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Na, mahã miwiemo̱i le̱ aba maṅ ne̱ no̱ ye̱ efõṅ gbe̱ ni dšee ekpakpa gbe̱, ni ame̱aba mli ye̱ ohĩe ye̱ no gbĩ le̱ no̱. *

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: Ṅõle̱ ni okwe̱le̱ dšogbāṅ, ni oka-fele̱ efõṅ, ši moṅ bo̱ni eekē̱o le̱, femo̱ nakai ohãle̱.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Ni maṅtše̱ we le̱ ke̱ maṅbii le̱ awei le̱ Kaldeabii le̱ ke̱ la šã, ni ame̱kũmo̱ Ierusalem gbogboi le̱.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Ni maṅbii le̱ ateṅ mei ní ašĩ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ le̱, ke̱ tšelo̱i ní tše ke̱-ba eṅõ ke̱ maṅbii le̱ ateṅ mei ní ſe̱ le̱, Nebuzaradan, oblafoi atše̱ le̱, ṅõame̱ nom ke̱-te Babel.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Ši Nebuzaradan, oblafoi atše̱ le̱, šĩ maṅ le̱ mli ohĩafoi ní be̱ nokonoko le̱ ateṅ meikomei ye̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni ehãame̱ weintromi ke̱ abō̱i nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Ni Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, wo Nebuzaradan, oblafoi atše̱ le̱, kitã ye̱ Ieremia hewo̱, ake̱:

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: ni ayaṅõ Ieremia ke̱-dše̱ *bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ baha †Gedalia, Šafan bi Ahikam bi le̱, koni eke̱le̱ aya ewe le̱; ni ehĩ maṅbii le̱ ateṅ. *

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Ši beni aṅã́ Ieremia yi ye̱ bulo̱i le̱ akpo le̱ no̱ le̱, Iehowa wiemo̱ ba eṅõ ake̱:

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: ši mahã odše mli kẽ, ni *onyõṅ ye̱ klante nā; ši osusuma aatšṍ hānõ ahão, edšake ohĩe kã mino̱, Iehowa kē̱. *Hiob

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: ni Iehowa ehã eba mli, ni efe bo̱ni ewie le̱; edšake̱ nyefe eša nyeši Iehowa, ni nyeboo egbē toi; nohewo ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ ba nyeno̱ ne̱.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Nohewo le̱ agbene, na, mifẽne onidši kõsõṅkõsõi le̱ ṅme̱ne̱: ke̱dši esa ohĩe ake̱ oke̱mi aate Babel le̱, ba, ni makwe̱o dšogbāṅ; ši ke̱dši esaa ohĩe ake̱ oke̱mi aate Babel le̱, no le̱ ahĩ ši; kwe̱, šikpoṅ mū le̱ fẽ kã ohĩe ne̱: heni ehĩ ke̱ heni sa ohĩe ake̱ oote le̱, ya dše̱i!

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Ši beni enáko ehã hetō le̱, ekē̱: Bĕlé̱ kũ ose̱ oya *Gedalia, Šafan bi Ahikam bi le̱, ni Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ ewole̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ ano̱ lumo̱ le̱, ṅõ, ni oke̱le̱ ayahĩ ši ye̱ maṅbii le̱ ateṅ, lo hefẽhe ní sa ohĩe ake̱ oote le̱, ya! Ni oblafoi atše̱ le̱ hãle̱ gbe̱ no̱ niyenii ke̱ nikēnii, ni ewole̱ gbe̱. *

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Ni Ieremia ba Gedalia, Ahikam bi le̱, ṅõ ye̱ Mizpa, ni eke̱le̱ hĩ ši ye̱ maṅ-bii ní eſe̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Ni Gedalia, Šafan bi Ahikam bi le̱, kãame̱ ke̱ ame̱webii le̱ akitã ake̱: Nyekašea Kaldeabii le̱ asúomo̱ gbeyei; nyehĩa šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni nyesúmo̱a Babel maṅtše̱ le̱, ni aahĩ ahãnye!

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Ni mi le̱, na, mibahĩ Mizpa, koni madamo Kaldeabii ní aaba wo̱ṅõ le̱ ahĩe; nohewo̱ le̱ nye le̱ nyeyabuaä wein ke̱ tšeiayibii ke̱ mũ nā nyewoa nyenii amli, ni nyehĩa nyemãdsi ní nyeṅõṅõi le̱ amli!

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Ši Iohanan, Karea bi le̱, ke̱ tai le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ fẽ ní yo̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱ ba Gedalia ṅõ ye̱ Mizpa,

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: ni ame̱bakē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani ole ake̱ Baalis, Amonbii le̱ amaṅtše̱ le̱, etšũ Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ní ebagbeo lo? Ši Gedalia, Ahikam bi le̱, heeame̱ eyee.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iohanan, Karea bi le̱, kē̱ Gedalia ye̱ Mizpa ye̱ tēmo̱ mli ake̱: Hã maya ni mayagbe Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ni mokomoko leṅ! Mẽhewo̱ ni eebagbeo, ni Iudafoi fẽ ní ebabua ame̱he nā ye̱ oṅõ ne̱ agbe̱ aſã, ni Iuda mei ni eſe̱ le̱ hĩe akpãtā?

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Ši Gedalia, Ahikam bi le̱, kē̱ Iohanan, Karea bi le̱, ake̱: Kāfe nakai; edšake̱ apasa wiemo̱ owieo̱ ye̱ Išmael he ne̱!

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni agbe Gedalia le̱ se̱ gbĩĩ enyo̱, ní mokomoko leko le̱,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Ni Išmael, Netania bi le̱, dše̱ Mizpa teame̱ kpēmo̱, eyaä fẽ le̱ ehĩe yāfó; ni eba mli ake̱, beni eke̱ame̱ kpe le̱, ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyebaä Gedalia, Ahikam bi le̱, ṅõ!

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Ši nubu le̱ ni Išmael še̱re̱ hĩĩ ní egbe ke̱-fata Gedalia he le̱ agbobĩĩ le̱ fẽ eſie mli le̱ dši noni *maṅtše̱ Asa dše ye̱ Baeša, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱, hewo̱ le̱: no mli Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ṅõ mei ní enyõnyõi le̱ ewo obõ. *

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Išmael ṅõ maṅbii ní eſe̱ ye̱ Mizpa le̱ fẽ, maṅtše̱ le̱ biyei le̱ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ní eſe̱ ye̱ Mizpa le̱, mei ní Nebuzaradan, oblafoi atše̱ le̱, eṅõ-to Gedalia, Ahikam bi le̱, šiši le̱ ſẽ, ni Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ṅõame̱ nom, ni eyiṅ ní efo mli ke̱-ya Amonbii le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: ame̱ṅõ hĩĩ le̱ fẽ ni ame̱yiṅ ke̱-te ni ame̱ke̱ Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ayawu; ni ame̱yaninale̱ ye̱ *nui babaō ní yo̱ Gibeon le̱ he. *

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Ši Išmael, Netania bi le̱, ke̱ hĩĩ kpānyo̱ dše Iohanan deṅ, ni eyiṅ ete Amonbii le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: ní ame̱bakē̱ gbalo̱ Ieremia ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ hã wo̱faikpamo̱ asa ohĩe, ni *okpa Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, fai ohãwo̱ ke̱ mei ní eſe̱ ne̱ fẽ , *

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: koni Iehowa, o-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, atšõwo̱ gbe̱ ní wo̱nyie no̱, ke̱ noni wo̱fe.

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni gbalo̱ Ieremia le̱ kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Minu; na, mibakpa Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, fai tamo̱ bo̱ni nyekē̱ le̱, ni aaba mli ake̱, wiemo̱-fẽ-wiemo̱ ní Iehowa ke̱-ahãnye hetō le̱, magbanye, mišiuṅnye sane ko no̱.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Ekpakpa ni dšio, efõṅ ni dšio, Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mo ṅõ ní wo̱tšũo̱o ne̱ gbē toi wo̱o̱bo, beni afe ní ahĩ ahãwo̱, ké̱ wo̱bo Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbē toi le̱.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ gbĩĩ nyoṅma se̱ le̱ Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Ieremia ṅõ;

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, mo ṅõ ní nyetšũmi, koni mike̱ nyefaikpamo̱ ayaṅmẽ ehĩe le̱, kē̱ ne̱:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Ké̱ nyeahĩ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ le̱, no le̱ mamãmo̱nye ši, ni mikũmo̱ṅnye, ni mate̱onye, ni mifãmo̱ṅnye; edšake̱ miſa mihe ye̱ efõṅ ní mifenye le̱ he.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ ní nyešeo̱le̱ gbeyei le̱, nyekašeale̱; nyekašeale̱ gbeyei, Iehowa kē̱; edšake̱ mike̱nye ye̱, koni mahere nyeyiwala, ni madšienye ke̱-dse̱ edeṅ!

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Ši mahã nyena mũsũṅtšõle̱ ni emũsũṅ atšõle̱ ye̱ nyehewo̱, ní ehã nyekũ nyese̱ ke̱-ba nyešikpoṅ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši nyeke̱ ake̱: Wo̱hĩĩ ši ye̱ ne̱ke̱ šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱! ni nyeboo Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbē toi,

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: ni nyekē̱ ake̱: Dabi! ši wo̱e̱te Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, heni wonaṅ ta ye̱, ni wo̱nuṅ te̱tre̱mantre̱ gbē̱mo̱, ni asaṅ abolo hõmo̱ yeṅwo̱, ní wo̱yahĩ ši ye̱ dše̱i le̱!

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: no le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeboa Iehowa wiemo̱ le̱ toi, nye Iuda mei ni eſe̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Ké̱ nyedšie nyehĩe nyeka Mizraim ake̱ nyemīya dše̱i ní nyeyato gbo̱ ye̱ dše̱i le̱:

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Edšake̱ bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Take̱ bo̱ni afo̱se mi-mlifũ ke̱ mimlila le̱ aſie Ierusalembii le̱ ano̱ le̱, nakai noṅṅ ké̱ nyete Mizraim ni aafo̱se mimlila le̱ aſie nyeno̱, ni nyeatšṍ kitãkãmo̱nõ ke̱ nākpenõ ke̱ lōmo̱ ke̱ ahorabō̱, ni nyenaṅ bie̱ ne̱ doṅṅ!

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Nye Iuda mei ní eſe̱, Iehowa ewie ye̱ nyehe ake̱: Nyekayaä Mizraim! Nyenáa nyelea kre̱dē̱ ake̱ miye odase mitšõnye ṅme̱ne̱!

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Ši nyeye nyedientše̱ nyesusumai le̱ akũtũmpo̱o; edšake̱ nye noṅṅ nyetšũmi Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, ṅõ nyekē̱: Kpa Iehowa, w̌o̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, fai ohãwo̱, ni *bo̱fẽbo̱ ní Iehowa, wo̱-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, aakē̱-wo̱ le̱, nakai ogbawo̱, ni wo̱o̱fe! *K.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Ni migbanye ṅme̱ne̱, ši nyeboo Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, gbē toi ye̱ nii fẽ ní eke̱-tšũmi nyeṅõ le̱ eko eko gbe̱fãṅ.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Ši moṅ Baruk, Neria bi le̱, tšire̱ oyise̱ wowo̱ ne̱, beni afe ní eṅõwo̱ ewo Kaldeabii le̱ adeṅ, ní ame̱gbewo̱ ni ame̱ṅõwo̱ nom ke̱-ya Babel!

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Ni Iohanan, Karea bi le̱, ke̱ tai le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ maṅ mū le̱ fẽ boo Iehowa gbē toi ní ame̱hī Iuda šikpon le̱ no̱;

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: ši Iohanan, Karea bi le̱, ke̱ tai le̱ ano̱ asafoiatše̱mei le̱ fẽ ṅõ Iuda mei ní eſe̱ le̱ fẽ ni kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ dšeṅmãdši fẽ ní agbe̱ame̱ aſã no̱ le̱ mli ke̱-ba ní ame̱bato gbo̱ ye̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱,

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: hĩĩ ke̱ yei ke̱ gbekẽbii ke̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ biyei le̱ ke̱ susumai fẽ ní Nebuzaradan, oblafoi atše̱ le̱, šĩ hã Gedalia, Šafan bi Ahikam bi le̱, ke̱ gbalo̱ Ieremia ke̱ Baruk, Neria bi le̱, fẽ,

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: ni *ame̱te Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱; edšake̱ ame̱boo Iehowa gbē toi; ni ame̱še̱ Takpanes. *

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba Ieremia ṅõ ye̱ Takpanes ake̱:

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa Zebaot, Israel Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, kē̱ ne̱: Na, mibatšũ ní ayaṅõ Nebukadnezar, Babel maṅtše̱ ní dši *mitšũlo̱ le̱, ke̱-ba, ni maṅõ esẽi le̱ mamã ne̱ke̱ te̱i ní miṅõ-ho̱lo̱ mli ne̱ ano̱, ni eeši ekatamanso le̱ ye̱ no̱; *

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: ni eeba ebatſia Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ nii: moni sa gbĕle le̱, eegbele̱, ni moni sa nomṅō̃ le̱, eeṅõle̱ nom, ni *moni sa klante le̱, eebãmo̱le̱ klante! *

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Wiemo̱ ní ba Ieremia ṅõ ye̱ Iudafoi fẽ ní yo̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, mei ni yo̱ Migdol ke̱ *Takpanes ke̱ Nof ke̱ Patros šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱ ahewo̱ no̱: *

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: ye̱ ame̱nifõdšianii ní amefe ame̱ke̱-wo mimli la le̱ ahewo̱, ake̱-ni ame̱te ame̱yašā tšofã-ke̱-ṅma, ni ame̱ke̱-súmo̱ nyoṅmo̱i krokomei ní ame̱ ke̱ nye ke̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ lee le̱.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Ni mitšũo̱ mitšũdši fẽ ní dši gbalo̱i le̱ ke̱-baã nyeṅõ, miteo̱ ši lebi mā̃ṅ-kpa mitšũo̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyekafea nihĩnii ní minye̱o̱ ne̱!

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱boo toi, ni asaṅ ame̱hãã ame̱-toi aba no̱ ní ame̱kpale ke̱-dše̱ amenifõdšianii le̱ ahe, ni ame̱kašã tšofã-ke̱-ṅma ame̱mīhã nyoṅmo̱i krokomei doṅṅ.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ afo̱se mimlila ke̱ mimlifũ le̱ aſie ši ni eyatšo ye̱ Iuda mãdši le̱ amli ke̱ Ierusalem blohũi le̱aṅ, ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ ole̱ṅle̱ ke̱ amaṅfõ, take̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱.

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: ake̱-ní nyeke̱ nyeninenā nitsumo̱i le̱ woo̱ mimli la, ni nyešãa tšofã-ke̱-ṅma nyehãa nyoṅme̱i krokomei ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ ne̱ heni nyete nyeyato gbo̱ ye̱ le̱, beni afe ní nyeplenē, ni nyetšṍ lōmo̱ ke̱ ahorabō̱ ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ mãdšimãdši fẽ ateṅ?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ani nyehĩe kpa nyetše̱mei le̱ ani-fõdši ke̱ Iuda maṅtše̱mei le̱ anifõdši ke̱ ame̱ṅãmei le̱ anifõdši ke̱ nyedientše̱ nyenifõdši ke̱ nyeṅãmei le̱ anifõdši ní amefe ye̱ Iuda šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Ierusalem blohũi le̱ amli le̱ ano̱?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ame̱bako ame̱he ši ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ni asaṅ ame̱šeko gbeyei, ni ame̱nyieko mimla ke̱ mikpoi le̱ ni miṅõ-māmo̱ nye ke̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ ahĩe le̱ amli.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ni maṅõ Iuda mei ní eſe̱, ní dšie ame̱hĩe ame̱ka Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ ní ame̱-yato gbo̱ ye̱ dše̱i le̱, ni ame̱fe ame̱atã; ame̱anyõnyõi ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱: ame̱atã ye̱ *klante ke̱ hõmo̱ nā, ame̱ agboi ye̱ klante ke̱ hõmo̱ nā ke̱-adše̱ mo bibiō no̱ ke̱-yaši mo wulu no̱, ni ame̱-atšṍ kitãkãmo̱nõ ke̱ nākpe̱nõ ke̱ lōmo̱ ke̱ ahorabō̱. *

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
