translation_verse: Nye *kue̱ṅwalo̱i ke̱ †tšuiiaṅ ke̱ toiiaṅ fōlo̱i! nye le̱, dāne̱ nyekũo̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ nā; bo̱ni nyetše̱mei le̱ fe le̱, nakai nye hũ nyefeo̱. *

english_verse: Is there one prophet that your ancestors didn't mistreat? They killed the prophets who told about the coming of the One Who Obeys God. And now you have turned against him and killed him.
translation_verse: Gbaloi le̱ ateṅ namo ni nyetše̱mei le̱ wakole̱ yi dã? ni ame̱gbe mei ni gba sá ye̱ dšalo̱ le̱ bā le̱ hewo̱ le̱, mo hũ ní agbe̱ne̱ nye nyetšṍmo̱ ese̱gbe̱tšõlo̱i ke̱ awuyelo̱i le̱,

english_verse: Angels gave you God's Law, but you still don't obey it. Stephen Is Stoned to Death
translation_verse: nye ní nyená mla le̱ ye̱ bo̱foi anitšumo̱ nā ní nyeyee no̱ le̱.

english_verse: When the council members heard Stephen's speech, they were angry and furious.
translation_verse: Ši beni amenu ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ le̱, etšuro̱ ame̱tšuiiaṅ, ni ame̱kpe ame̱nyā-nyōdsi ašiši ame̱ſie eno̱.

english_verse: But Stephen was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked toward heaven, where he saw our glorious God and Jesus standing at his right side.
translation_verse: Ši le̱ le̱, noni Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ eyile̱ obõ le̱, ekwe̱ ṅwei gā̃, ni ena Nyoṅmo̱ anumnyam le̱ ke̱ Iesu ní edamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ninedšŭrõ no̱,

english_verse: Then Stephen said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right side of God!”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: Na, mina ṅwei nā ní égble, ke̱ *gbomobi le̱ ní edamo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ninedšŭrõ no̱. *Luk.

english_verse: The council members shouted and covered their ears. At once they all attacked Stephen
translation_verse: Ši ame̱blo̱ ke̱ gbē wale̱, ni ame̱tšĩmo̱ ame̱toii, ni ame̱ke̱ dſẽṅmo̱ kome tšẽ foi ke̱-ba eno̱,

english_verse: and dragged him out of the city. Then they started throwing stones at him. The men who had brought charges against him put their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
translation_verse: ni ame̱tšire̱ eyi se̱ ke̱-dše mã le̱ṅ, ni ame̱yatſiale̱ te̱i. Ni odasefoi le̱ ṅõ ame̱mamai le̱ ame̱ſie oblanyo ko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Saulo le̱ nãdši anā,

english_verse: As Stephen was being stoned to death, he called out, “Lord Jesus, please welcome me!”
translation_verse: ni beni ame̱tſía Stefano te̱i le̱, efã́ Iesu ni ekē̱: *Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu, heremo̱ mimumo̱ le̱! *Lal.

english_verse: He knelt down and shouted, “Lord, don't blame them for what they have done.” Then he died.
translation_verse: Ni ekũla ši, ni ebo ke̱ gbē wale̱ ake̱: *Nuṅtšo̱, kāṅõ ne̱ke̱ eša ne̱ oṅmẽ ame̱no̱! Ni beni ekē̱ ne̱ke̱ le̱, etšṍ mli ewo̱. *Luk.

english_verse: Saul started making a lot of trouble for the church. He went from house to house, arresting men and women and putting them in jail. The Good News Is Preached in Samaria
translation_verse: Ši Saulo le̱, ekpãtã asafo le̱ hĩe butū, eboteo̱ šĩai ni eyagblaä hĩĩ ke̱ yei ni eyawoo̱ame̱ tšũṅ.

english_verse: They crowded around Philip because they were eager to hear what he was saying and to see him work miracles.
translation_verse: Ni mei babaō ke̱ dſẽṅmo̱ kome bo wiemo̱i ní Filipo wieo̱ le̱ toi, beni ame̱nu ni ame̱na okadii ní efe le̱.

english_verse: Everyone, rich and poor, crowded around him. They said, “This man is the power of God called ‘The Great Power.’ ”
translation_verse: ni mei bibii ke̱ mei wudši fẽ boo̱le̱ toi ame̱kē̱o̱ ake̱: Mone̱ dši Nyoṅmo̱ hewale̱ ní atšé̱o̱le̱ kpeteṅkple le̱.

english_verse: For a long time, Simon had used witchcraft to amaze the people, and they kept crowding around him.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱-ní edše̱ dšeeṅmõ bēbe eke̱ ekũnyāyeli le̱ ehã ame̱nā ekpe̱ ame̱he hewo̱ le̱, ame̱boo̱le̱ toi.

english_verse: Even Simon believed and was baptized. He stayed close to Philip, because he marveled at all the miracles and wonders.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Simon dientše̱ hũ hé ye, ni abaptisile̱, ni eke̱ ehe kpe̱te̱ Filipo, ni beni ena okadii ke̱ hewale̱nitšumo̱i wudši ní afe le̱, enā kpe̱ ehe.

english_verse: The apostles in Jerusalem heard that some people in Samaria had accepted God's message, and they sent Peter and John.
translation_verse: Ši beni bo̱foi le̱ ní yo̱ Ierusalem le̱ nu ake̱ Samariabii emo Nyoṅmo̱ wĩemo̱ le̱ mli le̱, ame̱tšũ Petro ke̱ Iohane ke̱-te ame̱ṅõ.

english_verse: When the two apostles arrived, they prayed that these people would be given the Holy Spirit.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ le̱, ameba dše̱i ame̱baso̱le ame̱hãame̱, beni afe ní ame̱na Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱.

english_verse: Peter and John then placed their hands on everyone who had faith in the Lord, and they were given the Holy Spirit.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱nidši ṅmĕlĕ ame̱no̱, ni ame̱ná Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱.

english_verse: and said to Peter and John, “Let me have this power too! Then anyone I place my hands on will also be given the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: ekē̱: Nyehãami hũ ne̱ke̱ hewale̱ ne̱, koni mofẽmo ní mĩke̱ minidšĩ aaṅmĕlẽ eno̱ le̱ aná Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱.

english_verse: Peter said to him, “You and your money will both end up in hell if you think you can buy God's gift!
translation_verse: Ši Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Oke̱ ošika le̱ fẽ hĩe ákpãtã, edšake̱ osusuo̱ ake̱, Nyoṅmo̱ nõkēnõ le̱, šika ake̱-heo̱!

english_verse: Get rid of these evil thoughts and ask God to forgive you.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ſa ohe ye̱ onõša ne̱ hewo̱, ni okpa Nyoṅmo̱ fai, ake̱ aleenō aaṅõ otšuiṅ dſẽṅmo̱ le̱ afao lo.

english_verse: I can see that you are jealous and bound by your evil ways.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mina ake̱ ko̱liko̱ dšōmo̱ le̱ ke̱ nõša kpã le̱ mli okã ne̱.

english_verse: Simon said, “Please pray to the Lord, so that what you said won't happen to me.”
translation_verse: Ni Simon here no̱ ekē̱: Nyedientše̱ nyekpaä Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ fai nyehãami, koni nibii ní nyewie ne̱ eko akaba mino̱.

english_verse: After Peter and John had preached about the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem. On their way they told the good news in many villages of Samaria. Philip and an Ethiopian Official
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱, beni ame̱ye odase ní ame̱wie Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ lo̱ ame̱tšõame̱ ni ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ame̱baä Ierusalem le̱, ame̱dšadše sanekpakpa le̱ ame̱tšõ ye̱ Samariabii akrowai pī amli.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said to Philip, “Go south along the desert road that leads from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
translation_verse: Ši Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ bo̱fo ko ke̱ Filipo bawie ake̱: Te ši ní oya wuoyigbe̱ ye̱ tempōṅ ní dše̱ Ierusalem ke̱-yaä Gaza ní efe amaṅfõ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: So Philip left. An important Ethiopian official happened to be going along that road in his chariot. He was the chief treasurer for Candace, the Queen of Ethiopia. The official had gone to Jerusalem to worship
translation_verse: Ni ete ši ni eyiṅ ete. Ni na, nū Etiopianyo ko ní dši Etiopiabii amaṅnye Kandake le̱ piafonyo ní abuo̱ ní kwe̱o̱ edſetri fẽ no̱ le̱ ne̱, ebaho Ierusalem eyadšá Nyoṅmo̱,

english_verse: and was now on his way home. He was sitting in his chariot, reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.
translation_verse: ni agbe̱ne̱ ekũ ese̱ etá eſīli mli ke̱-mīya, ni ēkane gbalo̱ Iesaia wolo le̱.

english_verse: The Spirit told Philip to catch up with the chariot.
translation_verse: Ni Mumo̱ le̱ kē̱ Filipo ake̱: Ya ní oyakpe̱te̱ ſīli ne̱ se̱.

english_verse: Philip ran up close and heard the man reading aloud from the book of Isaiah. Philip asked him, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
translation_verse: Ši beni Filipo hĩe foi ke̱-te le̱, enu ake̱ ekane gbalo̱ Iesaia wolo le̱, ni ebile̱ ake̱: Ani ōnu noni okaneo̱ le̱ šiši lo?

english_verse: The official answered, “How can I understand unless someone helps me?” He then invited Philip to come up and sit beside him.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Té mafe tẽṅ ní manyẽṅ, ake̱ dša moko tšõmi? Ke̱ke̱ ni ekpa Filipo fai ake̱ eba ni eke̱le̱ abatá ši.

english_verse: The man was reading the passage that said, “He was led like a sheep on its way to be killed. He was silent as a lamb whose wool is being cut off, and he did not say a word.
translation_verse: Ši ṅmãle̱ le̱ heni ekaneo̱ le̱ ne̱: *“Akplale̱ ke̱-te take̱ tōgwanteṅ ni ayagbele̱, ni bo̱ni tōgwanteṅbi feo̱ diō ye̱ ehetšo̱ikulo̱ hĩe le̱, nakai noṅṅ etſaa esẽṅ *Ies.

english_verse: He was treated like a nobody and did not receive a fair trial. How can he have children, if his life is snatched away?”
translation_verse: Ehešibā le̱ mli le̱ adšie ekodšomo̱ le̱ ke̱-te; ši eyino̱ le̱, namo aagba he sane? edšake̱ aṅõ ewala le̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱.”

english_verse: The official said to Philip, “Tell me, was the prophet talking about himself or about someone else?”
translation_verse: Ni piafonyo le̱ here Filipo no̱ ni ekē̱: Mikpao fai, namo he gbalo̱ le̱ wieo̱ ne̱? le̱dientše̱ ehe alo mokrokoṅ?

english_verse: So Philip began at this place in the Scriptures and explained the good news about Jesus.
translation_verse: Ni Filipo gble enā ni ebõi ke̱-dše̱ ne̱ke̱ ṅmãle̱ ne̱ no̱, ni edšadše Iesu he sanekpakpa le̱ etšõle̱.

english_verse: He ordered the chariot to stop. Then they both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
translation_verse: Ni efá ake̱ ſīli le̱ áwa, ni Filipo ke̱ piafonyo le̱ fẽ yimo̱ ši ke̱-te nu le̱ mli, ni ebaptisile̱.

english_verse: After they had come out of the water, the Lord's Spirit took Philip away. The official never saw him again, but he was very happy as he went on his way.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱dše nu le̱ mli le̱, Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ *Mumo̱ le̱ ša Filipo ke̱-te; ni piafonyo le̱ enaale̱ doṅṅ, ši eyi gbe̱ ke̱ nyã́mo̱. *

english_verse: Philip later appeared in Azotus. He went from town to town, all the way to Caesarea, telling people about Jesus.
translation_verse: Ši Filipo le̱, anale̱ ye̱ Azoto; ni beni efoo̱ mli le̱, edšadše sanekpakpa le̱ etšõ ye̱ mãdši le̱ fẽ mli ke̱-yaši ebaše̱ *Kaisarea. *

english_verse: Saul preached with such power that he completely confused the Jewish people in Damascus, as he tried to show them that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ši Saulo le̱, ená hewale̱ babaō, ni ehā Iudafoi ní yo̱ Damasko le̱ anā tã, edšake̱ etšõame̱ faṅṅ ake̱ mone̱ dši Kristo le̱.

english_verse: I will show him how much he must suffer for worshiping in my name.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mibatšõle̱ amanehũlũi abo̱ ní ebana ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ ahewo̱. K.

english_verse: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the followers. But they were all afraid of him, because they did not believe he was a true follower.
translation_verse: Ni beni Saulo ba Ierusalem le̱, eka kaselo̱i le̱ ahe kpe̱te̱mo̱; ši ame̱fẽ ame̱mīšele̱ gbeyei, ame̱hee ame̱yee ake̱ kaselo̱ dšile̱. Gal.

english_verse: and he has seen a vision. He saw a man named Ananias coming to him and putting his hands on him, so he could see again.”
translation_verse: ni ena ye̱ ninā mli ake̱ nū ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Anania le̱ mība eṅõ, ni eke enine mīṅmẽ eno̱, beni afe ni ena nii ekoṅ.

english_verse: When Saul had almost reached Damascus, a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
translation_verse: Ši beni enyie gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ni eyabe̱ṅke̱ Damasko le̱, trukā le̱ la kpe̱ ke̱-dše̱ ṅwei ke̱-babo̱lele̱,

english_verse: He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying, “Saul! Saul! Why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: ni efle̱o egbe ši, ni enu gbē ko mīkē̱le̱ ake̱: Saul, Saul, mẽba owaämi yi?

english_verse: The men with Saul stood there speechless. They had heard the voice, but they had not seen anyone.
translation_verse: Ši hĩĩ ní ke̱le̱ nyie le̱ eto̱ mũ ke̱-damo̱ ši, ame̱mīnu gbē le̱ moṅ, ši ame̱naa mokomoko.

english_verse: and for three days he was blind and did not eat or drink.
translation_verse: Ni enaa nii, ni asaṅ eyee nii ni enuu noko hũ gbĩĩ etẽ so̱ṅṅ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Ananias, “Go! I have chosen him to tell foreigners, kings, and the people of Israel about me.
translation_verse: Ši Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ya, edšake̱ mone̱ dši mideṅdade ní ahala ahãmi, koni ehĩe migbe̱i le̱ ke-ya *dšeṅmădši ke̱ †maṅtše̱mei ke̱ Israelbii le̱ hũ ahĩe, *Rom.

english_verse: Later some of them made plans to kill Saul,
translation_verse: Ši gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ se̱ le̱, Iudafoi le̱ te eyi no̱ apam ake̱ ame̱agbele̱.

english_verse: but he found out about it. He learned that they were guarding the gates of the city day and night in order to kill him.
translation_verse: Ni Saulo banu ame̱kpãṅmo̱ le̱ he. Ši ame̱sā ame̱buo̱ maṅ agboi le̱ anã dā ſane ke̱ nyōṅ, beni afe ni ame̱gbele̱.

english_verse: Then Barnabas helped him by taking him to the apostles. He explained how Saul had seen the Lord and how the Lord had spoken to him. Barnabas also said when Saul was in Damascus, he had spoken bravely in the name of Jesus.
translation_verse: Ši Barnaba ṅõle̱ ke̱-te bo̱foi le̱ aṅõ, ni eyagbaame̱ bo̱ni ena Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ni eke̱le̱ wie, ke̱ bo̱ni efe ekã ye̱ Iesu gbei le̱ amli ye̱ Damasko. K.

english_verse: Saul moved about freely with the followers in Jerusalem and told everyone about the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ame̱ yaä baä ye̱ Ierusalem, ni efe ekã ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu gbe̱i le̱ amli.

english_verse: He was always arguing with the Jews who spoke Greek, and so they tried to kill him.
translation_verse: Ni eke̱ Helenibii le̱ wie ni eke̱ame̱ tā nā; ši ame̱ le̱ ame̱taole̱ ame̱gbe.

english_verse: But the followers found out about this and took Saul to Caesarea. From there they sent him to the city of Tarsus.
translation_verse: Ši beni nyemimei le̱ nu he le̱, ame̱yawale̱ Kaisarea, ni ame̱hã *ete Tarso. *

english_verse: The church in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria now had a time of peace and kept on worshiping the Lord. The church became stronger, as the Holy Spirit encouraged it and helped it grow. Peter Heals Aeneas
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ le̱ asafo le̱ ná hedšo̱le̱ ye̱ Iudea ke̱ Galilea ke̱ Samaria ſẽ, ni enane mõ ši, ni enyieo̱ ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbeyeišemo̱ mli, ni eke̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ mīše̱dšemo̱ le̱ ſereo̱.

english_verse: There he met a man named Aeneas, who for eight years had been sick in bed and could not move.
translation_verse: Ni ebana nū ko ye̱ dše̱i ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Ainea ní ekã esā ne̱ ēye kū̃mo̱-hela afii kpānyo̱ so̱ṅṅ.

english_verse: Peter said to Aeneas, “Jesus Christ has healed you! Get up and make up your bed.” At once he stood up.
translation_verse: Ni Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ainea, Iesu Kristo mītšáo; te ši ni bodientše̱ oṅmẽ osa le̱! Ni amrõ le̱ ete ši.

english_verse: Many people in the towns of Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas and became followers of the Lord. Peter Brings Dorcas Back to Life
translation_verse: Ni mei fẽ ní yo̱ Lida ke̱ Šaron le̱ nale̱, ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ ame̱he ke̱-ba Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. Her Greek name was Dorcas, which means “deer.” She was always doing good things for people and had given much to the poor.
translation_verse: Ši yō kaselo̱ ko ye̱ Iopa ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Tabita, ešiši dši Dorka ; le̱ le̱ eyi obõ ke̱ nĩtšumo̱i kpakpai ke̱ edšudši ní efeo.

english_verse: But she got sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, nakai gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ ehe baye ni egbo. Ni ame̱dšu ehe, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ yaṅmẽ ṅweitšũ ko mli.

english_verse: Joppa wasn't far from Lydda, and the followers heard that Peter was there. They sent two men to say to him, “Please come with us as quickly as you can!”
translation_verse: Ši ake̱ noni Lida ke̱ Iopa dšeke̱e̱ ni kaselo̱i le̱ enu ake̱ Petro ye̱ dše̱i hewo̱ le̱, ame̱tšũ hĩī enyo̱ ke̱-te eṅõ ame̱yakpale̱ fai ake̱ ekaṅõ-šašao ši, ši eba ame̱ṅõ oyá.

english_verse: At once, Peter went with them. The men took Peter upstairs into the room. Many widows were there crying. They showed him the coats and clothes that Dorcas had made while she was still alive.
translation_verse: Ni Petro te ši ni eke̱ame̱ te. Ni beni eše̱ dše̱i le̱, ame̱ke̱le̱ te ṅweitšũ le̱ṅ, ni yei okũlafoi le̱ fẽ badamo̱damo̱ emase̱i ame̱mīfófói, ni ame̱ke̱ flakai ke̱ atadei ní Dorka fe, beni eke̱ame̱ yo̱ lolo le̱, mītšõle̱.

english_verse: After Peter had sent everyone out of the room, he knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body of Dorcas and said, “Tabitha, get up!” The woman opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
translation_verse: Ni Petro ſie ame̱fẽ ke̱-dše kpo, ni ekũla ši eso̱le, ni etšṍ ebe ke̱-te gbonyo le̱ ṅõ ekē̱: Tabita, *te ši! Ni egble ehĩṅme̱ii, ni beni ena Petro le̱, eho etá ši. *Mar.

english_verse: He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Peter called in the widows and the other followers and showed them that Dorcas had been raised from death.
translation_verse: Ni emõ enine mli, ni ewó eno̱; ni etšé̱ *meikroṅkroṅi le̱ ke̱ okũlafoi le̱ ke̱-ba, ni eke̱le̱ damo amehĩe hĩekãlo. *K.

english_verse: Everyone in Joppa heard what had happened, and many of them put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni anu he ye̱ Iopa fẽ, ni mei pī he Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ no̱ ame̱ye.

english_verse: Peter stayed on for a while in Joppa in the house of a man named Simon, who made leather.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ehĩ Iopa gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ ye̱ Simon, wolokpōlo̱ le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: He explained everything to them and sent them off to Joppa.
translation_verse: ni egbaame̱ nibii ne̱ fẽ, ni etšũame̱ Iopa.

english_verse: A voice said to him, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
translation_verse: Ni gbē ko kē̱le̱ ake̱: Petro, te ši, gbe ní oye!

english_verse: Hurry down and go with them. Don't worry, I sent them.”
translation_verse: nohewo̱ le̱ te ši ni okpleke ši oke̱ame̱ aya, ni okadše ṅwane ko, edšake̱ mi mitšũame̱.

english_verse: Peter invited them to spend the night. The next morning, Peter and some of the Lord's followers in Joppa left with the men who had come from Cornelius.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšé̱ame̱ ke̱-ba šīa le̱ ni ebafeame̱ gbo. Ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ Petro ke̱ame̱ yiṅ ke̱-te, ni nyemimei ní yo̱ Iopa le̱ ateṅ meikomei fata ehe.

english_verse: The next day they arrived in Caesarea where Cornelius was waiting for them. He had also invited his relatives and close friends.
translation_verse: Ni dšetše̱reno̱ ekoṅ le̱ ame̱yaše̱ Kaisarea. Ši Kornelio mīkwe̱ame̱ gbe̱, ni etšé̱ ewekumei ke̱ enanemei dšudši ke̱-kpe.

english_verse: When Peter arrived, Cornelius greeted him. Then he knelt at Peter's feet and started worshiping him.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni Petro boteo̱ šĩa le̱, Kornelio ke̱le̱ bakpe, ni eho egbe ši ye̱ enãdši anā ni edšále̱.

english_verse: But Peter took hold of him and said, “Stand up! I am nothing more than a human.”
translation_verse: Ši Petro wó eno̱, ni ekē̱: Te ši, ši mi hũ gbomo dšimi.

english_verse: I agreed to come here, but I want to know why you sent for me.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ hũ ni beni atšũ abakpēmi le̱, mitšee nā ni miba ne̱. Ni agbe̱ne̱ mībinye ake̱: Mẽ sane hewo̱ ni nyebakpēmi ne̱?

english_verse: Cornelius answered: Four days ago at about three o'clock in the afternoon I was praying at home. Suddenly a man in bright clothes stood in front of me.
translation_verse: Ni Kornelio kē̱ ake̱: Ṅme̱ne̱ dši gbĩĩ edſe̱ le̱ mihī ṅmā̃ ke̱-baši ne̱ke̱ ṅmle̱tſā ne̱ no̱, ni gbe̱ke̱ ṅme̱dši etẽ mli le̱ mīso̱le ye̱ miwe le̱; ni na, nū ko ní wo atade kaṅkaṅ badamo̱ mihĩe,

english_verse: Now send to Joppa for Simon Peter. He is visiting in the home of Simon the leather maker, who lives near the sea.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ tšũ mei ke̱-ya Iopa, ní ayakpē Simon ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Petro hũ le̱ ke̱-ba, eyato Simon wolokpōlo̱ le̱ ní šĩa kã ṅšo̱ nā le̱ ṅõ, ni ké̱ eba le̱, eebawie etsõo.

english_verse: I sent for you at once, and you have been good enough to come. All of us are here in the presence of the Lord God, so that we can hear what he has to say.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni amrõ le̱ noṅṅ ni mitšŭ oṅõ, ni ofe dsogbāṅ ake̱ oba ne̱. Nohewo le̱ agbe̱ne̱ wo̱fẽ wo̱ye̱ bie̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, koni wo̱bo nibii fẽ ní Nyoṅmo̱ ekē̱o eto le̱ atoi.

english_verse: God is pleased with everyone who worships him and does right, no matter what nation they come from.
translation_verse: ši moṅ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ mli le̱, moni šeo̱le̱ gbeyei ni etšuo̱ dšale̱ nii le̱, le̱ dši moni saä ehĩe. Ioh.

english_verse: This is the same message that God gave to the people of Israel, when he sent Jesus Christ, the Lord of all, to offer peace to them.
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ tšũ ake̱ wiemo̱ le̱ yahã Israelbii ni atšṍ Iesu Kristo no̱ adšadše hedso̱le̱ sanekpakpa atšõame̱, *le̱ dši mei fẽ a-Nuṅtšo̱. *Mat.

english_verse: You surely know what happened everywhere in Judea. It all began in Galilee after John had told everyone to be baptized.
translation_verse: Nyedientše̱ nyele sane le̱ ni ba Iudea fẽ ni edše šiši Ke̱-dše̱ Galilea, ye̱ baptisimo ní Iohane šie̱ le̱ še̱ le̱, Mat.

english_verse: God gave the Holy Spirit and power to Jesus from Nazareth. He was with Jesus, as he went around doing good and healing everyone who was under the power of the devil.
translation_verse: bo̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ Mnmo̱ kroṅkroṅ ke̱ hewale̱ *efo Iesu ní dše̱ Nazaret le̱ mū, ní ekpaä ši efeo̱ edšŭrõ ni etšáa mei fẽ ní abonsam haoo̱ame̱ le̱, edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱le̱ ye̱. *Ies.

english_verse: We all saw what Jesus did both in Israel and in the city of Jerusalem. Jesus was put to death on a cross.
translation_verse: Ni wo̱ dši nibii fẽ ní efe ye̱ Iudafoi ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱ Ierusalem le̱ he odasefoi; mo hũ ní ame̱se̱ṅle̱ ye̱ tšo no̱ ame̱gbele̱ le̱.

english_verse: Not everyone saw him. He was seen only by us, who ate and drank with him after he was raised from death. We were the ones God chose to tell others about him.
translation_verse: dšee maṅ mū le̱ fẽ, ši moṅ *odasefoi ní Nyoṅmo̱ ehala eto momo le̱, ní dši wo̱ mei ní wo̱ke̱le̱ ye nii ni wo̱ke̱le̱ nu, beni ete ši ke-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱ se̱ le̱. *Ioh

english_verse: God told us to announce clearly to the people that Jesus is the one he has chosen to judge the living and the dead.
translation_verse: Ni ewowo̱ kitã ake̱ wo̱šie̱ wo̱tšõ maṅ le̱ ni wo̱ye odase ake̱ le̱ dši moni Nyoṅmo̱ efă eto hĩekãlo̱i ke̱ gbohĩĩ *akodšolo̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Every one of the prophets has said that all who have faith in Jesus will have their sins forgiven in his name.
translation_verse: Le̱ ehe odase *gbalo̱i le̱ fẽ yeo̱, ake̱ mofẽmo ní heo̱ eno̱ yeo̱ le̱ aaná ehe ešai fā ye̱ egbe̱i le̱ ahewo. *Ies.

english_verse: While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit took control of everyone who was listening.
translation_verse: Beni Petro wieo̱ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ lolo le̱, Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ ba mei fẽ ní nu wiemo̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: Some Jewish followers of the Lord had come with Peter, and they were surprised that the Holy Spirit had been given to Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ni heyelilo̱i ní dše̱ ketiafō le̱ mli nī ke̱ Petro ba le̱ anā kpe̱ ame̱he ake̱ afo̱se Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ nõkēnõ le̱ aſie dšeṅmădšiaṅbii hũ ano̱;

english_verse: Now they were hearing Gentiles speaking unknown languages and praising God. Peter said,
translation_verse: edšake̱ amenu ake̱ ame̱mīwie *maṅse̱ wiemo̱i sro̱toi ni ame̱mīdsie Nyoṅmo̱ yi. Ke̱ke̱ ni Petro here no̱ ake: *

english_verse: “These Gentiles have been given the Holy Spirit, just as we have! I am certain that no one would dare stop us from baptizing them.”
translation_verse: Ani moko aanyẽ nu nā atšĩ, ní akabaptisi mene̱mei ní ná Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ tamo̱ wo̱ noṅṅ le̱?

english_verse: Peter ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they asked him to stay on for a few days.
translation_verse: Ni efã́ ake̱ abaptisiame̱ ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbe̱i le̱ amli. Ke̱ke̱ ni *ame̱kpale̱ fai ake̱ eke̱ame̱ ahĩ ši gbĩĩ fiō ko. *Ioh.

english_verse: they said, “You stayed in the homes of Gentiles, and you even ate with them!”
translation_verse: ame̱kē̱: Ote hĩĩ fõlo̱i aṅõ ni oke̱-ame̱ yaye nii. Gal.

english_verse: I heard a voice saying to me, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
translation_verse: Ni minu gbē ko hũ kē̱mi ake̱: Petro, te ši, gbe ní oye!

english_verse: I remembered that the Lord had said, “John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Ni mikai Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ní ekē̱ ake̱: “Iohane le̱ eke̱ nu baptisi, ši nye le̱ aabaptisinye ye̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ mli le̱.”

english_verse: When they heard Peter say this, they stopped arguing and started praising God. They said, “God has now let Gentiles turn to him, and he has given life to them!” The Church in Antioch
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱nu wiemo̱i ne̱ le̱, ame̱bu ame̱nā, ni ame̱wo Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe nyam ame̱kē̱: Bĕle̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ hũ Nyoṅmo̱ ehãame̱ tšuitšakemo̱ ní ako̱-ahere ame̱yiwala!

english_verse: Some of the Lord's followers had been scattered because of the terrible trouble that started when Stephen was killed. They went as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, but they told the message only to the Jews.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ mei *ni gbe̱ fã ye̱ Stefano amane̱hũlũ le̱ mli le̱ fo mli ke̱-te Foinike ke̱ Kipro ke̱ Antiokia tō̃, ši ame̱dšadšee wiemo le̱ ame̱tšõõ mokomoko ake̱ dša Iudafoi le̱ ke̱ke̱. *

english_verse: Some of the followers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and started telling Gentiles the good news about the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱teṅ meikomei le̱, Kiprobii ke̱ Kirẽnebii dšiame̱, ni mene̱mei ba Antiokia ame̱bawie ame̱tšõ Helabii le̱ hũ, ni ame̱dšadše Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu he sanekpakpa le̱ ame̱tšõame̱.

english_verse: News of what was happening reached the church in Jerusalem. Then they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱he sane ne̱ baše̱ Ierusalem asafo le̱ toiiaṅ, ni ame̱tšũ *Barnaba, koni eyaše̱ Antiokia le̱ tō̃. *

english_verse: When Barnabas got there and saw how God had blessed them with undeserved grace, he was very glad. So he begged them to remain faithful to the Lord with all their hearts.
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ dše̱i ní ebana Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ le̱, emĩ še̱ ehe, ni ewie etšõ ame̱fẽ ake̱ ame̱ke̱ tšui ní fĩ ši akpe̱te̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ he.

english_verse: Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ši gbomo kpakpa dšile̱ ni *eyi obõ ke̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ ke̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli. Ni †aṅõ mei babaō afata Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ he. *

english_verse: He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱ ame̱ke̱ asafo le̱ hĩ ši afi nākplo̱, ni ame̱tšõ mei babaō nii, ni Antiokia kleṅkleṅ awo kaselo̱i le̱ agbe̱i ake̱ Kristofoi ye̱.

english_verse: During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch.
translation_verse: Ši ne̱ke̱ gbĩĩ ne̱ amli le̱ *gbalo̱i komei dše̱ Ierusalem ba Antiokia. *

english_verse: One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱teṅ moko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ *Agabo le̱ te ši, ni etšõ ye̱ Mumo̱ le̱ nā ake̱ hõmo̱ kpeteṅkple baba dšeṅ fẽ, ni eba mli nakai ye̱ Kaisare Klaudio yino̱. *

english_verse: The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea.
translation_verse: Ši kaselo̱i le̱ *kpe̱ mli ake̱ ame̱atšũ noko ame̱mãdše nyemimei ní yo̱ Iudea le̱ ni ame̱ke̱-yafēneame̱, mofẽmo bo̱ni oonyẽ. *Gal,

english_verse: So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni amefe nakai, ni ame̱ṅõ-mãdše onukpai le̱ *ke̱-tšṍ Barnaba ke̱ Saulo nine no̱. *

english_verse: When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Ni beni ena ake̱ eṅõ Iudafoi le̱ anā le̱, ete no̱ ní emõ Petro hũ. Ši akpĩtĩ gbĩĩ le̱ amli ni.

english_verse: He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
translation_verse: Ni beni emõle̱ le̱, ewole̱ tšũṅ, ni etule̱ ewo asrafoi edſe̱dſe̱ kūi edſe̱ deṅ, ni ame̱bu ehe; ni esusu ake̱ Hehō le̱ se̱ le̱ eedšiele̱ etšõ maṅ le̱.

english_verse: and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.”
translation_verse: Ni bo̱fo le̱ kē̱le̱ ake: Mĩamo̱ ní ofĩ otokotai le̱! Ni efe nakai. Ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅō obò le̱ oke ohe ní onyie mise̱!

english_verse: Peter left with the angel, but he thought everything was only a dream.
translation_verse: Ni enyie ese̱ ke̱-dše kpo, ni elee ake̱ noni bo̱fo le̱ feo̱ le̱ ye̱ mli, ši efeo̱le̱ ake̱ nii enaä.

english_verse: They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱ho kleṅkleṅ bulo̱i le̱ ke̱ mei ní dši enyo̱ le̱ ahe le̱, ame̱še̱ dade agbó ní kã ke̱-yaä mã le̱ṅ le̱ he, ni le̱dientše̱ egble ehe ehãame̱, ni ame̱dše kpo ame̱fo blohũ kome mli, ni amrõ le̱ bo̱fo le̱ šĩle̱.

english_verse: Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer.
translation_verse: Ši beni Petro ši agbó le̱, oblayō ko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Rode le̱ ba toibō;

english_verse: When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
translation_verse: ni beni eyo Petro gbē le̱, mīše̱ so̱ṅṅ nā le̱ egblee agbó le̱, ši moṅ edšo foi ke̱-te eyakē̱ ake̱ Petro damo̱ agbó le̱ se̱.

english_verse: But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
translation_verse: Ši Petro kã he mīši; ni beni ame̱gble le̱, ame̱nale̱, ni ame̱nā kpe̱ ame̱he.

english_verse: The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter.
translation_verse: Ši beni dše tše̱re le̱, dšee haomo̱ fiō ba asrafoi le̱ ateṅ ye̱ nõ po ní efe Petro hewo̱.

english_verse: Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while. Herod Dies
translation_verse: Ši beni Herode taoo̱le̱ ni enaale̱ le̱, ekodšo bulo̱i le̱ ni afã́ ake̱ ayagbeame̱. Ni edše Iudea ete Kaisarea ni eyahĩ dše̱i.

english_verse: and a day was set for them to meet with him. Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech.
translation_verse: Ši gbĩ ní ato ko no̱ le̱ Herode wo *emaṅtše̱-atade le̱, ni eyatá kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ no̱, ni ewie ame̱nā.

english_verse: The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!”
translation_verse: Ni mei le̱ blo̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ gbē ne̱, ši dšee gbomo gbē ni. Ezek.

english_verse: At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
translation_verse: Ni amrõ le̱ noṅṅ le̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ bo̱fo tſale̱ nõ, edšake̱ *eke̱ anumnyam le̱ hãã Nyoṅmo̱, ni gõgõmii yele̱, ni edše dšeṅ. *Dan.

english_verse: God's message kept spreading.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ſere ni ete no̱.

english_verse: And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Ši beni Barnaba ke̱ Saulo *egbe ame̱súomo̱ le̱ nā le̱, ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ Ierusalem, ni ame̱ṅõ Iohane, moni atšé̱o̱le̱ †Marko hũ le̱, ame̱fata ame̱he. *

english_verse: Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
translation_verse: Ni Saulo, moni atšé̱o̱le̱ Paulo hũ, ni Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ eyile̱ obõ le̱, kwe̱le̱ gā̃

english_verse: The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out,
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ Israel maṅ ne̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ hala wo̱tše̱mei le̱, ni beni ame̱yato gbo̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, *ewó maṅ le̱ no̱, ni †eke̱ enine ní ewó no̱ dšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše̱i. *Ies.

english_verse: Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyekwe̱a ní ahĩa, koni bo̱ni awie ye̱ *gbalo̱i le̱ amli le̱ akaba nyeno̱ ake̱: *Hab.

english_verse: He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people.
translation_verse: ni ekpãtã *dšeṅmădši kpawo hĩe ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni †edša ame̱šikpoṅ le̱ mli ehãame̱, ni etšṍ ame̱nō. *

english_verse: But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized.
translation_verse: beni Iohane etšṍ hĩe ebašie̱ tšuitšakemo̱ baptisimo̱ etšõ Israel maṅ mū le̱ fẽ se̱ le̱. Luk.

english_verse: Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Iohane egbe egbe̱nyiemo̱ le̱ nă le̱, ekē̱: “Namo nyesusuo̱ ake̱ midši? Dšeemi dšile̱; ši na, moko mība ye̱ mise̱, ní misaa moni fẽneo̱ etokotai ye̱ enădši ahe.” Ioh.

english_verse: Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
translation_verse: ni edšie ehe kpo gbĩĩ pī etšõ mei ni ke̱le̱ dše̱ Galilea ba Ierusalem le̱, mei noṅṅ ní dši edasefoi hã maṅ le̱.

english_verse: God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news
translation_verse: Ni wo̱ le̱, ši ni ewo wo̱tše̱mei le̱ he sanekpakpa le̱ wo̱dšadšeo wotšõo̱nye ne̱, K.

english_verse: that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus, “You are my son because today I have become your Father.”
translation_verse: ake̱ no noṅṅ Nyoṅmo̱ ehã eba mli ehãwo̱ ni wo̱dši ame̱bii le̱, ake̱ nõ kẽ ní etē Iesu ši le̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni aṅmã *ye̱ lala enyo̱ le̱ mli hũ ake̱: “Mibi dsio, ṅme̱ne̱ mifo̱o” le̱. *Lal.

english_verse: God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said, “I will make to you the same holy promises that I made to David.”
translation_verse: Ši ake̱ noni etele̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ ní ekũṅ ese̱ ke̱-yaṅ fitemo̱ mli doṅṅ hewo̱ le̱, ekē̱ ne̱ke̱: *“Maṅō David dromo̱nii ní mãmo̱ ši šiṅṅ le̱ mahãnye.” *Ies.

english_verse: And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ hũ ni ekē̱ ye̱ hekroko ake̱: “Ohãṅ omokroṅkroṅ le̱ ana fitemo̱” le̱. Lal.

english_verse: When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ David le̱, beni etšu Nyoṅmo̱ yiṅtō nā nii ye̱ eyino̱ le̱, etšṍ mli ewo̱, ni aṅõle̱ afata etše̱mei le̱ ahe, ni ena fitemo̱.

english_verse: But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
translation_verse: Ši moni Nyoṅmo̱ tēle̱ ši le̱, enaa fitemo̱.

english_verse: My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, atāmei ke̱ anyemimei, nyenáa nyelea, ake̱ mone̱ noṅṅ no̱ atšṍo̱ adšadšeo̱ *ešaifā atšõo̱nye le̱; edšake̱ nibii fẽ ní †anyeṅ abunye bem ye̱ he ye̱ Mose mla le̱ nā le̱, *

english_verse: But everyone who has faith in Jesus is set free.
translation_verse: mone̱ mli le̱ mofẽmo ní heo̱ yeo̱ le̱, abuo̱le̱ bem. Rom.

english_verse: “Look, you people who make fun of God! Be amazed and disappear. I will do something today that you won't believe, even if someone tells you about it!”
translation_verse: “Nye heguo̱gbelo̱i, nyekwe̱a, ni nyehĩe afeanye yā, ni nyelādšea; edšake̱ mibatšu nitšumo̱ ko ye̱ nyeyino̱, nitšumo̱ ko ní ké̱ moko gbanye tete le̱, nyeheṅ nyeyeṅ ko̱kō̱ko̱.”

english_verse: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱dše Iudafoi akpẽhe le̱, dšeṅmădšiaṅbii le̱ kpaame̱ fai ake̱ ame̱badšadše ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ ame̱tšõame̱ ekoṅ ye̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ ní baä le̱ no̱.

english_verse: After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ši beni mei ni yo̱ kpēhe le̱ ekpá le̱, Iudafoi ke̱ Iudafoiahefatalo̱i ní šeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei le̱ ateṅ mei pī nyie Paulo ke̱ Barnaba se̱, ni ame̱wie ame̱tšõame̱ ni ame̱woame̱ ṅā ake̱ *ame̱kpe̱te̱ Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ lo̱ he.

english_verse: The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni hedšō̱mo̱gbī ní nyie se̱ le̱ no̱ le̱ ſe̱ fiō ní maṅ mū le̱ fẽ ababua ame̱he nā ame̱babo Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ toi.

english_verse: When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
translation_verse: Ši beni Iudafoi le̱ na asafoi le̱, awuṅãyelĩ te ši babaō ye̱ ame̱mli, ni ame̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ke̱ šimo̱ ke̱ musubō̱-wiemo̱ kū nii ní Paulo wieo̱ le̱ anā. K.

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas bravely said: We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ni Paulo ke̱ Barnaba wie ekã na ame̱kē̱: Nye *tšutšu esa ake̱ adšadše Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ atšõ; ši ake̱-ni nyeṅwã wiemo̱ le̱ ni †nyebuu nyehe ake̱ nyesa nāno̱ wala le̱ hewo̱ le̱, na, wo̱do̱ woyi ke̱-mīya dšeṅmādši le̱ aṅõ. *

english_verse: The Lord has given us this command, “I have placed you here as a light for the Gentiles. You are to take the saving power of God to people everywhere on earth.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ nakai Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wowo̱ kitā ake̱: *“Miṅõo mito ake̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ala, koni otšṍ yiwalaheremo̱ ke̱-yaši šikpoṅ le̱ nāgbēhei le̱.” *Ies.

english_verse: This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ši beni dšeṅmãdšiaṅbii le̱ nu ene̱ le̱, ame̱ná mīše̱, ni ame̱wo Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ hĩe nyam, ni *mei abo̱ ní adšie ato nāno̱ wala le̱ hé ye. *Rom.

english_verse: The message about the Lord spread all over this region.
translation_verse: Ni Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ le̱ gbe̱ ſā ye̱ dše̱i niiaṅ fẽ.

english_verse: But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
translation_verse: Ši Iudafoi le̱ wowō yei Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyeišelo̱i ní abuo̱ame̱ le̱ ke̱ mã le̱ṅ hĩenāno̱bii le̱ ayiṅ, ni ame̱hã yiwale̱ te ši wo Paulo ke̱ Barnaba, ni ame̱ſĩeame̱ ke̱-dše̱ ame̱kpokpai le̱ ano̱.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱ le̱ *ame̱kpokpo ame̱nãdši aši mlu ame̱ſie ame̱no̱, ni ame̱yiṅ ke̱-te Ikoniom. *

english_verse: But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
translation_verse: Ni kaselo̱i le̱ yimo̱ obõbõ ke̱ mīše̱ ke̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ.

english_verse: The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles.
translation_verse: Ši mã le̱ṅ bii le̱ amli gbá enyo̱, fã fata Iudafoi le̱ ahe, ni ſã hũ fata bo̱foi le̱ ahe.

english_verse: The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱tšé̱ Barnaba ake̱ Dio, ke̱ Paulo hũ Herme, edšake̱ le̱ titri ewieo̱,

english_verse: When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
translation_verse: Ši beni bo̱foi ni dši Barnaba ke̱ Paulo nu he le̱, ame̱gbla ame̱tadei ni ame̱ša foi ame̱yabote asafo le̱ teṅ ame̱hĩe blo̱mo̱

english_verse: Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
translation_verse: ake̱: Atāmei, meni nyefeo̱ ne̱? *Wo̱ hũ gbomei ádesãi dšiwo̱ tamo̱nye noṅṅ, ni wo̱mīdšadše sanekpakpa wo̱mītšõnye, koni nyekũ nyese̱ ke̱-dše̱ ne̱ke̱ yakayakanii ne̱ ahe ke̱-ba Nyoṅmo̱ hĩekãlo̱ le̱ ṅõ, mo noṅṅ ní fe ṅwei ke̱ šikpoṅ ke̱ ṅšo̱ ke̱ nii fẽ ní yo̱ ame̱mli le̱; *

english_verse: But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
translation_verse: ši kẽle̱ efõõ le̱dientše̱ ehe odaseyeli, ši moṅ efeo edšŭrõ ni ehãa nyoṅmo̱ dše̱o̱ ṅwei ne̱o̱ hãanye, ke̱ afii ní baä nii pī hũ, eke̱ ṅmā̃ ke̱ mīše̱ woo̱ nyetšuiiaṅ obõ. Lal.

english_verse: Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
translation_verse: Ni ekpakpa ame̱fe dãni ame̱ke̱ ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ tšĩ afo̱le ní kũle̱ mei le̱ bašã ahãame̱ le̱ nā.

english_verse: Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
translation_verse: Ši Iudafoi komei dše̱ Antiokia ke̱ Ikoniom ba dše̱i bawo asafoi le̱ ayiṅ, ni *ame̱tſia Paulo te̱i, ni ame̱gblale̱ ke̱-dše̱ mā le̱ṅ ame̱susuo̱ ake̱ egbo. *

english_verse: But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe. Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Ši beni kaselo̱i le̱ bo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe le̱, ete ši ni ete mã le̱ṅ. Ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ eke̱ Barnaba yiṅ ke̱-te Derbe.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱dšadše sanekpakpa le̱ ame̱tšõ maṅ le̱ ni ame̱hã mei pī etšṍmo̱ kaselo̱i le̱, ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-te Listra ke̱ Ikoniom ke̱ Antiokia,

english_verse: They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.”
translation_verse: ame̱sā ame̱wo kaselo̱i le̱ amumo̱ṅ wala le̱ hewale̱, ni ame̱wie ame̱tšõame̱, ake̱ ame̱hĩe hemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ mli, ni asaṅ esa ake̱ wo̱tšṍo̱ amanehũlũi pī amli ke̱-boteo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ maṅtše̱yeli le mli.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fãmo̱ onukpai ame̱to asafo-fẽ-asafo no̱, ni ame̱ke̱ so̱lemo̱ ke̱ ṅmãhile̱ tuame̱ ame̱wo Nuṅtšo̱ mo no̱ ní ame̱há ame̱ye le̱ deṅ.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fo mli ye̱ Pisidia ni ame̱ba Pamfilia.

english_verse: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱dšadše wiemo̱ le̱ ame̱tšõ ye̱ Perge le̱, ame̱ṅõ-ſie no̱ ke̱-ba Atalia.

english_verse: and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bote le̱le̱ mli ye̱ dše̱i, ni ame̱fã ke̱-ba Antiokia, heni atuame̱ awo Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ le̱ deṅ ke̱-hã nitšumo̱ ni ame̱tšu, ame̱gbe nā ne̱ ye̱ le̱.

english_verse: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱ba dše̱i ni ame̱babua asafo le̱ nā le̱, ame̱gbaame̱ nii ní Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ame̱ eyatšule̱ fẽ, ke̱ bo̱ni egble *hemo̱-ke̱-yeli šĩnā ehã dšeṅmãdši le̱. *

english_verse: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ke̱ kaselo̱i le̱ hĩ ši gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ.

english_verse: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ni bo̱foi le̱ ke̱ onukpai le̱ babua ame̱he nā, koni ame̱tao ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ mli.

english_verse: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
translation_verse: Simeon egba bo̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ basra dšeṅmãdši le̱ tšutšu ko ni ehala ame̱teṅ maṅ ko ehã egbe̱i le̱. K.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
translation_verse: “Nii ne̱ ase̱ le̱ makũ mise̱ maba, ni masā David bū ní ekũmo̱ le̱ mamã, ni etšũkoi le̱ hũ matſa ekoṅ, ni matēle̱ ši mamã ši;

english_verse: I promised it long ago.”
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ le enitšumo̱i le̱ fẽ ke̱-dše̱ dšeṅ šišidšē.

english_verse: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ noni mikē̱o̱ dši ake̱ akagba mei ní ekũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-dše̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ amli ke̱-ba Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ le̱ anā tūtu;

english_verse: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ke̱-dše̱ blema bēbe le̱ Mose ye̱ mei ní šie̱o̱le̱ ye̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ no̱, ni dā hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ akaneo̱ ewodši le̱ ye̱ kpēhei le̱.

english_verse: The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni esa bo̱foi le̱ ke̱ onukpai le̱ ke̱ asafo mū le̱ fẽ hĩe ake̱ ame̱afãmo̱ hĩĩ komei ye̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱teṅ, ní atšũame̱ ke̱ Paulo ke̱ Barnaba ke̱-ya Antiokia; ame̱dši Iuda moni atšé̱o̱le̱ Barsaba hũ le̱, ke̱ Sila, nyemimei le̱ ateṅ onukpai le̱.

english_verse: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅmã wolo áme̱hãame̱ ake̱: Bo̱foi le̱ ke̱ onukpai le̱ ke̱ nyemimei le̱ mibi nyemimei ní dše̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ateṅ ni yo̱ Antiokia ke̱ Siria ke̱ Kilikia le̱ dšogbāṅ.

english_verse: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
translation_verse: Ake̱ noni wo̱nu ake̱ wo̱teṅ meikomei yiṅ ame̱ba ame̱bagba nyenā ke̱ wiemo̱i komei, ni ame̱ke̱-futu nyedſẽṅmo̱i ame̱kē̱ ake̱ aflo̱nye ketia ní nyeye Mose mla le̱ no̱, tše̱ wo̱wokoame̱ nakai kitã ko, hewo̱ le̱ K.

english_verse: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: ní dši gbomei ni eše̱ ame̱he ame̱fõ ye̱ wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo gbe̱i ahewo̱ le̱ he wo̱tšũ nyeṅõ.

english_verse: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ esa Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ hĩe ni esa wo̱ hũ wo̱hĩe ake̱, wo̱ke̱ dšatšu ko akafõ nyeno doṅṅ, ake̱ dša nii ní he hãaä ne̱ noṅṅ:

english_verse: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱, beni awoame̱ gbe̱ le̱, ame̱ba Antiokia, ni ame̱babua asafo le̱ nā ni ame̱dšie wolo le̱ ame̱hãame̱.

english_verse: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱kane le̱, ame̱mī se̱ ame̱he ye̱ mīše̱dšemo̱ le̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Ši Iuda ke̱ Sila le̱, ake̱ noni ame̱dientše̱ hũ *gbalo̱i dšiame̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱ wiemo̱ babaō še̱dše nyemimei le̱ amī ni ame̱woame̱ hewale̱. *

english_verse: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱tše̱ flō ye̱ dše̱i le̱, nyemimei le̱ woame̱ gbe̱ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli ke̱-te mei ní tšũame̱ le̱ aṅõ.

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
translation_verse: Ši Paulo ke̱ Barnaba hĩ Antiokia ame̱tšõ nii ni ame̱dšadše Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ sanekpakpa le̱, ni meikrokomei pī hũ fe nakai.

english_verse: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
translation_verse: Ši gbĩĩ komei ase̱ le̱ Paulo kē̱ Barnaba ake̱: Hã wo̱kũ wo̱se̱ wo̱yasra wo̱nyemimei le̱ ye̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ ní wo̱dšadše Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ye̱ mli le̱ṅ, ni wo̱kwe̱ *bo̱ni ame̱yo̱. *

english_verse: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Ni Barnaba hĩe kã no̱ ake̱ ame̱aṅõ Iohane ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Marko le̱ ame̱fata ame̱he.

english_verse: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
translation_verse: Ši Paulo le̱, esusu ake̱ esaa ake̱ ame̱aṅõ moni kpale ye̱ ame̱se̱ ye̱ Pamfilia ní eke̱ame̱ eyaa nitšumo̱ le̱ ame̱fata ame̱he.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ efe béi āhũ po ni eha ame̱gbla ame̱mli, ni Barnaba ṅõ Marko efata ehe ni ame̱tsṍ le̱le̱ mli ke̱-te Kipro.

english_verse: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
translation_verse: Ši Paulo le̱, efã Sila efata ehe, ni beni nyemimei le̱ tule̱ ame̱wo Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ le̱ deṅ le̱, eyiṅ.

english_verse: They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
translation_verse: Ni etšṍ Siria ke̱ Kilikia eyawo asafoi le̱ ahewale̱.

english_verse: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
translation_verse: Le̱ Paulo taoo̱ ake̱ eke̱le̱ aya, ni eṅõle̱ efole̱ ketia ye̱ Iudafoi ní yo̱ dše̱i niiaṅ le̱ ahewo̱; edšake̱ ame̱fẽ ame̱le ake̱ etše̱ le̱ Helanyo ni.

english_verse: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱kpaä mãdši le̱ ano̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱ *mlai ní bo̱foi le̱ ke̱ onukpai le̱ ní yo̱ Ierusalem le̱ wo le̱ hãame̱, koni ame̱ye no̱. *

english_verse: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ asafoi le̱ ná hewale̱ ye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mli, ni ame̱yi fáa dāne̱.

english_verse: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
translation_verse: ni ameba Misia niiaṅ, ni ame̱ka ake̱ ame̱ate Bitinia, ši Iesu Mumo̱ le̱ eṅmẽẽame̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ho Misia he ni ame̱ba Troia.

english_verse: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
translation_verse: Ni nyōṅ le̱ Paulo na nii, ake̱ nū Makedonianyo ko damo̱ ši mikpale fai ake̱: Ba Makedonia ní obaye obuawo̱!

english_verse: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
translation_verse: Ši beni ena nii le̱ pe le̱, amrõ le̱ wo̱tao ake̱ wo̱ya Makedonia, edšake̱ wo̱ná wo̱le kre̱dē̱ ake̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ etšé̱wo̱ ke̱-mīya dše̱i, koni wo̱yadšadše sanekpakpa le̱ wo̱tšõame̱.

english_verse: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
translation_verse: ni wo̱dše̱ dše̱i le̱ wo̱te Filipi ní dši Makedonia šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ maṅ wulu ke̱ Romabii ašimõmo̱he le̱. Ni wo̱hĩ ne̱ke̱ mã ne̱ṅ gbĩĩ komei.

english_verse: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
translation_verse: Ni hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ wo̱dše̱ mã le̱ṅ wo̱te fā nā, heni afo̱ö̱ so̱lemo̱ ye̱ le̱, ní wo̱trá ši wo̱wie wo̱tšõ yei ní ebabua ame̱he nā ye̱ dše̱i le̱.

english_verse: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
translation_verse: Ni yō ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Lidia ní dši kō̱dšaṅhõlo̱ ko ni dše̱ Tiatira mã le̱ṅ ní šeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei le̱ hũ nu; le̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gble etšui nā, ake̱ ebo nii ni Paulo wieo̱ le̱ toi. Ioh.

english_verse: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
translation_verse: Ni beni abaptisile̱ ke̱ ewe le̱, ekpa wo̱ fai ake̱: Ke̱dši nyebumi ake̱ mihé Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ miye ano̱kwale mli le̱, no le̱ nyebaä miwe le̱, ní nyebahĩa dše̱i. Ni ehĩewo̱ āhũ ni wo̱kplẽ.

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Ši beni enuṅtšo̱mei le̱ nā ake̱ ame̱ninámo̱ no̱hĩekamo̱nõ le̱ be̱ doṅṅ le̱, ame̱mõmo̱ Paulo ke̱ Sila ni ame̱gblaame̱ ke̱-te lume̱i le̱ ahĩe ye̱ dšã le̱ no̱;

english_verse: They told the officials, “These Jews are upsetting our city!
translation_verse: ni benĩ ame̱kplaame̱ ke̱-te asafoatše̱mei le̱ ahĩe le̱, ame̱kē̱: Ne̱ke̱ gbomei ne̱ ní dši Iudafoi le̱ ewo wo̱mã le̱ṅ hirihiri,

english_verse: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱mītšõtšõ gbe̱nānii komei ní wo̱be̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ wo̱mõo̱ mli lo wo̱yeo̱ no̱, edšake̱ Romabii dšiwo̱.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱tſiaame̱ kpãi pī le̱, ame̱woame̱ tšũṅ, ni ame̱wo gbokle̱foi le̱ akwe̱lo̱ le̱ kitā ake̱ eṅõame̱ eto ſeſēſe;

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: ni ake̱-ní awole̱ ne̱ke̱ kitã hewo̱ le̱, eke̱ame̱ yawo tšũ ni yo̱ se̱gbe̱ le̱ mli, ni ebo̱ ame̱nãdši apã.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Ni trukā le̱ šikpoṅ hoso wā, ni tšũ le̱ fanesi le̱ gbũgbã, ni amrõ le̱ šĩnāi le̱ fẽ gblegblei ni ame̱fẽ ame̱kpãi le̱ kplo̱ke.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Ši beni gbokle̱foi akwe̱lo̱ le̱ he̱le ši ke̱-dše̱ wo̱ mli ni ena ake̱ tšũ le̱ nā šĩnāi le̱ fẽ kãmo̱ le̱, egbla eklante ní kũle̱ ebagbe edšeṅ nā, edšake̱ esusu ake̱ gbokle̱foi le̱ edšo foi.

english_verse: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
translation_verse: Ši Paulo bo ke̱ gbē wale̱ ekē̱: Kāfe ohe efõṅ ko, ši wo̱fẽ wo̱ye̱ bie̱.

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni etšé̱ ni abahāle̱ la, ni eša foi ke̱-bote tšũ le̱ṅ, ni eke̱ hekpokpomo̱ ho egbē Paulo ke̱ Sila hĩe,

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: ni eke̱ame̱ dše kpo ni ekē̱: Nuṅtšo̱mei, té mafe tēṅ ní maná yiwalaheremo̱ṅ?

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱kē̱: Hemo Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo le̱ no̱ oye, ni aahere oke̱ owe le̱ fẽ yiwala.

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱dšadše Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ wiemo̱ ame̱ tsõle̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní yo̱ ewe le̱.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Ni eṅõame̱ nakai nyō le̱ṅ ṅmle̱tſā le̱ mli noṅṅ, ni efó̱ ame̱kpāi le̱ anā ehãame̱, ni abaptisile̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ bii fẽ amrõ le̱ noṅṅ;

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: ni eke̱ame̱ te ewe, ni eyaṅme̱ame̱ okplõ, ni emli flĩle̱ ke̱ ewe le̱ fe ake ehé Nyoṅmo̱ eye.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Ši beni dše tše̱re le̱, asafoatše̱mei le̱ tšũ asrafoi bake: Ṅmē̃mo̱ gbomei le̱ ahe ní ameya.

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Ši gbokle̱foiakwe̱lo̱ le̱ dšadše ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ etsõ Paulo ake̱: Asafoatše̱mei le̱ etšũ ke̱-ba ake̱ aṅmē̃ nyehe, nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyedšea kpo ni nyeyabaä dšogbāṅ.

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Ši Paulo kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Wo̱ ní *Romabii dšiwo̱ ní abukowo̱ fo̱ le̱, ame̱yiwo̱ ye̱ dšā no̱, ni ame̱wowo̱ tšũṅ hũ: ni kpāko ameſieo̱wo̱ nĩgī̃ lo? Dabida, ši moṅ hã ame̱dientše̱ ame̱ba ní ame̱badšiewo̱. *

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Ni asrafoi le̱ yadšadše ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱i ne̱ ame̱tšõ asafoatše̱mei le̱; ni beni ame̱nu ake̱ Romabii dšiame̱ le̱, ame̱še gbeyei.

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ba ame̱bakpaame̱ fai, ni beni ame̱dšieame̱ le̱, ame̱tuto̱ame̱ ake̱ ame̱dše mã le̱ṅ.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱dše tšũ le̱ṅ le̱, ame̱te Lidia we le̱. Ni beni ame̱na nyemimei le̱ ni ame̱še̱dše ame̱mī le̱, ame̱yiṅ ame̱te.

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: ni egble nā etšõame̱ faṅṅ ake̱ dša Kristo le̱ na amanehũlũ ni ete ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ, ni ake̱ ne̱ke̱ Iesu, ní midšadšeo̱ ehe sane mitšõo̱nye ne̱, dši Kristo le̱. Luk.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱hé se̱damo̱nii ye̱ Iason ke̱ meikrokomei le̱ adeṅ le̱, ame̱ṅmē̃ ame̱he.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Ši mene̱mei asu hĩ fè mei ní yo̱ Tesalonika le̱, ni ame̱ le̱ ame̱dšie ame̱yitšoṅ ame̱mõ wiemo̱ le̱ mli, ni dā *ame̱kpaä ṅmãle̱i le̱ amli ame̱kwe̱o̱ ake̱ nibii ne̱ ye̱ mli nakai lo. *Ioh.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Šĩ beni Iudafoi ní yo̱ Tesalonika le̱ nu he ake̱ Paulo eyadšadše Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ye̱ Beroia hũ le̱, ame̱ba dše̱i hũ ní ame̱bawo mei le̱ ayiṅ, ni ame̱dšidšaame̱.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Ši mei ní yawa Paulo le̱ ke̱le̱ te Atēne tō̃; ni noni eše̱ame̱ ake̱ Sila ke̱ Timoteo aba eṅõ oyá le̱, ame̱yi mli.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ eke̱ Iudafoi ní yo̱ kpēhe le̱ ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyeišelo̱i le̱ ke̱ mei ní ke̱le̱ kpeo̱ dāne̱ ye̱ dšā le̱ no̱ le̱ yiyio̱;

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ṅõle̱ ke̱-te Areopago le̱, ni ame̱kē̱: Ani oohã wo̱le nõ tšõmo̱ hẽ ní owieo̱ he ne̱?

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ohã wo̱toii enu maṅse̱ sãdši; hewo̱ le̱ wo̱mītao šiši wo̱le.

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Ši Atēnebii fẽ ke̱ gbo̱i nī yo̱ dše̱i le̱, noni eſe̱ame̱ pe̱ dši sane hē ko gbā ke̱ toibō.

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Ši Paulo yadamo̱ Areopago le̱ teṅ ni ekē̱: Atāmei Atēnebii, miyoo ye̱ nibii fẽ mli ake̱ nyedšáa wo̱dši pe̱pē̱pe̱.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ beni mihoo̱ ni mikwe̱ nii ní nyedšáa le̱, mina afo̱lešãlate̱ ko hū nī aṅmã ye̱ no̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ nī aléko le̱ nõṅ. Nohewo̱ le̱ moni nyelee le̱ ni nyedšáale̱ kẽ le̱, le̱ noṅṅ ehe sane midšadšeo̱ mitšõo̱nye ne̱.

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: ni asaṅ ake̱ gbomei anidši dšáá le̱, tamo̱ *moko ní noko fĩo̱le̱, le̱ moṅ edeṅ wala ke̱ mumo̱ ke̱ nii fẽ dše̱o̱ hãa gbomei fẽ; *Lal.

english_verse: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
translation_verse: ni lá kome eṅõ-fe gbomei ádesãi fẽ, ní ame̱hĩ šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ hĩe, ni *yino̱i ní eto le̱ ke̱ ame̱šihĩle̱hei le̱ ahũsũi le̱ ekpe mli eto momo, *

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ emli noṅṅ wo̱hĩe kãmo̱ ni wo̱tšio̱ wohe ni wo̱yo̱ ye̱; tamo̱ bo̱ni nyedientše̱ nyelalatše̱mei le̱ ekomei hũ ekē̱ le̱ ake̱: Ši le̱ noṅṅ eſiei dšiwo̱ hũ.

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ Nyoṅmo̱ *ſīei dšiwo̱ le̱, esaa ake̱ wo̱susuo̱ ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ su le̱ tamo̱ šika lo dſie̱tei lo te̱ ko ní gbomo ke̱ eṅā ke̱ edſẽṅmo̱ fe. *

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, *bei ní alee le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ekũ ehĩe efõ no̱, ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ †ēwo gbomei fẽ ní yo̱ hefẽhe le̱ kitã ake̱ ame̱tšake ame̱tšai, *

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: edšake̱ eto gbĩ ko, nõ no̱ ní *ebatšṍ nū ní eto le̱ no̱ ekodšo dšeṅ mū le̱ fẽ ye̱ dšale̱ nā, ake̱-ní eke̱ †hemo̱-ke̱-yeli eto mofẽmo hĩe, edšake̱ etēle̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱. *

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱nu gbohĩĩašitē he le̱, meikomei ye ehe fe̱o, ni meikomei hū kē̱: Wo̱o̱sā wo̱boö toi ekoṅ ye̱ ene̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Bo̱ni fe ní Paulo dše ame̱teṅ ne̱.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ši hĩĩ komei ke̱ ame̱he kpe̱te̱ ehe ni ame̱hē ame̱ye; ame̱teṅ meikomei dši Dionisio, Areopagonyo le̱ hũ, ke̱ yō ko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Damari le̱, ke̱ meikrokomei ní fata ame̱he.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ši beni *Sila ke̱ Timoteo dše̱ Makedonia ba le̱, wiemo̱ le̱ ta Paulo mli ni eye odase vevēve etšõ Iudafoi le̱ ake̱ Iesu dši Kristo le̱. *

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni edše dše̱i ni ete Nyoṅmo̱ dšálo̱ ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Titio Iusto ní ešĩa kpe̱te̱ kpēhe le̱ ṅõ.

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Ni ehĩ dše̱i afi kome ke̱ nyõdši ekpa etšõ Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ye̱ ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Ši beni Galio yeo̱ amralo ye̱ Akaia le̱, Iudafoi le̱ ke̱ dſẽṅmo̱ kome te ši wo Paulo, ni ame̱kplale̱ ke̱-te kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ hĩe

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: ame̱kē̱: Nū ne̱ woo̱ mei le̱ ayiṅ ní ame̱dše mla le̱ se̱ ame̱dšá Nyoṅmo̱.

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Ši beni Paulo bagble enā pe̱ le̱, Galio kē̱ Iudafoi le̱ ake̱: Iudafoi, edši dšū ke̱ fõ sane ko ni kũle̱, esa ake̱ mabonye toi;

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Ni eſieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ hĩe.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱kpale̱ fai ake̱ etše̱ ye̱ ame̱ṅõ fiō le̱, ekplẽẽ;

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ni ehĩ dše̱i fiō, ni no se̱ le̱ eyi mli ekoṅ ni eyakpa Galatia ke̱ Frigia šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ pepē̱pe̱ ewo kaselo̱i le̱ fẽ hewale̱.

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Ni Iudanyo ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Apolo ní ese̱ dše̱ Aleksandria ní dši nū nātšelo̱ ní yo̱ hewale̱ ye̱ ṅmãle̱i le̱ amli hũ le̱ ba Efeso.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Atšõ nū ne̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbe̱ le̱ he nii, ni eye̱ ekã ye̱ mumo̱ mli ni ewieo̱ ni etšõo̱ Iesu he nii fitšofitšo, tše̱ *Iohane baptisimo̱ le̱ ke̱ke̱ ele. *

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Ni ebõi ekãnãwiemo̱ ye̱ kpēhe le̱. Ši beni Akwila ke̱ Priskila nu ehe le̱, ame̱ṅõle̱ ke̱-ba ame̱ṅõ, ni ame̱tšõle̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbe̱ le̱ fitšofitšo.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ši beni esusu ake̱ eefoṅ ke̱-ya Akaia le̱, nyemimei le̱ ṅmã wolo ame̱ṅõwo kaselo̱i le̱ aṅā ake̱ ame̱herele̱ hĩemẽ. Ni beni eba dše̱i le̱, ehĩ hã mei ní etšṍ dromo̱ le̱ no̱ ehé eye le̱ babaō.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ eke̱ hewale̱ kũ Iudafoi le̱ anā ni eke̱ ṅmãle̱i le̱ tšõame̱ faṅṅ ake̱ Iesu dši Kristo le̱.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Ni ehĩe nakai femo̱ āhũ afii enyo̱ so̱ṅṅ, ni mei fẽ ní yo̱ Asia le̱, Iudafoi ke̱ Helabii le̱ fẽ, nu Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu wiemo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Ši Iudafoi okõmfoi ní nyie kpaä ši le̱ ateṅ meikomei hũ ka ní ame̱ke̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu gbe̱i afã́ mei ní mumo̱i fõdši yo̱ ame̱mli le̱ ayi ake̱: Mina Iesu ni Paulo šie̱o̱ le̱. Luk.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Ši mumo̱ fõṅ le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iesu le̱, milele̱, ni Paulo hũ, milele̱; ši nye le̱, namei dšinye?

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Ni mei ni *ehé eye le̱ ateṅ mei pī hũ ba ni ame̱badšadše ame̱nifemo̱nii le̱ faṅṅ ame̱tšõ.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Ni ṅkũnyāyelo̱i le̱ hũ ateṅ mei babaō ba ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱wodši le̱ babua ši ni ame̱šã ye̱ mei fẽ hĩe; ni beni abu nā le̱, efe dſie̱te̱i kukudši akpei-nyoṅmai-enumo̱.

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Ši beni agbe nii ne̱ anā le̱, Paulo to eyiṅ ye̱ mumo̱ le̱ mli ake̱ eeyatšṍ Makedonia ke̱ Akaia ke̱-ya Ierusalem, ni ekē̱: Ké̱ miše̱ dše̱i le̱, dša miyakwe̱ *Roma hũ. *

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Ši beni etšŭ mei ní súmoo̱le̱ le̱ ateṅ mei enyo̱, *Timoteo ke̱ †Erasto, Makedonia le̱, le̱dientše̱ ehĩ Asia be fiō. *

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Ši nakai be le̱ mli noṅṅ le̱ sakasaka ko ni bate ši ye̱ tšõmo̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱ edšee ſe̱mo̱. K.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ dſie̱te̱iṅālo̱ ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Demetrio le̱ ke̱ dſie̱te̱i feo̱ Artemi so̱lemo̱tšũi, ni hãa nakai ṅālo̱i le̱ *náa nii pī ye̱ mli; *

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: ni etšé̱ame̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní tšuo̱ nakai nii le̱ eko le̱ ke̱-bakpe, ni ekē̱: Atāmei, nyele ake̱ ne̱ke̱ ṅā ne̱ wo̱ke̱-náa wo̱nii pī le̱.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Ni nyesā nyemīna ní nyemīnu ake̱, dšee Efeso ne̱ ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ ſe̱ fiō ni aše̱ Asia fẽ ni ne̱ke̱ Paulo ne̱ tšṍo̱ mei babaō yiṅ ni ekpaleo̱ame̱ ekē̱o̱ ake̱: Nii ní ake̱ nidsi fe le̱ dšee nyoṅmo̱i ni.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Ni dšee ake̱ wo̱nitšumo̱ ne̱ ke̱ke̱ he guo̱ heo̱ agbo, ši moṅ nyoṅmo̱yō Artemi kekenam le̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱ hũ abuṅle̱ ahãṅ nokonoko, ni enumnyam kpeteṅkple le̱ ní Asia ke̱ dšeṅ mū le̱ fẽ hũ dšáa le̱ babutu.

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱nu ene̱ le̱, ame̱mli wo la pam, ni ame̱blo̱ ame̱kē̱: Efesobii Artemi le̱ kekenam ni!

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Ni mã le̱ṅ fẽ fe sakasaka; ni ame̱ke̱ dſẽṅmo̱ kome tšẽ ke̱-te nikwe̱mo̱he le̱, ni ame̱yamõmo̱ *Gaio ke̱ Aristarko ní dši Makedoniabii ní fata Paulo he ke̱-fã gbe̱ le̱. *

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Ši beni Paulo susu ake̱ eete mei le̱ ateṅ le̱, kaselo̱i le̱ ekplẽẽ le̱;

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: ni Asia lume̱i le̱ ateṅ meikomei hũ ní dši Paulo šientše̱mei le̱ tšũ eṅõ abawole̱ ṅā, ake̱ ekakwe̱ ni ekē̱ ēya nikwe̱mo̱he le̱.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Agbene beni meikomei blo̱ö̱ ne̱ke̱ le̱, meikomei hũ mīblo̱ ekroko; edšake̱ mei le̱ efe gidigidi, ni mei kpotō lee nohewo̱ ní ame̱bakpe tete.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱gbla Aleksandro ke̱-dše̱ mei le̱ ateṅ, edšake̱ Iudafoi le̱ mītšire̱ eyi se̱ ke̱-mība hĩegbe̱. Ši Aleksandro fõ enine ētao ake̱ edšieo̱ enā etšõo̱ mei le̱.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱yo ake̱ Iudanyo dšile̱ le̱, ame̱fẽ ame̱ke̱ gbē kome blo̱ aafe ṅmle̱tſāi enyo̱ so̱ṅṅ ake̱: Efesobii Artemi le̱ kekenam ni!

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Ši beni maṅwoloṅmălo̱ le̱ ekpãtã mei le̱, ekē̱: Atāmei Efesobii, nẽ gbomo po lee ake̱ Artemi kekenam le̱ ke̱ amãgã ní kpleke ši ke̱-dše̱ Dio ṅõ le̱ Efesobii amã ne̱ṅ ewulo̱mo yo̱?

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ ake̱-ní ene̱ he be̱ ṅwanedšē hewo̱ le̱, esa ake̱ nyefeo̱ diō, ni nyekafe gidigidi ko.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ nyeke̱ hĩĩ ne̱ eba bie̱, ame̱dšee so̱lemo̱wenii dšulo̱i le̱, ame̱dšee nyenyoṅmo̱yō le̱ he musubo̱lo̱i hũ.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, ke̱dši Demetrio alo enanemei ṅālo̱i le̱ ke̱ moko ye̱ sane ko le̱, kodšomo̱gbĩĩ ye̱, ni amralofoi hũ ye̱; nyehãa ame̱ke̱ sane le̱ ayaä ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši sãdši krokomei anā nyetaoo̱ le̱, akuašoṅ le̱ aaye ye̱ mla nā.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱ná amane eſe̱e̱, ke̱dši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ no̱ hõfemo̱ ne̱ hewo̱ ní ayaflo̱ wo̱nā ake̱ atũatšemo̱ṅ le̱, mẽ sane wo̱teṅ moko yo̱ ní wo̱o̱nyẽ wo̱ṅõdšie wo̱nā? Ni beni ekē̱ ene̱ le̱, edšie asafo le̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Ni beni ebaninawo̱ ye̱ Aso le̱, wo̱ṅõle̱ ke̱-ba le̱le̱ le̱ mli, ni we̱ba Mitilēne.

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Ni edše̱ Mileto etšũ ayakpe Efeso asafo le̱ mli onukpai le̱ abahãle̱.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: bo̱ni mišiuu nii ní he yo̱ se̱námo̱ hãnye le̱ eko no̱, ni midšadše mitšõnye ye̱ faṅṅ ke̱ šĩa-fẽ-šĩa hũ;

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, na, efĩmi ye̱ mumo̱ mli hewo̱ le̱ miya Ierusalem, ni milee nii ní baba mino̱ ye̱ dše̱i,

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: ake̱ dša noni Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ yeo̱ odase faṅṅ ye̱ maṅ-fẽ-maṅ no̱ ekē̱o̱ ake̱ kpāi ke̱ amanehŭlũi mẽo̱mi le̱.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ši kẽle̱ mibuu ene̱mei ekomeflo, ni miwala hũ mibuu ake̱ edšra wa ye̱ mihĩe, beni afe ní mike̱ mīše̱ agbe migbe̱nyiemo̱ le̱ ke̱ súomo̱ ní miná ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu deṅ ake̱ miye Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ sanekpakpa le̱ he odase faṅṅ le̱ nā.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ mīye odase mītšõnye, ake̱ miyee nyeteṅ mokomoko lá yi sõ;

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: edšake̱ midšadše Nyoṅmo̱ yiṅtō mū le̱ fẽ mitšõnye ni mišiuu eko no̱.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyelea nyehe no̱kwe̱mo̱ ke̱ tōiku le̱ fẽ ní Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ éwonye ame̱no̱kwe̱lo̱i le̱, koni nyelè̱ Nyoṅmo̱ asafo le̱ ni eke̱ le̱dientše̱ elá hé le̱.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mile ake̱, ké̱ mikpa mihe le̱, *kiãdši fulo̱i babote nyeteṅ, ni ame̱bāṅ tōiku le̱ yi; *Mat.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: ni nyedientše̱ nyeteṅ hũ le̱, hĩĩ ní wieo̱ nii ní edšaa aate ši, ni ame̱akpla kaselo̱i le̱ ame̱ſie ame̱se̱.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ nyesraä, ni nyekaia ake̱ afii etẽ so̱ṅṅ mike̱ yāfónui efõõ nyeteṅ mofẽmo ko̱ko̱bō̱ nyōṅ ke̱ ſane.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, enyemimei, mītunye mīwo Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ edromo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ deṅ, le̱ eyo̱ hewale̱ ní eke̱-ahã nyenane amõ ši ní eke̱ wo̱fasenii le̱ ahãnye ye̱ mei ſẽ ní atšū ame̱he le̱ ateṅ.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Mihĩe ekõõ nyeteṅ moko dſie̱te̱i lo šika lo atade no̱; Mat.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
