translation_verse: nyedientše̱ nyele ake̱, nii ní hĩaämi ke̱ mei ní ke̱mi yo̱ le̱, ne̱ke̱ nidši ne̱ noṅṅ tšu he nii.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Mike̱ fẽ tšõnye ake̱ nakai sa ake̱ atšu nii ní ake̱-ye abua mei ní be̱ hewale̱, ni akai Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu wiemo̱i le̱, ake̱ le̱dientše̱ ekē̱: “Nõ hãmo̱ mli ye̱ dšō̱mo̱ fè hemo̱.”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Ni beni ewie ne̱ke̱ le̱, ekũla ši ni eke̱ ame̱fẽ so̱le.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱fẽ ame̱fó naakpa, ni ame̱gbēgbē Paulo kue̱ no̱, ni ame̱ſo̱ enā;

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: ni noni do̱ame̱ titri dši wiemo̱ ní ekē̱ ake̱ *ame̱naṅ ehĩe doṅṅ le̱. Ni ame̱yadšiele̱ gbe̱ ye̱ le̱le̱ le̱ mli. *K.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni wo̱ye gbĩĩ le̱ tã le̱, wo̱ṅõ-ſie no̱, ni ame̱ ke̱ ame̱ṅãmei ke̱ ame̱bii fẽ badsiewo̱ gbe̱ ke̱-dše̱ mã le̱ṅ; ni *wo̱kũla ši ye̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ nā ni wo̱so̱le. *

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ši beni wo̱nu ene̱ le̱, wo̱ke̱ dše̱ibii le̱ fẽ kpale̱ fai ake̱ ekaya Ierusalem le̱. Mat.

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní eṅõ-ṅmẽẽ gbe̱ hewo̱ le̱, wo̱fe diṅṅ wo̱kē̱: Afe noni Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ sumoo̱.

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱še̱ Ierusalem le̱, nyemimei le̱ herewo̱ hĩemẽ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ni beni eṅāame̱ le̱, egba nibii ní Nyoṅmo̱ tšṍ esúomo̱ le̱ no̱ etšu ye̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ateṅ le̱ ekomekome.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Ši abatã ohe sane ahãame̱, ake̱ otšõo̱ Iudafoi ní yo̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ateṅ le̱ ake̱ ame̱kwa Mose, ni okē̱o̱ ake̱ ame̱kaflo̱ ame̱bii aketia, ni asaṅ ame̱kanyie ame̱kusumnii ase̱.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: ṅõame̱ ní oke̱ ame̱fẽ ayatšũ nyehe, ni owo noni ahãa le̱ ohãame̱, koni ame̱še̱ ame̱yi, ni mei le̱ fẽ ana ake̱, sane ní abagbaame̱ ye̱ ohe le̱ be̱ṅ, ši moṅ bodientše̱ tete obaä odšeṅ ye̱ mla le̱ nā, ni oyeo̱ no̱.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ši dšeṅmãdšiaṅbii ní ehé eye le̱ ahewo̱ le̱ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱ṅmã ní wo̱kpe̱ mli ake̱ ame̱kaye ne̱ke̱ nibii ne̱ eko no̱, ši moṅ ame̱hĩ wo̱dši afo̱lei ke̱ lá ke̱ koloi ní ašõtõ ke̱ adſamaṅbō̱ ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ Paulo kpla hĩĩ le̱ ke̱-te, ni beni eke̱ ame̱fẽ etšū ame̱he le̱, eke̱ame̱ bote so̱lemo̱we le̱, ni eyadšadše hetšūmo̱ gbĩĩ le̱ anāgbē le̱ etšõ faṅṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní ašã *afo̱le ye̱ ame̱teṅ mofẽmo yi. *

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Ši beni eſe̱ fiō ní aagbe gbĩĩ kpawo le̱ nā le̱, Iudafoi ní dše̱ Asia le̱ nale̱ ye̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱, ni ame̱ta asafo le̱ fẽ mli, ni ame̱bamõle̱;

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱blo̱ ake̱: Atāmei Israelbii, nyebafataä wo̱he! Na nū le̱ ní wieo̱ maṅ ne̱ ke̱ mla le̱ ke̱ bie̱ ne̱ he efõṅ etšõo̱ mei fẽ ye̱ hefẽhe le̱; ni esā eke̱ Helabii eba so̱lemo̱we le̱ eke̱-babule hekroṅkroṅ ne̱ hũ.

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ame̱nale̱ ke̱ *Trofimo ní dše̱ Efeso le̱ ye̱ mã le̱ṅ momo hewo̱ le̱ ame̱susu ake̱ le̱ Paulo ke̱-ba so̱lemo̱we le̱. *

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ni maṅ mū le̱ fẽ bú, ni maṅbii le̱ ša foi ke̱-babua ame̱he nā; ni ame̱mõ Paulo ame̱gblale̱ ke̱-dše̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱ ke̱-dše kpo, ni amrõ le̱ noṅṅ aṅã́mo̱ šĩnāi le̱.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱heo̱le̱ ame̱gbe le̱, ayatſa asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ adafi ake̱ Ierusalem fẽ éfe gidigidi.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Ni amrõ le̱ eṅõ asrafoi ke̱ asafoatše̱mei ni eke̱ame̱ kpleke ši ke̱ foi ke̱-baninaame̱. Ši beni ame̱na asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ ke̱ asrafoi le̱, ame̱fõ Paulo yī.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ tši be̱ṅke̱ ni emõ emli, ni efã́ ake̱ *awole̱ kõsõṅkõsõi enyo̱, ni ebi moni dšile̱ ke̱ noni efe. *K.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ši asafo le̱ mli meikomei mīblo̱ ne̱ke̱ ni meikomei hũ mīblo̱ ekroko. Ni ake̱-ní enaa mli ano̱kwale ye̱ hōfemo̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱, efã́ ake̱ ake̱le̱ aya mō̃ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ni beni eše̱ atrakpoi le̱ anā le̱, eba mli ake asafo le̱ gidigidifemo̱ hewo̱ le̱ asrafoi le̱ wóle̱,

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: edšake̱ maṅbii asafo yū le̱ nyie se̱ mīblo̱ ake̱: Ake̱le̱ aya!

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Ši beni ake̱ Paulo babote mō̃ le̱ṅ le̱, ebi asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ ake̱: Miye hegbe̱ ake̱ mike̱o wieo̱ wiemo̱ ko lo? Ekē̱: Ole Hela wiemo̱?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ dšee bo dši Mizraimnyo le̱ ní nyese̱ ne̱ ni eke̱ atũatšemo̱ ba ni ekpla hĩĩ awuyelo̱i akpei-edſe̱ eſie ese̱ ke̱-te ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱?

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kē̱: Mi le̱ Iudanyo dšimi, ni midše̱ *Tarso, Kilikia maṅ ko ní yo̱ gbe̱i le̱ mli; ši mīkpao fai, hãmi gbe̱ ni mawie matšõ maṅ le̱. *

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Ni beni ehãle̱ gbe̱ le̱, Paulo damo̱ atrakpoi le̱ ano̱, ni efõ maṅ le̱ nine, ni beni dše̱i dšo̱ krãnā le̱, ewie ye̱ Hebri wiemo̱ lo̱ mli ekē̱:

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: bo̱ni oso̱fonukpa le̱ tete ke̱ onukpai le̱ fẽ yeo̱mi odase le̱; mei hũ ní hãmi wodši ní kũle̱ mike̱-yahã nyemimei ni yo̱ Damasko le̱, ní miyafĩmo̱ mei ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ hũ ke̱-ba Ierusalem, koni agblaame̱ toi.

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱, beni minyie gbe̱ le̱ no̱ ni mibabe̱ṅke̱ Damasko aafe hũlũdamo̱ mli le̱, trukā le̱ la ko ní kpe̱mo̱ nā wa dše̱ ṅwei babo̱lemi;

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Ni mikē̱: Meni mafe, Nuṅtšo̱? Ni Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kē̱mi ake̱: Te ši ni oya Damasko, ni dše̱i aatšõo nibii fẽ ni ato ake̱ ofe le̱.

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Ni beni minaa nii doṅṅ ye̱ nakai la le̱ kpe̱mo̱ nā le̱, mei ní ke̱mi nyie le̱ mõ minine mli ame̱yawami Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: Ši nū ko ye̱ ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Anania ní ešeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyei ye̱ mla le̱ nā, ni Iudafoi le̱ fẽ ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ wieo̱ ehe ekpakpa.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Wo̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ehalao eto, ní ole esuomo̱nānii, ni ona dšalo̱ le̱, ní onu edāṅ gbē ko;

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: Ni eba mli ake̱, beni mikũ mise̱ ke̱-ba Ierusalem ekoṅ ni miso̱leo̱ ye̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱, efe tamo̱ nõ enyõ mino̱,

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: ni minale̱ ní ēkē̱mi ake̱: Femo̱ kpa ní odše Ierusalem oyá mli, edšake̱ ame̱ boṅ mihe odase ní oyeo̱ le̱ toi.

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Ni mikē̱: Nuṅtšo̱, ame̱dientše̱ ame̱le ake̱ mi noṅṅ ni sá le̱ miwoo̱ mei ní heo̱ ono̱ yeo̱ le̱ tšũṅ, ni miyio̱ame̱ ye̱ kpēhe-fẽ-kpẽhe le̱; K.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: ni beni aſie Stefano, ohe odaseyelo̱ le̱, lá ši le̱, mi hũ midamo̱ dše̱i, ni miná egbĕle le̱ he tšui, ni *mibu mei ní gbele̱ le̱ mamai le̱ ahe. *

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ni ame̱bole̱ toi ke̱-baši ne̱ke̱ wiemo̱ ne̱ no̱, ni ame̱wó ame̱gbē no̱ ame̱kē̱: Ake̱ ne̱ke̱ gbomo adše šikpoṅ le̱ no̱! edšake̱ esaa ake̱ ehĩo̱ dšeṅ.

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱blo̱o̱ ni ame̱kplo̱ö̱ ame̱he atadei ni ame̱gbe̱o̱ mlu ame̱ſāa kō̱yo̱ mli le̱,

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: asafoiatšenukpa le̱ fã́ ake̱ ake̱le̱ aya mō̃ le̱ mli, ni ekē̱ ake̱ aṅõ kplebii atao eyitšoṅ, koni ená ele nõ sane hewo̱ ni ame̱blo̱ö̱ ame̱woo̱le̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Ši beni afĩle̱ ní abayile̱ le̱, Paulo kē̱ asafoatše̱ ní damo̱ ši le̱ ake̱: *Nyeye̱ hegbe̱ ake̱ nyeyio̱ Romanyo ko ní abukole̱ fo̱ le̱ kplebii lo? *

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Ši beni asafoatše̱ le̱ nu ene̱ le̱, ete asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ ṅõ ni eyakē̱le̱ ake̱: Meni obafe ne̱? edšake̱ ne̱ke̱ gbomo ne̱ Romanyoṅ.

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Ni asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ ba ni ebakē̱le̱ ake̱: Kē̱mo̱mi, ani Romanyo dsio lo? Ni ekē̱: Hē̃.

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Ni asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ here no̱ ake̱: Šika pī mike̱-hé ne̱ke̱ maṅnyotšṍmo̱ ne̱. Ni Paulo kē̱: Ši mi le̱, fo̱ ake̱-fo̱mi.

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni amrõ le̱ noṅṅ mei ni yatao eyitšoṅ le̱ dše emase̱i; ni asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ hũ, ake̱-ni efĩle̱ hewo̱ le̱, beni ená ele ake̱ Romanyo dšile̱ le̱, eše gbeyei,

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní ētao ele nõ hewo̱ kre̱dē̱ ní Iudafoi le̱ flo̱ö̱ enā hewo̱ le̱, dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ efẽnele̱, ni efã́ ake̱ oso̱fonukpai le̱ ke̱ ame̱kuašoṅ le̱ fẽ aba, ni eke̱ Paulo kpleke, ši, ni eke̱le̱ yadamo̱ ame̱hĩe.

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Ši mei ni damo̱ emase̱i le̱ kē̱: Ẽ! Nyoṅmo̱ oso̱fonukpa le̱ odšé̱o̱ ne̱?

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Ši beni ewie ne̱ke̱ le̱, béi ba Farisifoi le̱ ke̱ Sadukifoi le̱ ateṅ, ni asafo le̱ mli gba enyo̱.

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ši benĩ béi le̱ mli wa le̱, asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ še gbeyei ake̱ ekole̱ ame̱atše̱re̱ Paulo mli hewo̱ le̱, efã́ asrafoi le̱ ake̱ ame̱kpleke ši ní ame̱yašõle̱ ye̱ ame̱deṅ, ní ame̱ke̱le̱ aba mō̃ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Ši eno̱ nyōṅ le̱ Nuṅtšo̱ lo̱ badamo̱ emase̱i ni ekē̱: Paulo, *hã otšui anyõ omli, edšake̱ bo̱ni oye mihe odase ye̱ Ierusalem ne̱, dša oyaye odase nakai noṅṅ ye̱ †Roma hũ. *

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Ši Paulo nyemiyō bi ko nu ame̱káwō ne̱ he, ni eyiṅ ke̱-te mō̃ le̱ṅ eyatſa Paulo adafi.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo tšé̱ asafoatše̱mei le̱ ateṅ mokome ke̱-ba eṅõ, ni ekē̱: Ṅõ ne̱ke̱ oblanyo ne̱ ní oke̱le̱ aya asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱ ṅõ, edšake̱ eye̱ sane ko ní eyagbale̱.

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Ni asafoĩatše̱nukpa le̱ mõ enine mli, ni eke̱le̱ te afã, ni eyabile̱ ake̱: Mẽ sane oyo̱ ní obakē̱mi?

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Ni ekē̱: Iudafoi le̱ éfe ekome ake̱ ame̱babio, ní wó̱ ní oke̱ Paulo akpleke ši ke̱-ba akuašoṅ le̱ hĩe, tamo̱ ake̱ esane le̱ mli ame̱batao fitšofitšo.

english_verse: The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have
translation_verse: Ni etšé̱ asafoatše̱mei le̱ ateṅ mei enyo̱ ke̱-ba eṅõ, ni ekē̱: Nyesāa asrafoi ohai-enyo̱ ke̱ okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei nyoṅmai-kpawo ke̱ akplo̱iatše̱mei hũ ohai-enyo̱ ni ame̱ya Kaisarea gbeke̱ ṅmle̱ ne̱hũ mli;

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Klaudio Lisia mībi amralo dšŭrõ Felike dšogbāṅ!

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Ne̱ke̱ nū ne̱, Iudafoi le̱ mõle̱ ní kũle̱ ame̱bagbele̱; ši beni *miná mile ake̱ Romanyo dšile̱ le̱, mike̱ †asrafoi le̱ te miyašõle̱. *

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní mitao male nõ sane hewo̱ ni ame̱flo̱ö̱ enà le̱, mike̱le̱ te ame̱kuašoṅ le̱ hĩe,

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: ni mina ake̱ ame̱mla le̱ he ṅwanedšē-sãdši komei ahewo̱ ame̱flo̱ö̱ ena le̱, ši sane ko ní sa gbĕle lo tšũṅwō be̱ ehe. K.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Ši beni abatſami adafi ake̱ Iudafoi le̱ ewo nū le̱ ká le̱, amrõ le̱ mitšũ ake̱ ake̱le̱ aba oṅõ, ni mifã́ *enāflo̱lo̱i le̱ hũ ake̱ ame̱ba ohĩe ni ame̱badšadše sãdši ní ame̱ke̱le̱ yo̱ le̱. Ahĩ ahãol” *

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni asrafoi le̱ ṅõ Paulo take̱ bo̱ni afã́ame̱ le̱, ni amenyie nyō le̱ṅ ame̱ke̱le̱ ba Antipatri;

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: ši dše tše̱re le̱ ame̱hã okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei le̱ ke̱le̱ te, ni ame̱ le̱ ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba mō̃ le̱ṅ ekoṅ.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱še̱ Kaisarea ni ame̱ke̱ wolo le̱ yahã amralo le̱, ame̱ke̱ Paulo hũ badamo̱ ehĩe.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Ni beni amralo le̱ kane wolo le̱, ebi ake̱, nẽ šikpoṅ no̱ edše̱, ni beni ená ele ake̱ *Kilikia edše̱ le̱, *

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ekē̱: Ké̱ onāflo̱lo̱i le̱ hũ ba le̱, no dãni maboö toi dšogbāṅ. Ni efã́ ake̱ aṅõle̱ ato Herode mō̃ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: ši beni afe ní misane se̱ akadše̱ke̱ tūtu ko hewo̱ le̱, mikpao fai ní obowo̱ toi fiō ye̱ omlihĩle̱ nā.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: efã́ *enāflo̱lo̱i le̱ ake̱ ameba oṅõ), ni ke̱dši bodientše̱ obi enā sane le̱, oona sãdši ní wo̱flo̱ö̱ enā ye̱ hewo le̱ fẽ. *

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Ni Iudafoi le̱ hũ ká mli ni ame̱mã ne̱ mĩ́ ake̱ sãdši ne̱ ye̱ mli nakai.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: edšake̱ ké̱ obu le̱ oona ake̱ gbĩĩ nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ pe̱ ne̱ ní *mibaho Ierusalem ake̱ miyadšá Nyoṅmo̱. *

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: ni asaṅ sãdši ni ame̱ke̱-ſieo̱ mino̱ ne̱, ame̱nyẽṅ nā ametšõ.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Ši noni migbaä mli faṅṅ mikē̱o̱o dši ene̱ ake̱, tšõmo̱ ní ame̱tšé̱o̱le̱ ake *amaletšõmo̱ le̱ no noṅṅ nā midšáa wo̱tše̱mei a-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ye̱, miheo̱ nibii fẽ ní aṅmã ye̱ mla le̱ ke̱ gbalo̱i le̱ amli le̱ miyeo̱, *K.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Ene̱hewo̱ mike̱ mihe efõõ ši le̱, beni afe ní maná henilē ní sõ ko wulaale̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ gbomei ahĩe ye̱ nibii fẽ mli.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ši afii pī ase̱ le̱ miba nĩ mike̱ *nikēnii abahã mimaṅ le̱ ni mašã afo̱le hũ; *Rom.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: no mli ame̱nami ake̱ mītšū mihe ye̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱, ši ame̱naami ke̱ asafo ko le̱, ame̱naami ke̱ hōfemo̱ ko.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Ši Iudafoi komei ní dše̱ Asia le̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ame̱ le̱ kũle̱ sa ake̱ ame̱ba ohĩe, ni ké̱ ame̱ye̱ mihe sane ko le̱ ni ame̱badšadše.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Alo mene̱mei dientše̱ po, ke̱ ame̱na sane ko ni edšaa ye̱ mihe heni midamo̱ akuašoṅ le̱ hĩe le̱, ame̱kē̱;

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: ake̱ dša ne̱ke̱ wiemo kome ní beni midamo̱ ame̱teṅ ní mibo ake̱: Gbohĩĩašitē hewo̱ nyekodšoomi ṅmene̱ gbĩ ne̱ le ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní Felike le ne̱ke̱ tšõmo̱ ne̱ he sane pe̱pē̱pe̱ hewo̱ le̱, etsiame̱ eto, ni ekē̱: Ke̱dši asafoiatše̱nukpa *Lisia ba le̱, makwe̱ nyesane le̱ maye. *

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Ni efã́ asafoatše̱ le̱ ake̱ eṅõ Paulo eto, ní ehã ená hedšo̱le̱, ni ké̱ ehe gbomei mībale̱ súomo̱ lo sramo̱ le̱ ekatšĩame̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Ši gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ se̱ le̱ Felike ke̱ eṅã Drusila ní dši Iudayō le̱ ba, ni eha ayatšé̱ Paulo ke̱-ba, koni ebo Kristo no̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli he sane le̱ toi.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ši beni ewieo̱ dšale̱ ke̱ heno̱kwe̱mo̱ ke̱ kodšomo̱ ní baba le̱ he le̱, Felike še gbeyei pam, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ ya fẽdã; ši ké̱ miná mihe dekã dšiṅṅ, matšé̱o ekoṅ.

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Ši asaṅ ehĩe kã ne̱ ake̱ Paulo aahãle̱ šika ní eṅmē̃ ehe, nohewo̱ hũ ní etšé̱o̱le̱ kpitiokpitio ni eke̱le̱ bagbaä sane le̱.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Ši afii enyo̱ se̱ le̱, Porkio Festo ba baye Felike nãdšiaṅ; ni ake̱-ni Felike mīsumo̱ ake̱ efe noni sa Iudafoi le̱ ahĩe hewo̱ le̱, ešĩ Paulo ye̱ tšũ le̱ṅ.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni oso̱fonukpai ke̱ Iudafoi le̱ anukpai le̱ baflo̱ Paulo nā ame̱hãle̱, ni ame̱kpale̱ fai,

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: ni ame̱bi ake̱ ekwe̱ ame̱hĩe, ní etšũ ní ayaṅõ Paulo ke̱-ba Ierusalem; edšake̱ ame̱wo ká koni ame̱gbele̱ ye̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Festo here no̱ ake̱, Paulo ahĩ tšũ le̱ṅ ye̱ Kaisarea, ši le̱dientše̱ hũ etše̱ṅ ni ebaya dše̱i.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Hewo̱ le̱ ekē̱: Nyehãa nyeteṅ hĩenāno̱bii le̱ ke̱mi ayaä dše̱i, ni ké̱ sane fõṅ ko ye̱ nū le̱ he le̱, ní ame̱kē̱.

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Ni beni eye aafe gbĩĩ kpānyo̱ lo nyoṅma ye̱ ame̱ṅõ le̱, eyiṅ ete Kaisarea, ni dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ eyatá kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ no̱, ni efã́ ake̱ ake̱ Paulo aba.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Ši beni eba dše̱i le̱, Iudafoi ní dše̱ Ierusalem ba le̱ babo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱ke̱ nāflo̱mo̱i pī ní wa baſie Paulo no̱, ši ame̱nyãẽ nā ame̱tšõ;

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní Festo mīsumo̱ ake̱ efe noni sa Iudafoi le̱ ahĩe hewo̱ le̱, ekē̱ Paulo ake̱: Osumo̱ ake̱ oya Ierusalem ni miyakodšoö ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ ahewo̱ lo?

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Ši Paulo kē̱: Kaisare kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ hīe midamo̱ ne̱, heni sa ake̱ akodšoo̱mi ye̱ le̱; Iudafoi le̱, rnitõko ame̱no̱, tamo̱ bo̱ni ole dšogbāṅ le̱.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, ké̱ miye sane fõṅ ko ni mife noko ní sa gbĕle le̱, mikãmãã gbĕle; ši ké̱ Sãdši ní mene̱mei flo̱ö̱ minā ye̱ he ne̱ eko-eko be̱ mli le̱, moko nyẽṅ aṅõmi awo ame̱deṅ. Mike̱ misane le̱ mīhã Kaisare yeli.

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni Festo ke̱ adšinafoi le̱ hala mli, ni ekē̱ ake̱: Ni oke̱ osane le̱ ehã Kaisare yeli ne̱, Kaisare ṅõ noṅṅ oote.

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Ši gbĩ! komei ase̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ Agripa ke̱ Bernīkē ba Kaisarea ni ame̱baṅã Festo.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Ni beni ame̱ye gbĩĩ kplaṅṅ ye̱ dše̱i le̱, Festo dšadše Paulo sane le̱ etšõ maṅtše̱ le̱ ni ekē̱: Nū ko ye̱ bie̱ ní Felike *šīle̱ ye̱ tšũṅ, *

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: ni mito he mihãame̱ ake, ebe̱ Romabii amla mli ake̱ adšō̱o̱ moko no̱ ahãa gbĕle, dša moni aflo̱ enā le̱ ke̱ mei ní yaflo̱ enā le̱ ékpe hĩe ke̱ hĩe, ni mo le̱ ená hegbe̱ edšie anā ye̱ sane ní aṅõ-fõ eno̱ le̱ hewo̱ dã.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: ši moṅ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nyoṅmo̱dšámo̱ he ṅwanedšesãdši komei ke̱ Iesu ko ní egbo ní Paulo mã no̱ mĩ́ ake̱ ehĩe kã le̱ he sãdši ame̱hĩe ke̱-ba.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní milee bo̱ni mafe matao ne̱ke̱ sãdši ne̱ amli hewo̱ le̱, mibile̱ ake̱ ēsumo̱ ake̱ eya Ierusalem ní ayaye ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ ye̱ dše̱i lo?

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní Paulo édšō̱ ake̱ ake̱ esane le̱ ato ni Kaisare dientše̱ ayaye hewo̱ le̱, mifã́ ake̱ aṅõle̱ ato ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní mahã ake̱le̱ aya Kaisare ṅõ.

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ dšetše̱reno̱ le̱, beni Agripa ke̱ Bernīkē wula kiṅkā̃ ke̱-ba ni ame̱ke̱ asafoiatše̱mei-nukpai ke̱ mã le̱ṅ gbomei agboi le̱ babote sane-toibōhe le̱, Festo fã́ ní ake̱ Paulo ba.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni Festo kē̱: Maṅtše̱ Agripa, ke̱ nye mei fẽ ní nyeke̱wo̱ yo̱ bie̱, nyemīna nū ne̱ ní Iudafoi asafo mū le̱ fẽ bakpami fai ye̱ Ierusalem ke̱ bie̱ fẽ ni ame̱blo̱ ame̱womi, ake̱ esaa ake̱ ehĩo̱ dšeṅ doṅṅ le̱. K.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱, mina ake̱ efeko noko ní sa gbĕle, ni ake̱-ní le̱dientše̱ hũ etu esane le̱ ewo Kaisare deṅ hewo̱ le̱, mikpe̱ mli ake̱ ake̱le̱ ayahãle̱.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Ši mibe̱ sane kre̱dē̱ ko ní kũle̱ maṅmã mahã nuṅtšo̱ le̱, nohewo̱ hũ ni mike̱le̱ ba nyehĩe ne̱, ni titri le̱ bo maṅtše̱ Agripa ohĩe, beni afe ní ke̱dši atao sane le̱ mli le̱, maná noko maṅmã.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ši efeemi ake̱ edšaa ake̱ aṅõo̱ gbokle̱fonyo ko amãdšeo̱ ni atšõõ noni akē̱ efe.

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: Maṅtše̱ Agripa, eṅõ minā ake̱ mibadšie minā ṅme̱ne̱ ye̱ ohĩe, ye̱ nibii fẽ ní Iudafoi le̱ flo̱ö̱ minā ye̱ he le̱ hewo̱,

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱, ši ní Nyoṅmo̱ ewo wo̱tše̱mei le̱ no̱hĩekãmo̱ le̱ hewo̱ midamo̱ bie̱ ni akodšoo̱mi ne̱,

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: no no̱ wo̱kutšei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱ hĩe kã hewo̱ ní ame̱hĩe nyōṅ ke̱ ſane dšámo̱ ní nā wa le̱ mli, beni afe ní ame̱nine aše̱ no̱; maṅtše̱ Agripa, ne̱ke̱ hĩeno̱kãmo̱ ne̱ hewo̱ Iudafoi le̱ flo̱ö̱ minā ne̱.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Mẽba mo̱ ni nyebuo̱ ake̱ ebe̱ mli ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ tēo̱ gbohĩĩ aši le̱? (

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: Ši midientše̱ hũ efemi ake̱ esa ake̱ mafe nii pī maṅõ-kũ Iesu, Nazarenyo le̱, gbe̱i le̱ nā;

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: ni miná mife nakai hũ ye̱ Ierusalem, ni ake̱-ní miná hegbe̱ ye̱ oso̱fonukpai le̱ adeṅ le̱, miwo meikroṅkroṅi le̱ ateṅ mei pī tšũṅ, ni ké̱ abagbeame̱ le̱, minā ye̱ mli eko,

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: Ene̱ no̱ noṅṅ minyie ni mifã gbe̱ ke̱-mīya Damasko ye̱ oso̱fonukpai le̱ ahewale̱ ke̱ gbe̱ṅmē̃ nā,

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: ni ſane fintī̃, beni minyie gbe̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, maṅtše̱, mina la ko ní kpe̱o̱ fè hũlũ dše̱ ṅwei babo̱lemi ke̱ mei ní ke̱mi nyie le̱.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱fẽ wo̱gbēgbē ši le̱, minu gbē ko ke̱mi wie ye̱ Hebri wiemo̱ le̱ mli ake̱: Saul, Saul, mẽba owaämi yi? ewa hao ake̱ oofã ntia oši koloi akplamo̱tšo le̱ nā dade le̱.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Ni madšieo ke̱-dše̱ maṅ le̱ ke̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ní mitšũo̱o ke̱-ya ame̱ṅõ ne̱ adeṅ,

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ Agripa, migboo ne̱ke̱ ṅweikpodšiemo̱ le̱ no̱ toi; Gal.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Ši Nyoṅmo̱ yeli-ke̱-buamo̱ nā mike̱damo̱ ši ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ no̱, ni miyeo̱ odase mitšõo̱ mei bibii ke̱ mei wudši ne̱, ni miwiee wiemo̱ ko ake̱ dša nii ní *gbalo̱i le̱ ke̱ Mose hũ ewie ake̱ ebaba le̱, *Luk.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: boni Kristo le̱ bana amanehũlũ, bo̱ni ebatšṍ *kleṅkleṅmo ye̱ gbohĩĩašite le̱ mli, ní ebadšadše la le̱ he sane etšõ maṅ le̱ ke̱ dšeṅmădši le̱. *

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Ni beni Paulo dšie enā ne̱ke̱ le̱, Festo ke̱ gbē wale̱ kē̱: Paulo, se̱ke̱ oyeo̱ ne̱! woloṅkasemo̱ so̱ṅṅ ehã oyeo̱ se̱ke̱ ne̱.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: edšake̱ maṅtše̱ le̱ ní miwieo̱ ekã nā mitsõo̱le̱ ne̱ le sãdši ne̱ amli; ni mikpaa ši ake̱ nibii ne̱ eko ye̱ ni ake̱tēle̱; edšake̱ dšee *nifĩfĩaṅ heko afe ene̱ ye̱. *Ioh.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Nto oheo̱ gbalo̱i le̱ oyeo̱, maṅtše̱ Agripa? Mile ake̱ oheo̱ oyeo̱.

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Ši Agripa kē̱ Paulo ake̱: ſe̱ fiō ní ohã miyĩṅ atšṍ ni matšṍ Kristofonyo.

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Ši Paulo kē̱: Miná ní kũle̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hã ba mli ake̱, ſe̱ fio dšio, ſe̱ pī dšio, dšee bo okome ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ mei fẽ ní boo̱mi toi ṅme̱ne̱ ne̱ hũ atšṍ tamo̱mi, ši gbokle̱i ne̱ eko ke̱ke̱ ni akawoame̱.

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Ni beni ewie ne̱ke̱ le̱, maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ amralo le̱ ke̱ Bernīkē ke̱ mei ní ke̱ame̱ trá ši le̱ te ši,

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: ni ame̱te afã ni ame̱yawie ye̱ ame̱teṅ ake̱: Nū ne̱ efeko noko ní sa gbĕle lo tšũṅwō.

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ni Agripa kē̱ Festo ake̱: Edši nū ne̱ *eṅõko esane le̱ ehãko Kaisare yeli kũle̱, aanyẽ ehe aṅmē̃. *

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱fo Kilikia ke̱ Pamfilia ṅšo̱ le̱ṅ le̱, wo̱badamo̱ Mira ye̱ Likia.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩĩ pī wo̱nyie ble̱ō ni ekpakpa wo̱fe fẽdã ni wo̱še̱ Knido ṅe̱le̱no̱, ni ake̱-ní kō̱yo̱ le̱ eṅmẽẽwo̱ gbe̱ hewo̱ le̱, wo̱šrã Kreta meo le̱ ke̱-ba Salmone;

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: ni ekpakpa wo̱sā wo̱fe fẽdã ni wo̱foṅ ye̱ dše̱i ke̱-ba heko ní atšē̱o̱ dše̱i ake̱ Le̱dšiatōhe-fe̱fe̱o ni be̱ṅke̱ Lasea maṅ le̱.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱ beni be pī éfite ni *ṅšo̱-hĩe-nyiemo̱ le̱ hũ efe ahuntō, edšake̱ †buadayelibe le̱ eho momo hewo̱ le̱, Paulo woame̱ ṅā *

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní le̱dšiatōhe le̱ kãã ši dšogbāṅ bo̱ni aanyẽ aye fẽibe le̱ ye̱ dše̱i hewo̱ le̱, ame̱teṅ mei pī wo ṅā ake̱ afã ye̱ dše̱i akwe̱ ake̱ aanyẽ aše̱ Foinīke ní dši Kreta le̱dšiatōhe ni kã wuoyi-anai ke̱ kōyi-anai teṅ le̱ lo, koni aye fẽibe le̱ ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Ši beni wuoyigbe̱ kō̱yo̱ bõi tſā nyãrãkē le̱, efeame̱ ake̱ noni ame̱taoo̱ le̱ eba mli, ni ame̱fã ke̱-šrã Kreta he kpakpa.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Ši etše̱e̱ ke̱ke̱ le̱ ahum ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ kōyi-bokã kō̱yo̱ le̱ fã bakpēame̱.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Ši beni eta le̱le̱ le̱ mli ni enyẽẽ kō̱yo̱ le̱ ekpē le̱, wo̱hã ekpla.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱sa foi ke̱-šrã ṅšo̱kpo̱ fiō ko ni atšé̱o̱le̱ Klaudia le̱ meo le̱, ekpakpa wo̱fe fẽdã ni wo̱nyẽ bonto le̱ wo̱mõ,

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: ni beni ame̱wó le̱, ame̱ke̱ yeli-ke̱-buamo̱nibii fĩmo̱ le̱le̱ le̱, ni ake̱-ní ame̱mīše gbeyei ake̱ aleenõ ame̱agbē šia futufutu le̱ mli hewo̱ le̱, ame̱kpa abalā le̱, ni ame̱kpla ke̱ke̱.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Ni ake̱-ni ahum le̱ tſaäwo̱ basabasa naakpa hewo̱ le̱, dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ ame̱fã le̱le̱ le̱ mli nii le̱ eko ame̱ſie.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Ni gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ wo̱ke̱ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱nidši dšie le̱le̱ he nibii le̱ wo̱ſie.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ni wo̱naa hũlũ lo ṅulamii gbĩĩ pī ni asaṅ ahum ní tſaä kpeo̱wo̱ le̱ nā wa naakpa hewo̱ le̱, agbe̱ne̱ wo̱hĩe kãã wala no̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Ši beni awoo niyeli āhũ le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni Paulo te ši edamo̱ ame̱teṅ ni ekē̱: Atāmei, kũle̱ esa ake̱ nyeboo̱mi toi ní akafã ye̱ Kreta ni abaná ne̱ke̱ amanehũlũ ke̱ nilādšemo̱ ne̱.

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: ni ekē̱: *Kăše gbeyei, Paulo! dša ake̱o yadamo̱ Kaisare hĩe kẽ; ni na, Nyoṅmo̱ éṅõ mei fẽ ni ke̱o nyie le̱le̱ le̱ mli le̱ ekeo. *

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Ši befẽbe ní fe le̱ wo̱o̱yaša ṅšo̱kpo̱ ko no̱ kẽ.

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱flo̱ se̱ke̱i le̱ ame̱wo ṅšo̱ṅ, ni ame̱fẽne kudō̱ le̱ he kpãi le̱ hũ, ni ame̱ši teṅabalā le̱ ke̱-kpe kō̱yo̱ ní tſaä le̱, ni ame̱tšṍ eyi ame̱hã ṅso̱nāgbe̱.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱še gbeyei ake̱ aleenõ wo̱o̱yagbē te̱sāi ano̱, ni ame̱ṅmẽ se̱ke̱i edſe̱ ye̱ le̱le̱ le̱ se̱gbe̱, ame̱ke̱-mīmẽ dšetše̱remo̱.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: ní Paulo kē̱ asafoatše̱ le̱ ke̱ asrafoi le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši mene̱mei ehĩĩ le̱le̱ le̱ mli le̱, no le̱ nyeyi náṅ wala.

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni asrafoi le̱ flo̱ bonto le̱ be taṅkpēi le̱, ni ame̱hã eyagbē ši.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Nohewo le̱ mīkpanye fai ní nyéye nii; edšake̱ no aahã nyeyi aná wala, edšake̱ nyeteṅ moko *yitšo̱i kome edšeṅ eyiteṅ enyõṅ ši. *Mat.

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Ni beni ekē̱ nakai le̱, eko̱ abolo, ni *eda Nyoṅmo̱ ši ye̱ ame̱fẽ ame̱hĩe, ni ekũmo̱ mli ebõi yeli. *Ioh.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱fẽ ame̱ná tšui, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱ye nii.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Ši beni ame̱ye nii ni ame̱tŏ̱ro̱ le̱, ame̱še̱re̱ able ní ame̱wo le̱ ame̱ſie ṅšo̱ṅ, ni ame̱hã le̱le̱ le̱ fe fle̱fle̱.

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Ni beni dše tše̱re le̱, ame̱lee šikpoṅ le̱, ši ame̱na ble ko ke̱ enā šia, ni ame̱to ame̱yiṅ ake̱, ké̱ ame̱anyẽ le̱, ame̱ahã le̱le̱ le̱ ayaša ši ye̱ dše̱i.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní ame̱yagbe ṅšo̱i enyo̱ le̱ akpẽhe hewo le̱, ame̱ke̱ le̱le̱ le̱ yaša ši; ni eyitšogbe̱ le̱ yatše̱ke̱ ši šiṅṅ, ši ese̱gbe̱ le̱, ṅšo̱kei le̱ anāwale̱ le̱ dſărale̱.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Ši asrafoi le̱ ayiṅtō dši ake̱ ame̱agbe gbokle̱foi le̱, koni ame̱teṅ moko akasĕre ke̱-mīya ní edšo foi.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní asafoatše̱ le̱ taoo̱ Paulo yiwala ehere hewo̱ le̱ etšĩ ame̱yiṅtō le̱ nā, ni efã́ ake̱ mei ní le sẽremo̱ le̱ tšutšu atũ agbē ṅšo̱ le̱ṅ, ni ame̱ya šikpoṅ;

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: ši mei ni eſe̱ le̱ ateṅ meikomei abumo̱ ṅmoṅmodsi ano̱, ni meikomei hũ abumo̱ le̱le̱ koi le̱ ano̱. Ni bo̱ni fe ní *ame̱fẽ ame̱še̱ šikpoṅ ſeſēſe dši no. *K.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Ši heni dše̱ihii dšekõdši le̱ na kolo le̱ kpe̱te̱ enine he le̱, ame̱kē̱kē̱ ame̱he ake̱: Befẽbe ní fe le̱, ne̱ke̱ nū ne̱ awuyelo̱ ni, ni ahere eyiwala ke̱-dše̱ ṅšo̱ le̱ṅ moṅ, ši oweletō̱ eṅmẽẽle̱ gbe̱ ni eyi aná wala.

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Ni ehwãnyã kolo le̱ ewo la le̱ mli, ni eyeele̱ awui ko. Mar.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱ atridī ke̱ fo̱-ke̱-lá emõ Publio tše̱ ke̱-kã ši; ni Paulo te eṅõ, ni eso̱le eṅõ enidši eſie eno̱ ni etšále̱.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱yadamo̱ Sirakusa le̱, wo̱hĩ dše̱i gbĩĩ etẽ.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Ni beni nyemimei ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ nu wo̱he le̱, ame̱bakpēwo̱ ye̱ Apiiforo ke̱ Tretaberna; ni beni Paulo naame̱ le̱, eda Nyoṅmo̱ ši ni ená tšui.

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Ni beni wo̱baše̱ Roma le̱, asafoatše̱ le̱ dšie gbokle̱foi le̱ ehã asafoiatše̱nukpa le̱, ši Paulo le̱, aṅmẽle̱ gbe̱ ake̱ ehĩ heni esumoo̱, ši asrafonyo ko buo̱ ehe.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Ši eba mli ake̱ gbĩĩ etẽ se̱ le̱ Paulo ha atšé̱ Iudafoi le̱ anukpai ní yo̱ le̱ ke̱-bakpe; ni beni ame̱nā ebakpe ši le̱, ekē̱-ame̱ ake̱: Atāmei ke̱ anyemĩmei, mitõko maṅ le̱ lo wo̱tše̱mei le̱ agbe̱nānii le̱ ano̱, kẽle̱ aṅõmi awo Romabii le̱ adeṅ ye̱ Ierusalem ake̱ gbokle̱fonyo.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Ni ame̱ le̱, beni ame̱tao misane le̱ mli le̱, ame̱sumo̱ ake̱ ame̱ṅmē̃ mihe, edšake̱ gbĕle sane ko be̱ mihe kwrā.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Ši ake̱-ní Iudafoi le̱ ekplẽẽ hewo̱ le̱, efĩmi ake̱ maṅõ misane le̱ *mahã Kaisare yeli, ši dšee ake̱ miye̱ noko ní mike̱-baflo̱ mimaṅ le̱ nā. *

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ hewo̱ mĩtšé̱nye ke̱-ba, koni mananye ní mike̱nye awie; edšake̱ Israel *hĩeno̱kãmo̱ le̱ hewo̱ ni awomi ne̱ke̱ kõsõṅkõsõ ne̱. *

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Ši ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱ le̱ wo̱náko wodši komei ke̱-dše̱ko Iudea ye̱ ohewo̱, ni asaṅ nyemimei le̱ ateṅ moko bako bie̱ ebagbako ohe sane ko lo ohe wiemo̱ fõṅ ko.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Ši wo̱mīsumo̱ ake̱ wo̱o̱bo odſẽṅmo̱ le̱ toi; edšake̱ ne̱ke̱ *kufà ne̱ wo̱le ake̱ †awieo̱ he efõṅ ye̱ hefẽhe. *

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Ni meikomei hé wiemo̱i ní ewie le̱ ame̱ye, ši meikomei hũ hee yee.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ni ake̱-ní ame̱yakpãã gbē hewo̱ le̱, ame̱yĩṅ ame̱te, beni Paulo wie wiemo̱ kome ne̱: Odšogbāṅ ní Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱ wie ye̱ gbalo̱ Iesaia le̱ nā etšõ wo̱tše̱mei le̱,

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: *ake̱: “Ya maṅ ne̱ ṅõ ni oyakē̱: Nu le̱ nyebanu ne̱, šĩ nyenaṅ šĩši, ni na le̱ nyebana ne̱, ši nyeyoṅ se̱. *Ies.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Edšake̱ maṅ ne̱ tšui ekplim, ni ame̱toii ewa ke̱ ninumo̱, ni ame̱mĩamĩa ame̱hĩṅme̱ii, koni ame̱kana ke̱ ame̱hīṅme̱ii ni ame̱kanu ke̱ ame̱toii, ni ame̱tšui hũ akana šĩši, ní ame̱kpale ní mitšáame̱.”

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Ni beni ewie wiemo̱ ne̱, Iudafoi le̱ yiṅ ame̱te, ni ame̱dšedšē ṅwane babaō ye̱ ame̱teṅ.

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Ni Paulo hĩ šĩa ní aṅō-mãle̱ le̱ mli afii nakplo̱i enyo̱, ni ehereo̱ mei fẽ ní baã eṅõ le̱,

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: ni ešĩe̱o̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ he sane le̱, ni eke̱ ekã fẽ dšadšeo̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo be sădši le̱ etšõame̱, ni mokomoko etšũle̱ gbe̱. *K.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: ke̱-yahä mei ní Nyoṅmo̱ sumoo̱ nī dši *meikroṅkroṅi ní atšé̱ame̱ ni yo̱ Roma le̱ fẽ: †dromo̱ ke̱ hedšo̱le̱ ní dše̱ wo̱tše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo le̱ deṅ ahãnye! *

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: no dši ake̱, aše̱dše mike̱nye fẽ mī ye̱ nyeteṅ, ye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli ní yo̱ mike̱nye fẽ mli le̱ṅ.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: edšake̱ ame̱le Nyoṅmo̱ moṅ, ši ame̱woo ehĩe nyam ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱, ni ame̱daale̱ ši hũ, ši ame̱fe ſe̱m ye̱ ame̱dſẽṅmo̱i amli, ni *ame̱tšui ní ko̱o̱ sane se̱ le̱ wo duṅ. *Ef.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: ni Nyoṅmo̱ ní fitee le̱ anumnyam le̱ ame̱tšake ame̱hã gbomo ní fiteo̱ le̱ subāṅ heno̱ ko ke̱ lofõdši ke̱ koloi nādšiedſe̱dſe̱tše̱mei ke̱ wãmo̱nibii anõ.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ hũ ni Nyoṅmo̱ ṅmē̃ ame̱he ehā ame̱tšuiiaṅ ako̱no̱i ní yo̱ tãṅ le̱, beni afe ni amegbe ame̱dientše̱ ame̱gbomotšei le̱ ahe guo̱ ye̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱he, Bo̱f.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: mei ní ṅõo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ano̱kwale le̱ ame̱tšakeo̱ amale, ni ame̱dšáa ni ame̱súmoo̱ bo̱nõ le̱ fè bo̱lo̱ le̱, ní adšō̱o̱le̱ ke̱-yaši nāno̱ le̱. Amen.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Ene̱ hewo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅmẽ ame̱he ehā hĩegbedšianii ahe hĩedō̱i, le̱; edšake̱ noni ato ní afeo̱ le̱, ame̱yei le̱ etšake hĩe ehã noni afee le̱;

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: ni nakai noṅṅ ame̱hĩĩ le̱ hũ fõ yō he noni ato ní afeo̱ le̱, ni ame̱šãa ye̱ ame̱ko̱no̱ fõṅ lè̱ mli ke̱-nyieo̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱he se̱, ni hĩĩ ke̱ hĩĩ tšuo̱ hĩegbedšianii, ni ame̱ná ame̱tõmo̱ le̱ he nyõmo̱wo ní sa ye̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱he.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Ni take̱ bo̱ni ame̱buu ake̱ esa ake̱ ame̱hĩeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ ame̱nilē mli le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ hũ ṅmē̃ ame̱he ehã dſẽṅmo̱ ni esaa, ní ame̱fe nibii ní esaa;

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: mei ní eyimo̱ obõbõ ke̱ nišaianii, adſamaṅbō̱, efõṅfeme̱, hĩedšōmo̱, nifõdšianii; ame̱yimo̱ to̱ ke̱ nyē̱, awuyeli, béi, šišiumo̱, dšeṅba ša;

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: mei ni be̱ yitšeiaṅ, kpãṅmo̱-mli-kũlo̱i, mei ní edo̱o̱ mo he, kũtũmpo̱foi, yiwalo̱i;

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: mei ni le Nyoṅmo̱ dšale̱nii le̱ kre̱dē̱, ake̱ mei ní tšuo̱ nakai nii le̱ sa gbĕle, ní kẽle̱ dšee femo̱ ke̱ke̱ ame̱feo̱, ši moṅ ame̱náa mei ní tšuo̱ nakai nii le̱ ahe tšui hũ le̱.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mei abo̱ ní be̱ mla ní ame̱fe eša le̱, ame̱alādše hũ ní ame̱be̱ mla; ni mei abo̱ ní tšṍ mla no̱ fe eša le̱, mla noṅṅ ake̱-akodšoame̱;

english_verse: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
translation_verse: edšake̱ dšee mlanulo̱i le̱ dši dšalo̱i ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, ši mlano̱yelo̱i moṅ aabu-ame̱ ake̱ dšalo̱i. Mat.

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši bo le̱ atšé̱o̱o Iudanyo, ni ohĩe kã mla le̱ no̱, ni oſãa ofõo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ no̱,

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: ni ole esuomo̱nānii le̱, ni ole nii ní hĩ, edšake̱ adše̱ mla le̱ṅ atšõo,

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: ni obuo̱ ohe ake̱ odši ſilafoi agbe̱-tšõlo̱ ke̱ mei ní yo̱ duṅ mli le̱ ala, Mat.

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: okē̱o̱ ake̱ akabo̱ adſamaṅ, ši obo̱ö̱ adſamaṅ; ohĩo̱ wo̱dši, ši ohaä so̱lemo̱wenii;

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: bo ni oke̱ mla le̱ ſãa le̱, oke̱ mla le̱ no̱tõmo̱ le̱ gbeo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ he guo̱.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši fõlo̱ le̱ yeo̱ mla le̱ gbe̱nãi le̱ ano̱ le̱, ani abuṅ efõ le̱ ake̱ ketiafō? Gal.

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: ni fo̱mo̱ṅ fõlo̱ le̱ ní yeo̱ mla le̱ no̱ le̱ aakodšo bo ní otšṍ ṅmãle̱-okadi ke̱ ketiafō no̱ ofe ohe mlatõlo̱ le̱.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ dšee moni atšé̱o̱le̱ Iudanyo le̱ dō dši Iudanyo, ni asaṅ dšee kpono̱nõ ní yo̱ helo mli le̱ dši ketiafō; Ioh.

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: ši moṅ moni dši Iudanyo ye̱ mligbe̱ le̱ dši Iudanyo, ni tšuiṅ ketiafō ní yo̱ mumo̱ mli, ní dšee ṅmãle̱-okadi mli le̱, dši *ketiafō ní eyidšiemo̱ le̱ dše̱e̱ gbomei aṅõ, ši Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ moṅ edše̱o̱. *

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: *Gbonyobu ni agble nā dši ame̱sẽ le̱; ame̱ke̱ ame̱lile̱ii šišiuo̱ mo, †šikpãi anã ebō̱ ye̱ ame̱nãbu, *Lal.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: lōmo̱ ke̱ dšõmo̱ éyi ame̱dãṅ obõ; Lal.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyeišemo ko be̱ ame̱hĩe.” Lal.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: nohewo le̱ atšṍṅ *mla nitšumo̱ no̱ abuṅ helo ko helo ko bem ye̱ ehĩe; edšake̱ †mia no̱ atšṍo̱ aleo̱ eša. *Lal.

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: no dši Nyoṅmo̱ dšale̱ ní atšṍo̱ Iesu Kristo no̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli no̱ ake̱-hăa mei fẽ ni heo̱ yeo̱ le̱.

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ sro̱to ko be̱: edšake̱ *mei fẽ efe eša, ni Nyoṅmo̱ †anumnyam le̱ ebo̱ame̱, *K,

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: ni ake̱ edromo̱ le̱ buo̱ame̱ bem yaka ke̱-tšṍo̱ kpõmo̱ ní yo̱ Kristo Iesu mli le̱ ne̱,

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Agbe̱ne̱ nẽgbe̱ ſã le̱ yo̱? Atſa no ahã se̱. Mẽ mla ne̱ atšṍ? nitšumo̱i anõ le̱ no̱ lo? Dabi, ši hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mla le̱ no̱ moṅ atšṍ.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱buo̱ ake̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli no̱ atšṍo̱ abuo̱ gbomo bem, ši dšee mla nitšumo̱i ni. Gal.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Ši ani Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ Iudafoi ke̱ke̱ a-Nyoṅmo̱ ni? ani dšee dšeṅmădši le̱ hũ anõ ni? Hē̃, dšeṅmãdši le̱ hũ anõṅ.

english_verse: There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith.
translation_verse: Ké̱ eye̱ mli ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ kome ni, ni *hemo̱-ke̱-yeli nā ebuo̱ ketiafō bem, ni esā etšṍo̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ no̱ ebuo̱ fō bem le̱. *

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ wo̱mitšṍ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli no̱ wo̱hã mla le̱ afe yaka lo? Dabida, *ši wo̱ke̱-mĩmã mla le̱ ne̱ mĩ́ moṅ. *K.

english_verse: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
translation_verse: ni asaṅ efe ketiafolo̱i atše̱ hũ ehã *mei ní ame̱dšee ketiafolo̱i ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ ame̱ko̱ wo̱tše̱ Abraham nane ye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli ní ehe eye be mli ní edši fōlo̱ bēbe le̱, *Mat.

english_verse: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ké̱ mla šiši bii le̱ dši niyelo̱i le̱, bĕle̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ éfe yaka, ni šiwō le̱ hũ be̱ no̱ doṅṅ.

english_verse: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
translation_verse: Ši ene̱hewo̱ edše̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mli le̱, heni afe ní efe dromo̱ sane, ní šiwō le̱ amã ši šiṅṅ ahã eseši le̱ ſẽ, dšee mla šiši bii le̱ ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ mei ni dše̱ Abraham, ní dši wo̱fẽ wo̱tše̱ le̱, hemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ mli le̱ hũ;

english_verse: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
translation_verse: Ni heni kũle̱ hĩeno̱kãmo̱ ko be̱ le̱, ehĩe kã no̱ kẽ ni ehe eye, koni etšṍ dšeṅmãdši pī atše̱, take̱ bo̱ni akē̱le̱ ake̱: *“Nakai osešibii le̱ aatame̱.” *

english_verse: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
translation_verse: ni eyiṅ efeele̱ ko̱šiko̱ši ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ šiwō le̱ he tamo̱ ake̱ ehee eyee, ši moṅ ená hewale̱ ye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mli, ni ewo Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe nyam, Heb.

english_verse: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
translation_verse: ni eye̱ hewale̱ ye̱ no̱ dšogbāṅ, ake̱, noni ewo he ši le̱, eenyẽ efe hũ.

english_verse: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
translation_verse: Ši dšee le̱ ke̱ke̱ ebewo̱ aṅmã, ake̱ abu ahãle̱,

english_verse: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
translation_verse: ši moṅ wo̱ mei ní ababu ahãwo̱ le̱ hũ hewo̱, wo̱ mei ní wo̱héo̱ moni tē wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱ ne̱ wo̱yeo̱ le̱;

english_verse: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_verse: ši aṅõle̱ ahi *ye̱ wo̱tõmo̱i le̱ ahewo̱, ni atēle̱ ši ekoṅ †ye̱ wo̱-bembū hewo̱. *Ies.

english_verse: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, ní abuwo̱ bem ye̱ elá le̱ hewo̱ le̱, aatšṍ eno̱ ahere wo̱yiwala ke̱-dše̱ *mlifũ le̱ mli āhũ. *

english_verse: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ké̱ be mli ní we̱dši *henye̱lo̱i le̱ ni ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ bi le̱ gbĕle le̱ bakpãtã wo̱ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ teṅ le̱, agbene̱ ni akpãtã ne̱, aahere wo̱yiwala ye̱ ewala le̱ mli āhũ. *

english_verse: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
translation_verse: Ene̱hewo̱ le̱, take̱ bo̱ni gbomo kome no̱ eša tšṍ ke̱-ba dše le̱ṅ, ni gbĕle tšṍ eša no̱ ke̱-ba, ni no hã gbĕle le̱ tšēṅe gbomei fẽ, edšake̱ ame̱fẽ ame̱fe eša le̱: —

english_verse: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
translation_verse: edšake̱ eša ye̱ dšeṅ dãni ahã mla le̱; ši ake̱-ní *mla be̱ hewo̱ le̱, abuu eša le̱; *

english_verse: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
translation_verse: ši kẽle̱ gbĕle le̱ ye maṅtše̱ ke̱-dše̱ Adam yino̱ ke̱-baši Mose yino̱ ye̱ mei po ní efee eša ni tamo̱ *Adam ní dši moni baba le̱ he okadi le̱ no̱tõmo̱ le̱ ane̱ hũ.

english_verse: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
translation_verse: Ni bo̱ni etšṍ mokome ní fe eša le̱ no̱ ke̱-ba le̱, dšee nakai nõkēnõ le̱ yo̱: edšake̱ kodšomo̱ le̱ dše̱ mokome mli etšṍ fo̱bū; ši dromo̱ kēnõ le̱ dše̱ šigbēmo̱i pī amli etšṍ bembū.

english_verse: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ke̱ mokome šigbēmo̱ le̱ hewo̱ dše̱ ni gbĕle tšṍ nakai mokome le̱ no̱ ye maṅtše̱ le̱; bĕle̱ mei ní ená dromo̱ ke̱ dšale̱ nõkēnõ ní fá ke̱-teke no̱ le̱ aatšṍ mokome ní dši Iesu Kristo le̱ no̱ aye maṅtše̱ ye̱ wala mli āhũ.

english_verse: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, take̱ bo̱ni atšṍ mokome šigbēmo̱ no̱ abu gbomei fẽ fo̱ le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ atšṍ mokome dšale̱ no̱ abu gbomei fẽ wala bem.

english_verse: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
translation_verse: Ši *mla le̱ baho teṅ, koni šigbēmo̱ le̱ afá ke̱-teke no̱. Ši heni eša fá ye̱ le̱, dromo̱ le̱ fá ke̱-teke no̱ babaō; *

english_verse: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_verse: koni bo̱ noṅṅ ni eša le̱ ye maṅtše̱ ye̱ gbĕle mli le̱, nakai noṅṅ dromo̱ le̱ atšṍ dšale̱ no̱ aye maṅtše̱ hũ ke̱-ya nāno̱ wala mli ye̱ Iesu Kristo, wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ le̱, hewo̱.

english_verse: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ní egbo le̱, eša egbo ehã *šikome pe̱: ši ní ehīe kă ne̱, Nyoṅmo̱ ehĩe kã hã. *Heb.

english_verse: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
translation_verse: Nakai nye hũ nyebua nyehe ake̱ mei ní egboi ehã eša, ni ame̱hĩe kãmo̱ hã Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ Iesu Kristo, wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ le̱, mli.

english_verse: Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law. Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
translation_verse: Edšake̱ eša náṅ nyeno̱ hewale̱, edšake̱ dšee mla šiši nyeyo̱, ši moṅ dromo̱ šiši nyeyo̱.

english_verse: Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him.
translation_verse: Ani nyelee ake̱, moni nyeṅõo̱ nyehe nyefeo̱ tšũdši nyehãa ní nyeboo̱le̱ toi le̱, le̱ noṅṅ etšũdši dšinye ni nyeboo̱le̱ toi, eša nõ ní ke̱ mo yaä gbĕle mli le̱ dsio, alo toibō ni ke̱ mo yaä dšale̱ mli le̱ dsio? Ioh

english_verse: You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received.
translation_verse: Ši šidã ahã Nyoṅmo̱, ake̱ kũle̱ sa le̱ eša tšũdši dšinye, ši agbe̱ne̱ nyedše̱ nyetšuii fiā mli nyebo ne̱ke̱ tšõmo̱ ní aṅõnye awo mli le̱ toi.

english_verse: Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
translation_verse: Ši noni akpõnye ye̱ eša deṅ ni nyeye nyehe le̱, nyetšṍme̱ dšale̱ tšũdši. Ioh.

english_verse: I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
translation_verse: Bo̱ni gbomo wieo̱ miwieo̱ ne̱ ye̱ nyehelo gbedemo̱ hewo̱: edšake̱ take̱ bo̱ni nyeṅõ nyehenii le̱ nyefe nyãṅemo̱nii ke̱ mlatõmo̱ tšũdši ke̱-te mlatõmo̱ mli le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ agbe̱ne̱ nyeke̱ nyehenii le̱ afea dšale̱ tšũdši ke̱-yaä kroṅkroṅ-femo̱ mli.

english_verse: When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ beni nyedši eša tšũdši le̱, nyeye nyehe ke̱-dše̱ dšale̱ le̱ deṅ.

english_verse: But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ mẽ yibii nyewo ye̱ nakai be le̱ mli? Yibii ní *nyehĩe egboi ye̱ he agbe̱ne̱; edšake̱ nomei anāgbē dši †gbĕle. *Ezek.

english_verse: Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life.
translation_verse: Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱, ni akpõnye ye̱ eša deṅ ni nyetšṍmo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ tšũdši ne̱, nyewoo̱ nyeyibii nyehãa kroṅkroṅfemo̱, ni *enũgbē dši nāno̱ wala. *

english_verse: Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ eša deṅ nyōmo̱wo le̱ gbĕle ni; ši Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱-kēnõ le̱ nāno̱ walaṅ ye̱ Kristo Iesu, wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ le̱, mli.

english_verse: That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God.
translation_verse: Minyemimei, nakai noṅṅ nye hũ, ake̱ Kristo gbomotšo le̱ *egbenye ehā mla le̱, koni nyetšṍmo̱ mokroko, ní dši moni atēle̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱ nii, koni wo̱wo yibii wo̱hã Nyoṅmo̱. *Kol.

english_verse: Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ té wo̱o̱kē̱ tēṅ? Aso mla le̱ ešaṅ? Dabida! Ši moṅ, dšee mla le̱ he-wo̱ṅ kũle̱ milee eša; edšake̱ kũle̱ milee noni dši hĩekō̃, kē̱ dšee *mla le̱ kē̱ ake̱: “Ohĩe akakõ nii ano̱.” *

english_verse: Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life,
translation_verse: Ši mi le̱ mihĩ ši pēṅ ni mibe̱ mla ši beni kitã le̱ ba le̱, eša le̱ hĩe tšẽ ekoṅ;

english_verse: and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death.
translation_verse: ši mi le̱ *migbo, ni ana ake̱ kitã le̱ ni aṅõ-hãmi ye̱ †wala hewo̱ le̱, no noṅṅ etšé̱ gbĕle ehãmi. *Iak.

english_verse: Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ eša le̱, noni etšṍ kită le̱ no̱ ená hegbe̱ le̱, *ešišiumi ni eke̱ no noṅṅ gbemi. *Heb.

english_verse: We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱le ake̱ mla le̱ mumo̱ṅ nõ ni; ši mi le̱ *helo gbomo dšimi, ni ahõmi awo eša le̱ šiši. *K.

english_verse: Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ noni misumo̱o̱ le̱ noṅṅ mifeo̱ le̱, mikplẽo̱ ake̱ *mla le̱ hĩ. *K.

english_verse: I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mile ake̱ mimli, no dši mihelo le̱ mli le̱, *noko kpakpa ko be̱ dše̱i; edšake̱ suomo̱ le̱ miye̱ eko moṅ, ši ekpakpafemo̱ ni ebo̱mi. *

english_verse: Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ ekpakpa ní misumoo̱ le̱ mifee; ši efõṅ ní misumo̱o̱ le̱, no moṅ mifeo̱.

english_verse: And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ noni misumo̱o̱ le̱ kẽ mifeo̱ le̱, bĕle̱ dšee mi mitšuo̱ no doṅṅ, ši moṅ eša ní yo̱ mimli le̱ tšuo̱.

english_verse: The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right.
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ minaä mla ne̱ ake̱ mi ní misumoo̱ ake̱ mafe noni hĩ le̱, efõṅ moṅ kpe̱te̱ mihe.

english_verse: With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mimligbe̱ gbomo le̱ mĩ še̱o̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mla le̱ he;

english_verse: But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do.
translation_verse: ši minaä mla kroko ye̱ mihenii le̱ amli ni ke̱ midſẽṅmo̱ mla le̱ wuo̱ ta ni eṅõo̱mi nom ehãa eša mla le̱ ni yo̱ mihenii le̱ amli le̱. Gal.

english_verse: What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die?
translation_verse: Gbomo ní nii yo̱ mo̱be̱ dšimi; namo aadšiemi ke̱-adše̱ ne̱ke̱ gbĕle gbomotšo ne̱ deṅ?

english_verse: Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me. So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
translation_verse: Mītšṍ wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo no̱ *mīda Nyoṅmo̱ ši. Bĕle̱ agbe̱ne̱ mi noṅṅ mike̱ midſēṅmo̱ súmoo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mla le̱ moṅ, ši mike̱ mihelo súmoo̱ eša mla. *

english_verse: You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him.
translation_verse: Ši ke̱dši eye̱ mli ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ hĩo̱ nyemli le̱, no le̱ nyebe̱ helo le̱ šĩšì, ši moṅ mumo̱ le̱ šiši nyeyo̱. Ši ké̱ moko be̱ Kristo Mumo̱ le̱, bĕle̱ le̱ le̱ dšee enõ dšile̱.

english_verse: But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ Kristo ye̱ nyemli le̱, no le̱ gbomotšo le̱ egbo ye̱ eša hewo̱; ši mumo̱ le̱, wala ni, ye̱ dšale̱ hewo̱.

english_verse: My dear friends, we must not live to satisfy our desires.
translation_verse: Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, anyemimei, nyōdšiatše̱mei dšiwo̱, ši dšee helo le̱ nyõmo̱ wo̱hĩe ní wo̱o̱hĩ ši ye̱ helo nā.

english_verse: Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mei abo̱ ní Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ le̱ kplaäame̱ le̱, ame̱ ame̱dši Nyoṅmo̱ bii.

english_verse: God's Spirit doesn't make us slaves who are afraid of him. Instead, we become his children and call him our Father.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ dšee nyṍṅyeli mumo̱ nyená ní nyesā nyeaše gbeyei, ši moṅ nyená biiatšṍmo̱ mumo̱, mo mli ní wo̱blo̱ö̱ ye̱ ake̱: Aba, atā! le̱.

english_verse: Meanwhile, creation is confused, but not because it wants to be confused. God made it this way in the hope
translation_verse: Edšake̱ aṅõ bō̱nii le̱ awo yakayakanii ašiši, dšee ame̱dientše̱ ame̱suomo̱ nā, ši moṅ ye̱ moni baame̱ ši le̱ hewo̱, ye̱ no̱hĩekãmo̱ mli; Dsads.

english_verse: that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children.
translation_verse: ake̱ bō̱nii le̱ dientše̱ hũ baye ame̱he ke̱-dše̱ fitemo̱ nyõṅyeli le̱ mli ke̱-ya Nyoṅmo̱ bii le̱ anumnyam heyeli le̱ mli.

english_verse: We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ wo̱le ake̱ bō̱nii le̱ fẽ ke̱wo̱ do̱moo̱ ntšo̱ĩ ni ame̱ke̱wo̱ kõmoo̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱ṅme̱ne̱.

english_verse: And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ no̱hĩekãmo̱ nā ahere wo̱yiwala ye̱. Ši no̱hĩekãmo̱ ní anaä le̱, edšee no̱hĩekãmo̱: ši namo hĩe kãa noni enaä le̱ no̱?

english_verse: However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
translation_verse: Ši ké̱ noni wo̱naa le̱ no̱ wo̱hĩe kã le̱, bĕle̱ wo̱ke̱ tšuišiṅmē̃ kwe̱o̱le̱ gbe̱.

english_verse: In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words.
translation_verse: Ši nakai noṅṅ kẽ Mumo̱ le̱ hũ yeo̱ bua wo̱gbedemo̱i le̱; edšake̱ noni wo̱o̱so̱le wo̱bi ní dša le̱ wo̱lee; ši moṅ Mumo̱ le̱ dientše̱ ke̱ ntšo̱idõmo̱i ni anyẽṅ akē̱ le̱ damoo̱ mli hāawo̱.

english_verse: All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people.
translation_verse: Ši moni taoo tšuii amli le̱ le noni dši Mumo̱ le̱ dſẽṅmo̱ le̱, edšake̱ edamoo̱ mli ehãa meikroṅkroṅi le̱ bo̱ni sa Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe.

english_verse: We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose,
translation_verse: Ši wo̱le ake, mei ní sumoo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, nibii fiā yeo̱ buaäame̱ ní ahĩ ahãame̱, ame̱ mei ní atšé̱ame̱ ye̱ *yiṅtō nā le̱. *Ef.

english_verse: and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children.
translation_verse: Edšake̱ mei ní eleame̱ momo le̱, ame̱ edšie eto ní ame̱subãṅ atamo̱ ebi le̱ nõ le̱, koni efe nyemimei pī ateṅ *kromo̱bi; *Kol.

english_verse: God then accepted the people he had already decided to choose, and he has shared his glory with them. God's Love
translation_verse: ši mei ní edšie eto le̱, ame̱ noṅṅ etšé̱; ni mei ní etšé̱ le̱, ame̱ noṅṅ ebuame̱ bem; ni mei ní ebuame̱ bem le̱, ame̱ noṅṅ ame̱hĩe nyam ewo.

english_verse: What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us?
translation_verse: Bĕle̱ té wo̱o̱kē̱ tēṅ ye̱ nii ne̱ ahewo̱ṅ? Ké̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ wo̱se̱ le̱, namo aate ši awowo̱? Lal.

english_verse: God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else?
translation_verse: Mo noṅṅ ni kāmããwo̱ *le̱dientše̱ ebi le̱, ši moṅ eṅõle̱ ehā ye̱ wo̱fẽ wo̱nādšiaṅ le̱; ani eṅõṅ nibii fiã efataṅ ehe ekeṅwo̱? *Ioh.
