translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kã mi kitã yɛ nɔ dã!” Hewɔ lɛ Esau kã lɛ kitã ni ehɔ̃ɔ ekromɔbi gbɛnaa lɛ ehã Yakob.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob hã Esau aboloo kɛ abɔbɔi ni ehoo lɛ eko. Esau ye, ni enu nɔ ko eshwie nɔ; kɛkɛ ni ete shi, ni eyiŋ etee. Bɔ ni fee ni Esau ŋmɛɛ ekromɔbi gbɛnaa ni ebuuu lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Hɔmɔ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; soro klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ ni ba yɛ Abraham yinɔ lɛ. Isak yiŋ etee Filistibii amaŋtsɛ Abimelek ŋɔɔ yɛ Gerar.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Isak ni ekɛɛ: “Kaaya Ijipt; shi hii shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni matsɔ̃ɔ bo lɛ nɔ;

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: too gbɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ; ni mikɛ bo aaahi shi, ni majɔɔ bo, ejaakɛ bo kɛ oshwiei mikɛ nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ baahã,

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: ni maye kitã ni mikã otsɛ Abraham lɛ nɔ. Mibahã oshwiei afa tamɔ bɔ ni mikã otsɛ Abraham kitã lɛ. Mibahã oshwiei afa tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋulamii, ni mibaŋɔ nɛkɛ shikpɔji nɛɛ fɛɛ mahã oshwiei lɛ. Oshwiei lɛ mli aaajɛ ajɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jeŋ maji lɛ fɛɛ,

english_verse: because Abraham did everything I told him to do.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Abraham bo migbee toi, ni eye mimlai kɛ mikitãi lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Isak hi shi yɛ Gerar.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Ni be ni jɛibii lɛ bi eŋa lɛ he sane lɛ, eto he akɛ, “Minyɛmi yoo ni”. Ejaakɛ eeshe gbeyei ni ekɛɛɛ akɛ: “Miŋa ni.” Ni ekɛɛ hu yɛ eyiŋ akɛ, “Bɔ ni afee ni jɛibii lɛ akabagbe mi yɛ Rebeka hewɔ; ejaakɛ Rebeka he yɛ fɛo.”

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Isak ehi jɛi be kplaŋŋ lɛ, Filistibii amaŋtsɛ Abimelek bu samflɛ naa, ni ena ni Isak kɛ eŋa Rebeka miishwɛ.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abimelek tsɛ Isak ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Eei, asomoaŋ, yoo lɛ oŋa ni! Te fee tɛŋŋ ni okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Minyɛmi yoo ji lɛ lɛ?’ ” Ni Isak kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni afee ni akagbe mi yɛ ehewɔ, no hã mikɛɛ nakai lɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek kɛɛ, “Mɛni ofee wɔ nɛɛ? Shwɛ fioo ni maŋbii lɛ eko kɛ oŋa lɛ ana bɔlɛ. Eba lɛ nakai kulɛ ohã sɔ̃ etere wɔ.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni Abimelek wo maŋ lɛ fɛɛ kitã akɛ, “Mɔ ni aaata nuu nɛɛ loo eŋa lɛ he lɛ, gbe aaagbe lɛ!”

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Ni Isak fee ŋmɔ, ni edu nii yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni ena nakai bɔ toi oha yɛ nakai afi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ Yehowa jɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Ni Isak tsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ wulu. Ni eshwere aahu kɛyashi etsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ agbo kpanaa.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: Ena too kui kɛ tsina kui kɛ webii pii. Ni Filistibii lɛ ahiɛ kɔ̃ enɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abimelek kɛɛ Isak akɛ, “Jee wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oya. Ejaakɛ ohe ewa fe wɔ!”

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Ni Isak saa eje nubui lɛ ni aje yɛ etsɛ Abraham yinɔ lɛ, ejaakɛ Abraham gbele sɛɛ lɛ Filistibii lɛ tsimɔ; ni eŋɔ gbɛii ni etsɛ Abraham ŋɔ wo amɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ ewo amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Ni Isak bihii lɛ tsa nubu yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛna nu yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Ni Gerar koolookwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ Isak koolookwɛlɔi lɛ be ni amɛkɛɛ, “Nu nɛɛ wɔnɔŋ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Isak wo nubu lɛ gbɛi akɛ, “Esek”, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ lɛ be yɛ he.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Isak tsuji lɛ je nubu kroko, ni amɛbe yɛ no hu he. No hewɔ lɛ, Isak wo nubu lɛ akɛ, “Sitna”; eshishi ji “Hetsɛ̃”.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Isak fã eshi jɛi, ni eyaje nubu kroko ni no lɛ amɛbeee yɛ he; ni Isak tsɛ nubu lɛ akɛ “Rehobot”; eshishi ji, “Yehowa ehã wɔ gbɛ koni wɔshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Isak shi jɛi etee Beersheba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Yehowa jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni ekɛɛ, “Mi ji otsɛ Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ; kaashe gbeyei, ejaakɛ mikɛ bo yɛ, ni majɔɔ bo; mahã oshwiei afa yɛ mitsulɔ Abraham hewɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Isak mã afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi, ni eja Yehowa yɛ jɛi; ni eshi ebuu lɛ yɛ jɛi. Ni Isak je nubu yɛ jɛi hu. Isak kɛ Abimelek kpãŋ

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Abimelek kɛ enaanyo Ahuzal kɛ etatsɛ Fikol jɛ Gerar ba Isak ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Ni Isak kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ nyɛbaa miŋɔɔ, nyɛ ni nyɛnyɛɔ mi ni nyɛshwie mi yɛ nyɛmasɛi lɛ?”

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛɛ, “Naa, wɔna akɛ Yehowa kɛ bo yɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, hã ni wɔkɛ bo akpãŋ kpãŋmɔ ko,

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: akɛ ofeŋ wɔ efɔŋ ko ejaakɛ wɔfeko bo efɔŋ ko akɛ ja ekpakpa kɛkɛ; ni wɔsaa wɔwo bo gbɛ yɛ hejɔlɛ mli; ni Yehowa ejɔɔ bo!”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ni Isak ŋmɛ amɛ okplɔ̃, ni amɛye nii, ni amɛnu nɔ ko.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Ni amɛte shi leebi maŋkpa ni amɛkãmɔ amɛhe kitãi. Ni Isak wo amɛ gbɛ ni amɛshi eŋɔɔ yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ akɛ Isak tsuji lɛ ba ni amɛbagba lɛ nubu ni amɛje lɛ he sane akɛ, “Wɔyanina nu.”

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Ni Isak wo nubu lɛ akɛ “Shiba”. No hewɔ ni atsɛɔ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Beersheba” kɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ.

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Ni yei nɛɛ ahe sane lɛ fee Isak kɛ Rebeka dɔlɛ waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Be ni Isak egbɔ, ni ehiŋmɛii anɔ eha ni enaaa nii lɛ, etsɛ ebi nukpa Esau, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mibi!” Ni Esau here nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Naa mi!”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Isak kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, migbɔ, ni mileee migbele gbi.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɔlɔmɔ ogbɔbimɔ nibii lɛ, ogãi kotoku kɛ ogãi lɛ, ni oje kpo oya ŋa lɛ mli ni oyami milɛloo obahã mi

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: koni okɛbafee niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni misumɔɔ lɛ, ohã mi maye koni majɔɔ bo dani magbo.”

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Rebeka yakɛɛ ebi Yakob akɛ, “Minu akɛ otsɛ kɛ onyɛmi Esau miiwie akɛ,

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: ‘Yaatao milɛloo, ni okɛfee niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ obahã mi maye koni majɔɔ bo yɛ Yehowa hiɛ dani magbo.’

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, mibi, bo nɔ ni mikɛɔ bo nɛɛ toi!

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Yaa toi lɛ ateŋ ni oyamɔmɔ toobii kpakpai enyɔ yɛ abotiai lɛ ateŋ obahã mi ni mikɛfee niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ mahã otsɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: koni okɛyahã otsɛ ni eye, bɔ ni afee ni ejɔɔ bo dani egbo.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Shi Yakob kɛɛ enyɛ Rebeka akɛ, “Naa, minyɛmi Esau lɛ tsɔiatsɛ ji lɛ, shi mi lɛ, mihe yɛ trotro.

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Eko lɛ mitsɛ aaatara mihe ni matsɔ shishiulɔ yɛ ehiɛ ni maloo loomɔ mabua miyiteŋ, shi minaŋ jɔɔmɔ moŋ.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Enyɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Oloomɔ lɛ ababua mi miyiteŋ, mibi; bo mi toi kɛkɛ ni oyamɔmɔ toi lɛ obahã mi!”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob yiŋ etee ni eyamɔmɔ toobii lɛ ebahã enyɛ; ni enyɛ kɛfee niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rebeka kɔlɔ ebi nukpa Esau atadei fɛɛfɛji ni yɔɔ eŋɔɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ, ni ekɛwo Yakob, ebi gbekɛ lɛ,

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: ni ekɛ toobii lɛ ahewoji lɛ wo Yakob niji kɛ ekuɛ, hei ni yɔɔ trotro lɛ.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ kɛ aboloo ni eshã lɛ wo ebi Yakob dɛŋ.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob ba etsɛ ŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Ataa!” Ni etsɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Naa mi! Bo namɔ ni, mibi?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ni Yakob kɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Mi Esau, okromɔbi lɛ ni; mifee bɔ ni okɛɛ mi lɛ. Ofainɛ, tee shi ota shi ni oye mimilɛloo lɛ eko koni ojɔɔ mi!”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Isak kɛɛ ebi lɛ akɛ, “Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ona lɛ oya nɛkɛ, mibi?” Ni Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Ejaakɛ Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ye ebua mi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Isak kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Tsi oba, mibi, ni matara ohe makwɛ akɛ mibi Esau lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni, aloo jeee lɛ ni.”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob tsi ebɛŋkɛ etsɛ Isak, ni Isak tara ehe, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Gbee lɛ Yakob gbee ni, shi niji lɛ Esau niji ni.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ebi akɛ, “Ani bo mibi Esau pɔtɛɛ nɛ lo?” Ni Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Mi ni”.

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Isak kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Okɛ niyenii lɛ abahã mi koni maye mibi milɛloo lɛ eko koni majɔɔ bo.” No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob kɛ niyenii lɛ bahã lɛ, ni eye. Ebahã Isak wain hu, ni enu.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni etsɛ Isak kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mibi, tsi obɛŋkɛ mi koo koni obashwɔ minaa!”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Ni etsi ebɛŋkɛ ni ebashwɔ enaa, ni Isak nu Yakob atadei lɛ amli ŋma lɛ, ni ejɔɔ lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ bɔ ni mibi lɛ he jeɔ ŋma, tamɔ ŋa frɔ̃frɔ̃ ni Yehowa ejɔɔ.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ ahã bo ŋwɛi bɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli fɔ lɛ eko, kɛ ŋmãa kɛ wain babaoo hu.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Maji asɔ̃mɔ bo, ni je lɛŋ maji akoto bo. Ye onyɛmimɛi lɛ anɔ lumɔ, ni onyɛ bihii lɛ akoto bo. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaalomɔ bo lɛ, alomɔ lɛ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaajɔɔ bo lɛ, ajɔɔ lɛ!” Esau kpa fai koni Isak ajɔɔ lɛ

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Be ni Isak egbe Yakob jɔɔmɔ lɛ naa ni Yakob kɛɛ ejeɔ etsɛ Isak hiɛ nɔŋŋ pɛ lɛ, naa enyɛmi Esau hu; ejɛ emilɛ lɛ eba.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ni lɛ hu efee niyenii kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ ni ekɛmiiba ebahã etsɛ. Ni ekɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Ataa, tee shi ni ota shi ni oye obi milɛloo lɛ eko koni ojɔɔ mi.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Etsɛ Isak bi lɛ akɛ, “Bo namɔ ni?” Ni Esau to he akɛ, “Mi, okromɔbi Esau ni.”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Isak he kpokpo blibli waa diɛŋtsɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Namɔ mɔ ji mɔ ni kɛ milɛloo bahã mi ni miye fɛɛ dani obaa nɛɛ, ni mijɔɔ lɛ, ni aaajɔɔ lɛ hu lɛ?”

english_verse: Esau cried out in great distress, “Father, give me a blessing too!”
translation_verse: Be ni Esau nu etsɛ wiemɔi lɛ, ebo waa diɛŋtsɛ kɛ awerɛhoo babaoo ni ekɛɛ etsɛ Isak akɛ, “Mi hu jɔɔmɔ mi eko, Ataa!”

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Shi Isak kɛɛ, “Onyɛmi lɛ kɛ shishiumɔ ebahe ojɔɔmɔ lɛ kɛtee.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Esau kɛɛ, “Egbɛi Yakob ni awo lɛ lɛ, ebala lɛ. Shii enyɔ sɔŋŋ ni eshishiu mi nɛ; mikromɔbi gbɛnaa lɛ eshɔ̃, ni agbɛnɛ ebahe mijɔɔmɔ lɛ hu!” Ni Esau bi etsɛ akɛ, “Ani oshwɛɛɛ jɔɔmɔ lɛ eko ohãaa mi?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Isak to he ekɛɛ Esau akɛ; “Mifee lɛ onuŋtsɔ, ni mikɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ fɛɛ efee etsuji. Miŋɔ ŋmãa kɛ wain mihã lɛ; ni bo lɛ, mɛni mafee mahã bo mɔ, mibi?”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Esau kɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Ataa, ani jɔɔmɔ kome pɛ kɛkɛ oyɔɔ? Hã mi jɔɔmɔ ko kɛ̃, Ataa!” Ni Esau jwa yaafo.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Etsɛ Isak here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Shikpɔŋ ni fɔ bɛ mli nɔ ooohi, kɛ he ni ŋwɛi bɔ enyɔɔɔ yɛ.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Oklante naa oyi aaana wala yɛ, ni onyɛmi lɛ ooosɔ̃mɔ. Shi aaaba mli akɛ, kɛ opele ohe lɛ, oookpɔ̃ ohe yɛ edɛŋ.”

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Esau nyɛ Yakob yɛ jɔɔmɔ ni etsɛ jɔɔ lɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ekɛɛ yɛ eyitsoŋ akɛ, “Etsɛŋ tsɔ ko ni aaafee mitsɛ yara, kɛkɛ lɛ magbe minyɛmi Yakob.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Shi abagba Rebeka ebi nukpa Esau wiemɔi nɛɛ, ni etsu ayatsɛ Yakob, ebi gbekɛ lɛ, kɛba ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, onyɛmi Esau kɛ gbe ni ebaagbe bo miihã ehe tsui.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mibi, bo mi toi, joo foi oya kɛya minyɛmi Laban ŋɔɔ yɛ Haran

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: ni okɛ lɛ ayahi shi gbii fioo ko kɛyashi beyinɔ ni onyɛmi lɛ tsui he aaajɔ;

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: kɛyashi beyinɔ ni onyɛmi lɛ mlifu lɛ naa aaaba shi ni ehiɛ aaakpa nɔ ni ofee lɛ lɛ nɔ; kɛkɛ lɛ matsu ni abaŋɔ bo kɛku sɛɛ kɛba. Mɛɛba nyɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nyɛaaŋmɛɛ mi gbi kome?”

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rebeka kɛɛ Isak akɛ, “Esau ŋamɛi Hityei lɛ ehã mijeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine. Kɛji Yakob hu aaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ Hityei nɛɛ eko akɛ eŋa tamɔ mɛnɛɛmɛi lɛ, no lɛ faŋ nɔ ni migbo moŋ.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Isak tsɛ Yakob ni ejɔɔ lɛ, ni ewo lɛ akpɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Kaaŋɔ yoo yɛ Kanaan yei lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Yaa onyɛ tsɛ Betuel we lɛ, yɛ Mesopotamia, ni oyaŋɔ onyɛ nyɛmi nuu Laban biyei lɛ eko akɛ oŋa.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ ajɔɔ bo, ni ehã oshwere ni owo shwiei babaoo koni oshwiei atsɔ̃ majimaji asafo.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni ejɔɔ Abraham lɛ, ejɔɔ bo kɛ oshwiei nakai nɔŋŋ koni ogbɔtoo shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhã otsɛ Abraham lɛ atsɔ̃ onɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Isak wo Yakob gbɛ koni eya Mesopotamia yɛ Aramnyo Betuel bi Laban ni ji Yakob kɛ Esau nyɛ Rebeka nyɛmi nuu lɛ ŋɔɔ. Esau ŋɔ yoo kroko hu

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esau na hu akɛ etsɛ nyãaa Kanaan yei lɛ ahe.

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: Enɛɛmɛi ahewɔ lɛ, Esau yiŋ etee Abraham bi Ishmael ŋɔɔ, ni eyaŋɔ ebiyoo Mahalat, Nabaiot nyɛmi yoo lɛ, efata eŋãmɛi ni eyɔɔ lɛ ahe. Yakob la lamɔ ko yɛ Betel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Yakob jɛ Beersheba ni eyiŋ eeya Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Eshɛ he ko ni eto jɛi ejaakɛ hulu enyɔ shi. Ekɔ jɛi tɛi lɛ eko etsɔle, ni ekã jɛi ewɔ.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: Ni ela ni aŋtswere ko ma shikpɔŋ ni eyiteŋ eyashi ŋwɛi. Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfoi miikwɔ miikpeleke shi,

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: ni Yehowa damɔ aŋtswere lɛ yiteŋ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mi ji Yehowa, otsɛ Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ, kɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ; shikpɔŋ ni okã nɔ nɛɛ, bo kɛ oshwiei mikɛbaahã.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: Oshwiei aaafa tamɔ shikpɔŋ mlu, ni ooogbɛ oshwã anai kɛ bokã kɛ kooyi kɛ wuoyi. Bo kɛ oshwiei amli aaajɛ ajɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akutsei fɛɛ.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Na ole akɛ mikɛ bo yɛ ni he fɛɛ he ni oyaa lɛ, mabu ohe, ni mikɛ bo aaaba shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ejaakɛ mishiŋ bo kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni mafee nɔ ni mitsi tã mikɛɛ bo lɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob hiɛ tsɛ̃ kɛjɛ ewɔ lɛ mli, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa yɛ biɛ kwa, ni mi lɛ mileee nɛɛ!”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Yakob she gbeyei, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Biɛ nɛɛ yɛ gbeyei eei! Biɛ nɛɛ jeee he ko he ko akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ we, ni ŋwɛi naa agbo nɛ!”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Yakob te shi leebi maŋkpa ni etee tɛ lɛ ni etsɔle lɛ shi ema shi ekɛto okadi, ni efɔse mu eshwie nɔ.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: Ewo jɛi Betel; shi sa lɛ, nakai maŋ lɛ gbɛi ji Luz.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Yakob wo shi ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mi aaahi shi, ni eeebu mihe yɛ gbɛ ni miyanyiɛ nɛɛ mli, ni eeehã miŋmãa maye kɛ atade mawo,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ni maku misɛɛ maba mitsɛ we lɛ kɛ omanye lɛ, no lɛ Yehowa aaatsɔ̃ miNyɔŋmɔ,

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: ni nɛkɛ tɛ nɛɛ ni mikɛma shi mikɛto okadi nɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ we; ni maŋɔ nibii fɛɛ ni ooohã mi lɛ amlijaa nyɔŋma kome mahã bo.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Yakob wo enane nɔ yɛ egbɛfaa lɛ mli, ni eyashɛ bokãgbɛbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Be ni ewo ehiɛ nɔ lɛ, ena nubu ko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni ena too kui etɛ̃ bumɔ shi yɛ he ejaakɛ nakai bu lɛ mli nu ahãa amɛ amɛnuɔ. Tɛ ni kã bu lɛ naa lɛ da.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Kɛji too kui lɛ fɛɛ ebabua amɛhe naa yɛ bu lɛ he lɛ, tookwɛlɔi lɛ kokloɔ tɛ lɛ kɛjeɔ bu lɛ naa ni amɛhãa toi lɛ nu, kɛkɛ lɛ amɛkoklo tɛ lɛ amɛto bu lɛ naa ekoŋŋ yɛ egbɛhe.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yakob bi tookwɛlɔi lɛ akɛ, “Minyɛmimɛi, nɛgbɛ nyɛjɛ?” Amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔjɛ Haran.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Yakob bi amɛ akɛ, “Ani nyɛle Nahor bi Laban lɛ lo?” Amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔle lɛ.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Esaa ebi amɛ akɛ, “Eyɛ jogbaŋŋ lo?” Amɛto he akɛ, “Eyɛ jogbaŋŋ. Naa, ebiyoo Rahel po kɛ toi baa nɛɛ!”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, je nako kwraa. Eshɛko be ni abuaa toi lɛ anaa. Nyɛhãa amɛ nu amɛnua koni nyɛhãa amɛyayea nii.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Shi amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔnyɛŋ amɛ nu wɔhã akɛ ja abua too kuikui lɛ fɛɛ naa kɛkpe, ni akoklo tɛ lɛ kɛje bu lɛ naa dani wɔɔnyɛ amɛ nu wɔhã.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob kɛ amɛ wieɔ lolo lɛ, Rahel kɛ etsɛ toi lɛ bashɛ jɛi; ejaakɛ lɛ ekwɛɔ amɛ.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob shwɔ Rahel naa, ni Yakob jwa yaafo.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ Rahel akɛ, “Otsɛ wekunyo ji mi, ni Rebeka binuu ji mi.” Kɛkɛ ni Rahel sha foi etee eyagba etsɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Be ni Laban nu enyɛmi yoo bi Yakob he sane lɛ, esha foi etee lɛ kpeemɔ. Eloo Yakob atuu, ni eshwɔ enaa. Ekɛ lɛ ba ewe lɛ. Yakob gba Laban saji fɛɛ ni ba lɛ,

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: ni Laban kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Asonɔkwa, mi diɛŋtsɛ mila ji bo!” Yakob kɛ lɛ hi shi nyɔŋ kome. Yakob sɔ̃mɔ Laban yɛ Rahel kɛ Lea hewɔ

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Ni Laban kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Akɛni miwekuyo ji bo hewɔ lɛ ani esa akɛ osɔ̃mɔ mi yaka lo? Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ bɔ ni obaahe mi.”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Lea hiŋmɛii yɛ sukusuku, shi Rahel hiɛ yɛ fɛo ni egbɔmɔtso hu yɛ fɛo.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Yakob sumɔ Rahel, no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ Laban akɛ, “Mibasɔ̃mɔ bo afii kpawo yɛ Rahel, obiyoo fioo lɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Laban to he akɛ, “Ehi akɛ mikɛ lɛ ahã bo fe nɔ ni mikɛ lɛ aaahã nuu kroko. Okɛ mi ahi shi.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob sɔ̃mɔ afii kpawo yɛ Rahel hewɔ; ni suɔmɔ sɔŋŋ ni esumɔɔ Rahel hewɔ lɛ, afii lɛ ho oya yɛ ehiɛ tamɔ gbii fioo ko kɛkɛ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yakob kɛɛ Laban akɛ, “Okɛ miŋa lɛ ahã mi koni mikɛ lɛ ahi shi ejaakɛ migbe misɔ̃ɔmɔ be lɛ naa.

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Laban bua jɛi bii lɛ fɛɛ anaa, ni eŋmɛ okplɔ̃.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Shi be ni shɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, ekɛ ebiyoo Lea moŋ yahã Yakob ni Yakob kɛ Lea wɔ.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Be ni je tsɛre lɛ, Yakob na akɛ Lea ni. Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kɛɛ Laban akɛ, ‘Mɛni sane oye mi nɛɛ? Ani jeee Rahel hewɔ misɔ̃mɔ bo lɛ? Mɛɛ hewɔ mɔ ni oshishiu mi nɛkɛ?’ ”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Laban to he akɛ, “Wɔshikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, afeee nakai. Ahãaa gbekɛ gbãlã dani ahã onukpa gbãlã.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Gbee mɔ nɛ otsi lɛ naa ni wɔkɛ mɔ kome lɛ hu baahã bo, kɛji osɔ̃mɔ mi afii kpawo kroko.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Rahel hu bawɔ Yakob ŋɔɔ. Yakob sumɔ Rahel fe Lea; ni esɔ̃mɔ Laban afii kpawo kroko yɛ Rahel hewɔ. Bii ni Yakob kɛ Lea fɔ

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa na akɛ Yakob sumɔɔɔ Lea lɛ, egbele Lea musu naa, shi eŋa Rahel musu naa ni efee kene.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Lea na musu ni efɔ binuu. Ewo lɛ Ruben, ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ Yehowa ena mimanehulu lɛ. Agbɛnɛ lɛ miwu baasumɔ mi.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Lea na musu ekoŋŋ, ni efɔ binuu. Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Akɛni Yehowa enu akɛ asumɔɔɔ mi hewɔ lɛ, ehã mi binuu nɛɛ hu.” Ni ewo lɛ Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Esaa ena musu, ni efɔ binuu ekoŋŋ. Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, miwu kɛ ehe baakpɛtɛ mihe, ejaakɛ mikɛ lɛ efɔ bihii etɛ̃.” Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, ewo gbekɛ lɛ Levi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ena musu ekoŋŋ, ni efɔ binuu. Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ, majie Yehowa yi!” No hewɔ lɛ, ewo gbekɛ lɛ Yuda; kɛkɛ ni efo fɔmɔ dã.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Be ni Rahel na akɛ ekɛ Yakob fɔɔɔ lɛ, ebɔi enyɛmi yoo Lea lɛ he awuŋayeli, ni ekɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Okɛ mi afɔ, kɛjeee nakai lɛ magbo!”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Yakob mli wo Rahel la, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ani mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ ni etsi omusuŋbii anaa lɛ?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rahel kɛɛ, “Mikɛ miweyoo Bilha miihã bo ŋɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ lɛ afɔ ashwie mishuɔ nɔ mɔ, koni mi hu mana bii kɛtsɔ̃ enɔ.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Bilha na musu, ni ekɛ Yakob fɔ binuu.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rahel kɛɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ eye misane lɛ ehã mi, ebo mi toi, ni ehã mi binuu.” No hewɔ lɛ, ewo abifao lɛ Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Bilha, Rahel weyoo lɛ, na musu ekoŋŋ, ni ekɛ Yakob fɔ binuu ni ji enyɔ.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rahel kɛɛ akɛ, “Mikɛ minyɛmi yoo lɛ enɔ nɔmɔ ni mli wa, ni miye kunim.” No hewɔ lɛ, ewo abifao lɛ Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Be ni Lea na akɛ ekpa fɔmɔ lɛ, ekɛ eweyoo Zilpa hã Yakob gbãlã.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Lea weyoo Zilpa lɛ kɛ Yakob fɔ binuu.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Lea kɛɛ akɛ, “Omanye sane nɛ;” no hewɔ lɛ, ewo abifao lɛ Gad.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Lea weyoo Zilpa kɛ Yakob fɔ binuu ni ji enyɔ;

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: ni Lea kɛɛ akɛ, “Mina miishɛɛ ejaakɛ yei aaatsɛ mi yoo ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ;” ni ewo abifao lɛ Asher.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Be ni ŋmãakuu be shɛ lɛ, Ruben yana suɔmɔ tso yibii ko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni etse eko, ni ekɛbahã enyɛ Lea. Kɛkɛ ni Rahel kɛɛ Lea akɛ, “Miikpa bo fai ni ohã mi obi lɛ suɔmɔ tso yibii lɛ eko.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Shi Lea kɛɛ Rahel akɛ, “Aso ni oshɔ̃ miwu lɛ, no faaa hãaa bo, obaashɔ̃ mibi lɛ suɔmɔ tso yibii lɛ hu?” Rahel to he akɛ, “Kɛji ooohã mi obi lɛ suɔmɔ tso yibii lɛ eko lɛ, no lɛ obaanyɛ oyawɔ Yakob ŋɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛkɛ mli be ni Yakob jɛ ŋmɔ mli ebaa lɛ, Lea je kpo ni ekɛ lɛ yakpe, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ, ja obawɔ miŋɔɔ ejaakɛ mikɛ mibi lɛ suɔmɔ tso yibii lɛ ebɔ bo apaa!” No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob kɛ lɛ wɔ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ bo Lea sɔlemɔ toi, ena musu; ni ekɛ Yakob fɔ binuu ni ji enumɔ.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Lea kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ ehã mi mipaabɔɔnii, ejaakɛ mikɛ miweyoo lɛ ehã miwu gbãlã;” ni ewo abifao lɛ Isakar.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Lea kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ ehã mi gbãlãnii fɛɛfɛo. Agbɛnɛ miwu baawo mihiɛ nyam, ejaakɛ mikɛ lɛ efɔ bihii ekpaa sɔŋŋ.” No hewɔ lɛ, ewo gbekɛ lɛ Zebulon.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Lea fɔ biyoo, ni ewo lɛ Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Rahel na musu, ni efɔ binuu, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ ejie mihiɛgbele lɛ.”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Ewo gbekɛ lɛ Yosef, eshishi ji, “Yehowa ahã mafɔ binuu ekoŋŋ.” Yakob kɛ Laban ye nitsumɔ naa

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Rahel efɔ Yosef sɛɛ lɛ, Yakob kɛɛ Laban akɛ, “Wo mi gbɛ ni maya mijɛɛhe kɛ mishikpɔŋ nɔ.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Okɛ miŋamɛi kɛ nibii ni misɔ̃mɔ bo yɛ amɛhewɔ lɛ ahã mi ni maya ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ole bɔ ni misɔ̃mɔ bo mihã.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bo diɛŋtsɛ ole bɔ ni misɔ̃mɔ bo mihã kɛ bɔ hu ni okooloi lɛ eshwere yɛ midɛŋ.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni miba lɛ, kooloi fioo ko kɛkɛ oyɔɔ; shi amrɔ nɛɛ amɛshwere babaoo; mi mihewɔ Yehowa ejɔɔ bo babaoo nɛɛ. Shi agbɛnɛ mɛɛbe mabua nɔ ko naa mahã mi diɛŋtsɛ miwe hu.”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Laban bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni mahã bo?” Yakob hã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Kaahã mi nɔ ko nɔ ko. Kɛ ooofee nɔ ni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɛɛ ohã mi lɛ, no lɛ masaa malɛ okooloi lɛ ni makwɛ amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Ŋmɛnɛ hã ni makpa otoi lɛ fɛɛ mli ni mahala toobi fɛɛ toobi ni he yɔɔ truntrãi kɛ damdam yɛ gwantɛŋi lɛ amli, kɛ nii ni he yɔɔ damdam kɛ nii ni he yɔɔ truntrãi yɛ abotiai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nomɛi aaatsɔ minyɔmɔwoo.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Ni kɛfee sɛɛ ni ooobakwɛ minyɔmɔwoo lɛ, miye bo anɔkwale jio, miyeko bo anɔkwale jio, obaana. Abotiai lɛ amli eko fɛɛ eko ni he bɛ truntrãi kɛ damdam kɛ gwantɛŋi lɛ amli nii ni he diii lɛ kɛ ooona eko yɛ midɛŋ lɛ, belɛ no lɛ juunii ni.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Laban to he akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ; afee bɔ ni okɛɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbi lɛ Laban jie too kpakpoi ni he yɔɔ truntrãi kɛ damdam lɛ kɛ abotia yei ni he yɔɔ truntrãi kɛ damdam lɛ, eko fɛɛ eko ni eyɛŋ ta ehe, kɛ gwantɛŋbi fɛɛ gwantɛŋbi ni diɔ, ni etu amɛ ewo ebii lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ ebii lɛ shi Yakob kɛtee he kroko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji gbii etɛ̃ gbɛnyiɛmɔ, ni Yakob kwɛ Laban toi ni shwɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yakob kɔlɔ libne tsei ŋmɔji kɛ luz tsei kɛ blɔfoŋkatiɛ tsei ni eye amɛhe sãmãi yɛji, ni ehã tsei lɛ amli eyɛji lɛ je shi.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ekɛ tsei ni eye amɛhe sãmãi nɛɛ shwie tsesei ni toi lɛ banuɔ nu yɛ mli lɛ amli, bɔ ni toi lɛ aaana sãmãi lɛ kɛji amɛba nu lɛ numɔ lɛ; ejaakɛ kɛ amɛba nu lɛ numɔ lɛ, toohii lɛ kwɔɔ tooyei lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob tserɛ too gwantɛŋbii lɛ eto afã, ni etsɔ̃mɔ toi lɛ ahiɛ ehã Laban toi ni he yɔɔ sãmãisãmãi lɛ kɛ nii ni diɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etoo ku lɛ to afã, ni ekɛ amɛ futuuu Laban toi lɛ.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Kɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miina bɔlɛ lɛ, Yakob kɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsesei lɛ ahiɛ, koni toi lɛ ana bɔlɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Shi toi ni yɔɔ wudɔwudɔ lɛ ekɛ tsei lɛ eshwieee amɛhiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, toi wudɔwudɔi lɛ tsɔmɔ Laban nii, ni nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsɔmɔ Yakob nii.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yakob shwere waa naakpa. Ena toi babaoo kɛ weyei kɛ wehii kɛ yoomai kɛ tejii.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Yakob nu ni Laban bihii lɛ miiwiewie akɛ, “Yakob eshɔ̃ wɔtsɛ nii fɛɛ; wɔtsɛ nii lɛ ekɛna ehe nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yakob na akɛ gbii etɛ̃ nɛɛ Laban tseee ehiɛ ehãaa lɛ dɔŋŋ tamɔ sa lɛ.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ kɛya otsɛmɛi kɛ owekumɛi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mi kɛ bo aaahi shi.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob tsu ayatsɛ Rahel kɛ Lea kɛba ŋa lɛ nɔ, he ni etoi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ,

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mina akɛ gbii etɛ̃ nɛɛ nyɛtsɛ tseee ehiɛ ehãaa mi dɔŋŋ tamɔ sa lɛ. Shi Nyɔŋmɔ ni mitsɛ jaa lɛ kɛ mi yɛ.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛle akɛ mihewalɛ fɛɛ mikɛsɔ̃mɔ nyɛtsɛ;

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: kɛ̃lɛ nyɛtsɛ shishiu mi, ni etsake minyɔmɔwo shii nyɔŋma; shi Nyɔŋmɔ hãaa lɛ hegbɛ ni efee mi efɔŋ ko.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Kɛji ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Toi kɛ amɛhe truntrãi lɛ aaatsɔ onɔ lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ toi lɛ fɛɛ efɔ bii kɛ amɛhe damdam.’

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ Nyɔŋmɔ fee ni eshɔ̃ nyɛtsɛ kooloi lɛ ehã mi.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: “Toi lɛ amusunamɔ be mli lɛ, miwo mihiɛ nɔ, ni mina yɛ lamɔ mli akɛ too kpakpoi ni kwɔɔ tooyei lɛ, amɛhe yɛ truntrãi kɛ damdam kɛ ŋwãtãŋwãtã.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ mi yɛ lamɔ lɛ mli akɛ, ‘Yakob!’ Ni mikɛɛ akɛ, ‘Naa mi!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Wo ohiɛ nɔ, ni ooona akɛ too kpakpoi lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɔɔ tooyei lɛ amɛhe truntrãi kɛ damdam kɛ ŋwãtãŋwãtã ejaakɛ mina nii fɛɛ ni Laban feɔ bo lɛ.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ Betel, he ni oŋɔ tɛ okɛto okadi yɛ, ni ofɔ okadi tɛ lɛ mu, ni owo mi shi yɛ lɛ. Agbɛnɛ tee shi oyá ni oya; jee shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ koni oku osɛɛ oya shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni afɔ bo yɛ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ani jeee mɛi kpɔji ebuɔ wɔ? Ejaakɛ ehɔ̃ɔ wɔ, ni eye wɔyi nii lɛ hu.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Shi nii fɛɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ eshɔ̃ yɛ wɔtsɛ dɛ lɛ, no ji wɔ kɛ wɔbii anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ ekɛɛ bo lɛ feemɔ.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob te shi, ni eŋɔ ebii kɛ eŋãmɛi lɛ etara yoomai anɔ;

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: ni ekpala kooloi lɛ kɛ enii fɛɛ ni ena lɛ, ni ji nii ni ena yɛ Mesopotamia lɛ, ni eŋɔ eshwie nɔ kɛmiiya etsɛ Isak ŋɔɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Laban etee eyaaku etoi lɛ ahe tsɔi, ni Rahel ju etsɛ shĩa amãgãi lɛ.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Yakob laka Laban, Aramnyo lɛ ejaakɛ ekɛ efoijee lɛ tee Laban.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Yakob jo foi kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ, ni etee eyafo Eufrate Faa lɛ, ni ewo eyi ema he ni Gilead gɔji lɛ yɔɔ lɛ gbɛ. Laban tiu Yakob

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ayakɛɛ Laban akɛ Yakob ejo foi.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Laban ŋɔ ewekumɛi efata ehe, ni etiu Yakob gbii kpawo gbɛ kɛyashi eyanina lɛ yɛ Gilead gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Laban, Aramnyo lɛ, yɛ wɔ mli ni ekɛɛ Laban akɛ, “Kwɛmɔ ni ahi koni okɛ Yakob akawie wiemɔ fɔŋ ko.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Laban yanina Yakob. Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ, Yakob eshi ebuu yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ; ni Laban kɛ ewebii lɛ hu shi amɛbuu yɛ Gilead gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Laban kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Mɛni ofee nɛɛ? Olaka mi ni oŋɔ mibiyei lɛ kɛmiiya tamɔ mɛi ni aŋɔ amɛ nom yɛ ta mli nɛɛ?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ ni ojo foi dujiaŋ ni oshɛɛɛ mi koni kulɛ mikɛ lala kɛ milɛ̃ kɛ kpãa saŋku ayajie bo gbɛ kɛ miishɛɛ?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Ni mɛɛ hewɔ ohãaa mana hegbɛ koni mashwɔ minabihii kɛ mibiyei lɛ anaa mikɛ amɛ aye shɛɛ lɛ? Nɔ ni ofee lɛ kwashiai asane oye nɛɛ.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Kulɛ manyɛ mafee bo efɔŋ; shi otsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ mi wie nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ mli, ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Kwɛmɔ ohe ni ahi koni okɛ Yakob akawie wiemɔ fɔŋ ko.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, yaa oyaa nɛɛ, ejaakɛ ohiɛ etsɔ̃ otsɛ we lɛ; shi mɛɛba mɔ ni oju mimãgãi lɛ?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Yakob to he, ni ekɛɛ, “Miyashe gbeyei akɛ ekolɛ oooshɔ̃ obiyei lɛ yɛ midɛŋ akrananaa.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Shi mɔ fɛɛ mɔ dɛŋ ni ooona owɔŋ lɛ yɛ lɛ agbe lɛ. Taomɔ nɔ ni ji onɔ yɛ minibii nɛɛ ateŋ, yɛ wekumɛi ni yɔɔ biɛ nɛɛ ahiɛ koni okɔ onii.” Shi Yakob leee akɛ Rahel ni eju amãgãi lɛ.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Laban bote Yakob buu lɛ mli kɛ Lea buu lɛ mli kɛ weyei enyɔ lɛ hu abuu lɛ mli, shi enaaa ewɔŋ lɛ. Ni eje kpo yɛ Lea buu lɛ mli, ni ebote Rahel nɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Shi Rahel ekɔlɔ amãgãi lɛ, ni ekɛwo yooma nɔ nii lɛ mli, ni eho eta nɔ. Laban nyɛmɔnyɛmɔɔ shi yɛ buu lɛ mli fɛɛ, shi enaaa.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rahel kɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Ekafee minuŋtsɔ mlifu akɛ minyɛɛɛ shi mate yɛ ohiɛ ejaakɛ mifee yei anii.” No hewɔ lɛ, Laban tao amãgãi lɛ aahu, shi enaaa.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob mli wo la, ni ekɛ Laban be. Yakob kɛɛ Laban akɛ, “Mɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ mitɔ̃, ni mɛɛ esha hu mifee, ni ohiɛ edɔ kɛnyiɛ misɛɛ nɛkɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Kolɛ ni ota minibii lɛ fɛɛ mli nɛɛ, mɛni ona ni ji oshĩa nibii lɛ eko? Kɛji ona eko lɛ, okɛ sane nɛɛ aŋmɛ miwekumɛi kɛ bo hu owekumɛi nɛɛ ahiɛ koni amɛye wɔteŋ sane lɛ ni amɛbu bem ni amɛbu fɔ.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Kooloi lɛ ateŋ nii ni kooloi awuiyelɔi tserɛɔ lɛ, mikɛbahãaa bo, mitoɔ bo najiaŋ. Nyɔɔŋ aju eko jio, shwane jio mi, midɛŋ oheɔ yɛ.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni mishihilɛ lɛ fee nɛ: latsaa tsaa mi shwane, ni fɛ̃i yeɔ mi nyɔɔŋ, ni wɔ hu tseɔ yɛ mihiɛ.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Kɛjeee mitsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ji Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mɔ ni Isak sheɔ lɛ lɛ ni kɛ mi yɔɔ jikulɛ, anɔkwale sane ji akɛ obaawo mi gbɛ kɛya kɛ midɛ folo. Shi Nyɔŋmɔ na mimanehulu kɛ mininenaa nitsumɔ ni naa wa lɛ, hewɔ ni ekã ohiɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛŋ lɛ.” Yakob kɛ Laban Kpãŋ

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Laban here nɔ ni ekɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Biyei nɛɛ mibiyei ni, ni bii lɛ hu mibii ni; toi lɛ mitoi ni; ni nibii ni onaa nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ minɔ ni. Shi ŋmɛnɛ mɛni manyɛ mafee mibiyei lɛ loo amɛbii ni amɛfɔfɔɔ lɛ?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, ba ni mi kɛ bo akpãŋ koni no atsɔ̃ odase yɛ mi kɛ bo teŋ.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob wo tɛ ema shi, ni ekɛto okadi;

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ ewebii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbuaa tɛi anaa.” Amɛkɔlɔ tɛi, ni amɛto lɛ ku amɛma shi; ni amɛye nii yɛ jɛi yɛ tɛ ku lɛ he.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban wo tɛ ku lɛ Yegar-Sahaduta; shi Yakob lɛ, ewo lɛ Galed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban kɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛkɛ tɛ ku nɛɛ miiye odase yɛ mi kɛ bo teŋ ŋmɛnɛ.” No hewɔ ni atsɛɔ tɛ lɛ akɛ Galed lɛ.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ Mizpa hu ejaakɛ Laban kɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa hiŋmɛi ahi mi kɛ bo fɛɛ he, be mli ni wɔgbala mli nɛɛ.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Kɛji owa mibiyei lɛ ayi aloo oooyaŋɔ yei krokomɛi ofata mibiyei lɛ ahe lɛ, gbɔmɔ ko bɛ biɛ moŋ, shi kaimɔ akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ji odasefonyo yɛ mi kɛ bo teŋ.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ tɛ ku nɛɛ ji odase, ni nɛkɛ okadi tɛ nɛɛ hu ji odase akɛ, mi lɛ, mihoŋ tɛ ku nɛɛ he mibaŋ oŋɔɔ ni mibafee bo efɔŋ, ni bo hu ohoŋ tɛ ku nɛɛ kɛ okadi tɛ nɛɛ he obaŋ miŋɔɔ ni obafee mi efɔŋ.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ Nahor Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, amɛtsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, afee kojolɔ yɛ wɔteŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kã Mɔ ni gbeyei etsɛ Isak she lɛ kitã.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eshã afɔle yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni etsɛ ewekumɛi lɛ niyeli. Amɛye nii, ni amɛhi shi yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Laban te shi, ni eshwɔshwɔɔ enabii kɛ ebiyei lɛ anaa, ni ejɔɔ amɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Laban kɛ amɛ gbala mli, ni eku esɛɛ kɛtee emaŋ.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob hu kɛshwie nɔ. Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfoi kɛ lɛ bakpe.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Be ni ena amɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ, “Enɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ta nɛ!” Ni ewo jɛi Mahanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob tsu mɛi kɛtsɔ ehiɛ kɛtee enyɛmi Esau ŋɔɔ yɛ Seir yɛ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Wiemɔ ni ekɛtsu amɛ nɛ, “Nyɛkɛa minuŋtsɔ Esau akɛ, bɔ ni otsulɔ Yakob kɛɛ nɛ: ‘Miyato gbɔ yɛ Laban ŋɔɔ, ni mitsɛ yɛ jɛi aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Minã tsinai kɛ tejii kɛ toi kɛ tsuji hii kɛ tsuji yei, ni mitsu ni abakɛɛ bo, minuŋtsɔ, koni kɛ miba lɛ ona mihe tsuijurɔ.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Mɛi ni atsu lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba Yakob ŋɔɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔtee onyɛmi Esau ŋɔɔ, ni lɛ hu ekɛ hii ohai ejwɛ miiba abakpee bo.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob tsui fã, ni efee yeyeeye naakpa. Eja emɛi lɛ kɛ toi lɛ kɛ tsinai lɛ kɛ yoomai lɛ amli kui enyɔ ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: “Kɛji Esau batua ku kome nɛɛ ni etswia amɛ nii lɛ, koni ku kome ni eshwɛ lɛ ana gbɛ ajo foi.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob sɔle ekɛɛ, “Mitsɛ Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mitsɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ, Yehowa, bo mɔ ni okɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Kuu osɛɛ oya oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ owekumɛi aŋɔɔ, ni mafee bo jogbaŋŋ’ lɛ,

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Miikpa bo fai koni ojie mi yɛ Esau, minyɛmi lɛ, dɛŋ shi miishe lɛ gbeyei, koni ekaba ni ebatswia wɔ fɛɛ nii, mi kɛ nyɛmɛi lɛ kɛ bii lɛ.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Bo okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mafee bo jogbaŋŋ, ni mahã oshwiei afa tamɔ ŋshɔnaa shia, ni anyɛŋ amɛyibɔ akane yɛ amɛyifalɛ naa.’ ”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob wɔ jɛi nakai gbi lɛ, ni ekɛ nii ni ehiɛ lɛ eko yake enyɛmi Esau;

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: ni nyɛsaa nyɛkɛa lɛ akɛ, naa ‘Otsulɔ Yakob nyiɛ wɔsɛɛ.’ ” Esusumɔ ji akɛ, “Mikɛ nikeenii ni nyiɛ hiɛ nɛɛ yaakpãtã lɛ, ni no sɛɛ dani mayana ehiɛ; eko lɛ eeekwɛ mihiɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Mina Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ migbooo.” No hewɔ lɛ, ewo jɛi Peniel.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ nibii nɛɛ wo etsuji lɛ adɛŋ kuikui, ni ekɛɛ tsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtsɔa mihiɛ ni nyɛhãa gbɛ akãa ku kɛ ku teŋ.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Yakob wo klɛŋklɛŋ ku lɛ nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kitã akɛ, “Kɛji minyɛmi Esau kɛ bo kpe ni ebi bo akɛ, ‘Namɔ gbɔmɔ ji bo, ni nɛgbɛ oyaa, ni namɔ nii ji enɛɛmɛi ni nyiɛ ohiɛ nɛɛ?’ lɛ,

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: no lɛ ohã lɛ hetoo akɛ, ‘Otsulɔ Yakob nikeenii ni ekɛtsu akɛ akɛbake minuŋtsɔ Esau ni; ni naa, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ enyiɛ wɔsɛɛ?’ ”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Nakai kitã nɔŋŋ ewo mɔ ni ji enyɔ kɛ mɔ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ hu ni nyiɛ kui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛ nyɛnina Esau lɛ, bɔ ni nyɛkɛ lɛ awie nɛ;

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni akɛ nikeenii lɛ tsɔ Yakob hiɛ, shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ekɛ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ wɔ jɛi nakai gbi lɛ. Yakob kɛ nuu ko nɔ yɛ Peniel

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Be ni nuu lɛ na akɛ enyɛɛɛ Yakob lɛ, etswa Yakob joŋku nɔ, ni joŋku talɔ lɛ hwãŋ yɛ nɔmɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Hã maya, shi je miitsɛre!” Shi Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Mihaŋ oya, ja ojɔɔ mi dã.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ bi Yakob akɛ, “Te atsɛɔ bo tɛŋŋ?” Yakob to he akɛ, “Atsɛɔ mi Yakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Atsɛŋ bo Yakob dɔŋŋ, shi Israel aaatsɛ bo, ejaakɛ okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi eshi mple, ni oye kunim.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Miikpa bo fai ni otsɔ̃ɔ mi ogbɛi.” Shi nuu lɛ kɛɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ obiɔ migbɛi?” Ni ejɔɔ Yakob moŋ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Be ni efoŋ yɛ Peniel lɛ, je etsɛre lɛ, ni eetsutsɔ egboŋ.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ Israelbii yeee joŋku he loo, ejaakɛ nuu lɛ tswa Yakob joŋku lɛ nɔ, ni ejoŋku lɛ hwãŋ.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Ekɛ weyei lɛ kɛ amɛbii lɛ to hiɛgbɛ; Lea kɛ ebii lɛ nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ; ni Rahel kɛ Yosef nyiɛ sɛɛ kwraa.

translation_verse: Shi lɛ Yakob lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ eho eyi ekui lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ; ni be ni eyaa lɛ ekoto shi flɛoflɛo shii kpawo dani eyashɛ enyɛmi lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Shi Esau sha foi ekɛ lɛ bakpe. Eloo Yakob atuu, ni eho egbee ekuɛ nɔ, ni eshwɔ enaa, ni amɛfo.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Be ni Esau wo ehiɛ nɔ ni ena yei lɛ kɛ gbekɛbii lɛ, ebi Yakob akɛ, “Namɛi ji mɛi ni kɛ bo nyiɛ nɛɛ?” Ni Yakob to he akɛ, “Bii ni Nyɔŋmɔ eduro otsulɔ lɛ ni.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni weyei lɛ tsi ba, amɛ kɛ amɛbii lɛ, ni amɛbakoto Esau.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Lea hu kɛ ebii lɛ tsi ba ni amɛbakoto Esau. Ni naagbee kwraa lɛ Yosef kɛ Rahel hu ba ni amɛbakoto lɛ.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Esau bi akɛ, “Kuikui ni mikɛkpe nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ te eshishi hu?” Ni Yakob hã hetoo akɛ, “Bɔ ni afee ni minuŋtsɔ ahã mi hiɛ.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Shi Esau kɛɛ akɛ, “Minyɛmi nuu, nɔ ni miyɔɔ lɛ fa, hã onɔ lɛ ahi shi ahã bo!”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Shi Yakob kɛɛ, “Dabida; miikpa bo fai, kɛji mina hiɛ yɛ ohiɛ lɛ, no lɛ hemɔ midɛŋ nikeenii lɛ; ejaakɛ ohiɛ ni mina nɛɛ lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni mina Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ pɛ, ni ohere mi atuu hu.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Miikpa bo fai koni ohe midɛŋ nikeenii ni akɛbahã bo nɛɛ; ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ eduro mi, ni misaa miyɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ hu.” Ni Yakob hiɛ Esau kɛ wiemɔ aahu kɛyashi be ni ehe nikeenii lɛ.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Esau kɛɛ, “Hã ni wɔŋɔ shwie nɔ koni wɔya; mi lɛ matsɔ ohiɛ.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Shi Yakob kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ le akɛ gbekɛbii lɛ ahiɛ esako; asaŋ mihiɛ toi kɛ tsinai ni hãa amɛbii fufɔ; amɛsane kã mitsui nɔ; kɛji atsirɛ amɛyisɛɛ gbi kome jenamɔ lɛ, kooloi lɛ fɛɛ aaabagboi.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, minuŋtsɔ atsɔ̃ etsulɔ hiɛ, ni mi lɛ manyiɛ blɛooblɛoo bɔ ni kooloi lɛ ni nyiɛ mihiɛ lɛ kɛ gbekɛbii lɛ aaanyɛ anyiɛ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni mashɛ minuŋtsɔ ŋɔɔ yɛ Edom.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Ni Esau kɛɛ, “Hã mashi mɛi ni kɛ mi nyiɛ lɛ eko mato ohe.” Yakob to he akɛ, “Mɛɛ hiamɔ ehia? Hã mi mana hiɛ yɛ minuŋtsɔ hiɛ kɛkɛ!”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Yakob kɛshwie nɔ kɛtee Sukot ni eyama etsu yɛ jɛi, ni efee asesei ehã ekooloi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, awo jɛi Sukot.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Yakob kane shika jwiɛtɛi kukuji oha, ni ekɛhe shikpɔŋ he ni ebato shi yɛ lɛ yɛ Hamorbii lɛ adɛŋ. Shekem tsɛ ji Hamor nɛɛ.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Yakob ma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi, ni ewo lɛ gbɛi akɛ “El, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Shekem, Harmor Hivnyo lɛ, binuu na Dina, ni emɔ lɛ ekɛ lɛ wɔ akrananaa, ni efite lɛ.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.

translation_verse: Shekem kɛɛ etsɛ Hamor akɛ, “Yaakpee oblayoo nɛɛ ohã mi.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yakob nu akɛ abule ebiyoo Dina. Shi no mli lɛ, ebihii lɛ kɛ ekooloi lɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ. Hewɔ lɛ Yakob mɔ enaabu mli kɛyashi be ni amɛba.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob bihii lɛ nu he lɛ, amɛjɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ amɛba. Edɔ oblahii nɛɛ, ni amɛmli wo la naakpa ejaakɛ afee hiɛgbejianii yɛ Israel, akɛni nuu lɛ kɛ Yakob biyoo lɛ wɔ, shi esaaa akɛ afeɔ nakai nɔ ko lɛ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Shi Hamor kɛ amɛ wie ekɛɛ, “Mibinuu Shekem tsui emɔ nyɛbiyoo lɛ; miikpa nyɛ fai koni nyɛkɛ lɛ ahã lɛ gbãlã.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ wɔ ayea yooŋɔɔ; nyɛkɛ nyɛbiyei lɛ ahãa wɔ gbãlã, ni nyɛ hu nyɛŋɔa wɔbiyei nyɛfea ŋamɛi.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ wɔ ahia shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ kã shi hã nyɛ; nyɛhia nɔ ni nyɛtsua nɔ nii koni nyɛna nii yɛ nɔ nyɛhãa nyɛhe akɛ nyɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Shekem kɛɛ Dina tsɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa mihiɛ abaa nyam yɛ nyɛhiɛ shi nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛaabi mi lɛ mahã nyɛ.

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Nyɛbia mi gbãlãnii kɛ nikeenii; bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nyɛtaoɔ lɛ, mahã nyɛ koni nyɛkɛ oblayoo lɛ ahã mi.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob bii lɛ laka Shekem kɛ etsɛ Hamor hiɛ ejaakɛ Shekem ebule amɛnyɛmi yoo Dina lɛ.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Yakob bii lɛ kɛɛ Shekem kɛ etsɛ Hamor akɛ, “Wɔnyɛŋ nɛkɛ nɔ ko wɔfee ni wɔkɛ wɔnyɛmi yoo ahã mɔ ko ni ji foolɔ ejaakɛ no lɛ wɔto kpa.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni wɔtaoɔ kɛkɛ dani wɔɔkpɛ̃lɛ nɔ wɔhã nyɛ ji akɛ nyɛbaatsɔmɔ tamɔ wɔ, ni abaafolɔ nyɛteŋ hii lɛ fɛɛ ketia.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: No lɛ wɔkɛ wɔbiyei baahã nyɛ gbãlã, ni wɔ hu wɔɔŋɔ nyɛbiyei, ni wɔkɛ nyɛ aaahi shi, ni wɔɔtsɔ̃ maŋ kome.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji nyɛbooo wɔ toi koni nyɛhã afo nyɛ ketia lɛ, no lɛ wɔɔŋɔ wɔbiyoo lɛ ni wɔya.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Wiemɔ nɛɛ sa Hamor kɛ ebi Shekem hiɛ.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ kɛ sane lɛ shashaooo shi, ejaakɛ etsui emɔ Yakob biyoo lɛ. Oblanyo nɛɛ abuɔ lɛ fe etsɛ we lɛ mli bii fɛɛ.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Hamor kɛ ebi Shekem tee agbonaa koi lɛ shi, ni amɛkɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ mli hii lɛ wie amɛkɛɛ,

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ kɛ wɔ ye yɛ hejɔlɛ mli; no hewɔ lɛ, nyɛhãa amɛhia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtsu nɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu da aahu hã amɛ. Nyɛhãa wɔŋɔa amɛbiyei lɛ, ni wɔ hu wɔkɛ wɔbiyei lɛ ahã amɛ gbãlã.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Shi ja afo wɔteŋ hii fɛɛ ketia tamɔ bɔ ni afo amɛ lɛ dani gbɔmɛi lɛ aaakpɛ̃lɛ ni amɛkɛ wɔ ahi shi ni amɛkɛ wɔ aaafee maŋ kome.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Amɛkooloo kui kɛ amɛnii ni amɛyɔɔ kɛ amɛshĩa kooloi fɛɛ lɛ, ani jeee wɔnii ebaatsɔmɔ? Nyɛhãa wɔkpɛ̃lɛa nɔ wɔhãa amɛ kɛkɛ koni amɛkɛ wɔ ahi shi.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Shi gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ, be ni amɛfaji lɛ ewo wu lɛ, Yakob bihii enyɔ ni ji Simeon kɛ Levi, Dina nyɛmimɛi lɛ, kɔlɔ amɛklantei, ni amɛbatua maŋ lɛ trukaa, ni amɛgbe hii lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ klante gbe Hamor kɛ ebi Shekem hu, ni amɛyaŋɔ Dina yɛ Shekem we lɛ, ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob bii krokomɛi lɛ banina mɛi ni enyɔnyɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛha maŋ lɛ mli nii, ejaakɛ Shekem ebule amɛnyɛmi yoo lɛ.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Shekem maŋbii lɛ atoi kɛ amɛtsinai kɛ amɛtejii kɛ amɛnii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ nii ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ, Yakob bii lɛ loo fɛɛ kɛtee.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Amɛsaa amɛŋɔ maŋbii lɛ ajwetri fɛɛ kɛ amɛbii bibii fɛɛ kɛ amɛŋamɛi fɛɛ nom, ni amɛha amɛwei amli nibii fɛɛ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kɛɛ Simeon kɛ Levi akɛ, “Nyɛwo mi amaneŋ, ni nyɛhã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii ni ji Kanaanbii kɛ Perizbii lɛ baanyaŋe mi. Ni mi hu nɛ, ni miyikulɛ ji fioo nɛɛ. Kɛji amɛaabua amɛhe naa amɛbatua mi lɛ, amɛaagbe mi, ni amɛaakpãtã miwe lɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Shi Simeon kɛ Levi kɛɛ, “Ani eja gbɛ akɛ afee wɔnyɛmi yoo lɛ tamɔ afeɔ ajwamãŋ ko kɛkɛ lo?”

english_verse: God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Yaa Betel ni oyahi jɛi, ni oma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi ohã Nyɔŋmɔ ni jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ bo be ni ojo onyɛmi Esau naa foi lɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob kɛɛ ewe lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛjiea maŋsɛɛ wɔji ni yɔɔ nyɛteŋ lɛ nyɛshɛraa nyɛshwiea, ni nyɛtsua nyɛhe ni nyɛtsakea nyɛtadei.

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Nyɛhãa wɔyaa Betel koni mayama afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi mahã Nyɔŋmɔ, mɔ ni bo misɔlemɔ toi yɛ mifimɔ gbi lɛ nɔ ni ewa mi yɛ gbɛ ni mifã lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ maŋsɛɛ wɔji lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛdɛŋ lɛ kɛ amɛtoiaŋnii lɛ bahã Yakob; kɛkɛ ni Yakob kɛtee eyafu yɛ tso kpele ko ni ma Shekem masɛi lɛ shishi.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛŋɔ shwie nɔ. Nyɔŋmɔ he ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ maji fɛɛ ni bɔle amɛ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, amɛtiuuu Yakob webii lɛ.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Ema afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi, ni etsɛ jɛi El-Betel, ejaakɛ jɛi Nyɔŋmɔ jie ehe shi etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ, be ni ejo enyɛmi Esau naa foi lɛ.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Ni Debora, mɔ ni kwɛɔ Rebeka kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ, gbo ni afu lɛ yɛ Betel wuoyigbɛ yɛ tso kpele ko shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, awo tso lɛ gbɛi akɛ Allon-bakut.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛhã Abraham kɛ Isak lɛ, bo mikɛbaahã, ni oshwiei ni aaaba yɛ osɛɛ lɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ baahã.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Yakob ŋɔ tɛ eto okadi yɛ he ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ lɛ wie yɛ lɛ, ni efɔse wain kɛ mu eshwie nɔ.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob wo he ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ lɛ wie yɛ lɛ gbɛi akɛ Betel. Rahel gbele

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kɛ ewebii lɛ fã kɛjɛ Betel. Be ni eshwɛ gbɛ kukuoo ko lolo dani amɛshɛɔ Efrat lɛ, Rahel bɔi kɔ̃ɔmɔ, ni kɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ mli yawa.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
