translation_verse: Be ni fɔmɔ lɛ mli ewa nɛkɛ lɛ, yoofɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ Rahel akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei, ejaakɛ obaafɔ nuu ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Be ni Rahel etɔ biti ni eehe enyɔ lɛ, ewo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ Benoni; shi etsɛ wo lɛ Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Rahel gbo ni afu lɛ yɛ Efrat ni ji Betlehem gbɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ tɛ ko to okadi yɛ Rahel saŋ lɛ nɔ; ni no hewɔ lɛ, atsɛɔ lɛ Rahel saŋ nɔ tɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Israel ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yakob hu lɛ tsa egbɛfaa lɛ nɔ, ni eyashi ebuu lɛ yɛ Eder mɔɔ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ. Yakob bihii lɛ

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ruben yi mli etee ekɛ etsɛ hemɔ Bilha lɛ yawɔ; Yakob nu sane nɛɛ he. Yakob yɛ bihii nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Yakob ba etsɛ Isak ŋɔɔ yɛ Mamre loo Kiriat-Arba ni bɛŋkɛ Hebron lɛ, he ni Abraham kɛ Isak bato gbɔ yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esau ŋɔ Kanaan yei. Amɛ ji Hitnyo Elon biyoo Ada kɛ Hivnyo Zibeon bi Ana biyoo Oholibama lɛ,

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: kɛ Ishmael biyoo Basemat ni ji Nebaiot nyɛmiyoo lɛ.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Oholibama fɔ Yeush kɛ Yolam kɛ Kora. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Esau bihii ni efɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Esau ŋɔ eŋãmɛi kɛ ebihii kɛ ebiyei kɛ eshĩaŋbii fɛɛ kɛ etsinai kɛ ekooloi ni elɛɔ kɛ enitsumɔ kooloi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ enii fɛɛ ni ena yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni eshi enyɛmi Yakob kɛtee shikpɔŋ ko nɔ,

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ amɛnii ni amɛna lɛ fa tsɔ̃ fe bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ he kome. Amɛkooloi lɛ ahewɔ lɛ amɛhooo shikpɔŋ ni amɛbato gbɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Esau yahi Edom gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Shĩai ni jɛ Esau mli nɛ: Elifaz we, Esau kromɔbi lɛ, Teman we kɛ Omar we kɛ Zefo we kɛ Kenaz we,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: kɛ Kora we kɛ Gatam we kɛ Amalek we. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Elifaz lumɛi yɛ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni Ada shwiei ji amɛ.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Esau ŋa Oholibama we lɛ mli bii ji Yeush we kɛ Yalam we kɛ Kora we. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Ana biyoo Oholibama ni ji Esau ŋa lɛ shwiei bii.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi lɛ Esau bii ji amɛ, ni amɛwei nɛ. Esau lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ ji Edom lɛ. Seir Shwiei (

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Seir ni ji Hornyo lɛ shĩa lɛ mli bii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɛ: Lotan we kɛ Shobal we kɛ Zibeon we kɛ Ana we,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan shwiei ji Hori kɛ Heman; ni Lotan nyɛmi yoo ji Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Shobal shwiei ji Alvan kɛ Manahat kɛ Ebal kɛ Shefo kɛ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibeon bii ji Aia kɛ Ana. Mɔ nɛ ji Ana lɛ ni yana nuhiŋmɛi ni mli edɔ la yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ be ni elɛɔ etsɛ Zibeon tejii lɛ.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ana bii ji Dishon kɛ Oholibama.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dishon bii ji Hemdan kɛ Eshban kɛ Itram kɛ Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezer bii ji Bilhan kɛ Zaavan kɛ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Dishan bii ji Uz kɛ Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Horbii awei nɛ: Lotan we kɛ Shobal we kɛ Zibeon we kɛ Ana we,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: Oholibamabii, Elabii, Pinonbii,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: Kenazbii, Temanbii, Mibzarbii,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: Magdielbii, Irambii. Hei ni Edombii nɛɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko hi lɛ akɛ amɛgbɛi wo jɛi. Esau nɔŋŋ ji Edom ni ji Edombii atsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Yakob hi shi yɛ etsɛ gbɔtoo shikpɔŋ ni ji Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Ni nuu lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Amɛje biɛ, shi minu ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛhãa wɔyaa Dotan.’ ” No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef tiu enyɛmimɛi lɛ, ni eyanina amɛ yɛ Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Yakob sumɔɔ Yosef fe ebii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ, ejaakɛ egbɔlɛ mli binuu ni. Ekpɛ atade wuyaa fɛɛfɛo ko kɛ eniji kakadaji ehã Yosef.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ na akɛ amɛtsɛ sumɔɔ Yosef fe amɛ fɛɛ lɛ, amɛnyɛ lɛ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ lɛ awie yɛ tsuijurɔ naa dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Be ko lɛ Yosef la lamɔ ko ni be ni egba enyɛmimɛi lɛ lamɔ lɛ, ehã nyɛɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ lɛ lɛ mli wo wu moŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛboa lamɔ ni mila nɛɛ toi.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Wɔmiifimɔ ŋmãa kei yɛ ŋmɔshi; ni naa, miŋmãa ke lɛ te shi damɔ shi trɔmɔɔ, ni nyɛŋmãa kei lɛ babɔle miŋmãa ke lɛ, ni amɛkoto lɛ.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Aso osusuɔ akɛ obaatsɔ maŋtsɛ ni oye wɔnɔ lo?” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛ lɛ fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ elamɔi kɛ ewiemɔi lɛ ahewɔ.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni esaa ela lamɔ kroko hu, ni egba enyɛmimɛi lɛ ekɛɛ; “Naa, mila lamɔ ko ekoŋŋ. Mila ni hulu kɛ nyɔɔŋtsere kɛ ŋulamii nyɔŋma kɛ ekome bakoto mi.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Shi be ni egba etsɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ lamɔ lɛ, etsɛ kã ehiɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni lamɔ ola nɛɛ? Belɛ kotomɔ mi kɛ onyɛ kɛ onyɛmimɛi lɛ aaaba abakoto bo lo?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Enyɛmimɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ amɛwo amɛmli; shi etsɛ kɛ wiemɔ lɛ to enakutsoŋ. Ahɔ̃ɔ Yosef ni akɛ lɛ tee Ijipt

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Gbi ko be ni Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ etee amɛkwɛɔ amɛtsɛ toi lɛ yɛ Shekem lɛ,

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Te onyɛmimɛi lɛ miikwɛ toi yɛ Shekem? Ba ni matsu bo amɛŋɔɔ.” Ni Yosef here nɔ akɛ, “Naa mi, tsu mi.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni oyakwɛ akɛ onyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ toi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lo koni obakɛɛ mi.” Kɛkɛ ni etsu Yosef kɛjɛ Hebron jɔɔ lɛ mli; ni Yosef ba Shekem.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Nuu ko na Yosef ni eetsomlo yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni nuu lɛ bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni otaoɔ?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ, “Miitao minyɛmimɛi lɛ. Miikpa bo fai, tsɔ̃ɔmɔ mi he ni amɛlɛɔ amɛtoi lɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛna lɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ ni enako ebɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ, amɛkpãŋ eyinɔ akɛ amɛbaagbe lɛ.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Naa, lamɔiatsɛ lɛ baa lɛ.

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɛbaa, nyɛhãa wɔgbea lɛ ni wɔshɛa lɛ wɔfɔ̃a bui lɛ eko mli, ni wɔkɛɛ akɛ, ‘Kooloo fɔŋ ko eye lɛ,’ koni wɔkwɛ kɛji elamɔi lɛ aaaba mli.”

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Ruben nu yiŋ ni ato lɛ, akɛni eetao ni ejie lɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkahãa wɔgbea lɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Ruben saa kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashwiea lá shi, shi moŋ nyɛkɛ lɛ awoa bu nɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋa nɛɛ nɔ lɛ mli, ni nyɛkafea lɛ efɔŋ ko!” Ruben kɛɛ enɛ bɔ ni afee ni ejie lɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ koni ekɛ lɛ ayahã etsɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef shɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ, amɛkpɔlɔ atade wuyaa fɛɛfɛo kɛ eniji kakadaji lɛ yɛ ehe,

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛho amɛtara shi ni amɛbɔi niyeli. Be ni amɛwo amɛhiɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛna Ishmaelbii gbɛnyiɛlɔi aku ko ni jɛ Gilead miiba kɛ amɛyoomai ni tere tsofakɛŋmai kɛ gbonyowoo tsofa kɛ ohɛ ni jeɔ ŋma kɛmiiya Ijipt.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ sɛɛ wɔɔna yɛ mli kɛji wɔgbe wɔnyɛmi lɛ ni wɔtsimɔ nɔ?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Nyɛbaa, nyɛhãa wɔhɔɔa lɛ wɔhã Ishmaelbii lɛ; shi nyɛkahãa wɔkɛ wɔnine miita ehe, ejaakɛ wɔnyɛmi kɛ wɔla ji lɛ.” Ni enyɛmimɛi lɛ bo lɛ toi.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Ruben ku esɛɛ kɛba bu lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yosef bɛ bu lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni Ruben gbala ehe atadei lɛ,

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: ni eku esɛɛ kɛba enyɛmimɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ; “Gbekɛ lɛ bɛ jɛi; te mafee tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɔlɔ Yosef atade lɛ, ni amɛgbe too kpakpo ko ni amɛkɛ atade lɛ tsɔ la lɛ mli.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛ atade wuyaa fɛɛfɛo lɛ tsu ni akɛyatsɔ̃ɔ amɛtsɛ; amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Wɔna nii nɛɛ, kwɛmɔ akɛ obi lɛ atade lɛ ni loo jeee noŋ.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ni Yakob yoo atade lɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Mibi lɛ atade lɛ ni! Kooloo kakawua ko eye lɛ; tserɛmɔ etserɛ Yosef mli nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ni Yakob gbala ehe atade lɛ, ni ekɔ kpekpe emia ehɛ, ni eye ebi lɛ he ŋkɔmɔ gbii pii.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Ebihii kɛ ebiyei lɛ fɛɛ te shi koni amɛbashɛje emii, shi ekpɛlɛɛɛ miishɛjemɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ŋkɔmɔyeli mikɛaaya ayanina mibi lɛ yɛ gbohiiaje.” Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ Yosef tsɛ tsɔ efo lɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Midianbii lɛ eyahɔ̃ɔ Yosef yɛ Ijipt amɛhã Potifar ni ji Farao piafonyo kɛ eblafoiatsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Yuda shi enyɛmimɛi lɛ ni eyahi Adullamnyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Hira lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Yuda na Kanaannyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Shua lɛ biyoo ko yɛ jɛi; eŋɔ oblayoo lɛ efee eŋa.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Oblayoo lɛ na musu ni efɔ binuu. Yuda wo gbekɛ lɛ Er.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ na musu ekoŋŋ. Efɔ binuu ni ewo lɛ Onan.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Esaa efɔ binuu ekoŋŋ ni ewo lɛ Shela. Eyɛ Akzib be ni efɔ gbekɛ nuu lɛ.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Yuda ŋɔ yoo ehã Er, ebi kromɔ lɛ. Yoo lɛ gbɛi ji Tamar.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Shi Er, Yuda kromɔ lɛ fee ehe gbɔmɔ fɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni Yehowa gbe lɛ.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛɛ Onan akɛ, “Ŋɔɔ onyɛmi nuu lɛ ŋa lɛ akɛ kulayeli ŋa, koni owo shwiei ohã onyɛmi nuu lɛ.”

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Shi Onan le akɛ bii lɛ ebatsɔ̃ŋ enɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ etee enyɛmi lɛ ŋa lɛ ŋɔɔ ekɛ lɛ yawɔ lɛ, ejieɔ ehe nu lɛ eshwieɔ shikpɔŋ efiteɔ, koni ekahã enyɛmi lɛ miina shwiei.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni efee lɛ, efɔŋ ni yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; no hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa gbe Onan hu.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛɛ eshaayoo Tamar akɛ, “Yaahi shi akɛ okulafo yɛ otsɛ we lɛ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni mibi Shela lɛ aaada.” Ekɛɛ enɛ, ejaakɛ eeshe gbeyei akɛ Shela hu baagbo tamɔ enyɛmimɛi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Tamar tee eyahi etsɛ we lɛ.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Yɛ mli aahu lɛ, Yuda ŋa Shua biyoo lɛ bagbo; ni be ni Yuda etse etsui eŋmɛ emli lɛ, ekɛ enaanyo Hira, Adullamnyo lɛ, yiŋ tee etoohetsɔi kulɔi lɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Timna.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ayakɛɛ Tamar akɛ, “Oshaanuu miiya Timna eyaku etoi lɛ ahe tsɔi.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Tamar jie ekulafeemɔ atadei lɛ yɛ ehe efɔ shi, ni ekɛ hiɛhaanɔ ha ehiɛ, ni ekɛ mama bla ehe koni akayoo lɛ; ni eyata shi yɛ Enaim klotia, yɛ Timna gbɛ lɛ toi ejaakɛ ena akɛ Shela eda, shi kɛ̃lɛ aŋɔɔɔ lɛ, Tamar lɛ, ahãaa Shela gbãlã.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Be ni Yuda na Tamar lɛ, esusu akɛ yoo ajwamãŋ ko ni, ejaakɛ eha ehiɛ.

english_verse: and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
translation_verse: Yuda gba kɛtee eŋɔɔ yɛ gbɛ lɛ toi, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, hã ni maba oŋɔɔ,” ejaakɛ eleee akɛ eshaayoo lɛ ni. Tamar bi Yuda akɛ, “Mɛni obaahã mi koni okɛ mi ayawɔ?”

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Yuda to he akɛ, “Mahã amɔ too kpakpo bi ko yɛ toi lɛ ateŋ abahã bo.” Ni Tamar kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ nɔ ko aaato mi awaba kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni ooohã akɛ too lɛ aba lɛ.”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Yuda bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni mikɛto bo awaba lɛ?” Tamar to he akɛ, “Owolonaasɔomɔnɔ kɛ ehe kpãa lɛ kɛ odɛhiɛmɔtso lɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛ nibii lɛ hã Tamar, ni etee ekɛ lɛ yawɔ. Fee sɛɛ lɛ Tamar na musu,

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Tamar te shi, ni eyiŋ etee. Eyajie ehiɛhaanɔ lɛ efɔ shi, ni ekɔ ekulafeemɔ atade lɛ ewo.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Yuda kɛ too kpakpo bi lɛ hã enaanyo Adullamnyo lɛ kɛtee koni eyahe ewabatoo nii lɛ yɛ Tamar dɛŋ; shi enaanyo lɛ enaaa Tamar.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ebi maŋbii komɛi ni yɔɔ Enaim lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ yoo ajwamãŋ lɛ ni ta Enaim gbɛ lɛ toi lɛ yɔɔ?” Amɛhã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Yoo ajwamãŋ ko bɛ biɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Yuda naanyo lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Yuda ŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minaaa lɛ, ni asaŋ jɛibii lɛ kɛɛ, ‘Yoo ajwamãŋ ko bɛ biɛ nɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Yuda kɛɛ akɛ, “Hã ni eŋɔ kɛya, kɛjeee nakai lɛ wɔhiɛ aaashwie shi. Mihã okɛ too kpakpo bi lɛ tee, ni onaaa lɛ.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ̃ lɛ, abakɛɛ Yuda akɛ, “Oshaayoo Tamar eyabɔ ajwamãŋ, ni nɔ ni ena yɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ mli ji akɛ ena musu.” Yuda fã akɛ, “Amɔ lɛ kɛje kpo koni ashã lɛ.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ Tamar jeɔ kpo kɛbaa lɛ, etsu atee eshaanuu Yuda ŋɔɔ ayakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nuu mɔ ni nibii ji enɛɛmɛi lɛ, lɛ mikɛna musu lɛ.” Asaŋ Tamar kɛɛ, “Kwɛmɔ akɛ oooyoo mɔ ni nibii ji wolonaasɔomɔnɔ nɛɛ kɛ ehe kpãa nɛɛ kɛ tso nɛɛ lo?”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Yuda yoo nibii lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Akɛni miŋɔɔɔ lɛ mihãaa mibi Shela lɛ esane ja.” Ni Yuda etaaa Tamar he dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Be ni efɔɔ lɛ, hãaji lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome jie enine kɛje kpo, ni yoofɔlɔ lɛ mɔ mli. Ekɛ kpãa tsuru fi nine lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Mɔnɛ tsutsu ba.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Shi abifao lɛ su enine lɛ, kɛkɛ ni enyɛmi lɛ je kpo kɛba, ni yoofɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Bo diɛŋtsɛ ogbu gbɛ kɛje kpo.” Ni awo gbekɛ lɛ Perez.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, enyɛmi lɛ ni kpãa tsuru lɛ yɔɔ enineshi lɛ hu ba, ni awo lɛ Zera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ishmaelbii lɛ kɛ Yosef tee Ijipt, ni amɛyahɔ̃ɔ lɛ amɛhã Potifar, ni ji Farao piafonyo kɛ eblafoiatsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Enuŋtsɔ Ijiptnyo lɛ we lɛ eyɔɔ. Potifar na akɛ Yehowa kɛ Yosef yɛ, ni ehãa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni Yosef feɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ edɛŋ.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yosef na hiɛ yɛ enuŋtsɔ lɛ hiɛ, ni lɛ esɔ̃mɔɔ enuŋtsɔ lɛ. Potifar fee Yosef ewe lɛ nɔkwɛlɔ nukpa ni etu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ewo edɛŋ.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Potifar tu enibii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ewo Yosef dɛŋ, ni egbaaa ehe naa yɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he ja nɔ ni ebaaye kɛkɛ. Kɛji ona Yosef lɛ ehe yɛ fɛo naakpa.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Yɛ mli aahu lɛ, enuŋtsɔ lɛ ŋa lɛ kɛ hiŋmɛi ko bɔi Yosef kwɛmɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ mi abawɔ.”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Ni Yosef ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ; shi ekɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ gbaaa ehe naa yɛ enɔ ko nɔ ko he yɛ shĩa nɛɛ, ejaakɛ etu enii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ewo midɛŋ.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Ehã mi hewalɛ yɛ shĩa nɛɛ nɔ tamɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ, ni ekãmãaa mi nɔ ko nɔ ko akɛ ja bo pɛ kɛkɛ; ejaakɛ bo lɛ eŋa ji bo. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ mɔ ni mafee efɔŋ kpeteŋkple ni tamɔ nɛkɛ hu ni mafee esha mashi Nyɔŋmɔ hu?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ hiɛ Yosef kɛ wiemɔ daa nɛɛ, shi Yosef eŋɔɔɔ nɔ ni ekɛ lɛ awɔ aloo ebɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ gbi lɛ eko lɛ, Yosef tee shĩa lɛ eyaatsu nii. Shĩa lɛ mli bii lɛ ekoeko bɛ.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni yoo lɛ mɔ Yosef atade lɛ mli ni ekɛɛ, “Okɛ mi abawɔ!” Shi Yosef shi etade lɛ ewo edɛŋ, ni ejo foi kɛje kpo.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: etsɛ eshiaŋ bii lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbakwɛa nɔ ko! Miwu eyaŋɔ Hebrinyo bi nɛɛ kɛba shĩa nɛɛ koni ebaye wɔhe fɛo. Eba miŋɔɔ koni ekɛ mi abawɔ, ni mibolɔ waa.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni ena akɛ miwo migbee nɔ miibolɔ waa lɛ, eshi etade lɛ efɔ̃ mimasɛi, ni ejo foi kɛje kpo.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ Yosef atade lɛ fɔ̃ emasɛi kɛyashi Yosef nuŋtsɔ lɛ ba shĩa.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eyajaje sane lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ ewu lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɔŋnuu Hebrinyo lɛ ni okɛba shĩa nɛɛ lɛ, eba ni ebahɔlɔ mi.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Shi be ni mibo waa lɛ, eshi etade lɛ ehã mi, ni ejo foi.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ni Yosef nuŋtsɔ lɛ mɔ lɛ, ni eyawo lɛ tsuŋ yɛ he ni awoɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ gboklɛfoi atsuŋ yɛ lɛ, jɛi Yosef hi.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kɛ Yosef yɛ. Ena lɛ mɔbɔ ni ehã ena hiɛ yɛ gboklɛfoi akwɛlɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Gboklɛfoi akwɛlɔ lɛ tu gboklɛfoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ ewo Yosef dɛŋ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni atsuɔ yɛ jɛi lɛ, Yosef ni kwɛɔ nɔ.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Gboklɛfoi akwɛlɔ lɛ gbaaa ehe naa yɛ nii ni etu ewo Yosef dɛŋ lɛ he, ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ Yosef yɛ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efeɔ lɛ, Yehowa hãa eyeɔ omanye.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: ni eyawo amɛ tsuŋ yɛ blafoiatsɛ lɛ shĩa yɛ gboklɛfoi atsu lɛ mli he ni akɛ Yosef ewo lɛ.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Blafoiatsɛ lɛ tu piafoi lɛ ewo Yosef dɛŋ ni ekwɛɔ amɛnɔ. Piafoi enyɔ lɛ ye be kplaŋŋ yɛ tsu lɛ mli.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef tee amɛŋɔɔ leebi lɛ, eyoo akɛ amɛfee mɔbɔmɔbɔ.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔla lamɔi komɛi, ni mɔ ko bɛ ni aaatsɔ̃ɔ wɔ shishi.” Yosef kɛɛ, “Ani lamɔ shishitsɔɔmɔ lɛ jeee Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ ni? Nyɛfainɛ, nyɛgbaa mi lamɔi lɛ!”

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, daawolɔi anukpa lɛ gba Yosef elamɔ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Milamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mina ni waintso ko ma mihiɛ.

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: Egbala niji etɛ̃, amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efimɔ afofro kpɔi, ni egba afofro, ni ewo wainyibii shabii ni etsu.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Mihiɛ Farao kpulu mli; ni mitserɛ wain yibii lɛ, ni miŋa miwo kpulu lɛ mli, kɛkɛ ni mikɛ kpulu lɛ hã Farao.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa olamɔ lɛ shishitsɔɔmɔ. Niji etɛ̃ lɛ damɔ shi hã gbii etɛ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Biɛ gbii etɛ̃ lɛ, Farao aaajie bo yɛ tsuŋ, ni ekɛ bo aaayato ogbɛhe lɛ ekoŋŋ ni okɛ Farao kpulu lɛ aaawo edɛŋ tamɔ bɔ ni ofeɔ sa lɛ be ni bo ji edãawolɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji ehi ehã bo lɛ, miikpa bo fai koni okai mi, ni omli ahi ahã mi koni otsi mitã otsɔ̃ɔ Farao koni abajie mi yɛ tsu nɛɛŋ.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Shi ju aju mi yɛ Hebribii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni biɛ nɛɛ hu mifeko nɔ ko ni sa akɛ akɛ mi awo kpabuŋ nɛɛŋ.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Be ni abolooshãlɔi anukpa lɛ na akɛ lamɔ lɛ shishitsɔɔmɔ lɛ yɛ miishɛɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Mi hu mila lamɔ ko. Milamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mina ni mitere bodobodo kɛntɛŋi etɛ̃.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Kɛntɛŋ ni ma yiteŋ tɔɔ lɛ, niyenii srɔtoi fɛɛ ni ashãa ahãa Farao lɛ yɛ mli, ni loofɔji miiye yɛ kɛntɛŋ lɛ mli yɛ miyiteŋ.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Yosef hã hetoo ni ekɛɛ, “Naa olamɔ lɛ shishitsɔɔmɔ. Kɛntɛŋi etɛ̃ lɛ damɔ shi hã gbii etɛ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Biɛ gbii etɛ̃ lɛ, Farao aaajie bo yɛ tsuŋ ni eeefo oyi ni ekɛ bo aaatsotsoro tso nɔ, ni loofɔji aaaye oheloo.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ, Farao fɔmɔgbi ni. Eŋmɛ etsuji fɛɛ okplɔ̃ ni ejie edãawolɔi anukpa lɛ kɛ ebolooshãlɔi anukpa lɛ yɛ tsuŋ yɛ enukpai lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: Ehã edãawolɔi anukpa lɛ yaye egbɛhe lɛ ekoŋŋ; ni lɛ ekɛ kpulu lɛ wo Farao dɛŋ.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Shi abolooshãlɔi anukpa lɛ, esɛŋ lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni Yosef tsɔ̃ɔ amɛlamɔi lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Shi dãawolɔ nukpa lɛ eyakaiii Yosef; ehiɛ kpa enɔ.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Afii naakplɔi enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Farao la lamɔ ko. Ela ni edamɔ Nilo faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ naa, tsinayei dukudukuu fɛɛfɛji kpawo fã kpo kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli, ni amɛyabɔi niyeli yɛ faa naa glãi lɛ amli.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Esaa ewɔ ni ela ekoŋŋ. Lamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ena ni abele tso kome ekpɛ sɛɛbii kpawo ni eba kpokploo.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, abele tso ni ekpɛ sɛɛbii kpawo ni bokã kɔɔyɔɔ egbi amɛ kekree hu kwɛ̃.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni abele sɛɛbii kpawo ni egbi kekree lɛ mii abele sɛɛbii ni eba kpokploo lɛ. Farao hiɛ tsɛ̃ ni ena akɛ lamɔ ni.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Leebi lɛ etsui bɔ̃i yeli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etsu ayatsɛ Ijipt nifeelɔi lɛ kɛ nilelɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛba, ni egba amɛ elamɔ lɛ; shi amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛɛɛ Farao lamɔ lɛ shishi etsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni dãawolɔ nukpa lɛ kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Mikai mitɔ̃mɔ ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Omli fu wɔ, otsuji lɛ, ni owo wɔ tsuŋ yɛ blafoiatsɛ lɛ we lɛ, mi kɛ abolooshãlɔ nukpa lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: Be ni wɔyɔɔ jɛi lɛ, mi kɛ lɛ fɛɛ la gbi ko nyɔɔŋ, wɔteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ elamɔ kɛ lamɔ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Hebrinyo oblanyo ko ni ji blafoiatsɛ lɛ tsulɔ lɛ kɛ wɔ yɔɔ jɛi. Wɔgba wɔlamɔi lɛ wɔtsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ni etsɔ̃ɔ wɔ shishi, mɔ nɛ lamɔ kɛ eshishi, mɔ nɛ hu lamɔ kɛ eshishi.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni etsɔ̃ɔ shishi lɛ, eba mli nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Akɛ mita migbɛhe ekoŋŋ, ni abolooshãlɔ nukpa lɛ, lɛ lɛ, asɛŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao tsu ayatsɛ Yosef. Ajie lɛ yɛ gboklɛfoi akpabuŋ lɛ mli oya kɛba; ni eshɛ eyi ni etsake etade, ni eba ebadamɔ Farao hiɛ.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Farao kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Mila lamɔ ko, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛɛɛ mi shishi atsɔ̃ɔ. Minu ni akɛɛ yɛ ohe akɛ kɛji onu lamɔ ko lɛ, onyɛɔ shishi otsɔ̃ɔ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Yosef here Farao nɔ akɛ, “Jeee mi mihewalɛ naa, shi moŋ Nyɔŋmɔ ni aaahã Farao hetoo ni hi.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Milamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, midamɔ Nilo Faa lɛ naa,

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: ni tsinayei fɛɛfɛji kpawo ni amɛshwishwii dukudukuu fã kpo kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli, ni amɛbɔi niyeli yɛ faa lɛ naa glãi lɛ amli.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni tsinayei krokomɛi kpawo hu nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛba; amɛnii yɛ mɔbɔ, amɛhe yɛ nyaŋemɔ naakpa ni amɛtãrãtãrãa loo, bɔ ni minako amɛhenɔ pɛŋ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛye amɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛmusu etsɔ̃ɔɔ kwraa akɛ amɛye nɔ ko ejaakɛ amɛkã he amɛyɛ kanyakanya tamɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛkɛ ni mihiɛ tsɛ̃.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Misaa mina yɛ lamɔ mli ni abele sɛɛbii kpokploo kpawo ba tso kome yi.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, naa abele sɛɛbii kpawo ni ekwɛ̃. Abele sɛɛbii nɛɛ, nii bɛ yi ni amɛyɛ legelege ni bokã kɔɔyɔɔ egbi amɛ kekree.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Abeletsei legelegei nɛɛ mii abele sɛɛbii kpokplokpoo kpawo lɛ. Migba lamɔ nɛɛ mitsɔ̃ɔ nifeelɔi lɛ, shi amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko naaa he nɔ ko ekɛɛ mi.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Farao, lamɔi lɛ ekome ni. Nyɔŋmɔ ejie nɔ ni ebaafee kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Farao.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Tsinai kpakpai kpawo lɛ damɔ shi hã afii kpakpai kpawo, ni abele sɛɛbii kpakpai kpawo lɛ hu damɔ shi hã afii kpakpai kpawo, lamɔ lɛ lamɔ kome ni.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Tsinai kpawo ni etarataraa loo ni he yɔɔ nyaŋemɔ ni nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ ba lɛ, afii kpawo ni; ni abeletsei kpawo ni nɔ ko bɛ amɛsɛɛbii lɛ ayi ni bokã kɔɔyɔɔ egbi amɛ kekree lɛ damɔ shi hã hɔmɔyeli afii kpawo.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Enɛ ji nɔ ni mikɛɛ Farao akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ etsɔ̃ɔ Farao nɔ ni ebaafee lɛ.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Naa, afii kpawo miiba ni abaana niyenii babaoo yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Hɔmɔ ni baanyiɛ sɛɛ aba Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haŋ akai ŋmãa kpɔtɔɔ ni ba lɛ dɔŋŋ ejaakɛ enaa baawa naakpa.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Akɛni akɛ lamɔi srɔtoi enyɔ nɛɛ miitsɔ̃ɔ Farao nɔ koome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsɔ̃ɔ akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ yiŋtoo lɛ baaba mli lɛɛlɛŋ, ni etsɛŋ ni ebaaba mli.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ hã Farao atao mɔ ko ni hiɛ kã shi, ni ele nii koni ehã lɛ ekwɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Hã Farao ato nɔkwɛlɔi krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afii kpawo ni niyenii baaba kpɔtɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Farao aŋɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ amlijaa enumɔ mli ekome eto.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Asaŋ hã ni nɔkwɛlɔi lɛ abua niyenii fɛɛ ni aaana yɛ nakai afii kpakpai ni baaba lɛ amli lɛ naa; amɛbua abele naa amɛto koni no afee niyenii ni akɛto yɛ maji lɛ amli.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Aŋɔ nakai niyenii lɛ ato sɛɛ ahã shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ afii kpawo lɛ ni baaba Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ koni hɔmɔ lɛ akakpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ ahiɛ.” Ato Yosef Amralo yɛ Ijipt

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Wiemɔ lɛ sa Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ;

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: ni Farao kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Ani wɔɔnyɛ wɔna mɔ ko ni Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ yɔɔ emli tamɔ mɔnɛ?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Farao kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ ejie enɛ fɛɛ kpo etsɔ̃ɔ bo lɛ, belɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni hiɛ kã shi ni le nii tamɔ bo.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Bo obaaye miwe lɛ nɔ, ni bo toi mimaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ aaabo; sɛi lɛ gbɛfaŋ pɛ mafe bo yɛ.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao jie ewolonaasɔomɔ ga lɛ yɛ ewao, ni ekɛwo Yosef wao; ewula lɛ kɛ klala fɛɛfɛo atadei ni ekɛ shika kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ ŋmɛ ekuɛ.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ehã Yosef ta eshwiili ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni abɔ oshe kɛnyiɛ Yosef hiɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkotoa lɛ! Nyɛkotoa lɛ!” No hewɔ lɛ, Farao wo Yosef Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ onukpa.

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Farao wo Yosef Ijipt gbɛi akɛ Zafenat-Panea; ni eŋɔ Asenat, Heliopolis maŋ lɛ mli Osɔfo Potifera lɛ biyoo lɛ ehã lɛ gbãlã. Ni Yosef fãa gbɛ eyakpaa Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Niyenii kpɔtɔɔ afii kpawo lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ba niyenii babaoo kɛteke nɔ.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Yosef bua abele babaoo diɛŋtsɛ ni fa tamɔ ŋshɔnaa shia naa eto kɛyashi beyinɔ ni efɔ̃ɔ abele lɛ naa buu ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ eyikulɛ naa abu dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Dani hɔmɔ afii lɛ ba lɛ, Yosef efɔ bihii enyɔ. Ekɛ Asenat, Heliopolis maŋ lɛ Osɔfo Potifera biyoo lɛ, fɔ amɛ.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Yosef wo ekromɔbi lɛ Manase ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ehã mihiɛ ekpa mihaomɔ lɛ kɛ mitsɛ we lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ewo mɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ Efraim ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ehã miwo shwiei yɛ mimanehulu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: tamɔ bɔ ni Yosef ekɛɛ lɛ. Hɔmɔ ba shikpɔji krokomɛi fɛɛ nɔ; shi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ niyenii yɛ.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni hɔmɔ ba Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ fo tsɛ Farao ni ehã amɛ niyenii. Farao kɛɛ Ijiptbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa Yosef ŋɔɔ, ni nɔ ni eeekɛɛ nyɛ lɛ, nyɛfea.”

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni hɔmɔ lɛ egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Yosef gbele ŋmaatoohei lɛ fɛɛ anaa, ni ehɔ̃ɔ abele ehã Ijiptbii lɛ ejaakɛ hɔmɔ lɛ naa wa naakpa yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Asaŋ mɛi jɛ majimaji fɛɛ anɔ kɛba Ijipt koni amɛbahe abele yɛ Yosef ŋɔɔ yɛ Ijipt ejaakɛ hɔmɔ lɛ naa wa naakpa yɛ je lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob na le akɛ abele yɛ Ijipt lɛ, ekɛɛ ebii lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛkwɛkwɛɔ nyɛhiɛ gãagãa nɛkɛ?”

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Etee nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, minu akɛ abele yɛ Ijipt; nyɛyaa jɛi ni nyɛyahea abele nyɛbahãa wɔ koni wɔyi ana wala ni wɔkagboi.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef nyɛmimɛi ni ji etsɛbii nyɔŋma lɛ yiŋ kɛtee Ijipt koni amɛyahe abele.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Shi Yakob hãaa Benyamin, Yosef nyɛbi etsɛbi lɛ, kɛ etsɛbii krokomɛi lɛ aya, ejaakɛ ekɛɛ, “Koni aleee nɔ osharã ko akayasharã lɛ.”

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob bii lɛ yɛ mɛi ni ba abelehemɔ lɛ ateŋ; ejaakɛ hɔmɔ lɛ eba Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Yosef ji lumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni lɛ ehɔ̃ɔ abele ehãa mɛi fɛɛ. Enyɛmimɛi lɛ ba, ni amɛbakoto lɛ, ni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ bumɔ shi.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef kai lamɔi ni ela yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Saralɔi ji nyɛ; nyɛba ni nyɛbakwɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ yayaiaŋ.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Amɛhã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, dabi, shi moŋ niyenii hemɔ otsuji ba.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Nuu kome bii ji wɔ fɛɛ; anɔkwafoi ji wɔ; jeee saralɔi ji otsuji lɛ.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Dabi, nyɛba nyɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yayaiaŋ.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔ otsuji lɛ, nyɛmimɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ ji wɔ, nuu kome bii ji wɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; wɔteŋ gbekɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ wɔtsɛ ŋɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ; ni mɔ kome bɛ jeŋ.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Shi Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni mikɛɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɛ: Saralɔi ji nyɛ.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni akɛaana nyɛnɔkwale nɛ. Mina Farao akɛ nyɛjeŋ biɛ nyɛyaŋ, ja nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ ebashɛ biɛ dã.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Nyɛtsua nyɛteŋ mɔ kome ni eyaŋɔa nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ kɛba be mli ni nyɛ lɛ awo nyɛ kpabuŋ lɛ, koni akɛkpa nyɛ wiemɔi lɛ shi akɛ anɔkwafoi ji nyɛ lo; kɛjeee nakai lɛ, mina Farao akɛ saralɔi ji nyɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ewo amɛ fɛɛ tsuŋ gbii etɛ̃.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yosef kɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛfea nɔ ni mibakɛɛ nɛɛ, koni nyɛyi ana wala, shi mi lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishelɔ ji mi.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Kɛ anɔkwafoi ji nyɛ lɛ, nyɛhãa atsĩa nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome naa yɛ kpabuŋ lɛ mli, koni nyɛ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ nyɛŋɔ abele kɛya yɛ hɔmɔ ni yɔɔ nyɛshĩai lɛ hewɔ,

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ aba miŋɔɔ. No akɛaana akɛ nyɛwiemɔi lɛ anɔkwale ni, koni nyɛkagboi.” Amɛfee nakai.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Lɛɛlɛŋ, wɔyeɔ fɔ yɛ wɔnyɛmi lɛ hewɔ akɛni wɔna bɔ ni esusuma hao ni ekpa wɔ fai aahu ni wɔbooo toi lɛ. No hewɔ ni nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ eba wɔnɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ruben here amɛ nɔ akɛ, “Ani mikɛɛɛ nyɛ akɛ nyɛkafea gbekɛ lɛ esha ko, ni nyɛbooo toi? No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ ela shi abiɔ nɛɛ!”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Shi amɛleee akɛ Yosef enu nɔ ni amɛwieɔ lɛ shishi ejaakɛ mɔ ko yɛ ni jieɔ enaa.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef tsɔ̃ ehe kɛje amɛmasɛi ni eyafo. Eku esɛɛ kɛba amɛŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ amɛ bawie. Ejie Simeon yɛ amɛteŋ ni efi lɛ yɛ amɛhiɛ. Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee Kanaan

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef fã akɛ awo amɛkotokui lɛ amli abele obɔ̃bɔ̃, ni akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ shika aku sɛɛ awo ekotoku mli ekoŋŋ. Efã hu akɛ ahã amɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii. Ni afee nakai ahã amɛ.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjatsui lɛ tere amɛtejii lɛ, ni amɛyi gbɛ.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshɛ shitoohe ko ni amɛteŋ mɔ kome fɛne ekotoku naa ni ebaahã eteji niyenii lɛ, ena eshika lɛ kã abele lɛ nɔ yɛ ekotoku lɛ mli,

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Akpale mishika lɛ ahã mi, ni naa, no po yɔɔ mikotoku lɛ mli nɛɛ!” Enɛ hã amɛtsui fã kɛ hekpokpomɔ ni amɛbibii amɛhe akɛ, “Mɛni ji enɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ efee wɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Be ni amɛbashɛ amɛtsɛ Yakob ŋɔɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛgba lɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ba amɛnɔ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: “Nuu lɛ ni ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ lɛ hãhã ehiɛ ewo wɔ, ni ebu wɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ saralɔi.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Shi wɔkɛɛ lɛ akɛ ‘Anɔkwafoi ji wɔ; jeee saralɔi ji wɔ.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ ji wɔ, nuu kome musuŋ bii ji wɔ, mɔ kome bɛ jeŋ, ni gbekɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ wɔtsɛ ŋɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ!’

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nuu lɛ ni ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni mikɛbaana akɛ anɔkwafoi ji nyɛ nɛ: nyɛshĩa nyɛteŋ mɔ kome nyɛhãa mi ni nyɛŋɔa abele yɛ hɔmɔ ni yɔɔ nyɛshĩai amli lɛ hewɔ kɛyaa.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ abaa miŋɔɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ mibana akɛ jeee saralɔi ji nyɛ shi moŋ anɔkwafoi, koni majie nyɛnyɛmi lɛ mahã nyɛ ni nyɛye jara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛ jie amɛkotokui lɛ amli nii lɛ, naa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ shika ni afi kã ekotoku mli. Be ni amɛkɛ amɛtsɛ fɛɛ na shika ni afimɔfimɔɔ nɛɛ lɛ, amɛshe gbeyei.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Ni amɛtsɛ Yakob kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkpakpaa mibii yɛ mihe, Yosef bɛ, ni Simeon bɛ, ni nyɛbaaŋɔ Benyamin hu kɛya. Enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ lɛ haomɔ eji kɛhã mi.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ruben kɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Kɛ mikɛ Benyamin ekuuu sɛɛ ebahãaa bo lɛ, no lɛ gbee mibihii enyɔ lɛ; bo lɛ tuu lɛ owo midɛŋ, ni mikɛ lɛ baaku sɛɛ abahã bo ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Shi Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Mibi lɛ kɛ nyɛ eyaŋ ejaakɛ enyɛmi lɛ egbo, ni lɛ ekome pɛ eshwɛ; kɛji oshara ko yasharã lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni nyɛyaanyiɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ he ni miyi eyɛ kɛshɛ nɛɛ, nyɛbaahã magbo kɛ awerɛhoo sɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Hɔmɔ lɛ naa wa lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni amɛye amɛbele ni amɛkɛjɛ Ijipt kɛba lɛ etã lɛ, amɛtsɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa ekoŋŋ, nyɛyahea niyenii fioo nyɛbahãa wɔ.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: shi kɛji ohaŋ eya lɛ, no lɛ wɔyaŋ, ejaakɛ nuu lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛnaŋ mihiɛ akɛ ja nyɛnyɛmi lɛ fata nyɛhe kɛba dã.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Ni Yakob kɛɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛfee mi efɔŋ nɛkɛ akɛ nyɛtsi tã nyɛkɛɛ nuu lɛ akɛ nyɛyɛ nyɛmi kroko hu lɛ?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Amɛto he akɛ, “Nuu lɛ bi wɔ kɛ wɔweku he sane fitsofitso akɛ, ‘Ani nyɛtsɛ yɛ jeŋ lolo? Ani nyɛyɛ nyɛminuu kroko hu?’ Ni wɔhã lɛ nɛkɛ sanebimɔi nɛɛ ahetoo. Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔle akɛ eeekɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmi lɛ abaa’ lɛ?”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛɛ etsɛ Yakob akɛ, “Okɛ gbekɛ lɛ awo midɛŋ ni wɔyi mli kɛya, koni wɔ kɛ bo kɛ wɔbii bibii lɛ ayi ana wala, ni wɔkagboi.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Mikɛ miwala baato awaba yɛ enajiaŋ; bi eshi yɛ midɛŋ. Kɛji mikɛ lɛ ekuuu sɛɛ ebahãaa bo ni ona lɛ kɛ ohiŋmɛi lɛ, no lɛ mi, maye eyi sɔ̃ kɛya naanɔ,

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ kɛjeee shi wɔshashao lɛ kulɛ benɛ wɔtee Ijipt wɔba shii enyɔ momo.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛtsɛ Yakob kɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji nakai ni lɛ, no lɛ bɔ ni nyɛbaafee nɛ: nyɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ nibii kpakpai lɛ eko awoa nyɛjatsui amli koni nyɛkɛyakea nuu lɛ: gbonyowoo tsofa fioo, wo fioo, tso mli amã fioo, tsofakɛŋma, kɛ ohɛ ni jeɔ ŋma kɛ amitsrɔbi kɛ ŋmɛ.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Asaŋ shika ni nyɛkɛyaahe nii lɛ, nyɛhiɛa nakai toi enyɔ, ejaakɛ shika lɛ ni akɛwo nyɛkotokui amli lɛ, esa akɛ nyɛkɛku sɛɛ kɛya, benɛ ekolɛ hiɛ ni je nɔ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Nyɛŋɔa nyɛnyɛmi lɛ hu, ni nyɛyia mli nyɛyaa nuu lɛ ŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Aba mli akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ ahã nuu lɛ musuŋ atsɔ̃ lɛ yɛ nyɛhe, koni eŋmɛɛ nyɛnyɛmi mɔ kome lɛ kɛ Benyamin he ehã nyɛ. Shi mi lɛ, kɛji aaakpakpaa mibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ mihe jiŋŋ, efeee nɔ ko.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob bii lɛ ŋɔ nikeenii lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ shika falɛ toi enyɔ yɛ amɛdɛŋ, kɛ Benyamin; ni amɛŋɔ shwie nɔ kɛtee Ijipt, ni amɛyashɛ Yosef hiɛ.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef na Benyamin fata amɛhe lɛ, ekɛɛ ewe lɛ sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ nɛkɛ hii nɛɛ aya shĩa, ni omɔ kooloo okɛfee niyenii oto, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ mi baaye nii shwane nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ fee bɔ ni Yosef kɛɛ lɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ tee shĩa lɛ.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Shi amɛshe gbeyei yɛ Yosef shĩa lɛ ni akɛ amɛ tee lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Shika lɛ ni aku sɛɛ akɛwo wɔkotokui lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ be ni wɔba lɛ hewɔ akɛ wɔ ba biɛ nɛɛ, koni etao sane eshi wɔ koni ekɛ wɔ aye koni eŋɔ wɔ efee enyɔji ni eshɔ̃ wɔtejii lɛ yɛ wɔdɛŋ.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsi amɛbɛŋkɛ Yosef we lɛ sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ wie yɛ shĩa lɛ shinaa lɛ shi

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: amɛkɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, wɔnuŋtsɔ, klɛŋklɛŋ be ni wɔbahe niyenii lɛ

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: ni wɔyashɛ shitoohe ko ni wɔfɛne wɔkotokui lɛ anaa lɛ, naa, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ shika kã ebele lɛ nɔ yɛ ekotoku lɛ mli, wɔshika lɛ yɛ bɔ ni aŋmɛ lɛ naa pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔkɛhiɛ wɔdɛ̃ŋ kɛba ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Ni wɔkɛ shika kroko hu ehiɛ wɔdɛ̃ŋ kɛba kɛhã niyenii hemɔ. Wɔleee mɔ ni kɛ wɔshika lɛ wo wɔkotokui lɛ amli.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛnaa tsui; nyɛkashea gbeyei. Eeefee akɛ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ehã nyɛto ahuu yɛ nyɛkotokui lɛ amli ejaakɛ nyɛshika lɛ minine shɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni ejie Simeon ebahã amɛ.”

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Be ni sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ kɛ hii lɛ ba Yosef we lɛ, ehã amɛ nu ni amɛfɔ amɛnaji ahe; ni ehã amɛtejii lɛ niyenii.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob bihii lɛ fee nikee nii ni amɛhiɛ lɛ klalo amɛto Yosef shĩabaa shwane lɛ ejaakɛ amɛnu akɛ amɛ kɛ lɛ baaye nii yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef ba shĩa lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛnikeenii ni amɛhiɛ lɛ bahã lɛ ni amɛkoto lɛ.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef bi amɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ani nyɛtsɛ nuumo lɛ ni nyɛtsi etã lɛ, eyɛ jeŋ lolo? Ani eyɛ jogbaŋŋ lo?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Amɛto he amɛkɛɛ, “Otsulɔ, wɔtsɛ lɛ, eyɛ jeŋ lolo, ni eyɛ jogbaŋŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni amɛho amɛkula shi yɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef wo ehiɛ nɔ, ni ena enyɛmi Benyamin, enyɛ musuŋbi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ani nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ ni nyɛtsi etã nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi lɛ, lɛ nɛ lo?” Ni Yosef kɛɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ ajɔɔ bo, mibi!”

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni efɔ ehiɛ ni eje kpo. Emia ehiɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛkɛ niyenii abamamɔa shi!”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Akɛ enɔ eyimuu bama shi, ni ahã hii lɛ hu anɔ yimuuyimuu; ni ahã Ijiptbii lɛ hu ni kɛ Yosef yeɔ nii lɛ anɔ yimuuyimuu; ejaakɛ Ijiptbii kɛ Hebribii kaaa nine yɛ kã kome mli yeee nii; ejaakɛ Ijiptbii miihi no.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Be ni nyɛmimɛi lɛ batara ehiɛ, kromɔbi lɛ yɛ enukpa gbɛhe, ni gbekɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ hu yɛ egbekɛ gbɛhe lɛ, amɛkwɛkwɛɛ amɛhiɛiaŋ kɛ naakpɛɛ.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Ajie niyenii kɛjɛ niyenii ni ma Yosef okplɔ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ahã enyɛmimɛi lɛ; shi Benyamin nɔ lɛ fa fe amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nɔ lɛ toi enumɔ. Amɛkɛ Yosef ye nii, ni amɛkɛ lɛ nu nii, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛkɛ lɛ na miishɛɛ.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: ni okɛ mikpulu ni ji mijwiɛtɛi kpulu lɛ afata abele shika lɛ he okɛfɔ̃ gbekɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ abele lɛ nɔ yɛ ekotoku lɛ mli.” Sɔ̃ɔlɔ lɛ fee bɔ ni Yosef kɛɛ lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Leebi be ni hiɛ gbele pɛ ni awo Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ agbɛ kɛ amɛtejii lɛ.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛshɛko shɔŋŋ he ko kɛkɛ ni Yosef kɛɛ eshĩa lɛ mli sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ akɛ, “Tee shi ni otiu gbɔmɛi lɛ ni kɛ oyanina amɛ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ ‘Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkɛ efɔŋ eto ekpakpa najiaŋ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba nyɛju minuŋtsɔ jwiɛtɛi kpulu lɛ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: No minuŋtsɔ kɛnuɔ dãa, ni asaŋ no ekɛklaa. Nyɛfee efɔŋ naakpa akɛ nyɛfee enɛ.’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Be ni eyanina amɛ lɛ, eti nɛkɛ wiemɔi ni Yosef wie nɛɛ mli ehã amɛ.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Amɛhã hetoo akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ minuŋtsɔ wieɔ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ? Kpaoo, otsuji nyɛŋ nɛkɛ nɔ ko afee.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Shika lɛ ni wɔna jwere wɔbele lɛ nɔ yɛ wɔkotokui lɛ amli lɛ, bɛ wɔkɛku sɛɛ kɛjɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ wɔkɛbahã bo; te aaafee tɛŋŋ mɔ ni wɔɔju jwiɛtɛi loo shika yɛ onuŋtsɔ lɛ shĩa mli hu?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Otsuji nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ dɛŋ ni aaana yɛ lɛ, gbo eeegbo; ni wɔ hu wɔtsɔ̃mɔ minuŋtsɔ nyɔji.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Ni sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Afee bɔ ni nyɛkɛɛ lɛ; mɔ dɛŋ ni aaana yɛ lɛ eeetsɔ̃ minyɔŋ, shi nyɛ mɛi ni aaashwɛ lɛ sɔ̃ ko ewulaŋ nyɛyi.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛhe fee oya, ni amɛtotoo amɛjatsui lɛ amɛmamɔ shi, ni amɛfɛnefɛnee amɛkotokui lɛ anaa.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Yosef sɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa lɛ bɔi kpulu lɛ taomɔ kɛjɛ onukpa lɛ nɔ, ni eyagbe naa yɛ gbekɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ; ni eyana kpulu lɛ yɛ Benyamin kotoku lɛ mli.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛ dɔlɛ gbalagbalaa amɛhe atadei; ni amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ wo ejatsu etere eteji, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Be ni Yuda kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ bashɛ Yosef shĩa lɛ, Yosef yɛ jɛi lolo; ni amɛho amɛgbeegbee shikpɔŋ yɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛni pam nyɛfee nɛɛ? Ani nyɛleee akɛ gbɔmɔ ni tamɔ mi lɛ, ele klamɔ̃ lo?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Yuda here nɔ akɛ, “Mɛni wɔbaakɛɛ minuŋtsɔ? Mɛɛ wiemɔ kwraa yɔɔ wɔnaa? Aloo te wɔbaajie wɔnaa wɔhã tɛŋŋ? Nyɔŋmɔ ena otsuji anɔsha lɛ; naa, wɔtsɔ̃mɔ minuŋtsɔ nyɔji, wɔ kɛ mɔ dɛŋ ni ana kpulu lɛ yɛ lɛ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Shi Yosef kɛɛ akɛ, “Kpaoo! Enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ̃; mɔ dɛŋ ni ana kpulu lɛ yɛ lɛ, lɛ kɛkɛ eeetsɔ minyɔŋ; shi nyɛ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ, nyɛyaa nyɛtsɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.” Yuda kpa Benyamin he fai

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda tsi ebɛŋkɛ Yosef ni ekɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, minuŋtsɔ, hã otsulɔ awie nɔ kome pɛ, ni minuŋtsɔ abo mi toi ni kaahã omli wo otsulɔ la ejaakɛ otamɔ Farao diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Minuŋtsɔ bi etsuji akɛ, ‘Ani nyɛyɛ tsɛ loo nyɛmi nuu ko?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Ni wɔkɛɛ minuŋtsɔ akɛ, ‘Wɔyɛ tsɛ nuumo kɛ nyɛmi nuu gbekɛ ni ji wɔtsɛ nakutsoŋbi. Gbekɛ nɛɛ enyɛbi lɛ egbo; ni lɛ ji enyɛbi koome ni eshwɛ; ni etsɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni okɛɛ otsuji akɛ, ‘Nyɛyaŋɔa lɛ kɛbaa koni mana lɛ kɛ mihiŋmɛi.’

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Ni wɔkɛɛ minuŋtsɔ akɛ, ‘Gbekɛ lɛ nyɛŋ etsɛ eshi, ejaakɛ kɛji eshi etsɛ lɛ, etsɛ baagbo.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni okɛɛ otsuji akɛ, ‘Kɛji nyɛkɛ nɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmi gbekɛ nɛɛ baaa lɛ, nyɛnaŋ mihiɛ dɔŋŋ.’

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: “Be ni wɔku wɔsɛɛ wɔtee mitsɛ, otsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ, wɔgba lɛ wiemɔi ni minuŋtsɔ wie lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni wɔtsɛ kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛyaa ekoŋŋ ni nyɛyahea niyenii fioo ko nyɛbahãa wɔ’ lɛ, wɔkɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: ‘Wɔnyɛŋ wɔya, shi kɛji wɔnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ fata wɔhe lɛ, no lɛ wɔɔtee; shi wɔnyɛŋ nuu lɛ hiɛ wɔna akɛ ja wɔnyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ fata wɔhe dã.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mitsɛ, otsulɔ lɛ, kɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛle akɛ miŋa Rahel, lɛ ekɛ mi fɔ bihii enyɔ;

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: mɔ kome eshi mi ni mikɛɛ akɛ, tserɛmɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ kooloo ko etserɛ emli lɛ, ni minako lɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛŋɔ mɔ nɛ hu yɛ mihe kɛtee ni osharã ko yasharã lɛ lɛ, no lɛ he ni migbɔ kɛshɛ kɛ miyiteŋ waŋ nɛɛ, nyɛbaahã magbo kɛ awerɛhoo.’

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, kɛji mitee mitsɛ otsulɔ ŋɔɔ, ni gbekɛ lɛ fataaa wɔhe lɛ, akɛni ewala ji gbekɛ lɛ wala lɛ,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ otsulɔ kɛ ewala to mitsɛ awaba yɛ gbekɛ lɛ najiaŋ akɛ, ‘Kɛji mikɛ gbekɛ lɛ ekuuu sɛɛ ebahãaa bo lɛ, no lɛ no sɔ̃ lɛ atere mi yɛ mitsɛ hiɛ miwala bei abɔ fɛɛ.’

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, ofainɛ, hã otsulɔ ahi biɛ akɛ minuŋtsɔ nyɔŋ yɛ gbekɛ lɛ najiaŋ koni ohã gbekɛ lɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ aya.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ te mafee tɛŋŋ maku misɛɛ maya mitsɛ ŋɔɔ kɛji gbekɛ lɛ fataaa mihe hu? Nɔ ni baafee mitsɛ lɛ minyɛŋ makwɛ kɛ mihiŋmɛi.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yosef nyɛɛɛ ehiɛ emia dɔŋŋ yɛ mɛi ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ, kɛkɛ ni efã ekɛɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aje kpo ashi mi.” No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ emasɛi be ni ejie ehe shi etsɔ̃ɔ enyɛmimɛi lɛ.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ejwa yaafo bɔ ni Ijiptbii lɛ kɛ Farao we lɛ mli bii lɛ tete nu he.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Mi Yosef nɛ. Ani mitsɛ yɛ jeŋ lolo?” Shi enyɛmimɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ lɛ hetoo ahã ejaakɛ amɛ jijaa yɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef kɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtsia nyɛbɛŋkɛa mi koo!” Kɛkɛ ni amɛtsi amɛbɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mi ji nyɛnyɛmi Yosef mɔ ni nyɛhɔɔ kɛba Ijipt lɛ.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɛɛ nyɛkahãa edɔa nyɛ ni nyɛmli akawowoa nyɛhe la hu yɛ hɔɔmɔ ni nyɛhɔɔ mi kɛba biɛ lɛ hewɔ; ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni tsu mi kɛtsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ kɛba biɛ koni atsɔ̃ minɔ ahere mɛi ayiwala.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ afii enyɔ nɛ ni hɔmɔ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eshwɛ afii enumɔ hu lolo ni aduŋ nii ni akpãŋ nii hu.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ tsu mi kɛtsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ koni ahã nyɛteŋ mɛi komɛi kɛ̃ ashwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ahere nyɛteŋ mɛi babaoo ayiwala ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Belɛ jeee nyɛ nyɛhã mibaje biɛ, shi Nyɔŋmɔ moŋ ni; ni lɛ nɔŋŋ ehã mitsɔ̃ tamɔ nɔ ni Farao tsɛ ji mi, ni ewo mi ewe lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nuŋtsɔ kɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔyelɔ.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Nyɛhe afea oya ni nyɛyaa mitsɛ ŋɔɔ nyɛyakɛa lɛ akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni obi Yosef kɛɛ nɛ. Nyɔŋmɔ ewo mi Ijipt fɛɛ nɔ nuŋtsɔ, ba miŋɔɔ; kaatsɛ.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Ba ni obahi Goshen kpokpai anɔ yɛ Ijipt, bɔ ni afee ni obɛŋkɛ mi, bo kɛ obii kɛ onabii kɛ otoi kɛ otsinai kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni oyɔɔ;

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: ni malɛ bo yɛ jɛi; ejaakɛ eshwɛ hɔmɔ afii lɛ enumɔ lolo ni baaba; koni bo, kɛ owebii kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛ bo yɔɔ lɛ akabaye ohia.’

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: “Ni naa, nyɛhiɛ tua, ni minyɛmi Benyamin hu hiɛ tua akɛ mi Yosef diɛŋtsɛ; mi kɛ nyɛ wieɔ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Nyɛyagbaa mitsɛ bɔ ni mihiɛ eba nyam yɛ Ijipt lɛ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛna lɛ. Nyɛhe afea oya koni nyɛkɛ mitsɛ aba biɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Yosef saa eshwɔshwɔɔ enyɛmimɛi lɛ fɛɛ anaa ni efo. No sɛɛ lɛ, enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ lɛ bɔi wiemɔ.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Be ni anu sane nɛɛ he yɛ Farao we lɛ akɛ Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ eba lɛ, eŋɔɔ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Farao kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ onyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ nɔ ni misumɔɔ ni nyɛfee nɛ: Nyɛfimɔa jatsui nyɛterea nyɛtejii lɛ, ni nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ kɛyaa Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: ni nyɛyaŋɔa nyɛtsɛ kɛ nyɛbii kɛ nyɛhɔi kɛbaa. Mibahã nyɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛhi nɔ ni nyɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Asaŋ ofã amɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛfea enɛ; nyɛŋɔa shwiilii kɛjɛa Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa yɛ nyɛbii kɛ nyɛŋamɛi lɛ ahewɔ koni nyɛkɛ nyɛtsɛ aba.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɛkahaoa nyɛhe yɛ nyɛnibii ni nyɛbaashi hewɔ ejaakɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nibii kpakpai fɛɛ lɛ, nyɛnɔ ni.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Yakob bihii lɛ fee nakai; ni Yosef hã amɛ shwiilii yɛ Farao fãmɔ lɛ naa, ni ehã amɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii hu.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
