translation_verse: Asaŋ ehã amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hetsakemɔ atade; shi Benyamin lɛ, ehã lɛ shika jwiɛtɛi kukuji ohai etɛ̃ kɛ hetsakemɔ atadei srɔtoi enumɔ.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Nibii ni ekɛmaje etsɛ Ataa lɛ nɛ: tejii nyɔŋma ni tere Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kpakpai, kɛ tejiyei nyɔŋma ni tere abele kɛ aboloo ni etsɛ baaye yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ewo enyɛmimɛi lɛ gbɛ. Be ni amɛyiɔ mli lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkayabea yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛshwie nɔ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛba amɛtsɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Ni amɛbakɛɛ amɛtsɛ akɛ, “Ataa, Yosef yɛ jeŋ lolo, ni lɛ eyeɔ lumɔ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Yakob yiŋ fee lɛ kɔshikɔshi ejaakɛ eheee amɛ eyeee.”

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛgba lɛ wiemɔ ni Yosef kɛ amɛ wie lɛ fɛɛ ni ena shwiilii ni Yosef hã koni akɛbaŋɔ lɛ kɛba lɛ, amɛtsɛ Yakob he tse lɛ,

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Omanye sane! Mibi Yosef yɛ jeŋ lolo! Matee mayana ehiɛ dani magbo!”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob fã kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ, ni eba Beersheba. Eshã afɔlei ehã etsɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Yakob wie yɛ ninaa mli nyɔɔŋ ni ekɛɛ, “Yakob, Yakob!” Ni Yakob here nɔ akɛ, “Naa mi.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mi ji Yehowa, otsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Kaashe Ijipt yaa gbeyei ejaakɛ mahã oshwiei atsɔ̃ jeŋmaŋ kpeteŋkple yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kɛ amɛ aaatee Ijipt, ni mi kɛ oshwiei aaasaa aba ekoŋŋ; ni ooogbo ofɔ̃ Yosef tsitsiŋ.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Lea bihii kɛ amɛnyɛmi yoo Dina ni ekɛ Yakob fɔ yɛ Mesopotamia lɛ. Yakob bii ni ekɛ Lea fɔ fɛɛ feɔ gbɔmɛi nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ etɛ.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ, ‘Kɛ Farao aaabatsɛ nyɛ ni eeebi nyɛ akɛ, Mɛni ji nyɛnitsumɔ? lɛ’

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Shwiei nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa nɛɛ ji bii ni Yakob kɛ Zilpa, nyɔ́ŋyoo lɛ ni Laban kɛhã ebiyoo Lea lɛ fɔ.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Yakob shwiei diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛba Ijipt lɛ ayibɔ ji gbɔmɛi nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ ekpaa, esoro ebihii lɛ aŋamɛi lɛ.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yakob tsu Yuda kɛtsɔ ehiɛ kɛtee Yosef ŋɔɔ koni Yosef atsɔ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛ kɛya Goshen; ni amɛba Goshen.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef saa eshwiili ni eyiŋ etee koni eyakpee etsɛ Yakob yɛ Goshen; ni be ni Yosef na etsɛ lɛ, eloo lɛ atuu ni efo eshwie ekuɛ nɔ aahu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Israel kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ ni mina ohiɛ akɛ oyɛ jeŋ lolo nɛɛ, kɛ migbo tete po miyajɔɔ mihe.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef kɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ etsɛ we lɛ akɛ, “Miiya Farao ŋɔɔ mayagba lɛ akɛ, ‘Minyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ mitsɛ we lɛ ni yɔɔ Kanaan lɛ eba miŋɔɔ.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɛi lɛ tookwɛlɔi ji amɛ, ni amɛlɛɔ kooloi. Amɛkɛ amɛtoi kɛ amɛtsinai kɛ amɛnii fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ eba.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: nyɛkɛa lɛ akɛ, ‘Otsuji lɛɔ kooloi kɛjɛ wɔblahiaŋ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ; wɔ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ koni ehã nyɛhi Goshen shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ejaakɛ Ijiptbii nyaŋeɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ji koolookwɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Farao bi Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni ji nyɛnitsumɔ?” Amɛhã Farao hetoo akɛ, “Otsuji lɛ koolookwɛlɔi ji wɔ, wɔ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ni asaŋ amɛkɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Wɔba gbɔtoo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ejaakɛ otsuji kooloi lɛ naaa nii amɛye yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔmiikpa bo fai ni ohã otsuji ahi Goshen shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Otsɛ kɛ onyɛmimɛi lɛ eba oŋɔɔ.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Naa, Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ kã ohiɛ nɛɛ, hã otsɛ kɛ onyɛmimɛi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ; hã amɛhi Goshen shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛ ole amɛteŋ mɛi ni he esa yɛ koolookwɛmɔ mli lɛ, tuu mitsinai lɛ akwɛmɔ owo amɛdɛŋ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef kɛ etsɛ Yakob ba ni ekɛ lɛ batsɔ̃ɔ Farao, ni Yakob jɔɔ Farao.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Farao bi Yakob akɛ “Afii enyiɛ oye?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob jɔɔ Farao ni eje Farao hiɛ etee.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Ni Yosef hã etsɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ shihilɛhe. Ehã amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ebɛŋkɛ maŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Rameses lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni Farao efã lɛ akɛ efee lɛ.

english_verse: Joseph also provided food for their families. A Famine in Egypt
translation_verse: Yosef hã etsɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ etsɛ we lɛ fɛɛ niyenii yɛ amɛbii ayibɔ naa. Hɔmɔ be lɛ

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Ni Yosef bua shika ni mɛi ni jɛ Ijipt kɛ mɛi ni jɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbahe abele lɛ naa. Ni Yosef kɛ shika nɛɛ ba Farao we lɛ mli.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni shika fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ijipt kɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tã lɛ, Ijiptbii lɛ fɛɛ ba Yosef ŋɔɔ amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Hã wɔ nii wɔye! Shi mɛɛ hewɔ ni oookwɛ ni wɔɔgboi yɛ wɔshika ni etã hewɔ.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Ni nyɛshika etã nɛɛ, nyɛkɛ nyɛkooloi ahãa mi ni mahã nyɛ niyenii yɛ nyɛkooloi lɛ anaa.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Be ni nakai afi lɛ ho lɛ, amɛba Yosef ŋɔɔ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔnyɛŋ wɔkɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko atee wɔnuŋtsɔ, no ji akɛ, Wɔshika kɛ wɔkooloo kui lɛ fɛɛ etã; wɔkɛ fɛɛ ebahã wɔnuŋtsɔ; eshwɛko nɔ ko nɔ ko akɛ ja wɔgbɔmɔtsei ni onaa nɛɛ kɛ wɔshikpɔji pɛ.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ oookwɛ ni wɔgboi ni wɔshikpɔji lɛ hu aje wɔdɛŋ lɛ? Ŋɔɔ niyenii ohe wɔ kɛ wɔshikpɔji lɛ koni wɔtsɔ̃mɔ Farao nyɔji koni wɔshikpɔji lɛ hu atsɔ̃ enɔ. Hã wɔ dumɔwui koni wɔyi ana wala ni wɔkagboi ni wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ batsɔ amaŋfɔ̃.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef he Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ehã Farao ejaakɛ Ijiptnyo fɛɛ Ijiptnyo hɔ̃ɔ eshikpɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ waa ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsɔ̃ Farao nɔ̃;

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ ashikpɔji lɛ kɛkɛ ni eheee ejaakɛ amɛyɛ sisɛ̃ ni ato ni Farao hãa amɛ, ni sisɛ̃ nɛɛ amɛyeɔ; no hewɔ lɛ, amɛhɔ̃ɔɔ amɛshikpɔji lɛ.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ mihe nyɛ kɛ nyɛshikpɔji lɛ mihã Farao. Agbɛnɛ, naa dumɔwui! Nyɛdua yɛ nyɛŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Kɛ shɛ nikpamɔbe lɛ, nyɛbaaja nyɛŋmɔshinii lɛ mli enumɔ; Farao baaŋɔ ekome; ni nyɛbaaŋɔ ejwɛ lɛ. No eko nyɛbaadu, ni no nɔŋŋ eko nyɛbaaye, no nɔŋŋ eko nyɛwebii baaye, ni no nɔŋŋ eko nyɛbii bibii lɛ baaye.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ here Yosef nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Ohere wɔyiwala! Kɛ ooosumɔ lɛ, hã wɔtsɔmɔ Farao nyɔji.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef ŋɔ enɛ efee akpɔ efɔ̃ shi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ akɛ aja ŋmɔshinii mli enumɔ ni Farao aŋɔ ekome. Osɔfoi lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ kɛkɛ ni tsɔ̃ɔɔ Farao nɔ. Yakob naagbee shamaŋsheo ni ewo

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni fee ni Israelbii lɛ hi shi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Goshen lɛ nɛ. Israelbii nɛɛ nanaa shikpɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfɔfɔɔ ni amɛshwere babaoo diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob gbele be eshɛ etã lɛ, etsɛ ebi Yosef ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛ oyɛ mihe tsuijurɔ lɛ, okɛ onine abahɔ milagbaateŋ ni owo mi shi akɛ obaaye mi anɔkwa. Kaafu mi yɛ Ijipt.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ kɛji migbo lɛ, wo mi kɛje Ijipt ni oyafu mi yɛ mitsɛmɛi lɛ afũuhe lɛ.” Ni Yosef here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Mafee bɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Shi Yakob kɛɛ, “Kã mi kitã!” No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef kã lɛ kitã. Kɛkɛ ni Israel ma eyi shi yɛ esaatso lɛ yitsogbɛ ni esɔle.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ abakɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Naa, otsɛ he miiye.” No hewɔ lɛ, Yosef ŋɔ ebihii enyɔ ni ji Manase kɛ Efraim efata ehe kɛtee.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Ayakɛɛ Yakob akɛ, “Obi Yosef miiba oŋɔɔ.” Kɛkɛ ni Yakob mia ehiɛ ni ete shi eta saatso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Yakob kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ mi yɛ Luz yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ejɔɔ mi ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: ‘Naa, mahã ofɔ pii ni obaashwere, ni mahã oshwiei atsɔmɔ maji pii, ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ aaahã oshwiei ni aaaba yɛ osɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛnɔ kɛmiiya naanɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Yakob tsa ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Obihii enyɔ ni ji Efraim kɛ Manase ni ofɔ yɛ Ijipt dani miba oŋɔɔ lɛ, minii ji amɛ. Efraim kɛ Manase etsɔ̃mɔ mibii tamɔ Ruben kɛ Simeon nɔŋŋ;

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: ni bii ni ooofɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ afee bo onii; shi yɛ gboshiniiyeli gbɛfaŋ lɛ, aaabu amɛ ashi Efraim kɛ Manase nɔ.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni mijɛ Mesopotamia ni mibaa Kanaan lɛ, Rahel gbo shi mi yɛ gbɛ teŋ, be ni eshwɛ gbɛ kukuoo dani ashɛɔ Efrat lɛ, ni mifu lɛ yɛ jɛi yɛ gbɛ ni yaa Efrat ni ji ŋmɛnɛ Betlehem lɛ he.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yosef hole gbekɛbii lɛ yɛ Yakob nakutsei anɔ, kɛkɛ ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Yosef mɔmɔ gbekɛbii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amli, Efraim ye Yakob abɛku nɔ, ni Manase ye Israel ninejurɔ nɔ, ni etsi amɛ ebɛŋkɛ Yakob.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kpã eninejurɔ mli ni ekɛŋmɛ Efraim ni ji gbekɛ lɛ yiteŋ, ni ekɛ ebɛku tsɔ̃ eninejurɔ lɛ nɔ ekɛŋmɛ Manase yiteŋ, tsɛbelɛ Manase ji kromɔ.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob jɔɔ Yosef ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ, mɔ ni mitsɛmɛi Abraham kɛ Isak sɔ̃mɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni ekwɛ minɔ miwala gbii fɛɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: bɔfo ni jie mi kɛjɛ efɔŋ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ajɔɔ gbekɛbii nɛɛ. Amɛhewɔ lɛ, migbɛi kɛ mitsɛmɛi Abraham kɛ Isak agbɛi gboŋ kɔkɔɔkɔ. Amɛyi afa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef na akɛ etsɛ kɛ eninejurɔ eŋmɛ Efraim yiteŋ lɛ, enaaa he miishɛɛ, ni ewo etsɛ nine nɔ koni ejie kɛjɛ Efraim yiteŋ kɛyaŋmɛ Manase yiteŋ.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Ni Yosef kɛɛ etsɛ akɛ, “Jeee nakai ni Ataa, ejaakɛ mɔ nɛ ji kromɔbi; okɛ onine jurɔ aŋmɛ lɛ moŋ eyiteŋ.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Shi etsɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Mibi, mile, mile krɛdɛɛ akɛ onukpa lɛ hu aaatsɔ̃ maŋ kpele, ni eeetsɔ agbo; shi kɛ̃lɛ enyɛmi gbekɛ lɛ aaatsɔ̃ kpeteŋkple fe lɛ, ni eshwiei aaatsɔ majimaji babaoo.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yakob jɔɔ gbekɛbii lɛ nakai gbi lɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛ nyɛgbɛi Israelbii kɛaajɔɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ahã otsɔ̃ tamɔ Efraim kɛ Manase.’ ” Belɛ Yakob ŋɔ onukpa gbɛhe lɛ ehã Efraim.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob kɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Naa, mi lɛ, migbele be eshɛ etã, shi nyɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ nyɛ baahi shi, ni ekɛ nyɛ baaku sɛɛ kɛya nyɛblematsɛmɛi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yakob tsɛ ebii lɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛbuaa nyɛhe naa koni magba nyɛ wɔsɛɛ saji ni baaba nyɛ nɔ:

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: “Nyɛbuaa nyɛhe naa, ni nyɛboa mi toi; nyɛ Yakob bihii, nyɛboa nyɛtsɛ Yakob toi!

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: “Ruben, bo ji mikromɔbi, miblahiaŋ be hewalɛ mli bi, mɔ ni fe fɛɛ yɛ gbɛnaa kɛ hewalɛ gbɛfaŋ.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Otamɔ nu hamahama ni damɔɔɔ he kome; ofeŋ klɛŋklɛŋ mɔ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ okɛ mihemɔ wɔ, ni owo misaa he muji ni obule misaatso.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: “Simeon kɛ Levi lɛ, nyɛmimɛi ni; amɛkɛ amɛklantei lɛ tsuɔ yiwalɛnii.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Mihiŋ amɛ jinatoo mli, ni mitaŋ amɛkpei amli. Amɛmlifu mli lɛ, amɛgbe gbɔmɔ, ni amɛkɛ yiŋflɛflɛ fee tsinai akpaketsɛmɛi.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Alomɔ amɛmlifu, ejaakɛ enaa wa; alomɔ amɛmlila, ejaakɛ eyi wa. Magbala amɛmli mawo Israel magbɛ amɛ mashwã Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Yuda, onyɛmimɛi lɛ aaajie oyi. Oooye ohenyɛlɔi anɔ; otsɛbii lɛ aaakoto bo!

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Yuda lɛ, jata binuu ni; mibi yagbe milɛloo ni eku esɛɛ eeba! Eedɛkɛ shi, eebumɔ shi tamɔ jata, tamɔ jatayoo; namɔ aaanyɛ lɛ ajije?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛyeli ejeŋ Yuda dɛŋ, ni nɔyeli hu ejeŋ eshwiei adɛŋ; gbii abɔ ni jeŋmaji kɛ amɛ onia baa, ni amɛbaa amɛhe shi amɛhãa lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ekɛ etejibi aaaŋmɔ wain tso, ekɛ etejiyoo bi aaaŋmɔ wain tso ni wa. Ekɛ wain aaafɔ etade he, ekɛ wain tsuru fɔɔ aaafɔ ehebo he.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Ehiŋmɛii aaatsu fɔɔ fe wain, ni enyanyɔji aaayɛ futaa, fe fufɔ.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: “Zebulon aaahi ŋshɔ naa; ni ehilɛhe aaatsɔ̃ lɛji adaamɔhe, ni ekɛ Sidon aaaje husu.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: “Isakar lɛ, teji ni he wa ni, ni ebuɔ shi yɛ kooloi atsui ateŋ.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: Enaa akɛ hejɔɔmɔhe lɛ hi, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ akɔnɔ. Ni eŋɔɔ ekoto sɛɛ ehãa ni atere lɛ jatsu. Ni anyɛɔ enɔ ni etsu nii tamɔ nyɔŋ.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan aaatsɔ̃ lumɔ ehã emɛi lɛ ni amɛaatamɔ Israel akutsei krokomɛi lɛ.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Ni Dan aaatsɔ̃ onufu ni ble gbɛ toi, onaŋka ni naa yɔɔ ebɔɔ yɛ gbɛ lɛ toi, ni ekɔ̃ɔ okpɔŋɔ nanetsitsi, ni enɔtalɔ lɛ kpaa gbeɔ shi.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “Yehowa, oyiwalaheremɔ lɛ, gbɛ miikwɛɔ nɛɛ!

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: “Gad lɛ ojotswalɔi asafo aaabatua lɛ, shi lɛ moŋ eeewo amɛ foi.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Asher shikpɔŋ aaaba nii kpɔtɔɔ nii ni sa maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Naftali lɛ ofrote ni foɔ shi kɛkɛ ni; ni enaa ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Yosef lɛ, tso nine ni woɔ yibii ni, tso nine ni ma nuhiŋmɛi he, ni eniji kwɔlɔɔ gbogbo.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Gãitsɛ̃lɔi kɛ hiɛdɔɔ batua lɛ, ni amɛtsɛ̃rɛ̃ lɛ gãi kɛ yiwalɛ.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Shi egãi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kpɛŋŋ. Eniji kɛ ekɔ̃ɔji ahe yɛ oya; Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ ni hã lɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ. Tookwɛlɔ lɛ ni ji Israel tɛsaa lɛ, gbɛi lɛ tsu enɛ.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Otsɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ji mɔ ni aaaye abua bo. Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ baajɔɔ bo. Lɛ eeejɔɔ bo kɛ jɔɔmɔi ni jɛ ŋwɛi kɛ jɔɔmɔi ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi nui lɛ amli. Eeejɔɔ bo kɛ fufɔ ni kɔ̃ɔ, eeejɔɔ bo kɛ fɔmɔnii kpakpa.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Otsɛ jɔɔmɔi lɛ mli wa fe naanɔ gɔji lɛ, kɛ naanɔ gɔ̃ŋkpɔi lɛ ajɔɔmɔi lɛ. Jɔɔmɔi nɛɛ ashwie Yosef yiteŋ, eshwie lɛ mɔ ni ajie lɛ yɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ ato afã lɛ pampam.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: “Benyamin lɛ, klaŋ ni yɔɔ hahaaha ni. Leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ emɔɔ emilɛloo ni eyeɔ.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Israel akutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ; ni wiemɔi nɛɛ amɛtsɛ kɛ amɛ wie be ni ejɔɔ amɛ lɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ jɔɔmɔ ni sa lɛ lɛ, no ekɛjɔɔ lɛ. Yakob gbele kɛ efuu

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Abɔɔ nɛɛ kɛ tɛkplo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ahe yɛ Hitbii lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob ewo ebii lɛ kitãi nɛkɛ egbe naa lɛ, ebua enaji anaa eshwie saa lɛ nɔ, ni ebu enaa. Afu lɛ afata emɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef ho egbee etsɛ nɔ ni efo ni eshwɔ enaa.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for Jacob's body to be embalmed,
translation_verse: Yosef fã etsuji tsofawolɔi lɛ akɛ amɛwo etsɛ tsofa, ni amɛwo lɛ.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Be ni afo Yakob agbe naa lɛ, Yosef kɛɛ Farao we lɛ akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ, kɛ nyɛyɛ mihe tsuijurɔ lɛ, miikpa nyɛ fai, nyɛwoa Farao toi nɔ akɛ

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: mitsɛ hã mikã lɛ kitã akɛ, ‘Naa, eshɛ migbele be; mibu lɛ ni mitsa mihã mihe yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jɛi oyafu mi yɛ!’ No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni mayato mitsɛ ni maku misɛɛ maba.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Farao to he akɛ, “Yaa ni oyafu otsɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ehã okã lɛ kitã lɛ.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni amɛshɛ Atad abeleshaahe lɛ ni yɔɔ Yordan faa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛfee yara wulu yɛ jɛi; ni Yosef fo etsɛ gbii kpawo.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Yakob bii lɛ ye amɛtsɛ kitã ni ewo amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Amɛwo lɛ kɛtee Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyafu lɛ yɛ Makpela abɔɔ lɛ mli tɛkplo lɛ mli. Abɔɔ nɛɛ Abraham diɛŋtsɛ he kɛ tɛkplo lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Efron, Hitnyo lɛ, dɛŋ yɛ Mamre bokãgbɛ ni ekɛfee efuuhe lɛ.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Be ni Yosef efu etsɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛ lɛ tee etsɛ fuu lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee Ijipt ekoŋŋ. Yosef shɛje enyɛmimɛi lɛ amii

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni Yosef nyɛmimɛi lɛ na akɛ amɛtsɛ egbo lɛ, amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Ekolɛ Yosef ebɛ wɔ ewo emli, ni eeetɔ ehe owele yɛ efɔŋ fɛɛ ni wɔfee lɛ lɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛhã ayakɛɛ Yosef akɛ, “Otsɛ wo kitã dani egbo akɛ,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Bɔ ni nyɛkɛ Yosef awie nɛ, Miikpa bo fai ni okɛ onyɛmimɛi lɛ atɔ̃mɔi kɛ amɛhe eshai lɛ afa amɛ ejaakɛ amɛfee bo efɔŋ.’ No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ wɔmiikpa bo fai ni okɛ otsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ tsuji lɛ atɔ̃mɔi lɛ afa amɛ!” Be ni amɛkɛ Yosef wie nɛkɛ lɛ, efo.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni enyɛmimɛi lɛ tee amɛyabumɔ shi yɛ ehiɛ ni amɛkɛɛ, “Naa, otsuji ji wɔ!”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Yosef kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei! Minyɛŋ maye Nyɔŋmɔ najiaŋ mafee nɔ ko.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Tsɛbelɛ, nyɛ lɛ, nyɛto nyɛyiŋ akɛ nyɛaafee mi efɔŋ, shi Nyɔŋmɔ hã etsɔ̃ nɔ kpakpa; bɔ ni afee ni atsɔ̃ no nɔ ahere mɛi babaoo ayiwala, tamɔ bɔ ni eba mli ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkashea gbeyei! Mibalɛ nyɛ kɛ nyɛbii lɛ.” Bɔ ni ehã enyɛmimɛi lɛ atsui ni eshɛje amɛmii nɛ. Yosef gbele

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Yosef hi shi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ etsɛ we lɛ. Ni eye afii oha kɛ nyɔŋma.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Yosef na Efraim nanakansowai; ni Manase bi Makir bii lɛ hu afɔ amɛ ashwie eshuɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yosef kɛɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Migbele be eshɛ; shi saramɔ Nyɔŋmɔ aaabasra nyɛ kɛ̃, ni eeekpala nyɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ kɛaatee shikpɔŋ ni ekã Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob kitã yɛ he lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yosef hã enyɛmimɛi, Yakob bii, lɛ kã lɛ kitã ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ aaakai nyɛ kɛ̃. Kɛ eeebajie nyɛ lɛ, nyɛjiea miwui lɛ kɛjea biɛ kɛya.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Yosef kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ nakai yinɔbii lɛ fɛɛ bagboi.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Shi amɛshwiei, ni ji Israelbii lɛ, fɔfɔɔ ni amɛshwere babaoo. Amɛyi bafa, ni amɛna hewalɛ naakpa diɛŋtsɛ, ni amɛyi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ maŋtsɛ hee ko ni leee Yosef baye Ijipt nɔ.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ kɛɛ emaŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkwɛa, Israelbii lɛ ayi efa, ni amɛna hewalɛ hu fe wɔ.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɛhãa wɔkɛ amɛ ayea ŋaa mli koni amɛyi akafa dɔŋŋ ni ebaba akɛ be ni ta ehe shi lɛ amɛyafata wɔhenyɛlɔi lɛ moŋ ahe ni akɛ wɔ miiwu koni amɛjo foi kɛshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ijiptbii lɛ totoo nitsumɔ nɔkwɛlɔi yɛ Israelbii lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ nitsumɔi keketekeketei awa amɛ yi. Israelbii mamɔ nitoo maji ni ji Pitom kɛ Rameses amɛhã Farao.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Shi babaoo ni Ijiptbii lɛ waa Israelbii lɛ yi lɛ, babaoo moŋ ni Israelbii lɛ ayi faa ni amɛshwereɔ ji no. Enɛ hã Ijiptbii lɛ atsui su Israelbii lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhiɛ Israelbii lɛ nyɔji ahiɛmɔ shɛii.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Amɛhã amɛnaa su, ni amɛfo ntayaa, ni amɛtsu ŋmɔshi nitsumɔi srɔtoi, ni enɛ hã jeŋ shihilɛ je Israelbii lɛ atsine.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Shifra kɛ Pua, ni ji Hebriyei yoofɔlɔi lɛ, akɛ,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Kɛji nyɛtee Hebri yei lɛ fɔmɔ ni nyɛna yɛ sɛi ni yoofɔyoo lɛ taa nɔ efɔɔ lɛ shishi akɛ bi lɛ nuu ni lɛ, nyɛgbea lɛ; shi kɛji yoo ni lɛ ehi shi.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Shi yoofɔlɔi lɛ yashe Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni amɛfeee nɔ ni Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ amɛ lɛ, shi moŋ amɛhere gbekɛbii hii lɛ ayiwala.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ tsɛ yoofɔlɔi lɛ, ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛni nyɛfeɔ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba ni nyɛhãa gbekɛbii hii lɛ ayi naa wala lɛ?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Yoofɔlɔi lɛ kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Ejaakɛ Hebriyei lɛ tamɔɔɔ Ijipt yei lɛ; amɛ lɛ amɛyɛ kamkam bɔ ni be ni yoofɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ eshɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ lɛ amɛfɔ momo.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Akɛni yoofɔlɔi lɛ yashe Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei hewɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ to amɛ ejurɔ, ni eduro amɛ bii. Yɛ Israelbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, amɛtee nɔ amɛshwere, ni amɛna hewalɛ naakpa.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao wo emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ akpɔ akɛ, “Binuu fɛɛ binuu ni Hebri yoo aaafɔ lɛ nyɛshɛa lɛ nyɛfɔ̃a Nilo faa lɛ mli, shi biyoo lɛ nyɛhãa eyi ana wala.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ mli lɛ nuu ko ni jɛ Leviwe yaŋɔ Leviwe nɔŋŋ yoo ko.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ na musu, ni efɔ binuu. Ena akɛ abifao lɛ he yɛ fɛo, hewɔ lɛ ekɛ lɛ tee nyɔji etɛ̃.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Shi be ni eyanyɛɛɛ lɛ ekɛtee dɔŋŋ lɛ, etao adai kɛntɛŋ, ni ekɛ amã tsara he fɛɛ, ni ekɛ abifao lɛ ŋmɛ mli, ni eyashi lɛ ema glãi amli yɛ faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Belɛ abifao lɛ nyɛmiyoo damɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ eekwɛ nɔ ni aaaba enɔ.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Farao biyoo ba ehejuu yɛ faa lɛ naa, ni eweyei lɛ miishara shi yɛ faa lɛ toi. Kɛkɛ ni ehiŋmɛi gba kɛntɛŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ glãi lɛ ateŋ, ni etsu eweyei lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ni eyawo kɛba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Be ni Farao biyoo lɛ gbele naa lɛ, naa abifao kã mli ni eefo. Emusuŋ tsɔ̃ lɛ yɛ ehe, ni ekɛɛ, “Hebribii lɛ abihii lɛ eko nɛ.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni abifao lɛ nyɛmiyoo lɛ babi Farao biyoo lɛ akɛ, “Ani miyatsɛ Hebriyoo fufɔhãlɔ ko mibahã bo koni ehã lɛ fufɔ ehã bo lo?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Farao biyoo lɛ to he ekɛɛ, “Hɛɛ! Yaa!” Gbekɛyoo lɛ tee ni eyatsɛ abifao lɛ nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛba.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ni Farao biyoo lɛ kɛɛ yoo ni ayatsɛ kɛba lɛ akɛ, “Hemɔ abifao nɛɛ koni oyakwɛ lɛ ohã mi, ni mawo bo nyɔmɔ.” Ehe abifao lɛ kɛtee ni eyakwɛ lɛ.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Be ni gbekɛ lɛ bada lɛ, yoo lɛ kɛ lɛ tee eyahã Farao biyoo lɛ, ni etsɔ̃ Farao biyoo bi. Ewo lɛ gbɛi akɛ Mose, ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ mijie lɛ kɛjɛ nu mli.” Mose jo foi kɛtee Midian

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mose bada. Gbi ko lɛ etee eyasara emaŋbii Hebribii lɛ, ni eyana nii ni ahãa amɛtsuɔ lɛ. Ehiŋmɛiŋ, ni Ijiptnyo ko tswa Mose nyɛmimɛi Hebribii lɛ eko nɔ.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Mose kwɛ ehe biɛ kɛ biɛ, ni be ni enaaa mɔ ko lɛ, egbe Ijiptnyo lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ tee shia mli.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Je tsɛre nɔ hu Mose tee eyasara enyɛmimɛi lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ naa Hebribii enyɔ ni miinɔ. Ebi mɔ ni eye sane fɔŋ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ ni oyiɔ onyɛmi Hebrinyo?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni eye sane fɔŋ lɛ hã Mose hetoo akɛ, “Namɔ wo bo wɔnɔ lumɔ kɛ kojolɔ? Gbe otaoɔ ni ogbe mi tamɔ ogbe Ijiptnyo lɛ?” Kɛkɛ ni Mose tsui fã, ni ekɛɛ, “Ei, ana ale sane nɛɛ!”

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Shi tookwɛlɔi komɛi bashwie amɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Mose te shi ni efã oblayei lɛ ahe, ni ehã amɛtoi lɛ nu ehã amɛ.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Be ni oblayei lɛ ba amɛtsɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ, ebi amɛ akɛ, “Te fee tɛŋŋ ni nyɛba mra nɛkɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Amɛ jie naa akɛ, “Ijiptnyo ko bajie wɔ yɛ tookwɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ, ni esaa esha nu tete ehã toi lɛ amɛnu.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Yetro bi ebiyei lɛ akɛ, “Ni nɛgbɛ nuu lɛ yɔɔ? Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛshi lɛ? Nyɛyatsɛa lɛ kɛba koni ebaye nii.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Mose kpɛlɛ̃, ni ekɛ Yetro hi shi. Yetro kɛ ebiyoo Zipora hã Mose gbãlã.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora fɔ binuu, ni Mose wo lɛ Gershom ejaakɛ ekɛɛ, “Mibato gbɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Be kplaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ bagbo. Ni Israelbii lɛ dɔmɔ ŋtsɔi yɛ nyɔŋ ni ayeɔ amɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛfo amɛtsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ nu amɛkɔmɔyeli lɛ, ni ekai kpãŋmɔ ni ekɛ Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob kpãŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekwɛ nyɔŋ ni ayeɔ Israelbii lɛ, ni amɛsane bakã etsui nɔ.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Mose miikwɛ eshaanuu Yetro, Midian osɔfo lɛ, toi. Gbi ko lɛ ekpala toi lɛ kɛtee ŋa lɛ nɔ anaigbɛ, ni eyaje Horeb, Yehowa Gɔŋ lɛ he.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo bajie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ akɛ lalilɛi, yɛ ŋmeitso ko mli. Mose kwɛ ŋmeitso lɛ gãa ejaakɛ eetso nɛ, shi eshãaa.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ ehe akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ matsi mabɛŋkɛ ni mayakwɛ naakpɛɛ nii nɛɛ, nɔ hewɔ ni ŋmeitso lɛ eshãaa lɛ.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa na akɛ Mose miibɛŋkɛ ni eyakwɛ lɛ, ejɛ ŋmeitso lɛ teŋ etsɛ lɛ ekɛɛ, “Mose, Mose!” Mose here nɔ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, naa mi!”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kaatsi oba dɔŋŋ! Jiemɔ otokotai lɛ, shi he ni odamɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Esaa ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mi ji otsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Mose tsĩ ehiɛ, ejaakɛ eeshe gbeyei akɛ eeekwɛ Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, mina amanehulu mli ni miwebii lɛ yɔɔ yɛ Ijipt lɛ, ni minu ŋkɔmɔ blɔmɔ ni amɛbolɔɔ koni abahere amɛ yɛ amɛkpalalɔi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ hu. Amɛnidɔɔ nii lɛ kã mitsui nɔ pam.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Naa, mikpeleke shi miba amɛ jiemɔ yɛ Ijiptbii lɛ adɛŋ, koni makpala amɛ kɛshi Ijipt kɛya shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni da, ni yɔɔ frɔ̃frɔ̃ ni niyenii pii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni Kanaanbii kɛ Hitbii kɛ Amorbii kɛ Perizbii kɛ Hivbii kɛ Yebusbii yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ akɔmɔyeli lɛ jwere mitoiŋ, ni mihiɛ tua bɔ ni Ijiptbii haoɔ amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ba ni matsu bo Farao ŋɔɔ koni oyajie mimaŋ Israel kɛje Ijipt.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Shi Mose kɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, “Namɔ ji mi, ni matee Farao ŋɔɔ ni mayajie Israelbii lɛ kɛje Ijipt?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ to he akɛ, “Mi kɛ bo ni yaa lɛ, ni enɛ ji nɔ ni aaaye he odase akɛ mi mitsu bo lɛ. Kɛji oyajie Israelbii lɛ kɛje Ijipt kɛba lɛ, nyɛbaa gɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ nɛɛ he nyɛbajaa mi.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ni Mose here nɔ akɛ, “Kɛji mitee Israelbii lɛ aŋɔɔ miyakɛɛ amɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ tsu mi nyɛŋɔɔ nɛɛ’, ni amɛaabi mi akɛ, ‘Te egbɛi hu?’ lɛ, te mikɛɛ amɛ tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ, “Okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa, nyɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ji Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ji mɔ ni tsu mi nyɛŋɔɔ nɛɛ. Migbɛi kwraa nɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ, ni no yinɔi fɛɛ kɛtsɛ mi.’

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Yaa ni oyabua Israel onukpai lɛ anaa, ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, Yehowa, nyɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ji Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ejie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ mi, ni ekɛɛ, Mikwɛ, ni mina nyɛ kɛ nɔ ni afeɔ nyɛ yɛ Ijipt lɛ,

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: ni miiwo shi akɛ majie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt amanehulu lɛ mli kɛya Kanaanbii kɛ Hitbii kɛ Amorbii kɛ Perizbii kɛ Hivbii kɛ Yebusbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ frɔ̃frɔ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Israel onukpai lɛ aaabo bo toi, ni okɛ amɛ aya Ijipt Maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni oyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa, Hebribii aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ejie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ wɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔmiikpa bo fai, ŋmɛɛ wɔ gbɛ ni wɔya gbii etɛ̃ gbɛ nyiɛmɔ koni wɔyashã afɔle wɔhã Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Shi mi lɛ mile akɛ Ijipt Maŋtsɛ lɛ eŋmɛŋ gbɛ ni nyɛya, ja anyɛ enɔ.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, majie mihewalɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ Ijipt, ni mikɛ naakpɛɛ nii ni mafee yɛ jɛi lɛ aaagbala Ijipt toi, ni no sɛɛ dani eeehã nyɛya.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Yoo fɛɛ yoo amala shika nii kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ mamai yɛ Ijiptyoo ni ji ehe gbɔmɔ kɛ eshiaŋyoo dɛŋ, ni nyɛkɛwowoo nyɛbihii kɛ biyei. No nɔ baatsɔ̃ ni nyɛaakpakpaa Ijiptbii lɛ ahe nii kɛaatee.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Naa, Israelbii lɛ heŋ mi amɛyeŋ, amɛboŋ mi toi hu, ejaakɛ amɛaakɛɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa ejieko ehe kpo etsɔ̃ko bo.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa bi Mose akɛ, “Mɛni yɔɔ odɛ̃ŋ lɛ?” Ejie naa akɛ, “Tso.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Shɛ ofɔ̃ shikpɔŋ!” Mose shɛ tso lɛ efɔ̃ shikpɔŋ, kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔ̃ onufu, ni Mose jo onufu lɛ naa foi kɛtee sɛɛ.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpã onine mli ni omɔ elei!” Mose kpã enine mli, ni emɔ onufu lɛ lei lɛ, kɛkɛ ni etsɔ̃ tso ekoŋŋ yɛ edɛŋ.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Enɛ amɛkɛaahe amɛye akɛ Yehowa, ni ji Abraham Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Isak Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ejie ehe kpo etsɔɔ bo.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ okɛ onine ahɔ omiinaa.” Mose kɛ enine lɛ hɔ emiinaa, ni be ni ejie lɛ, naa nine lɛ ni hela ko tamɔ kpiti eshwie he fuu.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ onine ahɔ omiinaa ekoŋŋ.” Esaa ekɛ enine lɛ hɔ jɛi. Be ni ejie lɛ, naa ehewolo lɛ ni etsɔ̃ tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ sa lɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛji amɛheee bo amɛyeee yɛ okadii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ asɛɛ, ni amɛbooo bo toi hu lɛ, no lɛ yɛɛ Nilo Faa lɛ mli nu lɛ eko ni ofɔse oshwie shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ, ni nu lɛ ni oyɛ yɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ aaatsɔ̃ lá yɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Ofainɛ miNuŋtsɔ! Minaa tseee kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ beebe, ni kɛjɛ beyinɔ hu ni okɛ mi, otsulɔ, wie nɛɛ fɛɛ, minaa tseko, ni mililɛi tsii.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Yehowa bi lɛ akɛ, “Namɔ bɔ naabu hã gbɔmɔ? Namɔ bɔ mumui loo toimulɔ, loo mɔ ni naa nii, loo shwilafo? Ani jeee mi, Yehowa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, yaa otsumɔ lɛ, shi mibawa bo kɛ wiemɔ, ni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni owie.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Shi Mose here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, miNuŋtsɔ, tsu mɔ kroko.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa mli wo Mose la, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani onyɛmi Aaron, Levinyo lɛ, bɛ? Mile akɛ enaa tse. Ni ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ po enyiɛ gbɛ eeba ni ekɛ bo abakpe, ni kɛ ena bo lɛ eeenya ohe kɛ etsuiŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Aaron aaatsɔ̃ onaawielɔ yɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ teŋ, ni eeewie yɛ onajiaŋ, ni bo hu oootsɔ̃ tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ ohã lɛ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Okɔ tso nɛɛ ohiɛ odɛ̃, no okɛbaafee naakpɛɛ nii lɛ.” Mose ku esɛɛ etee Ijipt

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Mose ku esɛɛ etee eshaanuu Yetro ŋɔɔ, ni eyabi lɛ gbɛ ekɛɛ, “Miikpa bo fai, hã maku misɛɛ maya Ijipt mayakwɛ akɛ minyɛmimɛi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo lo.” Yetro to he akɛ, “Yoo, yaa ni oba, gbɛ aŋmɛ ahã bo.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Mose yɛ Midian lolo ni Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ oya Ijipt, ejaakɛ mɛi ni tao bo agbe lɛ egboi.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose ŋɔ eŋa kɛ ebihii lɛ etara teji nɔ, ni eyiŋ kɛmiiku esɛɛ kɛya Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni Nyɔŋmɔ tso lɛ hiɛ edɛ̃.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Kɛji oyashɛ Ijipt lɛ kwɛmɔ ni naakpɛɛ nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛ amɛnɔ hewalɛ ewo odɛ̃ŋ lɛ, ofee yɛ Farao hiɛ; shi mi lɛ mahã Farao akpliŋ etsui, ni ehãŋ maŋ lɛ aya.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Okɛɛ Farao akɛ mi Yehowa mikɛɛ, ‘Mikromɔ binuu ji Israel,

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: ni miikɛɛ bo akɛ, hã mibinuu lɛ aya, no lɛ naa, magbe okromɔ binuu lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Amɛyashɛ shitoohe ko yɛ gbɛteŋ, ni Yehowa bahɛŋ Mose, ni eetao lɛ egbe.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Zipora kɔ tɛ kakla ni naa ba, ni ekɛfo ebinuu lɛ ketia; ekɛ loo ni efo lɛ sa Mose naji ahe, ni ekɛɛ, “Lá ayɛmforowu ji bo”.

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ketiafoo lɛ hewɔ ni Zipora kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Eji anɔkwale akɛ nuu ni feɔ hii anii ji bo” lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ mli lɛ Yehowa ekɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Yaa ni okɛ Mose ayakpe yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.” Aaron tee, ni ekɛ Mose yakpe yɛ Sinai, Nyɔŋmɔ Gɔŋ lɛ he, ni eshwɔ enaa.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose jaje wiemɔi fɛɛ ni Yehowa kɛtsu lɛ lɛ, kɛ okadii fɛɛ hu ni efã lɛ akɛ efee lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ Aaron.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kɛ Aaron tee Ijipt, ni amɛyabua Israelbii lɛ anukpai lɛ fɛɛ anaa.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Aaron jaje wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni Yehowa kɛ Mose ewie lɛ, ni Mose fee okadii lɛ hu etsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ he lɛ ye. Ni be ni amɛnu akɛ Yehowa ekwɛ ni ena Israelbii lɛ amanehulu lɛ, amɛmamɔ amɛyitsei ashi ni amɛja.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mose kɛ Aaron tee Farao ŋɔɔ amɛyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Hã mimaŋ lɛ aya ni amɛyaye gbi jurɔ amɛhã mi yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Farao bi amɛ akɛ, “Namɔ ji nakai Yehowa lɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ mabo lɛ toi, ni mahã Israel aya? Mileee Yehowa ko, ni Israel hu mihãaa amɛya.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron to he akɛ, “Hebribii aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ wɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔmiikpa bo fai koni ohã wɔya gbii etɛ̃ gbɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni wɔyashã afɔle wɔhã Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, koni ekabatua wɔ kɛ gbele hela loo ta.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ moŋ ni maŋ lɛ yi efa momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni nyɛhãa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nɛɛ!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Farao wo Israelbii lɛ akpalalɔi lɛ kɛ amɛnɔkwɛlɔi lɛ kitã akɛ,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Nyɛkahãa Israelbii lɛ jwɛi tamɔ tsutsu lɛ ni amɛkɛfo ntayaa lɛ dɔŋŋ. Amɛya amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyatao jwɛi amɛhã amɛhe,

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: shi ntayaa abɔ ni amɛfoɔ kɛbashi amrɔ nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛhãa amɛfoa nakai nɔŋŋ, nyɛkatsea nɔ. Amɛmiifee anihao hewɔ ni amɛbolɔɔ akɛ, ‘Hã wɔya ni wɔyashã afɔle wɔhã wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ!’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Ahã nitsumɔ lɛ anyɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni etɔ amɛ ni amɛkana hiɛ amɛbo lakamɔ wiemɔi atoi.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ akpalalɔi lɛ kɛ amɛnɔkwɛlɔi lɛ yiŋ amɛtee, ni amɛyakɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Farao kɛɛ kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ lɛ, ehãaa nyɛ jwɛi dɔŋŋ;

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛyaa nyɛyataoa jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he ni nyɛaana eko yɛ; shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ atseŋ nyɛnitsumɔ lɛ nɔ dɛ̃rɛ̃.”

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Kpalalɔi lɛ tsirɛ Israelbii lɛ ayisɛɛ akɛ amɛgbe amɛdaa gbi nitsumɔ lɛ naa tamɔ be mli ni ahãa amɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ni Farao kpalalɔi lɛ yi Israelbii ni afee amɛ nɔkwɛlɔi akɛto nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni amɛbi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ni nyɛgbeee daa gbi ntayai ni ato ahã nyɛ ni nyɛfo lɛ anaa tamɔ sa lɛ?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ anɔkwɛlɔi lɛ tee Farao ŋɔɔ amɛyabolɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Mɛɛ sane okɛyeɔ wɔ, otsuji nɛɛ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Ahãaa wɔ jwɛi, shi akɛɛ doo wɔfo ntayaa kɛ̃. Aayi wɔ yɛ no hewɔ, tsɛbelɛ tɔ̃mɔ lɛ jɛ omaŋbii lɛ.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Farao here amɛnɔ ekɛɛ, “Hejɔ̃lɔi ni nyɛ ji hewɔ ni nyɛkɛɛ, ‘Hã wɔya ni wɔyashã afɔle wɔhã Yehowa lɛ.’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Nyɛyaa nyɛyatsua nii lɛ moŋ. Jwɛi ni ji jwɛi lɛ ahaŋ nyɛ eko, shi ntayai lɛ ayikulɛ lɛ nyɛbaafo nakai nɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ anɔkwɛlɔi lɛ na akɛ sane fɔŋ eye amɛ be ni akɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkatsea nyɛdaa gbi ntayaa ni sa ni nyɛfo lɛ nɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ” lɛ.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshi Farao ŋɔɔ amɛyaa lɛ, amɛyanina Mose kɛ Aaron yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmiimɛ amɛ.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛ Mose kɛ Aaron akɛ, “Yehowa akojo nyɛ ejaakɛ nyɛhã wɔsane eje Farao kɛ etsuji agugɔŋ fũ, ni nyɛwo amɛdɛ̃ŋ klante ni amɛkɛgbe wɔ.” Mose ye ŋkɔmɔ etsɔ̃ɔ Yehowa

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose saa eku esɛɛ etee Yehowa hiɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Ao! Yehowa, mɛɛba moŋ ofee wɔ, omaŋ lɛ, efɔŋ nɛkɛ? Mɛɛba kwraa otsu mi biɛ mɔ?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛjɛ beyinɔ ni miba mikɛ Farao bawie yɛ ogbɛi mli nɛɛ lɛ, efɔŋ moŋ sɔŋŋ efeɔ omaŋ lɛ, ni jiemɔ hu ojieko amɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpaako obaana nɔ ni mibafee Farao. Ja minineshiwalɛ naa dani eeehã Israelbii lɛ aya. Anɔkwa, minineshiwalɛ naa hu dani eeeshwie amɛ kɛje eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.” Nyɔŋmɔ tsɛ Mose

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: mi mijie mihe kpo mitsɔ̃ɔ Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ. Shi migbɛi Yehowa lɛ, mihãaa akɛ no ale mi.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Ni misaa mi kɛ amɛ kpãŋ akɛ mikɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ baahã amɛ, shikpɔŋ ko ni amɛyato gbɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ hu, minu Israelbii ni Ijiptbii lɛ yeɔ amɛ nyɔŋ lɛ akɔmɔyeli blɔmɔ lɛ he, ni mikai mi kɛ amɛteŋ kpãŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ mikɛɛ, ‘Mi ji Yehowa, ni majie nyɛ, ni mawo Ijiptbii lɛ ajatsu lɛ yɛ nyɛkuɛ nɔ, ni mahere nyɛ kɛje nyɔŋ ni amɛyeɔ nyɛ lɛ mli. Mikɛ mihewalɛ aaakpɔ̃ nyɛ, ni no nɔŋŋ mikɛaagbala Ijiptbii lɛ atoi.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Maŋɔ nyɛ mafee mi diɛŋtsɛ mimaŋ, ni matsɔ̃ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ, ni nyɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni jie nyɛ yɛ Ijipt nyɔŋyeli lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Mikɛ nyɛ aaatee shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikã he kitã akɛ mikɛbaahã Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob lɛ nɔ. Mi ji Yehowa.’ ”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Mose bɔ Israelbii lɛ amaniɛ, shi amɛbooo Mose toi yɛ amɛwerɛ ni eho amɛhe kɛ amɛnɔ nyɔŋyeli ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛ Mose wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Yaa ni okɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ ayawie, ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ ehã Israelbii lɛ aje eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛya.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Shi Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “MiNuŋtsɔ, Israelbii lɛ tete boko mi toi, te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni Farao aaabo mi toi hu; ni minaa hu tseee nɛɛ?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛ Mose kɛ Aaron wie, ni efã amɛ akɛ amɛya Israelbii lɛ kɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ, koni amɛyajie Israelbii lɛ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mose kɛ Aaron wekukpãa

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Yakob, ni batsɔ̃ Israel lɛ, kromɔbi Ruben bihii nɛ: Hanok kɛ Palu kɛ Hezron kɛ Karmi. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Ruben wekui lɛ ayitsei lɛ.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon bihii nɛ: Yemuel kɛ Yamin kɛ Ohad kɛ Yakin kɛ Zohar kɛ Shaul, Kanaanyoo lɛ bi lɛ. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Simeon wekui lɛ ayitsei.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gershon bihii nɛ: Libni kɛ Shimei. Amɛ hu amɛna wekui.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari bihii nɛ: Maheli kɛ Mushi. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Levi wekui lɛ ayitsei yɛ amɛfɔmɔ naa.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Izhar bihii nɛ: Kora kɛ Nefeg kɛ Zikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Uziel bihii nɛ: Mishael kɛ Elzafan kɛ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aaron ŋɔ Aminadab biyoo Elisheba, ni ji Nahashon nyɛmiyoo lɛ. Ekɛ lɛ fɔ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Eleazar kɛ Itamar.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aaron bi Eleazar yaŋɔ Putiel biyoo ni ekɛ lɛ hi shi, ni ekɛ lɛ fɔ Finehas. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji Levibii awei kɛ shĩai lɛ ayitsei lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ Mose nɛɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyajiea Israelbii lɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ” lɛ,

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: amɛ amɛyabi Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ koni eŋmɛɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe ni amɛshi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yehowa fã Mose kɛ Aaron

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Gbi nɔ ni Yehowa kɛ Mose wie yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ekɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mi ji Yehowa. Kɛɛmɔ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mikɛ bo wieɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Shi Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Naa, minaa tseee. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni Farao aaabo mi toi hu.”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Naa, miihã otsɔ̃ tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ ohã Farao, ni onyɛmi Aaron aaatsɔ̃ ogbalɔ.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mifã bo ni owie lɛ, kɛɛmɔ onyɛmi Aaron, ni lɛ ekɛ Farao awie koni eŋmɛɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe ni amɛshi eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛya.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛ migbala Ijiptbii lɛ atoi, ni mijie Israelbii lɛ kɛje amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no Ijiptbii kɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron fee bɔ ni Yehowa fã amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Kɛji Farao kɛɛ nyɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛfea naakpɛɛ nɔ ko’ lɛ, no lɛ Mose, kɛɛmɔ Aaron akɛ, ‘Kɔ otso lɛ ni okɛfɔ̃ shi yɛ Farao hiɛ; ni tso lɛ aaatsɔ̃ onufu.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose kɛ Aaron tee Farao ŋɔɔ, ni amɛfee bɔ ni Yehowa efã amɛ lɛ. Aaron kɛ etso lɛ fɔ shi yɛ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ ahiɛ, ni tso lɛ tsɔ onufu.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao hu hã ayatsɛ nilelɔi kɛ ŋkunyaayelɔi kɛba. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ji Ijipt ashwãifeelɔi lɛ. Amɛ hu amɛkɛ amɛkunyaayeli ŋai lɛ fee nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ etso fɔ̃ shikpɔŋ, ni tsei lɛ tsɔmɔ onufui; shi Aaron tso lɛ mimii amɛtsei lɛ.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Shi Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni ebooo Mose kɛ Aaron toi taakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa ewie eto lɛ. Amanehului ba Ijipt nɔ Nu tsɔ la

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Farao tsui wa, ekpɛlɛɛɛ ni maŋ lɛ yaa.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Yaa Farao ŋɔɔ leebi. Ebaaje kpo eya faa lɛ naa. Kɔ tso lɛ ni tsɔ onufu lɛ ohiɛ odɛ̃, ni oyadamɔ jɛi omɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa, ni ji Hebribii lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, tsu mi oŋɔɔ koni mibakɛɛ bo akɛ, hã mimaŋ lɛ aya ni amɛyaja mi yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; ni naa, okpɛ̃lɛko kɛbashi benɛ.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, enɛ okɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa lɛ. Naa, mikɛ tso ni mihiɛ yɛ midɛ̃ nɛɛ baatswa Nilo Faa lɛ mli, ni nu lɛ baatsɔ̃ lá.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Nilo Faa lɛ mli loi baagboi, ni faa lɛ baasha bɔ ni Ijiptbii aaanyaŋe Nilo numɔ!’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa fã Mose akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Aaron akɛ, ‘Kɔ otso lɛ ni okpã onine mli yɛ Ijipt nu fɛɛ nu, ni ji fai kɛ nujɔi ni aje gbɛ agbala kɛ bukoi kɛ nu ni bua shi fɛɛ, nɔ, ni amɛaatsɔmɔ lá. Nu ni yɔɔ tso kɛ tɛ gogai amli fɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ lá.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron fee bɔ ni Yehowa fã amɛ lɛ. Aaron wo etso lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛtswa Nilo Faa lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ ahiɛ, kɛkɛ ni faa lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ tsɔ̃ lá.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Loi ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ gboi, ni faa lɛ sha bɔ ni Ijiptbii lɛ nyɛɛɛ Nilo mli nu amɛnu. Lá sɔŋŋ ji Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Shi Ijipt ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ hu kɛ amɛkunyaayelɔi fee nakai nɔŋŋ. Enɛ hã Farao tee nɔ ekpliŋ etsui, ni ebooo Mose kɛ Aaron toi tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ewie eto lɛ.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Ni Farao ku esɛɛ etee ewe lɛ, ni nɔ ni afee lɛ gbaaa enaa kwraa.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ni Ijiptbii fɛɛ jejee nubui yɛ faa lɛ hewɔ koni amɛna nu amɛnu ejaakɛ amɛnyɛɛɛ Nilo mli nu amɛnu.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Yaa Farao ŋɔɔ koni oyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ; hã mimaŋ lɛ aya ni amɛyasɔ̃mɔ mi.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji okpɛ̃lɛɛɛ ni amɛya lɛ, mikɛ kɔkɔdenei baahao oshikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Nilo Faa lɛ baawo kɔkɔdenei nyɛŋɛnyɛŋɛ, ni kɔkɔdenei nɛɛ aaaba owe lɛ kɛ osa nɔ kɛshɛ osɛɛtsuŋ; amɛaaba otsuji ashĩai kɛ omaŋbii lɛ ateŋ kɛ nyɛflɔnɔi kɛ nyɛmã tsesei fɛɛ amli.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɔkɔdenei lɛ aaatumɔ kɛnyiɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ kɛ omaŋbii kɛ otsuji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ tete.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Aaron akɛ, ‘Kɔ otso lɛ ni okpã onine mli yɛ fai kɛ nujɔi ni agbala kɛ nu ni buabua shi lɛ anɔ, ni ohã kɔkɔdenei atumɔ kɛba Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Shi ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ kɛ amɛkunyaayeli ŋai lɛ fee nakai nɔŋŋ, ni amɛ hu amɛhã kɔkɔdenei ba Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao fã, ni ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkpaa Yehowa fai koni ejie kɔkɔdenei lɛ yɛ mi kɛ mimaŋbii lɛ anɔ, ni mahã Israelbii lɛ aya koni amɛyashã afɔle amɛhã Yehowa.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Mose here Farao nɔ akɛ, “Bo diɛŋtsɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ beyinɔ ni mikpa fai mihã bo kɛ otsuji kɛ omaŋbii lɛ koni ajie kɔkɔdenei lɛ yɛ bo kɛ owe lɛ kɛ omaŋbii ashĩai, ni ashwɛ faa lɛ mli nɔ lɛ kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Farao jie naa akɛ, “Wɔ”. Mose kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Aaafee bɔ ni obi lɛ koni okɛna ole akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni tamɔ Yehowa wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Kɔkɔdenei lɛ baaje bo kɛ owe lɛ kɛ otsuji lɛ kɛ omaŋbii lɛ anɔ aya. Nilo Faa lɛ mli nɔ lɛ kɛkɛ aaashwɛ.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kɛ Aaron gbala amɛhe shi, ni Mose tee eyasɔle etsɛ Yehowa yɛ shi ni ewo Farao yɛ kɔkɔdenei lɛ ahe lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Yehowa fee bɔ ni Mose bi lɛ lɛ, ni kɔkɔdenei lɛ gboi yɛ shĩai kɛ kpoi anɔ kɛ jwɛiaŋ.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Ni Ijiptbii lɛ buabua kɔkɔdenei gbohii lɛ anaa kuikui, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sha.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
