english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Aaron koni ekpã enine mli ni ekɛ etso lɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlu lɛ koni mlu lɛ atsɔ̃ tɔ̃ŋtɔ̃ŋ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron fee nakai. Aaron kpã enine mli, ni ekɛ etso lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ mlu lɛ, ni mlu lɛ tsɔ̃ tɔ̃ŋtɔ̃ŋ, ni eku eshwie gbɔmɔ kɛ kooloo fɛɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ mlu fɛɛ tsɔ tɔ̃ŋtɔ̃ŋ yɛ Ijipt.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ijipt ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ ka, yɛ amɛkunyaayeli ŋai lɛ anaa koni amɛhã tɔ̃ŋtɔ̃ŋ lɛ eko aba, shi amɛnyɛɛɛ. Tɔ̃ŋtɔ̃ŋ lɛ ha gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ tsu.” Shi Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni ebooo Mose kɛ Aaron toi tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ewie eto lɛ. Ofɔii ba

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Tee shi leebi maŋkpa ni oyafo Farao be mli ni eyaa faa lɛ naa, koni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ, ‘Hã mimaŋ lɛ aya ni amɛyaja mi.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Naa, kɛji oŋmɛɛɛ mimaŋ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛya lɛ, mahã ofɔii abaha bo kɛ otsuji kɛ omaŋbii lɛ. Ijiptbii ashĩai amli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ hu aaayi tɔ kɛ ofɔii lɛ.

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ni mikɛ tɛ̃ ni matɛ̃ amɛ mashi nɛɛ aaato bo okadi koni okɛna srɔto ni yɔɔ mi mimaŋ lɛ kɛ bo omaŋ lɛ teŋ. Wɔ ni ji wɔ lɛ mato nɛkɛ okadi nɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa fee nakai, ni ofɔii babaoo ba Farao we lɛ kɛ etsuji ashĩai lɛ kɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ni ofɔii lɛ hã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kpãtã.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao fã ni ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa nyɛyashãa afɔle lɛ nyɛhãa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shi moŋ nyɛshãa yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Shi Mose kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Ebahiŋ nakai feemɔ, ejaakɛ Ijiptbii anihiinii wɔkɛbaashã afɔle wɔhã Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Kɛji wɔkɛ Ijiptbii anihiinii shã afɔle yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ, ani amɛtswiaŋ wɔ tɛ?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Esa ni wɔnyiɛ gbii etɛ̃ gbɛ kɛya ŋa nɔ koni wɔyashã afɔle lɛ wɔhã Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, bɔ ni efã wɔ.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Farao to he ekɛɛ, “Mibaŋmɛ nyɛ gbɛ ni nyɛya koni nyɛyashã afɔle nyɛhã Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, shi shɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni nyɛkayaa. Nyɛsɔlea nyɛhãa mi.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose jie naa akɛ, “Naa, mibashi maya koni mayasɔle mabi Yehowa koni ofɔii lɛ aje Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ kɛ emaŋbii anɔ wɔ. Shi shishiumɔ sane kɛkɛ ni Farao akaye dɔŋŋ, akɛ ehaŋ maŋ lɛ aya ayashã afɔle ahã Yehowa.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ni Mose gbala ehe shi etee eyasɔle ekpa Yehowa fai.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa fee nɔ ni Mose bi lɛ lɛ, ni ejie ofɔii lɛ yɛ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ anɔ. Eshwɛɛɛ ekome folo.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Shi Farao kpliŋ etsui ekoŋŋ, ni ehãaa Israelbii lɛ aya.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Yaa Farao ŋɔɔ ni oyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa, Hebribii aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Hã mimaŋ lɛ aya koni amɛyasɔ̃mɔ mi.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: no lɛ Yehowa baatswia nyɛkooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ nii, ni ebaahã otswashiogbo ni naa wa abote nyɛkpɔŋɔi kɛ tejii kɛ yoomai kɛ tsinai kɛ toi lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa aaahã srɔto aba Israelbii akooloi kɛ Ijiptbii akooloi ateŋ, ni Israelbii akooloi lɛ ateŋ eko eko gboŋ.’

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa to be ekɛɛ, ‘Wɔ lɛ Yehowa baafee nii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Yehowa fee nɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ; Ijiptbii akooloi lɛ fɛɛ gboi, shi Israelbii akooloi lɛ ateŋ ekome folo nɛkɛ gbooo.

english_verse: When the king found out, he was still too stubborn to let the people go. Sores

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose kɛ Aaron akɛ, “Nyɛkpitía flɔɔnɔɔ mli lamlu nyɛkɔkɔi obɔ̃bɔ̃, ni Mose kɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ Farao hiɛ.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Lamlu nɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ mlu, ni eeegbɛ eshwã Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ; eeetsɔ̃ asane ni fuɔ, ni efɛlɛɔ yɛ gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi ahe yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron kpiti flɔnɔɔ mli lamlu lɛ, ni amɛbadamɔ Farao hiɛ, ni Mose kɛ lamlu lɛ shwã ŋwɛi. Kɛkɛ ni lamlu lɛ tsɔ̃ asane ni fuɔ ni fɛlɛɔ yɛ gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi ahe.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ijipt ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ Mose hiɛ tete amɛshɛ yɛ asanei lɛ ahewɔ, ejaakɛ asane lɛ etsɛ̃rɛ ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ kɛ Ijiptbii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa hã Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni ebooo Mose kɛ Aaron toi tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ewie eto lɛ. Nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi nɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Tee shi wɔ leebi maŋkpa ni oyadamɔ Farao hiɛ, ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa, Hebribii aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Hã mimaŋ lɛ aya koni amɛyasɔ̃mɔ mi,

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ agbɛnɛ lɛ mahã haomɔi srɔtoi fɛɛ aba bo diɛŋtsɛ kɛ otsuji lɛ kɛ omaŋbii lɛ anɔ koni okɛna ole akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni tamɔ mi yɛ je lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Kulɛ bɛnɛ mijie mihewalɛ kpo mitsɔ̃ɔ, ni mihã gbele hela etswa bo kɛ omaŋbii, ni nyɛhiɛ ekpãtã momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Shi enɛ hewɔ mihã oyɔɔ wala mli lolo koni majie mihewalɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ bo koni akɛtsi mitã yɛ jeŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Okã he oowo ohe nɔ yɛ mimaŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ohãaa amɛya.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Naa, wɔ aaafee benɛ mli lɛ mahã nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi ni naa wa naakpa diɛŋtsɛ anɛ bɔ ni anako ehenɔ dã yɛ Ijipt kɛjɛ ni ato maŋ lɛ nɛɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Farao tsuji lɛ ateŋ mɔ ni yashe Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ gbeyei lɛ, ehã etsuji kɛ ekooloi fɛɛ jo foi kɛba shĩa;

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: shi mɔ ni eyabuuu Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ, eshĩ etsuji kɛ ekooloi yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpã onine mli kɛya ŋwɛi koni nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi anɛ ashwie gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi kɛ ŋa nɔ bai fɛɛ nɔ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Be ni enɛɔ lɛ belɛ srawa lɛ hu miigbala plamplam kɛnyiɛ mli. Nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ nɛ waa naakpa bɔ ni anako ehenɔ dã yɛ Ijipt kɛjɛ be mli ni etsɔ̃ maŋ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Shi Goshen shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni Israelbii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, kɛkɛ ji he ni nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi nɛɛ eko enɛɛɛ yɛ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao tsu ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ mifee esha. Yehowa lɛ jalɔ ji lɛ, shi mi kɛ mimaŋ lɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji ji wɔ.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkpaa Yehowa fai koni ŋwɛi shiimɔ kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ akpa; shi efa; ni mahã nyɛya, ni mitsiŋ nyɛnaa dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mose kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Amrɔ pɛ ni maje kpo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, mahole miniji anɔ matsɛ Yehowa, ni ŋwɛi shiimɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ asɛɛ aaafo, ni eko eko baŋ dɔŋŋ, koni ona ole akɛ je lɛ Yehowa nɔ ni.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Shi mile akɛ bo kɛ otsuji lɛ nyɛnako nyɛshe Yehowa ni ji Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ gbeyei.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Akoko kɛ tso ni ajieɔ kpãa ni akɛloɔ ojarawa mama yɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ kpãtã, ejaakɛ akoko lɛ ewo, ni tso lɛ hu ehere momo.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Shi ŋmaa kɛ abele hiɛ kpãtãaa ejaakɛ amɛ lɛ amɛkpeɔ sɛɛ kɛ woo.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose shi Farao, ni eje maŋ lɛ mli hu, ni ehole eniji anɔ etsɛ Yehowa. Kɛkɛ ni ŋwɛi shiimɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ asɛɛ fo, ni nu lɛ kpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛmɔ.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Shi be ni Farao na akɛ nunɛmɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi shiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ efo lɛ, esaa efee esha ekoŋŋ, ni lɛ kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ saa kpliŋ amɛtsui.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Farao bakpliŋ etsui, ni ehãaa Israelbii lɛ aya tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ewie eto yɛ Mose naa lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Yaa Farao ŋɔɔ, shi mihã ekpliŋ etsui, ni etsuji lɛ hu ekpliŋ amɛtsui bɔ ni afee ni mafee naakpɛɛ nii nɛɛ fɛɛ matsɔ̃ɔ amɛ,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: koni ogba obii kɛ obii abii nibii ni mifee yɛ Ijipt, kɛ naakpɛɛ okadii ni mifee yɛ amɛteŋ, ni okpã owo amɛtoiiaŋ koni nyɛna nyɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron tee Farao ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa, Hebribii aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Mɛɛ beyinɔ po oookpɛ̃lɛ koni oba ohe shi ohã mi? Hã mimaŋ lɛ aya koni amɛyaja mi.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Shi kɛji okpɛ̃lɛɛɛ ni mimaŋ lɛ aya lɛ, no lɛ naa, wɔ kpaakpa wɔ lɛ, mahã baalabii aba okpokpai lɛ anɔ,

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: ni amɛaaha shi bɔ sɔŋŋ ni anaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ tete, ni amɛaaye nii fɛɛ ni shwɛ hã nyɛ yɛ ŋa nɔ ni nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ kpãtãaa hiɛ lɛ. Amɛaaye bai fɛɛ ni tsɛ̃rɛɔ yɛ nyɛtsei anɔ yɛ ŋa nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Ni amɛaayimɔ oshĩai kɛ otsuji fɛɛ ashĩai kɛ Ijiptbii fɛɛ ashĩai amli tɔtɔɔtɔ, bɔ ni otsɛmɛi kɛ oniimɛi enako ehenɔ pɛŋ kɛjɛ be ni afɔ amɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ.’ ” Ni Mose tsɔ̃ ehe, ni eshi Farao.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ ni nuu nɛɛ aaahao wɔ kɛyashi? Hã Israelbii lɛ aya ni amɛyasɔ̃mɔ Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Ani oleko lolo akɛ Ijipt hiɛ miikpãtã?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba Farao hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa ni nyɛyasɔ̃mɔ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Shi moŋ, namɛi kɛ namɛi ji mɛi ni baaya lɛ?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose jie naa ekɛɛ, “Wɔbii bibii lɛ ni jio, wɔnukpai lɛ ni jio, wɔbihii jio, wɔbiyei jio, wɔtoi kɛ wɔtsinai jio wɔkɛ fɛɛ baaya ejaakɛ wɔyaaye gbi jurɔ wɔhã Yehowa.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Farao kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Kɛ miŋmɛ gbɛ ni nyɛ kɛ nyɛbii lɛ tee fĩĩ bɛ Yehowa ejɔɔ nyɛ. Kolɛ jeee yiŋ fɔŋ ko nyɛto nɛɛ?

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Dabida, nyɛhii lɛ kɛkɛ nyɛyaa nyɛyasɔ̃mɔa Yehowa, ejaakɛ no nɔŋŋ ji nɔ ni nyɛtaoɔ.” Ni ashwie Mose kɛ Aaron kɛje Farao hiɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpã onine mli yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni baalabii aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaye bai fɛɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ eshi lɛ.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Mose wo etso lɛ nɔ, ni Yehowa hã bokã kɔɔyɔɔ ko batswa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, gbi lɛ shwane kɛ nyɔɔŋ fɛɛ, ni be ni je tsɛreɔ lɛ bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ baalabii lɛ eba.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Baalabii lɛ bashwie Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Amɛha Ijipt kpokpai lɛ anɔ nyɛŋɛnyɛŋɛ. Baalabii bako ni tamɔ amɛ nakai dã, ni amɛsɛɛ hu eko baŋ nakai dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛha shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wo duŋ, ni amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bai fɛɛ kɛ tsei ni nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi lɛ shi lɛ anɔ yibii fɛɛ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao tsu oya mli, ni ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mifee esha mishi Yehowa, nyɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni mifee nyɛ hu esha.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ okɛ mihe esha lɛ afa mi, shi kome nɛɛ kɛkɛ, ni nyɛkpa Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fai koni ejie nɛkɛ toigbalamɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ kɛkɛ yɛ minɔ.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Mose shi Farao etee, ni eyakpa Yehowa fai.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa hã anai kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naakpa batswa, ni eloo baalabii lɛ blublu kɛtee eyashwie Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ mli. Baalabii lɛ ateŋ ekome folo nɛkɛ eshwɛɛɛ yɛ Ijipt kpokpai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa hã Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni ehãaa Israelbii lɛ aya. Duŋ wo

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpã onine mli kɛya ŋwɛi koni duŋ awo yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, duŋ kabitii.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Mose kpã enine mli kɛtee ŋwɛi, kɛkɛ ni duŋ kpii wo yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ gbii etɛ̃.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Duŋ nɛɛ wo bɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa enaanyo, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko shiii he ni duŋ lɛ banina lɛ yɛ lɛ kɛyashi gbii etɛ̃. Shi jeŋ tse heŋŋ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ashihilɛhei lɛ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao tsɛ Mose ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa koni nyɛyasɔ̃mɔ Yehowa; nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛkɛ nyɛbii lɛ aya, shi nyɛshĩa nyɛtoi kɛ nyɛtsinai lɛ.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Shi Mose kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Ja ohã wɔna kooloi hu ni akɛshãa gbee afɔle kɛ shãa afɔlei wɔhiɛ wɔdɛ̃ ni wɔkɛyashã afɔle wɔhã Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Wɔkooloi aku lɛ hu ja wɔkɛtee, ni ashiŋ kooloo kome tete yɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ nomɛi eko wɔkɛyaasɔmɔ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Wɔ diɛŋtsɛ kwraa wɔleee amɛteiaŋ nii ni wɔkɛyaasɔmɔ Yehowa akɛ ja wɔshɛ jɛi dã.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa hã Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ Israelbii lɛ aya.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Ni Farao bɔ Mose kɔkɔ ekɛɛ, “Jee mihiɛ ni oya. Okwɛ ohe ni ahi koni okaba mihiɛ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ gbi nɔ ni ooobapue ekoŋŋ yɛ mihiɛ lɛ gbo ooogbo.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Mose here Farao nɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mibaŋ ohiɛ dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Eshwɛ amanehulu wulu kome ni mahã aba Farao kɛ Ijipt nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ eeehã nyɛje biɛ nyɛya. Be ni eeehã nyɛ fɛɛ nyɛya kwraa lɛ, shwiemɔ tete ebaashwie nyɛ kɛje biɛ.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ kpã owo Israelbii lɛ atoiŋ akɛ nuu fɛɛ nuu kɛ yoo fɛɛ yoo amala jwiɛtɛi nii kɛ shika nii yɛ enaanyo Ijiptnyo dɛŋ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã Ijiptbii lɛ ahiɛ sɔ Israelbii lɛ. Anɔkwa, Farao tsuji lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ buɔ Mose akɛ gbɔmɔ wulu diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ni Mose kɛɛ Farao akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: ‘Nyɔɔŋteŋ lɛ maje kpo makpa Ijipt,

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: ni Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kromɔbii fɛɛ aaagboi kɛjɛ Farao kromɔbi ni baaye esɛɛ yɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaashi nyɔŋyoo ni yɔɔ wiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kromɔbi lɛ tete nɔ. Kooloi po akromɔbii fɛɛ baagboi.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ni aaawo yara babaoo yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni anako ehenɔ dã, ni asaŋ ehenɔ ko hu baŋ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Shi yɛ Israelbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, gbɔmɔ jio, kooloo jio, gbee tete shiŋ esɛŋ ewoŋ lɛ, koni nyɛkɛna nyɛle akɛ Yehowa miitsɔ̃ɔ srɔto ni yɔɔ Ijiptbii kɛ Israelbii ateŋ.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ otsuji fɛɛ aaakpeleke shi aaaba miŋɔɔ, ni amɛaabakoto mi amɛkɛɛ, Jee biɛ ni oya, bo kɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oshishi lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ matee.’ ”

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Farao ebaboŋ nyɛ toi bɔ ni afee ni minaakpɛɛ nii lɛ afa yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron fee nɛkɛ naakpɛɛ nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ Farao nɛ, shi Yehowa hã Farao kpliŋ etsui ni ehãaa Israelbii lɛ ashi eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛya.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Nɛkɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ afi mli klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔɔŋ kɛ afi shishijee ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ awie akɛ, Nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ, Israelbii fɛɛ amɔmɔ toobi kome kome yɛ amɛtsɛmɛi awei lɛ anaa, shĩa fɛɛ shĩa lɛ toobi kome.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ toobi nɛɛ ato kɛyashi nyɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ koni Israelbii fɛɛ agbegbee amɛ gbɛkɛnaashi.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Akɛ lá lɛ eko adiki shĩai hei ni abaaye yɛ lɛ agboi lɛ ashinaatsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ yiteŋ nɔ lɛ hu he.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Aye loo lɛ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ. Ashã, ni akɛ aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã kɛ shwie ni joɔ aye.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Akaye lɛ eŋmɔŋ, ni akɛ nu akahoo, shi moŋ ashã, eyitso kɛ eshuɔji kɛ emlinii lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Nyɛkashwɛa eko nyɛtoa ni je tsɛre nɔ. Shi kɛji eko shwɛ ni je tsɛre nɔ lɛ, nyɛwoa mli la ni nyɛshãa.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ni bɔ ni nyɛye lɛ nɛ. Nyɛfimɔa nyɛmliteiaŋ, ni nyɛwoa nyɛtokotai, ni nyɛdɛ̃hiɛmɔtsei ahiɛa nyɛdɛ̃, ni nyɛyea lɛ paopao, shi Yehowa Hehoo ni.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Ejaakɛ matsɔ̃ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli, ni magbe Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kromɔbi fɛɛ kromɔbi, gbɔmɔ ni jio, kooloo ni jio, koni mahã Ijipt nyɔŋmɔi lɛ fɛɛ ahe guɔ agbo, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Lá lɛ aaatsɔ̃ shĩai amli ni nyɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe okadi. Kɛji mina lá lɛ pɛ mateke nyɛ, ni mikpataŋ nyɛhiɛ be ni matswia Ijipt gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi nii lɛ.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ gbi nɛɛ atsɔ̃ kaimɔ gbi ahã nyɛ, ni nyɛye lɛ akɛ Yehowa gbi jurɔ, ni etsɔ̃ akpɔ ehã nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei kɛya naanɔ.” Akpiti Gbijurɔyeli lɛ

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: “Aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã nɛɛ nyɛyea lɛ gbii kpawo. Shi klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ beebe lɛ, nyɛjiea masha fɛɛ masha yɛ nyɛshĩai amli. Ejaakɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baaye masha aboloo yɛ gbii kpawo nɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ, aaakpãtã ehiɛ yɛ Israel.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ akpe kpee krɔŋkrɔŋ kɛja Nyɔŋmɔ, ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ hu nɔ lɛ akpe kpee krɔŋkrɔŋ nakai nɔŋŋ. Akatsu nitsumɔ ko nitsumɔ ko yɛ gbii nɛɛ amli ja nitsumɔ ni kɔɔ nɔ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aaaye he kɛkɛ.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Nyɛyea nɛkɛ akpiti gbijurɔ nɛɛ nyɛkɛkaia gbi nɔ ni mijie nyɛ fɛɛ yuu kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyea gbijurɔ nɛɛ, nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei fɛɛ, ni etsɔ̃ akpɔ ehã nyɛ kɛya naanɔ.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Nyɛbɔ̃ia aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã nɛɛ yeli kɛyashi nyɔɔŋ lɛ gbi nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ekome lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Akana masha ko yɛ nyɛshiai amli gbii kpawo, ejaakɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaaye masha nii lɛ, gbɔ ni jio, Israel fɔmɔbi ni jio, ehiɛ aaakpãtã yɛ Israelbii ateŋ.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Nyɛkayea masha nii, nyɛyea akpiti yɛ nyɛshihilɛhei fɛɛ.” Klɛŋklɛŋ Hehoo lɛ

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose tsɛ Israel onukpai lɛ fɛɛ kɛbakpe, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛjiea toi nyɛtoa yɛ nyɛwekui lɛ anaa, ni nyɛgbea kɛyea Hehoo lɛ.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ lá lɛ awoa lalakã mli, ni nyɛkɛ ŋshɔŋ kotsa atsɔ lá nɛɛ mli koni nyɛkɛdiki agbo lɛ shinaatsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ yiteŋ nɔ lɛ hu, ni nyɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko akajea kpo kɛba shinaashi kɛyashi leebi.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa baaho koni eyatswia Ijiptbii nii. Kɛji ena lá lɛ yɛ shinaatsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ eyiteŋ nɔ lɛ he pɛ, Yehowa baateke nyɛshiai lɛ, ni eŋmɛŋ hiɛkpãtãlɔ lɛ gbɛ ni ebote nyɛshĩai lɛ amli koni ebatswia nyɛ nii.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ni kɛji nyɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni Yehowa kɛbaahã nyɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni ewo shi eto lɛ, nyɛhiɛa nɛkɛ jamɔ nɛɛ mli.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Ni kɛji nyɛbii aaabi nyɛ akɛ, ‘Te nyɛjamɔ nɛɛ shishi hu?’ lɛ,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa Hehoo afɔle ni, ejaakɛ be ni etswia Ijiptbii lɛ nii lɛ, eho Israelbii ashĩai lɛ ahe yɛ Ijipt ni etɛ̃ wɔshĩai lɛ eshĩ.’ ” Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ mamɔ amɛyi shi, ni amɛja Yehowa,

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: ni Israelbii lɛ gbɛlɛ mli, ni amɛyafee bɔ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ Mose kɛ Aaron akɛ afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kromɔbii lɛ agbele

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Gbi lɛ nyɔɔŋteŋ lɛ Yehowa tswia Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kromɔbii fɛɛ nii, kɛjɛ Farao kromɔbi lɛ ni baaye etsɛ sɛɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ, kɛyashi gboklɛfonyo ni kã kpabu mli lɛ kromɔbii kɛ shĩa kooloi akromɔbii fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Farao te shi nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ, lɛ kɛ etsuji fɛɛ kɛ Ijiptbii fɛɛ, ni amɛwo yara waa yɛ Ijipt fɛɛ, ejaakɛ eyashwɛɛɛ shĩa ko ni gbonyo bɛ mli.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni Farao tsu ni ayatsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛjea mimaŋbii ateŋ nyɛyaa, nyɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ, nyɛyasɔ̃mɔa Yehowa tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛbi lɛ.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ nyɛtoi kɛ nyɛtsinai lɛ hu ayaa tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛkɛɛ lɛ. Kɛfee lɛ nyɛsɔlea eko nyɛhãa mi koni jɔɔmɔ lɛ eko anina mi hu.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ni Ijiptbii lɛ tsirɛ Israelbii lɛ ayisɛɛ akɛ amɛhe afee oya ni amɛshi amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛkɛɛ, “Nyɛbaahã wɔ fɛɛ wɔgboi.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ hole amɛmai ni nako asha ni yɔɔ tsesei amli lɛ, ni amɛfimɔ tsesei lɛ amɛwowoo amɛmamai amli, kɛkɛ ni amɛhole amɛtswia amɛkɔ̃ji.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Nakai be mli lɛ Israelbii lɛ efee bɔ ni Mose ekɛɛ amɛ lɛ, ni amɛmala jwiɛtɛi nii kɛ shika nii kɛ mamai yɛ Ijiptbii lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã Ijiptbii lɛ ahiɛ sɔ Israelbii lɛ, ni amɛhãhãa amɛ nibii ni amɛbibii amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kpakpla Ijiptbii lɛ ahenii kɛtee. Israelbii lɛ shi Ijipt

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ yi mli kɛjɛ Rameses kɛtee Sukot, hii ni nyiɛ amɛnane aaafee akpei ohai ekpaa, soro yei kɛ gbekɛbii.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Maji srɔtoi anɔ bii babaoo hu fata he kɛtee kɛ agbɛnɛ toi kɛ tsinai babaoo diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛ mã ni amɛkɛjɛ Ijipt lɛ eko shã mã akpiti keeki ejaakɛ eshako akɛ ni Ijiptbii lɛ shwie amɛ bɔ ni amɛwooo mɛɛ koni mã lɛ asha lɛ, ni no hewɔ hu lɛ amɛsako niyenii amɛtoko gbɛnyiɛmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Ni akɛni Yehowa shi kpe nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ kɛjie Israelbii lɛ kɛje Ijipt hewɔ lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nyɔɔŋ lɛ batsɔ̃ kpeshii nyɔɔŋ ehã Israelbii kɛ amɛyinɔi fɛɛ, ni amɛyeɔ lɛ akɛ Yehowa gbijurɔ. Hehoo lɛ he akpɔi

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose kɛ Aaron akɛ, “Hehoo lɛ he akpɔi nɛ: Mɔkpɔŋ ko mɔkpɔŋ ko akaye eko.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Shi nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ ni akɛ shika he lɛ lɛ, ofo lɛ ketia dani eye eko.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni ebato nyɛ gbɔ kɛ apaafonyo hu akaye eko.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Shĩa fɛɛ shĩa aye enɔ, akɛ loo lɛ eko akaje kpo yɛ shĩa lɛ, asaŋ akajwa loo lɛ mli wui lɛ eko.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ aye gbɛjianɔtoi nɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Shi kɛji gbɔ ni ebato gbɔ miitao akɛ eyeɔ Hehoo lɛ ekɛwo Yehowa hiɛ nyam lɛ, hã afolɔ ebihii lɛ fɛɛ ketia dani eba ni ebaye eko, ni eeetsɔ̃ tamɔ Israelnyo nɔŋŋ. Shi foolɔ ko foolɔ ko akaye eko.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mla kome akã shi ahã maŋnyo kɛ mɔ ni bato nyɛ gbɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ fee bɔ ni Yehowa wo Mose kɛ Aaron kitã lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Yehowa jie Israelbii lɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛkutsei lɛ anaa.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Kromɔbi nuu fɛɛ kromɔbi nuu, ni ji binuu fɛɛ binuu ni gbeleɔ musu naa, yɛ Israelbii ateŋ lɛ ajɔɔ enɔ ahã mi, gbɔmɔ ni jio, kooloo ni jio, ajɔɔ enɔ ahã mi, ejaakɛ minɔ ni.” Akpiti Gbijurɔ lɛ

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Kɛji Yehowa kɛ nyɛ yashɛ Kanaanbii kɛ Hitbii kɛ Amorbii kɛ Hivbii kɛ Yebusbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ kpakpa ni da ni yɔɔ frɔ̃frɔ̃ ni niyenii pii yɔɔ nɔ, nɔ ni ekã nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kitã akɛ ekɛbaahã nyɛ, lɛ nɔ lɛ, jamɔ ni nyɛkɛja lɛ yɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ nɛ:

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã lɛ, nyɛyea lɛ gbii kpawo; shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ Yehowa gbijurɔ ni.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã lɛ nyɛyea lɛ gbii kpawo; akana masha aboloo ko yɛ nyɛŋɔɔ loo masha nɔ ko yɛ nyɛkpokpai anɔ he ko he ko.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛtsia tã, ni nyɛtsɔ̃a nyɛbii gbijurɔ nɛɛ shishi akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni Yehowa fee ehã wɔ be mli ni wɔjeɔ Ijipt lɛ hewɔ ni wɔfeɔ enɛ.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɛkaia gbijurɔ nɛɛ. Nyɛhãa efea tamɔ okadi ko ni fi nyɛnineshi aloo ni kpɛtɛ nyɛhiɛŋtso nɔ koni Yehowa mla lɛ akã nyɛdaaŋ, ejaakɛ nineshiwalɛ naa Yehowa jie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyea nɛkɛ akpɔ nɛɛ nɔ yɛ ebe lɛ mli. Kromɔbii kpɔ̃mɔ

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Kɛji Yehowa kɛ nyɛ yashɛ Kanaanbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ekã nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kitã akɛ ekɛaahã nyɛ lɛ,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: binuu fɛɛ binuu ni gbeleɔ musu naa lɛ, nyɛjɔa enɔ nyɛhãa mi, Yehowa. Nyɛshiai amli kooloi akromɔ bihii hu Yehowa nii ni.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Teji kromɔ binuu fɛɛ kromɔ binuu lɛ nyɛkɛ too akpɔ̃a lɛ. Shi kɛji nyɛkpɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ lɛ, no lɛ aku ekuɛŋ. Shi gbɔmɔ kromɔbi fɛɛ kromɔbi lɛ nyɛkpɔ̃a lɛ.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛbii bi nyɛ wɔsɛɛ ko akɛ, ‘Ni te gbijurɔ nɛɛ shishi hu lɛ,’ nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ, ‘Nineshiwalɛ naa Yehowa jie wɔ kɛje Ijipt he ni aye wɔ nyɔŋ yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni Farao kɛ kuɛŋtilɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ kwrakwra akɛ eŋmɛ wɔ gbɛ koni wɔshi Ijipt lɛ, Yehowa gbe Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kromɔbii fɛɛ kɛjɛ gbɔmɔ kromɔbi nɔ kɛyashi kooloo tete kromɔbi nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kooloo fɛɛ kooloo ni gbeleɔ musu naa, ni ji nuu lɛ, wɔkɛshãa afɔle wɔhãa Yehowa lɛ, shi wɔkromɔ bihii lɛ, amɛ lɛ wɔkpɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Nyɛhãa enɛ afea tamɔ okadi ko ni fi nyɛnine shi aloo ni kpɛtɛ nyɛhiɛŋtso nɔ ejaakɛ nineshiwalɛ naa Yehowa jie wɔ kɛje Ijipt.’ ” Atatu kutuu kɛ la kutuu

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Be ni Farao ŋmɛ Israelbii lɛ gbɛ akɛ amɛya lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ kpalaaa amɛ kɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ Filistibii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ; tsɛbelɛ jɛi gbɛ lɛ jɛkɛɛɛ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ, “Koni Israelbii lɛ kɛ ta ko akayakpe yɛ gbɛteŋ, ni no hã amɛshwa amɛhe ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee Ijipt ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Israelbii lɛ lɔgɔ shi kɛtsɔ̃ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ he ŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ. Israelbii lɛ fã yɛ Ijipt ni amɛsaa amɛhe amɛhã ta.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mose loo Yosef gbonyowui lɛ kɛtee tamɔ bɔ ni Yosef ehã Israelbii lɛ ekã kitã amɛto lɛ. Yosef ekɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ aaakpɔ̃ nyɛ kɛ̃ be ko; kɛji be lɛ shɛ lɛ koni nyɛwo migbonyo wui lɛ kɛje biɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ yiŋ kɛjɛ Sukot, ni amɛyato shi yɛ Etam yɛ ŋa lɛ naa.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛdɔ amɛyi ni amɛyato shi yɛ Pi-Hahirot hiɛ, yɛ Migdol kɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ teŋ, yɛ Baal-Zefon masɛi. Nyɛtoa shi yɛ eŋlɛ nɔ, yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: No aaahã Farao asusu ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Israelbii lɛ eyadu gbɛ yɛ gbɛteŋ, shiaŋa lɛ esa amɛyi’.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Mahã Farao akpliŋ etsui koni etiu nyɛ, ni no aaahã Farao kɛ eta lɛ fɛɛ ashe mi gbeyei, ni Ijiptbii baana ale akɛ mi ji Yehowa lɛ.” Israelbii lɛ fee bɔ ni akɛɛ amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Be ni ababɔ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ amaniɛ akɛ Israelbii lɛ ejo foi amɛtee lɛ, Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ tsake amɛjwɛŋmɔ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ mɛni po wɔfee nɛɛ, ni wɔhã Israelbii lɛ kpa wɔ sɔ̃ɔmɔ ni amɛtee nɛɛ?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Farao saa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etayaa shwiilii lɛ, ni eloo esraafoi efata ehe.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa hã Ijipt maŋtsɛ Farao kpliŋ etsui, ni etiu Israelbii lɛ ni Yehowa hewalɛ nine ni tsii lɛ hiɛ amɛ kɛyaa lɛ.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Ijiptbii lɛ yi Israelbii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ Farao okpɔŋɔi kɛ tayaa shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi kɛ asraafoi fɛɛ. Ni amɛyanina Israelbii lɛ ni amɛto shi yɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naa, yɛ Pi-hahirot masɛi yɛ Baal-Zefon hiɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Farao kɛ eta lɛ tsi bɛŋkɛ. Be ni Israelbii lɛ yaahole amɛhiŋmɛii anɔ lɛ, naa Farao kɛ Ijiptbii lɛ ni amɛnyiɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛmiiba. Gbeyei mɔmɔ Israelbii lɛ naakpa, ni amɛbolɔ amɛtsɛ Yehowa.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Ani gbonyobui ni bɛ Ijipt hewɔ ni okpala wɔ kɛba koni wɔbagboi yɛ ŋa nɛɛ nɔ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba oye wɔ nɛkɛ sane, ni oloo wɔ kɛjɛ Ijipt kɛba biɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ani jeee wiemɔ ni wɔkɛ bo wie yɛ Ijipt lɛ nɛ akɛ, ‘Fɔ̃ɔmɔ ni ohã wɔsɔ̃mɔ Ijiptbii lɛ kɛkɛ?’ Shi faŋ nɔ moŋ ni wɔsɔ̃mɔ Ijiptbii lɛ fe nɔ ni wɔɔyagboi yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Ni Mose here Israelbii lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei! Nyɛdamɔa shi shiŋŋ ni nyɛkwɛa nyɛyiwala ni Yehowa baahere ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ. Ejaakɛ Ijiptbii ni nyɛnaa ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛnaŋ amɛ dɔŋŋ kɛaatee naanɔ.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Yehowa baawu ahã nyɛ, nyɛ lɛ nyɛfea diŋŋ”.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni obolɔɔ otsɛɔ mi? Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛya amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Shi bo lɛ, wo otso lɛ nɔ ni okpã onine mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ koni ogba ŋshɔ lɛ mli enyɔ koni Israelbii lɛ anyiɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ kɛya.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Mahã Ijiptbii lɛ akpliŋ amɛtsui koni amɛnyiɛ Israelbii lɛ asɛɛ, ni maye Farao kɛ eta shwiilii kɛ ekpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni kɛji miye Farao kɛ eta shwiilii kɛ ekpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ijiptbii aaana amɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo lɛ ni nyiɛ Israelbii lɛ ata lɛ hiɛ lɛ gbala ehe shi eyaje amɛsɛɛgbɛ, ni atatu kutuu lɛ je amɛhiɛgbɛ ni eyashi yɛ amɛsɛɛgbɛ,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: yɛ Ijiptbii ata lɛ kɛ Israelbii ata lɛ teŋ. Shwane lɛ atatu lɛ woɔ Ijiptbii lɛ hiɛ duŋ, ni nyɔɔŋ lɛ ekpɛɔ ehãa Israelbii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbi lɛ nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mɛnɛɛmɛi nyɛɛɛ mɛnɛɛmɛi abɛŋkɛ.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Mose kpã enine mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ, ni Yehowa hã bokã kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni naa wa batswa nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni ehã ŋshɔ lɛ gbala kɛtee sɛɛ, yɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ, ni emli gba enyɔ, ni eshi shikpɔŋ gbiŋ efɔ̃ shi yɛ eteŋ,

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: ni Israelbii lɛ yi shikpɔŋ gbiŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ, ni nu lɛ ma shi tamɔ gbogbo yɛ amɛninejurɔ kɛ amɛbɛku.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Ni maŋkɛ mra mli lɛ Yehowa jɛ atatu kutuu kɛ la kutuu lɛ mli ekwɛ Ijiptbii ata lɛ, ni ehao amɛ.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Ehã amɛshwiilii lɛ anaji lɛ bɔi fuu, ni ekɛwo Ijiptbii lɛ hejaramɔ. Kɛkɛ ni Ijiptbii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔjoa Israelbii lɛ anaa foi ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ wɔ miiwu miihã amɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpã onine mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋshɔ lɛ abaha Ijiptbii kɛ amɛtayaa shwiilii kɛ amɛkpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose kpã enine mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni jetsɛremɔ mli leebi lɛ ŋshɔ lɛ yiridi kɛjɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ kɛmiiba abatsa ekoŋŋ, ni Ijiptbii lɛ wo foi, shi amɛkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ bakpe, ni Yehowa hã Ijiptbii lɛ ahiɛ kpãtã yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Ŋshɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ ba, ni ebaha Farao shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔiatsɛmɛi kɛ eta muu lɛ fɛɛ ni tiu Israelbii lɛ kɛtee ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ; eshwɛɛɛ amɛteŋ mɔ kome tete po.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Shi Israelbii lɛ nyiɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ, ni nu lɛ tsɔ̃ tamɔ gbogbo hã amɛ yɛ amɛninejurɔ kɛ amɛbɛku.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa fee ehere Israelbii lɛ ayiwala kɛjɛ Ijiptbii adɛŋ nɛ, ni Israelbii lɛ na Ijiptbii lɛ jwere ŋshɔ lɛ naa ni amɛgboi.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii lɛ na Yehowa hewalɛ wulu ni ejie lɛ kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Ijiptbii lɛ, ni Israelbii lɛ she Yehowa gbeyei, ni amɛhe Yehowa kɛ etsulɔ Mose amɛye.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Israelbii lɛ la nɛkɛ lala nɛɛ kɛjie Yehowa yi, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Mala majie Yehowa yi, ejaakɛ eye kunim kpeteŋkple kɛwo ehiɛ nyam; okpɔŋɔ kɛ enɔtalɔ lɛ etsirɛ amɛ ewo ŋshɔŋ.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Yehowa ji mihewalɛ kɛ milala, ni lɛ etsɔ̃ miyiwalaherelɔ. Lɛ ji miNyɔŋmɔ, ni majie eyi, mitsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ ni, ni mawo ehiɛ nyam.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Yehowa, lɛ tawulɔ ni. Ani jeee egbɛi ji Yehowa?

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: “Farao shwiilii lɛ kɛ eta lɛ eloo ewo ŋshɔŋ, ni etatsɛmɛi kpanakpanaa lɛ, amii amɛ nu yɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ mli.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Ŋshɔ lɛ ha amɛnɔ, ni amɛshiu kɛtee nu shishi tamɔ tɛ.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: Yehowa, ohewalɛ lɛ hiɛ eba nyam, Yehowa, ohewalɛ lɛ tserɛɔ henyɛlɔ mli.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Ogbojee lɛ naa sɔŋŋ lɛ, obutu mɛi ni te shi wo bo lɛ. Omlila lɛ gri wo amɛ, ni eshã amɛ tamɔ la shãa gbetseli.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Omu oshwie ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ, ni nu lɛ bua ehe naa, ni ŋshɔkei lɛ ho damɔ shi keikei, ŋshɔ teŋteŋ nu lɛ shɔ̃ etsɔ̃ kpɔ.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Henyɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ, ‘Matiu amɛ mayamɔmɔ amɛ. Maja nomŋɔɔnii lɛ, mitsui aaanyɔ mimli. Magbala miklante ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ohã kɔɔyɔɔ tswa, ni ŋshɔ lɛ ha amɛnɔ; amɛshiu tamɔ sumui yɛ nu hamahama lɛ mli.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: “Namɔ tamɔ Bo, Yehowa, yɛ nyɔŋmɔi lɛ ateŋ? Namɔ tsuɔ nyam nii ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ naakpɛɛ?

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Okpa oninejurɔ mli, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mi amɛ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Osuɔmɔ ni tsakeee lɛ naa lɛ okpala maŋ ni okpɔ̃ nɛɛ. Ohewalɛ naa lɛ otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛshɛ oshihilɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Jeŋ maji lɛ nu he, ni amɛhe kpokpo, ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ Filistibii lɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ shiofɔ̃ eshi Edom maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ anɔ, Moab kãkãlɔi lɛ ahe kpokpo; Kanaanbii fɛɛ ehao.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Gbeyei kɛ ŋmiŋmi eloo amɛ, onineshi tsiimɔ sɔŋŋ ehã amɛmu shi dɛoo kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni Yehowa, omaŋ lɛ aaaho, kɛyaashi mɛi ni okpɔ̃ lɛ aaaho.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Okɛ amɛ aaaba ni obato amɛ shi yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ogɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Yehowa aaaye maŋtsɛ kɛaatee naanɔi anaanɔ.” Miriam lala lɛ

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Be ni Farao okpɔŋɔi lɛ kɛ eshwiilii lɛ kɛ ekpɔŋɔiatsɛmɛi lɛ bote ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Yehowa hã ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ ku esɛɛ ebaha amɛnɔ, shi Israelbii lɛ nyiɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli kɛtee.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔyoo Miriam, Aaron nyɛmiyoo lɛ, kɔ fao ehiɛ edɛ̃, ni yei lɛ fɛɛ kɔlɔ fabii kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ, ni amɛsha ni amɛjo.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Miriam wo lala ekɛɛ, “Nyɛlaa nyɛhãa Yehowa ejaakɛ eye kunim kɛwo ehiɛ nyam; etsirɛ okpɔŋɔ kɛ enɔtalɔ lɛ ewo ŋshɔŋ.” Nu ni joɔ lɛ

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Mose kɛ Israelbii lɛ fã yɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naa kɛtee Shur ŋa lɛ nɔ. Amɛnyiɛ gbii etɛ̃ gbɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ ni amɛnaaa nu.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛyashɛ he ko ni gbɛi ji Mara lɛ amɛyanina nu; shi Mara nu nɛɛ ehiii numɔ ejaakɛ eejoo. No hewɔ awo jɛi Mara lɛ.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ wie huhuuhu amɛshi Mose amɛkɛɛ, “Mɛni wɔbaanu mɔ?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Mose bo etsɛ Yehowa, ni Yehowa tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ tso ko; ni be ni ekɔ ni eshɛ efɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ baŋɔɔ. Jɛi Yehowa wo Israelbii lɛ kitã kɛ akpɔ yɛ, ni jɛi hu ekã amɛ yɛ,

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ, “Kɛji nyɛaaye Yehowa, ni ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbee nɔ kadikadi, ni nyɛaafee nɔ ni ja gbɛ yɛ ehiɛ, ni nyɛaaye ekpɔi kɛ kitãi fɛɛ anɔ lɛ, no lɛ helai ni mihã ye Ijiptbii lɛ eko eko yeŋ nyɛ, ejaakɛ mi ji Yehowa, nyɛtsalɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Israelbii asafo lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Elim kɛtee Sin ŋa ni kã Elim kɛ Sinai teŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛyashɛ jɛi Ijipt shimɔ lɛ sɛɛ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ wie huhuuhu amɛshi Mose kɛ Aaron yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛ, “Yehowa hã wɔgboi yɛ Ijipt be ni wɔtara loo kɛ kukwɛii ahe ni wɔyeɔ nii wɔtɔrɔɔ lɛ moŋ kulɛ, ehi fe nɔ ni nyɛjie wɔ kɛba ŋa nɛɛ nɔ, ni nyɛkɛ hɔmɔ abagbe asafo muu nɛɛ fɛɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Naa, mibahã aboloo ajɛ ŋwɛi anɛ ashwie shi ahã nyɛ. Daa gbi lɛ maŋbii lɛ aje kpo ayabua naa bɔ pɛ ni aaashɛ amɛyeli gbi kome. Mikɛ enɛ baaka amɛ makwɛ akɛ amɛaaye mimla lɛ nɔ aloo amɛyeŋ nɔ.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Shi gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, hã ni amɛsaa nɔ ni amɛbuaa naa daa gbi lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ amɛto.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ lɛ nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ Yehowa ji mɔ ni jie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Leebi lɛ nyɛaana Yehowa anunyam lɛ, ejaakɛ enu huhuuhu wiemɔi ni nyɛwieɔ nyɛshiɔ lɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ wɔ lɛ namɛi ji wɔ ni nyɛwieɔ huhuuhu nyɛshiɔ wɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Mose tee nɔ ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Kɛji gbɛkɛ lɛ Yehowa hã nyɛ loo nyɛye, ni leebi lɛ ehã nyɛ aboloo nyɛye nyɛtɔrɔ, ejaakɛ enu huhuuhu wiemɔi ni nyɛwieɔ nyɛshiɔ lɛ lɛ, wɔ lɛ nɛgbɛ wɔdamɔ? Jeee wɔ nyɛwieɔ huhuuhu nyɛshiɔ lɛ, shi Yehowa mɔŋ ni.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛtsia nyɛbaa Yehowa hiɛ; enu nyɛ huhuuhu wiemɔi lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Be ni Aaron kɛ Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ wieɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ, ni naa, Yehowa anunyam lɛ epue yɛ atatu lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Minu Israelbii lɛ ahuhuuhu wiemɔi lɛ. Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, ‘Gbɛkɛnaashi lɛ nyɛaaye loo, ni leebi lɛ nyɛaaye aboloo nyɛtɔrɔ, ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Gbɛkɛnaashi mli lɛ trakɔkɔi baha Israelbii lɛ ashihilɛhe lɛ. Leebi mli lɛ bɔ nyɔ kɛbɔle Israelbii lɛ ahe fɛɛ kɛkpe kpula.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Be ni bɔ lɛ kpala lɛ, ana nibii tɛtɛrɛbii kokrobii bibiibii komɛi jwere ŋa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni efĩ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ na nibii nɛɛ, amɛbibii amɛhe akɛ, “Kolɛ mɛni nɛ?” Ejaakɛ amɛleee nɔ ni ji. Mose kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Aboloo ni Yehowa hã nyɛ koni nyɛye lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fee nakai. Mɛi komɛi kɔlɔ pii, ni mɛi komɛi kɔlɔ fioo.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose wo maŋbii lɛ shi ekɛɛ, “Mɔ ko akashwɛ eko ni je miitsɛre nɔ.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mɛi komɛi eyabooo Mose toi ni amɛshwɛ eko. Be ni je tsɛre lɛ ewo gɔgɔmi, ni esha. Enɛ hã Mose mli wo amɛ la.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ daa leebi lɛ Israelbii lɛ yakɔlɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ, bɔ ni eeenyɛ eye kɛkɛ. Kɛji hulu naa wa lɛ esereɔ.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛkɔlɔ daa gbi niyenii lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ, mɔ kome nɔ tsenesai enyɔ, ni maŋbii lɛ ateŋ onukpai lɛ babɔ Mose amaniɛ.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Yehowa fã: ‘Wɔ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni, Yehowa hejɔɔmɔ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni. Nyɛshãa nɔ ni nyɛyɔɔ shãa, ni nyɛhoa nɔ ni nyɛyɔɔ hoomɔ. Nɔ ni baashwɛ lɛ nyɛkɛtoa ni je atsɛrea nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ nii ni shwɛ lɛ to ni je tsɛre nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni Mose kɛɛ amɛ lɛ; niyenii lɛ eshaaa lɛ, ewooo gɔgɔmi hu.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Ni Mose kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyea enɛ ŋmɛnɛ ejaakɛ Yehowa hejɔɔmɔ gbi ji ŋmɛnɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛ nyɛnaŋ eko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ nyɛkɔlɔ.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyɛbuaa ŋmaa lɛ naa gbii ekpaa ejaakɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni, ni no nɔ lɛ eko baŋ.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛi komɛi je maŋbii lɛ ateŋ tee ŋmaa kɔlɔmɔ, shi amɛyanaaa eko amɛkɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛyaashi mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ nyɛaakwa mikitãi kɛ mimlai lɛ?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyɛnaaa akɛ ni Yehowa hã nyɛ hejɔɔmɔgbi lɛ, no hewɔ ni ehãa nyɛ gbii enyɔ niyenii yɛ gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ahi eshĩa, mɔ ko akaje egbɛhe yɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ wo niyenii nɛɛ gbɛi akɛ mana. Edalɛ tamɔ mlɛ bibii, ni eyɛɔ futafuta, ni eŋɔɔmɔ tamɔ akpãanɔɔ kɛ wo.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Kitã ni Yehowa ewo nɛ, ‘Nyɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ tsenesa kome falɛ atoa nyɛhãa nyɛshwiei koni amɛbana ŋmaa ni mikɛlɛ nyɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ be mli ni mijie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Wo kpulu ni osusu mana tsenesa kome falɛ owo mli, ni okɛyama Yehowa hiɛ koni akɛto ahã nyɛshwiei yɛ yinɔi fɛɛ mli.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ mana lɛ yama Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa fã Mose lɛ koni akɛto.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Sin ŋa lɛ nɔ. Amɛtotoo shi yɛ gbɛ teŋ yɛ Yehowa famɔ naa kɛyashi amɛyashɛ Refidim; shi nu bɛ jɛi ni maŋ lɛ baanu.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Hã wɔ nu wɔnu!” Mose here amɛ nɔ, ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkɛ mi beɔ? Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkaa Yehowa?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Shi kumai ye maŋ lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni amɛwie huhuuhu amɛshi Mose amɛkɛɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ obajie wɔ yɛ Ijipt? Koni okɛ kumai abagbe wɔ kɛ wɔbii kɛ wɔkooloi?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose bo etsɛ Yehowa ekɛɛ, “Te mafee maŋ nɛɛ mahã tɛŋŋ? Tɛ amɛheɔ amɛtswia mi nɛɛ!”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Halamɔ Israel onukpai lɛ ateiaŋ mɛi komɛi ofata ohe, ni okɔ otso lɛ ni okɛtswa Nilo Faa lɛ mli lɛ ohiɛ odɛ̃, ni okɛ amɛ atsɔ̃ maŋbii lɛ ahiɛ kɛya.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Naa, mibadamɔ tɛsaa lɛ nɔ, ni nu baajɛ mli aba koni maŋ lɛ anu.” Ni Mose fee nakai yɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Ni Mose wo jɛi gbɛi akɛ Masa kɛ Meriba yɛ shwamɔ ni Israelbii lɛ shwa Yehowa lɛ kɛ nɔ ni amɛwie amɛkɛka lɛ akɛ, “Ni Yehowa yɛ wɔteŋ kɛ̃ nɛ?” lɛ hewɔ. Israelbii kɛ Amalekbii wu ta

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amalekbii lɛ fã ta kɛbanina Israelbii lɛ yɛ Refidim, ni amɛkɛ amɛ wu.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose fã Yoshua ekɛɛ, “Halamɔ hii ni amɛya amɛkɛ Amalekbii lɛ ayawu ahã maŋ lɛ. Mi lɛ mibadamɔ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ yiteŋ wɔ, ni mahiɛ Nyɔŋmɔ tso lɛ yɛ midɛ̃.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Yoshua fee bɔ ni Mose fã lɛ lɛ, ni amɛtee amɛkɛ Amalekbii lɛ yawu, ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ Hur kwɔ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ kɛtee eyiteŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Kɛji Mose wo enine nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi pɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ anine miitsɔ̃ Amalekbii lɛ anɔ; shi kɛji Mose kɛ enine ba shi pɛ Amalekbii lɛ anine miitsɔ̃ Israelbii lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Shi Mose niji bɔ̃i lɛ shɔ̃ɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, awo tɛ akɛto Mose shishi ni eho eta nɔ, ni Aaron kɛ Hur hiɛ eniji lɛ amli, mɔ kome yɛ biɛ, ni mɔ kome hu yɛ biɛ, ni eniji lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi hulushinyɔɔ mli.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ni Yoshua kpãtã Amalek kɛ emaŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Ŋmaa kunimyeli nɛɛ he sane lɛ owo wolo mli ofɔ̃ shi koni etsɔ̃ kaimɔ nɔ; ni okpã owo Yoshua toiŋ akɛ mibagbe Amalek kwrakwra yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Ni Mose ma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi, ni ewo lɛ gbɛi akɛ “Yehowa ji miflaŋaa”,

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛwoa Yehowa aflaŋaa lɛ nɔ. Yehowa kɛ Amalek baawu kɛjɛ yinɔ kɛyaashi yinɔ.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Ni Yetro hã ayakɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mi oshaanuu, mi kɛ oŋa kɛ obihii enyɔ lɛ miiba oŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose je kpo ekɛ eshaanuu lɛ yakpe. Mose koto lɛ ni eshwɔ enaa; amɛflaflaa amɛhe, ni amɛba Mose buu lɛ mli.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Ni Mose gba eshaanuu lɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Yehowa fee Farao kɛ Ijiptbii yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ. Egba lɛ haomɔi hu ni ba Israelbii lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛgbɛfãa lɛ mli, kɛ bɔ ni fee ni Yehowa jie amɛ yɛ mli.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Kpaako mina mile akɛ Yehowa fe nyɔŋmɔi fɛɛ ejaakɛ eto Ijiptbii lɛ kpa, akɛni amɛwo amɛhe amɛhã Israelbii lɛ, ni Yehowa ba amɛ shi.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ni Yetro, Mose shaanuu lɛ, yashã shãa afɔle kɛ afɔlei krokomɛi ehã Yehowa, ni Aaron kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ fɛɛ ba koni amɛ kɛ Mose shaanuu lɛ abaye nii yɛ he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Kojolɔiwoo (Deuteronomio

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ebaatɔ bo kɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ hu. Nitsumɔ nɛɛ fa tsɔ̃ hã bo; okome too onyɛŋ otsu.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Mose ho eta shi, ni ekura maŋbii lɛ ateŋ saji, ni maŋ lɛ jwere enɔ kɛjɛ leebi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Be ni Mose shaanuu lɛ na nibii fɛɛ ni Mose tsuɔ ehãa maŋ lɛ, ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni ji nɔ ni otsuɔ ohãa maŋ lɛ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba okome too ota shi, ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ jwere onɔ nɛkɛ leebileebi jenamɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Mose hã lɛ hetoo ekɛɛ, “Ebaa lɛ nakai ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ baa amɛbabiɔ mi Nyɔŋmɔ daaŋ gbee.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Kɛji amɛna sane ko lɛ amɛkɛbaa miŋɔɔ, ni mikuraa, ni mitsɔ̃ɔ amɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpɔi kɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Mose shaanuu lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni ofeɔ nɛɛ ehiii.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ bo migbee toi; mawo bo ŋaa, ni Nyɔŋmɔ aye abua bo. Bo lɛ feemɔ maŋbii lɛ anaadamɔlɔ yɛ maŋbii lɛ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ teŋ koni okɛ amɛsaji lɛ ashwie Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ;

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: ni otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpɔi, nɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ, ni ohã amɛle bɔ ni sa akɛ amɛba amɛjeŋ amɛhã, kɛ nɔ ni sa akɛ amɛfee.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Ohã amɛ amɛkura saji ni baaba maŋbii lɛ ateŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be. Sane wulu fɛɛ sane wulu lɛ, no lɛ akɛba ohiɛ; shi saji bibii fɛɛ lɛ kui anɔkwɛlɔi lɛ aye, bɔ ni afee ni amɛkɛmɔ mli amɛhã bo koni efo tsɔ́ ehã bo.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ fãa bo nɛ. Kɛji ofee nakai lɛ, ooonyɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ naa odamɔ, ni maŋbii nɛɛ fɛɛ hu aaayashɛ amɛshɛɛhe yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.”

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Nɔkwɛlɔi nɛɛ kuraa maŋbii lɛ ateŋ saji be fɛɛ be. Saji wuji lɛ amɛkɛbaa Mose ŋɔɔ; shi saji bibii fɛɛ lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkuraa.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Mose shaanuu Yetro kɛ lɛ ye shɛɛ, ni Yetro ku esɛɛ etee emaŋ.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔɔ. Yehowa jɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɛ Mose, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Yakob shwiei, ni ji Israelbii, lɛ akɛ,
