english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: ‘Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛna nɔ ni mifee Ijiptbii lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni mihiɛ nyɛ kɛ hewalɛ tamɔ okropɔŋ, ni mikɛ nyɛ bashɛ miŋɔɔ yɛ biɛ nɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɛji nyɛaabo mi toi, ni nyɛaaye mikpãŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ nyɛaatsɔ̃ mi diɛŋtsɛ minɔ yɛ maji fɛɛ ateŋ; ejaakɛ je lɛ fɛɛ lɛ minɔ ni.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Mibafee nyɛ osɔfoi abladei, mibafee nyɛ maŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ. Nɔ ni okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ nɛ.’ ”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Mose ku esɛɛ eba, ni ebatsɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ nɔ ni Yehowa fã akɛ ekɛɛ amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Ni maŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ shi kome amɛkɛɛ, “Nibii fɛɛ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ wɔɔfee.” Mose hã Yehowa le hetoo ni maŋ lɛ hã lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Miiba oŋɔɔ yɛ atatu kpii mli koni kɛ mi kɛ bo miiwie lɛ, maŋ lɛ anu ni amɛhe bo hu amɛye kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Yaa maŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni otsuu amɛhe ŋmɛnɛ kɛ wɔ ni ohã amɛfɔ amɛtadei ahe,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: ni amɛsaa amɛhe amɛto gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ, ejaakɛ nakai gbi lɛ Yehowa baakpleke shi kɛba gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiŋmɛiŋ.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Foo akrabatsa okɛtsi maŋ lɛ gbɛ, ni obɔ amɛ kɔkɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkwɛa ni ahĩa koni nyɛkakwɔa gɔŋ lɛ, aloo ni nyɛtaa ehusu lɛ he.’ Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaata gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ gbe aaagbe lɛ.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko mɔ ko nine akata nakai gbɔmɔ lɛ he, shi atswia lɛ tɛ aloo atsɛ̃rɛ lɛ gãi. Kooloo ni jio, gbɔmɔ ni jio, akahã eyi na wala. Shi kɛji akpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ, ni esɛɛ tsɛ aahu lɛ, no dani amɛba gɔŋ lɛ he.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Mose kpeleke shi kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba maŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni etsuu maŋ lɛ he, ni amɛfɔfɔɔ amɛtadei ahe.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ni Mose kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛsaa nyɛhe nyɛtoa hã, wɔ bɛ mli, wɔsɛɛ. Nuu akaya yoo masɛi.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ leebi lɛ ŋwɛi shimɔ, ni srawa gbala ni atatu kpii ko baha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ; tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ ko gbɛɛ waa naakpa, ni mɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ shitoohe lɛ fɛɛ kpokpo.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ maŋ lɛ je kpo kɛjɛ shitoohe lɛ koni amɛkɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ayakpe, ni amɛyadamɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Sinai Gɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ miije lasu, ejaakɛ Yehowa ekpeleke shi kɛba gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ la mli. Lasu lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi tamɔ flɔnɔɔ mli lasu, ni gɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hoso waa naakpa.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Be ni tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ yaa nɔ gbɛɔ waa lɛ, kɛkɛ ni Mose wie, ni Nyɔŋmɔ here lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋwɛi shiimɔ.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa kpeleke shi kɛba Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, etsɛ Mose akɛ eba gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ; ni Mose tee.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kpelekemɔ shi ni oyakɛɛ maŋ lɛ kpɔ́kpɔ́ɔkpɔ́ akɛ amɛkatse mli kɛmiiba Yehowa ŋɔɔ amɛbakwɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ, koni amɛteŋ mɛi pii miiplenee.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Asaŋ hã osɔfoi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ Yehowa atsuu amɛhe koni Yehowa akakpãtã amɛhiɛ.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Maŋ lɛ nyɛŋ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpã owo wɔtoiŋ akɛ, ‘Nyɛfoa akrabatsa nyɛwoa gɔŋ lɛ he nyɛfea lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpelekemɔ shi oya ni okɛ Aaron akwɔ kɛba, shi kaahã osɔfoi lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ miiteke akrabatsa lɛ kɛkwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛba mi, Yehowa, miŋɔɔ koni mikaplene amɛ.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Mose kpeleke shi kɛba maŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni ebakɛɛ amɛ.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Ni Nyɔŋmɔ wie wiemɔi nɛɛ fɛɛ ekɛɛ:

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Shi maŋ lɛ damɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ lolo; kɛkɛ ni Mose tsi ebɛŋkɛ duŋ kpii lɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Afɔleshãa latɛi ahe mlai

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Mi ji Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni mi mijie bo yɛ nyɔŋyeli mli kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: “Kaana nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi yɛ misɛɛ.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: “Kaafee amãgã ko loo nɔ ko ni tamɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nii ni yɔɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ohã ohe.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: “Shi mɛi akpei abɔ fɛɛ ni sumɔɔ mi, ni amɛyeɔ mikitãi anɔ lɛ, misumɔɔ amɛ kɛ suɔmɔ ni tsakeee, ni minaa amɛ mɔbɔ.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: “Kaahiɛ Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbɛi mli yakayaka, ejaakɛ Yehowa ebuŋ mɔ ni tsɛɔ egbɛi yakayaka lɛ bem.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: “Ohiɛ ahi hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ ni oye lɛ akɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Tsu nii gbii ekpaa ni ofee onii fɛɛ,

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ, hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni hã Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. No nɔ lɛ okatsu nɔ ko, bo jio, obinuu jio, obiyoo jio, owenuu jio, oweyoo jio, okooloo jio, ogbɔ ni ebato omaŋ jio.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ gbii ekpaa Yehowa kɛbɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋshɔ kɛ amɛmli nibii fɛɛ; ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ ejɔɔ ehe. No hewɔ ni Yehowa jɔɔ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ, ni efee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: “Wo otsɛ kɛ onyɛ koni owala sɛɛ atsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi, Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛhãa bo lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: “Kaagbe gbɔmɔ.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: “Kaafite gbãlã.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: “Kaaye amale odase yɛ onaanyo he.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: “Ohiɛ akakɔ̃ onaanyo nɔ ko nɔ, eshĩa jio, eŋa jio, ewenuu jio, eweyoo jio, etsina jio, eteji jio, enɔ kroko jio, ohiɛ akakɔ̃ nɔ.” Israelbii lɛ she gbeyei (Deuteronomio

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Nyɛkafea mihenɔ jwiɛtɛi loo shika amãgãi; nyɛkafea eko eko nyɛhãa nyɛhe koni nyɛja amɛ nyɛfata mihe.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ na bɔ ni ŋwɛi shimɔɔ, ni srawa gbalaa, ni tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ gbɛɔ, ni gɔŋ lɛ fãa lasu lɛ, amɛshe gbeyei, ni amɛkpokpo, ni amɛdamɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Bo moŋ okɛ wɔ awie, ni wɔɔbo toi, shi kaahã Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ wɔ miiwie ni wɔbagboi.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Mose kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei, ejaakɛ kaa Nyɔŋmɔ ba nyɛ kaa, bɔ ni afee ni lɛ egbeyeishemɔ ahi nyɛmli daa koni nyɛkafee esha.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛna akɛ ŋwɛi mijɛ mikɛ nyɛ wie nɛɛ.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Nyɛshɔ̃a su afɔleshãa latɛ nyɛhãa mi, ni no nɔ nyɛshãa afɔlei yɛ, shãa afɔlei kɛ shidaa afɔlei kɛ gwantɛŋi kɛ tsinai lɛ yɛ. He fɛɛ he ni mato mahã nyɛ akɛ aja mi yɛ lɛ, maba nyɛŋɔɔ yɛ jɛi ni majɔɔ nyɛ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛkɛ tɛ miima afɔleshãa latɛ nyɛhã mi lɛ, akɛ tɛ ni ako akama ejaakɛ ŋaa dade naa ni aaasa tɛ lɛ he pɛ ebule lɛ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Ni okafee atrakpoi owo afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he koni akana oyayaiaŋ yɛ atrakpoi lɛ kwɔɔ mli.’ ”

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaagba etsɛ loo enyɛ ma lɛ agbe lɛ.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: “Kɛji hii miinɔ ni mɔ kome tswa enaanyo lɛ tɛ aloo ema lɛ atswɛrɛ, ni mɔ lɛ tsɔɔɔ mli gbooo, shi efee lɛ hela kɛkã shi lɛ,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ okɛ mlai nɛɛ ashwie Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Kɛji ohe Hebrinyo akɛ nyɔŋ lɛ esɔ̃mɔ afii ekpaa, ni afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ aŋmɛɛ ehe ni eye ehe tswaa.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Kɛji ekome eba lɛ, ekome nɔŋŋ eya. Shi kɛji ekɛ eŋa ba lɛ, no lɛ eŋa lɛ kɛ lɛ aya.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Kɛji enuŋtsɔ lɛ ehã lɛ ŋa, ni ekɛ yoo lɛ efɔ bihii loo biyei lɛ, no lɛ yoo lɛ kɛ ebii lɛ etsɔ̃ enuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ, ni nuu lɛ kome too aya.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji nyɔŋ lɛ gba mli kpoo ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Miisumɔ minuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ miŋa kɛ mibii lɛ, ni misumɔɔɔ akɛ mashi amɛ maya mayaye mihe lɛ,’

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: no lɛ enuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ lɛ aya Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ, ni ehã edamɔ jamɔhe lɛ shinaa lɛ naa loo shinaatso lɛ he, ni enuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ fitii agbu nyɔŋ lɛ toi, ni nyɔŋ lɛ asɔ̃mɔ enuŋtsɔ lɛ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: “Kɛji nuu ko hɔ̃ɔ ebiyoo akɛ nyɔŋ lɛ, biyoo nɛɛ akatsɔ̃ gbɛ nɔ ni hii nyɔji tsɔ̃ɔ yeɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ eye ehe.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Kɛ nyɔŋ yoo nɛɛ esaaa enuŋtsɔ lɛ hiɛ akɛ eeeŋɔ lɛ efee eŋa lɛ, no lɛ ehã abakpɔ̃ lɛ. Nuŋtsɔ lɛ bɛ hegbɛ ni ehɔ̃ɔ lɛ ehãa maŋsɛɛnyo, ejaakɛ no lɛ eku eshiwoo mli.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ yoo lɛ hã ebinuu gbãlã lɛ, nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ yoo nɛɛ ahi shi akɛ ebiyoo.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ yaŋɔ yoo ni ji enyɔ ebafata nyɔŋyoo lɛ he lɛ, no akahã etse nyɔŋyoo lɛ daaŋ ŋmaa kɛ ehebo kɛ egblãshihilɛ mli gbɛnaa nii nɔ.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ tsuuu nibii etɛ̃ nɛɛ ahe ehãaa nyɔŋ yoo lɛ, no lɛ nyɔŋ yoo lɛ aye ehe tswaa, ni nuŋtsɔ lɛ bɛ hegbɛ akɛ aheɔ eyi shika ko.” Awuiyeli he mlai

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Kɛjeee ka eyawo lɛ, shi osharã naa ni, enine kpa yɛ mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ ejo foi eyaba abo yɛ he ko ni mato mahã nyɛ.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji mɔ ko to ŋaa fɔŋ yɛ enyɛmi gbɔmɔ he, ni eje gbɛ eyatua lɛ, ni egbe lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ eyaba abo yɛ mifɔleshãa latɛ lɛ naa tete po, ajie lɛ kɛje jɛi ni ayagbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaaju gbɔmɔ lɛ, eyahɔɔ lɛ jio, eto lɛ akɛ nyɔŋ ehã ehe jio, agbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaalomɔ etsɛ loo enyɛ lɛ agbe lɛ.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: kɛji helatsɛ lɛ na ete shi ekoŋŋ, ni emɔ tso mli enyiɛ kɛje kpo lɛ, mɔ ni tswa lɛ nɔ lɛ eye ehe, shi moŋ ewo be ni helatsɛ lɛ efite lɛ he nyɔmɔ, ni ekwɛ koni atsa helatsɛ lɛ ni ehe atã kwrakwra.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji je tsɛre nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ lɛ, akatɔ owele yɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ nyɔŋ lɛ ni egbo lɛ, lɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ, eshika ni elaaje ni.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: “Kɛji hii miinɔ ni amɛkɛ nɔmɔ lɛ yapila yoohɔlɔ, ni emusu lɛ fite, shi eyeee lɛ awui kroko kɛfataaa he lɛ, agbe nuu mɔ ni pila yoohɔlɔ lɛ shika gbele. Yoo wu lɛ aaatsɔ̃ɔ nyɔmɔ ni ekɛfɔ̃ɔ nuu lɛ nɔ nɛ, shi moŋ bɔ ni saneyelɔi lɛ aaatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nakai nuu lɛ awo.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Shi kɛji sane fɔŋ ba yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ oweletɔɔ lɛ afee atoŋ kɛ atoŋ, no ji akɛ wala atse wala,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: ni akɛ hiŋmɛi atse hiŋmɛi, ni akɛ nyanyɔŋ atse nyanyɔŋ, akɛ nane atse nane,

english_verse: burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
translation_verse: akɛ la fala atse la fala, akɛ pilamɔ atse pilamɔ, ni akɛ kpelebi naa fala atse kpelebi naa fala.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko tswa enyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo hiŋmɛi nɔ, ni hiŋmɛi lɛ fite lɛ, ehã nyɔŋ lɛ aye ehe tswaa yɛ ehiŋmɛi lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ fã enyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo nyanyɔŋ lɛ, eŋmɛɛ nyɔŋ lɛ he koni eyaye ehe tswaa yɛ enyanyɔŋ lɛ hewɔ.” Kooloi anuŋtsɔmɛi asɔ̃

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: “Kɛji tsina shi nuu loo yoo, ni mɔ lɛ gbo lɛ, atswia tsina lɛ tɛ ni agbe lɛ, ni akaye eloo lɛ, shi tsinatsɛ lɛ aye ehe.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji tsina lɛ fɔɔ mɔ shimɔ kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ, ni abɔ nɔtsɛ lɛ kɔkɔ yɛ he, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo ekooloo lɛ tsuŋ, ni eyagbe gbɔmɔ lɛ, atswia tsina lɛ tɛ, ni tsinatsɛ lɛ hu agbe lɛ.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji aahe tsinatsɛ lɛ kpãtãmɔ nii lɛ, no lɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni aheɔ lɛ lɛ, ewo koni ekɛkpɔ̃ esusuma.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Kɛji tsina lɛ yashi mɔ ko binuu loo biyoo lɛ akɛ tsinatsɛ lɛ aye yɛ mla kome nɛɛ nɔŋŋ naa.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko shi bu naa eŋmɛ aloo eyatsa bu ni etsiii nɔ, ni tsina loo teji ko yagbee mli lɛ,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: mɔ ni tsa bu lɛ awo koolootsɛ lɛ ekooloo lɛ he nyɔmɔ koni bu tsɛ lɛ aŋɔ kooloo gbonyo lɛ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Kɛji mɔ ko tsina pila enaanyo tsina, ni kooloo lɛ gbo lɛ, mɛi enyɔ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tsina hiɛkãalɔ lɛ koni amɛja shika lɛ, ni kooloo ni egbo lɛ hu amɛja.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji ale ato akɛ tsina lɛ fɔɔ mɔshimɔ kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ, shi tsinatsɛ lɛ wooo tsina lɛ tsuŋ lɛ, no lɛ ekɛ tsina ato mɔ lɛ tsina lɛ najiaŋ ehã lɛ koni mɔ ni tsina yashi lɛ aŋɔ tsina ni egbo lɛ.”

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko yaju tsina loo too, ni eyagbe aloo eyahɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ekɛ tsinai enumɔ ato tsina kome najiaŋ, ni ekɛ toi ejwɛ ato too kome najiaŋ. Shi kɛ ebɛ nɔ ko lɛ, no lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ koni akɛtse nii ni eju lɛ.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko ŋmɛɛ ekooloo he, ni eyaye ŋmɔ loo waintrom ko mli nii, aloo mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ ekooloo lɛ nɔ, ni ekooloo lɛ yaye mɔ kroko ko ŋmɔshinii lɛ, koolootsɛ lɛ kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eŋmɔshi loo waintrom mli nii ni hi fe fɛɛ ato nii ni afite lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko wo la, ni etso kɛyamɔ ŋmeii, ni eshã abele kɛ aboŋo, loo abele ni akuko, loo ŋmɔ lɛ, mɔ ni wo la lɛ ato nii ni hiɛ kpãtã lɛ najiaŋ shishiishi.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko kɛ shika loo nibii hã enaanyo shitoo, ni aju nii lɛ yɛ mɔ lɛ we lɛ, ni amɔ julɔ lɛ, julɔ lɛ kɛ nii ni eju lɛ toi enyɔ ato najiaŋ.

english_verse: But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji anaaa julɔ lɛ, no lɛ shĩatsɛ lɛ aba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ ni ebatsɔɔ akɛ enine etako enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ he.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: “Niiaheplemɔ fɛɛ ni aaate shi lɛ, tsina he ejɛ jio, teji he jio, too he jio, atade he jio, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eji ni aaapele he ni mɔ ko aaakɛɛ akɛ enɔ ni lɛ, akɛ sane lɛ aba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ. Mɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaabu lɛ fɔ lɛ, ekɛ nɔ lɛ toi enyɔ ato enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko kɛ eteji loo tsina loo too loo kooloo fɛɛ kooloo hã enaanyo shitoo, ni kooloo lɛ gbo, aloo aye lɛ awui, aloo ofɔ̃yelɔi bamɔ lɛ kɛtee, shi anaaa mɔ ko aye he odase lɛ,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: mɔ ni akɛ nɔ lɛ hã shitoo lɛ ayakã Yehowa kitã akɛ enine etako enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ he. Nɔtsɛ lɛ akpɛlɛ̃ nɔ, ni mɔ ni akɛ nii lɛ hã shitoo etoŋ nɔtsɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji ju aju nii lɛ yɛ edɛŋ lɛ eto nɔtsɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Kɛji kooloo kakawua ko ni tserɛ kooloo lɛ, ekɛ kooloo gbonyo lɛ abaye odase koni ekato najiaŋ.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko yama kooloo ko yɛ enaanyo dɛŋ, ni eye kooloo lɛ awui, aloo egbo be mli ni nɔtsɛ lɛ bɛ jɛi lɛ, mɔ ni yama kooloo lɛ ato najiaŋ shishiishi;

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: shi kɛji nɔtsɛ lɛ yɛ jɛi lɛ, no lɛ akato najiaŋ. Kɛji apaayeli akɛ kooloo lɛ ba lɛ, no lɛ akato najiaŋ ejaakɛ epaayeli nyɔmɔ ni awo hewɔ eba.” Jeŋba he mlai

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: “Kɛji nuu ko yalaka oblayoo foro ni atsɛko ehe baa, ni ekɛ lɛ wɔ lɛ, nuu lɛ ahã yoo lɛ yinii koni etsɔ̃ eŋa.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji yoo lɛ tsɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ yoo lɛ kɛ nuu lɛ hãmɔ kwraa lɛ, nuu lɛ ahã bɔ ni ji oblayoo foro yinii kɛ̃.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: “Akaŋmɛ yoo ŋkunyaayelɔ gbɛ ni ehi jeŋ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ kooloo aaawɔ lɛ esa akɛ agbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaashi Yehowa sɛɛ ni eeeyashã afɔle ehã nyɔŋmɔ kroko ko yɛ Yehowa sɛɛ lɛ akpãtã ehiɛ butubutu.

english_verse: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Akaye gbɔ sane ni ejaaa, ni akawa lɛ yi ejaakɛ nyɛ hu nyɛyatsɔ̃mɔ gbɔi yɛ Ijipt dã.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Akawa yoo okulafo loo awusa yi.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: Kɛji awa amɛ yi, ni amɛfo amɛtsɛ mi lɛ, ja mibo amɛyaafo toi.

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: Mimlifu naa aaawa naakpa, ni magbe nyɛ yɛ ta mli, ni nyɛŋamɛi aaatsɔ̃mɔ okulafoi, ni nyɛbii aaatsɔ̃mɔ awusai.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: “Kɛji ofa mimaŋbii ni kɛ bo yɔɔ lɛ ateŋ ohiafo ko shika lɛ, kaaye lɛ wie, ni kaahe hekpa hu.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Kɛji eeeba lɛ po akɛ onaanyo kɛ ehebo aaato bo awaba lɛ, okɛ ehebo lɛ aku sɛɛ ohã lɛ dani hulu ayanyɔ shi,

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ no pɛ ji nɔ ni ekɛhaa ehe, ehewolo nɔ mama ni. Mɛni eha kɛwɔ? Kɛji efo etsɛ mi lɛ mabo lɛ toi ejaakɛ mɔbɔnalɔ ji mi.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: “Kaawie oshi Nyɔŋmɔ, ni kaalomɔ maŋ onukpa.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: “Kɛji oŋmɔshi nii ba, ni kɛ oŋa owain kɛ omu lɛ, kaashashao shi ni okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ abahã lɛ. Jɔɔmɔ obihii ateŋ kromɔ lɛ nɔ ohã mi.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Nakai nɔŋŋ hu ofee otsinai kɛ toi. Kooloo kromɔ nuu lɛ ehi enyɛ masɛi gbii kpawo, ni gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ ojɔɔ enɔ ohã mi.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: “Nyɛaatsɔ̃ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ nyɛhã mi. No hewɔ lɛ, loo ni ŋaŋ kooloo etserɛ lɛ lɛ nyɛkayea, ashɛrɛ ashwie ahã gbei.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Kaanyiɛ mɛi ni yi fa sɛɛ kɛyafee efɔŋ, ni kaanyiɛ nɔ ni mɛi pii kɛɔ sɛɛ ni okɛɛ nɔ ko ni aaahã atsɔ sane hiɛ abu shi,

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: asaŋ kaasaa ohiafo sane he ohã lɛ yɛ saneyeli mli.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: “Kɛji ona ohenyɛlɔ tsina loo teji ni edu gbɛ lɛ kplamɔ lɛ obahã lɛ.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Kɛ oyanina mɔ ni kɛ bo yeee kɛ eteji ni teji lɛ jatsu tsii fe lɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni okaho amɛhe otee, shi moŋ ye obua nɔtsɛ lɛ koni awo kooloo lɛ nɔ adamɔ shi.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: “Kaatsɔ̃ ohiafo sane hiɛ obu shi yɛ saneyeli mli.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Kaafo sane ofɔ̃ mɔ nɔ, ni kaagbe jalɔ kɛ mɔ ni he bɛ sane ko mli ejaakɛ mihaŋ efɔŋfeelɔ aye ehe kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
translation_verse: Kaahe nyɔɔŋnii ejaakɛ nyɔɔŋnii shwilaa nɔkwɛlɔ, ni efiteɔ mɔ ni sane ja sane.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Nyɛkawaa gbɔ yi, akɛ ni nyɛle bɔ ni gbɔ tsui nuɔ nii ahe ehãa lɛ, ejaakɛ nyɛ hu nyɛyatsɔ̃mɔ gbɔi yɛ Ijipt dã.” Afi ni ji kpawo lɛ kɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: “Ahu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akpa enɔ nibaanii lɛ kɛyashi afii ekpaa;

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: shi afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ ahã shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ekã shi efolo koni omaŋ lɛ mli ohiafoi lɛ ana enɔ nii amɛkɔlɔ amɛye, ni nɔ ni aaashwɛ lɛ ŋaŋ kooloi hu ana aye. Nakai nɔŋŋ ofee owain trom kɛ omutso trom.

english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: “Otsu nii gbi ekpaa, shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ okɛjɔɔ ohe, bɔ ni afee ni otsina kɛ oteji ajɔɔ amɛhe, ni nyɔŋ yoo bi kɛ ogbɔ awo amɛtsui.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: “Nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛɛ nyɛ lɛ nyɛyea nɔ. Nyɛkatsĩa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi agbɛii ata, akanu yɛ nyɛnaa tete.” Gbii juji etɛ̃ lɛ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: “Kooloo ni akɛbaashã afɔle ahã mi lɛ, nyɛkɛ masha aboloo akafataa he; ni kooloo ni akɛshã afɔle ahã mi lɛ, nyɛkahãa je miitsɛre emli fɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Yoo sharakeŋ, ni anaŋ yoo kene yɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mahã nyɛwala sɛɛ atsɛ.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: “Nyɛyea Nikpamɔ Gbijurɔ lɛ ni ji ŋmɔshinii lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ yibii agbijurɔ lɛ; ni nyɛyea Ŋmaa naabuamɔ kɛtoo Gbijurɔ lɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee mli, be ni nyɛbuaa ŋmɔshi nii anaa nyɛtoɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Daa afi lɛ nyɛteŋ nuu fɛɛ nuu abaja Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ shii etɛ̃ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii juji etɛ̃ nɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
translation_verse: “Daa afi lɛ nyɛyea gbii juji etɛ̃ nyɛhãa mi.

english_verse: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
translation_verse: Nyɛyea Akpiti Gbijurɔ lɛ. Bɔ ni miwo nyɛ ehe kitã lɛ, nyɛyea aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã. Nyɛyea lɛ gbii kpawo yɛ be ni ato lɛ, ni ji Abib nyɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ no nɔ nyɛshi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No be lɛ mli lɛ mɔ ko akaba mi jamɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ edɛŋ afɔle.

english_verse: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshinii ni nyɛbaakpa lɛ nyɛkɛbaa Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, we lɛ. Akahoo toobi kɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ enyɛ fufɔ mli nu.” Shiwoi kɛ akpɔi

english_verse: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
translation_verse: “Naa, miwo bɔfo gbɛ ni enyiɛ nyɛhiɛ koni ebaa nyɛyi yɛ gbɛteŋ koni ekɛ nyɛ ayashɛ he ni misaa mito lɛ.

english_verse: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
translation_verse: Nyɛkwɛa ni ahia yɛ egbɛfaŋ, ni nyɛyea ewiemɔ nɔ. Nyɛkatsea ehiɛ atua; ekɛ ewiemɔ lɛ nɔtɔmɔ ekeŋ nyɛ, ejaakɛ ehiɛ mihewalɛ.

english_verse: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
translation_verse: Mibɔfo lɛ aaanyiɛ nyɛhiɛ kɛyanina Amorbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ kɛ Perizbii lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ Hivbii lɛ kɛ Yebusbii lɛ, ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ butubutu.

english_verse: Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
translation_verse: Nyɛkajaa ni nyɛkasɔ̃mɔa amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, asaŋ nyɛkakasea gbɔmɛi nɛɛ anifeemɔ nii hu, shi moŋ nyɛbutua amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, ni nyɛkumɔa amɛshiui lɛ butubutu nyɛshwiea shi.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛsɔ̃mɔ mi, Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, madro nyɛ niyenii kɛ nu, ni makɔ hela yɛ nyɛteŋ mashɛ mafɔ̃ kwraa.

english_verse: I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you.
translation_verse: “Mahã miheŋmiŋmi atsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ amɔmɔ maji lɛ fɛɛ dani nyɛaayanina amɛ, ni maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ ni nyɛaashɛ lɛ aaajija yɛ nyɛhiɛ.

english_verse: I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach.
translation_verse: Matsu sosomootii kɛaatsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ. Mashwie Hivbii lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ.

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ mishwieŋ amɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ yɛ afi kome nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akabatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, koni ŋaŋ kooloi ayi bafa yɛ nɔ wo nyɛ.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: Fiofio mibashwie amɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni nyɛyi aaafa, ni nyɛaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: Mafo husu mahã nyɛ kɛjɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naa kɛyashi Filistibii lɛ aŋshɔ lɛ naa, agbɛnɛ kɛjɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi Eufrate Faa lɛ naa, ejaakɛ mahã nyɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ anɔ kunim koni nyɛshwie amɛ.

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: Amɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ jio, amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ jio, nyɛkɛ amɛ akakpãŋa kpãŋmɔ ko.

english_verse: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_verse: Nyɛkahãa amɛhia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiihã nyɛfee esha nyɛshi mi. Ejaakɛ kɛji nyɛsɔ̃mɔ amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ eeetsɔ̃ tsɔne ehã nyɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Bo kɛ Aaron kɛ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋmai kpawo akwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛba miŋɔɔ koni nyɛbaja yɛ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ.

english_verse: but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
translation_verse: Mose, okome pɛ otsi obɛŋkɛ Yehowa; mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ akatsi amɛbɛŋkɛ, ni maŋbii lɛ hu kɛ bo akakwɔ kɛmiiba.”

english_verse: Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!”
translation_verse: Mose ba ni ebajaje Yehowa wiemɔi lɛ kɛ akpɔi lɛ fɛɛ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ. Ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ kɛ gbee kome amɛkɛɛ, “Wiemɔi fɛɛ ni Yehowa ewie lɛ wɔɔye nɔ.”

english_verse: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Mose ŋmala Yehowa wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ eshwie shi. Kɛkɛ ni ete shi leebi maŋkpa, ni ema afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi, ni ehole tɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ edamɔ shi yɛ Israel akutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ anaa.

english_verse: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni etsu Israelbii lɛ ateŋ oblahii komɛi, ni amɛkɛ tsina hii yashã afɔle kɛ shidaa afɔle amɛhã Yehowa.

english_verse: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ lá lɛ fã wo lalakãi amli, ni lá lɛ fã ni shwɛ lɛ efɔ̃ eshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ekɔ kpãŋmɔ wolo lɛ, ni ekane yɛ maŋbii lɛ atoiŋ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Nii fɛɛ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ wɔɔfee, ni wɔɔbo lɛ toi.”

english_verse: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mose wo lá lɛ, ni ekɛshwã maŋbii lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa, kpãŋmɔ ni Yehowa kɛ nyɛ ekpãŋ yɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ fɛɛ he lɛ nɔ lá nɛ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Israel onukpai nyɔŋmai kpawo lɛ kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee,

english_verse: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
translation_verse: ni amɛyana Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛna ni enanemaahei lɛ efee tamɔ he ko ni akɛ safiro tɛ eka; safiro tɛ nɛɛ mlitsemɔ lɛ enɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ efeee Israel onukpai nɛɛ nɔ fɔŋ ko, shi amɛna Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ amɛhiŋmɛi, ni amɛye nii ni amɛnu nɔ ko. Mose yɛ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kwɔɔ kɛba miŋɔɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni obamɛ, ni mikɛ tɛi tɛtɛrɛbii ni maŋmala mlai lɛ kɛ kitãi lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ baahã bo, ni okɛtsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ nii.”

english_verse: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ etsulɔ Yoshua te shi, ni Mose kwɔ kɛtee Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
translation_verse: Shi ekɛɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhia biɛ nyɛmɛa wɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni wɔɔku wɔsɛɛ kɛba. Aaron kɛ Hur kɛ nyɛ yɛ biɛ. Kɛji mɔ ko hiɛ sane ko lɛ akɛyahã amɛ.”

english_verse: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ Mose kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee eyiteŋ, ni atatu lɛ baha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa anunyam la lɛ kpeleke shi kɛba Sinai gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Atatu lɛ ye gbii ekpaa ni eha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ Yehowa jɛ atatu lɛ mli etsɛ Mose.

english_verse: blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ kɛ klala kɛ abotia he tsɔi,

english_verse: Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you.
translation_verse: “Bi Israelbii lɛ koni amɛkɛ nikee nii aba. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ he tsui akɛ ehã lɛ, lɛ edɛŋ nikee nii nyɛhea nyɛhãa mi.

english_verse: Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze;
translation_verse: Ni nikee nii ni amɛkɛba lɛ nɛ: shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble,

english_verse: tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: kɛ ojwɛni wolo ni awo lɛ tsofa tsuru kɛ nuŋgbee he wolo kɛ tso.

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests;
translation_verse: Ekrokomɛi hu ji mu ni akɛsuɔ kane, kɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ mu ni akɛfɔɔ mɔ mu mli lɛ. Ekomɛi hu ji tsofai ni akɛfeɔ tsofakɛŋma ni ashãa.

english_verse: and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece.
translation_verse: Abake oniketɛi ni akɛbaamamɔ osɔfonukpa lɛ tsitsinɔhaa nii lɛ kɛ ehewulamɔ nii lɛ eko ni atsɛɔ lɛ efod lɛ amli lɛ.

english_verse: I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people.
translation_verse: Ohã Israelbii lɛ afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ ko amɛhã mi koni mahi amɛteŋ.

english_verse: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
translation_verse: Ashwie adeka lɛ mli kɛ ehe fɛɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi, ni akɛ shika abaŋ adeka lɛ naa fɛɛ kɛkpe kpula.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: Ashwie shika gai ejwɛ ato adeka lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ. Gai enyɔ aye afã kome, ni enyɔ hu aye afã kome lɛ.

english_verse: Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold
translation_verse: Akɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko agbɔlɔ tsei bloblobii ni ashwie amɛhe shika.

english_verse: and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles.
translation_verse: Akɛ tsei nɛɛ ahɔlɔ gai ni yɔɔ adeka lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ biɛ kɛ biɛ lɛ amli koni akɛwo.

english_verse: Don't ever remove the poles from the rings.
translation_verse: Tsei lɛ ahɔlɔ gai lɛ amli, akajie yɛ mli.

english_verse: Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest.
translation_verse: Kerub kome yɛ koŋ kome kɛ ekome hu yɛ koŋ kome lɛ. Sɔomɔ kerubim nɛɛ okpɛtɛ naanɔ lɛ koji enyɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
translation_verse: Okɛ odaseyeli tɛi lɛ ni mikɛbaahã bo lɛ awo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ mli koni okɛ naanɔ lɛ abu naa.

english_verse: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Gbɛ ni kã kerubim enyɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ̃ mi kɛ bo kpeehe, ni jɛi majɛ mi kɛ bo aaawie nibii fɛɛ ni mifã bo akɛ okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ. Okplɔ̃ ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Aboloo lɛ maa nɔ lɛ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Ogbɔ tso blawa ni elɛɛmɔ tamɔ dɛ̃ lɛɛmɔ koni okɛkpɛtɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ toi kɛbɔle lɛ kɛkpe, ni okɛ shika abaŋ tso blawa nɛɛ naa kpula.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs
translation_verse: Feemɔ shika gai ejwɛ okɛwo okplɔ̃ lɛ naji ejwɛ lɛ ahe.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko agbɔlɔ tsei nɛɛ, ni oshwie he shika koni akɛwo okplɔ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold
translation_verse: “Okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ni atswia afee kanetso. Otswia shika ŋmiiŋmi kɛfee eshimaatso lɛ kɛ eshishi nii ni ema nɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Ehe tɔi lɛ kɛ ehe kpɔbii lɛ kɛ ehe fɔfɔi samai lɛ fɛɛ atsa akɛ nɔ muu kome.

english_verse: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
translation_verse: Amɛhe tɔi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi samai lɛ kɛ shimaatso lɛ fɛɛ atsa akɛ nɔ muu kome, ni akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi atswia fɛɛ.

english_verse: The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold.
translation_verse: Kanetso lɛ he abɛɛlei lɛ kɛ ehe lagbee nii lɛ akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi afee.

english_verse: The lampstand and its equipment will require
translation_verse: Aŋmɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi talenta kome koni akɛfee kanetso lɛ kɛ ehe nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_verse: Kwɛmɔ ni ofee nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ bɔ ni mikɛtsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: “Ni buu lɛ naa shinaa lɛ, okɛ mama ni akɛ kpãa bluu kɛ kpãa afaseo kɛ kpãa tsuru fɔɔ kɛ kpãa yɛŋ futafuta ni anyɛne elo, asaŋ ni akɛ abui elo nii awo mli afee.

english_verse: As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth
translation_verse: Mama kome kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai etɛ̃, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔi ejwɛ. Mamai nyɔŋma kɛ ekome nɛɛ fɛɛ adaramɔ afee ekome.

english_verse: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: “Okɛ mamai nyɔŋma ni alo kɛ klala yɛŋ futaa kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ ni anyɛne afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Alo kerubim awo mli.

english_verse: Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent.
translation_verse: Otsara mamai enumɔ aŋklo kɛ mamai ekpaa hu aŋklo. Mama ni ji ekpaa ni baaye buu lɛ hiɛ lɛ odɔ mli enyɔ.

english_verse: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: “Okɛ ojwɛni wolo ni awo lɛ tsofa tsuru aha buu lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nuŋgbee wolo aha yiteŋ oto nɔ.

english_verse: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
translation_verse: Okɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ, ni ji kpãtãmɔ sɛi lɛ, abu naa yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ Fe Fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Okɛ tso afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mplaŋi ni baamamɔ shi lɛ.

english_verse: Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put
translation_verse: kɛ amɛshishi nibii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ ni enyɔ yɛ mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ shishi.

english_verse: For the back wall along the west side use six frames
translation_verse: Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ, he ni ye kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ, mplaŋi ekpaa aye jɛi.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Okɛ koŋ kome mplaŋi enyɔ lɛ abɔ he kɛkɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ; shi otsa amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ga lɛ yi. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni ofee koji enyɔ lɛ mplaŋi lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, abaana mplaŋi kpaanyɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ nɛɛ kɛ amɛshishi jwiɛtɛi nibii nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa ni amɛmamɔ nɔ, mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ ama enyɔ nɔ.

english_verse: with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Ni mlibɛlɛmɔ nii ni baaye mplaŋi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ekã shi emuu kɛjɛ koŋ kome kɛyagbe naa yɛ koŋ kome lɛ.

english_verse: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through.
translation_verse: Okɛ shika aha mplaŋi lɛ ahe, ni okɛ shika nɔŋŋ afee gai ni akɛ mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ baahɔlɔ mli lɛ; ni mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ hu okɛ shika aha he.

english_verse: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ bɔ ni ajie atsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, oma lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
translation_verse: Okɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ ama muhɔɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli kooyigbɛ, ni kanetso lɛ aye Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli wuoyigbɛ koni ekwɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Okɛ kpoji lɛ alala muhɔɔ lɛ kɛtsotsoro shi, ni okɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ abama muhɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni muhɔɔ lɛ afo He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ Fe Fɛɛ lɛ teŋ ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Ni okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko afee akulashiŋi enumɔ ohã shinaa lɛ naa mama lɛ. Okɛ shika aha tsei nɛɛ ahe, ni owo amɛhe shika kpoji kɛ amɛshishi akɔɔble nibii ni amɛmamɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Okɛ tsei nɛɛ ahɔlɔ gai lɛ amli yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ koni akɛwo.

english_verse: All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans.
translation_verse: Ofee latɛ lɛ he ŋɛsui ni akɛloo elamlu lɛ, asaŋ ofee ehe sofii kɛ ekpolui kɛ fakai kɛ lajee tsɛnsii hu. Okɛ akɔɔble afee nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Okɛ ŋmoŋmolo akpɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni gbɛ ahi emli. Okpɛ latɛ lɛ bɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie atsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ.” Kpee Buu lɛ he afabaŋ lɛ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
translation_verse: “Fã Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛbahã bo mutso mu ni mli tse krɔŋŋ ni akɛsu kane lɛ koni ahã kane lɛ ama nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english_verse: for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain
translation_verse: Amãmɔ muhɔɔ lɛ he akulashiŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ amɛshishi akɔɔble nibii nyɔŋmai enyɔ koni amɛmamɔ nɔ. Akulashiŋi lɛ ahe kpoji lɛ kɛ mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ akɛ jwiɛtɛi afee.

english_verse: Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
translation_verse: Kpo lɛ nɔ agbo lɛ naahaa nii lɛ akɛ mama ni alo kɛ kpãa bluu kɛ kpãa afaseo kɛ kpãa tsuru kɛ kpãa yɛŋ srãsrã ni anyɛne, asaŋ ni akɛ abui elo nii ewo mli afee. Ekɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ehe akulashiŋi ejwɛ kɛ amɛshishi nibii ejwɛ ni amɛmamɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ni nibii fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli nii kɛ ehe shiŋmlitsei lɛ kɛ kpo lɛ hu shiŋmlitsei lɛ akɛ akɔɔble afee fɛɛ.” Kanetso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ (Levitiko

english_verse: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ asu kane lɛ ama muhɔɔ ni etsĩ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ lɛ hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛkwɛ koni kane nɛɛ atso kɛjɛ gbɛkɛ kɛyashi leebi yɛ mi, Yehowa, mihiɛ. Enɛ atsɔ̃ akpɔ ni kã shi hã Israelbii ayinɔbii fɛɛ.”

english_verse: Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: “Ŋɔɔ onyɛmi Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ, ni ji Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Eleazar kɛ Itamar, kɛjɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛsɔmɔ mi akɛ osɔfoi.

english_verse: Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them.
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni miduro amɛ ŋaa ni baanyɛ nii ni obaahã amɛ lɛ amɛtsu lɛ, okɛ amɛ awie koni okɛ hewulamɔ nibii lɛ kpɛɛ awo amɛdɛŋ.

english_verse: Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests.
translation_verse: Ni hewulamɔ nibii ni abaakpɛ lɛ nɛ: tsitsinɔhaanii kɛ efod kɛ atade yuu kɛ flaka ni alo nii awo mli kɛ fai kɛ mliteŋfĩinii. Amɛkpɛ hewulamɔ nibii krɔŋkrɔŋi nɛɛ amɛhã onyɛmi Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ koni amɛkɛsɔ̃mɔ mi akɛ osɔfoi.

english_verse: Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes. The Vest for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Ahã ŋaalɔi nɛɛ kuŋtu wuɔfɔ kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ kɛ klala kpakpa.

english_verse: Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
translation_verse: Okɛ tɛi enyɔ nɛɛ amãmɔ efod lɛ he mamai hwĩahwĩabii ni baakã kɔŋ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni akɛkai Yakob bii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, be fɛɛ be ni Aaron aaaba Yehowa hiɛ lɛ, Israel akutsei lɛ agbɛii yɛ ekɔji enyɔ lɛ anɔ koni makai amɛ daa.

english_verse: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: ni okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi afee kɔsɔŋkɔsɔi enyɔ ni agbɔ tamɔ kpãa koni okɛlalaa shika ni asere abɔle tɛi lɛ.” Tsitsinɔhaa nii lɛ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do.
translation_verse: “Okɛ ŋaa afee tsitsinɔhaanii lɛ ohã osɔfonukpa lɛ, ni ekɛtao Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔnaanii ele. Nibii ni okɛfee efod lɛ okɛ no nɔŋŋ eko afee tsitsinɔhaa nii lɛ: kuŋtu wuɔfɔ kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ kɛ klala kpakpa.

english_verse: with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
translation_verse: Oto tɛi klɛmpɛi ejwɛ omamɔ tsitsinɔhaanii lɛ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ klɛmpɛ lɛ mli tɛi afee ojarawatɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ rubi kɛ topasiɔn kɛ garneto lɛ.

english_verse: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
translation_verse: Klɛmpɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli tɛi lɛ afee smaragdo kɛ safiro kɛ daiamɔnd.

english_verse: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
translation_verse: Klɛmpɛ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ mli ojarawatɛi lɛ afee tekwais kɛ kalkedɔn kɛ amɛtisto,

english_verse: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings
translation_verse: ni klɛmpɛ ni ji ejwɛ lɛ mli tɛi lɛ afee berilo kɛ onike kɛ yaspi.

english_verse: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: Kɔsɔŋkɔsɔi enyɔ ni agbɔ tamɔ kpãa lɛ anaabui enyɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ, okɛlala shika ni asere kɛbɔle tɛi enyɔ lɛ shishi lɛ amli, koni okɛŋmɔlɔ tɛi lɛ omɔmɔ efod lɛ he mamai hwĩahwĩabii lɛ ni kãa kɔŋ nɔ lɛ yɛ hiɛgbɛ.

english_verse: Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
translation_verse: Akɛ kpãa bluu aŋmɔlɔ tsitsinɔhaa nii lɛ he gai lɛ akpɛtɛ efod lɛ he gai lɛ, koni tsitsinɔhaanii lɛ akã efod lɛ mlifiinii lɛ nɔ, koni ekaje he.

english_verse: Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool
translation_verse: “Okɛ kuŋtu bluu sɔŋŋ akpɛ efod lɛ shishi atade yuu lɛ.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Ajie kuɛ awo atade lɛ he, ni akɛ mama ni alo abaŋ kuɛ lɛ naa kɛkpe koni ekagba.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them.
translation_verse: shika ŋmɛlɛ kome kɛ kpɔ kokroo kome kɛbɔle atade yuu lɛ naamuu lɛ kɛkpe.

english_verse: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
translation_verse: Atade nɛɛ Aaron awo ni ekɛsɔ̃mɔ akɛ osɔfo koni kɛ eeba mi, Yehowa, mihiɛ yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ jio, eeje kpo yɛ jɛi jio, anu ŋmɛji lɛ agbɛɛmɔ koni ekagbo.

english_verse: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
translation_verse: “Otswia shika ŋmiiŋmi fɛtɛfɛtɛ, ni oŋma yɛ nɔ, tamɔ nii ni aŋma yɛ wolonaasɔomɔ nɔ nɔ, akɛ, ‘Afee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ ahã Yehowa.’

english_verse: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
translation_verse: Okɛ shika ni atswia fɛtɛfɛtɛ nɛɛ akpɛtɛ mama bluu nɔ, ni okɛfi osɔfonukpa fai lɛ ni eta fai lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
translation_verse: Nii nɛɛ ahi Aaron hiɛnaa tuuŋtu koni tɔ̃mɔi fɛɛ ni Israelbii lɛ etɔ̃ yɛ nikee lɛ hãmɔ mli lɛ akã Aaron nɔ.

english_verse: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
translation_verse: “Aaron bihii lɛ hu, okpɛ flakai kɛ mlifiinii kɛ faii ohã amɛ. Ofee nibii nɛɛ ni efee nyam kɛ fɛo.

english_verse: Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
translation_verse: Okɛ nibii nɛɛ awula onyɛmi Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ hu ofata ehe, ni ofɔ amɛ mu, ni owo amɛ osɔfo, ni otsuu amɛhe koni amɛye osɔfo amɛhã mi.

english_verse: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
translation_verse: Okpɛ klala tswakoto ohã amɛ koni amɛwo kɛkete amɛyayaiaŋ kɛjɛ hɛ kɛyashi shuɔ.

english_verse: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ awo tswakoto nɛɛ kɛji amɛmiiba Kpee Buu lɛ mli aloo kɛ amɛmiibɛŋkɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he kɛbasɔ̃mɔ yɛ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkaloo musu ni amɛgboi. Enɛ atsɔ̃ akpɔ ni kã shi kɛmiiya naanɔ hã Aaron kɛ eshwiei ni baaba yɛ esɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
translation_verse: Gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ omɔ tsina kome koni okɛshã afɔle ni okɛkpãtã Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ esha ni afee hewɔ, ni okɛ kpãtãmɔ ni obaakpãtã nɛɛ nɔŋŋ akpala afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he esha, ni ofɔ latɛ lɛ mu koni okɛfee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Ŋɔɔ aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã kɛ mã akpiti keeki ni awo mli fɔ, kɛ mã akpiti akpãanɔɔ ni akpa hiɛ fɔ. Akɛ ŋmaa ma afee fɛɛ.

english_verse: Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
translation_verse: Okɛ nibii nɛɛ awo kɛntɛŋ kome mli, ni amɛhi kɛntɛŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni okɛba; tsina lɛ kɛ toi enyɔ lɛ afata he.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: “Ŋɔɔ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛba Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa, ni okɛ nu aju amɛhe.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ wulamɔ nibii lɛ awula Aaron: flaka lɛ kɛ efod lɛ shishi atade yuu lɛ, kɛ efod lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ tsitsinɔhaanii lɛ; naagbee lɛ okɛ efod lɛ mlifiinii lɛ afi emliteŋ.

english_verse: and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ owo mu ni akɛfɔɔ mɔ mu lɛ koni ofɔse oshwie Aaron yiteŋ ni okɛfɔ lɛ mu.

english_verse: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: “Ohã akɛ tsinanuu lɛ aba Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa, ni Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ amɛniji ashwie tsina lɛ yiteŋ,

english_verse: Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent.
translation_verse: ni ogbe tsina lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa.

english_verse: Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar.
translation_verse: Oŋɔ tsina lá lɛ eko koni okɛ owao atsɔ eko okpa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he akloŋtoi lɛ ahe, ni ofɔse lá ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ oshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
translation_verse: Shi tsina lɛ loo lɛ kɛ ehe wolo lɛ kɛ ewamɔ lɛ, ayashã fɛɛ yɛ shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ. Osɔfoi lɛ ahe esha afɔle ni.

english_verse: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: “Asaŋ oŋɔ toi ojwɛnii lɛ ateŋ ekome, ni Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ amɛniji ashwie eyiteŋ,

english_verse: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: ni ogbe too lɛ, ni okɛ elá lɛ ashwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he fɛɛ kɛkpe.

english_verse: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
translation_verse: Folɔmɔ too lɛ mli kukuji, ni ofɔ mlinii lɛ kɛ eshuɔji lɛ ahe, ni okɛfata loo kukuji lɛ kɛ yitso lɛ he,

english_verse: Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: ni oma too ojwɛni muu lɛ fɛɛ naa la yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. Eji afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ahãa mi, Yehowa; ni misumɔɔ eŋma lɛ.

english_verse: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: “Omɔ too ojwɛni kome lɛ hu agbɛnɛ, ni Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ amɛniji ashwie eyiteŋ,

english_verse: Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: ni ogbe too lɛ, ni okɛ too lá lɛ eko asa Aaron ninejurɔ toi naa kɛ ebihii lɛ hu aninejurɔ toii anaa kɛ amɛninejurɔ kɛ nanejurɔ gɔŋtii anaa, ni okɛ lá ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he fɛɛ kɛkpe.

english_verse: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ŋɔɔ lá ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ eko kɛ mɔmufɔɔ mu lɛ hu eko ni okɛshwã Aaron kɛ ehewulamɔ nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ; ni okɛshwã Aaron bihii lɛ hu kɛ amɛhewulamɔ nibii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, koni okɛfee Aaron kɛ ehewulamɔ nibii lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ hu kɛ amɛhewulamɔ nibii lɛ fɛɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: “Jiemɔ too ojwɛni lɛ fɔ lɛ kɛ elei ni ewo fɔ lɛ kɛ emlinii ahe fɔ lɛ, kɛ nɔ ni tsotsoro mlɛbo lɛ he, kɛ sabai enyɔ lɛ, kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ amɛhe lɛ hu, kɛ too lɛ ninejurɔ shuɔ ,

english_verse: and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: ni okɛwo Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛfɔ̃ niyenii nɛɛ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi akɛ afɔle ni amɛkɛhãa mi, Yehowa.

english_verse: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ ohe nibii lɛ yɛ amɛdɛ̃ ni oma fɛɛ naa la yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, ni oshã ofata shãa afɔle lɛ he akɛ afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ahãa mi, Yehowa; ni misumɔɔ eŋma lɛ.

english_verse: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: “Too ojwɛni lɛ ni akɛshã Aaron osɔfowoo afɔle lɛ, jiemɔ etsitsi lɛ koni ofɔ̃ otsɔ̃ɔ mi akɛ afɔle ni ajɔɔ nɔ ahã mi Yehowa ni. Tsitsi nɛɛ afee ogbɛfaŋ nɔ.

english_verse: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron binuu, mɔ ni baaye enajiaŋ akɛ osɔfonukpa, lɛ, ewo nibii nɛɛ gbii kpawo kɛji eeba Kpee Buu lɛ mli ebasɔ̃mɔ yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place,
translation_verse: “Oŋɔ osɔfowoo too ojwɛni lɛ loo lɛ koni ohoo yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ loo lɛ aye aboloo lɛ ni yɔɔ kɛntɛŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa.

english_verse: At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it.
translation_verse: Amɛye nii ni akɛkpãtãa ni akɛwo amɛ osɔfo, ni asaŋ akɛfee amɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Mɔ folo ko akaye nii nɛɛ eko ejaakɛ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni.

english_verse: If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Kɛji osɔfowoo afɔle loo aboloo lɛ eko shwɛ ni je tsɛre nɔ lɛ, no lɛ akɛ la ashã; akaye ejaakɛ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni.

english_verse: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni mifã bo nɛɛ, feemɔ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ nakai. Gbii kpawo okɛwo amɛ osɔfo lɛ.

english_verse: Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy. Daily Sacrifices (Leviticus
translation_verse: Okɛ gbii kpawo akpãtã Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he esha hewɔ koni okɛfee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛwula shi, bɔ ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aaasa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he lɛ afee krɔŋkrɔŋ.” Daa gbi afɔle (Numeri

english_verse: one in the morning and one in the evening.
translation_verse: Okɛ toobi kome ashã afɔle leebi, ni okɛ ekome hu ashã afɔle gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Ni toobi kome lɛ hu okɛshã afɔle gbɛkɛ. Okɛ niyenii kɛ dãa, tamɔ leebi nibii lɛ afalɛ nakai nɔŋŋ, afata he ni oshã, ni ahã eje ŋma. Eji afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ahãa mi, Yehowa, ni misumɔɔ eŋma lɛ.

english_verse: Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: Mahã Kpee Buu lɛ kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ afee krɔŋkrɔŋ, ni asaŋ mafee Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ fɛɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ koni amɛye osɔfo amɛhã mi.

english_verse: I will live among you as your God,
translation_verse: Ni mahi Israelbii lɛ ateŋ, ni matsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_verse: Ni amɛaana amɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mɔ ni jie amɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mahi amɛteŋ lɛ; mi Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves.
translation_verse: Tsofakɛŋma ni obaafee nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛkakwɛa bɔ ni afutu lɛ ahã lɛ nɔ ni nyɛmiifee eko nyɛmiihã nyɛhe. Abu lɛ akɛ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ hã mi, Yehowa.

english_verse: Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture
translation_verse: Futumɔ nibii nɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni ojeŋmafeelɔ futuɔ ojeŋma ehãa, ni okɛfee mu, ni ji mu krɔŋkrɔŋ ni akɛfɔɔ mɔ mu lɛ.

english_verse: the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand.
translation_verse: kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kɛ ehe tsɛnsi lɛ fɛɛ, kɛ okpolu lɛ ni yɔɔ nane ni ta shi lɛ.

english_verse: Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense.
translation_verse: “Oma latɛ ni ashã tsofakɛŋma yɛ nɔ. Akɛ tso afee.

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it.
translation_verse: Okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi aha he, eyiteŋ kɛ ehe fɛɛ kɛkpe, kɛ ehe akloŋtoi lɛ hu, ni okɛ shika abaŋ latɛ lɛ naa kɛkpe.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Ofee shika gai enyɔɔnyɔ owo latɛ lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ biɛ kɛ biɛ, yɛ shika ni akɛbaŋ naa lɛ shishi, koni akɛ tsei bloblobii ahɔlɔ gaii nɛɛ amli ni akɛwo.

english_verse: These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Okɛ tso lɛ eko agbɔ tsei nɛɛ ni aha he shika.

english_verse: Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there.
translation_verse: Okɛ latɛ lɛ ama muhɔɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ masɛi lɛ hiɛ, yɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ, ni ji he ni mikɛ bo aaakpe yɛ lɛ, hiɛ.

english_verse: Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings.
translation_verse: Akashã tsofakɛŋma ni bɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ loo kooloo loo niyenii afɔle ko kwraa yɛ nɔ, ni akafɔse wain akɛ dãa afɔle ashwie nɔ.

english_verse: Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me. The Money for the Sacred Tent
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ kooloo ni akɛkpãtãa Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ esha ni afee hewɔ lɛ lá lɛ akpa latɛ lɛ akloŋtoi lɛ ahe, ni ekɛkpãtã shi kome daa afi. Efee kpãtãmɔ nii nɛɛ shi kome daa afi yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ yinɔi fɛɛ amli. Eji nii ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ hã mi, Yehowa.” Kpee Buu Shihilɛhe lɛ hetooyeli

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them.
translation_verse: “Kanemɔ Israelbii lɛ, ni kɛ ona amɛyikulɛ lɛ, ohã amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ awo eyi too yɛ ekpɔ̃mɔ̃ hewɔ ehã mi Yehowa, koni gbele hela akaba amɛteŋ kɛbakpãtã amɛhiɛ yɛ kanemɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: , whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: koni Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛfɔflɔ amɛniji kɛ amɛnaji ahe.

english_verse: This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: Hemɔ kpãtãmɔ too nɛɛ yɛ Israelbii adɛŋ ni akɛto koni akɛtsu Kpee Buu lɛ mli sɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ he nii, koni ehã Yehowa akai Israelbii lɛ daa ejaakɛ nyɛkɛ too lɛ miikpãtã Nyɔŋmɔ nyɛhã nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛwala.” Akɔɔble okpolu lɛ

english_verse: If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_verse: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaafee eko tamɔ no, ni eeeshã lɛ atswa enaneshi tu.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
translation_verse: Ofee enɛ koni okɛtsuu amɛhe ni ehã amɛfee krɔŋkrɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛwula shi, bɔ ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he aaasa amɛhe lɛ aaafee krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Asaŋ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: for dedicating the tent and chest,
translation_verse: Okɛ mu nɛɛ ashwã Kpee Buu lɛ kɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils,
translation_verse: kɛ nibii nɛɛ hu: okplɔ̃ lɛ kɛ ehenii lɛ fɛɛ, kɛ kanetso lɛ kɛ ehenii lɛ, kɛ tsofakɛŋmashãa latɛ lɛ,

english_verse: When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil,
translation_verse: Ofɔ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ mu, ni ofee amɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ koni amɛye osɔfo amɛhã mi.

english_verse: and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, ‘Naa, enɛ baafee mimu krɔŋkrɔŋ ni akɛbaafɔ mɔ mu yɛ nyɛyinɔi fɛɛ mli.

english_verse: So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves.
translation_verse: Akɛkafɔ mɔ folo ko kɛkɛ, ni nyɛkafea eko hu ni afutu lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔ̃ afutu no lɛ. Nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni, ni ahi shi nakai ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.” The Sweet-Smelling Incense
translation_verse: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaafutu mu ko tamɔ no, aloo ekɛ mu nɛɛ eko aaasa mɔ folo ko kɛkɛ he lɛ atswa enaneshi tu.’ ” Tsofakɛŋma lɛ

english_verse: Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy.
translation_verse: ni okɛfee tsofakɛŋma ni ashãa. Awo mli ŋoo koni ekafite, ni afutu lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ojeŋmafeelɔ futuɔ ojeŋma ehãa. Emli atse, ni efee krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy.
translation_verse: Oshimɔ eko ni ebo mɔnyɔmɔnyɔ, ni okɛ eko ama Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ, yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ mli, he ni mikɛ bo aaakpe yɛ lɛ. Tsofakɛŋma nɛɛ afee nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛwula shi ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings.
translation_verse: “Naa, mije gbɛ mitsɛ Bezaleel, ni ji Hur bi Uri binuu lɛ ni jɛ Yuda akutso lɛŋ lɛ,

english_verse: I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you:
translation_verse: Ni naa, mi nɔŋŋ miŋɔ Ahisamak binuu Oholiab ni jɛ Dan akutso lɛŋ lɛ mifata Bezaleel he. Mɛnɛɛmɛi asɛɛ lɛ, mɛi fɛɛ ni ŋaa yɔɔ amɛhiŋmɛiŋ lɛ, miduro amɛ ŋaa koni amɛnyɛ nibii fɛɛ ni miwo bo he kitã nɛɛ amɛtsu:

english_verse: Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said: The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, ‘Asaŋ mihejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nyɛyea, ejaakɛ eji okadi yɛ mi kɛ nyɛ teŋ kɛmiiya nyɛyinɔi fɛɛ koni nyɛkɛna nyɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi mifeɔ nyɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Atsu nii gbii ekpaa, shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ, hejɔɔmɔ gbi kɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ ni hã mi, Yehowa. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaatsu nii yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ gbe aaagbe lɛ.

english_verse: This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
translation_verse: Mi kɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ okadi ji no kɛmiiya naanɔ; ejaakɛ gbii ekpaa, mi, Yehowa, mikɛbɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ, ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ mijɔɔ mihe, ni miwo mitsui.’ ”

english_verse: When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa kɛ Mose ewie egbe naa yɛ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ tɛi enyɔ ni ji tɛi tɛtɛrɛbii ni lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ ewao eŋma nii yɛ nɔ lɛ hã Mose.

english_verse: Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are,
translation_verse: Yehowa tee nɔ, ni ekɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mina nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ akɛ maŋ ko ni kuɛŋ ti.

english_verse: The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ maŋbii lɛ te shi maŋkɛ mra, ni amɛshãshãa shãa afɔlei, ni amɛkɛ niyenii afɔlei hu ba, ni maŋ lɛ ho tara shi, ni amɛye nii, ni amɛnu nii hu, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛte shi amɛshwɛ.
