english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Be ni maŋbii lɛ anaa ebabua kɛbaaya ayanina Mose kɛ Aaron lɛ, amɛtsɔ̃ amɛhiɛ amɛkwɛ Kpee Buu lɛ, ni naa, atatu kutuu lɛ ebaha Buu lɛ nɔ, ni Yehowa anunyam la lɛ epue.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron badamɔ Kpee Buu lɛ hiɛ,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Nyɛtsia nyɛhe kɛjea nɛkɛ asafo nɛɛ he kɛyaa sɛɛ koni makpãtã amɛhiɛ hiŋmɛitswaa mli.” Shi Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ amɛhiɛ bumɔ shi,

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Kɔ olajee tsɛnsi lɛ, ni oje afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ la lɛ eko owo mli, ni okɛ tsofakɛŋma ashwie nɔ, ni okɛya asafo lɛ ŋɔɔ mramra okɛyakpãtã ohã amɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa mlifu ete shi momo, ni gbele hela lɛ ebɔ̃i mɛi ahiɛ kpãtãmɔ.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Be ni gbele hela lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, Aaron ku esɛɛ kɛba Mose ŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Kɔlɔmɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛya Kpee Buu lɛ mli, ni okɛyashwie Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ he ni mi kɛ bo kpeɔ yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ ni ji mɔ ni miŋɔ lɛ, edɛhiɛmɔtso lɛ baagba afofro; ni mikɛ enɛ baahã huhuuhu ni Israelbii lɛ wieɔ amɛshiɔ nyɛ yɛ mihewɔ lɛ sɛɛ afo.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose bi Israelbii lɛ, kɛkɛ ni amɛkutseiatsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ bahã lɛ dɛhiɛmɔtso komekome yɛ amɛkutsei lɛ anaa. Fɛɛ fee dɛhiɛmɔtsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ, ni akɛ Aaron tso lɛ hu fata he.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ tsei lɛ tee eyashwie Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ mli.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ be ni Mose tee Kpee Buu lɛ mli lɛ, naa Aaron tso lɛ ni ji Levibii awe lɛ tso lɛ ni efrɔke ni egba afofro, ni ewo yibii hu.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Mose loo tsei lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ kɛje kpo kɛba Israelbii lɛ aŋɔ̃ɔ, ni ekɛbatsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ni akutsotsɛ fɛɛ akutsotsɛ kɔ etso.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpalemɔ ni okɛ Aaron tso lɛ ayafɔ̃ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ ekoŋŋ koni akɛto okadi ahã toigbolɔi lɛ bɔ ni afee ni huhuuhu ni amɛwieɔ amɛshiɔ mi lɛ sɛɛ afo, koni amɛkagboi.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Mose fee bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Naa, wɔmiiplene, wɔhiɛ miikpãtã! Wɔ bluublu wɔhiɛ miikpãtã.

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Ŋɔɔ onyɛmimɛi, Levibii ni ji otsɛ akutso lɛ mli bii lɛ, ofata ohe koni amɛwa bo be ni bo kɛ obii lɛ tsuɔ osɔfoi anitsumɔi lɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Amɛsɔ̃mɔ kɛtsu Kpee Buu lɛ mli nitsumɔi lɛ kɛkɛ yɛ oshishi; shi amɛkabɛŋkɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli nibii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ loo afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koni amɛ kɛ nyɛ fɛɛ akagboi.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Amɛ, amɛfata ohe koni amɛtsu amɛgbɛfaŋ nitsumɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Kpee Buu lɛŋ lɛ: shi moŋ mɔ ko ni jeee Levinyo akabɛŋkɛ nyɛ ni ebatsu jɛi nitsumɔ lɛ eko.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Bo kɛ obii lɛ pɛ akwɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he nitsumɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ bɔ ni afee ni mimli akafu Israelbii lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Ni naa, mijie nyɛnyɛmimɛi Levibii lɛ yɛ Israelbii fɛɛ ateŋ, ni mikɛ amɛ eke nyɛ akɛ mi, Yehowa, minikeenii, koni amɛsɔ̃mɔ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ mli.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Shi bo kɛ obihii lɛ pɛ asɔ̃mɔ akɛ osɔfoi yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he kɛ muhɔɔ lɛ mligbɛ hu. Miŋɔ osɔfoyeli lɛ mihã nyɛ akɛ sɔɔ̃mɔ ni aŋɔ ke. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ejeee osɔfo ni eeebɛŋkɛ nibii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, gbe aaagbe lɛ.” Osɔfoi agbɛnaanii

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amɛloo lɛ nyɛnɔ ni tamɔ bɔ ni kooloi krokomɛi ni akɛshãa afɔle atsitsinaa kɛ ninejurɔ shuɔji lɛ feɔ nyɛnɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Afɔlei krɔŋkrɔŋi ni fe fɛɛ lɛ amli nibii fɛɛ ni shwɛɔ yɛ afɔleshãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nyɛnɔ ni. Nibii fɛɛ ni akɛbakeɔ mi akɛ afɔle krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, niyenii afɔle ni jio, esha he afɔle ni jio, sɔ̃yeli he afɔle ni jio, mijɔɔ nɔ tswaa mikɛke bo kɛ oshwiei.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Nyɛyea nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ. Nuu fɛɛ nuu aaanyɛ aye eko; nyɛbua lɛ akɛ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: “Mikɛ nibii ni Israelbii lɛ kɛbahã mi akɛ shidaa afɔle lɛ hu eke nyɛ, ni ji bo kɛ oshwiei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ, akɛ amɛgbɛnaanii kɛmiiya naanɔ; ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ehe tse yɛ oshwiei ateŋ lɛ aaanyɛ aye eko.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Miijɔɔ mu kɛ wain kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ abele ni akuɔ lɛ mli ekpakpa fe fɛɛ ni Israelbii kɛbahãa mi Yehowa nɔ mihã bo.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai ni amɛtseɔ yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli ni amɛkɛhãa mi Yehowa lɛ, onɔ ni. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ehe tse yɛ oshwiei ateŋ lɛ aaanyɛ aye eko.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: “Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ajɔɔ nɔ akɛke mi yɛ Israel lɛ etsɔ̃ onɔ.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: “Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni gbeleɔ musu naa ni akɛbahãa Yehowa lɛ, gbɔmɔ ni jio, kooloo ni jio, mijɔɔ enɔ mihã nyɛ. Shi gbɔmɔ kromɔbi lɛ ohã akpɔ̃ lɛ; kooloi ni he tseee lɛ ohã akpɔ̃ amɛ

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: kɛji amɛye nyɔŋ kome lɛ, jara ni akɛkpɔ̃ amɛ ji jwiɛtɛi shekeli enumɔ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ jwiɛtɛi jara naa. Shekel kome feɔ gerai nyɔŋmai enyɔ.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Shi tsina loo gwantɛŋ loo abotia kromɔbi lɛ, okahã akpɔ̃ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛ lɛ amɛhe tse; amɛ okɛshã afɔle okɛhã mi. Okɛ amɛlá lɛ ashwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, ni oshã amɛmli fɔ lɛ koni efee afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ni jeɔ ŋma woɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Nibii fɛɛ ni Israelbii lɛ kɛbahãa mi akɛ afɔle krɛdɛɛ lɛ miijɔɔ fɛɛ nɔ miihã bo kɛ oshwiei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ akɛ amɛgbɛnaanii ni kã shi daa. Kpãŋmɔ ni mi kɛ bo kɛ oshwiei ekpãŋ nɛɛ akuŋ mli kɛmiiya naanɔ.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Onaŋ gboshinii ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni asaŋ onaŋ shikpɔŋ ni abaaja lɛ eko. Mi, Yehowa, mi ji ogbɛfaŋnɔ kɛ ogboshinii ni he hiaa bo yɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ.” Nɔ ni ahã Levibii lɛ

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Too fɛɛ too ni ji nii mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome ni awoɔ yɛ Israel ni akɛbahãa mi lɛ, mijɔɔ nɔ mihã Levibii lɛ akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋ gboshinii yɛ sɔ̃ɔmɔ ni amɛsɔ̃mɔɔ kɛtsuɔ Kpee Buu lɛ he nii lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ ji mɛi ni baatsu Kpee Buu lɛ he nii; ni kɛji nɔ ko tɔ̃ yɛ he lɛ sɔ̃yeli lɛ tere amɛ. Akpɔ nɛɛ akã shi daa ahã nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei. Levibii lɛ, amɛnaŋ gboshinii ko yɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ,

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ Levibii lɛ akɛ, kɛji nyɛnine shɛ nibii mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ ni mibi Israelbii koni amɛwo amɛhã nyɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ nyɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ, nyɛ hu nyɛjiea mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome nɛɛ mli mlijaa nyɔŋma kome koni nyɛkɛbahãa, mi Yehowa, akɛ afɔle krɛdɛɛ.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Ni abaabu nyɛfɔle krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ tamɔ abuɔ okwaafonyo ŋmãa hee kɛ wain hee ni ekɛbashãa afɔle lɛ.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ nibii fɛɛ ni akɛbaahã nyɛ lɛ amli nii kpakpa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashãa afɔle krɛdɛɛ lɛ nyɛkɛhãa Yehowa.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ Levibii lɛ akɛ, ‘Kɛji nyɛkɛ nyɛnibii lɛ amli nii kpakpa fe fɛɛ lɛ eshã afɔle lɛ, nyɛŋɔa nibii fɛɛ ni shwɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ akɛ nyɛnɔ tamɔ okwaafonyo ŋɔɔ eŋmɔshi nii loo wain ni shwɛɔ lɛ akɛ enɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei ayea nii ni shwɛɔ hãa nyɛ nɛɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he, ejaakɛ nyɛnii ni nyɛtsuɔ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nyɛyeee sɔ̃ ko yɛ no hewɔ, kɛji nyɛna nyɛkɛ nii lɛ mli nii kpakpa fe fɛɛ lɛ eshã afɔle momo lɛ. Nyɛkwɛa jogbaŋŋ kɛkɛ koni nyɛkabule nibii krɔŋkrɔŋi ni Israelbii kɛbahãa Yehowa lɛ koni nyɛbagboi.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Akpɔ ni mi, Yehowa, miwoɔ nɛ: Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛbahã bo tsinayoo tsuru ni kpa ko kpa ko bɛ ehe, ni asaŋ akɛ apã woko lɛ, ni akɛ lɛ tsuko nii dã.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Akɛ tsina lɛ ahã Osɔfo Eleazar, ni ekɛ kooloo lɛ aje kpo kɛya shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ koni agbe kooloo lɛ yɛ Eleazar hiɛ.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Eleazar asɔo tsina lɛ lá lɛ eko, ni ekɛ ewao atsɔ lá lɛ mli ni etsɛŋe lá lɛ eshwã Kpee Buu lɛ naagbɛ shii kpawo.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Ama tsinayoo muu lɛ fɛɛ naa la koni ashã lɛ kɛ ehewolo lɛ kɛ eloo lɛ kɛ elá lɛ kɛ ewamɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Osɔfo lɛ akɔlɔ tsenedru tso kɛ hisopo tso kɛ kpãa tsuru koni efɔ̃ ewo la ni akɛshãa tsinayoo lɛ mli.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni eju ehe dani ebote maŋbii lɛ ashitoohe lɛ mli. Shi enɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ osɔfo lɛ he tseee aahu kɛyashi gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni shã tsina lɛ hu afɔ etadei ahe, ni eju ehe. Lɛ hu ehe tseee kɛyashi gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ mɔ ko ni he tse aloo tsinayoo lɛ lamlu lɛ, ni ekɛya shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ he ko ni tse koni akɛ lamlu lɛ ayato jɛi. Akɛ lamlu nɛɛ awo nu ni akɛtsuɔ mɔ he akɛdãiɔ esha ni afee yɛ Israel lɛ mli. Enɛ ji hetsuumɔ afɔle.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Lɛ mɔ ni ebaaloo tsinayoo lɛ lamlu lɛ hu, ebaafɔ etadei ahe. Lɛ hu ehe tseee kɛyaashi gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ. Akpɔ nɛɛ baakã shi daa ahã Israelbii kɛ mɛi kpɔ̃ji ni ebato amɛ gbɔ fɛɛ. Mɔ ni eyata gbonyo he

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaata gbonyo ko he lɛ, ebule ehe kɛyaashi gbii kpawo.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ aju nu ni akɛtsuɔ mɔ he lɛ eko, yɛ gbi ni ji etɛ̃ kɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ, ni ehe aaatse. Shi kɛji ejuuu nu lɛ yɛ gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni ji kpawo lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ etsuuko ehe ni ehe tseŋ.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni aaata gbonyo ko he ni etsuuu ehe lɛ, eebule Yehowa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni abuŋ lɛ ashiŋ Israelbii lɛ anɔ, ejaakɛ ejuko nu ni akɛtsuɔ he lɛ ekɛdãiko ehe, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ekã muji lɛ mli lolo.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Kɛji mɔ ko gbo yɛ buu mli lɛ, ehe mla ni kã shi nɛ: mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ buu lɛ mli be ni mɔ lɛ nyɔ lɛ, kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaatee buu lɛ mli lɛ ebule ehe kɛyaashi gbii kpawo;

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: asaŋ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ buu lɛ mli ni abuko naa lɛ abule lɛ.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baata mɔ ko ni enyɔ yɛ klante naa gbonyo he, loo mɔ ni egbo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edɛŋ gbele gbonyo aloo eeeta gbonyo wu loo gbonyobu ko he yɛ jwɛiaŋ lɛ, ebule ehe kɛyashi gbii kpawo.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko ni ehe tse kɛ hisopo atsɔ nu kɛ lamlu lɛ mli koni ekɛshwã buu lɛ kɛ emli nibii fɛɛ kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ jɛi kɛ mɛi hu ni tee mli lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ akɛ nu nɛɛ ashwã mɔ ni eyata mɔ ni nyɔ yɛ klante naa gbonyo he loo mɔ ni gbo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edɛŋ gbele gbonyo he loo gbonyowu loo gbonyobu he lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: “Shi mɔ ni ebule ehe, shi etsuuu ehe koni ekɛfɔ ehe muji lɛ, abaashwie lɛ yɛ asafo lɛ mli, ejaakɛ eebule Yehowa He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Ejuko nu ni akɛtsuɔ he lɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ekã muji lɛ mli lolo.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Akpɔ nɛɛ akã shi ahã Israelbii lɛ daa. Mɔ ni kɛ hetsuumɔ nu lɛ shwãa lɛ, lɛ hu efɔ etadei lɛ ahe; ni mɔ ni aaata hetsuumɔ nu lɛ he lɛ, ebule ehe kɛyaashi gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mɔ ni ebule ehe aaata he lɛ, ebule nɔ lɛ; ni mɔ ni aaata nii ni abule he lɛ, lɛ hu ebule ehe kɛyaashi gbɛkɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ yashɛ Zin ŋa lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛto shi yɛ Kadesh. Biɛ Miriam gbo ni afu lɛ yɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Nu bɛ shitoohe nɛɛ hã maŋ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ bakpe

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: amɛwo Mose kɛ Aaron he. Amɛkɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Wɔgboi tamɔ wɔnyɛmimɛi lɛ gboi yɛ Yehowa Buu lɛ hiɛ moŋ kulɛ bɛ ehi:

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkɛ wɔ, Yehowa asafo lɛ, ebaŋa nɛɛ nɔ? Ani jeee koni wɔ kɛ wɔkooloi fɛɛ wɔbagboi yɛ biɛ?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Ni mɛni hewɔ nyɛkpala wɔ kɛjɛ Ijipt kɛba shikpɔŋ gbonyo tamɔ enɛ nɔ? Shikpɔŋ gbonyo ni ehiii enɔ nidumɔ, ni agbãmi kɛ waintso kɛ akutu ko bɛ enɔ he ko he ko; ni nu ni anuɔ tete po bɛ nɔ?”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron je gwabɔɔ lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛtee Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ shi; ni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ bumɔ shi; kɛkɛ ni Yehowa anunyam lɛ pue yɛ amɛnɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Kɔ tso lɛ, ni, bo kɛ onyɛmi Aaron, nyɛbuaa asafo lɛ naa, ni okɛ tɛsaa ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ awie yɛ amɛhiɛ akɛ ehã nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ atue. Nu baajɛ tɛsaa lɛ mli aba ahã maŋbii lɛ kɛ amɛkooloi lɛ koni amɛnu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose kɔ tso lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa fã lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron bua maŋ lɛ naa yɛ tɛsaa lɛ he, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛboa toi koo, nyɛ atuatselɔi! Ani wɔhã nu ajɛ tɛsaa nɛɛ mli ahã nyɛ lo?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mose wo enine nɔ, ni ekɛ etso lɛ tswa tɛsaa lɛ shii enyɔ, kɛkɛ ni nu tue babaoo, ni maŋbii lɛ kɛ amɛkooloi lɛ na nu amɛnu.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kã Mose kɛ Aaron hiɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Akɛni nyɛheee minɔ nyɛyeee koni nyɛhã maŋbii lɛ ana mihewalɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ kpele lɛ, nyɛkɛ asafo nɛɛ eyaŋ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhãa amɛ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Awo nu lɛ gbɛi akɛ Meriba nu lɛ, ejaakɛ Israelbii lɛ kɛ Yehowa taa naa yɛ jɛi, shi Yehowa tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jɛi akɛ Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ ji lɛ lɛɛlɛŋ. Edom Maŋtsɛ eŋmɛɛɛ Israelbii lɛ gbɛ

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Ni Mose tsu bɔfoi kɛjɛ Kadesh kɛtee Edom maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ayakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni onyɛmimɛi Israelbii kɛɛ nɛ: Bo diɛŋtsɛ ole, amanehului fɛɛ ni wɔna:

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: bɔ ni wɔblema tsɛmɛi lɛ tee Ijipt, kɛ bɔ ni wɔhi shi yɛ Ijipt be kplaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ, kɛ bɔ ni Ijiptbii fee wɔ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ niseniianii aahu.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Wɔfo wɔtsɛ Yehowa, ni ebo wɔ toi, ni etsu bɔfo ni ebajie wɔ kɛje Ijipt. Wɔbashɛ Kadesh amrɔ nɛɛ, ni ji maŋ ni yɔɔ ohusu lɛ naa kpaakpa.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Ofainɛ, ŋmɛɛ wɔ gbɛ koni wɔtsɔ̃ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kɛkɛ. Wɔyaŋ ŋmɔji loo wain tromi amli lɛ, wɔnuŋ nubui lɛ amli nu lɛ eko hu. Tɛmpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ wɔbaanyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ; wɔgbaŋ ninejurɔ loo abɛku kɛyaashi wɔɔfo mli yɛ okpokpai lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Shi Edombii lɛ hã hetoo akɛ, “Dabida! Nyɛkabatsɔ̃a wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛjeee nakai lɛ wɔbaafã ta wɔwo nyɛ.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ to he akɛ, “Tɛmpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ wɔbaanyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji wɔ kɛ wɔkooloi lɛ aaanu nyɛnu lɛ eko po lɛ, wɔbaawo nyɛ nyɔmɔ. Sane ko bɛ sɛɛ fe akɛ wɔmiitao wɔfo mli kpoo kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Edombii lɛ kɛɛ ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Wɔkpɛ̃lɛɛɛ!” Ni amɛfã ta kpeteŋkple kɛyasa Israelbii lɛ anaa.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Akɛni Edombii lɛ eyaŋmɛɛɛ Israelbii lɛ gbɛ koni amɛtsɔ̃ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ dɔ amɛyi, ni amɛyatsɔ̃ he kroko. Aaron gbele

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israelbii asafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Kadesh, ni amɛba Hor Gɔŋ lɛ he,

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aaron naji enyɔ yiŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛhã Israelbii lɛ nɔ; ebaagbo ejaakɛ nyɛbooo mi toi be ni nyɛyɔɔ Meriba lɛ.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ŋɔ̃ɔ Aaron kɛ ebinuu Eleazar koni okɛ amɛ aya Hor Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Jiemɔ osɔfoyeli atadei lɛ yɛ Aaron he yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni okɛwo ebinuu Eleazar. Aaron baagbo yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ni Mose fee bɔ ni Yehowa fã lɛ lɛ. Amɛkwɔ Hor Gɔŋ lɛ yɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ,

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: ni Mose jie osɔfoyeli atadei lɛ yɛ Aaron he, ni ekɛwo Aaron binuu Eleazar. Ni Aaron gbo yɛ jɛi yɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ, ni Mose kɛ Eleazar kpeleke shi kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Be ni Israel asafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ na akɛ Aaron eje jeŋ lɛ, amɛfo Aaron gbii nyɔŋmai etɛ̃.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fã kɛjɛ Hor Gɔŋ lɛ he, ni amɛtsɔ̃ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naagbɛ, he ni atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Akaba Ble lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni amɛtswa Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛfɔ̃. Nyiɛmɔ lɛ je Israelbii lɛ atsine yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: ni amɛwie amɛshi Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Mose amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba kwraa po nyɛjie wɔ yɛ Ijipt koni wɔbagboi yɛ ŋa nɛɛ nɔ nɛɛ? Niyenii bɛ lɛ, nu hu bɛ; niyenii gbonyogbonyo nɛɛ yeli eje wɔtsine.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa hã onufui ni anaa jaraa babote Israelbii lɛ ateŋ, ni amɛkɔ̃mɔ amɛ, ni Israelbii lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii gboi.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ ba Mose ŋɔɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔfee esha akɛ wɔwie wɔshi Yehowa kɛ bo fɛɛ. Kpa Yehowa fai ohã wɔ koni ejie onufui nɛɛ kɛje wɔteŋ.” Mose kpa fai lɛ ehã Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Okɛ dade ni kpɛlɛɔ afee onufu ni okɛtsotsoro tso bloblo nɔ, ni okɛma shi. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni onufui lɛ eko ekɔ̃ lɛ lɛ, kɛji ewo ehiɛ nɔ ekwɛ onufu lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyi baana wala.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose kɛ akɔɔble fee onufu, ni ekɛtsotsoro tso bloblo nɔ ni ekɛma shi. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni onufui lɛ eko ekɔ̃ lɛ lɛ, ewoɔ ehiɛ nɔ ekwɛɔ akɔɔble onufu lɛ, ni eyi naa wala. Israelbii lɛ yashɛ Moabbii ajɔɔ lɛ mli

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fã ekoŋŋ, ni amɛyato shi yɛ Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛfã ekoŋŋ lɛ, amɛyato shi yɛ Zered Jɔɔ lɛ mli;

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: ni kɛjɛ jɛi lɛ, Israelbii lɛ yato shi yɛ Arnon Faa lɛ kooyigbɛ ŋa kplanaa ni kã shi aahu kɛyaboteɔ Amorbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Arnon Faa nɛɛ ji Moabbii kɛ Amorbii lɛ ahusu.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, aŋmã yɛ Yehowa Tai Ahe Wolo lɛ mli akɛ, “Wɔtsɔ̃ Waheb yɛ Sufa, kɛ Arnon Faa lɛ jɔi lɛ amli,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: kɛ gɔji lɛ hu ni amɛjɔi lɛ yaa kɛyashɛɔ Ar maŋ lɛ shikãmɔhe lɛ anɔ ni ji Moab kpokpai lɛ ahusu lɛ.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fã kɛjɛ Arnon Faa lɛ kooyigbɛ ni amɛyato shi yɛ he ko ni atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Nubuianaa, he ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose yɛ akɛ, “Buamɔ maŋbii lɛ anaa, ni mahã amɛ nu koni amɛnu” lɛ.

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ Israelbii lɛ la nɛkɛ lala nɛɛ: “Nubu, hã nu atue, ni wɔɔɔbɔ oshe kɛhere lɛ atuu!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Nubu ni lumɛi lɛ tsa, ni maŋ abladei je kɛ amɛtsii kɛ amɛdɛhiɛmɔ tsei lɛ.” Israelbii lɛ shi ŋa lɛ nɔ kɛtee Matana,

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ Bamot lɛ amɛtee jɔɔ lɛ ni kã Moab ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli yɛ Pisga Gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛjɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ yiteŋ lɛ anaa shiaŋa kplanaa lɛ. Aye Maŋtsɛ Sihon kɛ Maŋtsɛ Og fɛɛ nɔ kunim (Deuteronomio

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Heshbon ji Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon lɛ maŋtsɛmaŋ. Sihon kɛ tsutsu Moab maŋtsɛ lɛ wu ni eshɔ̃ eshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ edɛŋ kɛbashi Arnon Faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ tsu bɔfoi kɛtee Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon ŋɔ̃ɔ ayakɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Ofainɛ, ŋmɛɛ wɔ gbɛ koni wɔtsɔ̃ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kɛkɛ. Wɔgbaŋ ŋmɔ ko loo waintrom ko mli lɛ, wɔnuŋ nubui lɛ amli nu lɛ eko hu. Maŋtsɛ tɛmpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ wɔbaanyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ; wɔgbaŋ ninejurɔ loo abɛku kɛyaashi wɔɔɔfo mli yɛ okpokpai lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ Sihon ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ nɔ akɛ Israelbii lɛ atsɔ̃ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho. No hewɔ lɛ, ebua etabilɔi anaa, ni efã ta kɛyanina Israelbii lɛ yɛ Yahaz ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ amɛ wu.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Shi Israelbii lɛ anine tsɔ̃ Amorbii lɛ anɔ, ni amɛgbe amɛ, ni amɛŋɔ Amorbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ Arnon Faa lɛ naa aahu kɛyashwie Yabok Faa lɛ naa, ni ji Amonbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ, ejaakɛ Amonbii lɛ etswa gbogboi yɛ amɛhusu lɛ naa.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii lɛ shɔ̃ Amorbii amaŋ ni ji Heshbon lɛ kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛhi mli.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: No hewɔ ni alaa akɛɔ akɛ, “Nyɛbaa Heshbon, nyɛhãa atswaa; asaa atswa Maŋtsɛ Sihon maŋ lɛ ama shi.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Nyɛsɛɛ ko lɛ, Heshbon maŋ nɛɛ mli Sihon tabilɔi fã kɛjɛ oookɛɛ la. Kɛyakpãtã Moab Ar maŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛ Arnon gɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ bii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Kpoo hã bo, bo Moab! Nyɛgbe nyɛjeŋ naa, nyɛ Kemosh jalɔi. Ehã ebihii lɛ etsɔ̃mɔ kobɔfoi, ni ebiyei lɛ hu etsɔ̃mɔ Amor Maŋtsɛ Sihon nomii.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwiei ahiɛ ekpãtã kɛjɛ Heshbon aahu kɛyashwie Dibon tɔ̃ɔ; kɛjɛ Nashim kɛtee Nofa yɛ Medeba masɛi.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Bɔ ni fee ni Israelbii lɛ hi Amorbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Mose tsu mɛi ni amɛtee amɛyasara Yazer maŋ lɛ amɛba; ni fee sɛɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ yatua maŋ lɛ, ni amɛŋɔ kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛshwie Amorbii ni yɔɔ jɛi momo sa lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ dɔ amɛyi, ni amɛyi Bashan gbɛ. Bashan maŋtsɛ Og fã ta, lɛ kɛ emaŋ lɛ fɛɛ, koni amɛkɛ Israelbii lɛ abawu yɛ Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kaashe lɛ gbeyei, ejaakɛ mijɔɔ lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ kɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ miwo odɛ̃ŋ. Obaaye enɔ kunim, koni ofee lɛ bɔ ni ofee Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon ni ye lumɔ yɛ Heshbon lɛ.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ gbe Maŋtsɛ Og kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ bɔ ni ashiii gbɔmɔ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ; ni amɛŋɔ eshikpɔŋ lɛ, ni amɛhi nɔ.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fã nyiɛmɔ, ni amɛyato shi yɛ Moab ŋa kplenee ni kã Yordan Faa lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ nɔ, yɛ Yeriko ŋlɛnɔ.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: kɛ Israelbii lɛ ayifalɛ hu; ni no hewɔ lɛ, lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ she gbeyei naakpa. Israelbii lɛ ahe ŋmiŋmi mɔ Moabbii lɛ.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Moabbii lɛ kɛɛ Midian maŋ onukpai lɛ akɛ, “Ataamɛi, gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ni baa kɛ ta nɛɛ baakpãtã nibii ni yɔɔ wɔkpokpai lɛ anɔ fɛɛ ahiɛ tamɔ tsina kpeɔ ŋa nɔ jwɛi lɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Moab Maŋtsɛ Balak

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: tsu bɔfoi akɛ amɛya Petor ni kã Eufrate Faa lɛ naa yɛ Amawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛyakpee Balaam, Beor bi lɛ amɛbahã lɛ. Wiemɔ ni bɔfoi lɛ kɛyahã Balaam ji, “Naa, mɛi komɛi, jaku muu, efã kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ni miwieɔ nɛɛ amɛbɛŋkɛ biɛ amɛtã, mihiɛ tua amɛ.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, ba nɔŋŋ, shi amɛyi fa fe wɔ, koni obalomɔ amɛ ohã mi akɛ aleenɔ minine aaatsɔ̃ amɛnɔ koni mashwie amɛ kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lo. Mile akɛ kɛji ojɔɔ mɔ ko lɛ, jɔɔmɔ baa mɔ lɛ nɔ; ni kɛji olomɔ mɔ ko hu lɛ, loomɔ baa mɔ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Moab onukpai lɛ kɛ Midian onukpai lɛ yi mli amɛtee; ni amɛhiɛ klamɔ nyɔmɔwoo shika kɛtee. Be ni amɛyashɛ Balaam ŋɔɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ wiemɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Balak kɛtsu amɛ lɛ hã lɛ.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛwɔa biɛ ŋmɛnɛ; wɔ lɛ mibaba mibakɛɛ nyɛ nɔ ni Yehowa aaakɛɛ mi.” No hewɔ lɛ, Moab onukpai lɛ kɛ Balaam hi shi gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Ni Nyɔŋmɔ ba Balaam ŋɔ̃ɔ, ni ebabi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hii yɔɔ oŋɔ̃ɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, “Moab Maŋtsɛ Balak, Zipor bi lɛ, tsu amɛ miŋɔ̃ɔ akɛ

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: maŋ muu ko, ni jɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eba, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ mibalomɔ amɛ mihã lɛ koni enyɛ amɛ ekɛwu, ni eshwie amɛ kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Okɛ bɔfoi lɛ akaya tsɛmɔ lɛ, ni asaŋ okalomɔ nakai mɛi lɛ hu, ejaakɛ mɛi ni mijɔɔ amɛ ni.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Balaam tee Balak bɔfoi lɛ aŋɔ̃ɔ, ni eyakɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ nyɛyaa nyɛmaŋ. Yehowa ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ nɔ ehãaa mi akɛ mikɛ nyɛ aya.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Moab onukpai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba Balak ŋɔ̃ɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Balaam ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ eba otsɛmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Balak saa tsu bɔfoi ni ahiɛ tsii, asaŋ ni amɛyi fa fe tsutsubii lɛ;

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: ni amɛtee Balaam ŋɔ̃ɔ, ni amɛyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Moab Maŋtsɛ Balak, Zipor bi lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Ofainɛ, ni okahã nɔ ko nɔ ko miitsi bo tsɛmɔ lɛ baa gbɛ!

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mibawo ohiɛ nyam babaoo diɛŋtsɛ, asaŋ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaakɛɛ mi lɛ, mibafee; no hewɔ lɛ, bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oba koni obalomɔ mɛi ni ebaje nɛɛ ohã mi kɛkɛ.’ ”

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ, nyɛ hu, nyɛwɔa biɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ tamɔ mɛi krokomɛi lɛ koni mabo nɔ ni Yehowa aaakɛɛ mi ekoŋŋ toi.”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Nyɔɔŋ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Kɛji tsɛmɔ kɛkɛ hii nɛɛ ba bo tsɛmɔ lɛ, saamɔ ohe koni okɛ amɛ aya; shi moŋ nɔ pɛ ni makɛɛ bo lɛ no ofee.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Balaam wo eteji nɔ nii, ni ekɛ Moab onukpai lɛ yi mli ni amɛtee. Balaam kɛ eteji lɛ

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ mli wo la akɛ Balaam miiya tsɛmɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, be ni Balaam ta eteji lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ni eblahii enyɔ lɛ kɛ lɛ nyiɛ lɛ, Yehowa bɔfo lɛ badamɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ koni esa enaa.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Be ni teji lɛ na Yehowa bɔfo lɛ damɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ ni egbala eklante ehiɛ edɛŋ lɛ, ewi gbɛ lɛ, ni eyanyiɛ ŋa lɛ mli. Balaam yi teji lɛ koni ekɛdɔ eyi kɛba gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo lɛ tee ni eyadamɔ gbɛ leleoo ko ni kã waintromi ateŋ lɛ nɔ; gbogbo yɛ gbɛ lɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Be ni teji lɛ na Yehowa bɔfo lɛ ekɛ ehe yakpɛtɛ gbogbo lɛ, ni emia Balaam nane ekpɛtɛ gbogbo lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Balaam yi teji lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Yehowa bɔfo lɛ saa etsi kɛtee ehiɛ, ni eyasa Balaam naa yɛ nififiaŋ he ko, he ni gbɛ bɛ ni akɛtsɔ̃ɔ he kɛyaa ninejurɔgbɛ loo abɛkugbɛ.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni teji lɛ na Yehowa bɔfo lɛ, eho ebu shi. Balaam mli wo la ni ebɔ̃i teji lɛ yii.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa hã teji lɛ wie, ni ebi Balaam akɛ, “Mɛni mifee bo hewɔ ni oyi mi shii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Balaam here teji lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ejaakɛ oofee mi buulu. Eji mihiɛ klante kulɛ benɛ migbe bo momo.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Teji lɛ kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Ani jeee mi ji oteji ni otaa minɔ daa nɛɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ? Ani mifee bo nɛkɛ nɔ ko dã lo?” Balaam jie naa akɛ, “Dabida!”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa gbele Balaam hiŋmɛii, ni ena Yehowa bɔfo lɛ damɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ eklante ni egbala ehiɛ edɛŋ. Balaam mã eyi shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Yehowa bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ni oyi oteji lɛ shii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ nɛɛ? Naa, miba koni mibasa onaa, ejaakɛ nyiɛmɔ nɔ ni onyiɛ nɛɛ ejaaa yɛ mihiɛ.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Teji lɛ na mi, ni ewi ehe kɛje mihiɛ shii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ. Ewiii ehe kɛjeee mihiɛ kulɛ, benɛ migbe bo momo, ni mihere teji lɛ kɛkɛ yiwala.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balaam hã Yehowa bɔfo lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Mifee esha; ejaakɛ mileee kwraa akɛ oba oosa minaa yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji minyiɛmɔ nɛɛ esaaa ohiɛ lɛ, maku misɛɛ mɔ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Okɛ hii lɛ aya kɛkɛ; shi moŋ wiemɔ ni mikɛ bo aaawie lɛ, no nɔŋŋ pɛ owie.” Kɛkɛ ni Balaam kɛ Maŋtsɛ Balak bɔfoi lɛ tsa nyiɛmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtee. Maŋtsɛ Balak here Balaam atuu

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Be ni Balak nu akɛ Balaam miiba etsɛmɔ lɛ, eyi mli kɛtee lɛ kpeemɔ yɛ Ar, ni ji Moabbii amaŋ ko ni kã Arnon Faa lɛ naa lɛ mli. Arnon Faa nɛɛ ji Moabbii ahusu.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Balak kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Ani jeee tsu mitsu kpɛkpɛ̃ɛkpɛ akɛ abatsɛ bo kɛba? Mɛɛba obaaa klɛŋklɛŋ tsɛmɔ lɛ? Ani osusuɔ akɛ minyɛŋ bo majuro bɔ ni sa lo?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Naa mi; miba. Shi moŋ, mɛɛ hewalɛ miyɔɔ? Wiemɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛbaawo minaa lɛ, no nɔŋŋ mawie.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balaam kɛ Balak shwie nɔ kɛba maŋ ni gbɛi ji Huzot lɛ mli;

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: ni Balak kɛ tsinai kɛ toi shã afɔle yɛ jɛi, ni ehã ayahã Balaam kɛ onukpai ni kɛ lɛ nyiɛ lɛ afɔleshãa loo lɛ eko.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Balak tsɛ Balaam fata ehe, ni amɛkwɔ Baal Gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee eyiteŋ; ni Balaam jɛ jɛi ni ena Israelbii asafo muu lɛ ayifalɛ.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Mãamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi kpawo yɛ biɛ ohã mi; ni obahã mi tsinahii kpawo kɛ ojwɛnii hu kpawo.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak fee nɔ ni Balaam kɛɛ lɛ lɛ ni lɛ kɛ Balaam shã tsinanuu kome kɛ ojwɛni hu kome yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ fɛɛ afɔleshãa latɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Yaadamɔ oshãa afɔle lɛ he, koni maya akɛ aleee nɔ mikɛ Yehowa aaakpe lo. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eeekɛɛ mi lɛ, mibaba mibakɛɛ bo.” Kɛkɛ ni eyi mli etee gɔŋ kpataa ko nɔ.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Balaam kpe, ni Balaam kɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, “Mimamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi kpawo, ni mishã tsinanuu kome kɛ ojwɛni hu kome yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ fɛɛ afɔleshãa latɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛ wiemɔ wo Balaam naa, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ kɛya Balak ŋɔɔ ni oyakɛɛ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛɛ bo lɛ.”

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Be ni Balaam ku esɛɛ kɛba Balak ŋɔɔ lɛ, Balak kɛ Moab lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ damɔ Balak shãa afɔle lɛ he.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balaam wo egbee nɔ, ni ebɔi gbaa ekɛɛ, “Moab Maŋtsɛ Balak yaŋɔ mi kɛjɛ Siria, yɛ bokã gɔji lɛ anɔ ekɛɛ: ‘Ba, baalomɔ Yakob; Baalomɔ Israelbii ohã mi!’

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Shi te aaafee tɛŋŋ malomɔ mɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ lomɔko lɛ hu? Te aaafe tɛŋŋ mashwe musu mahã mɔ ko be ni Yehowa ekɛko nakai?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Tɛsai ayiteŋ mijɛ mina amɛ; ni gɔŋkpɔi anɔ mijɛ mikwɛ amɛ akɛ maŋ ni amɛkome too amɛyɔɔ. Amɛle akɛ ajɔɔ amɛ fe maji fɛɛ.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Israel shwiei ayikulɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ mlu, Amɛyi fa fe bɔ ni aaanyɛ akane. Hã magbo jalɔi agbele koni minaagbee atamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ webii anɔ.”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balak kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Te okɛ mi yeɔ tɛŋŋ nɛɛ? Miyaŋɔ bo kɛba koni obalomɔ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ, shi jɔɔmɔ sɔŋŋ moŋ ojɔɔ amɛ nɛɛ!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Balaam here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ani esaaa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni mawie nɔ ni Yehowa kɛwo minaa lɛ?” Balaam gbalɛ ni ji Enyɔ

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Balak kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Ofainɛ, ba ni wɔtee he kroko, he ni ooona Israelbii lɛ yɛ. Obaana amɛfã ko kɛkɛ; onaŋ amɛ fɛɛ; koni olomɔ amɛ yɛ jɛi ohã mi.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Balak kɛ Balaam tee Zofim ŋa lɛ nɔ yɛ Pisga Gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ, ni eyamãmɔ afɔleshãa latɛi kpawo yɛ jɛi, ni ekɛ tsinanuu komekome kɛ ojwɛni hu komekome shã afɔle yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ fɛɛ afɔleshãa latɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balaam kɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Baadamɔ biɛ yɛ oshãa afɔle lɛ he, koni matsi kɛya hiɛ fioo koni mikɛ Yehowa ayakpe.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Balaam kpe, ni ekɛ wiemɔ wo enaa, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ kɛya Balak ŋɔɔ ni oyakɛɛ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛɛ bo lɛ.”

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Ni Balaam ku esɛɛ kɛba, ni ebanina Balak kɛ Moab onukpai lɛ fɛɛ damɔ Balak shãa afɔle lɛ he. Kɛkɛ ni Balak bi Balaam akɛ, “Mɛni Yehowa kɛɛ?”

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ jeee gbɔmɔ adesa ni eeemale, aloo gbɔmɔ ni eeeshwa ehe yɛ nɔ ni efee hewɔ. Mɛni ekɛɛ dã ni efeee; aloo ewo ehe shi ni eyeee nɔ?

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Naa, jɔɔmɔ efã mi akɛ mijɔɔ; Ena ejɔɔ amɛ momo, ni minyɛŋ hiɛ matsake

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Minaaa akɛ osharã ko basharã Israel, aloo Israel he baajara lɛ. Yehowa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ amɛ yɛ; lɛ amɛbɔɔ oshe amɛhãa akɛ amɛmaŋtsɛ.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ jie amɛ kɛje Ijipt; amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ he wa oookɛɛ wuo.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Ŋkunyaa ko nyɛŋ Israel, ni klamɔ ko hu mɔŋ lɛ. Odase ni abaaye yɛ Israel he ji akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ninenaa nitsumɔ nɛ.’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Naa, Israel teɔ shi tamɔ jata yoo; ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ tamɔ jata nuu. Ebuuu shi, ja egbe ni eye, ni enu mɛi ni egbegbee alá etã dã.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balak kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Kaalomɔ amɛ, ni kaajɔɔ amɛ hu.”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Shi Balaam here Balak nɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani mikɛɛɛ bo akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni Yehowa aaakɛɛ lɛ no mibafee lo?” Balaam gbalɛ ni ji Etɛ̃ lɛ

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Balak kɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ hã wɔya he kroko. Eko lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ aaana he tsui, ni eeeŋmɛ bo gbɛ akɛ olomɔ Israelbii lɛ yɛ jɛi ohã mi.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ni Balak kɛ Balaam shwie nɔ kɛtee Poer Gɔŋ ni kwɛɔ shiaŋa kplenee lɛ nɔ lɛ yiteŋ.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam kɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Mãamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi kpawo yɛ biɛ ohã mi; ni obahã mi tsinahii kpawo kɛ ojwɛnii hu kpawo yɛ biɛ.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak fee nɔ ni Balaam kɛɛ lɛ lɛ; ni Balak kɛ tsinanuu kɛ ojwɛni shã afɔle yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ fɛɛ afɔleshãa latɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Shi Balaam eyɔse akɛ Yehowa suɔmɔ naa ji akɛ ejɔɔ Israelbii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eyaaa tamɔ bei krokomɛi lɛ akɛ eyaatao okadii. Shi moŋ ewo ehiɛ nɔ, ni ekwɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Ena Israelbii lɛ ni amɛjwere shi yɛ amɛkutsei lɛ anaa. Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ lɛ bayi Balaam nɔ,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: ni ewo enaa nɔ, ni egba ekɛɛ akɛ, “Balaam, Beor bi lɛ, ninaa nɛ, nuu ninalɔ lɛ ninaa nɛ,

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: mɔ ni nuɔ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ ni enaa ninaa ni Ofe lɛ jieɔ etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, mɔ ni buɔ shi, shi enaa nii lɛ.

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Kwɛ bɔ ni Israel bui lɛ yɔɔ fɛo! Israel shihilɛhei amli yɛ akɔnɔ

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: tamɔ faa he jɔi ni elɛɛ shi oookɛɛ faa toi abɔi, tamɔ tsei fɛɛfɛji ni Yehowa tɛo oookɛɛ faa toi tsenedrutsei.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Nu aaajɛ onubui amli, Israel, ashwie shi ni oshwiei kɛaadu nii. Omaŋtsɛ lɛ baaje agbo fe Maŋtsɛ Agag, ni aaawo emaŋtsɛyeli nɔ.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ yajie amɛ yɛ Ijipt, ni amɛhe wa tamɔ wuo. Amɛbaaye amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ amaji anɔ, ni amɛbaajwara amɛwui wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ, ni amɛkɛ amɛgãii lɛ baatsɛ̃rɛ amɛ.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Edɛke shi; ebu shi tamɔ jata, tamɔ jatayoo; namɔ aaatsiɛ lɛ? Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni jɔɔ bo lɛ, aaajɔɔ lɛ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni lomɔɔ bo lɛ, aaalomɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Balak kɛ mlifu tswa edɛ̃, ni ekɛɛ Balaam akɛ, “Miyakpee bo kɛba koni obalomɔ mihenyɛlɔi ohã mi lɛ, jɔɔmɔ sɔŋŋ moŋ ojɔɔ amɛ shii etɛ̃ nɛɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kuu osɛɛ ni oya omaŋ. Mito miyiŋ akɛ majuro bo; shi Yehowa etsi juromɔ ni majuro bo lɛ naa.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Naa, kɛji Balak ŋɔ̃ ewe lɛ mli shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi tsu obɔ̃ tete eke mi lɛ, minyɛŋ maje Yehowa wiemɔ sɛɛ koni mato miyiŋ mafee nɔ kpakpa loo nɔ fɔŋ ko. Nɔ ni Yehowa aaakɛɛ lɛ no nɔŋŋ ji nɔ ni mawie.’ ” Balaam naagbee gbalɛ

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Balaam tee ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ Balak akɛ, “Mi lɛ miiya mimaŋ, shi dani mashwie nɔ lɛ, mibatswa bo adafi yɛ nɔ ni Israel maŋ nɛɛ baafee omaŋ lɛ wɔsɛɛ ko he.”

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balaam wo enaa nɔ, ni ebɔ̃i gbaa ekɛɛ, “Balaam, Beor binuu lɛ, ninaa nɛ. Nɔ ni mɔ ni agbele ehiŋmɛii lɛ kɛɛ nɛ:

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: ‘Mɔ ni nuɔ Nyɔŋmɔ wiemɔi lɛ, ni eleɔ Ŋwɛinyo lɛ yiŋtoi lɛ, ni Ofe lɛ jieɔ ninai etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ lɛ, ni ehiɛ bu shi, shi enaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɔ nɛ:

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Miina Israel, shi jeee bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ minaa lɛ, shi eyɛ shɔŋŋ. Ŋulami ko baaje yɛ Yakob, Maŋtsɛ tso ko baate shi yɛ Israel, ni ebaatswia Moab hiɛnaanɔbii lɛ anii, ni ebaaye Set shwiei lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Ebaaye Edom nɔ, ni eeeye Seir hu nɔ, eeeye ehenyɛlɔi lɛ hu anɔ ni eeeŋɔ amɛshikpɔji lɛ be mli ni Israel yeɔ kunim lɛ.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Israel jaku baanaanaa amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ, ni eeekpãtã mɛi ni aaashwɛ yɛ maji lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Balaam na Amalekbii lɛ yɛ ninaa lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni etsɔ̃ gbalɛ lɛ kɛtee amɛnɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Amalek ji majimaji lɛ ateŋ mɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ; shi naagbee mli aahu lɛ, ehiɛ baakpãtã kwraa.”

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Balaam na Kenbii lɛ hu yɛ ninaa lɛ mli, ni egba yɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Oshihilɛhe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe tamɔ loofɔlɔ tsu ni mã tɛsaa nɔ.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ Kenbii ahiɛ baakpãtã ni etsɛŋ ni Asiria aaaŋɔ̃ bo nom.”

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Akɛ ta lɛji aaajɛ Kipro aba ni aaabaye Asiria kɛ Eber nɔ. Shi tatsɛmɛi nɛɛ hu ahiɛ aaakpãtã kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Balaam yi mli, ni eku esɛɛ kɛtee emaŋ, ni Balak hu ku esɛɛ kɛtee ejɛɛhe.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ yɔɔ Shitim, Akasia tso Jɔɔ lɛŋ lɛ, amɛhii lɛ kɛ Moab yei lɛ bɔ̃i ajwamãŋbɔɔ.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Moab yei lɛ kpeɔ Israelhii lɛ kɛyaa hei ni amɛshãa afɔlei amɛkɛhãa amɛmaŋ wɔji lɛ yɛ lɛ; ni Israelhii lɛ yayeɔ afɔleshãa niyenii lɛ eko, ni amɛjaa Moabbii lɛ awɔji lɛ hu.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii lɛ kɛ amɛhe yabɔ jemawɔŋ Peor lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa mli wo la,

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mɔ̃ɔmɔ maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ fɛɛ koni agbe amɛ shwane ketekete yɛ mi, Yehowa, mihiɛ; bɔ ni afee ni Yehowa mli ni efu Israel fe nine lɛ sɛɛ afo.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mose kɛɛ Israel maŋ onukpai lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ agbe lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekutso lɛ mli nuu fɛɛ nuu ni etsɔ̃ ehe jemawɔŋ Peor jalɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ ateŋ nuu ko tee eyakpala Midianyoo ko ni ekɛ lɛ tee ebuu lɛ mli yɛ Mose kɛ Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ, be mli ni Mose kɛ Israel asafo muu lɛ yeɔ ŋkɔmɔ yɛ Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa lɛ.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Be ni Osɔfo Aaron binuu Eleazar binuu Finehas na nifeemɔ nɛɛ lɛ, ete shi yɛ asafo lɛ mli, ni eyakɔ akplɔ ehiɛ edɛ̃,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: ni etiu Israelnyo lɛ kɛtee buu lɛ mli, ni eyadu Israelnyo lɛ kɛ Midianyoo lɛ fɛɛ akplɔ bɔ ni etsɔ̃ amɛmli kɛyaje kpo. Biɛ tsɔ̃ ni gbele hela lɛ ni miikpãtã Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ sɛɛ fo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: “Mihe awuŋã ni Osɔfo Aaron binuu Eleazar binuu Finehas ye etsɔ̃ɔ Israelbii lɛ, ekɛku mimli ni efu Israelbii lɛ anaa, ni no hewɔ lɛ, mipleneee amɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: ni mijɔɔ osɔfoyeli lɛ nɔ mihã lɛ kɛ eshwiei kɛmiiya naanɔ, ejaakɛ eye awuŋã yɛ mi, mihewɔ, ni ehã akɛ tɔ̃mɔ ni maŋ lɛ tɔ̃ lɛ efa amɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Israelnyo lɛ ni agbe lɛ kɛ Midianyoo lɛ, egbɛi ji Zimri; ni etsɛ ji Salu, Simeonbii akutso lɛ mli wekui lɛ eko mli onukpa ni.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Ni Midianyoo lɛ ni agbe lɛ gbɛi ji Kozbi; etsɛ gbɛi ji Zur, Midianbii awekui lɛ eko mli onukpa ni.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Yehowa fã Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ amɛ hu amɛfee nyɛ efɔŋ kɛ lakamɔ ni amɛlaka nyɛ yɛ jemawɔŋ Peor lɛ jamɔ sane lɛ mli, agbɛnɛ amɛlaka nyɛ yɛ amɛnyɛmi yoo Midian onukpa ko biyoo Kozbi sane lɛ mli. Lɛ ji Midianyoo lɛ ni agbe lɛ yɛ gbele hela gbi lɛ nɔ yɛ Peor lɛ.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Gbele hela lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Mose kɛ Osɔfo Aaron binuu Eleazar akɛ,

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: “Nyɛkanea Israelbii asafo muu lɛ mli hii fɛɛ ni eye kɛjɛ afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛyaa ayikulɛ yɛ amɛtsɛmɛi awei lɛ anaa, no ji mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni eshɛ tayaa yɛ Israel lɛ.”

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Yuda shwiei lɛ akutso lɛ mli shĩai lɛ ji Shelawe kɛ Perezwe.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Osɔfo Eleazar kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ yɛ Moab ŋa kplenee lɛ nɔ yɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa yɛ Yeriko akɛ,

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu bi ji Eliab,

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: ni Eliab bihii ji Nemuel kɛ Datan kɛ Abiram. Datan kɛ Abiram nɛɛ ji hii komɛi ni maŋbii lɛ hala kɛjɛ asafo lɛ mli, ni amɛtse Mose kɛ Aaron hiɛ atua, ni asaŋ amɛyafata Kora sɛɛbii lɛ ahe kɛte shi amɛshi Yehowa lɛ.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ gba ni emĩ amɛ kɛ Kora fɛɛ kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ hu, be ni la lɛ je ni eshã hii ohai enyɔ kɛ nyɔŋmai enumɔ koni akɛto okadi lɛ.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ Kora diɛŋtsɛ musuŋbihii lɛ gboiii.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Mɛi abɔ ni Mose kɛ Aaron kane be ni amɛkane Israelbii lɛ ayikulɛ yɛ Sinai Shiaŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ateŋ mɔ kome folo nɛkɛ bɛ mɛi ni akane ehee nɛɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Ni Aaron fɔ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Eleazar kɛ Itamar.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ohã akutsei lɛ yɛ amɛmli gbɔmɛi lɛ ayikulɛ naa.”

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Mɛi ni yi fa kɛ mɛi ni yi faaa fɛɛ lɛ, afɔ oshiki koni akɛja amɛgbɛfaŋnii lɛ ahã amɛ.

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,
translation_verse: Yɛ Levi shwiei agbɛfaŋ lɛ, amɛshĩai wuji ni akane lɛ amɛmli bii ji Gershonwe kɛ Kohatwe kɛ Merariwe.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Shĩai bibii ni jɛ ewuji nɛɛ amli lɛ ji Libniwe kɛ Hebronwe kɛ Maheliwe kɛ Mushiwe kɛ Korawe. Kohat fɔ Amram,

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: mɔ ni kɛ Levi biyoo Yokebed, mɔ ni efɔ yɛ Ijipt lɛ, hi shi akɛ eŋa lɛ. Amran kɛ Yokebed fɔ Aaron kɛ Mose kɛ amɛnyɛmi yoo Miriam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Shi Nadab kɛ Abihu gboi be ni amɛkɛ la ni bɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ yashã afɔle yɛ Yehowa hiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ayikulɛ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Mose kɛ Osɔfo Eleazar na be ni amɛkane Israelbii lɛ yɛ Moab ŋa kplenee lɛ nɔ yɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa yɛ Yeriko ŋlɛnɔ lɛ.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ amɛhe akɛ gboimɔ amɛaagboi yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ. Mɛi ni shwɛ ji Kaleb, Yefune bi lɛ, kɛ Yoshua, Nun bi lɛ, kɛkɛ.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: ho damɔ Mose kɛ Osɔfo Eleazar kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ yɛ Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa, ni amɛkɛɛ amɛ akɛ,

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Wɔtsɛ Zelofehad gbo yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; efataaa Kora kɛ esɛɛbii ni te shi amɛshi Yehowa lɛ ahe. Egbo yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe esha hewɔ ni efɔɔɔ bihii.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba ni agbeɔ wɔtsɛ gbɛi yɛ etsɛmɛi awe lɛ mli? Binuu ni enaaa lɛ hewɔŋ lo? Nyɛhãa wɔ, wɔ hu wɔgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ wɔtsɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ!”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Zelofehad biyei lɛ asane lɛ yafɔ̃ Yehowa hiɛ,

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Nɔ ni Zelofehad biyei lɛ biɔ lɛ eja. Hã amɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ amɛtsɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ bɔ ni afee ni amɛ, amɛye amɛtsɛ gboshinii.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Kɛji ebɛ biyoo lɛ, no lɛ enyɛmimɛi hii aye egboshinii.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Kɛji ebɛ nyɛmimɛi hii hu lɛ, etsɛ nyɛmimɛi hii aye egboshinii.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Kɛji etsɛ bɛ nyɛmimɛi hii lɛ, no lɛ ewekunyo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ weku mli aye egboshinii lɛ. Enɛ ji mla ni akã shi ahã Israelbii bɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mifã bo lɛ.” Aŋɔ Yoshua koni eye Mose sɛɛ (Deuteronomio

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kwɔɔ Abarim Gɔŋ nɛɛ kɛya eyiteŋ koni okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhãa Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Kɛji okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ogbe naa lɛ, bo hu obaagbo tamɔ onyɛmi Aaron,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ nyɛku migbee nɔ yɛ Zin ŋa lɛ nɔ. Be ni maŋ muu lɛ wie amɛshi mi, ni kulɛ sa akɛ nyɛhã amɛna mihewalɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ kpele lɛ, koni amɛshe mi gbeyei yɛ Meriba lɛ, nyɛfeee nakai.”

english_verse: Moses replied,
translation_verse: Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ,

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: mɔ ni baanyɛ amɛnɔ ekwɛ, asaŋ ni enyiɛ amɛhiɛ kɛya ta kɛba bɔ ni afee ni Yehowa asafo lɛ akatsɔ̃ tamɔ toi ni bɛ kwɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã Mose hetoo akɛ, “Ŋɔ̃ɔ Nun binuu Yoshua lɛ, nuu hiɛwalɔ ni Mumɔ lɛ yɔɔ emli lɛ koni okɛ oniji ashwie enɔ,

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: ni okɛ lɛ adamɔ Osɔfo Eleazar kɛ asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ, ni otu nitsumɔ lɛ owo edɛŋ yɛ amɛhiɛ akɛ mɔ ni baaye osɛɛ;

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: asaŋ ni ohã lɛ hewalɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ eko bɔ ni afee ni Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ abo lɛ toi.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Ebo Osɔfo Eleazar toi be fɛɛ be. Eya eŋɔ̃ɔ, ni ebaafɔ̃ Urim lɛ koni ekɛbi mi nii ehã lɛ yɛ mihiɛ. Lɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ kɛ asafo lɛ fɛɛ ayaakɛbaa mli lɛ, amɛbo Osɔfo Eleazar wiemɔ toi.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Mose fee nɔ ni Yehowa fã akɛ efee lɛ. Eŋɔ Yoshua ni ekɛ lɛ yadamɔ Osɔfo Eleazar kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: ni ekɛ eniji shwie enɔ, ni etu nitsumɔ lɛ ewo edɛŋ akɛ mɔ ni baaye esɛɛ taakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: ni gwantɛŋbi kome he niyenii afee mamu kilo kome.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: ni gwantɛŋbi kome lɛ mamu kilo kome. Shãa afɔlei nɛɛ eji niyenii afɔle ni jeɔ ŋma woɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛhiɛ ahi minikeenii ni ji niyenii afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ni ejeɔ ŋma ewoɔ mi lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛbahã mi kɛji afɔle hãmɔ be shɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: “Gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ ahã gwantɛŋbii enyɔ ni eye afiafi asaŋ ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe koni akɛshã afɔle ahã mi.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Dãa afɔle lita kome afata gwantɛŋbi kome he, koni ofɔse dãa lɛ oshwie shi yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ okɛhã Yehowa.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: “Nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛshãa afɔle nyɛkɛhãa Yehowa. Nyɛkɛ tsina oblahii enyɔ kɛ ojwɛni kome kɛ gwantɛŋ bihii kpawo ni eye afifi ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe ashãa.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Niyenii afɔle ni ji ŋmãa mamu ni akɛ fɔ ekpɔtɔ ni akɛfata kooloi lɛ ahe nɛ: tsinanuu kome lɛ mamu kiloi etɛ̃, ojwɛni lɛ mamu kiloi enyɔ,

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: “Afi lɛŋ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ ji Yehowa Hehoo Gbijurɔ lɛ.
