english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
translation_verse: kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji nyɛbii aaabi nyɛ wɔsɛɛ ko akɛ, ‘Te nɛkɛ tɛi nɛɛ ashishi hu lɛ,’

english_verse: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ hã Yordan mli nu lɛ gbi hã nyɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni nyɛfo nyɛtã tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fee Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ, be ni ehã egbi ehã wɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni wɔfo wɔtã lɛ,

english_verse: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_verse: koni je lɛŋ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ana ale akɛ Yehowa yɛ hewalɛ, koni nyɛshe Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbeyei kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: Be ni Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Yordan sɛɛ yɛ anaigbɛ lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii amaŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa lɛ nu akɛ Yehowa hã Yordan lɛ mli nu lɛ gbi kɛyashi Israelbii lɛ fo faa lɛ tã lɛ, amɛtsui fã, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ mli ekãa laaje yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahewɔ. Afo Israel hii lɛ ketia yɛ Gilgal

english_verse: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Feemɔ tɛ kaklai koni ofolɔ Israelbii lɛ ketia.”

english_verse: Joshua made the knives, then circumcised those men and boys at Haaraloth Hill.
translation_verse: Yoshua fee tɛ kaklai lɛ, ni ekɛfolɔ Israelbii ketia yɛ Gibeat Haaralot .

english_verse: This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ hii nɛɛ abii ni ebaye amɛsɛɛ lɛ, amɛ ji mɛi ni Yoshua fo amɛ ketia nɛɛ, ejaakɛ foolɔi ji amɛ, akɛni afolɔko amɛ ketia lɛ.

english_verse: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
translation_verse: Be ni afo maŋ lɛŋ hii fɛɛ ketia lɛ agbe naa lɛ, maŋ muu lɛ hi shi yɛ shitoohe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyashi hii lɛ ahe tã.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, mifɔ nyɛhe muji ni awo yɛ Ijipt lɛ mishwie.” No hewɔ ni atsɛɔ shitoohe nɛɛ akɛ Gilgal kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ yɔɔ Gilgal lɛ, amɛye Hehoo Gbijurɔ lɛ yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ yɛ Yeriko ŋã kplanaa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields. Israel Captures Jericho
translation_verse: Ni gbi ni amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibaanii lɛ eko lɛ nɔ jetsɛremɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni mana lɛ sɛɛ fo, ni Israelbii lɛ naaa mana dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibaanii ji nii ni amɛye nakai afi lɛ nɔ. Yoshua kɛ Nuu ni hiɛ tayaa kakla lɛ

english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Be ni Yoshua ebɛŋkɛ Yeriko lɛ, gbi ko trukaa eyaawo ehiɛ nɔ lɛ, naa nuu ko damɔ ehiɛ ni egbala eklante ehiɛ. Yoshua tsi bɛŋkɛ nuu lɛ, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Wɔgbɛfaŋ oyɔɔ aloo wɔhenyɛlɔi lɛ agbɛfaŋ?”

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ to he ekɛɛ, “Dabi; miba akɛ Yehowa ta lɛ nɔ tatsɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni eja lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni minuŋtsɔ kɛɔ etsulɔ?”

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Yehowa ta lɛ nɔ tatsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Jiemɔ otokota lɛ yɛ onane, ejaakɛ he ni odamɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni.” Ni Yoshua fee nakai.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ mli lɛ aŋã Yeriko maŋ lɛ agbo lɛ naa kpɛŋŋ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahewɔ: mɔ ko mɔ ko ejɛɛɛ mli ejeee kpo lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko hu eyaaa mli.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi kpawo ahiɛ bɛji kpawo ni akɛ ojwɛni akloŋto fee kɛnyiɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ. Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛbɔlea maŋ lɛ shii kpawo be mli ni osɔfoi lɛ miikpã bɛji lɛ.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Kɛji amɛkpã ojwɛni akloŋto bɛji lɛ, ni nyɛnu gbɛɛmɔ lɛ ni esɛɛ tsɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ, maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ abɔ oshe waa, ni maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ baagbee shi shwɛtɛɛ, koni Israel tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛbote maŋ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Yoshua, Nun bi lɛ, tsɛ osɔfoi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛwoa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ, ni nyɛhãa osɔfoi kpawo ahiɛa ojwɛni akloŋto bɛji kɛnyiɛa Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
translation_verse: Yoshua hã akɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ bɔle Yeriko maŋ lɛ shi kome, ni asafo lɛ ba amɛshitoohe lɛ mli, ni amɛbawɔ jɛi.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, asafo lɛ te shi mra hiɛ futɛfutɛ mli be ni je bɔ̃i tsɛremɔ, ni amɛbɔle maŋ lɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ shii kpawo. Nakai gbi lɛ kɛkɛ nɔ lɛ amɛbɔle maŋ lɛ shii kpawo.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Shibɔlemɔ nɔ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ be ni osɔfoi lɛ ekpã bɛji lɛ, Yoshua kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbɔa oshe! Shi Yehowa kɛ maŋ lɛ eke nyɛ tswaa.

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, akpãtã hiɛ ahã Yehowa, ja Rahab, yoo ajwamãŋ lɛ, kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ eŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ ewe lɛ; amɛ kɛkɛ yi abaa, ejaakɛ Rahab ji mɔ ni kɛ bɔfoi lɛ ni wɔtsu lɛ tee.

english_verse: The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ jwiɛtɛi fɛɛ kɛ shika fɛɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ akɔɔble loo dade fee lɛ, ajɔɔ nɔ ahã Yehowa, ni no hewɔ lɛ, aloo ni akɛba Yehowa nitoohe lɛ.”

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ bɔ oshe, ni akpã bɛji lɛ. Be ni asafoi lɛ nu bɛji lɛ agbɛɛmɔ lɛ, amɛbɔ oshe kpeteŋkple. Kɛkɛ ni Yeriko maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ gbee shi shwɛtɛɛ, ni Israelbii lɛ bote maŋ lɛ mli, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛŋɔ̃ maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Ni Yoshua kã amɛ kitã yɛ nakai be lɛ mli akɛ, “Mɔ ni aaate shi akɛ ebaasaa Yeriko maŋ nɛɛ ema lɛ, alomɔ lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. Ekɛ ekromɔbi wala baatse nitsumɔ lɛ shishitoo, ni ekɛ ebi sɛɛkpelɔ wala baatse maŋ lɛ agboi lɛ taramɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Yehowa bu Yoshua he, ni no hewɔ lɛ, egbɛi hehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ tɔ̃, ni amɛyayeee kɔkɔ ni abɔ amɛ yɛ musunii lɛ gbɛfaŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ Akan, ni ji Zabdi bi Karmi bi lɛ, ni jɛ Zera we yɛ Yuda akutso lɛŋ lɛ, kɔlɔ musunii lɛ eko. Enɛ hã Yehowa mli fu Israelbii lɛ naakpa.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ gbala amɛhe atadei, ni amɛloo mlu amɛwo amɛyiteiaŋ, ni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛi bumɔ shi yɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ;

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: ni Yoshua kɛɛ akɛ, “Ao! Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, mɛni hewɔ ni okɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ fo Yordan lɛ kɛba? Koni okɛ wɔ abawo Amorbii lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkpãtã wɔhiɛ? Wɔle nɛkɛ kulɛ wɔkpɛ̃lɛ ni wɔhi Yordan lɛ sɛɛ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Ao! Nuŋtsɔ, te makɛɛ tɛŋŋ be ni Israel enaa sɛɛsɛɛ yɛ ehenyɛlɔi ahiɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii fɛɛ baanu he, ni amɛaaba amɛbabɔle wɔ kpula, ni amɛbaakpãtã wɔhiɛ butuu. No hewɔ lɛ, te ofeɔ tɛŋŋ yɛ ogbɛi kpeteŋkple lɛ hewɔ hu?”

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Tee shi; mɛni hewɔ ni okɛ ohiɛ ebu shi?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Naa, Israel etɔ̃ minɔ; amɛgbo toi, ni kɔkɔ ni mibɔ amɛ lɛ, amɛyayeee nɔ, ni amɛkɔlɔ musunii lɛ eko tete amɛkɛfutu amɛnibii amli; ni asaŋ amɛju, ni amɛmale hu.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi ahiɛ amɛdamɔ, amɛtsɔ̃ amɛsɛɛ amɛhã amɛhenyɛlɔi, ejaakɛ amɛloo musu. Mikɛ nyɛ ehiŋ shi dɔŋŋ ja nyɛjie musunii lɛ yɛ nyɛnibii amli nyɛshwie.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Tee shi; tsuumɔ maŋbii lɛ ahe. Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛtsua nyɛhe nyɛkɛfea nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ nyɛtoa wɔ’, ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Israelbii, nyɛkɔlɔ musu nibii lɛ eko, no hewɔ lɛ, nyɛnyɛŋ nyɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ nyɛdamɔ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni nyɛaajie musunii lɛ nyɛshwie.’

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, wɔ leebi lɛ, nyɛbaato kɛho yɛ akutsei lɛ anaa. Akutso ni Yehowa baatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaato kɛho yɛ emli wekui lɛ anaa; ni weku ni Yehowa baatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ ebaato kɛho yɛ emli shĩaishĩai lɛ anaa; ni shĩa ni Yehowa baatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli bii lɛ baato kɛho ekome kome.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Mɔ ni Yehowa baamɔ lɛ akɛ lɛ edɛŋ musu nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, abaashã lɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ, ejaakɛ etɔ̃ Yehowa kitã nɔ, ni asaŋ efee hiɛgbejianii yɛ Israel.”

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yoshua te shi leebi maŋkpa ni ehã Israelbii lɛ to kɛbaho yɛ akutseiakutsei anaa, ni amɔ Yuda akutso lɛ.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua hã Yuda akutso lɛ to kɛbaho, ni amɔ Zerabii aweku lɛ. Ehã Zerabii lɛ to kɛbaho yɛ shĩaishĩai anaa, ni amɔ Zabdi shĩa lɛ.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Be ni ehã Zabdi hii lɛ to kɛbaho ekomekome lɛ, amɔ Karmin bi Akan ni ji Zabdi nabi lɛ.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛɛ Akan akɛ, “Mibi, wo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hiɛ nyam, ni asaŋ jiemɔ eyi. Jajemɔ otsɔ̃ɔ mi nɔ ni ofee; kaashiu mi sane nɔ.”

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Akan to he ehã Yoshua akɛ, “Lɛɛlɛŋ, mifee esha mishi Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Bɔfoi lɛ famɔ nibii lɛ, ni amɛkɛbahã Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ, ni akɛ nibii lɛ shwie Yehowa hiɛ.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ mɔ Akan, Zeranyo lɛ, ni akɛ jwiɛtɛi lɛ kɛ mama lɛ kɛ shika antɛle lɛ kɛ ebihii kɛ ebiyei kɛ agbɛnɛ etoi kɛ etsinai kɛ etejii kɛ ebuu lɛ, no ji nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ, fɛɛ fata ehe ni akpala amɛ kɛtee Akor Jɔɔ lɛŋ.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Be ni ayashɛ jɛi lɛ Yoshua kɛɛ Akan akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni ogba wɔnaa nɛkɛ? Yehowa hu baahao bo ŋmɛnɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Israel muu lɛ fɛɛ tswia Akan tɛ, ni ama enaa la ni ashã lɛ.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Asafo lɛ loo tɛ amɛkɛbua Akan nɔ, ni tɛi lɛ tsɔ̃ gɔŋ ni ma shi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa mlifu ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ fo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Amanehulu Jɔɔ.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: Kɛfee nakai lɛ amɛbaatiu wɔ, kɛyaashi wɔɔgbala amɛ kɛshi maŋ lɛ; ni nɔ ni amɛbaakɛɛ ji akɛ, ‘Naa, wɔnaa foi amɛjoɔ ekoŋŋ tamɔ nyɛsɛɛ lɛ.’ Wɔ lɛ, wɔbaakwa wɔjo amɛnaa foi;

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: shi nyɛ lɛ, nyɛbaafamɔ kpo yɛ he ni nyɛwo ka lɛ yɛ lɛ koni nyɛbaŋɔ Ai maŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, baahã nyɛye maŋ lɛ nɔ kunim.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛnine shɛ maŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛmaa maŋ lɛ naa la, koni nyɛfea lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa efã lɛ. Naa, kitã miwoɔ nyɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Yoshua te shi leebi maŋkpa, ni ebua maŋbii lɛ anaa. Kɛkɛ ni lɛ kɛ Israel maŋ onukpai lɛ yi maŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛmiiya Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Tabilɔi fɛɛ ni kɛ Yoshua nyiɛ lɛ fã, ni amɛtee aahu kɛyashi amɛbɛŋkɛ Ai maŋ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni amɛwa yɛ Ai kooyigbɛ he ko; ni jɔɔ kã amɛ kɛ Ai teŋ.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Israel tabilɔi lɛ gba ta lɛ amɛhã lɛ nɛ: amɛtabilɔi lɛ tsiimɔ jwere Ai maŋ lɛ kooyigbɛ, ni fãbii ni ji sɛɛbii lɛ ewo ka yɛ Ai anaigbɛ. Yoshua kpeleke shi kɛtee jɔɔ lɛŋ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛŋ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Okɛ akplɔ ni ohiɛ lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ Ai gbɛ, ejaakɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ ehã bo.” Yoshua kɛ akplɔ ni ehiɛ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ Ai gbɛ.

english_verse: When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked. The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting.
translation_verse: Be ni Yoshua kɛ Israel asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ na akɛ kawolɔi lɛ eŋɔ̃ maŋ lɛ, ni asaŋ amɛma enaa la lɛ, amɛfo amɛhe kɛtua Ai hii lɛ, ni amɛgbe amɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ egbe Aibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋã lɛ nɔ he ni Aibii lɛ nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛtee lɛ, amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba Ai maŋ lɛ mli; ni amɛbagbe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hu ni yɔɔ jɛi.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. translation_verse: Esɛŋ Ai maŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ tso ko nɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi hulu lɛ shinyɔɔ be mli dani Yoshua fã, ni ayajie maŋtsɛ lɛ gbonyo lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ashɛ lɛ afɔ̃ maŋ lɛ agbo lɛ naa. Ato tɛ ashwie Ai maŋtsɛ lɛ gbonyo lɛ nɔ, ni etsɔ̃ gɔŋ ni ma shi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Akane Mla Wolo lɛ yɛ Ebal Gɔŋ lɛ he

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Shi Gibeonbii lɛ, be ni amɛnu nɔ ni Yoshua efee Yeriko kɛ Ai lɛ,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: amɛ lɛ amɛto ŋaa. Amɛtao gbɛ nɔ niyenii, ni amɛloo kpekpei memeji kɛ wain wolo tɔi memeji ni asaŋ egbalagbalai ni etserɛtserɛi, ni atratrai amɛkɛtere tejii.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Amɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ, amɛwowoo tokotai memeji ni atsaratsrai kɛ atadei memeji hu. Gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni amɛhiɛ lɛ tete egbi, ni asaŋ efufuui.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Ni amɛyi mli amɛtee Yoshua ŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ashitoohe lɛ yɛ Gilgal, ni amɛyakɛɛ lɛ kɛ Israelhii lɛ akɛ, “Maŋsɛɛ shɔŋŋ he ko wɔjɛ wɔbaa nɛɛ; ni wɔba koni nyɛ kɛ wɔ akpãŋ ni wɔfee ekome.”

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Amɛ jie Yoshua naa akɛ, “Maŋsɛɛ shɔŋŋ otsuji jɛ baa nɛɛ yɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hewɔ. Wɔnu ehe sane, ni ji nibii fɛɛ ni efee yɛ Ijipt lɛ,

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: kɛ nɔ ni efee Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi enyɔ ni yɔɔ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ, ni ji Heshbon maŋtsɛ Sihon kɛ Bashan maŋtsɛ Og, ni hi Ashtarot lɛ.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã wɔmaŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii fɛɛ wo wɔ gbɛ amɛkɛɛ, ‘Nyɛtaoa gbɛ nɔ niyenii, ni nyɛyaa koni nyɛkɛ amɛ ayakpea yɛ gbɛteŋ, ni nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ, wɔyɛ nyɛshishi; no hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkɛ wɔ akpãŋa.’

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Naa bɔ ni aboloo ni wɔhiɛ lɛ efee. Afã aboloo lɛ oheo nɔŋŋ ni wɔkɛyi gbɛ koni wɔbaye yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ; shi naa no; egbi ni asaŋ efu tete.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ wain wolo tɔi nɛɛ hu ehei ni, be ni wɔwowoo amɛmli wain lɛ; shi naa amɛ ni amɛgbalagbalaa; ni wɔtadei kɛ tokotai lɛ hu etserɛtserɛi yɛ gbɛ ni wɔnyiɛ ni jɛkɛ tsɔ̃ lɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ ye Gibeonbii lɛ aniyenii lɛ eko be mli ni amɛbiii Yehowa koni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nɔ ni sa akɛ amɛfee.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Yoshua here Gibeonbii nɛɛ atuu, ni ekɛ amɛ kpãŋ hu akɛ Israel efeŋ amɛ, Gibeonbii lɛ, efɔŋ ko. Israelbii lɛ anukpai lɛ kã Gibeonbii lɛ abɔfoi lɛ kitã akɛ amɛaaye kpãŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ fã nyiɛmɔ, ni gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛyanina amɛmaji lɛ ni ji Gibeon kɛ Kefira kɛ Beerot kɛ Kiriat Yearim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Shi Israelbii lɛ pleneee amɛ ejaakɛ amɛmaŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ekã amɛ kitã. No hewɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ wie huhuuhu amɛshi maŋ onukpai lɛ.

english_verse: but the leaders reminded them, “We promised these people in the name of the Lord God of Israel that we would let them live, so we must not harm them. If we break our promise, God will punish us. We'll let them live, but we'll make them cut wood and carry water for our people.”
translation_verse: Maŋ onukpai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkɛɛ asafo lɛ akɛ, akagbe amɛ, shi moŋ ahã amɛya lai kɛ faaŋ amɛhã Israel asafo lɛ fɛɛ.” Ŋãa ni lumɛi lɛ wo nɛ.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua hã atsɛ Gibeonbii lɛ kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni nyɛlaka wɔ akɛ, ‘Wɔ kɛ nyɛteŋ jɛkɛ naakpa lɛ?’ Asomoaŋ wɔmasɛi nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nyɛyɔɔ?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nyɛlomɔ nyɛhe, ni kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛteŋ nyɔji baajɛ aya lai kɛ faaŋ kɛba miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ.”

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Gibeonbii lɛ to he amɛhã Yoshua akɛ, “Agba otsuji bɔ ni Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, wo etsulɔ Mose shi akɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ baahã nyɛ, ni ebaakpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ ehã nyɛ. Sane nɛɛ hã wɔshe gbeyei; ni no hã wɔye nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɛɛ wɔyɛ odɛ̃ŋ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ja yɛ ohiɛ akɛ ofee wɔ lɛ feemɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Yoshua fee ni ekɛjie Gibeonbii lɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkagbe amɛ.

english_verse: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ Yoshua fee Gibeonbii nɛɛ lailɛlɔi kɛ faaŋyalɔi ehã Israelbii lɛ. Amɛ nɔŋŋ amɛyaa lai kɛ faaŋ kɛbaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ naa kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Yerusalɛm maŋtsɛ Adonizedek nu akɛ Yoshua eye Ai maŋ lɛ nɔ kunim, ni ekpãtã hiɛ butubutu, ni asaŋ efee Ai kɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ bɔ ni efee Yeriko kɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ. Agbɛnɛ enu hu akɛ Gibeonbii lɛ etee amɛkɛ Israelbii lɛ eyakpãŋ, ni amɛ kɛ amɛ efee ekome, ni amɛfutu amɛ tete amɛ kɛ amɛ yɛ. Be ni Adonizedek nu saji nɛɛ lɛ

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: amɛshe gbeyei naakpa. Eshishi ji akɛ maŋ wulu ji Gibeon; etamɔ maŋtsɛmaji lɛ eko nɔŋŋ, ni eda po fe Ai, asaŋ emli hii lɛ kãkãlɔi sɔŋŋ ni.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yerusalɛm maŋtsɛ Adonizedek tsu kɛtee Hebron maŋtsɛ Hoham kɛ Yarmut maŋtsɛ Piram kɛ Lakish maŋtsɛ Yafia kɛ Eglon maŋtsɛ Debir ŋɔɔ, ni ayakɛɛ amɛ akɛ,

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: “Nyɛbaa nyɛbafataa mihe koni wɔyatua Gibeon shikpɔŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ eyafee ekome.”

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Gibeon hii lɛ tsu mɛi Yoshua ŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ eshitoohe lɛ yɛ Gilgal, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ ebua amɛhe naa ewo wɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, ba mra koni obaye obua wɔ. Kaaŋmɛɛ wɔhe ohã amɛ, shi otsuji ji wɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yoshua kɛ Israel tabilɔi kãkãlɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛta lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Gilgal kɛtee.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Kaashe Amorbii lɛ gbeyei ejaakɛ mijɔɔ amɛnɔ momo mihã bo; amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛŋ ohiɛ edamɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Yoshua kɛ etabilɔi lɛ nyiɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ kɛjɛ Gilgal, ni amɛbahɛ̃ŋ Amorbii lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã Amorbii lɛ jijaa yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ, ni Israelbii lɛ gbe amɛ babaoo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Gibeon. Asaŋ amɛnyiɛ Amorbii lɛ asɛɛ kɛtsɔ̃ Bet Horon Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛgbe amɛ kɛyashi Azeka kɛ Makeda tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Be ni Amorbii lɛ joɔ Israelbii lɛ anaa foi kɛkpelekeɔ Bet Horon Gɔŋ lɛ, Yehowa hã nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi wuji jɛ ŋwɛi bashwie Amorbii lɛ anɔ aahu kɛyashi Azeka, ni amɛgboi. Mɛi abɔ ni tɛi nɛɛ gbe lɛ ayi fa kwraa fe mɛi ni gboi yɛ Israelbii lɛ aklante naa.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Hulu lɛ wa lɛɛlɛŋ, ni nyɔɔŋtsere lɛ hu wa kɛyashi Israelbii lɛ tɔ amɛhe owele amɛgbe naa yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ. Aŋma sane nɛɛ yɛ Yashar Wolo lɛ mli. Hulu wa edamɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛi aaafee gbi muu ni eyeee oyai ni eyanyɔ shi.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ henɔ bako pɛŋ dã, ni kɛjɛ no sɛɛ hu eko bako dɔŋŋ ni Yehowa ebo gbɔmɔ toi nɛkɛ, ejaakɛ gbi lɛ Yehowa wu Israel ta lɛ ehã lɛ.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Ta nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛba amɛshitoohe lɛŋ yɛ Gilgal. Yoshua mɔmɔ Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ jo foi yɛ ta lɛŋ, ni amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ tɛkplo ko ni yɔɔ Makeda lɛ mli.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Abatswa Yoshua adafi akɛ, “Ayana Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ ni amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ tɛkplo ni yɔɔ Makeda lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: No ni Yoshua fã akɛ, “Nyɛyakokloa tɛi kpeteŋkplei nyɛtsimɔa tɛkplo lɛ naa, ni nyɛshĩa hii yɛ jɛi koni amɛbu maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛ lɛ nyɛkadamɔa shi; nyɛtiua henyɛlɔi lɛ, ni nyɛjɛa amɛsɛɛgbɛ nyɛtswiaa amɛ nii. Nyɛkaŋmɛa amɛ gbɛ ni amɛyabote amɛmaji lɛ amli, ejaakɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ehã nyɛye amɛnɔ kunim momo.”

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ gbe amɛhenyɛlɔi Amorbii lɛ kɛyashi amɛyi tã; shi mɛi ni na gbɛ jo foi lɛ yabote maji ni atswa gbogbo kɛfofoo amɛhe lɛ amli.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii tabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ ku amɛsɛɛ shweshweeshwe kɛba Yoshua ŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ Makeda shitoohe lɛ. Mɔ ko mɔ ko etswaaa esɛŋ eshiii Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Yoshua fã ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛgbelea tɛkplo lɛ naa koni nyɛkɛ nakai maŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ abahãa mi.”

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ je kpo kɛba Yoshua ŋɔ̃ɔ lɛ, Yoshua tsɛ Israel hii lɛ fɛɛ kɛbakpe. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ tabilɔi ni kɛ lɛ tee ta lɛ anɔ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtsia nyɛbaa koni nyɛkɛ nyɛnaji abamãmɔa nɛkɛ maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ akuɛi anɔ.” Asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ ba, ni amɛkɛ amɛnaji bamãmɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ akuɛi anɔ.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Yoshua tee nɔ, ni ekɛɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei, ni nyɛtsuii hu akafãa; nyɛfea kakaaka kɛ ekãa fɛɛ, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Yehowa baafee nyɛhenyɛlɔi fɛɛ ni nyɛkɛbaawu lɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Yoshua tswia maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ nii, ni egbe amɛ; ni ekɛ amɛgbohii lɛ tsotsoro shi yɛ tsei enumɔ anɔ. Gbohii nɛɛ tsotsoro tsei lɛ anɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: be ni hulu yaanyɔ shi dani Yoshua hã ajie amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ, ni ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie tɛkplo lɛ ni amɛyatee yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛkɛ ni akoklo tɛi kpeteŋkplei akɛtsi tɛkplo lɛ naa; ni eyɛ nakai kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Yoshua shɔ̃ Amorbii ashikpɔji krokomɛi hu

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Yoshua yatua Makeda maŋ lɛ, ni egbe emaŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli bii fɛɛ; eshwɛɛɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ. Efee Makeda maŋtsɛ lɛ bɔ ni efee Yeriko maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ tse mli kɛjɛ Makeda kɛtee Libna, ni eyatua Libna maŋ lɛ hu.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Yehowa jɔɔ Libna kɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ehã Yoshua, ni eye amɛnɔ kunim. Yoshua kɛ klante kpãtã gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Libna lɛ ahiɛ. Efee Libna maŋtsɛ lɛ bɔ ni efee Yeriko maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ tse mli kɛjɛ Libna kɛtee Lakish, ni amɛyagba ta kɛbɔle maŋ lɛ he, ni amɛtua maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Yehowa jɔɔ Lakish nɔ ehã Yoshua, ni gbi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ eye nɔ kunim, ni Yoshua shɔ̃ maŋ lɛ. Ekɛ klante kpãtã maŋ lɛ kɛ emli gbɔmɛi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni efee Libna lɛ.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: No be lɛ mli ni Gezer maŋtsɛ Horam fã ta kɛba, ni ebawa Lakishbii lɛ. Shi Yoshua gbe lɛ kɛ emaŋbii lɛ kɛyashi eshwɛɛɛ Gezer tabilɔ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ tse mli kɛjɛ Lakish kɛtee Eglon, ni amɛyagba ta kɛbɔle maŋ lɛ he, ni amɛtua Eglonbii lɛ, ni amɛ kɛ amɛ wu.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Amɛshɔ̃ Hebron, ni amɛkɛ klante kpãtã Hebron maŋtsɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ akrowai lɛ hu fɛɛ amli bii ahiɛ butuu. Eshwɛɛɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ tamɔ bɔ ni efee yɛ Eglon lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ekpãtã maŋ lɛ kɛ emli gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Eye maŋ lɛ kɛ emli maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ akrowai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim. Amɛkɛ klante kpãtã maji lɛ kɛ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahiɛ butuu. Eshwɛɛɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ. Bɔ ni Yoshua fee Hebron kɛ Libna kɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ, nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ efee Debir kɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yoshua ye shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kunim: kɛjɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛmɔ wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, kɛbote jɔi lɛ amli aahu kɛyashwie ŋmeŋmei lɛ anɔ fɛɛ. Yoshua ye maji lɛ kɛ amɛmli maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim bɔ ni eshwɛɛɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko hiɛkãalɔ; ekpãtã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ hiɛ butuu tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ni ji Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ efã lɛ.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Yoshua ye maji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim kɛjɛ Kadesh Barnea kɛtee Gaza, kɛmɔ Goshen shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ aahu kɛtee Gibeon tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Be ni Hazor maŋtsɛ Yabin nu kunim ni Israelbii lɛ eye lɛ he lɛ, etsu maŋtsɛmɛi srɔtoi nɛɛ aŋɔɔ: Madom maŋtsɛ Yobab kɛ Shimron maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Ashkaf maŋtsɛ lɛ,

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ gɔji ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ Yordan jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ Galilea Kpaakpo lɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ, kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ashishi lɛ, kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ Dor ŋshɔnaa yɛ anaigbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Etsu Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ Yordan Faa lɛ bokãgbɛ kɛ anaigbɛ hu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Amorbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ kɛ Perizbii lɛ kɛ Yebusbii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ, kɛ Hivbii ni yɔɔ Hermon Gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ Mizpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu aŋɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ, “Kaashe amɛ gbeyei ejaakɛ wɔ be ni aaashɛ nɛkɛ be mli lɛ mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛnyɔnyɔi yɛ Israelbii ahiɛ. Nyɛfolɔa amɛkpɔŋɔi lɛ ananesɛɛ fãi lɛ, ni nyɛshãa amɛta shwiilii lɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yoshua kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ bahɛ̃ŋ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ yɛ Merom Faa lɛ toi.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yoshua ku esɛɛ kɛtee, ni eyaŋɔ̃ Hazor maŋ lɛ, ni egbe emli maŋtsɛ lɛ ejaakɛ nakai be mli lɛ Hazor ji jɛi kpokpai lɛ anɔ maŋtsɛyelihei lɛ fɛɛ kwa yitso.

english_verse: Joshua captured all the towns where the enemy kings had ruled. These towns were built on small hills, and Joshua did not set fire to any of these towns, except Hazor. The Israelites kept the animals and everything of value from these towns, but they killed everyone who lived in them, including their kings. That's what the Lord had told his servant Moses to do, that's what Moses had told Joshua to do, and that's exactly what Joshua did.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa wo etsulɔ Mose kitã lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ Mose hu wo Yoshua kitã lɛ, ni nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ Yoshua fee. Nii fɛɛ ni Yehowa wo he kitã lɛ, Yoshua shiii mli ekoeko ni etsuuu he nii. Shikpɔŋ ni Yoshua shɔ̃ lɛ

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Yoshua shɔ̃ shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni ji gɔji lɛ anɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, kɛ wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Goshen shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ ŋa nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ amɛjɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa ninenaa nitsumɔ nɛ, akɛ ehã maji lɛ amli bii lɛ kpliŋ amɛtsui, bɔ ni afee ni amɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ awu ta koni atsɔ̃ no nɔ amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ ni mɔbɔnalɛ bɛ mli, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa fã Mose lɛ.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Yoshua fã ta nakai be lɛ mli, ni etee eyabule Anakbii lɛ ashwiei lɛ shishi yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ hei ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ni ji Hebron kɛ Debir kɛ Anab kɛ Yuda gɔji lɛ anɔ fɛɛ kɛ Israel gɔji lɛ hu fɛɛ anɔ. Ekpãtã amɛ kɛ amɛmaji lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ butuu.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anakbii nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ kome nɛkɛ eshwɛɛɛ hiɛkãalɔ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gaza kɛ Gat kɛ Ashdod pɛ ji hei ni eshwɛ mɛi komɛi yɛ.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Yoshua ŋɔ̃ shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ Mose eto lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ; ni Yoshua ja shikpɔŋ lɛ ehã Israel akutsei lɛ akɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛhi nɔ. Agbɛnɛ taitai lɛ asɛɛ fo, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔ.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ ye maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ anɔ kunim, ni amɛŋɔ̃ amɛshikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli kɛtee kooyigbɛ aahu kɛyanina Hermon Gɔŋ lɛ. Maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ji

english_verse: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
translation_verse: Sihon, Amorbii amaŋtsɛ lɛ ni hi shi yɛ Heshbon lɛ. Emaŋtsɛyeli shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ eko ji kɛjɛ Aroer kɛmɔ Arnon Jɔɔ lɛ teŋ maŋ lɛ kɛyanina Yabok Faa lɛ ni ji Amonbii lɛ ahusu lɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɛɛ feɔ Gilead shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fã.

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Sihon nɛɛ nɔŋŋ shikpɔŋ ji Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ ni kã shi kɛjɛ Bet Yeshimot wuoyi kɛyashwie Pisga Gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ kome ko hu ji Bashan Maŋtsɛ Og. Hii oblaŋi gojogojoo ni shwɛ lɛ ateŋ eko ji lɛ. Eye emaŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ Ashtarot kɛ Edrei,

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: ni enɔyeli shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi ji Hermon Gɔŋ lɛ kɛ Salka kɛ Bashan muu fɛɛ kɛyashi Geshurbii lɛ kɛ Maakatbii lɛ ahusui lɛ anaa. Lɛ nɔŋŋ eshikpɔŋ ji Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ni kã shi kɛyashi Heshbon maŋtsɛ Sihon husu lɛ naa lɛ.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yehowa tsulɔ Mose kɛ Israelbii lɛ ye maŋtsɛmɛi enyɔ nɛɛ anɔ kunim, ni Mose kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ ashikpɔji lɛ hã Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manase akutso lɛ fã akɛ amɛnɔ. Maŋtsɛmɛi ni Yoshua ye amɛnɔ kunim

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Be ni Yoshua egbɔ lɛ Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ogbɔ, ni oye afii pii; shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lolo ni sa akɛ aŋɔ lɛ fa.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Manase akutso lɛ fã kome kɛ Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ ena amɛgbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ momo yɛ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa tsulɔ Mose kɛhã amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Amɛna kɛjɛ Aroer, ni ji Arnon Jɔɔ lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ, kɛ maŋ wulu ni kã jɔɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ, kɛ gɔŋ yiteŋ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ Medeba aahu kɛyashi Dibon.

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ amɛna Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon ni ye emaŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ Heshbon lɛ shishi maji lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi Amonbii lɛ ahusu lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Geshur and Maacah were part of this region, and so was the whole territory that King Og had ruled, that is, Gilead, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far east as Salecah. Og had lived in Ashtaroth part of each year, and he had lived in Edrei the rest of the year. Og had been one of the last of the Rephaim, but Moses had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land.
translation_verse: Akɛ Maŋtsɛ Og maŋtsɛyeli shikpɔji lɛ ni yɔɔ Bashan lɛ fɛɛ shi nɔ hã amɛ, ejaakɛ Og ji Ashtarot kɛ Edrei nɔ maŋtsɛ. Lɛ ji hii oblaŋi gojogojoo ni Mose ye amɛnɔ kunim ni eshwie amɛ lɛ ateŋ mɔ ni shwɛ.

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Shi Israelbii lɛ eshwieee Geshurbii lɛ kɛ Maakatbii lɛ; no hewɔ lɛ, Geshurbii lɛ kɛ Maakatbii lɛ futu Israelbii lɛ kɛhi shi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Levibii akutso lɛ kɛkɛ ni Mose hãaa amɛ amɛ kɔkrɔɔ amɛshikpɔŋ akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ. Afɔlei ni akɛ la shãa akɛhãa Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ji Levibii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ ni ahã amɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Mose ekɛɛ amɛ eto lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Rubenbii lɛ

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Mose hã Rubenbii akutso lɛ amɛgbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ ji Aroer, ni ji Arnon Jɔɔ lɛ, kɛ maŋ wulu lɛ ni kã jɔɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ, kɛ gɔŋ yiteŋ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Medeba lɛ,

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: Maji lɛ fɛɛ ni jwere gɔŋ yiteŋ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon ni ye maŋtsɛ yɛ Heshbon lɛ shikpɔji lɛ hu fɛɛ baje Rubenbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mose ji mɔ ni ye Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon nɛɛ nɔ kunim. Eye Midian lumɛi Evi kɛ Rekem kɛ Zur kɛ Hur kɛ Reba, ni ji Maŋtsɛ Sihon shishi lumɛi ni hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, fɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ gbe Bileam, Beor bi lɛ, ni ji klamɔ lɛ, hu amɛshi mɛi ni nyɔnyɔi yɛ ta mli lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yordan Faa lɛ tsɔ̃ Rubenbii lɛ ahusu, ni shikpɔŋ nɛɛ kɛ emli maji kɛ akrowai lɛ fɛɛ tsɔ̃ Rubenbii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Gadbii lɛ

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Mose hã Gadbii lɛ hu shikpɔŋ lɛ eko akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ehã amɛ kɛjɛ Yazer shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ maji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Gilead lɛ kɛmɔ Amonbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ fã kɛyashi Aroer ni kã Raba bokãgbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Ekɛ kɛjɛ Heshbon kɛyashi Ramat Mizpa kɛ Betonim hu hã amɛ nɔŋŋ. Agbɛnɛ hu ehã amɛ kɛjɛ Mahanaim kɛyashi Debir husu lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: kɛ Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli maji lɛ, ni ji Bet Haram kɛ Bet Nimra kɛ Sukot kɛ Zafon kɛ Heshbon maŋtsɛ Sihon shikpɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ kã shi kɛjɛ Yordan lɛ naa akɛ husu kɛtee Galilea Kpaakpo lɛ shishigbɛ he ni kpaakpo lɛ naa yatãa yɛ lɛ yɛ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ kɛ enɔ maji wuji kɛ akrowai fɛɛ ni Gadbii lɛ na yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Manasebii yɛ Bokãgbɛ lɛ

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Mose hã Manasebii akutso lɛ fã kome amɛgbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ koni etsɔ̃ akutso nɛɛ mli wekui lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: kɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ fã kɛ agbɛnɛ Ashtarot kɛ Edrei, ni ji Bashan maŋtsɛ Og maŋtsɛyelihe lɛ mli maji wuji lɛ. Akɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ hã Manase bi Makir shwiei lɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa akɛ Manasebii akutso lɛ fã lɛ gbɛfaŋ nɔ.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Belɛ nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Mose ja Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋã kplanaa ni yɔɔ Yordan lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ Yeriko bokãgbɛ lɛ, ehã Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Shi Levibii lɛ Mose hãaa amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko. Amɛ lɛ afɔlei ni akɛbahãa Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ji amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ ni amɛyɔɔ. Nakai ji bɔ ni Mose hã amɛnu shishi.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Yuda akutso lɛŋ bii lɛ ba Yoshua ŋɔɔ yɛ Gilgal; ni amɛteŋ mɔ kome ni ji Kaleb, Keniznyo, Yefune bi lɛ, kɛ sane bafɔ̃ Yoshua hiɛ akɛ, “Oookai wiemɔ ni Yehowa kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ Mose wie yɛ mihewɔ, kɛ bo hu ohewɔ, yɛ Kadesh Barnea lɛ.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛi lɛ ni kɛ mi tee lɛ bafã maŋ lɛ tsui; shi mi lɛ mibo Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toi kɛwula shi.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Mose kã kitã nakai gbi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Naa, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni onane eyanyiɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ bo kɛ obii agbɛfaŋnɔ kɛya naanɔ, ejaakɛ obo Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ toi kɛwula shi.’

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ okɛ nɛkɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahã mi, nɔ ni Yehowa wo shi yɛ he nakai gbi lɛ. Nakai bo diɛŋtsɛ onu kɛ otoi akɛ Anakbii lɛ ji mɛi ni yɔɔ jɛi yɛ maji wuji ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe akɛwaje amɛ lɛ mli. Eko lɛ Yehowa aaaye abua mi koni mashwie amɛ yɛ jɛi tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua jɔɔ Kaleb, ni ekɛ Hebron hã Kaleb, Yefune bi lɛ, akɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Hebron tsɔ̃ Kaleb, Yefune, Keniznyo lɛ bi lɛ, gbɛfaŋ nɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ, ejaakɛ ebo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toi kɛwula shi.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Amɛshikpɔŋ nɛɛ wuoyigbɛ husu lɛ jɛ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ naagbeehe lɛ, yɛ ble ni kã wuoyigbɛ lɛ naa,

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: ni etsɔ̃ Akrabim gɔji ateŋ gbɛ lɛ wuoyigbɛ kɛfo mli kɛtsɔ̃ Zin kɛyaje Kadesh Barnea wuoyigbɛ. Kɛkɛ ni husu lɛ sharã Hezron he kɛtee Adar, ni elɔgɔ kɛtee Karka.

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ biɛ lɛ husu lɛ tsɔ̃ Azmon kɛtee Ijipt faa lɛ naa, ni enaa yatã yɛ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ ji Yudabii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ wuoyigbɛ husu lɛ.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Bokãgbɛ husu lɛ ji Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ kɛlɛ kɛyashi he ni Yordan lɛ kɛ enaa woɔ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ mli yɛ lɛ. Kooyigbɛ husu lɛ jɛ ble ni yɔɔ he ni Yordan lɛ kɛ enaa woɔ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ mli yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ biɛ lɛ husu lɛ tee Bet Hogla; kɛkɛ ni etsɔ̃ Bet Araba Kooyigbɛ kɛtee Ruben bi Bohan tɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Husu lɛ wo ehe nɔ kɛjɛ Akor Jɔɔ lɛ mli kɛtee Debir, ni edɔ eyi kɛtsɔ̃ kooyigbɛ kɛtee Gilgal ni kwɛɔ Adumim gɔji ateŋ gbɛ lɛ ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ husu lɛ sharã Enshemesh nuhiŋmɛii lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ enaa yawo Rogel Nubu lɛ mli.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Husu lɛ tsa nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ̃ Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ mli, yɛ gɔŋ ni Yebusbii amaŋ ni ji Yerusalɛm lɛ mã nɔ lɛ wuoyigbɛ, ni ewo ehe nɔ kɛtee gɔŋ ni ye Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ yiteŋ anaigbɛ, yɛ he ni Refaim Jɔɔ lɛ naa yatãa yɛ, yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ husu lɛ kã shi kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ kɛtee Neftoa Nuhiŋmɛii lɛ ahe. Kɛjɛ jɛi lɛ etse mli kɛtsɔ̃ Efrom Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji lɛ ahe, ni edɔ eyi kɛtee Baala, ni ji Kiriat-Yearim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Elɔgɔ kɛjɛ Baala kɛtsɔ̃ anaigbɛ yɛ Edom gɔji ashikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtee Yearim Gɔŋ lɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Kesalon hu lɛ, kooyigbɛ. Ekpeleke shi kɛtee Bet Shemesh, ni esharã Timna he kɛho.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Kaleb fã kɛjɛ Hebron, ni etee ekɛ Debirbii lɛ yawu. Sa lɛ Debir gbɛi ji Kiriat Sefer.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Yoshua hã Kaleb, Yefune bi lɛ, egbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ yɛ Yudabii lɛ ateŋ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa efã lɛ, Yoshua lɛ. Maŋ ni eha Kaleb lɛ ji Hebron, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Kiriat Arba hu lɛ. Anak nɛɛ, etsɛ gbɛi akɛwo Kiriat Arba nɛɛ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Kaleb shwie Anak shwiei etɛ̃ lɛ, ni ji Sheshai kɛ Ahiman kɛ Talmai, kɛje Hebron.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Kaleb wo shi ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɔ ni aaanyɛ ayatua Kiriat Sefer, ni eshɔ̃ maŋ lɛ mikɛ mibiyoo Aksa baahã lɛ gbãlã.”

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Be ni Aksa tee ewu Otniel ŋɔɔ lɛ, Otniel wo Aksa yiŋ akɛ ebi etsɛ Kaleb koni efo shikpɔŋ ko ehã lɛ. Be ni Aksa shɛ etsɛ ŋɔɔ, ni ejɛ teji ni eta nɔ lɛ nɔ eyi shi lɛ, Kaleb bi lɛ akɛ, “Aksa, mɛni he hiaa bo?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Aksa jie naa akɛ, “Oha mi shikpɔŋ yɛ wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ lɛ nɔ; ha mi nubui hu ofata he akɛ gbɛwoo nii.” Kɛkɛ ni Kaleb ha Aksa nubui ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ kɛ nubui ni yɔɔ jɔɔ mli hu. Yudabii lɛ amaji wuji lɛ

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Yudabii akutso lɛ mli wekui lɛ maji ni ahã amɛ lɛ agbɛii baa nɛɛ.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: agbɛnɛ kɛ Lebaot kɛ Shilhim kɛ Ain kɛ Rimon. Maji lɛ fɛɛ fee nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ nɛɛhu kɛ amɛhe akrowai hu.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: kɛ Shaaraim kɛ Aditaim kɛ Gedera kɛ Gederotaim. Enɛɛmɛi feɔ maji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: kɛ Gederot kɛ Bet-Dagon kɛ Naama kɛ Makeda: maji nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages: Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ashdod kɛ ehe maji kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ, kɛ Gaza hu kɛ ehe maji kɛ ehe akrowai kɛyashi Ijipt faa lɛ naa kɛ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ hu naa lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋa nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Shi Yudabii lɛ eyanyɛɛɛ Yebusbii, ni ji mɛi ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ amɛshwie. No hewɔ lɛ, Yebusbii lɛ futu Yudabii lɛ kɛhi Yerusalɛm kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ ni ahã Efraimbii lɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa lɛ ji enɛ: Yɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ amɛhusu ji kɛjɛ Atarot-Adar kɛyashi Bet-Horon yiteŋgbɛ he ko.

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: Ahã amɛ maji hu kɛ amɛhe akrowai hu afata he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Manasebii lɛ akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Shi Efraimbii lɛ eshwieee Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ Gezer lɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, Kanaanbii nɛɛ kɛ Efraimbii lɛ futu kɛhi shi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ; ni Kanaanbii lɛ sɔ̃mɔ Efraimbii lɛ.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Manasebii lɛ ahusu lɛ, ekã shi kɛjɛ Asher kɛtee Mikmetat ni yɔɔ Shekem bokãgbɛ lɛ. Husu lɛ tsa nɔ kɛtee wuoyigbɛ kɛyanina En-Tapuabii lɛ, ni ekɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ eshi nɔ.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ni Tapua yɔɔ lɛ Manasebii lɛ anɔ ni; shi Tapua maŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ akɛhã Efraimbii lɛ.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Akɛ Isakarbii lɛ kɛ Asherbii lɛ ashikpɔji lɛ anɔ maji komɛi hã Manasebii lɛ. Maji nɛɛ ji Bet-Sham kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ kɛ Ibleam kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ kɛ Dorbii akrowai lɛ kɛ En-Dorbii kɛ amɛ akrowai lɛ kɛ Taanak kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ kɛ Megidobii kɛ amɛ akrowai lɛ .

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Shi Manasebii lɛ eyanyɛɛɛ Kanaanbii ni ji mɛi ni yɔɔ maji nɛɛ amli momo sa lɛ amɛshwie; ni no hewɔ lɛ, Kanaanbii lɛ tee nɔ, ni amɛhi maji nɛɛ amli.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Shi be ni Israelbii lɛ ahe bawa tete lɛ, amɛshwieee Kanaanbii lɛ; shi moŋ Israelbii lɛ ye amɛ nyɔŋ. Efraimbii lɛ kɛ Anaigbɛ Manasebii lɛ bi shikpɔŋ lɛ eko amɛfata he

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Yosef shwiei lɛ bi Yoshua akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni ofo shikpɔŋ kome pɛ kɛkɛ ohã wɔ akɛ wɔgbɛfaŋnɔ be mli ni wɔyi fa babaoo, ni Yehowa ehã wɔshwere lɛ?”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Yoshua to he akɛ, “Kɛji nyɛyi fa tsɔ̃, ni Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ edaaa hãaa nyɛ lɛ, no lɛ nyɛyaa Perizbii lɛ kɛ Refaimbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni nyɛyagbaa koo ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ eko, ni nyɛtoa maŋ yɛ jɛi nyɛhia mli.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Yosef shwiei lɛ jie naa akɛ, “gɔji lɛ anɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ edaaa hãaa wɔ moŋ nɛ, shi Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ dade tayaa shwiilii; mɛi ni yɔɔ Bet-Shean kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ mɛi hu ni yɔɔ Yezreel Jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu fɛɛ yɛ eko.”

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Yoshua kɛɛ Yosef shwiei lɛ, ni ji Efraimbii kɛ Manasebii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyi fa babaoo, ni nyɛyɛ hewalɛ naakpa hu; no hewɔ lɛ, nyɛbaana fe shikpɔŋ kome lɛ,

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ nyɛnɔ afata he. Nyɛ lɛ, nyɛgbaa koo ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛyashi he ni nyɛaanyɛ nyɛkɛ ehusu lɛ ayashi, koni nyɛkɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ Kanaanbii lɛ yɛ dade tayaa shwiilii, ni amɛhe wa moŋ nɛ, shi amɛnyɛŋ nyɛhiɛ amɛdamɔ.”

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Israel asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ naa bakpe shi yɛ Shilo, ni amɛshi Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ yɛ jɛi. Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ shikpɔŋ ni Israelbii lɛ eŋɔ̃ lɛ kã shi yɛ amɛhiɛ,

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Dani hii ni afamɔ koni amɛyaŋma shikpɔŋ lɛ he sane kɛba lɛ yi mli amɛtee lɛ, Yoshua kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa koni nyɛyakpaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nyɛŋma ehe sane, ni nyɛkɛku nyɛsɛɛ kɛba miŋɔ̃ɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ mafɔ̃ oshiki mabi Yehowa nii yɛ nyɛhewɔ yɛ Shilo nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii lɛ yi mli amɛtee, ni amɛyakpa shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni amɛŋma amɛwo wolo mli bɔ ni amɛjara shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kpawo lɛ amɛhã yɛ maji ni jwere shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba Yoshua ŋɔɔ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ashitoohe lɛ yɛ Shilo,

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: ni Yoshua fɔ̃ oshiki ni ekɛja shikpɔŋ lɛ eha amɛ, akutso fɛɛ akutso na egbɛfaŋnɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Benyaminbii lɛ

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ oshiki ni afɔ̃ lɛ gbee Benyaminbii akutso lɛ mli wekui lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ lɛ kã Yudabii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ Yosefbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Benyaminbii nɛɛ akooyigbɛ husu lɛ jɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa ni ekwɔ kɛtsɔ̃ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛtee anaigbɛ kɛyamɔ Bet-Aven shiaŋa lɛ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Husu lɛ lɔgɔ ehe yɛ gɔŋ ni ye wuoyigbɛ ni ekwɛɔ Bet-Horon hiɛ lɛ nɔ, ni enaa yatã yɛ Kiriat-Baal, ni ji Kiriat-Yearim, Yudabii amaŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji Benyaminbii lɛ anaigbɛ husu lɛ.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Amɛwuoyigbɛ husu lɛ jɛ Kiriat-Yearim kpokpai anɔ, ni etee anaigbɛ kɛyashi Neftoa Nuhiŋmɛii lɛ ahe.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Husu lɛ kpeleke shi kɛtee gɔŋ lɛ ni kwɛɔ Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi, yɛ ekooyigbɛ he ni Refaim Jɔɔ lɛ naa yatãa yɛ lɛ. Husu lɛ nyɔ Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ mli agbɛnɛ, ni etsɔ̃ Yebusbii lɛ awuoyigbɛ kɛtee En-Rogel Nubu lɛ naa.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Egba kɛyi kooyigbɛ kɛjɛ biɛ kɛyamɔ En-Shemesh; ni etse mli kɛtee Gelilot ni yɔɔ Adumim Gɔŋ kɛ Gɔŋ teŋ gbɛ lɛ ŋlɛnɔ lɛ; kɛkɛ ni ekpeleke shi kɛtee Ruben bi Bohan Tɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ jɛi lɛ husu lɛ sharã Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ kooyigbɛ kɛho kɛbote jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Husu lɛ tse mli, ni eyaje Bet-Hogla masɛi yɛ ekooyigbɛ, ni enaa yatã yɛ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ kooyigbɛ ble lɛ mli he ni Yordan lɛ naa yatãa yɛ, yɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ. Bɔ ni Benyaminbii lɛ awuoyigbɛ husu lɛ kã shi hã lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Belɛ Yordan Faa lɛ ji amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ husu yɛ bokãgbɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Benyaminbii lɛ akɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa lɛ, nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni ehe husui lɛ kamɔ shi hã.

english_verse: One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
translation_verse: Ekomɛi hu ji Kefar-Amonai kɛ Ofni kɛ Geba ni hiɛ maji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ kɛ amɛhe akrowai lɛ,

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Oshiki ni ji enyɔ ni afɔ̃ lɛ gbee Simeonbii akutso lɛ wekui lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Yudabii lɛ mli.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: kɛ Bet-Lebaot kɛ Sharuhem; fɛɛ fee maji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ jɛi lɛ husu lɛ tse mli kɛtsɔ̃ bokãgbɛ kɛyanina Gat-Hefer kɛ Et-Kazin. Etse mli ekoŋŋ kɛtee Rimon, kɛkɛ ni edɔ eyi kɛtee Neah.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Maji lɛ ekomɛi hu ji Ain kɛ Rimon kɛ Eter kɛ Ashan, maji ejwɛ kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: Akrowai fɛɛ ni jwere maji nɛɛ ahe kɛtee Baalat-Beer, ni ji Rama ni yɔɔ wuoyigbɛ ŋã lɛ nɔ lɛ, shi nɔ. Enɛ ji Simeonbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa lɛ.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Simeonbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ ni ahã amɛ nɛɛ lɛ, afo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Yudabii lɛ he, ejaakɛ Yudabii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ fa tsɔ̃ hã amɛ, ni no hewɔ ni akɛ eko hã Simeonbii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Zebulonbii lɛ

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Husu lɛ dɔ ehe yɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ kɛtee Hanaton, ni etsa nɔ kɛtee ni enaa yatã yɛ Ifta-El Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Zebulonbii nɛɛ nɔ maji lɛ ekomɛi ji Katat kɛ Nahalal kɛ Shimron kɛ Idala kɛ Betlehem. Maji lɛ fɛɛ fee nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ maji kɛ akrowai nɛɛ yɛ Zebulonbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ yɛ amɛwekui anaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Isakarbii lɛ

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ maji nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe akrowai lɛ yɛ Isakarbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Asherbii lɛ

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni husu lɛ dɔ eyi eŋmɛ bokãgbɛ kɛtee Bet-Dagon. Etse mli yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛtee Zebulon kɛ Ifta-El Jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛtee Bet-Emek kɛ Neiel. Etsa nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛtee kooyigbɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛyanina Kabul,

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: kɛ Ekron kɛ Rehob kɛ Hamon kɛ Kana kɛyashi Sidon.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ maji kɛ amɛhe akrowai nɛɛ ji Asherbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã amɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Naftalibii lɛ

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
