translation_verse: Isakarbii lɛ ahusu lɛ tsɔ̃ Tabor kɛ Shahazuma kɛ Bet-Shemesh hu, ni enaa yatã yɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa. Amɛna maji nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa kɛ amɛhe akrowai.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ maji nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe akrowai lɛ ji Naftalibii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ ni ahã amɛ yɛ amɛwekui lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã Danbii lɛ

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Osɔfo Eleazar kɛ Nun bi Yoshua kɛ Israel akutsei lɛ amli onukpai lɛ damɔ oshiki ni amɛfɔ̃, yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa, yɛ Shilo, lɛ nɔ kɛja shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛhã Israelbii lɛ awekui lɛ.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Ahala maji nɛɛ ato ahã Israelbii fɛɛ kɛ gbɔi hu ni ebato amɛ lɛ akɛ abobaa maji koni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaagbe mɔ ko ni jeee gbɛ eje lɛ, ajo foi kɛya eko mli eyaba abo, koni mɔ ni taoɔ lá he owele atɔ lɛ nine akashɛ mɔ ni egbe gbɔmɔ lɛ nɔ; asaŋ koni gbɔmɔgbelɔ nɛɛ ahi abobaahe lɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni aaatsɛ lɛ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ ni aaabote esane lɛ mli.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Yoshua akɛ,

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, nyɛhalaa maji ni nyɛfea amɛ abobaa maji nyɛtoa, tamɔ bɔ ni mitsɔ̃ Mose nɔ mikɛ nyɛ wie lɛ,

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni aaajo foi kɛaatee nɛkɛ maji nɛɛ eko mli lɛ, eyajaje esane lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ nakai maŋ lɛŋ onukpai lɛ yɛ maŋ agbo lɛ naa kojomɔhe lɛ. Maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ amɔ emli kɛba maŋ lɛ mli, ni ahã lɛ shihilɛhe koni ekɛ amɛ ahi shi.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Kɛji mɛi ni taoɔ owele atɔ lɛ tiu gbɔmɔgbelɔ lɛ kɛba maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, onukpai lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔgbelɔ ni ebaba abo lɛ akahã oweletɔlɔ lɛ ejaakɛ jeee gbɛ eje egbe enaanyo lɛ, ni asaŋ enyɛɛɛ lɛ etooo.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Abobalɔ lɛ ahi shi yɛ nakai abobaa maŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi beyinɔ ni aaatsɛ lɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ, ni aaaye esane lɛ, asaŋ kɛyashi beyinɔ hu ni osɔfonukpa ni yɔɔ be mli ni ebaba abo lɛ aaagbo. No sɛɛ dani gbɔmɔgbelɔ lɛ aaanyɛ aku esɛɛ aya ewe kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ he ni ejo foi kɛjɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ hala maji ni agbɛii baa nɛɛ to akɛ abobaa maji: Kadesh yɛ Galilea yɛ Naftali gɔji lɛ anɔ, kɛ Shekem yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ, kɛ Kiriat-Arba, ni ji Hebron, ni yɔɔ Yuda gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yɛ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ amɛkɔ Bezer ni kã Yeriko bokãgbɛ shiaŋa trɛnɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ Rubenbii lɛ akutso lɛ gbɛfaŋ nɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɔ Ramot ni yɔɔ Gilead lɛ yɛ Gadbii anɔ mli; amɛkɔ Golan ni yɔɔ Bashan yɛ Manasebii anɔ mli.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: Ni Levibii lɛ kɛɛ amɛ yɛ Shilo yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ, “Yehowa tsɔ̃ Mose nɔ, ni efã akɛ ahã wɔ maji kɛ amɛhe shikpɔji ni wɔkooloi aaaye nii yɛ nɔ koni wɔhi amɛmli.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kɔlɔ maji kɛ amɛhe shikpɔji yɛ shikpɔji ni ajara ahã akutsei lɛ akɛ amɛnɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛkɛhã Levibii lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa efã lɛ.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Oshiki ni afɔ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ gbee Levibii lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni ji Kohat shwiei lɛ awekui lɛ anɔ. Osɔfo Aaron diɛŋtsɛ shwiei lɛ ahã amɛ maji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ yɛ Yudabii lɛ kɛ Simeonbii lɛ kɛ Benyaminbii lɛ agbɛfaŋ shikpɔji lɛ amli.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ maji nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe shikpɔji lɛ hã Levibii lɛ yɛ oshiki ni afɔ̃ lɛ naa tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa etsɔ̃ Mose nɔ efã akɛ afee lɛ.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Maji fɛɛ ni Osɔfo Aaron shwiei ni ji osɔfoi lɛ na lɛ fee nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ kɛ amɛhe shikpɔji.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maji fɛɛ ni Gershonbii lɛ awekui srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ na fee nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ kɛ amɛhe shikpɔji.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ maji nɛɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehe shikpɔŋ ni bɔle lɛ kɛkpe. Israelbii lɛ ŋɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekã he kitã akɛ akɛbaahã Israelbii lɛ atsɛmɛi lɛ hã Israelbii lɛ, ni be ni amɛshɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ amɛhi nɔ kwraa.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã amɛna hejɔlɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he tamɔ bɔ ni ewo amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kwraa nyɛɛɛ amɛhiɛ adamɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa hã amɛye amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Nibii juji fɛɛ ni Yehowa wo Israel we lɛ shi yɛ he lɛ, amɛmli ekome folo nɛkɛ eyafeee yaka; fɛɛ kwa ba mli.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yoshua tsɛ Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ akutso lɛ fã kome lɛ kɛbakpe,

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Nyɛshiko nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ gbii abɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ; ni nyɛkwɛ ni nyɛye Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, wiemɔ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ehã nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ ahe ejɔ amɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ewo amɛ shi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ ni nyɛyaa nyɛshikpɔŋ ni Yehowa tsulɔ Mose kɛhã nyɛ momo, yɛ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ, akɛ nyɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ nyɛkwɛa nyɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ahia koni nyɛye kitãi kɛ mlai lɛ ni Yehowa tsulɔ Mose wo nyɛ lɛ anɔ. No ji akɛ nyɛsumɔ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni nyɛfee esuɔmɔnaanii, ni nyɛye ekitãi lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛye lɛ anɔkwa, ni nyɛsɔ̃mɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛtsui kɛ nyɛnyɛmɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ayagba Israelbii krokomɛi lɛ akɛ, “Shi nyɛtara lo? Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ akutso lɛ fã lɛ ema afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ Gelilot yɛ Yordan lɛ naa yɛ wɔgbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ tsu Osɔfo Eleazar bi Finehas kɛtee Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ahã lumɛi nyɔŋma komɛi fata Finehas he kɛtee tsumɔ nɛɛ. No ji akɛ Israelbii lɛ akutso fɛɛ akutso hã lumɔ kome, ni lumɛi nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yafee wekunukpa hu yɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Amɛtee Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii kɛ Manasebii lɛ aŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: ni amɛyawie Yehowa webii lɛ anaa, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ ni nyɛtɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ nɛɛ? Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛfɔleshãa latɛ ni nyɛma agbɛnɛ nɛɛ tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ nyɛkwa Yehowa, ni nyɛtse ehiɛ atua.

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Aso amanehulu ni wɔna yɛ esha ni afee yɛ Peor lɛ hewɔ ni kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ tete wɔhe ejeko nakai esha lɛ mli, tsɛbelɛ wɔna esɛɛ amanehulu lɛ, no kɛkɛ faaa hãaa wɔ,

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: hewɔ ni nyɛkpaleɔ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ yɛ Yehowa sɛɛ nɛɛ? Kɛji nyɛtse Yehowa hiɛ atua ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, wɔ lɛ, lɛ hu emli aaafu Israel asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛsusuɔ akɛ nyɛgbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhã nyɛ lɛ nɔ tseee lɛ, no lɛ nyɛfoa mli kɛbaa Yehowa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni Yehowa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, koni nyɛbaŋɔa shikpɔŋ lɛ eko yɛ wɔteŋ akɛ nyɛgbɛfaŋnɔ. Nyɛkwɛa kɛkɛ ni nyɛkatsea Yehowa hiɛ atua, ni nyɛkatsea wɔ hu wɔhiɛ atua koni kɛjɛ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛma nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛfɔleshãa latɛ kroko nyɛhã nyɛhe.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Be ni Zera bi Akan yata musunii he lɛ, ani jeee Israel asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ Yehowa mli fu lo? Bɛjeee lɛ ekome kɛkɛ ehiɛ kpãtã yɛ etɔ̃mɔ lɛ hewɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Ofe Koome, Nyɔŋmɔ Yehowa lɛ, lɛ ele wɔyitsoŋ eto, nɔ̃ hewɔ ni wɔfee nakai; no hewɔ lɛ, Israel hu ana ale. Kɛji Yehowa hiɛ atua ni wɔtse, aloo ŋmɛɛmɔ ni wɔŋmɛɛ hemɔkɛyeli ni wɔyɔɔ yɛ emli lɛ he, hewɔ ni wɔfee nɔ ni wɔfee nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛkɛ wɔhe akakea wɔ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ,

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: akɛ wɔma afɔleshãa latɛ bɔ ni afee ni wɔkpa Yehowa jamɔ. Aloo kɛji wɔma afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koni wɔkɛshã shãa afɔle loo niyenii afɔle loo shidaa afɔle lɛ, no lɛ Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ atɔ he owele.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ jɛ ni wɔkɛɛ wɔhe akɛ, ‘Nyɛhãa wɔmãa afɔleshãa latɛ ko, jeee koni wɔkɛshã shãa afɔle loo gbee afɔle,

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Finehas, Osɔfo Eleazar bi lɛ, kɛɛ Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ akɛ, “Wɔna wɔle ŋmɛnɛ akɛ nyɛ kɛ wɔ fɛɛ hiɛ Yehowa jamɔ lɛ mli, ejaakɛ nyɛtɔ̃ko Yehowa nɔ kɛ nɔ ni nyɛfee lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛhere Israel yɛ etoi ni kulɛ Yehowa baagbala lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Osɔfo Eleazar bi Finehas kɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛ Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ gbala mli yɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba Israelbii lɛ aŋɔ̃ɔ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbabɔ amɛ amaniɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ nya amaniɛ lɛ he, ni amɛ jie Nyɔŋmɔ yi. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛwieee he dɔŋŋ akɛ amɛmiifã ta koni amɛkɛ Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ ayawu koni amɛkpãtã shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ nɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Rubenbii lɛ kɛ Gadbii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Afɔleshãa latɛ nɛɛ ji odaseyeli nɔ hã wɔ akɛ Yehowa lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛwo afɔleshãa latɛ nɛɛ gbɛi akɛ, “Odasefonyo.”

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Be kplaŋŋ sɛɛ be ni Yoshua egbɔ kotokoto, ni Israelbii lɛ ahenyɛlɔi fɛɛ ni bɔle amɛ ekpa amɛnaagbamɔ lɛ,

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Yoshua fɔ̃ nine etsɛ Israel tso muu fɛɛ kɛbakpe. Maŋ onukpai kɛ weku nukpai kɛ kojolɔi kɛ maŋ nitsulɔi fɛɛ ba, ni Yoshua kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ migbɔ.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Te nyɛna nii fɛɛ ni Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, efee majimaji ni bɔle nyɛ nɛɛ fɛɛ yɛ nyɛhewɔ? Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, lɛ ewu nyɛtai lɛ ehã nyɛ.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, baashwie maji nɛɛ amli bii lɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ; ebaahã amɛjo nyɛnaa foi, ni nyɛbaaŋɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ewo nyɛ shi eto lɛ.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛfĩa shi jogbaŋŋ, nyɛyea nii fɛɛ ni aŋma yɛ Mose Mla Wolo lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni nyɛkɛba nyɛjeŋ hu. Nyɛkagbaa kɛmiiya abɛku hu,

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: bɔ ni afee ni maji krokomɛi anɔ bii ni ashi futu nyɛ lɛ asu ko akabagbale nyɛ ni nyɛmiitsɛ amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ agbɛii nyɛkɛmiikã kitã, aloo ni nyɛsɔ̃mɔ amɛ, aloo nyɛja amɛ.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ nyɛkpɛtɛa Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛfee kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ,

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Yehowa ehã maji wuji ni ahe wa ejo nyɛnaa foi, ni maŋ ko nyɛko nyɛhiɛ adamɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Nyɛteŋ gbɔmɔ kome aaashwie mɛi akpe kɛ foi. Ejaakɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, lɛ ji mɔ ni wuɔ nyɛta lɛ ehãa nyɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ewo nyɛ shi eto lɛ.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛlea nyɛhenɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni nyɛsumɔ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: nyɛnaa nyɛlea faŋŋ akɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, eyaŋ nɔ ehaŋ maji nɛɛ ajo nyɛnaa foi dɔŋŋ. Moŋ amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ tamɔ tsɔne loo akpa ni atsɔ̃ ato nyɛ, loo tamɔ kpelebii ni akɛmiiyi nyɛ ŋmawuiaŋ, loo tamɔ ŋmei ni miitsurɔ nyɛhiŋmɛiiaŋ; ni nii nɛɛ baaya nɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni nyɛhiɛ aaakpãtã yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ehã nyɛ nɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Eshɛ be ni mibaya jeŋjeŋ fɛɛ yaahe agbɛnɛ. Nyɛle anɔkwale mli yɛ nyɛtsuii amli krɛdɛɛ akɛ nɔ kpakpa ko kwraa bɛ ni Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, wo nyɛ shi akɛ ebaafee ehã nyɛ ni efeko ehako nyɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ eba mli, ni ekome folo nɛkɛ efeko yaka.

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Yoshua bua Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ anaa kɛba Shekem. Kɛkɛ ni etsɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ weku nukpai lɛ kɛ kojolɔi lɛ kɛ maŋ nitsulɔi lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛbadamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa nɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ, ‘Teteete lɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ sɛɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ hi. Jɛi ji he ni Tera, ni ji Abraham kɛ Nahor tsɛ, hi ni amɛja nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Miyaŋɔ̃ nyɛtsɛ Abraham kɛjɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ sɛɛ, ni mihã ekpa Kanaan shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni mihã ewo shwiei babaoo. Miduro lɛ Isak,

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: ni miduro Isak hu Yakob kɛ Esau. Mikɛ Seir Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hã Esau akɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ; shi Yakob kɛ ebii lɛ amɛ lɛ amɛyaje Ijipt.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ bolɔ amɛtsɛ Yehowa, ni ekɛ duŋ kpii fo nyɛ kɛ Ijiptbii lɛ ateŋ; asaŋ ehã ŋshɔ lɛ yi, ni eha Ijiptbii lɛ anɔ. Nyɛna nɔ ni mifee Ijiptbii lɛ kɛ nyɛhiŋmɛi. Nyɛhi ŋã lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: “‘Kɛkɛ ni mikɛ nyɛ bashɛ Amorbii ni yɔɔ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkɛ nyɛ wu, ni mijɔɔ amɛnɔ mihã nyɛ, ni nyɛye amɛnɔ kunim, ni nyɛŋɔ̃ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ, ni mikpãtã amɛhiɛ beiaŋ ni nyɛnyiɛ gbɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Moab maŋtsɛ Balak, Zipor bi lɛ, fã ta koni ekɛ Israel abawu. Etsu ayakpee Balaam, Beor bi lɛ, kɛba akɛ ebalomɔ nyɛ.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Shi mibooo lɛ toi; ni no hewɔ lɛ, jɔɔmɔ moŋ ejɔɔ nyɛ; ni mikɛjie nyɛ yɛ Balak dɛŋ.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ ni nyɛfo Yordan lɛ, ni nyɛba Yeriko. Yeriko lumɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛ wu, ni nakai nɔŋŋ Amorbii lɛ kɛ Perizbii lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ kɛ Girgashbii lɛ kɛ Hivbii lɛ kɛ Yebusbii lɛ hu kɛ nyɛ wu; shi mihã nyɛye amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ kunim.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Mitsu sosomootii kɛtsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ, ni amɛshwie Amorbii amaŋtsɛmɛi enyɔ lɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ; shi jeee nyɛklante loo gãi naa foi amɛjo lɛ.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛtsuko enɔ nii hã nyɛ, nyɛmiiye emli ŋɔɔmɔ; mikɛ maji hu ni jeee nyɛ ni nyɛto hã nyɛ, ni nyɛyɛ amɛmli. Nyɛmiiye wain tromi kɛ mutso ŋmɔji ni jeee nyɛ ni nyɛhu amli nii.’

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛshea Yehowa gbeyei, ni nyɛjiea nyɛyitsoŋ nyɛsɔ̃mɔa lɛ kɛ anɔkwayeli; nyɛkwaa nyɔŋmɔi ni nyɛtsɛmɛi atsɛmɛi lɛ sɔ̃mɔ yɛ Mesopotamia kɛ Ijipt hu lɛ koni nyɛsɔ̃mɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Kɛji esaaa nyɛhiɛ akɛ nyɛaasɔ̃mɔ Yehowa lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ nyɛkɔa mɔ ni nyɛaasɔ̃mɔ, nyɔŋmɔi ni nyɛtsɛmɛi atsɛmɛi lɛ sɔ̃mɔ yɛ Mesopotamia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni jio, Amorbii ni nyɛyɔɔ amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ nɛɛ anyɔŋmɔi lɛ ni jio, nyɛkɔa; shi mi lɛ, mi kɛ miwe lɛ wɔbaasɔmɔ Yehowa.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ to he, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Enɛ akagbale wɔ fɔ̃ŋfɔ akɛ wɔɔshi Yehowa sɛɛ koni wɔyasɔ̃mɔ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi,

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, lɛ ji mɔ ni jie wɔ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni aye wɔ nyɔŋ yɛ lɛ. Efee okadii wuji etsɔ̃ɔ wɔ, asaŋ ebaa wɔyi yɛ gbɛi ni wɔfãfãa fɛɛ mli kɛtsɔ̃ majimaji ateŋ kɛho.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Yehowa shwie Amorbii lɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bluublu yɛ wɔhiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔ hu wɔɔsɔ̃mɔ Yehowa, ejaakɛ lɛ ji wɔNyɔŋmɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Shi Yoshua kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛnyɛŋ Yehowa nyɛsɔ̃mɔ ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni; ni Nyɔŋmɔ ni yeɔ awuŋã ji lɛ, ni ekɛ nyɛtɔ̃mɔi lɛ kɛ nyɛhe eshai ekeŋ nyɛ.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Yɛ mli akɛ Yehowa efee nyɛ ejurɔ kɛho; shi kɛji nyɛshi lɛ esɛɛ, ni nyɛyasɔ̃mɔ maŋsɛɛ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi lɛ, no lɛ eeete shi ewo nyɛ, ni eeekpãtã nyɛhiɛ kɛmɔ shi.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ here Yoshua nɔ akɛ, “Dabi! Yehowa nɔŋŋ wɔbaasɔmɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yoshua kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ ji midasefoi mɔ akɛ nyɛkɔ Yehowa akɛ mɔ ni nyɛbaasɔ̃mɔ.” Maŋbii lɛ to he akɛ, “Wɔmiiye he odase.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua kɛɛ amɛ agbɛnɛ akɛ, “Nyɛŋmɛa maŋsɛɛ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi ni nyɛhiɛhiɛ lɛ ahe mɔ koni nyɛjie nyɛyitsoŋ fɛɛ nyɛsɔ̃mɔ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ here Yoshua nɔ akɛ, “Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, lɛ wɔɔsɔ̃mɔ, ni lɛ toi wɔɔbo!”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yoshua kɛ maŋbii lɛ kpãŋ nakai gbi lɛ, ni ewo maŋ lɛ akpɔ kɛ mla fɛɛ yɛ Shekem.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Yoshua ŋmã saji nɛɛ fɛɛ ewo Nyɔŋmɔ Mla Wolo lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni ewo tɛ kpeteŋkple ko ema tso wulu ni ma Yehowa Kpeehe Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛŋ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yoshua kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛkɛ tɛ nɛɛ aye wɔhe odase ejaakɛ enu wiemɔi ni Yehowa kɛ wɔ wie lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eeeye odase eshi nyɛ koni nyɛkakpa yɛ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoshua wo maŋbii lɛ gbɛ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee egbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yoshua kɛ Eleazar gbele

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Saji nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ Yehowa tsulɔ Yoshua, Nun bi lɛ, gbo be ni eye afii oha kɛ nyɔŋma.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Afu lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Timnat-Sera ni yɔɔ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ Gaash Gɔŋ lɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ sɔ̃mɔ Yehowa yɛ Yoshua wala be mli fɛɛ, kɛ Yoshua gbele sɛɛ be mli fɛɛ, be ni onukpai hu ni le nibii ni Yehowa efee ehã Israel lɛ yɔɔ walaŋ lɛ.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Yosef gbonyo wui lɛ ni Israelbii lɛ wo kɛje Ijipt lɛ, amɛbafu yɛ Shekem yɛ shikpɔŋ kuku ko ni Yakob he lɛ jwiɛtɛi kukuji oha yɛ Shekemtsɛ Hamor bii lɛ adɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔ̃ Yosef shwiei lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Aaron bi Eleazar hu gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ Gibea, ni ji maŋ ni akɛhã ebi Finehas yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Be ni Yoshua egbo sɛɛ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ bi Yehowa akɛ, “Mɛɛ akutso tsutsu afã yɛ wɔteŋ ni ekɛ Kanaanbii lɛ ayawu?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ, “Yuda tsutsu afã; mibahã eye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda kɛɛ enyɛmi Simeon akɛ, “Okɛ mi afã kɛya shikpɔŋ ni ji migbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ ni wɔkɛ Kanaanbii lɛ ayawu, ni mi hu mikɛ bo aaatee onɔ lɛ nɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Yudabii lɛ fã kɛyanina Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ Hebron lɛ. Shi sa lɛ Hebron gbɛi ji Kiriat-Arba. Yudabii lɛ ye Sheshaibii kɛ Ahimanbii kɛ Talmaibii lɛ anɔ kunim. Otniel ŋɔ Debir maŋ lɛ (Yoshua

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Adonibezek jo foi; shi amɛtiu lɛ, ni amɛyamɔ lɛ. Amɛfolɔ enine gɔntii kɛ enane gɔntii.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Yuda akutso lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ bawu. Amɛŋɔ maŋ lɛ. Amɛkɛ klante gbe emli bii lɛ, ni amɛma maŋ lɛ naa la.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Yudabii lɛ fã koni amɛkɛ Kanaanbii lɛ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛ wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋa nɔ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ keketee lɛ nɔ lɛ ayawu.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Yudabii lɛ fã kɛjɛ Hebron kɛyanina Debirbii lɛ. Shi Debir lɛ, sa lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ Kiriat-Sefer.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Yudabii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ni atsɛɔ lɛ Kaleb lɛ kɛɛ: “Mɔ ni aaayatua Kiriat-Sefer ni eeeŋɔ maŋ lɛ, mikɛ mibiyoo Aksa baahã lɛ gbãlã.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Otniel, Kaleb nyɛmi gbekɛ Kenaz bi lɛ, yaŋɔ maŋ lɛ; ni Kaleb kɛ ebiyoo Aksa lɛ hã lɛ gbãlã.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Be ni Aksa tee ewu Otniel ŋɔɔ lɛ, Otniel wo eyiŋ akɛ ebi etsɛ shikpɔŋ ko. Be ni Aksa shɛ etsɛ ŋɔɔ ni ejɛ teji ni eta nɔ lɛ nɔ eyi shi lɛ, etsɛ bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni otaoɔ?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Aksa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Hã mi gbɛwoo nii; akɛni ohã mi wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ keketee lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, hã mi nubui hu.” No hewɔ lɛ, Kaleb hã lɛ nubui ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ kɛ nubui ni yɔɔ jɔɔ mli hu. Kunim ni Yuda kɛ Benyamin akutsei lɛ ye

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Mose shaanuu Kennyo lɛ shwiei kɛ Yudabii lɛ yiŋ kɛjɛ Yeriko tɛ̃ŋ maŋ lɛ mli kɛba Yuda ŋã lɛ ni yɔɔ Arad wuoyigbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtee amɛkɛ jɛi bii lɛ yahi shi.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Yudabii kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi Simeonbii lɛ fã kɛtee amɛyaye Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ Zefat lɛ nɔ kunim, ni amɛfite maŋ lɛ butuu. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛwo maŋ lɛ gbɛi akɛ, Horma.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Akɛ Hebron hã Kaleb tamɔ bɔ ni Mose ekɛɛ lɛ, ni Kaleb shwie Anakbii etɛ̃ lɛ kɛje jɛi.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Shi Benyaminbii lɛ eshwieee Yebusbii ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Yebusbii lɛ kɛ Benyaminbii lɛ hi Yerusalɛm kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Efraim kɛ Manase akutsei lɛ ŋɔ Betel

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Saralɔi lɛ na nuu ko ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli miiba, ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, tsɔ̃ɔmɔ wɔ gbɛ ni akɛboteɔ maŋ lɛ mli, ni wɔkɛ bo baaye yɛ mlijɔlɛ naa.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ gbɛ ni akɛboteɔ maŋ lɛ mli. Amɛgbe maŋ lɛ mli bii lɛ; shi amɛshi nuu lɛ kɛ eŋã kɛ ebii fɛɛ.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ yiŋ etee Hitbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyato maŋ yɛ jɛi. Etsɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛi akɛ Luz, ni no ji maŋ lɛ gbɛi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Mɛi ni Israelbii lɛ eshwieee

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Efraim akutso lɛ eshwieee Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ Gezer lɛ, shi moŋ Kanaanbii lɛ hi amɛteŋ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebulon akutso lɛ eshwieee Kitronbii lɛ kɛ Nahalalbii lɛ, shi moŋ Kanaanbii nɛɛ hi amɛteŋ, ni amɛhã Kanaanbii lɛ sɔmɔ amɛ.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: shi Asherbii lɛ hi Kanaanbii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ, ejaakɛ amɛshwieee Kanaanbii lɛ.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naftali akutso lɛ eshwieee Bet-Shemeshbii lɛ kɛ Bet-Anatbii lɛ, shi amɛbahi Kanaanbii nɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ, ni Bet-Shemeshbii lɛ kɛ Bet-Anatbii lɛ sɔ̃mɔ amɛ.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amorbii lɛ tsi Danbii lɛ kɛtee gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni amɛhãaa Danbii lɛ akpeleke shi kɛba jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amorbii lɛ kã he amɛhi Heres gɔŋ lɛ kɛ Aiyalon kɛ Shalbim; shi Efraimbii lɛ kɛ Manasebii lɛ anine shi wa yɛ amɛnɔ, ni amɛhã Amorbii lɛ sɔmɔ amɛ.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amorbii lɛ ahusu lɛ jɛ Akrabim ŋmeŋme lɛ he yɛ Sela kɛtee yiteŋgbɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa bɔfo jɛ Gilgal kɛba Bokim ni ebakɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Mijie nyɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt ni mikɛ nyɛ ba shikpɔŋ ni mikã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ akitã yɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni mikɛɛ: ‘Mikuŋ mikpãŋmɔ ni mi kɛ nyɛ ekpãŋ lɛ mli gbi ko gbi ko,

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: ni nyɛ hu nyɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ bii lɛ akakpãŋa kpãŋmɔ ko; amɛfɔleshãa latɛi lɛ nyɛkumɔa.’ Shi nyɛbooo mifãmɔ lɛ toi. Mɛni nyɛfee nɛɛ?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ mi hu nɔ ni mikɛɔ ji mishwieŋ amɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ, shi moŋ amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ nyɛhenyɛlɔi, ni amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ aaatsɔ̃ nyɛ tsɔne.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Amɛwo jɛi gbɛi akɛ Bokim, ni amɛshã shãa afɔlei amɛhã Yehowa yɛ jɛi. Yoshua gbele

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Afu lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Timnat-Heres yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ Gaash gɔŋ lɛ kooyigbɛ.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Nakai yinɔbii lɛ hu fɛɛ gboi, ni yinɔ kroko ba yɛ amɛsɛɛ ni amɛleee Yehowa aloo nitsumɔi ni etsu ehã Israel lɛ. Israel fɔ̃ɔ Yehowa jamɔ

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: He fɛɛ he ni Israelbii lɛ aaafã ta kɛaatee lɛ, Yehowa kɛ amɛ yeɔ kɛ joomɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ebɔ amɛ kɔkɔ kɛ bɔ ni ekã amɛ kitã lɛ. Enɛ hã efi Israelbii lɛ waa naakpa.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa tee ta hiɛnyiɛlɔi ashi. Amɛ amɛhereɔ Israelbii lɛ yɛ mɛi ni bahaa amɛnibii kɛyaa lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Shi amɛhiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ hu amɛbooo amɛ toi, ejaakɛ amɛjeɔ Yehowa sɛɛ amɛyanyiɛɔ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi asɛɛ ni amɛjaa amɛ. Etsɛɛɛ kɛkɛ lɛ amɛŋmɛɛ shihilɛ ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ hi ni amɛye Yehowa kitãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he; amɛ lɛ amɛyeee kitãi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Be fɛɛ be ni Yehowa aaatee hiɛnyiɛlɔi ashi ehã Israelbii lɛ, Yehowa yeɔ ebuaa hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ ni amɛhereɔ Israelbii lɛ yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ gbii abɔ fɛɛ ni hiɛnyiɛlɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ; ejaakɛ ŋtsɔi ni Israelbii lɛ dɔmɔɔ yɛ mɛi ni waa amɛ yi kɛ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ dɔɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Shi kɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔ lɛ gbo pɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ ekoŋŋ, ni amɛjeŋba fiteɔ fe amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ tete yɛ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi asɛɛ ni amɛyanyiɛɔ ni amɛsɔmɔɔ amɛ, ni amɛjaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Amɛfɔ̃ɔɔ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ, ni amɛkpaaa amɛkuɛŋtimɔ jeŋba lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa mli woɔ la woɔ Israelbii lɛ, ni ekɛɔ akɛ, “Akɛni nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ etɔ̃ mikpãŋmɔ lɛ ni miwo amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ akitã yɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbooo mi toi

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ mi hu kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ mishwieŋ jeŋmaji ni shwɛ be ni Yoshua gbo lɛ eko eko yɛ amɛhiɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Mikɛ maji nɛɛ baaka Israel makwɛ akɛ amɛaajwɛŋ bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ akɛ amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ jwɛŋ nɔ lɛ lo, aloo amɛ lɛ amɛfeŋ nakai.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: No hewɔ ni Yehowa shi nakai jeŋmaji lɛ, ni eshwieee amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni ehãaa Yoshua aye amɛnɔ kunim lɛ.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: Efee enɛ bɔ ni afee kɛkɛ ni Israelbii ayinɔi lɛ, titri lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi ni wuko ta dã lɛ, ale ta he nɔ ko ni ekɛtsɔ̃ɔ amɛ tawuu.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Jeŋmaji ni ashi lɛ ji Filistibii alumɛi enumɔ lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Sidonbii kɛ Hivbii ni yɔɔ Lebanon gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛjɛ Baal-Hermon gɔŋ lɛ he kɛyashi he ni gɔji ateŋ gbɛ ni akɛyaa Hamat lɛ kã lɛ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ashi jeŋmaji nɛɛ ni akɛ amɛ aka Israelbii lɛ akwɛ akɛ amɛaaye Yehowa kitãi ni etsɔ̃ Mose nɔ ewo amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ anɔ lo.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ ŋɔ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ abiyei; amɛ hu amɛkɛ amɛbiyei hãahãa Israelbii lɛ abihii agbãla; ni Israelbii lɛ sɔ̃mɔ jeŋmaji nɛɛ anyɔŋmɔi lɛ. Otniel

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fee efɔŋ amɛshi Yehowa. Amɛhiɛ kpa Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyasɔmɔ Baal nyɔŋmɔi lɛ kɛ Ashera nyɔŋmɔi lɛ.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa mli wo Israelbii lɛ ala, ni ehã Mesopotamia maŋtsɛ Kushan-Rishataim ye amɛnɔ kunim ni amɛsɔmɔ lɛ afii kpaanyɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ bolɔ tsɛ Yehowa, ni etee herelɔ ko shi ehã amɛ, ni ehere amɛ. Lɛ ji Otniel, Kaleb nyɛmi gbekɛ Kenaz bi lɛ.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ saa fee efɔŋ ekoŋŋ amɛshi Yehowa. No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa hã Moab maŋtsɛ Eglon na hewalɛ fe Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Eglon bua Amonbii lɛ kɛ Amalekbii lɛ anaa eshi enɔ, ni eba ebaye Israelbii lɛ anɔ yɛ ta mli. Eŋɔ Yeriko, tɛŋ maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Then he ruled Israel for
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ sɔ̃mɔ Moab maŋtsɛ Eglon afii nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni Ehud kɛ nikeenii lɛ ehã Eglon etã lɛ, Ehud wo mɛi ni tere nikeenii lɛ agbɛ ni amɛtee.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Be ni Eglon kometoo ta shi yɛ eŋwɛitsu ni ehereɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Ehud tsi bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ekɛɛ Eglon akɛ, “Mihiɛ Nyɔŋmɔ naa wiemɔ ko ni mibakɛɛ bo.” Kɛkɛ ni Eglon te shi yɛ esɛi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ehud kpã enine abɛku lɛ mli, ni efã klante lɛ yɛ nanejurɔ shuɔ lɛ he, ni ekɛdu Eglon musuŋ.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ehud je kpo kɛtee ablanaa lɛ nɔ. Eŋãmɔ shinai lɛ ewo Eglon yi, ni eŋmɛlɛ mli.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Be ni Ehud eje kpo etee lɛ, tsuji lɛ ba; ni be ni amɛna akɛ aŋãmɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shinai lɛ amɛsusu akɛ, “Benɛ etee niiasɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔheremɔ tsu lɛ mli.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Amɛmɛ aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛjwɛŋmɔ shɛɛɛ he dɔŋŋ. Shi be ni egbeleee shinai lɛ lolo lɛ, amɛyakɔ samfee lɛ. Be ni amɛgbele shinai lɛ, naa amɛnuŋtsɔ lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni egbo!

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Be ni amɛlilaa shi lɛ Ehud ejo foi etee momo. Efoŋ yɛ tɛ amãgãi lɛ ahe, ni ejo foi kɛtee Seira.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛnyiɛa misɛɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa baahã nyɛye nyɛhenyɛlɔi Moabbii lɛ anɔ kunim.” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkpeleke shi kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ. Amɛŋɔ Yordan faafoohei ni atsɔ̃ɔ jɛi kɛyaa Moab lɛ, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko gbɛ ni efoɔ.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ aba Moab shi awo Israel shishi. Enɛ hã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔ afii nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ. Shamgar

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Hiɛnyiɛlɔ ni ba ye Ehud sɛɛ ji Shamgar, Anat bi lɛ. Ekɛ tsinakplamɔ tso gbe Filistibii lɛ ateŋ mɛi ohai ekpaa, ni lɛ hu ekɛhere Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehud gbele sɛɛ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ fee efɔŋ ekoŋŋ amɛshi Yehowa.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa hã Yabin, Kanaan maŋtsɛ ni yeɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ Hazor lɛ, ye amɛnɔ kunim. Etatsɛ ji Sisera, ni yɔɔ Jeŋmaji Haroshet lɛ.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Sisera kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Daamɔ buu lɛ shinaa lɛ shi. Kɛ mɔ ko ba ni ebi bo akɛ, ‘Ani mɔ ko yɛ biɛ lo? lɛ, okɛɛ mɔ lɛ akɛ, Dabi!’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, gbalɔ yoo Debora, Lapidot ŋã lɛ, ji Israelbii lɛ akojolɔ.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: He ni etaa ji tɛŋtso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Debora tɛŋtso lɛ shishi yɛ Rama kɛ Betel teŋ, yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ. Israelbii lɛ yaa eŋɔɔ yɛ jɛi ni eyeɔ amɛteŋ saji ehãa amɛ.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Debora tsu ayakpee Barak, Abinoam bi lɛ, kɛjɛ Kadesh ni yɔɔ Naftali lɛ kɛba, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Fãmɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fãa bo nɛ: ‘Yaaŋɔ hii akpei nyɔŋma kɛjɛ Naftalibii kɛ Zebulonbii lɛ ateŋ ni ofã ta kɛya Tabor gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Makpala Sisera, Yabin tatsɛ lɛ, kɛ eshwiilii kɛ etabilɔi babaoo lɛ kɛba oŋɔɔ yɛ Keshon Faa lɛ naa, ni mibahã oye enɔ kunim.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Debora kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mikɛ bo aaatee, kɛ̃lɛ nɔ ni oyaa oyatsu nɛɛ mli anunyam lɛ efeŋ onɔ; ejaakɛ yoo ko ji mɔ ni Yehowa baahã eye Sisera nɔ kunim.” Kɛkɛ ni Debora te shi ni ekɛ Barak tee Kadesh.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Shi Heber, Kennyo lɛ, etse ehe yɛ Kenbii ni ji Mose shaanuu Hobab shwiei lɛ ahe, ni eyashi ebuu lɛ yɛ tso kpele ni ma Zaananim ni yɔɔ Kadesh masɛi lɛ he tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Be ni ayatswa Sisera adafi akɛ Barak, Abinoam bi lɛ, efã ta kɛtee Tabor gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Debora kɛɛ Barak akɛ, “Tee shi, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ ji gbi ni Yehowa baahã oye Sisera nɔ kunim. Ani jeee Yehowa efã kɛnyiɛ ohiɛ nɛɛ?” No hewɔ lɛ, Barak kpeleke shi kɛjɛ Tabor gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hii akpei nyɔŋma lɛ nyiɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Yehowa hã Sisera kɛ eta lɛ gbɛ shwã yɛ Barak klante naa. Kɛkɛ ni Sisera yi shi yɛ eshwiili lɛ mli, ni ejo foi yɛ enane naa.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Barak kɛ emɛi lɛ tiu shwiilii lɛ kɛ tabilɔi lɛ kɛtee Jeŋbii amaŋ Haroshet lɛ, ni Sisera tabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ nyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa; eshwɛɛɛ mɔ kome nɛkɛ folo.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Shi Sisera jo foi yɛ enane naa kɛtee Yael, Kennyo Heber ŋã lɛ buu lɛ mli; ejaakɛ toiŋjɔlɛ yɛ Yabin, Hazor maŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛ Heber, Kennyo lɛ, we lɛ teŋ.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Yael je kpo ekɛ Sisera yakpe ni ekɛɛ Sisera akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, gba kɛba miŋɔɔ; kaashe gbeyei!” No hewɔ lɛ, Sisera gba kɛtee Heber ŋã lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ buu lɛ mli, ni Yael kɛ saanɔ bo ha Sisera nɔ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sisera kɛɛ Yael akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni ohã mi nu fioo manu, shi kumai miiye mi.” No hewɔ lɛ, Heber ŋã lɛ gbele fufɔ wolotɔ naa, ni ehã lɛ eko enu. Kɛkɛ ni eha Sisera nɔ.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Shi Yael, Heber ŋã lɛ, kɔ buu he shiŋmlitso, ni ekɔ hamle ehiɛ edɛŋ. Edɛke shi kɛtee Sisera ŋɔɔ, ni ekɛ shiŋmlitso lɛ yaka etoi shi kɛyamɔ shikpɔŋ, ejaakɛ etɔ Sisera ni ewɔ vii. No hewɔ lɛ, Sisera gbo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Be ni Barak tiuɔ Sisera lɛ, Yael je kpo ekɛ Barak yakpe ni ekɛɛ Barak akɛ, “Ba, ni mikɛ nuu lɛ ni otaoɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ bo.” Be ni Barak tee Yael buu lɛ mli lɛ, naa Sisera ni ekã shi ni egbo, ni shiŋmlitso lɛ tsɛkɛ etoi shi.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hã Israelbii lɛ ye Kanaan maŋtsɛ Yabin nɔ kunim.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ hãaa Yabin, Kanaan maŋtsɛ lɛ, ana mumɔ he kɛ ta kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛkpãtã ehiɛ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Debora kɛ Barak, Abinoam binuu lɛ, la nɛkɛ lala nɛɛ yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ akɛ,

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Akɛni tatsɛmɛi nyiɛ Israel ta lɛ hiɛ, ni maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ here amɛhe hewɔ lɛ, nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Nyɛboa toi! Nyɛ maŋtsɛmɛi! Nyɛfea toi! Nyɛ lumɛi! La mala, saŋku matswa mahã Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, Yehowa.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Gɔji lɛ hoso yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ hu Sinai fee yɛ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hiɛ.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: “Shamgar, Anat bi lɛ, yinɔ, Yael be lɛ mli lɛ, jarayeli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ kã efolo, ni gbɛnyiɛlɔi juɔ shi nyiɛɔ.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Mɛi ahe sɛ̃ yɛ Israel maji lɛ amli. Amɛhe sɛ̃ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni bo Debora, ote shi akɛ Nyɛ Awo yɛ Israel.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Amɛhala nyɔŋmɔi hei, kɛkɛ ni ta shɛ agboi lɛ anaa, Anãaa tsɛŋ loo akplɔ ko yɛ hii akpei nyɔŋmai ejwɛ dɛŋ yɛ Israel.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Mina Israel tatsɛmɛi lɛ ahe tsui, kɛ mɛi ni here amɛhe yɛ tsuijurɔ naa, yɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi.

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: “Nyɛgbaa, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛtara tejii yɛji anɔ, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛtara kuŋtui fɛɛfɛji anɔ, kɛ nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛnyiɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Be ni atswaa saŋku yɛ nuyɛɛhei lɛ, amɛaagba Yehowa kunim lɛ, Israel okwaafoi akunim lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa mɛi lɛ kpeleke shi kɛjɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Tee shi, Debora! Tee shi! Wo ohe nɔ, Barak, okɛ onomii lɛ aya, Tee shi, tee shi, la lala ko, bo Abinoam bi!

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni abladei lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ kpeleke shi. Yehowa mɛi lɛ kpeleke shi yɛ Yehowa hewɔ amɛyanina kãkãlɔi lɛ.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Efraim amɛyiŋ kɛjɛ kɛtee jɔɔ lɛ mli, ni bo Benyamin, amɛnyiɛ bo kɛ owekumɛi lɛ asɛɛ, Tatsɛmɛi lɛ kpeleke shi kɛjɛ Makir kɛba, ni Zebulon ji he ni tatsɛmɛi nukpai lɛ jɛ kɛba.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isakar lumɛi lɛ fata Debora he kɛba, Isakar ni yeɔ Barak anɔkwa, amɛsha foi kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ kpaakpa kɛtee jɔɔ lɛ mli; shi Ruben mli egba. Amɛyiŋ fee amɛ kɔshikɔshi. Amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ amɛfee akɛ amɛmiiba.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba omɛɔ yɛ too kui lɛ ateŋ, ni oboɔ blɛ ni akɛtsɛɔ toi lɛ toi? Ruben akutso lɛ mli egba, amɛyiŋ fee amɛ kɔshikɔshi.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead ta shi yɛ Yordan sɛɛ, Mɛɛba Dan mɛɔ yɛ lɛji lɛ amli? Asher esɛ̃ koniŋŋ kɛta ŋshɔ lɛ naa, eta ŋshɔ blei lɛ anaa.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Zebulon ji maŋ ni kɛ ehe wo osharã kɛ gbele mli, Naftali hu nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ba amɛbawu ta. Amɛkɛ Kanaan maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ bawu yɛ Taanak yɛ Megido fai lɛ anaa; shi amɛnaaa jwiɛtɛi ko amɛhã.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Ŋulamii jɛ ŋwɛi wu, Amɛjɛ amɛgbɛhei lɛ amɛkɛ Sisera wu.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kishon Faa lɛ loo amɛ kɛtee, Faa ni keɔ kɛbaa, Kishon Faa lɛ. Misusuma, fãa nyiɛmɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni okpɔŋɔ akoklotoi lɛ shimɔ shi waa, kɛ hurumɔ ni ekpɔŋɔi lɛ huruɔ kɛ foi lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Yehowa bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ, ‘Nyɛlomɔa Meroz, nyɛlomɔa emli bii lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbafataaa Yehowa he, amɛbafataaa Yehowa he yɛ kãkãlɔi lɛ ateŋ.’

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Ajɔɔ Yael yɛ yei fɛɛ ateŋ, Kennyo, Heber ŋã lɛ. Ajɔɔ lɛ fe yei ni hiɔ bui amli lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Eba nu, ni ehã lɛ fufɔ. Ekɛ fufɔ hiɛ fɔ bahã lɛ, yɛ abladei akpulu mli.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ekpã enine mli ekɔ shiŋmlitso. Ekɛ eninejurɔ kɔ nitsulɔi ahamle, ni ekɛka etoi shi. Etswa Sisera nɔ ni ejwara eyitso wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ;

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: “Sisera nyɛ miifili samflɛ lɛ mli, eekwɛ nii kɛmiitsɔ̃ samflɛ fɔji lɛ amli. Mɛɛba eshwiilii lɛ baa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛ nɛkɛ? Mɛɛba ekpɔŋɔi lɛ akoklotoi lɛ agbɛɛmɔ ekpe sɛɛ nɛkɛ?

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: ‘Amɛna haanii ko kɛ̃ ni amɛmiija, nuu fɛɛ nuu aaana oblayoo kome loo enyɔ tete; blɛ mi, Sisera, hu mana haanii lɛ amli mamai ni awo amɛ tsofa? Mamai enyɔ ni awo amɛ tsofa, ni alo nii awo mli koni mikɛha mikuɛ?’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Yehowa, bɔ nɔŋŋ ni ohenyɛlɔi fɛɛ ahiɛ aaakpãtã nɛ! Shi mɛi ni sumɔɔ bo lɛ aaatãmɔ hulu, be ni eteɔ shi yɛ ehewalɛ mli lɛ.” No sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔ afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fee efɔŋ amɛshi Yehowa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehã Midianbii ye Israelbii lɛ anɔ afii kpawo.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Midianbii lɛ anineshi wa naakpa yɛ Israelbii lɛ anɔ. Midianbii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ tao bui yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ, kɛ tɛkploi kɛ mɔji amɛhã amɛhe.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Kɛji Israelbii lɛ du nii lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ Midianbii kɛ Amalekbii kɛ bokãgbɛbii lɛ efã kɛbatua amɛ.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛbolɔɔ amɛtsɛɔ Yehowa yɛ Midianbii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Mikɛɛ nyɛ akɛ mi ji Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shi nyɛkashea Amorbii ni yɔɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anyɔŋmɔi lɛ agbeyei.’ Shi nyɛbooo migbee toi.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa bɔfo lɛ ba ebata Yoash, Abiezernyo lɛ, blɔfo yɔɔyitso ni yɔɔ Ofra lɛ shishi. Nakai be lɛ, Yoash bi Gideon lɛ miigbee ŋmãa yɛ wainbu mli, bɔ ni afee ni Midianbii lɛ akana.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo lɛ jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Gideon ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bo nuu kãkãlɔ, Yehowa kɛ bo yɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gideon kɛɛ bɔfo lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, minuŋtsɔ, kɛ Yehowa kɛ wɔ yɛ lɛ, mɛɛba mɔ ni enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ eba wɔnɔ nɛɛ? Nɛgbɛ enaakpɛɛnii lɛ fɛɛ ni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ gbaa wɔ ni amɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Ani jeee Ijipt Yehowa jie wɔ kɛjɛ’ lɛ yɔɔ? Ejaakɛ agbɛnɛ Yehowa eshɛ wɔ efɔ̃, ni eŋmɛɛ wɔhe ehã Midianbii lɛ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa tsɔ̃ ehiɛ ehã Gideon ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa kɛ ohewalɛ nɛɛ koni oyahere Israel yɛ Midianbii lɛ adɛŋ! Mi ji mɔ ni tsuɔ bo lɛ?”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Gideon kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, minuŋtsɔ, te mafee tɛŋŋ manyɛ mahere Israel lɛ? Naa, miweku lɛ ji weku ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ Manase, ni mi, mi ji bibioo fe fɛɛ yɛ mitsɛ we lɛ.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mibaye mabua bo, ni ooogbe Midianbii lɛ butuu tamɔ agbeɔ mɔ kome.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Gideon kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ kɛ ona mihe tsuijurɔ lɛ, no lɛ hã mi okadi ko akɛ bo okɛ mi wieɔ nɛɛ.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ofainɛ, kaaje biɛ kɛyashi be ni maba mikɛ nikeenii aaabama ohiɛ.” Yehowa to he akɛ; “Mahi shi kɛyashi be ni oooku osɛɛ oba.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Gideon tee ni eyasaa abotiabi. Ekɛ ma kiloi nyɔŋma fee akpiti. Ekɛ loo lɛ wo kafu mli ni ekɛ ehe nu lɛ wo kukwɛi mli. Ekɛ je kpo kɛba bɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ekɛbama ehiɛ.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ Gideon akɛ, “Okɛ loo lɛ kɛ akpiti lɛ ashwie tɛsaa lɛ nɔ, ni ofɔse ehe nu lɛ oshwie nɔ.”

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Gideon fee nakai. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo lɛ kpã edɛhiɛmɔtso lɛ mli, ni ekɛ tso lɛ naabu sa loo lɛ kɛ akpiti lɛ he. La jɛ tɛsaa lɛ mli ni ebashã loo lɛ kɛ akpiti lɛ wɛɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo lɛ laaje yɛ Gideon hiɛ.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Be ni Gideon yoo akɛ Yehowa bɔfo ni lɛ, ekɛɛ, “Ei! Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ! Yehowa bɔfo pam mina hiɛ kɛ hiɛ nɛkɛ nɛɛ!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Na tsui, kaashe gbeyei, ogboŋ!”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gideon ma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi ehã Yehowa, ni etsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yehowa ji hejɔlɛ.” Afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ yɛ Ofra ni ji Abiezerbii anɔ lɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ Gideon akɛ, “Yaaŋɔ otsɛ tsinanuu nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, ni eye afii kpawo lɛ, koni oyakumɔ Baal afɔleshãa latɛ ni ji otsɛ nɔ lɛ. Asaŋ foo nyɔŋmɔ yoo Ashera tso ni ma afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Maa afɔleshãa latɛ ohã Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yɛ tɛsaa ni yɔɔ biɛ nɛɛ yiteŋ. Too tɛi ni okɛbaama lɛ gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni sa akɛ ato lɛ; koni oŋɔ tsinanuu ni ji enyɔ lɛ, ni okɛshã shãa afɔle. Okɛ Ashera tso ni obaafo lɛ afee lai ni okɛshã.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Gideon ŋɔ etsuji lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋma, ni efee bɔ ni Yehowa efã lɛ lɛ. Shi akɛni eeshe etsɛ we lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ agbeyei hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɛɛ efee nii nɛɛ shwane, shi moŋ nyɔɔŋ efee.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Shi be ni maŋbii lɛ te shi leebi maŋkpa lɛ, naa Baal afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni akumɔ ashwie shi; afo Ashera tso ni ma emasɛi lɛ, ni akɛ tsinanuu ni ji enyɔ lɛ eshã shãa afɔle yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ ni ama lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ bibii amɛhe akɛ, “Namɔ ye nɛkɛ sane?” Be ni amɛtao mli ni amɛbi mli lɛ, akɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Gideon, Yoash bi lɛ, ji mɔ ni ye nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ Yoash akɛ, “Jiemɔ obi lɛ kɛba ni agbe lɛ; ejaakɛ ekumɔ Baal afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni efo Ashera tso ni ma emasɛi lɛ.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Shi Yoash bi mɛi fɛɛ ni ebakpe ewo ehe lɛ akɛ, “Ani nyɛ nyɛbaabe nyɛhã Baal lo? Aloo nyɛ, nyɛbaafã Baal he? Mɔ ni baabe ahã Baal lɛ, aaagbe lɛ dani je aaatsɛre. Kɛ nyɔŋmɔ ji Baal lɛ efã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe yɛ efɔleshãa latɛ ni akumɔ lɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ awo Gideon gbɛi akɛ, “Yerubaal”, eshishi ji “Baal kɛ lɛ atswa, ejaakɛ ekumɔ efɔleshãa latɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Midianbii kɛ Amalekbii kɛ bokãgbɛbii lɛ fɛɛ bua amɛhe naa. Amɛfo Yordan Faa lɛ, ni amɛyato shi yɛ Yezreel jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa Mumɔ lɛ bayi Gideon nɔ. Gideon kpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ ekɛtsɛ Abiezerbii lɛ koni amɛbanyiɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Etsu mɛi kɛtee Manase fɛɛ ni ayakpee amɛ hu koni amɛbanyiɛ esɛɛ. Etsu kɛtee Asher kɛ Zebulon kɛ Naftali; ni amɛba koni amɛkɛ lɛ abakpe.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: mikɛ gwantɛŋ wolo baaha ŋmãashaahe lɛ. Kɛji bɔ nyɔ wolo lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ nɔ, shi shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ egbi lɛ, no lɛ mana male akɛ minine nɔ obaatsɔ ohere Israel tamɔ bɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Eba mli nakai. Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Gideon te shi leebi mra. Eŋã toowolo lɛ mli, ni nu ni eŋã yɛ mli lɛ fee tsene obɔ̃.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gideon kɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, “Omli akafu mi; mawie shi kome nɛɛ pɛ. Miikpa bo fai, hã maka shi kome hu makwɛ: hã wolo lɛ kɛkɛ agbi, shi bɔ anyɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ hã eba mli nakai yɛ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli; wolo lɛ kɛkɛ gbi, shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ bɔ enyɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yerubaal ni ji Gideon lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ te shi leebi maaŋkpa, ni amɛyato shi yɛ Harod nubu lɛ naa. Midianbii atabilɔi lɛ jwere jɔɔ lɛ ni kã More gɔŋkpɔ lɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Gideon akɛ, “Mɛi ni fata ohe lɛ ayi fa tsɔ̃ hã mi bɔ ni matsɔ̃ amɛnɔ mahã oye Midianbii lɛ anɔ kunim, koni Israel akabashwã etsɔ̃ɔ mi akɛ, ‘Mi diɛŋtsɛ mihewalɛ mikɛhere miyiwala.’

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, hã ashiɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ toiŋ akɛ, ‘Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni sheɔ gbeyei ni ŋmiŋmi emɔ lɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ eya shĩa.’ ” Gideon ka amɛ ekwɛ ni mɛi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enyɔ ku amɛsɛɛ, ni mɛi akpei nyɔŋma hi shi.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji ooshe gbeyei akɛ oooyatua amɛ lɛ, no lɛ, kɛ otsulɔ Pura akpeleke shi kɛya nsra lɛ mli,

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Gideon akɛ, “Mɛi lɛ ayi fa tsɔ̃ lolo. Okɛ amɛ akpeleke shi kɛya nu lɛ he, ni maka amɛ yɛ jɛi mahã bo. Mɔ ni makɛɛ bo yɛ ehe akɛ, ‘Okɛ mɔnɛ akaya lɛ,’ okɛ lɛ akaya.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gideon kɛ mɛi lɛ kpeleke shi kɛtee nu lɛ he. Yehowa kɛɛ Gideon akɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ elilɛi aaalɛmɔ nu lɛ tamɔ gbei lɛmɔɔ nu lɛ, akɛ lɛ adamɔ afã; ni nakai nɔŋŋ ofee mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaakula enakutsei anaa ni eeenu nu lɛ.”
