translation_verse: Be ni amɛbɛŋkɛ Mika shĩa lɛ, oblanyo lɛ wiemɔ hã amɛyoo akɛ Levinyo ji lɛ. Amɛgba kɛtee shĩa lɛ, ni amɛbi lɛ akɛ, “Namɔ kɛ bo ba biɛ? Mɛni ofeɔ yɛ biɛ? Mɛni otsuɔ yɛ biɛ?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ to he akɛ, “Mika kɛ mi eye efua, ni ebɔ mi apaa koni maye osɔfo mahã lɛ.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, ni obi Nyɔŋmɔ ohã wɔ bɔ ni afee ni wɔle akɛ wɔgbɛ ni wɔnyiɛ nɛɛ aaafee omanye lo?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Osɔfo lɛ to he hã amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa kɛ omanye. Yehowa hiŋmɛi kã nyɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni nyɛnyiɛ nɛɛ mli!”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mɛi enumɔ lɛ kɛshwie nɔ kɛtee Laish. Amɛna jɛibii lɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe amɛhã, tamɔ Sidonbii lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kpoo ni amɛyiŋ efeee amɛ kɔshikɔshi yɛ mɔ ko he lɛ. Nɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ; niiatsɛmɛi ji amɛ. Amɛkɛ Sidonbii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛ, ni amɛkɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ sharamɔ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Be ni mɛi enumɔ lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛba amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Zora kɛ Eshtaol lɛ, amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ bi amɛ akɛ, “Te nyɛyana tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Kɛ nyɛtee lɛ, nyɛbaaya nyɛyanina gbɔmɛi ni kwɛɛɛ nɔ fɔŋ ko gbɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni da ni. Anɔkwale mli lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhã nyɛ. Eji he ko ni shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ mli ekoeko he bɛ ona yɛ.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii ohai ekpaa ni jɛ Danbii aweku lɛ mli ni emia kɛ tawuunii fã kɛjɛ Zora kɛ Eshtaol,

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee amɛyabɔ nsra yɛ Kiriat-Yearim yɛ Yuda. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Dan Shitoohe kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Eyɛ Kiriat-Yearim anaigbɛ.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Amɛfo mli yɛ jɛi kɛtee Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni amɛba Mika shĩa lɛ masɛi.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii enumɔ lɛ ni tee yasara Laish shikpɔŋ lɛ bi amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ akɛ, “Ani nyɛle akɛ shĩai nɛɛ ateŋ eko mli lɛ efod kɛ wɔji kɛ amãgã ni akpɛ kɛ amãgã ni ashwie yɛ mli lo? No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛkwɛa nɔ ni nyɛaafee.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Feemɔ diŋŋ; okɛ onine ato onaabu, ni obaho ni wɔtee koni oyatsɔ̃ wɔŋaawolɔ kɛ wɔsɔfo. Te emli nɔ ni hi hã bo lɛ, akɛ oooye osɔfo ohã gbɔmɔ kome we aloo akɛ oooye ohã Israel muu fɛɛ?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Sane lɛ ŋɔɔ osɔfo lɛ naa. Ehole amãgã ni akɛgbaa lɛ kɛ wɔji lɛ kɛ efod ni akpɛ lɛ, ni ekɛba mɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee. Amɛhã gbekɛbii lɛ kɛ shĩa kooloi lɛ kɛ nibii lɛ nyiɛ amɛhiɛgbɛ.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Be ni amɛkɛ Mika shĩai lɛ teŋ gbɛ ejekɛ lɛ, abo atsɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ shĩai ni bɛŋkɛ Mika shĩa lɛ amli lɛ, ni amɛtiu Danbii lɛ.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Amɛbolɔ amɛtsɛ Danbii lɛ ayisɛɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Danbii lɛ tsɔ̃ amɛhe ni amɛbi Mika akɛ, “Mɛni feɔ bo hewɔ ni okɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo baa nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Mika to he akɛ, “Nyɛŋɔ minyɔŋmɔi lɛ ni mifee lɛ kɛ osɔfo lɛ, kɛmiiya; mɛni eshwɛ mi dɔŋŋ? Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni nyɛbiɔ mi akɛ, ‘Mɛni feɔ bo’ lɛ?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Danbii lɛ kɛɛ Mika akɛ, “Kaahã anu ogbee yɛ wɔteŋ ni mlilatsɛmɛi nɛɛ miitsɛ̃ kɛmiiba onɔ ni amɛbakpãtã bo kɛ owe lɛ mli bii ahiɛ.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Danbii lɛ kɛshwie nɔ. Be ni Mika na akɛ amɛhe wa fe lɛ lɛ, etsɔ̃ ehe, ni eku esɛɛ kɛtee eshĩa.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ amɛtsɛ Dan ni ji Yakob bi lɛ gbɛi Dan lɛ wo maŋ lɛ. Shi sa lɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛi ji Laish.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Nakai bei lɛ amli be ni maŋtsɛ bɛ Israel lɛ, Levinyo ko yato gbɔ yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ he ko shɔŋŋ. Ekɛ yoo ko ni jɛ Betlehem yɛ Yuda lɛ fee hemɔ.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Shi yoo lɛ mlifu nuu lɛ ni eshi nuu lɛ etee etsɛ we yɛ Betlehem Yuda, ni eyaye nyɔji ejwɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ewu lɛ yiŋ etee koni eyatiu esɛɛ ni ekɛ lɛ awie yɛ tsuijurɔ naa koni ekpala lɛ kɛba ekoŋŋ. Nuu lɛ kɛ etsulɔ kɛ tejii enyɔ tee. Be ni Levinyo lɛ yashɛ yoo lɛ tsɛ lɛ we lɛ ni eshaanuu lɛ na lɛ lɛ, ehere lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Shaanuu lɛ tsĩ Levinyo lɛ naa, ni Levinyo lɛ kɛ shaanuu lɛ hi shi gbii etɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, nuu lɛ kɛ yoo lɛ ye nii, ni amɛnu nɔ ko ni amɛhi shi yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛte shi leebi maŋkpa, ni Levinyo lɛ miitao eyi mli, kɛkɛ ni eshaanuu lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ aboloo atrɔma kome ko asa onaa koni no sɛɛ dani nyɛyi mli.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, hii enyɔ lɛ ho amɛtara shi, ni amɛye nii, ni amɛnu nɔ ko. Kɛkɛ ni yoo lɛ tsɛ lɛ kɛɛ eshaanuu lɛ akɛ, “Kpɛlɛ̃mɔ ni owɔ biɛ ŋmɛnɛ hu ni omii ashɛ ohe!”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Be ni nuu lɛ te shi ni ebaayi mli lɛ, eshaanuu lɛ tsĩ enaa, ni ewɔ jɛi ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nuu lɛ te shi leebi maŋkpa ni ebaaya, kɛkɛ ni yoo lɛ tsɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Wo onaa nɔ ko dã. Hii shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi.” No hewɔ lɛ, shaahiimɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ye nii.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Be ni nuu lɛ kɛ ehemɔ lɛ kɛ etsulɔ lɛ te shi ni amɛbaayi mli lɛ, eshaanuu lɛ ni ji yoo lɛ tsɛ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Amrɔ nɛɛ, je ena etã, nyɛwɔa; duŋ baawo nɔŋŋ. Wɔ biɛ ni omii ashɛ ohe, koni nyɛte shi maŋkɛ mra ni nyɛyi mli, ni oya omaŋ.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Shi nuu lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ ni ewɔ jɛi nakai gbi lɛ; no hewɔ lɛ, ete shi ni eyi mli. Ebɛŋkɛ Yebus ni ji Yerusalɛm ŋlɛnɔ. Ekɛ ehemɔ lɛ nyiɛ kɛ tejii enyɔ ni awo amɛnɔ nii.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Be ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ Yebus lɛ, je ena etã. No hewɔ lɛ, tsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ enuŋtsɔ lɛ akɛ, “Hã ni wɔgba kɛya Yebusbii amaŋ nɛɛ mli ni wɔyawɔ jɛi.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfoŋ kɛtee amɛhiɛ. Be ni amɛbɛŋkɛ Gibea ni ji Benyaminbii amaŋ lɛ lɛ, hulu nyɔ shi wo amɛ.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgba Gibea koni amɛyawɔ jɛi. Be ni amɛshɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Levinyo lɛ ho eta maŋ lɛ blohuŋ, ejaakɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko eŋɔɔɔ amɛ kɛyaaa eshĩa koni amɛyawɔ jɛi.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ naa nuumo ko ni eyatsu nii yɛ eŋmɔ mli ni eku esɛɛ eeba gbɛkɛnaashi mli. Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ nyo ji lɛ, ni ebato gbɔ yɛ Gibea maŋ lɛ mli. Gibeabii lɛ Benyaminbii ni.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Be ni nuumo lɛ yaawo ehiɛ nɔ lɛ, ena nuu gbɛnyiɛlɔ lɛ yɛ blohu lɛ mli. Nuumo lɛ bi nuu lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ oyaa, ni nɛgbɛ ojɛ?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Levinyo lɛ to he akɛ, “Wɔjɛ Betlehem ni yɔɔ Yuda lɛ; wɔmiifo mli kɛya Efraim gɔji lɛ asɛɛgbɛ shɔŋŋ. Efraimnyo ji mi. Mitee Betlehem yɛ Yuda, shi mimaŋ miyaa nɛɛ; ni mɔ ko eŋɔɔɔ mi kɛyaaa eshĩa.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Shi wɔyɛ jwɛi kɛ niyenii hã wɔtejii lɛ, ni aboloo hu yɛ hã mi kɛ oblayoo lɛ kɛ oblanyo lɛ ni fata wɔhe lɛ; nɔ ko nɔ ko he ehĩaaa wɔ.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Nuumo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Oba kɛ omanye. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he aaahia bo lɛ, mahã bo; blohu lɛ mli kɛkɛ ni okawɔ.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nuumo lɛ ŋɔ lɛ kɛtee eshĩa. Ehã tejii lɛ anii. Gbɔi lɛ fɔfɔɔ amɛnaji ahe; ni amɛye nii, ni amɛnu nɔ ko.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛmii eshɛ amɛhe lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli bii komɛi ni ji hii yakagbɔmɛi babɔle shĩa lɛ kɛkpe. Amɛshimɔ shinaa lɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ shĩatsɛ ni ji nuumo lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ nuu lɛ ni bato oshĩa lɛ aje kpo kɛba ni wɔkɛ lɛ awɔ.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Shi nuumo lɛ ni ji shĩatsɛ lɛ je kpo kɛba amɛŋɔɔ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Dabida, minyɛmimɛi! Nyɛkafea efɔŋ ni tamɔ enɛ; akɛni nuu nɛɛ ebato mishĩa nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ nyɛkafea nɛkɛ hiɛgbejianii nɛɛ.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Naa, mibi oblayoo foro kɛ nuu lɛ hu hemɔ. Mikɛ amɛ moŋ baaje kpo kɛba ni nyɛfite amɛ ni nyɛfee amɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛsumɔɔ; shi nuu nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛkafea lɛ nɛkɛ hiɛgbejianii nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Shi hii lɛ booo lɛ toi. No hewɔ lɛ, Levinyo lɛ ŋɔ ehemɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ je kpo kɛba amɛŋɔɔ yɛ blohu lɛ mli. Amɛnyɛ yoo lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ lɛ wɔ, ni amɛfee lɛ niseniianii nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ ni be ni je bɔi tsɛremɔ lɛ, amɛŋmɛ̃ɛ ehe.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Hiɛfutɛfutɛ mli lɛ, yoo lɛ ba ni ebaho ebu shi yɛ nuumo lɛ shĩa lɛ he ni ewu lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ shi kɛyashi be ni hiɛ gbele.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Be ni ewu lɛ te shi leebi ni egbele shĩa lɛ shinaa lɛ ni ebaaje kpo eya lɛ, naa yoo lɛ ni ji ehemɔ lɛ bu shi yɛ shĩa lɛ shinaa lɛ shi, ni eniji jwere kpoku lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ewu lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Tee shi ni wɔtee” shi fɛɛ lɛ kranaa. Kɛkɛ ni ewu lɛ wo egbonyo lɛ eŋmɛ eteji lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛshwie nɔ kɛtee emaŋ.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Be ni eshɛ ewe lɛ, ekɔ kakla, ni emɔ ehemɔ lɛ mli, ni efolɔ emli yɛ etalɔi lɛ anɔ kukuji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ. Ehã akɛtee akutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amli akɛyatsɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni na lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Afeko nɛkɛ nɔ ko dã ni asaŋ anako nɛkɛ nɔ ko dã kɛjɛ gbi ni Israelbii jɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ba aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ. Nyɛsusua he, nyɛwoa he ŋaa, nyɛwiea he.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Levinyo lɛ ni ji yoo ni agbe lɛ wu lɛ hã hetoo ni ekɛɛ, “Mikɛ mihemɔ ba Benyaminbii amaŋ ni ji Gibea koni wɔbawɔ jɛi.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Miwo mihemɔ lɛ, ni mifolɔ emli dukuduku ni mikɛmaje Israelbii ashikpɔŋ ni ji amɛgboshinii lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he, ejaakɛ Benyaminbii ebɔ musu ni amɛfee hiɛgbejianii yɛ Israel.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Naa, nyɛ Israelbii fɛɛ nɛ. Mɛni nyɛkɛɔ; nyɛwoa he ŋaa!”

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ fĩ tɔo, ni amɛfee jwɛŋmɔ kome amɛwo Gibea maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Israel akutsei lɛ tsu mɛi kɛtee Benyamin akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ ŋɔɔ ayakɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ yiŋsha sane pam aye yɛ nyɛteŋ nɛɛ?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛjiea hii, yakagbɔmɛi lɛ ni yɔɔ Gibea lɛ kɛbaa, koni wɔgbea amɛ ni wɔkɛjie nɔ fɔŋ lɛ yɛ Israel.”

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Shi Benyaminbii lɛ booo amɛnyɛmimɛi Israelbii lɛ atoi. Shi moŋ amɛbua amɛhe naa kɛjɛ maji lɛ amli kɛtee Gibea, koni amɛkɛ Israelbii lɛ ayawu.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ te shi leebi ni amɛyabɔ nsra amɛwo Gibea.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Amɛfã kɛtee koni amɛkɛ Benyaminbii lɛ ayawu. Israelbii lɛ gba ta wo Benyaminbii lɛ yɛ Gibea.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Benyaminbii lɛ fã kpo kɛjɛ Gibea, ni amɛbakpãtã Israelbii lɛ ateŋ hii akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enyɔ ahiɛ kɛmɔ shi kwraa nakai gbi lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: ni mɔ ni sɔmɔɔ yɛ jɛi yɛ Yehowa hiɛ ji Finehas, Aaron bi Eleazar bi lɛ. Israelbii lɛ bi Yehowa akɛ, “Ani wɔfã ekoŋŋ ni wɔkɛ wɔnyɛmimɛi Benyaminbii lɛ ayawu aloo wɔfɔ̃ɔ?” Yehowa kɛɛ, “Nyɛfãa kɛyaa, ejaakɛ wɔ lɛ, mahã nyɛye amɛnɔ kunim.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ to kawolɔi kɛbɔle Gibea kɛkpe.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsɔ̃ amɛsɛɛ amɛ̃hã Israelbii lɛ, ni amɛjo foi kɛtee ŋã lɛ nɔ gbɛ; shi ta lɛ nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ waa. Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ fã nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛbote Benyaminbii lɛ ateŋ, ni amɛgbegbee Benyaminbii lɛ.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ sa Benyaminbii lɛ ayi, ni amɛnyiɛ Benyaminbii lɛ asɛɛ kɛyashi Noha. Amɛnaanaa Benyaminbii lɛ anɔ aahu kɛyashi Gibea ŋlɛnɔ yɛ bokãgbɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ tsɔ̃ amɛhe amɛwo Benyaminbii krokomɛi lɛ. Amɛkɛ klante gbegbee Benyaminbii lɛ; amɛgbe gbɔmɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ fɛɛ maŋ mli kɛ kooloi fɛɛ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni baje amɛgbɛ nɔ. Asaŋ maji fɛɛ ni amɛyanina lɛ, amɛmamɔ fɛɛ naa la.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Israel hii lɛ ekãmɔ kitãi yɛ Mizpa akɛ, “Wɔteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ ebiyoo akahã Benyaminnyo gbãlã.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ yiŋ kɛtee Betel. Amɛhi shi yɛ jɛi yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Amɛfo waa kɛ dɔlɛ

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: amɛkɛɛ: “Ao Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, mɛɛba enɛ ba yɛ Israel akɛ ŋmɛnɛ akutso kome elaaje yɛ Israel?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ te shi maŋkɛ mra, ni amɛma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi. Amɛshã shãa afɔlei kɛ hejɔlɛ afɔlei.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ bi akɛ, “Israel akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, te akutso ni fataaa Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ he kɛbaaa Yehowa ŋɔɔ lɛ? Ejaakɛ amɛkã kitã wulu akɛ mɔ ni baaa Yehowa ŋɔɔ yɛ Mizpa lɛ, ‘Gbe agbe lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Benyaminhii lɛ anii fee amɛnyɛmimɛi Israelbii lɛ mɔbɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ atse akutso kome yɛ Israel he ashɛ afɔ̃.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ hu ni wɔna ŋamɛi wɔhã mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ, akɛni wɔkã Yehowa kitã akɛ wɔkɛ wɔbiyei haŋ Benyaminbii gbãlã nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni akane maŋ lɛ, ana akɛ Yabesh-Gileadbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome nɛkɛ folo bɛ jɛi.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni kpee muu lɛ fɛɛ tsu akɛ wiemɔ yahã Benyaminbii ni yɔɔ Rimon tɛsaa lɛ he lɛ akɛ akɛ amɛ ekpãtã.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba nakai be lɛ mli, ni akɛ yei ni ahere amɛyiwala yɛ Yabesh-Gilead yei lɛ ateŋ lɛ hã amɛ gbãlã; shi no tete lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Benyaminbii lɛ anii fee maŋ lɛ mɔbɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa ehã mligbalamɔ eba Israel akutsei lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kpee lɛ mli onukpai lɛ kɛɛ, “Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔna ŋamɛi wɔhã mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ, akɛni akpãtã Benyamin yei lɛ ahiɛ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Shi wɔ lɛ, wɔnyɛŋ wɔkɛ wɔbiyei lɛ ahã amɛ gbãlã, ejaakɛ Israelbii ekã kitã akɛ, ‘Alomɔ mɔ ni aaaŋɔ yoo ko ahã gbãlã yɛ Benyamin.’ ”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛɛ: “Daa afi lɛ ayeɔ Yehowa gbijurɔ yɛ Shilo. Shilo kã Betel kooyigbɛ kɛ Lebona wuoyigbɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ ni kã kɛjɛ Betel kɛyaa Shekem lɛ bokãgbɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛfã Benyaminbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa ni nyɛyatea yɛ waintromi lɛ amli.

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: Kɛji Shilo oblayei lɛ je kpo ba amɛbajo lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ nyɛfãa kpo kɛjɛa waintromi lɛ amli kɛbaa koni nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ abamɔ eŋã yɛ Shilo oblayei lɛ ateŋ, koni nyɛkɛ amɛ aya Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛtsɛmɛi loo amɛnyɛmimɛi ba nyɛŋɔɔ amɛkɛ nyɛ babe lɛ, nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkwɛa wɔhewɔ kɛkɛ ni nyɛkɛ amɛ ahãa wɔ; ejaakɛ jeee ta mli wɔshɔ̃ amɛ yɛ, yɛ nyɛdɛŋ koni wɔkɛ amɛ afee wɔŋamɛi; ni asaŋ jeee nyɛ nyɛkɛ amɛ hã wɔ ni eeeba lɛ akɛ nyɛaatere wɔyi sɔ̃ ko.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Benyaminbii lɛ fee nakai. Amɛmɔmɔ ŋamɛi yɛ amɛyikulɛ naa yɛ mɛi ni bajo lɛ ateŋ, ni amɛŋɔ amɛ kɛtee. Kɛkɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ. Amɛsaa maji lɛ amɛmamɔ, ni amɛhi mli.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ hu shi jɛi. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ku esɛɛ kɛtee ekutso kɛ eweku mli, ni amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ nɔ.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, maŋtsɛ ko bɛ Israel; mɔ fɛɛ mɔ feɔ nɔ ni ja yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Naomi wu, Elimelek, gbo ni ebashwɛ Naomi kɛ ebihii enyɔ lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Bihii nɛɛ ŋɔ Moabyei. Yei nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ kome gbɛi ji Orpa, ni mɔ kome hu gbɛi ji Rut. Amɛhi jɛi aaafee afii nyɔŋma.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Naomi nu yɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ Yehowa ebaduro emaŋ Israel niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ eshaayei lɛ yiŋ kɛmiiku esɛɛ kɛjɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya Yuda.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛyaa lɛ, Naomi kɛɛ eshaayei enyɔ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ nyɛyaa; nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya enyɛ we. Yehowa afee nyɛ ejurɔ tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛfee mi kɛ gbohii lɛ ejurɔ lɛ.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Ehã nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ana he ko eta yɛ ewu we.” Ni eshwɔshwɔɔ amɛnaa, ni ekɛ amɛye shɛɛ. Kɛkɛ ni amɛjwa yaafo.

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛɛ Naomi akɛ, “Dabi, shi wɔkɛ bo aaatee omaŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ moŋ.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Shi Naomi kɛɛ, “Nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ, mibii! Mɛɛba nyɛkɛ mi aaatee? Ani bihii yɛ mimusuŋ lolo ni amɛbaatsɔ̃mɔ nyɛwumɛi?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Mibii, nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ nyɛyaa, ejaakɛ migbɔ tsɔ̃ bɔ ni mikɛ nuu aaayahi shi. Ni kɛji mikɛɛ miyɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ tete, ni maya nuu ko ŋɔɔ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛŋ koni mafɔ bihii tete lɛ,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: aso no hewɔ ni nyɛaamɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛaadara? Aloo no hewɔ ni nyɛaatsi nyɛhe naa, ni nyɛkɛ nuu ehiŋ shi? Dabi, mibii! Shi nyɛsane miidɔ mi naakpa; ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ mi eye kɛ joomɔ.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛjwa yaafo ekoŋŋ. Ni Orpa shwɔ eshaayoo lɛ naa, ni eku esɛɛ; shi Rut lɛ, lɛ lɛ ekpɛtɛ Naomi lolo.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Naa, obienyɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ etee emaŋ kɛ esɛɛ nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Kuu osɛɛ ni otiu lɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Shi Rut to he akɛ, “Kaahiɛ mi doo akɛ mishi bo, ni miku misɛɛ ni mifɔ̃ɔ osɛɛnyiɛmɔ! Shi he fɛɛ he ni oyaa lɛ matee, ni he ni oooyahi lɛ jɛi mahi. Omaŋ aaatsɔ̃ mimaŋ, ni oNyɔŋmɔ aaatsɔ mi hu miNyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: He ni ooogbo yɛ lɛ jɛi magbo yɛ, ni he ni aaafũ bo yɛ lɛ jɛi nɔŋŋ aaafu mi yɛ. Yehowa kɛ mi aye ni ekɛ mi aye ekoŋŋ, kɛjeee gbele kɛkɛ aaagbala mi kɛ bo teŋ fĩi.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni Naomi na akɛ Rut eŋmɔ eyiŋ kpɔ akɛ ekɛ lɛ aaatee lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ Rut kɛ nɔ ni ekɛ lɛ wieɔ lɛ he wiemɔ.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyi enyɔ lɛ amɛkɛshwie nɔ ekoŋŋ, kɛyashi amɛshɛ Betlehem. Be ni amɛshɛ jɛi lɛ, maŋ lɛ fɛɛ bu, ni yei lɛ kɛɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Naomi kɛ̃ nɛ?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Shi ehere amɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛkatsɛa mi Naomi dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ nyɛtsɛa mi Mara, ejaakɛ Ofe lɛ kɛ mi eye kɛ joomɔ tsɔ̃.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Mitee obɔ̃, shi Yehowa kɛ mi eku sɛɛ kɛba efolo. Mɛɛ hewɔ ni nyɛtsɛɔ mi Naomi, mi ni Yehowa kɛ mi eye kɛ joomɔ, ni Ofe lɛ eshwishwia mi shi lɛ?”

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Naomi ku esɛɛ kɛjɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba nɛ, lɛ kɛ eshaayoo Rut, Moabyoo lɛ. Ni be ni amɛba Betlehem lɛ abɔi akoko foo.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Boaz jɛ Betlehem eba, ni ehã nikpalɔi lɛ aekoo ekɛɛ, “Yehowa kɛ nyɛ ahi shi!” Ni amɛhere lɛ nɔ akɛ, “Yehowa ajɔɔ bo!”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Boaz bi etsulɔ ni ekɛto enikpalɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ oblayoo nɛ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Tsulɔ lɛ to he akɛ, “Moab oblayoo lɛ ni kɛ Naomi jɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ba lɛ ni.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ebakɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Ofainɛ, hã manyiɛ akoko kei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nikpalɔi lɛ asɛɛ maye kpɛkpɛo koni mabua naa.’ Ni kɛjɛ leebi tɔ̃ɔ ni eba lɛ, ejɔko ehe kwraa kɛbashi amrɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Boaz kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Mibi yoo, oobo toi? Kaaya ni oyaye kpɛkpɛo yɛ mɔ kroko ŋmɔshi, ni asaŋ okaje biɛ nɛɛ hu; shi moŋ kpɛtɛmɔ miblayei lɛ ahe yɛ biɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Ohiɛ ahi ŋmɔ ni amɛfoɔ akoko lɛ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni onyiɛ amɛsɛɛ. Miwo miblahii lɛ kitã akɛ mɔ ko akagba onaa. Kɛ kumai miiye bo lɛ, yaa gbɛi lɛ ahe koni oyanu nu ni oblahii lɛ eyayɛ lɛ eko.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rut ho ekula shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ni omli ejɔ ehã mi, ni otseɔ ohiɛ ohãa mi, mi mɔkpɔŋ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Boaz to he ehã lɛ akɛ, “Nii ni ofee ohã oshaayoo lɛ yɛ owu gbele lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, agba mi fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, bɔ ni oshi otsɛ kɛ onyɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni afɔ bo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ni oyiŋ kɛba mɛi ni oleee oto sa aŋɔɔ.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Yehowa ato bo nii ni otsu lɛ najiaŋ. Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mɔ abo ni obaba nɛɛ ato bo najiaŋ shishiishi.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rut kɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, omli jɔ hã mi, ejaakɛ oshɛje mimii, ni okɛ oweyoo ewie yɛ mlihilɛ naa, tsɛbelɛ mi kɛ oweyei lɛ ekoeko tete yeee hegbɔ.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Be ni shɛ niyeli be lɛ, Boaz kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Tsi oba biɛ koni obaye aboloo lɛ eko ni bo hu okɛ otrɔma lɛ atsɔ wain lɛ mli eko.” Ni Rut ba ebata nikpalɔi lɛ amasɛi; ni Boaz hã lɛ abelefɔ ni ashĩ lɛ eko, ni ekpe, ni etɔ, ni eshwɛ eko.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Be ni Rut te shi eyaaye kpɛkpɛo lɛ, Boaz wo eblahii lɛ shi akɛ, “Nyɛhãa eyea kpɛkpɛo lɛ yɛ kei ni afĩmɔ lɛ ateŋ hu; nyɛkanyafia lɛ.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Asaŋ nyɛfamɔa akoko lɛ eko yɛ kei lɛ amli nyɛshwiea shi nyɛhãa lɛ koni eye lɛ kpɛkpɛo; ni nyɛkawiea ehiɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Rut ye kpɛkpɛo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi. Egbee kpɛkpɛo ni eye lɛ, ni ena yiteremɔ aaafee kiloi nyɔŋma tsiimɔ.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ewo kɛtee maŋ lɛŋ, ni ekɛ kpɛkpɛo ni eyaye lɛ yatsɔ̃ɔ eshaayoo lɛ. Rut jie niyenii ni eye etɔ ni shwɛ lɛ ehã eshaayoo lɛ.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Naomi bi Rut akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ oyatsu nii yɛ? Namɔ ŋmɔshi otee oyaye kpɛkpɛo lɛ yɛ ŋmɛnɛ? Mɔ ni tse ehiɛ ehã bo lɛ, aaajɔɔ lɛ.” Rut gba eshaayoo lɛ mɔ ŋɔɔ ni eyatsu nii yɛ ekɛɛ, “Nuu ni miyatsu nii yɛ eŋɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ gbɛi ji Boaz.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Naomi kɛɛ eshaayoo lɛ akɛ, “Yehowa, mɔ ni hãko emɔbɔnalɛ sɛɛ afo yɛ hiɛkãalɔi kɛ gbohii fɛɛ anɔ lɛ ajɔɔ lɛ.” Naomi tee nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nuu lɛ wɔwekunyo ni; weku lɛ mli mɛi ni aaanyɛ akwɛ wɔ lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ji lɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rut, Moabyoo lɛ, kɛɛ, “Belɛ no hewɔ esaa ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Kpɛtɛmɔ mipaafoi lɛ ahe kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛaagbe minikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kɛɛ eshaayoo Rut akɛ, “Ehi, mibi, akɛ okɛ Boaz oblayei lɛ anyiɛ koni akagba onaa yɛ mɔ kroko ŋmɔshi.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Rut kpɛtɛ Boaz oblayei nitsulɔi lɛ ahe, ni eye kpɛkpɛo lɛ aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni agbe akoko kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ kpamɔ naa. Rut tee nɔ ekɛ eshaayoo lɛ hi shi.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Naomi kɛɛ eshaayoo Rut akɛ, “Mibi, jeee ja mitao he ko mihã bo ota ni ahi ahã bo?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Boaz mɔ ni okɛ eblayei lɛ yatsu nii lɛ, wɔwekunyo ni. Naa, eesha ekoko gbɛkɛnaashi nɛɛ yɛ ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, juu ohe, ni okpa mu, ni owo otade ni yɔɔ fɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛya ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ. Shi moŋ kaahã nuu lɛ miiyoo bo kɛyashi beyinɔ ni eeeye nii, ni eeenu nɔ ko dã.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ eyakã shi lɛ kadimɔ eshikamɔhe lɛ, ni oya oyakpa mama lɛ yɛ enane he, ni oho okã shi; ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni ofee.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Rut kɛɛ Naomi akɛ, “Nɔ ni okɛɛ mi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ mafee.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rut yiŋ etee ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ, ni eyafee bɔ ni eshaayoo lɛ kɛɛ lɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni Boaz eye nii, ni enu nɔ ko, ni emii eshɛ ehe lɛ, etee eyakã shi yɛ akoko ku lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Rut dɛke shi, ni eyakpa mama lɛ yɛ Boaz nane he, ni eho ekã shi.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Ni nyɔɔŋteŋ lɛ Boaz hɛle shi, ni etsɔ̃ ehe, ni naa, yoo ko kã enajiaŋshi.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ni Boaz bi akɛ, “Bo namɔŋ?” Ni Rut kɛɛ, “Mi oweyoo Rut ni. Ofainɛ, haa mi omama lɛ eko; ejaakɛ weku lɛ mli niyelɔ ji bo.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Boaz here nɔ akɛ, “Yehowa ajɔɔ bo, mibiyoo. Ejurɔ ni ofee sɛɛkpee nɛɛ fe tsutsu nɔ lɛ tete akɛ onyiɛɛɛ oblahii asɛɛ, niiatsɛmɛi jio, ohiafoi jio.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Ni agbɛnɛ, mibiyoo, kaashe gbeyei. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni okɛɔ lɛ mafee mahã bo, ejaakɛ mimaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ le akɛ yoo kpakpa ji bo.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Eyɛ mli lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ owu lɛ wekunyo ni aaanyɛ aŋɔ bo ji mi moŋ nɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ niyelɔ lɛ eko yɛ ni eyeɔ dani mi miyeɔ.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Hii shi ni je atsɛre. Kɛji je tsɛre ni eeefee niyelɔ gbɛnaanii lɛ ehã bo lɛ, ehi; shi kɛji esumɔɔɔ akɛ efee lɛ, no lɛ gbii abɔ kɛ̃ ni Yehowa hiɛ kã nɛɛ mafee. Kã shi ni je atsɛre.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Rut ho ekã Boaz najiashi kɛyashi jetsɛremɔ. Ni ete shi dani hiɛ gbele bɔ ni aaanyɛ mɔ ayoo. Shi Boaz kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Kaahã mɔ ko le akɛ yoo ko eba ŋmãagbeemɔhe nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Boaz kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Okɛ mama ni okɛha oyiteŋ lɛ aba, ni olɛɛ mii.” Rut kɛ mama lɛ ba, ni elɛɛ mli, ni Boaz ka akoko susumɔ tsenei ekpaa ni etsiimɔ aaafee kiloi nyɔŋmai enyɔ ewo mli, ni ekɛtere Rut, ni ekɛtee maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Rut kɛɛ akɛ, “Ehã mi akoko tsenei ekpaa nɛɛ ejaakɛ ekɛɛ, ‘Ebɛ ni okɛ odɛ̃ folo yaa oshaayoo lɛ ŋɔɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kɛɛ Rut akɛ, “Mɛɛ mibi, kɛyashi beyinɔ ni ooona bɔ ni sane lɛ naa aaayakpa; ejaakɛ nuu lɛ ejɔŋ ehe ja ena sane lɛ naa ŋmɛnɛ.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Boaz tee maŋ agbo lɛ naa ni ji amɛkoishi lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ naa niyelɔ lɛ ni Boaz tsi etã lɛ miiho. Kɛkɛ ni Boaz tsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Anyɛmi nuu, ofainɛ, baata shi fioo.” Ni eba ebata shi.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Boaz tsɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋma kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛfai nɛ, nyɛbataraa shi fioo.” Amɛbatara shi.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Ni Boaz kɛɛ niyelɔ lɛ akɛ, “Shikpɔŋ kuku ni ji wɔnyɛmi Elimelek shikpɔŋ lɛ, Naomi ni jɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ba lɛ miihɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ mikɛɛ mawo otoi nɔ koni ohe yɛ mɛi ni tara biɛ nɛɛ kɛ mimaŋ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ ooosumɔ ni oye mɔ ni egbo lɛ nii lɛ wiemɔ, ni kɛji osumɔɔɔ hu hã male; ejaakɛ mɔ ko bɛ ni eyeɔ nii lɛ fe bo; ni osɛɛ dani mi.” Niyelɔ lɛ jie naa ekɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, masumɔ maye.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Boaz kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Gbi nɔ ni oooŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ Naomi dɛŋ lɛ, belɛ ooŋɔ Rut, Moabyoo lɛ, ni ji mɔ ni egbo lɛ ŋa lɛ hu oofata he nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ, koni mɔ ni egbo lɛ gbɛi akagbo yɛ egboshinii lɛ he.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni niyelɔ lɛ hã hetoo akɛ, “Minyɛŋ maye nii lɛ, ejaakɛ kɛji miye lɛ tɔ̃tɔ̃mɔ baaba, mi diɛŋtsɛ migboshiniiyeli mli. Ŋɔɔ migbɛnaanii lɛ ohã ohe.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni niyelɔ lɛ kɛɛ Boaz akɛ eye nii lɛ, niyelɔ lɛ jie etokota ekɛhã Boaz.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Boaz kɛɛ onukpai lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “nyɛ ji midasefoi ŋmɛnɛ akɛ miŋɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ji Elimelek nɔ, kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ji Kilion kɛ Malon nɔ lɛ yɛ Naomi dɛŋ.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Rut, Moabyoo, ni ji Malon ŋa lɛ hu miiŋɔ lɛ, ni etsɔ̃ miŋa, koni mɔ ni egbo lɛ gbɛi akagbo yɛ egboshinii he, ni egbɛi akalaaje yɛ enyɛmimɛi ateŋ kɛ emaŋ koishi hu, nyɛ ji odasefoi ŋmɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ni maŋbii ni yɔɔ maŋ koi lɛ shi lɛ kɛ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Wɔji odasefoi! Yehowa ahã yoo lɛ ni baa owe lɛ atamɔ Rahel kɛ Lea ni amɛyi enyɔ lɛ pɛ mli Israel we lɛ jɛ lɛ. Otsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ agbo yɛ Efrata, ni ogbɛi ahehe yɛ Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Ni shwiei ni Yehowa aaahã oblayoo nɛɛ awo ahã bo lɛ, ahã owe lɛ atsɔ̃ tamɔ Tamar kɛ Yuda bi Perez we.” Boaz shwiei

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Boaz ŋɔ Rut ni etsɔ̃ eŋa; ni Boaz ta Rut he, ni Yehowa hã ena musu ni efɔ binuu.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ni maŋ lɛŋ yei lɛ kɛɛ Naomi akɛ, “Yijiemɔ ahã Yehowa! Ejaakɛ ehã bo gboshiniiyelɔ kɛ nabi ŋmɛnɛ. Ehã gbɛkɛ lɛ gbɛi ahehe yɛ Israel.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Gbekɛ nɛɛ, eeehã owala sɛɛ atsɛ, ni eeekwɛ bo yɛ ogbɔlɛ mli; ejaakɛ oshaayoo ni sumɔɔ bo, ni ehi hã bo fe bihii kpawo tete lɛ, ni fɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Ni Naomi he abifao lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ ŋmɛ ekpɔkɔiaŋ, ni etsɔ̃ abifao lɛ kwɛlɔ.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Ni Naomi kuuŋyei lɛ nya amɛkɛɛ, “Afɔ binuu ahã Naomi eei!” Ni amɛwo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ Obed. Obed nɛɛ lɛ efɔ Ishai, ni Ishai hu fɔ Maŋtsɛ David.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Nuu ko hi shi yɛ Rama yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ. Egbɛi ji Elkana, ni etsɛ gbɛi ji Yeroham. Zuf bi Tohu bi Elihu bi ji Elkana nɛɛ.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Elkana yɛ ŋamɛi enyɔ, mɔ kome gbɛi ji Hana, ni mɔ kome lɛ hu gbɛi ji Penina. Penina yɛ bii shi Hana bɛ bi.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Daa afi lɛ Elkana yaa Shilo eyasɔleɔ ni eshãa afɔle ehãa Yehowa ni ji Taiatsɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Eli bihii enyɔ lɛ, ni ji Hofni kɛ Finehas, miiye osɔfoi kɛha Yehowa yɛ Shilo.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Gbi fɛɛ gbi ni Elkana baaya eyashã afɔle lɛ, ehãa eŋa Penina kɛ Penina bihii lɛ kɛ ebiyei lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ loo kukuli.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Shi Hana lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ Elkana sumɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ nɛ, shi loo kukuli kome nɔŋŋ ehãa lɛ hu, ejaakɛ lɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hãko lɛ bi.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni nibii tee nɔ daa afi. Shii abɔ fɛɛ ni amɛyaa Yehowa we lɛ, ebienyɛ Penina yeɔ ehe fɛo. Kɛkɛ lɛ efeɔ Hana yaafo, ni eyeee nii.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Kɛfee nakai lɛ ewu Elkana kɛɔ Hana akɛ, “Hana, mɛɛba ni ofoɔ ni asaŋ oyeee nii? Mɛɛba ni oyeɔ otsui? Mihiii hãaa bo fe musuŋ bihii nyɔŋma?” Hana kɛ Eli

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Hana wo shi ekɛɛ, “Yehowa Taiatsɛ, kɛji oookwɛ mi, oweyoo, mimanehulu nɛɛ, ni oookai mi, ni ohiɛ kpaŋ mi, oweyoo, nɔ shi moŋ ooohã mi, oweyoo, binuu lɛ, no lɛ majɔɔ enɔ mahã bo, Yehowa, ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ; ni asooyi naa esaŋ eyiteŋ.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Shi Hana miiwie yɛ etsui mli. Anuuu egbee akɛ fe enaabu kɛkɛ ni tsɔmɔɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Eli susu akɛ dãa Hana etɔ.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Ni Eli kɛɛ Hana akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ ni oootɔ dãa kɛyashi? Hã ni owain lɛ atserɛ yɛ ohiɛ.”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Kaabu mi, oweyoo akɛ yoo yakagbɔmɔ ko shi mikɔmɔ kɛ mlila ni awoɔ sɔŋŋ naa miwieɔ yɛ kɛbashi amrɔ nɛɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Eli to he hã Hana ekɛɛ, “Omanye abla bo, ni Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ahã bo nii ni obi lɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Hana kɛɛ Eli akɛ, “Ofainɛ, ohã misane nɛɛ akã otsui nɔ.” Kɛkɛ ni Hana yiŋ etee, ni agbɛnɛ eyatao nɔ ko eye, ni ehiɛ efeee tɔtɔɔtɔ dɔŋŋ. Samuel fɔmɔ kɛ enɔjɔɔmɔ hã Nyɔŋmɔ

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ Elkana kɛ eŋãmɛi lɛ kɛ ebii lɛ te shi leebi maŋkpa, be ni amɛtee amɛyaja Yehowa sɛɛ lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee Rama. Elkana kɛ eŋa Hana yawɔ, ni Yehowa mɔbɔnalɛ naa lɛ,

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: be ni shɛɔ afi naakplɔ lɛ Hana ena musu, ni efɔ binuu. Hana wo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ Samuel, ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ miba lɛ yɛ Yehowa dɛŋ.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Be ni afi shɛ lɛ, Elkana kɛ eŋa kɛ ebii lɛ tee koni amɛyashã daa afi naakplɔ afɔle yɛ shi krɛdɛɛ ni ewo lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Shi Hana eyaaa eko ejaakɛ ekɛɛ ewu Elkana akɛ, “Mamɛ kɛyashi matse gbekɛ lɛ fufɔ dani mikɛ lɛ ayapue yɛ Yehowa hiɛ koni ehi jɛi kwraa.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Elkana to he ekɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ; feemɔ nɔ ni hi yɛ ohiɛ. Hii shi kɛyashi oootse abifao lɛ fufɔ. Yehowa ahã eshiwoo lɛ aba mli kɛkɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Hana hi shi, ni ekwɛ abifao lɛ kɛyashi etse lɛ fufɔ lɛ.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: ni Hana kɛɛ Eli akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, ookai mi. Mi ji yoo lɛ ni badamɔ omasɛi yɛ biɛ nɛɛ nyɛsɛɛ ko, ni ebakpa Yehowa fai ni eba lɛ nii lɛ.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Gbekɛ nɛɛ he fai mibakpa lɛ, ni Yehowa ehã mi nɔ ni mibaba lɛ lɛ hu.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, miijɔɔ enɔ kwraa miihã Yehowa. Mikɛ lɛ miike Yehowa ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni amɛja Yehowa yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hana sɔle yɛ jɛi ni ekɛɛ “Yehowa, ohã mimli efili mi, ni minyɛ mihiɛ nɔ miwo. Mibaŋmɔ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ, ejaakɛ ohere mi.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: “Mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ko bɛ tamɔ bo, Yehowa, osɛɛ lɛ mɔ ko bɛ dɔŋŋ; Mɔ ko bɛ hewalɛ tamɔ wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkawiea kɛ henɔwomɔ nɛkɛ dɔŋŋ; nyɛkawiea kɛ hetsɔ̃ɔmɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ nilelɔ ni, ni lɛ ekojoɔ adesai anifeemɔnii.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Kãkãlɔi lɛ agãitsei lɛ ekumɔ, ni mɛi ni he waaa lɛ ena hewalɛ.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni kulɛ amɛyeɔ nii amɛtɔrɔɔ lɛ, amɛmiiye apaa yɛ daaŋ ŋmãa hewɔ, ni mɛi ni kulɛ amɛwɔɔ hɔmɔ lɛ, amɛwɔɔɔ hɔmɔ dɔŋŋ. Naa, kene lɛ efɔ kpawo, ni biianyɛ lɛ moŋ etsɔ̃ mɔ kome mɔ.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Yehowa ni gbeɔ mɔ, ni etsiɛɔ mɔ hiɛ hu; ehãa ayaa gbohiiaje, ni ehãa akpaleɔ abaa ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Yehowa ni hãa ayeɔ ohia, ni ehãa anaa nii hu; Lɛ ebaa mɔ shi, asaŋ lɛ ewoɔ mɔ nɔ hu.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Eteɔ ohiafo shi kɛjɛɔ mlu mli, ni ewoɔ mɔ ni efi lɛ nɔ yɛ tumo nɔ, koni amɛ kɛ abladei atara shi, ni amɛna sɛii ni yɔɔ nyam anɔ amɛtara, ejaakɛ je lɛ shishitoo lɛ enɔ ni, ni lɛ etswa je lɛ ema nɔ.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Eeebaa enɔkwafoi lɛ ayi, shi mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ amɛhiɛ aaakpãtã yɛ duŋ mli, ejaakɛ jeee gbɔmɔ diɛŋtsɛ hewalɛ naa eyeɔ kunim yɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Yehowa henyɛlɔi lɛ, aaakumɔ amɛ dukuduku ashwie shi; eeehã ŋwɛi ashimɔ awo amɛ; Yehowa ji je lɛ fɛɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔ; ebaahã emaŋtsɛ lɛ ana hewalɛ, ni emɔ ni efɔ lɛ mu lɛ eeehã eye kunim.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elkana ku esɛɛ etee ewe lɛ yɛ Rama, ni eshi gbekɛnuu fioo, Samuel, lɛ koni esɔmɔ Yehowa yɛ Osɔfo Eli shishi. Osɔfo Eli bihii lɛ

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: loo osɔfoi lɛ agbɛnaanii ni sa akɛ amɛhe yɛ maŋ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni afeɔ ji akɛ kɛji mɔ ko ba afɔleshãa lɛ, osɔfo lɛ tsulɔ baa, be mli ni ahoɔ loo lɛ, ni ehiɛ faka kɛ enyanyɔji etɛ̃.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: Tsulɔ lɛ kɛ faka lɛ tsuɔ loo ni ahoɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛnsi loo dadesɛŋ loo kukwɛi lɛ mli, ni loo fɛɛ loo ni faka lɛ baatsu kɛje kpo lɛ osɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ. Nɛkɛ afeɔ Israelbii fɛɛ ni yaa afɔleshãa yɛ Shilo lɛ.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ be mli ni anako ashã loo lɛ mli fɔ lɛ tete lɛ, osɔfo lɛ tsulɔ lɛ baa ni ebakɛɔ mɔ ni shãa afɔle lɛ akɛ, “Jiemɔ loo ohã ni ayashã ahã osɔfo lɛ ejaakɛ esumɔɔɔ loo ni ahoo lɛ, eetao loo lɛ eŋmɔŋ.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Kɛji mɔ ni shãa afɔle lɛ kɛɛ tsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ koni ashã fɔ lɛ dã; no sɛɛ koni ojie loo lɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni osumɔɔ” lɛ, tsulɔ lɛ toɔ he akɛ, “Dabida, jiemɔ loo lɛ ohã nɔŋŋ, kɛjeee nakai lɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ majie loo lɛ ekãa naa.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Eli bihii lɛ anɔsha lɛ da yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ejaakɛ amɛhiɛ eyasɔɔɔ nii ni akɛshãa afɔle ahãa Yehowa lɛ. Samuel yɛ Shilo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Samuel sɔmɔɔ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. Ewoɔ tsitsinɔhaanii ni akɛ klala kpɛ, ni efiɔ emliteŋ.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Enyɛ kpɛɔ atade yuu pɛmpɛoo ko, ni ekɛbahãa Samuel koni ewo kɛji ekɛ ewu ba daa afi afɔleshãa lɛ.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Kɛji amɛba lɛ, Eli jɔɔ Elkana kɛ eŋa lɛ ni ekɛɔ akɛ, “Yehowa ahã yoo nɛɛ awo shwiei ahã bo yɛ ebi nɛɛ ni ejɔɔ enɔ ehã Yehowa hewɔ.” Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee amɛmaŋ.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Yehowa jɔɔ Hana, ni efɔ Samuel sɛɛ bihii etɛ̃ kɛ biyei enyɔ hu. Ni oblanyo fioo, Samuel, lɛ bada yɛ Yehowa we lɛ. Eli kɛ ebihii lɛ

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Eli egbɔ naakpa; ni ababɔɔ lɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ebihii lɛ feɔ Israelbii lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛkɛ yei ni batsuɔ nii yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ shi lɛ wɔɔ.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Nyɛkafea nakai kɔkɔɔkɔ, mibii. Saji ni minuɔ yɛ Yehowa webii anaa yɛ nyɛhe lɛ, ehiii.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Kɛji gbɔmɔ fee enyɛmi gbɔmɔ esha lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ ji mɔ ni kojoɔ lɛ; shi kɛji gbɔmɔ fee esha eshi Yehowa lɛ, namɔ po ni aaakpa fai ahã lɛ?” Shi oblahii lɛ eyabooo amɛtsɛ, Eli, toi ejaakɛ Yehowa eto akɛ ebaagbe amɛ.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Oblanyo fioo, Samuel, lɛ bada ni esane sa gbɔmɛi kɛ Yehowa fɛɛ hiɛ. Agba ashi Eli weku

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Gbalɔ ko ba Eli ŋɔɔ be ko ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, Mijie mihe mitsɔ̃ɔ otsɛ we lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ Ijipt akɛ Farao nyɔji lɛ.

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba mɔ ni nyɛhiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mi hu migbɛfaŋnii ni yɔɔ gbee afɔlei kɛ niyenii afɔlei lɛ amli lɛ anɔ, be mli ni miwo nyɛ he kitã; ni obuɔ obihii lɛ moŋ fe mi, ni nyɛkɛ mimaŋbii lɛ afɔle fɛɛ afɔle mli nii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ lɛɔ nyɛ moŋ nyɛhe lɛ?

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mi, Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mikɛɛ akɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛɛ akɛ owe lɛ kɛ otsɛmɛi awe lɛ ni baasɔ̃mɔ mi akɛ osɔfoi kɛya naanɔ, shi agbɛnɛ miigbala nakai shiwoo lɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ mɛi ni buɔ mi lɛ, mawo amɛhiɛ nyam: shi mɛi ni ebuuu mi lɛ, abuŋ amɛ ahaŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Naa, be lɛ miiba, ni mibagbe owe lɛ kɛ otsɛmɛiawe lɛ mli bii fɛɛ yɛ amɛblahiiaŋ koni akana nuumo yɛ oweku mli.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ni okɛ hejaramɔ baana shweremɔ ni abaahã Israel ashwere lɛ: shi owe lɛ nuumo ehiŋ mli kɛaatee naanɔ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Ni owekunyo ni mahã ashwɛ ni esɔmɔ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ naa lɛ tete, ehiŋmɛii baajwara, ni ebaaye awerɛho kɛteke nɔ; ni shwiei fɛɛ ni abaawo yɛ owe lɛ baagbo akranaŋ naa gbele.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni baaba obihii enyɔ lɛ, Hofni kɛ Finehas, nɔ lɛ baatsɔ̃ okadi ahã bo. No ji akɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛaagboi gbi kome.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Matee osɔfo anɔkwafo ko shi mahã mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe, mɔ ni baafee miyiŋtoo kɛ mitsuinaanii, ni mahã ewo shwiei ni shishi etaŋ, mɛi ni baasɔ̃mɔ yɛ mɔ ni mifɔ lɛ mu lɛ hiɛ daa.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni mahã ashwɛ yɛ owe lɛ aaaba abakoto gbɔmɔ nɛɛ koni ebaba edɛŋ jwiɛtɛi loo aboloo akwaabɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Miikpa bo fai ni ohã mi osɔfo nitsumɔ lɛ mli nii lɛ eko matsu bɔ ni afee ni mana midaaŋ ŋmaa kɛkɛ.’ ”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: ni Yehowa kane lɛ ma nɔ lolo ni enako egbo, ni Samuel hu kã shi yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli he ni Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa tsɛ Samuel ekɛɛ, “Samuel! Samuel!” Ehere nɔ akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, Naa mi!”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Samuel sha foi kɛtee Eli ŋɔɔ eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, naa mi; minu akɛ ootsɛ mi.” Shi Eli kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Mitsɛko bo, mibi; kuu osɛɛ ni oyakã shi.” No hewɔ lɛ, Samuel tee ni eyakã shi.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Yehowa saa tsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ ekɛɛ, “Samuel!” Samuel te shi ni etee Eli ŋɔɔ eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, naa mi; minu akɛ ootsɛ mi.” Eli kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mitsɛko bo, mibi; kuu osɛɛ ni oyakã shi ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Samuel nako ale Yehowa ni asaŋ Yehowa kɛ lɛ ewieko dã.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Yehowa saa etsɛ Samuel nɔ ni tĩa shii etɛ̃; ni Samuel te shi etee Eli ŋɔɔ eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, naa mi, minu akɛ ootsɛ mi.” Kɛkɛ ni Eli bayoo sɛɛ agbɛnɛ akɛ Yehowa ni tsɛɔ oblanyo fioo lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Yaakã shi; kɛji atsɛ bo ekoŋŋ lɛ, heremɔ nɔ akɛ, ‘Wiemɔ Yehowa, shi mi, otsulɔ, miibo bo toi!’ ” Kɛkɛ ni Samuel tee eyakã shi yɛ ewɔɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Yehowa ba ni ebadamɔ shi, ni etsɛ lɛ tamɔ tsuutsu lɛ akɛ, “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel here nɔ akɛ, “Wiemɔ, shi otsulɔ miibo toi.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Naa, mibafee nɔ titri ko yɛ Israel, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaanu he lɛ he aajɔ̃ ehe.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nakai gbi lɛ mahã nibii fɛɛ ni miwie yɛ Eli we lɛ he lɛ aba mli kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyashi naagbee.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Mikɛɛ lɛ mito akɛ mibagbala ewe lɛ toi kɛya naanɔ yɛ nɔ sha ni ele lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ ebihii lɛ bɔ musu amɛshi mi, Nyɔŋmɔ, shi etutuuu ehiɛ ewooo amɛ.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mikã Eli we lɛ he kitã akɛ kɛji akɛ gbee afɔle loo niyenii afɔle ko aaakpãta Eli we lɛ nɔ sha lɛ kɛyashi naanɔ fĩi.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel ho ekã shi kɛyashi je tsɛre ni egbele Yehowa we lɛ shinai lɛ. Samuel she he gbeyei akɛ eeegba Eli ninaa lɛ.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Shi Eli tsɛ Samuel ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mibi Samuel,” Ehere nɔ akɛ, “Naa mi.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni Yehowa kɛɛ bo lɛ? Kaashiu mi nɔ. Kɛji oshiu mi wiemɔi fɛɛ ni ekɛ bo wie lɛ eko nɔ lɛ, Yehowa baagbala otoi yɛ no hewɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel gba Eli nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eshiuuu lɛ sane lɛ eko nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni Eli to he ekɛɛ, “Lɛ ji Yehowa, nɔ ni hi yɛ lɛ ehiɛ lɛ efee!”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samuel bada, ni Yehowa kɛ lɛ yɛ, ni ehãaa Samuel naa wiemɔ ko afee yaka.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɛi ni yɔɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ, kɛjɛ Dan aahu kɛyashwie Beersheba, na le akɛ Samuel lɛ Yehowa gbalɔ anɔkwafo ni.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Yehowa kã he etsɔ̃ɔ ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ ejieɔ ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ Samuel yɛ Shilo. Ni kɛji Samuel wie lɛ, Israel fɛɛ boɔ lɛ toi.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ fã ta koni amɛkɛ Israelbii lɛ ayawu. Israelbii lɛ yagba ta yɛ Ebenezer, ni Filistibii lɛ hu gba ta yɛ Afek.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, atsu atee Shilo, ni ayawo Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛ enɔ kerubim lɛ, ni ji Yehowa sɛ̃i lɛ, kɛba. Hofni kɛ Finehas, ni ji Eli bihii enyɔ lɛ, fata he ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Be ni Israel tabilɔi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ ta lɛ naa kɛba amɛshitoohe lɛ, Israel maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ni Yehowa ŋmɛ gbɛ ni Filistibii lɛ anine tsɔ̃ wɔnɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛkɛ? Nyɛhãa ni wɔyaŋɔa Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yɛ Shilo kɛbaa biɛ koni ebahi wɔteŋ, koni ehere wɔyiwala yɛ wɔhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ bashɛ shitoohe lɛ mli lɛ, Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ bɔ oshe waa bɔ ni ehã shikpɔŋ hoso.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Be ni Filistibii lɛ nu oshebɔɔ lɛ, amɛbi akɛ, “Mɛɛ oshe abɔɔ waa yɛ Hebribii lɛ ashitoohe lɛ mli nɛkɛ nɛɛ?” Be ni amɛbana amɛle akɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ebashɛ Israelbii lɛ ata lɛ mli lɛ,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ she gbeyei, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Jemawɔŋ ko eba amɛta lɛ mli. Sane eye wɔ ei! Nɛkɛ nɔ ko bako dã.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Sane eye wɔ! Namɔ po aaajie wɔ yɛ jemawɔji ni ahe yɔɔ gbeyei nɛɛ adɛŋ? Jemawɔji nɛɛ ni hã haomɔ ba Ijiptbii lɛ anɔ yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Nyɛwajea nyɛhe, Filistibii, ni nyɛfea hii koni nyɛkatsɔmɔ Hebribii lɛ anyɔji tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛye amɛ nyɔŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ashɔ̃, ni Hofni kɛ Finehas, Eli bihii enyɔ lɛ, nyɔ. Eli gbele

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Benyaminnyo ko jo foi kɛjɛ ta lɛ naa kɛba Shilo nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ atade ni etserɛ kɛ eyiteŋ su.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Nuu nɛɛ bashɛ shi be mli ni Eli ta sɛ̃i nɔ yɛ agbo lɛ naa ni eesra, ejaakɛ etsui enyɔɔɔ emli yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hewɔ. Nuu lɛ bote maŋ lɛŋ ni be ni ebabɔ amaniɛ ni ekɛjɛ ta lɛ naa lɛ, maŋ lɛ fɛɛ wo yara.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Bɔfo lɛ here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Israel ejo foi yɛ Filistibii lɛ ahiɛ, wɔmaŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo diɛŋtsɛ enyɔ. Obihii, Hofni kɛ Finehas hu enyɔ, ni asaŋ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ashɔ̃.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ tã ni atsi nɛkɛ pɛ ni Eli kpa yɛ esɛi lɛ nɔ eyagbee esɛɛgbɛ yɛ maŋ agbo lɛ he, ni ekuɛŋ wu kũ, ni egbo, ejaakɛ egbɔ ni egbɔmɔtso tsii. Nakai be mli lɛ Eli ekwɛ Israelbii anɔ afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ. Finehas ŋa lɛ hu gbele

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Eli shaayoo, ni ji Finehas ŋa lɛ, hiɛ musu, ni eshɛ efɔmɔ be etã. Be ni yoo lɛ nu amaniɛ lɛ akɛ ashɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ, ni eshaanuu lɛ kɛ ewu lɛ fɛɛ hu egboi lɛ, fɔmɔ ta ehe amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni eho esɔ̃ shi ni efɔ.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Be ni yoofɔyoo lɛ heɔ egbo yɛ fɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, yei ni yɔɔ emasɛi ni amɛwaa lɛ kɛ fɔmɔ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei, shi ofɔ binuu.” Shi efooo mli, asaŋ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ efɔ̃ɔɔ nɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Be ni Filistibii lɛ shɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ, amɛwo kɛjɛ Ebenezer kɛtee Ashdod,

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: ni amɛkɛtee nyɔŋmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni egbɛi ji Dagon lɛ we lɛ, ni amɛkɛyama Dagon amãgã lɛ masɛi.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi maŋkpa be ni Ashdodbii te shi lɛ, naa, Dagon amãgã lɛ ni ekpa egbee shi, ni ehiɛ bu shikpɔŋ yɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Ashdodbii lɛ wo Dagon amãgã lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ ma emaahe lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
