translation_verse: Shi enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi maaŋkpa be ni Ashdodbii lɛ te shi ekoŋŋ lɛ, naa, Dagon ekpa egbee shi ekoŋŋ, ni ehiɛ bu shikpɔŋ yɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ. Eyitso kɛ eniji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ hu etserɛ yɛ ehe, ni amɛjwere kpoku lɛ nɔ. Dagon amãgã kuku lɛ kɛkɛ eshwɛ.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ ni Dagon wulɔmɛi, kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hu ni boteɔ Dagon we lɛ, enaaa Dagon kpoku lɛ nɔ yɛ Ashdod kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Yehowa piŋ Ashdodbii lɛ waa diɛŋtsɛ. Ehã abua fuufuu amɛ, ni gbeyei mɔmɔ amɛ yɛ Ashdod maŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ, kɛ ekpokpai anɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Be ni Ashdod hii lɛ na nɔ ni eba lɛ, amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Akahã Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ miihi wɔŋɔɔ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ wɔ kɛ wɔnyɔŋmɔ Dagon fɛɛ miiye kɛ joomɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsu ni ayakpee Filistibii lɛ alumɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛba, ni amɛbi amɛ akɛ, “Te wɔfee Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ tɛŋŋ?” Lumɛi lɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Awo Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛba Gat.” No hewɔ lɛ, awo Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛtee Gat.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ eyashɛ Gat sɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ abua piŋ maŋ lɛ mli mɛi bibii kɛ mɛi wuji fɛɛ, ni ekɛgbala Gatbii atoi, ni enɛ hã amɛ jijaa.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhã awo Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛtee Ekron. Shi be ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yashɛ jɛi lɛ, Ekronbii lɛ bolɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Naa, akɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ eba wɔŋɔɔ koni ebagbe wɔ kɛ wɔbii.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsu ni ayakpee Filistibii lɛ alumɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛbakpe, ni amɛkɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa akɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ akua sɛɛ kɛyaa he ni ejɛ koni ekabagbe wɔ kɛ wɔbii.” Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ejijaa ni yɛ gbeyei; ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ amɛ miiye kɛ joomɔ ni naa wa yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni gboiii lɛ abua fuufuu amɛ, ni maŋ lɛ bolɔ waa amɛtsɛ akɛ ahere amɛ.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ye nyɔji kpawo yɛ Filistibii lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Filistibii lɛ kpee amɛsɔfoi kɛ mɛi ni feɔ nii ni amɛgbaa lɛ, ni amɛbi amɛ akɛ, “Te wɔfee Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ tɛŋŋ? Nyɛtsɔa wɔ nɔ ni sa akɛ wɔkɛfata adeka lɛ he ni wɔkɛku sɛɛ kɛya he ni ejɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ to he akɛ, “Kɛji nyɛmiikpale Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛya lɛ, nyɛkahãa akɛ adeka lɛ miiyaa efolo. Ja nyɛkɛ afɔle fata he kɛtee nyɛyahã Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ akɛ nyɛye sɔ̃; no dani nyɛhe aaatã, ni asaŋ nyɛaale nɔ hewɔ ni ekpako nyɛ piŋmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ bi akɛ, “Mɛni ji sɔ̃yeli afɔle ni wɔkɛyahã lɛ?” Osɔfoi lɛ jie naa akɛ, “Abua ni fũufuu nyɛ lɛ henɔ nibii enumɔ ni akɛ shika fee, kɛ kwakwei hu enumɔ ni akɛ shika fee yɛ Filistibii amaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ayikulɛ naa, ejaakɛ hela kometoo lɛ nɔŋŋ ye nyɛ kɛ nyɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛfea abua ni fũufuu nyɛ lɛ henɔ kɛ kwakwei ni bafite nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ henɔ okadii, asaŋ nyɛwoa Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Eko lɛ eeegbɔjɔ piŋmɔ lɛ mli ehã nyɛ kɛ nyɛjemawɔji lɛ kɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ hu.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ nyɛkpliŋ nyɛtsui tamɔ Ijiptbii lɛ kɛ amɛmaŋtsɛ lɛ fee lɛ? Kwɛ, be ni ehã amɛna amɛnii ni amɛleee sɛɛ lɛ, bɛ amɛŋmɛɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe ni amɛtee?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛfea shwiili hee; nyɛmɔa tsinayei enyɔ ni aaye amɛ fufɔ lolo, asaŋ ni apã eyako amɛkuɛ dã, ni nyɛfimɔa amɛ nyɛwo shwiili lɛ naa. Amɔmɔ tsinabii lɛ yɛ amɛnyɛmɛi lɛ ahe kɛya shĩa.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, awo Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ama shwiili lɛ nɔ. Ato shika nibii ni akɛyaahã Yehowa akɛ sɔ̃yeli he afɔle lɛ awo adeka fioo mli, ni akɛma Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ masɛi, ni nyɛjie lɛ gbɛ ni eya.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Nyɛkwɛa eyisɛɛ. Kɛji adeka lɛ wo ehiɛ ema lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ kɛtee Bet-Shemesh lɛ, no tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ji mɔ ni ye wɔ awui kpeteŋkple nɛɛ lɛ; shi kɛji shwiili lɛ eyaaa jɛi lɛ belɛ wɔna wɔle akɛ jeee Yehowa piŋ wɔ lɛ, shi osharã ko kɛkɛ ni basharã wɔ.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Amɛfee bɔ ni akɛɛ amɛ lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ tsinayei enyɔ ni aaye amɛfufɔ lolo, ni amɛfimɔ amɛ amɛwo shwiili lɛ naa, ni amɛŋa amɛbii lɛ ayi yɛ shĩa.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Amɛwo Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ amɛma shwiili lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo adeka lɛ ni amɛto shika kwakwei lɛ kɛ shika abua lɛ amɛwo mli lɛ hu amɛma shwiili lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Tsinai lɛ yi tɛmpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛwo amɛyi amɛma Bet-Shemesh tɔ̃ɔ. Be ni amɛyaa nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ belɛ tsinai lɛ miibolɔ. Amɛgbaaa ninejurɔ lɛ, amɛgbaaa abɛku hu. Filistibii alumɛi lɛ nyiɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛ tsinai lɛ kɛ shwiili lɛ sɛɛ aahu kɛyashɛ Bet-Shemesh husu lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Bet-Shemeshbii miiku ŋmãa nɛkɛ be mli yɛ gɔji ateŋ jɔɔ lɛ mli. Be ni amɛyaawo amɛhiɛ nɔ lɛ, naa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ; amɛnya jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filistibii amaŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ na nɔ ni afee lɛ, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛtee Ekron nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Abua ni fuufuu Filistibii lɛ henɔ shika nii ni Filistibii lɛ fee lɛ, bɔ ni amɛkɛyahã Yehowa akɛ amɛsɔ̃yeli he afɔle yɛ maji lɛ agbɛii amli nɛ: Ashdod nɔ ekome, kɛ Gaza nɔ ekome, kɛ Ashkelon nɔ ekome.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Nakai nɔŋŋ akɛ shika kwakwei lɛ hu yahã yɛ Filistibii lɛ amaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛmɛi enumɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ ayikulɛ naa. Maji ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe kɛ akrowai fɛɛ shi nɔ. Tɛ kpeteŋkple lɛ ni akɛ Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ma nɔ yɛ Yoshua, Bet-Shemeshnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ jɛi eeye sane nɛɛ he odase kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ hã BetShemeshbii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ; “Namɔ po aaanyɛ Yehowa Nyɔŋmɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ nɛɛ hiɛ adamɔ? Ni kɛ adeka lɛ jɛ wɔŋɔɔ lɛ, namɛi aŋɔɔ po eeeya?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Bet-Shemeshbii lɛ tsu bɔfoi kɛtee Kiriat-Yearimbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni amɛyakɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa, Filistibii lɛ ekpale Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ amɛkɛbahã wɔ. Nyɛbaŋɔa kɛyaa.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Kiriat-Yearimbii lɛ bawo Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ, ni amɛkɛtee Abinadab we lɛ ni ma Kiriat-Yearim gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli; ni amɛwo Abinadab bi Eleazar osɔfo koni ebu Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ he. Samuel kwɛ Israel nɔ

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji nyɛmiikpale kɛba Yehowa ŋɔɔ kɛ nyɛtsui fɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ nyɛjiea maŋsɛɛ jemawɔji lɛ kɛ Astarte amãgãi lɛ hu ni nyɛyɔɔ yɛ nyɛteŋ lɛ nyɛsherɛa nyɛshwiea koni nyɛkɛ nyɛhe ahãa Yehowa kwraa; asaŋ koni nyɛsɔmɔ ekome too; ni lɛ hu eeejie nyɛ yɛ Filistibii lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ damɔ wiemɔ nɛɛ nɔ ni amɛ jie Baal kɛ Astarte amãgãi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ amɛsherɛ amɛshwie, ni amɛsɔmɔ Yehowa kome pɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyabuaa nyɛhe naa yɛ Mizpa, ni masɔle makpa Yehowa fai mahã nyɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ Mizpa. Amɛyɛ nu amɛshwie shi yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni amɛhi ŋmãa nakai gbi lɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Wɔtɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ.” Ni Samuel hi Mizpa, ni ekojo Israelbii lɛ ateŋ saji yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Be ni Filistibii lɛ nu akɛ Israelbii lɛ ebabua amɛhe naa yɛ Mizpa lɛ, Filistibii amaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ fã ta koni amɛbatua Israelbii lɛ. Be ni Israelbii lɛ nu ta ni Filistibii lɛ efã lɛ he lɛ, amɛshe gbeyei,

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: ni amɛkɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Yaa nɔ ni otsɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ohã wɔ koni ehere wɔ yɛ Filistibii lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Be ni Samuel shãa afɔle lɛ, Filistibii lɛ tsi bɛŋkɛ koni amɛbatua Israelbii lɛ. Shi Yehowa hã ŋwɛi shimɔ gbeyeigbeyei wo Filistibii lɛ nakai gbi lɛ, ni ehã amɛhiɛ bɔ, ni amɛnyɛɛɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ amɛdamɔ.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ fã kɛjɛ Mizpa ni amɛnyiɛ Filistibii lɛ asɛɛ ni amɛtswia amɛ nii aahu kɛyashɛ Bet-Kar jɔɔŋgbɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Aye Filistibii lɛ anɔ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni kɛjɛ no sɛɛ lɛ amɛnaji enyɔ nɛkɛ yiii Israelbii lɛ akpokpai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Ni Samuel yinɔ fɛɛ lɛ Yehowa eŋmɛɛɛ Filistibii lɛ agbɛ koni amɛbatua Israel.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Maji fɛɛ ni Filistibii lɛ eshɔ̃ yɛ Israelbii lɛ adeŋ lɛ, amɛkpale fɛɛ amɛhã Israel ekoŋŋ, kɛjɛ Ekron aahu kɛyashwie Gat. Israel nine shɛ eshikpɔji fɛɛ hu ni yaje Filistibii lɛ adɛŋ lɛ anɔ. Kɛkɛ ni toiŋjɔlɛ ba Israelbii lɛ kɛ Amorbii lɛ hu ateŋ.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel kwɛ Israel nɔ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Ni daa afi lɛ efãa gbɛ eyasaraa Betel kɛ Gilgal kɛ Mizpa, ni ekojoɔ sajisaji ni eba hei nɛɛ,

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa Rama, ejaakɛ jɛi ewe yɔɔ; ni jɛi hu ekwɛɔ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ saji yɛ. Samuel ma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ Rama ehã Yehowa.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Ekromɔbi ni gbɛi ji Yoel lɛ, kɛ lɛ esɛɛho ni gbɛi ji Abia lɛ ji nɔyelɔi ni ekɛto Beersheba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Shi Samuel bihii lɛ eyakɔɔɔ amɛtsɛ jeŋba kwraa. Amɛyadi ninamɔ sɛɛ ni amɛhehee nyɔɔŋnii, ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ saji ahiɛ amɛbumɔ shi.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Israel maŋ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ bua amɛhe naa, ni amɛba Samuel ŋɔɔ yɛ Rama,

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Amrɔ nɛɛ ogbɔ, ni obihii lɛ eyakɔɔɔ ojeŋba. No hewɔ lɛ, wo maŋtsɛ ohã wɔ koni lɛ ekwɛ wɔnɔ tamɔ eyɔɔ yɛ majimaji krokomɛi fɛɛ anɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Sane lɛ eyaŋɔɔɔ Samuel naa akɛ amɛaakɛɛ akɛ, “Hã wɔ maŋtsɛ ni ekwɛ wɔnɔ lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Samuel sɔle etsɛ Yehowa,

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: ni Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Nibii fɛɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛɔ bo lɛ, feemɔ ohã amɛ; ejaakɛ jeee bo amɛkwa; shi mi moŋ amɛkwa akɛ mikaye amɛnɔ dɔŋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Bɔ pɛ ni amɛfee mi kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni mijie amɛ kɛje Ijipt aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, ni amɛkwa mi ni amɛyasɔmɔ nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ amɛfeɔ bo hu nɛɛ.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bo amɛ toi; shi kɛ̃lɛ gba mli kpoo okɛɛ amɛ, ni otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nibii ni mɔ ni baaye amɛnɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ baatao yɛ amɛdɛŋ.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samuel gba maŋbii ni biɔ lɛ koni ewo maŋtsɛ ehã amɛ lɛ nɔ ni Yehowa wie lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ “Bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ni baaye nyɛnɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛ baaye ehã nɛ: Ebaaŋɔ nyɛbihii lɛ, ni ebaahã amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi ahi eshwiilii ahe, ni mɛi komɛi akwɛ ekpɔŋɔi, ni mɛi komɛi ajojoo foi kɛnyiɛ eshwiilii ahiɛ.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Nyɛbiyei lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, ebaafee mɛi komɛi tsofakɛŋma futulɔi, kɛ mɛi komɛi nihoolɔi kɛ mɛi komɛi hu aboloo shãlɔi.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Ebaashɔ̃shɔ̃ɔ nyɛŋmɔji kɛ nyɛwain abɔi kpakpai kɛ nyɛmutsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ, ni ekɛbaahã etsuji.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛkpa ŋmɔshi ŋmãa kɛ nyɛwain abɔi amli nii lɛ hu, ebaaŋɔ amɛmlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome ni ekɛbaahã epiafoi kɛ etsuji.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ebaashɔ̃ nyɛwehii kɛ nyɛweyei kɛ nyɛblahii fɛɛfɛji kɛ nyɛtsinai kɛ nyɛteji kpakpai ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛyatsu lɛ enii amɛhã lɛ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Ebaaŋɔ nyɛtooi amlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome ehã ehe, ni nyɛaatsɔ̃mɔ enyɔji.

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: koni wɔ hu wɔtamɔ majimaji fɛɛ akɛ wɔyɛ maŋtsɛ, ni lɛ ekwɛɔ wɔnɔ, koni asaŋ kɛ ta ba lɛ enyiɛ wɔhiɛ kɛ wu tai lɛ ehã wɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Be ni Samuel nu hetoo ni maŋbii lɛ hã lɛ ejaje etsɔ̃ɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Bo amɛ toi, ni owo maŋtsɛ ohã amɛ.” Samuel kɛɛ Israel hii lɛ agbɛnɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ! Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ.”

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Benyamin nuu niiatsɛ ko hi shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ Kish. Etsɛ gbɛi ji Abiel, Benyaminnyo Afia bi Bekorat bi Zeror lɛ bi ni.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Kish nɛɛ yɛ binuu, oblanyo nɛɛ he yɛ fɛo yɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ; ni kɛjɛ ekɔŋ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ oblanyo lɛ kwɔ fe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ Israel.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Saul tsɛ Kish tejii laaje. Kɛkɛ ni Kish kɛɛ ebi Saul akɛ, “Ŋɔɔ tsuji lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ofata ohe koni oya oyatao tejii lɛ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ tsulɔ lɛ yakpa Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛyaje Shalisha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiitao kooloi lɛ, shi amɛnaaa amɛ. Amɛyakpa Shaalim shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi amɛnaaa amɛ; kɛkɛ ni amɛtee Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ; shi amɛnaaa tejii lɛ.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kɛ tsulɔ lɛ yashɛ Zuf shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Saul kɛɛ oblanyo ni fata ehe lɛ akɛ, “Hã wɔku wɔsɛɛ wɔya shĩa; kɛjeee nakai lɛ mitsɛ aaafɔ̃ɔ tejii lɛ ahe jwɛŋmɔ, ni etsui baaye yɛ wɔ moŋ wɔhe.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Ole? Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ko yɛ maŋ nɛɛ mli ni abuɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni egbaa lɛ baa mli; hã wɔtee wɔyana lɛ; eko lɛ eeegba wɔ nyiɛmɔ ni wɔnyiɛ nɛɛ he nɔ ko.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ oblanyo lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni nɛkɛ wɔhiɛ ni kɛ wɔtee ni wɔkɛbaayahã nuu lɛ? Aboloo ni yɔɔ wɔkotokui amli lɛ hu etã. Mɛni dɔŋŋ wɔhiɛ ni wɔkɛaatee wɔyake Nyɔŋmɔ gbalɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ hã Saul hetoo ekɛɛ, “Mihiɛ jwiɛtɛi shekel mlijaa ejwɛ mli ekome yɛ biɛ; mikɛbaahã Nyɔŋmɔ gbalɔ lɛ koni etsɔ̃ɔ wɔ he ni wɔtsɔ̃.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ oblanyo lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ! Hã wɔtee.” Ni amɛyi mli kɛtee maŋ lɛ mli he ni Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Be ni amɛhereɔ ŋmeŋme lɛ kɛyaa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛkɛ oblayei komɛi kpe ni amɛmiiya amɛyayɛ nu, ni amɛbi amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛfai nɛ! Ninalɔ lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lo?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Amɛhere nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Eyɛ. Naa, lɛ eyaa yɛ nyɛhiɛ nɔŋŋ nɛɛ. Nyɛhe afea oya. Amrɔ nɛɛ ebashɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ miishã afɔle ŋmɛnɛ yɛ jamɔhe lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ mli botemɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nyɛaana lɛ dani eya gɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyaye nii. Ja eyashɛ shi dani maŋbii lɛ baaye nii lɛ, ejaakɛ lɛ ebaajɔɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ dani mɛi ni akpee lɛ aye. Nyɛyaa oya, ejaakɛ be mli nɔŋŋ ni nyɛnine aaashɛ enɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul kɛ etsulɔ lɛ yiŋ kɛtee maŋ lɛ mli. Be ni amɛboteɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛna Samuel ni eeya jamɔhe grɔŋŋ lɛ. Ni amɛkɛ lɛ kpe.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Gbi ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ dani Saul ba maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Yehowa ekɛɛ Samuel akɛ,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Wɔ benɛ mli lɛ mibatsu nuu ko ni jɛ Benyamin akutso lɛ mli oŋɔɔ koni ofɔ lɛ mu, ni owo lɛ mimaŋ Israel maŋtsɛ. Lɛ ebaahere mimaŋbii lɛ yɛ Filistibii lɛ adɛŋ. Mina amɛnɔnaa lɛ, ni minu tsɛmɔ ni amɛtsɛɔ koni ahere amɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Be ni Samuel na Saul lɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ “Mɔ he ni mi kɛ bo wie lɛ nɛ. Mɔnɛ ji mɔ ni baaye mimaŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Saul kɛ Samuel kpe yɛ maŋ lɛ agbo lɛ naa, kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni otsɔ̃ɔ mi ninalɔ lɛ shĩa lɛ.”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samuel here Saul nɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Mi ni. Tsɔ̃ mihiɛ kɛya gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ nyɛkɛ mi baaye nii ŋmɛnɛ; wɔ leebi lɛ mawo bo gbɛ, ni magba bo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni gbaa ojwɛŋmɔ naa lɛ.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Kɛ ka nyɛtejii lɛ ni laaje ŋmɛnɛ ji gbii etɛ̃ lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, kaaye otsui, ejaakɛ ana amɛ. Namɔ ole ni Israel shweɔ amrɔ nɛɛ fe bo kɛ otsɛ we lɛ fɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Saul here nɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Benyaminnyo ji mi, no hewɔ lɛ, mijɛ Israel akutsei lɛ ateŋ bibioo fe fɛɛ lɛ mli; ni Benyamin akutso lɛ mli wekui lɛ ateŋ humi fe fɛɛ mli mijɛ? Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni okɛɔ mi enɛ nɛɛ lɛ?”

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Saul nyiɛ Samuel kɛ etsulɔ lɛ hiɛ kɛtee niyelihe asa lɛ nɔ, ni ehã amɛyatara mɛi aaashɛ nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ ni akpee amɛ niyeli lɛ ayitso.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Nihoolɔ lɛ yawo loo shuɔ lɛ kɛba ni ekɛbama Saul hiɛ. Ni Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Nɔ ni akɛsara osɛɛ nɛ. Ye, ejaakɛ bo ohewɔ akɛto koni kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ shɛ lɛ okɛ mɛi ni akpee lɛ afutu aye nii.” No hewɔ lɛ, Saul kɛ Samuel ye nii nakai gbi lɛ.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshi gɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛkpeleke shi kɛba maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, afee saa yɛ shĩa lɛ yiteŋ ahã Saul, ni ekã jɛi ewɔ.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Enɔ maŋkɛ mra be ni je bɔ̃i tsɛremɔ lɛ, Samuel tsɛ Saul yɛ shĩa lɛ yiteŋ ekɛɛ, “Tee shi ni oba koni mawo bo gbɛ ni oya.” Saul te shi, ni lɛ kɛ Samuel fɛɛ je kpo amɛyi tɛmpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Be ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ maŋ lɛ klotia lɛ Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ tsulɔ lɛ koni ebaho eyi wɔhiɛ koni ekitee. Kɛji eyi hiɛ ni eekitee lɛ, bo lɛ owa ni omɛ shrao koni magba bo nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ yɔɔ bo kɛɛmɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel jie mu kɛ tɔ ko, ni efɔse mu lɛ eshwie Saul yiteŋ. Kɛkɛ ni eshwɔ Saul naa ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, Yehowa efɔ bo mu koni oye ewebii lɛ anɔ akɛ amɛlumɔ, koni ohere amɛ yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi ni ebɔle amɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Ni okadi ni atoɔ bo yɛ he akɛ Yehowa efɔ bo mu koni oye emɛi lɛ anɔ lumɔ nɛ.

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Kɛji okɛ mi gbala mli ŋmɛnɛ ni ooya lɛ, okɛ hii enyɔ komɛi baakpe yɛ Rahel saŋ lɛ he yɛ Zelza, yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ baakɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Tejii lɛ ni otee amɛtaomɔ lɛ ana amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, otsɛ efɔ̃ɔ tejii lɛ ahe jwɛŋmɔ, ni etsui miiye yɛ ohewɔ.’ Eekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Te mafee tɛŋŋ yɛ mibi lɛ hewɔ hu?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Kɛji oshi jɛi lɛ obaaya ohiɛ aahu kɛyashi oooyashɛ Tabor odum kpeteŋkple lɛ he. Hii etɛ̃ komɛi ni miiya Betel ayashã afɔle ahã Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ bo baakpe yɛ jɛi. Amɛteŋ mɔ kome hiɛ abotiabii etɛ̃, ni mɔ kome hu hiɛ aboloo akwaabɔi etɛ̃, ni mɔ kome hu hiɛ wain wolo tɔ kome.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Amɛbaafala bo, ni amɛbaahã bo aboloo akwaabɔi enyɔ; hemɔ.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, obaaya oyashɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Gibea he ni Filistibii asraafoi yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji obɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ, okɛ gbalɔi asafo ku baakpe ni amɛjɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛmiikpeleke shi, ni akɛ obenta kɛ milɛ kɛ blɛ kɛ saŋku nyiɛ amɛhiɛ, ni asaŋ amɛmiigba.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Yehowa mumɔ lɛ baatsi bo, ni obaaya oyashi gbalɔi nɛɛ anɔ kɛgba, ni obaatsɔ gbɔmɔ kroko kwraa.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Kɛji okadii nɛɛ ba mli nakai hã bo lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aaaje ogbɛfaŋ lɛ ofee ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni baakpala bo.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, otsɔ̃ mihiɛ kɛya Gilgal. Miiba jɛi ni mibashã shãa afɔlei kɛ shidaa afɔlei. Hii shi yɛ jɛi ni omɛ gbii kpawo kɛyashi mibaba mibanina bo, ni matsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni ofee.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul tsɔ̃ ehe ni eshi Samuel lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ tsake Saul tsui. Okadii lɛ fɛɛ ba mli nakai gbi lɛ.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ oblanyo tsulɔ lɛ yashɛ Gibea pɛ, ni gbalɔi asafo ku ko kɛ Saul bakpe. Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ lɛ bayi Saul nɔ, ni eyashi gbalɔi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ amɛ gba.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni le Saul sa ni asaŋ amɛna akɛ ekɛ gbalɔi lɛ miigba lɛ kɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Mɛni feɔ Kish bi lɛ nɛɛ? Saul hu etsɔ̃ gbalɔ lo?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ mli nyo ko here nɔ akɛ, “Shi mɛi krokomɛi lɛ, namɛi po ji amɛtsɛmɛi?” Bɔ ni fee ni ana abɛ akɛ, “Mɛni, Saul hu etsɔ̃ gbalɔ lo” lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul egba etã lɛ, etee afɔleshãahe lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Saul tsɛkwɛ ko bi Saul kɛ eblanyo tsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ nyɛjɛ?” Saul jie naa akɛ, “Wɔtee tejii ataomɔ, ni be ni wɔyanaaa amɛ lɛ wɔtee Samuel ŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Saul tsɛkwɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Gbaa mi nɔ ni Samuel kɛɛ nyɛ.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ etsɛkwɛ̃ lɛ akɛ, “Ekɛɛ wɔ akɛ ana tejii lɛ.” Shi Saul egbaaa etsɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ ni Samuel kɛɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ ni ebaye lɛ he lɛ. Ato Saul Maŋtsɛ

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuel kpee Israelbii lɛ kɛba Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Mizpa,

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Mi, mikpala Israel kɛje Ijipt, ni mijie nyɛ yɛ Ijiptbii adɛŋ kɛ majimaji ni gba nyɛnaa lɛ hu adɛŋ.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Shi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, nyɛ lɛ nyɛkwa mi, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ni hereɔ nyɛyiwala kɛjeɔ nyɛmanehului kɛ nyɛfimɔi fɛɛ amli lɛ, ni nyɛkɛɛ dabida, shi bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ mito maŋtsɛ mihã nyɛ.’ No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛtoa kɛbaa mi Yehowa mihiɛ yɛ nyɛkutsei kɛ nyɛshĩai anaa.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samuel hã Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ tsi ba ekomekome, ni oshiki ni afɔ̃ lɛ yagbee Benyamin akutso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ehã Benyamin akutso lɛ tsi ba yɛ amɛwekui anaa, ni oshiki ni afɔ̃ lɛ yagbee Matribii awe lɛ nɔ. Naagbee lɛ ehã Matribii awe lɛ mli hii lɛ tsi ba ekomekome, ni oshiku ni afɔ̃ lɛ yagbee Kish bi Saul nɔ. Shi be ni atao lɛ lɛ, anaaa lɛ.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, aku sɛɛ ni abi Yehowa nii ekoŋŋ akɛɛ, “Ani gbɔmɔ lɛ hu ba biɛ lo?” Yehowa to he akɛ, “Naa, eyateee ehe yɛ jatsui lɛ ateŋ.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Oya ni asha foi ni ayaŋɔ lɛ kɛba. Be ni Saul badamɔ mɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ekwɔ fe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛjɛ ekɔŋ kɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛna mɔ ni Yehowa eŋɔ lɛ? Mɔ ko mɔ kɔ kɛ lɛ yeee egbɔ yɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ.”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Samuel gba maŋ lɛ nɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ baatsu ahã amɛ kɛ amɛ hu amɛgbɛnaanii ni amɛbaatsu amɛhã maŋtsɛ lɛ. Samuel ŋmala nibii lɛ fɛɛ ewo wolo mli, ni ekɛŋmɛ Yehowa He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛŋ. Kɛkɛ ni Samuel wo maŋ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee eshĩa.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Saul hu tee ewe lɛ yɛ Gibea, ni hii kakabãŋi ni Nyɔŋmɔ etsake amɛtsuii fata ehe kɛtee.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Shi hii yakagbɔmɛi komɛi kɛɛ akɛ “Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mɔnɛ nɛɛ aaahere wɔyiwala lɛ?” Amɛgbe Saul he guɔ, ni amɛbakeee lɛ nɔ ko. Shi Saul ekɛɛɛ nɔ ko.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Amonbii amaŋtsɛ Nahash fã ta kɛba, ni ebasa Yabesh yɛ Gilead maŋbii lɛ ayi. Kɛkɛ ni Yabesh hii lɛ tsu ayakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Nahash akɛ, “Okɛ wɔ akpãŋ ni wɔɔsɔ̃mɔ bo.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Shi Nahash, Amonbii amaŋtsɛ lɛ, hã amɛ hetoo ekɛɛ, “Dani mikɛ nyɛ aaakpãŋ ni wɔfee ekome lɛ, ja nyɛhã mifamɔ nyɛninejurɔ hiŋmɛii fɛɛ yɛ nyɛyitsei ahe koni kpa ni nyɛbaaje lɛ ahã Israel muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ ashwie shi.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Yabesh maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ Nahash akɛ, “Hã wɔ gbii kpawo. Wɔbaatsu bɔfoi kɛya Israel maji fɛɛ anɔ. Kɛji ayanaaa mɔ ko abahere wɔ lɛ koni wɔkɛ wɔhe abahã bo.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Be ni Yabesh bɔfoi lɛ yashɛ maŋ ni ji Gibea, he ni Saul yɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛbɔ amɛmaniɛ lɛ, maŋtso muu lɛ wo yara.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Nakai be mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Saul miikpala tsinai kɛjɛ ŋa nɔ kɛmiiba shĩa, ni ebi mɔ ko akɛ, “Mɛni eba ni awo yara nɛkɛ nɛɛ?” Ni abɔ lɛ amaniɛ ni Yabesh bɔfoi lɛ kɛba lɛ.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ lɛ wo Saul ekãa titri ko be ni enu amaniɛ lɛ, asaŋ emli hu wo la naakpa.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Emɔmɔ tsinai enyɔ egbe, ni efolɔ amɛmli bibiibii, ni ekɛtsu Yabesh bɔfoi lɛ akɛ amɛkɛyakpa Israel majimaji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Ni wiemɔ ni fata he ji akɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni efãaa ta kɛbaaa ebawaaa Saul kɛ Samuel lɛ, nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni abaafee mɔ lɛ tsinai lɛ.” Israelbii lɛ she nɔ ni Yehowa aaafee amɛ lɛ he gbeyei, ni no hewɔ lɛ, eshwɛɛɛ nuu kome ni emĩaaa kɛyaaa ta lɛ eko.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul shɛ bɔfoi lɛ ni atsu kɛba lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyakɛa Yabeshbii yɛ Gilead akɛ, ‘Wɔ be ni hulu kɛɛ edamɔɔ lɛ ahere nyɛyiwala.’ ” Be ni bɔfoi lɛ babɔ Yabeshbii lɛ amaniɛ lɛ amɛtsui nyɔ amɛmli,

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: ni amɛhã ayakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Nahash akɛ, “Wɔ ni ji wɔ lɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe baaba abahã nyɛ koni nyɛfee wɔ bɔ ni nyɛsumɔɔ.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ Saul ja etabilɔi lɛ amli kui etɛ̃, ni amɛyatua Amonbii lɛ maŋkɛ hima mli, yɛ amɛnsra lɛ mli, ni amɛtswia amɛ nii kɛyashi shwane fintiŋŋ. Amonbii ni je gbele mli lɛ gbɛ shwã bɔ ni onaŋ amɛteŋ mɛi enyɔ nɛkɛ yɛ he kome.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ nakai mɛi ni kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mɛɛ Saul hu ni baaye wɔnɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ yɔɔ? Akɛ amɛ aba ni wɔgbe amɛ!’ ”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Shi Saul to he ekɛɛ, “Ashwieŋ la shi ŋmɛnɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ Yehowa ehere Israel yiwala.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbaa ni wɔtea Gilgal koni wɔsaa wɔwo Saul maŋtsɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ fɛɛ loo mli kɛtee Gilgal, ni amɛyawo Saul maŋtsɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ jɛi. Amɛshãshãa shidaa afɔlei yɛ jɛi yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni Saul kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ nya jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Israel fɛɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni nyɛbi mi lɛ mifee, ni miwo maŋtsɛ mihã nyɛ.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ nyiɛ nyɛhiɛ nɛɛ. Mi lɛ amrɔ nɛɛ migbɔ ni miyi eyɛ, ni mibihii lɛ nyɛ kɛ amɛ yɔɔ. Mikwɛ nyɛnɔ kɛjɛ miblahiaŋ aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Mi nɛ; nyɛyea odase nyɛshia mi yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, kɛ emɔ̃ ni efɔ lɛ mu lɛ hu hiɛ. Namɔ tsina mishɔ̃, ni namɔ teji mishɔ̃? Aloo namɔ ojo mitswa, aloo namɔ yi miwa? Ni namɔ dɛŋ mihe nyɔɔŋnii yɛ koni maku mihiɛ mafɔ esane nɔ? Nyɛwiea koo, koni mato nyɛ najiaŋ.”

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ here nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Otswako wɔ ojo lɛ, owako wɔ yi lɛ, oshɔ̃ko mɔ ko dɛŋ nɔ ko hu.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Samuel to he ni ekɛɛ, “Yehowa ji midasefonyo mɔ, ni emɔ̃ ni efɔ lɛ mu lɛ hu miiye he odase ŋmɛnɛ akɛ mɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ midɛŋ.” Amɛto he akɛ, “Lɛ ji odasefonyo lɛɛlɛŋ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Yehowa ji odasefonyo lɛɛlɛŋ, lɛ mɔ ni ehala Mose kɛ Aaron ni ejie nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba lɛ.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛdamɔa shi nyɛmɛa koni mi kɛ nyɛ akojoa yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, yɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ekɛhere nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ ahewɔ.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Be ni Yakob tee Ijipt ni Ijiptbii lɛ yeɔ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ anyɔŋ lɛ, nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ bolɔ amɛtsɛ Yehowa, ni Yehowa tsu Mose kɛ Aaron ni amɛyajie nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ yɛ Ijipt kɛba, ni amɛhã amɛbahi biɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Shi nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ ahiɛ kpa Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa ŋmɛɛ amɛhe ehã, ni Hazor Maŋtsɛ Yabin tatsɛ Sisera lɛ, kɛ Filistibii lɛ hu kɛ Moab maŋtsɛ lɛ hu kɛ amɛ wuwuu tai, ni gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ye nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ bolɔ amɛtsɛ Yehowa, ni amɛkɛɛ, ‘Wɔfee esha, ejaakɛ wɔkwa bo, Yehowa, ni wɔyasɔmɔ Baali kɛ Astarte moŋ. Shi agbɛnɛ heremɔ wɔ yɛ wɔhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ, ni wɔbaasɔmɔ bo.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa tsu Gideon kɛ Barak kɛ Yefta kɛ mi Samuel hu, ni etsɔ̃ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ anɔ ehere nyɛ yɛ nyɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ yɛ hei fɛɛ; kɛkɛ ni nyɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Shi be ni nyɛna akɛ Nahash, Amonbii lɛ amaŋtsɛ lɛ, efã nyɛyi nɔ ta lɛ, nyɛkɛɛ mi akɛ ‘Dabi, wɔkpɛ̃lɛɛɛ; ja wɔna maŋtsɛ ni eye wɔnɔ,’ tsɛbelɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ji nyɛmaŋtsɛ.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, naa, maŋtsɛ lɛ ni nyɛtao ni nyɛbi lɛ, ahã nyɛ. Naa, Yehowa ewo maŋtsɛ ehã nyɛ.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛaashe Yehowa gbeyei, ni nyɛaasɔmɔ lɛ, ni nyɛaaye egbee nɔ, ni nyɛtseŋ ekitã lɛ hiɛ atua, ni asaŋ nyɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ni yeɔ nyɛnɔ lɛ fɛɛ aaanyiɛ Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛjeŋ baaja ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji nyɛyayeee Yehowa gbee nɔ; shi nyɛtse ekitã lɛ hiɛ atua lɛ no lɛ Yehowa baagbala nyɛ kɛ nyɛmaŋtsɛ lɛ fɛɛ toi.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛdamɔa shi ni nyɛkwɛa naakpɛɛ nɔ ko ni Yehowa baafee.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Ani jeee ŋmãakuu be mli ji ŋmɛnɛ? Ojogbaŋŋ! Mibasɔle matsɛ Yehowa koni ehã ŋwɛi ashimɔ, ni nu hu anɛ koni nyɛkɛna nyɛle akɛ nɔ fɔŋ ni nyɛfee nyɛshi Yehowa kɛ maŋtsɛ ni nyɛbi akɛ ahã nyɛ lɛ, eda naakpa.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel sɔle etsɛ Yehowa, ni ehã ŋwɛi shimɔ, ni nu nɛ nakai gbi lɛ, ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ she Yehowa kɛ Samuel gbeyei.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ kpa Samuel fai amɛkɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, kpa Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fai ohã wɔ otsuji koni wɔkagboi, ejaakɛ eshai fɛɛ ni wɔfee sa lɛ wɔfee eko hu wɔfata he akɛ wɔbi akɛ ahã wɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Shi Samuel kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei; nyɛna nyɛfee nɛkɛ nɔ fɔŋ nɛɛ moŋ, shi kɛ̃lɛ nyɛkakpalea kɛjea Yehowa sɛɛ, shi moŋ nyɛsɔmɔa lɛ kɛ nyɛtsui fɛɛ.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Nyɛkagbaa afã kɛyanyiɛ yaka nibii ni ahe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni asaŋ nyɛɛɛ mɔ yiwala ahere lɛ asɛɛ; ejaakɛ yaka nibii ni.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa kwaŋ nyɛ yɛ egbɛi kpeteŋkple lɛ hewɔ; asaŋ esa ehiɛ hu akɛ ekɛ nyɛ afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Mi hu enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ akɛ makpa sɔlemɔ kɛ nyɛ hãmɔ ni mikɛfee esha mishi Yehowa. Shi moŋ mibatsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni ja ni sa akɛ nyɛfee.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Nyɛshea Yehowa kɛkɛ gbeyei; asaŋ nyɛsɔmɔa lɛ yɛ anɔkwayeli mli kɛ nyɛtsui fɛɛ. Nyɛkaia nibii wuji abɔ ni etsu ehã nyɛ lɛ.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Shi naa, kɛji nyɛkã he nyɛfee nifɔɔjianii lɛ, no lɛ aaabɛɛ nyɛ kɛ nyɛmaŋtsɛ lɛ fɛɛ ashwie.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Naa, Saul eyaye Filistibii asraafoi aku ko nɔ kunim, ni no hewɔ lɛ, Filistibii lɛ ekã kɛbaaye wie!” Israelbii here tsɛmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtiu Saul yɛ Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Be ni Israel hii lɛ na akɛ nine miitao akɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ, mɛi yateetee amɛhe yɛ tɛkploi kɛ bui kɛ tɛsai kɛ gbonyobui kɛ nubui amli,

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: ni mɛi komɛi hu jo foi amɛyafo Yordan Faa lɛ kɛtee Gad kɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be nɛɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Saul yɛ Gilgal lolo, ni mɛi ni ena nyiɛ esɛɛ lolo fɛɛ miikpokpo kɛ gbeyei.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Saul mɛ Samuel gbii kpawo, ni ji be ni Samuel to lɛ lɛ; shi Samuel eyashɛɛɛ shi, ni maŋ lɛ hu miijwa kɛmiishi Saul.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Saul fã akɛ, “Akɛ shãa afɔle lɛ kɛ shidaa afɔlei lɛ abahã mi yɛ biɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Saul shã afɔle lɛ.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Shi afɔle lɛ ni eshã egbe naa pɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ naa Samuel ni ebashɛ shi. Saul tee ni ekɛ Samuel yakpe ni efala lɛ.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel bi Saul akɛ, “Kwɛ, mɛni ofee nɛɛ?” Saul jie enaa akɛ, “Be ni mina akɛ maŋ lɛ miijwa kɛmiishi mi, ni gbi ni oto lɛ ebaho fɛɛ ni obashɛko shi, ni asaŋ Filistibii lɛ anaa ebakpe shi yɛ Mikmash lɛ,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: nɔ ni misusu ji akɛ Filistibii lɛ baaba abatua mi yɛ Gilgal, be mli ni mibiko Yehowa dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, fimɔ naa lɛ, mimia mihiɛ, ni mishã afɔle lɛ.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel to he ehã Saul akɛ, “Oye gbekɛbii asane pam. Oyeko kitã ni Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ wo bo lɛ nɔ. Kulɛ kpaako Yehowa baawaje omaŋtsɛyeli yɛ Israel nɔ ema shi shiŋŋ kɛya naanɔ.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ lɛ omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ sɛɛ baafo. Yehowa ŋɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsui naa gbɔmɔ ni ewo lɛ emaŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ; mɛni hewɔ lɛ oyayeee kitã ni Yehowa wo bo lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Saul shi Gilgal ni etee Geba yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekane hii tabilɔi ni fata ehe lɛ, ena mɛi aaafee ohai ekpaa.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan kɛ tabilɔi ni fata amɛhe lɛ wa yɛ Geba, yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No mli lɛ Filistibii lɛ ewo shi yɛ Mikmash.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Filistibii lɛ wo asafoi etɛ̃ agbɛ kɛjɛ amɛta lɛ mli koni amɛyatua Israelbii lɛ koni amɛha amɛnii. Ku kome tsɔ̃ Ofra gbɛ kɛtee Shual shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni ku kome hu tsɔ̃ Bet-Horon gbɛ,

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: ni ku kome ko hu tsɔ̃ husu lɛ ni kwɛɔ Zeboim Jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛtee shiaŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ sɔ̃lɔ kome nɛkɛ bɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko he ko, ejaakɛ Filistibii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji afeee nakai lɛ, no lɛ Hebribii lɛ aaasɔ̃ klantei kɛ akplɔi ato amɛhe.”

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Aheɔ amɛ nɔ ko fioo ko kɛji ajɔ tsina kɔi loo shitsaa kɔi naa. Shi kɛji ajɔ tsinakplamɔ dade naa lɛ, aheɔ jwiɛtɛi shekel kome mlijaa etɛ̃ mli enyɔ ni kɛhã lema lɛ naajɔɔ lɛ aheɔ shekel kome mlijaa etɛ̃ mli ekome.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, gbi ni atswa ta lɛ, anaaa Saul kɛ Yonatan sɛɛbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kwraa ni ehiɛ klante loo akplɔ, fe Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan kɛkɛ ni amɛ lɛ amɛhiɛ eko.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ wo asraafoi aku gbɛ kɛtee Mikmash jɔɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyabu jɛi tsɔ̃mɔhe lɛ he.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ oblanyo ni hiɛ edama lɛ akɛ, “Wɔfo mli wɔtee wɔyahɛŋ foolɔi nɛɛ asraafoi lɛ; shi eko lɛ Yehowa aaaye abua wɔ ejaakɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko etsiii Yehowa naa akɛ ekɛ mɛi pii loo mɛi fioo aaahere yiwala.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ ni hiɛ tawuunii lɛ to he ekɛɛ, “Bɔ ni oookɛɛ; mi kɛ bo, yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ; wɔbaafo mli kɛya amɛŋɔɔ, ni wɔbajie wɔhe kpo koni amɛna wɔ.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Kɛji no sɛɛ ni amɛkɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛmɛa, shi wɔmiiba wɔkɛ nyɛ abakpe’ lɛ, wɔbaawa wɔdamɔ wɔnajiaŋ.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛji amɛkɛɛ wɔ akɛ ‘Nyɛ lɛ nyɛbaa’ lɛ, no lɛ wɔbaaya wɔyanina amɛ, ejaakɛ no ji okadi akɛ Yehowa ejɔɔ amɛnɔ ewo wɔdɛŋ koni wɔye amɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Ni Filistibii asraafoi lɛ bo tsɛ Yonatan kɛ oblanyo ni hiɛɔ edama lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛ lɛ nyɛbaa! Wɔbaatsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɔ ko.” Kɛkɛ ni Yonatan kɛɛ oblanyo ni hiɛɔ edama lɛ akɛ, “Nyiɛmɔ misɛɛ, shi Yehowa ejɔɔ amɛnɔ ewo Israel dɛŋ.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Yonatan nyiɛ yɛ eniji kɛ enaji anɔ kɛkwɔ tɛsaa lɛ, ni etawuuniihiɛlɔ lɛ hu fee nakai nɔŋŋ kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ. Yonatan yatua Filistibii lɛ ni eku mɛi fɛɛ ni baje hiɛ lɛ eshwie shi, bɛlɛ etawuuniihiɛlɔ lɛ hu miigbe mɛi kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Eji ŋmɛnɛ lɛ maŋbii lɛ yeyee amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ anibii ni amɛna ni ashishii lɛ eko, bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛkɛ kulɛ, aso agbeŋ Filistibii lɛ fɛɛ nɛkɛ aahu?”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ tabilɔi fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ mia ni agbɛnɛ amɛfã kɛtee ta lɛ naa. Amɛyanina ni Filistinyo klante kã enyɛmi Filistinyo nɔŋŋ nɔ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ hiɛ etsɔ̃ ebu shi efee basaa.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Filistibii ni yɔɔ nsra lɛ mli kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa lɛ nɔ kɛ maji fɛɛ amli fɛɛ jijaa, ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ asraafoi ni yɔ nsra lɛ mli lɛ kɛ mɛi ni tee amɛyaaye ofɔ̃ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ hu hoso, ni ehã jijaamɔ lɛ mli wo wu. Aye Filistibii lɛ anɔ kunim

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Saul sɛɛ tabilɔi ni ahã amɛbuɔ yɛ Gibea yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaakwɛ lɛ naa Filistibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛmiiya kɛmiiba.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ esɛɛbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkanea mɛi lɛ koni wɔkɛtao mɔ ni eje wɔteŋ.” Be ni akane mɛi lɛ, Yonatan kɛ etawuuniihiɛlɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni bɛ mɛi lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ni Saul kɛɛ Ahia, osɔfo lɛ, akɛ, “Yaawo Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛba biɛ.” Nɛkɛ beiaŋ lɛ he fɛɛ he ni Israelbii lɛ yaa lɛ amɛ kɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yaa.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Saul kɛ osɔfo lɛ hiɛ wiemɔ ni hoofeemɔ lɛ naa bawa yɛ Filistibii lɛ ansra lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ osɔfo lɛ akɛ, “Ahi shi dã!”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hebribii ni kɛ Filistibii lɛ yɔɔ sa, asaŋ ni amɛshi Filistibii lɛ anɔ kɛba ta lɛ naa lɛ, kpa amɛhe ni amɛyafata Israelbii lɛ ni kɛ Saul kɛ Yonatan nyiɛ lɛ ahe.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Nakai nɔŋŋ hu Israelbii ni jojoo foi amɛyateetee yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ hu fee. Be ni amɛnu akɛ Filistibii lɛ miijo foi yɛ ta lɛ naa lɛ, amɛ hu amɛbafata he ni anyiɛ Filistibii lɛ asɛɛ waa.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Israelbii tabilɔi lɛ na nɔ kɛ hɔmɔ nakai gbi lɛ, ejaakɛ Saul kã maŋ lɛ kitã akɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaasa enaa nɔ ko dani je aaana ni matɔ mihe owele yɛ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ magbe naa lɛ, loomɔ aaalomɔ mɔ lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, gbi muu lɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko kwraa esaaa enaa nɔ ko.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Be ni tabilɔi lɛ shɛ koo nɛɛ mli lɛ, wo tsereɔ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ; shi mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ ewao esaaa eko wooo edaaŋ, ejaakɛ tabilɔi lɛ miishe gbeyei yɛ kitã lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Akɛni Yonatan nuuu be ni etsɛ kãa maŋ lɛ kitã lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ tso ni ehiɛ lɛ naa tsɔ wo agbaku lɛ mli, ni eye wo lɛ eko, kɛkɛ ni ekpɔiaŋ tse lɛ.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Shi tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko kɛɛ Yonatan akɛ, “Otsɛ kã maŋ lɛ kitã veveeve akɛ, ‘Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaasa enaa nɔ ko ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, loomɔ kɛ̃ aaalomɔ lɛ; ni no ji biti ni maŋbii lɛ etɔ kɛ hɔmɔ nɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Yonatan to he akɛ, “Mitsɛ egba maŋ lɛ naa pam, ejaakɛ wo nɛɛ fioo ko kɛkɛ ni mikɛsa minaa lɛ, nyɛkwɛa bɔ ni mikpɔiaŋ etse mi.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ Israelbii lɛ gbe Filistibii lɛ kɛjɛ Mikmash aahu kɛyashi Ayalon. Ni etɔ Israelbii lɛ butuu.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Amɛbɔi nihaa, ni amɛmɔmɔ toi kɛ tsinai kɛ tsinabii fɛɛ, ni amɛgbegbee amɛ yɛ amɛnajiaŋ nɔŋŋ, ni amɛye loo lɛ be mli ni loo lɛ mli lá fɛɛ tsereko.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Ayabɔ Saul amaniɛ akɛ, “Naa, maŋbii lɛ miitɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛmiiye loo ni emli lá fɛɛ tsereko.” Saul here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛnɔkwayeli faaa! Nyɛkokloa tɛ kpeteŋkple nyɛbahãa mi yɛ biɛ!”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Saul tee ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛgbɛa nyɛshwãa maŋbii lɛ ateŋ, ni nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ, ‘Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ etsina loo etoo lɛ aba ni ebagbe lɛ yɛ biɛ ni eye, shi akaye loo lɛ be mli ni emli lá fɛɛ tsereko koni nyɛkɛmiitɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ.’ ” No hewɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ mɔ etsina kɛba, nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni amɛbagbegbee kooloi lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Ni Saul mã afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi ehã Yehowa. No ji klɛŋklɛŋ afɔleshãa latɛ ni Saul mã ehã Yehowa.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ ni Saul kɛɛ ewebii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔyaa koni wɔyatuaa Filistibii lɛ nyɔɔŋ koni wɔgbe amɛ kɛyashi jetsɛremɔ wɛlɛŋŋ; ni wɔkashi amɛteŋ hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ.” Maŋbii lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Bɔ ni oookɛɛ.” Shi osɔfo lɛ hu kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔbia Nyɔŋmɔ nii dã.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Saul bi Nyɔŋmɔ nii ekɛɛ, “Miyatua Filistibii lɛ lo? Obaahã Israel aye amɛnɔ kunim lo?” Shi Nyɔŋmɔ hãaa Saul hetoo nakai gbi lɛ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul tsu atsɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ abahã lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbaa ni nyɛbataoa mli akɛ nyɛaana he ni ajɛ afee esha ni ebaje kpo ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lo?

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Mina Yehowa, Israel yiwalaherelɔ lɛ, kɛji mibi Yonatan tete ni fee esha nɛɛ lɛ ja egbo.” Shi tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko hãaa hetoo.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛ fɛɛ nyɛbaaye afã kome, ni mi kɛ mibi Yonatan hu baaye afã kome.” Maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Bɔ ni oookɛɛ.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ akɛ, “Ao! Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, mɛɛba ni ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ ohãaa otsulɔ hetoo? Kɛji esha lɛ mi, loo mibi Yonatan ni fee lɛ, hã Urim atsɔ̃ɔ; shi kɛji owebii Israelbii lɛ ateŋ ajɛ ni afee esha lɛ, no lɛ hã Tumim atsɔ̃ɔ.” Oshiki lɛ gbee Saul kɛ Yonatan nɔ, ni maŋbii lɛ ahe je mli.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛfɔ̃a oshiki lɛ yɛ mi kɛ mibi Yonatan nɔ.”

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ Yonatan akɛ, “Gbaa mi nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ofee lɛ.” Yonatan gba Saul sane lɛ ekɛɛ, “Mikɛ tso ko ni mihiɛ sa wo fioo, ni mikɛsa minaa. Naa mi, mifee kralo, abaanyɛ agbe mi.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Saul to he ekɛɛ, “Kɛji mihãaa ogbo fii, Yonatan, no lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ agbe mi, ni egbe mi ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Shi maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Yonatan baagbo lo? Lɛ mɔ ni eye kunim kpeteŋkple nɛkɛ nɛɛ ehã Israel lɛ? Akaba mli nakai! Wɔna Yehowa akɛ Yonatan yiteŋ tsɔi kome nɛkɛ efaŋ egbeŋ shi, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni kɛ lɛ tsu nɔ ni etsu ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ.” Biɛ tsɔ̃ ni maŋbii lɛ here Yonatan yiwala kɛje gbele mli.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Saul fɔ̃ɔ Filistibii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ; ni Filistibii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛtee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Saul maŋtsɛyeli kɛ eŋa kɛ ebii lɛ

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Saul yinɔ fɛɛ lɛ, Israelbii kɛ Filistibii ateŋ ejɔɔɔ kɛ taitai ni naa wa sɔŋŋ. Ni no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji Saul na nuu hiɛwalɔ loo kãkãlɔ pɛ, eŋɔ lɛ efata tabilɔi ni buɔ ehe lɛ ahe.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Mi ji mɔ ni Yehowa tsu koni mibafɔ bo mu kɛwo bo emaŋ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ bo nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ toi.”

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Yehowa ni ji Tatsɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Mibagbala Amalekbii lɛ atoi yɛ shi ni amɛte amɛwo Israel be mli ni Israel jɛ Ijipt ebaa lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, yaa ni oyatua Amalekbii lɛ, ni okpãtã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ hiɛ. Okɛ amɛhe akake amɛ, shi ogbe amɛ, nuu ni jio, abifao ni kã fufɔ naa ni jio, tsina ni jio, yooma ni jio, teji ni jio, ogbe fɛɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: No ni Saul hã akpee maŋbii lɛ kɛba, ni akane amɛyibɔ yɛ Telem. Ana hii ni nyiɛ amɛnane nɔ akpei ohai enyɔ; kɛ Yuda kɔkrɔɔ hii akpei nyɔŋma ashi nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Samuel wie ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ tabilɔi lɛ fã kɛba Amalekbii amaŋ wulu lɛ niiaŋ, ni ebawo ka yɛ maŋ lɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛ shɛɛ maje Kenbii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ, “Nyɛshia Amalekbii lɛ ateŋ nyɛyaa koni mikakpãtã nyɛ kɛ amɛ fɛɛ hiɛ, ejaakɛ nyɛ lɛ nyɛfee Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ ejurɔ, be ni amɛjɛ Ijipt amɛbaa lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Kenbii lɛ shi Amalekbii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛtee.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ Amalekbii lɛ wu, ni eplenee amɛ kɛjɛ Hawila aahu kɛyashi Shur ni yɔɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: Emɔ Amalekbii amaŋtsɛ Agag hiɛkãalɔ; shi agbe emaŋbii lɛ blublu.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Saul kɛ etabilɔi lɛ baa Agag yi. Asaŋ amɛbaa toi kɛ tsinai kɛ tsinabii kɛ gwantɛŋi abii lɛ ateŋ kooloi kpakpai fe fɛɛ lɛ hu yi; ni amɛkpãtãaa amɛhiɛ; shi nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he bɛ sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa ko, aloo ni abɛ he nɔ ko feemɔ lɛ amɛkpãtã hiɛ. Akpoo Saul akɛ Maŋtsɛ

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “Mishwa mihe akɛ miwo Saul maŋtsɛ, ejaakɛ ekpale yɛ misɛɛ, ni eyeee mikitãi lɛ anɔ.” Sane lɛ fee Samuel mlifu, ni esɔle ekpa Yehowa fai nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Ni Samuel te shi enɔjetsɛremɔ maŋkɛ mra koni enine ayashɛ Saul nɔ leebi. No mli lɛ abatswa Samuel adafi akɛ, “Saul ba Karmel, ni ebama shiu koni akɛkai kunim ni eye lɛ; ni no sɛɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ etee Gilgal.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Be ni Samuel yashɛ Saul ŋɔɔ lɛ, Saul kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yehowa ajɔɔ bo! Miye Yehowa famɔ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Samuel bi Saul akɛ, “Ni mɛni ji toi kɛ tsinai fɛɛ abolɔmɔ ni jwere mitoiŋ nɛɛ mɔ?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Saul jie naa ekɛɛ, “Amalekbii lɛ aŋɔɔ akɛjɛ. Maŋbii lɛ baa toi kɛ tsinai lɛ ateŋ kooloi kpakpai fe fɛɛ lɛ ayi koni amɛkɛbashã afɔle amɛhã Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ; shi nibii ni shwɛ lɛ wɔkpãtã fɛɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Mɛɛ! Magba bo nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi nyɔɔŋ nɛɛŋ.” Saul to he ekɛɛ akɛ, “Wiemɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bo lɛ onaa ohe akɛ mɔ folo ko kɛkɛ; shi ani jeee bo ji Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ atsɛ? Yehowa fɔ bo mu kɛwo bo Israel maŋtsɛ,

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: ni Yehowa tsu bo, ni ekɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Yaa koni oyaplenee Amalekbii eshafeelɔi lɛ. Okɛ amɛ awu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni oookpãtã amɛhiɛ kwrakwra.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ mɔ ni oyabooo Yehowa toi, ni otee oyaha ofɔ̃yeli nii, ni okɛtɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Saul here Samuel nɔ akɛ, “Mibo Yehowa toi. Mimɔ Agag, Amalekbii amaŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛba; ni Amalekbii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ mikpãtã amɛhiɛ musumusu.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Shi tabilɔi lɛ ŋɔ ofɔ̃yeli nibii lɛ amli toi kɛ tsinai ni kulɛ sa amɛhiɛ kpãtãmɔ lɛ ateŋ kooloi kpakpai fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛbashã afɔle amɛhã Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ yɛ Gilgal.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Shi Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Ani Yehowa nyaa shãa afɔlei kɛ gbee afɔlei ahe fe ni abaabo lɛ toi lo? Naa, toiboo hi fe afɔleshãa, ni ehi fe toi agboi amli fɔ.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ atuatsemɔ lɛ esha ni tamɔ klamɔ nɔŋŋ, ni kuɛŋtimɔ lɛ esha ni tamɔ amãgãjamɔ nɔŋŋ. Akɛni okwa Yehowa naa wiemɔ lɛ, lɛ hu ekwa bo maŋtsɛ lɛ yeli.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Mifee esha, ejaakɛ mitɔ̃ Yehowa fãmɔ lɛ kɛ bo hu owiemɔi lɛ anɔ, ejaakɛ miyashe tabilɔi lɛ agbeyei ni miyabo amɛnaawiemɔ toi.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ miikpa bo fai, koni okɛ mihe esha lɛ afa mi, ni okɛ mi aku osɛɛ kɛya koni mayaja Yehowa.”
