english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Mikɛ bo ekuŋ sɛɛ kɛyajaŋ ejaakɛ oyayeee fãmɔ ni Yehowa fã bo lɛ nɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa hu ekwa bo maŋtsɛ lɛ yeli yɛ Israel.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Be ni Samuel tsɔ̃ ehe koni eya lɛ, Saul mɔ Samuel atade lɛ naamuu lɛ mli, kɛkɛ ni atade lɛ gba.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Yehowa shɔ̃ Israel nɔ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ odɛ̃ŋ kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛ, ni ekɛhã onaanyo ni hi fe bo.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Naa, Israel Anunyamtsɛ lɛ emaleŋ ni eshwaŋ ehe hu ejaakɛ jeee gbɔmɔ adesa ji lɛ, ni eeeshwa ehe.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ akɛ, “Mifee esha; shi kɛ̃lɛ wo mihiɛ nyam yɛ mimaŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ Israel fɛɛ hiɛ, ni okɛ mi aku sɛɛ kɛya ni mayaja Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Samuel ku esɛɛ ni ekɛ Saul tee, ni Saul yaja Yehowa yɛ Gilgal.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ Agag, Amalekbii amaŋtsɛ lɛ abaa miŋɔɔ.” Agag bashɛ Samuel hiɛ kɛ ehiɛ miishɛɛmiishɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ yɛ eyitsoŋ akɛ, “Ekã shi faŋŋ akɛ benɛ ejie gbele sane yɛ eyiŋ.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Shi Samuel kɛɛ Agag akɛ, “Bɔ ni oklante hã yei etsɔmɔ yei ni bɛ bii lɛ, nakai bo hu onyɛ baatsɔ̃ yoo ni bɛ bi yɛ enanemɛi yei ateŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni Samuel bamɔ Agag kɛ klante, ni efolɔ emli dukuduku yɛ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ yɛ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel yi mli etee Rama, ni Saul hu yi mli ni etee ewe yɛ Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Samuel kɛ ehiŋmɛitsei enyɔ nɛkɛ enaaa Saul dɔŋŋ aahu kɛyashi Saul gbo; shi Samuel ye Saul he ŋkɔmɔ. Ni Yehowa shwa ehe akɛ ewo Saul Israel maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ ni oooye Saul he ŋkɔmɔ kɛyashi, be mli ni ona ole akɛ mikwa lɛ Israel maŋtsɛyeli? Wo okoŋ lɛ mli mu obɔ̃; mibatsu bo Yeshai, Betlehemnyo lɛ, ŋɔɔ ejaakɛ miŋɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ ebihii lɛ ateŋ mihã mihe.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Samuel to he ekɛɛ, “Te mafee tɛŋŋ matee tsumɔ nɛɛ hu? Kɛji Saul nu he lɛ eeegbe mi.” Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Ŋɔɔ tsinabi ohiɛ odɛ̃ kɛya, ni oyakɛɛ akɛ, ‘Miba mibashã afɔle mahã Yehowa.’

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Kpeemɔ Yeshai kɛba afɔleshãahe lɛ, ni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni ofee koni ofɔ mɔ ni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo lɛ mu ohã mi.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel fee nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ lɛ. Be ni eshɛ Betlehem lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ kɛ Samuel bakpe kɛ hekpokpomɔ, ni amɛbi lɛ akɛ, “Hejɔlɛ baa oba nɛɛ lo?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Samuel jie naa ekɛɛ akɛ, “Hejɔlɛ baa miba! Miba mibashã afɔle mahã Yehowa. Nyɛtsuua nyɛhe, ni nyɛ kɛ mi ayaa afɔle lɛ shãa.” Etsuu Yeshai kɛ ebihii lɛ ahe, ni ekpee amɛ kɛtee afɔleshãahe lɛ.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Be ni Yeshai kɛ ebihii lɛ ba ni Samuel na Yeshai bi Eliab lɛ, ekɛɛ yɛ eyitsoŋ akɛ, “Mɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu lɛ damɔ Yehowa hiɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Kaahã ehiɛŋtso loo ekwɔlɛ nyɛnyereŋŋ lɛ miilaka bo. Jeee bɔ ni gbɔmɔ adesa kwɛɔ nii Yehowa kwɛɔ nii. Gbɔmɔ adesa kwɛɔ kpo nɔ gbɛ nii ekɛyeɔ sane, shi Yehowa lɛ kwɛɔ tsuiŋ.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeshai tsɛ ebi Abinadab ni ehã etsɔ̃ Samuel hiɛ kɛho. Shi Samuel kɛɛ akɛ, “Mɔnɛ hu Yehowa eŋɔko lɛ.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Yeshai hã ebi Shama hu baho; shi Samuel kɛɛ ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Mɔnɛ hu Yehowa eŋɔko lɛ.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Yeshai hã ebihii lɛ ateŋ mɛi kpawo baho yɛ Samuel hiɛ; shi Samuel kɛɛ Yeshai akɛ, “Yehowa eŋɔko obii nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel bi Yeshai akɛ, “Ani, oblahii lɛ fɛɛ nɛ?” Yeshai to he akɛ, “Eshwɛ amɛteŋ gbekɛ kwraa fe fɛɛ lɛ; amrɔ nɛɛ eekwɛ mitoi lɛ.” Samuel kɛɛ Yeshai akɛ, “Tsu koni ayaŋɔ lɛ kɛba, ejaakɛ wɔwoŋ afɔle lɛ shãa ja ebashɛ biɛ dã.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Yeshai tsu ni ayaŋɔ ebi gbekɛ lɛ kɛba: etsuɔ fioo, ni ehiŋmɛii yɛ fɛo; anɔkwa ehe yɛ fɛo. Yehowa kɛɛ Samuel akɛ, “Tee shi ni ofɔ oblanyo lɛ mu, ejaakɛ lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Samuel wo mu kɛ koŋ lɛ, ni efɔ David mu yɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa mumɔ lɛ yi David nɔ! Kɛkɛ ni Samuel te shi, ni eyiŋ etee Rama. David yɛ Saul we lɛ mli

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Yehowa mumɔ lɛ je Saul nɔ agbɛnɛ, ni Yehowa hãa mumɔ fɔŋ ko moŋ bahaoɔ lɛ.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔsusuɔ akɛ mumɔ fɔŋ ko ni Nyɔŋmɔ ehã haoɔ bo nɛɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Ofãa wɔ otsuji ni damɔ ohiɛ amrɔ nɛɛ kulɛ, wɔɔɔya wɔyatao mɔ ko ni he esa jogbaŋŋ kɛ saŋkutswaa kɛba koni kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ hã mumɔ fɔŋ lɛ bayi onɔ lɛ, etswa saŋku lɛ koni ahi ahã bo.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyataoa mɔ ko ni le saŋkutswaa jogbaŋŋ nyɛhãa mi, ni nyɛkɛ lɛ abaa.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Oblahii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mile Yeshai, Betlehemnyo lɛ, binuu ko ni ehe esa kɛ saŋkutswaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ; oblanyo kãkãlɔ ni sheee ta naa gbeyei, ni ele mɔ kɛ wiemɔ, ni ehe hu yɛ fɛo, ni Yehowa kɛ lɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul tsu bɔfoi kɛ wiemɔ kɛtee Yeshai ŋɔɔ akɛ, “Hã obi David lɛ ni kwɛɔ otoi lɛ abana mi.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Yeshai kɛ aboloo kɛ wain ni yɔɔ kooloo wolo tɔ mli kɛ abotiabi tere teji, ni ekɛhã David koni ekɛyahã Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: David yashɛ Saul ŋɔɔ, ni ebɔi lɛ sɔ̃ɔmɔ. Saul basumɔ David sane bɔ sɔŋŋ ni efee lɛ etawuuniihiɛlɔ.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Saul kɛ shɛɛ maje ayahã Yeshai akɛ, “Hã David ahi biɛ kwraa, ni esɔmɔ mi ejaakɛ miisumɔ esane.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ nakai be lɛ, be fɛɛ be ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaahã mumɔ fɔŋ lɛ aba Saul nɔ lɛ, David tswaa saŋku lɛ, ni mumɔ fɔŋ lɛ jeɔ Saul nɔ; ni Saul he jɔɔ lɛ, ni ehiɔ ehãa lɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ bua amɛtabilɔi lɛ anaa hã ta, ni amɛnaa bakpe shi yɛ Soko, ni ji Yudabii amaŋ ko, ni amɛbagba ta yɛ Efes-Damim yɛ Soko kɛ Azeka teŋ.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ jwere gɔŋ kome ko hiɛshi, ni Israelbii lɛ hu jwere gɔŋ kroko ko hu hiɛshi, ni jɔɔ kã amɛteŋ.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nuu tatsɛlɔ ko jɛ Filistibii lɛ ateŋ eje kpo koni ebatsɛ ta. Atsɛɔ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ Goliat ni ejɛ Gat. Ekwɔlɛ feɔ ninetalɔi ekpaa.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Ewo akɔɔble tswakoto ni etsimɔ enaji ahe, ni akɔɔble fitii bloblo ko ble ekɔji asɛɛ.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, be ni David eyagbe Goliat ni eku esɛɛ ebaa lɛ, Abner kɛ lɛ tee Saul hiɛ, ni David hiɛ Goliat yitso lɛ.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Akplɔ ni hiɛ edɛ lɛ tilɛ tamɔ tso ni bleɔ mamaloo tsɔne yiteŋ tilɛ, ni ekpɔlɔ nɛɛ yitso dade tsiimɔ ji shekeli ohai ekpaa; ni mɔ ni hiɛɔ etsɛŋ lɛ nyiɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliat baho edamɔ shi, ni ebo etsɛ Israel tabilɔi lɛ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛba nyɛbagba sa kɛbaatswa ta? Filistinyo ji mi, ni nyɛ hu Saul tsuji ji nyɛ? Nyɛfãa nuu kome ni ekpeleke jɔɔ lɛ ni edamɔ nyɛnaa koni ekɛ mi abakpe.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Kɛji enyɛ mi ekɛnɔ ni egbe mi lɛ, wɔɔɔtsɔ̃mɔ nyɛtsuji. Shi kɛji mi minyɛ lɛ migbe lɛ, no lɛ nyɛaatsɔ̃mɔ wɔtsuji koni nyɛsɔ̃mɔ wɔ.”

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Filistinyo lɛ kɛɛ, “Miitswa Israel ta lɛ mpoa ŋmɛnɛ! Nyɛfãa nuu kɛbaa koni ekɛ mi abanɔ.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kɛ Israelbii lɛ nu Filistinyo nɛɛ wiemɔi lɛ, ŋmiŋmi diɛŋtsɛ mɔmɔ amɛ, ni amɛshe gbeyei naakpa. David yɛ Saul tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Efraimnyo ko ni jɛ Betlehem yɛ Yuda ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yeshai lɛ bi ji David. Yeshai nɛɛ yɛ bihii kpaanyɔ, Saul yinɔ lɛ Yeshai egbɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army. David was Jesse's youngest son.
translation_verse: David ji Yeshai bii lɛ ateŋ gbekɛ kwraa. Be ni ebihii Onukpai etɛ̃ lɛ kɛ Saul tee ta lɛ,

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: kɛfee lɛ David jɛɔ Saul ŋɔɔ ni eyaa eyakwɛɔ etsɛ toi lɛ fioo yɛ Betlehem ni ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Filistinyo lɛ jeɔ kpo daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ, ni ebadamɔɔ shi ni etsɛɔ Israelbii lɛ ŋa nɔ. Efee nakai gbii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ sɔŋŋ.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: ni ekɔ edɛ̃hiɛmɔtso lɛ ehiɛ, ni etee faa lɛ naa eyahala fɔbitɛi enumɔ ekɛwo tookwɛlɔi akotoku ni etsotsoro lɛ mli; asaŋ ejie ekromia lɛ ehiɛ, ni etsi ebɛŋkɛ Filistinyo lɛ.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Yeshai kɛɛ ebi David akɛ, “Hemɔ mamu kiloi nyɔŋma nɛɛ kɛ aboloo akwaabɔi nyɔŋma nɛɛ ni osha ohe oya nsra lɛ mli okɛyahã onyɛmimɛi lɛ.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Okɛ keesui nyɔŋma nɛɛ hu ahã asraafoi akpetsɛ lɛ, mɔ shishi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Okwɛ bɔ ni onyɛmimɛi lɛ yɔɔ, ni okɛ amɛhe okadi ko aba ni tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ ona amɛ, ni asaŋ amɛyɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Saul kɛ amɛ kɛ Israel tabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ela Jɔɔ lɛ mli amɛ kɛ Filistibii lɛ miiwu.”

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: David te shi leebi maaŋkpa, ni etu toi lɛ ewo tookwɛlɔ ko dɛŋ ni ewo niyenii lɛ, kɛkɛ ni eshwie nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ Yeshai fã lɛ lɛ. Ebashɛ Israelbii lɛ ashitoohe lɛ be mli ni tabilɔi lɛ efã, ni amɛmiibɔ oshe kɛmiiya ta lɛ naa.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ ata lɛ kɛ Filistibii lɛ hu ata lɛ tsi ba, ni ta miikwɛ ta hiɛ.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: David shi ejatsu lɛ ehã mɔ ni kwɛɔ tabilɔi lɛ ajatsui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni esha foi kɛbote tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ, ni eyaŋa enyɛmimɛi hii lɛ.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Ekɛ amɛ hiɛ wiemɔ nɔŋŋ ni nuu tatsɛ kpanaa ko jɛ Filistibii ata lɛ mli ebadamɔ shi, ni ebabɔ̃i Israelbii lɛ mpoatswaa tamɔ efeɔ daa lɛ. David nu wiemɔi ni ewie lɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Be ni Israel tabilɔi lɛ na Goliat lɛ amɛjo foi ejaakɛ gbeyei mɔmɔ amɛ naakpa.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Wiemɔ fo shi fee sɛɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛmiina nuu lɛ ni efã kpo lɛ, eeba ebabɔ Israel ahora. Naa, mɔ ni baanyɛ lɛ egbe lɛ maŋtsɛ baahã mɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ niiatsɛ wulu, asaŋ maŋtsɛ kɛ ebiyoo baahã lɛ gbãlã; no sɛɛ hu lɛ abaahã lɛ kɛ eweku fɛɛ akpa toowoo yɛ Israel.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: David bihii komɛi ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni akɛɛ abaafee ahã mɔ ni aaagbe Filistinyo nɛɛ koni ekpa ahora ni ebɔɔ Israel nɛɛ? Kwɛ Filistinyo foolɔ nɛɛ, lɛ ebɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ tai lɛ ahora?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Hii lɛ here David nɔ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ ni akɛɛ abaafee ahã mɔ ni aaagbe Filistinyo lɛ.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Shi Eliab, David nyɛminukpa lɛ, nu be ni David kɛ hii lɛ wieɔ lɛ, ni Eliab mli wo la wo David ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛni feemɔ oba yɛ biɛ? Namɔ oshi toi fioo lɛ ohã yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ? Ona onukpaianii ni ofeɔ lɛ? Te ta lɛ kwɛmɔ hewɔ oba nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: David jie enaa ekɛɛ, “Mɛni mifee? Jeee sane kɛkɛ mibi?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: David shi enyɛmi lɛ sɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ ehe ekɛ mɔ kroko wie. Ebi sane kome lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni hetoo koome lɛ nɔŋŋ hu ahã lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Be ni anu wiemɔ ni David wie lɛ, ayabɔ Saul amaniɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Saul tsu ni ayaŋɔ David abahã lɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Mɔ ko mɔ ko tsui akafã yɛ nuu nɛɛ hewɔ. Otsulɔ aaatee ekɛ nɛkɛ Filistinyo nɛɛ ayakpe.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ David akɛ, “Onyɛŋ Filistinyo nɛɛ hiɛ odamɔ, ejaakɛ bo lɛ gbekɛ kɛkɛ ji bo, shi lɛ lɛ ewu ta aahu kɛjɛ eblahiiaŋ tɔ̃ɔ.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Shi David here Saul nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Otsulɔ kwɛɔ etsɛ toi. Be fɛɛ be ni jata loo oshishibrishi ko aaabamɔ toi lɛ ateŋ toobi ko lɛ,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mitiuɔ kooloo lɛ miyatswaa lɛ nɔ, ni mishɔ̃ɔ toobi lɛ yɛ edɛŋ. Kɛji jata loo oshishibrishi lɛ te shi ewo mi lɛ, mimɔɔ etsɛŋ, ni mitswiaa lɛ nii, ni migbeɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ, jata kɛ oshishibrishi po migbe amɛ. Akɛni nɛkɛ Filistinyo foolɔ nɛɛ miibɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ tai lɛ ahora hewɔ lɛ, eeena nɔ ni kooloi lɛ na yɛ midɛŋ lɛ eko.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Yehowa, mɔ ni jie mi yɛ jata kɛ oshishibrishi daaŋ lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ eeejie mi yɛ Filistinyo nɛɛ dɛŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ Saul kɛɛ David akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ! Yaa, ni Yehowa aye abua bo.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ edade atade lɛ wo David, ni ekɛ akɔɔble fai lɛ bu lɛ, ni ewo lɛ dama eshwie atade lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: David ŋmɔ Saul tawuu klante lɛ yɛ atade lɛ nɔ. Shi be ni David ka nyiɛmɔ lɛ eyanyɛɛɛ, ejaakɛ ewoko nakai atade dã. Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Minyɛŋ mawo nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ mikɛyanɔ, ejaakɛ mikako eko mikwɛko dã.” No hewɔ lɛ, David jie nibii lɛ yɛ ehe,

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Filistinyo lɛ hu tsi eba, ni ebabɛŋkɛ David.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Be ni Filistinyo lɛ fɔ̃ ehiɛ ni ena David lɛ, ebuuu lɛ, ejaakɛ ena lɛ akɛ oblanyo fioo kɛkɛ ni tsuɔ oo, kɛ ehiɛ fɛo.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Ebi David akɛ, “Ani gbee ji mi hewɔ ni ohiɛ tso kɛbaa minɔ lɛ?” Be ni Goliat etsɛ esɛɛ jemawɔŋ ekɛlomɔ David sɛɛ lɛ,

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: ekɛɛ David akɛ, “Ba! Bo lɛ shɛ biɛ; mikɛ oloo baahã loofɔji kɛ ŋaŋ kooloi ni amɛye.”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: David to he ehã Filistinyo lɛ akɛ, “Bo lɛ ooba minɔ kɛ klante kɛ akplɔ kɛ tsɛŋ; shi mi lɛ mikɛ bo miiba abakpe yɛ Yehowa ni ji Tatsɛ lɛ, Israel tai ni obɔɔ amɛ ahora lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbɛi mli.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ Yehowa baahã maye onɔ kunim, ni mafo oyi, ni mikɛ Filistibii ata lɛ mli gbohii lɛ baahã ŋwɛi loofɔji kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi kakawuai koni amɛye, koni jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ana ale akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ko yɛ Israel.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Asaŋ asafo ni ekpe nɛɛ fɛɛ kɛaana ale akɛ jeee klante loo akplɔ Yehowa kɛhereɔ mɔ yiwala, ejaakɛ ta lɛ Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ ji mɔ ni wuɔ, ni ebaaŋɔ nyɛ ewo wɔdɛŋ.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ enine wo ekotoku lɛ mli, ni ekɔ tɛ ewo akromia lɛ mli ni efɔ̃. Tɛ lɛ yatswa Goliat hiɛnaa ni ebote ehiɛŋtso mli; kɛkɛ ni Goliat gbee shi, ni ehiɛ yabu shi.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Belɛ David kɛ akromia kɛ tɛ ye Goliat nɔ, ni egbe lɛ tsɛbelɛ ehiɛɛɛ klante po.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: David sha foi oya, ni eyaho edamɔ Goliat nɔ; emɔ Goliat klante lɛ egbala yɛ ehebo lɛ mli ni ekɛfo Goliat yi. Be ni Filistibii lɛ na akɛ agbe amɛtatsɛ ni tsɛɔ Israel ŋa nɔ lɛ, amɛjo foi.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel kɛ Yuda hii lɛ bɔ oshe, ni amɛtiu Filistibii lɛ kɛ foi. Amɛnyiɛ Filistibii lɛ asɛɛ kɛyashi Gat kɛ Ekron agboi lɛ anaa. Gbi lɛ Filistibii pilafoi jwere shi kɛjɛ Shaaraim aahu kɛyashi Gat kɛ Ekron fɛɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ je Filistibii lɛ asɛɛ, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba lɛ, amɛbaha Filistibii lɛ anibii yɛ amɛshitoohe lɛ mli.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: David kɔ Goliat yitso lɛ kɛba Yerusalɛm; shi Goliat tawuu dade dama lɛ, David hã ehi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enine nɔ yɛ ebuu lɛ mli. Akɛ David tsɔ̃ɔ Saul

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kwɛɔ David yisɛɛ be ni eyaa koni ekɛ Goliat ayakpe lɛ, ebi tatsɛ Abner akɛ, “Abner, namɔ bi ji nɛkɛ oblanyo nɛɛ?” Abner to he akɛ, “Nii, mina onane akɛ mileee,”

english_verse: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaabi mɔ bi ni ji oblanyo lɛ.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Saul bi David akɛ, “Namɔ bi ji bo, oblanyo?” David jie lɛ naa ekɛɛ, “Otsulɔ Yeshai, Betlehemnyo lɛ, bi ji mi.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Saul hu ŋɔ David nakai gbi lɛ, ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ David aku esɛɛ kɛya etsɛ we lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Bɔ sɔŋŋ ni Yonatan sumɔ David tamɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ David bɔ naanyo ni amɛkpãŋ.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yonatan jie ehe nibii ni ekɛwula David, ekɛ etade lɛ kɛ edama lɛ kɛ eklante lɛ kɛ egãi lɛ kɛ emlifiinɔ lɛ hã lɛ.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Tai fɛɛ ni Saul tsu David wuu lɛ, etee eba kɛ omanye; ni no hewɔ lɛ, Saul fee David etatsɛmɛi ateŋ mɔ kome, amɛ ji nɔ ko ni sa Israel hii tabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Saul tsuji lɛ tete fɛɛ ahiɛ. Saul ye David he awuŋã

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Be ni David egbe Filistinyo Goliat lɛ, ni Israel tabilɔi lɛ eku amɛsɛɛ kɛbaa shĩa lɛ, Israel yei lɛ jɛjɛɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli amɛkɛ lala kɛ joo bakpee Maŋtsɛ Saul. Amɛhiɛ fa bii kɛ ŋoŋoi kɛ miji; ni amɛnya;

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: ni amɛla be mli ni amɛnyaa lɛ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Saul egbe akpekpei abɔ, shi David egbe akpei nyɔŋmai abɔ.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Wiemɔ nɛɛ eyaŋɔɔɔ Saul naa kwraa ni emli wo la, ni wiemɔ ni je enaa ji, “Ei! Akɛɛ David egbe gbɔmɛi akpei nyɔŋmai abɔ, shi mi lɛ akpeii amli kɛkɛ. Mɛni shwɛɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ mɔ fe maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔtamɔ?”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ jetsɛremɔ, be mli ni David tswaa saŋku ehãa Saul tamɔ bɔ ni efeɔ daa gbi lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ hã mumɔ fɔŋ ko bayi Saul nɔ, ni egri yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli. No mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Saul akplɔ lɛ hiɛ edɛ̃.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Saul ekɛɛ yɛ eyitsoŋ akɛ, “Matsu David akplɔ lɛ,” shi David wi ehe shii enyɔ sɔŋŋ ni ehe je mli.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Saul she David gbeyei, ejaakɛ ena akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ David yɛ, shi lɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ekwa lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: ni eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛ David yayeɔ kunim, ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ lɛ yɛ.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Shi Israel kɛ Yuda fɛɛ sumɔ David sane ojogbaŋŋ, ejaakɛ enyiɛɔ amɛhiɛ kɛyaa ta ni ekɛ amɛbaa kɛ omanye. David ŋɔ Saul biyoo ŋa

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Saul wo David shi akɛ, “Bɛ ona mibiyoo nukpa Merab lɛ? Mikɛ lɛ baahã bo gbãlã kɛji ooofee ekãa kɛkɛ ni okɛ Yehowa henyɛlɔi lɛ aaawu ahã mi lɛ.” Saul susumɔ ji akɛ, lɛ tuuŋtu lɛ, ekɛ enine etaŋ David he, shi Filistibii lɛ ji mɛi ni baagbe David ahã lɛ yɛ tai lɛ eko mli.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Namɔ ji mi, ni namɛi ji miwekumɛi kɛ mitsɛ weku lɛ yɛ Israel, ni matsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ shaanuu?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Be ni shɛ be ni esa akɛ akɛ Saul biyoo, Merab, ahã David gbãlã lɛ, akɛ Merab hã Adriel, Meholatnyo lɛ, moŋ.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Nakai be mli lɛ Saul biyoo ni gbɛi ji Mikal lɛ miisumɔ David. Be ni atswa Saul adafi akɛ Mikal miisumɔ David lɛ ena mishɛɛ,

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ “Yiɛ! Mikɛ Mikal baahã lɛ koni etsɔ̃ tamɔ akpa ehã lɛ, koni Filistibii lɛ anine agbe lɛ ahã mi.” Enɛ hã Saul wo David shi nɔ ni ji shii enyɔ nɔ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ obaatsɔ mishaanuu.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul tsuji lɛ kɛ David yawie wiemɔ nɛɛ lɛ, David kɛɛ tsuji lɛ akɛ, “Kolɛ nyɛkɛɛ benɛ maŋtsɛ shaanuu tsɔ̃mɔ lɛ shwɛmɔ sane ni? Mi hu nɛ, ohiafobi humi ni mijeee mɔ ko.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Saul tsuji lɛ yabɔ lɛ hetoo ni David hã amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Shi Saul tsu amɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyakɛa David akɛ aheee Mikal yinii ko kwraa fe Filistibii lɛ afoo naa loo komekomei oha kɛkɛ, koni akɛtɔ maŋtsɛ he owele yɛ ehenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ.” Saul susumɔ ji akɛ foo naa loo lɛ taomɔ nɔ baatsɔ̃ ni Filistibii lɛ anine baagbe David.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Be ni Saul tsuji lɛ yabɔ David amaniɛ lɛ, emii shɛ ehe akɛ ebatsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ shaanuu. No hewɔ lɛ, be ni eshwɛ fioo ni gbi lɛ shɛɔ lɛ,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Saul kɛ ehiŋmɛi ŋmɛ shi ni ena akɛ Yehowa miibu David he, ni asaŋ akɛ Israel fɛɛ miisumɔ David sane lɛ,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: gbeyei ni Saul sheɔ David lɛ mli bawa fe tsuutsu ko lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Saul tsɔ̃ David henyɛlɔ kwraa.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Filistibii amaŋtsɛmɛi fãfãa tai; shi be fɛɛ be ni amɛaafã ta lɛ, David yeɔ Filistibii lɛ anɔ kunim fe Saul tsuji krokomɛi fɛɛ. Enɛ hã David gbɛi hehe naakpa.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Saul wo ebi Yonatan kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ ayitsoŋ akɛ amɛgbe David kɛji nine shɛ enɔ. Shi akɛni Saul bi Yonatan sumɔɔ David sane

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Mi lɛ mibaya mitsɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋa lɛ mli, he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, koni mi kɛ lɛ ayawie ohe. Bɔ ni mibana lɛ mahã ole.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Edɔɔɔ ewala he, ni no hewɔ lɛ, etee ni ekɛ Goliat, Filistinyo lɛ, yakpe, ni egbe lɛ, ni Yehowa hã Israel fɛɛ ye kunim kpeteŋkple. Bo diɛŋtsɛ hu ona kunim ni eye lɛ, ni onya he. Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni otaoɔ akɛ ofee mɔ ni efeko efɔŋ ko lɛ esha, ni ogbe David yakatswaa lɛ?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Saul bo ebi Yonatan toi, ni Saul kã kitã ekɛɛ, “Mina Yehowa akɛ agbeŋ David.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yonatan tee ni eyatsɛ David yɛ eteemɔhe lɛ; ni be ni egba lɛ nɔ ni etee nɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yonatan kɛ David ba Saul ŋɔɔ, ni David ku sɛɛ ebahi Saul ŋɔɔ ni esɔmɔ lɛ tamɔ tsuutsu lɛ.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Yɛ mli aahu lɛ ta ba ekoŋŋ. David fã kɛtee eyawu ta lɛ, ni eye Filistibii lɛ anɔ butuu, ni amɛjo foi yɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Saul ka akɛ etsu David akplɔ lɛ kɛmɔ gbogbo lɛ, shi David sha ehe, ni akplɔ lɛ yatsɛkɛ gbogbo lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni David jo foi, ni eje Saul dɛŋ.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, Saul wo mɛi agbɛ akɛ amɛyawo David ka yɛ ewe lɛ bɔ ni afee koni lɛ Saul lɛ, enine ashɛ David nɔ enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi koni egbe lɛ. Shi David ŋa, Mikal, wo David ŋaa ekɛɛ, “Kɛji ohereee oyiwala ŋmɛnɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ, wɔ lɛ abaagbe bo.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Mikal shi David kɛtsɔ̃ samflɛ mli kɛyi shi ni David jo foi etee, ni eje Saul dɛŋ.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mikal wo nɔ ko ni agbɔ lɛ tamɔ gbɔmɔ efɔ̃ David saatso lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ nɔ lɛ yitso tsɔle abotia he tsɔi sune lɛ, ni eha nɔ lɛ mama.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Be ni Saul bɔfoi ni etsu akɛ amɛyamɔ David amɛbahã lɛ lɛ shɛ David we lɛ mli lɛ, Mikal kɛɛ bɔfoi lɛ akɛ David naaa hetselɛ.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Shi Saul saa wo bɔfoi lɛ agbɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtee David we lɛ akɛ amɛyana lɛ kɛ amɛhiŋmɛi; ni akɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛwoa lɛ kɛ saa lɛ fɛɛ nyɛbahãa mi koni magbe lɛ.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Be ni bɔfoi lɛ ba lɛ amɛbanina amãgã ni tsɔle abotia he tsɔi sune kã David saatso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Saul bi Mikal akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ ni olaka mi nɛkɛ, ni ojie mihenyɛlɔ lɛ gbɛ etee, ni ohã eje midɛŋ nɛɛ?” Mikal hã Saul hetoo ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ewo mi shi ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Kɛji owaaa mi koni majo foi lɛ, no lɛ magbe bo.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Be ni David jo foi lɛ eba Samuel ŋɔɔ yɛ Rama, ni ebagba lɛ saji fɛɛ ni Saul kɛye lɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ Samuel fɛɛ tee ni amɛyahi Naiot.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Ayatswa Saul adafi akɛ, “Naa, David yɛ Naiot yɛ Rama.”

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul wo bɔfoi agbɛ koni amɛyamɔ David kɛba. Be ni bɔfoi nɛɛ yashɛ Naiot ni amɛyanina Samuel damɔ gbalɔi aku lɛ naa akɛ amɛnukpa ni amɛmiigba lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ lɛ bayi bɔfoi lɛ anɔ ni amɛ hu amɛbɔi gbaa.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ababɔ Saul amaniɛ; no hewɔ lɛ, esaa etsu bɔfoi krokomɛi; shi amɛ hu amɛyashi gbalɔi lɛ anɔ. Saul ku sɛɛ etsu bɔfoi ekoŋŋ nɔ ni ji shii etɛ̃ nɔ; shi amɛ hu amɛyatsɔ̃mɔ gbalɔi nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul diɛŋtsɛ yi mli ni etee Rama. Be ni eyashɛ nubu wulu ni yɔɔ Seku lɛ he lɛ, ebi David kɛ Samuel shi ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ji he ni Samuel kɛ David yɔɔ lɛ?” Mɔ ko tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ ekɛɛ, “Amɛyɛ Naiot yɛ Rama.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul shwie nɔ kɛjɛ Seku ni eeya Naiot yɛ Rama; shi Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ lɛ yi lɛ hu enɔ, ni ehiɛ gbaa yɛ gbɛteŋ aahu kɛyashi eyashɛ Naiot yɛ Rama.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul hu kpɔlɔ ehe atadei lɛ ni egba yɛ Samuel hiɛ; ni ekã shi kɛ ehe folo nakai gbi lɛ shwane muu lɛ fɛ̃ɛ kɛ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛ̃ɛ. Bɔ ni fee ni abɔi kɛɛmɔ akɛ, “Mɛni, Saul hu etsɔ̃ gbalɔ hu?” lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ David jo foi yɛ Naiot yɛ Rama kɛba Yonatan ŋɔɔ, ni ebabi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni mifee? Mɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ mitɔ̃, ni mɛɛ esha po mifee otsɛ hewɔ ni etaoɔ mi egbe nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Mɛɛ nakai hu ni akɛ abaagbe bo? Nɔ ko bɛ ni mitsɛ baafee ni ewooo mitoi nɔ, nɔ wulu ni jio, nɔ bibioo ni jio. Mɛni hewɔ mitsɛ kɛ sane nɛɛ baatee mi? Ebɛ mli nakai.”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Shi David to he ekɛɛ, “Otsɛ le faŋŋ bɔ ni osumɔɔ misane, ni no hewɔ lɛ, eyiŋtoo ji akɛ okale, no lɛ sane lɛ baadɔ bo. Mina Yehowa kɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ hu akɛ ekã shi faŋŋ akɛ mikɛ gbele teŋ jekɛɛɛ.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Bi mi nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni otaoɔ, ni mafee mahã bo.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Yonatan akɛ, “Wɔ lɛ nyɔŋ hee baaje, ni kulɛ esa akɛ mikɛ maŋtsɛ ayata shi aye nii; shi ofainɛ, ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni maya ni mayatee mihe yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi biɛ gbii etɛ̃ gbɛkɛ.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Kɛji otsɛ bi mishi lɛ, okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘David bi mi gbɛ kpɛ̃kpɛ̃ɛkpɛ̃ akɛ eesha foi eya emaŋ Betlehem nɔŋŋ ni eba, ejaakɛ eweku fɛɛ miishã daa afi afɔle yɛ jɛi.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Kɛji eto he akɛ ‘Ojogbaŋŋ,’ lɛ; no lɛ miye mihe. Shi kɛji emli fu lɛ, no tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ eto eyiŋ akɛ ebaafee mi efɔŋ.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, feemɔ mi ejurɔ nɛɛ, yɛ kpãŋmɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni okɛ mi ekpãŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji miyeɔ fɔ lɛ, bo diɛŋtsɛ gbee mi; ejaakɛ mɛɛ hewɔ ni okɛ mi aaayahã otsɛ?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ̃. Kɛji efo mitoi naa kɛkɛ po akɛ mitsɛ etswa fai shi akɛ ebaafee bo efɔŋ lɛ, ani mikɛŋ bo?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Yonatan to he ekɛɛ, “Ba ni wɔtee ŋa lɛ nɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyi mli, amɛyi enyɔ lɛ, ni amɛtee ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛyashɛ jɛi lɛ, Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, aaaye mi odase. Kɛji mita mitsɛ yitso he mikwɛ, ni mina akɛ eyɛ ohe tsuijurɔ lɛ matsu oŋɔɔ wɔ, loo wɔsɛɛ, nɛkɛ be mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, koni abawo otoi nɔ.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji mitsɛ eto eyiŋ doo akɛ efɔŋ nɔŋŋ ebafee bo, ni mihãaa ole koni ojo foi oya shweshweeshwe lɛ, no lɛ Yehowa awo mi he nyɔmɔ kɛteke nɔ. Yehowa kɛ bo ahi shi tamɔ bɔ ni ekɛ mitsɛ ehi shi lɛ.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: ohiɛ akakpa nɔ koni ofee mishwiei ejurɔ kɛya naanɔ. Be ni Yehowa aaakpãtã ohenyɛlɔi fɛɛ ahiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Yonatan hã David saa kã lɛ kitã ekoŋŋ akɛ ehiɛ akakpa amɛteŋ suɔmɔ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ Yonatan sumɔɔ David tamɔ bɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe lɛ.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Wɔ lɛ nyɔŋ hee baaje, ni aaabi oshi, ejaakɛ osɛi lɛ nɔ baakã efolo.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Ni gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ abaakɔ sɛɛ fe nine akɛ obɛ. Nakai gbi lɛ yaa ni oyatee ohe yɛ tɛi ni bua shi yɛ jɛi lɛ ahe he ni oyatee ohe yɛ be ni sane nɛɛ tsɔ̃ naa shi lɛ.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Mibatserɛ̃ gãii etɛ̃ mawo tɛi lɛ amasɛi gbɛ oookɛɛ mitsɛ̃ nɔ ko pɔtɛɛ ko gãi.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ mibatsu oblanyo fioo ko, ni makɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Yaatao gãii lɛ kɛba.’ Kɛji mikɛshi sɛɛ fee sɛɛ akɛ, ‘Okwɛɛɛ, gãii lɛ yɛ obiɛgbɛ moŋ, kɔlɔmɔ kɛba lɛ,’ no tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ oba, ejaakɛ mina Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ sane fɔŋ ko yeŋ bo, ni obaafee shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji mikɛɛ oblanyo lɛ akɛ, ‘Okwɛɛɛ? Gãii lɛ eteke bo’ lɛ, no tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ ojo foi ni oya, ejaakɛ Yehowa ejie bo gbɛ.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Yehowa ji mi kɛ bo teŋ odase yɛ shii ni wɔwoowoo wɔhe nɛɛ he kɛmiiya naanɔ.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David yatee ehe yɛ ŋa lɛ mli. Be ni nyɔŋ hee lɛ je lɛ Maŋtsɛ Saul ba niyenii lɛ ashi.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Eta esɛ̃i ni maa gbogbo lɛ he lɛ nɔ, nɔ nɔ ni etaa daa lɛ, ni Yonatan ta ehiɛ tuuŋtu, ni Abner ta Saul masɛi. David tamɔhe lɛ kã efolo;

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: shi Saul ekɛɛɛ nɔ ko nakai gbi lɛ, ejaakɛ esusumɔ ji, “Sane ko eba David nɔ, ni etsuuko ehe, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ehe tseee.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Shi enɔ jetsɛremɔ, ni ji nyɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji gbii enyɔ lɛ, be ni David tamɔhe lɛ kã efolo ekoŋŋ lɛ, Saul bi Yonatan akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ Yeshai bi lɛ bako niyeli nyɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛ fɛɛ nɛɛ lɛ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Ofainɛ, ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ ni maya maba, ejaakɛ wɔweku lɛ miishã afɔle yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni minyɛminuu lɛ eshɛ mi akɛ miba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji oosumɔ misane lɛɛlɛŋ lɛ hã maya ni mayasara minyɛmimɛi lɛ maba.’ Enɛ hewɔ ni ebako maŋtsɛ okplɔŋmɛɛ lɛ shishi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Saul mli fu wo Yonatan naakpa, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Gbee yoo yakagbɔmɔ fɔŋ kɛ atuatselɔ bi ni tamɔ bo! Okɛ Yeshai bi lɛ miibɔ, ni okɛmiiwo bo diɛŋtsɛ kɛ onyɛ fɛɛ hiɛ mama nɔ yɛ maŋ.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Naa, gbii abɔ ni Yeshai bi nɛɛ hiɛ kã lɛ, bo diɛŋtsɛ ni jio, omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ni jio, eko fɛɛ eko yi etɔ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, tsu koni ayaŋɔ lɛ abahã mi ejaakɛ ja egbo.”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Yonatan here etsɛ Saul nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ sa akɛ egbo? Mɛni efee?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Shi kometoo lɛ Saul fɔ̃ ekpɔlɔ lɛ, ni kulɛ ekɛmiitsu Yonatan koni egbe lɛ. Enɛ Yonatan kɛna akɛ etsɛ eŋmɔ eyiŋ kpɔ lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ ebaagbe David.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Yonatan te shi kɛ mlifu ni naa wa kɛshi okplɔ̃ lɛ shi; ni nakai gbi lɛ, ni ji nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yonatan yeee nii lɛ eko, ejaakɛ David sane miidɔ lɛ tsɔ̃, ni asaŋ akɛ etsɛ Saul ewo lɛ Yonatan lɛ hiɛgbele nɛkɛ.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Gbi lɛ nɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Yonatan tee ŋa lɛ nɔ bɔ ni ato lɛ, ni ekɛ oblanyo fioo ko nyiɛ.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ oblanyo fioo lɛ akɛ, “Sha foi koni oyatao gãii ni matserɛ̃ lɛ kɛba.” Be mli ni oblanyo lɛ hiɛ foi kɛyaa lɛ Yonatan tsɛ̃ gãi kroko kɛteke lɛ.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Ni be ni oblanyo lɛ yashɛ he ni gãi lɛ yagbee lɛ, Yonatan bo ni ekɛɛ oblanyo lɛ akɛ, “Okwɛɛɛ? Gãi lɛ eteke bo!

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Feemɔ mramra, ohe afee oya, kaadamɔ shi!” Oblanyo lɛ yakɔlɔ gãii lɛ kɛba enuŋtsɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, oblanyo lɛ leee nɔ ni afee lɛ shishi kwraa. Yonatan kɛ David kɛkɛ ni le.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛ enibii lɛ hã oblanyo lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Baaho, ni okɛya maŋ lɛŋ.”

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ tee nɔŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ ni David fã kpo kɛjɛ tɛi ni bua shi lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ ehiɛ babu shi ni ekoto Yonatan shii etɛ̃. Be ni David kɛ Yonatan eshwɔshwɔɔ amɛnaa sɛɛ lɛ, amɛwo yara amɛfo aahu kɛyashi David nɔ teke nɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Anyɛmi, gbii abɔ kɛ̃ ni wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔkamɔ wɔhe kitã yɛ Yehowa gbɛi mli akɛ, ‘Yehowa aye abua mi kɛ bo, kɛ mishwiei kɛ bo hu oshwiei kɛya naanɔ’ lɛ, yaaba jogbaŋŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni David tsɔ̃ ehe ni etee, ni Yonatan hu ku esɛɛ etee maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: David ba Osɔfo Ahimelek ŋɔɔ yɛ Nob maŋ lɛ mli. Ahimelek kɛ hekpokpomɔ bakpee David ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni okome too onyiɛ, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko fataaa ohe lɛ?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Osɔfo Ahimelek akɛ, “Minyiɛ maŋtsɛ tsumɔ ko nɔ. Ebɔ mi kɔkɔ akɛ, ‘Kaahã mɔ ko mɔ ko miile nɔ tsumɔ ni mitsu bo nɛɛ kɛ kitã hu ni miwo bo yɛ he lɛ.’ Oblahii ni mikɛyaa lɛ, mitsɔ̃ɔ amɛ he ko ni amɛ kɛ mi akpe yɛ.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Mɛni oyɔɔ yɛ onine nɔ? Hã mi aboloo akwaabɔi enumɔ loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ooona koni mikɛhiɛ midɛŋ.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Osɔfo Ahimelek here David nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mibɛ aboloo ko kwraa yɛ biɛ fe aboloo krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji oblahii lɛ eko etako yoo he lɛ no lɛ sane ko bɛ he.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: David to he ehã osɔfo lɛ akɛ, “Anɔkwale mli lɛ wɔtako yoo he tamɔ bɔ ni kɛji wɔnyiɛ tsumɔ folo po nɔ ni wɔtaaa yoo he lɛ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛji oblahii lɛ nyiɛ ŋmɛnɛ tsumɔ wulu ni tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛhiɛŋ amɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ?”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni osɔfo lɛ kɛ aboloo krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ hã David, ejaakɛ aboloo ko aboloo ko bɛ enine nɔ akɛ ja aboloo ni akɛmãa Yehowa hiɛ lɛ, nɔ ni kɛji ajie yɛ jɛi lɛ ja akɛ aboloo kla to emomo lɛ najiaŋ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Gbi nɛɛ lɛ maŋtsɛ Saul tookwɛlɔ nukpa ni atsɛɔ lɛ Doeg, Edomnyo lɛ, yɛ jɛi ni atsi enaa yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Osɔfo Ahimelek akɛ, “Obɛ klante loo akplɔ ko yɛ onine nɔ? Maŋtsɛ tsumɔ lɛ yafee kplakpla, ni no hewɔ lɛ, miklante lɛ jio, mikpɔlɔ lɛ jio, mikɔɔɔ ekoeko mihiɛɛɛ midɛŋ kɛbaaa.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Osɔfo Ahimelek jie naa ekɛɛ, “Goliat, Filistinyo lɛ ni ogbe yɛ Ela Jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ klante lɛ yɛ biɛ. Ekã tsitsinɔhaanii lɛ sɛɛ ni abla he. Kɛji oosumɔ lɛ no lɛ kɔ, ejaakɛ no sɛɛ lɛ klante kroko ko bɛ biɛ dɔŋŋ.” Ni David to he ekɛɛ akɛ, “Enɔ bɛ po; kɔ ohã mi.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: David shi Nob maŋ lɛ mli nakai gbi lɛ; eejo Saul naa foi; ni etee Gat Maŋtsɛ Akish ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Akish tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ, jeee David lɛ ni etsɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ nɛ?” Jeee mɔ nɛ he lala alaa akɛjoɔ akɛ, “Saul egbe akpei, ni David egbe akpei nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Wiemɔ nɛɛ hã David hɛle shi, ni ebɔ̃i Gat Maŋtsɛ Akish gbeyeishemɔ naakpa.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, David tsake enifeemɔ yɛ maŋbii lɛ ahiɛ. Ekwa eye sɛkɛ, ni efee enii oookɛɛ sɛkɛyelɔ kɛji ahiɛ emli. Eŋmala nii yɛ maŋ agbo lɛ shinaa lɛ nɔ, ni ehã lajɔ̃ tete wu etsɛ̃ŋ mli kpɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Akish bi etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ, gbɔmɔ ni nyɛna akɛ eye sɛkɛ lɛ mɛni nyɛkɛ lɛ baa abahã mi afee?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Sɛkɛyelɔi ahe miihia mi hewɔ ni nyɛyakpala mɔnɛ nɛɛ kɛba koni ebafee sɛkɛyelɔi anii etsɔ̃ɔ mi lɛ? Aso esa kwraa akɛ gbɔmɔ nɛkɛ hiɔ miwe nɛɛ mli tete?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: David shi Gat maŋ lɛ mli, ni ejo foi kɛtee eyahi Adullam tɛkplo lɛ mli. Be ni enyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ etsɛ we lɛ fɛɛ na le lɛ, amɛtee eŋɔɔ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mɛi fɛɛ ni aawa amɛ yi kɛ mɛi hu ni hiɛhiɛ nyɔji kɛ mɛi fɛɛ hu ni bɛ shihilɛ he miishɛɛ lɛ bua amɛhe naa ni amɛyafata David he. Kɛkɛ ni David batsɔ̃ amɛsafoiatsɛ. Hii aaafee ohai ejwɛ sɔŋŋ ni bafata David he nɛɛ.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: David shi Adullam tɛkplo lɛ mli ni etee Mizpa yɛ Moab shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyakɛɛ Moab maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, hã mitsɛ kɛ minyɛ afã kɛba ni amɛbahi nyɛŋɔɔ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni male bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaato mi ahã.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David shi efɔlɔi lɛ ehã Moab maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni efɔlɔi lɛ hi Moab Maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ bei abɔ fɛɛ ni David yɔɔ tɛkplo lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ gbalɔ lɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Gad lɛ ba, ni ebakɛɛ David akɛ, “Kaahi tɛkplo nɛɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Shi biɛ ni oya Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ, David shi tɛkplo lɛ mli ni etee eyahi Heret koo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Gbi nɛɛ Saul yɛ Gibea, ni eta shi yɛ tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ tamariske tso lɛ shishi yɛ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ nɔ; ehiɛ ekpɔlɔ yɛ edɛŋ, ni etsuji lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛkpe.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni abakɛɛ lɛ akɛ ayana he ni David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ etsuji ni damɔ ehe lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛmiibo toi, nyɛ Benyaminbii! Ani Yeshai bi lɛ baahã nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔji kɛ waintromii hu; aloo eeewo nyɛ mɛi akpekpe akui kɛ mɛi ohaohai akui asafoiatsɛmɛi hu,

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: hewɔ ni nyɛ fɛɛ tswɛm nyɛkpãŋ miyi nɔ lɛ? Te mɔ ko ejeee nyɛteŋ ebawooo mitoi nɔ akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mimusuŋbi lɛ kɛ Yeshai bi lɛ efee ekome? Mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ nyɛteŋ ni misane dɔɔ lɛ bɔ ni eeewo mitoi nɔ akɛ mimusuŋbi lɛ ewo mitsulɔ lɛ yiŋ koni ete shi ewo mi tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛnaa ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Doeg, Edomnyo lɛ, damɔ Saul tsuji lɛ amasɛi. Kɛkɛ ni ehere nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mina Yeshai bi lɛ yɛ Nob ni eba Osɔfo Ahimelek, Ahitub bi lɛ, ŋɔɔ,

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: ni Ahimelek bi Yehowa nii ehã lɛ, ni ehã lɛ gbɛnɔ niyenii, ni asaŋ ekɛ Goliat, Filistinyo lɛ, klante lɛ hu ehã lɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Saul tsu koni ayakpee Ahimelek, Ahitub bi lɛ, kɛ etsɛ we lɛ mli bii ni amɛ nɔŋŋ ji osɔfoi ni yɔɔ Nob lɛ fɛɛ abahã lɛ. Be ni gbɔmɛi nɛɛ fɛɛ bashɛ Maŋtsɛ Saul hiɛ lɛ,

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ akɛ, “Oobo toi lo, Ahitub bi?” Ahimelek here lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Hɛɛ, minuŋtsɔ!”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni, bo kɛ Yeshai bi lɛ, nyɛkpãŋ miyi nɔ, ni ohã lɛ niyenii, ni asaŋ owo edɛŋ klante, ni obi Nyɔŋmɔ nii ohã lɛ, ni no hewɔ ni ete shi ewo mi, ni ewo mi ka bɔ ni nyɛnaa ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ?”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ahimelek to he ehã maŋtsɛ lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nɔ ni mile ji akɛ maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko bɛ ni eji ehe anɔkwafo tamɔ David. Maŋtsɛ shaanuu ji lɛ, ni agbɛnɛ maŋtsɛ he bulɔi lɛ asafoiatsɛ ji lɛ, ni awoɔ lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Jeee ŋmɛnɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbi nɔ ni mibi Nyɔŋmɔ nii mihã David. Enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ akɛ Maŋtsɛ kɛ sane aaafɔ̃ mi, etsulɔ, loo mitsɛ we lɛ mli mɔ ko kwraa nɔ, ejaakɛ mileee sane nɛɛ he nɔ ko nɔ ko kwraa.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Ahimelek, ja agbe bo kɛ otsɛ we lɛ mli bii fɛɛ.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã ehebulɔi ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛtsɔ̃a nyɛhe ni nyɛgbea Yehowa osɔfoi nɛɛ, ejaakɛ amɛ hu amɛwa David eko. Amɛna amɛle akɛ David miijo foi, shi amɛbawooo mitoi nɔ shi maŋtsɛ lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ amɛawo amɛnine nɔ amɛtswia osɔfo lɛ nii.”

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Saul hã akɛ klante kpãtã Nob maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ; agbe hii kɛ yei kɛ gbekɛbii kɛ abifabii kɛ tsinai kɛ teji kɛ toi fɛɛ.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Shi Ahitub bi Ahimelek bihii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Abiatar lɛ he je mli, ni ejo foi etee David ŋɔɔ,

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: ni eyabɔ lɛ amaniɛ akɛ Saul egbe Yehowa osɔfoi lɛ.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Abiatar akɛ, “Nakai gbi lɛ beebe, be ni mina Doeg, Edomnyo lɛ, yɛ Nob lɛ pɛ ni mina akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ lɛ ebaaya eyakɛɛ Saul. Mi ejɛ ni otsɛ we lɛ mli bii fɛɛ egboi nɛɛ.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Okɛ mi ahi shi; ni okashe gbeyei, ejaakɛ mɔ ni taoɔ mi egbe lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ etaoɔ bo hu egbe nɛɛ; shi kɛji oyɛ mimasɛi lɛ oyɛ shweshweeshwe.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Abagba David akɛ Filistibii lɛ eyatua Keila maŋ lɛ, ni amɛmiiha ŋmaa ni yɔɔ ŋmashaahei lɛ.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David bi Yehowa nii akɛ, “Ani miya ni miyatua Filistibii lɛ kɛhere Keila lo?” Yehowa here David nɔ ekɛɛ, “Yaa ni oyatua Filistibii lɛ ni ohere Keila.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Shi David webii lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni wɔyɔɔ yɛ biɛ nɛɛ po lɛ, wɔmiishe gbeyei, aahu ni wɔtee Keila wɔkɛɛ wɔkɛ Filistibii atai lɛ yaawu.”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã David ku sɛɛ ni ebi Yehowa nii ekoŋŋ. Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa Keila lɛ, shi mibahã oye Filistibii lɛ anɔ kunim.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David kɛ ewebii lɛ fã kɛtee Keila ni amɛkɛ Filistibii lɛ yawu, ni amɛgbe Filistibii lɛ butuu, ni amɛloo Filistibii lɛ akooloi kɛtee. Bɔ ni fee ni David here Keilabii ayiwala nɛ.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Be ni David na le akɛ Saul miito ehe yiŋ fɔŋ lɛ, ekɛɛ Osɔfo Abiatar akɛ, “Kɔ efod lɛ kɛba.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Be ni Abiatar kɛ efod lɛ ba lɛ, David bi Yehowa nii ekɛɛ, “Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, otsulɔ enu akɛ Saul miitao aba Keila koni ebakpãtã maŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ mi mihewɔ.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ani Keilabii baajie mi awo edɛŋ lo? Ani Saul baana aba lɛɛlɛŋ? Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, otsulɔ miikpa bo fai koni ohã male enɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ni David bi ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Ani Keilabii lɛ aaajie mi kɛ miwebii lɛ amɛwo Saul dɛŋ lo?” Yehowa here nɔ akɛ, “Amɛbaajie nyɛ amɛhã Saul.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ David yabɔ ehe agwaa yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ tɛkploi lɛ amli yɛ Zif Ŋa lɛ nɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ. Gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ Saul miitao David, shi Nyɔŋmɔ hãaa enine ashɛ David nɔ.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ David she gbeyei ejaakɛ ena akɛ Saul eba ebaatao lɛ koni egbe lɛ. David yɛ Zif Ŋa lɛ nɔ yɛ Horesh niiaŋ,

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: ni Saul bi Yonatan tiu lɛ kɛtee jɛi, ni eyawo David hewalɛ koni ekɛ ehiɛ afɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛɛ David akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei, ejaakɛ mitsɛ Saul nine shɛŋ onɔ. Ele enɛ faŋŋ akɛ bo obaaye Israel nɔ maŋtsɛ, ni mi matsɔ̃ osɛɛmɔ.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: David kɛ Yonatan kamɔ amɛhe kitã yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɛi mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ Yonatan ku esɛɛ etee shĩa; shi David tee nɔ ehi Horesh.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Zif hii komɛi yakɛɛ Saul yɛ Gibea akɛ, “Naa, David ebatee yɛ wɔŋɔɔ yɛ Horesh tɛkploi lɛ amli yɛ Hakila Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Yuda shiaŋa lɛ wuoyigbɛ.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ Zif hii nɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa ajɔɔ nyɛ akɛ nyɛnu he nyɛhã mi.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ nyɛyaa, ni nyɛyataoa esaji amli jogbaŋŋ. Nyɛtaoa nyɛlea hei pɔtɛɛ ni eshwɛɔ lɛ, kɛ mɔ hu ni ena lɛ yɛ jɛi kɛ ehiŋmɛitsei enyɔ, ejaakɛ ahã mile akɛ ele ŋaa naakpa.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyataoa hei pɔtɛɛ ni eteɔteɔ ehe yɛ lɛ, ni nyɛbaa nyɛbakɛa mi; ni mikɛ nyɛ baaya. Anɔkwa, kɛji David yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ no lɛ matao lɛ fitsofitso kɛkpa Yuda muu fɛɛ.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ Zif hii lɛ shi Saul, ni amɛtsɔ̃ ehiɛ kɛtee Zif. Nakai be mli lɛ David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ yɛ Maon shiaŋa lɛ nɔ yɛ jɔɔ ko ni ye Yuda shiaŋa lɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kɛ ewebii lɛ yiŋ amɛtee koni amɛyatao David lɛ, abatswa David adafi, ni no hewɔ lɛ, David shi jɔɔ lɛ mli kɛtee Maon tɛsaa lɛ mli yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ. Saul na ele enɛ, kɛkɛ ni etiu David kɛtee Maon shiaŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kɛ ewebii lɛ nyiɛ gɔŋ lɛ biɛgbɛ lɛ, David kɛ ewebii lɛ hu nyiɛ gɔŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ, ni David he miitswa shi koni eshi gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ fiofio lɛ Saul kɛ ewebii lɛ miibɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbamɔmɔ amɛ.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Shi bɔfo ko ba trukaa ebakɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Akɛɛ oye ohe oyai ni oba, shi Filistibii lɛ ebatua shikpɔŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul je David sɛɛ, ni eyiŋ etee ekɛ Filistibii lɛ yawu. Sane nɛɛ hã awo nakai kpɔ lɛ mli gbɛi akɛ, “Foijee Tɛsaa.”

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David shi Maon, ni etee eyahi En-Gedi tɛkploi lɛ amli.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul kɛ Filistibii lɛ eyawu ni eku esɛɛ eba lɛ, abatswa lɛ adafi akɛ, “Naa, David yɛ En-Gedi Shiaŋa lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Amɛyashɛ tɛkplo ko he yɛ toi atsui komɛi ahe yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni Saul tee niiaŋ yɛ tɛkplo nɛɛ mli. Asomoaŋ David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ eyatee yɛ tɛkplo kometoo nɛɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David webii lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Shi ni Yehowa wo bo akɛ, ‘Majie ohenyɛlɔ lɛ mawo odɛ̃ŋ koni ofee lɛ bɔ ni osumɔɔ’ lɛ no eba mli ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni David te shi, ni etee ni eyafo Saul atade lɛ naabu nigii.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Shi fee sɛɛ lɛ David henilee bɔi lɛ haomɔ yɛ Saul atade lɛ naabu ni eyafo lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: David kɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ jɔɔ ewebii lɛ ahe, ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ amɛ akɛ amɛtua Saul. Saul te shi eshi tɛkplo lɛ mli, ni eyi egbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ David hu je kpo yɛ tɛkplo lɛ mli, ni eyabo Saul yisɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, Maŋtsɛ!” Be ni Saul fo ehe ni ekwɛ esɛɛ lɛ, David kɛ ehiɛ bu shi ni ekoto Saul,

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ni oboɔ mɛi anaa toi akɛ mi David, miitao bo efɔŋ lɛ?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Bɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ ona kɛ ohiŋmɛi tsei enyɔ bɔ ni Yehowa jie bo wo midɛŋ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ yɛ tɛkplo lɛ mli? Mɛi kɛɛ mi akɛ migbe bo; shi mikɛ ohe ke bo. Nɔ moŋ ni mikɛɛ ji akɛ, ‘Mikɛ minine esaŋ minuŋtsɔ he ejaakɛ gbɔmɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu ni.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Mitsɛ Ataa, Okwɛɛɛ? Otade lɛ naabu ko ni mifo lɛ mihiɛ nɛɛ. Akɛ mifo otade lɛ naabu, ni mitswaaa bo nɔ migbeee bo lɛ, no aaatsɔ̃ɔ bo koni ona ole akɛ mibɛ ohe yiŋtoo fɔŋ ko. Mifeko bo esha ko, shi kɛ̃lɛ bo lɛ gbɔbimɔ sɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ogbɔbiɔ mi koni ogbe mi.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Mikɛ misane lɛ fɛɛ ehã Yehowa koni eye ehã mi; ni lɛ nɔŋŋ ebaatɔ mihe owele yɛ onɔ; shi mi ni ji mi lɛ, mikɛ minine esaŋ ohe kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Onukpai buɔ abɛ akɛ ‘Mɛi fɔ̃ji adɛŋ nɔ fɔŋ jɛɔ, shi mi lɛ minine esaŋ ohe.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Ni namɔ sɛɛ po Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efã kɛnyiɛ nɛɛ? Namɔ po otiuɔ nɛɛ? Gbee gbonyo ni; oflikiti ni!

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Yehowa aaaye misane lɛ ehã mi, ni eeekojo mi kɛ bo teŋ, ni eejie mi yɛ odɛ̃ŋ?”

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ David akɛ, “Oja fe mi, ejaakɛ be mli ni ofeɔ mi ekpakpa lɛ belɛ mi lɛ miifee bo efɔŋ moŋ kɛmiito bo najiaŋ.
