english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Otsɔ̃ɔ faŋŋ ŋmɛnɛ akɛ ekpakpa otaoɔ mi, akɛni Yehowa tu mi wo odɛ̃ŋ shi ogbeee mi lɛ.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ namɔ hu nine shɛɔ ehenyɛlɔ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe keɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa aaafee bo ejurɔ yɛ nɔ ni ofee ohã mi ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ lɛ efee faŋŋ ehã mi akɛ bo kɛ̃ obaaba obaye Israel maŋtsɛ, ni Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ baahe shi.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ Yehowa akã mi kitã akɛ ogbeŋ mishwiei ni baa yɛ misɛɛ lɛ bɔ ni afee ni migbɛi akalaaje.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: David kã Saul kitã ni ebi lɛ lɛ, kɛkɛ ni Saul yiŋ etee ewe; shi David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee tɛkplo lɛ mli.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: nyɛkɛa lɛ akɛ, Miihã lɛ omanye! Omanye abla lɛ kɛ ewe lɛ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Minu akɛ aba aaku otoi lɛ ahetsɔi. Otookwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ wɔbahi shi yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ, ni wɔfeee amɛ efɔŋ ko lɛ, amɛnɔ ko nɔ ko elaajeee gbii abɔ fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ Karmel lɛ.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bo lɛ bi oblahii lɛ, ni amɛbaagba bo. No hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, kwɛmɔ miblahii lɛ ahiɛ, ejaakɛ wɔba yɛ gbi kpakpa nɔ be ni ooŋmɛ okplɔ̃. Ofainɛ, ohã otsuji nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oyɔɔ yɛ onine nɔ lɛ eko koni okɛmaje obi David.”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Be ni David oblahii lɛ yashɛ, ni amɛkɛ David shɛɛ lɛ hã Nabal ni amɛmɛɔ hetoo lɛ,

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Nabal hetoo ni ehã amɛ ji akɛ, “Namɔ ji nakai David lɛ? Namɔ ji Israel lɛ? Tsuji ni ejojoo foi amɛshi amɛnuŋtsɔmɛi efa gbii etɛ̃ nɛɛ.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Ani nyɛmiikɛɛ mi akɛ miboloo kɛ minu kɛ miloo ni migbe, ni mikɛbaahã mɛi ni eba ni amɛkuɔ toi ahetsɔi lɛ, mikɛhã mɛi komɛi hu ni mileee he ni amɛjɛ bɛɛ?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David oblahii lɛ tsɔ̃ amɛhe, ni amɛtee koni amɛyabɔ David amaniɛ.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, ni osusu sane nɛɛ he, ni okwɛ bɔ ni obaafee, ejaakɛ ashwã wɔnuŋtsɔ kɛ ewe lɛ fɛɛ ayinɔ. Tamɔ bɔ ni ole lɛ, wɔnuŋtsɔ feɔ gbɔmɔ fɔŋ bɔ ni ehiii lɛ sane kɛɛmɔ.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: ni asaŋ ewo eblahii komɛi agbɛ kɛ jatsu lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛtsɔa mihiɛ nyɛkitea; minyiɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɔŋŋ.” Shi etsiii tã ekɛɛɛ ewu Nabal.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Abigail ta teji nɔ kɛmiiya, ni be ni elɔgɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɔŋtɔ̃ ko nɔŋŋ pɛ, naa David kɛ ewebii lɛ hu ni miiba. Kɛkɛ ni Abigail kɛ amɛ yakpe.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Nakai be mli lɛ David ekɛɛ momo sa akɛ, “Yakatswaa po mibaa nibii ni gbɔmɔ nɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ yi mihã lɛ, ni amɛmli ekoeko elaajeee lɛ. Ekpakpa ni mifee lɛ lɛ, mishidaa ji enɛ?

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ agbe mi kɛji wɔ be ni je aaatsɛre lɛ mishi ewebii lɛ ateŋ nuu kome nɛkɛ hiɛkãalɔ yɛ enii ni eyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Be ni Abigail na David lɛ ehe fee oya ni eje eteji lɛ nɔ eyi shi, ni eyabu shi yɛ David hiɛ ni ekoto lɛ.

english_verse: Then she said: Sir, please let me explain!
translation_verse: Abigail ho gbee David naji anaa ni ekɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: “Ofainɛ, minuŋtsɔ, kaadi nɛkɛ nuu kwashia Nabal nɛɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ eetsu egbɛi lɛ he nii. Gbɛi ni awo lɛ ji Nabal, ni lɛɛlɛŋ kwashiai asane pɛ eyeɔ. Anɔkwale mli lɛ, mi lɛ, oblahii lɛ ni minuŋtsɔ tsu lɛ, minaaa amɛ kwraa.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Ofainɛ, okɛ tɔ̃mɔ fɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ ni mitɔ̃ lɛ afa mi. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ Yehowa baahã owe aye ejurɔ, ni ehe shi, ejaakɛ minuŋtsɔ miiwu Yehowa tai lɛ ehã lɛ, ni akana nɔ fɔŋ ko nɔ fɔŋ ko yɛ ogbɛfaŋ owala be fɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Kɛji gbɔmɔ adesa ko aaate shi awo bo, ni enyiɛ osɛɛ akɛ bo nɔŋŋ etaoɔ egbe lɛ, no lɛ, Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, aaafi minuŋtsɔ wala afata mɛi ni yɔɔ wala lɛ ahe ato Yehowa oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Shi ohenyɛlɔi lɛ, Yehowa aaasherɛ amɛ ashwie shwiaa tamɔ afɔ̃ɔ akromia mli tɛ.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Kɛji be lɛ shɛ, ni Yehowa fee nibii juji lɛ fɛɛ ni ewo amɛhe shi eto lɛ ehã minuŋtsɔ, ni ewo bo Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: efeŋ minuŋtsɔ dɔlɛ, ni ojwɛŋmɔ hu gbaŋ onaa akɛ oshwie lá shi yakatswaa aloo akɛ minuŋtsɔ tɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe owele. Kɛji Yehowa na fee bo ejurɔ nɛɛ lɛ, ofainɛ, ohiɛ akakpa oweyoo nɔ.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David here Abigail nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ajie Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, lɛ mɔ ni tsu bo koni okɛ mi abakpe ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ yi;

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ yiwala dɔŋŋ yɛ ohiɛshikamɔ nɛɛ hewɔ; ni bo diɛŋtsɛ hu oyiwala dɔŋŋ akɛ otsi minaa ŋmɛnɛ koni mikaye lá ko yi sɔ̃, ni asaŋ mikatɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe owele.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, mina Yehowa Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mɔ ni tsi minaa ni mifeko bo efɔŋ ko nɛɛ, akɛ eji ohe efeee oya koni okɛ mi abakpe kulɛ wɔ be ni je aaatsɛre lɛ eshwɛŋ nuu kome nɛkɛ hiɛkãalɔ ehaŋ Nabal!”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David mɔ nikeenii ni Abigail kɛba lɛ mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ! Kuu osɛɛ ni oya shĩa kɛ omanye. Minu nɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ, ni mikpɛ̃lɛ̃ nɔ.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Be ni Abigail ku esɛɛ ni eshɛɔ shĩa lɛ Nabal eŋmɛ okplɔ̃ yɛ ewe lɛ mli tamɔ maŋtsɛ. Nabal mii eshɛ ehe fe nine, ni etɔ dãa kpɔtɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, Abigail ebɔɔɔ lɛ amaniɛ ko kɛyashi je tsɛre nɔ leebi,

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: be mli ni wain lɛ etserɛ yɛ ehiɛ lɛ. Be ni Nabal ŋa Abigail gba lɛ nibii ni tee nɔ lɛ, Nabal tsui sɔŋŋ ni fã lɛ hã eniji kɛ enaji fɛɛ gboi amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ehe.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ aaafee gbii nyɔŋma lɛ Yehowa tswa Nabal nɔ ni egbo.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Abigail te shi, ni ekoto tsuji lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛnuŋtsɔ weyoo ji mi, ni mifee kralo tsɔ̃ akɛ mafɔ minuŋtsɔ tsuji anaji ahe.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Abigail yaho eta teji nɔ; kɛkɛ ni lɛ kɛ eblayei enumɔ komɛi ni sɔmɔɔ lɛ lɛ yi David tsuji lɛ asɛɛ kɛtee, ni Abigail yatsɔ David ŋa.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ David kɛ Ahinoam, ni jɛ Yezreel lɛ, hu hi shi; ni yei enyɔ nɛɛ ni ji Abigail kɛ Ahinoam, tsɔ̃mɔ David ŋamɛi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Saul kɛ ebiyoo Mikal, David klɛŋklɛŋ ŋa lɛ, ehã Palti, ni ji Laish ni jɛ Galim lɛ binuu, gbãlã.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Zifbii komɛi ba Saul ŋɔɔ yɛ Gibea amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, David ebatee ehe yɛ Hakila Gɔŋkpɔ ni yɔɔ Yuda ŋa kplanaa lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saul yato shi yɛ Hakila Gɔŋkpɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛ ni kã Yuda ŋa lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Shi David tee nɔ ehi shiaŋa lɛ nɔ. Be ni enu yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ Saul enyiɛ esɛɛ kɛba shiaŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: etsu mɛi kɛtee amɛyasara amɛkwɛ akɛ Saul eba shiaŋa lɛ nɔ lɛɛlɛŋ lo.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ David diɛŋtsɛ tee Saul shitoohe lɛ, ni eyana he pɔtɛɛ ni Saul kɛ etatsɛ Abner, Nerbi lɛ, kãmɔ. Saul kã shi ewɔ, ni ewebii tabilɔi ebɔle ehe kɛkpe.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David bi Ahimelek, Hitnyo lɛ, kɛ Zeruia bi Abishai, Yoab nyɛminuu lɛ, akɛ, “Nyɛteŋ namɔ kɛ mi aaatee Saul shitoohe lɛ mli?” Abishai here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Mi kɛ bo aaatee!”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David kɛ Abishai tee Saul tabilɔi lɛ ashitoohe lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛyanina Saul ni ekã ewebii lɛ ateŋ ewɔ, ni ekpɔlɔ lɛ tsɛkɛ shi yɛ eyitsogbɛ; ni Abner kɛ tabilɔi lɛ kãmɔ ehewɔ kɛbɔle lɛ kɛkpe.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abishai kɛɛ David akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ ejie ohenyɛlɔ lɛ ewo odɛ̃ŋ ŋmɛnɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ hã matsu lɛ akplɔ lɛ shi koome kɛmɔ shikpɔŋ nyɔŋlo, mihaŋ etia shii enyɔ.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Shi David kɛɛ Abishai akɛ, “Kaakpãtã ehiɛ, ejaakɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni baawo enine nɔ yɛ mɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu nɔ ni mɔ lɛ aaaŋɔ ehe aye.”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Abishai ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Mina Yehowa akɛ Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ ni aaatswa Saul nɔ, aloo ebe baashɛ ni eeegbo, aloo eeetee ta ni eeeyanyɔ yɛ ta lɛ mli.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Yehowa akpa ashwie akɛ mi mawo minine nɔ yɛ mɔ ni lɛ Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu lɛ nɔ. Bo lɛ fãa akplɔ lɛ ni tsɛkɛ shi yɛ eyitsogbɛ lɛ, ni owo nu kɛ kpulu lɛ kɛkɛ ni wɔtee.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɔ akplɔ lɛ ni ewo nu kpulu lɛ yɛ Saul yiteŋgbɛ, ni amɛje jɛi amɛtee. Mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa amɛ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko hiɛ hu etsɛ̃ɛɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko hu leee. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ewɔ ejaakɛ Yehowa ehã wɔ ni tsii enyɔ amɛnɔ.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Be ni David etse mli kɛtee eyadamɔ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ yɛ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ, he ni gbɛ shwaŋŋ kã ekɛ Saul teŋ lɛ,

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: ebolɔ etsɛ Saul tabilɔi lɛ kɛ Abner, Ner bi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ohereee nɔ lo, Abner?” Abner here nɔ akɛ, “Bo namɔ obolɔɔ otsimɔɔ maŋtsɛ toi lɛ?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: David here Abner nɔ akɛ, “Abner, kwɛɛ, jeee mikɛɛ bo ji hii fɛɛ amli nuu yɛ Israel lɛ? Te aye tɛŋŋ ni obuuu onuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ he, ni mɔ ko jɛ mɛi lɛ ateŋ ba ni kulɛ ebaakpãtã onuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Ofeee ni ahi kwraa! Mina Yehowa akɛ nyɛsa gbele, ejaakɛ nyɛnyɛɛɛ nyɛbu nyɛnuŋtsɔ, ni ji gbɔmɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu, lɛ he. Agbɛnɛ, kwɛ nɛgbɛ maŋtsɛ akplɔ lɛ kɛ enu kɛ kpulu ni ma eyitsogbɛ lɛ yɔɔ?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Saul yoo David gbee ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mibi David, bo owieɔ lɛ?” David here nɔ akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, mi ni.

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Shi mɛɛba ni minuŋtsɔ nyiɛ etsulɔ sɛɛ nɛkɛ nɛɛ? Mɛni mifee; mɛɛ efɔŋ po mifee?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Taflatsɛ, minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ abo nɔ ni etsulɔ yɔɔ kɛɛmɔ toi fioo. Kɛji Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ ni etee bo shi ewo mi lɛ, mibashã he afɔle kɛkpa he fai. Shi kɛji gbɔmɛi adesai abii ni ehã ote shi owo mi lɛ, no lɛ Yehowa aaawo amɛ he nyɔmɔ, ejaakɛ amɛshwie mi ŋmɛnɛ akɛ mikahi Yehowa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi moŋ miya ni miyasɔmɔ jemawɔji.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Kɛji magbo po lɛ, kaahã migbo yɛ he ko ni jeee Yehowa shikpɔŋ nɔ, ejaakɛ naa Israel maŋtsɛ eba mi oflikiti taomɔ tamɔ agbɔbiɔ afi yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul here nɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mifee efɔŋ! Mibi David, kpalemɔ ni oba. Mifeŋ bo efɔŋ ko dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ otsɔ̃ɔ mi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ akɛ miwala jara wa hã bo. Miye kwashiai asane lɛɛlɛŋ, ni mitɔ̃ fe nine.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: David to he ehã Saul akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, naa okpɔlɔ lɛ. Hã oblahii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome aba ni ebaŋɔ.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Yehowa woɔ mɔ nyɔmɔ yɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ ejalɛ kɛ enɔkwayeli naa. Yehowa tu bo ewo midɛŋ ŋmɛnɛ, shi mi ni misumɔɔɔ akɛ miwoɔ minine nɔ yɛ mɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Bɔ ni mikɛ ohe ke bo ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ mi hu Yehowa aaabaa miwala yi, ni eeejie mi yɛ nɔnai fɛɛ mli.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ David akɛ, “Mibi David, Naa Nyɔŋmɔ aaajɔɔ bo. Oootsu nibii wuji, ni oooye fɛɛ mli kunim.” Kɛkɛ ni David yiŋ etee, ni Saul hu ku esɛɛ kɛtee ejɛɛhe lɛ.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ ehe akɛ, “Mihiɛ nɛkɛ aahu ni Saul nine aaashɛ minɔ gbi ko, ni eeegbe mi. Nɔ pɛ ni sa mi feemɔ agbɛnɛ ji akɛ majo foi kɛya Filistibii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No baahã Saul nijiaŋ aje wui, ni ebaafɔ̃ɔ mi gbɔbimɔ yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni maye mihe.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul na le akɛ David ejo foi kɛtee Gat lɛ, Saul kpa David sɛɛ tiumɔ.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Akish akɛ, “Kɛji ona mihe tsuijurɔ lɛ hã mi he ko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ maji lɛ eko mli koni mayahi jɛi, ejaakɛ efeee mi akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mi kɛ bo fɛɛ aaahi maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Akish damɔ David wiemɔ nɛɛ nɔ ni ekɛ Ziklag hã David nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ. Biɛ tsɔ̃ ni Ziklag maŋ lɛ tsɔ̃ Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi anɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: David hi shi afi kɛ nyɔji ejwɛ yɛ Filistibii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ David kɛ ewebii lɛ fãa, ni amɛyatuaa Geshurbii lɛ kɛ Girzibii lɛ kɛ Amalekbii ejaakɛ amɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ Shur aahu kɛyashwie Ijipt kɛjɛ sa.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: David yatuaa gbɔmɛi nɛɛ, ni egbeɔ hii kɛ yei fɛɛ, ni eloɔ amɛtoi kɛ tsinai kɛ tejii kɛ yoomai kɛ atadei hu, kɛkɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ kɛba Akish ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Kɛji Akish bi David akɛ, “Ni namɛi ofɔ̃ nyɛyaye ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?” David kɛɔ Akish akɛ, “Wɔyatua Yudabii lɛ awuoyigbɛ, aloo Wɔyatua Yerameelbii lɛ awuoyigbɛ lɛ, aloo Wɔyatua Kenbii lɛ awuoyigbɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Kɛji David tee ofɔ̃yeli lɛ, nuu ni jio, yoo ni jio, David shiii mɔ ko mɔ ko hiɛkãalɔ koni akabagba yɛ Gat akɛ, “Nɛkɛ kɛ nɛkɛ ji nɔ ni David feɔ.” Bɔ ni David hi shi nɛ, bei abɔ fɛɛ ni eye yɛ Filistibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Akish he David eye, ni ekɛɛ yɛ ehe akɛ, “Bɔ ni ehã esane eje emaŋ Israelbii amɛtsine hewɔ lɛ eeesɔmɔ mi daa.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filistibii atai lɛ bua amɛhe naa ni amɛfã ta kɛba Shunem ni amɛbato shi yɛ jɛi. Saul hu bua Israel tai lɛ anaa kɛkpe, ni amɛfã kɛba Gilboa amɛbato shi yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul na Filistibii lɛ ayikulɛ lɛ eshe gbeyei, ni etsui fã naakpa.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Saul tee eyabi Yehowa nii. Shi yɛ lamɔ mli jio, yɛ Urim lɛ naa jio, yɛ gbalɔi anaa jio, Yehowa efooo Saul daaŋ.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul fã etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyataoa yoo okɔmfo ko nyɛhãa mi koni maya eŋɔɔ mayabi nii.” Etsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yoo okɔmfo ko yɛ Endor.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul bakɔlɔ atadei komɛi kɛkɛ ewo ekɛtsake ehe koni akayoo lɛ, ni ekɛ hii enyɔ komɛi fata ehe, ni eyiŋ etee yoo okɔmfo lɛ ŋɔɔ nyɔɔŋ. Saul kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Miitao koni ofee nii ohã mi, ni otsɛ mɔ tã ni matsi mahã bo lɛ ohã mi.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ to he akɛ, “Bɛ ole nɔ sane ni Maŋtsɛ Saul eye kɛho lɛ fɛɛ, bɔ ni ekpãtã okɔmfoi kɛ klamɔfoi ahiɛ ehã yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Mɛɛba ni oba otsɔ̃ɔ mi tsɔne koni ohã agbe mi nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Shi Saul kã yoo okɔmfo lɛ kitã ekɛɛ, “Mina Yehowa akɛ onaŋ amane ko amane ko yɛ nɔ ni obaatsu ohã mi nɛɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ bi Saul akɛ, “Namɔ mitsɛ mihã bo lɛ?” Saul to he akɛ, “Tsɛ Samuel ohã mi.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Be ni yoo okɔmfo lɛ na Samuel susuma lɛ, ebo waa ni ekɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Mɛɛba olaka mi nakai? Maŋtsɛ Saul ji bo.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Saul kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei. Mɛni onaa?” Yoo lɛ jie naa akɛ, “Mina sisa ko ni miifã kpo kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ kɛmiiba.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Ni Saul bi lɛ akɛ, “Te esu hu?” Yoo lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Nuumo ko ni baa lɛ; ewo atade yuu ko.” Kɛkɛ ni Saul yoo akɛ Samuel ni, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto sisa lɛ.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Samuel bi Saul akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ obagba minaa kɛ tsɛmɔ ni obatsɛ mi nɛɛ?” Saul jie naa ekɛɛ akɛ, “Efi mi naakpa. Filistibii lɛ kɛ mi jwere ta nɔ, ni Nyɔŋmɔ hu eje misɛɛ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni yɛ gbalɔi anaa jio, yɛ lamɔ mli jio, Nyɔŋmɔ efooo midaaŋ kwraa dɔŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ ni mibatsɛ bo nɛɛ koni otsɔ̃ɔ mi nɔ ni mifee.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Samuel kɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Kɛji Yehowa eje osɛɛ, ni etsɔ̃ ohenyɛlɔ lɛ, mɛɛba oba obiɔ mi nii?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Yehowa tsɔ̃ minɔ ewo bo shi, ni no he nii etsu lɛ. Eshɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ odɛ̃ŋ, ni ekɛhã omaŋnyo David.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ obooo Yehowa gbee toi; ni emli ni fu Amalek waa lɛ oyatsuuu he nii ohãaa lɛ. No hewɔ ni Yehowa feɔ bo nɔ ni efeɔ bo ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Fɛɛ ayakã, Yehowa baahã Filistibii lɛ aye bo kɛ Israel fɛɛ nɔ kunim. Wɔ ni ji wɔ lɛ, bo kɛ obihii baaba abashɛ gbohiiaje he ni miyɔɔ nɛɛ, ni Filistibii lɛ baaye Israel ta lɛ hu nɔ kunim.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Saul flɛo kɛjɛ ŋwɛi egbee shi ejaakɛ gbeyei wulu mɔ lɛ yɛ Samuel naa wiemɔi lɛ ahewɔ. Egbɔjɔ bliboo hu, ejaakɛ eyeko nɔ ko nɔ ko shwaneshwane kɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ be ni yoo okɔmfo lɛ tsi ebɛŋkɛ Saul, ni ena akɛ gbeyei emɔ lɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ Saul akɛ, “Oweyoo bo bo toi bianɛ, ni mikɛ mihe wo osharã mli, ni mifee nɔ ni obi mi akɛ mifee lɛ.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, agbɛnɛ bo hu bo oweyoo toi. Mahã bo niyenii fioo ko ni oye bɔ ni afee ni ona hewalɛ okɛnyiɛ ogbɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Saul ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Miyeee.” Shi Saul tsuji lɛ kɛ yoo okɔmfo lɛ fɛɛ nyɛ Saul nɔ; ni naagbee mli lɛ ebo amɛ toi. No hewɔ lɛ, Saul te shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni eho eta saa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Oya nɔŋŋ ni yoo lɛ mɔ etsinabi ko ni ewo fɔ lɛ, ni egbe lɛ; ni ekpɔtɔ mamu ekɛshã mã akpiti aboloo.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Ekɛ niyenii nɛɛ bama Saul kɛ etsuji lɛ ahiɛ, ni amɛye. Niyeli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Saul kɛ etsuji lɛ yiŋ ni amɛtee nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Shi Filistibii atatsɛmɛi lɛ amli fu Akish naakpa, ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wo lɛ gbɛ, ni ohã eku esɛɛ eya maŋ ni ohã lɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ. Wɔnyɛŋ wɔ kɛ lɛ aya ta nɛɛ naa koni ekayatsɔ̃ ehe moŋ ewo wɔ yɛ ta lɛ mli. Mɛni osusuɔ akɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ kɛ aaakpãtã enuŋtsɔ ni etɔ̃ enɔ lɛ, fe wɔwebii ni yɔɔ biɛ nɛɛ ayitsei?”

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Kolɛ jeee nɛkɛ David nɛɛ he lala amɛwoɔ ni ahereɔ nɔ yɛ joi amli akɛ, “Saul egbe ekpekpei lɛ; shi David egbe akpei nyɔŋmanyɔŋmai lɛ?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Akish tsɛ David, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mina Yehowa akɛ anɔkwafo ji bo, ejaakɛ kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni obaje miŋɔɔ aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, minako nɔ ko fɔŋ ko yɛ ohe. Kulɛ misumɔ akɛ oshi minɔ kɛya ta nɛɛ naa, shi maŋtsɛmɛi krokomɛi lɛ nyãaa ohe.

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Akish akɛ, “Shi mɛni kwraa ji nɔ ni mifee? Mɛni, aleee nɔ, ona yɛ mihe kɛjɛ gbi ni mikɛ bo bahi shi aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, hewɔ ni mikɛ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ akaya, koni mikɛ ohenyɛlɔi yawu lɛ?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Akish here David nɔ akɛ, “Mi mihiɛ lɛ, mile akɛ ohi tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo; shi Filistibii atatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛɛ okashi amɛnɔ kɛtee ta lɛ.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛtea shi wɔ leebi maŋkpa, bo kɛ owebii lɛ ni fata ohe kɛba lɛ, koni jeŋ ni aaatse pɛ nyɛyia mli kɛkua nyɛsɛɛ.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David kɛ ewebii lɛ te shi leebi mra, ni amɛyiŋ koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛya Filistibii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni Filistibii atai lɛ hu fã koni amɛya Yezreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Gbii etɛ̃ sɛɛ be ni David kɛ ewebii lɛ bashɛ Ziklag lɛ, amɛyanina akɛ Amalekbii lɛ ebatua Yuda wuoyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ Ziklag hu, ni amɛwo Ziklag mli la amɛshã maŋ lɛ,

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni David kɛ ewebii lɛ shɛɔ shi lɛ ashã maŋ lɛ, ni aŋɔ amɛŋamɛi kɛ amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei fɛɛ nom kɛtee.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ ewebii ni ekɛnyiɛ lɛ wo yara, ni amɛfo kɛyashi etɔ amɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛfo dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: David ŋamɛi enyɔ lɛ, ni ji Ahinoam, Yezreelyoo lɛ, kɛ Abigail Nabal Karmelnyo lɛ ŋa okulafo lɛ, hu Amalekbii lɛ ŋɔ amɛ nom kɛtee.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Sane wulu bakã David nɔ, ni ehe jara lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ, ejaakɛ ewebii lɛ kɛɛ amɛbaatswia lɛ tɛ, ejaakɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ musuŋ miishã lɛ yɛ ebihii kɛ ebiyei lɛ ahewɔ. Shi Yehowa, David Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, waje David ni ewo lɛ hewalɛ.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ Osɔfo Abiatar, ni ji Ahimelek bi lɛ akɛ, “Yaakɔ nɔ ni akɛbiɔ nii lɛ obahã mi.” Abiatar kɛ nii lɛ bahã David.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David bi Yehowa nii ekɛɛ, “Mitiu gbɔmɛi nɛɛ lo?” Yehowa hã hetoo akɛ, “Tiumɔ amɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ obaaya oyanina amɛ yɛ gbɛteŋ, ni onine baashɛ nyɛgbɔmɛi lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Be ni amɛyaa lɛ, David webii lɛ na Ijiptnyo oblanyo fioo ko yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ batsɔ̃ɔ David. Ahã oblanyo nɛɛ niyenii eye, kɛ nu hu ni enu;

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: ni asaŋ ahã lɛ agbãmi kɛ wainyibii shabii enyɔ hu. Be ni eye nii nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ ehiɛ tserɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ oblanyo nɛɛ eye gbii etɛ̃ ni nɔ ko eyako edaaŋ, niyenii jio, nu jio.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ David bi oblanyo lɛ akɛ, “Namɔ bi ji bo; ni nɛgbɛ hu ojɛ?” Oblanyo lɛ jie naa akɛ, “Ijiptnyo bi ji mi. Ŋmɛnɛ ji gbii etɛ̃ ni minuŋtsɔ lɛ shi mi eŋmɛ shi ni etee, ejaakɛ hela bamɔ mi.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Wɔtee wɔyatua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Keretibii lɛ awuoyigbɛ he ni yɔɔ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ Kalebbii hu awuoyigbɛ, ni wɔma Ziklag maŋ lɛ naa la wɔshã.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: David bi oblanyo lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji mikɛɛ oyatsɔ̃ɔ mi ofɔ̃yelɔi nɛɛ lɛ, obaaya lo?” Oblanyo lɛ here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akã mi kitã akɛ ogbeŋ mi, ni asaŋ okpaleŋ mi ohaŋ minuŋtsɔ lɛ, ni mikɛ bo baaya miyatsɔ̃ɔ bo ofɔ̃yelɔi lɛ.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Be ni oblanyo lɛ kɛ David tee lɛ ayanina ofɔ̃yelɔi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ni amɛyato shi yɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ni aayeyee nii, ni aanunuu dãi, ni aajojoo yɛ nibii babaoo ni amɛyahahaa yɛ Filistibii ashikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ lɛ ahewɔ.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛshwie amɛnɔ, ni egbe amɛ kɛjɛ hulushinyɔɔ mli aahu kɛyashi enɔ jetsɛremɔ gbɛkɛ mli. Amalekbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko he ejeee gbele mli fe oblahii ohai ejwɛ komɛi ni shara yoomai ni amɛtara nɔ kɛjo foi lɛ.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: David nine shɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Amalekbii lɛ baloo kɛtee lɛ anɔ, kɛ eŋãmɛi enyɔ lɛ hu.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Nibii ni Amalekbii lɛ baloo lɛ ateŋ eko kwraa elaajeee. Nɔ bibioo ni jio, nɔ wulu ni jio, binuu ni jio, bo biyoo ni jio, David nine shɛ fɛɛ tswɛm nɔ kɛba.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Ni David loo toi kɛ tsinai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Amalekbii anine nɔ lɛ, ni akpala kooloi nɛɛ kɛnyiɛ hiɛ belɛ aapai aakɛɛ akɛ, “Enɛ lɛ David ofɔ̃yelinii nɛ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mɛi ni kɛ David tee lɛ ateŋ yitsoŋwalɔi kɛ yakagbɔmɛi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Akɛni amɛbɛ mli ni wɔtee lɛ hewɔ lɛ nibii ni wɔyashɔ̃ kɛba lɛ, amɛnɔ bɛ mli fe mɔ oŋa kɛ obii ni obaanyɛ obakpala amɛ kɛya kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Shi David here amɛ nɔ akɛ, “Anyɛmimɛi, kɛji Yehowa ebu wɔhe, ni ehã wɔye mɛi ni batua wɔ lɛ anɔ kunim lɛ, nyɛkafea nakai yɛ nii ni Yehowa ehã wɔ lɛ he.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ni namɔ po aaabu nyɛ bem yɛ nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ mli? Naa, bɔ ni mɔ ni tee ta lɛ baana akɛ egbɛnaa lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ mɔ ni bu nibii ahe yɛ sɛɛ hu baana akɛ egbɛnaa. Abaaja mɔ fɛɛ mɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ David wiemɔ nɛɛ tsɔ̃ akpɔ kɛ mla ehã Israelbii, ni ekã shi nakai kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Be ni David bashɛ Ziklag lɛ, etsu akɛ nibii ni eyaye amɛ ofɔ̃ lɛ eko tee ayake Yuda maŋ onukpai fɛɛ ni ji ehe gbɔmɛi kpakpai lɛ kɛ shɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, miyaye ofɔ yɛ Yehowa henyɛlɔi lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni mikɛɛ akɛbake nyɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ wu ta, ni Filistibii lɛ anine tsɔ̃ Israelbii lɛ anɔ, ni amɛgbe Israelbii lɛ amɛshwie Gilboa Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ nyiɛ Saul kɛ ebihii lɛ asɛɛ waa. Amɛnine shɛ Saul bihii Yonatan kɛ Abinadab kɛ Malkishua nɔ, ni amɛgbe amɛ.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Akɛ ta lɛ nina Saul kpaakpa. Henyɛlɔi lɛ ateŋ gãitsɛ̃lɔi lɛ na Saul, ni amɛtsɛ̃ lɛ gãi, ni apila lɛ ablaŋ.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Saul kɛɛ oblanyo ni hiɛɔ etawuunii lɛ akɛ, “Gbalamɔ oklante lɛ, ni okɛdu mi bɔ ni afee ni foolɔi nɛɛ akaba amɛbagbe mi, ni amɛfee mi niseniianii.” Shi oblanyo lɛ emiii nakai feemɔ ejaakɛ gbeyei emɔ lɛ naakpa. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Saul gbala lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eklante lɛ, ni eho egbee nɔ.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Be ni oblanyo lɛ na akɛ Saul egbo lɛ, lɛ hu eho egbee eklante lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ Saul fɛɛ gbo.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Saul kɛ ebihii etɛ̃ lɛ kɛ oblanyo ni hiɛɔ Saul tawuunii lɛ kɛ Saul he gbɔmɛi fɛɛ gboi shi kome yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii ni yɔɔ Yezreel Jɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ mɛi hu ni yɔɔ Yordan bokãgbɛ lɛ na akɛ, Israelbii lɛ ejo foi yɛ Filistibii lɛ ahiɛ, ni asaŋ Saul kɛ ebihii etɛ̃ lɛ egboi lɛ, amɛjojoo foi amɛshishii amɛmaji amɛshwie shi, ni Filistibii lɛ baŋɔ maji lɛ ni amɛhi mli.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ be ni Filistibii lɛ ba ta lɛ mli gbohii lɛ ahe nii kpɔlɔmɔ lɛ, naa Saul kɛ ebihii etɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛnyɔnyɔi yɛ Gilboa Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Yabeshbii ni yɔɔ Gilead lɛ nu bɔ ni Filistibii lɛ efee Saul lɛ,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: maŋ lɛ mli hii kãkãlɔi lɛ fɛɛ te shi, ni amɛnyiɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ kɛtee, ni amɛyajie Saul gbonyo lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ hu agbohii lɛ yɛ Bet-Shan gbogbo lɛ he, ni amɛkɛba Yebesh amɛbashã.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Amɛloo gbohii lɛ awui lɛ, ni amɛfu yɛ tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ tamariske tso ni yɔɔ Yabesh lɛ shishi, ni maŋ lɛ hi ŋmaa gbii kpawo.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Saul gbele sɛɛ be ni David ku esɛɛ kɛjɛ ta ni efã kɛyaplene Amalekbii lɛ eba lɛ, ebahi shi gbii enyɔ yɛ Ziklag.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Ni gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Saul tabilɔi lɛ eko kɛ ehe atade ni etserɛ kɛ eyiteŋ hu mlu ba David ŋɔɔ kɛjɛ ta lɛ naa. Be ni nuu lɛ shɛ David hiɛ lɛ eho egbee shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto David.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: David bi nuu lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ojɛ obaa nɛɛ?” Nuu lɛ to he akɛ, “Israel nsra lɛ mli mijo foi kɛjɛ kɛbaa nɛɛ.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: David saa ebi nuu lɛ akɛ, “Te nibii amli tamɔ tɛŋŋ? Gbaa mi.” Nuu lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Wɔtabilɔi lɛ ejo foi yɛ henyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ; agboi babaoo diɛŋtsɛ. Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan fɛɛ enyɔnyɔi.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: David bi oblanyo lɛ ni gbaa lɛ sane lɛ akɛ, “Te ofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan egboi hu?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Oblanyo lɛ hã David hetoo ni ekɛɛ, “Heniianaa ni miyaje Gilboa Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni miyanina Saul ni ebu ekpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ, be mli ni henyɛlɔi lɛ ashwiilii lɛ kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ waa lɛ.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul fo ehe ekwɛ esɛɛ ni ena mi lɛ, etsɛ mi; ni mihere lɛ nɔ akɛ, ‘Ofainɛ, naa mi.’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ebi mi akɛ, ‘Bo namɔ ni?’ Mijie naa akɛ, ‘Ofainɛ, Amaleknyo ji mi’.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Tsi oba ni obagbe mi, ejaakɛ ŋmiŋmi emɔ mi, tsɛ wala fioo yɛ mimli’.

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mitsi mibɛŋkɛ lɛ, ni migbe lɛ, ejaakɛ mina akɛ eshigbeemɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ eyi naŋ wala. No sɛɛ lɛ, mijie maŋtsɛ akekre ni fi eyitso lɛ kɛ ga ni ewo yɛ ekɔŋ lɛ, ni mikɛba mikɛbaahã bo, minuŋtsɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: ni amɛye ŋkɔmɔ, ni amɛwo yara, ni amɛfo, ni amɛhi ŋmaa kɛyashi gbɛkɛ yɛ Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan kɛ Yehowa maŋbii ni enyɔnyɔɔ yɛ ta lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: David bi oblanyo lɛ ni gbaa lɛ sane lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ nyo ji bo?” Oblanyo lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Gbɔ ni ji Amaleknyo ko bi ji mi.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Ni etswa oblanyo lɛ nɔ, ni egbo. Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ, “Oyi sɔ̃ atere bo diɛŋtsɛ, ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ onaabu eye odase eshi bo, ejaakɛ okɛɛ, ‘Migbe mɔ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu lɛ.’ ” David fo Saul kɛ Yonatan

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ lala nɛɛ fo Saul kɛ ebi Yonatan,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Ao Israel, onunyam lɛ, ehiɛ akpãtã yɛ ogɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ nɛɛ. Te aye tɛŋŋ ni kãkãlɔi enyɔnyɔi nɛɛ?

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Nyɛkayagbaa enɛ yɛ Gat; akatsi enɛ tã yɛ Ashkelon blohuiaŋ koni Filistibii lɛ abiyei lɛ akanya, ni foolɔi lɛ abiyei lɛ miitumɔ.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ Gilboa gɔji, bɔ loo nu akanɛ nyɛnɔ, ni nyɛnɔ ŋmɔji aŋala. Ejaakɛ jɛi abule kãkãlɔi lɛ atsɛŋi lɛ yɛ, kɛ Saul tsɛŋ lɛ po, ejaakɛ afɔŋ he mu dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni nyɔnyɔɔ lɛ ala lɛ kɛ kãkãlɔi lɛ hu afɔ lɛ Yonatan gãi lɛ ekuuu esɛɛ efolo kɛjɛɛɛ he; ni Saul klante lɛ hu gbe henyɛlɔi lɛ.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: “Asumɔ Saul kɛ Yonatan amɛwala be mli, ni amɛhe yɛ fɛo. Amɛgbele mli tete, amɛmli gbalaaa; amɛhe yɛ oya fe okropɔŋ po, ni amɛhe wa hu fe jata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ Israel biyei, nyɛfoa Saul, mɔ ni bumɔ nyɛ mamai tsuji fɛɛfɛji, ni ehã nyɛ shika jwinei nyɛshwie nyɛtadei anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: “Te aye tɛŋŋ ni kãkãlɔi enyɔnyɔi yɛ ta teŋ tuuŋtu nɛɛ hu? Agbe Yonatan yɛ ogɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: “Osane miidɔ mi, minyɛmi Yonatan; osane eŋɔɔ minaa kɛho. Osuɔmɔ ni okɛsumɔ mi lɛ yɛ naakpɛɛ, efe yei asuɔmɔ tete.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: “Te aye tɛŋŋ ni kãkãlɔi enyɔnyɔi ni tawuunii hu ahiɛ ekpãtã nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ David yabi Yehowa nii akɛ, “Ani miya ni miyaŋɔ Yuda maji lɛ eko lo?” Yehowa hã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Yaa!” David bi akɛ, “Mɛɛ maŋ nɔ miya?” Yehowa to he akɛ, “Yaa Hebron.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David yiŋ kɛtee Hebron, lɛ kɛ eŋãmɛi enyɔ lɛ, Ahinoam, Yezreelyoo lɛ, kɛ Abigail ni ji Nabal Karmelnyo lɛ okulafo lɛ.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: David kɛ hii tabilɔi ni fata ehe lɛ kɛ amɛŋamɛi lɛ kɛ amɛbii fɛɛ hu tee, ni amɛyahi Hebron maji lɛ amli.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Yuda hii lɛ ba Hebron amɛbafɔ David mu kɛwo lɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ. Be ni agba David akɛ Yabesh Gileadbii lɛ ji mɛi ni fu Saul gbonyo lɛ,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: David tsu bɔfoi kɛtee Yabesh-Gileadbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni ayakɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Yehowa ajɔɔ nyɛ akɛ nyɛfu nyɛnuŋtsɔ Saul nyɛkɛfee lɛ ejurɔ nɛkɛ.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Yehowa asumɔ nyɛ kɛ suɔmɔ ni bɛ naagbee, ni eye nyɛ anɔkwa; ni mi hu mafee nyɛ ejurɔ mato najiaŋ yɛ nɔ ni nyɛfee nɛɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛwajea nyɛhe, ni nyɛfea ekãa, ejaakɛ nyɛmaŋtsɛ Saul egbo, ni Yuda akutso lɛ ebafɔ mi mu kɛwo mi amɛmaŋtsɛ.” Awo Ishboshet Israel Maŋtsɛ

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Saul tatsɛ Abner, Ner bi lɛ, mɔ ni Saul bi Ishboshet kɛjo foi kɛtee Mahanaim,

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: ni jɛi eyawo lɛ Gilead kɛ Ashur kɛ Yezreel kɛ Efraim kɛ Benyamin kɛ Israel fɛɛ maŋtsɛ yɛ.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: David ye Yuda maŋtsɛ yɛ Hebron afii kpawo kɛ nyɔji ekpaa. Israel kɛ Yuda wu

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Abner, Ner bi lɛ, kɛ Saul bi Ishboshet tsuji lɛ jɛ Mahanaim ni amɛba Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruia bi lɛ, hu kɛ David tsuji lɛ fã, ni amɛkɛ Ishboshet tsuji lɛ yakpe yɛ Gibeon kpaakpo lɛ naa. Mɛnɛɛmɛi bua kpaakpo lɛ he afã kome nɛɛ, ni Mɛnɛɛmɛi hu bua kpaakpo lɛ he afã kome nɛɛ hu.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abner kɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ hã oblahiabii lɛ aba amɛbaka amɛ kpɔiaŋ yɛ wɔhiɛ.” Yoab here lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, amɛmiiba.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ jɛ Benyaminbii, ni ji Saul bi Ishboshet sɛɛbii, lɛ ateŋ ni amɛ kɛ David tabilɔi lɛ hu ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ yaka amɛkpɔiaŋ.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ mɔ ehenyɛlɔ yitso, ni edu ehenyɛlɔ lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ kakla, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyashwie shi, ni amɛnyɔnyɔi shi kome. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɛɔ Gibeon kpɔ nɛɛ mli he ni sane nɛɛ ba yɛ lɛ akɛ “Kakla Ŋa nɔ.”

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ta ni awu gbi lɛ mli yawa naakpa, ni David tsuji lɛ wo Abner kɛ Israelbii lɛ afoi.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Zeruia bihii etɛ̃, Yoab kɛ Abishai kɛ Asahel, yɛ ta lɛ naa gbi lɛ. Ni Asahel, amɛteŋ mɔ ni joɔ foi tamɔ ŋa nɔ soŋai lɛ,

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Abner kwɛ esɛɛ kɛkɛ ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ, Asahel, bo ni?” Asahel here nɔ akɛ, “Hɛɛ! Mi ni.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abner kɛɛ Asahel akɛ, “Gba oninejurɔ gbɛ loo obɛkugbɛ koni omɔ oblahiabii lɛ moŋ eko koni oshɔ̃ etawuunii yɛ edɛŋ.” Shi Asahel ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ ekpale yɛ Abner sɛɛ.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abner ku sɛɛ ekɛɛ Asahel akɛ, “Kpalemɔ ni oku osɛɛ ni oya. Mɛɛba ni obaahã minine akpa yɛ onɔ nɛɛ? Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mihiɛ nɔ yɛ onyɛmi Yoab hiɛ hu kɛji eeeba lɛ nakai lɛ?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Shi Asahel emiii akɛ ejeɔ Abner sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Abner kɛ ekpɔlɔ lɛ shishi gbu Asahel musu, ni akplɔ lɛ yafã kpo yɛ Asahel sɛɛ, kɛkɛ ni Asahel gbee shi, ni egbo yɛ enajiaŋ nɔŋŋ. Mɛi fɛɛ ni bashɛɔ he ni Asahel gbonyo lɛ kã lɛ waa damɔɔ shi.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Shi Yoab kɛ Abishai nyiɛ Abner sɛɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛyashɛ Ama Gɔŋkpɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ Gia bokãgbɛ, yɛ Gibeon ŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ lɛ he; kɛkɛ ni hulu nyɔ shi.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Benyaminbii lɛ bua amɛhe naa akɛ asafo ku, ni amɛbafata Abner he, ni amɛyadamɔ gɔŋ ko yiteŋ.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abner bo etsɛ Yoab, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Aso nɛkɛ sɔŋŋ wɔɔhã klante aye awui lo? Oleee akɛ kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ joomɔ kɛkɛ ji nɔ ni baaba lo? Mɛɛ be nɔŋŋ omɛɔ dani ofã owebii lɛ koni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Yoab hã Abner hetoo ekɛɛ, “Mina Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ kɛjeee wiemɔ ni owie nɛɛ hewɔ ni kulɛ ja wɔ leebi dani miwebii lɛ baafɔ̃ɔ amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab hã akpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ, ni ewebii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ Israelbii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ, ni asaŋ amɛkpa amɛ kɛ ta lɛ wuu.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Abner kɛ ewebii lɛ nyiɛ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛfo mli kɛtsɔ̃ Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛyafo Yordan lɛ, ni amɛtsa nyiɛmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛba Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Be ni Yoab ekpa Abner kɛ ewebii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ, ni ebua ewebii lɛ anaa lɛ, ena akɛ eshwɛ Asahel kɛ David webii lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋma kɛ nɛɛhu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Amɛwo Asahel gbonyo lɛ, ni amɛyato lɛ yɛ ewekumɛi afũuhe ni yɔɔ Betlehem lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, Yoab kɛ ewebii lɛ tsa nɔ, ni amɛnyiɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ, ni be ni je kɛɛ etsɛreɔ wɛlɛŋŋ lɛ amɛyashɛ Hebron.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul we lɛ kɛ David we lɛ wuɔ ta lɛ, Abner bana hewalɛ yɛ Saul we lɛ.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Saul yɛ hemɔ ko ni gbɛi ji Rizpa, ni atsɛɔ etsɛ Aia. Gbi ko lɛ Ishboshet bi Abner sane yɛ Rizpa nɛɛ he ekɛɛ, “Mɛɛba ni oyata mitsɛ hemɔ lɛ he lɛ?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abner mli fu naakpa yɛ sane ni Ishboshet bi lɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ Ishboshet akɛ, “Te osusuɔ yɛ mihe tɛŋŋ nɛɛ? Akɛ miyɛ Yuda sɛɛ? Mi ni misɔmɔ otsɛ Saul we lɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi kɛ enanemɛi fɛɛ kɛ anɔkwayeli kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ, ni miŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni David anyɛ nyɛnɔ kunim eye lɛ, sane ni ofoɔ oŋmɛɔ minɔ yɛ yoo hewɔ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɛ?

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Ojogbaŋŋ! Mi Abner, Nyɔŋmɔ agbe, ni esaa egbe mi ekoŋŋ kɛji mihãaa shi ni Yehowa wo David lɛ aba mli fĩi,

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: akɛ ebaahe maŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ Saul we lɛ dɛŋ, ni ebaahã David maŋtsɛyeli lɛ ahe shi akɛ Israel kɛ Yuda fɛɛ maŋtsɛ kɛjɛ Dan aahu kɛyashwie Beersheba.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ishboshet nyɛɛɛ he eko eto dɔŋŋ ejaakɛ eeshe Abner gbeyei.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Abner tsu bɔfoi kɛtee David ŋɔɔ yɛ Hebron kɛ shɛɛ akɛ, “Namɔ osusuɔ akɛ ebaaye shikpɔŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ nɔ? Hã ni wɔkpãŋ wɔfee ekome, ni magbala Israel fɛɛ mibawo oshishi.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: David hã shɛɛ lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mi kɛ bo baakpãŋ; shi ja otsu nɔ kome nɛɛ dã: ni no ji akɛ kɛji ooba obana mi lɛ, okɛ Saul biyoo Mikal lɛ aba, kɛjeee nakai lɛ onaŋ mihiɛ.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: David saa je gbɛ etsu bɔfoi kɛtee Saul bi Ishboshet ŋɔɔ kɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ akɛ, “Miitao miŋa Mikal, mɔ ni mikɛ Filistibii afoonaa loi oha hã esɛɛnii lɛ.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ishboshet tsu ni ayakpala Mikal yɛ ewu Paltiel, Laish bi lɛ, ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ni Mikal wu lɛ fo kɛnyiɛ Mikal sɛɛ aahu kɛyashɛ Bahurim. Be ni eyashɛ jɛi lɛ Abner kɛɛ Paltiel akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ ni oya!” Kɛkɛ ni eku esɛɛ ni etee.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abner kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ tee ajina, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ lɛ kulɛ nyɛmiitao David ni eye nyɛmaŋtsɛ?

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Be lɛ eshɛ nɛɛ; nyɛtsua he nii ejaakɛ Yehowa ewo shi yɛ David he akɛ, ‘Mitsulɔ David nine nɔ matsɔ̃ mahere mimaŋ Israel yiwala yɛ Filistibii kɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi fɛɛ adɛŋ.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abner kɛ Benyaminbii lɛ hu yawie; ni no sɛɛ lɛ eŋɔ shwie nɔ, ni etee eyabɔ David amaniɛ, yɛ Hebron, nɔ ni Israelbii lɛ kɛ Benyaminbii lɛ eto amɛyiŋ akɛ amɛbafee lɛ.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Be ni Abner bashɛ David ŋɔɔ yɛ Hebron lɛ, David ŋmɛ lɛ kɛ mɛi nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni fata ehe kɛba lɛ fɛɛ okplɔ̃.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Abner kɛɛ David akɛ, “Mibaya agbɛnɛ koni mayabua Israel fɛɛ naa mahã minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ, koni amɛ kɛ bo abakpãŋ kɛfee ekome, koni oye amɛmaŋtsɛ bɔ ni oshweɔ lɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni David jie Abner gbɛ, ni eshi etee shweshweeshwe. Abner gbele

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Shi be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ Yoab kɛ David tsuji lɛ jɛ ojoyeli amɛba kɛ nibii babaoo ni amɛyaha. No mli lɛ Abner bɛ David ŋɔɔ yɛ Hebron, ejaakɛ David ejie lɛ gbɛ eshi etee shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Be ni Yoab kɛ tabilɔi ni kɛ lɛ tee lɛ fɛɛ ebato shi sɛɛ lɛ, agba Yoab akɛ, “Ner bi Abner ba maŋtsɛ ŋɔɔ, ni maŋtsɛ eŋmɛɛ ehe, ni etee shweshweeshwe.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab tee Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kwɛ, mɛni ofee nɛɛ? Abner ba biɛ ni oŋmɛɛ ehe ni etee?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Ole Ner bi Abner oto? Eba bo lakamɔ kɛkɛ koni ele oyaa kɛ obaa mli, asaŋ ni ele onibii amli hu.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Be ni Yoab shi David eba sɛɛ lɛ, eyatsu bɔfoi koni amɛtiu Abner ni amɛyatsɛ eyisɛɛ amɛhã lɛ. Bɔfoi lɛ yanina Abner yɛ Siria nubu lɛ he, ni amɛ kɛ lɛ ku sɛɛ kɛba. Shi enɛ fɛɛ lɛ, David leee he nɔ ko.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Be ni Abner ku esɛɛ ebashɛ Hebron lɛ, Yoab tsɛ lɛ kɛtee afãgbɛ yɛ maŋ koi lɛ shi akɛ ekɛ lɛ yaato ajina. Kɛkɛ ni Yoab du Abner musuŋ kakla ni enyɔ yɛ enajiaŋ, ni Yoab kɛtɔ enyɛminuu Asahel lá lɛ he owele.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Be ni fee sɛɛ ni David nu nɔ ni eba lɛ, ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mi kɛ mimaŋtsɛyeli lɛ, wɔyeee Ner bi Abner lá yi sɔ̃ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Elá lɛ abua Yoab kɛ etsɛ we lɛ yiteŋ, ni mɔ ni he hoɔ lá loo kpitiyelɔ loo mɔ ni ekumɔ ni ja ehiɛ tso dani ehiɔ lɛ nyiɛmɔ, loo mɔ ni gboɔ klante naa gbele loo hɔmɔwɔlɔ akakpa yɛ Yoab sateŋ.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ Yoab kɛ enyɛmi Abishai tsɔ ni amɛgbe Abner ejaakɛ egbe amɛnyɛminuu Asahel yɛ Gibeon ta lɛ mli. Abner Fũu

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: David fã Yoab kɛ ewebii lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛnyiɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛgbalaa nyɛhe atadei, ni nyɛbua kpekpe nyɛwoa yara nyɛfoa.” Maŋtsɛ David nyiɛ Abner gbonyo adeka lɛ sɛɛ.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Ato Abner yɛ Hebron. Be ni ayɔɔ gbonyobu lɛ naa lɛ, Maŋtsɛ David fo Abner, ni ehã maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu wo yara amɛfo.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛ lala fo Abner, ni ekɛɛ, “Esa akɛ Abner anyɔ tamɔ yakagbɔmɔ nyɔɔ lo?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Afimɔko oniji lɛ, awoko onaji gboklɛ hu. Bɔ ni mɛi nyɔɔ yɛ yiwalɔi adɛŋ lɛ, nakai onyɔ nɛɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni maŋ lɛ saa wo yara ni amɛfo Abner aahu.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tutɔ David gbi lɛ fɛɛ akɛ eye nii, shi Maŋtsɛ David kã kitã ekɛɛ, “Kɛji misa minaa aboloo loo nɔ ko dani hulu nyɔ shi fĩĩ, Nyɔŋmɔ awo mi nyɔmɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ yoo nɔ ni David fee lɛ sɛɛ, ni esa amɛhiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efeɔ saa amɛhiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Israel hu fɛɛ na le akɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ nine bɛ Abner, Ner bi lɛ, gbele lɛ mli.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛleee akɛ lumɔ kɛ gbɔmɔ wulu ko enyɔ ŋmɛnɛ yɛ Israel lo?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Afɔ mi mu awo mi Israel Maŋtsɛ moŋ nɛ, shi amrɔ nɛɛ nɛkɛ Zeruia bihii nɛɛ asane lɛ ebaje mi ablaŋ, ni ehiii mi nɔ ko feemɔ. Yehowa awo efɔŋfeelɔ lɛ nyɔmɔ yɛ enɔfɔŋ lɛ naa!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Be ni Saul bi Ishboshet nu akɛ Abner egbo yɛ Hebron lɛ, enijiaŋ je wui; ni Israel muu fɛɛ hu fee yɔɔ.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ishboshet yɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi enyɔ komɛi ni amɛ kɛ mɛi yaa amɛyayeɔ ofɔ̃ kɛbaa. Mɔ kome gbɛi ji Baana, ni mɔ kome hu gbɛi ji Rekab. Amɛtsɛ ji Rimon, Benyaminnyo ni jɛ Beerot lɛ (ejaakɛ abuɔ Beerot hu ashiɔ Benyaminbii amaji lɛ anɔ;

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: shi Beerotbii lɛ ejo foi kɛtee Gitaim, ni amɛyato gbɔ yɛ jɛi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.)

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Saul binuu Yonatan yɛ binuu ni enaji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ eje kpa. Gbekɛ nuu nɛɛ eye afii enumɔ be ni Saul kɛ Yonatan gbele lɛ he sane lɛ bashɛ Yezreel. Kɛkɛ ni oblayoo ni kwɛɔ gbekɛ lɛ wo lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ jo foi. Shi be ni oblayoo lɛ yeɔ oyai kɛjoɔ foi lɛ, gbekɛ nuu nɛɛ gbee shi, ni enaji kumɔ. Gbekɛnuu nɛɛ gbɛi ji Mefiboshet.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Rekab kɛ Baana, ni ji Beerotnyo Rimon bihii lɛ, yi mli kɛtee Ishboshet we lɛ. Amɛshɛ jɛi shwane fintiŋŋ be mli ni Ishboshet kã shi ewɔɔ eshwane wɔ lɛ.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Amɛyanina Ishboshet ni ekã esaa nɔ yɛ epia lɛ mli ewɔ; kɛkɛ ni amɛgbe lɛ, ni amɛfo eyitso. Amɛkɔ Ishboshet yitso lɛ; ni amɛnyiɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ kɛtsɔ̃ ŋa kplenee lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: ni amɛkɛba David ŋɔɔ yɛ Hebron. Amɛbakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Ohenyɛlɔ Saul ni tao bo egbe lɛ, ebi Ishboshet lɛ yitso nɛ. Yehowa etɔ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ he owele ŋmɛnɛ yɛ Saul kɛ eshwiei anɔ.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Shi hetoo ni David hã Rekab kɛ enyɛminuu Baana, ni ji Beerotnyo Rimon bihii lɛ, ji “Mina Yehowa, mɔ ni ebaa miyi yɛ fimɔi fɛɛ amli lɛ,

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: be ni mɔ ko ba ebagba mi akɛ ‘Naa, Saul egbo,’ ni eyiŋ fɛɛ lɛ eba ebagba mi sane kpakpa ko lɛ, mimɔ lɛ, ni migbe lɛ yɛ Ziklag, ni mikɛ no wo lɛ nyɔmɔ.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Enyiɛ nɔŋŋ ni kɛji gbɔmɛi fɔ̃ji etee amɛyagbe jalɔ yɛ wɔmli, yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshĩa teŋ, ni mibiŋ elá shi yɛ nyɛdɛŋ, ni mikpãtãŋ nyɛhiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David fã eblahii lɛ, ni amɛgbe Rekab kɛ Baana, ni amɛfolɔ amɛniji kɛ amɛnaji, ni amɛkɛtsotsro kpaakpo ni yɔɔ Hebron lɛ masɛi. Ni amɛkɔ Ishboshet yitso lɛ, ni amɛyafu yɛ he ni afu Abner yɛ lɛ, yɛ Hebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tiro maŋtsɛ Hiram wo kapintafoi kɛ tɛ gbogbotswalɔi agbɛ, ni amɛkɛ tsenedru tsei ba, ni amɛkɛbama maŋtsɛ we amɛhã David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Eye Yuda kɔkrɔɔ maŋtsɛ afii kpawo kɛ nyɔji ekpaa, ni eye Israel kɛ Yuda fɛɛ maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ etɛ̃ yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛ ewebii lɛ fã ta kɛyanina Yebusbii ni ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikwɛ̃ɛbii lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm. Yebusbii nɛɛ asusumɔ ji akɛ David nyɛŋ maŋ lɛ eshɔ̃, ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛtswa David mpoa akɛ, “Onyɛŋ biɛ oba; shwilafoi kɛ akpakei sɔŋŋ baashwie bo.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: David hewalɛ tee nɔ eshwere ejaakɛ Yehowa, ni ji Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ, fĩ esɛɛ.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Be ni David efã kɛjɛ Hebron kɛba Yerusalɛm sɛɛ lɛ, esaa eŋɔ hemɛi, ni ekpeekpee yei efata eŋãmɛi lɛ ahe, ni efɔ bihii kɛ biyei efata ebii krokomɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: kɛ Ibhar kɛ Elishua kɛ Nefeg kɛ Yafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: kɛ Elishama kɛ Eliada kɛ Elifelet. David ye Filistibii anɔ kunim (

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Be ni Filistibii lɛ nu akɛ awo David Israel fɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, Filistibii fɛɛ fã ta akɛ amɛyaamɔ David. Shi David nu he, ni no hewɔ lɛ, etee ehe yɛ mɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David yabi Yehowa nii ekɛɛ, “Ani mifã ta kɛyanina Filistibii lɛ lo? Ooohã maye amɛnɔ kunim lo?” Yehowa here David nɔ akɛ, “Fãa ta okɛyanina amɛ, ejaakɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ mahã oye amɛnɔ kunim.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David fã ta kɛyanina Filistibii lɛ yɛ Baal-Perazim, ni eye amɛnɔ kunim yɛ jɛi. David kɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa etsɔ̃ minine nɔ egba kɛtsɔ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ ateŋ tamɔ nu ni eje ŋa gbaa lɛ.” No hewɔ ni atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Baal-Perazim lɛ.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistibii lɛ shi amɛmãgãi lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni amɛjo foi, ni David kɛ ewebii lɛ loo amãgãi lɛ kɛtee.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Shi Filistibii lɛ fã ta kɛba ekoŋŋ, ni amɛbagba ta yɛ Efraim Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Be ni David tee eyabi Yehowa nii lɛ, hetoo ni ehã lɛ ji akɛ, “Kaafã ta lɛ kɛyatua amɛ kɛjɛ biɛ, shi lɔgɔmɔ kɛyaje amɛsɛɛgbɛ, koni ojɛ Balsam tsei lɛ aŋlɛnɔ obatua amɛ.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Kɛ onu gbɛɛmɔ yɛ Balsam tsei lɛ ayiteŋ tamɔ naneshi gbɛɛmɔ lɛ, ohe afee oya ni otua amɛ, ejaakɛ no tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ miyi ohiɛ miyatswia Filistibii lɛ atabilɔi lɛ anii.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: David fee bɔ ni Yehowa fã lɛ lɛ, ni egbe Filistibii lɛ, ni eshwie amɛ kɛjɛ Geba aahu kɛyashwie Gezer.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Kɛji mɛi ni tere Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ famɔ amɛnaji shii ekpaa lɛ, David gbeɔ tsina kɛ too ni ewo fɔ ekɛshãa afɔle.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David jo kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ekɛwo Yehowa hiɛ nyam, ni emia kɛ klala efod pɛ.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Lɛ kɛ Israel maŋ muu fɛɛ kɛ oshebɔɔ kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ yawo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ shɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, Mikal, Saul biyoo lɛ, bu samflɛ naa, ni ena Maŋtsɛ David ni eehuru ni eejo kɛmiiwo Yehowa hiɛ nyam, ni David he fee Mikal hiɛgbele.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
