translation_verse: Amɛyawo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yɛ Abinadab we lɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛma shwiili hee ko nɔ. Abinadab bihii, Uza kɛ Ahio, kudɔ shwiili hee ni adeka lɛ ma nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ yiŋ kɛtee Baala maŋ lɛ mli yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, koni amɛyawo Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ. Akɛ Yehowa Ofe ni elumɔyeli sɛi lɛ ma kerubim lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛi ewo adeka lɛ.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Ni Ahio nyiɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: David kɛ Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nya kɛ lalai kɛ saŋkui kɛ obentai kɛ fabii kɛ miji kɛ ŋoŋoi amɛkɛwo Yehowa hiɛ nyam kɛ amɛnyɛmɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Be ni ashɛ Nakon ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ, tsinai lɛ tɛ ni Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kpa ni eyaagbee shi. No hewɔ lɛ, Uza kpã enine mli ni ekɛmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Yehowa mli wo Uza la, ni etswa lɛ nɔ amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ enine ni ekɛta Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ he lɛ hewɔ, ni Uza gbo yɛ enajiaŋ yɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ masɛi.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, atsɛ jɛi Perez-Uza kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Sane lɛ dɔ David akɛ Yehowa kɛ Uza ye kɛ joomɔ nakai.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: David she Yehowa gbeyei nakai gbi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato Yehowa Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hu?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, David sumɔɔɔ akɛ ekɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yaa Yerusalɛm. No hewɔ lɛ, David wo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛgba afã kɛtee Obed-Edom, Gitnyo lɛ, we lɛ.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Abagba Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Yehowa ejɔɔ Obed-Edom we lɛ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ yɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hewɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ, David tee, ni eyawo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yɛ Obed-Edom we lɛ kɛba Yerusalɛm kɛ nyamɔ.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Ni akɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ba, ni akɛyama gbɛhe ni ato ahã lɛ yɛ buu ni David eshi ehã lɛ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, David shã afɔlei kɛ shidaa afɔlei ehã Yehowa.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Be ni David egbe shãa afɔlei lɛ kɛ shidaa afɔlei lɛ ashãa naa lɛ, ejɔɔ maŋbii lɛ yɛ Yehowa Ofe lɛ gbɛi mli,

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: ni eja maŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ni ji Israel asafo muu lɛ mli hii kɛ yei fɛɛ, niyenii. Ehã mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aboloo akwaabɔ kome kɛ loo kukuli kome kɛ wainyibii ni aka ni egbi akwaabɔ kome. Ni no sɛɛ lɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ mli, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee ewe.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni David yiŋ etee ewe lɛ ni eyahã sɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ, Mikal, Saul biyoo lɛ, je kpo ekɛ lɛ bakpe, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Aso nyam pi Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ wo ehiɛ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ kɛ ehe bo ni ejie yɛ etsuji kɛ eweyei ahiɛ tamɔ mɛi ni ahiɛgble tɔ ejwa feɔ lɛ!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Shi David hã Mikal hetoo, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, Yehowa, mɔ ni shi otsɛ kɛ ewe lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ ni ebaŋɔ mi, ni ewo mi Israel, ni ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ lɛ, nɔ lumɔ lɛ, lɛ ehiɛ nyam mijo mikɛwo lɛ; ni majo ŋmɛnɛ, ni majo wɔ mikɛwo ehiɛ nyam.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Maya nɔ moŋ mawo mihe hiɛgbele fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ bo ohiɛ; shi weyei lɛ ni otsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, amɛ lɛ nyam moŋ mihiɛ aaaba yɛ amɛhiɛ.”

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Mikal, Saul biyoo lɛ, naaa bi kɛyashi egbo.

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mimɔbɔnalɛ sɛɛ efoŋ yɛ egbɛfaŋ tamɔ bɔ ni mihã mimɔbɔnalɛ lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ Saul gbɛfaŋ lɛ, mɔ ni mikpa lɛ ni obaye esɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: etsɛ gbalɔ Natan ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɛ oona akɛ, mi lɛ, mina tsenedru tsu mli mikã be mli ni Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ yɛ buu mli?”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Natan hã Maŋtsɛ David hetoo akɛ, “Feemɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kã otsui nɔ akɛ ofee lɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa fi osɛɛ.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Shi nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nyɔɔŋ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ Natan akɛ,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Yaa ni oyakɛɛ mitsulɔ David akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: Bo omaa tsu ohãa mi mahi mli?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ be nɔ ni miyakpala Israelbii yɛ Ijipt aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ, mihiko tsu mli dã, fe buu mli sɔŋŋ kɛkɛ miyɔɔ.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Hei fɛɛ ni mikɛ Israel fɛɛ enyiɛnyiɛ lɛ, mibiko Israel maŋ hiɛnyiɛlɔi ni mifãa amɛ akɛ amɛkura mimaŋ Israel lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko yɛ he ko pɛŋ akɛ mɛɛba po ni nyɛmako tsenedru tsu nyɛhãko mi lɛ?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ mitsulɔ David akɛ, mi, Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, miikɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Too okpalaa, ni miŋɔ bo, ni mifee bo Israel nɔyelɔ,

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: ni he fɛɛ he ni oyaa lɛ mifata ohe, ni miplenee ohenyɛlɔi fɛɛ yɛ ohiɛ, ni mihã ona gbɛi kpeteŋkple tamɔ gbɔmɛi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Asaŋ mato he ko mahã mimaŋ Israel koni amɛyahi jɛi akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnɔ mli, he ni agbaŋ amɛnaa yɛ dɔŋŋ, ni yiwalɔi haoŋ amɛ dɔŋŋ tamɔ sa,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: be ni mito hiɛnyiɛlɔi koni amɛkura mimaŋ Israel lɛ. Ni mahã ohe ajɔ bo yɛ ohenyɛlɔi lɛ fɛɛ agbɛfaŋ. Asaŋ mi, Yehowa, miiwo bo shi akɛ mibahã owo shwiei babaoo,

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: ni ogbele sɛɛ lɛ matee mɔ ko shi kɛjɛ oshwiei lɛ amli akɛ maŋtsɛ, ni mahã emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Lɛ ji mɔ ni baama Sɔlemɔ we ehã mi ni mahã emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ kɛya naanɔ.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Mibatsɔ̃ etsɛ, ni eeetsɔ̃ mibi. Kɛji efee nɔ fɔŋ lɛ mibagbala etoi tamɔ bɔ ni tsɛ gbalaa ebi toi lɛ.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Akɛ bo Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, diɛŋtsɛ ojie nii nɛɛ otsɔ̃ɔ mi otsulɔ, ni okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mahã oshwiei atsɔmɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ,’ no hã mi, otsulɔ, mina ekãa misɔle nɛkɛ sɔlemɔ nɛɛ.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David bote Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ mli, ni eho eta shi, ni esɔle ekɛɛ, “Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, namɔ ji mi, ni mɛni mli miwe lɛ yɔɔ hewɔ ni ohiɛ mi kɛbashi be nɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Ni kɛ̃lɛ enɛ jeee nɔ ko srɔto ko hã bo, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ. Otsɔ̃ɔ wɔsɛɛ shɔŋŋ nibii ni baaba, mi otsulɔ, miwe lɛ nɔ hu. Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, otsɔ̃ɔ mi shwiei ni mawo.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Mɛni po yɔɔ mi David minaa ni makɛɛ dɔŋŋ? Ejaakɛ bo Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, ole mi, otsulɔ.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Shi ni owo lɛ, akɛ ni eji bo diɛŋtsɛ osuɔmɔnaa hewɔ lɛ, ofee nibii wuji nɛɛ fɛɛ koni okɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi, otsulɔ, nii.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, oda kpeteŋkple, Ofe, ejaakɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ bo yeee egbɔ, ni asaŋ yɛ nii fɛɛ ni wɔnu kɛ wɔtoi lɛ naa lɛ, osɛɛ lɛ nyɔŋmɔ ko nyɔŋmɔ ko bɛ.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ maŋ kroko ko yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etamɔ omaŋ Israel, ni ji maŋ ni bo Nyɔŋmɔ otee oyakpɔ̃ amɛ; ni ofee amɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ owebii, ni okɛhe gbɛi, ni otsu nibii wuji ni yɔɔ gbeyei ohã amɛ, akɛ ogbɛ maŋ muu kɛ amɛnyɔŋmɔi fɛɛ oshwã yɛ amɛhiɛ?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Oma omaŋ Israel nɔ mi akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ omaŋ kɛmiiya naanɔ, ni bo Yehowa otsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ, Yehowa Nyɔŋmɔ, maa shi ni owo yɛ mi, otsulɔ, kɛ ewe lɛ he lɛ nɔ mi kɛya naanɔ; ofee nɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ,

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: ni ogbɛi lɛ aaada kpeteŋkple, ni aaakɛɛ kɛya naanɔ akɛ, ‘Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ Israel;’ ni mi otsulɔ David we lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ yɛ ohiɛ.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: “Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, bo ji Nyɔŋmɔ, ni owiemɔ lɛ anɔkwale ni; ni okɛ nɔ kpakpa nɛɛ ewo otsulɔ shi.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, na he tsui koni ojɔɔ otsulɔ we lɛ bɔ ni afee ni miwe lɛ ahi shi kɛya naanɔ. Ejaakɛ Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, owo shi, ni jɔɔmɔ lɛ aaahi mishwiei lɛ anɔ kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia, Yehoiada bi lɛ, ji tabilɔi ni buɔ David he tuuŋtu lɛ atsɛ, ni David bihii lɛ miisɔmɔ akɛ osɔfoi.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, David ye Moabbii lɛ hu anɔ kunim. Ehã Moabbii ni amɔmɔ lɛ kamɔ shikpɔŋ. Ni kɛji ekɛ susumɔ kpãa susu gbɔmɛi nɛɛ, ni ena kpãi enyɔ lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ ehã agbe amɛ; kɛkɛ lɛ esusu kpãa kome, kɛkɛ lɛ ehã amɛyi ena wala. Moabbii lɛ tsɔmɔ David tsuji, ni amɛtsu onia amɛhã lɛ.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: David ye Zoba Maŋtsɛ Hadadezer, Rehob bi lɛ, hu nɔ kunim, be ni Hadadezer yiŋ etee akɛ eyaapele hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kã Eufrate Faa lɛ naa lɛ he lɛ.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Siriabii ni yɔɔ Damasko lɛ ba koni amɛbawa Zoba maŋtsɛ Hadadezer; shi David gbe Siriabii lɛ ateŋ mɛi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David shi asraafoi eto Siriabii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni Siriabii lɛ tsɔmɔ David tsuji, ni etsũ amɛ onia. Yehowa hã David ye kunim yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David shɔ̃ shika tsɛŋi ni Hadadezer tsuji lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ni ekɛba Yerusalɛm;

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: asaŋ eloo akɔɔble babaoo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Beta kɛ Berotai, maji ni yɔɔ Hadadezer shishi lɛ.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: etsu ebi, Yoram, Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ koni eyaŋa lɛ ni ehã lɛ aekoo ehã lɛ, yɛ Hadadezer nɔ kunim ni eye lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ Hadadezer kɛ Toi lɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe wuwuu tai saŋŋ. Yoram hiɛ jwiɛtɛi nibii kɛ shika nibii kɛ akɔɔble nibii ekɛbake David.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David jɔɔ nibii nɛɛ hu anɔ eke akɛ akɛsɔmɔ Yehowa tamɔ bɔ ni ejɔɔ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika ni eshɔ̃ kɛjɛ majimaji ni eye amɛnɔ lɛ amli kɛba lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: ni Zadok, Ahitub bi lɛ, kɛ Ahimelek, Abiatar bi lɛ, amɛ ji osɔfoi; ni Seraia ji maŋtsɛ we woloŋmalɔ.

english_verse: David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
translation_verse: David ye Israel maŋtsɛ, ni eye jalɛ sane ehã mɔ fɛɛ mɔ.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.

translation_verse: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni oku, mi Yehowa, migbee nɔ, ni ofee efɔŋ nɛɛ? Ogbe Uria, Hitnyo lɛ. Ohã Amonbii lɛ gbe lɛ, kɛkɛ ni oŋɔ eŋa lɛ ofee oŋa.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, bo hu kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ lɛ klante naa gbele kpãŋ yɛ oshwiei ateŋ, ejaakɛ obuuu mi, ni oŋɔ Uria Hitnyo lɛ ŋa lɛ ofee oŋa.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Miiwo bo shi! Mahã gbɔmɔ ajɛ bo nɔŋŋ owe lɛ mli ate shi awo bo; ni ohiɛ tua ookwɛ nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ ni mashɔ oŋamɛi lɛ mahã owekunyo, ni ekɛ oŋamɛi lɛ baawɔ shwane fintiŋŋ.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Bo lɛ otee ohe, ni ofee esha lɛ, shi mi lɛ mibafee nɔ ni mikɛɛ lɛ yɛ Israel fɛɛ hiɛ shwane fintiŋŋ?’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ akɛ obuuu Yehowa yɛ nɔ ni ofee lɛ hewɔ lɛ, bi lɛ ni abaafɔ ahã bo lɛ yi naŋ wala; gbo eeegbo.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Natan shi David ni etee ewe. Batsheba bi gbo Yehowa hã hela shi bi lɛ ni Uria ŋa lɛ kɛ David fɔ lɛ nɔ, ni gbekɛ lɛ he ye waa naakpa.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: David sɔle ekpa Nyɔŋmɔ fai ehã gbekɛ lɛ koni ehe awa lɛ; David hi ŋmaa, ni eho ekã shikpɔŋ yɛ etsu lɛ mli nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ewe lɛ mli onukpai lɛ tee koni amɛyawo enɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ, shi David ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ, ni nii hu emiii akɛ eye.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Gbi ni hela lɛ na otsi lɛ, gbekɛ lɛ gbo; shi David tsuji lɛ she gbeyei akɛ amɛaakɛɛ lɛ gbekɛ lɛ gbele lɛ ejaakɛ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Be ni gbekɛ lɛ hiɛ kã lolo po lɛ, wɔkɛ lɛ wie lɛ ebooo wɔ toi. Te wɔɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔkɛɛ lɛ akɛ gbekɛ lɛ egbo hu? Kɛji akwɛɛɛ ni ahi lɛ eeefee ehe efɔŋ ko.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Shi be ni David na bɔ ni etsuji lɛ wieɔ ablɛbi lɛ pɛ, kɛkɛ ni eyoo sɛɛ akɛ gbekɛ lɛ egbo. No hewɔ lɛ, David bi etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Gbekɛ lɛ egbo, bɛɛ?” Amɛhere lɛ nɔ akɛ, “Egbo”.

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: David tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔnuuu bo shishi! Ejaakɛ be ni gbekɛ lɛ hiɛ kã lɛ, ohi ŋmaa, ni ofo ohã lɛ; shi ni egbo moŋ lɛ ni oyeɔ nii nɛɛ?”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: David kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Be ni gbekɛ lɛ hiɛ kã lolo lɛ, mihi ŋmãa ni mifo, ejaakɛ misusumɔ ji akɛ eko lɛ Yehowa aaana mi mɔbɔ, ni eeehã gbekɛ lɛ yi ana wala;

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: shi agbɛnɛ ni ena egbo lɛ, mɛni mahi ŋmãa mafee? Manyɛ mahã eba wala mli ekoŋŋ? Mi moŋ maya he ni eyɔɔ lɛ; shi lɛ lɛ ekpaleŋ ebaŋ miŋɔɔ dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: David shɛje eŋa Batsheba mii; ni fee sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ lɛ na bɔlɛ ni Batsheba fɔ binuu, ni David wo lɛ gbɛi akɛ Solomon. Yehowa na gbekɛ lɛ he tsui,

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: ni etsu Natan gbalɔ lɛ kɛtee ni eyawo gbekɛ lɛ gbɛi “Yedidia” ehã Yehowa. David yaŋɔ Raba maŋ lɛ (

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Ni Yoab fã ta kɛyatua Amonbii amaŋ wulu ni atsɛɔ lɛ Raba lɛ, ni ekɛ amɛwu; ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaaŋɔ maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab tsu bɔfoi David ŋɔɔ kɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ: “Miyatua Rababii, ni miŋɔ maŋ lɛ he ni amɛnaa nu kɛjɛɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ buamɔ maŋ lɛ tabilɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ anaa, koni okɛ amɛ abatua amɛmaŋ wulu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni oŋɔ, bɔ ni afee ni mi mikayaŋɔ ni akɛ migbɛi wo maŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Enɛ hã David bua etabilɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ anaa. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ amɛ fã kɛtee eyatua Raba ni eŋɔ maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Maŋbii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehã amɛ nitsumɔ ni amɛkɛ saalai kɛ kɔi kɛ lema atsu; asaŋ enyɛ amɛnɔ hu ni amɛfo ntayaa amɛhã lɛ. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni ekɛ Amonbii amaji lɛ fɛɛ ye ehã. Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛba Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: David binuu Absalom yɛ nyɛbiyoo fɛɛfɛo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Tamar. David binuu kroko ni gbɛi ji Amnon lɛ basumɔ Tamar.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Amnon sumɔ enyɛmi yoo nɛɛ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni suɔmɔ lɛ wo lɛ hela tete, ejaakɛ Amnon leee gbɛ koome nɔ ni eeetsɔ̃ ni enine aaashɛ Tamar nɔ, ejaakɛ Tamar lɛ oblayoo foro ni.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Amnon yɛ naanyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yonadab, ni ji David nyɛmi nuu, Shimea, lɛ binuu. Mɔlakalɔ jogbaŋŋ ji Yonadab nɛɛ.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Yonadab bi Amnon akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni bo maŋtsɛbi muu lɛ otãa loo gbi fɛɛ gbi nɛɛ? Ogbaaa mi nɔ ni gbaa onaa?” Amnon jie naa ekɛɛ, “Miisumɔ Tamar, minyɛmi Absalom nyɛbiyoo lɛ.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yonadab kɛɛ Amnon akɛ, “Yaahɔ osaa mli, ni okwa akɛ ohe miiye; ni kɛji otsɛ ba bo saramɔ lɛ okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Ataa, ofainɛ ni ohã minyɛmiyoo Tamar aba ni ebafee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enine naa niyenii yɛ mihiɛ ni ehiɛ yɛ edɛŋ, ni maye.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Amnon tee eyakã shi lɛɛlɛŋ, ni ekwa akɛ ehe miiye. Be ni etsɛ, Maŋtsɛ David, ba lɛ saramɔ lɛ, Amnon kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ataa, ofainɛ ni ohã minyɛmi yoo Tamar aba ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebashã aboloi enyɔ oo ko yɛ mihiɛ ni ehiɛ yɛ edɛŋ ni maye.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Tamar yiŋ etee enyɛmi Amnon we lɛ, ni eyanina lɛ ni ekã saa nɔ. Tamar tĩ ma, ni ekpɔtɔ ekɛfee niyenii lɛ be mli ni Amnon miikwɛ lɛ; kɛkɛ ni eshã aboloo lɛ.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Amnon miikwɛ nɔŋŋ ni Tamar wo nishãa tsɛnsi lɛ ni etsɔ̃ niyenii lɛ yɛ mli ehã lɛ. Amnon ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ yeli, shi moŋ ekɛɛ akɛ, “hã mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ashi mimasɛi.” Ni mɛi lɛ fɛɛ je kpo yɛ tsu lɛ mli.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Amnon kɛɛ Tamar akɛ, “Okɛ niyenii lɛ aba pia lɛ mli koni ohiɛ yɛ odɛ̃ŋ ni maye.” Tamar wo aboloo ni eshã lɛ kɛtee enyɛmi Amnon ŋɔɔ yɛ pia lɛ mli.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Shi be ni Tamar tsi bɛŋkɛ Amnon kɛ niyenii lɛ koni eye lɛ, Amnon mɔ Tamar mli, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minyɛmi yoo, hã ni wɔna bɔlɛ.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Tamar kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Dabida, minyɛmi nuu! Kaamɔ mi akranaŋ naa, ejaakɛ aahi nɛkɛ nɔ ko yɛ Israel! Kaafee nɛkɛ hiɛgbejianii nɛɛ!

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Bo lɛ oootsɔ̃ tamɔ Israel hii yakagbɔmɛi lɛ eko kɛkɛ, shi mi lɛ, nɛgbɛ po mi kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛgbele nɛɛ aaatee? Shi moŋ okɛ maŋtsɛ ayawie he, ni mile akɛ ekɛ mi baahã bo aahu.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ Amnon booo Tamar toi, ni akɛni ehe wa fe Tamar hewɔ lɛ, emɔ lɛ akranaŋ naa, ni ekɛ lɛ wɔ.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Amnon he tsɛ̃ Tamar waa bɔ ni hetsɛ̃ lɛ naa yawa fe suɔmɔ ni ekɛsumɔ Tamar lɛ; ni ekɛɛ Tamar akɛ, “Tee shi ni oya.”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Tamar kɛɛ Amnon akɛ, “Dabida, kaafee mi nakai, ejaakɛ shwiemɔ ni oshwieɔ mi nɛɛ moŋ ji efɔŋ ni naa wa fe klɛŋklɛŋ efɔŋ ni ofee mi lɛ.” Shi Amnon booo lɛ toi;

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: shi moŋ etsɛ oblanyo ni sɔmɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Shwiemɔ yoo nɛɛ yɛ mihiɛ kɛje kpo, ni ola shinaa lɛ sɛɛ.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Tsulɔ lɛ shwie Tamar kɛje kpo, ni ela shinaa lɛ sɛɛ. Tamar wo atade wuyaa kɛ ehe niji kakadaji; blema lɛ no ji maŋtsɛmɛi abiyei froi atade.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Tamar loo lamlu eshwie eyiteŋ, ni egbala atade wuyaa fɛɛfɛo ni ewo lɛ, ni ekɔlɔ eniji eshwie eyiteŋ, ni ehiɛ yaafo gegeege kɛtee.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Enyɛmi Absalom bi lɛ akɛ, “Ani onyɛmi Amnon eta ohe lo? Minyɛmi yoo! Kaahã enɛ miiye otsui tsɔ̃, shi moŋ feemɔ dioo; ni kaagba mɔ ko, ejaakɛ onyɛmi ni.” Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Tamar wa enyɛmi Absalom we lɛ, ni ewo ehe tsuŋ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ David nu saji fɛɛ ni eba lɛ he lɛ, emli wo la naakpa.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Absalom nyɛ Amnon waa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ enyɛbiyoo Tamar ni Amnon mɔ lɛ lɛ hewɔ; shi moŋ ejieee dɔlɛ lɛ kpo etsɔ̃ɔɔ Amnon. Absalom tɔ owele

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ afii enyɔ lɛ, aaku Absalom toi ahetsɔi yɛ Baal-Hazor ni bɛŋkɛ Efraim maŋ lɛ, ni ekpee maŋtsɛ bihii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ amɛba jɛi.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Absalom ba Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nii, aaku mitoi ahetsɔi. Ofainɛ koni Nii kɛ etsuji lɛ abafata mihe kɛnya yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David here Absalom nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Dabida, mibi! Kɛji wɔ fɛɛ wɔba lɛ, ebaafee tɔlɛ kɛ naagba tsɔ̃ ehã bo.” Absalom fi nɔ doo akɛ eekpee mɔ fɛɛ mɔ, shi Maŋtsɛ David ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ nɔ; shi moŋ ejɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Absalom kɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji nakai lɛ, ofainɛ, hã minyɛmi Amnon kɛ wɔ aya mɔ.” Maŋtsɛ lɛ bi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ekɛ bo aya?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Absalom hiɛ sane lɛ mli aahu ni naagbee lɛ Maŋtsɛ David ŋmɛ gbɛ, ni Amnon kɛ maŋtsɛ bihii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Absalom tee.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Absalom kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Kɛfee lɛ nyɛkwɛa Amnon, kɛji nyɛna akɛ wain lɛ ehã emli efili lɛ, ni mifã akɛ atswa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛgbea lɛ. Nyɛkashea gbeyei ejaakɛ mi mifã nyɛ. Nyɛfea ekãa; nyɛfea hii!”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Absalom tsuji lɛ ye efãmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛgbe Amnon. Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ bihii krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ho tara amɛtejiokpɔŋɔi anɔ, ni amɛjo foi.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛbii lɛ nyiɛ gbɛ lolo, ni abatswa David adafi akɛ, “Shi ota? Absalom egbe obihii lɛ fɛɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ kome folo nɛkɛ eshwɛko!”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni Maŋtsɛ David ho edamɔ shi, ni egbala atadei lɛ yɛ ehe, ni eho ekã shikpɔŋ. Etsuji fɛɛ ni damɔ emasɛi nakai be lɛ gbalagbalaa amɛ hu amɛtadei.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David nyɛmi nuu, Shimea, bi Yonadab kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Nii, agbeko obihii lɛ fɛɛ. Amnon kome kɛkɛ agbe, ejaakɛ kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni Amnon mɔ Absalom nyɛbiyoo Tamar, ni efite lɛ lɛ beebe, ni Absalom to eyiŋ akɛ ebaafee nɛkɛ nɔ ko.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kaahe sane nɛɛ oye akɛ maŋtsɛ bihii lɛ fɛɛ ni egboi lɛ, ejaakɛ Amnon kome kɛkɛ ji mɔ ni egbo lɛ.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Ni fee nakai lɛ Absalom jo foi. Shi trukaa lɛ oblanyo tabilɔ ni miibu lɛ yaawo ehiɛ nɔ lɛ, ena mɛi babaoo ni miiba yɛ Horonaim gbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ he. Etee ni eyagba Maŋtsɛ David nɔ ni ena lɛ.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yonadab kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Naa, maŋtsɛbii lɛ miiba. Bɔ ni otsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ, nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ ni.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Yonadab naa ni nyɔ shi nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ pɛ, naa maŋtsɛbii lɛ ni amɛba. Kɛkɛ ni amɛwo yara, ni Maŋtsɛ David hu kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ wo yara amɛfo aahu.

english_verse: David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead. David Lets Absalom Come Home Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud.
translation_verse: Be ni Absalom jo foi lɛ, etee Geshur maŋtsɛ Talmai, ni ji Amihud bi lɛ, ŋɔɔ, ni ekɛ lɛ yahi shi afii etɛ̃. David ye ebinuu Absalom he awerɛho daa gbi.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ni eshwe Absalom; shi Amnon gbɛfaŋ lɛ, David tse etsui eŋmɛ emli ejaakɛ lɛ lɛ egbo momo.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Be ni Zeruia bi Yoab na bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ lɛ tsui yeɔ yɛ Absalom he ehãa lɛ,

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Be ni Tekoayoo lɛ yashɛ Maŋtsɛ David hiɛ lɛ, eho egbee shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Nii, ofainɛ ni oye obua mi.”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: David bi yoo lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni ji osane lɛ?” Yoo lɛ jie naa akɛ, “Miwu egbo, ni eshi mi okulafo.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Oweyoo bihii enyɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ be yɛ ŋa nɔ; ni akɛni mɔ ko bɛ jɛi ni aaakpãtã amɛ hewɔ lɛ, mɔ kome tswa mɔ kome nɔ, ni egbe lɛ.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ weku lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm ete shi ewo mi. Amɛkɛɛ mijie binuu ni tswa enyɛmi lɛ nɔ ni egbe lɛ lɛ mihã amɛ, koni amɛgbe lɛ kɛtɔ enyɛmi ni egbe lɛ he owele. Be lɛ amɛbaakpãtã mibiiatsɛ lɛ niyelɔ lɛ hu hiɛ. Ni kɛji eba lɛ nakai lɛ, amɛbaahã mihiɛnɔkãmɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ atã, ni miwu lɛ hu gbɛi loo eseshi baalaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, bo lɛ yaa owe lɛ; ni matsu osane lɛ he nii.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Tekoayoo lɛ kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, kɛji tɔ̃mɔ ko aaaba lɛ, ekã mi kɛ mitsɛ we lɛ nɔ. Sɔ̃ ko sɔ̃ ko akawula maŋtsɛ kɛ eshwiei ayiteŋ.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ bo aaawie nɔ ko lɛ, okɛ mɔ lɛ aba miŋɔɔ; ni kɛjɛ no sɛɛ lɛ mɔ lɛ etaŋ ohe dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Tekoayoo lɛ to he ekɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, ofainɛ, ni okpa Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fai koni mɔ ni taoɔ etɔ mibi lɛ lá lɛ he owele lɛ yiŋ atsake koni ekashwie mibi ni eshwɛ lɛ lá shi.” Maŋtsɛ David to he ekɛɛ, “Mina Yehowa akɛ kɛji obi lɛ yiteŋ tsɔi kome nɛkɛ nyɔ shi fĩĩ.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, ni oŋmɛ oweyoo gbɛ koni ekɛɛ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ nɔ ko.” Maŋtsɛ David here nɔ ekɛɛ, “Wiemɔ”.

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Tekoayoo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba mɔ ni okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ webii lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ sane? Bɔ ni obua sane lɛ he ohã nɛɛ lɛ, belɛ gbii abɔ ni maŋtsɛ eyakpalako ebi ni enyɔ kooŋ lɛ kɛbako lɛ, maŋtsɛ miibu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ ehe fɔ mɔ.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Gbele kã shi hã wɔ fɛɛ, ni ehãa wɔtsɔ̃ɔ tamɔ nu ni atsi ashwie shikpɔŋ, ni ehiii loomɔ dɔŋŋ. Shi mɔ ni toɔ gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni afee ni mɔ ni enyɔ kooŋ aba shĩa lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ egbeee lɛ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Nii, nɔ hewɔ ni miba mikɛ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ bawie nɛkɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ ji akɛ maŋbii lɛ wo mihe gbeyei. Enɛ hã mito miyiŋ akɛ maya mikɛ maŋtsɛ ayawie akɛ aleenɔ eeefee nɔ ni mi, otsulɔyoo, aaabi lɛ lɛ lo.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mile faŋŋ akɛ maŋtsɛ aaabo mi toi, ni eeejie mi yɛ nuu ni taoɔ akɛ ejie mi kɛ mibi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhã ewebii lɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Mina hiɛnɔkãmɔ akɛ hetoo ni minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ aaahã mi lɛ baahã mitsui anyɔ mimli, ejaakɛ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo, ni enaa nɔ kpakpa kɛ nɔ gbonyo. Yehowa oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ajɔɔ bo.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ Tekoayoo lɛ akɛ, “Sane ni mibabi bo agbɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ, gbaa mi anɔkwale ni yɔɔ mli.” Yoo lɛ to he ekɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ awie.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David bi yoo lɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni obafee nɛɛ lɛ, Yoab nine yɛ mli lo?” Yoo lɛ jie sane lɛ naa, ni ekɛɛ, “Mina minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ akɛ anɔkwale lɛ shishiishi owie lɛ. Otsulɔ Yoab ni tsu mi, asaŋ, lɛ nɔŋŋ eta wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ ewo minaa.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Otsulɔ Yoab to ŋaa nɛɛ bɔ ni afee ni atsake sane lɛ hiɛ. Shi akɛni minuŋtsɔ le nii tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo hewɔ lɛ, ele nibii fɛɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ mikpɛ̃lɛ̃; no hewɔ lɛ, yaa koni okɛ Absalom aba.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Ni Yoab ho egbee shi ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto Maŋtsɛ David, ni eda lɛ shi ekɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, ŋmɛnɛ mi, otsulɔ, ena ele akɛ oyɛ mihe tsuijurɔ ejaakɛ, maŋtsɛ, ofee nɔ ni mibi lɛ ohã mi.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yoab te shi, ni eyiŋ etee Geshur, ni eyaŋɔ Absalom kɛba Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, Maŋtsɛ David hã wiemɔ akɛ, “Eya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewe lɛ mli eyahi jɛi. Mitaooo ehiɛ mana.” Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Absalom gba kɛtee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshĩa lɛ, ni enaaa maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ. David kɛ Absalom kpãtã

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Kɛji eku eyiteŋ tsɔi lɛ eyiteŋ tsɔi lɛ shekeli ohai enyɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ nsɛnitɛ naa.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom fɔ bihii etɛ̃ kɛ yoo kome ni atsɛ lɛ Tamar; ni eji yoo ko ni he yɛ fɛo naakpa.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom ye afii enyɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm ni enaaa Maŋtsɛ David hiɛ nɛkɛ.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Absalom tsu atsɛ Yoab ahã lɛ koni etsu lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Shi Yoab sumɔɔɔ akɛ eyaa. Absalom ku sɛɛ etsu atsɛ Yoab nɔ ni ji shii enyɔ nɔ, shi no hu Yoab eyaaa.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Absalom kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛna Yoab ŋmɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ minɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ, nyɛyaa, ni nyɛyamaa akoko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa la.” Absalom tsuji lɛ tee ni amɛyama ŋmɔ lɛ naa la.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab tee eyanina Absalom yɛ eshĩa lɛ mli, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni otsuji lɛ yama miŋmɔ lɛ naa la lɛ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Absalom jie naa akɛ, “Akɛni mitsu ni atsɛ bo ahã mi, ni obaaa lɛ hewɔ. Miitao bo matsu maŋtsɛ ŋɔɔ koni oyabi lɛ ohã mi nɔ hewɔ kwraa ni mishi Geshur kɛba lɛ. Miyɛ jɛi lolo kulɛ, bɛ no moŋ hi hã mi?” Absalom tee nɔ ni ekɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Yaatsu he nii ohã mi koni mana maŋtsɛ hiɛ. Kɛji mitɔ̃ enɔ lɛ koni egbe mi.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Yoab tee eyana maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ebɔ lɛ amaniɛ; ni Maŋtsɛ David tsu ayatsɛ Absalom. Be ni Absalom shɛ shi lɛ eho egbee shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto Maŋtsɛ David. Maŋtsɛ David shwɔ Absalom naa ekɛhere lɛ atuu.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Absalom to shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔi ehã ehe; ni esaa hii tabilɔi nyɔŋmai enumɔ eto koni amɛnyiɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Eteɔ shi maŋkɛ mra, ni eyadamɔɔ gbɛ ni kã kɛyaa maŋ agbo lɛ naa lɛ toi. Ni kɛji ena mɔ ko ni ehiɛ bei sane ko kɛmiiba koni maŋtsɛ lɛ akwɛ ahã lɛ lɛ, Absalom tsɛɔ mɔ lɛ, ni ebiɔ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ maŋ nɔ ojɛ?” Kɛji mɔ lɛ to he, ni etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ Israel akutso mli ni ejɛ lɛ,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom kɛɔ mɔ lɛ akɛ, “Anɔkwa, osane yɛ mli, ni eja hu; shi naa, mɔ ko bɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ he ni aaabo bo toi.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Kɛ mɔ ni Absalom kɛwieɔ lɛ tsi bɛŋkɛ koni ekoto Absalom lɛ, Absalom kpãa enine mli, ni emɔɔ mɔ lɛ mli, ni eshwɔɔ enaa.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Absalom fee egbe Israelbii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛsane baa yeli yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ yitso, ni ekɛkpala Israelbii fɛɛ eshwie esɛɛ akɛ lɛ ji amɛgbɔmɔ kpakpa, ni ehã Israel hii fɛɛ kɛ amɛyitso hã lɛ.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Afii ejwɛ baho; kɛkɛ ni Absalom kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni oŋmɛ mi gbɛ koni maya Hebron mayaye shi ko ni miwo Yehowa lɛ nɔ maba.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be mli ni miyɔɔ Geshur yɛ Siria lɛ, miwo Yehowa shi akɛ kɛji ekɛ mi aaatee Yerusalɛm ekoŋŋ lɛ no lɛ maba Hebron mi diɛŋtsɛ mabaja lɛ, ni mashã afɔle mahã lɛ.”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David to he akɛ, “Yaa, okɛ gbɛnyiɛmɔ jurɔ.” No hewɔ lɛ, ete shi, ni etee Hebron.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Bɔfo ko batswa David adafi ekɛɛ, “Israelbii atsui emɔ Absalom.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hã David kɛɛ etsuji fɛɛ ni ekɛyɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtea shi, nyɛhãa wɔjoa foi, kɛjeee nakai lɛ wɔjeŋ Absalom dɛŋ! Nyɛfea mramra ni wɔtea koni ekabanina wɔ trukaa koni ehã sane fɔŋ baye wɔ, ni ebagbe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ here nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ baakɛɛ.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛ esɛɛ tabilɔi lɛ fã ni amɛshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛyawa yɛ tsu ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ klotia lɛ masɛi,

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: ni etsuji ni ji Keretifoi lɛ kɛ Peletifoi lɛ fɛɛ to kɛbatsɔ̃ emasɛi kɛho. Be ni Gatbii hii ohai ekpaa lɛ ni nyiɛ Maŋtsɛ David sɛɛ kɛjɛ Gat kɛba lɛ hu hoɔ kɛyi ehiɛ lɛ,

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ Itai, Gatbii lɛ ahiɛnyiɛlɔnukpa lɛ, akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni bo hu okɛ wɔ yaa? Kuu osɛɛ moŋ ni okɛ maŋtsɛ hee lɛ ayahi shi, ejaakɛ gbɔ ni ebabɔ mɔfro ji bo.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Kolɛ gbii enyiɛ nɛ ni obadɔmɔ wɔ, hewɔ ni mahã okɛ wɔ aya ni oyatsomlo, be mli hu ni he pɔtɛɛ po ni miyaa lɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ mileee lɛ? Kuu osɛɛ ni okɛ owebii lɛ aya, ni Yehowa aaana bo mɔbɔ; asaŋ eeeye bo anɔkwa hu.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Shi Itai here Maŋtsɛ David nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Mina Yehowa, ni mina minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ nane hu akɛ he fɛɛ he ni oyaa lɛ, gbele mli jio, wala mli jio, mi kɛ bo aaatee.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ Itai akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, ba ni obaho”. Kɛkɛ ni Itai, Gatnyo lɛ kɛ esɛɛ hii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛbii kɛ amɛhɔi fɛɛ ni ekɛnyiɛ lɛ baho.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ wo yara amɛfo be ni David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ fã kɛhoɔ lɛ. Ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ yafo Kidron Faa lɛ, ni amɛwo amɛyi amɛma ŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Abiatar ba; ni Osɔfo Zadok hu shɛ shi ni Levibii lɛ fɛɛ fata he ni amɛtere Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ; ni ato Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ ama shi kɛyashi maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ je maŋ lɛ mli ho amɛgbe naa.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ Zadok akɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ okɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ aya maŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji Yehowa miisumɔ lɛ no lɛ wɔsɛɛ ko kɛ̃, eeehã maku misɛɛ koni maba mabana Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛ etoohe lɛ mli fɛɛ ekoŋŋ;

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: shi kɛji jeee esuɔmɔ naa ji nakai lɛ miyɛ edɛŋ, bɔ ni eeeto mi kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: David tee nɔ ni ekɛɛ Osɔfo Zadok akɛ, “Ole nɔ ko? Ŋɔɔ obi Ahimaaz kɛ Abiatar bi Yonatan, ofata ohe kɛku sɛɛ kɛya maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Mibamɛ yɛ faafoohe lɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni minine aaashɛ nyɛdɛŋ adafitswaa ko nɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Zadok kɛ Abiatar wo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛku sɛɛ kɛtee Yerusalɛm, ni amɛyahi jɛi.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kwɔ Mu Gɔŋ lɛ ni yaafonu jwere ehiɛ, ni eha eyiteŋ, ni asaŋ enyiɛ enane folo. Ni esɛɛbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ lɛ nyiɛ lɛ hu eha eyiteŋ; ni be ni amɛyaa lɛ amɛmiifo.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ni mɔ ko bagba Maŋtsɛ David akɛ Ahitofel hu shi maŋjwalɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛkɛ ni David sɔle ekpa Yehowa fai, ni ekɛɛ, “Oo, Yehowa, miikpa bo fai, hã ŋaa fɛɛ ŋaa ni Ahitofel baawo lɛ atsɔ̃ kwashiai aŋaa.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Be ni David shɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ he ni ajaa Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ lɛ, ekɛ Hushai, enaanyo Arkinyo lɛ, kpe kɛ ehe atade ni egbala, asaŋ kɛ eyiteŋ fɛɛ mlu.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Hushai akɛ, “Minaŋ ohe sɛɛ ko kɛji okɛ mi tee;

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: shi kɛji moŋ oku osɛɛ otee maŋ lɛ mli, ni oyakɛɛ Absalom akɛ, ‘Maŋtsɛ, otsulɔ ji mi; nyɛsɛɛ ko lɛ otsɛ tsulɔ ji mi;’ shi agbɛnɛ lɛ mitsɔ̃ otsulɔ lɛ, jɛi baatsɔ̃ ni ooonyɛ ofite ŋaa ni Ahitofel aaawo Absalom lɛ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Zadok kɛ Osɔfo Abiatar fɛɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli. Sane fɛɛ sane ni ooonu kɛaajɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ, obɔ amɛ.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Naa, amɛbihii enyɔ, ni ji Zadok bi Ahimaaz kɛ Abiatar bi Yonatan, yɛ jɛi. Okɛ sane fɛɛ sane ni ooonu lɛ atsu amɛ koni amɛkɛbahã mi.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David naanyo Hushai ku esɛɛ, ni etee maŋ lɛ mli; ni ekɛ Absalom Yerusalɛm shɛɛ yafee pɛ.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: David efo mli yɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ fioo kɛmiiya kɛkɛ ni Ziba, Mefiboshet tsulɔ lɛ, kɛ lɛ bakpe trukaa ni ehiɛ tejii enyɔ ni tere aboloo akwaabɔi ohai enyɔ kɛ wainyibii ni aka ni egbi shabii oha, kɛ agbãmi ŋmɔŋ shabii oha, kɛ wain wolotɔ kome.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David bi Ziba akɛ, “Mɛni okɛ enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ yaafee?” Ziba jie naa ni ekɛɛ, “Tejii lɛ, koni akɛhã maŋtsɛ weku lɛ ni amɛtara nɔ; ni aboloo lɛ kɛ tsei ayibii lɛ, akɛyahã oblahii lɛ ni amɛye, ni wain lɛ, kɛji etɔ amɛteŋ mɔ ko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, koni ahã mɔ lɛ eko ni enu.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David bi Ziba akɛ, “Ni nɛgbɛ onuŋtsɔ bi Mefiboshet yɔɔ?” Ziba here maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ, “Eyɛ Yerusalɛm ejaakɛ esusumɔ ji akɛ Israelbii baakpale enii, Saul, maŋtsɛyeli lɛ ahã lɛ agbɛnɛ.”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: David kɛɛ Ziba akɛ, “Naa, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ji Mefiboshet nii lɛ, fɛɛ etsɔ̃ onɔ.” Kɛkɛ ni Ziba here nɔ akɛ, “Miyɛ odɛ̃ŋ Maŋtsɛ; omɔbɔnalɛ gbɛ kɛkɛ mikwɛɔ.”

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ David shɛ Bahurim akrowa lɛ, Saul wekunyo ko ni egbɛi ji Shimei ni atsɛɔ etsɛ akɛ Gera lɛ je kpo ekɛ David bakpe, ni be ni ebaa fɛɛ lɛ, belɛ eelomɔ Maŋtsɛ David.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Etswia David kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ tɛi, tsɛbelɛ tabilɔi hii kakabãi ebɔle David he yɛ eninejurɔ kɛ ebɛku fɛɛ.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Shimei lomɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Jee jɛi ni oya! Gbɔmɔgbelɔ! Yakagbɔmɔ!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Yehowa miiwo bo Saul wekumɛi alá shi ni oshwie lɛ fɛɛ he nyɔmɔ. Obashɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ Saul dɛŋ, ni Yehowa hu eshɔ̃ ekɛhã obinuu Absalom. Bɛ ona akɛ gbɔmɔgbelɔ ni oji hewɔ lɛ ohiɛ ekpãtã?”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abishai, ni atsɛɔ enyɛ Zeruia lɛ, kɛɛ David akɛ, “Nii, mɛɛ hewɔ oŋmɛ gbee nɛɛ gbɛ, ni elomɔ bo? Ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni maya mayafo eyitso.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Shi David kɛɛ Abishai kɛ enyɛbi Yoab akɛ, “Nyɛhe sane ko mɛ? Kɛji eelomɔ mi, ejaakɛ Yehowa ni tsu lɛ koni ebafee nakai lɛ, namɔ yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ebiɔ he sane ko?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ Abishai kɛ lɛ David etsuji krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji mi diɛŋtsɛ mimusuŋbi miitao mi egbe lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ nɔ ni Benyaminnyo nɛɛ feɔ lɛ afee nyɛ naakpɛɛ? Nyɛŋmɛa ehe ni elomɔa, ejaakɛ Yehowa ni tsu lɛ koni ebafee.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Eko lɛ Yehowa aaana mi mɔbɔ yɛ mimanehulu nɛɛ hewɔ, ni ekɛ nɔ kpakpa moŋ aaato mi loomɔ ni elomɔɔ mi ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ najiaŋ.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ tsa amɛnyiɛmɔ lɛ nɔ. Be ni amɛyaa lɛ belɛ Shimei hu nyiɛ David ŋlɛnɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eelomɔ lɛ, asaŋ eetswia lɛ tɛi, ni eegbɛ mlu eewo ehe hu.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Etɔ Maŋtsɛ David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ bliboo be ni amɛyashɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa lɛ. Amɛwa, ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ jɛi. Absalom yɛ Yerusalɛm

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ Israel hii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ bashɛ Yerusalɛm. Ahitofel fata amɛhe.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Be ni David naanyo Hushai, Arkinyo lɛ, kɛ Absalom kpe lɛ Hushai ŋa lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nii, hã manye.”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Shi Absalom bi Hushai akɛ, “Aso bɔ ni akɛ naanyo nyiɛɔ nɛ? Mɛɛba ni okɛ onaanyo lɛ eyaaa lɛ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Hushai jie naa ekɛɛ, “Mɛɛ nakai hu ni? Mɔ ni Yehowa kɛ maŋbii nɛɛ kɛ Israelbii fɛɛ ehala lɛ, lɛ egbɛfaŋ miyɔɔ, ni lɛ mikɛyaa.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, namɔ po esa akɛ misɔmɔɔ yɛ minuŋtsɔ bi sɛɛ? Bɔ ni misɔmɔ otsɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ masɔmɔ bo hu.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Absalom kɛɛ Ahitofel akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ, wo mi ŋaa. Mɛni feemɔ wɔyɔɔ?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ahitofel kɛɛ Absalom akɛ, “Yaa ni okɛ otsɛ hemɛi lɛ ni eshi yɛ sɛɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ shĩa lɛ ayawɔ, koni okɛhã Israel muu fɛɛ ana ale akɛ okɛ otsɛ teŋ etse. No baahã hii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ osɛɛ lɛ ahe awa amɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ashi buu yɛ tsu lɛ yiteŋ ahã Absalom, ni ekɛ etsɛ hemɛi lɛ wɔ yɛ jɛi yɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ ŋaa fɛɛ ŋaa ni Ahitofel aaawo lɛ, aŋɔɔ lɛ tamɔ nii ni atee ayabi Nyɔŋmɔ. No hewɔ ni David kɛ Absalom fɛɛ buɔ eŋaawoo lɛ.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Ni wɔbaatiu David kɛya he fɛɛ he ni eyɔɔ, ni be ni eeehɛle shi lɛ wɔɔɔshwie enɔ tamɔ bɔ nyɔɔ lɛ, ni lɛ kɛ mɛi ni fata ehe lɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ kome nɛkɛ eshwɛŋ.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Maya mayatua lɛ be ni etɔ lɛ, ni enijiaŋ eje wui lɛ. Etsui baafã, ni maŋbii fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ aaajo foi ashi lɛ; magbe lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛkɛ,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: ni mikɛ maŋbii ni nyiɛ esɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ aaaku sɛɛ abahã bo tamɔ ayɛmforo ni akɛ lɛ miiya ayahã ewu. Gbɔmɔ kome kɛkɛ gbele otaoɔ, ni maŋbii fɛɛ atoiŋ aaajɔ amɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Ŋaawoo nɛɛ sa Absalom kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Shi Absalom kɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛtsɛa Hushai, Arkinyo lɛ, hu kɛbaa koni wɔbo nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ hu enaa toi.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Be ni Hushai ba Absalom ŋɔɔ lɛ, Absalom kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ŋaa ni Ahitofel ewo nɛ, ani wɔye nɔ lo? Kɛjeee nakai lɛ, bo hu te okɛɔ tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Hushai hã Absalom hetoo ni ekɛɛ, “Ŋaa ni Ahitofel wo ŋmɛnɛ lɛ ehiii.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ole akɛ otsɛ kɛ ewebii lɛ tabilɔi hii kakabãi ji amɛ, ni amrɔ nɛɛ amɛhiɛ edɔ tamɔ oshishibrishi yoofɔyoo ni ayaju ebii yɛ ehe yɛ jwɛiaŋ. Ole hu akɛ otsɛ lɛ tatsɛ kpanaa ni, ni ekɛ maŋbii lɛ ehiŋ he kome nyɔɔŋ nɛɛŋ.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Naa, amrɔ nɛɛ eeeyatee ehe yɛ tɛkplo ko mli loo he ko. Kɛji anu akɛ David etua owebii lɛ, nɔ nɔŋŋ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaanu sane lɛ baakɛɛ kɛkɛ ji akɛ, ‘Agbe Absalom webii lɛ bluublu.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Kɛ eba lɛ nakai lɛ mɔ po ni eji kãkãlɔ, ni etsui wa tamɔ jata tsui lɛ, etsui baafã, ni ehe baajɔ, ejaakɛ Israel fɛɛ le akɛ otsɛ lɛ nuu kakabãa ji lɛ, ni hii ni fata ehe lɛ hu kãkãlɔi ni.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ŋaa ni miwoɔ ji akɛ obua Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa, kɛjɛ Dan aahu kɛyashwie Beersheba, amɛyi baafa tamɔ ŋshɔnaa shia. Bo diɛŋtsɛ hu oya ta lɛ eko.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Kɛji eeeba lɛ akɛ eeegbala ehe shi kɛaayabote maŋ ko mli lɛ, wɔwebii lɛ fɛɛ baaya ayakɔlɔ taŋkpei, ni wɔkɛbaashãtã maŋ lɛ wɔyawo jɔɔ mli kɛyashi beyinɔ ni anaŋ fɔbitɛ kome nɛkɛ yɛ nakai maŋ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Hushai, Arkinyo lɛ ŋaawoo lɛ hi fe Ahitofel nɔ lɛ.” Ejaakɛ Yehowa eto akɛ akaye Ahitofel ŋaawoo kpakpa lɛ nɔ bɔ ni afee ni Yehowa ahã nɔ fɔŋ aba Absalom nɔ. Atswa David adafi, ni ejo foi

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hushai tee, ni eyabɔ Osɔfo Zadok kɛ Osɔfo Abiatar nɔ ŋaa ni Ahitofel wo Absalom kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ, kɛ nɔ ŋaa ni lɛ, Hushai lɛ, hu ewo lɛ; ni ekɛshi sɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛtsua koni aya mramra ni ayakɛɛ David akɛ ekawɔ faafoohei lɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛŋ kɔkɔɔkɔ, shi moŋ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ efo faa lɛ kɛya sɛɛ koni nine akabashɛ lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ anɔ ni agbe amɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Osɔfo Abiatar bi Yonatan kɛ Osɔfo Zadok bi Ahimaaz etee amɛhe yɛ Rogel nubu lɛ he, yɛ Yerusalɛm klotia, ni kɛfee lɛ atsuɔ oblayoo ko kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli, ni ekɛ wiemɔ yahãa amɛ, ni amɛkɛyahãa Maŋtsɛ David. Bɔ ni afee ni akana amɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yonatan kɛ Ahimaaz eyaaa maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ oblanyo ko na amɛ gbi ko, ni etee eyakɛɛ Absalom. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛsha amɛhe oyaoya kɛyabote nuu ko shĩa yɛ Bahurim. Nuu lɛ yɛ nubu ko yɛ ekpo lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyabote mli.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ ŋa kɔ mama, ni ekɛha bu lɛ naa, kɛkɛ ni egbɛ ŋmaa mli eka mama lɛ nɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, akɔɔɔ sɛɛ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be ni Absalom tsuji lɛ bashɛ yoo lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ, amɛbi lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ Yonatan kɛ Ahimaaz yɔɔ.” Yoo lɛ jie naa ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Amɛfo faa nine lɛ kɛtee.” Hii lɛ tiu amɛ, ni amɛyatao amɛ, shi be ni amɛnaaa amɛ lɛ, amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛbaho Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Be ni Absalom tsuji lɛ ebaho amɛtee sɛɛ lɛ, Yonatan kɛ Ahimaaz je kpo yɛ nubu lɛ mli, ni amɛyi mli amɛtee Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ amɛyabɔ lɛ amaniɛ akɛ, “Ŋaa ni Ahitofel ewo yɛ ohe nɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ohe afee oya ni ofo faa lɛ.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛ mɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ te shi, ni amɛyafo Yordan Faa lɛ; ni be ni je kɛɛ etsɛreɔ lɛ eshwɛko amɛteŋ mɔ kome nɛkɛ ni efoko Yordan.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Be ni Ahitofel na akɛ ayeee ŋaa ni ewo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ewo eteji nɔ nii, kɛkɛ ni eshi kɛtee emaŋ; ni be ni eto enibii fɛɛ gbɛjianɔ lɛ, eyawo esɛ̃ kpãa, ni egbe ehe. Afu lɛ yɛ etsɛ gbonyo fuuhe lɛ mli.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: David eshɛ Mahanaim momo dani Absalom kɛ Israelbii fɛɛ fo Yordan lɛ.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Absalom efee Amasa etatsɛ yɛ Yoab najiaŋ. Amasa nɛɛ Ishmaelnyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yeter lɛ kɛ Yoabnyo Zeruia nyɛmi yoo Nahash biyoo Abigail fɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ ewebii lɛ yato shi yɛ Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Be ni David yashɛ Mahanaim lɛ, gbɔmɛi nɛɛ: Shobi, ni ji Nahash ni jɛ Amonbii amaŋ Raba lɛ mli lɛ bi lɛ, kɛ Makir, ni ji Amiel ni jɛ Lo-Debar lɛ bi lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ Barzilai, Gileadnyo lɛ ni jɛ Rogelim lɛ ba eŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: kɛ wo kɛ butru kɛ too kɛ tsina keesui, ni amɛkɛbahã David kɛ ewebii ni fata ehe lɛ koni amɛye, ejaakɛ amɛle akɛ etɔ amɛ, ni hɔmɔ kɛ kumai hu fɛɛ eye amɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, eja eta tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli etɛ̃. Ekɛ mlijaa etɛ̃ nɛɛ mli ekome wo Yoab shishi, ni ekɛ ekome hu wo Abishai, Zeruia bi Yoab nyɛmi lɛ shishi, ni ekɛ ekome ni eshwɛ lɛ wo Itai, Gatnyo lɛ shishi. Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ etabilɔi lɛ akɛ, “Mi diɛŋtsɛ hu mikɛ nyɛ miiya.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Shi tabilɔi lɛ here David nɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Dabida! Okɛ wɔ akaya ta lɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛji wɔjo foi yɛ henyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ amɛgbaŋ amɛhe naa yɛ wɔhe; ni kɛji agbe wɔyibɔ nɛɛ fã tete lɛ, amɛtsɛŋ lɛ nɔ ko. Shi bo lɛ ojara wa tamɔ wɔyi akpei nyɔŋma. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi moŋ akɛ ohi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni ojɛ biɛ oye obua wɔ.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: David webii lɛ eko na Absalom, ni etee eyakɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Miyana Absalom tsotsoro shi yɛ blɔfo yɔɔyi tso ko nɔ.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Ta lɛ gbɛ shwã jɛi kpokpai lɛ anɔ fɛɛ, ni koo lɛ kpãtã gbɔmɛi ahiɛ kwraa fe klante tete.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ David tabilɔi lɛ ekomɛi yakpe trukaa. Absalom ta tejiokpɔŋɔ nɔ; ni etee eyatsɔ̃ blɔfo yɔɔyi tso wulu ko shishi, kɛkɛ ni eyitso yaka tso lɛ niji ni ebu kusuu lɛ amli, kɛkɛ ni tejiokpɔŋɔ lɛ sha kɛje Absalom shishi etee, ni eshi Absalom ni etsotsoro ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ teŋ.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Yoab kɛɛ mɔ ni bagba lɛ sane lɛ akɛ, “Ona lɛ lɛɛlɛŋ? Ni mɛɛba ogbeee lɛ yɛ jɛi nɔŋŋ. Kulɛ make bo jwiɛtɛi kukuji nyɔŋma kɛ mlifiinɔ ko hu.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Kɛji migbo maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ toi, ni migbe Absalom lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ baana ele kɛ̃, ejaakɛ sane ko kwraa bɛ ni enaaa ele; ni ofaŋ mihe.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Yoab to he akɛ, “Miifite be po!” Kɛkɛ ni Yoab kɔlɔ akplɔi etɛ̃, ni etee ekɛyatsulɔ Absalom tsuiŋ be mli ni ehiɛ kã lolo yɛ yɔɔyi tso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Oblahii nyɔŋma ni hiɛɔ Yoab tawuu nibii lɛ babɔle Absalom kɛkpe, ni amɛtswia lɛ nii, ni amɛgbe lɛ.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab hã akpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ, ni akpa ta lɛ wuu, ni no hewɔ lɛ, etabilɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ Israelbii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ajie Absalom gbonyo lɛ, ni ashɛ afɔ̃ bu agbo ko mli yɛ koo lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni amɛto tɛ amɛshwie enɔ aahu ni etsɔ̃ ku kpeteŋkple. Israelbii lɛ jo foi, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee ewe.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Be ni Absalom yɔɔ wala mli lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ema shiu ko yɛ Maŋtsɛ Jɔɔ lɛ mli akɛ akɛkai lɛ, ejaakɛ ekɛɛ ebɛ binuu ni baafɔ ewo lɛ koni egbɛi akagbo. Absalom kɛ egbɛi wo shiu nɛɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ atsɛɔ shiu lɛ akɛ Absalom Kaimɔ shiu. Abakɛɛ David Absalom gbele

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahimaaz, Zadok bi lɛ, kɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Hã ni masha foi maya mayabɔ maŋtsɛ amaniɛ akɛ Yehowa ehere eyiwala yɛ ehenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Yoab here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Dabida, jeee bo obaaya ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ oyabɔ amaniɛ. Gbi kroko jiŋŋ, oooya oyabɔ amaniɛ; ŋmɛnɛ lɛ oyabɔŋ amaniɛ ejaakɛ maŋtsɛbi ni enyɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab kɛɛ enyɔŋ, Kushnyo lɛ, akɛ, “Yaa ni oyagba maŋtsɛ nɔ ni ona.” Kushnyo lɛ koto Yoab kɛkɛ ni ewo foi kɛtee.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Shi Ahimaaz, Zadok bi lɛ, fi nɔ, ni ekɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Hã ni mi hu maya ni mayabɔ amaniɛ; nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aaaba lɛ eba!” Yoab here Ahimaaz nɔ akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ osumɔɔ doo akɛ bo hu obaaya oyabɔ amaniɛ lɛ? Naa, aekoo ko bɛ ni abaahã bo yɛ he!”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ahimaaz to he akɛ, “Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ, eba! Miisumɔ akɛ mi hu maya.” Yoab to he akɛ, “Yaa mɔ!” No hewɔ lɛ, Ahimaaz wo foi kɛyi Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli gbɛ lɛ nɔ; ni eyaho Kushnyo lɛ he.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ David ta shi yɛ maŋ agboi enyɔ lɛ ateŋ koi lɛ shi; ni mɔ ni buɔ lɛ kwɔ kɛtee maŋ gbogbo lɛ nɔ yɛ maŋ agbo lɛ yiteŋ. Eyaawo ehiɛ nɔ lɛ, naa nuu ko hiɛ foi ekome too kɛmiiba.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Bulɔ lɛ bo etsɛ, ni ekɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David. Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ bulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji ekome too ni lɛ, belɛ no lɛ atsu lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ sane.” Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ hiɛ baa aahu kɛyashi ebɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
