translation_verse: Shi bulɔ lɛ na nuu kroko ko hu ni hiɛ foi kɛmiiba. Kɛkɛ ni ebo etsɛ agbonaa bulɔ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, nuu kroko ko hu hiɛ foi ekome too kɛmiiba.” Maŋtsɛ David here nɔ akɛ, “Lɛ hu ehiɛ miishɛɛ sane kɛmiiba.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Bulɔ lɛ tee nɔ ekɛɛ, “Mɔ ni nyiɛ hiɛ lɛ foijee tamɔ Osɔfo Zadok bi Ahimaaz foijee pɛpɛɛpɛ.” Maŋtsɛ David to he, ni ekɛɛ, “Gbɔmɔ kpakpa ni; ni ehiɛ sane kpakpa kɛmiiba.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ahimaaz bo ni ekɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Wɔye omanye eei!” Kɛkɛ ni eho egbee shi, ni ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ekoto maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ada Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shi akɛ ehã oye mɛi ni te shi amɛwo bo, maŋtsɛ, lɛ anɔ kunim.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David bi akɛ, “Ani oblanyo Absalom lɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lo?” Ahimaaz jie naa akɛ, “Ofainɛ, be ni Yoab tsu mi otsulɔ lɛ, mi lɛ mina ni aafee gidigidi ko; shi moŋ minaaa male nɔ ni eba.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, bo lɛ tsi ohe oyadamɔ afã dã.” No hewɔ lɛ, etsi ehe ni eyadamɔ afã.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Ni naa, Kushnyo lɛ ni atsu lɛ hu ba. Ekɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, mihiɛ miishɛɛ sane kɛba; ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ Yehowa ehã oye mɛi ni te shi amɛwo bo lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David bi Kushnyo lɛ akɛ, “Ani oblanyo Absalom lɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lo?” Kushnyo lɛ here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Mina ni nɔ ni eba enɔ lɛ kulɛ nakai nɔ ko aba ohenyɛlɔi kɛ mɛi ni te shi amɛwo bo lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Amaniɛ lɛ hã Maŋtsɛ David jijaa. Kɛkɛ ni ekwɔ kɛtee pia ni yɔɔ maŋ agbo lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli, ni eyafo. Be ni eyaa lɛ, efo ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ao! Mibi oo! Mibi Absalom! Mibi Absalom eei! Mina ni kulɛ, mibi, mi moŋ migbo yɛ onajiaŋ nɛɛ. Absalom mibi oo, mibi.”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ayagba Yoab akɛ Maŋtsɛ David ewo yara eefo yɛ Absalom hewɔ.

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kunimyeli nyamɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ ŋkɔmɔyeli moŋ ehã maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nakai gbi lɛ, ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ nu akɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ miiye ŋkɔmɔ yɛ ebinuu lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã maŋbii lɛ ju shi kɛtee maŋ lɛ mli liɔɔliɔɔ tamɔ tabilɔi ni aye amɛnɔ ni amɛjo foi yɛ ta naa kɛba shĩa.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David ha ehiɛ, kɛkɛ ni ebo waa, “Ao! Mibi Absalom eei! Ao! Mibi, mibi Absalom!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Yoab ba Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli, ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nii, owo otabilɔi fɛɛ ni here bo kɛ obihii lɛ kɛ obiyei lɛ kɛ oŋamɛi lɛ kɛ ohemɛi lɛ ayiwala lɛ hiɛgbele pam ŋmɛnɛ;

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ otsɔ̃ɔ akɛ osumɔɔ ohenyɛlɔi lɛ moŋ, ni onyɛɔ osuɔlɔi lɛ, ejaakɛ otsɔ̃ɔ faŋŋ ŋmɛnɛ akɛ tatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ tabilɔi lɛ awala jeee fɛifɛi yɛ ohiɛ. Bɔ ni minaa sane lɛ ji akɛ Absalom yɛ wala mli, ni wɔ fɛɛ wɔgboi ŋmɛnɛ kulɛ eŋɔɔ onaa!

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Wo ohe nɔ, agbɛnɛ, ni oje kpo, ni oyashɛje otabilɔi lɛ amii. Ejaakɛ kɛjeee nakai lɛ, mina Yehowa akɛ, wɔ be ni je aaatsɛre lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ eshi bo. Ni kɛ eba lɛ nakai lɛ, amanehulu ni ekɛbaaba onɔ lɛ, onako ehenɔ pɛŋ kɛjɛ oblahiiaŋ kɛbashi amrɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David wo ehe nɔ, ni etee eyata maŋ agboi lɛ ateŋ koi lɛ shi. Be ni etabilɔi lɛ nu akɛ ebata koi lɛ shi lɛ, amɛtee amɛyabua ehe. David ku esɛɛ kɛtee Yerusalɛm Be nɛɛ mli lɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ ejojoo foi kɛtee amɛshĩai,

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Be ni David na enu nɔ ni Israelbii lɛ wieɔ lɛ, etsu ayakɛɛ Osɔfoi Zadok kɛ Abiatar akɛ amɛyakɛɛ Yuda maŋ onukpai lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni nyɛ moŋ nyɛkpe sɛɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kplamɔ mli kɛ ewe lɛ mli baa nɛɛ? Israelbii fɛɛ adaaŋ gbee ebashɛ midɛŋ.

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Mɛɛba ni nyɛ ni ji minyɛmimɛi ni mi kɛ nyɛ laŋmɔ kpãa kome lɛ, nyɛ moŋ nyɛkpe sɛɛ yɛ mikpalamɔ kɛbaa mli nɛɛ?”

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Asaŋ David shɛ amɛ koni amɛyakɛɛ Amasa akɛ, “Miwekunyo ji bo, kɛji mitooo bo mitatsɛ yɛ Yoab najiaŋ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ awo mi nyɔmɔ.”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David wiemɔ hã Yudabii fɛɛ atsui mɔ lɛ; hewɔ lɛ amɛtsu ayakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ lɛ kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba.

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Benyaminnyo, Gera, ni jɛ Bahurim lɛ binuu Shimei, ye ehe oyai, ni ekɛ Yuda hii lɛ kpeleke shi kɛba Yordan naa koni ekɛ Maŋtsɛ David abakpe.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ, ofainɛ, mile faŋŋ akɛ mifee esha; ni no hewɔ ni naa, mi ji mɔ tsuutsu ni jɛ kooyi akutsei lɛ amli miba bo kpeemɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfo faa lɛ kɛtee faa lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛ jie maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ fɛɛ faa, koni amɛkɛsa Maŋtsɛ David hiɛ. David kɛ Shimei he ke lɛ Maŋtsɛ David efee kralo kɛbaabote faafoo lɛlɛ lɛ mli pɛ, kɛkɛ ni Shimei, Gera binuu lɛ, ho ekula enaji anaa,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: ni ekpa lɛ fai ekɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, ofainɛ, ni ohiɛ akpa efɔŋ ni mifee bo gbi ni oshiɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ nɔ. Kɛ onane ashushua nɔ kwraa koni okakai dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Shi Zeruia bi Abishai here Shimei wiemɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Loomɔ ni Shimei lomɔ mɔ ni Yehowa eto lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, esa gbele.”

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Shi David to he ni ekɛɛ Zeruia bi Abishai kɛ enyɛmi Yoab akɛ, “Nyɛhe sane ko mɛ? Nyɛkawoa minajiaŋ. Ani ŋmɛnɛ ni mitsɔ̃ Israel fɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, ani abaagbe Israelnyo lo?”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni David kɛɛ Shimei akɛ, “Agbeŋ bo!” Ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kã Shimei kitã. David na Mefiboshet mɔbɔ

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: Be ni Mefiboshet bashɛ shi kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm koni ebakpee maŋtsɛ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ David bi lɛ akɛ, “Mefiboshet, mɛɛba ni ofataaa mihe kɛyaaa lɛ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Mefiboshet jie naa akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, ole akɛ akpaketsɛ ji mi. Mikɛɛ mitsulɔ lɛ akɛ ewo teji nɔ nii ehã mi koni mata nɔ ni mikɛ bo aya, shi elaka mi kɛ̃,

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: ni ebafo minaa moŋ efite mi ehã maŋtsɛ. Shi maŋtsɛ tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfo, no hewɔ lɛ, miyɛ odɛ̃ŋ, bɔ ni ooofee mi.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Kulɛ esa akɛ ogbeɔ mitsɛ we lɛ mli bii fɛɛ, shi ohã mibafata mɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ okplɔ̃ he lɛ ahe. Mɛɛ ejurɔ mitaoɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ dɛŋ dɔŋŋ?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ David to he akɛ, “Kaawie dɔŋŋ! Nɔ ni mikɛɛ ji akɛ Ziba kɛ bo baaja Saul gboshinii lɛ.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Mefiboshet here nɔ akɛ, “Ebaanyɛ fɛɛ tete eŋɔ. Akɛ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ ebashɛ ewe lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ, no kɛkɛ fa hã mi.” David na Barzilai mɔbɔ

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Barzilai, Gileadnyo lɛ, jɛ Rogelim eba koni ebakwɛ Maŋtsɛ David yisɛɛ. Ejie Maŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛyashɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa koni ewa lɛ ni efo faa lɛ.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Hã wɔtee Yerusalɛm koni mayakwɛ bo yɛ miwe lɛ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Shi Barzilai to he ehã Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, gbii enyiɛ po eshwɛ mi, hewɔ ni mikɛ bo aaatee Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Miyiŋtoo kɛkɛ ji akɛ miiba mibakwɛ minuŋtsɔ yisɛɛ koni efo Yordan lɛ koni mi kɛ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛkɛ. Mɛɛba ni maŋtsɛ aaato mi najiaŋ?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Ofainɛ, hã maku misɛɛ maya koni miyagbo yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mimaŋ, ni afu mi yɛ mitsɛ kɛ minyɛ mlishi. Naa, mibinuu Kimham moŋ. Maŋtsɛ aŋɔ lɛ kɛya ni eyasɔmɔ Maŋtsɛ koni Nii afee lɛ ejurɔ bɔ ni Nii sumɔɔ.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Mi kɛ Kimham baaya, ni mafee lɛ ejurɔ ni baasa ohiɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ooobi mi lɛ mafee mahã bo.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ David shwɔ Barzilai naa, ni ejɔɔ lɛ. Maŋtsɛ David kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ fɛɛ fo Yordan Faa lɛ, kɛkɛ ni Barzilai hu ku esɛɛ kɛtee emaŋ. Yudabii kɛ Israelbii taa naa

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ David kɛ Yuda maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Israelbii fã ni yakpa lɛ gbɛ lɛ yiŋ kɛtee Gilgal. Kimham fata ehe kɛtee.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ tee Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, mɛɛba wɔnyɛmimɛi Yudabii lɛ kɛkɛ ni ba amɛbakpee bo, ni amɛ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ amɛfo maŋtsɛ kɛ ebii kɛ hɔi kɛ esɛɛbii lɛ fɛɛ faa lɛ?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Yudahii lɛ here Israelbii lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ wɔ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ jɛ weku kome. Mɛɛba ni enɛ feɔ nyɛ mlifu? Mɛni nyɛle ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ehã wɔ wɔye, aloo ni eke wɔ?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ to he amɛhã Yudabii lɛ akɛ, “Gbɛnaa nii ni nyɛyɔɔ yɛ Maŋtsɛ David gbɛfaŋ lɛ, wɔyɛ nakai toi nyɔŋma yɛ egbɛfaŋ. Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni nyɛbuuu wɔ. Kwɛ jeee wɔ tsuutsu moŋ wɔwo ŋaa akɛ ayaŋɔ wɔmaŋtsɛ lɛ kɛba lɛ?” Shi Yudabii lɛ anaa yawa fe Israelbii lɛ yɛ sane nɛɛ mli.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Nuu yakagbɔmɔ ko baje Gilgal. Atsɛɔ lɛ Sheba, ni etsɛ gbɛi ji Bikri, Benyaminnyo lɛ. Sheba kpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ ni ebo ekɛɛ akɛ, “Israel eei! Wɔbɛ gbɛnaa ko yɛ David gbɛfaŋ. Wɔ kɛ Ishai bi lɛ ejaaa nɔ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya ewe.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israelhii lɛ kpa yɛ David sɛɛ, ni amɛyanyiɛ Bikri bi Sheba sɛɛ. Shi Yudahii lɛ kpɛtɛ amɛmaŋtsɛ lɛ kɛjɛ Yordan naa aahu kɛyashɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ David bashɛ ewe lɛ mli yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, ehã akɛ yei nyɔŋma ni ji ehemɛi lɛ ni eshi, akɛ amɛkwɛ shĩa lɛ, yato he ko banee, ni atsi amɛna awo shĩa ko mli. Elɛ amɛ, shi eyaaa amɛmasɛi, ni ehã amɛhi shi tamɔ okulafoi kɛyashi amɛgbele be.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Amasa akɛ, “Yaa ni oyakpee Yudahii fɛɛ obahã mi yɛ biɛ gbii etɛ̃ mli; ni bo diɛŋtsɛ hu oba biɛ eko.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amasa yiŋ etee koni eyakpee Yudahii lɛ ebahã maŋtsɛ lɛ; shi eyatsɛ fe be ni ato lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Abishai akɛ, “Etamɔ nɔ ni Bikri bi Sheba baagba wɔnaa fe Absalom tete. Ŋɔɔ mitabilɔi lɛ, ni nyɛtiua lɛ koni ekayana maji ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe lɛ amli eyabote ni etsɔ̃ jɛi eje wɔdɛŋ.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Abishai kɛ Yoab kɛ tabilɔi lɛ ni ji Keretifoi lɛ kɛ Peletifoi lɛ ni buɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ he lɛ, kɛ hii kakabãi lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm koni amɛyatiu Sheba, Bikri bi lɛ.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛyaa ni amɛyashɛ tɛkplo ni yɔɔ Gibeon lɛ he lɛ, Amasa kɛ amɛ bakpe. No mli lɛ Yoab emia kɛ tawuu atade. Afi atade ni ewo lɛ mli, ni klante fi nɔ yɛ ehɛ. Klante lɛ je ehebo lɛ mli egbee shi, be ni Yoab tsiɔ ebɛŋkɛɔ Amasa lɛ.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Yoab ŋa Amasa akɛ, “Te oyɔɔ tɛŋŋ, anyɛmi nuu?” Kɛkɛ ni Yoab kɛ eninejurɔ mɔ Amasa tsɛŋ mli koni eshwɔ enaa.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Amasa enaaa akɛ Yoab hiɛ klante yɛ edɛŋ; ni no hewɔ lɛ, Yoab kɛ klante lɛ du Amasa musuŋ ni Amasa musuŋnii tue shwie shi. Eduuu lɛ nɔ ni ji shii enyɔ, ni egbo. Kɛkɛ ni Yoab kɛ enyɛmi Abishai tsa amɛnyiɛmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtiu Sheba, Bikri bi lɛ.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Oblahii tabilɔi ni yɔɔ Yoab shishi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ko ho yadamɔ Amasa gbonyo lɛ masɛi, ni ebo ekɛɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ Yoab kɛ David sɛɛ lɛ, eyi Yoab sɛɛ.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Belɛ Amasa gbonyo lɛ kã shi ni lá ewu ehe kpɔtɔɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋ tuuŋtu. Ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni hoɔ ni ehiɛ gbaa enɔ lɛ, ewaa edamɔɔ shi. Be ni oblanyo lɛ na akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni bashɛɔ gbonyo lɛ he yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ waa damɔɔ shi lɛ, ewo Amasa kɛjɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ lɛ yaŋmɛ ŋa lɛ mli, ni ekɛ mama ha enɔ.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Be ni ajie gbonyo lɛ kɛje gbejegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛi lɛ fɛɛ loo mli kɛnyiɛ Yoab sɛɛ kɛtiu Sheba, Bikri bi lɛ.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Sheba tsɔ̃ Israel akutsei lɛ ashikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kɛho, ni be ni eyashɛ Abel Bet-Maaka lɛ, Bikribii lɛ bua amɛhe naa, ni amɛnyiɛ esɛɛ kɛbabote maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yoab shishi tabilɔi lɛ basa Sheba yi amɛwo Abel Bet-Maaka maŋ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ su tswa kpoku ni ekwɔlɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ kwɔlɛ ye hegbɔ. Asaŋ amɛshimɔshimɔɔ gbogbo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu koni amɛwule lɛ amɛshwie shi.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Shi yoo nilelɔ ko bo kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛboa toi! Nyɛboa toi! Nyɛtsɛa Yoab nyɛhãa mi koni mi kɛ lɛ awiea.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Yoab tsi bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yoo lɛ bi lɛ akɛ, “Bo ji Yoab lɛ?” Yoab here nɔ akɛ, “Mi ni.” Yoo lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni obo mi toi.” Yoab kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Miibo bo toi.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni yoo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Sa lɛ kɛji anaaa sane ko naa lɛ bɔ ni akɛɔ ji akɛ, ‘Aya Abel ni ayabi?’

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Israel maji ni sumɔɔ hejɔlɛ kɛ anɔkwayeli lɛ ateŋ eko ji Abel. Oba ootao okpãtã maŋ ni ji biianyɛ hã Israel lɛ hiɛ. Mɛɛba ni obaakpãtã Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ nii ahiɛ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Yoab here yoo lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Kpaoo! Enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ̃ akɛ makpãtã nyɛmaŋ lɛ hiɛ?

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Jeee nakai nyiɛmɔ kwraa wɔnyiɛ. Sane lɛ moŋ ji akɛ nuu ko ni jɛ Efraim gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Sheba, Bikri binuu lɛ, ete shi ewo Maŋtsɛ David. Nyɛjiea lɛ nyɛhãa wɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ wɔbaashi nyɛmaŋ lɛ ni wɔya.” Yoo lɛ kɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Kɛfee lɛ abaafɔ̃ eyitso kɛtsɔ̃ gbogbo lɛ nɔ ahã bo.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ tee ekɛ sane lɛ yafɔ̃ maŋbii lɛ ahiɛ, ni ehã amɛfo Sheba yitso, ni afɔ̃ kɛtsɔ̃ gbogbo lɛ nɔ ahã Yoab. Enɛ hã Yoab kpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ, ni etabilɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ tuamɔ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee eshĩa. Kɛkɛ ni Yoab ku esɛɛ eba Maŋtsɛ David ŋɔɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm. David tsuji lɛ

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yoab ji Israel fɛɛ tatsɛnukpa, ni Benaia, Yehoiada bi lɛ, ji Keretifoi kɛ Peletifoi ni ji maŋtsɛ hebulɔi lɛ atsɛ.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoniram ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ, ni Yehoshafat, Ahilud bi lɛ, buɔ nibii ahe akɔntaa.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Sheva ji woloŋmalɔ, ni Zadok kɛ Abiatar ji osɔfoi,

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: ni David osɔfo kroko hu ji Ira, Yairnyo lɛ.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Gibeonbii nɛɛ, jeee Israelbii ni, shi moŋ Amorbii ni shwɛ ji amɛ. Israelbii lɛ ekã amɛ kitã akɛ amɛkpãtãŋ amɛhiɛ, shi be ni Saul hiɛ dɔ yɛ Israelbii kɛ Yudabii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, kulɛ eetao ekpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, David tsɛ Gibeonbii lɛ, ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛni mifee mihã nyɛ, ni mɛni mikɛkpãtã nyɛ bɔ ni afee ni nyɛjɔɔ Yehowa webii lɛ?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Gibeonbii lɛ to he akɛ, “Saul tao akɛ ekpãtã wɔhiɛ kɛbule wɔshishi kwraa yɛ Israel,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ eshwiei amli hii kpawo ohã wɔ koni wɔyasɛŋ amɛ wɔtsɔ̃ɔ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Gibea, yɛ Saul, mɔ ni Yehowa wo lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli.” Maŋtsɛ David to he ni ekɛɛ, “Mibahã nyɛ mɛi lɛ.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Kitã ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛ Saul bi Yonatan kãmɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ David shi Yonatan bi Mefiboshet, ni ji Saul nabi lɛ, sɛɛ,

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: David kɛ amɛ wo Gibeonbii lɛ adɛŋ, ni Gibeonbii lɛ sɛŋ amɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyi kpawo lɛ fɛɛ amɛgboi shi kome. Ŋmɔshi nikpamɔ shishijee be mli asɛŋ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ; no mli lɛ abɔi akoko foo.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Aia biyoo, Rizpa, Saul hemɔ lɛ, kɔ kpekpe ni eshi lɛ buu eha enɔ yɛ tɛsaa lɛ nɔ he ni gbohii lɛ jwere lɛ, kɛjɛ nikpamɔ shishijee be lɛ mli kɛyashi be ni nu bɔi nɛmɔ kɛ amɛnɔshwiemɔ. Shwane lɛ eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ koni loofɔji abasɔmɔ gbohii lɛ anɔ, ni nyɔɔŋ hu eshwieɔ ŋaŋ kooloi yɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: etee ni eyaŋɔ Saul wui lɛ kɛ Yonatan hu wui lɛ yɛ Yabesh Gileadbii lɛ adɛŋ kɛba. Ejaakɛ gbi ni Filistibii lɛ gbe Saul yɛ Gilboa lɛ, amɛkɛ Saul kɛ Yonatan gbohii lɛ ba, ni amɛkɛbatsotsro shi yɛ Bet-Shan blohu lɛ mli; ni Yabesh-Gileadbii lɛ baju gbohii lɛ kɛtee.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Akɛ Saul kɛ Yonatan wui lɛ tee, ni ayafu yɛ Saul tsɛ Kish fuuhe lɛ, yɛ Zela yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Afee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ efã lɛ. No sɛɛ dani Nyɔŋmɔ bo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ afai ni amɛkpa amɛhã shikpɔŋ lɛ toi. Tai ni akɛ Filistibii oblaŋi gojogojoo wu lɛ (

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nuu oblaŋ gojoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Ishbi-Benob lɛ fã kɛba kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ ebaagbe David. Edɛŋ akplɔ tsiimɔ ji akɔɔble shekeli ohai etɛ̃, ni klante hee ŋmɔ ehɛ.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Shi Abishai, ni ji Zeruia bi lɛ, bahere David. Ebatswa Filistinyo lɛ nɔ, ni egbe lɛ. Jɛi ni David tabilɔi lɛ hã David kã amɛ kitã akɛ efataŋ amɛhe kɛyaŋ ta dɔŋŋ. Amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Okɛ wɔ akaya ta dɔŋŋ koni okabahã Israel hiɛnɔkãmɔ miitã.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ kɛ Filistibii lɛ wu ta ekoŋŋ yɛ Gob. Ta nɛɛ mli ni Sibekai, Hushanyo lɛ, gbe hii oblaŋi gojogojoo lɛ ashwiei lɛ ateŋ eko ni gbɛi ji Saf lɛ.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ kɛ Filistibii lɛ ku sɛɛ amɛwu ta yɛ Gob ekoŋŋ. No mli Elhanan, ni ji Betlehemnyo Yaare-Oregim bi lɛ, gbe Goliat, Gatnyo lɛ ni ekpɔlɔ mlitso ti tamɔ mamalolɔ agba tso tilɛ lɛ.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Nuu nɛɛ tswa Israelbii lɛ mpoa, kɛkɛ ni Yonatan, ni ji David nyɛmi Shimei bi lɛ, tswa lɛ nɔ, ni egbe lɛ.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Hii oblaŋi gojogojoo ni hi shi yɛ Gat lɛ ashwiei ji oblaŋi ejwɛ nɛɛ ni David kɛ tabilɔi lɛ gbe lɛ.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Ehere mi yɛ mihenyɛlɔi ni he wa lɛ adɛŋ; kɛ mɛi ni nyɛɔ mi lɛ hu adɛŋ, ejaakɛ amɛhe wa tsɔ̃ fe mi.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa jie David yɛ ehenyɛlɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Saul hu dɛŋ lɛ, David la lala nɛɛ:

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, majie oyi, Yehowa, matsɔ̃ɔ majimaji lɛ; mala makafo bo.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: Yehowa ji mitɛsaa, kɛ mimɔɔ kɛ miherelɔ.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: MiNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ji mitɛsaa, mɔ mli ni mibaa abo yɛ. Ebuɔ mihe tamɔ tsɛŋ, ni efãa mihe, ni ehãa mifeɔ shweshweeshwe. Lɛ ji miyiwalaherelɔ ni buɔ mihe, ni hereɔ mi kɛjɛɔ nɔnaa mli.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Mibo mitsɛ Yehowa, mɔ ni sa yijiemɔ lɛ, ni ehere mi yɛ mihenyɛlɔi adɛŋ. Ajie Yehowa yi!

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Gbele ŋshɔkei bɔle mi kɛkpe, ni fai fɔ̃ji wo mihe gbeyei.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Gbohiiaje kpãi bɔle mi kɛkpe, ni gbele tsɔ̃ mi tsɔne.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Mifimɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mibo mitsɛ Yehowa, mibo mitsɛ miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Ejɛ eSɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni enu migbee; mibolɔmɔ lɛ yashɛ etoiŋ.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hoso; ni ekpokpo, ŋwɛi shishitoi lɛ hu hoso, ni amɛkpokpo ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mli efu.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Lasu fã kɛjɛ egugɔ mli, ni la ni kpãtãa nii ahiɛ jɛ edaaŋ; ŋai ni miitsɛ̃ hu jɛ edaaŋ.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Egba ŋwɛi mli, ni ekpeleke shi, Yehowa hã ŋwɛi kpoo enaa shi, ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni duŋ kpii yɛ enaneshi.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Eta Kerub nɔ, ni efiliki; ana lɛ ni eta kɔɔyɔɔ fiji anɔ.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Ekɛ duŋ kpii ha ehe, ni atatui kpiikpii ni eyi kɛ nu bɔle ehe kɛkpe.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Ŋai ni miitso kpɛlɛ la kɛjɛ ehiɛ ni kpɛɔ hɛŋŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Yehowa gbee shi kɛjɛ ŋwɛi; Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ wo egbeeŋ.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: Etsɛ̃rɛ egãii lɛ ekɛgbɛ ehenyɛlɔi lɛ eshwã; ni ekɛ srawa hu wo amɛ foi.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ana ŋshɔ shishi kã shi, ni agbele je lɛ shishitoo atsɔ̃ɔ faŋŋ, be ni Yehowa kã ehenyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ, ni ekɛ mlifu bolɔ ewo amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Yehowa jɛ ŋwɛi ekpã enine mli emɔ mimli, ni esha mi kɛjɛ bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Amɛbatua mi yɛ amanehulu be mli, shi Yehowa bu mihe.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: Ejie mi yɛ osharã mli, ni ehere mi, ejaakɛ eyɛ mihe tsuijurɔ.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Yehowa duro mi, ejaakɛ mifee nii ni ja; ni ejɔɔ mi, ejaakɛ mifeko efɔŋ ko.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Miye Yehowa mlai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, ni mishiko miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Miye emlai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, ni mitɔ̃ko ekpɔi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Ele akɛ fɔbuu ko bɛ mihe, ni ele akɛ miwi mihe kɛje nɔ fɔŋ he.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa fee mi ejurɔ yɛ mijalɛ naa, yɛ fɔbuu ko ni bɛ mihe lɛ naa.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni yeɔ bo anɔkwa lɛ bo hu oyeɔ amɛ anɔkwa; ni mɔ ni fɔbuu ko bɛ ehe lɛ naa bo akɛ mɔ ni eye emuu.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni he tse lɛ, okɛ ohe tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ akɛ mɔ ni he tse; shi mɔ ni yi wa lɛ, okɛ lɛ yeee.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Ohereɔ humii ayiwala, shi henɔwolɔi lɛ obaa amɛ shi.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Yehowa, lɛɛlɛŋ bo ji kane, ni miNyɔŋmɔ hãa minaa nii yɛ duŋ mli.

english_verse: You help me defeat armies and capture cities.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, bo ohewalɛ mikɛyeɔ henyɛlɔi anɔ, ni miNyɔŋmɔ hewalɛ mikɛhuruɔ henyɛlɔ gbogbo.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shwamɔ ko bɛ enifeemɔ he; ni ewooo shi ni efee yaka. Etsɔ̃ɔ tamɔ tsɛŋ ehãa mɛi fɛɛ ni baa lɛ abo lɛ.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Yehowa pɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ, ni Nyɔŋmɔ pɛ ji wɔhefãlɔ.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ mibobaa mɔɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji lɛ; ehãa migbɛ jaa hãa mi.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ehãa minajiaŋ waa tamɔ ofrote, ni ebaa miyi yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Etsɔ̃ɔ mi tawuu, koni manyɛ akɔɔble gãi matsɛ̃.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Yehowa, obaa miyi, ni ohere mi; oyelikɛbuamɔ ehã mitsɔ̃ mɔ wulu.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Ohã mi foijeehei babaoo, ni migbeko shi pɛŋ.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Mitiuɔ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ, ni mikpãtãa amɛhiɛ, ni mikpaleee kɛyashi mipleneɔ amɛ.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Mitswiaa amɛ nii bɔ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ shi amɛte dɔŋŋ, ni amɛnyɔnyɔi yɛ minaji ashi.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ omiaa mi kɛhã tawuu; ohãa mihenyɛlɔi lɛ nyɔnyɔɔ yɛ minaji ashi.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Ohãa mihenyɛlɔi joɔ minaa foi, ni mikpãtãa mɛi ni nyɛɔ mi lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Amɛkwɛ gbɛ, shi yiwalaheremɔ ko bɛ; amɛkwɛ Yehowa gbɛ; shi efooo amɛdaaŋ.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Mishimɔ amɛ muɛmuɛ tamɔ mlu; minaanaa amɛnɔ tamɔ gbɛteŋ ŋmɔtɔ.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Ojie mi yɛ mimaŋ maŋsɔi amli, ni obaa miyi akɛ majimaji anɔ maŋtsɛ; ni mɛi kpɔji ni mileee tete ebatsɔ̃ mishishibii agbɛnɛ.

english_verse: They obey and come crawling.
translation_verse: Maŋsɛɛbii kotoɔ mi, ni kɛ miwie lɛ amɛboɔ mi toi.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Maŋsɛɛbii lɛ anijiaŋ je wui, ni amɛshi amɛmɔji lɛ amli amɛba kɛ hekpokpomɔ.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Yehowa hiɛ kã! Ajie mihefãlɔ lɛ yi! Akafo Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni ji miyiwalaherelɔ lɛ agbojee.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ ni tɔ mihe owele ni eba maji ashi ewo mishishi,

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: asaŋ ni ehere mi yɛ mihenyɛlɔi adɛŋ lɛ. Yehowa, owoɔ mi otaa mihenyɛlɔi lɛ ayiteŋ, ni obaa miyi kɛjɛ yiwalɔi adɛŋ.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Ohã maŋtsɛ lɛ eye kunim wuji yɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ, ni osumɔɔ mɔ ni ofɔ lɛ mu owo lɛ maŋtsɛ, ni ji David kɛ eshwiei fɛɛ kɛyaa naanɔ.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Yehowa mumɔ lɛ tsɔɔ minɔ ewieɔ; ewiemɔ kã mililɛi nɔ.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ena ewie; Israel hebulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Mɔ ni yeɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ jalɛ naa, ni eyeɔ nɔ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishemɔ naa lɛ,

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: etamɔ leebi hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ nunɛmɔ sɛɛ, be ni oblɔtu bɛ; etamɔ nu ni hãa jwɛifɔ kwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ.”

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ baajɔɔ miwe lɛ nɛ, ejaakɛ ekɛ mi ekpãŋ naanɔ kpãŋmɔ, kpãŋmɔ ko ni akuŋ mli, shiwoo ko ni atsakeŋ hiɛ. Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ baahã mi yelikɛbuamɔ ni he ehia, kɛ mitaomɔ nii fɛɛ.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Mɛi ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei lɛ, amɛtamɔ ŋmei ni ashɛrɛ ashwie; anyɛɛɛ akɛ nine folo ata amɛhe;

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: mɔ ni aaata amɛhe lɛ, ja ehiɛ dade kɛ akplɔ; ni akɛ la shãa amɛ wɛɛ. David Tabilɔi Kakabãi lɛ (

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: edamɔ shi akɛ nuu, ni ekpee ta lɛ naa, ni egbe Filistibii lɛ aahu kɛyashi ekɔ̃ji gboi yɛ ehe bɔ sɔŋŋ ni ehiii lɛ eklante lɛ nɔwomɔ dɔŋŋ. Yehowa ye kunim kpeteŋkple nakai gbi lɛ ehã Israelbii lɛ. Fee sɛɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ ba he ni Eleazar wu ta lɛ yɛ lɛ, ni amɛbakpɔlɔ gbohii lɛ ahe nibii kɛtee.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Egbɛi hehe fe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ hii kãkãlɔi nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ lɛ ateŋ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, etsɔ amɛnukpa, shi moŋ eninaaa kakabãi etɛ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: David tabilɔi kakabãi lɛ agbɛii nɛ: Klɛŋklɛŋ mɔ lɛ ji Yosheb-bashebet, Takemonnyo lɛ, mɔ ni ji “kakabãi etɛ̃” lɛ ateŋ onukpa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Ewo ekpɔlɔ nɔ lɛ ekɛgbe mɛi ohai kpaanyɔ yɛ ta kome mli.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Esɛɛmɔ yɛ hii kakabãi etɛ̃ lɛ ateŋ ji Eleazar, Dodo Ahohinyo lɛ, bi lɛ. Gbi ko lɛ efata David he, ni amɛtswa Filistibii ni ebabua shi akɛ amɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ baawu lɛ mpoa. Israelbii lɛ naa sɛɛsɛɛ, shi

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: Shi Shama ho edamɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni egbe Filistibii lɛ ekɛfã ŋmɔ lɛ he. Ni Yehowa ye kunim kpele ehã Israelbii lɛ nakai gbi lɛ.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Be ni eshwɛ fioo ni abɔiɔ ŋmɔshi nikpamɔ lɛ, Israel hii kakabãi nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ lɛ ateŋ mɛi etɛ̃ komɛi ba David ŋɔɔ yɛ Adullam tɛkplo lɛ mli. Nakai be mli lɛ Filistibii lɛ efã ta kɛba, ni amɛbato shi yɛ Refaim Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: No mli lɛ David yɛ tɛkplo lɛ mli, ni Filistibii asraafoi lɛ ebaŋɔ Betlehem.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: David shwe shĩa ekɛɛ akɛ, “Namɔ po mana koni eya Betlehem eyayɛ nubu lɛ ni yɔɔ maŋ agbo lɛ masɛi lɛ mli nu ebahã mi manu?”

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii kakabãi etɛ̃ nɛɛ gba kɛtsɔ̃ Filistibii atabilɔi lɛ ateŋ ekãa naa kɛho, ni amɛtee amɛyayɛ nubu lɛ ni yɔɔ Betlehem maŋ agbo lɛ masɛi lɛ mli nu, ni amɛkɛbahã David. David enuuu, shi moŋ efɔse eshwie shikpɔŋ akɛ nɔ ko ni ekɛmiishã afɔle ehã Yehowa;

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa, enɛ akagbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ̃ akɛ manu nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ, ejaakɛ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ lɛ, hii lɛ ni shã amɛhe afɔle lɛ alá ni.” No hewɔ lɛ, David enuuu nu lɛ. Ekãa naa nibii krokomɛi ni hii Kakabãi Etɛ̃ lɛ tsu lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
