translation_verse: Ni maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ kpãkpãa bɛji ni amɛnyiɛ Solomon sɛɛ kɛ nyamɔ kpele kɛba maŋ lɛ mli. Ni amɛhoofeemɔ lɛ hã shikpɔŋ hoso waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Ni be ni Adonia kɛ emɛi lɛ eye nii lɛ etã lɛ, Adonia kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni ekpee ni yɔɔ eŋɔɔ lɛ nu hoofeemɔ lɛ he. Be ni Yoab nu tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ lɛ, ebi akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ afeɔ hoo kɛ bolɔmɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli nɛkɛ?”

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni ewieɔ lolo ni enaa enyɔko shi lɛ, naa, Osɔfo Abiatar bi Yonatan ni eba jɛi; ni Adonia kɛɛ, “Ba, ejaakɛ gbɔmɔ kpakpa ji bo, ni sane kpakpa okɛbaa.”

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Yonatan to he ehã lɛ akɛ, “Dabida, wɔnuŋtsɔ David ewo Solomon maŋtsɛ!

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: Be ni Osɔfo Zadok kɛ Gbalɔ Natan efɔ lɛ mu amɛwo lɛ maŋtsɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛ nyamɔ kɛba maŋ lɛ mli. No ji bolɔmɔ kɛ nyamɔ ni nyɛnu he lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Awo Solomon maŋtsɛ ata etsɛ sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Ni asaŋ maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ ba, ni amɛjɔɔ wɔnuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ, ‘oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ahã Solomon gbɛi ahehee shi fe ogbɛi lɛ, ni emaŋtsɛyeli mli alɛɛ fe onɔ lɛ.’ Maŋtsɛ David kã esaa lɛ nɔ nakai be lɛ mli, ni ema eyi shi ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: ‘Ajie, Yehowa, wɔ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ yi, lɛ mɔ ni ehã mɔ kome yɛ mimusuŋbii lɛ ateŋ ebata misɛ̃i lɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ; ni mihiŋmɛi enã!’ ”

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Adonia kɛ maŋ ni ekpee lɛ fɛɛ atsui fã, ni amɛtetee shi, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɔ egbɛ.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ayagba Maŋtsɛ Solomon akɛ, “Naa, Adonia miishe bo gbeyei, ni eyamɔmɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ aklontoi lɛ amli, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Maŋtsɛ Solomon akã kitã akɛ ekɛ klante egbeŋ mi.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Ni Solomon kɛɛ, “Kɛji efee ehe gbɔmɔ kpakpa lɛ eyiteŋtsɔi kome nɛkɛ enyɔŋ shikpɔŋ; shi kɛjeee nakai lɛ, no lɛ ebaagbo.”

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon tsu ayaŋɔ Adonia kɛjɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he kɛba; ni eba ebakoto Maŋtsɛ Solomon. Ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa owe!”

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Mibi, eshwɛ fioo pɛ ni magbo tamɔ bɔ ni adesai fɛɛ gboiɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ohe awa, ni ofee ekãa taakɛ nuu.

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: “Solomon, ohiɛ akakpa nɔ ni Zerua bi Yoab fee mi lɛ nɔ, bɔ ni egbe Israel tatsɛmɛi enyɔ. Ner bi Abner kɛ Yeter bi Amasa, kɛtɔ ta mli lá shi ni ashwie he owele, be mli ni ta bɛ lɛ. Etɔ̃, ni no hewɔ lɛ, okɛ lɛ aye

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: yɛ onilee naa bɔ ni sa ohiɛ pɛ. Shi moŋ kaahã ekɛ eyiteŋ waji miikpeleke shi kɛmiiya gbohiiaje yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: Ni naa, mɔ kroko hu ji Gera bi Shimei, ni jɛ Bahurim lɛ. Lɛ lɛ elomɔ mi dikadika gbi ni mitee Mahanaim lɛ. Shi fee sɛɛ be ni ekɛ mi bakpe yɛ Yordan Faa lɛ naa lɛ, mikɛ Yehowa gbɛi kã kitã akɛ, ‘Migbeŋ bo kɛ klante!’

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Shi bo lɛ kaahã ni eye ehe. Nilelɔ ji bo; ni ole bɔ pɛ ni ooofee lɛ; egbɔ moŋ nɛ, shi ohã ni agbe lɛ kɛ eyiteŋ waŋ lɛ.” Maŋtsɛ David gbele (

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be ni Shimei nu enɛ lɛ ewo eteji nɔ nii, ni eyiŋ etee Akish ŋɔɔ yɛ Gat ni eyatao enyɔji lɛ. Ni Shimei tee eyakpala etsuji lɛ kɛjɛ Gat kɛba.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: Amɛlá abua Yoab kɛ eshwiei ayiteŋ kɛya naanɔ; shi Yehowa ajɔɔ David we lɛ, eshwiei kɛ emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ kɛya naanɔ!”

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Ebi Solomon baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ, ni emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ma shi kpɛŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Adonia gbele

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Hagit bi Adonia ba Solomon nyɛ Batsheba ŋɔɔ. Ni Batsheba bi Adonia akɛ, “Ani oba yɛ hejɔlɛ mli lo?” Ni Adonia kɛɛ, “Hɛɛ, hejɔlɛ mli miba.

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Asaŋ miyɛ sane ko ni mi mibakɛɛ bo.” Ni Batsheba kɛɛ Adonia akɛ, “Mɛni sane ni; wiemɔ!”

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Ni Adonia kɛɛ, “Ole akɛ kulɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ minɔ ni; ni Israel fɛɛ hiɛ kã minɔ akɛ mi mibaye maŋtsɛ lɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ etsɔ̃ ehã he kroko, ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ suɔmɔ naa lɛ etsɔ̃ minyɛmi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Nɔ kome pɛ kɛkɛ he fai mikpaa bo; kaakãmã mi!” Ni Batsheba kɛɛ, “Wiemɔ!”

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Ni Adonia kɛɛ, “Ofainɛ, okɛ minyɛmi Maŋtsɛ Solomon awie, ejaakɛ mile akɛ ekamaŋ bo, koni ekɛ Abishag, Shunam yoo lɛ, ahã mi gbãlã.”

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Ni Batsheba kɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mi kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ baawie ahã bo.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Batsheba tee Maŋtsɛ Solomon ŋɔɔ, ni ekɛ lɛ yawie ehã Adonia. Be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ na enyɛ Batsheba lɛ, ete shi ekɛ lɛ yakpe, ni ekoto lɛ; kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon ho eta emaŋtsɛ sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ehã ayawo sɛ̃i kroko abahã enyɛ lɛ, ni eta maŋtsɛ ninejurɔgbɛ.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Ni Batsheba kɛɛ Solomon akɛ, “Nɔ ko bibioo ko mibaba bo nɛɛ; kaakãmã mi.” Ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ, “Bi mi, nyɛ awo, ni mikãmãŋ bo.”

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ, “Hã aŋɔ Abishag, Shunam yoo lɛ, ahã onyɛmi Adonia gbãlã.”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon to he akɛ, “Shi mɛɛba obiɔ Abishag, Shunam yoo lɛ, shi ohã Adonia? Bi maŋtsɛyeli lɛ hu ohã lɛ, ejaakɛ lɛ ji minyɛmi nukpa. Mɛɛba obiii nɔ ko ohãaa Osɔfo Abiatar kɛ Zerua bi Yoab hu.”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon kã Yehowa kitã ekɛɛ, “Kɛji wiemɔ ni Adonia wie nɛɛ lɛ jeee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esusuma ewie eshi fii, Nyɔŋmɔ awo mi he nyɔmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbii abɔ ni Yehowa, mɔ ni ehã mimaŋtsɛyeli lɛ emã shi kpɛŋŋ, ni eŋɔ mi eta mitsɛ David sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ, ni eŋɔ maŋtsɛyeli ehã mi kɛ mishwiei taakɛ bɔ ni ewo shi lɛ, ja agbe Adonia ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Solomon tsu Yehoiada bi Benaia kɛtee ni eyatswa Adonia nɔ, ni egbe lɛ. Ashwie Abiatar

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon kɛɛ Osɔfo Abiatar akɛ, “Yaa Anatot yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; kulɛ osa gbele; shi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ migbeee bo, ejaakɛ bo ji mɔ ni otere Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Adeka lɛ kɛnyiɛ mitsɛ David hiɛ, ni ona mitsɛ amanehului ni ena lɛ eko.

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Shi moŋ mihaŋ ni oye Osɔfo dɔŋŋ, bɔ ni afee ni Yehowa wiemɔ ni ewie yɛ Eli we lɛ he yɛ Shilo lɛ aba mli.” Agbe Yoab

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Yoab waaa Absalom shi moŋ ewa Adonia. No hewɔ lɛ, be ni enu akɛ Adonia egbo lɛ ejo foi kɛtee Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ mli, ni eyamɔmɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he aklontoi lɛ amli.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Ni ayagba Maŋtsɛ Solomon akɛ Yoab ejo foi kɛtee Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ mli; ni naa, eyɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he. Kɛkɛ ni Solomon tsu Yehoiada bi Benaia ekɛɛ, “Yaa ni oyagbe lɛ.”

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Ni Benaia tee Yehowa Buu lɛ mli, ni eyakɛɛ Yoab akɛ, “Bɔ ni maŋtsɛ kɛɛ nɛ, jee kpo.” Shi Yoab kɛɛ, “Dabida, shi biɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ magbo yɛ!” Ni Benaia yakɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ akɛ bɔ ni Yoab kɛɛ nɛ, ni hetoo ni ehã mi nɛ.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Yehowa ahã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ elá abua eyiteŋ, ejaakɛ ekɛ klante gbe mɛi enyɔ be ni mitsɛ David leee he nɔ ko. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ji gbɔmɛi ni ji jalɔi kɛ mɛi kpakpai fe lɛ. Amɛ ji Abner, Ner bi lɛ, Israel Tatsɛ lɛ, kɛ Yeter bi Amasa, Yuda tatsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Yehoiada bi Benaia yiŋ etee Yehowa Buu lɛ mli, ni eyagbe Yoab, ni afu lɛ yɛ ewe lɛ, yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon ŋɔ Yehoiada bi Benaia efee tatsɛ yɛ Yoab najiaŋ, ni eŋɔ Zadok efee Osɔfo yɛ Abiatar najiaŋ. Agbe Shimei

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ Solomon tsu ayatsɛ Shimei kɛba eŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maa tsu ohã ohe yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni ohi jɛi; ni okaje jɛi kɛmiiya he ko he ko.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ gbi nɔ ni oooje kpo oyafo Kidron faa lɛ, na ole akɛ gbo obaagbo, olá abua bo diɛŋtsɛ oyiteŋ!”

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Ni Shimei kɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wiemɔ lɛ hi; bɔ ni minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ kɛɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ otsulɔ baafee.” Ni Shimei hi Yerusalɛm gbii kplaŋŋ.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Afii etɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ eba mli akɛ Shimei tsuji lɛ ateŋ mɛi enyɔ jo foi kɛtee Gat Maŋtsɛ Akish, Maaka bi lɛ ŋɔɔ. Ni atswa Shimei adafi akɛ, “Naa onyɔji lɛ yɛ Gat.”

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko yabɔ Maŋtsɛ Solomon amaniɛ akɛ Shimei eyiŋ kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm kɛtee Gat, ni eku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ tsu ayatsɛ Shimei kɛba. Ni Solomon kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Te mitsɛ́ Yehowa mikɛkã bo kitã akɛ gbi nɔ ni oooje kpo ni oooyanyiɛ kɛaatee he ko lɛ, na ole akɛ gbo ooogbo lɛ? Okɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Wiemɔ lɛ hi, minu!’

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ mɔ oyeee Yehowa kitã lɛ kɛ akpɔ ni miwo bo lɛ nɔ?

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Shimei akɛ, ‘Ole efɔŋ fɛɛ ni ohiɛ kã he ni ofee mitsɛ David lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa ahã efɔŋ ni ofee lɛ aku sɛɛ abua bo diɛŋtsɛ oyiteŋ.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ Solomon lɛ aaajɔɔ lɛ, ni mitsɛ David sɛ̃i lɛ aaama shi shiŋŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ kɛaatee naanɔ!’ ”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã Yehoida bi Benaia, ni eje kpo ni eyagbe Shimei. Ni maŋtsɛyeli lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ yɛ Solomon dɛŋ.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Nakai be mli lɛ akɛni amako tsu ahãko Yehowa hewɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ shã afɔle yɛ wɔŋkoi lɛ amli.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Ni asaŋ nɔ ni obiko tete hu maŋɔ mafata he mahã bo; ninamɔ kɛ anunyam fɛɛ, bɔ ni maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ateŋ fɛɛ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ bo yeŋ hegbɔ owala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Solomon sumɔɔ Yehowa, ni enyiɛ etsɛ David tsɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ; shi Solomon hu shã afɔle kɛ tsofakɛŋma yɛ jemawɔji ajamɔhei lɛ.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Nyɔɔŋ be ni eyɔɔ jɛi lɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Naa Nyɔŋmɔ jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ lamɔ mli. Ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bi mi nɔ ni otaoɔ ni mahã bo!”

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Ni Solomon kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofee mitsɛ David ejurɔ, ni osumɔ lɛ kɛ suɔmɔ kpele, ejaakɛ eye bo anɔkwa; eja, ni ekɛ bo hi shi kɛ tsui krɔŋŋ. Ni bo hu osumɔ lɛ, ni ohã lɛ binuu koni eta esɛ̃i lɛ nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni eba mli ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Ni amrɔ nɛɛ, Ao Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ, owo mi, otsulɔ, maŋtsɛ yɛ mitsɛ sɛɛ. Gbekɛ bibioo kɛ minaa fufɔ sã kɛkɛ ji mi, ni mileee maŋnɔyeli.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Shi esa akɛ maye omaŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ nɔ, maŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ ohala, maŋ ni amɛfa babaoo bɔ ni anyɛŋ amɛ akane tete lɛ.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, dromɔ mi, otsulɔ, nilee koni mikɛye omaŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ jalɛ mli. Hã mayoo srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni ehiii teŋ; kɛjeee nakai lɛ te mafee tɛŋŋ manyɛ maye omaŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ nɔ hu?”

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Akɛni obi enɛ, shi obiii ni ahã bo wala sɛɛtsɛlɛ, ni asaŋ obiii ninamɔ ohãaa ohe, ni osaa obiii ohenyɛlɔi agbele; shi moŋ obi ni ahã bo jwɛŋmɔ kɛ niiasɛɛyoomɔ lɛ,

english_verse: So I'll make you wiser than anyone who has ever lived or ever will live.
translation_verse: mɔ ko ehiŋ shi ni aaale nii tamɔ bo, ni mɔ ko hu baŋ yɛ osɛɛ ni aaatamɔ bo.

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Kɛ ooobo mi toi, ni oooye mikpɔi kɛ mimlai lɛ anɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni otsɛ David fee lɛ, no lɛ mahã ni otsɛ yɛ jeŋ.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Solomon hiɛ tsɛ̃, ni naa lamɔ ni. Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ lɛ ewie yɛ mli. Eba Yerusalɛm, ni ebadamɔ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ, ni eshã shãa afɔle. No sɛɛ lɛ, eŋmɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ okplɔ̃. Solomon bu atɛŋ

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ yei ajwamãŋi enyɔ komɛi badamɔ Maŋtsɛ Solomon hiɛ.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Ni yei lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome kɛɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ, ofainɛ, mi kɛ nɛkɛ yoo nɛɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ tsu kome mli yɛ shĩa kome mli. Ni mifɔ bi yɛ shĩa lɛ mli.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ yoo nɛɛ binuu lɛ bagbo, ejaakɛ eyakã enɔ.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Ni nyɔɔŋteŋ be ni mi oweyoo, miwɔ lɛ, ete shi, ni ebawo mibi nuu lɛ yɛ mimasɛi, ni eŋɔ lɛ eyawo emlishi, ni ewo ebi nuu ni egbo lɛ ebawo mimlishi.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Be ni mite shi leebi ni mibahã mibi lɛ fufɔ lɛ, naa, egbo! Shi be ni je tsɛre ni mikwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, mina akɛ jeee mibi ni mifɔ lɛ ni.”

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Ni yoo kroko lɛ hu kɛɛ, “Dabi, mibi ji hiɛkãalɔ lɛ, ni bo obi ji mɔ ni egbo lɛ.” Yoo mɔ ni wie klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ bo akɛ, “Dabida, mɔ ni egbo lɛ ji obi lɛ! Mɔ ni egbo lɛ ji obi lɛ, mɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ ji mibi lɛ!” Kɛkɛ ni amɛbɔ̃i naataamɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Ni maŋtsɛ lɛ saa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbahãa mi klante!” Ni akɛ klante bahã maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ, “Nyɛjaa bi hiɛkãalɔ lɛ mli enyɔ, ni nyɛŋɔa fã nyɛhãa mɔ kome, ni akɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahã mɔ kome!”

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni yoo mɔ bi ni ji hiɛkãalɔ lɛ bo akɛ, “Ao, minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ, mimusuŋ miishã mi yɛ mibi lɛ he. Ofainɛ, ŋɔɔ bi hiɛkãalɔ lɛ ohã lɛ; akagbe lɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ!” Shi mɔ kome lɛ kɛɛ, “Akɛ lɛ akahã wɔteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko, aja emli enyɔ!”

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Solomon kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkagbea lɛ. Nyɛŋɔa bi hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nyɛhãa yoo mɔ ni wie klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Ejaakɛ lɛ ji bi lɛ nyɛ!”

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii fɛɛ nu bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon bua sane nɛɛ he ehã lɛ, amɛkɛ bulɛ kpele hã maŋtsɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛna akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nilee yɛ emli, ni no hã enyɛ nɛkɛ kojomɔ ekojo!

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon hala nitsulɔi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ yɛ Israel maŋ fɛɛ. Amɛ amɛkɛ niyenii baa maŋtsɛ we lɛ daa afi. Daa afi mli lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ nyɔɔŋ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii baa.

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Ben-Deker kwɛɔ Makaz kɛ Shaalbim kɛ Bet-Shemash kɛ Elon-Bet-Hanan.

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: Ben-Abinadab kwɛɔ Nafat-Dor. Eŋa ji Tafat, Solomon biyoo lɛ.

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Ben-Geber kwɛɔ Ramot-Gilead, lɛ nɔŋŋ ekwɛɔ akrowai komɛi ni ji Manase bi Yair nɔ lɛ anɔ, nɔ ní yɔɔ Gilead lɛ. Ekwɛɔ Argob kpokpai ni yɔɔ Bashan lɛ. Maji nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ amɛhe gbogboi kɛ shinai ni akɔɔble adabaŋi yɔɔ he ni.

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Ahimaaz kwɛɔ Naftali. Ekpee Basemat, Solomon biyoo lɛ.

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Ur bi Geber kwɛɔ Gilead he ni Amorbii amaŋtsɛ Sihon kɛ Bashanbii amaŋtsɛ Og hi lɛ. Mɛnɛɛmɛi fɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ mɔ kome ko yɛ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Solomon Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ dalɛ

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Solomon ye maŋtsɛyelii fɛɛ nɔ lumɔ kɛjɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ naa, kɛ Filistibii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashwie Ijipt husui lɛ anɔ. Amɛtsu onia amɛhã Solomon, ni amɛsɔmɔ lɛ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him.
translation_verse: Solomon ye shikpɔji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ, kɛjɛ Tifsa aahu kɛyashwie Gaza, lɛ nɔ. Eye maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Solomon na toiŋjɔlɛ yɛ ehewɔhewɔ maji lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Ni Solomon yinɔ fɛɛ lɛ, Yuda kɛ Israel hi shi shweshweeshwe. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hi shi yɛ ewain tso kɛ egbami tso shishi kɛjɛ Dan aahu kɛyashwie Beersheba.

english_verse: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,
translation_verse: Mɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ ni kwɛɔ Solomon niyenii anɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii baa daa kɛhã mɛi ni bayeɔ nii yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ. Mɔ kome yɛ nyɔɔŋ kome nɔ. Ni amɛhãaa nɔ ko nɔ ko he ahia.

english_verse: as well as barley and straw for the horses. Solomon's Wisdom
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ akoko kɛ jwɛi hu ni akɛbaahã okpɔŋɔi kɛ kooloi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ baa, bɔ ni afo tɛ ahã amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
translation_verse: Ni Nyɔŋmɔ hã Solomon jwɛŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ kɛ niiashishinumɔ kpele diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Ele nii fe jeŋ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ; ele nii fe Etan, Ezrahinyo lɛ kɛ Heman kɛ Kalkol kɛ Darda, Mahol bii lɛ. Solomon gbɛi hehee yɛ jeŋ maji lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛkpe.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
translation_verse: Ewie tsei ahe, kɛjɛ tsenedru tso ni yɔɔ Lebanon nɔ aahu kɛyashi tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbogboi anɔ ahe. Ewie kooloi kɛ loofɔji kɛ waamɔ nii kɛ nuŋloi hu ahe.

english_verse: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ jeŋ fɛɛ nu Solomon nilee lɛ he, no hewɔ lɛ, amɛhã mɛi ba, ni amɛbabo Solomon naa wiemɔ toi.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: Hiram, Tiro maŋtsɛ lɛ, naanyo ji Maŋtsɛ David yɛ ewala beiaŋ fɛɛ. Be ni Hiram nu akɛ afɔ Solomon mu awo lɛ maŋtsɛ yɛ etsɛ David sɛɛ lɛ, etsu etsuji kɛba Solomon ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
translation_verse: Yehowa wo mitsɛ David shi akɛ, ‘Obi mɔ ni maŋɔ ta osɛi lɛ nɔ yɛ osɛɛ lɛ, lɛ eeema tsu ehã mi.’ Hewɔ lɛ mito miyiŋ akɛ mamã nakai tsu lɛ mahã Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ jamɔ.

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ tsu koni omɛi lɛ ayatoo tsenedru tsei yɛ Lebanon ahã mi; bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ooohe mi lɛ mawo akɛ apaafoi lɛ anyɔmɔwo. Mahã mitsuji lɛ tete abafata amɛhe. Ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ole akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ wɔteŋ ni le tsotoomɔ tamɔ Sidonbii.”

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Maŋtsɛ Hiram nu Maŋtsɛ Solomon wiemɔi lɛ, ena miishɛɛ babaoo ni ekɛɛ, “Ajie Yehowa yi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, akɛ ehã David bi nilelɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ ni baaye nɛkɛ maŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Ni Hiram tsu abakɛɛ Solomon akɛ, “Minu oshɛɛ ni oshɛ mi lɛ; ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni otaoɔ lɛ mafee. Mahã bo tsenedru tsei kɛ sɛsɛo lɛ.

english_verse: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
translation_verse: Mitsuji lɛ aaaŋɔ tsei lɛ kɛjɛ Lebanon kɛba ŋshɔ lɛ naa, ni mahã afimɔ amɛ atsara kɛtsɔ̃ ŋshɔ hiɛ kɛyashwie he ni oootsɔ̃ɔ mi. Mahã afɛne amɛ yɛ jɛi, koni ohã abahole kɛya. Nɔ pɛ ni mitaoɔ ni ofee ji akɛ ohã minitsulɔi lɛ niyenii.”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa hã Solomon nilee tamɔ bɔ ni ewo lɛ shi lɛ; hejɔlɛ hi Hiram kɛ Solomon teŋ. Ni amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãŋ.

english_verse: and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of
translation_verse: Aja mɛi lɛ amli kui etɛ̃. Mɛi akpei nyɔŋma yaa amɛyayeɔ nyɔŋ kome yɛ Lebanon, ni amɛbayeɔ nyɔji enyɔ yɛ shĩa.

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: Ni Solomon fã amɛ, ni amɛgbala tɛi agboi kɛba, tɛi ni jara wa koni akɛto shĩa lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_verse: Ni Solomon nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ Hiram nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ Giblibii lɛ ko tɛi lɛ, ni amɛsaa tsei kɛ tɛi lɛ koni akɛma tsu lɛ.

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: Afee samfɛji awo tsu lɛ he. Samfɛji nɛɛ lɛɛ yɛ mligbɛ fe ekponɔ gbɛ.

english_verse: Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room.
translation_verse: Solomon kɛ kerubim nɛɛ wo mligbɛ tsu lɛ teŋ: kerubim lɛ egbɛgbɛɛ amɛfijiaŋ, bɔ ni ekome fine saa gbogbo kome he, ni kerub kroko lɛ fine saa gbogbo kroko lɛ he. Amɛfiji lɛ kpeɔ yɛ tsu lɛ teŋ.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Solomon tswa tsu lɛ egbe naa, ni ekɛ tsenedru mplaŋi kɛ sɛsɛo ŋmoŋmolo sɛŋ nɔ.

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: Tsui ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kwraa lɛ ekome lɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi enumɔ. Nii ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ, ekome lɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi ekpaa, ni nii ni yɔɔ yiteŋ kwraa lɛ, ekome lɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi kpawo. Afee kpokui yɛ tsu lɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe kɛkpe, bɔ ni afee ni nɔsɛŋmɔ mplaŋi lɛ akabote tsu lɛ gbogboi lɛ amli.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Tɛi ni akɛmã tsu lɛ ako fɛɛ yɛ tɛgbamɔ he lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akanu hamle loo lema loo dade ko naa he be ni amãa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛi tsui etɛ̃ ni amãmɔ kɛbɔle Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ ekome kwɔlɛ ji ninetalɔi enumɔ. Ni akɛ tsenedru tso mɔmɔ amɛ akpɛtɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Solomon akɛ,

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: Akɛ tsenedru ŋmoŋmolo ha tsu lɛ mligbɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe, kɛjɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋwɛi nɔsɛŋmɔ tsei lɛ anaa. Ni akɛ sɛsɛo ka Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: He Krɔŋkrɔŋ Fe Fɛɛ lɛ amã no yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ sɛɛgbɛ. Ekɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai enyɔ. Ni akɛ tsenedru ŋmoŋmolo fo ekɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ teŋ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛyi shi.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Tsenedru ŋmoŋmolo ni akɛha tsu lɛ mli lɛ ayeyee fɔfɔi kɛ akpaki sãmãi awo he. Ŋmoŋmolo lɛ eha tɛi lɛ anɔ, hewɔ lɛ anaaa tɛi lɛ ekome nɛkɛ.

english_verse: The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place.
translation_verse: Tsu ni amã yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mligbɛ kwraa lɛ jɛi akɛ Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ mã.

english_verse: This room was nine meters long, nine meters wide, and nine meters high, and it was lined with pure gold. There were also gold chains across the front of the most holy place. The inside of the temple, as well as the cedar altar in the most holy place, was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni afee ni shĩa lɛ aye emuu hewɔ lɛ, asaa akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ha mli fɛɛ. Aha afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ tete ni yɔɔ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he fɛɛ kɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall
translation_verse: Ni akɛ mutso gbɔ kerubim enyɔ ni kwɔlɔmɔ ji ninetalɔi nyɔŋma awo He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and four and a half meters across. They had two wings, and the wings were just over two meters long.
translation_verse: Kerub kome kwɔlɛ ji ninetalɔi nyɔŋma, ni ekroko lɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The creatures were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Ni akɛ shika eha kerubim lɛ ahe.

english_verse: The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Ni aye kerubim kɛ tɛŋ kɛ fɔfɔii ni egblegblee sãmãi yɛ shĩa lɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe fɛɛ kɛkpe, yɛ mligbɛ kɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Even the floor was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Ni shĩa lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi eka mli.

english_verse: The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Ni aye kerubim kɛ tɛŋi kɛ fɔfɔii ni egblegblee sãmãi awo he; ni akɛ shika eha he fɛɛ.

english_verse: The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
translation_verse: Ni akɛ tɛ ni ako kɛ tsenedru mplaŋi mã mligbɛ kpo lɛ. Kɛ atswa tɛ klɛmpɛi etɛ̃ lɛ, akɛ tsenedru mplaŋ klɛmpɛ kome foɔ mli.

english_verse: Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Solomon maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ Zif nyɔŋ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ, ato Yehowa we lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.

translation_verse: Ni ŋɔɔ ofa omaŋ ni efee esha lɛ eshi bo kɛ efɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛfee lɛ. Hã amɛnomŋɔlɔi lɛ amusuŋ atsɔ̃ amɛ yɛ amɛhe ni amɛna amɛ mɔbɔ.

english_verse: Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ omaŋ kɛ onii ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛjɛ dade flɔnɔɔ mli, ji amɛ.

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help.
translation_verse: Wo ohiɛ nɔ okwɛ otsuji kɛ omaŋ Israelbii, ni obo amɛ toi be fɛɛ be ni amɛaabolɔ amɛtsɛ bo lɛ.

english_verse: When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.” Solomon Blesses the People
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ. Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, oŋɔ amɛ ohã ohe, ni okɛ amɛ fee omaŋ yɛ majimaji lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ, taakɛ owo shi kɛtsɔ̃ Mose nɔ, be ni ojie wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt lɛ.” Naagbee sɔlemɔ

english_verse: When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Maŋtsɛ Solomon egbe sɔlemɔ kɛ fai ni ekpa Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa lɛ, ete shi kɛjɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ, he ni ekũla ni egbɛ enijiaŋ kɛtee ŋwɛi yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
translation_verse: “Ajie Yehowa, mɔ ni ehã emaŋ Israel toiŋjɔlɛ taakɛ bɔ ni ewo shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eshiwoi kpakpai fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ etsulɔ Mose nɔ ewo lɛ, emli wiemɔ lɛ ekome folo nɛkɛ efeko yaka.

english_verse: The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us.
translation_verse: Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ wɔ ahi shi, taakɛ bɔ ni ekɛ wɔblematsɛmɛi lɛ hi shi lɛ. Ekashi wɔ, ni esaa ekakwa wɔ hu.

english_verse: May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ehã ni wɔbo lɛ toi kɛ wɔtsui fɛɛ, koni wɔhi shi bɔ ni etaoɔ. Wɔye ekitãi kɛ emlai ni ewo wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hiɛ ahi misɔlemɔ kɛ faikpamɔi nɛɛ anɔ, shwane kɛ nyɔɔŋ, koni eye ebua mi, etsulɔ, kɛ emaŋ Israel be fɛɛ be ni nɔ ko aaahia wɔ lɛ.

english_verse: On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ maŋtsɛ jɔɔ kpo lɛ ni yɔɔ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ efee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ, ejaakɛ jɛi eshã shãa afɔlei kɛ niyenii afɔlei kɛ kooloo muu afɔlei lɛ fɛɛ afɔi lɛ yɛ. english_verse: Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Solomon kɛ Israel maŋ muu fɛɛ ye Asesei Agbijurɔ lɛ gbii kpawo. Asafo yuu diɛŋtsɛ ba kɛjɛ Hamat niiaŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛ Ijipt niiaŋ yɛ wuoyigbɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Solomon wo asafo yuu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ amɛtee. Amɛ jie eyi, ni amɛtee shĩa kɛ miishɛɛ kɛ tsuijurɔ yɛ ejuji fɛɛ ni Yehowa efee etsulɔ David kɛ emaŋ Israel lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: no lɛ makpãtã Israel hiɛ kɛje shikpɔŋ ni miŋɔ hã amɛ lɛ nɔ. Makwa nɛkɛ Sɔlemɔ we nɛɛ ni mifee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ mihã mihe akɛ jɛi aaaja mi yɛ lɛ. Mɛi aaaye Israel he fɛo, ni eeetsɔ̃ nyaŋemɔnɔ yɛ maji krokomɛi ateŋ.

english_verse: They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon saa emãmɔ maji ni akɛ enibii toɔ amɛmli lɛ fɛɛ: maji ni atoɔ etayaa shwiilii kɛ maji ni ekpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi yɔɔ amɛmli, kɛ nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni eshwe akɛ emamɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm kɛ Lebanon kɛ hei ni eyeɔ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
translation_verse: Shi Ijipt maŋtsɛbi yoo lɛ shi David maŋ lɛ mli kɛtee eshĩa ni Solomon emã ehã lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni Solomon saa shikpɔŋ ni kã Yerusalɛm bokãgbɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Afi kome mli lɛ, Solomon shãa afɔlei srɔtoi etɛ̃: eshãa shãa afɔlei kɛ shidaa afɔlei yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ ni emã ehã Yehowa lɛ nɔ; ni eshãa tsofakɛŋma yɛ nɔ ni ma Yehowa hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Belɛ egbe Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mãa lɛ naa.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.

translation_verse: Amɛtee Ofir shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyaŋɔ shika ni tsiimɔ ji talentai ohai ejwɛ kɛ nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni amɛkɛbahã Maŋtsɛ Solomon.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ hã lɛ saji lɛ fɛɛ hetoo, ni eshwɛɛɛ nibimɔ ko ni enyɛɛɛ lɛ hetoo ehã.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: kɛ ekpɔlɔ̃ nɔ niyenii kɛ elumɛi ashitaramɔ kɛ bɔ ni etsuji ni wo atadei fɛɛfɛji sɔmɔɔ yɛ niyeniiashi, kɛ shãa afɔlei ni eshãa yɛ Yehowa we lɛ, ehe jɔ̃ ehe naakpa.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Sheba maŋnyɛ lɛ kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Solomon akɛ, “Ohe saji kɛ onilee ni minu he yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ anɔkwale ni.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: Kulɛ miheee miyeee kɛyashi miba, ni mibana kɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihiŋmɛii nɛɛ. Ni naa, jeee emli fã tete agba mi lɛ; onilee kɛ oshweremɔ lɛ fa aahu fe yijiemɔ ni minu lɛ tete.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Ajɔɔ oŋamɛi kɛ otsuji nɛɛ ni sɔmɔɔ bo ni amɛboɔ onilee wiemɔi lɛ atoi daa lɛ.

english_verse: He was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Solomon tsɔ̃ kpanaa yɛ ninamɔ kɛ nilee mli fe maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ;

english_verse: The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
translation_verse: Esoro shika hu ni jɛɔ jarayelɔi lɛ kɛ guɔyelɔi lɛ kɛ Arabia maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ amraloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ akɛ too ni amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ shuɔ wu fee maŋtsɛ sɛ̃i kpeteŋkple ko, ni ekɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ha he.

english_verse: Since silver was almost worthless in those days, everything was made of gold, even the cups and dishes used in Forest Hall.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon kpuji fɛɛ ni ekɛnuɔ nii lɛ, shika sɔŋŋ akɛfee; ni nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Lebanon Koo Asa lɛ nɔ lɛ, shika ŋmiiŋmi ni; jwiɛtɛi bɛ mli ejaakɛ abuuu no fɛifɛi yɛ Solomon bei amli.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ Tarshish lɛji babaoo yɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ fata Hiram lɛji lɛ ahe. Ni daa afii etɛ̃ lɛ, elɛji lɛ baa shi kome amɛkɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shuɔ wu kɛ ofoi kɛ aduji kɛ mɛleoi baa.

english_verse: People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him.
translation_verse: ni jeŋ fɛɛ tao akɛ amɛbana lɛ koni amɛbo enilee ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhã lɛ lɛ toi.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ba lɛ hiɛ keenii ko kɛba; jwiɛtɛi nibii kɛ shika nibii, atadei wuyawuyaa kɛ tawuu nii kɛ tsofakɛŋmai kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tejiokpɔŋɔi. Daa afi akɛ nibii nɛɛ baa.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon hã jwiɛtɛi bu aahu bɔ ni jwiɛtɛi tsɔ̃ tamɔ tɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm; nakai nɔŋŋ tsenedru tsei hu fa babaoo tamɔ sikamore tsei yɛ Shefela jɔɔ lɛ he.

english_verse: Seven hundred of his wives were daughters of kings, but he also married
translation_verse: Be ni Solomon gbɔ lɛ, eŋãmɛi lɛ etsake lɛ kwraa, ni ekpa yɛ Yehowa eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni eyayeee Yehowa anɔkwa tamɔ etsɛ David fee lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Solomon yaja Astarte, Sidonbii lɛ anyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ Molek, Amonbii lɛ anyɔŋmɔ, ni Yehowa hiɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Solomon fee nɔ ni ji efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni eyeee Yehowa anɔkwa kɛwulaaa shi tamɔ etsɛ David.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Solomon mã jamɔhe ehã Kemosh, Moabbii anyɔŋmɔ ni Yehowa hiɔ lɛ, kɛ Molek ni ji Amonbii anyɔŋmɔ ni Yehowa hiɔ lɛ hu, yɛ Yerusalɛm bokãgbɛ.

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: Ni efee nakai nɔŋŋ ehã eŋãmɛi fɛɛ hu ni jɛ majiasɛɛ, mɛi ni shãa tsofakɛŋma kɛ afɔlei hu amɛhãa amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry,
translation_verse: Yehowa ewo lɛ enɛ he kitã akɛ ekaja nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi; shi Solomon yeee kitã ni Yehowa wo lɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ Solomon akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni oyeee mikpãŋmɔ kɛ mikpɔi lɛ ni miwo bo lɛ anɔ lɛ, shɔ̃ kɛ̃ mashɔ̃ omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ odɛ̃ŋ, ni mikɛaahã otsuji lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ, otsɛ David hewɔ lɛ mifeŋ enɛ yɛ oyinɔ; shi obi ni maŋɔ mahã lɛ dɛŋ mashɔ̃ yɛ.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Asaŋ mishɔŋ omaŋtsɛyeli muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaŋ; maŋɔ akutso kome mahã obi lɛ, yɛ mitsulɔ David kɛ Yerusalɛm ni mihala lɛ hewɔ.” Solomon Henyɛlɔi Lɛ

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa tee henyɛlɔ ko shi ewo Solomon; lɛ ji Hadad, Edomnyo lɛ; ejɛ Edom odehei aweku mli.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Hadad kɛ Tapene nyɛmi yoo lɛ fɔ ebi nuu Genubat. Tapene tse Genubat fufɔ, ni alɛ lɛ yɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli; ni Genubat kɛ maŋtsɛ bihii lɛ hi shi yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Be ni Hadad yɔɔ Ijipt lɛ, enu akɛ David egbo, ni etatsɛ Yoab lɛ hu egbo. Kɛkɛ ni Hadad yakɛɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni maya mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Shi Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Hadad akɛ, “Mɛni po he hiaa bo yɛ biɛ hewɔ ni otaoɔ akɛ oya bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?” Hadad hã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Nɔ ko nɔ ko he ehĩaaa mi, shi kɛ̃lɛ, ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni maya.” Rezon tsɔ̃ Solomon henyɛlɔ

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ tee henyɛlɔ kroko shi ewo Solomon. Lɛ ji Eliada bi Rezon, mɔ ni jo foi kɛjɛ enuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ Hadadezer ni jɛ Zoba lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko hu ni te shi wo Maŋtsɛ Solomon ji etsulɔ Yeroboam, ni ji Nebat, Efraimnyo ko ni jɛ Zereda, bi lɛ. Yeroboam nyɛ ji Zerua, yoo okulafo ko.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Nɔ ni kɛ atuatsemɔ lɛ ba nɛ. Solomon miisaa eetswa Milo ni ji Yerusalɛm gbogbo ni yɔɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ. Gbogbo nɛɛ ni yɔɔ etsɛ maŋ lɛ he lɛ he ko ekumɔ.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Solomon yoo akɛ nɛkɛ nuu Yeroboam nɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ nii waa, hewɔ lɛ ewo lɛ onukpa yɛ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ Manase kɛ Efraimwe lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: Mitsulɔ David hewɔ kɛ Yerusalɛm, maŋ ni mikɔ kɛjɛ Israel akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ hu hewɔ lɛ, Solomon baaye akutso kome nɔ.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Mibafee enɛ, ejaakɛ Solomon ekwa mi, eyaja Astarte, Sidonbii lɛ anyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ Kemosh, Moab nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ Molek, Amonbii anyɔŋmɔ lɛ; ebaaa ejeŋ jogbaŋŋ koni efee jalɛnii ni sa mihiɛ ni eye mikpɔi kɛ mimlai lɛ anɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ David fee lɛ.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mishɔŋ maŋtsɛyeli muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ edɛŋ; shi moŋ mahã eye lumɔ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ. Mafee enɛ yɛ mitsulɔ David mɔ ni mihala ni eye mikitãi kɛ mikpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Mashɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ yɛ Solomon bi dɛŋ, ni maŋɔ emli akutsei nyɔŋma mahã bo.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Shi maŋɔ akutso kome mahã ebi lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni David shwie ko ahi shi ahã lɛ daa yɛ mihiɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm, maŋ ni mikɔ mihã mihe koni aja mi yɛ jɛi lɛ.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Yeroboam, mibawo bo maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel ni oye shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ bɔ ni otaoɔ.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Kɛji ooobo mi toi, ni oooye kitãi ni miwoɔ bo lɛ nɔ, ni oooba ojeŋ jogbaŋŋ, ni ooofee nɔ ni ja yɛ mihiɛ, ni oooye mikpɔi kɛ mikitãi lɛ anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mitsulɔ David fee lɛ, no lɛ mi kɛ bo aaahi shi; mawo bo Israel nɔ maŋtsɛ, ni mahã oshwiei aye lumɔ yɛ osɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni mifee mihã David lɛ.

english_verse: “I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, magbala David shwiei lɛ atoi; shi jeee kɛmiiya naanɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Solomon fee kɛ enitsumɔ kɛ enilee lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Solomon he Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Solomon gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛ David maŋ lɛ mli, ni ebi Rehoboam baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Maŋbii ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ akutsei lɛ amli tsu koni ayaŋɔ lɛ kɛba. Kɛkɛ ni Yeroboam kɛ Israel asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ ba, ni amɛbakɛɛ Rehoboam akɛ

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Rehoboam kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa dã; ni biɛ gbii etɛ̃ lɛ koni nyɛku nyɛsɛɛ nyɛba miŋɔɔ koni nyɛbahe hetoo.” No hewɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ shi lɛ amɛtee.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam bi ŋaawoo kɛjɛ onukpai ni sɔ̃mɔ etsɛ Solomon, be ni eyɔɔ jeŋ lolo lɛ adɛŋ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ ŋaa nyɛwoɔ mi yɛ sane ni maŋbii nɛɛ ebabi mi lɛ hetoo he?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Amɛhã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Kɛji ooofee ohe tsulɔ ohã nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ, ni ooosɔ̃mɔ, ni ooobo amɛtoi, ni okɛ amɛ aaawie yɛ tsuijurɔ naa lɛ, no lɛ amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ otsuji kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam kwa onukpai lɛ aŋaawoo lɛ, ni ekɛ oblahii ni ji etipɛŋfoi ni ekɛje nɔ ni agbɛnɛ amɛtsɔ̃mɔ esɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ moŋ tee ajina.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Ebi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ ŋaa nyɛ hu nyɛwoɔ ni wɔkɛhã maŋbii nɛɛ ni bakɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Feemɔ jatsu kɛ tsiimɔ ni otsɛ kɛtere wɔ lɛ huyɛɛ ohã wɔ lɛ?’ ”

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors.
translation_verse: Rehoboam hã maŋ lɛ hetoo gbonyo. Ekwa ŋaa ni onukpai lɛ wo lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Ekɛ amɛ wie yɛ oblahii lɛ aŋaa ni amɛwo lɛ lɛ naa akɛ, “Miwao sɛɛkpelɔ ti fe mitsɛ hɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsɛ hã nyɛtsu nii keketee moŋ nɛ, shi mi lɛ, mahã nyɛtsu nii keketee fe nakai. Mitsɛ kɛ kpelebii yi nyɛ, shi mi lɛ, mikɛ dade kpelebii baayi nyɛ!”

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ nu akɛ Yeroboam eku esɛɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt kɛba ekoŋŋ lɛ, amɛtsu ayaŋɔ lɛ kɛba Israel asafo muu ni ekpe hiɛ, ni amɛwo lɛ Israel fɛɛ nɔ maŋtsɛ. Mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni nyiɛ David we lɛ sɛɛ akɛ ja Yuda akutso lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ. Shemaia gbalɛ lɛ (

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Be ni Rehoboam yashɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ ebua hii tawulɔi akpei oha kɛ nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ naa kɛjɛ Yuda we lɛ kɛ Benyamin akutso lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ Israel we lɛ ayawu, koni amɛshɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ amɛhã Solomon bi Rehoboam ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Shemaia, Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ, wie akɛ,

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ. ‘Nyɛkayaa, ni asaŋ nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmimɛi Israelbii lɛ akawua. Nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aku esɛɛ eya ewe; ejaakɛ midɛŋ nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ jɛ.’ ” No hewɔ lɛ, Rehoboam kɛ Yudabii kɛ Benyaminbii kɛ maŋbii lɛ bo Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ toi, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛtee amɛshĩai ekoŋŋ yɛ Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ naa. Yeroboam fee shika tsinabii

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam yato Shekem yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni eyahi jɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, ejɛ jɛi ni eyato Penuel hu.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeroboam kɛɛ ehe akɛ, “Bɔ ni nibii yaa lɛ nɛɛ, kɛji mimaŋbii lɛ aaakã he ayaja Yehowa yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, no lɛ maŋbii nɛɛ atsui aaatsɔ̃, ni amɛaagbe mi amɛhã amɛnuŋtsɔ Rehoboam, Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ, koni maŋtsɛyeli lɛ aku sɛɛ aya David we lɛ ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ejwɛŋ sane lɛ he sɛɛ lɛ, efee shika tsinabii amãgãi enyɔ, ni ekɛɛ emaŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Shii abɔ ni nyɛyaa Yerusalɛm nyɛyajaa lɛ efa. Ao Israel, naa onyɔŋmɔi ni yajie bo kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ!”

english_verse: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
translation_verse: Ni eŋɔ shika tsinabii amãgãi lɛ ateŋ ekome emã Betel, ni ekɛ ekome hu mã Dan.

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni enɛ tsɔ̃ esha ehã maŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛyajaa amãgã ni akɛmã Betel lɛ kɛ nɔ ni akɛma Dan tɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Yeroboam mamɔ shĩai yɛ he grɔŋŋi lɛ, ni eŋɔɔ mɛi kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he kɛkɛ, ni ewoɔ amɛ osɔfoi, tsɛbelɛ amɛjɛɛɛ Leviwe lɛ.

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nyɔŋ ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ, gbi ni lɛ pɛ eto lɛ nɔ lɛ, etee eyashã afɔle yɛ Betel yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ ni efee lɛ nɔ. Eto gbijurɔ nɛɛ ehã Israel, no hewɔ ni etee eyashã tsofakɛŋma yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: Yɛ Yehowa famɔ naa lɛ, gbalɔ lɛ gba eshi afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Ao afɔleshãa latɛ, afɔleshãa latɛ, naa, abaafɔ binuu ko yɛ David we lɛ, ni aaatsɛ egbɛi Yosia. Lɛ ebaagbe osɔfoi ni shãa afɔlei yɛ onɔ lɛ, ni gbɔmɛi awui tete lɛ eeeshã yɛ onɔ.”

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Ni gbalɔ lɛ to okadi yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Enɛ ji okadi ni aaatsɔ̃ɔ akɛ Yehowa ŋɔɔ gbalɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ jɛ. Afɔleshãa latɛ nɛɛ abaawule lɛ ashwie shi, ni enɔ lamlu lɛ akɛbaashwã.”

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ wule, ni lamlu ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ shwã tamɔ okadi ni gbalɔ lɛ kɛɛ yɛ Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ naa lɛ.

english_verse: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam kɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, kpa Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fai ni osɔle ohã mi koni atsa minine lɛ ahã mi ekoŋŋ.” No hewɔ lɛ, gbalɔ lɛ kpa Yehowa fai, ni atsa maŋtsɛ lɛ nine lɛ ahã lɛ, ni enine lɛ ba eblema ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ gbalɔ lɛ akɛ, “Ba koni wɔtee shĩa ni oyaye nɔ ko, ni make bo nɔ ko.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Shi gbalɔ lɛ kɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji okɛ omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli fã aaahã mi tete po lɛ, mi kɛ bo eyaŋ, ni asaŋ miyeŋ nii, ni minuŋ nɔ ko yɛ biɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nakai Yehowa wiemɔ fã mi akɛ, kaaye nɔ ko, ni kaanu nu, ni gbɛ ni otsɔ̃ nɔ kɛtee lɛ, kaatsɔ̃ no nɔŋŋ nɔ dɔŋŋ kɛba.”

english_verse: Then he started home down a different road. An Old Prophet from Bethel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, etsɔ̃ gbɛ kroko nɔ kɛtee, ni ekuuu esɛɛ etsɔ̃ɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba Betel lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Betel gbalɔ nuumo lɛ

english_verse: At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ gbalɔ nuumo ko hi shi yɛ Betel. Ebihii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome bagba lɛ nii fɛɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ni jɛ Yuda lɛ etsu yɛ Betel nakai gbi lɛ; egba lɛ wiemɔ ni ekɛ maŋtsɛ Yeroboam wie lɛ hu.

english_verse: “Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road.
translation_verse: Nuumo lɛ bi akɛ, “Be ni eshi jɛi lɛ nɛgbɛ etsɔ̃?” Ni ebii lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ni jɛ Yuda kɛba lɛ tsɔ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
translation_verse: Nuumo lɛ kɛɛ ebii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛwoa teji nɔ nii nyɛhãa mi.” Kɛkɛ ni amɛwo teji nɔ nii amɛhã lɛ, ni eho eta nɔ.

english_verse: and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah. The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?” “Yes, I am.”
translation_verse: Nuumo gbalɔ lɛ tiu Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ni jɛ Yuda lɛ, ni eyanina lɛ ni eta tso agbo ko shishi. Ebi lɛ akɛ, “Ani bo ji Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ni jɛ Yuda ba lɛ?” Ni ehã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Mi ni.”

english_verse: “Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔ nuumo lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ba wɔtee shĩa ni oyaye nii.”

english_verse: “I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you.
translation_verse: Shi gbalɔ ni jɛ Yuda lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minyɛŋ misɛɛ maku ni mikɛ bo aya, ni asaŋ mi kɛ bo yeŋ nii, ni mi kɛ bo enuŋ nu yɛ biɛ.

english_verse: The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa wo mi kitã akɛ, kaaye nii, ni kaanu nɔ ko hu yɛ jɛi, asaŋ kaatsɔ̃ gbɛ ni otsɔ̃ nɔ kɛtee lɛ nɔ kɛmiiba dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ nuumo ni jɛ Betel lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mi hu gbalɔ ji mi tamɔ bo nɔŋŋ, ni Yehowa fã ebɔfo, ni ekɛ mi bawie akɛ, yaakpale lɛ ni okɛ lɛ aba shĩa koni ebaye nii ni enu nu.” Shi gbalɔ nuumo lɛ miimale.

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: ni egba ekɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ni jɛ Yuda eba lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Akɛni obooo Yehowa wiemɔ toi, ni oyeee kitã ni Yehowa oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ wo bo lɛ nɔ,’

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: ni oku osɛɛ oba obaye nii, ni onu nii, yɛ he ni ekɛɛ bo yɛ he akɛ, ‘Kaaye nii, ni kaanu nɔ ko hu yɛ jɛi,’ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, gbo ooogbo, ni ogbonyo eyaŋ otsɛmɛi lɛ afũuhe lɛ.”

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ ni jɛ Yuda lɛ yiŋ etee; shi be ni eyaa lɛ jata ko kɛ lɛ bakpe ni egbe lɛ. Egbonyo lɛ kã gbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni teji lɛ kɛ jata lɛ damɔ emasɛi.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Mɛi komɛi ni batsɔ̃ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ na gbonyo lɛ kã gbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni jata lɛ damɔ gbonyo lɛ masɛi. Ni amɛba amɛbagba yɛ Betel maŋ lɛ mli he ni gbalɔ nuumo lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Be ni gbalɔ nuumo lɛ ni yakpale lɛ kɛjɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛba lɛ nu sane lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ ni yabooo Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ toi lɛ ni; no hewɔ ni Yehowa jie jata ewo ehe lɛ, ni etserɛ emli, ni egbe lɛ yɛ wiemɔ ni Yehowa kɛ lɛ wie lɛ naa nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ ebii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛwoa teji nɔ nii nyɛhãa mi.” Ni amɛwo enɔ nii.

english_verse: he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eyiŋ etee, ni eyana gbonyo lɛ kã gbɛ lɛ nɔ; teji lɛ kɛ jata lɛ damɔ gbonyo lɛ masɛi; jata lɛ yeko gbonyo lɛ, ni esaa etserɛko teji lɛ.

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Gbalɔ nuumo lɛ wo Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ ŋmɛ teji lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ lɛ ku sɛɛ kɛba emaŋ lɛ mli koni amɛbafo lɛ ni amɛfu lɛ.

english_verse: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
translation_verse: Eto gbonyo lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbonyobu mli; ni amɛfo lɛ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Kpoo, minyɛmi nuu!”

english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam efɔ̃ɔɔ efɔŋ ni efeɔ lɛ feemɔ, shi moŋ eŋɔ mɛi komɛi kɛkɛ, ni ewo amɛ hei grɔŋŋi jamɔhei lɛ osɔfoi. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni sumɔɔ akɛ eye osɔfo lɛ, ewoɔ lɛ osɔfo.

english_verse: This sinful thing led to the downfall of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ enifeemɔ nɛɛ batsɔ̃ esha kpele ehã Yeroboam we lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni hã emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ gbee shi.

english_verse: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ Yeroboam bi Abia he baye.

english_verse: She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah was now old and blind,
translation_verse: Yeroboam ŋa lɛ fee nakai, ni etee Shilo, ni eba Ahia we lɛ. Shi Ahia enaaa nii, ejaakɛ gbɔlɛ ehã ehiŋmɛii anɔ eha.

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: Shi be ni eshɛ shinaa lɛ shi ni Ahia nu enaneshi gbɛɛmɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ba mli, Yeroboam ŋa! Mɛɛba otsake ohe tamɔ mɔ kroko nɛɛ? Naa, atsu mi oŋɔɔ kɛ sane ko ni wa.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Yaa, ni oyakɛɛ Yeroboam akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Mikɔ bo pɛ yɛ mimaŋ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ, ni miwo bo maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: Mishɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ tete yɛ David we lɛ dɛŋ mihã bo; shi kɛ̃lɛ otamɔɔɔ mitsulɔ David ni eye mikitãi anɔ ni enyiɛ misɛɛ kɛ etsui fɛɛ lɛ. Efee nɔ ni sa sɔŋŋ yɛ mihiɛ.

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: Shi bo lɛ, ofee efɔŋ fe mɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ ohiɛ lɛ. Oto oyiŋ, ni oyafee nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi kɛ amãgãi ni ashwie ohã ohe, ni okɛwo mimli la; ni mi lɛ oshɛ mi ofɔ̃ osɛɛ kwa.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, naa, mahã sane fɔŋ aye Yereboam we lɛ. Maplene Yereboam we lɛ mli nuu fɛɛ nuu hiɛ yɛ Israel: nyɔŋ kɛ mɔ ni eye ehe fɛɛ. Makpãtã Yeroboam we lɛ hiɛ kwraa tamɔ abɛɔ wamɔ, ni awoɔ mli la yɛ tumo nɔ ashãa kɛyashiɔ beyinɔ ni fɛɛ shãa wɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Israel fɛɛ aaafo lɛ, ni amɛaafu lɛ; ejaakɛ lɛ pɛ ejɛ Yeroboam we lɛ mli ni aaafu lɛ; ejaakɛ lɛ pɛ emli ana nɔ kpakpa ko yɛ yɛ Yeroboam we lɛ ni sa Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Yehowa baatee maŋtsɛ ko shi ahã ehe yɛ Israel, mɔ ni baakpãtã Yeroboam we lɛ hiɛ ŋmɛnɛ, amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeroboam ŋa lɛ te shi, ni eyi mli etee Tirza. Be ni eshɛ shĩa lɛ shinaa lɛ shi lɛ pɛ, kɛkɛ ni gbekɛ lɛ gbo.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Israel fɛɛ fo lɛ, ni amɛfu lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa wie kɛtsɔ̃ etsulɔ gbalɔ Ahia nɔ lɛ. Yeroboam Gbele

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yeroboam he saji fɛɛ, nii ni efee, bɔ ni ewu tai kɛ bɔ ni eye maŋtsɛ ehã lɛ, aŋma yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Yudabii lɛ fee esha shi Yehowa, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe eshai ni amɛfee lɛ hã Yehowa ye awuŋã. Eshai ni amɛfee lɛ fa kwraa fe nii ni amɛblematsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛ hu amɛmãmɔ jamɔhei grɔŋŋi amɛhã amɛhe; amɛkɛ tɛi mãmɔ shiui kɛ Ashera amãgãi, ni amɛjaa yɛ gɔŋkpɔ fɛɛ gɔŋkpɔ ni kwɔ nɔ kɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni ebu kusuu shishi.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ ji akɛ, hii kɛ yei yɛ jɛi ni kɛ amɛhe bɔɔ ajwamãŋ yɛ jamɔhei lɛ. Yudabii lɛ fee hiɛgbejianii ni jeŋmaji abii ni Yehowa shwie yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ fee lɛ.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ijipt Maŋtsɛ Shishak fã ta ebatua Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Ebaloo Yehowa we lɛ mli jwetri lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli jwetri lɛ; eloo fɛɛ kwa kɛtee. Esaa eloo shika tsɛŋi lɛ ni Solomon fee lɛ kɛtee.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam hã afee akɔɔble tsɛŋi eto najiaŋ, ni etu fɛɛ ewo bulɔi ni buɔ maŋtsɛwe lɛ agbo lɛ naa lɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Be fɛɛ be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ yaa Yehowa we lɛ bulɔi lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋi lɛ, ni kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ amɛkɛkuɔ sɛɛ amɛkɛyatoɔ bulɔi lɛ atsu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Rehoboam he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Rehoboam gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ afũuhe ni yɔɔ David maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni enyɛ gbɛi ji Naama, Amonyoo lɛ. Ni ebi Abia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Asa kpa enyɛ Maaka tete maŋnyɛyeli; ejaakɛ enyɛ nɛɛ fee Ashera amãgã ko ni eji nihii nii. Asa folɔ tso amãgã lɛ mli, ni eyashã yɛ Kidron jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Be ni Nebat bi Yeroboam eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ yɛ Israel lɛ, no mli Abia bɔ̃i maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Yuda.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Asa hã ashiɛ yɛ Yuda fɛɛ, ashiii mɔ ko mɔ ko yɛ mli. Maŋbii lɛ tee Rama ni amɛyaloo Rama tɛi lɛ kɛ mplaŋi lɛ ni Baasha kɛtswaa gbogbo ewo Rama he lɛ kɛba. Maŋtsɛ Asa kɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ yawaje Geba, ni yɔɔ Benyamin kpokpai anɔ lɛ kɛ Mizpa.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Eshai ni etsɛ fee kɛtsɔ̃ hiɛ lɛ, nomɛi nɔŋŋ lɛ hu efee, ni eyeee Yehowa eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ anɔkwa tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ David ye anɔkwa lɛ.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Yehowa fee enɛ, ejaakɛ David fee nɔ ni sa Yehowa hiɛ, ni egbaaa afã yɛ kitãi ni ewo lɛ lɛ eko eko he ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ, akɛ ja yɛ Uria, Hitnyo lɛ, sane lɛ mli pɛ.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Abia he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Abia gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli, ni ebi Asa baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa (

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nibii fɛɛ ni etsɛ Abia fee, kɛ nii ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu efee ni atsuu he yɛ tsuijurɔ naa ahã Yehowa lɛ, eyaloo kɛba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ: jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika kɛ tsɛnsii fɛɛ.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha Maŋtsɛyeli beiaŋ fɛɛ lɛ ta kã amɛteŋ.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Asa fee nɔ ni sa Yehowa hiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni eblematsɛ David fee lɛ.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Be ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam eye afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ yɛ Israel sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ lɛ, no mli Asa bɔ̃i maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Yuda.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Eshwie hii kɛ yei fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe bɔɔ ajwamãŋ yɛ jamɔhei lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ejie amãgãi ni etsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ fɛɛ hu.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Yɛ mli akɛ Asa fiteee jamɔhei grɔŋŋi lɛ moŋ nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ eye Yehowa anɔkwa ewala bei abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha fã ta kɛbatua Yuda, ni eŋɔ Rama. Kɛkɛ ni etswa gbogbo ewo Rama he bɔ ni afee ni mɔ ko mɔ ko akaje kpo kɛmiiya Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa ŋɔɔ aloo eeje eŋɔɔ kɛmiiba.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Asa loo shika fɛɛ kɛ jwiɛtɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ Yehowa We lɛ nitoohe lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ nitoohe lɛ hu; etu ewo etsuji lɛ adɛŋ, ni etsu amɛ kɛtee Damasko koni akɛyahã Siria Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad, Tabrimon bi, ni eji Hezion nabi lɛ. Wiemɔ ni fata he ji:

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
