translation_verse: “Hã kpãŋmɔ ko akã mi kɛ bo teŋ tamɔ bɔ ni ekã mitsɛ kɛ otsɛ teŋ lɛ. Naa, miimaje jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika nikeenii. Yaa ni oyaku kpãŋmɔ ni kã okɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha teŋ lɛ mli, koni ejie etabilɔi lɛ kɛje mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad kpɛlɛ̃ Maŋtsɛ Asa wiemɔ lɛ nɔ, ni etsu etatsɛmɛi kɛtee ni amɛyatua Israel maji lɛ. Tatsɛmɛi lɛ ŋɔ maji nɛɛ: Yion kɛ Dan kɛ Abel-Bet-Maaka kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ Galilea kpaakpo lɛ kɛ Naftali kpokpai anɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ Baasha nu nɔ ni eba lɛ he lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ gbogbo lɛ tswaa kɛ Rama he woo, ni etee eyahi shi yɛ Tirza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Maŋtsɛ Asa he saji fɛɛ ni eshwɛ kɛ ekãa ni efee, kɛ nii fɛɛ kɛ maji ni ewajewaje lɛ aŋma yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Asaji Awolo lɛ mli. Shi egbɔlɛ be mli lɛ, nane hela ko kumɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Be ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa eye afii enyɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam bi Nadab baye maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel. Eye maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel afii enyɔ.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Efee efɔŋ tamɔ etsɛ ni nyiɛ ehiɛ lɛ fee ni ekɛhã Israel fee esha lɛ.

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah was from the tribe of Issachar, and he made plans to kill Nadab. When Nadab and his army went to attack the town of Gibbethon in Philistia, Baasha killed Nadab there. So in the third year of Asa's rule, Baasha became king of Israel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Baasha gbe Nadab be ni Asa eye maŋtsɛ afii etɛ̃ yɛ Yuda. Kɛkɛ ni lɛ Baasha lɛ ebaye Nadab sɛɛ akɛ maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni Baasha baye maŋtsɛ lɛ, egbe Yeroboam we lɛ mli bii lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni muɔ tete yɛ Yeroboam we lɛ. Efee enɛ koni wiemɔ ni Yehowa wie kɛtsɔ̃ etsulɔ Ahia, Shilonyo lɛ, nɔ lɛ aba mli.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Eba mli nɛkɛ ejaakɛ Yeroboam fee eshai eshi Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ no hã Israel fɛɛ hu fee esha kɛwo Yehowa mli la.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Nadab he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ aŋma yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Ni ta kã Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha teŋ amɛwala beiaŋ fɛɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Be ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa ye afii etɛ̃ yɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, no mli Ahia bi Baasha babɔ̃i Israel fɛɛ nɔ maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Tirza; ni eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ejwɛ.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Efee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; eba ejeŋ gbonyo tamɔ Yeroboam ni hã Israel fɛɛ fee esha lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Hanani bi Yehu wie, ni ekɛ shɛɛ nɛɛ hã lɛ akɛ ekɛyahã Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha:

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “Kulɛ ojeee mɔ ko, shi miwo onɔ kɛjɛ mlu mli, ni mifee bo lumɔ kɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔ yɛ mimaŋ Israel. Oyakɔ Yeroboam jeŋba lɛ, ni ohã mimaŋ Israel fee esha, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe eshai lɛ wo mimli la.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ mibabɛɛ Baasha kɛ ewe lɛ mashwie, ni mibafee ewe lɛ tamɔ mifee Nebat bi Yeroboam we lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Baasha wekunyo fɛɛ wekunyo ni aaagbo yɛ maŋ lɛ, gbei aaaye egbonyo lɛ; ni ewekunyo ni aaagbo yɛ ŋa nɔ lɛ, ŋwɛi loofɔji aaaye eloo.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Yehowa wiemɔ ni ekɛshiɔ Baasha kɛ ewe lɛ akɛtsɔ̃ Hanani bi Yehu nɔ, yɛ eshai ni Baasha fee eshi Yehowa lɛ ahewɔ. Baasha wo Yehowa mli la, jeee yɛ nibii fɔ̃ji ni efee, tamɔ bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam efee kɛtsɔ̃ ehiɛ momo lɛ kɛkɛ ahewɔ, shi moŋ akɛ egbe Yeroboam we lɛ mlibii fɛɛ lɛ. Ela ye Israel Maŋtsɛ

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Baasha musuŋ binuu Ela bɔ̃i Israel maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Tirza. Eye maŋtsɛ afii enyɔ.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omri fee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hiɛ. Efee esha fe maŋtsɛmɛi ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Shi etsulɔ Zimri, etayaa shwiili lɛ amlijaa fã kome ko nɔ asafoiatsɛ lɛ, kpãŋ eyinɔ. Gbi ko be ni Maŋtsɛ Ela etɔ dãa kpɔtɔɔ yɛ etsulɔ Arza, mɔ ni kwɛɔ Tirza maŋtsɛwe lɛ nɔ lɛ we lɛ mli lɛ,

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Zimri bote Arza we lɛ mli, ni eyatswa Maŋtsɛ Ela nɔ, ni egbe lɛ. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ sane nɛɛ ba. Kɛkɛ ni Zimri baye Israel maŋtsɛ yɛ Ela sɛɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ ni shɛ Zimri dɛŋ nɔŋŋ pɛ, kɛkɛ ni egbe Baasha we lɛ mlibii fɛɛ, eshiii Baasha we lɛ mli nuu kome nɛkɛ; egbe kɛ Baasha nanemɛi tete hu.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Belɛ Zimri kpãtã Baasha we lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm hiɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa etsɔ̃ gbalɔ Yehu nɔ ewie eshi Baasha,

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: yɛ eshai fɛɛ ni Baasha fee kɛ eshai ni ebi Ela hu fee, ni amɛkɛhã Israel fee esha, ni amɛkɛ amãgãjamɔ wo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mli la lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni Ela fee kɛ ehe saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, aŋma yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli. Israel Maŋtsɛ Zimri

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Gbi ni tabilɔi lɛ nu akɛ Zimri etee Maŋtsɛ Ela yinɔ apam, ni egbe lɛ lɛ, Israel tso muu fɛɛ wo Omri ni ji tabilɔi lɛ atsɛ lɛ Israel maŋtsɛ gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ta lɛ naa.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Omri fã kɛjɛ Gibeton kɛba ni Israel fɛɛ fata ehe, ni amɛbasa Tirza yi.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Be ni Zimri na akɛ aŋɔ maŋ lɛ, eyabote maŋtsɛwe lɛ mɔɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ ni ema maŋtsɛwe lɛ naa la, ni eshã shĩa lɛ eshwie enɔ, ni egbo.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Egbo yɛ eshai ni efee, kɛ efɔŋ ni efee yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, kɛ Yeroboam jeŋba lɛ ni ekɔ efɔ̃ enɔ lɛ hewɔ, asaŋ kɛ efɔŋ ni efee ni ekɛhã Israel hu fee esha lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Nibii krokomɛi ni Zimri fee kɛ Maŋtsɛ Ela yinɔ apam ni etee lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli. Israel Maŋtsɛ Omri

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel maŋ lɛ mli gba enyɔ; maŋ lɛ fã kome yɛ Ginat bi Tibni lɛ sɛɛ akɛ lɛ eye maŋtsɛ, ni fã hu yɛ Omri sɛɛ.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ ekome lɛ nɔ. Omri ye Israel maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ. Eye maŋtsɛ lɛ afii ekpaa yɛ Tirza. Samaria tsɔ̃ Israel Maŋtsɛ maŋ

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ebakɔ Nebat bi Yeroboam jeŋba lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehã maŋbii lɛ bote eshafeemɔ kɛ amãgãjamɔ mli, nifeemɔ ni woɔ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ mli la lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Omri he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni efee, kɛ ekãa ni efee lɛ aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Omri gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ Samaria; kɛkɛ ni ebi Ahab baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Ahab ye Israel Maŋtsɛ

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Ato Omri bi Ahab maŋtsɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ. Ahab ye Israel maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enyɔ yɛ Samaria.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omri bi Ahab fee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ fe maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Akɛni eshai ni Nebat bi Yeroboam fee lɛ jeee fɛifɛi yɛ Ahab hiɛ hewɔ lɛ, etee nɔ, ni eyaŋɔ Sidonbii amaŋtsɛ Etbaal biyoo Yezebel lɛ akɛ ŋa. No hewɔ lɛ, Ahab tee ni eyaja, ni esɔ̃mɔ Baal.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Emã afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli ehã Baal.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ hu eshɔ̃ jemawɔŋ yoo Ashera lɛ amãgã ema shi. Ahab wo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mli la waa fe Israel maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ kɛho.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Ahab yinɔ ni Hiel, Betelnyo lɛ, yasaa etswa Yeriko maŋ lɛ mli tsui koikoi lɛ. Hiel kromɔbi ni egbɛi ji Abiram lɛ nyɔ yɛ Yeriko saamɔ lɛ shishitoo mli, ni ebi sɛɛkpelɔ Segub hu nyɔ be mli ni ataraa maŋ lɛ naa agboi lɛ. Sane nɛɛ ba mli nɛkɛ taakɛ Yehowa etsɔ̃ Nunbi Yoshua nɔ egba eto momo lɛ.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔ ko ni gbɛi ji Elia, Tishbinyo ni ejɛ Gilead, lɛ kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahab akɛ, “Miikɛɛ bo, yɛ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ, mɔ ni misɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ, gbɛi mli akɛ bɔ enyɔŋ, ni nu hu enɛŋ kɛyashi biɛ afii enyɔ loo afii etɛ̃, bɛja mi, miwie dã.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Elia akɛ,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Shi biɛ nɛɛ koni oya bokãgbɛ oyatee ohe yɛ Kerit faa nine lɛ masɛi yɛ Yordan lɛ bokãgbɛ.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Obaana faa nine lɛ mli nu onu, ni mifã kwãakwãalabitei koni amɛlɛ bo yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Kwãakwãalabitei lɛ yahãa lɛ aboloo kɛ loo daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ, ni faa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nu ni enuɔ.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Shi be ko sɛɛ lɛ, faa lɛ baŋala, ejaakɛ nu enɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Elia kɛ Zarefat Okulafo lɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Elia akɛ,

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ yaa Zarefat, Sidonbii amaŋ lɛ mli, koni oyahi jɛi. Mifã yoo okulafo ko koni elɛ bo yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Elia yi mli, ni etee Zarefat. Be ni eshɛ maŋ lɛ agbo lɛ naa lɛ, ena yoo okulafo ko yɛ jɛi ni eebua lai ŋmɛŋmlɛbii anaa. Elia kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni ohã mi nu fioo manu.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Be ni yoo lɛ yaa koni eyayɛ nu lɛ, Elia tsɛ eyisɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ ni oŋɔ aboloo atrɔma ko ohiɛ odɛ̃ obahã mi.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Yoo okulafo lɛ to he akɛ, “Mina Yehowa hiɛkãalɔ, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, akɛ mibɛ aboloo kuku nɛkɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni miyɔɔ ji mamu dɛ̃ kɔkɔ obɔ̃ kome pɛ yɛ gbɛ mli, kɛ mu fioo yɛ tɔ mli. Miilɛ lai ŋmɛŋmlɛbii enyɔ oo ko koni mikɛyashã aboloo mahã mi kɛ mibi lɛ koni wɔye; no sɛɛ lɛ wɔɔgboi kɛ hɔmɔ.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Elia kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei! Yaa koni oyafee bɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ. Shi moŋ ŋɔɔ mamu lɛ eko okɛshã aboloo fioo ko obahã mi tsuutsu dã; no sɛɛ dani ofee bo kɛ obi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Mamu kɛ gbɛ lɛ etaŋ, ni mu kɛ tɔ lɛ hu etaŋ aahu kɛyashi gbi nɔ ni Yehowa aaahã nu abanɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ yi mli etee, ni eyafee bɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni Elia kɛɛ lɛ lɛ; ni Elia kɛ yoo lɛ kɛ ewe lɛ na nii amɛye gbii kplaŋŋ.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Taakɛ Yehowa tsɔ̃ Elia nɔ ekɛɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, mamu kɛ gbɛ lɛ etãaa, ni mu kɛ tɔ lɛ hu etãaa. Elia tsiɛ̃ Okulafo lɛ Binuu hiɛ

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ saji nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, yoo lɛ ni ji shĩanyɛ lɛ, binuu lɛ he baye; ehela lɛ mli wo wu, ni naagbee lɛ egbo.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni yoo lɛ kɛɛ Elia akɛ, “Ao Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ, mɛni mifee bo! Obato mi koni akai efɔŋ ni mifee, koni agbe mibinuu lɛ lo?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Elia kɛɛ yoo lɛ akɛ, “Kɛ obi lɛ ahã mi!” Elia he gbekɛ lɛ yɛ yoo lɛ kpɔkɔiaŋ; kɛkɛ ni ehiɛ lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi tsu lɛ mli he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ gbekɛ lɛ yaŋmɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esaa nɔ.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia bo etsɛ Yehowa, ni ekɛɛ, “Ao Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ! Aso yoo okulafo ni mibato eŋɔɔ nɛɛ hu okɛyeɔ sane kɛ joomɔ nɛkɛ, ni ogbeɔ ebi lɛ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Elia ho ekpã emli ebu gbekɛ lɛ nɔ shii etɛ̃. Kɛkɛ ni ebo waa etsɛ Yehowa ekɛɛ, “Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ! Miikpa bo fai; hã gbekɛ nɛɛ mumɔ akpale aba emli ekoŋŋ koni ehiɛ atsɛ̃!”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ lɛ bo Elia faikpamɔ lɛ toi, ni gbekɛ lɛ mumɔ kpale kɛba emli ekoŋŋ, ni ehiɛ tsɛ̃.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Elia wo gbekɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ kpeleke shi kɛjɛ ŋwɛi tsu lɛ mli kɛba shĩa lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ bahã enyɛ lɛ; ni Elia kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa obi lɛ; eyi ena wala.”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Yoo lɛ here Elia nɔ ekɛɛ, “Kpaako mina mile akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ ji bo lɛɛlɛŋ, ni asaŋ Yehowa wieɔ kɛtsɔ̃ɔ onɔ!”

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: ejaakɛ be ni Yezebel kpãtãa gbalɔi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, Obadia ŋɔ gbalɔi oha, ni ekɛ amɛ tee tɛkploi enyɔ amli, mɛi nyɔŋmai enumɔenumɔ, ni ekɛ aboloo kɛ nu lɛ amɛ.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Ahab kɛɛ Obadia akɛ, “Yaa koni oyakpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei fɛɛ ni nuhiŋmɛii kɛ jɔi yɔɔ akɛ eko lɛ wɔɔna jwɛi yɛ he ko koni wɔkɛhere okpɔŋɔi lɛ ayiwala, koni shĩa kooloi fɛɛ akaŋmɛɛ wɔ.”

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahab kɛ Obadia ja shikpɔŋ lɛ mli enyɔ amɛhã amɛhe, koni amɛyakpa nɔ kɛho.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Be ni Obadia nyiɛ gbɛ eyaa lɛ, ekɛ Elia yakpe trukaa. Be ni Obadia yoo Elia lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Ani bo, minuŋtsɔ Elia, nɛ?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Obadia to he akɛ, “Mɛɛ efɔŋ mifee hewɔ ni okɛ otsulɔ woɔ nɛkɛ haomɔ mli nɛɛ?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Mina Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, akɛ maŋ ko maŋ ko loo nɔyelihe ko nɔyelihe ko kwraa bɛ jeŋ ni minuŋtsɔ tsuko kɛyako jɛi akɛ ayatao bo ahã lɛ. Kɛji he ko bii kɛ wiemɔ ba akɛ, ‘Ebɛ biɛ lɛ,’ ehãa nakai maŋtsɛyeli loo maŋ lɛ kãa lɛ kitã akɛ amɛnako bo lɛɛlɛŋ.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Shi ŋmɛnɛ, naa bo ni ookɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Yaakɛɛ onuŋtsɔ akɛ, naa, Elia yɛ biɛ.’

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Amrɔ pɛ ni mibashi bo matee lɛ, Yehowa Mumɔ lɛ aaabakpla bo kɛya he ko ni mileee. Kɛji mitee miyakɛɛ Ahab, ni eba, ni ebaninaaa bo lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, ebaagbe mi. Kaimɔ akɛ Yehowa jalɔ ji otsulɔ kɛjɛ migbekɛbiiashi beebe.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Elia hã hetoo ekɛɛ, “Mina Yehowa hiɛkãalɔ, Ofe lɛ, mɔ ni misɔmɔɔ lɛ, akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ mikɛ mihe baatsɔ̃ɔ Ahab ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Obadia yi mli etee, ni eyabɔ Ahab amaniɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Ahab yiŋ koni ekɛ Elia ayakpe.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Be ni Ahab na Elia lɛ, Ahab kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bo Israel haolɔ lɛ, bo nɛ?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Elia to he ekɛɛ, “Mihaoko Israel! Bo kɛ otsɛ we lɛ moŋ ni ehao Israel, ejaakɛ nyɛkwa Yehowa kitãi lɛ, ni nyɛtee nyɛmiija Baal moŋ.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ahab tsu atee, ni ayatsɛ Israelbii fɛɛ kɛba; asaŋ ebua gbalɔi lɛ hu anaa kɛbakpe yɛ Karmel Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia tsi ebɛŋkɛ asafo muu ni ewo shi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ nyɛyiŋ aaafee nyɛ enyɔnyɔɔnyɔ kɛyashi yɛ saji enyɔ nɛɛ ahe? Kɛji Yehowa ji Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, nyɛjaa lɛ, ni kɛji Baal ji Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ nyɛjaa lɛ.” Shi maŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko etswaaa esɛŋ.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Abahã wɔ tsinahii enyɔ. Baal webii lɛ amɔ tsinai lɛ ateŋ ekome, nɔ ni amɛ amɛsumɔɔ amɛhã amɛhe; amɛgbe tsina lɛ koni amɛfolɔ emli dukuduku, ni amɛkɛ loo lɛ ashwie lai nɔ; shi moŋ amɛkawo eshishi la. Mi hu masaa tsinanuu kome lɛ, koni mikɛ eloo lɛ ashwie lai nɔ; ni mi hu miwoŋ minɔ lɛ shishi la.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛsɔlea nyɛtsɛa nyɛnyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni mi hu masɔle matsɛ Yehowa; amɛteŋ mɔ ni kɛ la baahere tsɛmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ.” Maŋbii lɛ here nɔ kɛɛ akɛ, “Eja nakai!”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ Baal gbalɔi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛmɔa tsinahii lɛ ateŋ ekome nyɛhãa nyɛhe, ni nyɛ tsuutsu nyɛsaa nyɛkooloo lɛ, ejaakɛ nyɛ lɛ nyɛyi fa; no sɛɛ lɛ nyɛsɔlea kɛtsɛa nyɛnyɔŋmɔ lɛ; shi moŋ nyɛkasɔa lai lɛ naa la.”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Baal gbalɔi lɛ mɔ tsinanuu ni akɛhã amɛ lɛ, ni amɛsaa, ni amɛsɔle kɛ blɔmɔ amɛtsɛ Baal kɛjɛ leebileebi aahu kɛyashi shwane fintiŋŋ amɛkɛɛ, “Baal, heremɔ wɔ nɔ!” Amɛtumɔ kɛbɔle afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni amɛmã lɛ, shi anuuu gbee ko lɛ, nɔheremɔ ko hu jɛɛɛ he ko baaa.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Shwane mli lɛ Elia ye Baal gbalɔi lɛ ahe fɛo, ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛbolɔa waa, ejaakɛ nyɔŋmɔ ji lɛ! Eko lɛ benɛ eeshwie eyiŋ, aloo eje kpo, aloo edom, aloo eko lɛ ewɔ koni ehiɛ atsɛ̃.”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbalɔi lɛ bolɔ waa fe tsuutsu lɛ, ni amɛkɛ kakla kɛ klante folɔflɔɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛkusum naa kɛyashi lá bɔ̃i hoo yɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Amɛtee nɔ kɛ blɔmɔ hoo lɛ kɛyashi eshɛ shwane niyenii afɔleshãa be; shi fɛɛ lɛ gbee ko ejijeee lɛ, hetoo ko baaa.

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtsia nyɛbɛŋkɛa mi.” Maŋ lɛ tsi bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Elia saa Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ ni ekumɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: ni ekɛ tɛi lɛ mã afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ Yehowa gbɛi mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, etsa bu ni baaye nu litai nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ kɛbɔle afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he kpula.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Nu lɛ tsere kɛnyiɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he kɛbote latɛ lɛ he bu lɛ mli; bu lɛ yi obɔ̃ kɛ nu lɛ.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Shwane niyenii afɔle be lɛ, Gbalɔ Elia tsi ebɛŋkɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni esɔle ekɛɛ, “Ao Yehowa, Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ, hã ana ale ŋmɛnɛ akɛ bo ji Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, asaŋ akɛ bo otsulɔ ji mi, ni owiemɔ naa mifeɔ nii nɛɛ fɛɛ yɛ.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Heremɔ mi nɔ! Ao Yehowa, heremɔ mi nɔ, koni maŋ nɛɛ kɛna ale akɛ bo, Yehowa, ji Nyɔŋmɔ; ni asaŋ akɛ bo nɔŋŋ oŋɔɔ amɛtsuii ekpale kɛba ekoŋŋ!”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa hã la gba kɛbabote afɔle lɛ mli, ni eshã afɔle lɛ kɛ lai lɛ kɛ tɛi lɛ kɛ su lɛ, ni nu lɛ tete ni yɔɔ bu ni bɔle afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ mli lɛ ŋala wɛɛ.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Be ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ na nɔ ni eba lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhiɛiaŋ bumɔ shi, ni amɛbolɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Yehowa lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ! Yehowa lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ!”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia fã maŋbii lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛmɔmɔa Baal gbalɔi lɛ; akahã amɛteŋ mɔ kome nɛkɛ miijo foi!” Amɔmɔ Baal gbalɔi lɛ, ni Elia ŋɔ amɛ kɛkpeleke shi kɛtee Kishon Faa lɛ naa, ni eyagbe amɛ yɛ jɛi. Nuhɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ yaa koni oyaye nii ni onu nɔ ko ejaakɛ minu nugbɔ shiimɔ he kɛmiiba.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahab yi mli etee koni eyaye nii, asaŋ ni enu nɔ ko; shi Elia kwɔ kɛtee Karmel Gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ; edɔ emli, ni ekɛ eyitso hɔ enakutsei ateŋ.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ etsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Kwɔɔ kɛya gɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ ŋshɔŋgbɛ.” Tsulɔ lɛ tee eba, ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ. “Nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ jɛi gbɛ.” Elia kɛɛ etsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa shii kpawo ni oyakwɛ.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Shii kpawo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ Elia akɛ, “Naa, atatu bibioo ko ni edaaa fe gbɔmɔ nine miite shi kɛmiijɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli.” Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ etsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Yaakɛɛ Ahab akɛ, ‘Saamɔ otayaa shwiili lɛ koni okpeleke shi koni nu lɛ akatsi onaa.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Ahab bagba eŋa Yezebel nibii fɛɛ ni Elia efee lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni etsɔ̃ ekɛ klante gbe gbalɔi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yezebel tsu bɔfo kɛtee Elia ŋɔɔ ayakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔi lɛ atswa mi nɔ koni magbo kɛji wɔ benɛ yinɔ lɛ mifeko bo bɔ ni ofee gbalɔi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Elia she gbeyei, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ete shi, ni ejo foi koni ehere esusuma yiwala. Etee Beersheba yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshi etsulɔ lɛ yɛ jɛi,

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: ni ekome enyiɛ gbi kome jenamɔ gbɛ kɛtee ŋa lɛ nɔ. Eyata shi yɛ tso kusuu ko shishi, ni ebɔ̃i gbele shwee. Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ao Yehowa, efa agbɛnɛ, ejaakɛ mihiii fe mitsɛmɛi lɛ.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eho ekã tso kusuu lɛ shishi, ni ewɔ. Trukaa lɛ ŋwɛi bɔfo ko bata ehe, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Tee shi koni oye nii!”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Elia kwɛ ehe, ni ena aboloo ni ashã yɛ tɛi ni edɔ anɔ kɛ kpulu kɛ nu ma eyitsogbɛ. Eye nii lɛ, ni enu nu lɛ, kɛkɛ ni eho ekã shi ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia te shi, ni eye nii, ni enu nu eshwie nɔ. Niyenii nɛɛ mli hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hã enyɛ enyiɛ shwaneshwane kɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ gbii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛtee Nyɔŋmɔ Gɔŋ Horeb lɛ he.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Eyashɛ tɛkplo ko he yɛ jɛi, ni ewɔ jɛi nakai gbi lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ. Trukaa lɛ Yehowa bi lɛ yɛ jɛi akɛ, “Elia, mɛni ofeɔ yɛ biɛ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Elia to he ekɛɛ, “Miye Yehowa, Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ, he awuŋã kɛ hiɛdɔɔ, ejaakɛ Israelbii lɛ ekwa Bo kɛ amɛteŋ kpãŋmɔ lɛ, amɛkumɔ ofɔleshãa latɛi lɛ, ni amɛkɛ klante egbe ogbalɔi lɛ hu, ni mi, mi pɛ eshwɛ, ni amɛmiitao mi hu amɛgbe.” Elia kɛ Yehowa kpe yɛ Horeb

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Elia akɛ, “Jee kpo koni oyadamɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa baaho.” Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa baho: ahum ni naa wa ko tswa, ni egbala gɔji, ni ejwra tɛsai kɛnyiɛ Yehowa hiɛ; shi Yehowa bɛ ahum lɛ mli. Ahum lɛ sɛɛ lɛ shikpɔŋ hoso, shi Yehowa bɛ shikpɔŋhosomɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hosomɔ sɛɛ lɛ, la je; shi Yehowa bɛ la lɛ mli; ni la lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ nyrakee ko gbɛɛ kɛho.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Be ni Elia nu gbɛɛmɔ nyrakee lɛ he lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ hɔ etade yuu lɛ mli, kɛkɛ ni eje kpo, ni eyadamɔ tɛkplo lɛ naa. Kɛkɛ ni gbee ko bi lɛ akɛ, “Elia, mɛni ofeɔ yɛ biɛ?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Elia jie enaa ekɛɛ, “Miye Yehowa, Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ, he awuŋã kɛ hiɛdɔɔ, ejaakɛ Israelbii lɛ ekwa Bo kɛ amɛteŋ kpãŋmɔ lɛ, amɛkumɔ ofɔleshãa latɛi lɛ, ni amɛkɛ klante egbe ogbalɔi lɛ hu ni mi pɛ eshwɛ, ni amɛmiitao mi hu amɛgbe.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Elia akɛ. “Kuu osɛɛ ni oya Damasko ŋa lɛ nɔ; otsɔ̃ jɛi kɛbote maŋ lɛ mli, koni ofɔ Hazael mu okɛwo lɛ Siria maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, ofɔ Nimshi bi Yehu hu mu okɛwo lɛ Israel maŋtsɛ, asaŋ ofɔ Shafat ni jɛ Abel-Mehola lɛ bi Elisha lɛ mu kɛwo lɛ gbalɔ, mɔ ni baaye onajiaŋ.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Naa, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaaje Hazael klante naa gbele mli lɛ, Yehu baagbe lɛ, ni mɔ ni baaje Yehu klante naa gbele mli lɛ, Elisha baagbe lɛ.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Elia shi jɛi; eyanina Shafat bi Elisha ni eekwɛ tsinai ntai ni miihu nɔ. Tsinai ntai nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ nyiɛ ehiɛ, ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ekɛ naagbee tsinai nta lɛ miihu. Be ni Elia hoɔ Elisha he lɛ, ejie etade yuu ni ewo lɛ, ni ekɛwo Elisha.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Elisha shi tsinai lɛ, ni esha foi kɛyi Elia sɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Hã maya koni mayashɔ mitsɛ kɛ minyɛ naa koni mikɛ amɛ aye shɛɛ dani mabanyiɛ osɛɛ.” Elia to he ekɛɛ, “Kuu osɛɛ koni oya, shi moŋ ohiɛ ahi nɔ ni mifee bo lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elisha ku esɛɛ, ni eyamɔmɔ tsinai nta ni ekɛhuɔ lɛ, ni egbe amɛ, ni ekɛ tsinai lɛ akuɛŋtsei lɛ fee lai, ni ekɛhoo amɛloo lɛ. Ekɛ loo lɛ hã maŋbii ni ekɛ amɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛye. Kɛkɛ ni Elisha tee, ni eyanyiɛ Elia sɛɛ akɛ etsulɔ.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ben-Hadad tsuji lɛ kɛ kpekpe ŋmɔlɔ amɛhɛ, ni amɛkɛ taŋkpee fimɔ amɛyitsei, ni amɛba Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Otsulɔ Ben-Hadad kɛɛ, ‘Miikpa bo fai; hã miyi ana wala.’ ” Ahab bi amɛ akɛ, “Ani ehiɛ kã lolo? Etamɔ minyɛmi pɛ!”

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: Etsu bɔfoi kɛtee Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab ŋɔɔ yɛ Samaria maŋ lɛ mli, ni ayakɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Bɔfoi lɛ ba ekoŋŋ, ni amɛbakɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Naa bɔ ni Ben-Hadad kɛɛ, mitsu aba oŋɔɔ akɛ oŋɔ ojwiɛtɛi kɛ oshika kɛ oŋamɛi kɛ obii lɛ ohã mi;

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: kɛ̃lɛ wɔ nɛkɛ be mli lɛ, mibatsu mitsuji oŋɔɔ koni amɛbakpa owe lɛ kɛ otsuji lɛ awei lɛ amli, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aaasa amɛhiɛ lɛ, amɛŋɔ amɛhiɛ amɛdɛ̃ kɛba.”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni onukpai lɛ fɛɛ kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Kaafo mli, ni kaakpɛlɛ̃ hu.”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ahab kɛɛ Ben-Hadad bɔfoi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyakɛa minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ akɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nibii fɛɛ hewɔ ni otsu otsulɔ ŋɔɔ lɛ, mibafee; shi enɛ lɛ minyɛŋ mafee.” Bɔfoi lɛ yi mli amɛtee, ni amɛyabɔ Ben-Hadad amaniɛ.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad saa etsu Ahab ŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ, ni abakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji mikɛ tabilɔi bɔ ni sa baaa koni abakpãtã omaŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛloo emli mlu lɛ tete amɛhiɛ amɛdɛ̃ kɛya fĩi, no lɛ nyɔŋmɔi lɛ atswa mi nɔ amɛgbe mi.”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Shi Israel Maŋtsɛ lɛ hã hetoo ekɛɛ, “Nyɛyakɛa Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad akɛ, tabilɔ kpakpa lɛ, ta sɛɛ dani eshwãa, shi jeee be ni ajeko shishi.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad nine shɛ Ahab shɛɛ lɛ nɔ be mli ni lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi krokomɛi ni fata ehe kɛfã ta lɛ miinu dãa yɛ amɛbuui lɛ amli. Kɛkɛ ni efã esɛɛ tabilɔi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛgbaa sa!” Ni amɛgba sa amɛwo maŋ lɛ he.

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Nakai be mli nɔŋŋ ni gbalɔ ko ba Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab ŋɔɔ, ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ: ‘Te ona asafo kpekpeŋkpekpeŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ? Naa, mibahã oye amɛnɔ kunim ŋmɛnɛ, koni ona ole akɛ mi ji Yehowa.’ ”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Ahab bi akɛ, “Namɔ baanyiɛ hiɛ kɛyatua amɛ?” Gbalɔ lɛ to he ekɛɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Oblahiiabii tabilɔi ni yɔɔ kpokpai anɔ amralofoi lɛ ashishi lɛ ji mɛi ni anyiɛ hiɛ.’ ” Kɛkɛ ni Ahab bi akɛ, “Namɔ baatsɛ ta lɛ?” Gbalɔ lɛ to he akɛ, “Bo ni.”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Amralofoi lɛ ashishi oblahiiabii tabilɔi lɛ tsutsu ni fã. Saralɔi ni Ben-Hadad etsu sa lɛ babɔ lɛ amaniɛ akɛ, “Hii komɛi miiba kɛjɛ Samaria.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad kɛɛ akɛ, “Hejɔlɛ hewɔ amɛbaa jio, ta hewɔ amɛbaa jio, nyɛmɔmɔa amɛ hiɛkãalɔi.”

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: ni amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ gbe Siria tabilɔ ni ekɛkpe. Kɛkɛ ni Siriabii lɛ jo foi, be mli ni Israelbii lɛ miitiu amɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Shi Siria Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad kɛ ekpɔŋɔiatsɛmɛi komɛi ho tara okpɔŋɔi anɔ kɛjo foi.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahab je kpo kɛjɛ ta lɛ naa, ni ekpãtã Siria okpɔŋɔi kɛ shwiilii lɛ ahiɛ; ekpãtã Siriabii lɛ ahiɛ butuu naakpa.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ lɛ tee Maŋtsɛ Ahab ŋɔɔ, ni eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa koni oyasaa ohe oto. Ojwɛŋ nɔ ni eba lɛ he, ejaakɛ wɔsɛɛ afi nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baaba ebatua bo.” Aye Siriabii anɔ kunim

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Siria Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Israelbii anyɔŋmɔi lɛ gɔji anɔ nyɔŋmɔi ni, no hewɔ ni amɛnine tsɔ̃ wɔnɔ lɛ. Shi hã wɔkɛ amɛ awu yɛ ŋa kplenee nɔ, koni okwɛ akɛ wɔnine tsɔŋ amɛnɔ lo?

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, obua tabilɔi ni falɛ shɛɔ ta ni hiɛ kpãtã lɛ naa, kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tayaa shwiilii abɔ tamɔ tsutsu nibii lɛ afalɛ lɛ, koni wɔ kɛ Israelbii lɛ awu yɛ ŋa kplenee nɔ, koni okwɛ akɛ wɔnine tsɔŋ amɛnɔ lo.” Ben-Hadad bo etsuji lɛ agbee toi, ni efee bɔ ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Be ni eshɛ afi naakplɔ lɛ, Ben-Hadad bua Siria tabilɔi anaa, kɛkɛ ni efã kɛba Afek koni ebatua Israelbii lɛ.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔ ko yanina Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, akɛni Siriabii lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ gɔji anɔ Nyɔŋmɔ ji mi, shi jeee jɔiaŋ Nyɔŋmɔ hewɔ lɛ, mibahã oye asafo kpekpeŋkpekpeŋ nɛɛ nɔ kunim, koni nyɛkɛna nyɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa lɛ.”

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Asafoi enyɔ lɛ jwere shi gbii kpawo bɔ ni mɔnɛ miikwɛ mɔnɛ hiɛ. Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛ ta lɛ yakũa naa, ni Israelbii lɛ gbe Siria tabilɔi nanenɔnyiɛlɔi akpei oha gbi kome jenamɔ.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ben-Hadad tsuji lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, wɔna wɔnu akɛ Israel we lɛ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ, maŋtsɛmɛi mɔbɔnalɔi ji amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hã wɔkɔlɔ kpekpe wɔŋmɔlɔ wɔhɛ, koni wɔkɛ taŋkpee hu afimɔ wɔyitsei koni wɔya Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ; ekolɛ eeehere oyiwala.”

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad tsuji lɛ eka amɛtoi kɛmiibo Ahab naa toi; no hewɔ lɛ, oya nɔŋŋ ni amɛtse naa akɛ, “Lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ onyɛmi ji Ben-Hadad.” Kɛkɛ ni Ahab kɛɛ tsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa koni nyɛkɛ lɛ abaa!” No hewɔ lɛ, Ben-Hadad je kpo kɛba Ahab ŋɔɔ. Ahab hã Ben-Hadad kwɔ etayaa shwiili lɛ.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ben-Hadad kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Maji ni mitsɛ shɔ̃ yɛ otsɛ dɛŋ lɛ mibadãi mahã bo. Obaanyɛ hu obafo jara yɛ Damasko ohã ohe, tamɔ bɔ ni mitsɛ bafee yɛ Samaria lɛ.” Ahab dãi sɛɛ ekɛɛ, “Mi hu miidãmɔ kpãŋmɔ nɛɛ nɔ miiŋmɛɛ ohe.” Amɛkpãŋ yɛ jɛi, kɛkɛ ni Ahab jie Ben-Hadad gbɛ. Gbalɔ ko bu Ahab fɔ

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Yɛ Yehowa fãmɔ naa lɛ, gbalɔi abii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko kɛɛ enaanyo gbalɔi abii lɛ nɔŋŋ eko akɛ, “Ofainɛ, tswaa mi nɔ!” Shi enaanyo lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ ni etswa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbalɔ bi lɛ kɛɛ enaanyo lɛ akɛ, “Akɛni obooo Yehowa gbee toi hewɔ lɛ, amrɔ pɛ ni oooshi mi lɛ jata aaagbe bo.” Be ni enaanyo nɛɛ kɛ lɛ egbɛ mli ni eyaa lɛ jata ko yatua enaanyo lɛ, ni egbe lɛ.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Gbalɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ na nuu kroko ko, ni ekɛɛ mɔ lɛ akɛ, “Ofainɛ, tswaa mi nɔ!” Mɔ lɛ tswa lɛ nɔ, ni epila lɛ.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ lɛ tee, ni eyadamɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ eemɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab hoo mli. No mli lɛ gbalɔ lɛ kɛ yitsofii nɔ efĩ ehiɛsɛɛ ekɛtsake ehe.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ Ahab hoɔ lɛ, gbalɔ lɛ bo etsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Otsulɔ tee ta lɛ eko. Ta lɛ mli lɛ tabilɔ ko kɛ henyɛlɔ ko ni emɔ bahã mi shitoo, ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Okɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ ato. Kɛji ejo foi lɛ, no lɛ okɛ owala baatse, aloo obaawo eyi nyɔmɔ jwiɛtɛi talenta kome.’

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Shi be ni otsulɔ hiɛ edɔ yɛ nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, nuu lɛ jo foi.” Maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛɛ akɛ, “Obu atɛŋ lɛ, bo diɛŋtsɛ. Ja ona owo shika lɛ.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Gbalɔ lɛ he fee oya nɔŋŋ ni ekpɔ yitsofii nɔ lɛ yɛ ehiɛsɛɛ. Jɛi ni Israel Maŋtsɛ lɛ yoo lɛ akɛ gbalɔi lɛ eko ni.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ lɛ kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahab akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: ‘Akɛni oŋmɛɛ mɔ ni mijɔɔ enɔ mihã bo koni ogbe lɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe baatse yɛ enajiaŋ kɛ omaŋ lɛ hu yɛ emaŋ lɛ najiaŋ.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahab yiŋ etee ewe yɛ Samaria be mli ni efee gblinii, asaŋ ni ehao hu.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Ahab kɛɛ Nabot akɛ, “Ŋɔɔ owaintrom lɛ ohã mi koni mikɛfee ameo kɛ shitɔ kɛ amɛhenɔi lɛ abɔɔ, ejaakɛ ebɛŋkɛ miwe nɛɛ; mikɛ waintrom ni hi fe onɔ lɛ baato bo najiaŋ, aloo kɛji ooosumɔ lɛ, mawo bo nyɔmɔ kɛji oootsɔ̃ɔ mi ejara.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Shi Nabot kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Yehowa akahã enɛ miigbale mi fɔ̃ŋfɔ̃ akɛ maŋɔ mitsɛmɛi agboshinii lɛ mahã bo.”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Ahab ku esɛɛ etee ewe lɛ ni efee gblinii, ni emli ewo la yɛ wiemɔ ni Nabot, Yezreelnyo lɛ, kɛ lɛ wie lɛ hewɔ; ejaakɛ ekɛɛ akɛ. “Mikɛ mitsɛmɛi agboshinii lɛ haŋ bo.” Eho ekã esaa nɔ, ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ ehã gbogbo, ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ niyeli.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Eŋa Yezebel ba eŋɔɔ, ni ebabi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba ni ofee gblinii nɛkɛ, ni oyee nii nɛɛ?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Ahab here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ mikɛ Nabot, Yezreelnyo lɛ, wie ni mikɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Ŋɔɔ owaintrom lɛ ohã mi, ni mahe, aloo kɛji oosumɔ lɛ mikɛ waintrom kroko aaato bo no najiaŋ.’ Shi ekɛɛ mi akɛ, mikɛ miwaintrom lɛ hãaa bo.”

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yezebel kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Aso maŋtsɛ kɛ̃ oyeɔ yɛ Israel nɛɛ? Tee shi ni oye nii, ni ona tsui. Mi, mahã onine ashɛ Nabot, Yezreelnyo lɛ, waintrom lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: Amɛshiɛ akɛ ahĩ ŋmãa, ni amɛhã Nabot yata kpee ni atsɛ lɛ yitso.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Amɛhã hii yakagbɔmɛi enyɔ komɛi sɛ̃i, ni amɛmiikwɛ Nabot hiɛ. Hii yakagbɔmɛi enyɔ nɛɛ kɛ sane shi Nabot yɛ maŋbii lɛ ahiɛ akɛ Nabot lomɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kpala Nabot kɛshi maŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛyatswia lɛ tɛ ni amɛgbe lɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni atsu ayakɛɛ Yezebel akɛ, “Atswia Nabot tɛ agbe lɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Shɛɛ lɛ ni shɛ Yezebel dɛŋ nɔŋŋ pɛ, kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Tee shi koni oyaŋɔ Nabot, Yezreelnyo lɛ, abɔɔ lɛ ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ akɛ ekɛaahã bo ni ohe kɛ shika lɛ, ejaakɛ Nabot egbo.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Elia, Tishbinyo lɛ, akɛ,

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: “Yaa koni okɛ Ahab, Israel Maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni yeɔ lumɔ yɛ Samaria lɛ ayakpe. Naa, eyɛ Nabot waintrom lɛ mli; etee akɛ eyaaŋɔ trom lɛ.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ lɛ akɛ, ‘Ei Ahab, ogbe gbɔmɔ lɛ, koni oŋɔ enii lɛ okɛfee onɔ bɛɛ?’ Kɛɛmɔ lɛ ofata he akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: He ni gbei lɛmɔ Nabot lá yɛ lɛ, jɛi nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ gbei aaalɛmɔ bo hu olá yɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Be ni Ahab na Elia lɛ, ekɛɛ, “Ei mihenyɛlɔ, bo onine egbe mi nɛɛ.” Elia here lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Minine egbe bo lɛɛlɛŋ, ejaakɛ ohã efɔŋfeemɔ eŋɔ bo nom yɛ Yehowa hiɛ.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, naa nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ bo: ‘Mahã sane fɔŋ aye nyɛ, mibaplene bo kɛ nuu fɛɛ nuu ni okɛyɔɔ weku yɛ Israel, nyɔŋ kɛ mɔ ni eye ehe fɛɛ.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Mafee owe lɛ tamɔ mifee Nebat bi Yeroboam we lɛ kɛ Ahia bi Baasha hu we lɛ, ejaakɛ ohã mimli efu, ni ohã Israel efee esha.’

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ni yɛ Yezebel hu gbɛfaŋ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ ‘Gbei baaye eloo yɛ Yezreel maŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.’

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Kɛji owekunyo ko gbo yɛ maŋ lɛ, gbei aaaye eloo, ni owekunyo ni aaayagbo yɛ ŋa nɔ lɛ, loofɔji aaaye eloo.”

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni maŋtsɛ kɛɛ nɛ: ‘Nyɛwoa lɛ tsuŋ, ni ahã lɛ aboloo fioo kɛ nu fioo pɛ daa gbi akɛ eniyenii kɛyashi beyinɔ ni maya mayaye omanye maba.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Ahab kɛɛ etsuji lɛ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛle akɛ Ramot-Gilead lɛ wɔnɔ ni? Ni kɛ̃lɛ wɔtara shi, ni wɔfeee he eko koni wɔshɔ̃ yɛ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ?”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahab bi Yehoshafat akɛ, “Bɛ okɛ mi aaatee koni wɔyatua Ramot-Gilead?” Yehoshafat kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Mi nɔŋŋ ji bo; mimaŋbii lɛ omaŋbii ni, mikpɔŋɔi lɛ okpɔŋɔi ni.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Shi Yehoshafat bi akɛ, “Ani Yehowa gbalɔ ko bɛ biɛ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ, koni wɔyabi nii yɛ eŋɔɔ?”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahab tsɛ piafonyo ko, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa koni okɛ Imla bi Mikaia lɛ ashɛ biɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ!”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat ewula kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi atadei kɛtara amɛmaŋtsɛ sɛ̃ii anɔ, yɛ ŋmãagbeemɔhe ni yɔɔ Samaria agbo lɛ naa kpataa lɛ, ni gbalɔi lɛ fɛɛ miigba yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Gbalɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko ni ji Kenaana bi Zedekia lɛ fee dade akloŋtoi, kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: ‘Enɛɛmɛi okɛbaashimɔ Siriabii lɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni oookpãtã amɛhiɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Bɔfo ni tee Mikaia tsɛmɔ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, gbalɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ naabu kome egba gbalɛ kpakpa ehã maŋtsɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hã ogbalɛ lɛ kɛ amɛteŋ mɔ kome pɛ nɔ afee pɛ.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Shi Mikaia to he akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni Yehowa hiɛkãalɔ lɛ yɔɔ nɛɛ lɛ, nɔ ni Yehowa aaakɛɛ mi lɛ, no mawie.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Be ni Mikaia shɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahab hiɛ lɛ, Ahab bi lɛ akɛ, “Ani mikɛ Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat aya koni wɔyatua Ramot-Gilead, aloo wɔkaya?” Mikaia here nɔ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa; nyɛbaaye omanye. Yehowa baajɔɔ maŋ lɛ nɔ ahã nyɛ.”

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Shi Ahab kɛɛ Mikaia akɛ, “Shii enyiɛ po mahã okã mi kitã akɛ, kɛji okɛ mi miiwie yɛ Yehowa gbɛi mli lɛ, okagba mi nɔ kroko fe anɔkwale lɛ kɛkɛ?”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mikaia to he akɛ, “Miina Israel tabilɔi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã gɔji lɛ anɔ tamɔ toi ni bɛ kpalalɔ. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Hii nɛɛ bɛ nuŋtsɔ; hã amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aku esɛɛ eya shĩa yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Mikaia tee nɔ ekɛɛ, “Agbɛnɛ bo Yehowa naa wiemɔ toi! Mina Yehowa ta emaŋtsɛ sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋwɛi, ni ebɔfoi asafo lɛ fɛɛ damɔ emasɛi yɛ eninejurɔ nɔ kɛ ebɛku nɔ.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ni Mikaia mu ewiemɔ lɛ naa nɛkɛ, “Enɛ ji nɔ ni eba lɛ. Yehowa ehã ogbalɔi nɛɛ egba amale gbalɛ amɛkɛlaka bo. Shi lɛ lɛ eto akɛ okɛ amanehulu baaya ayakpe!”

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Kenaana bi Zedekia, gbalɔ lɛ, tsi bɛŋkɛ Mikaia, ni egba Mikaia hiɛ mã, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ be nɛ ni Yehowa mumɔ lɛ je minɔ, ni ekɛ bo bawie?”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahab fã etsulɔ ko ekɛɛ, “Mɔ Mikaia koni okɛ lɛ ayawo Amon maŋ lɛ amralo lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛbi Yoash dɛŋ.”

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Shi Siria asraafonyo ko gãi ni etsɛ̃ ni jeee gbɛ eje etsɛ̃ lɛ yatsu Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ trukaa, yɛ eŋwɛigbɛ dama lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ dama lɛ kpeehe lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ eshwiili kudɔlɔ lɛ akɛ, “Dɔɔ oyi koni okɛ mi aje ta lɛ naa, shi mipila.”

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat fã kɛtee koni amɛyatua Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Ahab kɛɛ Yehoshafat akɛ, “Mibatsake mihe kɛya ta lɛ naa; shi bo lɛ wulamɔ kɛ obladei atadei lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Ahab tsake ehe kɛtee ta lɛ naa.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni Siria asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ na Yehoshafat lɛ, amɛsusu akɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ni, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ pi nɛ!” Kɛkɛ ni amɛgba kɛtee koni amɛkɛ lɛ ayawu. Shi Yehoshafat bolɔ, kɛkɛ ni ayoo lɛ.

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: Be ni shwiilii lɛ anɔ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ na akɛ jeee Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ni lɛ, amɛkpa esɛɛnyiɛmɔ.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Hulushinyɔɔ mli lɛ, ashiɛ yɛ ta lɛ naa akɛ, “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya eshikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ emaŋ.”

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Ayafɔ Ahab shwiili lɛ he yɛ Samaria kpaakpo lɛ naa, ni gbei yalɛmɔ Ahab lá lɛ, ni yei ajwamãŋi yaju amɛhe yɛ mli taakɛ Yehowa ewie eto lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ahab he saji krokomɛi ni eshwɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee kɛ shuɔ wu tsu ko ni ema kɛ maji fɛɛ ni eto lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king. King Jehoshaphat of Judah (
translation_verse: Ahab gbele sɛɛ lɛ, ebi Ahazia baye esɛɛ akɛ Israel maŋtsɛ. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat maŋtsɛyeli (

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Asa bi Yehoshafat bɔ̃i Yuda maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ mli lɛ maŋtsɛ ko bɛ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; amralo ko ni yeɔ maŋtsɛ najiaŋ yɔɔ jɛi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat kpɛ Tarshishbii alɛlɛ henɔi komɛi koni akɛtsɔ̃ ŋshɔ hiɛ kɛya Ofir yɛ jɛi shika tsuru hewɔ; shi ayanyɛɛɛ akɛya, ejaakɛ lɛji lɛ jwara yɛ Ezion-Geber.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahazia, Ahab bi lɛ, kɛɛ Yehoshafat akɛ, “Hã otsuji lɛ abashi mitsuji lɛ anɔ yɛ lɛji lɛ amli.” Shi Yehoshafat eyakpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Yehoshafat gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ eblematsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ yɛ David maŋ lɛ mli; kɛkɛ ni ebi Yehoram baye esɛɛ akɛ maŋtsɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahazia

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ahab bi Ahazia baye Israel maŋtsɛ, ni eye maŋtsɛ afii enyɔ yɛ Samaria.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Ekɔ etsɛ Ahab kɛ enyɛ Yezebel yitsoŋwalɛ jeŋba lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɛ Nebat bi Yeroboam, mɔ ni hã Israel fee esha lɛ, hu jeŋba lɛ.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: Esɔ̃mɔ, ni eja Baal, ni ewo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mli la tamɔ etsɛ fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahazia, jɛ eŋwɛi asa ni yɔɔ Samaria lɛ samflɛ mli eyagbee shi, ni epila waa. No hewɔ lɛ, etsu bɔfoi koni amɛyabi Baal-Zebub, Filistibii anyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ekron lɛ nii akɛ, “Ani hela ni yeɔ mi nɛɛ, mana hewalɛ lo?”

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa bɔfo lɛ fã Elia, Tishbinyo lɛ, akɛ, “Tee shi ni oya koni okɛ Samaria maŋtsɛ lɛ bɔfoi lɛ ayakpe, ni obi amɛ akɛ, ‘Aso Nyɔŋmɔ ko ni bɛ Israel hewɔ ni nyɛyaa nyɛyabi nii yɛ Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ nɛɛ?’

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Oteŋ shi yɛ hela saa ni okã nɔ nɛɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ gbo kɛ̃ obaagbo.’ ” No hewɔ lɛ, Elia yiŋ etee taakɛ Yehowa fã lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni bɔfoi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛba maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Maŋtsɛ lɛ bi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛku nyɛsɛɛ?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Amɛhã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Nuu ko kɛ wɔ bakpe, ni ekɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ kɛyaa maŋtsɛ ni tsu nyɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni nyɛyakɛa lɛ akɛ, Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, aso Nyɔŋmɔ ko ni bɛ Israel hewɔ ni otsuɔ koni ayabi nii yɛ Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ nɛɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, oteŋ shi yɛ hela saa ni okã nɔ nɛɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ gbo kɛ̃ obaagbo.’ ”

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Amɛhã lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ lɛ tsɔiatsɛ ni. Ewo atade wuyaa, ni ekɛ kooloo hewolo efi emliteŋ.” Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Elia, Tishbinyo lɛ ni”.

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Naa, la ejɛ ŋwɛi ebayi shi, ni ebashã klɛŋklɛŋ asafoiatsɛmɛi enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛmɛi nyɔŋmai enumɔi lɛ fɛɛ; shi agbɛnɛ, mi lɛ, naa mi mɔbɔ, hã misusuma jara awa yɛ ohiɛ.”

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ Elia akɛ, “Okɛ lɛ akpeleke shi kɛya, kaashe lɛ gbeyei!” Kɛkɛ ni Elia te shi, ni ekɛ lɛ tee maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Akɛ nɔ kɛ̃ ni otsu bɔfoi kɛtee koni amɛyabi nii yɛ Baal-Zebub, Ekron nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ, tamɔ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ ko bɛ Israel ni aaabi edaaŋ gbee, hewɔ lɛ oteŋ shi yɛ hela saa ni okã nɔ nɛɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ, gbo kɛ̃ obaagbo.’ ”

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ Ahazia gbo yɛ Yehowa wiemɔ ni Elia wie lɛ naa; ni akɛni Ahazia bɛ bi kwraa hewɔ lɛ, enyɛmi Yoram baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ yɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ Yehoram ni ji Yehoshafat bi lɛ yinɔ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nibii fɛɛ ni maŋtsɛ Ahazia fee lɛ, aŋmã fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be bashɛ ní Yehowa baaŋɔ Elia kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ lasuogbele mli. Elia kɛ Elisha nyiɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ Gilgal;

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: ni be ni amɛyaa yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Elia kɛɛ Elisha akɛ, “Miikpa bo fai, mɛɛ yɛ biɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa etsu mi Betel.” Shi Elisha to he akɛ, “Bei abɔ ni Yehowa hiɛ kã ni bo hu ohiɛ kã nɛɛ lɛ, mishiŋ bo.” Kɛkɛ ni amɛyi mli kɛtee Betel.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔi aku ko ni yɔɔ Betel lɛ mli bii lɛ je kpo kɛba Elisha ŋɔɔ, ni amɛbabi lɛ akɛ, “Ani ole akɛ ŋmɛnɛ Yehowa baaŋɔ onuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛje oŋɔɔ kɛya?” Ni ehã amɛ hetoo akɛ, “Mi hu mile; nyɛfea diŋŋ kɛkɛ!”

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ Elisha akɛ, “Elisha, mɛɛ yɛ biɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa etsu mi Yeriko.” Shi Elisha kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bei abɔ ni Yehowa hiɛ kã ni bo hu ohiɛ kã nɛɛ lɛ, mishiii bo!” Kɛkɛ ni amɛba Yeriko.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔi aku ko ni yɔɔ Yeriko lɛ mli bii lɛ ba Elisha ŋɔɔ ni amɛbabi lɛ akɛ, “Ani ole akɛ ŋmɛnɛ Yehowa baaŋɔ onuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛje oŋɔɔ kɛya?” Ni ehã amɛ hetoo akɛ, “Mi hu mile, nyɛ lɛ, nyɛfea diŋŋ kɛkɛ!”

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia kɛɛ Elisha akɛ, “Mɛɛ yɛ biɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa etsu mi Yordan Faa lɛ naa.” Shi Elisha kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Bei abɔ ni Yehowa hiɛ kã ni bo hu ohiɛ kã nɛɛ lɛ, mishiŋ bo.” Hewɔ lɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ amɛyi mli kɛtee.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Ni gbalɔi aku lɛ mli bii nyɔŋmai enumɔ ni nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛtee lɛ, yadamɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ, shi amɛyi enyɔ lɛ amɛdamɔ Yordan Faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elia jie etade yuu lɛ ni ekota, ni ekɛtswa nu lɛ mli, ni nu lɛ mli gba kɛtee biɛ kɛ biɛ; ni amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ kɛfo faa lɛ.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Be ni amɛfo faa lɛ kɛtee faa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Elia kɛɛ Elisha akɛ, “Bi mi nɔ ni osumɔɔ ni mafee mahã bo, dani aŋɔ mi kɛje oŋɔɔ kɛya.” Ni Elisha kɛɛ, “Hã mana omumɔ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ eko bɔ ni aaaha matsɔ mɔ ni baaye onajiaŋ.”

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Elia kɛɛ Elisha akɛ, “Obi nɔ ko ni wa naakpa, shi kɛ̃lɛ kɛji oona mi ni aawo mi kɛmiije oŋɔɔ kɛya lɛ, no lɛ aaaba mli nakai ahã bo; shi kɛji onaaa mi lɛ, no lɛ onine shɛŋ nɔ.”

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛnyiɛ gbɛ kɛyaa ni amɛwieɔ lolo lɛ, naa, la shwiili kɛ la okpɔŋɔi ba, ni amɛbagbala Elia kɛ Elisha teŋ. Ni Elia tsɔ̃ lasuogbele lɛ mli kɛtee ŋwɛi.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Elisha na nii nɛɛ, ni ebo etsɛ Elia akɛ, “Mitsɛ, mitsɛ! Israel hefãlɔ kpele! Ao, tee otee lɛ?” Ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ enaaa Elia dɔŋŋ. Ni emɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etade yuu lɛ mli ni etse mli enyɔ.

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɔ Elia atade lɛ ni je ehe egbee shi lɛ, ni eku esɛɛ, ni eyadamɔ Yordan Faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɔ Elia atade ni je ehe egbee shi lɛ, ni ekɛtswa nu lɛ mli, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ Yehowa, Elia Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yɔɔ?” Ni be ni ekɛ atade lɛ tswa nu lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ mli gba enyɔ, kɛtee biɛ kɛ biɛ. Ni Elisha tsɔ̃ mli kɛho.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Be ni gbalɔi aku lɛ mli bii nyɔŋmai enumɔ ni jɛ Yeriko lɛ ni damɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ lɛ na lɛ lɛ, amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Elia mumɔ lɛ ebayi Elisha nɔ.” Amɛ kɛ lɛ bakpe, ni amɛkoto lɛ,

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛhiɛ enaagbamɔ aahu ni efee lɛ ahuntoo lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtsũa kɛyaa.” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsũ hii nyɔŋmai enumɔ kɛtee, ni amɛyatao lɛ gbii etɛ̃, shi amɛnaaa lɛ.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba Elisha ŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ Yeriko, he ni emɛɔ yɛ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Ani mikɛɛɛ nyɛ akɛ nyɛkaya lo?” Elisha naakpɛɛ nitsumɔi lɛ

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ hii komɛi ní jɛ Yeriko maŋ lɛ mli tee Elisha ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, maŋ nɛɛ kãmɔhe lɛ hi moŋ nɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni, bo wɔnuŋtsɔ, onaa nɛɛ; shi nu lɛ ehiii, ni ehã asharãkeɔ bii, asaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ hãaa niyenii aba.”

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Ni efã mɛi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ ŋoo awoa kã hee mli ni nyɛkɛbahãa mi.” Ni amɛkɛbahã lɛ.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Ni etee nuhiŋmɛi lɛ he, ni eyatsi ŋoo lɛ ewo mli, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Mifee nu nɛɛ krɔŋŋ, ni ehaŋ gbele loo sharakemɔ aba dɔŋŋ.’ ”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Ni nakai nu lɛ fee krɔŋŋ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ, yɛ Elisha wiemɔ lɛ naa.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Elisha jɛ Yeriko eeya Betel; ni be ni eyaa lɛ, gbekɛbii hii bibii komɛi jɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛba eŋɔɔ amɛbaye ehe fɛo amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Yiteŋ kpataatsɛ, jee biɛ ní oya! Yiteŋ kpataatsɛ, jee biɛ ní oya!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Elisha tsɔ̃ ehe, ni ekwɛ amɛ, ni ekɛ Yehowa gbɛi lomɔ amɛ. Kɛkɛ ni oshishibrishi yei enyɔ jɛ koo lɛ mli ba, ni amɛbatserɛ gbekɛbii hii lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛ enyɔ mli.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Elisha tee Karmel Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ejɛ jɛi kɛtee Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Yuda maŋtsɛ, Yehoshafat maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ahab bi Yehoram baye Israel nɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ Samaria afii nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Efee esha eshi Yehowa, shi kɛ̃lɛ etamɔɔɔ etsɛ loo enyɛ Yezebel nɔ lɛ; ejaakɛ lɛ lɛ, ekumɔ Baal amãgãi lɛ ni etsɛ fee lɛ eshwie shi.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ esha ni klɛŋklɛŋ Israel Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ, fee lɛ, nakai esha lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ hu efee, ejaakɛ ehã Israel fee esha, shi kɛ̃lɛ ekpaleee.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Moab maŋtsɛ Mesha lɛ lɛɔ toi, ni daa afi lɛ eyahãa Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ too gwantɛŋ bii akpei oha kɛ too ojwɛnii akpei oha ahe tsɔi akɛ daa afi too ni ewoɔ ehãa lɛ.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Israel maŋtsɛ Ahab gbo lɛ, Moab maŋtsɛ lɛ tse Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ atua.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
