translation_verse: Ni bulɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hiɛ etawuu nii yɛ edɛ̃ŋ, ni amɛdamɔ shi kɛjɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ wuoyigbɛ aahu kɛtee maŋtsɛ we lɛ kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ he kɛkpe, koni amɛbu maŋtsɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: Be ni eyaakwɛ lɛ, naa maŋtsɛ hee lɛ damɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ agbo lɛ naa akulashiŋ lɛ he, bɔ ni ji gbɛnaa lɛ; ni asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛkpãlɔi yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ masɛi, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii fɛɛ miinya, ni amɛmiikpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛi. Kɛkɛ ni Atalia gbala ehe atadei, ni ebolɔ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Maŋjwaa sane nɛ, maŋjwaa sane nɛ!”

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada fã asraafoi ohahai anɔ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ Atalia ajea asraafoi lɛ ateŋ kɛyaa, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaanyiɛ esɛɛ ni aaaba lɛ shɔ̃mɔ lɛ nyɛgbea lɛ.” Ejaakɛ osɔfo lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Akagbe lɛ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ.”

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni osɔfo Yehoiada hã Maŋtsɛ Yoash kɛ maŋbii lɛ kɛ Yehowa kpãŋ akɛ amɛbaaba amɛjeŋ akɛ Yehowa maŋ. Ni ehã maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ hu kpãŋ.

english_verse: Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars. After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ yiŋ ni amɛyabote Baal we lɛ, ni amɛkumɔ Baal we lɛ amɛshwie shi. Baal afɔleshãa latɛi lɛ kɛ emãgãi lɛ amɛkumɔ amɛ dukuduku; ni Mattan, ni ji Baal osɔfo lɛ, amɛgbe lɛ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛkɛ ni osɔfo Yehoiada to gbɛjianɔ ni bulɔi abu Yehowa we lɛ he.

english_verse: he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni lɛ kɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ hebulɔi lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ he bulɔi lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ ŋɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛkpeleke shi kɛjɛ Yehowa we lɛ kɛtsɔ Bulɔi Agbo lɛ naa gbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛba maŋtsɛ we lɛ, ni amɛhã eyata maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Akɛni agbe Atalia kɛ klante yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ hewɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli jɔ ni maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ na miishɛɛ.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord.
translation_verse: Yoash fee nɔ ni ja yɛ Yehowa hiɛ bei abɔ fɛɛ ni ehi shi lɛ, ejaakɛ Osɔfo Yehoiada tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nii.

english_verse: The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
translation_verse: Shi shika ni anaa kɛjɛɔ sɔ̃ afɔle kɛ esha afɔle lɛ mli lɛ, akɛ nomɛi baaa Yehowa we lɛ, nomɛi lɛ osɔfoi lɛ anɔ ni.

english_verse: But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ jeŋbii ajamɔhei grɔŋŋi lɛ akumɔɔɔ ashwieee shi; maŋbii lɛ kã he amɛmiishã afɔlei kɛ tsofaikɛŋmai yɛ jɛi lolo.

english_verse: One day, Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money that has been given to the Lord's temple, whether from taxes or gifts,
translation_verse: Yoash kɛɛ osɔfoi lɛ akɛ, “Shika fɛɛ ni ajɔɔ nɔ ake ni akɛbaa Yehowa we lɛ, ni ji mɔ fɛɛ mɔ too ni sa akɛ ewo lɛ, kɛ shika fɛɛ shika ni mɔ ko jɛɔ etsui mli ekɛbaa Yehowa we lɛ,

english_verse: But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule,
translation_verse: Shi eba mli akɛ kɛbashi Yoash maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ esako Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hei ni ekumɔ lɛ eko eko kwraa lolo.

english_verse: Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Yoash tsɛ osɔfo Yehoiada kɛ osɔfoi krokomɛi lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛsaaa Yehowa we lɛ tsu koi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, nyɛkɛ shika ni nyɛheɔ lɛ akatoa dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ nyɛŋɔa nyɛhãa koni akɛsaa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ.”

english_verse: The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ kpɛlɛ̃ nɔ akɛ amɛheŋ shika yɛ maŋbii lɛ adɛŋ dɔŋŋ, ni amɛsaŋ Yehowa we lɛ hu.

english_verse: Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada wo adeka ko, ni egbu enaanɔ lɛ mli folɔ, ni ekɛ adeka lɛ ma afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ masɛi. Kɛji oobote Yehowa we lɛ mli lɛ, adeka lɛ ye oninejurɔgbɛ; ni osɔfoi ni kwɛɔ shinaa lɛ naa lɛ ŋɔɔ shika fɛɛ ni akɛbaa Yehowa we lɛ amɛwoɔ mli.

english_verse: When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags.
translation_verse: Ni ebaa mli akɛ be fɛɛ be kɛji amɛna akɛ shika lɛ efa yɛ adeka lɛ mli lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ woloŋmalɔ lɛ kɛ osɔfonukpa lɛ baa, ni amɛbakaneɔ shika ni ana yɛ Yehowa we lɛ, ni amɛbafimɔɔ shika lɛ amɛwoɔ kotokui amli.

english_verse: Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛtuɔ shika ni ana lɛ amɛwoɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ Yehowa we lɛ nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ adɛŋ; ni amɛ hu amɛkɛwoɔ kapintafoi kɛ tsumalɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ Yehowa we lɛ anyɔmɔ.

english_verse: the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
translation_verse: Ni akɛ eko woɔ bliglɛfoi kɛ tɛkolɔi anyɔmɔ, ni akɛ eko heɔ mplaŋi kɛ tɛ ni akɛsaa Yehowa we lɛ tsukoi lɛ, ni akɛ eko woɔ nyɔmɔ ni abɔɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ saamɔ he lɛ.

english_verse: While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple.
translation_verse: Shi shika ni akɛbaa Yehowa we lɛ aŋɔɔɔ no eko akɛfeee Yehowa we lɛ jwiɛtɛi kãi, lagbee nii, lalakãi, tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛi aloo shika nii loo jwiɛtɛi nii krokomɛi;

english_verse: It went only to pay for repairs.
translation_verse: shi akɛhãa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ, koni akɛsaa Yehowa we lɛ.

english_verse: The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: Akɛni mɛi adɛŋ ni akɛ shika lɛ woɔ lɛ yeɔ anɔkwa hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa akɛ amɛbuɔ shika lɛ he akɔntaa ko.

english_verse: About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ Siria Maŋtsɛ Hazael fã ta kɛba, ni ekɛ Gat, maŋ wulu lɛ, bawu, ni eŋɔ maŋ lɛ. Shi be ni Hazael jie ehiɛ eka Yerusalɛm lɛ,

english_verse: So Joash collected everything he and his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated to the Lord, as well as the gold in the storage rooms in the temple and palace. He sent it all to Hazael as a gift, and when Hazael received it, he ordered his troops to leave Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yoash, Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ, ŋɔ nibii krɔŋkrɔŋi fɛɛ ni etsɛmɛi Yehoshafat kɛ Yehoram kɛ Ahazia, ni ji Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi ni eho lɛ, ejɔɔ nɔ eke lɛ, kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, kɛ shika fɛɛ ni ana yɛ Yehowa we lɛ, kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ nitoohe lɛ hu, ni etsu akɛyahã Hazael, Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Hazael shi Yerusalɛm sɛɛ ni etee.

english_verse: Everything else Joash did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yoash he saji kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: At the end of his rule, some of his officers rebelled against him. Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him in a building where the land was filled in on the east side of Jerusalem, near the road to Silla. Joash was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Amaziah became king.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni tswia lɛ nii ni egbo lɛ ji Yozakar, Shimeat bi lɛ kɛ Yehozabad, Shomer bi lɛ. Ni amɛfu lɛ yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ amasɛi yɛ David maŋ lɛ mli; ni Yoash bi Amazia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yoash, Ahazia bi lɛ yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehoahaz, Yehu bi lɛ bɔ̃i maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Samaria. Eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋma kɛ kpawo.

english_verse: and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
translation_verse: Ni Elisha kɛɛ, “Gbelemɔ bokãgbɛ samflɛ lɛ.” Ni egbele. Ni Elisha kɛɛ “Tsɛ̃!” Ni etsɛ̃ gãi lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Elisha kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yehowa kunimyeli gãimlibi kɛ Siria nɔ kunimyeli gãimlibi nɛ, ejaakɛ obaatswia Siriabii lɛ nii yɛ Afek kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni oooplene amɛ.”

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Efee esha yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; eshai ni Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ, hã Israel fee lɛ, nomɛi nɔŋŋ efee, ni efɔ̃ɔɔ feemɔ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa mli wo Israel la, ni no hewɔ lɛ, daa nɛɛ Yehowa tuɔ amɛ ewoɔ Siria Maŋtsɛ Hazael kɛ ebi Ben-Hadad dɛŋ.

english_verse: Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz
translation_verse: Shi Yehoahaz kpa Yehowa fai, ni Yehowa bo lɛ toi; ejaakɛ Yehowa, ena bɔ ni Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ haoɔ Israel ehãa lɛ.

english_verse: by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa jie herelɔ ko ehã, koni ebakpɔ̃ amɛ kɛje Siriabii lɛ adɛŋ; no hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ hi amɛshĩai lɛ amli tamɔ tsutsu lɛ yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli.

english_verse: Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yoash yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehoash bɔ̃i Israel maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Samaria. Eye maŋtsɛ yɛ Samaria afii nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yehoahaz he saji kɛ nibii ni efee kɛ ekãa ni efee lɛ aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king. King Jehoash of Israel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehoahaz gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ afũuhe lɛ yɛ Samaria; ni ebi Yehoash baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash

english_verse: “Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elisha kɛɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ta gãi lɛ!” Ni eta. Ni Elisha ŋɔ eniji eshwie maŋtsɛ lɛ niji anɔ.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by doing just like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Lɛ hu efee esha yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; efɔ̃ɔɔ eshai ni Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ fee, ni no hã Israelbii fee esha lɛ, shi ekã he efee eshai lɛ lolo.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Yoash he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee, kɛ ekãa ni efee yɛ ta ni ekɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia lɛ wu lɛ mli lɛ, aŋma yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king. Elisha the Prophet Dies
translation_verse: Ni Yoash gbo ni ebi Yeroboam bata esɛ̃i lɛ nɔ. Afu Yoash yɛ Samaria yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ amasɛi. Elisha gbele

english_verse: Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, be ni hela ni baagbe gbalɔ Elisha lɛ mɔ lɛ lɛ, Israel Maŋtsɛ Yoash tee eŋɔɔ eyasara lɛ. Eyafo yɛ ehiɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mitsɛ, mitsɛ! Israel hefãlɔ kpele!”

english_verse: Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elisha tee nɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “kɔlɔmɔ gãimlibii lɛ. Tsɛ̃rɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ gãi!” Ni etsɛ̃rɛ shii etɛ̃, ni ekpa.

english_verse: Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ mli fu lɛ, ni ekɛɛ, “Eji otsɛ̃rɛ shii enumɔ loo shii ekpaa kulɛ, no lɛ obaatswia Siriabii lɛ nii aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni oooplene amɛ; shi enɛ lɛ, shii etɛ̃ pɛ obaaye Siriabii anɔ kunim.”

english_verse: Elisha died and was buried. Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Elisha gbo, ni afu lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, Moab ojoyeli tai lɛ batua Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nakai afi lɛ mli.

english_verse: Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up. Israel Defeats Syria
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ, gbi ko be ni amɛyaafu nuu ko lɛ, naa, amɛna ojoyeli ta ko. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshɛ nuu lɛ gbonyo amɛfɔ̃ Elisha gbonyo bu lɛ mli, kɛkɛ ni amɛjo foi. Ni be ni nuu lɛ gbonyo lɛ he yasa Elisha wui lɛ ahe pɛ, kɛkɛ ni gbonyo lɛ hiɛ tsɛ̃, ni ete shi edamɔ enaji anɔ. Israel kɛ Siria wu ta

english_verse: Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Siria Maŋtsɛ Hazael hao Israelbii yɛ Yehoahaz maŋtsɛyeli be mli fɛɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ Yehowa musuŋ tsɔ̃ lɛ yɛ amɛhe, ni etse ehiɛ ehã amɛ yɛ ekpãŋmɔ ni ekɛ Abraham kɛ Yakob kɛ Isak ekpãŋ lɛ hewɔ, ni esumɔɔɔ akɛ ekpãtã amɛhiɛ, ejaakɛ ehiɛ kpako emaŋ Israel lɛ nɔ kɛbashi benɛ.

english_verse: Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria.
translation_verse: Be ni Siria Maŋtsɛ Hazael gbo lɛ, ebi Ben-Hadad baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash, Yehoahaz bi lɛ, ye Ben-Hadad, Hazael bi lɛ, nɔ kunim shii etɛ̃, ni eshɔ̃ maji ni Hazael shɔ̃ yɛ etsɛ Yehoahaz dɛŋ yɛ ta mli lɛ.

english_verse: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
translation_verse: Lɛ ehã Israel husui lɛ shɛ amɛdɛŋ ekoŋŋ, kɛjɛ Lebo-Hamat ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ kɛyashi ŋa kplenee lɛ nɔ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ naa, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, tsɔ̃ etsulɔ Yona, Amitai bi gbalɔ ni jɛ Gat-Hefer lɛ, nɔ ewie lɛ.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ni efee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; ni efɔ̃ɔɔ eshai ni Yereboam, Nebat bi lɛ fee, ni no hã Israelbii fee esha lɛ.

english_verse: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
translation_verse: Yeroboam gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ Israel maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ, ni ebi Zakaria baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
translation_verse: Efee Yehowa suɔmɔnaanii, kɛ̃lɛ etamɔɔɔ David, mɔ seshi mli ni ejɛ lɛ. Bɔ ni etsɛ Yoash fee lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ efee.

english_verse: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ekumɔɔɔ wɔŋjamɔhei grɔŋŋi lɛ eshwieee shi; maŋbii lɛ miishã afɔlei kɛ tsofakɛŋmai lɛ yɛ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ lolo.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Amazia maŋtsɛyeli he shi lɛ, emɔmɔ tsuji ni gbe etsɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni egbe amɛ.

english_verse: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni gbe etsɛ lɛ abii lɛ, egbeee amɛ; ejaakɛ edamɔ Yehowa Mla ni ewo yɛ Mose Wolo lɛ mli akɛ, “Akagbe fɔlɔi yɛ amɛbii atɔ̃mɔi ahewɔ, ni asaŋ akagbe bii hu yɛ amɛtsɛmɛi atɔ̃mɔi ahewɔ, shi moŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ, efɔŋ ni eeefee lɛ, no he gbele lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbo.”

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ogbe Edombii, hewɔ lɛ no ehã oowo ohe nɔ. Okɛ no ashwã; shi okɛ no awa owe lɛ. Mɛɛba oshwɛɔ ohiɛkpãtãmɔ he, koni bo okɛ Yuda fɛɛ hiɛ akpãtã nɛɛ?”

english_verse: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: No mli Amazia tsu bɔfoi kɛtee Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash, Yehu bi Yehoahaz bi lɛ bi, ŋɔɔ ayatsɛ lɛ ŋa nɔ akɛ, “Ba ni wɔkpe nuu kɛ nuu.”

english_verse: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Shi Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash tsu ayakɛɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia akɛ, “Naa, gbi ko lɛ ŋmei tso ko ni yɔɔ Lebanon tsu ayakɛɛ tsenedru tso ni yɔɔ Lebanon akɛ, ‘Ŋɔɔ obiyoo lɛ ohã mibinuu lɛ gbãlã.’ Ni ŋaŋ kooloo ko ni yɔɔ Lebanon lɛ baho, ni ebanaanaa ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Shi Amazia booo toi. No hewɔ lɛ, Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash fã kɛtee, ni ekɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia yakpe hiɛ kɛ hiɛ yɛ ta mli yɛ Bet-Shemesh ni yɔɔ Yuda nɔ mli lɛ.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Israel ta lɛ ye Yuda ta lɛ nɔ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ jo foi kɛtee ewe.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash then marched to Jerusalem and broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash mɔ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia, yɛ Bet-Shemesh, ni eŋɔ lɛ nom. Ni eba Yerusalɛm, ni ebakumɔ Yerusalɛm gbogboi lɛ, kɛjɛ Efraim Agbo lɛ naa kɛyashi Koŋ Agbo lɛ naa ni ekɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi ohai ejwɛ.

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni eloo shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi fɛɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ana yɛ Yehowa we lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ nitoohei lɛ kɛ nomii hu kɛku esɛɛ kɛtee Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yehoash he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nii ni efee lɛ, kɛ ekãa ni efee lɛ kɛ bɔ ni ekɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia wu ehã lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Ni Yuda maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ŋɔ Azaria, ni amɛwo lɛ maŋtsɛ yɛ etsɛ Amazia sɛɛ.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Azaria ye Elat nɔ kunim, ni ekpɔ̃ maŋ lɛ ehã Yuda, yɛ etsɛ Amazia gbele sɛɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam ni ji enyɔ lɛ

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia, Yoash bi lɛ, yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yeroboam, Israel Maŋtsɛ Yohoash bi lɛ, baye maŋtsɛ yɛ Samaria, ni eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛ ekome.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa na akɛ Israel amanehulu ni enaa lɛ naa wa naakpa, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni ji nyɔŋ aloo mɔ ni hiɛ ehe, ni aaaye abua Israel.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni Yehowa ekɛko akɛ eeegbe Israel gbɛi yɛ ŋwɛi shishi nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, etsɔ̃ Yeroboam, Yoash bi lɛ, nine nɔ ehere amɛyiwala.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yeroboam he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee kɛ ekãa ni efee kɛ bɔ ni ewuwuu tai kɛ bɔ ni eshɔ̃ Damasko kɛ Hamat lɛ, aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Pekahia he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli. Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Azaria yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Menahem bi Pekahia bɔ̃i Israel nɔ maŋtsɛyeli, ni eye maŋtsɛ afii enyɔ yɛ Samaria.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Ni Azaria fee nɔ ni ja yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ Amazia fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ ekumɔɔɔ jamɔhei ni yɔɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ eshwieee shi; maŋbii lɛ kã he amɛmiishã afɔlei kɛ tsofakɛŋmai yɛ jamɔhei ni yɔɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ lolo.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛ hela fɔŋ piŋ maŋtsɛ Azaria, ni eye kpiti kɛyashi egbele gbi; aŋmɛɛɛ lɛ gbɛ koni ehi maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli. Ni maŋtsɛ Azaria bi Yotam kwɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ sɛɛ akɛ maŋtsɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ, ni eye maŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Azaria he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Ni Azaria gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ eblematsɛmɛi lɛ afũuhe lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm, kɛkɛ ni ebi Yotam baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Zakaria

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Yuda maŋtsɛ Azaria yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Zakaria baye Israel nɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ Samaria nyɔji ekpaa.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Ni Yabesh bi Shalum tee Maŋtsɛ Zakaria yinɔ apam, ni etswa lɛ nɔ ni egbe lɛ yɛ maŋ hiɛ, kɛkɛ ni ebaye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Belɛ wiemɔ ni Yehowa kɛ Yehu wie akɛ, “Oshwiei lɛ aaata Israel sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ lɛ,” na ba mli. Israel Maŋtsɛ Shalum

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Yabesh bi Shalum baye maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel. Yuda maŋtsɛ Azaria yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ; ni eye maŋtsɛ nyɔŋ kome yɛ Samaria.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Azaria yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ lɛ, Gadi bi Menahem babɔ̃i Israel nɔ maŋtsɛyeli, ni eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋma yɛ Samaria.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Shi efɔ̃ɔɔ eshai ni Nebat bi Yeroboam fee, ni no hã Israelbii lɛ fee esha lɛ feemɔ.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Asiria Maŋtsɛ Tiglat Pileser batua Israel, ni Menahem hã Tiglat Pileser jwiɛtɛi talentai akpe koni ewa lɛ ni ehã emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ama shi yɛ Israel.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Efee nɔ ni ja yɛ Yehowa hiɛ; bɔ ni etsɛ Azaria fee lɛ, nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ efee.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Menahem he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Menahem gbo, ni afu lɛ, yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ amasɛi, ni ebi Pekahia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Israel Maŋtsɛ Pekahia

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Efee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ejaakɛ efɔ̃ɔɔ eshai ni Nebat bi Yeroboam fee, ni no hã Israelbii lɛ fee esha lɛ feemɔ.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Efee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ejaakɛ efɔ̃ɔɔ eshai ni Nebat bi Yeroboam fee, ni no hã Israelbii lɛ fee esha lɛ feemɔ.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka yinɔ lɛ Tiglat-Pileser, Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ, fã ta kɛba Israel. Ebaŋɔ Gilead kɛ Galilea shikpɔji lɛ kɛ amɛmli maji nɛɛ: Iyon, Abel-Bet-Maaka, Yanoa, Kedesh, Hazor. Eŋɔ Naftali shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu. Kɛkɛ ni eŋɔ Israelbii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ nom kɛtee Asiria.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yotam yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ela bi Hoshea tee Maŋtsɛ Peka, Remalia bi lɛ, yinɔ apam, ni etswa lɛ nɔ egbe lɛ, ni ebaye maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Peka he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, naa, aŋma yɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yotam (

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka, Remalia bi lɛ, yinɔ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yuda Maŋtsɛ Azaria bi Yotam baye maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ ekumɔɔɔ jamɔhei ni yɔɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ eshwieee shi; maŋbii lɛ kã he amɛmiishã afɔlei kɛ tsofakɛŋmai yɛ jamɔhei ni yɔɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ lolo. Yotam ji mɔ ni tswa Kooyigbɛ Agbo ni yɔɔ Yehowa we lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yotam he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ aŋma yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli Yehowa hã Siria Maŋtsɛ Rezin kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka, batua Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yotam gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ amasɛi yɛ Yerusalɛm; kɛkɛ ni ebi Ahaz baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka, Remalia bi lɛ, yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ, Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yotam bi Ahaz bɔ̃i maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Yuda.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Egbo ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛmɛi lɛ amasɛi yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni ebi Hezekia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Uria fee bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahaz fã lɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Efee esha fe Israel maŋtsɛmɛi ni nyiɛ ehiɛ lɛ tete. Egbe lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emusuŋbi ekɛshã afɔle ehã amãgãi, nɔ ko ni Yehowa hiɔ, ni no hã eshwie jeŋmajiabii lɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Eshãshãa afɔlei kɛ tsofakɛŋmai yɛ amãgãi ajamɔhei grɔŋŋi lɛ kɛ gɔji anɔ kɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni ebu kusuu shishi hu.

english_verse: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Siria Maŋtsɛ Rezin saa eshɔ̃ Elat maŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni eshwie Yudafoi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Edombii bahi jɛi, ni amɛyɛ jɛi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahaz tsu bɔfoi kɛtee Asiria Maŋtsɛ Tiglat-Pileser ŋɔɔ kɛ wiemɔ akɛ, “Otsulɔ kɛ obi ji mi. Ba ni obahere mi yɛ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ, maŋtsɛmɛi ni ete shi ewo mi lɛ, adɛŋ.”

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Ahaz ŋɔ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika ni ana yɛ Yehowa we lɛ mli kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ nitoohe lɛ mli hu, ni ekɛtsu ni akɛyake Asiria maŋtsɛ Tiglat Pileser.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Tiglat Pileser fee nɔ ni Ahaz babi lɛ lɛ. Efã ta eyatua Damasko, ni eye enɔ, ni egbe Maŋtsɛ Rezin, ni eŋɔ Damaskobii lɛ nom kɛtee Kir.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahaz yiŋ kɛtee Damasko koni ekɛ Asiria Maŋtsɛ, Tiglat-Pileser ayakpe. Ahaz yana afɔleshãa latɛ ko yɛ Damasko. Ehã atɛŋ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ su, bɔ ni eyɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ekɛtsu akɛyahã osɔfo Uria.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Ni Osɔfo Uria ma afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni akɛmaje lɛ lɛ henɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ; ema egbe naa dani Maŋtsɛ Ahaz jɛ Damasko eba.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ Ahaz jɛ Damasko eba lɛ, ebana afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni Ahaz tsi ebɛŋkɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ekwɔ kɛtee ehe,

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: ni eshã eshãa afɔle kɛ niyenii afɔlei yɛ nɔ, efɔse edãa afɔle lɛ eshwie nɔ, ni eŋɔ eshidaa afɔlei lɛ alá lɛ eshwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Akɔɔble afɔleshãa latɛ ni ma Yehowa hiɛ lɛ, Ahaz tsi kɛje Yehowa we lɛ hiɛgbɛ he ni ema, yɛ efɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kɛ Yehowa we lɛ teŋ lɛ, ni ekɛyama lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kooyigbɛ.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahaz fã Osɔfo Uria akɛ, “Mifɔleshãa latɛ wulu nɛɛ nɔ oshã afɔlei nɛɛ fɛɛ yɛ: leebi shãa afɔle lɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ niyenii afɔle lɛ, kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shãa afɔle kɛ eniyenii afɔle lɛ, kɛ maŋbii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shãa afɔlei lɛ, kɛ amɛniyenii afɔlei lɛ kɛ amɛdãa afɔlei lɛ. Oŋɔ shãa afɔlei alá lɛ kɛ afɔlei krokomɛi lɛ alá lɛ fɛɛ oshwã nɔ. Shi akɔɔble afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, no ahi shi ahã mi koni mikɛbi Yehowa nii.”

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahaz fãmɔ akɔɔble shwiili ni akɛsɔ̃mɔɔ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ anaji lɛ, ni ehole tsɛnsii ni mamɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ. Ewo akɔɔble gbudugbaŋ lɛ hu yɛ akɔɔble tsinai nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ akotosɛɛ, ni eŋɔ ma tɛi ni akɛka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: Hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ gbɛ ni aha eyiteŋ ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli kɛ maŋtsɛ tsɔ̃mɔhe ni yɔɔ agbonaa gbɛ lɛ, Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Ahaz tsɔ̃ amɛnaa ehã he kroko.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Ahaz he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, aŋma yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Ahaz yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ela bi Hoshea babɔ̃i Israel maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Samaria. Ni eye maŋtsɛ afii nɛɛhu.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: Efee esha yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, kɛ̃lɛ enɔ lɛ tamɔɔɔ Israel maŋtsɛmɛi ni tsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Asiria Maŋtsɛ Shalmaneser batua Israel, ni Hoshea tsɔ̃ Shalmaneser tsulɔ, ni daa afi lɛ Hoshea woɔ too ehãa lɛ.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Shi fee sɛɛ lɛ Hoshea kpa too lɛ woo, kɛkɛ ni eyabi So, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ, dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni etse atua. Be ni Shalmaneser na le enɛ lɛ, etsu ayamɔ Hoshea, ni ewo lɛ tsuŋ. Samaria Shigbeemɔ

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asiria Maŋtsɛ Shalmaneser fã ta ebatua Israel, ni ebasa Samaria yi afii etɛ̃.

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Hoshea yinɔ afi ni ji nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ lɛ, Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔ Samaria. Kɛkɛ ni eŋɔ Israelbii nom kɛtee Asiria; eŋɔ amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi kɛtee Hala maŋ wulu lɛ mli; ekɛ mɛi komɛi hu tee Habor Faa lɛ naa yɛ Gozan kpokpai anɔ; ekɛ mɛi komɛi hu tee Media maji wuji lɛ amli.

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Samaria gbee shi, ejaakɛ Israelbii lɛ fee esha shi Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ, mɔ ni kpɔ̃ amɛ kɛjɛ Farao, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ, ni ejie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛyaja nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi moŋ.

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: Amɛyanyiɛ jeŋmaji ni Yehowa shwie amɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ akusumi lɛ asɛɛ, ni amɛyaye Israel maŋtsɛmɛi srɔtoi lɛ akusumi ni amɛsɔ̃sɔ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Ni Israelbii lɛ fee nii ni ejaaa gbɛ amɛshi Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛmamɔ jamɔhei grɔŋŋi amɛhã amɛhe yɛ amɛmajimaji lɛ fɛɛ amli, amɛmamɔ kɛjɛ bulɔi amɔɔ ni kwɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee maŋ ni atswa gbogbo awo he lɛ mli.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Ni amɛfee Ashera amãgãi, ni amɛfee wɔŋkoi yɛ gɔŋkpɔ fɛɛ gɔŋkpɔ ni kwɔ nɔ, kɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni ebu kusuu shishi.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Ni amɛshãshãa tsofakɛŋma yɛ jamɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ fɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni jeŋmaji ni Yehowa shwie amɛ kɛje amɛhiɛ lɛ fee lɛ; ni amɛfee nibii fɔ̃ji amɛkɛwo Yehowa mlila.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Ni amɛja wɔji ni tsɛbelɛ Yehowa ewo amɛ shi yɛ he akɛ, “Nyɛkafea nɛkɛ nɔ ko” lɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Yehowa tsɔ̃ gbalɔi lɛ kɛ ninalɔi lɛ anɔ, ni ebɔ Israel kɛ Yuda kɔkɔ akɛ, “Nyɛkpalea kɛjea nyɛgbɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛyea mikitãi lɛ kɛ mikpɔi lɛ anɔ, kitãi fɛɛ ni mitsɔ̃ mitsuji gbalɔi lɛ anɔ miwo nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ, ni nyɛ hu gbalɔi lɛ kɛba hã nyɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ amɛbooo toi; amɛfee amɛhe kuɛŋtilɔi tamɔ amɛtsɛmɛi ni heee Yehowa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ amɛyeee lɛ.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Amɛkwa ekpɔi lɛ kɛ ekpãŋmɔ ni ekɛ amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kpãŋ lɛ, kɛ kɔkɔ ni ebɔ amɛ lɛ. Amɛyaja yakayaka amãgãi, ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ yaka gbɔmɛi; ni amɛyanyiɛ jeŋmaji ni ebɔle amɛ kɛkpe ni Yehowa ewo amɛ kitã yɛ amɛhe akɛ amɛkafee amɛnii tamɔ amɛ lɛ asɛɛ.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Ni amɛkwa Yehowa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ kitãi lɛ, ni amɛfee shika tsinabii enyɔ amãgã amɛhã amɛhe. Amɛfee Ashera amãgã, ni amɛja ŋulamii, ni amɛsɔ̃mɔ Baal.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Amɛŋɔ amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei amɛshãshãa afɔle amɛhã jemawɔji, amɛkala, ni amɛsaa amɛyeyee ŋkunyai. Amɛhɔ̃ɔhɔ̃ɔ amɛhe amɛhã efɔŋfeemɔ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni amɛkɛwo Yehowa mli la.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa mli fu Israel naakpa, ni ehã aŋɔ amɛ nom; eshwɛɛɛ akutso ko akutso ko akɛ ja Yuda akutso lɛ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Shi Yudabii lɛ hu yeee Yehowa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ kitãi lɛ anɔ, shi moŋ amɛyanyiɛ Israelbii lɛ akusumi lɛ asɛɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa kwa Israel kɛ Yuda shwiei lɛ fɛɛ, ni ehã amɛna amanehulu, ni egbala amɛtoi, ni etu amɛ ewo nihalɔi adɛŋ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni eshwie amɛ kɛjɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa tse Israel kɛjɛ Yuda he lɛ, Israelbii lɛ wo Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ, amɛmaŋtsɛ. Yeroboam hã Israel je Yehowa sɛɛ, ni ehã amɛfee esha kpeteŋkple.

english_verse: The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam,
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ yanyiɛ eshai ni Yeroboam fee lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ, ni amɛkpaleee kɛjeee he,

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: kɛyashi beyinɔ ni Yehowa shwie amɛ kɛje ehiɛ kwraa tamɔ bɔ ni ewie kɛtsɔ̃ etsuji gbalɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, aŋɔ Israelbii anom kɛje amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtee Asiria, ni jɛi amɛyɔɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Asiriabii bahi shi yɛ Israel

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ yaŋɔ mɛi kɛjɛ Babilon kɛ Kuta kɛ Ava kɛ Hamat kɛ Sefarwaim, ni ekɛ amɛ ba Israel; ni amɛbahi maji ni kulɛ Israelbii ni yɔɔ nomŋɔɔ mli lɛ hi lɛ. Ni amɛŋɔ Samaria maŋ wulu lɛ hu amɛfata he.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni amɛbahi jɛi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, amɛjaaa Yehowa; no hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa hã jatai yabote amɛteŋ, ni amɛgbegbee amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ayakɛɛ Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Jeŋmaji lɛ anɔ bii ni oyaloo obato Israel maji lɛ amli lɛ, amɛleee shikpɔŋ ni amɛbato nɔ lɛ nyɔŋmɔ lɛ jamɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, etsu jatai kɛba maŋbii lɛ ateŋ, ni naa, amɛgbegbee maŋbii lɛ ekomɛi, ejaakɛ amɛleee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ suɔmɔnaa nii.”

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ fã akɛ, “Nyɛhãa osɔfoi ni nyɛyaŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ayaa ni eyahi jɛi, koni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔŋmɔ lɛ suɔmɔnaa nii lɛ.”

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni osɔfoi ni amɛyaŋɔ amɛ nom kɛjɛ Samaria kɛtee Asiria lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome tee, ni eyahi Betel, ni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ bɔ ni amɛja Yehowa amɛhã.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Shi maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ bii ni aloo amɛ kɛtee Israel nɛɛ feefee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɔŋmɔi, ni amɛŋɔ amɛ amɛto jamɔhei grɔŋŋi ni Israelbii ni aŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ efee momo lɛ. Maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ bii kɛ amɛnyɔŋmɔ lɛ to hei ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Babilonbii lɛ fee Sukot Benot, ni Kutabii lɛ fee Nergal, ni Hamatbii lɛ fee Ashima,

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: ni Avabii lɛ fee Nibhaz kɛ Tartak; ni Sefarwaimbii lɛ kɛ amɛmusuŋbii shãshãa afɔle amɛhãhãa amɛnyɔŋmɔi ni ji Adramelek kɛ Anamelek.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjaa Yehowa, ni asaŋ amɛjaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɔmɔi lɛ hu, tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni ayaloo amɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛba lɛ akusumi yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔ lɛ amɛkã he amɛmiifee nakai kusumi lɛ lolo. Amɛjaaa Yehowa kome pɛ kɛkɛ, ni amɛyeee akpɔi kɛ kitãi ni Yehowa wo Yakob shwiei lɛ anɔ. Yakob mɔ ni Yehowa tsake egbɛi, ni ewo lɛ Israel lɛ.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ amɛ kpãŋ, ni ewo amɛ kitã akɛ, “Nyɛkajaa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi, ni nyɛkakotoa amɛ hu, ni nyɛkasɔmɔa amɛ, ni nyɛkashãa afɔle nyɛhãa amɛ.

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ nyɛjaa Yehowa, mɔ ni kɛ hewalɛ kpele kpɔ̃ nyɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba lɛ. Lɛ nyɛjaa, ni lɛ nɔŋŋ nyɛshãa afɔle nyɛhãa.

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Ni kpãŋmɔ ni mi kɛ nyɛ kpãŋ lɛ, nyɛhiɛ akakpaa nɔ. Nyɛkajaa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi.

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: Nyɛjaa Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni lɛ ebaajie nyɛ yɛ nyɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ fɛɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ amɛbooo toi, ni amɛkã he amɛfee amɛsá nii lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ jeŋmaji nɛɛ ja Yehowa, shi amɛsɔ̃mɔ amɛmãgãi lɛ hu. Amɛbii kɛ amɛbii abii hu, bɔ ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ amɛ hu amɛfeɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ.

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Nyɛkahãa Hezekia milakaa nyɛ; ejaakɛ enyɛŋ ejie nyɛ kɛje midɛŋ.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Nyɛkaboa Hezekia toi! Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Nyɛkɛ mi abakpãtãa, ni nyɛjea kpo kɛbaa miŋɔɔ. No dani nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aaaye ewain tso kɛ egbami tso yibii, ni nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aaanu enubu mli nu,

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: Ni efee nɔ ni ja yɛ Yehowa hiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni eblematsɛ David fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: Lɛ efite hei grɔŋŋi lɛ, ni ekumɔ amãgãi lɛ, ni egba Ashera wɔŋkoo lɛ. Ni ekumɔ akɔɔble onufu ni Mose fee lɛ, ejaakɛ kɛbashi nakai gbii lɛ anɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ shãa tsofakɛŋma amɛhãa onufu lɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Nehushtan.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Hezekia ŋɔ ehiɛ efɔ̃ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, bɔ sɔŋŋ ni Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi ni baye nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ ehiɛ kɛ mɛi ni nyiɛ esɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko ninaaa lɛ.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa anɔkwa; ni ejeee Yehowa sɛɛ, ni eye kitãi ni Yehowa wo Mose lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛ lɛ yɛ, ni he fɛɛ he ni eyaa lɛ eyayeɔ omanye. Etse Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ atua, ni esɔ̃mɔɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Lɛ etswia Filistibii lɛ anii kɛyashwie Gaza kɛ ekpokpai lɛ anɔ tɔ̃ɔ, kɛjɛ akrowa bibioo nɔ kɛyashi maŋ wulu ni atswa gbogbo awo he nɔ.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia yinɔ afi ni ji ejwɛ, ni ji Israel Maŋtsɛ Hoshea, Ela bi lɛ, yinɔ afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Asiria Maŋtsɛ Shalmaneser fã batua Samaria ni ji Israel maŋ wulu lɛ.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Ni afii etɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ eŋɔ maŋ lɛ. Hezekia yinɔ afi ni ji ekpaa, ni ji Israel Maŋtsɛ Hoshea yinɔ afi ni ji nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ, aŋɔ Samaria.

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Asiria Maŋtsɛ Sankerib fã ebatua Yuda maji ni atswa gbogboi awo he lɛ fɛɛ, ni eŋɔ maji lɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Hezekia tsu ayakɛɛ Asiria Maŋtsɛ Sankerib yɛ Lakish akɛ, “Mitɔ̃, hewɔ lɛ ofainɛ ni oku osɛɛ oya, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ooohe mi lɛ mawo.” Ni Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Hezekia abahã lɛ jwiɛtɛi talentai ohai etɛ̃ kɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi talentai nyɔŋmai etɛ̃.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, Hezekia kpɔlɔ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ shinai kɛ shinaatsei lɛ ahe shika nii ni lɛ Hezekia, Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ, diɛŋtsɛ eŋɔ ha he lɛ, ni eŋɔ fɛɛ ehã Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ tsu Tartan kɛ Rabsaris kɛ Rabshake kɛ ta babaoo kɛjɛ Lakish kɛtee Maŋtsɛ Hezekia ŋɔɔ, yɛ Yerusalɛm. Be ni amɛyashɛ jɛi lɛ, amɛyadamɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kpaakpo lɛ nujɔɔ lɛ masɛi, yɛ niiahefɔlɔi abɔɔ lɛ tɛmpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛtsɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, Hilkia bi Eliakim ni kwɛɔ maŋtsɛ shĩa lɛ, kɛ Shibna, woloŋmalɔ lɛ kɛ Asaf bi Yoa ni ji maŋtsɛ we lɛ woji anɔkwɛlɔ lɛ, je kpo tee amɛŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ani osusuɔ akɛ naafuu wiemɔ kɛkɛ ji tawuu he ŋaatoo, loo no ji hewalɛ ni akɛwuɔ ta lo? Namɔ nɔ po ohiɛ kã, hewɔ ni otse mihiɛ atua nɛɛ?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Naa, oŋɔ ohiɛ ofɔ̃ Ijipt nɔ, nakai glã ni eku momo, ni kɛji akpasa lɛ ni egbuɔ mɔ dɛ̃ kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ. Nakai Farao, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ, ji hã mɛi fɛɛ ni ŋɔɔ amɛhiɛ amɛfɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ.’ ”

translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ba, koni okɛ minuŋtsɔ Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ abata abasa, ni majie okpɔŋɔi akpei enyɔ mahã bo, akɛ ooona bo diɛŋtsɛ omɛi otara amɛnɔ lo?

translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hilkia bi Eliakim kɛ Shebna kɛ Yoa kɛɛ Rabshake akɛ, “Ofainɛ, okɛ wɔ otsuji lɛ awie yɛ Arambii awiemɔ mli, ejaakɛ wɔnuɔ; shi okɛ wɔ akawie Hebribii awiemɔ, ejaakɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ gbogbo lɛ nɔ lɛ miibo toi.”

translation_verse: Shi Rabshake kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Ani osusuɔ akɛ minuŋtsɔ tsu mi bo kɛ onuŋtsɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ? Ani jeee hii lɛ ni tara gbogbo lɛ nɔ lɛ hu aŋɔɔ etsu mi, mɛi ni alomɔ amɛ kɛ nyɛ fɛɛ akɛ ja amɛye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwamɔ ni amɛnu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshãmɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!

translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, bo Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ, miikpa bo fai, heremɔ wɔyiwala kɛjɛ edɛŋ, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛyelii fɛɛ ana ale akɛ bo, Yehowa, okome too pɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ.” Yesaia wiemɔ ni akɛyahã Maŋtsɛ lɛ (Yesaia

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: “Namɔ ahora obɔ, ni owie musubɔɔ wiemɔi oshi lɛ lɛ? Namɔ obolɔ owo lɛ; ni namɔ ogbɛ ohiŋmɛiŋ owo lɛ? Israel Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni!

translation_verse: Obɔfoi lɛ anɔ otsɔ̃ ni obabɔ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ ahora, ni okɛɛ, ‘Mikɛ mita shwiilii ekwɔ kɛtee gɔji ayiteiaŋ kɛtee Lebanon sɛɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Mifolɔ emli tsenedru tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ kɛ emli sɛsɛoi ni hi lɛ mishwie shi, ni mibote ekoo hayii lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ.

translation_verse: “Mile oshitee kɛ oshitamɔ kɛ oyaa kɛ obaa fɛɛ kɛ ogrimɔ ni ogri owo mi lɛ hu.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: Akɛni ogri owo mi, ni oshwãa lɛ ekwɔ kɛbashɛ mitoiŋ hewɔ lɛ, mikɛ mikpoŋ baawo ogugɔŋ, ni mikɛ mimanyoflɛ baawo odaaŋ, ni mikpala bo kɛku sɛɛ kɛtsɔ̃ gbɛ ni otsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.”

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ Yehowa kɛɛ Hezekia akɛ, “Ni enɛ baafee okadi ahã bo. Afi nɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛaaye nii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃, ni afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli hu, nyɛaaye nii ni kwɛ̃ yɛ nomɛi asɛɛ lɛ; shi afi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ mli lɛ, nyɛdua nii ni nyɛkpaa; ni nyɛfea waintromi hu ni nyɛyea emli yibii.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni eshwɛ ni hiɛ kã yɛ Yuda we lɛ, amɛaatsɛ̃rɛ fãi ekoŋŋ kɛya su mli tɔ̃ɔ tamɔ waintso, ni amɛaawo yibii.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mɛi komɛi kɛ̃ baashwɛ kɛaajɛ Yerusalɛm kɛ Zion aba ni amɛhiɛ kã, ejaakɛ Yehowa eto akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ ebaafee enɛ.

english_verse: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ Asiria Maŋtsɛ lɛ he nɛ, ‘Ebaŋ maŋ nɛɛ mli, ni etsɛ̃ŋ gãi kuli kome gaŋŋ ewoŋ maŋ nɛɛ mli. Ni asraafoi ni hiɛ tsɛŋi bɛŋkɛŋ maŋ lɛ, ni amɛkɛ kotokui ni shia yɔɔ mli efeŋ tasu kɛsa maŋ lɛ yi.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Gbɛ ni etsɔ̃ kɛba lɛ, no nɔŋŋ nɔ eeetsɔ̃ kɛaaku esɛɛ, ni ebaŋ maŋ nɛɛ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ. Mi, Yehowa mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mafã maŋ nɛɛ he, ni mahere eyiwala, yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihiɛ nyam hewɔ, kɛ shi ni miwo mitsulɔ David lɛ hu hewɔ.’ ” Maŋtsɛ Sankerib gbele (Yesaia

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asiria maŋtsɛ Sankerib shi jɛi kɛtee Nineve eyahi jɛi.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Hezekia gbo, ni ebi Manase baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: “Ao, Yehowa, kaimɔ bɔ ni misɔ̃mɔ bo, ni miye bo anɔkwa kɛ mitsui fɛɛ, ni mifee nɔ ni ja yɛ ohiɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Hezekia fo waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace,
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni Yesaia kɛɛ ejeɔ kpo yɛ mɔɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ:

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: “Kũu osɛɛ ni oyakɛɛ Hezekia, mimaŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ lɛ, akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Yehowa, otsɛ David Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, minu ofaikpamɔ lɛ, ni mina ohiɛ yaafonu lɛ; naa, mibatsa bo; ni biɛ gbii etɛ̃ lɛ, ooonyiɛ onane nɔ kɛaaya Yehowa we lɛ.

english_verse: “What did you show them?” Isaiah asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Gbalɔ Yesaia bi akɛ, “Mɛni amɛna yɛ owe lɛ mli?” Ni Hezekia hã hetoo akɛ, “Amɛna nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miwe lɛ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ minitoohei lɛ ni mikɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ.”

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yesaia kɛɛ maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ agbãmi adufao abaa! Aŋɔ eko akɛto asane lɛ nɔ, ni ehe baawa lɛ.”

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Yesaia kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Enɛ aaafee okadi ni jɛ Yehowa dɛŋ ahã bo, akɛ Yehowa baaye eshi ni ewo bo lɛ nɔ. Ani ooosumɔ akɛ atrakpoi lɛ asusuma ni kã atswere lɛ nɔ lɛ atsi kɛya hiɛ nane fãamɔi nyɔŋma aloo eba sɛɛsɛɛ nanefaamɔi nyɔŋma?”

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Hezekia hã hetoo akɛ, “Ewaaa hãaa susuma lɛ akɛ eeeya hiɛhiɛ nane fãamɔi nyɔŋma lɛ, shi moŋ, hã susuma lɛ aba sɛɛsɛɛ nanefaamɔi nyɔŋma lɛ.”

english_verse: Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz. The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ Yesaia sɔle ekpa Yehowa fai, ni Yehowa hã susuma ni etee hiɛhiɛ momo lɛ ba sɛɛsɛɛ yɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahaz atrakpoi lɛ anɔ nanefaamɔi nyɔŋma. Tsuji ni jɛ Babilon lɛ (Yesaia

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ Merodak-Baladan, Baladan bi ni ji Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, nu akɛ Maŋtsɛ Hezekia he miiye, hewɔ lɛ eŋma lɛ wolo, ni ekɛ nikeenii fata he ekɛtsu tsuji akɛyahã lɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia here mɛi ni atsu eŋɔɔ lɛ atuu, ni eŋɔ ejwetri ni eyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ejwiɛtɛi kɛ shika kɛ tsofakɛŋma, kɛ mui ni jara wa kɛ etawuu nibii lɛ atoohe fɛɛ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ewe lɛ loo enɔyelihei lɛ fɛɛ he ko he ko ni Hezekia kɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ.

english_verse: Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbalɔ Yesaia ba Maŋtsɛ Hezekia ŋɔɔ, ni ebabi lɛ akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ jɛ kɛba, ni mɛni wiemɔ amɛkɛba?” Hezekia hã hetoo akɛ, “Amɛjɛ Babilon tɔ̃ɔ kɛba.”

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yesaia kɛɛ Hezekia akɛ, “Bo Yehowa wiemɔ toi.

english_verse: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
translation_verse: ‘Naa, gbii miiba, be ni abaaloo nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ owe lɛ kɛ nibii ni otsɛmɛi lɛ ebua naa eto kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔ lɛ kɛaatee Babilon, ni ashiŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko.’ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Asaŋ bo diɛŋtsɛ omusuŋbii lɛ ekomɛi tete lɛ, aaaloo amɛ kɛaatee; ni aaafee amɛ osaii ni baasɔ̃mɔ yɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ mɔɔ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.” Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Hezekia nu Yesaia wiemɔ lɛ shishi akɛ, toiŋjɔlɛ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ baaba yɛ lɛ Hezekia lɛ ebe mli; no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ Yesaia akɛ, “Yehowa wiemɔ ni owie lɛ, wiemɔ jurɔ ni.” Hezekia gbele (

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Hezekia he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ ekãa ni efee lɛ kɛ kpaakpo kɛ ehe nujɔɔ ni efee ni ekɛtsɛ nu kɛba Yerusalɛm lɛ, aŋma yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.
translation_verse: Lɛ hu eba ejeŋ tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ Manase ba ejeŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it.
translation_verse: bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Naa, mikɛ nɔ fɔŋ baaba Yerusalɛm kɛ Yuda nɔ, koni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaanu he lɛ etoii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ mli aaafee lɛ heŋŋ.’

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ jamɔhei grɔŋŋi lɛ ni etsɛ Hezekia fite lɛ esaa emamɔ ekoŋŋ. Emamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi koni akɛshã afɔle ahã Baal; ni efee jemawɔŋ yoo Ashera amãgã tamɔ bɔ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab fee lɛ. Asaŋ Manase ja ŋwɛi ŋulamii lɛ, ni esɔ̃mɔ amɛ hu.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Emamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi ehã jemawɔji yɛ Yehowa we lɛ, he ni Yehowa ekɛɛ yɛ he akɛ, “Yerusalɛm ji he ni aaaja mi yɛ” lɛ.

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple,
translation_verse: Emamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi ehã ŋwɛi ŋulamii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ kpoi enyɔ lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: Ekɛ jemawɔŋyoo Ashera lɛ amãgã ni efee lɛ yama Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, he ni Yehowa kɛ David kɛ Solomon wie yɛ he akɛ, “Yerusalɛm Sɔlemɔ we nɛɛ ji he ni miŋɔ yɛ Israel akutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ akɛ he ni aja mi yɛ kɛya naanɔ lɛ.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Asaŋ mihaŋ Israel afã enane kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni miŋɔ mihã amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ nɔ, ni eyatsomlo dɔŋŋ; kɛji amɛjwɛŋ nɔ, ni amɛye kitãi fɛɛ ni miwo amɛ lɛ, kɛ mlai fɛɛ ni mitsulɔ Mose wo amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Shi Israel booo toi; ni Manase laka amɛ, ni amɛfee efɔŋ fe jeŋmaji ni Yehowa kpãtã amɛhiɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ tete.

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa tsɔ̃ etsuji ni ji gbalɔi lɛ anɔ ewie akɛ,

english_verse: King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols.
translation_verse: “Akɛni Manase, Yuda maŋtsɛ, tsu nɛkɛ nihiinii nɛɛ, ni efee efɔŋ fe nii ni Amorbii ni tsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ fee lɛ fɛɛ, ni ekɛ ewɔji lɛ hã Yuda hu fee esha hewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
translation_verse: Ni magbala Yerusalɛm toi tamɔ bɔ ni mifee Samaria lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni mifee Israel maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛ eshwiei lɛ. Mabɛɛ Yerusalɛmbii fɛɛ mashwie tamɔ atsumɔɔ kã mli keŋkeŋ, ni atsɔ̃ɔ abuɔ shi lɛ.

english_verse: I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies.
translation_verse: Ni makwa miwebii ni aaashwɛ lɛ, ni matu amɛ mawo amɛhenyɛlɔi adɛŋ, ni amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ nomii, ni aaaha amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii fɛɛ.

english_verse: My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛfee efɔŋ ni mihiɔ lɛ yɛ mihiɛ, ni amɛwowoo mimli la kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ je Ijipt lɛ aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni asaŋ Manase kpãtã mɛi babaoo diɛŋtsɛ ni efeko nɔ ko fɔŋ ko ahiɛ, kɛyashi beyinɔ ni Yerusalɛm he fɛɛ he yi tɔ kɛ la; dani esoro esha ni ehã Yuda fee, esha ni eji efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Manase he saji ni eshwɛ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni efee kɛ esha ni efee lɛ, aŋma fɛɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Manase gbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ Uza abɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ maŋtsɛ shĩa lɛ mli; ni ebi Amon baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amon (

english_verse: refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ekwa Yehowa, etsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ebaaa ejeŋ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Ni Amon tsuji lɛ tee eyinɔ apam, ni amɛgbe lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewe lɛ.

english_verse: While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.” Shaphan read it,
translation_verse: Be ni Shafan yɔɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, Hilkia kɛ wolo ko hã lɛ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Miyana Mla Wolo lɛ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ.” Shafan kane wolo lɛ.

english_verse: and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated.
translation_verse: “Yaa osɔfonukpa Hilkia ŋɔɔ, koni ekane shika ni akɛbaa Yehowa we lɛ ni shinaanaakwɛlɔi lɛ ebua naa kɛjɛ mɛi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ lɛ koni etu shika lɛ ewo nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ Yehowa we lɛ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ, koni amɛ hu amɛkɛhã nitsulɔi ni saa Yehowa we lɛ.

english_verse: the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work.
translation_verse: Amɛ ji kapintafoi lɛ kɛ tsumalɔi lɛ kɛ gbogbotswalɔi lɛ, koni akɛ eko ahe mplaŋi kɛ tɛi ni ako koni akɛsaa shĩa lɛ.

english_verse: They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: Akahã amɛbu shika ni atuɔ awoɔ amɛdɛŋ lɛ he akɔntaa ko, ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ anɔkwa.”

english_verse: then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Shafan, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, ba maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ebagba lɛ akɛ, “Otsuji lɛ eyaŋɔ shika ni yɔɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni amɛtu amɛwo mɛi ni kwɛɔ Yehowa we lɛ nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.
translation_verse: Ni Shafan, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, tsi tã etsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Osɔfonukpa Hilkia kɛ wolo ko ehã mi.” Ni Shafan kane wolo lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni be ni Maŋtsɛ Yosia nu Mla Wolo lɛ mli wiemɔi lɛ, ekɛ dɔlɛ gbala etadei yɛ ehe.

english_verse: At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã osɔfo Hilkia kɛ Shafan bi Ahikam, kɛ Mikaia bi Akbor, kɛ Shafan mɔ ni ji woloŋmalɔ lɛ, kɛ Asaia, maŋtsɛ tsulɔ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: “The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
translation_verse: “Nyɛyaa ni nyɛyabia Yehowa nii nyɛhãa mi kɛ maŋbii lɛ kɛ Yuda maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɛkɛ wolo ni ana nɛɛ mli wiemɔi lɛ ahewɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa mli ni ewo la ewo wɔ nɛɛ naa wa naakpa, ejaakɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ booo wiemɔi ni yɔɔ wolo nɛɛ mli lɛ toi koni amɛye emli wiemɔi ni kɔɔ wɔhe lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: The five men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Osɔfo Hilkia kɛ Ahikam kɛ Akbor kɛ Shafan kɛ Asaia yiŋ amɛtee gbalɔyoo Hulda ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyabɔ lɛ amaniɛ. Yerusalɛm akutso hee ko mli Hulda yɔɔ. Hulda nɛɛ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ atadei ni yɔɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: she said: You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him:
translation_verse: Hulda kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, nyɛyakɛa maŋtsɛ lɛ ni tsu nyɛ miŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ:

english_verse: “Josiah, I am the Lord! And I will see to it that this country and everyone living in it will be destroyed. It will happen just as this book says.
translation_verse: ‘Naa, mahã nɔ fɔŋ aba biɛ nɛɛ kɛ biɛbii lɛ anɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma yɛ wolo ni Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ kane lɛ mli lɛ.

translation_verse: Akɛni amɛkwa mi, ni amɛyashã tsofakɛŋma amɛhã nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi, ni amɛkɛ amɛninenaa nitsumɔi lɛ ewo mimli la hewɔ lɛ, mimli baawo la awo Yerusalɛm naakpa.’

english_verse: Josiah sent some men to Hinnom Valley just outside Jerusalem with orders to make the altar there unfit for worship. That way, people could no longer use it for sacrificing their children to the god Molech.

english_verse: Some of the kings of Judah, especially Manasseh, had built altars in the two courts of the temple and in the room that Ahaz had built on the palace roof. Josiah had these altars torn down and smashed to pieces, and he had the pieces thrown into Kidron Valley, just outside Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni afɔleshãa latɛ ni yɔɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahaz ŋwɛitsu lɛ yiteŋ ni Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ fee, kɛ afɔleshãa latɛi lɛ ni maŋtsɛ Manase fee yɛ Yehowa we lɛ kpoi enyɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Yosia kumɔ eshwie shi, ni egbɛlɛ, ni eloo kɛjɛ jɛi, ni ekɛyawo Kidron Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: After that, he closed down the shrines that Solomon had built east of Jerusalem and south of Spoil Hill to honor Astarte the disgusting goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.

english_verse: He tore down the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole used in the worship of Asherah. Then he had the whole area covered with human bones.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Yosia kumɔ amãgãi lɛ, ni egba Ashera wɔŋkoi lɛ eshwie shi, ni ekɛ gbɔmɛi awui shwã jɛi.

english_verse: But Josiah was not finished yet. At Bethel he destroyed the shrine and the altar that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built and that had caused the Israelites to sin. Josiah had the shrine and the Asherah pole burned and ground into dust.

english_verse: Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
translation_verse: Gedalia kãmɔ amɛ kɛ amɛwebii lɛ kitã akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei yɛ Babilon tsuji lɛ ahewɔ, nyɛhia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nyɛsɔ̃mɔa Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni aaahi ahã nyɛ.”

english_verse: Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Shi eba mli akɛ nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ Elishama bi Ishmael, ni eji Netania nabi lɛ ni ejɛ maŋtsɛ shwiei lɛ ateŋ lɛ kɛ mɛi nyɔŋma ba, ni amɛbatswia Gedalia nii ni egbo. Amɛgbe Yudafoi kɛ Babilonbii ni kɛ Gedalia yɔɔ Mizpa lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ te shi, kɛjɛ mɔ bibioo nɔ kɛyashi mɔ wulu nɔ, amɛ kɛ asraafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee Ijipt; ejaakɛ amɛmiishe Babilonbii lɛ gbeyei. Ajie Yehoiakin kɛje gboklɛfoi atsuŋ (Yeremia

english_verse: Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ewil-merodak kɛ Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakin wieɔ kɛ naajɔlɛ, ni ehã lɛ gbɛhe ni kwɔ fe maŋtsɛmɛi krokomɛi ni kɛ Yehoiakin yɔɔ nomŋɔɔ mli yɛ Babilon lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ehã Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakin kpa gboklɛfoi atade woo, ni ekɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ye nii daa, ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Japheth was the father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Yafet fɔ bihii kpawo, amɛ ji Gomer kɛ Magog kɛ Madai kɛ Yavan kɛ Tubal kɛ Meshek kɛ Tiras.

english_verse: Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Abraham yɛ hemɔ ko ni gbɛi ji Ketura. Abraham kɛ lɛ fɔ bihii ekpaa: Zimran kɛ Yokshan kɛ Medan kɛ Midian kɛ Ishbak kɛ Shua. Yokshan fɔ bihii enyɔ: Sheba kɛ Dedan.

english_verse: Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior.
translation_verse: Kush fɔ binuu ko ni atsɛ lɛ akɛ Nimrod. Lɛ eje shishi efee ehe nuu kãkãlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
translation_verse: Ham bi Ijipt lɛ eshwiei ji Lidiabii lɛ kɛ Anambii lɛ kɛ Lehabbii lɛ kɛ Naftubii lɛ
