english_verse: Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
translation_verse: Belɛ nii fɛɛ ni Solomon wo amɛtsumɔ nɔ kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni ato Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ shishi aahu kɛyashi agbe naa ni Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ ye emuu lɛ, atsu kɛgbe naa kɛ omanye.

english_verse: Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Solomon yiŋ etee lɛji amaamɔhei enyɔ ni ji Ezion-Geber kɛ Elat yɛ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋshɔnaa.

english_verse: Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hiram wo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esɛrɛfoi ni ahe esa gbɛ kɛ lɛji kɛba eŋɔɔ, ni Solomon tsuji bafata asrɛfoi lɛ ahe ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee Ofir amɛyaloo shika ŋmiiŋmi ni tsiimɔ ji talentai ohai ejwɛ kɛ nyɔŋmai enumɔ amɛbahã Maŋtsɛ Solomon.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Solomon hã lɛ saji ni ebibii lɛ lɛ fɛɛ hetoo; ekoeko kwraa bɛ mli ni Solomon nyɛɛɛ lɛ naa atsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Solomon akɛ, “Ohe saji kɛ onilee ni minu yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔkwale ni.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told.
translation_verse: Tsɛbelɛ miheee saji ni minu lɛ miyeee kɛyashi mibashɛ biɛ. Shi agbɛnɛ mibana kɛ mihiŋmɛitsei enyɔ nɛɛ. Moaŋ saji ni agbagbaa mi lɛ shɛɛɛ onilee lɛ mlijaa fã tete. Nibii ni agba mi lɛ baaa he kwraa.

english_verse: Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Ajɔɔ owebii. Otsuji ni sɔmɔɔ bo, ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɛŋkɛ bo be fɛɛ be ni amɛnaa hegbɛ amɛboɔ onaa nilee toi lɛ, amɛto aahu kpele.

english_verse: I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
translation_verse: Ajie Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yi akɛ esa ehiɛ ni ekɛ bo ta emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ koni oye maŋtsɛ yɛ biɛ. Akɛni oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ miidɔ Israel he ni eeesumɔ akɛ ebaa amɛyi kɛya naanɔ lɛ, no hewɔ eto bo Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ koni okojo ni oye jalɛ sane yɛ amɛteŋ.”

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, a large amount of jewels, and the best spices anyone had ever seen.
translation_verse: Sheba Maŋnyɛ lɛ ke maŋtsɛ Solomon shika ŋmiiŋmi ni tsiimɔ ji talentai oha kɛ nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ tsofakɛŋma pii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ ojarawatɛi hu. Anako tsofakɛŋma ni tamɔ nɔ ni Sheba Maŋnyɛ lɛ kɛbake Maŋtsɛ Solomon lɛ eko dã.

english_verse: not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
translation_verse: dani soro shika ni jarayelɔi lɛ kɛ guɔyelɔi lɛ hu kɛbaa lɛ. Arabia maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ kɛ amralofoi ni kwɛɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpokpai lɛ anɔ lɛ hu bahãa Maŋtsɛ Solomon shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, aŋmala kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyata enaagbee yɛ woji ni agbɛii baa nɛɛ amli: Natan he Saji Awolo lɛ, kɛ Ahia, Shilonyo Gbalɔ lɛ, kɛ Gbalɔ Ido Ninaa lɛ ni ji wolo lɛ ni wieɔ Nebat bi Yeroboam Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ hu he lɛ.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon hã akɛ shuɔ wu fee maŋtsɛ sɛi kpeteŋkple ko, ni akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ha he.

english_verse: It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne,
translation_verse: Akwɔɔ atrakpoi ekpaa dani ashɛɔ maŋtsɛ sɛi nɛɛ he; ni nane shi maŋoo ni akɛ shika eha he hu ma maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ hiɛ. Nine yɛ maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ he biɛ kɛ biɛ, ni jata ni ashɔ̃ kome damɔ sɛi lɛ nine lɛ masɛi.

english_verse: and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Ato jatai ni ashɔ̃ nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ amãmɔ atrakpoi ekpaa lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Atrakpoi lɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko naabu yɛ ekoŋgbɛ lɛ, jata kome ma jɛi. Afeko nii nɛɛ henɔ pɛŋ yɛ maŋtsɛ ko maŋtsɛ ko yinɔ.

english_verse: Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon kpuji fɛɛ ni ekɛnuɔ nii lɛ shika akɛfee. Tsɛnsii kɛ amɛhenɔi nibii fɛɛ hu ni yɔɔ Lebanon Kooŋ Tsu lɛ mli lɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi nɔŋŋ akɛfee. Solomon yinɔ lɛ abuuu jwiɛtɛi ahãaa fɛifɛi.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ eyɛ lɛji ni fata Maŋtsɛ Huram lɛji lɛ ahe kɛyaa Tarshish kɛbaa. Daa afii etɛ̃ lɛ Solomon lɛji lɛ jɛɔ Tarshish baa ni amɛhiɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shuɔwu kɛ ofoi kɛ aŋfraŋi.

english_verse: Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ maŋtsɛ ko maŋtsɛ ko kɛ Solomon yeee egbɔ yɛ ninamɔ kɛ nilee gbɛfaŋ.

english_verse: Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hiɛɔ edɛŋ nikee kɛbaa: jwiɛtɛi nibii kɛ shika nibii kɛ atadei kɛ tawuunii kɛ tsofakɛŋma kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tejiokpɔŋɔi; ni nɛkɛ akɛ nibii nɛɛ yaa ni abaa daa afi.

english_verse: He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ yɛ Solomon shishi kɛjɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ naa kɛyashi Filistibii ashikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ Ijipt husui lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon hã jwiɛtɛi bu tamɔ tɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni ehã tsenedru tsei tsɔ̃mɔ tamɔ sikamore tsei ni yɔɔ Israel gɔji ajɔiaŋ shikpɔji anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri. Solomon Dies (
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Solomon shɛɔ okpɔŋɔi kɛjɛɔ Ijipt kɛ maŋsɛɛ majimaji fɛɛ anɔ kɛbaa. Maŋtsɛ Solomon he sane lɛ naamuu (

english_verse: he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Solomon tsɔ̃ esɛɛ, ni afu lɛ yɛ etsɛ David maŋ lɛ mli, kɛkɛ ni ebi Rehoboam baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
translation_verse: Rehoboam yiŋ etee Shekem ejaakɛ Kooyigbɛ Akutsei lɛ fɛɛ anaa ebakpe shi yɛ jɛi koni amɛwo lɛ maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon.
translation_verse: Be ni Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ, nu he yɛ Ijipt, he ni ejo Maŋtsɛ Solomon naa foi kɛtee eyatee yɛ lɛ, eku esɛɛ eba.

english_verse: The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Kooyigbɛ Akutsei lɛ tsu koni ayakpee Yeroboam abahã amɛ; ni amɛ kɛ lɛ fɛɛ tee amɛkɛ Rehoboam yawie akɛ,

english_verse: “Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
translation_verse: “Jatsu ni otsɛ hã wɔtere lɛ tsii tsɔ̃ kwraa. Kɛji ogbɔ́ sɔɔmɔ ni otsɛ hã wɔsɔmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni shihilɛ mli fee mɛlɛo ehã wɔ lɛ, no lɛ wɔɔɔsɔmɔ bo.”

english_verse: Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Rehoboam hã amɛ hetoo akɛ, “Nyɛhãa mi gbii etɛ̃ koni nyɛbahea sane lɛ hetoo.” Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ ni amɛtee.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam tsɛ hii onukpai ni sɔmɔ etsɛ Solomon akɛ ŋaawolɔi lɛ ajina, ni ebi amɛ ŋaawoo ni ekɛɛ, “Te mihã maŋbii lɛ asane lɛ hetoo mikɛɛ tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Hii onukpai lɛ jie maŋtsɛ lɛ naa akɛ, “Kɛji omli hi hã maŋbii nɛɛ, ni ofee nii ni sa amɛhiɛ ni ohã amɛ naajɔlɛ hetoo lɛ, no lɛ amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ otsuji daanɛɛ.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Shi Rehoboam shi ŋaa ni hii onukpai lɛ wo lɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni ekɛ obalahii ni ji etipɛŋfoi, ni asaŋ amɛ amɛ ji eŋaawolɔi agbɛnɛ lɛ tee sane lɛ he ajina.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ ŋaa nyɛwoɔ mi? Mɛɛ hetoo mihãa gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ni ebabi mi akɛ migbɔ́ sɔɔmɔ ni mitsɛ hã amɛsɔmɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Mitsɛ tere nyɛ jatsu ni tsii; shi mibaŋmɛ jatsu lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsii aahu fe mitsɛ nɔ lɛ. Ekɛ kpãa yi nyɛ, shi mi lɛ mikɛ kpelebi baagwao nyɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly
translation_verse: Shi Rehoboam kɛ maŋbii lɛ ewieee kɛ naajɔlɛ. Ekwa ŋaa ni hii onukpai lɛ wo lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam ŋɔ oblahii lɛ aŋaawoo lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mitsɛ tere nyɛ jatsu ni tsii, shi mijatsu lɛ baatsii aahu fe mitsɛ nɔ lɛ. Mitsɛ kɛ kpãa yi nyɛ; shi mi lɛ mikɛ kpelebi baagwao nyɛ.”

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Be ni Rehoboam shɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, ebua Yuda kɛ Benyamin akutsei lɛ amli hii tabilɔi akpei oha kɛ nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ anaa. Eyiŋtoo ji akɛ ekɛ Israel kooyigbɛ akutsei lɛ miiya ayawu ta koni akutsei lɛ abaje emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin. The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
translation_verse: agbɛnɛ tsɛŋi kɛ akplɔi fɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ̃ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ Rehoboam ye Yuda kɛ Benyamin akutsei lɛ anɔ. Osɔfoi kɛ Levibii kɛ amɛhe badɔmɔ Yudabii

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Gbalɔ Shemaia akɛ,

english_verse: “The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops. Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
translation_verse: “Nyɛkayaa ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ yawua ta. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ akpale aya ewe, ejaakɛ mi mihã nɔ ni eba lɛ ba.” Amɛbo Yehowa toi, ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛyaaa dɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ Yeroboam ayawu. Rehoboam waje maji lɛ

english_verse: Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included
translation_verse: Rehoboam hi Yerusalɛm, ni ehã atswa gbogboi awo Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji wuji ni agbɛii baa nɛɛ ahe, ni akɛ wajewajee amɛ:

english_verse: Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
translation_verse: Betlehem kɛ Etam kɛ Tekoa,

english_verse: Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam,
translation_verse: kɛ Bet-Zur kɛ Soko kɛ Adullam,

english_verse: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
translation_verse: kɛ Gat kɛ Maresha kɛ Zif,

english_verse: Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
translation_verse: kɛ Adoraim kɛ Lakish kɛ Azeka,

english_verse: he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine,
translation_verse: Ehã awaje maji wuji nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ, ni eto tatsɛnukpa koni ekwɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ; asaŋ ebua niyenii kɛ mu kɛ wain hu naa eto eko fɛɛ eko mli, kɛ

english_verse: The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi kɛ Levibii ni yɔɔ Israel kooyigbɛ kpokpai lɛ anɔ fɛɛ bua amɛhe naa kɛba wuoyi ni amɛkɛ amɛhe badɔmɔ Yuda.

english_verse: And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah.
translation_verse: Levibii nɛɛ shi amɛŋmɔji kɛ shikpɔji, ni amɛba Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm ejaakɛ Maŋtsɛ Yeroboam kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni ba yɛ esɛɛ lɛ eŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛtsu amɛnii akɛ Yehowa osɔfoi.

english_verse: Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
translation_verse: Yeroboam wo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esɔfoi koni amɛsɔmɔ yɛ wɔji ajamɔhei lɛ kɛ tsinabi amãgãi ni efee lɛ.

english_verse: But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã mɛi fɛɛ ni miitao akɛ amɛja Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, anɔkwale mli lɛ, fã kɛjɛ Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ amli kɛba Yerusalɛm bɔ ni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛshã afɔle amɛhã amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon. Rehoboam's Family
translation_verse: Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ abaa lɛ bawo Solomon bi Rehoboam maŋtsɛyeli lɛ hewalɛ yɛ Yuda, ni amɛhã ehi shi shweshweeshwe afii etɛ̃ ejaakɛ amɛhi shi bɔ pɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ David kɛ Solomon yinɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Rehoboam ŋamɛi kɛ ebii

english_verse: Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
translation_verse: Amɛfɔ bihii etɛ̃: Yeush kɛ Shemaria kɛ Zaham.

english_verse: Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Rehoboam yaŋɔ Maaka, Absalom biyoo lɛ, hu akɛ eŋa, ni ekɛ lɛ fɔ bihii ejwɛ: Abia kɛ Atai kɛ Ziza kɛ Shelomit.

english_verse: so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king.
translation_verse: Asaŋ ewo ekɛ Maaka bi Abia lɛ onukpa kɛ lumɔ hã enyɛmimɛi lɛ ejaakɛ Rehoboam to eyiŋ akɛ eeewo lɛ maŋtsɛ koni eye esɛɛ.

english_verse: Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_verse: Rehoboam ye hiɛshikãmɔ sane akɛ ejara ebihii lɛ fɛɛ ewowoo Yuda kɛ Benyamin shikpɔji lɛ anɔ maji wuji ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe lɛ amli akɛ lumɛi. Ehã amɛ niyenii babaoo, asaŋ ebibii yei babaoo ashi ehã amɛ akɛ amɛŋamɛi.

english_verse: but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Rehoboam fee nɔ ni ejaaa ejaakɛ ekɛ etsui efɔɔɔ nɔ akɛ eeetao koni ele nɔ ni ji Yehowa suɔmɔnaanii.

english_verse: So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam yinɔ afi ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛni amɛtɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ lɛ, Ijipt Maŋtsɛ Shishak batua Yerusalɛm

english_verse: He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Shishak shɔ̃ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ, kɛkɛ ni efã koni ebatua Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gbalɔ Shemaia tee ni eyanina Rehoboam kɛ Yuda maŋ onukpai ni ebabua amɛhe naa yɛ Yerusalɛm yɛ Shishak hewɔ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ, ‘Nyɛkwa mi, no hewɔ lɛ, mi hu miŋmɛɛ nyɛhe mihã Shishak.’ ”

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ kpɛlɛ amɛtɔ̃mɔ nɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa sane ja.”

english_verse: When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah: The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry,
translation_verse: Be ni Yehowa na akɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ enukpai lɛ eje amɛhe sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ Gbalɔ Shemaia akɛ, “Amɛje amɛhe sɛɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, mikpataŋ amɛhiɛ, shi mibahere amɛ fioo ko kɛji Shishak batua maŋ lɛ koni Shishak akafee Yerusalɛm butuu yɛ mimlifu lɛ naa.

english_verse: he will conquer and rule them. Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ amɛbaatsɔ̃mɔ Shishak tsuji bɔ ni afee ni amɛna srɔto ni yɔɔ mi sɔɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ hu sɔɔmɔ teŋ.”

english_verse: Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Ijipt Maŋtsɛ Shishak batua Yerusalɛm, ni eloo Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛŋ jwetrii lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛŋ hu jwetrii fɛɛ, kɛ shika tsɛŋi ni Solomon fee lɛ hu kɛtee.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Rehoboam hã afee akɔɔble tsɛŋi akɛto shika tsɛŋi lɛ anajiaŋ; ni etu akɔɔble tsɛŋi nɛɛ ewo mɛi ni buɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ agboi lɛ anaa lɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
translation_verse: Ni be fɛɛ be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ miiya Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli lɛ, bulɔi lɛ yakɔlɔɔ tsɛŋi nɛɛ amɛhiɛɔ, ni kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpaleɔ kɛyaa amɛkɛyatoɔ bulɔi atsu lɛ mli.

english_verse: Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again. Rehoboam's Rule in Judah (
translation_verse: Akɛ ni Rehoboam ba ehe shi ehã Yehowa hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa ŋmɛɛ emli ni fu Rehoboam lɛ he, ni ekpãtãaa nibii ahiɛ tsɔ̃ ko, ni no hewɔ lɛ, nibii shwere kɛ̃ yɛ Yuda. Rehoboam he sane lɛ naamuu

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Rehoboam he saji lɛ aŋmala kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyata naagbee yɛ Gbalɔ Shemaia kɛ Ninalɔ Idomei ahe saji lɛ amli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ ta kã Yeroboam kɛ Rehoboam teŋ.

english_verse: When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_verse: Rehoboam tsɔ̃ esɛɛ ni afu lɛ yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ. Ebinuu Abia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Be ni Yeroboam na afii nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ akɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni awo Abia hu akɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army.
translation_verse: kɛkɛ ni Yudabii lɛ bɔ oshe. Abia kɛ Yudabii lɛ fã kɛyatua Israelbii lɛ yɛ oshebɔɔ lɛ mli, ni Nyɔŋmɔ ye Yeroboam kɛ Israelbii lɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you.
translation_verse: Ŋmɛnɛ lɛ nyɛ hu nyɛte shi kɛmiishi hewalɛ ni Yehowa ejɔɔ nɔ ehã David shwiei lɛ ejaakɛ nyɛyi fa, ni asaŋ nyɛhiɛ shika tsinabii lɛ ni Yeroboam fee hã nyɛ akɛ nyɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ.

english_verse: and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other.
translation_verse: Abia ye maŋtsɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm afii etɛ̃. Abia nyɛ gbɛi ji Milkaia ni ji Uriel ni jɛ Gibea maŋ lɛ mli lɛ biyoo lɛ. Ta te shi yɛ Abia kɛ Yeroboam teŋ.

english_verse: Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted: Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites!
translation_verse: Tai enyɔ lɛ yakpe yɛ Efraim gɔji shikpɔji lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni Abia tee eyadamɔ gɔŋ lɛ eko ni gbɛi ji Zemaraim Gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ, ni ebo etsɛ Yeroboam kɛ Israel ta lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Agoo! Yeroboam kɛ Israel hii!

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family.
translation_verse: Nyɛleee kwraa akɛ yɛ Kpãŋmɔ ni emli ehiii kuu ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ David kpãŋ naa lɛ Yehowa jɔɔ Israel maŋtsɛyeli nɔ ehã David kɛ eshwiei kɛmiiya naanɔ lo?

english_verse: But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled.
translation_verse: Shi Yeroboam, Nebat bi lɛ te shi, ni etse enuŋtsɔ Solomon ni ji David bi lɛ hiɛ atua.

english_verse: Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
translation_verse: Ena hii fɔ̃ji kɛ yakagbɔmɛi efata ehe kɛwo lɛ hewalɛ, ni akɛni nakai be mli lɛ Rehoboam edako, asaŋ ehiɛ waaa hu hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ amɛ.

english_verse: You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
translation_verse: Te nyɛshwie Aaron shwiei ni ji mɛi ni yeɔ Yehowa osɔfo lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ hu, ni nyɛwowoo nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛsɔfoi moŋ tamɔ bɔ ni shikpɔji krokomɛi lɛ anɔ bii feɔ lɛ? Te mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni hiɛɔ edɛŋ tsina oblayoo loo ojwɛnii kpawo kɛba lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ awo lɛ nakai nibii ni jeee Nyɔŋmɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni wo lɛ osɔfo?

english_verse: But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants.
translation_verse: “Wɔ lɛ, Yehowa ji wɔNyɔŋmɔ, ni wɔkwako lɛ. Aaron shwiei lɛ ji mɛi ni yeɔ osɔfo, ni amɛsɔmɔɔ Yehowa yɛ wɔteŋ, ni Levibii lɛ hiɛ amɛnitsumɔi lɛ amli amɛmiitsu pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him!
translation_verse: Daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ amɛshãa shãa afɔlei kɛ tsofakɛŋma amɛhãa Yehowa. Amɛkɛ aboloo ni akɛmaa Yehowa hiɛ lɛ maa ehiɛ yɛ okplɔ̃ ni atsuu he lɛ nɔ, ni daa gbɛkɛ lɛ amɛsuɔ shika kanetso lɛ nɔ kanei lɛ. Wɔ lɛ, wɔhiɛ mli wɔmiifee nibii ni Yehowa eto akɛ afee lɛ; shi nyɛ lɛ nyɛkwa Yehowa.

english_verse: That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
translation_verse: Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ wɔ yɛ, ni lɛ enyiɛ wɔta lɛ hiɛ, asaŋ esɔfoi lɛ hu yɛ biɛ kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛi, ni amɛbaakpã kɛbɔ tawuu oshe amɛwo nyɛ. Ataamɛi Israelbii, nyɛkakaa kwraa akɛ nyɛkɛ Yehowa, nyɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ baawu ta. Nyɛyeŋ kunim kɔkɔɔkɔ.”

english_verse: Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Belɛ Yudabii lɛ ye Israelbii lɛ anɔ kunim ejaakɛ Yudabii lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ Yehowa ni ji amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
translation_verse: Abia tiu Yeroboam kɛ etabilɔi lɛ kɛ eta lɛ, ni eyashɔ maji komɛi yɛ edɛŋ. Maji nɛɛ ji Betel kɛ Yeshana kɛ Efron, amɛteŋ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ kɛ ehe akrowai hu.

english_verse: Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_verse: Abia wala he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ji wiemɔi ni ewie kɛ nibii ni efee lɛ aŋmala yɛ Gbalɔ Ido wala he sane wolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right.
translation_verse: Asa jeŋba sa Yehowa eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ ejaakɛ efee nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni ja hu.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Egu maŋsɛɛ jemawɔji lɛ ajamɔhei lɛ hu, asaŋ ekumɔ shiui ni amãmɔ lɛ, ni efolɔ Ashera jemawɔŋ lɛ atsei lɛ eshwie shi.

english_verse: Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni efã Yudabii fɛɛ akɛ amɛja Yehowa, ni ji amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ, asaŋ amɛye emlai lɛ kɛ ekitãi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns.
translation_verse: Ena hiɛ kɛtswa gbogbo ewo Yuda maji lɛ ekomɛi ahe ekɛwaje amɛ ejaakɛ afii babaoo ni ta bɛ eyinɔ ejaakɛ Yehowa hã etoiŋ jɔ lɛ.

english_verse: He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ Yudabii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔtswaa gbogboi wɔwoa maji nɛɛ ahe, ni wɔmamɔa mɔji hu wɔwoa amɛmli; asaŋ wɔtara amɛnaa agboi, ni wɔwo amɛsɛɛ adabaŋi koni wɔkɛwaje amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejɔ ni ekã shi ehã wɔ nɛɛ, ejaakɛ wɔfee nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ taoɔ lɛ. Wɔfee esuɔmɔnaanii, no hewɔ lɛ, ehã wɔhe ejɔ wɔ yɛ wɔhe fɛɛ he.” No hewɔ lɛ, Yudabii lɛ wajewajee maji lɛ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwere jogbaŋŋ.

english_verse: Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Asa hu fã kɛ etabilɔi koni ekɛ Zera eyakpe. Biɛ kɛ biɛ lɛ gba ta yɛ Zefata Jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ Maresha.

english_verse: Asa prayed: Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asa sɔle etsɛ Yehowa, eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Oo! Yehowa, bo lɛ mɔ ko bɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa hewalɔ kɛ mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tamɔ ofeɔ lɛ. Ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ mli lɛ ye obua wɔ, Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ, ejaakɛ bo onɔ wɔhiɛ kã, ni asaŋ bo ogbɛi mli wɔba yɛ wɔkɛ ta kpeteŋkple nɛɛ baawu. Ao! Yehowa, bo ji wɔNyɔŋmɔ, ni kaahã adesa ko nine miitsɔ̃ wɔnɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away,
translation_verse: Yehowa ye Etiopiabii ata lɛ nɔ be ni Asa kɛ Yudabii kɛ amɛ bɔi nɔmɔ lɛ, ni Etiopiabii lɛ jo foi.

english_verse: but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back! The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians.
translation_verse: Asa kɛ ta ni fata ehe lɛ tiu Etiopiabii lɛ kɛyashi Gerar tɔ̃ɔ. Etiopiabii lɛ nyɔnyɔɔ bɔ ni eshwɛɛɛ amɛteŋ hiɛkãalɔ kome po, ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ Asa ta lɛ fee Etiopiabii lɛ butuu. Yuda tabilɔi lɛ ha nii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ kɛtee.

english_verse: The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns.
translation_verse: Amɛkpãtã maji fɛɛ ni bɔle Gerar lɛ ahiɛ ejaakɛ Yehowa he ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ maji nɛɛ fɛɛ amli bii lɛ. Ni Yudabii lɛ ha maji lɛ fɛɛ amli nii ejaakɛ haanii babaoo yɛ amɛmli.

english_verse: They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amɛtua kooloialɛlɔi komɛi hu yɛ amɛshitoohei amli, ni amɛloo amɛtoi kɛ yoomai babaoo diɛŋtsɛ kɛtee, ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ lɛ ba Obed bi Azaria nɔ,

english_verse: At once, Azariah went to Asa and said: Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
translation_verse: ni eyiŋ etee koni ekɛ Maŋtsɛ Asa ayakpe. Be ni amɛkpe lɛ Azaria kɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ Asa kɛ Yuda kɛ Benyamin fɛɛ, nyɛboa mi toi. Gbii abɔ ni nyɛmiibo Yehowa toi lɛ, lɛ hu ekɛ nyɛ yɛ. Kɛji nyɛtao lɛ lɛ, nyɛbaana lɛ, shi kɛji nyɛkwa lɛ lɛ, lɛ hu ebaakwa nyɛ.

english_verse: For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law.
translation_verse: Israel hi shi be kplaŋŋ ni ebɛ anɔkwa Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ebɛ osɔfoi ni tsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ anii, ni ebɛ mla hu.

english_verse: But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni fimɔ ba ni amɛkpale kɛyatao Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amɛna lɛ.

english_verse: There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Nakai bei lɛ amli lɛ mɔ ni yaa ni jio, mɔ ni baa ni jio, amɛ fɛɛ amɛbɛ hejɔlɛ, ejaakɛ kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ ejɔɔɔ kɛ basabasa nifeemɔi.

english_verse: Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii ateŋ egbala kuikui ejaakɛ jaku ete shi ewo jaku, ni maŋ kome kɛ maŋ kome miitswa, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ jaramɔi srɔtoi miiye amɛtsui.

english_verse: As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Be ni Asa nu gbalɛ ni Obed bi Azaria gba lɛ, ena ekãa, ni egu musubɔɔ amãgãi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Yuda kɛ Benyamin shikpɔji lɛ anɔ hei fɛɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ maji ni eshɔ̃shɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ hu amli. Esaa Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni ma Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ koi lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: Mɛi babaoo diɛŋtsɛ ni ji Efraimbii kɛ Manasebii kɛ Simeonbii tse amɛhe kɛjɛ Israel, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe badɔmɔ Maŋtsɛ Asa be ni amɛna akɛ Yehowa, eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ lɛ yɛ lɛ. Maŋtsɛ Asa tsɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ kɛ Yudabii kɛ Benyaminbii fɛɛ kpee.

english_verse: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amɛnaa babua yɛ Yerusalɛm yɛ Asa maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped,
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛkã kitã akɛ amɛbaaja Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ amɛtsui kɛ amɛyitsoŋ fɛɛ,

english_verse: The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ gbee walɛ kã Yehowa kitã lɛ, kɛkɛ ni amɛbɔ oshe, ni akpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ kɛ koofɛŋ.

english_verse: Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
translation_verse: Yuda tso muu fɛɛ nya kitã ni amɛkã lɛ he akɛ amɛjɛ amɛtsuiŋ fɛɛ ni amɛkã; ejaakɛ amɛtao Yehowa sɛɛgbɛ kɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ, ni amɛna lɛ. Yehowa hã amɛna toiŋjɔlɛ yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ he kɛkpe.

english_verse: Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Asa kpa enyɛ Maaka tete po akɛ maŋnyɛ ejaakɛ Maaka fee hiɛgbejianii, no ji akɛ ema amãgã ehã jemawɔŋ Ashera lɛ. Asa kumɔ amãgã ni enyɛ ma lɛ, ni ejwra lɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ ni eyashã amãgã lɛ yɛ Kidron Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Asa naaa egu jemawɔji ajamɔhei ni yɔɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ moŋ, shi kɛ̃lɛ eye Yehowa anɔkwa ewala beiaŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Eyaŋɔ nibii fɛɛ ni etsɛ ejɔɔ amɛnɔ ekɛhã Yehowa, kɛ agbɛnɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi nibiinibii ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu ejɔɔ amɛnɔ ekɛhã Yehowa lɛ kɛba Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ.

english_verse: There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ ta ko ta ko baaa aahu kɛyashi Asa maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ni fee nakai lɛ Asa jie Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ nitoohe lɛ mli shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi lɛ eko, ni ekɛtsu koni akɛyahã Siria Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad yɛ Damasko. Shɛɛ ni fata shika lɛ he ji akɛ,

english_verse: “I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Kpãŋmɔ kã mi kɛ bo teŋ akɛ nanemɛi tamɔ bɔ ni eko hi mitsɛ kɛ bo hu otsɛ teŋ lɛ. Naa jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika ni mimaje bo. Kuu kpãŋmɔ ni kã okɛ Israel Maŋtsɛ Baasha teŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ etabilɔi lɛ aje mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aya.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad kpɛlɛ̃ nɔ ehã Asa, ni ewo etatsɛmɛi agbɛ ni amɛyatua Israel maji komɛi. Amɛshɔ̃ Iyon kɛ Dan kɛ Abel-Main kɛ Naftali kpokpai lɛ anɔ maji ni atoɔ niyenii yɛ amɛmli lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
translation_verse: Be ni Baasha nu he lɛ ekpa nitsumɔ ni etsuɔ ekɛwajeɔ Rama lɛ, ni etee.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood. Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Asa bua hii anaa kɛjɛ Yuda heihei fɛɛ, ni ekɛ amɛ tee, ni ayaloo tɛi kɛ mplaŋi ni Baasha kɛtsuɔ nii ekɛwajeɔ Rama lɛ, ni ekɛtee ekɛyatswa gbogbo ewo Geba kɛ Mizpa maji lɛ ahe ekɛwaje amɛ. Gbalɔ Hanani gbalɛ lɛ

english_verse: Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said: You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Gbalɔ Hanani ba Yuda Maŋtsɛ Asa ŋɔɔ, ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Akɛni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ, shi okɛ ohe eyafɔɔɔ Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, nɔ hewɔ lɛ bɛ ona akɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ta lɛ je odɛ̃ŋ?

english_verse: Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them.
translation_verse: Ani Etiopiabii lɛ kɛ Libiabii lɛ ayi faaa kwraa fe amɛ, asaŋ kɛ amɛtayaa shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi hu babaoo diɛŋtsɛ? Shi te ni nakai be lɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ lɛ, ehã oye amɛnɔ kunim?

english_verse: The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
translation_verse: Yehowa, ehiŋmɛi kã je lɛ fɛɛ he, ni ehãa mɛi fɛɛ ni yeɔ lɛ anɔkwa kɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ lɛ naa hewalɛ. Oye kwashiai asane pam, ni no hewɔ lɛ, kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ lɛ, taitai sɔŋŋ ahe obaakã.”

english_verse: When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people. Asa Dies (
translation_verse: Gbalɛ nɛɛ hã Asa mli fu moŋ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni ehã awo gbalɔ lɛ gboklɛ yɛ mɔɔŋ. Be nɛɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni Asa bɔi maŋbii lɛ ekomɛi niseniianiifeemɔ. Asa ye hela (

english_verse: Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Asa wala mli saji lɛ aŋmala kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyashi naagbee fɛɛ yɛ Yuda kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Nane hela ko bamɔ Asa yɛ efi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ nɛɛhu akɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ. Hela lɛ mli bawo wu, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Asa eyatiuuu Yehowa dɛŋ tsamɔ sɛɛ; shi moŋ eyadi tsofatsɛmɛi asɛɛ.

english_verse: Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_verse: ni afu lɛ yɛ gbonyobu ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekpɛ eto lɛ mli yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli. Tsofakɛŋmai kpakpai srɔtoisrɔtoi diɛŋtsɛ akɛsaa egbonyo lɛ, ni ashɛre la gregre kpeteŋkple akɛfee eyara.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel.
translation_verse: Yehoshafat baye etsɛ Asa sɛɛ akɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ, ni ewaje ehe eto Israel.

english_verse: He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
translation_verse: Eto tabilɔi ta muu yɛ Yuda maji wuji ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni eto tabilɔi kuikui hu yɛ Yuda koiasɛɛ heihei kɛ Efraim shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji wuji ni etsɛ shɔ̃ lɛ hu amli.

english_verse: and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa hã Yehoshafat maŋtsɛyeli lɛ hewalɛ he shi yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni abake lɛ nii babaoo, ni ena nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehiɛ hu ba nyam.

english_verse: he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni eye Nyɔŋmɔjamɔ he awuŋã hewɔ lɛ, egu hei ni ajaa jemawɔji yɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ni asaŋ efolɔ jemawɔŋ yoo Ashera lɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ hu yɛ Yuda.

english_verse: Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along.
translation_verse: Levibii nɛɛhu kɛ osɔfoi enyɔ fata gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ahe kɛtee. Lɛvibii nɛɛ ji Shemaia kɛ Netania kɛ Zebadia kɛ Asahel kɛ Shemiramot kɛ Yehonatan kɛ Adonia kɛ Tobia kɛ Tob-Adonia. Ni osɔfoi lɛ ji Elishama kɛ Yehoram.

english_verse: They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
translation_verse: Amɛhiɛ Yehowa Mla Wolo lɛ, ni amɛkɛkpa Yuda maji blublu amli amɛkɛtsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ anii. Yehoshafat gbɛi hehe

english_verse: The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat.
translation_verse: Yehowa he ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ shikpɔji fɛɛ ni bɔle Yuda lɛ anɔ bii lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, eko kwraa ekaaa akɛ ekɛ Yehoshafat aaawu ta.

english_verse: As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities
translation_verse: Yehoshafat agbojee lɛ tee nɔ shwere. Emamɔ mɔji kɛ nitoohei yɛ Yuda hei fɛɛ,

english_verse: where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers
translation_verse: ni etĩa niyenii babaoo etotoo maji nɛɛ amli. Eto hii kãkãlɔi yɛ Yerusalɛm;

english_verse: from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans. Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had
translation_verse: ni bɔ ni ehala amɛ kɛjɛ amɛtsɛmɛi awei lɛ amli ehã lɛ nɛ: Adna ji Yuda akutso lɛŋ tabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ atatsɛ nukpa, ni eyɛ hii kakabãŋi akpei ohai etɛ̃ yɛ eshishi.

english_verse: Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with
translation_verse: Yehohanan sɛɛmɔ ji Zikri bi Anasia, mɔ ni jɛ tsuijurɔ naa ekɛ ehe hã Yehowa sɔɔmɔ lɛ; ehiɛ hii akpei ohai enyɔ yɛ eshishi.

english_verse: These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi sɔmɔɔ Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat yɛ Yerusalɛm. Amɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ etotoo tabilɔi yɛ Yuda maji wuji ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat fã ta koni amɛyatua Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead,
translation_verse: Afii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Yehoshafat yiŋ etee Samaria maŋ lɛ mli ni eyasara Ahab. Ahab gbe toi kɛ tsinai babaoo ekɛfee Yehoshafat kɛ esɛɛbii ni ekɛnyiɛ lɛ gbɔ. Ahab bɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ egbe Yehoshafat yitso koni eyawa lɛ ni efã ta kɛyatua Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?” “Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command.
translation_verse: Ahab bi Yehoshafat akɛ, “Bɛ oooyawa mi koni mayatua Ramot-Gilead?” Yehoshafat to he akɛ, “Mifee kralo tamɔ ofee kralo lɛ, ni nakai nɔŋŋ ji mimaŋ lɛ; wɔ kɛ bo aaatee ta lɛ.”

english_verse: But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
translation_verse: Shi Yehoshafat kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Shi bi Yehowa daaŋ gbee dã.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehoshafat bi akɛ, “Yehowa gbalɔ ko bɛ biɛ dɔŋŋ ni wɔɔbi Yehowa daaŋ gbee kɛtsɔ̃ enɔ lo?”

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Ahab here nɔ akɛ, “Mɔ kome ko yɛ ni kulɛ wɔɔnyɛ wɔbi lɛ Yehowa daaŋ gbee. Lɛ ji Imla bi Mikaia lɛ; shi mitaooo esane ejaakɛ egbako gbalɛ jurɔ yɛ mihe dã, fe be fɛɛ be lɛ efɔŋ egbaa yɛ mihe.” Shi Yehoshafat kɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Nii akakɛɛ nakai.”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahab tsɛ tsulɔ ko, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa ni oyatsɛ Imla bi Mikaia obaha mi mramra.”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat ewula jogbaŋŋ akɛ maŋtsɛmɛi kɛtara maŋtsɛmɛi asɛii anɔ yɛ ŋmãagbeemɔhe ni yɔɔ Samaria maŋ agbo lɛ naa nɔŋŋ lɛ, ni gbalɔi lɛ miigbagbaa yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Gbalɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ni egbɛi ji Zedekia, ni ji Kenaana bi lɛ, kɛ dade fee aklonto. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ Ahab akɛ, “Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Enɛɛmɛi akɛbaashimɔ Siriabii lɛ kɛaayashi oooye amɛnɔ kunim.’ ”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Gbalɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ gba nakai nɔŋŋ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Yaatua Ramot-Gilead, ni obaaye kunim. Yehowa baahã maŋtsɛ aye kunim.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Tsulɔ ni tee eyatsɛ Mikaia lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, gbalɔi lɛ fɛɛ anaa efee ekome kɛgba gbalɛ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ toiŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, bo hu yaawie wiemɔ ni baaŋɔɔ maŋtsɛ naa nakai nɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Mikaia kɛɛ tsulɔ lɛ akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni Yehowa yɔɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ baakɛɛ mi lɛ no mibawie.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
translation_verse: Be ni Mikaia bashɛ shi lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Ahab bi lɛ akɛ, “Mikaia, miya Ramot-Gilead miyawu ta aloo mikaya?” Mikaia to he akɛ, “Nyɛyaa! Bɛ nyɛbaaye omanye! Bɛ Yehowa baahã nyɛye omanye?”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Shi Ahab kɛɛ Mikaia akɛ, “Shii enyiɛ mawo bo shi akɛ kɛji oogba Yehowa daaŋ gbee ohã mi lɛ, okakɛɛ mi nɔ ko fe anɔkwale lɛ kɛkɛ?”

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mikaia kɛɛ akɛ, “Mina Israel tabilɔi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ tamɔ toi ni bɛ kwɛlɔ.” Ni Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Hii nɛɛ bɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔ; amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya ewe yɛ hejɔlɛ mli mɔ.”

english_verse: Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahab kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat akɛ, “Ani mikɛɛɛ bo akɛ egbaŋ gbalɛ jurɔ yɛ mihe kɔkɔɔkɔ akɛ ja gbalɛ fɔŋ?”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Shi Mikaia tee egbalɛ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛboa nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ toi: Mina Yehowa ni eta emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ, ni ŋwɛi bɔfoi fɛɛ ewo shi yɛ eninejurɔ nɔ kɛ ebɛku fɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?” They talked about it for a while,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Namɔ po aaaya koni eyalaka Israel maŋtsɛ Ahab koni efã ta kɛya Ramot-Gilead koni eyanyɔ yɛ jɛi?’ Be ni bɔfoi lɛ ekomɛi miikɛɛ nɛkɛ lɛ, mɛi komɛi hu miikɛɛ nɛkɛ.

english_verse: then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.” “How?” the Lord asked.
translation_verse: Ahiɛ mli nakai kɛyashi mumɔ ko je kpo ni ebadamɔ Yehowa hiɛ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Maya mayalaka lɛ.’ Yehowa bi mumɔ nɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ obaatsɔ?’

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
translation_verse: Mumɔ lɛ jie naa akɛ, ‘Matsɔ̃ Ahab gbalɔi lɛ alilɛi nɔ mahã amɛgba gbalɛ ni amale ni.’ Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mumɔ lɛ akɛ, ‘Yaa koni oyalaka lɛ; ni onine baashɛ enɔ hu.’

english_verse: Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gbalɔ Zedekia, ni ji Kenaana bi lɛ, tsi eba, ni ebagba Mikaia toiŋ ma, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛbe mumɔ lɛ je minɔ, ni ekɛ bo bawie lɛ?”

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
translation_verse: Mikaia here lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Gbi nɔ ni obaaya oyatee ohe yɛ pia mli lɛ, gbi lɛ obaana ole.”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ni fee nakai lɛ, Israel Maŋtsɛ Ahab fã ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛmɔa Mikaia koni nyɛkɛ lɛ ayahãa Amon, maŋ lɛ amralo lɛ, kɛ Yoash, maŋtsɛ binuu lɛ.

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛa amɛ akɛ amɛwo lɛ tsuŋ, asaŋ amɛhã lɛ niyenii fioo kɛkɛ kɛ nu hu fioo kɛkɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni maya maba kɛ omanye.”

english_verse: Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!” Ahab Dies at Ramoth (
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mikaia to he ehã Ahab ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji otee oba kɛ omanye fĩĩ belɛ jeee Yehowa ni tsɔ̃ minɔ wie lɛ.” Asaŋ ekɛshi sɛɛ akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛmiibo toi, nyɛ maŋbii fɛɛ?” Ahab gbele (

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Ahab kɛɛ Yehoshafat akɛ, “Kɛji wɔmiiya ta lɛ tswaa lɛ mibatsake mihewulamɔ; shi bo lɛ owo otadei lɛ nɔŋŋ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ tee ta lɛ naa ni etsake ehe.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni tayaa shwiilii anɔ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ na Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat lɛ, amɛsusu akɛ Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ni; no hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsɛ̃ kɛba koni amɛ kɛ lɛ abanɔ. Shi Yehoshafat bo waa etsɛ, ni Yehowa ye bua lɛ. Nyɔŋmɔ hã henyɛlɔi lɛ dɔ amɛyi amɛŋmɛ he kroko,

english_verse: And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ be ni tayaa shwiilii asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ na akɛ jeee Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ ni lɛ, amɛkpale yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Shi trukaa lɛ, gãi ko ni nuu ko tsɛ̃ lɛ yatsu Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ he ni eshishigbɛ dama lɛ kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dama lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ hã Ahab kɛɛ mɔ ni kudɔɔ eshwiili lɛ akɛ, “Dɔɔ ohe koni okɛ mi ashi ta lɛ naa, shi mipila!”

english_verse: The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_verse: Ta lɛ naa yawa pam nakai gbi lɛ, shi Maŋtsɛ Ahab hã ahiɛ emli kɛdamɔ eshwiili lɛ mli, ni ekɛ Siriabii lɛ kpe kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi. Aaafee hulushinyɔɔ mli lɛ ni Ahab nyɔ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yehoshafat ni ji Yuda Maŋtsɛ lɛ ku esɛɛ shweshweeshwe kɛba ewe lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said: By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you!
translation_verse: Be ni Yehoshafat baa lɛ gbalɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yehu, Hanani bi lɛ, tee ni ekɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ yakpe, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Aso eja gbɛ akɛ owa yitsoŋwalɔ, ni osumɔ mɛi ni nyɛɔ Yehowa lo? Nɔ ni ofee nɛɛ lɛ ehã Yehowa mli efu bo.

english_verse: But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord. Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
translation_verse: Shi ana nibii kpakpai komɛi kɛ̃ yɛ ohe. Eko ji jemawɔŋ Ashera lɛ amãgãi ni okumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ. Eko hu ji akɛ oto oyiŋ akɛ okɛ otsui fɛɛ baasɔ̃mɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.” Yehoshafat tsake nibii ahiɛ

english_verse: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
translation_verse: Yerusalɛm kwraa ji Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat shihilɛhe. Shi etoɔ be ni efãa gbɛ kɛyanyiɛɔ emaŋbii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ Beersheba aahu kɛyashiɔ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ bɔ ni afee ni ekpale amɛ koni amɛbaja Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah
translation_verse: Eto kojolɔi ehã Yuda maji wuji ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko,

english_verse: and told them: Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ kojolɔi nɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkwɛa jogbaŋŋ kɛji nyɛbuaa sane ko he, ejaakɛ jeee gbɔmɛi adɛŋ hewalɛ ahã nyɛ lɛ, shi Yehowa dɛŋ hewalɛ ni; ni eyɛ nyɛmasɛi be mli ni nyɛmiibua sane ko he.

english_verse: So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛhãa Yehowa hegbeyeishemɔ ahia nyɛmli; nyɛkwɛa nyɛnifeemɔnii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, miihi kutumpɔoyeli kɛ hiɛiaŋkwɛmɔ kɛ nyɔɔŋnihemɔ.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yɛ Yerusalɛm diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, Yehoshafat hala Levibii komɛi kɛ osɔfoi hu komɛi kɛ agbɛnɛ shĩai amli weku nukpai lɛ hu ateiaŋ mɛi komɛi koni amɛkwɛ Yehowa Mla lɛ nɔtɔmɔ saji kɛ maŋbii ateŋ bei hu.

english_verse: The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
translation_verse: Ni be fɛɛ be ni nyɛnyɛmimɛi ni yɔɔ maji krokomɛi lɛ amli kɛ sane ko aaabahã nyɛ yeli lɛ, gbɔmɔgbee ni jio, mla loo kitã loo akpɔ nɔ ni atɔ̃ jio, nyɛtsɔa amɛ mla naa ni abaaye sane lɛ yɛ, bɔ ni afee ni nyɛkaye sɔ̃ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ koni Yehowa mli miifu, ni egbala nyɛ kɛ nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ fɛɛ toi.

english_verse: Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_verse: Yɛ saji fɛɛ ni kɔɔ Yehowa he gbɛfaŋ lɛ, bɔ ni Amaria, osɔfonukpa lɛ, baabua he lɛ no ji naagbee. Ni saji ni kɔɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ he gbɛfaŋ lɛ, bɔni Ishmael bi Zebadia ni ji Yuda amralo lɛ baabua he lɛ, no ji naagbee. Levibii lɛ baakwɛ akɛ aaye kojomɔhei lɛ amli buamɔi fɛɛ anɔ. Nyɛfea ekãa kɛtsua nyɛnii; ni Yehowa aye mɔ ni sane yɔɔ mli lɛ sane ehã lɛ!”

english_verse: Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
translation_verse: Be ni bɔfoi komɛi batswa Yehoshafat adafi amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, ta kpeteŋkple ko ejɛ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ Edom kɛba amɛbatua Yuda, ni amɛshɔ̃ Hazazon-Tamar ni ji En-Gedi momo” lɛ,

english_verse: Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Yehoshafat she gbeyei. No hewɔ lɛ, eto eyiŋ akɛ eeesɔle kɛbi Yehowa dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ. Enɛ hã efã akɛ ahi ŋmaa yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yudabii jɛjɛɛ Yuda maji wuji lɛ fɛɛ amli amɛbabua amɛhe naa yɛ Yerusalɛm koni atao Yehowa dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english_verse: After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard
translation_verse: Yuda maji lɛ anɔ bii lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛmbii lɛ hu yabua shi yɛ kpo hee lɛ nɔ yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ hiɛ. Ni Yehoshafat ho edamɔ shi yɛ asafo lɛ hiɛ,

english_verse: and prayed: You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa, wɔtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ, bo ji Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, asaŋ mɔ ni yeɔ je lɛ mli maji fɛɛ anɔ. Bo oyɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ, ni mɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni baanyɛ bo onaa aku.

english_verse: Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever.
translation_verse: WɔNyɔŋmɔ, oshwie shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ bii lɛ yɛ omaŋ ni ji Israel hiɛ, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hã oshieŋtsɛ Abraham shwiei lɛ akɛ amɛgboshinii kɛmiiya naanɔ.

english_verse: Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you.
translation_verse: Amɛhi shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ bei abɔ; ni amɛma Sɔlemɔtsu yɛ nɔ kɛwo ohiɛ nyam, asaŋ kɛ hemɔkɛyeli akɛ

english_verse: They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
translation_verse: kɛji nɔ gbonyo ko, tamɔ ta loo gbele hela loo hɔmɔ, ba wɔnɔ lɛ, wɔbaaba wɔbadamɔ Sɔlemɔtsu nɛɛ ni ajaa bo yɛ mli lɛ hiɛ, ni wɔbaasɔle kɛbi bo odɛ̃ŋ wamɔ yɛ wɔnɔnaa lɛ mli, ni obaabo wɔ toi, ni obaahere wɔyiwala.

english_verse: You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed.
translation_verse: “Ŋmɛnɛ, naa Amonbii lɛ kɛ Moabbii lɛ, ni ji Seir Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ, ni amɛbatua wɔ. Be ni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ jɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaa lɛ, ohã amɛtsɔ̃ afã kɛlɔgɔ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ahe kɛho, ni no hewɔ lɛ, wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ tuaaa amɛ ni amɛaakpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni amɛkɛdaa wɔ shi ji ba ni amɛto kɛba kɛbashwie wɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bo okɛhã wɔ akɛ wɔgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
translation_verse: WɔNyɔŋmɔ, tɔɔ wɔhe owele ohã wɔ ejaakɛ wɔhe waaa, ni ta kpeteŋkple ni baa wɔnɔ nɛɛ lɛ wɔnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ wɔdamɔ. Ataa, wɔleee bɔ ni wɔɔfee, bo kɛkɛ wɔkwɛɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple,
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Yuda hii fɛɛ kɛ amɛŋamɛi kɛ amɛbii kɛ hɔi blublu ewo shi yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Then Jahaziel said: Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yahaziel kɛɛ asafo lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ kɛ Yudabii kɛ Yerusalɛm maŋbii fɛɛ ni naa ekpe shi, nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nyɛ nɛ, ‘Nyɛkashea gbeyei, asaŋ nyɛtsui akafãa hu yɛ ta babaoo nɛɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ ta ni abaawu lɛ ebɛ nyɛdɛŋ, Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ eyɔɔ.’

english_verse: So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley.
translation_verse: Wɔ́ ni ji wɔ́ lɛ, nyɛfãa ta koni nyɛ kɛ amɛ ayakpea. Amɛbaatsɔ̃ Ziz ŋmeŋme lɛ nɔ kɛba. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyaninaa amɛ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ naagbeehe lɛ ni yɔɔ Yeruel shiaŋa lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ mli.

english_verse: You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
translation_verse: Ta nɛɛ lɛ nyɛtswaŋ eko. Nyɛ lɛ nyɛgbaa nyɛta lɛ kɛkɛ koni nyɛdamɔa shi nyɛmɛ koni nyɛkwɛ kunim ni Yehowa baaye ahã nyɛ Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛmbii. Nyɛkashea gbeyei, asaŋ nyɛtsui akafãa hu. Wɔ lɛ, nyɛfãa ta koni nyɛ kɛ amɛ ayakpea ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ nyɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ni Levibii ni jɛ Kohat shwiei lɛ kɛ Kora shwiei lɛ hu ateŋ lɛ ho amɛdamɔ shi, ni amɛla kɛ gbee ni wa kɛkafo Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.”
translation_verse: Yuda hii lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm hii lɛ fã enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛtee Tekoa shiaŋa lɛ nɔ. Shi dani amɛfã lɛ Yehoshafat ho edamɔ shi ni ekɛ ta lɛ wie. Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Agoo! Yuda hii kɛ Yerusalɛm hii, nyɛhea Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, nyɛyea, ni nyɛbaanyɛ shi nyɛfi; ni nyɛhea gbalɔi lɛ hu nyɛyea, ni nyɛbaaye omanye.”

english_verse: Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing: “Praise the Lord! His love never ends.”
translation_verse: Be ni Yehoshafat kɛ maŋ lɛ eto ajina sɛɛ lɛ, ehala lalatsɛmɛi komɛi akɛ amɛwula kɛ atadei ni amɛwoɔ yɛ gbii krɔŋkrɔŋi anɔ lɛ koni amɛla kɛjie Yehowa yi kɛnyiɛ tabilɔi lɛ ahiɛ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Ajie Yehowa yi, ejaakɛ esuɔmɔ sɛɛ efooo kɛyaa naanɔ!”

english_verse: so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
translation_verse: Ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ butuu. Kɛkɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ, Amonbii lɛ kɛ Moabbii lɛ sɔŋŋ hu gba wo amɛhe, ni amɛ kɛ amɛhe wu kɛkpãtã amɛ sɔŋŋ amɛhiɛ butuu.

english_verse: When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground.
translation_verse: Be ni Yudabii lɛ yashɛ mɔɔ ko he yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkwɛ he ni henyɛlɔi lɛ baa yɛ lɛ gbɛ lɛ, amɛna akɛ henyɛlɔi lɛ etsɔmɔ gbohii jwere shi ni hiɛkãalɔ kome nɛkɛ ejeee amɛmli.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ Yudabii lɛ babua amɛhe naa yɛ Yijiemɔ Jɔɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛ jie Yehowa yi yɛ jɛi. Bɔ ni fee ni atsɛɔ jɔɔ nɛɛ akɛ Yijiemɔ Jɔɔ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ he ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ shikpɔji anɔ majimaji lɛ fɛɛ be ni amɛnu bɔ ni Yehowa efee Israel henyɛlɔi lɛ yɛ ta mli yɛ Israelbii ahewɔ lɛ.

english_verse: While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel.
translation_verse: Yɛ mli aahu lɛ Yehoshafat, Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ, tee ni ekɛ Ahazia, Israel maŋtsɛ, ni feɔ nibii gbohii lɛ yafee ekome,

english_verse: Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done,
translation_verse: Ehi shi tamɔ etsɛ Asa hi shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyagbaaa afã shi eba ejeŋ bɔ pɛ ni Yehowa taoɔ,

english_verse: but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: shi moŋ eguuu jemawɔji lɛ ajamɔhei lɛ, ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ bɔiko amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ jamɔ kɛ amɛyitsoŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yehoshafat he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, kɛjɛ shishijee aahu kɛyagbe naa lɛ, aŋmala yɛ Hanani bi Yehu he saji ni yɔɔ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber.
translation_verse: koni amɛkpɛ lɛji ni akɛfã gbɛ kɛya Tarshish jarayeli. Akpɛ lɛji lɛ yɛ Ezion-Geber.

english_verse: But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_verse: Shi Eliezer, Dodawahu bi lɛ, jɛ Maresha maŋ lɛ mli ni ebagba eshi Yehoshafat ekɛɛ akɛ, “Akɛ ni okɛ Ahazia eyafee ekome hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa baakpãtã nii ni otsu lɛ hiɛ.” Lɛji lɛ jwara ni no hewɔ lɛ, eyahiii amɛ Tarshish lɛ yaa.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Yehoshafat tsɔ̃ esɛɛ, ni afu lɛ afata etsɛmɛi lɛ ahe yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni ebi Yehoram baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoram (

english_verse: King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah.
translation_verse: Yehoram yɛ nyɛmimɛihii ekpaa ni amɛ hu Israel maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat bii ji amɛ. Amɛ ji Azaria kɛ Yehiel kɛ Zakaria kɛ Azariahu kɛ Mikael kɛ Shefatia.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Edombii lɛ tse Yuda hiɛ atua yɛ Yehoram yinɔ, ni amɛwo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmaŋtsɛ.

english_verse: The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa hã Filistibii lɛ kɛ Arabiabii ni yɔɔ Etiopiabii lɛ amasɛi lɛ ahe tsɛ̃ Yehoram,

english_verse: Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
translation_verse: Amɛtsɛ lɛ ke amɛ nii babaoo. Ehã amɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika kɛ nibii ni jara wa. Enɛɛmɛi asɛɛ lɛ ehã amɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji wuji ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe lɛ ekomɛi hu. Shi akɛni Yehoram ji kromɔbi hewɔ lɛ, lɛ lɛ amɛtsɛ lɛ kɛ emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ hã lɛ koni eye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders.
translation_verse: Be ni Yehoram ebata etsɛ maŋtsɛyeli sɛi lɛ nɔ, ni emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ehe shi lɛ, egbe enyɛmimɛihii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Israel maŋ onukpai komɛi hu.

english_verse: Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong,
translation_verse: Shihilɛ mli ni Israel maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ hi, tamɔ Ahab ba ejeŋ lɛ, nakai shihilɛ mli Yehoram bahi ejaakɛ ekɛ Ahab biyoo yɛ akɛ ŋa. Etɔ̃ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ,

english_verse: but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
translation_verse: shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yehowa emiii akɛ ekpãtãa David shwiei ahiɛ yɛ kpãŋmɔ ni ekɛ David kpãŋ lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ ewo David shi akɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ shiŋ ewe lɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ.

english_verse: but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time. Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Edom bɛ Yuda shishi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Libna hu tse Yehoram hiɛ atua, ni eje enɔyeli shishi, ejaakɛ Yehoram etɔ̃ Yehowa, etsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
translation_verse: Asaŋ efee jemawɔji ajamɔhei hu yɛ Yuda gɔji ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehã Yerusalɛmbii kɛ Yuda shi Yehowa sɛɛ, ni amɛja jemawɔji, ni amɛkɛtɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ.

english_verse: One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said: I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Gbalɔ Elia ŋma Maŋtsɛ Yehoram wolo, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa nɔ ni Yehowa, ni ji otsɛ David Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ: ‘Ohiko shi tamɔ otsɛ Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat, loo onii Maŋtsɛ Asa, hi shi lɛ.

english_verse: Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
translation_verse: Moŋ okɔ Israel maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ajeŋba lɛ, ni okɛhã Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛmbii lɛ miija jemawɔji tamɔ Ahab kɛ eshwiei fee ni Israel shi Yehowa sɛɛ kɛyaja jemawɔji lɛ. Asaŋ onyɛmimɛihii ni ji otsɛ bii lɛ hu ogbe amɛ; ni amɛhi fe bo.

english_verse: Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa baagbala omaŋbii lɛ kɛ oŋamɛi kɛ obii atoi waa, ni ebaakpãtã onii ni oyɔɔ hu hiɛ.

english_verse: You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
translation_verse: Bo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ musuŋ hela kpakpataa ko baamɔ bo, ni hela nɛɛ mli baawo wu daa gbi kɛyashi omlinii baatue.’ ”

english_verse: They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
translation_verse: ni amɛfã ta kɛbatua Yuda, ni amɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛna yɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli, ni amɛloo kɛtee. Asaŋ amɛŋɔ Yehoram ŋamɛi lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ fɛɛ nom kɛtee ja enakutsoŋ binuu lɛ pɛ.

english_verse: After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease.
translation_verse: Shi enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ musuŋ hela ni ehiii tsamɔ piŋ Yehoram,

english_verse: About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
translation_verse: kɛyashi afii enyɔ sɛɛ be mli ni emusuŋnii lɛ tue, ni egbo kɛ hejaramɔ. Emaŋbii lɛ shɛreee la akɛwooo egbonyo lɛ hiɛ nyam tamɔ afee ahã etsɛmɛi maŋtsɛmɛi ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot,
translation_verse: Be ni Yehu miifee nɔ ni Yehowa efã akɛ efee ekɛgbala Ahab we lɛ toi lɛ, ekɛ maŋ tsuji lɛ kɛ Ahazia nyɛmimɛihii abii lɛ ni fata Ahazia he kɛba lɛ kpe, ni egbe amɛ.

english_verse: then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord. There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah. Queen Athaliah of Judah (
translation_verse: Etao Ahazia, ni ayamɔ lɛ ni eyatee yɛ Samaria. Akɛ lɛ bahã Yehu, ni agbe lɛ. Shi awo egbonyo lɛ ayafu yɛ enii Maŋtsɛ Yehoshafat hewɔ, ejaakɛ lɛ lɛ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni esɔmɔ Yehowa kɛ eyitsoŋ fɛɛ. Enɛ ha gbɔmɛi tã yɛ Ahab we lɛ mli bɔ ni mɔ ko kwraa bɛ jɛi dɔŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ maŋtsɛ eye. Maŋnyɛ Atalia (

english_verse: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
translation_verse: Efee efɔŋ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ tamɔ Ahab fee lɛ, ejaakɛ etsɛ Yehoram gbele sɛɛ lɛ, Ahab we lɛ mli ajɛ ni awoɔ lɛ ŋaa ni naagbee mli aahu lɛ no kpãtã ehiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Amɛŋaawoo lɛ nɔ enyiɛ ni etee eyawa Israel Maŋtsɛ Yoram, Ahab bi lɛ, ta ni ekɛ Siria Maŋtsɛ Hazael yawu yɛ Ramot-Gilead lɛ. Siriabii lɛ pila Yoram yɛ ta lɛ mli.

english_verse: and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yoram tee eyahi Yezreel koni etsa ehe, ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Ahazia tee Yezreel koni eyasara Yoram yɛ ehela lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
translation_verse: Shi eji Nyɔŋmɔ yiŋtoo akɛ Ahazia shigbeemɔ atsɔ̃ nɛkɛ saramɔ ni etee eyasara Yoram nɛɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ be ni eyashɛ jɛi sɛɛ lɛ, etee ni eyawa Yoram koni ekɛ Yehu, Nimshi bi lɛ, ni Yehowa ekɔ lɛ koni ekpãtã Ahab we lɛ hiɛ lɛ ayawu.

english_verse: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ Yehoram biyoo ni gbɛi ji Yehosheba lɛ ju shi, ni emɔ Ahazia bi ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yoash lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi abihii ni abaagbe lɛ ateŋ, ni ekɛ lɛ kɛ ekwɛlɔ lɛ fɛɛ yato yɛ sɛɛtsu ko mli yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Yehoram biyoo ni ji Yehosheba, Osɔfo Yehoiada ŋa lɛ, fee ni ejie Yoash yɛ Atalia daaŋ, ni enaaa lɛ egbe ejaakɛ Ahazia nyɛmiyoo ji lɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ Ahazia nyɛ Atalia nu akɛ ebi Ahazia egbo lɛ, efã akɛ agbe maŋtsɛmɛi ashwiei hii ni yɔɔ Yuda fɛɛ.

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_verse: Ekɛ amɛ tee Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ mli kɛyashi afii ekpaa. Atalia ye maŋnyɛ yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english_verse: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
translation_verse: Naa bɔ ni wɔbaafee. Nyɛteŋ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ hu ni baaba nitsumɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ baaja amɛmli kui etɛ̃. Kui etɛ̃ nɛɛ ateŋ ekome baabu Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ agboi lɛ anaa;

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ fɛɛ nya, ni maŋ lɛ mli jɔ akɛ ni agbe Atalia lɛ.

english_verse: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
translation_verse: Shi afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Osɔfo Yehoiada kanya ehe. Enine shɛ asraafoi oha ku asafoiatsɛmɛi enumɔ komɛi anɔ, ni ekɛ amɛ kpãŋ. Asafoiatsɛmɛi nɛɛ ji Yeroham bi Azaria, kɛ Yohohana bi Ishmael, kɛ Obed bi Azaria, kɛ Adaia bi Maaseia, kɛ Zikri bi Elishafat.

english_verse: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
translation_verse: Amɛ fɛɛ amɛnaa yabua yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ, kɛkɛ ni asafo lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ binuu Yoash kpãŋ. Osɔfo Yehoiada kɛɛ asafo lɛ akɛ, “Naa, maŋtsɛ ni etsɔ̃ esɛɛ lɛ binuu lɛ nɛ. Lɛ esa akɛ eyeɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ agbɛnɛ yɛ shi ni Yehowa ewo yɛ David shwiei ahe lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
translation_verse: ku kome baahi maŋtsɛ we lɛ, ni ku kome hu baabu Shishitoo Agbo lɛ naa. Maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ baahi kpoi lɛ anɔ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ mli.

english_verse: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko mɔ ko akabote Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli ja osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii ni eshɛ be ni amɛsɔmɔɔ yɛ jɛi lɛ. Amɛ lɛ amɛaanyɛ amɛbote Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛtsuu amɛhe. Maŋbii fɛɛ aye Yehowa gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ baabɔle maŋtsɛ lɛ he kɛkpe, ni amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baahiɛ etawuunii. He fɛɛ he ni maŋtsɛ lɛ yaa lɛ, amɛhi ehe kɛbu ehe. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baabote Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli lɛ agbe lɛ.”

english_verse: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ kɛ Yuda hii lɛ fɛɛ fee bɔ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada wo amɛ kitã akɛ amɛfee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ ewebii ni baa nitsumɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ ba, ni amɛbafata kui ni kulɛ amɛmiikpa nitsumɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe; ejaakɛ Osɔfo Yehoiada kpaaa amɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛya shĩa.

english_verse: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada jara akplɔi kɛ tsɛŋi wuji kɛ tsɛŋi bibii ni Maŋtsɛ David yɔɔ ni akɛto Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ ekɛhã asraafoi oha kui asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ.

english_verse: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, eto tabilɔi lɛ edamɔ shi yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ kɛjɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ ninejurɔ koŋ lɛ kɛho kɛyashi tsu lɛ abɛku koŋ lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni amɛfo sa kɛbu maŋtsɛ lɛ he. Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tawuunii hiɛ edɛ̃.

english_verse: As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple.
translation_verse: Atalia nu bolɔmɔ ni maŋbii ni yaa baa kɛ foi lɛ bolɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, etiu maŋbii lɛ kɛtee Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he ni amɛwo shi yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: Be ni Atalia shɛ jɛi ni ebaakwɛ lɛ, naa maŋtsɛ lɛ ni edamɔ maŋtsɛ shidaamɔhe lɛ yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ shinaa lɛ shi, ni asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛkpãlɔi lɛ efo ehe sa kpula. Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ miibɔ oshe kɛ nyamɔ, ni aakpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ, ni Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli lalatsɛmɛi lɛ miitswa saŋku, ni akɛmiila yijiemɔ lalai. Kɛkɛ ni Atalia kɛ dɔlɛ gbala ehe atadei lɛ, ni ebo ekɛɛ akɛ, “Maŋjwaa sane! Maŋjwaa sane!”

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada tsɛ tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ, ni efã amɛ akɛ amɛmɔ Maŋnyɛ Atalia kɛje kpo kɛtsɔ̃ tabilɔi lɛ ateŋ; shi moŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaaba akɛ enyiɛ Maŋnyɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbe lɛ. Afee nakai ejaakɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ esaaa akɛ agbeɔ maŋnyɛ lɛ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ mli.

english_verse: She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
