translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, asafo lɛ ŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɔ Maŋnyɛ Atalia kɛtsɔ amɛtɛŋ kɛho. Shi be ni akɛ lɛ shɛ Okpɔŋɔi Agbo lɛ naa, he ni atsɔ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli lɛ, ni agbe lɛ yɛ jɛi. Yehoiada tsake nibii (

english_verse: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
translation_verse: Nii nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Osɔfo Yehoiada kɛ Maŋtsɛ Yoash kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ fee ekome ni amɛkpãŋ akɛ amɛbaahi shi akɛ Yehowa webii.

english_verse: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ maŋbii lɛ yabote jemawɔji ajamɔhei lɛ, ni amɛyakumɔ jemawɔji lɛ amãgãi lɛ kɛ jemawɔji lɛ afɔleshãa latɛi lɛ kɛ jemawɔji lɛ ajamɔhei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ fɛɛ amɛshwie shi. Naagbee mli lɛ amɛgbe Matan ni ji jemawɔji lɛ awulɔmɔ lɛ amɛfata he.

english_verse: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Osɔfo Yehoiada tu Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli nitsumɔi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ hegbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ewo Levibii osɔfoi lɛ adɛŋ. Ni yɛ Levibii krokomɛi lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, bɔ ni David jara amɛmli koni amɛsɔmɔ yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli lɛ, asaŋ akɛ amɛ amɛshã Yehowa shãa afɔlei lɛ bɔ ni yɔɔ Mose Mla lɛ mli lɛ, Osɔfo Yehoiada saa ekɛhã amɛ bɔ pɛ ni David eja ehã amɛ eto lɛ. Nakai nɔŋŋ efee kui ni amɛgbɛnaa ji akɛ amɛla lɛ.

english_verse: Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
translation_verse: Asaŋ ekɛ bulɔi to Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ agboi lɛ anaa bɔ ni afee ni mɔ ko ni ebule ehe yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ akabote Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli.

english_verse: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ osɔfo Yehoiada tsɛ tabilɔi lɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛŋ hiɛnaanɔbii lɛ kɛ akutsei lɛ amraloi lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ kɛfata ehe, ni amɛkpala maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛjɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli, ni amɛ kɛ lɛ nyiɛ kɛtsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ we lɛ ŋwɛi agbo lɛ mli kɛbote maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ lɛ yata maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right.
translation_verse: Yoash hi shi bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ yɛ Osɔfo Yehoiada yinɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Osɔfonukpa Yehoiada kɛ shika lɛ hãa mɛi ni kwɛɔ nii ni atsuɔ yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛ hu amɛkɛbɔɔ tɛ gbogbotswalɔi lɛ kɛ kapintafoi lɛ kɛ dade kɛ akɔɔbleŋaalɔi lɛ apaa koni amɛsaa Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ.

english_verse: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
translation_verse: Afu lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ yɛ David maŋ lɛ mli yɛ nibii kpakpai ni etsu ehã Israel kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ eWe lɛ hu he nitsumɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
translation_verse: Yehoiada kpee yei enyɔ ehã Maŋtsɛ Yoash, ni ekɛ amɛ fɔ bihii kɛ biyei.

english_verse: Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple.
translation_verse: Eshɛ be ko ni Yoash to eyiŋ akɛ eeesaa Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ heihei ni efitefitee lɛ.

english_verse: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
translation_verse: Enɛ hã Yoash tsɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ, ni etsu amɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa Yuda maji fɛɛ amli nyɛyatsua maŋbii fɛɛ too bɔ ni abaana shika koni akɛ eko asaa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ daa afi. Nyɛtsua sane nɛɛ he nii kɛ hiɛdɔɔ.” Shi Levibii lɛ ahiɛ eyadɔɔɔ yɛ sane lɛ he.

english_verse: So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Yoash tsɛ Osɔfonukpa Yehoiada, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni hewɔ okwɛɛɛ koni Levibii lɛ ayatsu Yudabii lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛmbii atoo lɛ ni Mose, Yehowa tsulɔ lɛ, fo ehã Israel fɛɛ koni akɛtsu Yehowa Kpee Buu lɛ he nii lɛ?”

english_verse: Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Yoash fã, ni Levibii lɛ kpɛ adeka ko ni amɛkɛma Yehowa We lɛ agbo lɛ naa.

english_verse: He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni atswa he ŋoŋo yɛ Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm fɛɛ akɛ too lɛ ni Mose, Nyɔŋmɔ tsulɔ lɛ, fo ehã Israelbii be mli ni amɛnyiɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aba ni ebawo enɔ lɛ ehã Yehowa.

english_verse: The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box.
translation_verse: Maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ na sane lɛ he tsuijurɔ, ni amɛkɛ amɛtoo lɛ ba amɛbawo adeka lɛ mli. Abaa aahu kɛyashiɔ adeka lɛ yiɔ tɔ.

english_verse: Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside. This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected.
translation_verse: Kɛji fee nakai lɛ Levibii lɛ woɔ adeka lɛ koni akɛtsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adeka lɛ ba lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ woloŋmalɔ lɛ kɛ osɔfonukpa lɛ hu naadamɔlɔ baa ni amɛbatsɔ̃ɔ shika lɛ yɛ adeka lɛ mli, kɛkɛ lɛ Levibii lɛ ewo adeka lɛ amɛkɛyama emaahe lɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni afee daa gbi, ni akɛbua shika babaoo naa.

english_verse: These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new.
translation_verse: Nitsulɔi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ni nitsumɔ lɛ tee nɔ jogbaŋŋ; ni amɛsaa Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ, ni ena hewalɛ, ni eba eblema.

english_verse: They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple. Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived.
translation_verse: Be ni agbe Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ saamɔ naa lɛ, shika ni shwɛ lɛ akɛbahã maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Osɔfonukpa Yehoiada. english_verse: He died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Osɔfo Yehoiada gbɔ kotokoto; ni be ni ena afii oha kɛ nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ lɛ egbo.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted.
translation_verse: Yehoiada gbele sɛɛ lɛ Yuda lumɛi lɛ bɔi amɛhe kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ fufuamɔ. Maŋtsɛ lɛ bɔi amɛnaa toiboo.

english_verse: The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kpa jamɔ yɛ Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli, ni amɛyaja Asherim jemawɔŋ lɛ kɛ amãgãi. Tɔ̃mɔ nɛɛ hã Yehowa mli fu Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃ lɛ Yehowa tsu gbalɔi kɛba ni amɛbabɔ amɛ kɔkɔ; asaŋ koni amɛkpale Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛmbii koni amɛhi shi bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ; shi maŋbii lɛ booo toi.

english_verse: God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ Mumɔ lɛ ba Osɔfo Yehoiada bi Zakaria nɔ, ni eho edamɔ he ko grɔŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ, Tsɛ lɛ, kɛɛ, ‘Te tɛŋŋ ni nyɛyeee mikitãi lɛ anɔ ni nyɛbaaloo haomɔ nɛɛ? Akɛni nyɛkwa Yehowa lɛ, lɛ hu ekwa nyɛ.’ ”

english_verse: King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.” Joash Is Killed
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Yoash kaiii kwraa anɔkwayeli ni Zakaria tsɛ Yehoiada kɛsɔmɔ lɛ lɛ, ni egbe Zakaria yakatswaa. Be ni Zakaria gboɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa aaabi migbele nɛɛ shi, ni eeetɔ he owole.” Yoash maŋtsɛyeli naagbee

english_verse: In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus.
translation_verse: Afi nɔ ni sane nɛɛ ba lɛ gbele mli lɛ, Siriabii lɛ fã ta kɛbatua Yoash kɛ Yuda. Be ni amɛbashɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ amɛkpãtã maŋ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ, ni amɛkɛ nii ni amɛha lɛ fɛɛ tee yahã Damasko maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
translation_verse: Tabilɔi ni Siriabii lɛ kɛba ta lɛ ayikulɛ fioo, kɛ̃lɛ Yehowa hã amɛye Yuda tabilɔi babaoo lɛ anɔ kunim, ejaakɛ Yudabii lɛ ekwa Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Enɛ nɔ tsɔ̃ ni agbala Maŋtsɛ Yoash toi.

english_verse: The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_verse: Saji ni kɔɔ Yoash musuŋ bihii lɛ ahe, kɛ gbalɛi srɔtoi ni agba ashi Yoash lɛ, kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ saamɔ mli saji lɛ aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Maŋtsɛmɛi ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli. Yoash bi Amazia baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel,
translation_verse: Shi gbalɔ ko ba Maŋtsɛ Amazia ŋɔɔ, ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nii, okɛ Israel tabilɔi nɛɛ akaya ta lɛ, ejaakɛ Yehowa bɛ Efraimbii nɛɛ asɛɛ.

english_verse: Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?” “The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Amazia bi gbalɔ lɛ akɛ, “Te wɔfee tɛŋŋ mɔ yɛ jwiɛtɛi ni tsiimɔ ji talentai oha ni mikɛbɔ Israel tabilɔi lɛ apaa lɛ gbɛfaŋ hu?” Gbalɔ lɛ to he akɛ, “Yehowa baanyɛ eto bo najiaŋ kɛteke nɔ.”

translation_verse: Amazia fee nuu, ni enyiɛ tabilɔi lɛ ahiɛ kɛtee Ŋoo Jɔɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛ kɛ Edombii lɛ yatswa ta ko yɛ jɛi. Yudabii lɛ gbe Edom tabilɔi akpei nyɔŋma yɛ jɛi,

english_verse: But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.” The prophet stopped. english_verse: King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia kɛ eŋaawolɔi tee ajina. Kɛkɛ ni etsu ni ayakɛɛ Yehoash ni ji Yehu bi Yehoahaz bi lɛ, ni ji Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ, akɛ eetsɛ lɛ ŋa nɔ.

english_verse: Jehoash sent back a reply that said: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Shɛɛ nɛɛ hetoo ni Yehoash bahã Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia ji akɛ, “Be ko lɛ Lebanon ŋmei tso tsu ni ayakɛɛ Lebanon tsenedrutso akɛ, ‘Kɛ obiyoo lɛ ahã mibinuu lɛ gbãlã.’ Shi ŋaŋ kooloo ko ni miiho yɛ jɛi ni nu shɛɛ lɛ tee ni eyanaanaa ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ooshwã akɛ, ‘Bɛ oona akɛ miye Edombii anɔ kunim?’ Oyitso efuu. Ole sane ko? Taomɔ ohe ko ota yɛ oshĩateŋ kpoo. Mɛɛba oyatao sane ni baahã bo kɛ Yuda fɛɛ hiɛ akpãtã nɛɛ?”

english_verse: so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash fã ta kɛbanina Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yudabii lɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ damɔ shi hiɛ kɛ hiɛ yɛ Bet-Shemesh.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Israelbii lɛ ye Yudabii lɛ anɔ kunim, ni Yudabii lɛ jojoo foi kɛtee amɛshĩaiaŋ.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Israel Maŋtsɛ Yehoash mɔ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Amazia, ni ji Ahazia bi Yoash bi lɛ, yɛ Bet-Shemesh, ni ekɛ lɛ ba Yerusalɛm. Yehoash bakumɔ Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ eshwie shi kɛjɛ Efraim Agbo lɛ naa aahu kɛyashi Koŋ Agbo lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni kã agboi enyɔ nɛɛ ateŋ lɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi ohai ejwɛ.

english_verse: He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria. Amaziah Is Killed (
translation_verse: Eloo Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ mli shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ tsɛnsii kɛ kpuji fɛɛ ni ana lɛ, ni emɔmɔ Obed-Edom shwiei ni buɔ nibii nɛɛ ahe lɛ efata nibii lɛ ahe. Eku sɛɛ eloo maŋtsɛ we lɛŋ hu jwetri fɛɛ, ni emɔmɔ nomii babaoo hu ofɔ̃ kɛku esɛɛ kɛtee Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Amazia wala he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ aŋmala fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyata naagbee yɛ Yuda kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there.
translation_verse: Abɔi Amazia yinɔ apamtoo yɛ Yerusalɛm kɛjɛ beyinɔ ni ekwa Yehowajamɔ beebe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, naagbee mli aahu lɛ Amazia jo foi kɛtee Lakish. Shi atiu lɛ kɛtee Lakish lɛ, ni ayagbe lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Awo egbonyo lɛ afɔ okpɔŋɔ nɔ kɛba Yerusalɛm, ni abafu lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging.
translation_verse: Uzia fee tsɛŋi kɛ akplɔi kɛ dade faii kɛ dade damai kɛ gãii kɛ akromiai wuji amli tɛi tete ehã Yuda tabilɔi lɛ.

english_verse: Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Uzia ye hewolo nɔ hela nɛɛ kɛtee egbele mli. Hela lɛ hewɔ lɛ atsi lɛ Yehowa We lɛ mli gbɛ, ni ehi shi yɛ shĩa ko mli banee kɛ hela lɛ. Ni fee nakai lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Uzia bi Yotam kwɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ etsɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
translation_verse: Uzia he saji ni eshwɛ lɛ, Amoz bi Gbalɔ Yesaia eŋmala fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyagbe naa.

english_verse: Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall. God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world. Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
translation_verse: Ŋaalɔi sɔ̃sɔ̃ɔ tsɔnei hã Maŋtsɛ Uzia koni akɛmamɔ mɔji gojogojoo lɛ amli kɛ maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ koji lɛ koni akɛtsɛrɛ̃ gãi, asaŋ ni akɛfɔ̃ tɛi wuji hu. Bɔ ni atsɔ̃ aye abua Maŋtsɛ Uzia ni ena hewalɛ lɛ eyɛ naakpɛɛ; ni ehã egbɛi hehe kɛtee shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Yehowa gbala Uzia toi

english_verse: God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ ye ebua lɛ ni eye Filistibii lɛ kɛ Arabiabii ni yɔɔ Gur-Baal lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ Meunbii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english_verse: After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Uzia eye afii nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa be ni ebɔi maŋtsɛyeli lɛ, ni eye maŋtsɛ afii nyɔŋmai enumɔ kɛ enumɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm. Enyɛ ni fɔ lɛ gbɛi ji Yekolia ni jɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Hewalɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Uzia na nɛɛ hã ewo ehe nɔ, ni no kɛ eshigbeemɔ ba. Uzia je Yehowa, eNyɔŋmɔ, lɛ ŋwane, ni etee Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli akɛ eyaashã tsofakɛŋma lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsofakɛŋmashãa latɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Eba ejeŋ bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ tamɔ etsɛ Amazia fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
translation_verse: Zakaria ji mɔ ni wo lɛ ŋaa, ni etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ bɔ ni ehi shi ehã yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɛfaŋ; ni gbɔmɔ nɛɛ wala be mli fɛɛ lɛ Maŋtsɛ Uzia sɔmɔ Nyɔŋmɔ ni bei abɔ fɛɛ ni Uzia sɔmɔ Yehowa lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ hã eshwere.

english_verse: While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Uzia fã ta ni ekɛ Filistibii lɛ yawu, ni ekumɔ amɛmaji ni ji Gat kɛ Yabine kɛ Ashdod ahe gbogboi lɛ eshwie shi. No sɛɛ lɛ, etotoo maji wuji kɛ amɛhe gbogboi yɛ Ashdod kpokpai anɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ yɛ Filistibii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei krokomɛi hu.

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Amonbii lɛ tsu too amɛkɛsɔmɔ Uzia; ni Uzia batsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ wulu naakpa, ni egbɛi hehe kɛshɛ Ijipt kpokpai anɔ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Uzia mamɔ mɔji gojogojoo komɛi, ni ekɛwaje Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ. Mɔji nɛɛ ekome yɛ Koŋ Agbo lɛ naa, ni ekome yɛ Jɔɔ Agbo lɛ naa, ni ekome hu yɛ Gbogbo Lɔgɔmɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: Emamɔ mɔji gojogojoo lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ hu; ni etsara nubui pii ejaakɛ eyɛ kooloi babaoo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ jɔɔ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋa lɛ hu nɔ. Akɛni Uzia sumɔɔ humɔ hewɔ lɛ, ehã mɛi hu ŋmɔji, ni amɛfeefee waintromii yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛ jɔi lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Maŋtsɛ Uzia yɛ tabilɔi ni efee kralo hã ta be fɛɛ be. Ajara amɛmli asafoiasafoi, ni Yeiel, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, kɛ maŋtsɛ tsulɔ Maaseia ji mɛi ni buɔ tabilɔi lɛ ayikulɛ he akɔntaa. Ni amɛ hu amɛyɛ Hanania ni ji maŋtsɛ tatsɛmɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome lɛ shishi.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
translation_verse: ni amɛyatsi lɛ gbɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ Uzia, ejeee ogbɛnaa akɛ oshã tsofakɛŋma ohã Yehowa. Osɔfoi, ni ji Aaron shwiei, lɛ pɛ ji mɛi ni ajɔɔ tsofakɛŋmashãa nɔ ahã. Shi He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni oya! Otɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ, ni obɛ Yehowa dɛŋ jɔɔmɔ ko ni obaana dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Uzia mli fu. No mli lɛ ehiɛ tsɛnsi ni ekɛbaashã tsofakɛŋma lɛ. Emli lɛ ni fu osɔfoi lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni hewolo nɔ hela ko ni asheɔ lɛ gbeyei shwie ehiɛnaa kplitsaa yɛ osɔfoi lɛ ahiɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Be ni Azaria kɛ osɔfoi krokomɛi lɛ na hewolo nɔ hela kplitsaa lɛ ni shwie Uzia hiɛnaa lɛ, amɛtsirɛ eyisɛɛ akɛ eshi Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli. Ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ po ehe fee oya ni eje kpo ejaakɛ Yehowa egbala etoi.

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Uzia tsɔ̃ esɛɛ, ni afu lɛ banee yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ hela lɛ hewɔ lɛ akɛ lɛ futuuu maŋtsɛmɛi agbohii lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni ebi Yotam baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Yotam ba ejeŋ bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ tamɔ bɔ ni etsɛ Uzia fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, fe akɛ lɛ lɛ ekaaa akɛ ekɛ ehe aaawo sɔ̃ɔmɔ ni asɔmɔɔ yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli lɛ mli. Shi maŋbii lɛ tee nɔ amɛja jemawɔji komɛi.

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Yotam baje agbo ejaakɛ eshihilɛ mli lɛ ebo Yehowa, eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toi.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Yotam he saji krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ tai ni ewu lɛ, kɛ emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli nibii ni etsu lɛ aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Israel kɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛmɛi Ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: ni egbo, ni afu lɛ yɛ David Maŋ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ ni ebinuu Ahaz baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahaz tee hei grɔŋŋi ni ji jemawɔji ajamɔhei ni yɔɔ gɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ tsei kusukusuu lɛ ashishi lɛ ni eyashãshãa afɔlei, ni eshãshãa tsofakɛŋma hu yɛ jɛi ekɛja jemawɔji lɛ. Yuda kɛ Siria kɛ Israel ta (

english_verse: So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse.
translation_verse: Be ni Asiria Maŋtsɛ Tiglat Pileser ba lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewa Ahaz kɛwo lɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebawo Ahaz nɔnaa lɛ mli wu moŋ

english_verse: and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: ni eshã tsofakɛŋma yɛ Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ mli ekɛja jemawɔji lɛ. Etee nɔ po esha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emusuŋbii akɛ afɔle ekɛhã jemawɔji lɛ. Gbɔmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sa, shi Yehowa shwie amɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ agbɛ nɔ be ni Israelbii lɛ jɛ Ijipt amɛbaa lɛ akusum ni ehiɔ ji enɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them. The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed
translation_verse: ejaakɛ gbi kometoo nɔ lɛ, Israel Maŋtsɛ Peka, Remalia binuu lɛ, gbe Yuda tabilɔi kãkãlɔi lɛ ateŋ mɛi akpei oha kɛ nyɔŋmai enyɔ sɔŋŋ. Eba lɛ nɛkɛ ejaakɛ Yudabii lɛ ekwa Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ hu lɛ, nyɛto yiŋ akɛ nyɛbaafee Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm hii kɛ yei nyɛnyɔji. Aso nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu nyɛtɔ̃ko Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, nɔ nyɛtoko?

english_verse: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
translation_verse: Nyɛle sane ko? Nyɛhãa nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ ni nyɛyaŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ akua amɛsɛɛ ayaa ejaakɛ Yehowa mli ni efu nyɛ lɛ jeee hiɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Asaŋ Efraimbii lɛ amaŋ onukpai ejwɛ komɛi hu te shi amɛshi tabilɔi ni jɛ ta amɛbaa shĩa lɛ. Amɛ ji Azaria, Yehohanan bi lɛ, kɛ Berekia, Meshilemot bi lɛ, kɛ Yehizkia, Shalum bi lɛ, kɛ Amasa, Hadlai bi lɛ.

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɛ tabilɔi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ nomii nɛɛ akabaa maŋ nɛɛ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ. Tɔ̃mɔ ni wɔtɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ momo sa lɛ eda, ni eyɛ wɔhe mlifu ni naa wa. Nyɛmiifee nɛkɛ koni nyɛkɛyawo tɔ̃mɔ hee nyɛbashi nɔ ni kã wɔnɔ lɛ nɔ nyɛhã wɔ?”

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Wiemɔ nɛɛ hã tabilɔi lɛ shi nomii lɛ kɛ nii ni amɛha lɛ fɛɛ amɛhã maŋ onukpai lɛ kɛ maŋbii ni ewo shi yɛ jɛi lɛ.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋ onukpai ejwɛ lɛ kɔlɔ mamai yɛ haanii lɛ amli amɛhã nomii lɛ ateiaŋ mɛi ni mama bɛ amɛhe ekpakpa ko lɛ. Amɛhã amɛ atadei kɛ tokotai amɛwo; ni ahã nomii lɛ anii amɛye amɛtɔrɔ kɛ nɔ ko hu amɛnu. Mɛi hu ni ena faji lɛ, atotoo nɔ kɛ mu ahã amɛ. english_verse: Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places. Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Filistibii lɛ ebatua Yuda maji ni yɔɔ Yuda anaigbɛ gɔji lɛ ahiɛshi lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ ewuoyigbɛ maji lɛ hu. Amɛshɔ̃shɔ̃ɔ̃ maji nɛɛ, Bet-Shemesh kɛ Ayalon kɛ Gederot kɛ Soko kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ, kɛ Timna kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ, kɛ Gimzo hu kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ, ni amɛbahi maji nɛɛ amli kwraa.

english_verse: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
translation_verse: Yehowa ba Yuda shi nɛkɛ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Ahaz hewɔ, ejaakɛ Ahaz bɔ nyɛnyɛŋtswi yɛ Yuda, ni eyayeee Yehowa anɔkwa.

english_verse: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Ahaz loo Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli jwetri lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ hu mli nɔ lɛ, kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ hu ashĩai amli jwetri fɛɛ, ni ekɛhã Tiglat Pileser, Asiria Maŋtsɛ lɛ; shi enɛ tete yeee buaaa Ahaz yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ kwraa. Maŋtsɛ Ahaz he eshai

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Shi efimɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahaz kã he moŋ egbo Yehowa nɔ toi fe tsuutsu lɛ.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: Eshã afɔlei ehã Damaskobii ni ye enɔ kunim yɛ ta mli lɛ ajemawɔji lɛ. Ekɛɛmɔ ji akɛ, “Siriabii ajemawɔji lɛ yeɔ buaa Siria maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji mi hu mishã afɔle mihã amɛ lɛ, amɛaaye amɛbua mi.” Shi enɛ ni efee lɛ moŋ hã Ahaz kɛ Israel fɛɛ hiɛ kpãtã butuu

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ahaz bua Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ mli tsɛnsii kɛ kpuji kɛ nibii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ anaa, ni ejwra amɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, eŋmɛ Yehowa We lɛ naa shinai lɛ amli; ni etee eyamamɔ afɔleshãa latɛi ehã ehe yɛ Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ mli akutso fɛɛ akutso mli.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ efee hei grɔŋŋi koni ashã tsofakɛŋma akɛja jemawɔji yɛ jɛi yɛ Yuda maji wuji fɛɛ amli. Jeŋba nɛɛ hã Yehowa, etsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mli fu lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahaz shihilɛ mli saji krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ, aŋmala kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyagbe naa yɛ Yuda kɛ Israel Maŋtsɛmɛi Ahe Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Ahaz gbo ni afu lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm, shi jeee yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi afũuhe lɛ. Ebinuu Hezekia ji mɔ ni baye maŋtsɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: Hezekia ba ejeŋ ekpakpa bɔ ni Yehowa taoɔ tamɔ eseshinyo Maŋtsɛ David fee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ He tsuumɔ

english_verse: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ tee Maŋtsɛ Hezekia ŋɔɔ amɛyabɔ lɛ amaniɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔtsuu Yehowa sɔlemɔ shĩatso muu lɛ he wɔgbe naa. Shãa afɔle afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kɛ ehe nibii lɛ fɛɛ, kɛ okplɔ̃ ni akɛ Yehowa aboloo lɛ maa nɔ lɛ, kɛ ehe nibii lɛ fɛɛ hu wɔtsuu he.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Hezekia hã Levibii lɛ yadamɔ Yehowa We lɛ mli kɛ ŋoŋoi kɛ obentai kɛ saŋkui bɔ ni Yehowa etsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ ninalɔ Gad kɛ agbɛnɛ Gbalɔ Natan nɔ etsɔ̃ɔ Maŋtsɛ David akɛ efee lɛ.

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Be ni ashã afɔle lɛ agbe naa lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Hezekia kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ koto shi, ni amɛja Yehowa.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: Etsɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ, ni ekɛ amɛ kpe yɛ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ bokãgbɛ kpo teŋ lɛ mli,

english_verse: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: ni ekɛ amɛ wie. Ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Agoo Levibii, agbɛnɛ nyɛtsuua nyɛhe ni nyɛfea nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ, koni nyɛfea Yehowa, nyɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, We lɛ hu krɔŋkrɔŋ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni buleɔ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ, nyɛjiea yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ eyayeee anɔkwa, ni amɛfeefee nibii ni ejaaa yɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, hiɛ. Amɛkwa lɛ, amɛkɔ amɛnane yɛ biɛ ni ji Yehowa We lɛ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ amɛsɛɛ amɛhã Yehowa.

english_verse: They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Amɛŋamɔ Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ naa shinai lɛ, amɛkwɛ ni Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli kanei lɛ gboi, ni tsofakɛŋma ni jio, shãa afɔlei ni jio, amɛbashãaa eko yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ amɛhãaa Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
translation_verse: Yehowa mli fu Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm naakpa yɛ enɛɛmɛi ahewɔ; ni nɔ ni efee amɛ lɛ nyɛ fɛɛ nyɛna bɔ ni eyɔɔ tsuifãa ehã, asaŋ ni ehãa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: Agbegbee wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ yɛ ta mli, ni naa, wɔbihii kɛ wɔbiyei kɛ wɔŋamɛi lɛ aŋɔ amɛ nom kɛtee maŋsɛɛ ni ayaye amɛ nyɔŋ.

english_verse: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
translation_verse: “Mito miyiŋ akɛ mi kɛ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, baakpãŋ bɔ ni afee ni efo emlifu lɛ sɛɛ ehã wɔ.

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Mibii, nyɛkafea hejɔ̃ yɛ sane nɛɛ mli ejaakɛ nyɛ, nyɛ ji mɛi ni Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ ehala akɛ nyɛdamɔ ehiɛ nyɛsɔmɔ lɛ, asaŋ ni nyɛshã tsofakɛŋma nyɛhã lɛ.”

english_verse: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ tee ni amɛyabua amɛnyɛmimɛi Levibii lɛ anaa, ni amɛtsuu amɛhe kɛfee amɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛtee, bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ efã amɛ yɛ Yehowa wiemɔ naa lɛ, koni amɛyatsuu Yehowa We lɛ mli.

english_verse: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ bote Yehowa We lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛyatsuu jɛi. Amɛloo nibii fɛɛ ni buleɔ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ kɛje kpo kɛba Yehowa We lɛ kpo teŋ lɛ mli; kɛkɛ ni Levibii lɛ hu loo nibii nɛɛ kɛtee amɛkɛyawo Kidron faa lɛ mli.

english_verse: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
translation_verse: Amɛbɔi hetsuumɔ nitsumɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ, ni gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ, amɛshɛ Yehowa We lɛ koi lɛ shi. Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ gbii kpaanyɔ tsuu Yehowa We lɛ he. Amɛgbe nitsumɔ lɛ naa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa lɛ nɔ. Agbele Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ naa ekoŋŋ

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: Nibii fɛɛ ni kulɛ akɛjaa shi Maŋtsɛ Ahaz shi amɛ sɛɛ be mli ni ekpa Yehowa jamɔ be ni eyeɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ, wɔkɛ fɛɛ eba, ni wɔtsuu amɛhe. Amrɔ nɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ mamɔ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Oya nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Hezekia bua maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ amɛ tee Yehowa sɔlemɔ shia lɛ mli.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ tsinahii kpawo kɛ ojwɛnii kpawo kɛ toobii kpawo kɛ tookpakpoi hu kpawo ba koni akɛshã afɔle kɛfɔ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ kɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ Yuda maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ he muji lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã osɔfoi lɛ, ni ji Aaron shwiei lɛ, akɛ amɛkɛ kooloi lɛ ashã afɔle yɛ Yehowa afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ amɛmɔmɔ too kpakpoi lɛ, ni amɛkɛ amɛ ba maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋbii ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni amɛkɛ amɛniji shwieshwie kooloi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ gbe too kpakpoi lɛ, ni akɛ amɛlã lɛ fee Israel he esha hefaikpamɔ afɔle yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ efã akɛ shãa afɔle lɛ kɛ esha he afɔle lɛ ashã fɛɛ ahã Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ hiɛhiɛ David yinɔ lámɔ nibii krokomɛi lɛ, ni osɔfoi lɛ hiɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia fã akɛ abɔi shãa afɔle lɛ shãa. Be ni aje afɔle lɛ shãa shishi nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ wo lala, ni akɛkafo Yehowa, ni lalatsɛmɛi lɛ hu bɔi David yinɔ obentai lɛ kɛ ŋoŋoi lɛ kɛ saŋkui lɛ tswaa kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ hu kpãmɔ.

english_verse: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, Hezekia kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ bi Levibii lɛ akɛ amɛla lalai ni David folɔ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni Gbalɔ Asaf hu folɔ lɛ amɛkɛjie Yehowa yi. Kɛkɛ ni asafo lɛ koto shi, ni amɛja Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ ni nyɛtsuu nyɛhe nyɛhã Yehowa nɛɛ, nyɛtsia nyɛbɛŋkɛa kɛ nyɛfɔlei lɛ nyɛkɛbadaa Yehowa shi.” Asafo lɛ kɛ afɔlei lɛ ba, ni mɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ he tsui lɛ kɛ shãa afɔlei hu ba.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Shi akɛ ni osɔfoi lɛ ayi eyafaaa bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kooloi ni akɛbaashã shãa afɔle lɛ fɛɛ ahe woji amɛkpɔlɔ hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛmimɛi Levibii lɛ wa amɛ kɛyashi agbe nitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa. Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ ekomɛi yatsuu amɛhe, ni amɛbamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni shãa afɔle lɛ yafa babaoo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ yeli kɛ shidaa afɔle kooloi lɛ amli fɔi lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ shãa afɔle lɛ he dãa afɔle lɛ hu yafa babaoo. Gbɛ nɔ ni tsɔ̃ ni atsuu Yehowa We lɛ he, asaŋ ni agbele naa ekoŋŋ koni aja yɛ mli lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia kɛ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ nya naakpa yɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ etsu ehã amɛ lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ nitsumɔ lɛ tee nɔ oya.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛma sane lɛ nɔ mi akɛ ashiɛ ahã Israelbii fɛɛ kɛjɛ Beersheba, yɛ wuoyigbɛ, aahu kɛyashwie Dan, yɛ kooyigbɛ, akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aba koni abaye Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Hehoo Gbijurɔ lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm ekɛwo Yehowa hiɛ nyam, ejaakɛ nakai be mli lɛ mɛi babaoo baaa gbijurɔ lɛ yeli dɔŋŋ tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ŋmala woji, ni amɛkɛtsu bɔfoi kɛtee Israel kɛ Yuda heihei fɛɛ. Maŋtsɛ lɛ shɛɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Israelbii, nyɛkpalea nyɛbaa Yehowa, ni ji Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni lɛ hu eeebɛŋkɛ nyɛ, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛhe je mli, ni Asiria maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ anine eyashɛɛɛ nyɛnɔ koni amɛŋɔ nyɛ nom lɛ.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Nyɛkafea nyɛhe kuɛŋtilɔi tamɔ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ; shi moŋ nyɛbaa nyɛhe shi nyɛhãa Yehowa. Nyɛbaa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm; etsuu he eto kɛmiiya naanɔ koni nyɛbaja Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yɛ jɛi koni Yehowa mli ni efu nyɛ lɛ sɛɛ afo.

english_verse: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛji nyɛkpale kɛba Yehowa ŋɔɔ lɛ, mɛi ni baŋɔ nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛbii lɛ hu nom kɛtee maŋsɛɛ lɛ amusuŋ baatsɔ̃ amɛ yɛ amɛhe, ni amɛbaaŋmɛɛ nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛbii lɛ ahe koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, durolɔ kɛ mɔbɔnalɔ ji lɛ; ni kɛji nyɛkpale nyɛba eŋɔɔ lɛ, ebaahere nyɛ atuu.”

english_verse: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mɛi fioo ko jɛ Asher kɛ Manase kɛ Zebulonbii ateŋ ba amɛhe shi amɛbo tsɛmɔ lɛ toi, ni amɛba gbijurɔ lɛ yeli yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ nine kã Yudabii lɛ ahe, ni ehã amɛ fɛɛ amɛna jwɛŋmɔ kome kɛfee ekome, ni amɛye maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ agbɛjianɔtoi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛkɛfee Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔnaanii. Aye Hehoo Gbijurɔ lɛ

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, asafo babaoo diɛŋtsɛ naa bakpe shi yɛ Yerusalɛm koni amɛbaye Ma Akpiti Gbijurɔ lɛ.

english_verse: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Asafo lɛ kumɔ afɔleshãa latɛi kɛ tsofakɛŋmashãa latɛi ni amãmɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm heihei fɛɛ ni amɛloo fɛɛ amɛyatsi amɛshwie Kidron Faa lɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.”
translation_verse: “Yehowa, wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ, yɛ omlihilɛ naa lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni miitao osɛɛgbɛ kɛ etsuiŋ fɛɛ lɛ, kɛji etsuuko ehe yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mlai lɛ anaa tete lɛ okɛ etɔ̃mɔ lɛ afa lɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
translation_verse: Yehowa bo Hezekia sɔlemɔ lɛ toi, ni ekɛfa amɛ, ni efɔŋ ko baaa amɛnɔ.

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii ni anaa bakpe shi yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ ye Ma Akpiti Gbijurɔ lɛ kɛyashi gbii kpawo sɔŋŋ kɛ nyamɔ kpele. Daa gbi lɛ Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ laa kɛjieɔ Yehowa yi kɛ amɛnyɛmɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni Maŋtsɛ Hezekia jie Levibii lɛ ayi pam yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe esa kɛ sɔɔmɔ kɛji aaja Yehowa lɛ hewɔ. Atsa Gbijurɔ lɛ yeli nɔ Maŋbii lɛ shãshãa shidaa afɔlei, ni amɛyeyee nii kɛyashi gbii kpawo, ni amɛda Yehowa, amɛtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shi.

english_verse: Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
translation_verse: Shi gbii kpawo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, maŋ lɛ fɛɛ ye fua akɛ atsa afiyeli lɛ nɔ gbii kpawo ekoŋŋ. Ni afee nakai kɛ miishɛɛ.

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yudabii blublu kɛ amɛsɔfoi lɛ kɛ amɛteŋ Levibii fɛɛ hu, kɛ asafo ni jɛ Israel ba lɛ, kɛ gbɔi hu ni jɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ gbɔi ni yɔɔ Yuda lɛ fɛɛ na miishɛɛ.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Nyamɔ ni anya yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ jeee hiɛ nɛ, ejaakɛ kɛjɛ Maŋtsɛ David bi Solomon yinɔ lɛ, ayeko afi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm dã.

english_verse: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ ba Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ jɔɔmɔ amɛhã maŋbii lɛ. Nyɔŋmɔ nu sɔlemɔ lɛ, ni ebo toi.

english_verse: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia hã akɛ bɔ ni ajara osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ amli kuikui sa lɛ bɔ̃i nitsumɔ ekoŋŋ bɔ ni ku fɛɛ ku yɛ enitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Mɛi yɛ ni shãa afɔle ni ashãa fɛɛ lɛ, kɛ shidaa afɔlei lɛ; ni mɛi yɛ ni sɔmɔɔ yɛ jamɔ lɛ mli, ni mɛi yɛ ni laa kɛjieɔ Yehowa yi; dani mɛi yɛ ni buɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ agboi lɛ anaa.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ aŋmala amɛ kɛ amɛbii bibii kɛ amɛŋamɛi kɛ amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei fɛɛ agbɛii, no ji amɛsafoi kuikui lɛ amlibii fɛɛ. Ni amɛyeɔ anɔkwa kɛhiɛɔ amɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ hu ejaakɛ aakwɛ gbɛ akɛ be fɛɛ be ni aaatsɛ amɛ amɛnitsumɔi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ atsumɔ lɛ, amɛyɛ kralo.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Maŋtsɛ Hezekia fã Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ mli bii lɛ akɛ amɛhã osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ nii ni ji amɛ, osɔfoi lɛ, kɛ Levibii lɛ, amɛgbɛfaŋ nii lɛ bɔ ni afee ni osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɛɛ ahã kɛsɔmɔ yɛ Yehowa Mla lɛ naa.

english_verse: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
translation_verse: Be ni agbe gbijurɔ lɛ yeli naa lɛ, Israelbii fɛɛ ni baye gbijurɔ lɛ teetee Yuda kɛ Benyamin maji lɛ amli, ni amɛyakumɔ jemawɔji amãgãi lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛgba Asherim jemawɔŋ lɛ koi lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛfitefitee hei grɔŋgrɔŋŋ ni ajaa jemawɔji yɛ lɛ fɛɛ, kɛ afɔleshãa latɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ hu. Amɛyafite nibii nɛɛ ahenɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Efraim kɛ Manase hu fɛɛ kɛyashi eshwɛɛɛ ekome folo. Kɛkɛ ni Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ hu ku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee amɛkutsei ashikpɔji lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tee ewe.

english_verse: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛfaŋ nii ni etsu ji akɛ emɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekooloi ni eyɔɔ lɛ eko ehãa, ni akɛshãa daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ afɔlei lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ afɔlei ni ashãa yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ hei shishijee nɔ, kɛ gbii juji krokomɛi lɛ hu anɔ lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ Yehowa Mla lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni anu famɔ nɛɛ he lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ abele kɛ wain kɛ mu kɛ wo kɛ ŋmɔshinii srɔtoi ni amɛkpa lɛ amli nii babaoo ba. Amɛkɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome babaoo hu ba.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yudabii kɛ Israelbii ni yɔɔ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji lɛ amli lɛ hu kɛ toi kɛ tsinai kɛ nii ni amɛjɔɔ nɔ amɛkɛke Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ amlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome ba, ni amɛto nibii lɛ kuikui.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ akɛ nibii lɛ bɔi baa; ni ahiɛ kɛbaa aahu kɛyashi nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ, ni agbe naa.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Be ni Maŋtsɛ Hezekia kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ bana nibii kuikui ni maŋbii lɛ kɛbahã lɛ, amɛ jie Yehowa kɛ emaŋ Israel fɛɛ yi.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Hezekia bi osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ nibii lɛ ahe sane,

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: ni Osɔfonukpa Azaria, ni eji Zadok shwie lɛ, kɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛjɛ beyinɔ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛ afɔlei lɛ bɔi Yehowa we lɛ baa nɛɛ lɛ, wɔnaa nii wɔyeɔ wɔtɔrɔɔ aahu ni eshwɛɔ babaoo tete. Ejaakɛ Yehowa ejɔɔ emaŋ lɛ, ni no hewɔ nii ni shwɛɔ lɛ sɔŋŋ ji babaoo nɛɛ.”

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hezekia fã akɛ asaa tsui lɛ yɛ sɔlemɔ shĩa lɛ amli. Asaa tsui lɛ,

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: Yɛ Maŋtsɛ Hezekia kɛ Osɔfonukpa Azaria hewalɛ naa lɛ, ahala Levibii nyɔŋma komɛi hu akɛ Konania kɛ enyɛmi Shimei shishibii kɛhã nibii lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ji Yehiel kɛ Azazia kɛ Nahat kɛ Asahel kɛ Yerimot kɛ Yozabad kɛ Eliel kɛ Ismakia kɛ Mahat kɛ Benaia.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Kore ni ji Imna, Levinyo onukpa ni kwɛɔ Bokãgbɛ Agbo lɛ nɔ lɛ, bi lɛ ji mɔ ni ato akɛ ehe nibii ni abakeɔ Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ tsuijurɔ naa lɛ; asaŋ ejie nikee nɛɛ mli nii ni ji krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ ni ji tuuŋtu gbɛfaŋ nii lɛ yɛ afɔlei lɛ amli eto afã.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: shi jeee yɛ weku kpãa naa. Hii fɛɛ ni eye afii nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛyaa ni amɛyaa Yehowa we lɛ amɛyatsuɔ amɛgbɛnaa nitsumɔ yɛ amɛwekui anaa lɛ, ahãa amɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnii daa gbi.

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Aaron shwiei, ni ji osɔfoi, ni yɔɔ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ maji ni akɛhã Aaron shwiei ahewɔ lɛ anɔ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, hii krɛdɛɛ yɛ ni ato amɛ, ni amɛ amɛjaa nii, yɛ maji srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ amli; ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhãa osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ hu ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aŋma egbɛi egbɛfaŋnii.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ewo ehe nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ, yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli jamɔ gbɛfaŋ jio, Mla lɛ gbɛfaŋ jio, eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ taomɔ jio, etsu kɛ etsui fɛɛ, ni no hewɔ hu lɛ eye omanye.

english_verse: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
translation_verse: Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ tsuji lɛ bolɔ kɛ gbee waa yɛ Yudafoi amaŋ wiemɔ lɛ mli amɛtsɛ Yerusalɛmbii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ gbogbo lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛwo amɛhe gbeyei, ni amɛhã amɛ jijaa bɔ ni afee ni amɛnyɛ maŋ lɛ amɛŋɔ.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: Nyɛleee kwraa nɔ ni mi kɛ Asiria maŋtsɛmɛi ni etsɔ̃ mihiɛ efee shikpɔji krokomɛi anɔ bii lo? Shikpɔji lɛ eko nɔ jemawɔji lɛ eko enyɛ emaŋbii lɛ ayiwala ehere yɛ midɛŋ pɛŋ lo?

english_verse: The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa fee ehere Hezekia kɛ Yerusalɛmbii lɛ ayiwala yɛ Asiria Maŋtsɛ Sankerib kɛ mɛi krokomɛi fɛɛ adɛŋ nɛ. Asaŋ ehã amɛ kɛ amɛhewɔ maji fɛɛ hi shi yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.

english_verse: The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa yakpala Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛba, ni ebatua Yudabii lɛ, ni egbe Yuda oblahii lɛ kɛnyiɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli tete po. Eyanaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko mɔbɔ, oblanyo jio, oblayoo jio, nuumo jio, yoomo jio, gbɔmɔ kpiŋtiŋkpliŋŋ jio, helatsɛ jio, egbe fɛɛ.

translation_verse: Zedekia hu tse Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar hiɛ atua be mli ni Nebukadnezar ehã Zedekia kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ekã lɛ, Nebukadnezar lɛ, kitã. Zedekia kuɛŋ yati, ni ekpliŋ etsui, ni emiii akɛ ejeɔ ehe sɛɛ ni eboɔ Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toi.

english_verse: The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship.
translation_verse: Asaŋ osɔfoi lɛ ateiaŋ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ hu yanyiɛ maji ni bɔle amɛ lɛ ajeŋba gbohii lɛ asɛɛ, ni amɛkɛtɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ babaoo, ni amɛbule Yehowa we lɛ ni Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ etsuu he, ni efee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins.
translation_verse: Shi Yehowa, ni ji Yudabii lɛ atsɛmɛi lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kã he etsuɔ bɔfoi kɛbaa amɛŋɔɔ ejaakɛ emusuŋ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ emaŋ lɛ kɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem. Jerusalem Is Destroyed (
translation_verse: Shi Yudabii lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ bɔfoi lɛ, he fɛo moŋ amɛyeyee, ni amɛgbe amɛwiemɔi lɛ ahe guɔ, ni amɛliɔ gbalɔi lɛ. Amɛfee nɛkɛ aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni Yehowa mli fu emaŋ lɛ kɛteke nɔ bɔ ni ehiii he nɔ ko feemɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall.
translation_verse: Ema Sɔlemɔ we lɛ naa la ni eshã lɛ, ni ekumɔ Yerusalɛm he gbogbo lɛ eshwie shi. No sɛɛ lɛ, ema maŋ muu lɛ naa la ni eshã lɛ kɛ emli mɔji fɛɛfɛji lɛ kɛ jwetrii fɛɛ.

english_verse: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven, who is also the God of Israel, has made me the ruler of all nations on earth. And he has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over and encourage any of his people who want to go back to Jerusalem and help build the temple.
translation_verse: Yehowa webii ni yɔɔ nyɛteŋ lɛ, Yehowa efã amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ koni efã kɛya Yerusalɛm yɛ Yuda, koni ayama Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, shĩa lɛ; lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni ajaa yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, we lɛ.

english_verse: The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni kɛ amɛ je shwieka lɛ fɛɛ wa amɛ kɛ jwiɛtɛi okpolui pɛmpɛbii kɛ shika kɛ nibiinibii kɛ kooloi kɛ nibii ni jara wa; ni asaŋ amɛhã nikeenii yɛ tsuijurɔ naa.

english_verse: King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods.
translation_verse: Yehowa we lɛ okpolui kɛ kpuji ni Nebukadnezar yaloo kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm kɛba ekɛbawo ejemawɔŋ lɛ we lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Koresh jie amɛ kpo.

english_verse: Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Koresh tu nibii nɛɛ ewo Mitredat, shikatolɔ lɛ dɛŋ; ni Mitredat kane ni eŋmala ewo wolo mli ehã Sheshbazar, Yuda lumɔ lɛ.

english_verse: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
translation_verse: Be ni mɛi ni ku amɛsɛɛ kɛba lɛ bashɛ Yehowa we lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, tsɛmɛi awei lɛ onukpai lɛ ekomɛi bake nii yɛ tsuijurɔ naa yɛ Yehowa we lɛ hewɔ, koni akɛsaa ama Yehowa we lɛ yɛ etsutsu shimaahe lɛ.

english_verse: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi hi Yerusalɛm kɛ ehewɔ akrowai amli; ni lalatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ Sɔlemɔ we sɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ hi maji ni ahã amɛ lɛ amli; ni Israelbii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ hi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmaji amli.

english_verse: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be ni nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ shɛ ni Israelbii ni ba lɛ ehe shi yɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli lɛ, amɛ bluublu amɛbabua amɛhe naa yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeshua, Yehozadak bi lɛ, kɛ enanemɛi osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Zerubabel, Shealtiel bi lɛ, kɛ ewekumɛi kɛ nitsumɔ wo mli, ni amɛma Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koni amɛshã shãa afɔlei yɛ nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Gbɔmɔ Mose Mla lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Tsɛbelɛ nomii lɛ she maŋsɛɛbii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbeyei moŋ, shi kɛ̃lɛ amɛma afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ yɛ eshimaahe lɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛshã leebi shãa afɔlei kɛ gbɛkɛ shãa afɔlei yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ nɛɛ nɔ amɛhã Yehowa.

english_verse: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
translation_verse: Amɛye asesei agbijurɔ lɛ hu, tamɔ bɔ ni ato lɛ, ni amɛshã daa gbi shãa afɔlei lɛ yɛ yibɔ ni ato ahã daa gbi lɛ naa.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
translation_verse: Enɛɛmɛi asɛɛ hu amɛshã daa shãa afɔlei lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ hee afɔlei lɛ kɛ gbii krɔŋkrɔŋi fɛɛ anɔ shãa afɔlei ni Yehowa etsɔ̃ɔ akɛ ashã lɛ, kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nii ni ekɛbakeɔ Yehowa yɛ tsuijurɔ naa lɛ.

english_verse: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
translation_verse: Nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ amɛjɛ amɛbɔ̃i shãa afɔlei lɛ ashãa kɛ Yehowa hãmɔ, tsɛbelɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ anako ato shishi. Abɔ̃i Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ maa

english_verse: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ hã shika kɛhã gbogbotswalɔi kɛ srɛŋkifoi lɛ anyɔmɔwoo. Asaŋ amɛhã niyenii kɛ dãa kɛ mu akɛ akɛhã Sidonbii lɛ kɛ Tirobii lɛ, koni amɛyaŋɔ tsenedru tsei kɛjɛ Lebanon kɛba Yopa ŋshɔ lɛ naa tamɔ bɔ ni Koresh, Persia maŋtsɛ lɛ, ehã amɛ hegbɛ akɛ afee lɛ.

english_verse: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni Israelbii lɛ ba Yehowa we lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, enɔ afi ni ji enyɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Zerubabel, Shealtiel bi lɛ, kɛ Yeshua, Yozadak bi lɛ, kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ, kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni ku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ nomŋɔɔ lɛ mli kɛba Yerusalɛm lɛ bɔ̃i nitsumɔ lɛ. english_verse: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
translation_verse: Yeshua kɛ ebii kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ, kɛ Kadmiel kɛ ebii lɛ ni ji Yuda weku lɛ, fee ekome kɛkɔ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ nitsumɔi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ lɛ amɛfɔ̃ amɛnɔ. Levibii ni jɛ Henadad weku lɛ mli kɛ amɛbii kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi hu ye bua amɛ.

english_verse: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
translation_verse: Be ni tsumalɔi lɛ to Yehowa Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ shishi lɛ, osɔfoi ni ewula kɛ amɛtadei lɛ badamɔ shi kɛ amɛtɛtrɛmantrɛi ni amɛhiɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ kɛ Levibii lɛ ni ji Asafbii lɛ hu kɛ amɛŋoŋoi, koni amɛkafo Yehowa tamɔ bɔ ni Israel Maŋtsɛ David eto gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english_verse: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
translation_verse: Amɛla ni amɛhereheree nɔ amɛkɛkafo Yehowa, ni amɛkɛda lɛ shi amɛkɛɛ, “Ejaakɛ ehi, ejaakɛ esuɔmɔ ni ekɛsumɔɔ Israel lɛ yɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ.” Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ bɔ oshe waa amɛkɛkafo Yehowa yɛ Yehowa shĩa lɛ shishitoo lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
translation_verse: Shi Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ tsɛmɛi awei lɛ onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii, mɛi ni ji hiimeji ni na klɛŋklɛŋ shĩa lɛ fo waa, be ni ato shĩa nɛɛ shishi yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ; shi mɛi babaoo hu bɔ oshe waa kɛ nyamɔ.

english_verse: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋbii lɛ yooo emli nɔ ni ji nyamɔ oshebɔɔ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni ji yaafo blɔmɔ lɛ, ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ bɔ oshe waa diɛŋtsɛ, ni anu yɛ shɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni Yuda kɛ Benyamin henyɛlɔi lɛ nu akɛ mɛi ni jɛ nomŋɔɔ mli ba lɛ miima Sɔlemɔtsu amɛha Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ,

english_verse: So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: amɛba Zerubabel kɛ tsɛmɛi awei lɛ onukpai lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔkɛ nyɛ amãa; ejaakɛ nyɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni nyɛjaa lɛ nɔŋŋ wɔ hu wɔjaa, ni lɛ nɔŋŋ wɔshãa afɔle wɔhãa kɛjɛ Esar-Hadon Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ŋɔ wɔ kɛba biɛ lɛ yinɔ.”

english_verse: But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
translation_verse: Shi Zerubabel kɛ Yeshua kɛ Israel tsɛmɛi awei lɛ onukpai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Kɛ wɔmiima shĩa wɔhã wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, jeee wɔkɛ nyɛ sane ni; shi wɔ sɔŋŋ wɔɔɔma wɔhã Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni maŋtsɛ Koresh, Persia maŋtsɛ lɛ ewo wɔ kitã lɛ.”

english_verse: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mɛi ni eba ebahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tao akɛ amɛhã Yudafoi lɛ anijiaŋ aje wui ni amɛwo Yudafoi lɛ ahe gbeyei koni amɛkama shĩa lɛ.

english_verse: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
translation_verse: Amɛbɔ amralofoi apaa amɛwo Yudafoi lɛ koni amɛhã Yudafoi lɛ ayiŋtoo lɛ afee efolo kɛjɛ Koresh, Persia maŋtsɛ lɛ, be mli aahu kɛyashi Dario, Persia maŋtsɛ lɛ, yinɔ.

english_verse: In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be mli ni Ahashwerosh bɔ̃i maŋtsɛyeli lɛ, gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ŋmãa wolo kɛyafolɔɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ anaa.

english_verse: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Artashasta yinɔ lɛ Bislam kɛ Mitredat kɛ Tabeel kɛ enanemɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ŋmã wolo yahã Artashasta, Persia maŋtsɛ lɛ. Aŋmã wolo lɛ yɛ Siriabii aniŋmãa mli, ni atsɔ̃ɔ shishi hu yɛ Siria wiemɔ mli.

english_verse: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
translation_verse: Wolo lɛ mli sane nɛ, “Aaŋmã wolo nɛɛ ayahã maŋtsɛ Artashasta. Maŋtsɛ Artashasta tsuji ni yɔɔ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ lɛ adɛŋ wolo nɛɛ jɛ.

english_verse: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
translation_verse: Wɔmiitao ni Maŋtsɛ ana ale akɛ Yudafoi lɛ ni jɛ oŋɔɔ ba wɔŋɔɔ nɛɛ ebahe shi yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni amɛmiito atuatselɔi amaŋ fɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Amɛtswa ehe gbogboi lɛ amɛgbe naa etã, ni amɛmiisaa eshishitoo lɛ hu.

english_verse: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
translation_verse: Shi belɛ, Maŋtsɛ ana ale akɛ kɛji ato nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ ekoŋŋ ni agbe ehe gbogboi lɛ anaa lɛ, no lɛ maŋbii lɛ woŋ onia kɛ maŋ too kɛ gbɛjee too lɛ dɔŋŋ, ni be ni yi yaawula shi lɛ, ebaaye maŋtsɛ fotro lɛ awui.

english_verse: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, akɛni Nii dɛŋ nii wɔyeɔ hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ wɔɔɔkwɛ ni Maŋtsɛ he guɔ agbo; ni no hewɔ wɔtsu koni abatswa Maŋtsɛ adafi nɛɛ,

english_verse: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
translation_verse: koni atao yɛ otsɛmɛi awolo ni aŋmã nibii ni eba awo mli afɔ̃ shi lɛ mli. Kɛji akwɛ wolo nɛɛ mli lɛ, abaana yɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ atuatselɔi amaŋ ni. Amɛwoɔ maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mlijai anɔyelɔi anaagba; ni kɛjɛ teteete lɛ, mɛi ayiŋ amɛwoɔ koni atse atua. Enɛ nɔŋŋ hewɔ ajwa maŋ nɛɛ.

english_verse: If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
translation_verse: Wɔmiihã Maŋtsɛ ale akɛ kɛji ato nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ ekoŋŋ, ni atswa ehe gbogboi lɛ, no lɛ, bo Nii, onaŋ nɔyeli he ko yɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ tsu akɛ hetoo ba akɛ, “Miiŋma wolo nɛɛ mayahã Rehum, ajinafoiatsɛ lɛ, kɛ Shimshai, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, kɛ amɛhefatalɔi ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ Samaria kɛ hei krokomɛi yɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ biɛ lɛ, miiŋa nyɛ.

english_verse: After your letter was translated and read to me,
translation_verse: “Wolo ni nyɛkɛtsu akɛbahã wɔ lɛ, akane shishitsɔɔmɔ atsɔ̃ɔ mi.

english_verse: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
translation_verse: Mifã ni atao mli; ni ana akɛ kɛjɛ teteete lɛ maŋ nɛɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ; atseɔ atua, yɛ mli, ni awoɔ mɛi ayiŋ yɛ nɔyelɔi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: And powerful kings have ruled Western Province from Jerusalem and have collected all kinds of taxes.
translation_verse: Asaŋ maŋtsɛmɛi wuji hu ehi Yerusalɛm ni amɛye Eufrate Faa lɛ biɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni atsuɔ onia kɛ maŋ too kɛ gbɛjee shika ahãa amɛ.

english_verse: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛwoa akpɔ koni nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ afɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ too, kɛyashi beyinɔ ni akpɔ aaajɛ miŋɔɔ aba.

english_verse: Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ sane nɛɛ akashashaoa shi, koni nibii akabafite waa wo mi.”

english_verse: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
translation_verse: Be ni akane Maŋtsɛ Artashasta wolo ni eŋmã lɛ yɛ Rehum kɛ Shimshai, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, kɛ mɛi ni fata amɛhe kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, amɛyiŋ kɛba Yerusalɛm oya, ni amɛbanina Yudafoi lɛ. Amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ tsi Yudafoi lɛ anaa. Abɔ̃i Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ maa ekoŋŋ

english_verse: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni afɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ he nitsumɔ; ni ekã shi nakai kɛyashi Maŋtsɛ Dario, Persia maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ gbalɔ Hagai kɛ gbalɔ Zakaria, Ido bi lɛ, gba yɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ gbɛi mli amɛhã Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Zerubabel, Shealtiel bi lɛ, kɛ Yeshua, Yozadak bi lɛ, te shi ni amɛbɔi Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ mãa. Nyɔŋmɔ gbalɔi enyɔ lɛ fĩ amɛsɛɛ, ni amɛwa amɛ.

english_verse: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Tatnai ni ji amralo ni kwɛɔ Eufrate Faa lɛ anaigbɛ biɛgbɛ lɛ kɛ Shetar-Boznai kɛ amɛnanemɛi lɛ, ba mɛi ni maa tsu lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni nɔ ni amɛbi mɛi ni maa lɛ nɛ, “Namɔ fã nyɛ akɛ nyɛma nɛkɛ tsu nɛɛ ni nyɛgbe naa?”

english_verse: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
translation_verse: Shi Yudafoi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ hiŋmɛi kã Yudafoi onukpai lɛ ahe, ni mɛi ni ba lɛ, atsiii amɛ gbɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni sane lɛ yashɛ Dario ŋɔɔ ni eŋma hetoo kɛba.

english_verse: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
translation_verse: “Akɛ wolo nɛɛ miitsu ayahã Maŋtsɛ Dario. Nii hã manye!

english_verse: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
translation_verse: Wɔmiitao ni Maŋtsɛ ana ale akɛ wɔyiŋ wɔtee Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni wɔtee Nyɔŋmɔ kpeteŋkple lɛ we lɛ. Aama kɛ tɛi kpeleikpelei, ni akɛ tsei eshwie egbogboi lɛ anɔ. Ahiɛ nɛkɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ mli kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ, ni eeya nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni wɔbi amɛnukpai lɛ mɔ ni fã amɛ akɛ amɛma nɛkɛ shĩa nɛɛ ni amɛsaa ehe kɛ emli amɛgbe naa lɛ.

english_verse: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
translation_verse: Asaŋ wɔbibii amɛgbɛii hu, koni wɔŋmala amɛnukpai lɛ agbɛii ni wɔhã ole.

english_verse: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
translation_verse: Hetoo ni amɛhã wɔ nɛ, ‘Ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ tsuji ji wɔ. Wɔmiisaa shĩa ni Israel maŋtsɛ agbo ko ma ni egbe naa jeeŋmɔ afii babaoo nɛ lɛ.

english_verse: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
translation_verse: Shi akɛni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ wo ŋwɛi Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ mli la hewɔ lɛ, ehã Babilon maŋtsɛ, Nebukadnezar, Kaldeanyo lɛ, baye amɛnɔ kunim. Nebukadnezar kumɔ nɛkɛ shĩa nɛɛ, ni eŋɔ maŋbii lɛ nom kɛtee Babilon.

english_verse: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nɛkɛ Sheshbazar nɛɛ ba ni ebato Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ shishi. Kɛjɛ nakai be lɛ mli aahu kɛbashi amrɔ nɛɛ akã he aama, shi agbeko naa lolo.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji esa Maŋtsɛ hiɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehã atao yɛ he ni akɛ saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ toɔ, yɛ Babilon lɛ, akɛ eyɛ mli akɛ Maŋtsɛ Koresh ewo akpɔ akɛ ayama nɛkɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We nɛɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ Yerusalɛm lo, koni Maŋtsɛ atsu ni abakɛɛ wɔ nɔ ni esumɔɔ ni afee yɛ sane nɛɛ he.”

english_verse: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Dario fã koni ayatao yɛ shĩa ni akɛ saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ toɔ mli yɛ Babilon lɛ.

english_verse: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
translation_verse: Shi Ekbatana, maŋtsɛmaŋ ni yɔɔ Media shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ji he ni ayana wolo ko yɛ; ni sane ni aŋmã yɛ mli nɛ,

english_verse: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ Koresh klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ewo akpɔ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ he akɛ: ‘Nyɔŋmɔ shĩa ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm ni ashãa afɔlei yɛ mli lɛ, ama, ni ahã eshishitoo lɛ awa. Ekwɔlɛ ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai ekpaa ni elɛɛmɔ hu nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
translation_verse: Egbogboi lɛ bɔ ni abaatswa lɛ nɛ, Kɛ atswa tɛi wuji klɛmpɛi etɛ̃ lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ ashwie nɔ tso klɛmpɛ kome. Nyɔmɔ ni aaabɔ yɛ he lɛ, ajɛ maŋtsɛ we fotro lɛ mli awo.

english_verse: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
translation_verse: Asaŋ shika ŋmiiŋmi kɛ jwiɛtɛi nibii ni Nebukadnezar yaloo kɛjɛ Sɔlemɔtsu ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ mli ni ekɛba Babilon lɛ, akɛku sɛɛ ahã ni akɛya Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ mli ni akɛyato amɛtoohe koni ahã ahi Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ.’ ” Dario fã ni aya nɔ atsu nii lɛ

english_verse: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Dario ŋmã hetoo eyahã Tatnai, faa lɛ anaigbɛ amralo lɛ, kɛ Shetar-Boznai kɛ amraloi ni fata amɛhe yɛ faa lɛ anaigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efã amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛjea jɛi nyɛyaa sɛɛ flɛŋŋ.
