translation_verse: Amralo lɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ amɛkaye nii krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ eko, kɛyashi beyinɔ ni osɔfoi lɛ aaaba ni aaanyɛ atsɔ̃ Urim kɛ Tumim nɔ akɛle nɔ gbɔmɛi ni ji amɛ.

english_verse: Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave
translation_verse: Nɔ ni maŋbii ni eshwɛ lɛ hã ji shika ŋmiiŋmi kiloi oha kɛ nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ kpaanyɔ kɛ jwiɛtɛi kiloi oha kɛ nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛ osɔfoi atadei nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ kpawo.

english_verse: bowls to be used in the temple, and
translation_verse: Reaiabii kɛ Rezinbii kɛ Nekodabii lɛ,

english_verse: And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ lalɔi lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi kɛ Sɔlemɔ we sɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ kɛ Israel muu lɛ fɛɛ bahi amɛmaji lɛ amli.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, the people came together in the open area in front of the Water Gate. Then they asked Ezra, who was a teacher of the Law of Moses, to read to them from this Law that the Lord had given his people. Ezra the priest came with the Law and stood before the crowd of men, women, and the children who were old enough to understand.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Osɔfo Ezra kɛ Mla lɛ ba asafo lɛ hiɛ. Hii kɛ yei kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛji amɛnu wiemɔi lɛ ni amɛaanu shishi lɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
translation_verse: Ezra, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, damɔ nɔ ko ni kwɔ ni akɛ tso fee nɔ. Afee yɛ Mla lɛ kanemɔ lɛ hewɔ. Matitia kɛ Shema kɛ Anaia kɛ Uria kɛ Hilkia kɛ Maaseia damɔ emasɛi yɛ eninejurɔ, ni Pedaia kɛ Mishael kɛ Malkiya kɛ Hashum kɛ Hash-Badana kɛ Zakaria kɛ Meshulam damɔ ebɛku.

english_verse: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
translation_verse: Ezra gbele wolo lɛ mli yɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ. He ni edamɔ lɛ kwɔ fe he ni maŋ lɛ damɔ lɛ. Be ni egbele wolo lɛ mli lɛ, maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ te shi damɔ shi.

english_verse: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ezra jie Yehowa, Nyɔŋmɔ kpeteŋkple lɛ, yi. Maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Amen! Amen!” Amɛhole amɛniji anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛmamɔ amɛyi shi, ni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ bumɔ shi, ni amɛja Yehowa.

english_verse: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni kaneɔ wolo lɛ ni ji Nyɔŋmɔ Mla lɛ, kane lɛ faŋŋ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔ shishi koni anu nɔ ni akaneɔ lɛ shishi faŋŋ.

english_verse: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nehemia ni ji amralo lɛ kɛ Osɔfo Ezra ni ji woloŋmalɔ lɛ kɛ Levibii ni tsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ nii lɛ kɛɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ ni hã Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkayea ŋkɔmɔ, ni nyɛkafoa hu!” Amɛkɛɛ maŋ lɛ nɛkɛ, ejaakɛ be ni maŋ lɛ nu Mla lɛ mli wiemɔi lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛfo.

english_verse: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
translation_verse: Ezra kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyaa ni nyɛyayea nii ni hi naakpa, ni nyɛnua wain ni ŋɔɔ dɔkɔdɔkɔ. Ni nyɛkɛ eko amajea mɛi ni afeko nɔ ko atoko amɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ ni hã wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ. No hewɔ hu lɛ nyɛwerɛ akahoa nyɛhe, ejaakɛ Yehowa he nyamɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni baawo nyɛ hewalɛ.”

english_verse: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ shɛje maŋ lɛ fɛɛ mii amɛkɛɛ, “Nyɛfɔa ŋkɔmɔyeli, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ ni, hewɔ lɛ nyɛwerɛ akahoa nyɛhe.”

english_verse: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ yiŋ amɛtee, ni amɛyaye nii, ni amɛnu nɔ ko. Amɛkɛ eko maje, ni amɛna miishɛɛ babaoo; ejaakɛ wiemɔi ni akane atsɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ, amɛnu shishi faŋŋ. Asesei Agbijurɔ

english_verse: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ tsɛmɛi awei lɛ amli onukpai ni yɔɔ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ babua amɛhe naa yɛ Ezra, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ koni amɛbabo Mla Wolo lɛ mli wiemɔi lɛ toi.

english_verse: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
translation_verse: Amɛna akɛ aŋma yɛ Mla ni Yehowa tsɔ Mose nine nɔ ewo lɛ mli, akɛ Israelbii lɛ ahi asesei amli yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ, be ni ayeɔ Asesei Agbijurɔ lɛ.

english_verse: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
translation_verse: Amɛna akɛ aŋma hu akɛ amɛjaje, ni amɛshiɛ yɛ maji lɛ fɛɛ amli kɛ Yerusalɛm hu akɛ, “Nyɛjea kpo nyɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nyɛyaŋɔa mutsei aniji kɛ ŋkutsei aniji kɛ merto tsei aniji kɛ blɛoi kɛ tsei kusukusui aniji koni nyɛkɛbafee asesei, tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ.”

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋ lɛ je kpo amɛtee, ni amɛyaŋɔ tsei aniji lɛ kɛba, ni amɛkɛbafee asesei amɛhã amɛhe, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ yɛ etsu yiteŋ. Amɛfee asesei yɛ amɛkpoi anɔ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ kpoi lɛ anɔ kɛ Nu Agbo lɛ naa blohu lɛ mli kɛ Efraim Agbo lɛ naa blohu lɛ mli.

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
translation_verse: Mɛi abɔ fɛɛ ni ku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ nomŋɔɔ lɛ mli kɛba lɛ fee asesei, ni amɛhi mli. Israelbii lɛ efeko nakai nɔ ko dã kɛjɛ Yoshua, Nun bi lɛ, yinɔ aahu kɛbashi nakai gbi lɛ nɔ. Amɛmii shɛ amɛhe naakpa.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Gbi fɛɛ gbi, kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ kɛyashi naagbee gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, akaneɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Mla Wolo lɛ. Amɛye gbijurɔ lɛ gbii kpawo, ni gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛkpe naagbee kpee, tamɔ bɔ ni ato lɛ.

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Nakai nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ bakpe. Amɛhi ŋmãa; amɛbumɔ kpekpe, ni amɛkɛ mlu wo amɛyiteŋ.

english_verse: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni ji Israel fɔmɔbii lɛ tse amɛhe yɛ mɛi kpɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe; amɛho amɛdamɔ shi, ni amɛjaje amɛhe eshai lɛ kɛ amɛtsɛmɛi anifɔ̃ɔjianii ni amɛfee lɛ.

english_verse: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Amɛte shi amɛdamɔ shi, ni amɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai etɛ̃ kane Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Mla Wolo lɛ. Amɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai etɛ̃ hu jaje amɛhe eshai, ni amɛja Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Yeshua kɛ Bani kɛ Kadmiel kɛ Shebania kɛ Buni kɛ Sherebia kɛ Bani kɛ Kenani ho damɔ Levibii lɛ akpoku lɛ nɔ, ni amɛsɔle waa amɛtsɛ Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeshua kɛ Kadmiel kɛ Bani kɛ Hashabneia kɛ Sherebia kɛ Hodia kɛ Shebania kɛ Patahia ni amɛ fɛɛ lɛ Levibii ji amɛ lɛ, kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛtea shi ni nyɛjiea Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, yi; nyɛjiea eyi kɛjɛ naanɔ kɛyashi naanɔ! Aaajie egbɛi ni yɔɔ nyam lɛ yi, tsɛbelɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ajieɔ egbɛi yi ni akafoɔ lɛ ahãa tete lɛ, eshɛɛɛ egbɛi lɛ dalɛ.”

english_verse: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
translation_verse: “Bo okome too ji Yehowa, Bo obɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋwɛii amli ŋwɛi kɛ ŋwɛinii huhai abɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Bo obɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ, ŋshɔi kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli; ni bo nɔŋŋ ohãa amɛ fɛɛ kwa naa wala ni ŋwɛinii babaoo lɛ, bo nɔŋŋ amɛjaa.

english_verse: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
translation_verse: Bo Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ oŋɔ Abram. Ojie lɛ kɛjɛ Ur yɛ Babilon, ni otsake egbɛi ofee lɛ Abraham.

english_verse: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
translation_verse: Ona akɛ eyeɔ bo anɔkwa, ni okɛ lɛ kpãŋ akɛ okɛ Kanaanbii kɛ Hitbii kɛ Amorbii lɛ kɛ Perizbii kɛ Yebusbii kɛ Girgashbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ baahã eshwiei lɛ; ni oye oshiwoo lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ jalɔ ji bo.

english_verse: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
translation_verse: “Ona amanehulu ni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ na yɛ Ijipt lɛ, ni obo amɛtsɛmɔ ni amɛtsɛ bo lɛ toi yɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naa.

english_verse: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
translation_verse: Ofee okadii, ni otsu naakpɛɛnii yɛ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ, ejaakɛ ole akɛ Farao kɛ etsuji lɛ wo amɛhe amɛwo wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ; okɛ enɛ he gbɛi ohã ohe, tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
translation_verse: Ohã ŋshɔ lɛ mli gba yɛ amɛhiɛ, ni amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ. Shi mɛi ni tiuɔ amɛ lɛ oshɛrɛ amɛ oshwie ŋshɔ kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛshiu tamɔ tɛ yɛ nu hamahama lɛ mli.

english_verse: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
translation_verse: Okɛ atatu ni ma shi kutuu tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ gbɛ shwane, ni nyɔɔŋ hu lɛ, okɛ la kutuu tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛna nii yɛ gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
translation_verse: Okpeleke shi kɛba Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ojɛ ŋwɛi okɛ amɛ wie; ohã amɛ mlai kpakpai kɛ akpɔi kɛ kitãi kpakpai.

english_verse: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
translation_verse: Ohejɔɔmɔ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ohã amɛle, ni otsɔ̃ otsulɔ Mose nine nɔ owo amɛ kitãi kɛ akpɔi kɛ mlai.

english_verse: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
translation_verse: “Be ni hɔmɔ ye amɛ lɛ, ohã amɛ aboloo ni jɛ ŋwɛi, ni be ni kumai ye amɛ hu, ohã nu jɛ tɛsaa mli ba, ni amɛkɛgbe amɛkumai. Okɛɛ amɛ akɛ amɛba ni amɛbaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okã he kitã akɛ okɛbaahã amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: Shi amɛ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ wo amɛhe; amɛfee amɛhe kuɛŋtilɔi, ni amɛyeee okitãi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Amɛfee tsinabi ni ashwie amɛhã amɛhe, ni amɛkɛɛ no ji amɛnyɔŋmɔ ni jie amɛ kɛje Ijipt; amɛbɔ musu babaoo amɛshi bo.

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: Omɔbɔnalɛ babaoo lɛ hewɔ lɛ, oshiii amɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; shwane lɛ atatu ni ma shi yɛ amɛhiɛ ni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ gbɛ lɛ, ejeee amɛhiɛ; ni nyɔɔŋ hu la ni damɔ amɛhiɛ ni hãa amɛnaa nii yɛ gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ejeee amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: Okɛ omumɔ kpakpa lɛ hã amɛ koni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nii; ohã amɛ mana amɛye, ni ohã amɛ nu amɛkɛgbe amɛkumai.

english_verse: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
translation_verse: Afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ sɔŋŋ okwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; nɔ ko nɔ ko he ehiaaa amɛ; amɛtadei suuu lɛ, amɛnaji hu efuuu.

english_verse: You let them conquer kings and take their land, including King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.
translation_verse: “Ohã amɛye maji kɛ maŋtsɛyelii anɔ kunim. Amɛye shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ, kɛyashi amɛŋɔ Heshbon ni ji Maŋtsɛ Sihon shikpɔŋ lɛ, kɛ Bashan ni ji Maŋtsɛ Og shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Ohã amɛbii lɛ hu ayi fa tamɔ ŋulamii, ni oŋɔ amɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛɛ amɛtsɛmɛi akɛ amɛya amɛyaŋɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni bii lɛ ba koni amɛbaye Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ anɔ; amɛfee amɛ bɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ.

english_verse: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
translation_verse: Amɛyaye maji ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe kɛ shikpɔji ni baa nii anɔ kunim, ni amɛna shĩai ni eyimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ nibii kpakpai fɛɛ: nubui ni atsatsai, wain tromi kɛ mutso tromi kɛ yelitsei babaoo amɛye, ni amɛtɔrɔ, ni amɛshwishwii; ni amɛmii shɛ amɛhe yɛ omlihilɛ kpele lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
translation_verse: “Shi enɛ moŋ sɛɛ lɛ amɛtoi gbo, ni amɛtse ohiɛ atua; amɛkɛ mla lɛ efeee nɔ ko nɔ ko; amɛgbe gbalɔi lɛ ni bɔ amɛ kɔkɔ lɛ, koni amɛkɛkpale amɛ kɛba oŋɔɔ; ni amɛfee musubɔɔ nibii wuji amɛshi bo.

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɛɛ amɛhe ohã amɛhenyɛlɔi, ni amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ hao amɛ. Amɛhaomɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ amɛfo amɛtsɛ bo, ni ohere amɛ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi. Omɔbɔnalɛ babaoo lɛ naa lɛ, ojie hiɛnyiɛlɔi ohã amɛ koni amɛhere amɛ yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ amɛna hejɔlɛ pɛ lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ efɔŋ amɛshiɔ bo, ni oŋmɛɔ amɛhe owoɔ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ; ni henyɛlɔi lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ. Shi kɛ̃lɛ kɛ amɛtao osɛɛgbɛ ekoŋŋ, ni amɛfo amɛtsɛ bo lɛ, oboɔ amɛ toi yɛ ŋwɛi, ni omɔbɔnalɛ babaoo lɛ naa lɛ, ohereɔ amɛ shii abɔ yɛ amɛnɔnaa lɛ mli.

english_verse: You warned them to turn back and discover true life by obeying your laws. But they stubbornly refused and continued to sin.
translation_verse: Obɔ amɛ kɔkɔ koni amɛbɔ̃i omla lɛ nɔyeli ekoŋŋ; shi amɛwo amɛhe, ni amɛbooo okitãi lɛ atoi; amɛfee esha amɛshi omlai lɛ ni kɛji gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi naa wala lɛ. Amɛtsi amɛhe kɛje ohe; amɛfee amɛhe kuɛŋtilɔi, ni amɛbooo bo toi.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ oto otsui shi ohã amɛ afii pii; okɛ omumɔ lɛ wo gbalɔi lɛ amli, ni otsɔ̃ amɛnɔ obɔ obii lɛ kɔkɔ; shi amɛbooo toi; No hewɔ lɛ, ohã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ bii lɛ ye amɛnɔ.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ omɔbɔnalɛ babaoo lɛ naa lɛ, oŋmɛɛɛ amɛhe, ni asaŋ okpãtãaa amɛhiɛ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni musuŋ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ ni enaa mɔbɔ ji bo.

english_verse: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
translation_verse: “WɔNyɔŋmɔ, oje agbo! Ohe wa, ohe yɛ gbeyei, ni onaa mɔbɔ; kɛji okɛ mɔ ko kpãŋ ni owo shi lɛ, oyeɔ nɔ. Kɛjɛ Asiria maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ ayinɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, kaahã amanehulu ni ba wɔ kɛ wɔmaŋtsɛmɛi kɛ wɔnukpai kɛ wɔsɔfoi kɛ wɔgbalɔi kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ omaŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, miifee sane bibioo yɛ ohiɛ.

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: Shi bo lɛ, saji ni eba wɔnɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, onɔ ja, ejaakɛ bo lɛ oye anɔkwa, shi wɔ lɛ wɔfee efɔŋ.

english_verse: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
translation_verse: Wɔmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ hu kɛ wɔnukpai lɛ kɛ wɔsɔfoi lɛ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ yeko omla lɛ nɔ, ni asaŋ amɛboko okitãi kɛ kɔkɔ ni obɔ amɛ lɛ toi.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: Be mli tete ni ohã amɛmaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ma shi ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ kplɛlɛɛ ni ewo fɔ nɔ nii lɛ, amɛsɔ̃mɔɔɔ bo, ni amɛfɔ̃ɔɔ amɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ feemɔ.

english_verse: Now we are slaves in this fruitful land you gave to our ancestors.
translation_verse: Naa, ŋmɛnɛ wɔtsɔmɔ nyɔji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛhã wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ akɛ amɛye enɔ yibii kɛ enɔ nii kpakpai lɛ, naa, wɔtsɔ̃mɔ nyɔji yɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibaanii babaoo lɛ yaa maŋtsɛmɛi ni akɛto wɔnɔ yɛ wɔhe eshai ahewɔ lɛ moŋ aŋɔɔ. Amɛyeɔ wɔ kɛ wɔkooloi anɔ bɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ: ni wɔyɛ haomɔ kpeteŋkple mli.” Maŋbii lɛ kpãŋ kpãŋmɔ ko

english_verse: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
translation_verse: Enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ ahewɔ lɛ, wɔ Israelbii, wɔmiikpãŋ kpãŋmɔ ni mli wa, ni wɔmiiŋma; ni wɔnukpai lɛ kɛ wɔLevibii lɛ kɛ wɔsɔfoi lɛ kɛ amɛgbɛii miiwo shishi amɛkɛmiisɔo naa.

english_verse: The Levites who signed were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, Kadmiel,
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ ji: Yeshua, Azania bi lɛ, Binui ni jɛ Henadad tsɛmɛi awe lɛ, Kadmiel,

translation_verse: Ahia, Hanan, Anan,

english_verse: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah. The Agreement
translation_verse: Maluk, Harim kɛ Baana. Kpãŋmɔ lɛ

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: wɔ kɛ wɔnyɛmimɛi ni ji wɔhiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ efee ekome kɛmiikã kitã. Kɛ wɔku mli lɛ, efee loomɔ ehã wɔ. Wɔmiikã kitã akɛ wɔbaaye Nyɔŋmɔ mla lɛ ni atsɔ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ tsulɔ Mose nine nɔ awo lɛ nɔ. Wɔbaajwɛŋ nɔ ni wɔye Yehowa, wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ, kitãi kɛ emlai kɛ ekpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: We won't let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Wɔkɛ wɔbiyei haŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ gbãlã, ni asaŋ wɔŋɔŋ amɛbiyei wɔhaŋ wɔbihii.

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ kɛ guɔnii loo abele ba hɔ̃ɔmɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ loo gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ eko nɔ lɛ wɔheŋ. Asaŋ daa afi nɔ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, wɔhuŋ wɔŋmɔji lɛ, ni nyɔmɔ fɛɛ nyɔmɔ ni ahiɛ wɔ lɛ wɔkɛbaake.

english_verse: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Asaŋ wɔmiikã kitã akɛ daa afi lɛ, wɔɔhã jwiɛtɛi talenta kome mlijaa etɛ̃ mli ekome yɛ sɔ̃ɔmɔ ni asɔ̃mɔɔ yɛ wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ kɛ nibii krokomɛi hu hewɔ.

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: Nibii nɛɛ ji aboloo ni akɛmaa Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ daa gbi lɛ, kɛ shãa afɔle lɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ anɔ nii lɛ kɛ nyɔji hei anɔ afɔlei lɛ kɛ gbii juji ni ato lɛ anɔ nii lɛ kɛ nii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ kɛ esha afɔlei lɛ ni akɛkpãtã ahãa Israel lɛ. Wɔbaahã kɛhã wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nitsumɔi lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: Wɔ ni ji osɔfoi kɛ Levibii kɛ maŋbii lɛ, wɔfɔ̃fɔ̃ɔ oshiki yɛ laihamɔ hewɔ, koni ato naa akɛba wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ yɛ wɔtsɛmɛi awei lɛ anaa, yɛ bei ni ato lɛ amli daa afi, koni ashã yɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni aŋmã yɛ mla lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: Asaŋ wɔkɛ wɔŋmɔshi klɛŋklɛŋ nibaanii kɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii aaaba Yehowa we lɛ daa afi.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: Tamɔ bɔ ni aŋmã yɛ Mla lɛ mli lɛ, wɔkɛ wɔkromɔbihii kɛ wɔkooloi akromɔbii hu kɛ wɔtsinai akromɔbii kɛ wɔtoi akromɔbii aaaba wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ wɔkɛbahã osɔfoi lɛ ni sɔ̃mɔɔ yɛ jɛi lɛ.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: Wɔkɛ mã ni ana yɛ abele ni akpa klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ mli kɛ tso fɛɛ tso klɛŋklɛŋ yibii, kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ wain kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ mu aaaba abahã osɔfoi lɛ koni akɛwo wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ nitoohe lɛ mli. Wɔkɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibaanii amlijai nyɔŋma mli ekome kome baahã Levibii lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛ ji mɛi ni baŋɔɔ nibaanii amlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome kome lɛ yɛ akrowai ni wɔhuɔ yɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
translation_verse: Kɛ Levibii lɛ miihe nibii amlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ ni ji Aaron bii lɛ afata amɛhe. Levibii lɛ kɛ mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ hu mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome aba wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ ni akɛwo nitoohe lɛ mli.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ esa akɛ Israelbii lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ abele kɛ wain hee kɛ mu lɛ aya ayawo nitoohe lɛ mli he ni he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nibii lɛ kɛ osɔfoi lɛ ni sɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ lalatsɛmɛi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Wɔŋmɛŋ wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ he nitsumɔ lɛ he wɔfɔŋ shi dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ kɛ onukpai lɛ hi Yerusalɛm, ni maŋbii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɔ̃fɔ̃ɔ oshikii koni akɛtao mɔ kome yɛ mɛi nyɔŋma fɛɛ mɛi nyɔŋma ateŋ koni ebahi Yerusalɛm, maŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli, koni mɛi nɛɛhu ni eshwɛ lɛ ayahi maji krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ jie hii fɛɛ ni here amɛhe akɛ amɛaahi Yerusalɛm lɛ yi.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Yuda maji lɛ amli lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ: Israelbii, kɛ osɔfoi kɛ Levibii kɛ Sɔlemɔ we sɔ̃ɔlɔi kɛ Solomon tsuji abii lɛ.

english_verse: From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez,
translation_verse: Perizbii fɛɛ ni hi Yerusalɛm lɛ ayibɔ feɔ mɛi ohai ejwɛ kɛ nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ kpaanyɔ; hii kãkãlɔi sɔŋŋ ji amɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
translation_verse: Salu seshi lɛ mli mɛi komɛi hu ji Gabai kɛ Salai. Benyaminbii ni hi Yerusalɛm lɛ fɛɛ naa shiɔ mɛi ohai nɛɛhu kɛ nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ kpaanyɔ.

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: Yoel, Zikri bi lɛ, ji amɛhiɛnyiɛlɔ; ni Yuda, Hasenua bi lɛ, ji esɛɛmɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi ji Yedaia, Yoiarib bi, kɛ Yakin.

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: Kɛ Seraia, Hilkia bi ni ji Meshulam nabi lɛ. Eseshi lɛ mli mɛi komɛi ji Ahitub, mɔ ni ye Osɔfonukpa yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ.

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ ji Shemaia, Hashub ni ji, Azrikam nabi lɛ. Eseshi lɛ mli mɛi komɛi ji Hashabia Buni.

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: Shabetai kɛ Yozabad ji Levi onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni kwɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: Mɛi komɛi hu ji Matania, Mika bi ni ji Zabdi nabi mɔ ni eji Asaf shwie lɛ. Lɛ enyiɛ lalɔi lɛ ahiɛ kɛlaa kɛdaa Nyɔŋmɔ shi lɛ. Mɔ ko hu ji Bakbukia ni ji Matania sɛɛmɔ kɛ Abda, Shamua bi lɛ ni ji Galai ni ji Yedutun nabi lɛ.

english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Agbonaabulɔi lɛ ji Akub kɛ Talmon kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ. Amɛyibɔ ji mɛi oha kɛ nyɔŋmai kpawo kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Israelbii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ hi Yuda maji lɛ fɛɛ amli, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ nɔ.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni sɔ̃mɔɔ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hi Ofel. Amɛnukpai ji Ziha kɛ Gishpa.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Mɔ ni kwɛ Levibii ni hi Yerusalɛm lɛ nɔ ji Uzi, Bani bi Hashabia bi Matania bi Mika bi lɛ. Ejɛ Asaf bii alalatsɛmɛi ni kwɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ewo kitã yɛ lalatsɛmɛi lɛ ahewɔ, ni ato amɛgbɛnaa afɔ̃ shi kɛhã gbi fɛɛ gbi nɔ nitsumɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Petahia, Meshezabel ni jɛ Zera tsɛmɛi awe lɛ kɛ Yuda weku lɛ mli lɛ bi lɛ ji Persia Maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋaawolɔ yɛ sane fɛɛ sane ni kɔɔ maŋ lɛ he lɛ mli. Maji bibii kɛ ewuji krokomɛi lɛ amli bii

english_verse: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
translation_verse: Yɛ akrowai kɛ humɔhei amlihilɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yudabii lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi hi Kiriat-Arba kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ amli, kɛ Dibon kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ amli, kɛ Yekabzeel kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ amli.

english_verse: Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
translation_verse: kɛ Zanoa kɛ Adullam kɛ amɛhe akrowai lɛ amli. Amɛhi Lakish kɛ ehumɔhei lɛ kɛ Azeka kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ amli.

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Benyaminbii lɛ hi Geba, Mikmash, Aia kɛ Betel kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ ni ji

english_verse: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
translation_verse: Anatot kɛ Nob kɛ Anania amli.

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: kɛ Hadid kɛ Zeboim kɛ Nebalat,

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: kɛ Lod kɛ Ono ni ji Ŋaalɔi Ajɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Levibii akui lɛ ekomɛi ni hi Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yabɔ Benyaminbii lɛ ahe.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Osɔfoi kɛ Levibii ni kɛ Zerubabel, Shealtiel bi lɛ, kɛ Yeshua jɛ nomŋɔɔ mli ba lɛ agbɛii nɛ: Osɔfoi Seraia kɛ Yeremia kɛ Ezra

english_verse: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
translation_verse: kɛ Amaria kɛ Maluk kɛ Hatush,

english_verse: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
translation_verse: Shekania kɛ Rehum kɛ Meremot,

english_verse: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
translation_verse: Ido kɛ Ginetoi kɛ Abia,

english_verse: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
translation_verse: Miyamin kɛ Maadia kɛ Bilga,

english_verse: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
translation_verse: Shemia kɛ Yoiarib kɛ Yedaia

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: Salu kɛ Amok kɛ Hilkia kɛ Yedaia. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ji osɔfoi lɛ kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ onukpai yɛ Yoshua be lɛ mli. Levibii

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ ji Yeshua kɛ Binui kɛ Kadmiel kɛ Sherebia kɛ Yuda kɛ Matania. Matania ji lalɔi akui lɛ atsɛ,

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: ni ekɛ enyɛmimɛi ni ji Levibii: Bakbukia kɛ Uno damɔɔ shi ni mɛnɛɛmɛi miikwɛ mɛnɛɛmɛi ahiɛ, ni amɛhereɔ lala lɛ nɔ lɛ. Osɔfonukpa Yoshua shwiei

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Yeshua fɔ Yoiakim, ni Yoiakim fɔ Eliashib, ni Eliashib fɔ Yoiada.

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: Yoiada fɔ Yonatan, ni Yonatan fɔ Yadua. Osɔfoi awei lɛ ayitsei

english_verse: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Be ni Yehoiakim yeɔ osɔfonukpa lɛ, osɔfoi atsɛmɛi awei lɛ ayitsei nɛ: Seraiatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Meraiatsɛ we; Yeremia lɛ yitso ji Hanania.

english_verse: Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah,
translation_verse: Ezratsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Meshulam, Amariatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Yehohanan.

english_verse: Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah,
translation_verse: Melukitsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Yonatan; Shebaniatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Yosef.

english_verse: Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth,
translation_verse: Harimtsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Adna; Meraiottsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Helkai.

english_verse: Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon,
translation_verse: Idotsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Zakaria; Ginetontsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Meshulam.

english_verse: Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah,
translation_verse: Bilgatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Shamuatsɛ we; Shemaia lɛ yitso ji Yehonatan.

english_verse: Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah,
translation_verse: Yoairibtsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Matenai; Yedaiatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Uzi.

english_verse: Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok,
translation_verse: Salaitsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Kalai; Amoktsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Eber.

english_verse: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
translation_verse: Hilkiatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Hashabia; Yedaiatsɛ we lɛ yitso ji Netanel. Aŋmã osɔfoi awei kɛ Levibii awei ayitsei agbɛii

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Osɔfonukpai ni ji Eliashib kɛ Yoiada kɛ Yohanan kɛ Yadua yinɔ lɛ, aŋmã Levibii lɛ atsɛmɛi awei lɛ ayitsei lɛ kɛ osɔfoi lɛ agbɛii. Agbe gbɛiŋmaa nɛɛ naa yɛ Dario, Persianyo lɛ maŋtsɛyeli be lɛ mli.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Shi Levibii ni ji tsɛmɛi awei lɛ amɛyitsei lɛ, aŋmã amɛgbɛii yɛ wolo ni Yinɔi Anɔ Saji yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Aŋmã Levibii awei lɛ ayitsei lɛ agbɛii nɛɛ kɛyashi Yohanan, Eliashib nabi lɛ, yinɔ. Aja Sɔlemɔtsu lɛ mli nitsumɔi lɛ

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ atsɛmɛi awei lɛ ayitsei ni ji Hashibia kɛ Sherebia kɛ Yeshua, Kadmiel bi lɛ, to gbɛjianɔ. Afee kui enyɔ; ku kome miijie Nyɔŋmɔ yi, ni amɛmiida lɛ shi; belɛ ku ni ji enyɔ ni yɔɔ amɛhiɛ lɛ miihere nɔ. Amɛ jie Nyɔŋmɔ yi, ni amɛda lɛ shi tamɔ bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ David ewo kitã lɛ.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Matania kɛ Bakbukia kɛ Obadia kɛ Meshulam kɛ Talmon kɛ Akub ji agbonaakwɛlɔi. Amɛ amɛbuɔ agboi lɛ anaa nitoohei lɛ ahe.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi hi shi yɛ Yoakim, Yozadak bi Yeshua bi lɛ, kɛ Amralo Nehemia kɛ Osɔfo Ezra ni ji woloŋmalɔ lɛ yinɔ. Nehemia fee Yerusalɛm Gbogbo lɛ Krɔŋkrɔŋ

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Be ni abaajɔɔ Yerusalɛm gbogbo lɛ nɔ afee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ayatao Levibii yɛ hei ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ, ni akɛ amɛ ba Yerusalɛm koni amɛbaye hetsuumɔ gbijurɔ lɛ kɛ nyamɔ kɛ shidaa lalai kɛ ŋoŋoi kɛ kpãa saŋkui.

english_verse: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
translation_verse: Mɛi komɛi hu jɛ Bet-Gilgal kɛ Geba koi asɛɛ kɛ Azmavet, ejaakɛ lalɔi nɛɛ etotoo akrowai kɛbɔle Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ tsuu amɛhe. Asaŋ amɛtsuu maŋ lɛ kɛ agboi lɛ kɛ gbogbo lɛ hu ahe.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mihã Yuda onukpai lɛ kwɔ kɛba gbogbo lɛ nɔ. Mifee lalɔi akui kpelekplei enyɔ koni amɛto kɛnyiɛ gbogbo lɛ nɔ kɛ shidaa lalai. Ku kome tsɔ̃ ninejurɔgbɛ yɛ gbogbo lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya Tumo Agbo lɛ naa gbɛ.

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: Hoshaia kɛ Yuda onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi fã nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
translation_verse: Mɛi ni fata he ji Azaria kɛ Ezra kɛ Meshulam kɛ

english_verse: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Yuda kɛ Benyamin kɛ Shemaia kɛ Yeremia.

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: Ewekumɛi ji Shemaia kɛ Azarel Malalai kɛ Gilalai kɛ Maai kɛ Netanel kɛ Yuda kɛ Hanani. Amɛ hu amɛnyiɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛhiɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɔmɔ David nibii ni akɛtswaa lalai aloo akɛkpãa lalai lɛ. Ezra, woloŋmalɔ kpanaa lɛ nyiɛ ku nɛɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Amɛtsɔ̃ Nubu Agbo lɛ he; ni amɛtee amɛhiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyakwɔ atrakpoi ni akwɔɔ kɛyaa David maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkwɔ yɛ kwɔɔhe lɛ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ David we lɛ he kɛtee Nu Agbo lɛ he yɛ bokãgbɛ.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Lalɔi ni daa Nyɔŋmɔ shi lɛ aku ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ abɛkugbɛ. Mi kɛ maŋ lɛ fã nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ yɛ gbogbo lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ Flɔɔnɔi Amɔ̃ɔ lɛ yiteŋ aahu kɛyashi Gbogbo Lɛkɛtɛɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
translation_verse: Wɔtse mli kɛtsɔ̃ Efraim Agbo lɛ kɛ Agbo Momo lɛ kɛ Loi Agbo lɛ he. Wɔyawa wɔdamɔ shi yɛ Bulɔi Agbo lɛ naa.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, lalɔi akui enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni daa Nyɔŋmɔ shi lɛ kɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ ateŋ mɛi fã ni fata mihe lɛ yashɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ.

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi ni fata he ji Eliakim kɛ Maaseia kɛ Miniamin kɛ Mikaia kɛ Elioenai kɛ Zakaria kɛ Hanania ni amɛhiɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛi.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ ji Maaseia kɛ Shemaia kɛ Eleazar kɛ Uzi kɛ Yohanan kɛ Malia kɛ Elam kɛ Ezer. Yezrahia kɛ elalɔi aku lɛ la waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ amɛshã shãa afɔlei babaoo, ni amɛnyã, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ehã amɛmii eshɛ amɛhe waa naakpa. Yei kɛ gbekɛbii lɛ hu nyãnyãa waa bɔ ni anu nyamɔ ni anyãa yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ he yɛ shɔŋŋ tete. Ato gbɛjianɔ ahã jamɔ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afamɔ hii komɛi ato nitoohei lɛ anɔ: nitoohei nɛɛ ji hei ni akɛ nɔwomɔ afɔlei kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii afɔlei lɛ kɛ nibii amlijai nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ toɔ. Afamɔ hii nɛɛ koni amɛbua ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ maji lɛ ahe lɛ amli nii lɛ amlijai nyɔŋma ni mla lɛ to lɛ naa amɛwo nitoohei lɛ amli amɛhã osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ. Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii na osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii ni damɔɔ shi sɔmɔɔ lɛ ahe miishɛɛ;

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ ye hetsuumɔ mlai lɛ kɛ gbɛnai krokomɛi ni amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ to lɛ anɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ lalɔi lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ tsu amɛgbɛnaanii tamɔ bɔ ni Maŋtsɛ David kɛ ebi Solomon wo kitã ni afee lɛ.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Maŋtsɛ David kɛ Lalatsɛ Asaf yinɔ beebe ato lalɔi lɛ ahiɛnyiɛlɔ; ni amɛla yijiemɔ kɛ shidaa lalai amɛhã Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Zerubabel yinɔ kɛ Nehemia yinɔ lɛ, Israelbii fɛɛ hãa nikeenii daa gbi, ni akɛkwɛɔ lalɔi lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ. Maŋ lɛ jieɔ Levibii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ amɛfɔ̃ɔ shi; ni Levibii lɛ hu jieɔ nɔ ni ji Aaronbii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ amɛfɔ̃ɔ shi amɛhãa amɛ.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ be ni akaneɔ Mose Mla lɛ yɛ maŋbii lɛ atoiŋ lɛ, ana ni aŋmã yɛ mli akɛ Amonnyo loo Moabnyo akaba Nyɔŋmɔ maŋbii lɛ ahenaabuamɔ lɛ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ;

english_verse: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ amɛkɛ aboloo kɛ nu ebakpeee Israelbii lɛ, shi moŋ amɛyabɔ Bileam apaa akɛ ebalomɔ amɛ; shi wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ hã loomɔ lɛ moŋ tsɔ̃ jɔɔmɔ.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Be ni Israelbii lɛ nu mla lɛ, amɛ jie mɛi fɛɛ ni ji futufutu gbɔmɛi lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ. Nehemia tsake nibii komɛi

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Shi dani abaafee enɛ lɛ, osɔfoi Eliashib ni akɛ lɛ eto nitoohei ni yɔɔ wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ anɔ lɛ, kɛ Tobia efee ekome kɛto gbɛjianɔ.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: Eliashib saa tsu kpeteŋkple ko ehã Tobia ni ehi mli. Tsu nɛɛ, sa lɛ akɛ nibii komɛi toɔ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ji niyenii afɔlei kɛ krɔbɔo kɛ Sɔlemɔ we tsɛnsii kɛ ŋmɔshinii ni ji abele kɛ wain kɛ mu mlijai nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ, ni awo he kitã akɛ akɛhã Levibii lɛ kɛ Sɔlemɔ we lalɔi lɛ kɛ agbonaakwɛlɔi lɛ. Nɔ ni fata nibii ni akɛtoɔ tsu nɛɛ mli lɛ he ji afɔlei ni akɛhãa osɔfoi lɛ.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Shi nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mibɛ Yerusalɛm, ejaakɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ Artashasta yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mitee eŋɔɔ. Be kplaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, mibi maŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛ,

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: ni miku misɛɛ kɛba Yerusalɛm. Mibana sane gbonyo ni Eliashib eye akɛ esaa tsu ehã Tobia yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ kpoi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Mimli wo la naakpa, ni mijie Tobia nibii fɛɛ yɛ tsu lɛ mli mishwie.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mifã akɛ asha nitoohei lɛ amli koni akɛtsuu amɛmli: ni mihã akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ mli nibii lɛ kɛ niyenii afɔlei lɛ kɛ krɔbɔo lɛ ku sɛɛ akɛbato jɛi ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: Minu hu akɛ Levibii lɛ kɛ Sɔlemɔ we lalɔi lɛ ni amɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ amɛgbɛnaa nitsumɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ejo foi etee eŋmɔ mli, ejaakɛ ahãaa amɛ amɛgbɛnaa niyenii lɛ.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mihiɛ dɔ wo hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ, ni mibi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ ajo foi ashi Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ?” Mibua Levibii lɛ kɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli lalɔi lɛ anaa kɛba, ni mikɛ amɛ yato amɛgbɛhe.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yuda maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ bɔ̃i abele kɛ wain kɛ mu mlijai nyɔŋma mli ekomekome lɛ kɛ nitoohei lɛ amli woo ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Mito nitoohe lɛ nɔkwɛlɔi: amɛ ji Osɔfoi Shelemia kɛ Zadok, woloŋmalɔ lɛ, kɛ Pedaia ni jɛ Levibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛsɛɛmɔ ji Hanan, Matania bi Zakur bi lɛ. Mito gbɔmɛi nɛɛ, ejaakɛ abuɔ amɛ anɔkwafoi. Amɛnitsumɔ ji akɛ amɛja nii lɛ amɛhã amɛnyɛmimɛi nitsulɔi lɛ.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: MiNyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ mi yɛ enɛ hewɔ, ni ohiɛ akakpa nitsumɔi kpakpai ni mitsu yɛ owe lɛ kɛ emli sɔ̃ɔmɔ ahe lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli mina akɛ mɛi ŋaa wainyibii yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ yɛ Yuda. Mina akɛ akɛ abele kɛ wain kɛ wainyibii kɛ agbãmi jatsui kɛ jatsui srɔtoi fɛɛ tereɔ tejii kɛbaa Yerusalɛm yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ. Migbɛ miwo amɛ yɛ gbi nɔ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Tirobii komɛi ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ kɛ loo kɛ guɔnii srɔtoi fɛɛ baa amɛbahɔ̃ɔ amɛhãa Yudabii lɛ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ tete yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: Mikã Yuda abladei lɛ ahiɛ, ni mikɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ sane fɔŋ nyɛyeɔ ni nyɛkɛbuleɔ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Ani jeee nɛkɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fee ni wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ hã efɔŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ ba wɔ kɛ maŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛkɛ bulemɔ ni nyɛbuleɔ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ miitsɛ mlifu kɛba Israel nɔ nyɛfata he.”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, dani aaaje hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ shishi lɛ, kɛji hiɛ bɔ̃i tuutuu feemɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm agboi lɛ amli pɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ mifãa ni aŋamɔ agboi lɛ, ni miwoɔ kitã akɛ akagbele, ja hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ eho dã. Asaŋ mifamɔ mitsuji lɛ ekomɛi mito agboi lɛ anaa koni akɛ jatsu ko akaba maŋ lɛ mli yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Jarayelɔi lɛ kɛ guɔyelɔi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii srɔtoi fɛɛ lɛ bato agboi lɛ asɛɛ shi kome loo shii enyɔ.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Mibɔ amɛ kɔkɔ ni mikɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛbatoɔ gbogbo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ nyɛfee nakai ekoŋŋ lɛ, mibamɔmɔ nyɛ.” Kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛbaaa hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mifã Levibii lɛ akɛ amɛtsuu amɛhe koni amɛba amɛbabu agboi lɛ anaa, bɔ ni afee ni afee hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ. MiNyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ mi yɛ enɛ hu hewɔ koni okɛ mihe eshai afa mi yɛ osuɔmɔ ni fa lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Nakai bei lɛ amli lɛ mina akɛ Yudafoi pii eŋɔ Ashdodyei kɛ Amonyei kɛ Moabyei.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Amɛbii lɛ wieɔ Ashdod wiemɔ lɛ loo wiemɔ kroko fã kɛ fã, ni amɛnyɛɛɛ Yudafoi awiemɔ lɛ amɛwie.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Mihiɛ dɔ wo amɛ, ni milomɔ amɛ. Miyi amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi, ni mifamɔ amɛyiteŋ tsɔi. Mihã amɛkã Nyɔŋmɔ kitã akɛ amɛkɛ amɛbiyei lɛ haŋ maŋsɛɛbii abihii gbãlã, ni amɛŋɔŋ maŋsɛɛbii abiyei amɛhaŋ amɛbihii lɛ. Asaŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu amɛkɛ maŋsɛɛbii ehiŋ shi.

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Aso wɔɔkɔ nyɛnane ni wɔfee nɛkɛ efɔŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ? Aso wɔɔŋɔ maŋsɛɛ yei ni wɔje wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Osɔfonukpa Eliashib bi ji Yoiada. Yoiada bii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome yaŋɔ Sanbalat Horonnyo lɛ biyoo, ni ekɛ Sanbalat fee shaanuu. No hewɔ lɛ, mishwie Yoiada bi lɛ yɛ mihe.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: MiNyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi nɛɛ wo osɔfoyeli he muji ni amɛfite kpãŋmɔ ni okɛ osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ ekpãŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsɔ̃ mijie maŋ lɛ kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni buleɔ mɔ mli. Mito osɔfoi lɛ kɛ Levibii lɛ asɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ gbɛjianɔ, bɔ ni afee ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ale enitsumɔ ni akɛhã lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: Ni mito gbɛjianɔ mihã be ni akɛ afɔleshãa lai kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yelitso yibii aba. MiNyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ mi ni ahi ahã mi.

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Susa maŋ lɛ mli ji he ni emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ yɔɔ, ni jɛi ejɛɔ ni eyeɔ maji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: Emaŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh ŋmɛ okplɔ̃ ehã elumɛi kɛ etsuji fɛɛ yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli. Mɛi okplɔ̃ ni eŋmɛ lɛ ji Persia kɛ Media shikpɔji lɛ anɔ tatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ amralofoi lɛ.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ nibii lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ agbe naa lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh tsɛ mɛi wujiwuji kɛ mɛi bibii hu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Susa maŋ lɛ mli nakai beiaŋ lɛ okplɔ̃, gbii kpawo yɛ trom ko ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ he lɛ kpo teŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni awula kpo teŋ lɛ mli ahã nɛ. Akɛ tɛi eŋɔlii kɛ tɛi yɛji kɛ tɛi bluu kɛ tɛi diji eka kpo lɛ nɔ; ni akɛ tɛi yɛji akulashiŋi emamɔ tɛi ni aka lɛ anɔ. Jwiɛtɛi gai yɛ akulashiŋi nɛɛ ahe. Akɛ kpãa yɛŋ fɛɛfɛo kɛ kpãa afaseo emɔmɔ mamai yɛji fɛɛfɛji kɛ mamai bluu lɛ hu anaa; kɛkɛ ni akɛŋmɔlɔ jwiɛtɛi akulashiŋi lɛ ahe gai lɛ, ni ehã mamai lɛ tsotsoro shi. Mlikpãmɔ saatsei pɛmpɛbii ni akɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi fee mamɔ kpo teŋ lɛ mli hei komɛi.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Gbi lɛ awo dãa yɛ shika kpuji srɔtoisrɔtoi amli. Maŋtsɛ lɛ hã awo mɛi ni ekpee lɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edãa ni enuɔ lɛ eko babaoo, bɔ ni ewo ehiɛ nyam akɛ maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ wo ewe lɛ mli tsuji lɛ mla akɛ ahã mɔ fɛɛ mɔ dãa bɔ ni mɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu; mɔ ni enuuu lɛ akɛkafi enɔ; ni mɔ ni baanu lɛ akakama lɛ.

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Maŋnyɛ Vashti ŋmɛ yei sɔŋŋ hu okplɔ̃ yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ be ni dãa lɛ ehã maŋtsɛ lɛ mli efili lɛ lɛ, etsɛ epiafoi kpawo ni sɔmɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ. Amɛ ji Mehuman kɛ Bizta kɛ Harbona kɛ Bitha kɛ Abagta kɛ Zeter kɛ Karkas.

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni efã amɛ akɛ amɛya koni amɛyaŋɔ Maŋnyɛ Vashti kɛba ehiɛ; ebu emaŋnyɛ fai lɛ kɛba. Anɔkwa emaŋnyɛ lɛ he yɛ fɛo jogbaŋŋ, ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh miitao akɛ egbɔi lɛ ana emaŋnyɛ lɛ he fɛo lɛ.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Shi Maŋnyɛ Vashti kwa, ni eyaaa tsɛmɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ tsu piafoi lɛ akɛ abatsɛ lɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ mli fu naakpa ni emli wo la.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: Mɛi adɛŋ ŋaawoo ni efɔɔ bimɔ ji Karshena kɛ Shetar kɛ Admata kɛ Tarshish kɛ Meres kɛ Marsena kɛ Memukan ni ji Persia kɛ Media lumɛi ni hiɛ gbɛnai wujiwuji yɛ emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ ŋaawolɔi nɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛni, yɛ mla lɛ naa, esa akɛ afeɔ Maŋnyɛ Vashti akɛni mi, Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh, mitsu piafoi kɛ wiemɔ kɛtee eŋɔɔ, ni ekwa, ni eyeee wiemɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Memukan kɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ elumɛi lɛ akɛ, “Jeee Maŋtsɛ kɛkɛ nɔ Maŋnyɛ Vashti etɔ̃ lɛ, shi moŋ etɔ̃ lumɛi fɛɛ kɛ majimaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh shishi shikpɔji fɛɛ anɔ lɛ mli bii lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛji ayagba akɛ, ‘Naa, Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh fã akɛ ayatsɛ Maŋnyɛ Vashti abahã lɛ lɛ, maŋnyɛ lɛ baaa lɛ,’ sane lɛ baagbɛ eshwã yei fɛɛ ateŋ, ni ebaahã yei awumɛi ahe guɔ agbo yɛ amɛŋamɛi ahiɛ.

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Persia kɛ Media lumɛi lɛ aŋamɛi ni baanu nɔ ni maŋnyɛ lɛ efee lɛ baabɔ amɛwumɛi amaniɛ. Wumɛi ahe guɔ baagbo yɛ ŋamɛi ahiɛ, ni enɛ kɛ mlifu babaoo baaba.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji Maŋtsɛ miisumɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ awo akpɔ, ni aŋma ashi Persia kɛ Media mlai lɛ anɔ, akɛ Maŋnyɛ Vashti akana Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh hiɛ dɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, Nii, okɛ emaŋnyɛyeli lɛ ahã yoo kroko ni fe lɛ.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Kɛji ashiɛ Maŋtsɛ dɛŋ akpɔ nɛɛ yɛ omaŋtsɛyeli shikpɔŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ heihei fɛɛ lɛ, ebaahã yeigbãyei fɛɛ ahiɛ asɔ amɛwumɛi, mɛi wuji kɛ mɛi bibii fɛɛ.”

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh tsu kɛ woji kɛtee eshikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Aŋma shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ wolo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ niŋmaa kɛ ewiemɔ mli akɛ, “Nuu fɛɛ nuu lɛ, lɛ eye ewe nɔ; ni nɔ ni lɛ ebaakɛɛ lɛ, no afee naagbee.”

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Saji nɛɛ asɛɛ, be mli ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh mlila lɛ naa eba shi tete po lɛ, kɛfee lɛ ekaiɔ Vashti kɛ nɔ ni efee lɛ, kɛ nɔ hu ni afee lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋaawolɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ko wo maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋaa ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, hã atao oblayei froi ni ahe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko ahã bo.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ baanyɛ eto tsuji yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni amɛbua oblayei froi ni ahe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ fɛɛ anaa kɛba yei awe lɛ mli yɛ Susa, ni ji maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ mli. Atu oblayei nɛɛ awo Hegai ni ji maŋtsɛ piafonyo ni kwɛɔ yei asaji anɔ lɛ dɛŋ koni ekwɛ ni ahiɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Ni oblayoo ni baasa maŋtsɛ hiɛ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ aŋɔ lɛ akɛ maŋnyɛ ato Vashti najiaŋ.” Maŋtsɛ lɛ na akɛ ŋaawoo lɛ hi, ni no hewɔ lɛ, eye nɔ.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Nakai be mli lɛ Yudanyo ko yɛ Susa, maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Mɔdekai. Benyaminnyo Yair bi ji lɛ, ni efeɔ Shimei nabi kɛ Kish nanakansowa.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Eshi nomii ni fata Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yekonia he lɛ anɔ, be ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar yaŋɔ Yekonia nom kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm kɛba Babilon lɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Be ni Mɔdekai baa lɛ ekɛ etsɛkwɛ̃ ko biyoo ko ba, ejaakɛ awusa ni. Oblayoo nɛɛ gbɛi ji Ester, shi Hebri mli lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ Hadasa. Oblayoo lɛ he yɛ fɛo, ni ehiɛŋtso yɛ akɔnɔ pam. Be ni enyɛ kɛ etsɛ fɛɛ gboi lɛ, Mɔdekai ŋɔ lɛ ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebiyoo.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Be ni ashiɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh kitã kɛ akpɔ lɛ, ni abua oblayei pii anaa kɛtee Susa mɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Ester fata he eko kɛtee, ni akɛ amɛ yahã Hegai yei akwɛlɔ lɛ.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Ester hiɛ ba nyam yɛ Hegai hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, etsɛɛɛ kwraa kɛkɛ ni Hegai kɛ mui kɛ niyenii kpakpai kuma Ester. Fee sɛɛ lɛ Hegai jie Ester ni ekɛ lɛ yato yei awe lɛ mli he ko ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ, ni eje gbɛ hu ehala oblayei kpawo yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli ablawai lɛ ateŋ, ni ekɛ amɛ to Ester he koni amɛsɔmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Ŋaa ni Mɔdekai wo Ester hewɔ lɛ, Ester ni egbaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko emaŋ kɛ eweku mli ni ejɛ.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Daa gbi lɛ Mɔdekai yasharaa shi yɛ yei awe lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ bɔ ni afee ni ele bɔ ni Ester yɔɔ, kɛ bɔ ni eyaa nɔ ehãa.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Be ni ayeɔ akɛsaa oblayoo gbɔmɔtso ji nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ. Oblayoo lɛ kɛ mire mu gbɔleɔ egbɔmɔtso nyɔji ekpaa; ni ekɛ nyɔji ekpaa kroko hu kpaa krɔbɔo kɛ tsofakɛŋmai. Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, atoɔ naa ni aŋɔɔ oblayoo fɛɛ oblayoo akɛyahãa Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oblayoo lɛ biɔ lɛ ahãa lɛ yɛ yei awe lɛ mli ni ekɛ saa ehe kɛyaa maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Eyaa maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ gbɛkɛ, ni enɔ leebi lɛ akpalaa lɛ kɛyaa yei awe kroko mli, ni akɛ lɛ yawoɔ Shaashgaz, maŋtsɛ piafonyo ni kwɛɔ maŋtsɛ hemɛi lɛ, dɛŋ. Oblayoo lɛ eyaaa maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ bɛja maŋtsɛ lɛ ena ehe tsui ni etsu kɛ yoo lɛ gbɛi akɛ atsɛ lɛ ahã lɛ.

english_verse: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni aŋɔ Ester ayahã Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh yɛ emaŋtsɛyeli we lɛ mli. Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji kpawo lɛ mli Tebet nyɔŋ lɛ ni ji nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ akɛ Ester yahã lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ sumɔ Ester fe oblayei krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ. Ester hiɛ ba nyam jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ fe yei fɛɛ; ni ena ehe miishɛɛ fe oblayei lɛ fɛɛ ni no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ maŋnyɛyeli akekre lɛ fi Ester yitso kɛkɛ ni ewo lɛ maŋnyɛ yɛ Vashti najiaŋ.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh tsɛ okplɔ̃ kpeteŋkple ekɛwo Ester hiɛ nyam; ni ekpee eshishi lumɛi kɛ etsuji fɛɛ kɛba okplɔ̃ lɛ shishi. Ehã eshishi shikpɔji lɛ ye gbi ko akɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi; ni ekekee mɛi nii babaoo bɔ ni sa maŋtsɛ. Mɔdekai here Maŋtsɛ lɛ yiwala

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Be ko hu be ni abua oblayei lɛ anaa ekoŋŋ nɔ ni ji shii enyɔ nɔ ahã maŋtsɛ lɛ, no mli lɛ Mɔdekai shi maŋtsɛ koishi onukpai lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli fɛɛ lɛ Ester egbako mɔ ko kwraa akɛ Yudayoo ji lɛ, taakɛ bɔ ni Mɔdekai ewo lɛ kitã lɛ. Ejaakɛ Ester miiye Mɔdekai gbee nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ tamɔ be mli ni Mɔdekai kwɛɔ enɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Be mli ni Mɔdekai tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ koishi lɛ, Bigtan kɛ Teresh, maŋtsɛ piafoi enyɔ komɛi ni shi mɛi ni buɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli shinai anaa lɛ ahe lɛ, na maŋtsɛ lɛ he mlifu; ni amɛto amɛyiŋ akɛ amɛbaagbe Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Be ni Mɔdekai na nu yiŋtoo nɛɛ lɛ, eyakɛɛ Maŋnyɛ Ester; ni Ester hu bɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ amaniɛ lɛ ni Mɔdekai ebabɔ lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Be ni atao sane lɛ mli lɛ, ebakã shi faŋŋ akɛ eyɛ mli anɔkwale. No hewɔ lɛ, asɛŋ Bigtan kɛ Teresh yɛ tso nɔ, ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh fã, ni aŋma sane nɛɛ awo Yinɔ Asaji wolo lɛ mli yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Saji nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh wo nuu ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Haman lɛ maŋsɔ̃ɔlɔ nukpa ni fe fɛɛ. Haman nɛɛ tsɛ gbɛi ji Hamedata, ni ejɛ Agag seshi mli.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh fã akɛ etsuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ esɔ̃ɔmɔ mli lɛ akula shi ni amɛkoto Haman be fɛɛ be. Tsuji lɛ fɛɛ fee nakai, ja Mɔdekai pɛ ni kotooo Haman.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh tsuji krokomɛi lɛ bi Mɔdekai akɛ, “Mɛɛba otɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ kitã lɛ?”

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Be ni tsuji lɛ kɛ Mɔdekai ewie gbii abɔ, shi fɛɛ lɛ Mɔdekai ekpɛlɛɛɛ akɛ eeekoto Haman lɛ, Mɔdekai kɛɛ tsuji lɛ akɛ Yudanyo ji lɛ ni no hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ ekoto Haman. Tsuji lɛ yabɔ Haman amaniɛ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji Haman baakpɛlɛ nɔ ehã Mɔdekai lo.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Ni be ni Haman na akɛ Mɔdekai kulãaa shi haaa lɛ, ni ekotooo lɛ lɛ, Haman mli fu naakpa.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Akɛni akɛɛ Haman akɛ Yudanyo ji Mɔdekai hu hewɔ lɛ, Haman to eyiŋ akɛ ekpãtãŋ Mɔdekai kome kɛkɛ hiɛ, shi moŋ ekɛ Mɔdekai he nu baaju Yudafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh maŋtsɛyeli shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ lɛ ahe.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Nisan lɛ nɔ lɛ, Haman hã abɔ̃i oshiki, ni ji Pur, fɔ̃ɔ daa gbi kɛtao gbi ni hi hã eyiŋtoo lɛ he nitsumɔ. Afɔ̃ oshiki nɛɛ aahu kɛyashi nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ, ni ji Adar nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Haman kɛɛ maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh akɛ, “Nii, Gbɔmɛi komɛi egbɛ eshwã omaŋtsɛyeli shikpɔji kɛ kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ, ni amɛ lɛ esoro amɛkusum kwraa yɛ maŋbii krokomɛi lɛ anɔ he, ni amɛyeee maŋtsɛ mlai lɛ anɔ hu. Enɛ lɛ esaaa akɛ Nii aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ nakai.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Kɛji esa Maŋtsɛ hiɛ lɛ, no lɛ Nii awo akpɔ akɛ agbe amɛ. Kɛji maŋtsɛ kpɛlɛ̃ nɔ nakai lɛ, no lɛ miiwo shi akɛ mahã jwiɛtɛi ni tsiimɔ ji talentai akpei nyɔŋma koni akɛwo maŋ fotro lɛ mli koni akɛtsu maŋ lɛ he nii.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ jie ewolonaasɔomɔ waoga ni ewo lɛ yɛ enine, ni ekɛhã Hamedata bi Haman ni ji Yudafoi lɛ ahenyɛlɔ lɛ.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, afi lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Haman kpee maŋtsɛ lɛ woloŋmalɔi lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛnaa bakpe shi. Amɛŋma wolo lɛ bɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni Haman fã amɛ akɛ amɛŋma lɛ koni akɛyahã amraloi lɛ kɛ lumɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ maŋ fɛɛ maŋ mli onukpa fɛɛ onukpa hu. Shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋma ewolo lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniŋmãa mli, ni maŋ fɛɛ maŋ lɛ aŋma ewolo lɛ yɛ ewiemɔ mli. Aŋmala woji lɛ yɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh gbɛi mli, ni akɛ ewolonaasɔomɔ waoga lɛ sɔo naa.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni akɛ woji lɛ tsu bɔfoi kɛtee maŋtsɛ lɛ shishi shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Wiemɔ ni yɔɔ woji lɛ amli ji akɛ gbi kome jenamɔ, ni ji nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ, ni ji Adar nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ, gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, aplenee Yudafoi ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he, oblahii jio, hiimeji jio, gbekɛbii jio, yei, jio agbe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni akɛbule amɛshishi ni asaŋ aha nibii ni amɛyɔɔ.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Bɔfoi lɛ kɛ woji lɛ shi kɛ foi yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ fãmɔ naa kɛtee shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Ashiɛ akpɔ lɛ yɛ Susa ni ji maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ mli hu. Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh kɛ Haman ho tara shi ni amɛnu dãa, be mli ni akpɔ lɛ ehã Susa maŋ lɛ fɛɛ ejijaa lɛ.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Be ni Mɔdekai na le nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ, ekɛ awerɛho gbala ehe atadei lɛ, ni ekɔ kpekpe ebu; asaŋ eloo lamlu ewo eyiteŋ. Kɛkɛ ni eje kpo kɛbote maŋ lɛ mli kɛ yaafo gegeege.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Etee eyawa maŋtsɛ we lɛ agbo lɛ naa; ejaakɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ hegbɛ akɛ ebuɔ kpekpe kɛboteɔ maŋtsɛ agbo lɛ mli.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kitã kɛ akpɔ lɛ yashɛ lɛ, ŋkɔmɔyeli kpeteŋkple bagbee shi yɛ jɛi Yudafoi lɛ ateŋ. Amɛhi ŋmãa, amɛye ŋkɔmɔ, amɛwo yara amɛfo, ni mɛi babaoo kɔlɔ kpekpe amɛbu, ni amɛho amɛkamɔ lamlu mli.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Be ni Ester ablawai lɛ kɛ epiafoi lɛ bagba lɛ nɔ ni Mɔdekai feɔ lɛ, Ester ye jaramɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Etsu ni akɛ atadei tee yahã Mɔdekai koni ekɛtsake kpekpe lɛ yɛ ehe; shi Mɔdekai heee atadei lɛ.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ester tsɛ Hatak, maŋtsɛ lɛ piafoi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ko ni ato akɛ esɔmɔ lɛ maŋnyɛ lɛ, ni etsu lɛ Mɔdekai ŋɔɔ koni eyatao nɔ sane ni eba lɛ kɛ nɔ ni kɛba hu.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatak tee Mɔdekai ŋɔɔ yɛ blohu ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛ agbo lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Mɔdekai gba lɛ sane ni eba enɔ lɛ, ni etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ shika hu ni Haman ewo shi akɛ ebaana ewo maŋ fotro lɛ mli kɛji ana aplenee Yudafoi lɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Ekɛ mla ni awo yɛ Susa akɛ akpãtã Yudafoi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ nɔ wolo hã Hatak akɛ ekɛyatsɔ̃ɔ Ester. Asaŋ ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ eya maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni eyakpa lɛ fai, ni ewie he ehã emaŋbii Yudafoi lɛ.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Hatak tee ni eyabɔ Ester nɔ ni Mɔdekai kɛɛ lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
