translation_verse: “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ, nuu ni jio, yoo ni jio, ni eeeya eyanina maŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ ewe lɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ trukaa, be mli ni maŋtsɛ lɛ tsuko kɛ mɔ lɛ gbɛi tuuŋtu akɛ atsɛ mɔ lɛ ahã lɛ lɛ, mla ni kã shi ji akɛ abaagbe mɔ lɛ. Mla ni kã shi ni ale kɛjɛ maŋtsɛ tsuji anɔ aahu kɛyashi maŋbii fɛɛ anɔ ji enɛ. Shi kɛji maŋtsɛ lɛ wo eshika tsi lɛ nɔ etsɔ̃ɔ mɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ no dani mɔ lɛ yi naa wala. Kɛjɛ gbii nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ nɛ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ tsuko koni atsɛ mi ahã lɛ.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Be ni wiemɔ nɛɛ shɛ Mɔdekai dɛŋ lɛ,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Mɔdekai hu tsu kɛ hetoo nɛɛ koni akɛyahã Ester, “Kaasusu akɛ ni oyɔɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ bo lɛ ohe baaje Yudafoi fɛɛ asane nɛɛ mli.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛji omua onaa kɛta shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli tete, yelikɛbuamɔ baajɛ he ko kɛ̃ aba ahã Yudafoi, ni abaahere amɛyiwala, shi bo kɛ otsɛ we lɛ hiɛ aaakpãtã. Namɔ aaale akɛ eko lɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ hewɔ ni ahã obatsɔ̃ maŋnyɛ nɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ester kɛ hetoo nɛɛ tsu akɛyahã Mɔdekai.

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Yaa ni oyabua Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Susa maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ anaa kɛkpe; ni nyɛhia ŋmãa, ni nyɛsɔlea nyɛhãa mi. Nyɛkayea nii, ni nyɛkanua nu hu shwaneshwane kɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ gbii etɛ̃. Mi hu mi kɛ miblayei lɛ baahi ŋmãa nakai nɔŋŋ. Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ mibaya mayana maŋtsɛ lɛ, tsɛbelɛ mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ nakai. Kɛji miyagbo yɛ no hewɔ po jiŋŋ efeee nɔ ko.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mɔdekai yiŋ etee, ni eyafee bɔ ni Ester kɛɛ eyafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Be ni Ester ehi ŋmãa gbii etɛ̃ lɛ ekɔlɔ emaŋnyɛ atadei lɛ ewo, kɛkɛ ni ebote maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli, ni etee eyadamɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ asa lɛ ŋlɛnɔ. Nakai be mli lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ asa lɛ nɔ. Eta emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ, ni ehiɛ miikwɛ asa lɛ shinaa lɛ naagbɛ.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ na Maŋnyɛ Ester damɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ena maŋnyɛ lɛ he tsuijurɔ, kɛkɛ ni ekpã enine mli ni ekɛ shika tsi ni ehiɛ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ Ester hiɛ. Ester tsi ebɛŋkɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ enine ta tsi lɛ he.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋnyɛ Ester, mɛni sane ni, mɛni otaoɔ? Nɔ ni ji lɛ bi, ni abaafee ahã bo aahu, kɛji mimaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mlijaa ni po.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ester to he akɛ, “Kɛji Maŋtsɛ baasumɔ lɛ, no lɛ Nii kɛ Haman aba okplɔ̃ ko ni miiŋmɛ mahã Nii lɛ he ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã akɛ atsɛ Haman kɛba mramra koni amɛya Ester okplɔ̃ ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ lɛ he amɛyaye nii. Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Haman tee okplɔ̃ ni Maŋnyɛ Ester ŋmɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Be mli ni anuɔ wain lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ bi Ester akɛ, “Mɛni ji osane lɛ; mɛni otaoɔ? Nɔ ni ji lɛ bi, ni mafee mahã bo aahu kɛji mi maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mlijaa ni po.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: “Kɛji mihiɛ eba nyam yɛ Maŋtsɛ hiɛ, ni Nii yɛ he suɔmɔ akɛ eeefee nɔ ni mabi lɛ ehã mi lɛ, no lɛ Nii kɛ Haman aba okplɔ̃ kroko ko ni mibaŋmɛ amɛ wɔ lɛ he koni mikɛ nɔ ni miyɔɔ ni mabi lɛ aŋmɛ Nii hiɛ wɔ.” Haman to Mɔdekai gbele he ŋaa

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Haman shi maŋtsɛ we lɛ gbi lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ kɛ mliflimɔ. Shi be ni ena Mɔdekai yɛ maŋtsɛ koi lɛ shi, ni Mɔdekai eteee shi ehãaa lɛ, asaŋ ni ehe hu kpokpooo lɛ, Haman mli wo Mɔdekai la naakpa.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ Haman ye ehe nɔ, ni eyiŋ etee ewe lɛ, ni etsu ayatsɛ enanemɛi abahã lɛ; etsɛ eŋa Zeresh hu ebafata enanemɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Haman kɛ enii ni eyɔɔ kɛ emusuŋbii ayifalɛ kɛ bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ewo enɔ grɔŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ fe lumɛi kɛ maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ shi ehe nɔ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Etee nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Maŋnyɛ Ester po hãaa mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ aba okplɔ̃ ni eŋmɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ he akɛ ja mi, ni wɔ hu ekpee mi kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛmiiya wɔyaye nii.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, gbii abɔ ni minaa Mɔdekai Yudanyo lɛ ta maŋtsɛ koi shi lolo lɛ mitsui etɔɔɔ.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ wɔ tse yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hiŋmɛiŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, efã akɛ ayakɔ yinɔi asaji ahe wolo lɛ kɛba koni abakane atsɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ bi akɛ, “Mɛni afee akɛwo Mɔdekai hiɛ nyam yɛ nɔ ni etsu nɛɛ hewɔ?” Maŋtsɛ lɛ sɔ̃ɔlɔi ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Afeko nɔ ko nɔ ko ahãko lɛ.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ bi akɛ, “Namɔ yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?” No mli nɔŋŋ lɛ Haman ebashɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ agbonaagbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ, ni eeba ekɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ abawie he koni asɛŋ Mɔdekai yɛ tso ni ehã akla ama shi ahã Mɔdekai sɛŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ sɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Haman eshɛ shi, edamɔ kpo lɛ nɔ.” Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Hã ni eba mli!”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Be ni Haman ba lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji maŋtsɛ miisumɔ akɛ ewo nuu ko hiɛ nyam lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ afee ahã mɔ lɛ?” Haman susu yɛ eyiŋ ekɛɛ, “Namɔ po maŋtsɛ baasumɔ akɛ ewo ehiɛ nyam nɛɛ akɛ ja mi?”

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Haman hã maŋtsɛ lɛ hetoo akɛ, “Nuu lɛ ni maŋtsɛ sumɔɔ akɛ ewo ehiɛ nyam lɛ hewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ ahã akɔlɔ maŋtsɛ atadei ni maŋtsɛ woɔ daa lɛ ekomɛi, ni aŋɔ okpɔŋɔ ni maŋtsɛ eta nɔ dã, ni akɛ maŋtsɛ akekre afata he.

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Haman akɛ, “Ohe afee oya, koni oŋɔ atade kɛ okpɔŋɔ lɛ, ni oyafee bɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ohã Mɔdekai, Yudanyo lɛ, ni taa maŋtsɛ koi lɛ shi lɛ. Okashi nɔ ko ni otsɔ̃ɔ akɛ afee lɛ ekoeko.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Haman ŋɔ atade lɛ kɛ okpɔŋɔ lɛ kɛtee. Ekɛ atade lɛ yawula Mɔdekai, ni ehã ekwɔ eta okpɔŋɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eta nɔ kɛfo blohuiaŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni Haman bɔ oshe kɛnyiɛ Mɔdekai hiɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, bɔ ni afeɔ ahãa mɔ ni Maŋtsɛ miisumɔ akɛ ewo ehiɛ nyam lɛ nɛ!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Mɔdekai ku esɛɛ kɛba maŋtsɛ koi lɛ shi; shi Haman he fee oya ni eyiŋ kɛtee ewe lɛ kɛ ŋkɔmɔyeli ni eha eyi nɔ.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Egba eŋa Zeresh kɛ enanemɛi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ osharã ni eyasharã lɛ lɛ. Haman nanemɛi nilelɔi lɛ kɛ eŋa lɛ hu kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji abɔ̃i bo shibaa yɛ Mɔdekai ni jɛ Yudafoi aseshi mli lɛ hiɛ lɛ, belɛ no lɛ onyɛŋ lɛ mɔ; bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ ebaafe bo.” Haman gbele

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Ahiɛ sanegbaa lɛ mli nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ piafoi komɛi bashɛ shi, ni amɛbaŋɔ Haman kplakpla kɛtee Maŋnyɛ Ester okplɔŋmɛɛ lɛ he.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ Haman tee amɛkɛ Maŋnyɛ Ester yaaye nii.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Be ni anuɔ dãa yɛ niyenii lɛ ashi yɛ gbi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Ester ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Maŋnyɛ Ester, mɛni ji osane lɛ; mɛni otaoɔ? Nɔ ni ji lɛ bi, ni mafee mahã bo aahu, kɛji maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mlijaa po ni.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Maŋnyɛ Ester here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, kɛji mihiɛ eba nyam yɛ ohiɛ, ni maŋtsɛ yɛ he tsuijurɔ akɛ ebaafee nɔ ni mibabi lɛ lɛ, nɔ ni mibiɔ ji akɛ akɛ miwala ake mi; asaŋ akɛ mimaŋbii hu awala ake amɛ.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ wɔ, mi kɛ mimaŋbii lɛ, ahã koni akpãtã wɔhiɛ, ni agbe wɔ kɛbule wɔshishi. Eji ahɔ̃ɔ wɔ akɛ nyɔji hii kɛ nyɔji yei kɛkɛ kulɛ egbaŋ minaa, ni kulɛ mikɛŋ nɔ ko, ejaakɛ piŋmɔ ni abaapiŋ wɔ lɛ ejeee nɔ ko kwraa kɛji akɛto maŋtsɛ nii ni baafite he.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Maŋnyɛ Ester to he akɛ, “Wɔhenyɛlɔ kɛ wɔyinɔ apamtolɔ lɛ, lɛ ji Haman, gbɔmɔ fɔŋ nɛɛ.” Kɛkɛ ni Haman tsui fã yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ maŋnyɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ te shi kɛ mlifu kɛshi okplɔ̃ lɛ he kɛtee trom ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ he lɛ mli. Haman na maŋtsɛ lɛ hiŋmɛi sha akɛ kɛji ena lɛ Haman lɛ efɔŋ lɛ, eeefee. No hewɔ lɛ, Haman te shi koni ekpa Maŋnyɛ Ester fai koni akɛ ewala ake lɛ.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Ho ni Haman ho egbee shi yɛ saatso fioo ko ni Ester ta nɔ lɛ naa, koni ekpa lɛ fai pɛ, kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ jɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ he trom lɛ mli kɛba he ni aŋmɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ yɛ lɛ. Ni ebanina Haman nɛkɛ lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, “Aso ebaatua maŋnyɛ lɛ yɛ mihiɛ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ miwe mli lo?” Maŋtsɛ lɛ naa ni nyɔɔ shi nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni piafoi lɛ ha Haman hiɛ.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, atee ni ayasɛŋ Haman moŋ yɛ tso ni ekala akɛ ebaasɛŋ Mɔdekai yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ mlila lɛ jɔ.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh ŋɔ Haman, Yudafoi lɛ ahenyɛlɔ lɛ, shĩa ni ekɛhã Maŋnyɛ Ester; ni Mɔdekai bɔ̃i maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ yaa ejaakɛ Maŋnyɛ Ester tsɔ̃ɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh emɔ ni ji Mɔdekai.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ jie ewaoga ni ekɛsɔoɔ wolo naa, ni ehe yɛ Haman dɛŋ lɛ yɛ ewao ni ekɛhã Mɔdekai. Ester tu Haman shĩa lɛ ewo Mɔdekai dɛŋ koni ekwɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ester kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ yawie ekoŋŋ. Eyaho ekula Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh naji anaa, ni ekɛ yaafo kpa lɛ fai akɛ efo efɔŋ ni Haman, Agagnyo lɛ, eto akɛ afee Yudafoi lɛ mli ehã amɛ.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nii, kɛji esa ohiɛ lɛ, no lɛ hã aŋmã wolo koni akɛyatsi yiŋsha ni Hamedata bi Haman, Agagnyo lɛ, to koni ekɛkpãtã Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Maŋtsɛ shikpɔji fɛɛ anɔ lɛ ahiɛ lɛ naa.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ aso manyɛ naa madamɔ kɛji sane fɔŋ nɛɛ banina mimaŋbii lɛ, ni akpãtã amɛhiɛ kɛbule amɛshishi?”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh kɛɛ Maŋnyɛ Ester kɛ Mɔdekai, Yudafonyo lɛ, akɛ, “Naa, mihã asɛŋ Haman yɛ Yudafoi lɛ ayinɔ ni ekpãŋ lɛ hewɔ, ni mikɛ shĩa lɛ hu eke Ester.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛŋma Yudafoi lɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛaasumɔ yɛ sane nɛɛ he yɛ mi, migbɛi mli. Asaŋ nyɛkɛ miwolo naasɔomɔ ga lɛ asɔoa wolo lɛ naa, ejaakɛ wolo ni aŋmã yɛ maŋtsɛ gbɛi mli, asaŋ ni akɛ ewolo naasɔomɔ ga lɛ esɔo naa lɛ, anyɛŋ emli sane lɛ mli afo.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Mɔdekai hã aŋmala woji lɛ yɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh gbɛi mli, ni akɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ wolonaasɔomɔ ga lɛ sɔo amɛnaa. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ woji lɛ tsu bɔfoi ni tara maŋtsɛ lɛ okpɔŋɔi ni afoijee naa wa lɛ ekomɛi anɔ kɛtee.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Mɔdekai je maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ etee, ni ewo maŋtsɛ atade ni akɛ mama bluu kɛ mama yɛŋ ekpɛ, kɛ enɔ atade wuyaa ni akɛ klala yɛŋ kɛ kuŋtu tsuru faa kpɛ. Shika akekre agbo fi eyitso. Susa maŋ lɛ nya ni amɛna miishɛɛ.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Yudafoi lɛ ahe tse amɛ, ni amɛnya, ni amɛmli fili amɛ jogbaŋŋ; asaŋ hiɛ sɔ amɛ.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ ni Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh shɛɛ kɛ akpɔ lɛ yashɛ lɛ, jɛi Yudafoi lɛ na miishɛɛ, ni amɛnya, ni amɛŋmɛŋmɛɛ okplɔ̃, ni amɛyeyee gbii juji. Shikpɔji anɔ bii lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo tsɔ̃mɔ amɛhe Yudafoi tete, ejaakɛ Yudafoi lɛ ahe ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ amɛ.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Adar lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ lɛ bashɛ, ni ji gbi ni abaaye maŋtsɛ kitã kɛ akpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Be mli ni Yudafoi lɛ ahenyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ kã nɔ akɛ amɛbaana Yudafoi lɛ anɔ hewalɛ lɛ, amɛhiɛnɔkãmɔ nɛɛ tsake ekroko, ni Yudafoi lɛ moŋ na hewalɛ yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Yudafoi lɛ buabua amɛhe naa kuikui yɛ amɛkutsei lɛ amli yɛ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh nɔyelihei lɛ amli majimaji lɛ amli akɛ amɛkɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni baatua amɛ lɛ baawu. Ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛɛɛ amɛhiɛ adamɔ, ejaakɛ Yudafoi lɛ ahe ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ maji lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, shikpɔji lɛ anɔ onukpai lɛ kɛ amraloi lɛ kɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni tsuɔ maŋtsɛ nii ye bua Yudafoi lɛ, ejaakɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miishe Mɔdekai gbeyei.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Mɔdekai etsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ wulu yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli, ni daa gbi lɛ nɛkɛ ehewalɛ lɛ daa kɛyaa nɔ; ni egbɛi ehehe kɛkpele shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yudafoi lɛ fee amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ bɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ. Amɛfã klante yɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛgbegbee amɛ, ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ayabɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh mɛi ayibɔ ni agbe yɛ Susa ni ji maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Maŋnyɛ Ester akɛ, “Yɛ Susa maŋtsɛmaŋ lɛ kɛkɛ mli lɛ, Yudafoi lɛ egbegbee mɛi ohai enumɔ kɛ Haman bihii nyɔŋma lɛ hu. Belɛ te amɛfee tɛŋŋ mɔ yɛ nɔyelihei lɛ fɛɛ hu? Kɛ̃lɛ mɛni oyɔɔ ni obaabi lolo? Mɛni otaoɔ ekoŋŋ, ni aaafee ahã bo!”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ester to he ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji Nii baasumɔ lɛ, aŋmɛ Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Susa maŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ agbɛ koni wɔ hu lɛ, amɛfee bɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɛnɛ yɛ mla lɛ naa lɛ ekoŋŋ; asaŋ akɛ Haman bihii nyɔŋma lɛ agbohii lɛ atsotsoro tso nɔ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ fee nakai. Awo mla yɛ Susa, ni ahole Haman bihii nyɔŋma lɛ agbohii lɛ, ni akɛ amɛ tsotsoro shi yɛ maŋ jara nɔ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Susa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbe amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ yɛ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ etɛ̃ kɛ nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ anɔ, kɛkɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkɛfee okplɔŋmɛɛ kɛ nyamɔ gbijurɔ.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yudafoi ni yɔɔ akrowai amli, ni ji maji ni atswako gbogbo awoko amɛhe lɛ, yeɔ Adar nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ akɛ gbijurɔ kɛ okplɔŋmɛɛ kɛ nyamɔ, ni amɛkekeɔ amɛhe nii. Purim Gbijurɔyeli lɛ

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Mɔdekai hã aŋmãla nɛkɛ saji nɛɛ, ni ekɛ woji tsu, ni akɛyahã Yudafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh nɔyelihei lɛ fɛɛ, mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fɛɛ,

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: ni ekɛfo efɔ̃ shi ehã Yudafoi lɛ akɛ amɛye Adar nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ kɛ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ akɛ gbijurɔ daa afi,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ anɔ Yudafoi lɛ ahe jɔ amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ. Nyɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ amɛwerɛho lɛ tsɔ̃ miishɛɛ, ni amɛkɔmɔyeli lɛ tsɔ̃ nyamɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfee nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ okplɔŋmɛɛ kɛ nyamɔ kɛ henikee kɛ ohiafoi anikee gbii.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Yudafoi lɛ kɔ fɔ̃ amɛnɔ ni amɛfee tamɔ bɔ ni Mɔdekai ŋmã akɛ amɛfee lɛ, kɛkɛ ni etsɔ̃ afiyeli ehã amɛ.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Haman, Hamedata, Agagnyo lɛ bi lɛ, ni fee ehe Yudafoi lɛ fɛɛ ahenyɛlɔ tsɔ̃ ŋaa koni ekpãtã Yudafoi lɛ ahiɛ. Efɔ̃ oshiki, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Pur lɛ, koni ena gbi nɔ ni akpãtã Yudafoi lɛ ahiɛ kɛbule amɛshishi.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Shi Ester yana maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋmã wolo, ni naagbee mli lɛ ehã Yudafoi lɛ ayinɔ ŋaa fɔŋ ni Haman etsɔ̃ lɛ babua lɛ moŋ eyiteŋ, ni asɛŋ lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tso nɔ yɛ maŋ jara nɔ.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, awo gbii nɛɛ gbɛi akɛ Purim yɛ gbɛi Pur lɛ hewɔ. Wolo ni Mɔdekai ŋmã lɛ mli saji lɛ kɛ nɔ ni amɛ, Yudafoi lɛ, diɛŋtsɛ hu na yɛ nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ mli, kɛ nɔ ni ba amɛnɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Maŋnyɛ Ester, Abihail biyoo lɛ, kɛ Mɔdekai, Yudanyo lɛ, ŋma wolo yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛna lɛ naa, ni amɛkɛma Purim gbijurɔyeli lɛ he wolo ni Mɔdekai eŋmã lɛ nɔ aduatsɔ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: koni amɛ kɛ amɛshwiei aye Purim gbii lɛ yɛ be ni ato lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni amɛto be kɛ gbɛjianɔ ni amɛkɛhiɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkɛfeɔ yara lɛ.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Maŋnyɛ Ester wolo ni eŋmã lɛ ma nɛkɛ Purim gbijurɔyeli kusum nɛɛ nɔ aduatsɔ ni aŋmã awo wolo mli afɔ̃ shi.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh tsu enɔyeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ onia kɛjɛ ŋshɔnaa aahu kɛyagbee koiasɛɛ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: He ni egbojee shɛ kɛ nibii ni etsu yɛ ehewalɛ kɛ enyɛmɔ naa, kɛ he ni ewo Mɔdekai nɔ grɔŋŋ kɛyashɛ lɛ aŋmala fɛɛ yɛ Media kɛ Persia Maŋtsɛmɛi Ayinɔ Saji Awolo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Mɔdekai, Yudanyo lɛ, batsɔ̃ Maŋtsɛ Ahashwerosh diɛŋtsɛ sɛɛmɔ tuuŋtu, kɛ gbɔmɔ wulu hu yɛ enyɛmimɛi Yudafoi lɛ ateŋ; amɛbuɔ lɛ, ni amɛsumɔɔ esane; ni lɛ hu be fɛɛ be lɛ etaoɔ emaŋbii lɛ kɛ amɛshwiei fɛɛ ekpakpa; ni ekɛ amɛ wieɔ kɛ naajɔlɛ.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Nuu ko hi shi yɛ Uz shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; egbɛi ji Hiob. Esheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he. Eji gbɔmɔ ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, asaŋ efeɔ nii ni ja hu.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ bi Abonsam akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ojɛ obaa nɛɛ?” Abonsam to he akɛ, “Mijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpaa kɛ shisharamɔ yɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Hiob bihii lɛ toɔ naa ekomekome ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe okplɔ̃. Kɛji eshɛ mɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebihii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ yaa mɔ lɛ we lɛ. Hii lɛ tsuɔ kɛyaa, ni ayatsɛɔ amɛnyɛmimɛi yei etɛ̃ lɛ hu kɛbaa, ni amɛkɛ amɛ bayeɔ nii, ni amɛnuɔ dãa.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Kɛji aŋmɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ kɛbɔle bihii lɛ anɔ kɛkpe lɛ, Hiob teɔ shi daa leebi maŋkpa, ni eyashãa shãa afɔlei ehãa ebii lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ, yɛ amɛyibɔ naa koni akɛtsuu amɛhe. Ejaakɛ Hiob kɛɔ akɛ, “Benɛ mibihii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko efee esha ko ni aleee, ni ekwa Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ etsuiŋ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni Hiob feɔ daa.”

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Be ko lɛ ŋwɛi bɔfoi lɛ ni sɔmɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tee Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ. Abonsam futu amɛ kɛtee, ni lɛ hu eyadamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ eko.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Osusu mitsulɔ Hiob he akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tamɔ lɛ ni eji nuu anɔkwafo ni sheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he, ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja?”

english_verse: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
translation_verse: Abonsam kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani yaka Hiob sheɔ bo, Nyɔŋmɔ, gbeyei lɛ?

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Bɛ ofo afabaŋ okɛbaa lɛ kɛ ewe kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yi shweshweeshwe. Ojɔɔ eninenaa nitsumɔ nɔ, ni ekooloi eshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ bo lɛ kpã onine mli ofite enii ni eyɔɔ lɛ, koni okwɛ akɛ ekwaŋ bo yɛ ohiɛ lo.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Abonsam akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mijɔɔ enii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ nɔ miwo odɛ̃ŋ. Lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛkɛ ni okɛ onine akasa.” Kɛkɛ ni Abonsam je Yehowa hiɛ ni etee. Hiob bii lɛ kɛ ejwetri hiɛ kpãtã

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Hiob bihii lɛ kɛ ebiyei lɛ eyakpe, ni amɛmiiye nii, ni amɛmiinu wain yɛ amɛnyɛmi nuu onukpa lɛ we lɛ mli.

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: Bɔfo ko ba Hiob ŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Tsinai lɛ miihu, ni teji yei lɛ hu miiye nii yɛ amɛmasɛi.

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Trukaa ni Sabiabii batua amɛ, ni amɛmɔmɔ kooloi lɛ kɛtee; amɛgbe otsuji lɛ kɛ klante; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Tsulɔ lɛ hiɛ wiemɔ lɛ mli lolo kɛkɛ ni tsulɔ kroko ko ba, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Srawa gba kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni ebayi toi lɛ kɛ tsuji lɛ anɔ, ni eplene amɛ fɛɛ; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Be ni lɛ hu ewieɔ lolo lɛ, tsulɔ kroko ko hu bashɛ shi, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Kaldeabii ba kɛ kui etɛ̃ amɛbatua yoomai lɛ, ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛ kɛtee, ni amɛkɛ klante gbe tsuji lɛ, mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Tsulɔ lɛ wiemɔ lɛ ma enaa lolo kɛkɛ lɛ naa tsulɔ kroko ko hu eba, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Obihii lɛ kɛ obiyei lɛ miiye nii, ni amɛmiinu wain yɛ amɛnyɛmi nuu nukpa lɛ we lɛ mli

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: kɛkɛ ni ahum kpele ko tswa kɛjɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ, ni ebabote shĩa lɛ mli, ni eshimɔ shĩa lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ, ni eshĩa lɛ wule eshwie oblahii lɛ anɔ, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛgboi; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hiob te shi, ni ekɛ awerɛho gbala ehe atade lɛ, eshɛ eyi, ni eho ebu shikpɔŋ, ni esɔle.

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yayai mikɛjɛ minyɛ musuŋ miba, ni yayai mikɛaaku misɛɛ kɛaatee. Yehowa ni ŋɔ hã, ni Yehowa ebaŋɔ kɛtee; aaajie Yehowa gbɛi lɛ yi kɛ̃!”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Saji ni ba nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Hiob shwaaa Nyɔŋmɔ ni no atsɔ̃ esha ahã lɛ.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ojɛ obaa nɛ?” Abonsam to he akɛ, “Mijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; miyakpa nɔ; ni miyashara shi yɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Osusu mitsulɔ Hiob he akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tamɔ lɛ, ni anɔkwafo ni, ni esheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he; ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja? Ehiɛ enɔkwayeli lɛ mli kpɛŋŋ lolo tsɛbelɛ ohã mite shi miwo lɛ koni mikpãtã ehiɛ yakatswaa!”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Abonsam to he hã Yehowa akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ baaŋmɛɛ nii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ he bɔ ni afee kɛkɛ ni eyi ana wala.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Shi bo lɛ taa egbɔmɔtso he kɛkɛ okwɛ akɛ ekwaŋ bo yɛ ohiɛ lo?”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Abonsam akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mijɔɔ enɔ miwo odɛ̃ŋ; shi obaa ewala yi kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Abonsam shi Yehowa hiɛ, ni etee; ni ehã asane ni waa mɔ he waa tsɛ̃rɛ Hiob kɛjɛ enaneshi aahu kɛyashi epampam.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Hiob ŋa bi lɛ akɛ, “Ohiɛ anɔkwayeli nɛɛ mli kpɛŋŋ lolo? Mɛɛba okwaaa Nyɔŋmɔ koni ogbo?”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Hiob kɛɛ eŋa lɛ akɛ, “Oowie tamɔ bɔ ni yei kwashiai lɛ wieɔ lɛ. Nɔ kpakpa lɛ wɔhe kɛjɛ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ. Mɛɛba ni nɔ fɔŋ lɛ wɔkahe?” Enɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, Hiob naa tɛɛɛ shi, ni ewieee wiemɔ gbonyo ko. Hiob nanemɛi ba eŋɔɔ

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Be ni nanemɛi etɛ̃ komɛi ni Hiob yɔɔ lɛ nu amanehulu fɛɛ ni eba Hiob nɔ lɛ he lɛ, amɛjɛjɛɛ amɛshihilɛhei amɛba Hiob ŋɔɔ. Enaanyo Elifaz jɛ Teman, ni Bildad jɛ Shua, ni Zofar jɛ Naama. Nanemɛi nɛɛ ye fua akɛ amɛaatee kutuu amɛyaye Hiob ŋkɔmɔ, ni amɛshɛje emii.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Nanemɛi nɛɛ na Hiob yɛ shɔŋŋ, shi amɛyooo lɛ. Shi be ni amɛyoo Hiob lɛ, amɛfo waa; amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ dɔlɛ gbala ehe atade, ni amɛloo mlu amɛwo amɛyiteiaŋ.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Nanemɛi lɛ ho amɛta Hiob masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ, shwaneshwane kɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ gbii kpawo sɔŋŋ. Amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ Hiob ewieee wiemɔ kome nɛkɛ, ejaakɛ amɛna akɛ eena nɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Hiob gbele enaa, ni elomɔ gbi ni afɔ lɛ lɛ.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Hiob kɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “Oo Nyɔŋmɔ, hã gbi nɔ ni afɔ mi lɛ hiɛ akpãtã; hã gbi gbɛkɛ ni akɛɛ akɛ, ‘Ana binuu musu lɛ hiɛ akpãtã.’

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ, hã nakai gbi lɛ atsɔ̃ tamɔ yoo kene; akanu miishɛɛ gbee he yɛ nɔ!

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Hã mɛi ni lomɔɔ gbi alomɔ lɛ, mɛi ni le bonso hiɛlawoo lɛ.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Hã emaŋkɛ̃ ŋulamii lɛ afɔ̃ɔ kpɛmɔ; hã etao la, shi ekana eko; ni ekana hulu haaigbalamɔ.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ ni afɔ mi ni etsiii minyɛ musu naa, ni ehã miina jaramɔ.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Mɛɛba shuɔ he mi fɔ̃ enɔ; ni mɛɛba fufɔ hã mina lɛ miye?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Kulɛ benɛ miho mikã shi kpoo; kulɛ bɛ miwɔ ni kulɛ benɛ mihe ejɔ mi

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: kɛkã maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ jeŋ ajinafoi lɛ, mɛi ni saa mamɔɔ mɔji ni ekumɔ hãa amɛhe lɛ,

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: loo tamɔ lumɛi shikatsɛmɛi, mɛi ni shĩaiaŋ eyimɔ kɛ jwiɛtɛi lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Aloo mɛɛba mitsɔ̃ɔɔ sharakemɔ bi ni enãaa hulu la lɛ?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Jɛi lɛ yitsoŋwalɔi kpaa mɔ haomɔ; ni mɛi ni etɔ amɛ woɔ amɛtsui.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Mɔ bibioo kɛ mɔ wulu feɔ pɛ yɛ jɛi, ni nyɔŋ yeɔ ehe yɛ enuŋtsɔ dɛŋ.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: “Mɛɛba ahãa mɔ ni yɔɔ haomɔ mli lɛ lá; ni ahãa mɔ ni werɛ eho ehe wala?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni shweɔ gbele, shi gbele baaa lɛ, ni etsaa shi etaoɔ gbele fe bɔ ni atsaa shi ataoɔ jwetri ni akɛtee lɛ;

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: mɔ ni mii shɛɔ fe nine, ni enyaaa kɛji ena gbonyobu lɛ.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Mɛɛba ahãa gbɔmɔ ni aŋɔ ewala atee, gbɔmɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ esa eyi lɛ la?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Ŋkɔmɔyeli etsɔ̃ miniyenii, ni mifɔseɔ mligbigblimɔ mishwieɔ shi tamɔ nu.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Mihe ejɔko mi, ni minako miyitso toohe; mibɛ hejɔlɛ shi haomɔ miiba lolo.”

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Kɛji aka bo kɛ wiemɔ lɛ, eeefee bo mlifu lo? Shi kɛ̃lɛ namɔ aaanyɛ enaa emua?

english_verse: But now you feel discouraged when struck by trouble.
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ lɛ eshɛ onɔ, shi onaaa tsui; esa ohe, no ojijaa nɛɛ.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: Kwɛ jeee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei ni osheɔ lɛ no nɔ ohiɛ kã, ni onɔkwayeli jeŋba lɛ ji ohiɛnɔkãmɔ?

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Bɔ pɛ ni mina nɛ: Mɛi ni huɔ nɔsha ŋmɔ, ni amɛduɔ yiwalɛ wui lɛ nomɛi nɔŋŋ amɛkpaa.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ ni shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ kpãtãa amɛhiɛ, ni emlifu kɔɔyɔɔ pleneɔ amɛ.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Ajɔɔ jata huumɔ kɛ oloowɔ gbee he, ni akumɔ jatabii atsoji fɛɛ.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Jata ni he wa gboɔ kɛ enaaa kooloo emɔ ni eye, ni jata yoo bii gbɛɔ shwãa.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: “Be ko lɛ, minu wiemɔ ko; efo mitoi naa nyɔɔŋ

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: be ni wɔ ni tsii nyɔɔ mɛi anɔ, ni ninai ahejwɛŋmɔ

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Mumɔ ko bafo mihiɛ; mihe tsɔi te shi damɔ shi.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Mumɔ lɛ wa edamɔ shi keŋŋ; shi miyooo esu.” Shi su ko badamɔ mihiɛ, jɛi fee koniŋŋ, kɛkɛ ni minu gbee ko:

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: “Aso adesa ko aaaja yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ? Aso adesa ko he aaatse yɛ ebɔlɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ ehe efɔ̃ɔɔ etsuji anɔ, ni enaa tɔ̃mɔ yɛ ebɔfoi tete ahe lɛ,

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: ani osusuɔ akɛ ekɛ ehe baafɔ gbɔmɔ adesa nɔ, gbɔmɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ su mli ni afufluɔ lɛ tamɔ omlɛgɛ?

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ hiɛ kãa leebi, shi egboɔ trukaa gbɛkɛnaashi. Ehiɛ kpãtãa, ni mɔ ko ebuuu ehe akɔntaa.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Kɛji atserɛ emli fãi lɛ; aso amɛgboiii yɛ be mli ni amɛnako jwɛŋmɔ lolo lɛ?”

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ Hiob, boo ni otsɛ akɛ mɔ ko kwraa yɛ ni aaahere bo nɔ lo? Bɔfoi lɛ ateŋ namɔ ŋɔɔ oootee?

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Eji anɔkwale sane akɛ mlila sɔŋŋ gbeɔ kwashia, ni awuŋayeli gbeɔ mɔ ni hiɛ etɛ̃ɛɛ.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Mina kwashiai ni miihe shi ahe dã; shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni milomɔ amɛwe lɛ.

english_verse: Then hungry and greedy people gobble up their crops and grab their wealth.
translation_verse: Hɔmɔwɔlɔi aaaye enikpamɔ nii, ŋmei ateŋ nii eeena ekɔlɔ; mɛi aaaye enii he kumai.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Amanehulu jɛɛɛ mlu mli baaa, ni haomɔ hu ekwɛ̃ɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ;

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: shi gbɔmɔ lɛ, afɔ lɛ ahã haomɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni lalilɛi tsɛ̃rɛɔ kɛjɛɔ la mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: “Mi ji bo kulɛ, matao Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ, ni Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ matu misane lɛ mawo,

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: lɛ mɔ ni efeɔ nibii wuji ni anaaa naa, kɛ naakpɛɛ nibii hu ni ehiii kanemɔ lɛ.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Ehãa nu nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eshwieɔ ŋmɔji anɔ nu;

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Eholeɔ humii anɔ grɔŋŋ, ni eshɛjeɔ ŋkɔmɔyelɔi amii.

english_verse: God swiftly traps the wicked
translation_verse: Efiteɔ ŋai ni hiɛtɛ̃lɔi tsɔ̃ɔ, ni ehãa amɛnine nyɛɔ shi.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: Ekɛ ŋaatsɔlɔi nɔŋŋ aŋaa duɔ amɛ, ni efiteɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji ayiŋtoi fɔ̃ji lɛ.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Duŋ woɔ amɛ shwane fintiŋŋ, ni amɛgbugbuɔ shi shwane mlemle tamɔ mɛi ni nyiɛɔ nyɔɔŋ.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Ehereɔ awusai ayiwala kɛjeɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji adaaŋ, ni ehereɔ ohiafo yɛ yiwalɔ dɛŋ.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ohiafo yɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ, ni toikɔdɔmɔ saneyeli muɔ shi kɔ̃i.

english_verse: Consider yourself fortunate if God All-Powerful chooses to correct you.
translation_verse: “Naa, ajɔɔ mɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kãa lɛ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, ekafee bo dɔlɛ kɛji Ofe lɛ kã bo.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ epilaa mɔ, shi lɛ nɔŋŋ efiɔ nɔ, etswaa mɔ nɔ, ni enine nɔŋŋ tsaa.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Ebaajie bo yɛ amanehului babaoo amli hu, nɔ ko nɔ ko efeŋ bo.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ebaajie bo yɛ gbele mli, ni ta mli hu lɛ, oooje klante naa.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ baabaa oyi kɛjɛ gbɔmɔ naabu fitemɔ mli; ni kɛji hiɛkpãtãmɔ miiba lɛ osheŋ gbeyei.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Oooŋmɔ hiɛkpãtãmɔ kɛ hɔmɔ fɛɛ, ni osheŋ ŋaŋ kooloi agbeyei.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Tɛi ehiŋ shikpɔŋ ni ohuɔ nɔ, ni ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ bo aaahi shi kpoo.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Enɛ aaahã ole akɛ owe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, ni oookpa otoi anaa, ni ooona akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Ooona hiɛnɔkãmɔ akɛ oshwiei ayi aaafa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Ooogbɔ kotokoto dani ooogbo, tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa tsɛɔ ni esaa dani ebashɛɔ ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Hiob, nɔ ni wɔkpa shi wɔna nɛ. Anɔkwale ni, no hewɔ lɛ, okɛbu ohe.”

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: “Oo, mina ni aŋmɛ minaagbai kɛ mihejaramɔ fɛɛ yɛ nsɛni mli.

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ aaana akɛ etsii fe ŋshɔnaa shia, ni no hewɔ ni minaa wiemɔi lɛ efeŋ yiŋ flɛflɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Ofe lɛ etsɛ̃rɛ mi gãi, ni miinu gãimlibii lɛ anaa ebɔɔ lɛ he yɛ mimli; Nyɔŋmɔ he ŋmiŋmi emɔ mi emuu.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Ani ŋaŋ teji bolɔɔ be ni ena jwɛi eekpe, aloo tsina bolɔɔ yɛ eniyeniiashi?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Ani ayeɔ nii mutɛ ni ŋoo bɛ mli? Aloo mɛɛ ŋɔɔmɔ yɔɔ wuɔwɔlɔ mli eyɛŋ lɛ mli?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Nii ni misusuma sumɔɔɔ akɛ eyeɔ lɛ nomɛi nɔŋŋ etsɔ̃ miniyenii ni minyaŋeɔ nɛɛ.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
translation_verse: “Oo, mina ni kulɛ mina mitaomɔnii; ni Nyɔŋmɔ hã mi mishweenii.

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Kulɛ mimii aaashɛ mihe, mimli aaafli mi pam yɛ minɔnaa ni akɛfaaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ mikwako Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ wiemɔi lɛ.

english_verse: Why should I patiently hope when my strength is gone?
translation_verse: Mihewalɛ enyiɛ hewɔ ni mamia mihiɛ mamɛ? Mɛɛ ji minaagbee hewɔ ni mato mitsui shi?

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: Ani mihewalɛ lɛ tɛ hewalɛ ni? Loo miheloo lɛ akɔɔble ni?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, mibɛ hewalɛ ko dɔŋŋ, minyɛmɔ fɛɛ etã.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: “Mɔ ni kwaa enaanyo ejurɔfeemɔ lɛ, esheee Ofe lɛ gbeyei.

english_verse: then suddenly disappear in the summer heat.
translation_verse: Kɛji dɔlɛ ba pɛ amɛlaaje; kɛ jeŋ dɔ pɛ amɛmii.

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Gbɛnyiɛlɔi asafo gbaa afã kɛjeɔ amɛgbɛ nɔ, amɛyafoɔ shi kɛtaoɔ nu yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛ kpãtãa.

english_verse: Caravans from Tema and Sheba
translation_verse: Tema kɛ Sheba gbɛfalɔi asafoi taoɔ kɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ,

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: shi amɛhiɛ gboiɔ akɛ amɛŋɔ amɛhiɛ amɛfɔ nɔ; ejaakɛ kɛji amɛshɛ he pɛ, amɛhiɛ shwieɔ shi.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Bɔ pɛ ni nyɛ ji nyɛhã mi nɛ, mimanehulu ni nyɛna lɛ, ehã nyɛmiishe gbeyei.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: Ani mibi akɛ nyɛke mi nɔ ko, aloo nyɛkɛ nyɛnii ni nyɛyɔɔ ayawo mɔ ko daaŋnii ahã mi?

english_verse: or to purchase my freedom from brutal enemies?
translation_verse: Aloo nyɛhere mi yɛ henyɛlɔ lɛ dɛŋ, aloo nyɛkpɔ̃ mi yɛ yiwalɔi adɛŋ?

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Nyɛtsɔa mi; nyɛhãa manua shishi, koni nɔ mli ni mitɔ̃ yɛ lɛ, mafee diŋŋ.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Anɔkwa wiemɔ yɛ hewalɛ; shi mɛni kãmɔ ni nyɛkãa mi lɛ baanyɛ etsu?

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Ani nyɛsusuɔ akɛ nyɛaanyɛ nyɛkã gbɔmɔ yɛ wiemɔ hewɔ, be mli ni mɔ ni bɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ wiemɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni lɛ?

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Nyɛaafɔ̃ awusa nɔ oshiki, ni nyɛaaye nyɛnaanyo yi jara.

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ, nyɛtɛjea nyɛhiɛ nyɛkwɛa mi; ejaakɛ mimaleŋ mitsɔŋ nyɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ!

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Nyɛfainɛ, awa jɛi! Nyɛkafea esha; awa jɛi, misane lɛ ja.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Ani wiemɔ ko ni ejaaa eje minaa dã? Ani mileee nɔ kpakpa yɛ nɔ fɔŋ he?”

english_verse: Why is life so hard? Why do we suffer?
translation_verse: “Ani gbɔmɔ wala yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ jeee tɔlɛ kɛ deŋmegbomɔ? Ani ewala gbii tamɔɔɔ apaafonyo wala gbii?

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Ani etamɔɔɔ bɔ ni apaafonyo kwɛɔ epaabɔɔnii gbɛ lɛ?

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Nakai mihi shi shwɛm nyɔji abɔ ni mikã jaramɔ mli nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: Kɛji miho mikã shi lɛ, bɔ ni mibablaa shi nɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɔɔŋ hu sɛɛ jɛkɛɔ, ni mibiɔ mihe akɛ, mɛɛbe je aaatsɛre ni mate shi?”

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Miheloo ewo gɔgɔmi kɛ muji; miheloo lɛ hiɛ gbiɔ kɛkɛ lɛ eflɛ.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Migbii lɛ hoɔ oyayaaya fe mamalolɔ akokrowa tete, ni amɛmiitã ni hiɛnɔkãmɔ ko bɛ.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: “Nyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ akɛ miwala lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni, ni nɔ kpakpa bɛ ni mihiŋmɛi baana dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Mɔ hiŋmɛi ni naa mi nɛɛ, enaŋ mi dɔŋŋ. Ookwɛ mi nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ, ni malaaje.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni atatu tseɔ, ni elaajeɔ lɛ, nakai mɔ ni yaa gbohiiaje ekuuu esɛɛ ebaaa dɔŋŋ;

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: ekuuu esɛɛ ebaaa ewe dɔŋŋ, ni hiɛ kpaa enɔ kwraa.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mimuaŋ minaa! Mikɛ mimumɔŋ hejaramɔ baawie; mibawie misusuma nidɔɔnii.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: Ani ŋshɔ loo bonso ji mi hewɔ ni otoɔ mɔ ko ni ebu mihe lɛ?”

english_verse: I go to bed, hoping for rest,
translation_verse: Kɛji mikɛɛ akɛ, “Misaa aaashɛje mimii, ni mipiŋmɔ he aaajɔ yɛ misaa nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: kɛkɛ lɛ okɛ lamɔi miiwo mihe gbeyei, ni okɛ ninai hãa ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ mi.

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: Ni no hewɔ lɛ, masumɔ ni amia misɛ̃ ni magbo moŋ fe nɔ ni makã lootãa wuiwui nɛɛ amli.

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: Jeŋhilɛ eje mitsine; mihiŋ shi kɛyaŋ naanɔ. Ŋmɛɛmɔ mihe, ejaakɛ miwala tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english_verse: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
translation_verse: Namɔ ji gbɔmɔ, hewɔ ni obuɔ ehe akɔntaa nɛkɛ, ni ojwɛŋɔ ehe kwraa po;

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: ni osaraa lɛ daa leebi, ni okaa lɛ okwɛɔ hiŋmɛitswaa fɛɛ hiŋmɛitswaa nɛɛ?

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Mɛɛ beyinɔ okpaŋ nii kwɛmɔ; mɛɛbe po oooŋmɛɛ mihe, koni mana be mami misɛŋ nu?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Bo adesai ahebulɔ, kɛji mifee esha lɛ, mɛni po mina mifee bo? Mɛɛba ni ojie ohiɛ oka mi? Mɛɛba mitsɔ̃ jatsu mihã mi diɛŋtsɛ nɔŋŋ mihe nɛɛ?

english_verse: Why do you refuse to forgive? Soon you won't find me, because I'll be dead.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba okɛ mitɔ̃mɔi lɛ efaaa mi koni ofɔ minɔsha lɛ yɛ mihe? Ejaakɛ agbɛnɛ su mli makã ni obaatao mi, shi onaŋ mi yɛ he ko he ko.”

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Mɛɛbe po ooohiɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ amli kɛyashi, onaa wiemɔi ni tamɔ ahum wulu nɛɛ?

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Ani Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ jalɛ hiɛ ebuɔ shi? Aloo Ofe lɛ kɔdɔ̃ɔ etoi eyeɔ sane?

english_verse: He made your children pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Kɛji obii lɛ tɔ̃ enɔ lɛ, no lɛ egbala amɛtoi bɔ ni sa amɛ.

english_verse: So why don't you turn to him
translation_verse: Kɛji obaatao Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni okpa Ofe lɛ fai,

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: ni kɛji ohe tse ni oja lɛ, no lɛ anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ baaye ebua bo, ni ebaaduro bo we kpakpa ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Osa shihilɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ko bibioo, shi owɔsɛɛ shihilɛ baafe nɔ wulu.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ wɔ lɛ, nyɛ kpaakpa nyɛ afɔ wɔ, ni wɔleee nɔ ko nɔ ko, ejaakɛ wɔgbii yɛ jeŋ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ.

english_verse: But they will instruct you with great understanding.
translation_verse: Ani blematsɛmɛi nɛɛ etsɔŋ bo nii; ani amɛgbaŋ bo, ani amɛwieŋ amɛnilee mli wiemɔi?

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Be mli ni amɛgba afofro, ni anako afolɔ lɛ, amɛŋalaa amɛshiɔ jwɛi krokomɛi fɛɛ.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni hiɛ kpaa Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ, bɔ ni amɛnaagbee yɔɔ nɛ; mɔ ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei lɛ, ehiɛnɔkãmɔ aaafite.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Ehiɛnɔkãmɔ mli tserɛɔ, ehiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ tamɔ anaanu ntaŋ.

english_verse: they take hold and fall because it's so flimsy.
translation_verse: Ehoɔ ekpasaa ewe lɛ, shi ewe lɛ nyɛɛɛ shi ema; emɔɔ mli waa; shi no nyɛɛɛ lɛ asɔo.”

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ shwereɔ yɛ hulu hiɛ, ni niji ni etsɛ̃rɛ lɛ haa etrom lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: Efãi blaa tɛi kui, etsɔ̃ɔ tɛsai amli tete.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Shi naa, miishɛɛ ni eyɔɔ ji akɛ gbɔmɛi krokomɛi baakwɛ̃ kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: “Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ kwaaa mɔ ni tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ ehe; ni asaŋ etooo he nine ehãaa efɔŋfeelɔi.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Ebaahã odaa aaayi obɔ̃ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni odaa ayi obɔ kɛ oshebɔɔ.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ohenyɛlɔi ahiɛ aaagboi, ni yiwalɔi awei aaalaaje.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: Mile lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ nakai ji sane lɛ, shi te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni adesa aja yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛŋ?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ ekɛ Nyɔŋmɔ aaataa naa lɛ, mɔ lɛ nyɛŋ Nyɔŋmɔ saji akpe mli ekome kɛkɛ naa ejie.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Nilelɔ ji lɛ, ni eyɛ hewalɛ; namɔ ete shi ewo lɛ, ni eye kunim pɛŋ?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Efãmɔɔ gɔji, ni amɛleee kwraa kɛji etsɔ̃mɔ amɛ ebu shi yɛ emlifu mli.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Ehosoɔ je lɛ kɛmɔɔ eshishitoo; ni ekulashiŋi ni tere je lɛ hosoɔ.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Efãa hulu, ni ehiii lɛ shitee; ni esɔoɔ ŋulamii anaa, ni amɛkpɛɛɛ.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: Lɛ ekoome ekpã ŋwɛi mli elɛɛ shi, ni enaanaa bonso nɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋ.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Lɛ ebɔ Jeŋ kpawo kɛ Oŋwɛ kɛ Wuɔ kɛ ebii kɛ wuoyigbɛ ŋulamii lɛ.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Efeɔ nibii wuji ni anaaa naa; kɛ naakpɛɛnii ni aleee amɛyibɔ.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Naa Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ mihe kɛhoɔ, ni minaaa lɛ; ehoɔ eyaa, ni miyooo lɛ.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Naa, nɔ ni etaoɔ lɛ ekɔɔ; namɔ aaanyɛ enaa atsi? Namɔ aaanyɛ akɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ?

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ eŋmɛŋ emlifu lɛ he, ni mɛi ni ye bua Rahab lɛ aaabakua lɛ.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã lɛ hetoo hu? Mɛɛ wiemɔi anɔ matsɔ̃ mi kɛ lɛ awie?

english_verse: Even though I am innocent, I can only beg for mercy.
translation_verse: Yɛ mli akɛ tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ mihe moŋ, shi minyɛŋ lɛ hetoo mahã; hewɔ lɛ fai moŋ makpa mikojolɔ lɛ.

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Kɛji mitsɛ lɛ ni ehere minɔ po, miheŋ miyeŋ akɛ eebo mi toi.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ekɛ ahum kumɔɔ mi, ni ehãa mifaji lɛ faa yakatswaa.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Ehãaa mana mumɔhe, shi ewoɔ mi jaramɔ moŋ.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Kɛji aaye lɛ hewalɛ naa lɛ, naa, lɛ nɛ; ni kɛji aafee jalɛnii lɛ, namɔ kɛ lɛ kedeɔ?

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: Shwamɔ ko bɛ mihe, shi mitsɛɛɛ mihe nɔ ko. Jeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Fɛɛ ekome!” No hewɔ lɛ, miikɛɛ akɛ, “Jeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine; mɔ ni shwamɔ bɛ ehe, kɛ mɔ fɔŋ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ baakpãtã amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Kɛji osharã gbe mɔ ko ni tɔ̃mɔ bɛ ehe lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ ŋmɔɔ.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Ekɛ je lɛ ewo mɔ fɔŋ dɛŋ; eha enɔ kojolɔi ahiɛ. Kɛjeee Nyɔŋmɔ ni lɛ, namɔ ni mɔ?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: “Migbii lɛ ahe yɛ oya fe foijolɔ, amɛhoɔ amɛyaa, ni amɛnaaa nɔ kpakpa ko.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Amɛhoɔ amɛyaa shwiaa tamɔ glã lɛji, tamɔ okropɔŋ gbaa eyiɔ kooloo nɔ.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Kɛji mikɛɛ majie mihiɛ yɛ mikɔmɔi lɛ anɔ, ni masaa mihiɛ, ni mana tsui lɛ,

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: mipiŋmɔi lɛ aaawo mihe gbeyei moŋ, ejaakɛ mile akɛ obuŋ mi bem.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
translation_verse: Ni abaabu mi fɔ kɛ̃; mɛɛba mɔ magba mihe naa yaka?

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Kɛji miju mihe kɛ snoo nu, ni mifɔ midɛ̃ hu kɛ samla lɛ,

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: kɛ̃lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ, oootsi mi owo bu mli; ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe atade tete aaahã mihe anyaŋe mi.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ jeee adesa tamɔ mi koni mahã lɛ hetoo; ni wɔya ni akojo wɔ yɛ kojomɔhe.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Mɔ ko bɛ ni aaadamɔ wɔteŋ, ni eeeŋɔ enine efɔ̃ wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔnɔ, ni ekpãtã wɔteŋ.

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: Hã ekpa mi piŋmɔ, koni ehe ŋmiŋmi akamɔ mi.

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ mawie, ni lɛ gbeyeishemɔ bɛ mli; ejaakɛ jeee nakai miyɔɔ.”

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: “Mijeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine. Mikɛ mikɔmɔi lɛ baashwie shi kpookpoo. Mibawie mitsui mli dɔlɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Don't just condemn me! Point out my sin.
translation_verse: Mibakɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, ‘Kaabu mi fɔ!’ Tsɔɔmɔ mi nɔ hewɔ ni okɛ mi ena nɛɛ.

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: Aso eja gbɛ yɛ ohiɛ, akɛ owa mɔ yi, ni onyaŋe bo diɛŋtsɛ oninenaa nitsumɔnii. Ni ona mɛi fɔ̃ji ayiŋtoi moŋ ahe tsuijurɔ lo?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Ani adesa hiŋmɛi ohiɛ, ni okwɛɔ nii tamɔ adesa?

english_verse: Is your life as short as ours?
translation_verse: Ani ogbii tamɔ adesa gbii, loo ofii tamɔ adesa afii;

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: hewɔ ni otiuɔ mitɔ̃mɔi asɛɛ, ni odiɔ esha ni mifee sɛɛ;

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: tsɛbelɛ ole akɛ miyeee fɔ, ni mɔ ko bɛ ni aaanyɛ ashɔ̃ mi yɛ odɛ̃ŋ?

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Kaimɔ akɛ okɛ sũ bɔ mi. Ani oohã matsɔ̃ sũ ekoŋŋ?

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Ohã mitsɛ hewalɛ, ni ekɛfɔ mi, ni ohã mida yɛ minyɛ musuŋ.

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Okɛ wui kɛ fãi tsara migbɔmɔtso, ni okɛ loo kɛ hewolo ha mihe.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Oduro mi wala, ni suɔmɔ ni okɛsumɔ mi sɛɛ efooo, ni odɛ̃ŋ kwɛmɔ ebaa miyi.

english_verse: You have not explained all of your mysteries,
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ okɛ nibii ni eba minɔ nɛɛ tee mi yɛ otsui mli, yɛ oyiŋtoo naa.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Kɛji mifee esha lɛ, okadiɔ ohãa mi, ni okɛ mitɔmɔ lɛ efaaa.

english_verse: No matter how hard I try, you keep hunting me down like a powerful lion.
translation_verse: Kɛji mikanya mihe lɛ, ogbɔbiɔ mi tamɔ jata, ni ofeɔ naakpɛɛ nibii oshiɔ mi.

english_verse: You never stop accusing me; you become furious and attack over and over again.
translation_verse: Otsakeɔ odasefoi ni wieɔ shiɔ mi, ni ohãa omlifu naa waa yɛ minɔ, ni ohãa ta nyiɛɔ ta sɛɛ kɛtuaa mi.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ, mɛɛba oŋmɛ gbɛ ni afɔ mi mɔ? Mina ni migbo dani hiŋmɛi ko na mi;

english_verse: and been carried to the grave without ever breathing.
translation_verse: ni kɛjɛ musuŋ lɛ awo mi ayafu, ni mitsɔ̃ tamɔ mɔ ko ni afɔko lɛ kwraa.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: Te miwala gbii faaa? Ŋmɛɛmɔ mihe koni mawo mitsui fioo,

english_verse: of darkness and despair, the place of no return.
translation_verse: duŋ kpii shikpɔŋ kɛ enɔ sakasaka, he ni la ji duŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: Hiob, aso owiemɔi babaoo nɛɛ aaahã mɛi afee dioo? Ni kɛji oye mɛi ahe fɛo lɛ, mɔ ko akawo bo hiɛgbele?

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Okɛɛ nɔ ni owieɔ lɛ anɔkwale ni, ni yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ lɛ ohe tse.

english_verse: But I wish God would speak
translation_verse: Oo, kulɛ Nyɔŋmɔ awie, egbɛ edaaŋ ekɛ bo awie,

english_verse: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
translation_verse: koni egbele teemɔŋ nilee hiɛ etsɔ̃ɔ bo, ejaakɛ enilee yɛ naakpɛɛ. Na ole akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ bo yeko bɔ ni sa otɔ̃mɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Can you understand the mysteries surrounding God All-Powerful?
translation_verse: Ani ooonyɛ ona Nyɔŋmɔ teemɔŋ nibii anaa? Ani ooonyɛ ole he ni Ofe lɛ hewalɛ yatãa?

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ kwɔ fe ŋwɛii amli ŋwɛi; mɛni obaanyɛ ofee yɛ he? Ni emli kwɔ voo fe gbohiiaje; mɛni obaanyɛ ofee yɛ he?

english_verse: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
translation_verse: Ekɛ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛlɛ, ni elɛɛ fe ŋshɔ.

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ ba, ni ebamɔ bo ewo kpabuŋ, ni etsɛ bo kojomɔ lɛ, namɔ aaanyɛ enaa atsi?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: Akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ le mɛi ni ji yakagbɔmɛi lɛ, kɛji ena nɔ sha lɛ, aso eeeku ehiɛ efɔ̃ nɔ?

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Kwashiai baabɔ̃i jwɛŋmɔ namɔ, be ni ŋaŋ teji baafɔ bi ni he jɔ tamɔ gbɔmɔ.

english_verse: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
translation_verse: Kɛji osaa otsuiŋ ekpakpa lɛ, ooohole oniji anɔ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.

english_verse: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
translation_verse: Kɛji nɔ sha ko yɛ odɛ̃ŋ lɛ, hã eya sɛɛ flɛŋŋ ni ogu nɔ ni ejaaa gbɛ yɛ owe lɛ mli.

english_verse: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ, anɔkwa, ooonyɛ ohiɛ nɔ owo, ni kpa ko bɛ ohe, ni ooona ekãa ni osheŋ gbeyei.

english_verse: Your troubles will go away like water beneath a bridge,
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ohiɛ aaakpa ohaomɔi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ; obaakai haomɔi lɛ tamɔ faaŋ nu ni eho etee kɛkɛ.

english_verse: and your darkest night will be brighter than noon.
translation_verse: Owala be mli aaatse fe shwane, ni kɛji duŋ wo yɛ mli tete lɛ, eeetsɔ tamɔ leebi.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Otsui aaakã omli, ejaakɛ oyɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ; Nyɔŋmɔ aaabu ohe, ni ooojɔɔ ohe, ni ooofee shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
translation_verse: Oookã shi, ni mɔ ko woŋ ohe gbeyei; mɛi babaoo aaababi odɛ̃ŋ wamɔ.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Shi mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ aaashwila, ni amɛnaŋ foijeehe. Amɛhiɛnɔkãmɔ pɛ ji gbele.”

english_verse: Job said to his friends:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: You think you are so great, with all the answers.
translation_verse: “Ŋwanejee bɛ he akɛ nyɛ ji maŋ lɛ, ni kɛji nyɛgboi pɛ, nilee hu egbo.

english_verse: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
translation_verse: Shi mi hu miyɛ jwɛŋmɔ tamɔ nyɛ nɔŋŋ; Nyɛfeee mi nilee. Namɔ leee wiemɔi ni nyɛwie nɛɛ?

english_verse: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
translation_verse: Naa mi ni mitsɔ̃ hefɛoyeli nɔ mihã minanemɛi. Mi ni mitsɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, ni ehereɔ mi nɔ, ni miyeɔ jalɛ sane, ni shwamɔ ko bɛ mihe lɛ; mi, mitsɔ̃ hefɛoyeli nɔ nɛɛ.

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Julɔi atoiiaŋ ejɔ amɛ yɛ amɛshĩai amli, ni mɛi ni woɔ Nyɔŋmɔ mli la hu yɛ shweshweeshwe, tsɛbelɛ amɛhewalɛ ji amɛnyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: Bo lɛ bi kooloi, ni amɛaatsɔ̃ɔ bo nii; bi loofɔji, ni amɛaagba bo sane;

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: Te nibii nɛɛ ateŋ nɔ ni leee akɛ Yehowa nine ji nɔ ni bɔ lɛ lɛ?

english_verse: Every living creature is in the hands of God.
translation_verse: Lɛ edɛŋ nibii fɛɛ ni muɔ awala kɛ adesa mumɔ fɛɛ yɔɔ.

english_verse: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
translation_verse: Bɔ ni toi kaa wiemɔi ekwɛɔ lɛ, nakai lilɛi hu saa niyenii naa ekwɛɔ.

english_verse: and gain some wisdom from those who have lived a long time.
translation_verse: Nilee yɛ onukpai adɛŋ, shi walasɛɛtsɛlɛ mli jwɛŋmɔ yɔɔ.

english_verse: But God is the real source of wisdom and strength.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, eyɛ nilee kɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋaawoo kɛ jwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ.

english_verse: just as he rules over liars and those they lie to.
translation_verse: Lɛ edɛŋ hewalɛ kɛ nilee fɛɛ yɔɔ; mɔ ni eshishiuɔ mɔ kɛ mɔ ni ashishiuɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, enɔ ji amɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: God shames counselors, turns judges into fools,
translation_verse: Ehãa nilee ŋmɛɔ ajinafoi, ni ehãa kojolɔi tsɔ̃ɔ kwashiai.

english_verse: and makes slaves of kings.
translation_verse: Ekpaa maŋtsɛmɛi, ni ekɛ kpãa fimɔɔ amɛhɛ.

english_verse: God removes priests and others who have great power—
translation_verse: Ekpɔlɔɔ osɔfoi ahewulamɔnii yɛ amɛhe, ni ebaa mɛi ni hiɛ hewalɛ shi.

english_verse: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
translation_verse: Ehãa lumɛi ahe guɔ gboɔ, ni efoɔ hewalɔi ahewalɛ sɛɛ.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: Eshɔ̃ɔ nilee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii amaŋtsɛmɛi adɛŋ; ni ehãa amɛtsomloɔ yɛ ŋa nɔ he ni nanegbɛ tete bɛ.

english_verse: lost in the dark, staggering like someone drunk.
translation_verse: Amɛgbugbuɔ shi yɛ duŋ ni la ko bɛ mli lɛ mli, ni ehãa amɛdidãa tamɔ dãatɔlɔi.

english_verse: I know and understand every bit of this.
translation_verse: Naa, mina nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ kɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihiŋmɛi, ni mitoi hu enu, ni minu shishi.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni nyɛle lɛ, mi hu mile; nyɛfeee mi yɛ enɛɛmɛi agbɛfaŋ.

english_verse: But I prefer to argue my case with God All-Powerful—
translation_verse: Shi mi lɛ Ofe lɛ mitaoɔ mikɛwie, Nyɔŋmɔ ji mɔ ni mitaoɔ mikɛyiyi ni matsɔ̃ɔ lɛ misane lɛ naa.

english_verse: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
translation_verse: Shi nyɛ lɛ, nyɛkɛ abla eto nyɛhiɛ, tsofatsɛmɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko mli ji nyɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Oo, nyɛmuaa nyɛnaa moŋ kulɛ eeehi pam, ejaakɛ no aaatsɔ̃ nyɛnilee.

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: Ani nyɛmiiwie kɛmiifã Nyɔŋmɔ he lo? Ani nyɛbaawie nyɛhã Nyɔŋmɔ?

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: Ani kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ tao nyɛsaji amli lɛ, nyɛaaye nyɛhe? Ani nyɛaanyɛ nyɛlaka Nyɔŋmɔ tamɔ alakaa adesa lo?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ baakã nyɛhiɛ kɛji nyɛkwɛ hiɛiaŋ yɛ dujiaŋ tete.

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: Aso egbojee lɛ woŋ nyɛhe gbeyei ni ehe ŋmiŋmi hu mɔŋ nyɛ?

english_verse: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
translation_verse: Abɛi ni nyɛbubuɔ lɛ tamɔ lamlu; wiemɔi ni nyɛkɛfãa nyɛhe lɛ tamɔ magbɛ.

english_verse: Be quiet while I speak, and we'll see what happens.
translation_verse: Nyɛfea dioo koni manyɛ mawie, ni nɔ ni aaaba minɔ lɛ aba.

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ hewɔ maŋɔ miheloo makɔ̃ minaa koni mahiɛ miwala yɛ midɛŋ?

english_verse: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
translation_verse: Naa, kɛji eeegbe mi tete lɛ, mibɛ sane ko; mibafã mijeŋba he yɛ ehiɛ kɛ̃.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Enɛ nɔŋŋ aaatsɔ̃ miyiwalaheremɔ, ejaakɛ mɔ fɔŋ nyɛŋ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ aba.

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: Naa, misaa minaajiemɔ mito; mile akɛ abaabu mi bem.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: Namɔ yɔɔ jɛi ni ekɛ mi batao naa? Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ ni lɛ, no lɛ mibafee diŋŋ koni magbo kɛkɛ.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: Feemɔ nibii enyɔ nɛɛ pɛ ohã mi, ni miteŋ mihe yɛ ohiɛ.

english_verse: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
translation_verse: Oo Nyɔŋmɔ, tsɛ mi, ni mibahere bo nɔ, aloo ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni mawie ni ohã mi hetoo.

english_verse: Please point out my sins, so I will know them.
translation_verse: Minishaianii kɛ mihe eshai lɛ, enyiɛ ni? Hã male minishaianii kɛ mihe eshai lɛ.

english_verse: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
translation_verse: Mɛɛba okɛ ohiɛ teɔ mi, ni obuɔ mi akɛ ohenyɛlɔ lɛ?

english_verse: Do you really enjoy frightening a fallen leaf?
translation_verse: Aso obaafã baa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ehuu lɛ tsui; ni obaanyiɛ abele shishi tutuu sɛɛ?

english_verse: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ okɛ saji ni naa wa miishi mi, ootsɛ miblahiaŋ tɔ̃mɔi tete asɛɛ.

english_verse: You have tied my feet down and keep me surrounded;
translation_verse: Obɔ minaji apã, ni ohiŋmɛi kã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mifeɔ he; minanefaamɔi hu owo he husu.

english_verse: I am rotting away like cloth eaten by worms.
translation_verse: Adesa tamɔ nɔ ko ni ekpɔtɔ, etamɔ mama ni omlɛgɛ eye.

english_verse: We are flowers that fade and shadows that vanish.
translation_verse: Ewala nɛɛ tamɔ fɔfɔi; ekwɛ̃ɔ, ni eŋalaa shwiaa; ehoɔ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ, ni etsɛɛɛ.

english_verse: And so, I ask you, God, why pick on me?
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ ona be ookwɛ lɛ, ni ootao okɛ lɛ aye sane lo?

english_verse: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
translation_verse: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ana nɔ ni he tse kɛ nɔ ni he tseee teŋ srɔto lɛ?

english_verse: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
translation_verse: Akɛni ato ewala be lɛ, ni nyɔji abɔ ni ebaaye yɛ odɛ̃ŋ lɛ, belɛ owo ewala he husu momo.

english_verse: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
translation_verse: Jiemɔ ohiɛ yɛ enɔ; kaafo edaaŋ koni emii ashɛ ehe yɛ ewala mli tamɔ apaafonyo.

english_verse: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
translation_verse: Tso tete yɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ akɛ kɛji atoo lɛ lɛ, eeehere ekoŋŋ, ni niji ni ebaatsɛ̃rɛ lɛ baadara, amɛgboiŋ.

english_verse: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
translation_verse: shi nu ni eeena nɛkɛ pɛ, eeetsɛ̃ ekoŋŋ, ni eeetsɛ̃rɛ niji tamɔ tso ŋmɔŋ.

english_verse: Humans are different— we die, and that's the end.
translation_verse: Shi gbɔmɔ gboɔ, ni enyɔɔ shi. Kɛji mumɔ na fã yɛ emli lɛ, nɛgbɛ lɛ yɔɔ dɔŋŋ?

english_verse: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
translation_verse: Bɔ ni nu tãa yɛ kpaakpo mli, ni faa miiɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ,

english_verse: we fall into the sleep of death, never to rise again, until the sky disappears.
translation_verse: nakai gbɔmɔ hoɔ ekãa shi ni eteee shi dɔŋŋ. Kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni ŋwɛi aaaho aya lɛ, ehiɛ etsɛŋ, ni atsiɛŋ lɛ yɛ wɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
translation_verse: Mina ni kulɛ oŋɔ mi otee yɛ gbohiiaje, ni oŋɔ mi ohɔ shi kɛyashi beyinɔ ni omlifu lɛ aaaho, koni oto be ohã mi, ni okai mi.

english_verse: Will we humans live again? I would gladly suffer and wait for my time.
translation_verse: Kɛji gbɔmɔ gbo lɛ, ehiɛ aaakã ekoŋŋ? Mibato mitsui shi mamɛ yɛ misɔ̃ɔmɔ be lɛ mli kɛyaashi be aaashɛ ni aaaŋmɛ̃ɛ mihe.
