english_verse: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
translation_verse: nyɛŋɔŋɔa yei ni nyɛfɔfɔɔ bihii kɛ biyei; nyɛŋɔa ŋamɛi hu nyɛhãa nyɛbihii; nyɛkɛ nyɛbiyei lɛ ahãa gbãlã koni amɛ hu amɛfɔfɔɔ, bɔ ni afee ni nyɛyi afa yɛ jɛi, koni nyɛnɔ akagbɔ!

english_verse: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
translation_verse: Shi nyɛtaoa maŋ nɔ ni mihã aŋɔ nyɛ nom kɛtee lɛ nɔyaa kɛ eshweremɔ; ni nyɛsɔlea nyɛkpaa Yehowa fai nyɛhãa maŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ kɛji maŋ lɛ he jɔ lɛ lɛ, no dani nyɛ hu nyɛhe baajɔ nyɛ.

english_verse: I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering.
translation_verse: “Mi pɛ mile jwɛŋmɔi ni mijwɛŋɔ yɛ nyɛhe, nyɛhe jwɛŋmɔi kpakpa, shi jeee efɔŋ, nɔ ni baahã nyɛ wɔsɛɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ aba mli ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ nyɛaafo nyɛtsɛ mi, ni nyɛaaba nyɛbasɔle nyɛkpa mi fai, ni mibabo nyɛ toi.

english_verse: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
translation_verse: Nyɛaatao mi, ni nyɛaana mi, kɛji nyɛtao misɛɛgbɛ kɛ nyɛtsui fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
translation_verse: “Shi kɛɛmɔ ni nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Yehowa etee gbalɔi ashi yɛ Babilon ehã wɔ, hewɔ lɛ,’

english_verse: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
translation_verse: Nyɛboa Yehowa wiemɔ toi, nyɛ nomii fɛɛ ni mihã nyɛshi Yerusalɛm kɛtee Babilon,

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
translation_verse: bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Akɛni oŋmala woji yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ogbɛi mli okɛmaje abahã Yerusalɛm maŋbii blublu kɛ Maaseia bi Zefania, ni ji osɔfo lɛ, kɛ osɔfoi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
translation_verse: Yehowa ewo bo osɔfo yɛ Osɔfo Yehoiada najiaŋ koni otsɔ̃ Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ nɔkwɛlɔ koni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yiŋ kãa lɛ ni efeɔ ehe gbalɔ lɛ, obɔ lɛ apã ni owo lɛ gboklɛ lɛ,

english_verse: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
translation_verse: mɛɛba ni okãaa Yeremia, Anatotnyo lɛ, ni egbaa etsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ lɛ?

english_verse: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ekɛ wiemɔ emaje akɛbahã wɔ yɛ Babilon nɛɛ akɛ, nyɛnomŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ baatsɛ; nyɛmamɔa tsui ni nyɛhia mli; ni nyɛfea abɔi koni nyɛye amɛmli yibii.’ ”

english_verse: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Zefania kane nɛkɛ wolo nɛɛ yɛ Gbalɔ Yeremia toiŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
translation_verse: “Tsu kɛya ni ayakɛɛ nomii lɛ akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ yɛ Shemaia, Nehelamnyo lɛ he ji enɛ: Shemaia egba gbalɛi etsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ be mli ni mitsuko lɛ, ni ehã nyɛkɛ nyɛhiɛ efɔ amale nɔ.’

english_verse: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, mi, Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ, ‘Naa, mibagbala Shemaia, Nehelamnyo lɛ, kɛ eshwiei fɛɛ atoi. Eshwiei ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ ni ehiŋmɛii baana ejurɔ ni mibafee miwebii lɛ. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ, ejaakɛ ewie wiemɔ ni baahã maŋbii lɛ atse atua awo mi Yehowa.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
translation_verse: Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Ŋmãa wiemɔi ni mikɛ bo ewie lɛ fɛɛ owo wolo mli.

english_verse: Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
translation_verse: Shi naa, gbii miiba ni mibahã miwebii Israelbii kɛ Yudabii anine ashɛ amɛnibii fɛɛ ni amɛlaaje lɛ anɔ. Mikɛ amɛ baaku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni amɛbaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ amɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
translation_verse: Nyɛbia nyɛkwɛa; Ani nuu ekɔ̃mɔ efɔ bi pɛŋ? Mɛɛba mɔ ni minaa nuu fɛɛ nuu efua emusu tamɔ yoo ni miikɔmɔ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hiɛ eshale nɛkɛ?

english_verse: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
translation_verse: Ao! Nakai gbi lɛ, gbi wulu ni; ehenɔ bako pɛŋ. Yakob hejaramɔ gbi ni, kɛ̃lɛ abaahere eyiwala yɛ gbele mli.”

english_verse: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
translation_verse: Ni mi, Yehowa Taiatsɛ, miikɛɛ akɛ nakai gbi lɛ mibakumɔ apã lɛ yɛ amɛkuɛ, ni mibatserɛ kpãi ni fimɔ amɛ lɛ; ni mɛi kpɔji yeŋ amɛ nyɔŋ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
translation_verse: Shi moŋ amɛbaasɔ̃mɔ Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ David shwie ni mibato lɛ maŋtsɛ mibahã amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bo, mitsulɔ Yakob, kaashe gbeyei; ni Israel, otsui akafã, ejaakɛ mibahere nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei hu, kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛjɛ amɛnomŋɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yakob baaku esɛɛ eba ni ebahi shi yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ kɛ hejɔlɛ mli; ni mɔ ko mɔ ko woŋ ehe gbeyei. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mikɛ nyɛ yɛ koni mahere nyɛyiwala. Mibakpãtã majimaji fɛɛ ni migbɛ nyɛ mishwã amɛnɔ lɛ ahiɛ kɛmɔ shi. Shi bo lɛ, mikpãtãŋ ohiɛ kɛmɔŋ shi; shi kɛ̃lɛ mibagbala otoi bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ, ni mihaŋ oŋɔ ohe oye tswaa.”

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ, mi Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛpilamɔ lɛ bɛ tsabaa, ni nyɛfala lɛ ewo wu.

english_verse: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
translation_verse: Mɔ ko bɛ ni baaye nyɛsane lɛ; nyɛfala lɛ he tsofa bɛ lɛ, nyɛhela lɛ bɛ tsabaa.

english_verse: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
translation_verse: Nyɛsuɔlɔi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ ekpa nyɛnɔ, jeee amɛhe sane ko ji nyɛ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ mitswa nyɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ nɔŋŋ ni henyɛlɔ baatswa nyɛ nɔ; ejaakɛ nyɛtɔ̃mɔ lɛ da.

english_verse: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
translation_verse: Shi mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kpãtãa nyɛhiɛ lɛ, aaakpãtã ehiɛ; ni abaaŋɔ nyɛhenyɛlɔi ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nom. Mɛi fɛɛ ni aaaha nyɛ nii lɛ aaaha amɛ nii; ni mɛi ni feɔ nyɛ niseniianii lɛ, mahã afee amɛ niseniianii.

english_verse: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mahã nyɛna hewalɛ ekoŋŋ, ni matsa nyɛfaji lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛtsɛ bo mɔ ni ashwie lɛ, ‘Zion ni jeee mɔ ko he sane ji lɛ.’ Mi, Yehowa mikɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
translation_verse: Naa, mibahã miwebii ashwere ekoŋŋ; ni mimusuŋ aaatsɔ̃ mi yɛ shĩa fɛɛ shĩa he. Abaasaa Yerusalɛm atswa ama egɔ̃ŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ni mɔɔ lɛ aaama etsutsu maahe lɛ.

english_verse: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
translation_verse: Shidaa lalai aaagbɛɛ kɛjɛ mli, mɛi ni miinya agbee aaajije kɛjɛ jɛi. Mibahã amɛyi afa, ni amɛnɔ gbɔŋ; mibawo amɛhiɛ nyam; abuŋ amɛ akɛ maŋ bibioo.

english_verse: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
translation_verse: Amɛbii ashihilɛ aaafee tamɔ sa shihilɛ, ni amɛsafo lɛ baahe shi yɛ mihiɛ, ni mibagbala mɛi fɛɛ ni waa amɛyi lɛ atoi.

english_verse: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
translation_verse: Amɛteŋ mɔ ko nɔŋŋ baatsɔ̃ amɛlumɔ; amɛnɔyelɔ lɛ baajɛ amɛ nɔŋŋ amɛteŋ. Mahã etsi ebɛŋkɛ mi, ni ebaaba mimasɛi, ejaakɛ namɔ aaanyɛ ashi etsitsi, ni eba mi, mimasɛi? Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
translation_verse: Naa, Yehowa mlifu lɛ, ahum ni, ni efã kɛje kpo tamɔ lasuogbele, ni ebaalota mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ kɛya.

english_verse: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
translation_verse: Yehowa mlifu ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ efoŋ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni nɔ ni eto eyiŋ akɛ ebaafee lɛ, ena efee kɛgbe naa. Wɔsɛɛ ko dani nyɛaanu sane nɛɛ shishi faŋŋ.

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Be ko miiba, ni nakai be lɛ mibatsɔ̃ Israel akutsei lɛ fɛɛ aNyɔŋmɔ, ni amɛ hu amɛbaatsɔ̃ miwebii.

english_verse: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
translation_verse: Maŋbii ni je klante naa gbele mli lɛ, mina amɛ mɔbɔ yɛ shiaŋa lɛ mli. Be ni Israel shwe ni ena hejɔlɛ lɛ,

english_verse: Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say: Israel, I will always love you; that's why I've been so patient and kind.
translation_verse: mi Yehowa, mijie mihe kpo yɛ shɔŋŋ mitsɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Misumɔ bo kɛ naanɔ suɔmɔ; no hewɔ ni mikã he misumɔɔ bo lolo lɛ.

english_verse: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
translation_verse: Ao! Oblayoo foro Israel! Mibasaa matswa bo tamɔ tsu mama shi ekoŋŋ, ni oooma shi hu. Oookɔlɔ omiji lɛ otsotsoro ekoŋŋ ni oooje kpo okɛ mɛi ni amli efili amɛ aaayajo kɛ miishɛɛ.

english_verse: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
translation_verse: Ooofee waintromii yɛ Samaria gɔji lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ, ni mɛi ni tɛoɔ waintsei lɛ baaye tsei lɛ ayibii.

english_verse: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ko miiba, ni bulɔi aaabolɔ yɛ Efraim gɔji lɛ anɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛtea shi koni wɔya Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ yɛ Zion.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Nyɛlaa waa kɛ miishɛɛ nyɛhãa Israel nyɛbɔa oshe nyɛhãa maji fɛɛ ayitso lɛ. Nyɛshiɛa, nyɛkafoa, ni nyɛkɛa akɛ, ‘Yehowa ehere ewebii Israelbii ni shwɛ lɛ ayiwala.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
translation_verse: Naa, mibakpala amɛ kɛjɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ naagbeehei tɔ̃ɔ. Mikɛ asafo yuu ni shwilafoi kɛ akpaketsɛmɛi kɛ yeihɔlɔi kɛ yeifɔyei fɛɛ tswɛm futu mli aaaku sɛɛ aba biɛ nɛɛ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
translation_verse: Amɛbaaba kɛ yaafo kɛ faikpamɔ ni mibakpala amɛ kɛku sɛɛ kɛba. Mibahã amɛnyiɛ fai atoii kɛ gbɛ trɔmɔɔ nɔ, he ni amɛtɛrɛŋ yɛ. Ejaakɛ Israel Tsɛ ji mi, ni mikromɔbi ji Efraim.

english_verse: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
translation_verse: “Nyɛ majimaji, nyɛboa mi toi, ni nyɛgbaa yɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa majiaŋ. Nyɛkɛa akɛ, ‘Mɔ ni gbɛ Israel shwã lɛ ebaabua amɛnaa, ni ebaakwɛ amɛ tamɔ tookwɛlɔ kwɛɔ etoo ku pɛ.

english_verse: I will rescue them from enemies who could overpower them.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa ekpɔ̃ Israel, ni ehere lɛ yɛ mɔ ni he wa tsɔ̃ fe lɛ lɛ dɛŋ.

english_verse: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
translation_verse: Amɛbaaba ni amɛbala waa kɛ nyamɔ yɛ Zion Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni amɛmii baashɛ Yehowa mlihilɛ lɛ he, yɛ abele kɛ wain kɛ mu, kɛ toobii kɛ tsinai ahewɔ. Amɛshihilɛ baatsɔ̃ tamɔ abɔɔ ni ashwie emlinii nɔ nu, ni amɛtɔŋ biti dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ oblayei lɛ baajo kɛ nyamɔ, ni oblahii kɛ hiimeji amii aaashɛ amɛhe. Mibahã amɛkɔmɔyeli atsɔ̃ mliflimɔ; mibashɛje amɛmii, ni yɛ awerɛho najiaŋ lɛ mahã amɛnya.

english_verse: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
translation_verse: Mibahã osɔfoi ana nii babaoo amɛye amɛtɔrɔ, ni mimaŋbii lɛ atsui aaatɔ kɛ mimlihilɛ lɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.’ ” Yehowa na Israel mɔbɔ

english_verse: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Anu gbee ko yɛ Rama, yarawoo kɛ yaafo ni mli wa; Rahel miifo ebii ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ kpãtãmɔ yɛ ebii lɛ ahewɔ ejaakɛ amɛbɛ.”

english_verse: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Fɔ̃ɔmɔ yaafo lɛ, ohiŋmɛiŋ akakpala nu; ejaakɛ abaawo bo onii ni otsu lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ akɛ, Obii lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ henyɛlɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba.

english_verse: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
translation_verse: “Minu ni Israel ye ŋkɔmɔ akɛ, ‘Ogbala mitoi, ni okɛtsɔse mi tamɔ tsinabi ni atsɔseko lɛ. Kpalemɔ mi kɛba oŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ, ni mibakpale, ejaakɛ bo ji Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
translation_verse: Be ni mikwa bo lɛ, mishwa mihe; ni be ni atsɔ̃ɔ mi nii sɛɛ lɛ, miyi mishuɔ he ma; mihiɛ gbo, ni mihiɛ shwie shi, ejaakɛ miblahiaŋ hiɛgbele lɛ kpɛ misɛɛ lolo.’

english_verse: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Israel ji mibinuu kpakpa lɛ. Lɛ ji misuɔmɔ bi lɛ. Shii abɔ fɛɛ ni miwieɔ mishiɔ lɛ lɛ, mikaiɔ lɛ kɛ̃ kɛ dɔlɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mitsui shweɔ lɛ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ mana lɛ mɔbɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
translation_verse: Mãamɔ gbɛkadimɔ nii ohã ohe; too okadii ni aaatsɔ̃ɔ bo gbɛ. Jwɛŋmɔ gbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ, gbɛ ni onyiɛ nɔ kɛtee lɛ. Ao! Oblayoo foro Israel! Kpalemɔ kɛba omaji nɛɛ amli.

english_verse: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
translation_verse: Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ oooshashao shi kɛyashi, bo, biyoo ni yeee anɔkwa? Ejaakɛ naa, mi, Yehowa, mikɛ nɔ hee ko eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yoo dedenyɛ miibu nuu he.” Nyɔŋmɔ Webii baashwere wɔsɛɛ

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa, Taiatsɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɔ nɛ, “Kɛji mihã amɛnine shɛ amɛnibii ni amɛlaaje lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ, amɛbaakɛɛ yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ enɔ maji lɛ amli akɛ, ‘Bo shihilɛhe ni ayeɔ jalɛ sane yɛ omli, Yehowa ajɔɔ bo, bo Gɔŋ Krɔŋkrɔŋ.’

english_verse: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji fɛɛ amli baahi shi akɛ gbɔmɛi kome, okwaafoi kɛ tookwɛlɔi ni kɛ amɛtoi kpaa shi;

english_verse: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
translation_verse: ejaakɛ mibahã mɔ ni etɔ lɛ mii ashɛ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni hɔmɔ ehã etɔ biti lɛ mahã ena nii eye ni etɔ.”

english_verse: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mihiɛ tsɛ̃, ni mina akɛ miwɔ wɔ kpakpa.

english_verse: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, be ko miiba, ni nakai be lɛ mahã gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi hu afɛo yɛ Israel kɛ Yuda fɛɛ tamɔ dumɔwu.

english_verse: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
translation_verse: Ni ebaaba mli akɛ bɔ ni mishi amɛhe kpe ni mifamɔ amɛ mishwie, ni mikumɔ amɛ mishwie shi, ni mibutu amɛ, ni mikpãtã amɛhiɛ ni mifee amɛ efɔŋ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ mashi amɛhe kpe ni matɛo amɛ, ni matswa amɛ mama shi.

english_verse: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ amɛkɛŋ dɔŋŋ akɛ, ‘Tsɛmɛi eye wainyibii ŋmilikitii, ni bii moŋ anyanyɔji eshɔ̃.’

english_verse: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Shi moŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yeɔ wainyibii ŋmilikiti lɛ, lɛ enyanyɔŋ baashɔ̃, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baagbo yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔsha hewɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ, “Naa be miiba, ni nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, mi kɛ Israel kɛ Yuda hu baakpãŋ kpãŋmɔ hee.

english_verse: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
translation_verse: Kpãŋmɔ hee nɛɛ tamɔɔɔ kpãŋmɔ ni mi kɛ amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kpãŋ be ni mimɔ amɛnine shi ni mikpala amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nakai mikpãŋmɔ lɛ amɛku mli, tsɛbelɛ mi ji amɛwu.

english_verse: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: Kpãŋmɔ hee ni mikɛ Israel baakpãŋ yɛ nakai gbi lɛ sɛɛ nɛ: Mibaŋɔ mimla lɛ mawo amɛmli, ni mibaŋmã mlai lɛ mawo amɛtsuii amli, ni mibatsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ, ni amɛbaatsɔ mimaŋ.

english_verse: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
translation_verse: Ni mɔ ko etsɔŋ enaanyo, ni mɔ ko hu etsɔŋ enyɛmi dɔŋŋ akɛ, ‘Le Yehowa’, ejaakɛ amɛ fɛɛ kwa amɛaale mi, kɛjɛ amɛteŋ mɔ bibioo nɔ kɛyashi mɔ wulu nɔ, ejaakɛ mikɛ amɛnishaianii lɛ baafa amɛ, ni mikaiŋ eshai ni amɛfee lɛ dɔŋŋ. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa, Lɛ mɔ ni ebɔ hulu koni etso shwane; ni eto nyɔɔŋtsere kɛ ŋulamii gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkpɛ nyɔɔŋ; Lɛ mɔ ni etaa ŋshɔ mli ni ehãa ŋshɔkei huuɔ ni egbɛi ji Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ,

english_verse: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Miikɛɛ akɛ ja gbɛjianɔ ni ato nɛɛ sɛɛ efo yɛ mihiɛ, no dani Israelbii ashwiei ayi aaatã, ni amɛfeŋ maŋ yɛ mihiɛ dɔŋŋ kɛaatee naanɔ.”

english_verse: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kɛji aaanyɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ wɔyiteŋ nɛɛ asusu, ni aaanyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo shi akpa lɛ, no lɛ, mi hu makwa Israel fɛɛ kwa yɛ nibii fɛɛ ni amɛfee lɛ ahewɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, be miiba, ni abaasaa atswa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ ahã mi, Yehowa, kɛjɛ Hananel Mɔɔ ni kwɔ lɛ he kɛyashi Koŋ Agbo lɛ naa.

english_verse: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
translation_verse: Abaatsa husu lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ jɛi tɛ̃ɛ kɛyatsɔ̃ Gareb Gɔ̃ŋkpɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaadɔ eyi kɛya Goa.

english_verse: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_verse: Jɔɔ ni eyi obɔ̃ kɛ gbohii kɛ tumo lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ aahu kɛyashi Kidron Faa lɛ naa, kɛyashi Okpɔŋɔi Agbo lɛ koŋ ni ye bokãgbɛ lɛ he lɛ, enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ baatsɔ̃ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ahã Yehowa. Akumɔŋ, ni abutuŋ maŋ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ kɔkɔɔkɔ kɛaatee naanɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma, ni ji Nebukadnezar yinɔ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ, lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards.
translation_verse: No mli lɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ tabilɔi miisa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ yi, ni atsi Gbalɔ Yeremia naa yɛ Bulɔi Akpo lɛ nɔ yɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli.

english_verse: Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said: I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia ewo Yeremia kpabuŋ ejaakɛ ekɛɛ Yeremia kɛɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Naa miijɔɔ maŋ nɛɛ nɔ miihã Babilon Maŋtsɛ, ni ebaaŋɔ.

english_verse: King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia ejeŋ Babilonbii lɛ adɛŋ kɔkɔɔkɔ; shi abaamɔ lɛ, ni akɛ lɛ baawo Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ, Ebaana lɛ kɛ ehiŋmɛitsei enyɔ, ni ekɛ lɛ baawie hiɛ kɛ hiɛ;

english_verse: Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: ni Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ baakpala Zedekia kɛya Babilon; ni Zedekia baaya eyahi jɛi kɛyashi beyinɔ ni mibana lɛ mɔbɔ. Kɛji nyɛ kɛ Babilonbii lɛ wu tete po lɛ, nyɛyeŋ kunim. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yeremia kɛɛ akɛ, “Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
translation_verse: Naa, Hanamel ni ji otsɛkwɛ Shalum binuu lɛ baaba oŋɔɔ ebakɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Miihɔ̃ɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Anatot lɛ. Hemɔ, ejaakɛ bo oyɔɔ hegbɛ akɛ okpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.’

english_verse: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Hanamel, mitsɛkwɛ binuu lɛ ba miŋɔɔ yɛ Bulɔi Akpo lɛ nɔ, bɔ pɛ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ ebakɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Miihɔ̃ɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Anatot yɛ Benyaminbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Hemɔ, ejaakɛ bo oyɔɔ hegbɛ akɛ oyeɔ gboshinii; ni no hewɔ lɛ, bo oyɔɔ hegbɛ akɛ okpɔ̃ɔ, hewɔ lɛ hemɔ ohã ohe.’ Kɛkɛ ni mina akɛ Yehowa kɛ mi ewie lɛɛlɛŋ.

english_verse: Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything.
translation_verse: “Ao! Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, bo obɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ohewalɛ kpeteŋkple lɛ kɛ onyɛmɔ naa; nɔ ko nɔ ko shɛɛɛ bo feemɔ.

english_verse: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
translation_verse: ni mikɛ woji lɛ hã Baruk, ni ji Maesia bi Neria bi lɛ, yɛ mitsɛkwɛ binuu Hanamel hiɛ. Odasefoi lɛ ni kɛ amɛgbɛii wo nihɔɔmɔ nɔ woji lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ Yudafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Bulɔi Akpo lɛ koi lɛ shi lɛ hu yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: I told Baruch that the Lord had said: Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
translation_verse: ‘Bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɛ, ji akɛ, ohe nɛkɛ woji nɛɛ ni ji nihɔɔmɔ nɔ wolo ni asɔo naa kɛ nɔ ni asɔoko naa nɛɛ fɛɛ koni okɛyato gbɛ mli, bɔ ni afee ni wolo lɛ atsɛ be babaoo.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, abaatse shika akɛhe shĩa kɛ ŋmɔ kɛ waintrom ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.’ ” Yeremia sɔlemɔ lɛ

english_verse: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Osuɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo hã mɛi akpeiakpei abɔ; shi okɛ tsɛmɛi anishaianii lɛ ahe toigbalamɔ hãa amɛbii ni baa yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Ao! Nyɔŋmɔ hewalɔ kpele, bo ni ogbɛi ji Yehowa Taiatsɛ,

english_verse: With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
translation_verse: oŋaalee mli kwɔ, ni ofeɔ nibii wuji. Bo ni onaa gbɔmɛi ajeŋbai fɛɛ, ni bɔ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nifeemɔ yɔɔ lɛ nakai he nyɔmɔ owoɔ lɛ; ni nɔ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ duɔ lɛ no yibii ohãa ekpaa.

english_verse: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
translation_verse: Ofee okadii kɛ naakpɛɛ nibii yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ oofee nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ Israel kɛ majimaji blublu anɔ, ni okɛhe gbɛi tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: Otsɔ̃ okadii kɛ naakpɛɛ nibii kɛ ohewalɛ lɛ kɛ onyɛmɔ ni hã ashe gbeyei lɛ nɔ ni ojie owebii kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
translation_verse: ni oŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ni okã amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kitã yɛ he akɛ okɛbaahã amɛ lɛ ohã amɛ, eji shikpɔŋ kɛ emli fɔ ni baa nii.

english_verse: Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
translation_verse: “Naa, kpokui ni maŋ lɛ yisalɔi lɛ tswaa amɛkɛsa maŋ lɛ yi lɛ, enina maŋ lɛ etã; ni abaaŋɔ maŋ lɛ. Klante kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela baahã Babilonbii ni ebatua maŋ lɛ aye maŋ lɛ nɔ kunim. Owiemɔ lɛ eba mli, ni oona.

english_verse: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
translation_verse: Tsɛbelɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, bo nɔŋŋ okɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Tse shika okɛhe shikpɔŋ lɛ; ni otsɛ mɛi abaye he odase; asomoaŋ ojɔɔ maŋ lɛ nɔ owo Babilonbii lɛ adɛŋ momo!’ ”

english_verse: Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
translation_verse: “Naa, mi ji Yehowa, gbɔmɛi adesai fɛɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Ani nɔ ko shɛɔ mi feemɔ?

english_verse: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, naa, miijɔɔ maŋ nɛɛ nɔ miiwo Babilonbii kɛ amɛmaŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar dɛŋ, koni amɛbaŋɔ.

english_verse: The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
translation_verse: Babilonbii ni ebatua maŋ lɛ baana abote maŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛbaama maŋ lɛ naa la koni amɛshã. Amɛbaashã shĩai ni maŋbii lɛ shã tsofakɛŋma yɛ amɛyiteiaŋ amɛkɛhã Baal, asaŋ ni amɛfɔse wain hu amɛshwie shi akɛ afɔle yɛ jɛi amɛhã nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi, ni amɛkɛ nakai feemɔ wo mimli la lɛ.

english_verse: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ amɛnihiinii lɛ yamamɔ shĩa ni ajaa mi yɛ mli lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛbule jɛi.

english_verse: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Amɛmamɔ Baal jamɔhei grɔŋgrɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ Hinom Jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛgbe amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei yɛ jɛi amɛkɛshã afɔle amɛkɛhã jemawɔŋ Molek lɛ. Tsɛbelɛ mifãko amɛ, ni asaŋ ebako miyiŋ tete akɛ amɛfee nɛkɛ musubɔɔnii nɛɛ ni amɛkɛhã Yuda fɛɛ agbee esha mli.” Hiɛnɔkãmɔ he Shiwoo

english_verse: Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Yeremia, nɔ ni mikɛɔ yɛ maŋ nɛɛ ni okɛɛ yɛ ehe akɛ, ‘Ajɔɔ enɔ ahã Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ̃ klante kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela nɔ’ lɛ he nɛ.”

english_verse: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
translation_verse: Naa, mi nɔŋŋ mabua maŋbii ni mikɛ mlifu kɛ mlila kɛ grimɔ ni naa wa jogbaŋŋ eshwie amɛ kɛtee maŋsɛɛ lɛ anaa kɛjɛ nakai shikpɔji lɛ anɔ, ni mikɛ amɛ baaku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ; ni mahã amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe;

english_verse: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: ni amɛbaatsɔ̃ miwebii, ni mibatsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni, mi Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, bɔ ni mihã nɛkɛ efɔŋ kpeteŋkple nɛɛ ba gbɔmɛi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ hu mibahã ekpakpa fɛɛ ekpakpa ni miwo amɛ he shi lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english_verse: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ni nyɛkɛɔ yɛ he akɛ etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, ni gbɔmɔ kɛ kooloo tete bɛ nɔ, asaŋ ni ajɔɔ nɔ ahã Babilonbii lɛ, abaatse shika akɛhe shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Abaahɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ, ni abaahe shikpɔŋ, ni abaafee nɔ woji, abaasɔo woji nɛɛ anaa, ni abaatsɛtsɛɛ mɛi amɛbayeyee he odase yɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ Yerusalɛm niiaŋ kɛ Yuda maji lɛ amli kɛ gɔji anɔ maji lɛ amli kɛ ŋa nɔ maji lɛ amli kɛ Yuda wuoyigbɛ maji lɛ hu amli, ejaakɛ mibahã amɛnibii fɛɛ ni amɛlaaje lɛ amɛnine ashɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me: I am the Lord, and I created the whole world.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mɔ ni bɔ jeŋ, ni etee lɛ shi ema shi, lɛ mɔ ni egbɛi ji Yehowa, kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ,

english_verse: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
translation_verse: “Tsɛ mi, ni mahere bo nɔ, ni magba bo teemɔŋ nibii ni oleee.

english_verse: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
translation_verse: Shi naa, mi nɔŋŋ mibasaa maŋ lɛ ni matee lɛ shi ekoŋŋ ni mahã emli bii ana toiŋjɔlɛ babaoo, amɛbaashwere ni amɛbaafee shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
translation_verse: Ni mahã Yuda kɛ Israel nine ashɛ amɛnibii ni amɛlaaje lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni matswa amɛ ekoŋŋ mama shi taakɛ amɛyɔɔ tsuutsu lɛ.

english_verse: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
translation_verse: Ni maŋ nɛɛ gbɛi baahã mimli afili mi, ni ebaatsɔ̃ miyijiemɔ kɛ mihiɛ nyam yɛ jeŋ maji fɛɛ ni aaanu ejuji fɛɛ ni mifee amɛ lɛ he lɛ ahiɛ. Amɛtsui baafã, ni amɛhe baakpokpo yɛ ejuji fɛɛ ni mifeɔ maŋ nɛɛ kɛ shweremɔ ni mihãa amɛshwereɔ lɛ hewɔ.”

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Biɛ nɛɛ ni nyɛkɛɔ yɛ he akɛ ehiɛ ekpãtã, ni gbɔmɔ loo kooloo bɛ biɛ dɔŋŋ, kɛ Yuda maji lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm blohuiaŋ ni etsɔ̃mɔ amaŋfɔ̃i, ni gbɔmɛi loo kooloi bɛ amɛmli lɛ, abaanu

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: nyamɔ kɛ mliflimɔ kɛ ayɛmforowu kɛ ayɛmforo gbee ekoŋŋ yɛ jɛi. Abaanu mɛi ni kɛ amɛshidaa afɔlei baa Yehowa we lɛ he ni amɛmiila akɛ, ‘Nyɛdaa Yehowa, Taiatsɛ lɛ, shi ejaakɛ Yehowa hi, ni esuɔmɔ ni tsakeee lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyaa naanɔ!’ Ejaakɛ mibahã shikpɔŋ lɛ ashwere tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ tsuutsu lɛ. Mi Yehowa mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: Ni tookwɛlɔi ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ maji lɛ kɛ ŋa nɔ maji lɛ kɛ Yuda wuoyigbɛ maji lɛ kɛ Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akrowai ni bɔle Yerusalɛm he lɛ kɛ Yuda maji lɛ hu amli lɛ, baakane amɛtoi ayifalɛ ekoŋŋ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ, “Naa, be miiba, ni mahã shi ni miwo Israelbii kɛ Yudabii lɛ hu aba mli.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mibahã David shwie jalɔ ko abaye esɛɛ akɛ maŋtsɛ; ebaakojo yɛ jalɛ naa, ni ebaaye jalɛ sane yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ aaahere Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛm yiwala, ni amɛaahi shi shweshweeshwe; ni gbɛi ni akɛaatsɛ Yerusalɛm ji ‘Yehowa ji wɔjalɛ.’

english_verse: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, ‘Nuu ni baata Israel maŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔŋ David kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: Asaŋ Levinyo ni aaasɔ̃mɔ yɛ mihiɛ koni eshã shãa afɔlei kɛ niyenii afɔlei gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ ebɔŋ Levibii ni ji osɔfoi lɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie,

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛku kpãŋmɔ ni mi, mikɛ shwane kɛ nyɔɔŋ ekpãŋ akɛ amɛba ni amɛya yɛ be ni mito mihã amɛ naa mli lɛ,

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: no lɛ aaanyɛ aku kpãŋmɔ ni mi, mikɛ mitsulɔ David ekpãŋ lɛ mli, ni no hewɔ lɛ, enaŋ binuu ko ni aaata esɛi lɛ nɔ eye maŋtsɛ. Ni nakai nɔŋŋ aaanyɛ aku mi kɛ Levibii, ni ji misɔ̃ɔlɔi osɔfoi lɛ, akpãŋmɔ lɛ hu mli.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni anyɛŋ ŋwɛi ŋulamii afalɛ akane, ni anyɛŋ ŋshɔnaa shia falɛ akane lɛ, nakai mahã mitsulɔ David shwiei kɛ Levibii ni ji misɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ hu ayi afa.”

english_verse: The Lord also said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia, wie ni ekɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: “Oyɔseko nɔ ni mɛi nɛɛ wieɔ akɛ mi Yehowa, mikwa Israel kɛ Yuda, ni ji wekui enyɔ ni mihala lɛ lo? Ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ mimaŋbii lɛ efee shikpɔŋ, ni amɛjeee shikwɛ̃ɛ maŋ ko yɛ amɛhiɛ?

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: Kɛji mihãko mishwane kɛ nyɔɔŋ he kpãŋmɔ lɛ ama shi, ni mitoko ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ he gbɛjianɔ no dani makwa Yakob shwiei lɛ kɛ mitsulɔ David hu shwiei lɛ, ni miŋɔŋ David shwiei lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko koni eye Abraham kɛ Isak kɛ Yakob shwiei lɛ anɔ. Shi agbɛnɛ mahã amɛshwiei lɛ anine ashɛ nibii ni amɛŋmɛɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ, ni mimusuŋ baatsɔ̃ mi yɛ amɛhe.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie be mli ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ tabilɔi krokomɛi ni jɛ jeŋ maji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ enɔyeli shishi kɛ mɛi krokomɛi fɛɛ eba, ni amɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm kɛ ehe maji lɛ fɛɛ miiwu ta lɛ.

english_verse: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
translation_verse: Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Yaa koni okɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia ayawie, ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, miijɔɔ maŋ nɛɛ nɔ miihã Babilon maŋtsɛ, ni ebaama maŋ lɛ naa la ni eshã.

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Bo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ojeŋ edɛŋ; shi mɔ kɛ̃ aaamɔ bo, ni akɛ bo baaya ayawo edɛŋ. Okɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ baakpe hiɛ kɛ hiɛ, ni okɛ lɛ baawie hiɛ kɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
translation_verse: Obaagbo yɛ hejɔlɛ mli; ni bɔ ni maŋbii shãshãa ohɛ amɛhã otsɛmɛi ni ji maŋtsɛmɛi ni ebaye nɔ kɛtsɔ̃ ohiɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ maŋbii baashãshãa ohɛ amɛhã bo kɛfee oyara; ni amɛaawo yara amɛfo bo akɛ, ‘Nuŋtsɔ, kpoo oŋ!’ Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeremia hã wiemɔ lɛ shɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia dɛŋ yɛ Yerusalɛm,

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: be ni Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ tabilɔi lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm kɛ Yuda maji ni eshwɛ, ni ji Lakish kɛ Azeka, wuɔ ta lɛ; ejaakɛ nomɛi pɛ ji Yuda maji ni eshwɛ ni atswa gbogbo awo amɛhe. Ayeee anɔkwa yɛ nyɔji agbɛfaŋ

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ maŋbii fɛɛ ni kpãŋ akɛ amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ahã enyɔŋnuu kɛ enyɔŋyoo aye amɛhe koni mɔ ko mɔ ko akaye enyɛmi Hebrinyo nyɔŋ dɔŋŋ lɛ ye kpãŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛŋmɛɛ nyɔji lɛ ahe.

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Shi fee sɛɛ lɛ amɛku sɛɛ ni amɛyaŋɔ amɛnyɔji ni kulɛ amɛhã amɛye amɛhe lɛ kɛba ekoŋŋ, ni amɛbaye amɛ nyɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: “Nɔ ni mi, Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Mikɛ nyɛblematsɛmɛi lɛ kpãŋ be mli ni miyakpɔ̃ amɛ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni aye amɛ nyɔŋ yɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Shi nyɛku nyɛsɛɛ nyɛtsake nyɛjwɛŋmɔ, ni nyɛwo migbɛi lɛ he muji. Ejaakɛ nyɛyaŋɔ nyɛwehii kɛ nyɛweyei ni nyɛhã amɛye amɛhe yɛ amɛsuɔmɔ naa lɛ kɛba ekoŋŋ ni nyɛbaye amɛ nyɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mi, Yehowa, miikɛɛ nyɛ akɛ nyɛgbo minɔ toi, ejaakɛ nyɛhãko nyɛnyɛmimɛi Israelbii kɛ nyɛnanemɛi aŋɔ amɛhe amɛye tswaa. Shi naa, mi lɛ mahã ta kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela kɛ nyɛ aye. Jeŋ shikpɔji fɛɛ ahe aaajɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ nɔ ni mafee nyɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
translation_verse: Be mli ni Yosia bi Yehoiakim yeɔ Yuda maŋtsɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: “Yaa Rekab webii lɛ aŋɔɔ koni okɛ amɛ ayawie; ni okɛ amɛ aba Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli piai lɛ eko mli koni ohã amɛ wain amɛnu yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mitee, ni miyaŋɔ Yaazania, ni atsɛɔ etsɛ Yeremia, Habazinia bi lɛ, kɛ enyɛmimɛi hii lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ Rekab weku lɛ fɛɛ,

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: ni mikɛ amɛ ba Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni wɔtee Igdalia bi Gbalɔ Hanan kaselɔi lɛ apia lɛ mli, yɛ lumɛi apia lɛ masɛi, yɛ Shalum, shinaanaabulɔ lɛ, bi Maaseia pia lɛ yiteŋ.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mikɛ gbɛi ni eyimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ wain kɛ kɔɔpoi bamamɔ Rekab weku lɛ hiɛ, ni mikɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛnua wain koo!”

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Shi amɛto he akɛ, “Wɔnuuu wain ejaakɛ wɔtsɛ Yonadab, ni ji Rekab bi lɛ, wo wɔ kitã akɛ, ‘Nyɛkanua wain gbi ko gbi ko, nyɛ kɛ nyɛshwiei fɛɛ.

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: Nyɛkamamɔa tsui, ni nyɛkadua nii, ni nyɛkafea wain trom nyɛhãa nyɛhe, shi moŋ nyɛwala bei amli fɛɛ lɛ, nyɛhia bui amli bɔ ni afee ni nyɛhi shi be babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛbato gbɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
translation_verse: Shi wɔhi bui amli, ni bɔ ni wɔtsɛ Yonadab wo wɔ kitã lɛ wɔbo toi, ni wɔye nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar fã ta kɛba ebatua shikpɔŋ lɛ, wɔye wɔfua akɛ wɔɔba Yerusalɛm yɛ gbeyei ni wɔshe Babilon ta lɛ kɛ Siria ta lɛ hu hewɔ. No ji Yerusalɛm ni wɔyɔɔ nɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: “Yaa ni oyakɛɛ Yudahii lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛmbii lɛ akɛ mi, Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, miibi akɛ, ‘Aso nyɛkpɛlɛŋ tsɔsemɔ koni nyɛbo miwiemɔ lɛ toi?’

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Kitã ni Rekab bi Yonadab, wo eshwiei akɛ amɛkanu wain lɛ, amɛye nɔ, ni amɛnuuu wain kɛ ŋmɛnɛ, ejaakɛ amɛye amɛtsɛ kitã lɛ nɔ. Mitee nɔ mikɛ nyɛ ewie shii abɔ, shi nyɛbooo mi toi.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: Mitsu mitsuji, ni ji gbalɔi lɛ nyɛŋɔɔ shii abɔ kɛ wiemɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ashi ejeŋba gbonyo lɛ sɛɛ koni etsake, ni nyɛkayanyiɛa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi asɛɛ ni nyɛsɔ̃mɔ amɛ; ja no dani nyɛaahi shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhãa nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ nɔ. Shi nyɛbooo mi toi, ni nyɛfeee nɔ ni mikɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Rekab bi Yonadab shwiei lɛ eye kitã ni amɛtsɛ lɛ wo amɛ lɛ nɔ; shi nyɛ maŋ nɛɛ nyɛbooo mi toi.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, naa, mi Yehowa, Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ, ni ji Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mibahã saji fɔ̃ji fɛɛ ni mito miyiŋ akɛ mahã aye Yuda kɛ Yerusalɛmbii fɛɛ lɛ aba amɛ amɛnɔ, ejaakɛ miwie mitsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ni amɛbooo mi toi, ni mitsɛ amɛ, ni amɛhereee mi nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Shi Yeremia kɛɛ Rekabbii lɛ akɛ, nɔ ni Yehowa, Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ yɛ amɛhe nɛ; “Akɛni nyɛye kitã ni nyɛtsɛ Yonadab wo nyɛ lɛ nɔ, ni nyɛhiɛ akpɔi ni ewo lɛ amli, ni nyɛfee nibii fɛɛ ni ekɛɛ nyɛfee lɛ,

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, mi Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ, miikɛɛ akɛ be ko baŋ ni anaŋ Rekab bi Yonadab shwie ni aaasɔmɔ mi.”

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim, Yosia bi lɛ, maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: “Kɔ wolo kpo ko koni oŋmã wiemɔi fɛɛ ni mikɛ bo ewie yɛ Israel kɛ Yuda kɛ maji krokomɛi fɛɛ ahe, kɛjɛ Yosia yinɔ aahu kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, owo mli.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Aleenɔ, ekolɛ kɛji Yudabii aaanu efɔŋ ni mito miyiŋ akɛ mafee amɛ lɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aaakpa enifɔɔji anii ni efeɔ lɛ, ni no aaahã mikɛ amɛnishaianii kɛ amɛhe eshai lɛ afa amɛ.”

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeremia tsɛ Neria bi Baruk kɛba, ni Yeremia wie wiemɔi fɛɛ ni Yehowa kɛ lɛ, Yeremia, ewie lɛ, ni Baruk ŋmã ewo wolo kpo lɛ mli.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Ni Yeremia fã Baruk akɛ, “Mi lɛ atsi mi gbɛ, ni ehiii mi Yehowa we lɛ mli yaa.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bo yaa koni oyakane Yehowa wiemɔi ni onu kɛjɛ minaa ni oŋmã owo wolo kpo lɛ mli lɛ, faŋŋ otsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ yɛ Yehowa we lɛ, yɛ ŋmaahilɛ gbi lɛ eko nɔ. Asaŋ okane faŋŋ otsɔ̃ɔ Yudabii ni jɛɔ amɛmaji krokomɛi amli amɛbaa lɛ hu.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: Eko lɛ amɛfaikpamɔ aaashɛ Yehowa hiɛ, ni amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aaakpa enifɔɔji anii ni efeɔ, ejaakɛ Yehowa mli ni efu kɛ emli ni ewo la lɛ naa wa naakpa.”

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Baruk kane wiemɔi ni Yeremia wie ni yɔɔ wolo lɛ mli lɛ faŋŋ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ, yɛ woloŋmalɔ Shafan bi Gemaria pia lɛ mli, yɛ Yehowa we lɛ yiteŋgbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ, yɛ Agbo Hee lɛ naa. Akane Wolo kpo lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ Maŋ Lumɛi lɛ

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Be ni Mikaia, ni ji Shafan bi Gemaria bi lɛ, nu Yehowa naa wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wolo ni akane lɛ mli lɛ,

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: eyiŋ etee maŋtsɛ we lɛ, ni ebote woloŋmalɔ lɛ pia lɛ mli. Eyanina woloŋmalɔ lɛ kɛ Delaia, Shemaia bi lɛ, kɛ Elnatan, Akbor bi lɛ, kɛ Gemaria, Shafan bi lɛ, kɛ Zedekia, Hanania bi lɛ, kɛ maŋ lumɛi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Mikaia gba amɛ nibii fɛɛ ni enu be ni Baruk kane wolo lɛ faŋŋ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Be ni eshɛ jɛi lɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛɛ Baruk akɛ, “Ta shi koni okane wolo lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, Baruk kane wolo lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Be ni amɛnu wolo lɛ mli sane lɛ, amɛkwɛkwɛɛ amɛhiɛiaŋ kɛ tsuifãa, ni amɛkɛɛ Baruk akɛ, “Ja wɔyakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ wolo nɛɛ mli sane lɛ.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Baruk to he akɛ, “Lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enaa wiemɔi ni. Lɛ ewie; ni be mli ni ewieɔ lɛ belɛ mikɛ blɛgi miiŋma miiwo wolo lɛ mli.”

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Shi moŋ maŋtsɛ lɛ fã Yerameel, maŋtsɛ binuu lɛ, kɛ Seraia, Azriel bi lɛ, kɛ Shelemia, Abdeel bi lɛ, akɛ amɛyamɔ Gbalɔ Yeremia kɛ woloŋmalɔ Baruk kɛba; shi Yehowa kɛ amɛ to. Yeremia ŋma wolo kroko

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ shã wolo kpo lɛ ni Gbalɔ Yeremia naa wiemɔi ni woloŋmalɔ Baruk ŋmã lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: “Kɔ wolo kpo kroko koni oŋmã tsuutsu wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ wolo kpo lɛ ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim shã lɛ mli lɛ owo mli.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim lɛ, nɔ ni okɛɛ yɛ ehe nɛ. Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Bo lɛ oshã nɛkɛ wolo kpo nɛɛ, ni obi Yeremia akɛ mɛni hewɔ oŋma yɛ wolo kpo lɛ mli akɛ, Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ baaba kɛ̃ koni ebafite shikpɔŋ nɛɛ, koni ekpãtã enɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ.’

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mi Yehowa, nɔ ni mikɛɔ yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim he ji akɛ eshwie ko eshwie ko taŋ David maŋtsɛ sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ; ni abaashɛ egbonyo afɔ̃ he ko ni baahã hulu ashã lɛ shwane, ni bɔ baanyɔ enɔ nyɔɔŋ.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: Mibagbala lɛ kɛ eshwiei kɛ etsuji lɛ atoi yɛ nishaianii ni amɛfee lɛ hewɔ; ni mibahã haomɔi fɛɛ ni mi kɛ amɛ ewie he, shi amɛbuuu lɛ aba amɛ kɛ Yerusalɛmbii kɛ Yudabii anɔ.”

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeremia kɔ wolo kpo kroko, ni ekɛhã Neria bi Baruk ni ji ewoloŋmalɔ lɛ. Yeremia saa ewie wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsuutsu wolo kpo ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim shã lɛ mli lɛ, ni Baruk ŋmã fɛɛ ewo wolo hee lɛ mli. Ni Yeremia kɛ wiemɔi krokomɛi ni tamɔ wiemɔi ni ewie ni Baruk ŋmã lɛ shi nɔ.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar to Zedekia, Yosia bi lɛ, Yuda maŋtsɛ, yɛ Yehoiakin, Yehoiakim bi lɛ, najiaŋ.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Shi Zedekia ni jio, etsuji lɛ ni jio, maŋbii lɛ ni jio, mɔ ko mɔ ko yeee wiemɔi ni Yehowa kɛtsɔ̃ Gbalɔ Yeremia nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction. One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
translation_verse: Farao tabilɔi efã kɛjɛ Ijipt kɛba. Be ni Babilonbii ni amɛba amɛmiisa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ yi lɛ nu akɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ ewo tabilɔi agbɛ kɛmiiba lɛ, Babilonbii lɛ gbala amɛhe shi kɛje Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: ni Babilonbii baaku amɛsɛɛ kɛba amɛbatua maŋ nɛɛ. Amɛbaaye maŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaama enaa la amɛshã.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ ji akɛ, ‘Nyɛkashishiua nyɛhe ni nyɛmiikɛɛ akɛ Babilonbii lɛ etee kwraa; ejaakɛ jeee tee amɛtee lɛ.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛye Babilonbii ni kɛ nyɛ wuɔ nɛɛ anɔ, ni eshwɛ amɛpilafoi sɔŋŋ ni kamɔ amɛbuui amli kɛkɛ po, pilafoi nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baate shi, ni amɛbaama maŋ lɛ naa la amɛshã.’ ” Awo Yeremia tsuŋ

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Be ni Babilon tabilɔi lɛ egbala amɛhe shi amɛshi Yerusalɛm amɛtee yɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ ta ni fã kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Yeremia je Yerusalɛm akɛ eeya Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaŋɔ egbɛfaŋnii ko yɛ eweku gboshinii mli.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Be ni eyashɛ Benyamin Agbo lɛ naa lɛ, asafoiatsɛ ni kwɛɔ agbo lɛ naa bulɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ Iriya ni eji Shelemia binuu kɛ Hanania nabi lɛ, mɔ Gbalɔ Yeremia, ni ebi lɛ akɛ, “Te Babilonbii lɛ aŋɔɔ ojoɔ foi kɛyaa nɛɛ bɛɛ?”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Yeremia jie naa akɛ, “Dabida! Jeee Babilonbii lɛ aŋɔɔ mijoɔ foi kɛya.” Shi Iriya eŋɔɔɔ nɔ ehãaa Yeremia, ni emɔ lɛ kɛba lumɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ Maŋtsɛ Zedekia tsu ayaŋɔ Yeremia nigii abahã lɛ, ni ebi Yeremia yɛ teemɔ mli yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli akɛ, “Ani Yehowa kɛ bo ewie nɔ ko lo?” Yeremia to he akɛ, “Hɛɛ, ekɛɛ mi nɔ ko.” Asaŋ Yeremia kɛɛ akɛ, “Aaaŋɔ bo awo Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeremia bi Maŋtsɛ Zedekia akɛ, “Mɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ mitɔ̃ bo loo otsuji lɛ loo maŋ nɛɛ mli bii anɔ, hewɔ ni nyɛwo mi tsuŋ nɛɛ?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Nɛgbɛ nyɛgbalɔi lɛ ni gba tsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ akɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ baŋ ebatuaŋ maŋ nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, ofainɛ ni ona tsui fioo ohã mi koni omɔ fai ni mikpaa bo nɛɛ mli ohã mi, koni okahã akɛmi ku sɛɛ kɛtee woloŋmalɔ Yonatan we lɛ dɔŋŋ koni mikayagbo yɛ jɛi.”

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Zedekia fã, ni agbɛnɛ awo Yeremia kpabuŋ yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ hebulɔi lɛ akpo lɛ nɔ. Jɛi ehi, ni daa gbi lɛ ahãa lɛ aboloo akwaabɔ kome kɛjɛɔ abolooshãlɔi lɛ adɛŋ. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni afee aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli aboloo fɛɛ tã.

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni lumɛi nɛɛ tee ni amɛyakɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Zedekia akɛ, “Hã agbe nɛkɛ nuu nɛɛ, ejaakɛ tabilɔi ni eshwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ anijiaŋ miije wui yɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ ni ewieɔ ewoɔ amɛtoiiaŋ lɛ ahewɔ. Nuu nɛɛ taooo maŋbii lɛ ekpakpa, fe efɔŋ moŋ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Zedekia here amɛnɔ akɛ, “Naa, eyɛ nyɛdɛŋ, ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ nyɛŋ nyɛsɛɛ eje efee nɔ ko.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔ Yeremia, ni amɛkɛ taŋkpee shiu lɛ amɛwo maŋtsɛ binuu Malkia nubu lɛ mli yɛ maŋtsɛ we lɛ hebulɔi akpo lɛ nɔ. Nu bɛ bu lɛ mli fe ŋmɔtɔ sɔŋŋ kɛkɛ; ni Yeremia fũ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “Minuŋtsɔ Maŋtsɛ, hii nɛɛ efee Gbalɔ Yeremia efɔŋ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ shɛmɔ ni amɛshɛ lɛ amɛfɔ̃ nubu lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaagbo kɛ hɔmɔ yɛ jɛi ejaakɛ amrɔ nɛɛ niyenii bɛ maŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ebed-Melek ŋɔ hii lɛ efata ehe, ni eyiŋ etee mamai kɛ atadei atoohe lɛ ni yɔɔ maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli. Eyakɔlɔ mamashwɛi kɛ atadei ni etserɛ yɛ jɛi; ni ekɛ taŋkpee shiu nibii nɛɛ ekɛhã Yeremia yɛ bu lɛ mli.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ebed-Melek, Kushnyo lɛ, kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Okɛ mamashwɛi lɛ kɛ atadei tserɛitserɛi lɛ ahɔlɔ oŋaashi kɛ taŋkpei lɛ ateŋ.” Yeremia fee nakai,

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛ taŋkpee lɛ sha Yeremia, ni amɛ jie lɛ yɛ bu lɛ mli. Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yeremia hi maŋtsɛ we lɛ he bulɔi akpo lɛ nɔ. Maŋtsɛ Zedekia bi Yeremia dɛŋ ŋaawoo

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Be ko lɛ Maŋtsɛ Zedekia tsu, ni ayaŋɔ Gbalɔ Yeremia abahã lɛ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ naa agbo ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ naa. Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Mibabi bo nɔ ko; kaashiu mi sane ko nɔ!”

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: Yeremia kɛɛ Maŋtsɛ Zedekia akɛ, “Kɛji migba bo anɔkwale lɛ, ani oyɛ nɔmimaa akɛ ogbeŋ mi? Ni kɛji miwo bo ŋaa hu lɛ te oboŋ toi.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Zedekia kã Yeremia kitã, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mina Yehowa, mɔ dɛŋ ni wɔwala nɛɛ yɔɔ akɛ migbeŋ bo, ni asaŋ miŋmɛŋ ohe mihaŋ hii nɛɛ ni taoɔ bo amɛgbe nɛɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yeremia kɛɛ Zedekia akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, ni ji Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ nɛ, “Kɛji okɛ ohe hã Babilon maŋtsɛ lumɛi lɛ, oyi aaana wala, ni amaŋ maŋ nɛɛ naa la ashaŋ, ni bo kɛ owe lɛ fɛɛ yi aaana wala.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛji okɛ ohe hãaa Babilon maŋtsɛ lumɛi lɛ, no lɛ aaaŋɔ nɛkɛ maŋ nɛɛ awo Babilonbii lɛ adɛŋ, ni amɛbaama naa la amɛshã, ni ojeŋ amɛdɛŋ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Shi Maŋtsɛ Zedekia kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Miishe wɔmaŋ Yudabii ni eyafata Babilonbii lɛ ahe lɛ moŋ gbeyei, akɛ eko lɛ Babilonbii lɛ kɛ mi baawo amɛdɛŋ, ni amɛbaashwie mihiɛ shi.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Yeremia to he akɛ, “Akɛ bo haŋ amɛ. Bo lɛ, ye wiemɔi ni Yehowa kɛtsɔ̃ minɔ ni mikɛ bo ewie lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ, ni ebaahi ehã bo, ni oyi aaana wala.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Shi kɛji okpɛ̃lɛɛɛ akɛ okɛ ohe aaahã henyɛlɔi lɛ, nɔ ni Yehowa ejie etsɔ̃ɔ mi yɛ ninaa mli nɛ.

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Naa, mina yei fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ Yuda maŋtsɛ we lɛ mli lɛ ni aakpala amɛ ayahã Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ lumɛi lɛ; ni amɛmiikɛɛ akɛ, ‘Onanemɛi ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ amɛnɔ lɛ elaka bo, ni amɛye onɔ; ni agbɛnɛ ni onaji efu ŋmɔtɔ mli nɛɛ lɛ, amɛtsɔ̃mɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhã bo.’ ”

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: “Abaakpala oŋamɛi lɛ kɛ obihii lɛ hu fɛɛ ayahã Babilonbii lɛ; ni bo diɛŋtsɛ hu ojeŋ amɛdɛŋ. Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ aaamɔ bo, ni aaama maŋ nɛɛ naa la, ashã.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Zedekia kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Kaahã mɔ ko mɔ ko miile wɔsanegbaa nɛɛ, ni obaana akɛ owala tɔ̃ŋ.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Kɛji lumɛi lɛ na le akɛ mi kɛ bo egba sane, ni amɛba oŋɔɔ amɛbakɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Kɛɛmɔ wɔ nɔ ni okɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ; bo lɛ kaashiu wɔ sane ko nɔ, ni wɔgbeŋ, bo’ lɛ,

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, ‘Mibakpa maŋtsɛ fai yɛ heshibaa mli akɛ akɛ mi akaya kpabu ni yɔɔ Yonatan we lɛ mli dɔŋŋ koni mikayagbo yɛ jɛi.’ ”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ ba Yeremia ŋɔɔ, ni amɛbabi lɛ sane, ni ekɛɛ amɛ bɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ eta ewo enaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, lumɛi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ Yeremia daaŋtaa ejaakɛ Yeremia kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ sanegbaa lɛ mli nɔ ko ejeee kpo.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Ni Yeremia hi bulɔi akpo lɛ nɔ kɛyashi gbi nɔ ni henyɛlɔi ŋɔ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Be ni Yuda Maŋtsɛ Zedekia kɛ etabilɔi lɛ na Babilon maŋtsɛ tsuji lɛ, amɛka foijee; amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ; amɛtsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ trom lɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ agbo lɛ ni yɔɔ maŋ gbogboi enyɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛyi Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli gbɛ.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: “Yaa koni oyakɛɛ Ebed-Melek, Kushnyo lɛ, akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Naa, mibahã nɔ ni mikɛɛ yɛ maŋ nɛɛ he lɛ aba mli, ebaana nɔ fɔŋ, shi jeee nɔ kpakpa; ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baaba mli, ni okɛ ohiŋmɛi baana.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Ŋɔɔ Yeremia, ni okwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Okafee lɛ efɔŋ ko, shi moŋ bɔ ni eeekɛɛ bo lɛ, ofee nakai ohã lɛ.”

english_verse: In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls. After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
translation_verse: Be ni henyɛlɔi lɛ ŋɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ, Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ ba, ni amɛbatara shi yɛ Teŋ Koi lɛ shishi. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ji: Nergal-Sarezer kɛ Samgar-Nebo kɛ Sarsekim piafoiatsɛ lɛ, kɛ Nergal-Sarezer kroko ko hu kɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ tsuji krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ hu.

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Shi Babilon tabilɔi lɛ tiu amɛ, ni amɛyanina Zedekia yɛ Yeriko ŋa kplanaa lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmɔ lɛ. Amɛkɛ lɛ ba Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar ŋɔɔ yɛ Ribla, yɛ Hamat shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nebukadnezar bu Zedekia fɔ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Be ni atsi Yeremia naa yɛ Bulɔi Akpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ lɛ wie, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ,

translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie be ni Nebuzaradan tabilɔiatsɛ lɛ, eŋmɛɛ ehe yɛ Rama lɛ sɛɛ. Nebuzaradan eŋɔ Yeremia, ni ewo lɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ efata Yerusalɛm kɛ Yuda nomi fɛɛ ni abaŋɔ kɛyaa Babilon lɛ ahe.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Yeremia nako ehã hetoo kɛkɛ ni Nebuzaradan kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji obaahi shi lɛ, no lɛ kuu osɛɛ mɔ koni oya Ahikam bi kɛ Shafan bi Gedalia, mɔ ni Babilon maŋtsɛ ewo lɛ Yuda maji lɛ anɔ amralo lɛ ŋɔɔ, koni okɛ lɛ ayahi shi yɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ, aloo yaahi he fɛɛ he ni sa ohiɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, tabilɔiatsɛ lɛ hã Yeremia gbɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ nikeenii, ni ewo lɛ gbɛ.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Gedalia, Shafan bi Ahikam bi lɛ, kã amɛ kɛ amɛwebii lɛ kitã akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei akɛ nyɛaasɔ̃mɔ Babilonbii lɛ. Nyɛhia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni nyɛsɔ̃mɔa Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni aaahi ahã nyɛ.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Mi lɛ mibahi Mizpa, koni madamɔ nyɛnaa kɛji Babilonbii lɛ ba wɔŋɔɔ. Shi nyɛ lɛ nyɛhia maji ni nyɛŋɔŋɔɔ lɛ amli, ni nyɛbuaa wain kɛ aduawai kɛ mu naa nyɛwoa nyɛnibii amli nyɛtoa.”

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yudafoi lɛ fɛɛ ku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ hei fɛɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtee lɛ, ni amɛba Gedalia ŋɔɔ yɛ Mizpa yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbua wain kɛ aduawai babaoo diɛŋtsɛ naa amɛto. Agbe Gedalia (

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani ole akɛ Baalis, Amonbii amaŋtsɛ lɛ, etsu Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ, koni ebagbe bo lo?” Shi Gedalia, Ahikam bi lɛ heee amɛ eyeee.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ, kɛɛ Gedalia yɛ teemɔ mli yɛ Mizpa akɛ, “Ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni mayagbe Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ nigii. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ egbe bo koni Yudafoi fɛɛ ni ebabua amɛhe naa yɛ oŋɔɔ nɛɛ agbɛ ashwã, koni mɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ akpãtã lo?”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Shi Gedalia, Ahikam bi lɛ, kɛɛ Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ akɛ, “Kaafee nakai nɔ ko; ejaakɛ nɔ ni owieɔ yɛ Ishmael he nɛɛ ebɛ mli.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Elishama bi Netania bi Ishmael ni ejɛ maŋtsɛyeli weku mli, asaŋ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ he onukpai lɛ eko ji lɛ lɛ, ŋɔ hii nyɔŋma komɛi efata ehe kɛba Ahikam bi Gedalia ŋɔɔ yɛ Mizpa. Be ni amɛtara shi amɛyeɔ nii yɛ Mizpa lɛ,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ, kɛ hii nyɔŋma ni fata ehe lɛ te shi, ni amɛbamɔ Gedalia, Ahikam bi kɛ Shafan nabi lɛ, ni amɛgbe lɛ. Nɛkɛ be mli lɛ Gedalia ji mɔ ni Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ ewo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɔ.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Ishmael gbe Yudafoi fɛɛ hu ni kɛ Gedalia yɔɔ Mizpa lɛ kɛ Babilon tabilɔi fɛɛ hu ni yaje jɛi.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Gbi ni agbe Gedalia lɛ nɔ jetsɛremɔ be mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwraa nuko he lɛ,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ, jɛ Mizpa etee eyakpee amɛ. Be ni eyaa lɛ fɛɛ lɛ belɛ eefo. Be ni ekɛ amɛ kpe lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛfainɛ, nyɛbaa nyɛbaŋaa Gedalia, Ahikam bi lɛ.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshɛ maŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ, kɛ hii lɛ ni fata ehe lɛ gbe amɛ, ni amɛshɛrɛ amɛgbohii lɛ amɛshwie nubu ko mli.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Shi hii gbɔi lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋma komɛi kɛɛ Ishmael akɛ, “Ofainɛ, kaagbe wɔ! Wɔyɛ ŋmaa kɛ akoko kɛ mu kɛ wo babaoo ni wɔkɛto yɛ wɔŋmɔjiashi.” No hewɔ lɛ, Ishmael kɛ amɛhe ke amɛ, ni egbeee amɛ kɛ amɛnanemɛi lɛ.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
