english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ishmael ŋɔ maŋtsɛ biyei lɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni tatsɛ Nebuzaradan eŋɔ ewo Gedalia nɔkwɛmɔ shishi yɛ Mizpa kɛ maŋbii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ Mizpa lɛ nom, ni ekɛ amɛ yi mli, ni efo mli kɛtee Amonbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

translation_verse: Be ni mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛ Ishmael nyiɛ lɛ na Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ, kɛ tatsɛmɛi lɛ ni fata ehe lɛ amɛnya.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Shi Ishmael kɛ esɛɛ hii kpaanyɔ komɛi je Yohanan dɛŋ, ni amɛjo foi kɛtee Amonbii lɛ aŋɔɔ.

translation_verse: ejaakɛ gbee ni Ishmael, Netania bi lɛ, gbe Gedalia, Ahikam bi lɛ, mɔ ni Babilon maŋtsɛ eto akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amralo lɛ ehã amɛmiishe gbeyei yɛ Babilonbii lɛ ahewɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Amɛ hu amɛkɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Yehowa afee odasefonyo anɔkwafo ashi wɔ kɛji wɔyeee wiemɔ fɛɛ wiemɔ ni Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛaatsu bo okɛbahã wɔ lɛ nɔ.

translation_verse: Gbii nyɔŋma sɛɛ lɛ Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: “Shi kɛji nyɛkɛɛ akɛ, ‘Wɔhiii shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ’, ni nyɛbooo Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toi,

translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni aaatswa amɛfai shi, ni amɛaaya Ijipt amɛyahi jɛi lɛ aaatsɔ̃ ta loo hɔmɔ loo gbele hela nɔ amɛgboi; ni amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko eshwɛŋ ni ehe baaje sane fɔŋ ni mikɛaaye amɛ lɛ mli.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. translation_verse: “Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni mimli fu Yerusalɛmbii, ni mimli wo amɛ la lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ mimli baafu nyɛ kɛji nyɛtee Ijipt. Akɛ nyɛ baakã kitã, ni akɛ nyɛ baalomɔ; nyɛhe baafee mɛi naakpɛɛ, ni abaabɔ nyɛ ahora; ni nyɛnaŋ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.’ ”

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.

english_verse: And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛnaa nyɛlea krɛdɛɛ akɛ ta kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela baakpãtã nyɛhiɛ yɛ he ni nyɛshweɔ akɛ nyɛaatee nyɛyahi lɛ.”

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Azaria, Hoshaia bi lɛ, kɛ Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ, kɛ hii hewolɔi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Oomale! Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, tsuko bo koni obakɛɛ wɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkayaa Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɛyahi jɛi.’

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Baruk, Neria bi lɛ, moŋ ji mɔ ni ehã ote shi owo wɔ nɛɛ, bɔ ni afee ni eŋɔ wɔ ewo Babilonbii lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛgbe wɔ aloo amɛŋɔ wɔ nom kɛya Babilon.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ, kɛ tabilɔi lɛ anɔ tatsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ yeee Yehowa wiemɔ akɛ amɛhi shi yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Shi Yohanan, Karea bi lɛ, kɛ tai lɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ ŋɔ Yudabii ni shwɛ lɛ, mɛi ni ku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ jeŋmaji fɛɛ ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ kɛba ni amɛbahi Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛtee Ijipt.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Mɛi nɛɛ ji hii kɛ yei kɛ gbekɛbii kɛ maŋtsɛ biyei kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni Nebuzaradan tu ewo Gedalia, Shafan bi Ahikam bi lɛ, nɔkwɛmɔ shishi lɛ. Amɛkɛ Gbalɔ Yeremia kɛ Baruk, Neria bi lɛ, hu fata gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ahe,

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: ni amɛŋɔ amɛ kɛtee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbooo Yehowa wiemɔ lɛ toi. Amɛtee, aahu kɛyashɛ Tahapanes maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Holemɔ tɛi wuji koni okɛyahɔlɔ su ni akɛtsara ntayai ni akɛka Farao shinaa lɛ shi lɛ mli yɛ Tahapanes, yɛ Yuda hii lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ Yuda hii lɛ akɛ, mi Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mikɛɛ akɛ mibaŋɔ mitsulɔ Nebukadnezar, Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛba, mikɛ emaŋtsɛyeli sɛi lɛ baama nɛkɛ tɛi ni mikɛhɔlɔ shi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ebaashi ekatamanso lɛ ema amɛnɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ Yeremia wie Yudafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ijipt yɛ Migdol kɛ Tahapanes kɛ Memfis kɛ Ijipt wuoyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahe.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ Yeremia akɛ, “Bɛ nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛna sane fɔŋ ni mihã eye Yerusalɛm kɛ Yuda maji lɛ fɛɛ? Naa, ŋmɛnɛ amɛtsɔ̃mɔ amaŋfɔ̃i, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiii amɛmli,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: yɛ nifɔɔjianii ni amɛfee amɛkɛwo mimli la lɛ hewɔ. Ejaakɛ amɛtee, ni amɛyashãshãa tsofakɛŋma, ni amɛsɔ̃mɔ nyɔŋmɔi ni amɛ kɛ nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fɛɛ leee.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ mitee nɔ mitsu mitsuji ni ji gbalɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛba nyɛŋɔɔ kɛ wiemɔ akɛ, ‘Ao, nyɛkafea nɛkɛ musubɔɔnii nɛɛ ni mihiɔ lɛ.

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Shi amɛyabooo mi toi, ni amɛyabuuu miwiemɔ lɛ koni amɛkpa amɛnifɔ̃ɔjianii lɛ, ni amɛkashã tsofakɛŋma amɛhã nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mifɔse mimlila lɛ kɛ mimlifu lɛ mishwie amɛnɔ, ni ehere tamɔ la, ni eshã Yuda maji lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm blohui lɛ tete; kɛkɛ ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ amaŋfɔ̃i bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba nyɛkɛ nyɛninenaa nitsumɔi woɔ mimli la? Nyɛshãa tsofakɛŋma nyɛhãa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni nyɛba nyɛbato gbɔ yɛ lɛ ni nyɛhiɛ akpãtã bɔ ni afee ni jeŋ majimaji lɛ abɔ nyɛ ahora, ni atsɛ nyɛ gbɛi akɛlomɔ lo?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ani nyɛhiɛ ekpa nibii fɔ̃ji ni nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ amɛŋamɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu nyɛŋamɛi lɛ feefee yɛ Yerusalɛm blohui lɛ amli lɛ anɔ lo?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛbako nyɛhe shi, ni nyɛsheko gbeyei, ni asaŋ nyɛbako nyɛjeŋ yɛ mlai kɛ akpɔi ni miwo nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ anaa.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mi, Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, nɔ ni mikɛɔ ji akɛ, Naa, mibajie mihiɛ maka nyɛ, ni mibaplenee Yuda muu fɛɛ.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ni Yudabii ni eshwɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni etswa fai shi akɛ amɛaatee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛyahi jɛi lɛ, mahã, amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛ baakpãtã. Amɛbaanyɔnyɔi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ta kɛ hɔmɔ baahã amɛplenee; kɛjɛ mɔ bibioo nɔ kɛyashi mɔ wulu nɔ lɛ ta kɛ hɔmɔ baakpãtã amɛhiɛ; ni amɛsane lɛ baatsɔ̃ musu kɛ tsuifãa sane ni akɛbaalomɔ, ni akɛbaabɔ amɛ ahora.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Mibagbala mɛi ni yɔɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atoi tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛ ta kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela gbala Yerusalɛmbii lɛ atoi lɛ,

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: bɔ ni baahã Yudabii ni shwɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni eba amɛbahi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko he ejeŋ mli; eyi naŋ wala; ekuŋ esɛɛ kɛyaŋ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni amɛshweɔ akɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛya koni amɛyahi jɛi ekoŋŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛkuŋ amɛsɛɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ akɛ ja mɛi komekomei kɛkɛ ni aaana foijee hegbɛ.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni hii fɛɛ ni le akɛ amɛŋamɛi eshã tsofakɛŋma amɛhã nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi pɛŋ lɛ, kɛ yei fɛɛ ni damɔ jɛi lɛ kɛ Israelbii amaŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Patros maŋ lɛ mli, yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, asafo babaoo diɛŋtsɛ, to he amɛhã Yeremia akɛ,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Wiemɔ ni okɛ wɔ ewie yɛ Yehowa gbɛi mli nɛɛ lɛ, wɔboŋ toi.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ nɔ ni wɔwo he shi akɛ wɔbaafee lɛ, no nɔŋŋ wɔbaafee. Wɔbaashã tsofakɛŋma wɔkɛhã jemawɔŋ yoo ŋwɛi maŋnyɛ lɛ, ni wɔbaafɔse dãa wɔshwie shi wɔhã lɛ tamɔ wɔ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ wɔmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ wɔwulɔmɛi lɛ fee yɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm blohui lɛ amli lɛ. Ejaakɛ nakai be mli lɛ wɔyɛ niyenii, ni wɔshwere, ni wɔnaaa efɔŋ ko yɛ mli.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Shi kɛjɛ beyinɔ ni wɔfɔ̃ɔ tsofakɛŋma shãa, asaŋ ni wɔfɔ̃ɔ dãa fɔsemɔ kɛ shishwiemɔ kɛ ŋwɛi maŋnyɛ lɛ hãmɔ nɛɛ lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ eŋmɛɛ wɔ, ni ta kɛ hɔmɔ ekpãtã wɔhiɛ.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Yei lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Kɛji wɔkɛ keekii ni abɔlɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ŋwɛi maŋnyɛ lɛ su yɔɔ shã afɔle, ni wɔshã tsofakɛŋma wɔkɛhã lɛ, ni wɔfɔse dãa wɔshwie shi wɔkɛhã lɛ lɛ, ani wɔwumɛi lɛ leee mli eko lo?”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Tsofakɛŋma ni nyɛ kɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ nyɛlumɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ shãshãa yɛ Yuda maji lɛ kɛ Yerusalɛm blohui lɛ amli lɛ, ani Yehowa kaiii? Ani ebaaa ejwɛŋmɔ mli lo?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: No hã be ni Yehowa nyɛɛɛ nifɔɔji kɛ musubɔɔ nibii ni nyɛfeɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ, ehã nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, shikpɔŋ ni hiɛ ekpãtã, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ jɛi, ni atsɛɔ egbɛi akɛlomɔɔ kɛ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ amanehulu nɛɛ eba nyɛnɔ tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ, ejaakɛ nyɛshãshãa tsofakɛŋma, ni nyɛfee esha nyɛshi Yehowa; ni nyɛbooo Yehowa toi lɛ, nyɛbaaa nyɛjeŋ yɛ emlai kɛ ekpɔi kɛ ehe odasei ni aye lɛ anaa.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ, nyɛ kɛ nyɛŋamɛi lɛ, eje nyɛnaa nyɛkɛɛ, ni nyɛfee hu. Nyɛkɛɛ akɛ ‘Wɔwowoo shi akɛ wɔbaashã tsofakɛŋma wɔkɛhã ŋwɛi maŋnyɛ lɛ, ni wɔbaafɔse dãa wɔshwie shi wɔkɛhã lɛ, ni ja wɔye nɔ.’ Belɛ nyɛyea nyɛshiwoi lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛfea bɔ ni nyɛwowoo shi lɛ!

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ Yudabii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nyɛboa nɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ toi, naa, mikã migbɛi wulu lɛ akɛ Yudanyo ko Yudanyo ko naŋ naabu ekɛtsɛ migbɛi kɔkɔɔkɔ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ nɔ ekɛkã kitã akɛ, ‘Mina Yehowa’.

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Naa, miishi amɛhe kpe koni sane fɔŋ aye amɛ; shi jeee sane kpakpa. Yudabii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ta kɛ hɔmɔ baaplenee amɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛaatã.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Mɛi fioo ko kɛkɛ ji mɛi ni aaaje ta gbele mli, ni amɛaaku amɛsɛɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nakai be lɛ mli Yudabii ni tee yato gbɔ yɛ Ijipt lɛ ateŋ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ aaana ale kɛji mi miwiemɔ lɛ jio, amɛ amɛnɔ lɛ jio ji nɔ ni ena eba mli shiishi nɛɛ.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Mi, Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ enɛ afee okadi ahã nyɛ akɛ mibagbala nyɛtoi yɛ biɛ nɛɛ, bɔ ni afee ni nyɛna nyɛle akɛ efɔŋ ni mikɛɛ akɛ ebaaba nyɛnɔ lɛ, ebaana eba nyɛnɔ kɛ̃.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: No ji akɛ mibaŋɔ Maŋtsɛ Hofra, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ, mawo ehenyɛlɔi ni taoɔ lɛ agbe lɛ adɛŋ tamɔ bɔ ni miŋɔ Zedekia, Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ, miwo Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar ni ji ehenyɛlɔ ni taoɔ lɛ egbe lɛ dɛŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim, Yosia bi lɛ, yinɔ afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Gbalɔ Yeremia kɛ Baruk, Neria bi lɛ, wie, ni Baruk ŋma Yeremia naa wiemɔi lɛ ewo wolo mli akɛ,

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: “Baruk, nɔ ni Yehowa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɔ bo nɛ.

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: Okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Kpoo hã mi, ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ ŋkɔmɔ ebashi minɔnaa lɛ nɔ ehã mi! Etɔ mi kɛ kɔ̃ɔmɔ, ni minaaa hejɔlɛ.’ ”

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ani bo lɛ nibii wuji otaoɔ ohã ohe nɛɛ? Kaadi nomɛi asɛɛ, ejaakɛ mibahã sane fɔŋ aye gbɔmɛi adesai fɛɛ. Shi bo lɛ mibaŋɔ owala make bo tamɔ ta mli juromɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he ni oootee. Mi Yehowa mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ gbalɔ Yeremia wie yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ majimaji lɛ ahe.

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Nɔ ni ekɛɛ yɛ Ijipt he nɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ Ijipt Maŋtsɛ Neko tabilɔi ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar ye amɛnɔ kunim, yɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ naa yɛ Karkemish, yɛ Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim yinɔ afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ,

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Nyɛsaa tsɛŋi bibii kɛ tsɛŋi wuji; ni nyɛfãa ta.

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi, nyɛwoa okpɔŋɔi anɔ nii; nyɛhoa nyɛtaraa nyɛkpɔŋɔi anɔ, nyɛbumɔa nyɛdade faii; Nyɛtoa kɛdamɔa shi, nyɛjɔa nyɛkplɔi anaa nyɛwoa nyɛdade damai lɛ!

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: “Shi mɛni po minaa nɛɛ? Amɛtsui efã, ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛmiiya. Atswia amɛhii kãkãlɔi lɛ nii, ni amɛjo foi kɛ he oyaiyeli; amɛkwɛɛɛ amɛsɛɛ, he fɛɛ he efee gbeyei.” Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: “Mɔ ni le foijee nyɛŋ foi aje, ni nuu kakabãŋ he ejeŋ mli; amɛtɛrɛtɛrɛi, ni amɛnyɔnyɔi yɛ kooyigbɛ, yɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ naa.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Namɔ po ji mɔ ni efã kɛbaa tamɔ Nilo Faa nɛɛ, ni tamɔ faa ni esram nɔ nɛɛ?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Ijipt ni efã kɛbaa tamɔ Nilo Faa nɛɛ, etamɔ faa ni esram nɔ. Ijipt kɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mibasram nɔ, ni maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mibakpãtã maji kɛ amɛmli bii ahiɛ.’

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Okpɔŋɔi, nyɛfãa kɛyaa, Ta shwiilii, nyɛwoa foi kɛyaa! Nyɛhãa kãkãlɔi lɛ afã; Etiopiabii kɛ Libiabii ni hiɛɔ tsɛŋi, kɛ Ludiabii ni le gãitsɛ̃mɔ, nyɛfãa.”

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, gbi nɛ, gbi nɛɛ ji oweletɔɔ gbi ni ekɛbaatɔ ehe owele yɛ ehenyɛlɔi lɛ anɔ. Klante baaye nii ni etɔ, klante baanu lá ni etɔ lɛ dãa, ejaakɛ Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ miigbe ehenyɛlɔi tamɔ afɔle kooloi yɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Eufrate Faa lɛ he.

english_verse: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
translation_verse: Ao! Ijipt biyoo, yaa Gilead oyahe tsofa kpakpa; yakatswaa po ofeɔ tsofai pii nɛɛ; nɔ ko bɛ ni baatsa bo.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Majimaji lɛ enu ohiɛgbele lɛ he, ni obolɔmɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ̃ tɔ; ejaakɛ kakabãŋ kɛ kakabãŋ ehãlã mli ni amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛyagbeegbee shi. Nebukadnezar tua Ijipt

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Nyɛbɔa oshe yɛ Ijipt kɛ Migdol; nyɛshiɛa yɛ Memfis kɛ Tahpanhes, akɛ, ‘Nyɛfea kralo, ni nyɛsaa nyɛhe nyɛtoa, ejaakɛ klante baaye nii kɛbɔle nyɛ.’

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Mɛɛba ni Apis, tsina wɔŋ lɛ, jo foi ni edamɔɔɔ shi lɛ? Ejaakɛ Yehowa tsi lɛ etswa shi.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Otabilɔi lɛ tɛrɛtɛrɛi, ni amɛgbeegbee shi, ni amɛkɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, ‘Nyɛtea shi, nyɛhãa wɔkua wɔsɛɛ kɛyaa wɔmaŋbii aŋɔɔ; wɔtee wɔjaku shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ henyɛlɔ klante lɛ hewɔ.’

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: “Gbɛi ni okɛtsɛ Farao, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ, agbɛnɛ ji ‘Naafuutsɛ ni hã be ho yaka.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Gbii abɔ ni mihiɛ kã nɛɛ, mi Maŋtsɛ ni migbɛi ji Yehowa, Taiatsɛ lɛ mikɛɛ, “Bɔ ni Tabor Gɔŋ yɔɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ ateŋ, ni Karmel yɔɔ yɛ ŋshɔnaa lɛ, nakai mɔ ni aaabatua bo lɛ hewalɛ aaatamɔ.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Ao, Ijiptbii, nyɛsaa nyɛjatsui nyɛtoa nyɛnomŋɔɔ; ejaakɛ Memfis baatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, amaŋfɔ̃ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Ijipt tamɔ tsina biyoo fɛɛfɛo; shi ofɔi ejɛ kooyigbɛ ebatsɛ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Tabilɔi ni eyabɔ amɛ apaa lɛ tamɔ tsinabii ni eshwishwii yɛ amɛteŋ; amɛ fɛɛ amɛtsɔ̃ amɛhe amɛjo foi amɛtee; amɛdamɔɔɔ shi kwrakwra, ejaakɛ amanehulu gbi ebanina amɛ, amɛtoigbalamɔ gbi ebanina amɛ.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Ijipt daaŋ baagbɛɛ tamɔ onufu ni miijo gbeyei naa foi, ejaakɛ ehenyɛlɔ miiba kɛ hewalɛ, amɛkɛ lema miiba abatua bo tamɔ tsotoolɔi.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Amɛbaagba koo hayii lɛ ni kulɛ emli ehiii tsɔ̃mɔ lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛyi fa fe baalabii, anyɛɛɛ amɛ akane.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Abaashwie Ijiptbii ahiɛ shi, ni abaaŋɔ amɛ awo kooyigbɛbii lɛ adɛŋ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, mibagbala Amon, ni ji Tebes wɔŋ lɛ kɛ Farao kɛ Ijipt kɛ enyɔŋmɔi lɛ kɛ enɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ atoi, ni mibaŋɔ Farao kɛ mɛi ni ahiɛ kã enɔ lɛ,

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: ni mibatu amɛ mawo mɛi ni taoɔ amɛ amɛgbe lɛ adɛŋ, mɛi nɛɛ ji Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar kɛ etsuji lɛ. Shi naagbee mli aahu lɛ, Ijipt nine baashɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ŋmɛɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ, ni mɛi aaabahi emli. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Yehowa baahere Ewebii lɛ

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: “Miwebii Yakob shwiei, nyɛkashea gbeyei! Ao Israel! Kaaye ŋkɔmɔ, ejaakɛ, naa, mibahere oyiwala kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ; mibahere oshwiei ayiwala hu kɛjɛ nomŋɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yakob shwiei aaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛbaana hejɔlɛ kɛ toiŋjɔlɛ, ni mɔ ko woŋ amɛhe gbeyei dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Miwebii Yakob shwiei, nyɛkashea gbeyei, Yehowa kɛɛ, ejaakɛ mi kɛ nyɛ yɛ. Mibakpãtã maji fɛɛ ni mishwie nyɛ kɛtee amɛŋɔɔ lɛ ahiɛ butuu, shi nyɛ lɛ mikpãtãŋ nyɛhiɛ kɛmɔŋ shi. Mibagbala nyɛtoi bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ, mikɛ nyɛhe ekeŋ nyɛ efolo tswaa nakai. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Wiemɔ ni Yehowa kɛ Gbalɔ Yeremia wie yɛ Filistibii ahe dani Ijipt maŋtsɛ yatua Gaza nɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa! Fai miiyimɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ, ni amɛbaaje ŋa kɛba; amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ enɔ nibii fɛɛ kɛ maji kɛ amɛmli bii fɛɛ anɔ. Gbɔmɛi baabolɔ kɛtsɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii fɛɛ baawɔ lele.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Okpɔŋɔi ananeshi gbɛɛmɔ kɛ ta shwiilii agbɛɛmɔ kɛ shwiilii ananeshi jijemɔ hewɔ lɛ tsɛmɛi tete efoŋ amɛhe amɛkwɛŋ he ni amɛbii yɔɔ. Ejaakɛ amɛnijiaŋ eje wui

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: yɛ Filistibii ahiɛkpãtãmɔ ni baa lɛ hewɔ; gbi ni abaaplenee Tiro kɛ Sidon ni ji Filistibii abualɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ Yehowa baakpãtã Filistibii ni ji Kreta ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Ŋkɔmɔyeli ehã Gaza yiteŋ ekpa, ni akpãtã Ashkelon hiɛ. Ao! Nyɛ jɔɔŋbii ni eshwɛ, mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ nyɛaabamɔ nyɛhe kakla kɛye awerɛhoo kɛyashi?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: ‘Yehowa klante! Mɛɛ beyinɔ ohe aaajɔ? Kuu osɛɛ oyahɔ ohebo lɛ mli, ni ojɔɔ ohe, ni ofee kpoo!’

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ehe aaajɔ hu, be mli ni Yehowa efã lɛ lɛ? Efã lɛ ewo Ashkelon kɛ ŋshɔnaa maji lɛ ahe.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɛ yɛ Moab he nɛ, “Kpoo hã Nebobii ejaakɛ akpãtã amɛmaŋ lɛ hiɛ. Aŋɔ Kiriataim nom, ni ehiɛ eshwie shi; akumɔ emɔji gojogojoo lɛ ashwie shi.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Moab hiɛ nyam lɛ sɛɛ efo; ato ehe ŋaa fɔŋ yɛ Heshbon; Akɛɛ akɛ, nyɛhãa wɔbule eshishi koni ekatsɔ̃ maŋ yɛ je lɛ mli dɔŋŋ! Bo Madmen maŋ, nakai nɔŋŋ aaakpãtã ohiɛ; akɛ ta baanyiɛ osɛɛ.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Naa, aaawɔ lele kɛjɛ Horonaim akɛ, ‘Niiahiɛkpãtãmɔ kɛ Nifitemɔ.’

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Akpãtã Moab hiɛ, ebii bibii lɛ miibolɔ.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Amɛmiifo kɛmiikwɔ Luhit ŋmeŋme lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛmiinu niiahiɛkpãtãmɔ blɔmɔ he kɛjɛ Horonaim shikpelekemɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Nyɛjoa foi! Nyɛherea nyɛyiwala! Nyɛjoa foi tamɔ ŋaŋ teji yɛ shiaŋa nɔ.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nyɛ Moabbii, akɛni nyɛkɛ nyɛhiɛ fɔ̃ nyɛhewalɛ lɛ kɛ nyɛjwetrii lɛ anɔ hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ hu abaaŋɔ nyɛ nom. Abaaŋɔ nyɛwɔŋ Kemosh lɛ kɛ ewulɔmɛi kɛ ehe lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm hu nom.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Hiɛkpãtãlɔ lɛ baafite maŋ fɛɛ maŋ. Maŋ ko maŋ ko he ejeŋ mli, jɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ baakpãtã, ni abaafite ŋa kplanaa lɛ hu. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Nyɛhãa Moab fiji koni ekɛfiliki kɛya, ejaakɛ emaji lɛ baatsɔ̃mɔ amaŋfɔ̃ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi.

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: “Moab yɛ hejɔlɛ mli kɛjɛ eblahiiaŋ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe; atsɔ̃ko lɛ kɛjɛko nɔ kome mli awoko nɔ kroko mli dã; Aŋɔko lɛ nom dã, no hewɔ lɛ, etamɔ dãa ni enaanu gboko dã, ni eŋma hu tsakeko.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ Kemosh baawo Maobbii hiɛgbele tamɔ bɔ ni Betel, ni Israelbii ahiɛ kã enɔ lɛ, wo Israel hiɛgbele lɛ.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Moabbii, te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, kãkãlɔi kɛ ta mli kãkãlɔi ji wɔ?

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Moab kɛ emaji lɛ ahiɛ akpãtã nɛɛ; ni amɛmli hii kãkãlɔi lɛ hu ni enyɔnyɔi nɛɛ. Mi, Maŋtsɛ ni atsɛɔ mi Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, mi, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab hiɛkpãtãmɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ, ni emanehulu lɛ eshɛ shi etã.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: “Nyɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ Moab, nyɛyea lɛ ŋkɔmɔ; kɛ nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛle bɔ ni egbɛi ehehe, nyɛkɛa akɛ, ‘Te aye tɛŋŋ ni otsi wulu lɛ kɛ otsiamɛtso ekumɔ nɛɛ?’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ Dibon, nyɛshia nyɛgbojee sɛɛ nyɛkpelekea shi nyɛbataraa shikpɔŋ mlu mli, ejaakɛ Moab hiɛkpãtãlɔ lɛ ete shi ewo nyɛ, ni ekumɔ nyɛmɔji lɛ eshwie shi.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ Aroer, nyɛdamɔa gbɛ lɛ he nyɛsaraa koni nyɛbia mɔ ni ena foijee he gbɛ nuu ni jio, yoo ni jio, akɛ ‘Mɛni eba?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Amɛbaahere nɔ akɛ, ‘Ashwie Moab hiɛ shi, ejaakɛ akpãtã ehiɛ; Nyɛgbaa yɛ Arnon Faa lɛ kpokpai anɔ akɛ akpãtã Moab hiɛ!’

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: “Akpãtã maji ni jwere gɔji lɛ ayiteŋ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Amɛ ji Holon kɛ Yaza kɛ Mefat,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibon kɛ Nebo kɛ Bet-Diblataim,

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: kɛ Kiriataim kɛ Bet-Gamul kɛ Bet-Meon,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Moab akloŋto ni ji ehewalɛ lɛ, akpɔ, ni akpãtã ehewalɛ lɛ hiɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Abaaba Moab shi

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa Moab atɔa dãa, ejaakɛ ewo ehe nɔ yɛ Yehowa nɔ. Moab baakoklo shi yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ eshwee ni eshwe mli, ni abaaŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Te oŋmɔ Israel? Ani ona Israel akɛ efutu julɔi ateŋ hewɔ ni be fɛɛ be ni oootsi etã lɛ ohosoɔ oyitso lɛ?

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ Moab, nyɛshia nyɛmaji wuji lɛ amli koni nyɛbahia tɛkploi amli. Nyɛtsɔ̃mɔa nyɛhe tamɔ okpo ni feɔ etsu yɛ gɔji afɔjiaŋ.

english_verse: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
translation_verse: Wɔnu bɔ ni Moab wo ehe nɔ ehã; etsɛ ehe tsɔ̃. Anu ehenɔwomɔ kɛ ntɛŋfeemɔ kɛ ehetsɔ̃ɔmɔ kɛ ekuɛŋtimɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But I also know bragging will never save you.
translation_verse: Mile shwãa ni eshwã lɛ. Eshwãa ni eshwã lɛ kɛ enifeemɔnii fɛɛ lɛ yakanii ni.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mawo yara yɛ Moabbii ahewɔ; mafo Moabbii fɛɛ; mafo, maye Kir-Heresbii ŋkɔmɔ.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Ao Sibma, mafo bo fe bɔ ni mafo Yazer. Sibma, otamɔ waintso, ni ohe niji eteke Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ kɛtee kɛyashɛ Yazer tɔ̃ɔ. Shi naa, otsei ayibii kɛ owainyibii lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ ekpãtã.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Nyamɔ kɛ mliflimɔ sɛɛ efo yɛ Moab shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Mihã wain tsereee yɛ wain bui amli dɔŋŋ; mɔ ko eŋaaa wain yɛ jɛi kɛ nyamɔ lala; blɔmɔ ni anuɔ lɛ ejeee miishɛɛ blɔmɔ.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Heshbonbii kɛ Elealebii miibolɔ, ni aanu amɛbolɔmɔ nɛɛ yɛ Yahaz. Anu blɔmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ Zoar aahu kɛtee Horanaim kɛ Eglat-Shelishiya tɔ̃ɔ, ejaakɛ Nimrim Faa lɛ tete eŋala.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mi, Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ mibahã mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni shãa afɔle yɛ hei grɔŋgrɔŋŋ lɛ kɛ mɔ ni shãa tsofakɛŋma hãa Moab nyɔŋmɔi lɛ akpa feemɔ.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, Moabbii kɛ Kir-Heresbii ahe ŋkɔmɔ miibo yɛ mitsui mli tamɔ awerɛho lala ni aakpã kɛ bɛlɛ, ejaakɛ amɛjwetrii fɛɛ ni amɛtĩa lɛ efee yaka.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Moab tsui ayiteiaŋ fɛɛ kɛ eblohuiaŋ fɛɛ lɛ ŋkɔmɔ sɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ayeɔ yɛ jɛi, ejaakɛ mi, Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ mijwara Moab tamɔ kpulu ni mɔ ko mɔ ko taooo.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Te akpãtã Moab hiɛ ahã tɛŋŋ nɛɛ? Kwɛ bɔ ni emli bii lɛ ewo yara! Kwɛ bɔ ni etsɔ̃ esɛɛ ehã henyɛlɔ kɛ hiɛgbele. Etsɔ̃ fɛoyeli nɔ kɛ gbeyei nɔ ehã maji fɛɛ ni bɔle lɛ lɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Moab naŋ foijee hegbɛ

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa mɔ ko baaba ebayi Moab nɔ gleŋ tamɔ okropɔŋ ni egbɛ efijiaŋ,

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: ni ebaaŋɔ Moab maji ni ebaashɔ̃ emɔji lɛ. Ni nakai be lɛ Moab hii kãkãlɔi lɛ atsui aaatsɔ̃ tamɔ yoo ni miikɔmɔ tsui.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Abaakpãtã Moab hiɛ bɔ ni etsɔŋ maŋ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ ewo ehe nɔ yɛ Yehowa nɔ.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni aaajo gbeyei lɛ naa foi lɛ, eeeyagbee bu lɛ mli; ni mɔ ni aaakwɔ kɛje bu lɛ mli lɛ, eeeyadu tsɔne lɛ. Ejaakɛ mahã nɛkɛ jaramɔi nɛɛ aba Moabbii anɔ, afi nɔ ni mibagbala amɛtoi lɛ.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Foijelɔi ni amɛtɔ biti tao hejɔɔmɔhe yɛ Heshbon hɔ̃ɔŋ lɛ mli, shi la efã kɛjɛ Heshbon; la lilɛi efã kɛjɛ Maŋtsɛ Sihon we lɛ. Eshã Moab hiɛnaa ni ji bii hoofeelɔi lɛ apampam.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Ao Moab, kpoo hã bo. Kemosh egbe ejeŋ naa, ejaakɛ aŋɔ emli bihii lɛ nom, ni amɔmɔ yei lɛ hu nyɔji.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Shi naagbee mli aahu lɛ, mibahã Moab nine ashɛ nibii ni eŋmɛɛ lɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ, ‘Bɔ ni mikɛ Moab baaye mahã kɛyata nɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ Amonbii ahe nɛ, “Ani Israel bɛ bihii, aloo Israel bɛ mɛi ni yeɔ enii hewɔ ni mɛi ni jaa wɔŋ Molek lɛ ebaŋɔ Gadbii ashikpɔŋ, ni amɛbahi jɛi maji lɛ amli lɛ?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Naa, mi Yehowa, miikɛɛ akɛ be miiba, be ni mahã mɛi ni yɔɔ Amonbii amaŋ wulu Raba lɛ mli anu ta oshebɔɔ he. Ebaatsɔ̃ koikoi, ni abaashã ekrowai lɛ wɛɛ kɛmɔ shi, ni Israel baaye mɛi ni baye enɔ lɛ anɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Ao Heshbon, wɔ lele, shi akpãtã Ai maŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nyɛ Raba yei, nyɛfoa, nyɛmiaa kɛ kpekpe, nyɛyea ŋkɔmɔ; nyɛjoa foi kɛyaa kɛbaa yɛ koowieiaŋ, ejaakɛ abaaloo nyɛwɔŋ Molek kɛ ewulɔmɛi lɛ kɛ esɔ̃ɔlɔi lɛ kɛya nomŋɔɔ mli.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ni nyɛkwa nyɛhemɔkɛyeli, mɛɛba ni nyɛshwãa nyɛfɔ̃ɔ nyɛhewalɛ ni miigbɔjɔ nɔ, ni nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Namɔ baanyɛ shi ete ewo wɔ?’

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Naa, nɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ nyɛ ji akɛ mibahã mɛi fɛɛ ni bɔle nyɛ abahɛŋ nyɛ kɛ tsuifãa sane, ni abaashwie nyɛ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baajo foi bɔ ni ekwɛŋ esɛɛ tete, ni mɔ ko ehiŋ shi ni baabua foijelɔi lɛ anaa.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Shi naagbee mli lɛ mibahã Amonbii anine ashɛ nibii ni eŋmɛɛ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Yehowa baagbala Edombii atoi

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa, Taiatsɛ kɛɛ yɛ Edombii ahe nɛ, “Ani nilee bɛ Teman dɔŋŋ? Ani ŋaawoo elaaje hiɛshikãlɔi lo? Ani amɛnilee etã?

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Dedanbii, nyɛdɔa nyɛyi, ni nyɛjoa foi nyɛyatea nyɛhe yɛ nififiaŋ bui amli, ejaakɛ mibahã amanehulu aba Esaubii anɔ.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Kɛji wainyibiitselɔi ba nyɛŋɔɔ lɛ, ani amɛshiii yibii lɛ ashishi ni aye lɛ kpɛkpɛo lo? Aloo kɛji julɔi tete ba oŋmɔshinii juu nyɔɔŋ lɛ, amɛjuuu bɔ pɛ ni amɛtaoɔ lo?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Shi naa, mi lɛ mifee Esaubii pasaa; mijie amɛteemɔhei lɛ kpo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe amɛtee dɔŋŋ. Akpãtã Edombii kɛ amɛnyɛmimɛi kɛ amɛshwiei kɛ amɛnanemɛi fɛɛ ahiɛ. Ŋmɛnɛ, Edom bɛ nɔ ko mli dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Shi owusai lɛ ohã mi; mibakwɛ amɛnɔ shweshweeshwe; ni hã okulafoi lɛ ahe mi aye.”

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kɛji mɛi ni kulɛ esaaa akɛ agbalaa amɛtoi lɛ abaagbala amɛtoi lɛ, ani bo lɛ obaaye ohe? Oŋɔŋ ohe oyeŋ tswaa; esa akɛ agbala otoi kɛ̃.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mikã mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe kitã akɛ Bozra sane lɛ baafee gbeyei, abaabɔ lɛ ahora, ni abaakpãtã ehiɛ ni akɛ egbɛi baakã kitã ni emaji fɛɛ baatsɔ̃mɔ amaŋfɔ̃ kɛya naanɔ.”

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Minu saji ni jɛ Yehowa ŋɔɔ; ni awo bɔfo hu gbɛ kɛtee majimaji lɛ anɔ kɛ wiemɔ akɛ, “Nyɛbuaa nyɛtabilɔi anaa kɛkpea koni nyɛbatua Edom.

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ naa, mibaba bo shi kwraa yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ, ni ohe guɔ baagbo yɛ mɛi ahiɛ.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Bo mɔ ni ohɔ tɛkplo mli, kɛ bo mɔ hu ni oyɔɔ gɔŋ yiteŋ, oshishiu bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe kɛ gbeyei ni owo ohe kɛ ohe ni owo lɛ. Kɛji oshihilɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ niiaŋ tete po tamɔ okropɔŋ feɔ lɛ, mibaba bo shi.” Yehowa, kɛɛ.

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: “Edom sane baatsɔ̃ gbeyei nɔ, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baatsɔ̃ Edom he kɛho lɛ baashe gbeyei, ni ebaabo lɛ ‘gbeeakle’.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni atsɔ abutu Sodom kɛ Gomora kɛ amɛhewɔ maji lɛ, mi, Yehowa miikɛɛ akɛ nakai nɔŋŋ abaafee Edom bɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi, ni mɔ ko hu eyatoŋ gbɔ yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Naa, bɔ ni jata fãa kɛjɛɔ Yordan Faa he koo hayii mli kɛbaa ebatuaa too ku yɛ amɛniyelihe lɛ, nakai mibaba trukaa, ni mahã Edombii ajo foi amɛshi amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mi, mibato mɔ ni misumɔɔ koni eye Edom nɔ. Ejaakɛ namɔ kɛ mi ye egbɔ? Namɔ baanyɛ mi sane ebi? Mɛɛ maŋ hiɛnyiɛlɔ baanyɛ mihiɛ edamɔ?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Edom shigbeemɔ lɛ baahã shikpɔŋ tete ahoso, ni blɔmɔ ni amɛbaablɔ lɛ abaanu yɛ Akaba Bele lɛ kpokpai anɔ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Naa, nakai be lɛ mɔ ko baagba shi shwiaa kɛba tamɔ okropɔŋ ni egbɛ efijiaŋ kɛbatua Bozra, ni Edom hii kãkãlɔi lɛ atsui baatsɔ̃ tamɔ yoo ni miikɔmɔ tsui.” Yehowa baagbala Damaskobii atoi

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ Damaskobii ahe nɛ, “Hamatbii kɛ Arpadbii ejijaa, ejaakɛ amɛnu sane fɔŋ; amɛtsui efã fe nine, ni amɛyoyro; amɛfee tamɔ ŋshɔ ni efee hamahama ni amɛnaaa hejɔlɛ.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damaskobii egbɔjɔ, ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛjo foi; ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ amɛ; amɛhe miijara amɛ, ni amɛmiiye ŋkɔmɔ tamɔ yoo ni miikɔmɔ.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Te aye tɛŋŋ ni maŋ ni miishɛɛ yɔɔ mli sa lɛ, ajwa sam ashi lɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ eblahii lɛ baanyɔnyɔi yɛ eblohuiaŋ, ni abaaplenee etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ. Mi, Yehowa Taiatsɛ, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Mama Damasko maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ naa la, ni ebaashã Maŋtsɛ Ben-Hadad mɔji lɛ blublu.” Agbala Kedar kɛ Hazar Maŋ wulu lɛ toi

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ yɛ Kedar kɛ maji bibii ni yɔɔ Hazor maŋ lɛ shishi ni Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar ye amɛnɔ lɛ ahe nɛ, Bɔ ni, Yehowa, kɛɛ nɛ, “Nyɛtea shi, nyɛyatuaa Kedar, ni nyɛkpãtãa bokãgbɛbii lɛ ahiɛ!

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ Hazorbii, nyɛjoa foi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ nyɛyahɔlɔa bui amli, ejaakɛ naa, Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar eto nyɛhe yiŋ fɔŋ.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Nyɛtea shi, nyɛyatuaa maŋ ni he ejɔ lɛ ni eyɔɔ shweshweeshwe, maŋ ni agboi loo agbosɛɛ adabaŋi ahe ehiaaa amɛ, maŋ ko ni ekɛ ehe ebɔɔɔ maŋ ko he, shi ekome eyɔɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: “Abaahã amɛfukpɔŋɔi lɛ, ni amɛtsinai lɛ baatsɔ̃ ojoyelinii. Mibagbɛ mɛi ni kuɔ amɛyi fãfãafãi lɛ mashwã jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛjɛɔ kɛbaa lɛ; mibahã amɛmanehului ajɛ he fɛɛ he abanina amɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Hazor baatsɔ̃ ŋaŋgbei ashihilɛhe; ebaatsɔ̃ naanɔ amaŋfɔ̃, ni adesa ko adesa ko ehiŋ jɛi, ni mɔ ko hu eyatoŋ gbɔ yɛ jɛi. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Yehowa baagbala Elam toi

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa, Taiatsɛ lɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, “Naa, mibakpãtã Elam gãitsɛ̃lɔi ni ji Elam hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ,

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Makpãtã amɛmaŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ lumɛi lɛ ahiɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ mikɛ mimaŋtsɛyeli sɛi lɛ aaabama Elam. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Shi naagbee mli aahu lɛ, mibahã Elam nine ashɛ nibii ni eŋmɛɛ lɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Mi, Yehowa mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Yehowa tsɔ̃ Gbalɔ Yeremia nɔ ewie yɛ Babilon maŋ lɛ kɛ emli bii lɛ ahe nɛ,

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: “Shiɛmɔ koni okɛɛ jeŋ majimaji lɛ, shii aflaŋaa, ni oshiɛ; okashiu nɔ ko nɔ; kɛɛmɔ akɛ Aye Babilon nɔ kunim. Awo lɛ hiɛgbele Mardruk werɛ eho ehe. Ashwie Babilon amãgãi lɛ ahiɛ shi, amɛnaa diɛŋtsɛ ekpɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: “Ejaakɛ maŋ ko efã ta kɛjɛ kooyigbɛ kɛmiiba ebatua Babilon, ni ebaahã Babilon atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ bɔ ni gbɔmɔ ni jio, kooloo ni jio, fɛɛ baajo foi ashi jɛi, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi.” Israelbii asɛɛkuu

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kɛ Yudabii lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm baabua amɛhe naa amɛba kɛ yaafo amɛbatao Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, sɛɛgbɛ.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Amɛbaabi he ni gbɛ ni yaa Zion lɛ kã, ni amɛbaatsɔ̃ amɛhiɛ amɛhã jɛi gbɛ, ni amɛaakɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛbaa koni wɔ kɛ Yehowa ayakpãŋ kpãŋmɔ ni akuŋ mli asaŋ ni hiɛ kpaŋ nɔ kɛaatee naanɔ.’

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: “Mimaŋbii lɛ tamɔ toi ni elaaje; amɛnɔkwɛlɔi lɛ ehã amɛdu gbɛ, amɛkpala amɛ kɛnyiɛ gɔji anɔ, amɛkɛ amɛ ejɛ gɔŋ wulu nɔ kɛtee gɔŋ bibioo nɔ, ni shĩagbɛ elaaje amɛ.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni naa amɛ lɛ kpãtãa amɛhiɛ, ni amɛhenyɛlɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Wɔyeee fɔ, ejaakɛ amɛfee esha amɛshi Yehowa, mɔ ŋɔɔ ni amɛshihilɛhe diɛŋtsɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ji amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ ahiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ.’

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: “Nyɛjoa foi yɛ Babilon; nyɛshia Babilonbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nyɛfea nyɛhe tamɔ tookpakpoi kɛnyiɛ tookui lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ naa, mitee maji wuji shi yɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikɛ amɛ miiba abatua Babilon. Amɛbaagba ta amɛwo Babilon, ni jɛigbɛ abaajɛ aye Babilon nɔ kunim. Amɛgãii lɛ tamɔ hii kãkãlɔi ni jɛɛɛ ta mli baaa shĩa kɛ amɛniji nyɔŋma.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Abaaha Babilon, ni mɛi fɛɛ ni baayaha Babilon lɛ baana nii bɔ ni amɛtsuii baatɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Babilon shigbeemɔ

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛha miwebii anii, eyɛ mli akɛ nyɛmiinya, ni nyɛmli efili nyɛ tamɔ tsinabi oblayoo ni miigbɛlɛ abele; ni nyɛmiibolɔ tamɔ okpɔŋɔ nuu moŋ nɛ,

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: shi naa, nyɛ nyɛhiɛ baagbo kpɔtɔɔ; yoo ni fɔ nyɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baashwie shi pam. Naa, nyɛmaŋ wulu lɛ baatsɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maji lɛ ateŋ bibioo fe fɛɛ; ebaatsɔ̃ ŋa kpataa ni enɔ egbi tamɔ shiaŋa.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa mlifu naa lɛ, adesa ko ehiŋ jɛi, shi ebaatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ kwrakwra. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaatsɔ̃ Babilon he kɛho lɛ naa aaakpɛ ehe, ni eeebo lɛ ‘gbeeakle’ yɛ bɔ ni afee lɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ gãitsɛ̃lɔi, nyɛgbaa ta kɛbɔlea Babilon he kɛkpea. Nyɛtsɛ̃rɛa lɛ nyɛgãii lɛ, nyɛkasɛ̃sɛ̃a gãimlibii lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ Babilon efee esha eshi Yehowa.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Nyɛbɔa oshe kɛbɔlea lɛ. Babilon ehole eniji anɔ akɛ enyɛɛɛ ta lɛ dɔŋŋ; ehe gbogboi lɛ ewule, akumɔ amɛ ashwie shi, ejaakɛ Yehowa oweletɔɔ ji no. Nyɛtɔa nyɛhe owele yɛ enɔ; bɔ ni efee mɛi komɛi lɛ, nyɛ hu nyɛfea lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Nyɛkaŋmɛa mɔ ko gbɛ ni edu nii yɛ Babilon, ni nyɛkaŋmɛa mɔ ko gbɛ ni ekpã ŋmɔshinii yɛ Babilon. Henyɛlɔi aklante hewɔ lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baatao emaŋbii asɛɛgbɛ, ni ebaajo foi kɛya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ nɔ.” Israelbii lɛ asɛɛkuu kɛbaa

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: “Israel tamɔ toi ni gbɔbimɔ ni jatai gbɔbiɔ amɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ji mɔ ni ye eloo, ni sɛɛkpee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar ji mɔ ni ekpe ewui lɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Naa, mibagbala Babilon maŋtsɛ kɛ emaŋ lɛ fɛɛ toi tamɔ bɔ ni migbala Asiria maŋtsɛ lɛ toi lɛ.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Mibakpale Israel kɛba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye Karmel kɛ Bashan shikpɔji lɛ anɔ nii, ni eeetɔ kɛ Efraim kɛ Gilead gɔji lɛ anɔ nii lɛ.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Kɛji nakai be lɛ shɛ lɛ, aaatao nishaianii yɛ Israel, shi anaŋ eko, ni anaŋ esha ko yɛ Yuda hu, ejaakɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni mibahã ashwɛ lɛ, maŋɔ amɛhe mafa amɛ. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.’ ” Nyɔŋmɔ baagbala Babilon toi

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: “Nyɛfãa nyɛyatuaa Merataimbii kɛ Pekodbii lɛ. Nyɛgbea amɛ, nyɛnyiɛa amɛsɛɛ, nyɛplenea amɛ kwrakwra. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ; nyɛfea bɔ ni mifã nyɛ akɛ nyɛfee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Aanu tawuu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni aakpãtã nibii ahiɛ pam.

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Te aye tɛŋŋ ni jeŋjeŋ fɛɛ hamle lɛ ajwara lɛ ni akumɔ lɛ ashwie shi nɛɛ? Te aye tɛŋŋ ni Babilon etsɔ̃ gbeyei nɔ yɛ maji ateŋ nɛɛ?

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Ao, Babilon, mitsɔ̃ bo tsɔne, ni odu; shi oleee; ana bo, ni amɔ bo, ejaakɛ okɛ Yehowa fu daa.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Yehowa egbele etawuu nibii atoohe lɛ naa, ni ejie emlifu tawuu nibii lɛ kpo, ejaakɛ Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ, yɛ nitsumɔ ni ebaatsu yɛ Babilonbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Nyɛjɛa hei fɛɛ nyɛbatuaa lɛ, nyɛjwaraa eboŋoi ashinai lɛ; nyɛbuaa haanii lɛ anaa tamɔ ŋmaa kei, ni nyɛkpãtãa maŋ lɛ hiɛ butuu, ni nyɛkashĩa enɔ ko nɔ ko.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Nyɛgbea Babilon hii lɛ tamɔ agbeɔ tsina hii; nyɛkpalaa amɛ kɛyaa nyɛyagbea amɛ fɛɛ tswɛm. Kpoo hã amɛ! Ejaakɛ amɛtoigbalamɔ be lɛ eshɛ.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: “Naa, mɛi ni eje gbele mli lɛ ejo foi kɛjɛ Babilon shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee Yerusalɛm, ni amɛmiigba akɛ Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, etɔ eSɔlemɔ we lɛ he owele.

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: “Nyɛtsɛa gãitsɛ̃lɔi lɛ nyɛwoa Babilon he, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni le gãitsɛ̃mɔ aya eko. Nyɛsaa maŋ lɛ yi kɛkpea; ni nyɛkahãa mɔ ko naa fɔijee hegbɛ. Bɔ ni Babilon fee mɛi komɛi lɛ nyɛkɛ lɛ ayea nakai nɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ ekɛ Yehowa, Israel Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, fũ daa.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, abaagbegbee eblahii lɛ ashwã eblohuiaŋ, ni abaaplene etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: “Bo maŋhewolɔ, naa, mi kɛ bo ena. Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Taiatsɛ lɛ, kɛɛ, ejaakɛ ogbi lɛ eshɛ be ni mibagbala otoi lɛ.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Hewolɔ lɛ baatɛ, ni ebaagbee shi, ni enaŋ mɔ ko awo enɔ. Mibama emaji wuji lɛ anaa la, ni ebaashã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni bɔle lɛ.”

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa, Taiatsɛ, kɛɛ nɛ, “Aaye Israelbii lɛ kɛ Yudabii lɛ hu fɛɛ anɔ keketee; ni mɛi ni baŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ hiɛ amɛ kpɛŋŋ, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛya amɛmaŋ.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Shi amɛ-Kpɔlɔ lɛ he wa, ni egbɛi ji Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ. Ye kɛ̃ ebaaye amɛsane lɛ ehã amɛ koni hejɔlɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; shi Babilonbii lɛ, haomɔ ji nɔ ni baanina amɛ.”

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Ta baanina Babilon, gbele baanina emaŋbii kɛ elumɛi lɛ kɛ enilelɔi lɛ.

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Ta baanina okɔmfoi nifeelɔi lɛ, ni amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ kwashiai. Ta baanina ehii kãkãlɔi lɛ, koni amɛhiɛ akpãtã.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Ekpɔŋɔi kɛ taayaa shwiilii lɛ ahiɛ baakpãtã; maŋsɛɛ tabilɔi ni futu amɛ lɛ, hu ahiɛ baakpãtã; ni amɛaatsɔ̃mɔ tamɔ yei! Abaagbɛ amɛ ashwã koni aha amɛ.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Nu enɛŋ, hewɔ lɛ fai fɛɛ baaŋala, ejaakɛ Babilon eyi tɔ kɛ amãgãi, ni amãgãi nɛɛ asɔ̃ɔmɔ eye amɛ sɛkɛ.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: tamɔ bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ butu Sodom kɛ Gomora kɛ amɛhewɔ majimaji lɛ bɔ ni mɔ ko ehiii jɛi, ni asaŋ mɔ ko ni jɛ yoo musuŋ eyatoŋ gbɔ yɛ jɛi lɛ, mi Yehowa mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Naa, maŋ wulu ko miijɛ kooyigbɛ aba, maŋ ko ni he wa, kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi babaoo miijɛ je lɛ naagbeehei shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ amɛba kɛ ta.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Amɛhiɛ amɛgãi kɛ akplɔi; amɛyi wa, ni amɛnaaa mɔbɔ. Kɛji anu amɛkpɔŋɔi ni amɛtara amɛnɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, egbɛɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ. Amɛmia tamɔ nuu ni miiya ta. Ao! Babilon, amɛmiiba amɛkɛ bo abawu.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babilon maŋtsɛ nu amɛhe pɛ, kɛkɛ ni enijiaŋ je wui, ni etsui fã tamɔ yoo ni miikɔmɔ ni ebaafɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Naa, mafã tamɔ jata ni ejɛ Yordan Faa lɛ he koo hayii lɛ mli ni ebatua kooloi yɛ jwɛifɔ ŋa nɔ, ni mahã amɛjo foi trukaa kɛje jɛi; ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mafã mɔ ko koni eye maŋ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ namɔ tamɔ mi? Namɔ baanyɛ mi ekɛfu daa? Namɔ baanyɛ mi mihiɛ edamɔ?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Kɛji anu he akɛ aŋɔ Babilon nom lɛ, shikpɔŋ baahoso, ni abaanu Babilon awerɛho blɔmɔ yɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Matee mumɔ ko ni fiteɔ nii shi mawo Babilon kɛ emli bii ni ji Kaldeabii lɛ,

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: ni matsu mɛi kpɔ̃ji kɛya Babilon koni amɛsha emli tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ shaa ŋmaa mli lɛ. Nakai gbi fɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaajɛ Babilon hewɔ hei fɛɛ abatua lɛ, ni amɛbaafee eshikpɔŋ lɛ shwɛm.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Akaŋmɛ gãitsɛ̃lɔ ko gbɛ ni etsɛ̃ egãi lɛ, ni akaŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ewo edade dama tete. Akɛ eblahii lɛ eko kwraa he akake lɛ; akpãtã etabilɔi lɛ ahiɛ butuu.

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Mɛi baanyɔnyɔi yɛ Babilon shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni pilafoi baajwere blohui lɛ amli.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Israelbii lɛ kɛ Yudabii lɛ aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni ji Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, ekwako amɛ; shi Babilonbii lɛ, amɛ lɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi tɔ kɛ nifɔɔjianii babaoo ni amɛkɛtɔ̃ Israel Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Nyɛjoa foi kɛjea Babilon teŋ; mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ahere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiwala. Nyɛkahãa aplenea nyɛ yɛ Babilon toigbalamɔ lɛ mli, ejaakɛ Yehowa oweletɔɔ be lɛ eshɛ, no ji Babilon toi ni egbalaa nɛɛ.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilon tamɔ shika kpulu yɛ Yehowa dɛŋ, ni kɛtsɔ̃ enɔ lɛ ehã jeŋ maji fɛɛ tɔrɔ dãa; jeŋ maji lɛ nu edɛŋ wain lɛ eko, no hewɔ lɛ, jeŋ maji lɛ ye sɛkɛ.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Babilon egbee shi trukaa, ni ehiɛ ekpãtã; nyɛfoa lɛ; akɛ tsofa ato epilamɔ lɛ nɔ, eko lɛ aaatsa lɛ.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Kulɛ wɔɔtsa Babilon, shi ehiii lɛ tsamɔ. Nyɛshia lɛ, ni nyɛhãa wɔteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋ nɔ he ni ejɛ, ejaakɛ Babilon toigbalamɔ lɛ eshɛ ŋwɛi, ni awo nɔ kɛyashɛ atatuiaŋ tɔ̃ɔ.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: “Yehowa etsiɛ Mediabii amaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ amumɔ hiɛ, ejaakɛ yiŋ ni eto yɛ Babilon maŋ lɛ he ji akɛ ebaakpãtã ehiɛ, ejaakɛ ekɛ no baatɔ eSɔlemɔ we lɛ he owele. Tabilɔi ni eba maŋ lɛ tuamɔ lɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ fã akɛ, ‘Nyɛjɔa gãimlibii lɛ anaa, ni nyɛkɔlɔa tsɛŋi!’

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Ao! Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ he ni nu babaoo yɔɔ, ni nyɛyɔɔ jwetri babaoo, nyɛnaagbee eshɛ, ni afo nyɛwala sɛɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ, ekã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kitã akɛ, ‘Mahã tabilɔi tamɔ baalabii afalɛ abayi omli obɔ̃ tɔ, ni amɛbaabɔ kunimyeli oshe.’ ” Nyɔŋmɔ yijiemɔ lala

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Kɛji ewo egbee lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shimɔɔ, ni ehãa afua teteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naagbeehei fɛɛ. Ehãa srawa gbalaa yɛ nunɛmɔ mli, ni ehãa ahum fãa kɛjɛɔ he ni eto amɛ yɛ.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: “Yehowa bɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, yɛ ehewalɛ naa, ni ejɛ nilee mli ebɔ je lɛ, ni elɛɛ ŋwɛi mli kɛ ŋaa.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Adesa lɛ kwashia ni, enilee faaa; shikaŋaalɔ fɛɛ shikaŋaalɔ hiɛ egbo, yɛ amãgãi ni efee lɛ ahewɔ; lakamɔ nibii ni, ni mumɔ bɛ amɛmli.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Amɛhe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ, mɔ akɛlakaa; be ni abaagbala amɛtoi lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛ baakpãtã.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ tamɔɔɔ enɛɛmɛi, ejaakɛ lɛ ebɔ nibii fɛɛ kwa; ni Israel ji maŋ ni eŋɔ akɛ enɔ.” Yehowa Taiatsɛ lɛ ji egbɛi. Yehowa hamle lɛ

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Babilon, bo ji mihamle, bo ji mitawuunii. Bo mikɛjwaraa majimaji wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ, bo mikɛkpãtãa maŋtsɛyelii ahiɛ.

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: Bo onɔ mitsɔ̃ɔ migbeɔ nuu kɛ yoo, kɛ onukpa kɛ gbekɛ, kɛ oblanyo kɛ oblayoo;

english_verse: shepherds and their flocks, farmers and their oxen, and governors and leaders.
translation_verse: Bo mikɛkpãtãa tookwɛlɔ kɛ etoi ahiɛ, kɛ okwaafonyo kɛ ehumɔ kooloi ahiɛ, kɛ amraloi kɛ lumɛi hu ahiɛ.” Babilon toigbalamɔ

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Mibawo Babilon maŋ lɛ kɛ Babilonbii fɛɛ anifɔ̃ɔjianii ni amɛfee Yerusalɛm lɛ he nyɔmɔ yɛ nyɛhiɛ.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Ao, Babilon ni otsɔ̃ ohe gɔŋ ni oofite shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ, naa, mikɛ bo ena; mawo minine nɔ yɛ onɔ, ni makoklo bo kɛjɛ tɛsai lɛ anɔ matswa shi, ni mahã otsɔ̃ gɔŋ ni eshã.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Akɔŋ omli tɛ ko akɛtswaŋ koŋtɛ loo akɛto tsu shishi; shi moŋ obaatsɔ maŋ amaŋfɔ̃ kɛya naanɔ. Mi Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: “Nyɛshia tayaa aflaŋaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nyɛkpãa tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ yɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ. Nyɛsaa maji lɛ nyɛhãa ta nyɛwoa Babilon. Nyɛwoa maŋtsɛyeli ni ji Ararat kɛ Mini kɛ Ashkenaz ŋaa koni amɛfã ta amɛwo Babilon. Nyɛfãa tatsɛ koni enyiɛ tabilɔi lɛ ahiɛ kɛyatua lɛ. Nyɛkɛ okpɔŋɔi abaa babaoo tamɔ baalabii.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Nyɛsaa maji lɛ kɛhã ta nyɛwoa Babilon. Maji nɛɛ ji, Media maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ amɛshishi amraloi lɛ kɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ afee kralo.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ejijaa, ni eekpokpo, ejaakɛ Yehowa miitsu eyiŋ ni eto akɛ ebaahã Babilon atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi lɛ he nii.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilon tabilɔi kãkãlɔi lɛ ekpa ta lɛ wuu; amɛhɔlɔ amɛmɔji lɛ amli, amɛhewalɛ egbɔjɔ, ni amɛtsɔ̃mɔ tamɔ yei. Akumɔ amɛgboi lɛ asɛɛ adabãi lɛ, ni eshĩai lɛ miitso kɛ la.

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: Aŋɔ maŋ lɛ faafoohe lɛ, ni hebuu mɔji lɛ ashã, ni tabilɔi lɛ atsui efã.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Yehowa Taiatsɛ, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Babilon kɛ emli bii etsɔ̃ tamɔ ŋmãagbeemɔhe ni aagbee ŋmaa yɛ jɛi; eshwɛ fioo kɛkɛ ni be lɛ baashɛ, ni abaaloo amɛ kɛya tamɔ ŋmɔshinii ni akpa.’ ”

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar eye mi, ni ekpãtã mihiɛ; ehã mitsɔ̃ tsɛnsi folo; ni emi mi tamɔ jeŋ miɔ nii; ewo emusu obɔ̃ kɛ minibii ni ŋɔɔŋɔɔ lɛ, ni eŋa mimli nu fɛɛ tswɛm.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Zionnyo akɛɛ akɛ, “Yi ni awa mi kɛ miwekumɛi lɛ yi sɔ̃ atere Babilon.” Yerusalɛm akɛɛ akɛ, “Babilonbii aye milá yi sɔ̃!” Yehowa baaye ebua Israel

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, mibaye osane lɛ mahã bo, ni mibatɔ ohe owele. Mibahã he ni Babilon naa enu kɛjɛɔ lɛ agbi, ni mahã emli fai lɛ aŋala;

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: ni Babilon baatsɔ̃ koikoi kɛ ŋaŋgbei ashihilɛhe, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baatsɔ̃ jɛi kɛho naa baakpɛ ehe, ni ebaabo lɛ ‘gbeeakle,’ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ jɛi.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: Babilonbii fɛɛ baahuu tamɔ jatai, ni amɛbaablɔ tamɔ jatabii.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Be mli ni amɛmli ewo la lɛ, mibaŋmɛ amɛ okplɔ̃, ni mahã amɛtɔrɔ dãa koni amɛmli afili amɛ, ni wɔ baanyɔ amɛnɔ, ni amɛhiɛ etsɛ̃ŋ kɛaatee naanɔ. Mi, Yehowa mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Mibakpala amɛ tamɔ gwantɛŋbii kɛ gwantɛŋhii kɛ tookpakpoi kɛya koni agbe amɛ.” Bɔ ni Babilon naagbee baatamɔ

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Ŋshɔ tete egri ewo Babilon, ni ŋshɔkei wujiwuji ni gbɛɔ lɛ ebaha enɔ.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Emaji wuji lɛ etsɔ̃mɔ gbeyei nɔ; amɛtsɔ̃mɔ hei ni nu enɛɛɛ yɛ kɛ shiaŋa, shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiii nɔ, ni gbɔmɔ adesa ko tsɔ̃ɔɔ jɛi kɛhooo.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Mibagbala Bel, Babilonbii awɔŋ lɛ toi, ni mahã egɔi nibii fɛɛ ni emimii. Majimaji anɔ bii eloŋ amɛhe kɛyaŋ eŋɔɔ dɔŋŋ. Babilon maŋ lɛ he gbogbo lɛ ekumɔ eshwie shi.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: Miwebii Israelbii, nyɛshia Babilon. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ajo Yehowa mlifu ni naa wa lɛ naa foi ni ehere eyiwala.

english_verse: Don't be afraid or lose hope, though year after year there are rumors of leaders fighting for control in the city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Nyɛtsui akafãa, ni nyɛkashea gbeyei kɛji nyɛnu sane ko yɛ afi ko nɔ, ni afi kroko hu nɔ lɛ nyɛnu sane kroko. Nyɛtsui akayea, ni nyɛkashea gbeyei kɛji nyɛnu henitswiamɔ ni maŋtsɛmɛi tswiaa amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ miiba be ni mikɛ Babilon shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amãgãi lɛ baaye kɛ joomɔ lɛ. Abaashwie Babilon shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ shi, ni emli gbɔmɛi lɛ baanyɔnyɔi yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ emli.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ amɛmli nibii fɛɛ baala kɛ miishɛɛ kɛye Babilon he fɛo, ejaakɛ mɛi baajɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ abakpãtã ehiɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: Esa akɛ Babilon agbee shi yɛ Israelbii ni egbegbee lɛ ahewɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni Babilon hewɔ lɛ agbegbee jeŋ majimaji anɔ bii lɛ.” Wiemɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhã Israelbii ni yɔɔ Babilon

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛje klante naa gbele mli, nyɛyaa, nyɛkadamɔa shi. Nyɛkaia Yehowa yɛ shɔŋŋ he ni nyɛyɔɔ lɛ tete, ni nyɛkaia Yerusalɛm hu.

english_verse: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, naa, be miiba ni mikɛ Babilon amãgãi lɛ baaye kɛ joomɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pilafoi fɛɛ baakɛ̃mɔ.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɛ Babilon kwɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi tamɔ mɛ, ni kɛ ewaje emɔji lɛ akɛ mɛ, kɛ̃lɛ mibawo mɛi gbɛ kɛyakpãtã ehiɛ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” Babilon hiɛkpãtãmɔ kroko hu

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛboa toi! Aabolɔ kɛjɛ Babilon! Babilon shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛkpãtãmɔ kpeteŋkple lɛ he blɔmɔ ni.

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Yehowa miifee Babilon amaŋfɔ̃, ni eefo efuufeemɔ sɛɛ. Henyɛlɔi tabilɔi keɔ kɛbaa kɛ blɔmɔ tamɔ ŋshɔke gbɛɛmɔ.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ hiɛkpãtãmɔ eba Babilon nɔ, ni amɔmɔ etabilɔi lɛ, ni akumɔ amɛgãii amli dukuduku, ejaakɛ Yehowa Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, toigbalalɔ ji lɛ, ni ewoɔ nifeemɔ fɔŋ he nyɔmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.
