translation_verse: Mikwɛ, ni naa, mina nɔ ko ni tamɔ gbɔmɔ. Kɛjɛ ehɛgbɛ kɛbaa eshishigbɛ su lɛ anaa lɛ tamɔ la; ni kɛjɛ ehɛgbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛigbɛ su lɛ kpɛlɛɔ tamɔ akɔɔble ni asha he.

english_verse: It reached out what seemed to be a hand and grabbed my hair. Then in my vision the Lord's Spirit lifted me into the sky and carried me to Jerusalem. The Spirit took me to the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard, where there was an idol that disgusted the Lord and made him furious.
translation_verse: Ekpã nɔ ko ni esu tamɔ nine mli ni ekɛmɔ̃ miyiteŋ tsɔi ni efi tɔo lɛ mli. Mumɔ lɛ wo minɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋwɛi teŋ, ni ekɛ mi tee Yerusalɛm yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ he ninai lɛ amli. Ekɛ mi ba mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ agbo ni kwɛɔ kooyigbɛ shinaa lɛ naa, he ni amãgã ni hãa Nyɔŋmɔ yeɔ awuŋã lɛ ma lɛ.

english_verse: Then I saw the brightness of the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River.
translation_verse: Ni naa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ anunyam lɛ kpɛ yɛ jɛi tamɔ ninaa ni mina yɛ Kebar Faa lɛ naa lɛ.

english_verse: God said to me, “Ezekiel, son of man, look north.” And when I did, I saw that repulsive idol by the altar near the gate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, wo ohiɛ nɔ ni okwɛ kooyigbɛ.” Ni miwo mihiɛ nɔ mikwɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ, ni naa, afɔleshãa latɛ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ agbo lɛ naa lɛ, nakai amãgã lɛ ni haa Nyɔŋmɔ yeɔ awuŋã lɛ ma jɛi.

english_verse: God then said, “Do you see the terrible sins of the people of Israel? Their sins are making my holy temple unfit as a place to worship me. Yet you will see even worse things than this.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, oona nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ? Musubɔɔnii wuji ni Israelbii lɛ feɔ yɛ biɛ bɔ ni afee ni maje mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛya sɛɛ shɔŋŋ. Osaa ooona musubɔɔnii wuji krokomɛi ni fe enɛ.”

english_verse: Next, I was taken to the entrance of the courtyard, where I saw a hole in the wall.
translation_verse: Ekɛ mi ba kpo lɛ nɔ shinaa lɛ naa, ni be ni mikwɛ lɛ mina folɔ ko yɛ gbogbo lɛ mli.

english_verse: God said, “Make this hole bigger.” And when I did, I realized it was a doorway.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbuu gbogbo lɛ mli.” Ni be ni migbu gbogbo lɛ mli lɛ mina shinaa ko.

english_verse: “Go in,” God said, “and see what horrible and evil things the people are doing.”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Botemɔ mli ni oyakwɛ nɔ musubɔɔnii ni amɛfeɔ yɛ biɛ.”

english_verse: Inside, I saw that the walls were covered with pictures of reptiles and disgusting, unclean animals, as well as with idols that the Israelites were worshiping.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mibote mli ni miyakwɛ; ni mina akɛ atɛŋ waamɔnii kɛ kooloi ni ahiɔ srɔtoi abɔ, kɛ Israel we lɛ wɔji lɛ fɛɛ amɛfonirii yɛ gbogbo lɛ he kɛbɔle kɛkpe.

english_verse: Seventy Israelite leaders were standing there, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each of these leaders was holding an incense burner, and the smell of incense filled the room.
translation_verse: Ni Israel we lɛ mli hii onukpai nyɔŋmai kpawo damɔ wɔji lɛ ahiɛ, ni Shafan bi Yaazania damɔ amɛteŋ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hiɛ etsofakɛŋmashaa ŋɛsu yɛ edɛŋ, ni tsofakɛŋma ni ashãa lɛ lasu lɛ teɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi tamɔ atatu.

english_verse: God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, oona nɔ ni Israel we lɛ onukpai lɛ feɔ yɛ dujiaŋ akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miija amãgãi yɛ esɛɛtsu mli lo? Nɔ ni amɛkɛɔ ji akɛ, ‘Yehowa enaaa wɔ. Yehowa ekwa shikpɔŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: But I will show you something even worse than this.”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Osaa ooona musubɔɔnii krokomɛi ni fe enɛ ni amɛfeɔ.”

english_verse: He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ ekɛ mi ba Yehowa shĩa lɛ agbo lɛ shinaa ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ naa; ni naa, yei tara jɛi ni amɛmiifo jemawɔŋ Tamuz.

english_verse: God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ona enɛ? Osaa ooona musubɔɔnii wuji ni fe enɛɛmɛi.”

english_verse: God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ona enɛ? Ani nihiinii ni Yuda we lɛ feɔ yɛ biɛ nɛɛ lɛ efaaa ehãaa amɛ lo? Ni amɛhã yiwalɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ̃ tɔ kɛmiiwo mimli la amɛfata he nɛɛ lo? Naa, amɛmaa mi gɔnti amɛjɛɔ mi.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mikɛ amɛ baaye kɛ joomɔ yɛ mimlifu lɛ naa. Mihaŋ amɛŋɔ amɛhe amɛye; minaŋ amɛ mɔbɔ. Amɛaabolɔ amɛwo mitoiŋ kɛ gbee ni wa shi miboŋ amɛ toi.”

english_verse: After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
translation_verse: Minu akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ bo kɛ gbee ni wa akɛ, “Nyɛbaa biɛ, nyɛ, maŋ blafoi; mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ahiɛ gbɔmɔgbee dade yɛ edɛŋ.”

english_verse: I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ni naa, hii ekpaa jɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ agbo ni ye kooyigbɛ lɛ naagbɛ amɛba. Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hiɛ emɔgbee dade yɛ edɛŋ. Nuu ko hu fata amɛhe ni ewo niyɛŋ, ni etsotsoro nɔ ko ni nibii ni akɛŋmãa nii yɛ mli. Amɛtee mli ni amɛyadamɔ akɔɔble afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ masɛi.

english_verse: The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ anunyam lɛ wo ehe nɔ kɛjɛ bɔɔ nibii kɛ amɛfiji lɛ anɔ, he ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaa lɛ shi: Etsɛ nuu lɛ ni wo niyɛŋ ni etsotsoro nɔ ko ni akɛŋmãa nii lɛ.

english_verse: “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaakpa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ; hii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛi ni amɛyeɔ ŋkɔmɔ yɛ musubɔɔnii ni afeɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kadimɔ amɛhiɛnai.”

english_verse: He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.” The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
translation_verse: Nyɛgbea onukpai kɛ oblahii kɛ oblayei kɛ gbekɛbii kɛ yei blublu, shi mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni akadi ehiɛnaa lɛ, lɛ lɛ nyɛkataa ehe. Nyɛjea shishi kɛjɛa mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɔi kɛjɛ onukpai lɛ ni yɔɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ hii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛbulea Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni nyɛkɛ mɛi ni egboi lɛ agbohii lɛ ashwiea kpoi lɛ anɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃. Agbɛnɛ, nyɛjea kpo!” No hewɔ lɛ, amɛje kpo amɛbote maŋ lɛ mli amɛyatswia mɛi anii ni amɛgbe amɛ.

english_verse: I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
translation_verse: Be ni amɛgbeɔ mɛi lɛ ni ashi mikome too lɛ, miho migbee shi, ni mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi ni mibo mikɛɛ akɛ, “Ao, Nuŋtsɔ, Yehowa ani ookpãtã Israel mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ yɛ omli ni efu Yerusalɛm waa lɛ naa lo?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Israel kɛ Yuda efee esha kpele, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ̃ tɔ kɛ lashishwiemɔ, ni toikɔdɔmɔ saneyeli hu eyi maŋ lɛ mli obɔ̃; ejaakɛ amɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Yehowa ekwa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni Yehowa enaaa wɔ.’

english_verse: And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mihaŋ mɔ ko aŋɔ ehe aye; minaŋ mɔbɔ; shi moŋ mahã amɛmusu abua amɛyiteŋ.”

english_verse: Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
translation_verse: Ni naa, nuu lɛ ni bu niyɛŋ lɛ, mɔ ni tsotsoro nɔ ko ni nibii ni akɛŋmãa nii yɔɔ mli lɛ, ku esɛɛ eba, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Mifee bɔ ni ofã mi lɛ.”

english_verse: I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ lɛ mikwɛ, ni naa nɔ ko pue yɛ atatu ni yɔɔ bɔɔ nibii lɛ ayiteŋgbɛ lɛ mli, nɔ lɛ tamɔ maŋtsɛ sɛi ni akɛ safiro ojarawatɛ fee.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nuu lɛ ni bu niyɛŋ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa kokolontoi ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ateŋ ni oyakpiti ŋai ni miitso owo okɔkɔi amli obɔ̃bɔ̃ ni okɛshwã maŋ lɛ mli.” Ni etee yɛ mihiɛ.

english_verse: The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard,
translation_verse: Adebɔɔ nibii lɛ damɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ wuoyigbɛ he ni nuu lɛ bote mli yɛ lɛ; kɛkɛ ni atatu ko yi Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ tɔ.

english_verse: and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa anunyam lɛ kpɛmɔ lɛ wo ehe nɔ yɛ bɔɔ nibii lɛ anɔ kɛtee Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaa lɛ shi; ni atatu lɛ yi Sɔlemɔ we lɛ obɔ̃, ni Yehowa anunyam kpɛmɔ lɛ yi kpo lɛ nɔ obɔ̃.

english_verse: The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: Anu adebɔɔ nibii lɛ afijiaŋ gbɛɛmɔ lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ. Ni gbɛɛmɔ lɛ tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ gbee kɛji eewie lɛ.

english_verse: One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni adebɔɔ nibii lɛ ateŋ ekome kpã enine mli kɛjɛ adebɔɔ nibii lɛ ateŋ ewo la ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ nibii ateŋ lɛ mli, ni ekpiti la lɛ eko, ni ekɛwo nuu ni bu niyɛŋ lɛ kɔkɔiaŋ; nuu lɛ he, kɛkɛ ni eje kpo.

english_verse: I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings,
translation_verse: Mina akɛ adebɔɔ nibii nɛɛ yɛ niji tamɔ gbɔmɛi aniji yɛ amɛfiji lɛ ashishi.

english_verse: and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite.
translation_verse: Mikwɛ ni mina akɛ kokolontoi ejwɛ yɛ adebɔɔ nibii lɛ ahe; kokolonto kome yɛ bɔɔnɔ kome he. Kokolontoi lɛ ahe kpɛlɛɔ tamɔ ojarawatɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ krisolito lɛ.

english_verse: Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Kɛji okwɛ amɛ lɛ, kokolontoi ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ su kome, tamɔ nɔ ni eko hɔ eko mli.

english_verse: I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes.
translation_verse: Hiŋmɛii yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe: amɛkotosɛɛ kɛ amɛniji ahe kɛ amɛfiji ahe fɛɛ hiŋmɛii sɔŋŋ. Kokolontoi ni adebɔɔ nibii ejwɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tete ahe eyi obɔ̃ kɛ hiŋmɛii sɔŋŋ.

english_verse: And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
translation_verse: Ni kokolontoi lɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ minu kɛ mitoi akɛ atsɛ amɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ̃ɔɔ amɛhe.

english_verse: Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle.
translation_verse: Nibii ni hiɛ gbɔmɛi asu nɛɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ hiɛi srɔtoi ejwɛ: Klɛŋklɛŋ hiɛ lɛ tsinanuu hiɛ, ni hiɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛ, ni hiɛ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ jata hiɛ, ni hiɛ ni ji ejwɛ lɛ okropɔŋ hiɛ ni.

english_verse: These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
translation_verse: Kɛji bɔɔ nibii lɛ wa damɔ shi lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ kokolontoi lɛ hu ewa kɛdamɔ shi, kɛ amɛfliki kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ amɛkɛ kokolontoi lɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋwɛi, ejaakɛ bɔɔ nibii lɛ amumɔ yɛ amɛmli.

english_verse: Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa anunyam lɛ je Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaa lɛ shi ni eyadamɔ bɔɔ nibii lɛ ayiteŋgbɛ.

english_verse: They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
translation_verse: Miikwɛ nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ, ni bɔɔ nibii lɛ hole amɛfiji anɔ, ni amɛfliki kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee, ni kokolontoi lɛ kpɛtɛ amɛhe. Amɛyadamɔ Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ bokãgbɛ agbo lɛ shinaa lɛ shi; ni Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ anunyam lɛ kpɛ yɛ amɛnɔ.

english_verse: I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River.
translation_verse: Nibii ni tamɔ gbɔmɛi asu ni mina yɛ Kebar Faa lɛ naa yɛ Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ nɛ; miyoo akɛ bɔɔ nibii ni.

english_verse: They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
translation_verse: Shi amɛhiɛi lɛ tamɔ hiɛi ni mina yɛ Kebar Faa lɛ naa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nyiɛɔ kɛyaa ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english_verse: and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni migba nomii lɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Yehowa jie kpo tsɔ̃ɔ mi lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Mumɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mɛnɛɛmɛi ji mɛi ni toɔ yiŋshai, ni amɛwoɔ ŋai gbohii yɛ maŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ.

english_verse: They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’
translation_verse: Amɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Be ni akɛmaa tsu shɛko. Maŋ nɛɛ tamɔ dadesɛŋ ni ma la nɔ, ni wɔji emli loo lɛ.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, condemn them!”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa oshi amɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders: I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa Mumɔ lɛ yi minɔ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni mi, Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, ‘Nyɛ Israelbii, nakai nyɛsusuɔ; mile nibii ni nyɛsusuɔ yɛ nyɛyitseiaŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies!
translation_verse: Nyɛha mɛi ni nyɛgbegbee lɛ ayi efa yɛ maŋ nɛɛ mli, ni eblohuiaŋ eyi tɔ kɛ gbohii babaoo.’ ”

english_verse: This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, “Mɛi ni nyɛgbegbee nyɛshwie maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛ ji loo lɛ, ni maŋ nɛɛ ji dadesɛŋ lɛ; shi nyɛ lɛ, abaashwie nyɛ kɛje maŋ nɛɛ mli.”

english_verse: and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛshe klante gbeyei, shi klante nɔŋŋ mahã afa awo nyɛyi.

english_verse: Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies.
translation_verse: Mibashwie nyɛ kɛbaaje maŋ nɛɛ mli, ni mikɛ nyɛ baawo gbɔi adɛŋ, ni makojo nyɛ.

english_verse: You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Ni klante naa nɔŋŋ nyɛanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ; makojo nyɛ yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ husu nɔ, ni nyɛkɛaana nyɛle akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel.
translation_verse: Maŋ nɛɛ tsɔŋ dadesɛŋ ehaŋ nyɛ, ni nyɛ hu nyɛtsɔŋ emli loo. Mikɛ nyɛ baaye yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ husui lɛ fɛɛ anaa.

english_verse: You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
translation_verse: Ni nyɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa, ejaakɛ nyɛhiko shi yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa, ni nyɛbako nyɛjeŋ yɛ mimlai lɛ anaa; shi moŋ maŋsɛɛbii ni bɔle nyɛ lɛ moŋ amlai lɛ anɔ nyɛye.”

english_verse: Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ be ni migbaa lɛ, Benaia bi Pelatia tswa shi egbo trukaa. Kɛkɛ ni miho migbee shi mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi, ni mibo waa akɛ, “Ao, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, ani obaakpãtã mɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ Israel lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ?” Nyɔŋmɔ wo nomii lɛ ashi

english_verse: The Lord replied:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mɛi ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm lɛ miiwie bo kɛ onyɛmimɛi, ojakubii ni ji Israelbii fɛɛ ni aŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ ahe. Amɛkɛɛ, ‘Nomii lɛ eyaje shɔŋŋ bɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ Yehowa amɛja. Yehowa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ehã wɔ akɛ wɔnɔ.’

english_verse: But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia: It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ nomii lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, yɛŋ akɛ mijie amɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ kɛyafutu maji krokomɛi amli bii, ni migbɛ amɛ mishwã shikpɔji anɔ moŋ nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ, mitsɔ̃ teemɔhe krɔŋkrɔŋ mihã amɛ be fioo ko kɛ̃ yɛ hei ni amɛtee lɛ.”

english_verse: And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ mikɛɛ nɛ, mabua amɛnaa kɛaajɛ maji amli ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã lɛ, shikpɔji hu ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛba, ni maŋɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ maha amɛ.’

english_verse: When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much.
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛba lɛ amɛaajie taŋtaŋnii kɛ musubɔɔnii lɛ fɛɛ kɛaaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me
translation_verse: Ni mahã amɛ tsui kroko, ni mikɛ mumɔ hee baawo amɛmli; majie amɛtsui ni wa tamɔ tɛ lɛ kɛje amɛmli ni mahã amɛ loo tsui;

english_verse: and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: bɔ ni afee ni amɛba amɛjeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa, ni amɛye mimlai lɛ anɔ, koni amɛtsɔ̃ miwebii ni mi hu matsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni atsui nyiɛ taŋtaŋnii kɛ musubɔɔnii asɛɛ lɛ, magbala amɛtoi, ni mahã amɛsɔ̃ abua amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyiteŋ. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɛ.” Nyɔŋmɔ anunyam lɛ je Yerusalɛm

english_verse: After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni bɔɔ nibii lɛ hole amɛfiji anɔ, ni kokolontoi lɛ kɛ amɛ hole amɛhe nɔ, ni Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ anunyam lɛ shĩ yɛ amɛyiteŋgbɛ.

english_verse: left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
translation_verse: Yehowa anunyam lɛ wo ehe nɔ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ teŋ, kɛtee gɔŋ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away,
translation_verse: Mina yɛ ninaa lɛ mli akɛ Mumɔ lɛ wo mi, ni ekɛ mi tee nomii lɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Babilon; kɛkɛ ni mumɔ lɛ je minɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mɛi ni toi egbo ateŋ oyɔɔ lɛ; shi amɛyɛ hiŋmɛii, shi amɛnaaa nii; amɛyɛ toii hu shi amɛnuuu nii, ejaakɛ maŋ ni toi egbo ji amɛ.”

english_verse: So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɔ adesa, too onibii tamɔ mɔ ni aŋɔ lɛ nom, koni ofã shwane be ni amɛmiikwɛ bo. Jee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛya he kroko ni amɛmiikwɛ bo. Eko lɛ amɛaakɔ nɔ ni ofeɔ lɛ sɛɛ, tsɛ, gbɔmɛi toigbolɔi ji amɛ.

english_verse: After you have done this, return to your house. Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile.
translation_verse: Okɛ onibii ni tamɔ nomŋɔɔ jatsu lɛ aje kpo shwane yɛ amɛhiɛ; shi yi mli gbɛkɛ yɛ amɛhiɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ooya nomŋɔɔ mli.

english_verse: Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching.
translation_verse: Gbuu gbogbo lɛ mli yɛ amɛhiɛ koni otsɔ̃ jɛi kɛje kpo yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛji hiɛ bu lɛ, wo ogbɛfaa jatsu lɛ otswa okɔŋ yɛ amɛhiɛ ni okɛje kpo. Haa ohiɛ koni okana shikpɔŋ ni oyaa nɔ lɛ. Mikɛ bo miito okadi mahã Israel we lɛ.

english_verse: I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mifee bɔ ni Yehowa fã mi lɛ. Mikɛ minibii lɛ je kpo shwane tamɔ mɔ ni aŋɔ lɛ nom, ni gbɛkɛ mli lɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ migbu gbogbo lɛ mli; ni be ni hiɛ bu lɛ miwo mijatsu lɛ mitswa mikɔŋ ni mije kpo yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, the Lord
translation_verse: Ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ,

english_verse: reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ani Israel we lɛ, ni ji toigbolɔi awe lɛ, biko bo akɛ, ‘Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ lo?’

english_verse: So he sent me back to tell them: The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, nɔ ni ofee nɛɛ gbalɛ ni; ni ekɔɔ lumɔ ni yeɔ nɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, kɛ Israel we lɛ mli bii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni ofee nɛɛ ji okadi hã amɛ; bɔ ni ofee otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ, nakai abaafee amɛ; abaaŋɔ amɛ nom, ni amɛbaatsɔmɔ nomii.’

english_verse: The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving.
translation_verse: Amɛteŋ lumɔ lɛ ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ, lɛ ebaawo ejatsu etswa ekɔŋ kɛje kpo be mli ni hiɛ ebu. Ebaatsɔ̃ gbogbo ni agbu aha lɛ mli kɛje kpo. Ebaaha ehiɛ, ni ekana shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eyaa lɛ kɛ ehiŋmɛi.

english_verse: The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there.
translation_verse: “Maŋmɛ miyaa lɛ, ni eeedu lɛ tamɔ tsɔne, ni mikɛ lɛ baaba Babilon maŋ wulu lɛ mli. Shi jɛi shikpɔŋ lɛ tete ehiŋmɛi enaŋ, tsɛbelɛ jɛi nɔŋŋ eeegbo yɛ.

english_verse: His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
translation_verse: Mɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle lɛ kɛkpe lɛ, kɛ eyelikɛbualɔi lɛ kɛ etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, magbɛ amɛ mashwã kɔɔyɔŋ yɛ jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni magbala klante kɛnyiɛ amɛsɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things.
translation_verse: “Kɛji migbɛ amɛ mishwã majimaji kɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ no amɛkɛaale akɛ, mi mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way. A Sign of Fear
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mashi mɛi fioo ko ni amɛaaje klante kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbele hela gbele mli. Amɛaajaje nihiinii ni amɛfee lɛ fɛɛ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ yɛ majimaji ni amɛyaa mli lɛ anɔ, ni amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Gbalɔ ni miikpokpo lɛ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye nii; kɛji ooye lɛ, ha ohe akpokpo ni kɛji oonu nu lɛ, ha ohe ajo kɛ gbeyeishemɔ.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ kɛɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ akɛ, Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ yɛ Yerusalɛmbii ni yɔɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nɛ, amɛniyenii lɛ, tsuiyeli amɛkɛaaye, ni amɛnu lɛ hu, hejɔ̃mɔ amɛkɛaanu; ejaakɛ yiwalɛnii ni maŋ lɛ mli bii lɛ fɛɛ fee lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ahaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ aba niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord. The Words of the Lord Will Come True
translation_verse: Maji ni ahi mli dã lɛ fɛɛ baatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu aaatsɔ̃ shiaŋa, ni amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Abɛi ni ale kɛ gbalɛ ni aleee

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie, ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.”
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mɛni ji abɛ ni nyɛbuɔ yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɛ, ‘Gbii miiho kɛmiiya, ni gbalɛ ko baaa mli lɛ?’

english_verse: Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true!
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, mibaha nɛkɛ abɛ ni abuɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ afo, ni abuŋ dɔŋŋ yɛ Israel.’ Shi moŋ kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ be ni eshɛ, ni gbalɛ fɛɛ gbalɛ baana aba mli.

english_verse: The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amale ninaa ko ejeŋ kpo dɔŋŋ, ni gbalɛ ni akɛlakaa mɔ ko hu baŋ mli dɔŋŋ yɛ Israel we lɛ.

english_verse: I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Shi mi, Yehowa, mibawie, ni wiemɔ ni mibawie lɛ baaba mli. Atsiŋ atoŋ dɔŋŋ. Ao! Nyɛ toigbolɔi awe, nyɛyinɔ nɛɛ mibawie, ni mibafee hu. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, naa, Israelbii lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Oninaa lɛ yeɔ bei pii dani ebaa mli, ni ogbalɛi lɛ hu kɔɔ be ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ he.’

english_verse: So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, atsiŋ miwiemɔ lɛ eko atoŋ dɔŋŋ, shi wiemɔ ni miwieɔ lɛ baaba mli. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa oshi Israel gbalɔi lɛ ni sɔ̃ɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalɛi lɛ. Kɛɛmɔ gbalɔi nɛɛ akɛ nyɛboa Yehowa wiemɔ toi.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages!
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kpoo ha gbalɔi kwashiai lɛ ni nɔ ni amɛmumɔ kɛɔ amɛ lɛ, no amɛgbaa, tsɛ amɛnako nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ.

english_verse: Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city.
translation_verse: Ao, Israelbii, nyɛgbalɔi lɛ etsɔmɔ osɔi ni hɔlɔ tsukoi amli.

english_verse: They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me.
translation_verse: Amɛbuuu fɔji lɛ anaa, ni amɛtswaaa gbogbo amɛwooo Israel we lɛ he, bɔ ni eeenyɛ ekpee ta naa yɛ Yehowa gbi lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true.
translation_verse: Amɛfoɔ amale saji amɛtãa, ni amɛgbaa amale gbalɛi. Amɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Yehowa kɛɛ,’ be mli ni Yehowa tsuko amɛ; ni kɛ̃lɛ amɛkpaa gbɛ akɛ amɛwiemɔi lɛ aba mli.

english_verse: They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
translation_verse: Ani kɛji miwieko, shi nyɛaakɛɛ akɛ, ‘Yehowa kɛɛ’ lɛ, no lɛ ani jeee yaka ninaa nyɛnaa, ni amale gbalɛ nyɛgbaa lɛ lo?”

english_verse: So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ amɛ nɛ, “Akɛni nyɛkɛɔ nibii ni bɛ mli, ni nyɛmaleɔ hewɔ lɛ, naa, mikɛ nyɛ ena; mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mate shi mawo gbalɔi ni naa ninai ni bɛ mli, ni amɛmaleɔ lɛ; amɛhiŋ mimaŋ lɛ gwabɔɔ lɛ mli, ni asaŋ aŋmaŋ amɛgbɛii yɛ Israel we lɛ wolo lɛ mli, ni amɛyiŋ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu; ni nyɛkɛale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa lɛ.

english_verse: Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint.
translation_verse: “Naa! Akɛni amɛlakaa mimaŋ lɛ akɛ ‘Omanye eba,’ be mli ni omanye ko bɛ lɛ. Mimaŋbii lɛ tswaa gbogbo ni amale gbalɔi lɛ shaa he kaaloo;

english_verse: But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse.
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ mɛi ni kɛ kaaloo shaa gbogbo lɛ he lɛ akɛ ebaagbee shi. Nu baanɛ waa, nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi wuji baanɛ, ni ahum baatswa,

english_verse: People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
translation_verse: Ni no lɛ gbogbo lɛ baagbee shi; ani abiŋ nyɛ akɛ, ‘Kaaloo lɛ ni nyɛkɛsha gbogbo lɛ he lɛ, nɛgbɛ ehe sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ?’

english_verse: That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mikɛ mlifu aaahã ahum atswa, ni mikɛ mlila aaahã nu anɛ waa, ni mahã nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi wuji aaanɛ kɛkpãtã nii ahiɛ.

english_verse: The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
translation_verse: Makumɔ gbogbo ni nyɛkɛ kaaloo esha he lɛ mashwie shi; ni eshishitoo lɛ aaaje kpo faŋŋ. Eshigbeemɔ mli lɛ eeegbee nyɛ nɔ, ni eeekpãtã nyɛhiɛ, ni nyɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead,
translation_verse: “No ni mimli baafu gbogbo lɛ, kɛ mɛi ni sha he kaaloo lɛ. No ni makɛɛ nyɛ akɛ gbogbo lɛ bɛ dɔŋŋ, ni mɛi ni sha he lɛ hu bɛ dɔŋŋ,

english_verse: because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Women Who Wear Magic Charms The Lord said:
translation_verse: mɛi ni ji Israel gbalɔi ni gba yɛ Yerusalɛm he, ni amɛna omanye ninai yɛ ehe, tsɛbelɛ, omanye ko bɛ lɛ; mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mi, mikɛɛ.” Gbalɛ ni kɔɔ yei amale gbalɔi ahe

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ owo omaŋ lɛ mli biyei lɛ ni kaa amɛhiɛ amɛgbaa lɛ; gbaa oshi amɛ.

english_verse: Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies.
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ akɛ, nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, kpoo ha yei ni kpɛɔ sɛbɛi amɛŋmɔlɔɔ mɛi anijiashi, ni amɛkpɛɔ yitso fɛɛ yitso dalɛ he yiteŋhaa mama amɛhãa mɛi, ni amɛkɛlakaa gbɔmɛi kɛjeɔ Nyɔŋmɔ he nilee he. Ani nyɛbaadu miwebii lɛ, ni nyɛbaa susumai krokomɛi ayi yɛ nyɛsɛɛnamɔ hewɔ?

english_verse: They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
translation_verse: Akoko dɛ kɔkɔi obɔ̃bɔ̃i kɛkɛ kɛ aboloo atrɔmai kɛkɛ ahewɔ lɛ, nyɛbuleɔ mi yɛ mimaŋ mli, ni nyɛgbeɔ mɛi ni esaaa akɛ amɛgboiɔ, ni nyɛhereɔ mɛi ni sa akɛ amɛgboi lɛ moŋ ayiwala. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛmaleɔ nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ mimaŋbii lɛ ni boɔ toi lɛ.”

english_verse: I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, mitaooo sɛbɛi ni nyɛkɛlakaa mɛi lɛ, ni matserɛ amɛ yɛ nyɛnijiashi mashwie, ni mibaha susumai ni nyɛdu tamɔ loofɔji lɛ aye amɛhe.

english_verse: I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ni matserɛ nyɛyiteŋhaa mamai lɛ hu, ni makpɔ̃ miwebii lɛ kɛjɛ nyɛdɛŋ, ni amɛhiŋ nyɛdɛŋ kwraa dɔŋŋ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin.
translation_verse: “Nyɛkɛ amale hãa jalɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui, tsɛbelɛ, mi lɛ mihako enijiaŋ aje wui; ni nyɛwoɔ mɔ fɔŋ moŋ ekãa, no hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɛɛ ekpale kɛje egbɛ fɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ahere eyiwala.

english_verse: I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nyɛnaŋ lakamɔ ninai dɔŋŋ, ni klamɔ hu nyɛklaŋ dɔŋŋ, shi moŋ makpɔ̃ mimaŋ lɛ yɛ nyɛdɛŋ ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Israel onukpai lɛ ekomɛi ba amɛbabi Yehowa nii. Amɛtara shi yɛ mihiɛ

english_verse: While they were there, the Lord said:
translation_verse: ni Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ akɛ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ kɛ amɛtsuii eŋmɛ amɛmãgãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛhã amɛnishaianii lɛ etsɔ̃ pampi ma amɛhiɛ. Ani esa akɛ maŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛbabi mi nii kwraa lo?”

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ amɛ awie ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni jɛ Israel we ni kɛ etsui ŋmɛɔ emãgãi anɔ, ni ehaa enishaianii tsɔ̃ɔ pampi maa ehiɛ, ni kɛ̃lɛ, ebaa gbalɔ ŋɔɔ ebabiɔ nii lɛ, mi, Yehowa, mi diɛŋtsɛ mahã lɛ hetoo yɛ emãgãi lɛ ayikulɛ lɛ naa,

english_verse: When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
translation_verse: bɔ ni afee ni matsake Israelbii lɛ atsui, ejaakɛ amɛtsɔ̃ amɛmãgãi lɛ anɔ amɛtse amɛhe kɛje mihe.

english_verse: Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel: I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuii ni nyɛkpalea kɛjea nyɛmãgãi lɛ ahe, ni nyɛjiea nyɛhe kɛjea nihiinii lɛ fɛɛ ahe.”

english_verse: Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer
translation_verse: “Ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni jɛ Israel we, loo gbɔi ni ebato gbɔ yɛ Israel he ko ni tseɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ mihe, ni ekɛ etsui ŋmɛɔ amãgãi lɛ anɔ, ni ehãa enishaianii tsɔ̃ɔ pampi ehaa lɛ, ni kɛ̃lɛ ebaa gbalɔ ŋɔɔ ni ebi mi nii eha lɛ lɛ, mi, Yehowa diɛŋtsɛ maha lɛ hetoo.

english_verse: by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: Majie mihiɛ maka nakai mɔ lɛ, mikɛ lɛ baafee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni akɛbuɔ abɛ, ni majie lɛ yɛ miwebii lɛ ateŋ, ni nyɛkɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people,
translation_verse: “Ni kɛji nɔ ko aaalaka gbalɔ lɛ ni ewie wiemɔ ko lɛ, belɛ mi, Yehowa, mi ji mɔ ni laka nakai gbalɔ lɛ, ni mikɛ lɛ aaaye; makpãtã ehiɛ kɛaaje mimaŋ Israelbii lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way.
translation_verse: Abaagbala amɛ fɛɛ amɛtoi. Gbalɔ lɛ kɛ mɔ ni yabiɔ gbalɔ lɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ aaana toigbalamɔ kome.

english_verse: I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise. Judgment on a Sinful Nation
translation_verse: Mibafee enɛ bɔ ni afee ni Israel we lɛ akatse amɛhe kɛmiije mihe ni amɛyadu gbɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛ nifɔɔjianii lɛ miibule amɛhe dɔŋŋ; shi moŋ amɛtsɔ̃ miwebii, ni mi hu matsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.” Noa, Daniel kɛ Hiob

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ ni ekɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛji shikpɔŋ ko nɔ bii fee esha shi mi, ni amɛyeee mi anɔkwa, ni mite shi miwo amɛ, ni mifo amɛniyeniinamɔ sɛɛ, ni mihã hɔmɔ ba nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikpãtã gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ ahiɛ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
translation_verse: kɛji nɛkɛ hii etɛ̃ nɛɛ, ni ji Noa kɛ Daniel kɛ Hiob, futu amɛ tete po lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛjalɛ lɛ aaahere amɛ pɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyiwala; Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert.
translation_verse: “Kɛji miha kooloi awuyelɔi bakpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ̃ ni amɛplenee enɔ bii lɛ fɛɛ, ni etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, bɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko tsɔ̃ɔɔ nɔ kɛhooo yɛ kooloi lɛ ahewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
translation_verse: kɛji nɛkɛ jalɔi etɛ̃ nɛɛ yɛ jɛi tete lɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛbihii loo amɛbiyei po yiwala amɛhere. Amɛaahere amɛ pɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyiwala, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃.

english_verse: Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock.
translation_verse: “Aloo kɛji mifã klante miwo nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii, ni mikɛɛ akɛ, akɛ klante akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikpãtã gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ ahiɛ kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
translation_verse: kɛji nɛkɛ hii jalɔi etɛ̃ nɛɛ yɛ jɛi tete lɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, amɛnyɛŋ binuu loo biyoo po yiwala ahere; shi amɛ pɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyiwala amɛaahere.

english_verse: And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation.
translation_verse: “Nakai nɔŋŋ kɛji mihã gbele hela ko ba nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikɛ mlifu hã lá shwie shi koni makpãtã gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ;

english_verse: Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
translation_verse: kɛji Noa kɛ Daniel kɛ Hiob tete po yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ nɛɛ, mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɛ akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛbihii loo amɛbiyei tete po ayiwala amɛhere; amɛkɛ amɛjalɛ lɛ baahere amɛ pɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyiwala.”

english_verse: I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Te eeetamɔ tɛŋŋ kɛji miha nibii ejwɛ ni mikɛgbalaa toi, ni ji klante kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ kooloi awuiyelɔi kɛ gbele hela lɛ ba Yerusalɛm, ni miha amɛkpãtã gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi ahiɛ yɛ mli?

english_verse: And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Ni kɛji hiɛkãalɔi komɛi aaashwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛaanyɛ amɛhere amɛbihii kɛ biyei ayiwala lɛ, kɛji nakai bihii kɛ biyei lɛ ba nyɛŋɔɔ ni nyɛna amɛjeŋba kɛ amɛnifeemɔi pɛ, nyɛbaanu shishi akɛ toigbalamɔ ni mikɛba Yerusalɛm yɛ enifɔɔji anii ni efee lɛ he lɛ, esa lɛ.

english_verse: You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛna amɛjeŋba kɛ amɛnifeemɔnii lɛ pɛ nyɛbaanu shishi, no aaahã nyɛle akɛ nii fɛɛ ni mifee Yerusalɛm lɛ mifee ni shishinumɔ yɛ he.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekɛɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest,
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mɛni waintso kɛfe tso kroko? Mɛni waintso nine kɛfe tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english_verse: because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on.
translation_verse: Ani akɛ etso lɛ feɔ nɔ ko kwraa? Ani gbɔmɔ kɛ eko gbɔɔ shiŋmlitso ni akɛ nii tsotsoroɔ nɔ lo?

english_verse: It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything.
translation_verse: Naa, akɛfeɔ lai ni ashãa. Kɛji enaabu biɛ kɛ biɛ shã, ni eteŋ hu fɛɛ eshã etsɔ̃ ŋai lɛ, ani ehiɔ kɛhã nɔ ko feemɔ kwraa lo?

english_verse: The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
translation_verse: Naa, be ni eji waintso muu po, akɛtsuuu nɔ ko, ni kɛji la ŋala lɛ ni etsɔ ŋai lɛ, no lɛ ani aaanyɛ akɛtsu nɔ ko kwraa lo?”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, promise that just as the wood of a grapevine is burned as firewood,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Bɔ ni mihãa la shãa waintso kɛ tsei krokomɛi fɛɛ yɛ koo mli lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ maŋɔ Yerusalɛmbii lɛ mahã.

english_verse: I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Majie mihiɛ maka amɛ, ni kɛji amɛje la lɛ mli tete lɛ, la lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ baakpãtã amɛhiɛ. No ni nyɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, kɛji mijie mihiɛ mika amɛ lɛ.

english_verse: I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mibaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, ejaakɛ amɛyeee mi anɔkwa.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, remind the people of Jerusalem of their disgusting sins
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, jajemɔ musubɔɔnii ni Yerusalɛm efee lɛ otsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ni okɛɛ Yerusalɛm akɛ,

english_verse: and tell them that I, the Lord God, am saying: Jerusalem, you were born in the country where Canaanites lived. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ Yerusalɛm nɛ, ojɛ Kanaanbii ashikpɔŋ nɔ, ni jɛi afɔ bo yɛ. Amornyo ji otsɛ, ni Hityoo ji onyɛ.

english_verse: When you were born, no one cut you loose from your mother or washed your body. No one rubbed your skin with salt and olive oil, and wrapped you in warm blankets.
translation_verse: Asaŋ yɛ ofɔmɔ mli lɛ, gbi ni afɔ bo lɛ, afooo olaŋmɔ, akɛ nu hu juuu ohe ni ohe aje, akɛ ŋoo kpaaa ohe hu, ni akɛ mama hu ebalaaa ohe.

english_verse: Not one person loved you enough to do any of these things, and no one even felt sorry for you. You were despised, thrown into a field, and forgotten.
translation_verse: Mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa bo mɔbɔ ni emusuŋ aaatsɔ̃ lɛ ni eeefee nibii nɛɛ ateŋ ekoeko ehã bo, shi moŋ ashɛ bo afɔ ŋa kplanaa nɔ, ejaakɛ anyaŋe bo kɛjɛ gbi ni afɔ bo lɛ beebe.

english_verse: I saw you lying there, rolling around in your own blood, and I couldn't let you die.
translation_verse: “No ni be ni mibatsɔ̃ omasɛi kɛho lɛ, mina bo ni ookoklo shi yɛ ola mli. Mikɛ bo wie yɛ ola lɛ mli akɛ,

english_verse: I took care of you, like someone caring for a tender, young plant. You grew up to be a beautiful young woman with mature breasts and hair, but you were still naked.
translation_verse: ‘Oyi ana wala koni oda tamɔ ŋanɔtso.’ Kɛkɛ ni oda, ni okwɔ, ni oshɛ oblayoo, ni oje fufɔ, ni oyitsɔi kɛlɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ onyiɛ yayai kɛ ohe pasaa.

english_verse: When I saw you again, you were old enough to have sex. So I covered your naked body with my own robe. Then I solemnly promised that you would belong to me and that I, the Lord God, would take care of you.
translation_verse: “Be ni mibatsɔ̃ omasɛi kɛho ekoŋŋ lɛ, naa, mina akɛ oda ni oshɛ gbãlã, ni miha bo mimama lɛ eko ni mikɛtsi oyayai nɔ. Hɛɛ, misumɔ bo kɛha gbãlãshihilɛ, ni mikɛ bo kpãŋ, ni otsɔ̃ minɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: I washed the blood off you and rubbed your skin with olive oil.
translation_verse: “Kɛkɛ ni mikɛ nu ju ohe ni mifɔ ohe lá lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ohe, ni mikpa bo mu.

english_verse: I gave you the finest clothes and the most expensive robes, as well as sandals made from the best leather.
translation_verse: Mibu bo mama hu ni aye samai yɛ mli, ni miwo bo nuŋgbee wolo tokota; mifi bo duku yɛŋ, ni mibu bo sliki mama.

english_verse: a ring for your nose, some earrings, and a beautiful crown.
translation_verse: Miwo ogugɔŋ ga, ni miwo otoiiaŋ toiiaŋnii. Mikɛ akekre fɛɛfɛo fi oyitso.

english_verse: Your jewelry was gold and silver, and your clothes were made of only the finest material and embroidered linen. Your bread was baked from fine flour, and you ate honey and olive oil. You were as beautiful as a queen,
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ awula bo kɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi ni owoɔ. Ni ohebo ji klala fɛɛfɛo kɛ sliki kɛ mama ni alo nii awo mli. Oye shikishaŋnii kpakpa kɛ wo kɛ mu, ni ohe fee fɛo jogbaŋŋ naakpa, ni otsɔ̃ maŋnyɛ.

english_verse: and everyone on earth knew it. I, the Lord God, had helped you become a lovely young woman.
translation_verse: Ogbɛi hu hehe kɛtee jeŋ maji srɔtoi anɔ yɛ ohe fɛo lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ bɔ ni miwula bo lɛ hã ohe fee fɛo kɛmɔ shi.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: You learned that you were attractive enough to have any man you wanted, so you offered yourself to every passerby.
translation_verse: “Shi odi ohe fɛo kɛ ogbɛi ni ehehe lɛ sɛɛ ni obɔ ajwamãŋ; ni okɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni hoɔ wɔɔ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: You made shrines for yourself and decorated them with some of your clothes. That's where you took your visitors to have sex with them. These things should never have happened!
translation_verse: Okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ otadei lɛ ekomɛi wulaa ohei krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, ni obɔɔ ajwamãŋ yɛ amɛnɔ, nɔ ni afeko eko dã, ni asaŋ afeŋ nakai nɔ ko hu.

english_verse: You made idols out of the gold and silver jewelry I gave you, then you sinned by worshiping those idols.
translation_verse: Osaa oŋɔ ojwinei fɛɛfɛji ni ji mishika kɛ mijwiɛtɛi ni mihã bo lɛ eko okɛfee hii amãgãi ohã ohe, ni okɛ amɛbɔ ajwamãŋ.

english_verse: You dressed them in the clothes you got from me, and you offered them the olive oil and incense I gave you.
translation_verse: Okɛ otadei ni aye ŋaabii awo amɛmli lɛ ha amãgãi lɛ anɔ, ni okɛ mimu kɛ mitsofakɛŋma lɛ mamɔ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: I supplied you with fine flour, olive oil, and honey, but you sacrificed it all as offerings to please those idols. I, the Lord God, watched this happen.
translation_verse: Asaŋ milɛ bo kɛ ashikishaŋ kpakpa kɛ mu kɛ wo, ni miniyenii ni mikɛhã bo lɛ, nomɛi okɛmamɔ amãgãi lɛ ahiɛ koni eje ŋma ewo amɛ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: But you did something even worse than that—you sacrificed your own children to those idols!
translation_verse: “Asaŋ obihii kɛ obiyei ni ofɔ ohã mi lɛ hu ogbe amɛ okɛshã afɔlei ohã amãgãi lɛ ni amɛye.

english_verse: You slaughtered my children, so you could offer them as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ani ajwamãŋbɔi nɛɛ faaa hãaa bo hewɔ ni ogbe mibii lɛ, ni okɛ amɛ shã afɔlei ohã amãgãi lɛ?

english_verse: You were so busy sinning and being a prostitute that you refused to think about the days when you were young and were rolling around naked in your own blood.
translation_verse: Be ni ofeɔ musubɔɔnii nɛɛ ni obɔɔ ajwamãŋ lɛ, okaiii be ni oji abifao ni onyiɛ yayai kɛ ohe pasaa, ni okokloɔ yɛ olá mli lɛ.” Yerusalɛm Ajwamãŋbɔɔ

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God, say you are doomed! Not only did you do these evil things,
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ, “Kpoo, kpoo hã bo! Ejaakɛ onifɔɔjianii nɛɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ,

english_verse: but you also built places on every street corner
translation_verse: ofo akrabatsa fɛɛfɛo ohã ohe, ni ofee otutui wuji ohã ohe yɛ blohu fɛɛ blohu mli.

english_verse: where you disgraced yourself by having sex with anyone who walked by. And you did that more and more every day!
translation_verse: Omamɔ otutui wuji lɛ yɛ ŋmaŋmasha fɛɛ ŋmaŋmasha nɔ, ni okɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni hoɔ kɛkɛ wɔɔ shii abɔ.

english_verse: To make me angry, you even offered yourself to Egyptians, who were always ready to sleep with you.
translation_verse: Okɛ Ijiptbii, mɛi ni amɛkɔnɔ fa, ni okɛ amɛ je husu lɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ; ni obɔ ajwamãŋ shii abɔ ni okɛwo mimli la.

english_verse: So I punished you by letting those greedy Philistine enemies take over some of your territory. But even they were offended by your repulsive behavior.
translation_verse: “Naa, agbɛnɛ, mite shi miwo bo, ni magbala otoi; ni mitse nɔ ni ji ogbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ. Mikɛ bo hã ohenyɛlɔi fulɔi ni ji Filistibii lɛ abiyei lɛ ni hiɛ gboɔ yɛ onifɔɔji anifeemɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english_verse: You couldn't get enough sex, so you chased after Assyrians and slept with them. You still weren't satisfied,
translation_verse: “Osaa okɛ Asiriabii lɛ hu bɔ ajwamãŋ ejaakɛ otɔɔɔ; okɛ amɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ eshɛɛɛ onaa.

english_verse: so you went after Babylonians. But those merchants could not satisfy you either.
translation_verse: Nakai nɔŋŋ okɛ Babilonbii ni ji jarayelɔi lɛ hu bɔ ajwamãŋ, ni no tete hu shɛɛɛ onaa.”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, say that you were so disgusting that you would have done anything to get what you wanted.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kwɛ bɔ ni akɔnɔ eyi otsuiŋ obɔ̃, ni okɛbɔɔ ajwamãŋ, ni ohiɛ gbooo he;

english_verse: You had sex on every street corner, and when you finished, you refused to accept money. That's worse than being a prostitute!
translation_verse: ni omamɔɔ opiai lɛ omaa ŋmaŋmasha fɛɛ ŋmaŋmasha ni ofeɔ ojamɔhe krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ yɛ blohu fɛɛ blohu mli; tsɛ ofeee onii tamɔ ajwamãŋ tete; ejaakɛ bo lɛ oheee shika.

english_verse: You are nothing but an unfaithful wife who would rather have sex with strangers than with your own husband.
translation_verse: Bo lɛ, oji ohe ŋã gbãlãfitelɔ ni jeɔ ewu sɛɛ.

english_verse: Prostitutes accept money for having sex, but you bribe men from everywhere to have sex with you.
translation_verse: Hii keɔ ajwamãŋi fɛɛ anii, shi bo lɛ bo moŋ oŋɔɔ onikeenii lɛ okeɔ osuɔlɔi fɛɛ, ni ohãa amɛ nyɔɔŋnii koni amɛjɛ he fɛɛ he amɛba oŋɔɔ ni amɛkɛ bo ababɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you prostitute, listen to me.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, bo ajwamãŋ, bo nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ toi.

english_verse: You chased after lovers, then took off your clothes and had sex. You even worshiped disgusting idols and sacrificed your own children as offerings to them.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Oshwie ohiɛ shi, yɛ osuɔlɔi kɛ wɔji ahiɛ, ni ojie oyayaiaŋ kpo yɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ mli. Ni ogbe obii okɛshã afɔle oha wɔji.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will gather every one of your lovers, those you liked and those you hated. They will stand around you, and I will rip off your clothes and let all of those lovers stare at your nakedness.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, naa, mabua osuɔlɔi ni okɛ amɛ ye ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ anaa, mɛi ni osumɔɔ kɛ mɛi ni osumɔɔɔ hu fɛɛ naa kɛkpe. Mabua amɛnaa kɛjɛ hei fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mawo bo, ni majie oyayaiaŋ matsɔɔ amɛ, koni amɛna oyayaiaŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: I will find you guilty of being an unfaithful wife and a murderer, and in my fierce anger I will sentence you to a violent death!
translation_verse: Asaŋ makojo bo tamɔ akojoɔ yei ni kuɔ gbãlã mli ni amɛshwieɔ lá shi hu lɛ; ni mikɛ mlifu kɛ awuŋayeli aaatɔ lá he owele yɛ onɔ.

english_verse: Then I will hand you over to your lovers, who will tear down the places where you had sex. They will take your clothes and jewelry, leaving you naked and empty-handed.
translation_verse: Ni maŋɔ bo mawo osuɔlɔi lɛ adɛŋ, ni amɛbaakumɔ opiai lɛ, ni amɛbaafite ohei grɔŋŋi ni oja yɛ lɛ. Osuɔlɔi lɛ aaakpɔlɔ ohe atadei hu, ni amɛaaŋɔ ojwinei fɛɛfɛji lɛ, ni amɛaashi bo kɛ ohe yayai kɛ ohe pasaa.”

english_verse: Your lovers and an angry mob will stone you to death; they will cut your dead body into pieces
translation_verse: “Osuɔlɔi lɛ kɛ mɛi asafo yuu aaate shi awo bo ni atswia bo tɛi, ni amɛ kɛ amɛklantei aaafolɔ omli dukuduku.

english_verse: and burn down your houses. Other women will watch these terrible things happen to you. I promise to stop you from being a prostitute and paying your lovers for sex.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ la aaashã oshĩai lɛ, ni amɛaakojo bo yɛ yei babaoo ahiɛ; ni maha ofɔ̃ɔ ajwamãŋbɔɔ, ni owoŋ osuɔlɔi ni kɛ bo wɔɔ lɛ anyɔmɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Only then will I calm down and stop being angry and jealous.
translation_verse: Ni maha mimli ni ewo bo la lɛ naa ajɔ, ni miyeŋ ohe awuŋã, mafee diŋŋ, ni mimli fuŋ bo dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: You made me furious by doing all these disgusting things and by forgetting how I took care of you when you were young. Then you made things worse by acting like a prostitute. You must be punished! I, the Lord God, have spoken. Jerusalem's Two Sisters The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Akɛni okaiii bɔ ni mikɛ bo hi shi hã yɛ oblayeiaŋ, shi moŋ okɛ onifɔɔjianii nɛɛ fɛɛ wo mi mlifu hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, naa, maha onifɔɔjianii lɛ abua oyiteŋ. Bɛ obɔ nyɛnyɛŋtswi hu oshi nifɔɔjianii fɛɛ nɔ?

english_verse: People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.”
translation_verse: “Naa, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni buɔ abɛ lɛ, aaabu nɛkɛ abɛ nɛɛ ashi bo akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni nyɛ yɔɔ lɛ, nakai ebiyoo yɔɔ.’

english_verse: You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
translation_verse: Onyɛ ni nyaŋe ewu kɛ ebii lɛ, ebiyoo ji bo; ni onyɛmimɛi yei ni nyaŋe amɛwumɛi kɛ amɛbii lɛ amɛnyɛmi yoo ji bo. Hityoo ji nyɛnyɛ, ni Amornyo ji nyɛtsɛ.

english_verse: Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages.
translation_verse: “Onyɛmi yoo nukpa ji Samaria, mɔ ni kɛ ekrowai yɔɔ okooyigbɛ lɛ; ni onyɛmi yoo gbekɛ ji Sodom, mɔ ni kɛ ekrowai lɛ yɔɔ owuoyigbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
translation_verse: Shi obaaa ojeŋ tamɔ amɛ, ni ofeee amɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ eko moŋ nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ, be fioo mli lɛ ofite fe amɛ yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli.”

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, onyɛmi yoo Sodom kɛ okrowai lɛ efeee nɔ fɔŋ tamɔ bɔ ni bo kɛ obiyei lɛ fee lɛ.

english_verse: They were arrogant and spoiled; they had everything they needed and still refused to help the poor and needy.
translation_verse: Naa, efɔŋ ni onyɛmi yoo ni ji Sodom fee lɛ ji akɛ ekɛ ebiyei lɛ woɔ amɛhe, ejaakɛ amɛyɛ ŋmãa babaoo ni amɛyɛ toiŋjɔlɛ hu, shi amɛyeee amɛbuaaa ohiafoi kɛ mɛi ni efi amɛ.

english_verse: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
translation_verse: Amɛwo amɛhe, ni amɛfee musubɔɔnii yɛ mihiɛ, hewɔ lɛ be ni mina lɛ, mishwie amɛ.

english_verse: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
translation_verse: “Samaria hu efeee eshai ni ofee lɛ mli fã tete po, shi bo lɛ ofee musubɔɔnii babaoo ni fe amɛnɔ lɛ, ni kɛji akɛ omusubɔɔnii lɛ to onyɛmimɛi yei lɛ anɔ lɛ he lɛ abuɔ amɛ jalɔi fe bo.

english_verse: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, bo diɛŋtsɛ hu ohiɛgbele aaatere bo; ejaakɛ obu onyɛmimɛi yei lɛ bem, ejaakɛ musubɔɔnii ni mihiɔ ni ofee lɛ fa fe amɛnɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ amɛja fe bo. Agbɛnɛ hã ohiɛ agbo ni otere ohiɛgbele, ejaakɛ obu onyɛmimɛi yei lɛ abem.” Abaasaa Sodom kɛ Samaria ekoŋŋ

english_verse: Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Makpale Sodom kɛ ekrowai lɛ anibii lɛ mahã amɛ ekoŋŋ, ni nakai nɔŋŋ maha Samaria kɛ ekrowai lɛ anine ashɛ amɛnibii lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ, ni makpale bo hu onibii lɛ maha bo yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Koni otere ohiɛgbele lɛ ni ohiɛ agbo yɛ musubɔɔnii ni ofee lɛ fɛɛ hewɔ, koni onyɛmimɛi lɛ ana akɛ amɛhi fe bo.

english_verse: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
translation_verse: Onyɛmimɛi yei ni ji Sodom kɛ ekrowai lɛ kɛ Samaria kɛ ekrowai lɛ aaaku amɛsɛɛ kɛaaba amɛsa shihilɛhe lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ bo hu okɛ okrowai lɛ aaaku nyɛsɛɛ kɛaaba nyɛsa shihilɛhe lɛ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
translation_verse: Te be mli ni okɛ hewoo yeɔ omle lɛ, onyɛmi yoo ni ji Sodom lɛ ji odaaŋ kotsa,

english_verse: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: dani ajie onifɔɔjianii lɛ kpo. Agbɛnɛ okɛ lɛ eye hegbɔ, ni Edombii lɛ kɛ mɛi ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, aaaye ohe fɛo, ni nakai nɔŋŋ Filistibii kɛ amɛkrowai ni amɛhe tsɛ̃ɔ bo lɛ aaaye ohe fɛo.

english_verse: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aaagbala otoi yɛ nifɔɔjianii kɛ nihiinii ni ofeɔ lɛ hewɔ.” Yehowa kɛɛ. Kpãŋmɔ ni aaahi shi kɛaatee naanɔ

english_verse: Jerusalem, you deserve to be punished, because you broke your promises and ignored our agreement.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Bɔ ni ofee lɛ nakai pɛ mikɛ bo baaye, ejaakɛ otswa okitã lɛ ofɔ̃ afã, ni oku kpãŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ makai kpãŋmɔ ni mikɛ bo kpãŋ yɛ oblayeiaŋ lɛ, ni mikɛ bo aaakpãŋ naanɔ kpãŋmɔ.

english_verse: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
translation_verse: “No dani oookai ojeŋba fɔŋ lɛ, ni ohiɛ aaagbo, kɛji miŋɔ onyɛmimɛi yei onukpai kɛ onyɛmimɛi yei gbekɛbii lɛ mibahã bo akɛ obiyei lɛ, shi jeee akɛ mikɛ bo teŋ kpãŋmɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: “Maha mikɛ bo teŋ kpãŋmɔ lɛ ama shi, ni obaale akɛ mi ji, Yehowa;

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Oookai enɛ ni ohiɛ aaagbo, ni okatswa odaaŋ dɔŋŋ yɛ ohiɛgbele lɛ hewɔ, be ni mikɛ nifɔɔjianii ni ofee lɛ fɛɛ efa bo lɛ,” Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gba Israelbii lɛ ajenu, ni obu amɛ abɛ akɛ

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, okropɔŋ kpeteŋkple kɛ efiji agboi kɛ etsɛji kakadaji ko ni yɔɔ. Eyɛ tsɛji fɛɛfɛji bibii kɛ emli samaisamai. Eba Lebanon gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaku tsenedrutso lɛ yiteŋ.

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: Eku eniji fɔbii lɛ ayiteŋ fɔflɔoo lɛ eko ni ekɛkɔ̃ enaa kɛtee jarayeli shikpɔŋ ko nɔ. Ekɛtee eyatɛo yɛ guɔyelɔi amaŋ ko mli.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ esaa ekɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔ wu lɛ eko ni ekɛtee eyadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ. Ekɛ dumɔ wu lɛ tee he ni nu pii yɔɔ, ni edu yɛ faa lɛ toi kpaakpa.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Wu lɛ kwɛ̃ ni eda etsɔ waintso agbo ni ebu gbidii; eniji lɛ kwɔlɔ kɛtee okropɔŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ gbɛ, ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ he shi. Kɛkɛ ni etsɔ̃ waintso, ni egbala niji, ni etsɛ̃rɛ bai hu.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: “Shi okropɔŋ kpeteŋkple kroko hu ni yɔɔ kɛ efiji kpelei kɛ etsɛji pii. Ni naa, nɛkɛ waintso nɛɛ dɔrɔ eshishifãi lɛ kɛ eniji lɛ kɛba okropɔŋ kroko nɛɛ ŋɔɔgbɛ, koni okropɔŋ nɛɛ ashwie waintso lɛ nɔ nu pii fe he ni eyɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Okropɔŋ lɛ fã waintso lɛ kɛjɛ akofi nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni eyatɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni nu pii yɔɔ no nɔ, koni egbala niji, ni ewo yibii ni etsɔ̃ waintso kpakpa.

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa biɔ nɛ. Ani nɛkɛ waintso nɛɛ aaahere? Ani klɛŋklɛŋ okropɔŋ lɛ baŋ ni ebafã waintso lɛ kɛ eshishifã fɛɛ, ni efolɔ eniji lɛ eshwie, koni eyibaa fɔbii lɛ fɛɛ aŋala? Ebiŋ hewalɛ tsɔ̃ loo mɛi babaoo ni akɛfã tso lɛ kɛ eshishifã fɛɛ afɔ̃ shi.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Naa, kɛji afã ayatɛo lɛ, ani eeehere? Ani kɛ bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ lɛ jeee ŋalamɔ eeeŋala kwraa yɛ akofi nɔ he ni atɛo lɛ yɛ lɛ!” Atsɔ̃ɔ Abɛi lɛ shishi

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Bi atuatselɔi awe lɛ akɛ, ani nyɛnaaa abɛ nɛɛ shishi? Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, naa, Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ ba Yerusalɛm ni ebaŋɔ emli maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ emli lumɛi lɛ, ni ekpala amɛ eshwie esɛɛ kɛtee Babilon.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: Ni eŋɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ odehei lɛ eko, ni ekɛ lɛ kpãŋ; ni ehã odehe lɛ kã lɛ kitã akɛ ebaaye lɛ anɔkwa. Kɛkɛ ni emɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hiɛnaanɔbii lɛ kɛtee,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: koni ekɛba jɛi maŋtsɛyeli lɛ shi ni ekawo ehe nɔ dɔŋŋ, ni kɛ eye ekpãŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ ama shi.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Shi Israel maŋtsɛ lɛ tse Babilon maŋtsɛ nɛɛ hiɛ atua, ni etsu bɔfoi kɛtee Ijipt, koni ahã lɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tabilɔi babaoo. Ani eeehi ehã lɛ? Aso gbɔmɔ ni feɔ nibii tamɔ enɛɛmɛi lɛ eeeye ehe lo? Ani eeeku kpãŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni kɛ̃lɛ eeeye ehe lo?”

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, Babilon, he ni maŋtsɛ, mɔ ni wo lɛ maŋtsɛ, kɛ mɔ ni ekwa ekitã lɛ, kɛ mɔ kpãŋmɔ mli ni eku yɔɔ lɛ, jɛi nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ eeegbo yɛ.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Kɛji Babilonbii lɛ tswa kpokui, ni amɛtswa kawoo gbogboi koni akɛkpãtã mɛi pii ahiɛ lɛ, Farao kɛ eta kpele lɛ kɛ esafo babaoo lɛ nyɛŋ Yuda eye ebua yɛ ta mli.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: Akɛni ebuuu kitã ni ekã lɛ, ni eku kpãŋmɔ lɛ mli, akɛni ekpɛlɛ̃ nɔ, ni kɛ̃lɛ efee enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ hewɔ lɛ ehe ejeŋ mli.”

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, mikitã ni ebuuu lɛ, kɛ mikpãŋmɔ lɛ ni eku mli lɛ, mikɛ he sɔ̃ aaabua eyiteŋ.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Mafɔ̃ enɔ miyaa lɛ, ni eeedu mitsɔne, ni mikɛ lɛ aaaba Babilon, ni magbala etoi yɛ jɛi, yɛ shi ni ete ewo mi lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ni akɛ klante aaakpãtã etabilɔi kãkãlɔi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ, ni mɛi ni aaashwɛ lɛ aaagbɛ amɛ ashwã jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, Yehowa, miwie lɛ.” Nyɔŋmɔ wo hiɛnɔkãmɔ he shi

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Mi diɛŋtsɛ maku tsenedrutso yiteŋ kɔŋ ni kwɔ lɛ ni mayatɛo. Maku eniji fɔbii lɛ ayiteŋ fɔflɔooi lɛ, ni mayatɛo yɛ gɔŋ ni kwɔ grɔŋŋ ko nɔ.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Israel gɔŋ ni kwɔ lɛ nɔ matɛo yɛ; ni eeegbala niji, ni eeewo yibii, ni eeetsɔ̃ tsenedrutso fɛɛfɛo, ni loofɔji srɔtoi fɛɛ aaabahi enɔ, amɛaahi eniji ashishi hɔɔŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Ni ŋa nɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ aaana ale akɛ mi, Yehowa, mihãa tso ni kwɔ lɛ baa shi, ni miwoɔ tso tɛkɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi; Mihãa tso ŋmɔŋ gbiɔ ni mihãa tso gbiŋ fɛoɔ. Mi, Yehowa, miwie, ni mafee hu.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Mɛni ji shishinumɔ ni nyɛkɛbuɔ abɛ nɛɛ yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɛ, ‘Tsɛmɛi lɛ eye wainyibii ŋmilikitii, ni bii lɛ moŋ anyanyɔji eshwã’ lɛ?

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, nyɛbuŋ nɛkɛ abɛ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ Israel.” Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: “Naa, gbɔmɛi fɛɛ awala lɛ, minɔ ni. Bɔ ni tsɛ wala ji minɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ bi hu nɔ ji minɔ. Gbɔmɔ ni feɔ esha lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ eeegbo.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: “Ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ mɔ ko yɛ ni ji jalɔ, ni eyeɔ jalɛ sane, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja.

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: Eyeee nii ni akɛshã afɔle ahã wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ. Ni ewooo ehiɛ nɔ ekwɛɛɛ Israel we lɛ wɔji lɛ tete, ni enyiɛɛɛ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ, ni ebɛŋkɛɛɛ yoo ni etee tsuiasɛɛ.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: Ewaaa mɔ yi; shi ekpaleɔ nyɔmɔtsɛ awabatoonii ehãa lɛ; ni etswaaa ojo; ehaaa mɔ ko nɔ ko, shi moŋ ehãa mɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ nii eyeɔ; asaŋ mɔ ni nyiɛ yayai lɛ ebuɔ lɛ mama.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: “Ekɛ shika efaaa ni ehe hekpa fe nine. Ewiɔ ehe yɛ eshafeemɔ he, ni ekojoɔ mɔ kɛ mɔ teŋ yɛ jalɛ naa.

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: Ebaa ejeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ mimlai lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ jalɔ ji lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ fɔ binuu yiwalɔ kɛ gbɔmɔgbelɔ.

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: Bi nɛɛ efeee nii ni sa feemɔ nɛɛ ateŋ ekoeko; shi moŋ eyeɔ nii ni akɛshãa afɔle ahãa wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ; ni enyiɛɔ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ.

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: Ewaa ohiafo kɛ mɔ ni efi lɛ yi. Etswaa ojo, ni ekpaleee nyɔmɔtsɛ awabatoonii ehãaa lɛ. Ejaa amãgã, ni efeɔ musubɔɔnii.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: Efaa shika ni eheɔ hekpa fe nine. Aso nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ yi aaana wala? Eyi naŋ wala. Akɛni efee nɛkɛ musubɔɔnii nɛɛ fɛɛ eko hewɔ lɛ gbo kɛ̃ eeegbo; ela aaabua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiteŋ.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: “Shi agbɛnɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ fɔ binuu ko, ni ebinuu nɛɛ na eshai fɛɛ ni etsɛ lɛ efee lɛ, ni eshe gbeyei, ni efeee nakai eshai lɛ eko.

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: Ni eyeee nii ni akɛshã afɔle ahã wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni ejaaa Israel we lɛ amãgãi lɛ ekoeko. Ni enyiɛɛɛ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: Ni efeee mɔ ko efɔŋ, eheee mɔ ko awabatoonii; etswaaa mɔ ko ojo. Shi moŋ ehãa mɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ aboloo, asaŋ mɔ ni nyiɛ yayai lɛ, ebuɔ lɛ mama.

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: Ewiɔ ehe yɛ eshafeemɔ he, ni ekɛ shika efaaa ni ehe hekpa ni fe nine. Ni eyeɔ mimlai lɛ anɔ, ni ebaa ejeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ egboŋ yɛ eshai ni etsɛ efee lɛ ahewɔ, shi moŋ eyi aaana wala kɛ̃.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: “Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛbiɔ akɛ, ‘Mɛɛ hewɔ esaaa akɛ bi naa amanehului yɛ esha ni etsɛ efee hewɔ?’ Kɛji bi lɛ yeɔ jalɛ sane, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja, ni eyeɔ mikpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ esa akɛ eyi ana wala kɛ̃.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ ni feɔ esha lɛ gbo eeegbo. Bi enaŋ amanehulu yɛ eshai ni etsɛ efee ahewɔ, ni tsɛ hu enaŋ amanehulu yɛ eshai ni ebii efee ahewɔ. Jalɔ aaana ejalɛnii ni efee lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo, ni mɔ fɔŋ hu aaana efɔŋ ni efee lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: “Shi kɛji eshafeelɔ fɔ̃ɔ eshai fɛɛ ni efeɔ, ni eye mikpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, ni eye jalɛ sane, ni efee nɔ ni ja lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, egboŋ.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Tɔ̃mɔi ni etɔ̃ lɛ akaiŋ ekoeko dɔŋŋ, akɛaafa lɛ. Ejalɛnii ni efee lɛ hewɔ lɛ eyi aaana wala.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa miibi akɛ, “Aso minyaa efɔŋfeelɔ gbele he lo? Dabida, nɔ ni mitaoɔ moŋ ji akɛ etsake ejeŋba koni eyi ana wala.”

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: “Shi kɛji jalɔ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ja feemɔ ni efee esha, ni efee musubɔɔ nii ni mɔfɔŋ feɔ lɛ, aso eyi aaana wala lo? Jalɛnii ni efee lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, akaiŋ ekoeko. Etɔmɔi ni etɔ̃ lɛ kɛ eshai ni efee lɛ, eeegbo yɛ nomɛi ahewɔ.

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: “Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛkɛɔ akɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ yeee jalɛ sane. Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, nyɛboa toi ko! Ani mi, miyeee jalɛ sane? Ani jeee nyɛ moŋ ni nyɛyeee jalɛ sane?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Kɛji jalɔ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ja feemɔ, ni efee efɔŋ lɛ, gbo eeegbo yɛ no hewɔ. Ebaagbo yɛ efɔŋ ni efee lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Asaŋ kɛji mɔ fɔŋ fɔ̃ɔ eshai ni efeɔ lɛ fɛɛ, ni eye mikpɔi lɛ anɔ, ni efee nɔ ni ja ni ehi lɛ, eeehere eyiwala.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ekɔ eyiŋ, ni efɔ̃ɔ enifɔɔji anii lɛ fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, egboŋ.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nuŋtsɔ lɛ yeee jalɛ sane.’ Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, ani mi ni miyeee jalɛ sane lo? Ani jeee nyɛ moŋ ni nyɛyeee jalɛ sane?

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, makojo nyɛ, makojo nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ enifeemɔ nii anaa. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. Nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ, ni nyɛfɔ̃a nyɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ fɛɛ; koni nyɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ akakpãtã nyɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Nyɛkpaa efɔŋ fɛɛ efɔŋ ni nyɛfee nyɛshi mi lɛ feemɔ, ni nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ ni nyɛnaa mumɔ hee. Ao, Israelbii, shi mɛɛba ni nyɛaagboi?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Minyaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko gbele he. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ koni nyɛyi anaa wala.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Wo yaafo lala nɔ okɛfo Israel lumɛi lɛ, ni okɛɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
