translation_verse: “Ani onyɛ lɛ jeee jatayoo ni? Ni ebu jata oblahii ateŋ ni elɛ ebii lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ?

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ni etsɔse ebii lɛ ateŋ ekome ni etsɔ̃ jata oblanyo; ekase loomɔmɔ, ni eyeɔ gbɔmɔ tete?

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Jeŋmaji lɛ bɔ ehe oshe; ni adu lɛ yɛ amɛbu lɛ mli; ni amɛkɛ kpoji gbala lɛ kɛtee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Be ni enyɛ mɛ aahu lɛ, ehiɛnɔkãmɔ tã. Esaa eŋɔ ebii lɛ ateŋ ekroko efee jata oblanyo.

english_verse: He hunted with other lions and learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Be ni eda etsɔ̃ jata oblanyo lɛ ekɛ jatai lɛ nyiɛ aahu. Ekase gbɔbimɔ ni eyeɔ gbɔmɔ tete.

english_verse: He destroyed fortresses and ruined towns; his mighty roar terrified everyone.
translation_verse: Ejwra amɛ mɔji, ni efite maji hu; ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ she gbeyei yɛ ehuumɔ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ hewɔ.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni jeŋmaji lɛ gba wo lɛ kɛkpe, ni amɛfɔ̃ enɔ yaa, ni adu lɛ yɛ amɛbu lɛ mli.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛ kpoji gbala lɛ amɛwo kooloi adeka mli; ni amɛkɛ lɛ yahã Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni akɛ lɛ to mɔɔ lɛ mli; bɔ ni afee ni akanu egbee yɛ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Onyɛ tamɔ waintso ni atɛo yɛ faa toi; egbala niji, ni ewo yibii babaoo, ejaakɛ enaa nu pii.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Eniji lɛ na hewalɛ tamɔ maŋtsɛ tsi. Ni ewo ekwɔlɛ nɔ yɛ niji kusukusuu lɛ ateŋ. Ni ana ekwɔlɛ kɛ eniji kusukusuu lɛ.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Shi akɛ mlila fã lɛ kɛ eshishi fɛɛ ni ashɛ lɛ afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ, ni bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbi lɛ, ni eyibii lɛ kpala, ni etso ni wa lɛ gbi, ni eshã wɛɛ.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ afã lɛ ayatɛo yɛ ŋa nɔ, yɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ ni nu bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Ni la jɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli ni eshã eniji lɛ kɛ eyibii lɛ fɛɛ; ni tso bɛ emli dɔŋŋ ni aaanyɛ akɛfee maŋtsɛ tsi dɔŋŋ. Awerɛho lala nɛɛ alaa akɛyeɔ ŋkɔmɔ daa.

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Yɛ wɔnomŋɔɔ afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ, nyɔŋ ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ, Israel onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi ba miŋɔɔ koni amɛbabi Yehowa nii. Amɛbatara shi yɛ mihiɛ.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, okɛ Israel maŋ onukpai nɛɛ awie ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ani mi nibimɔ nyɛbaa nɛɛ? Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, Mihaŋ nyɛbi mi nii.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ani oookojo amɛ, Gbɔmɔ Adesa? Ani oookojo amɛ? Belɛ hã amɛle musubɔɔnii ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ, ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ,

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, gbi ni miŋɔ Israel lɛ mikã Yakob shwiei lɛ akitã ni mihã amɛle mi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mikã amɛ kitã akɛ, ‘Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ mikã amɛ kitã akɛ majie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ko ni mito miha amɛ lɛ nɔ; shikpɔŋ ni hi ni ebaa nii, ni eji shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: Mikɛɛ amɛ akɛ, nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ashɛrɛ musubɔɔnii ni ehiŋmɛii nyaa he lɛ eshwie; ni nyɛkɛ Ijipt wɔji lɛ akabulea nyɛhe! Mi ji Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ!

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Shi amɛtse mihiɛ atua, ni amɛbooo mi toi. Amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko shɛrɛɛɛ musubɔɔnii ni ehiŋmɛii nyaa he lɛ eshwieee, ni Ijipt wɔji lɛ hu ahewɔ lɛ, mito miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mlila kɛ mlifu aaafee amɛ efɔŋ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mifeee; mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ yɛ migbɛi hewɔ, bɔ ni afee ni mikagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ, mɛi ahiɛ ni mihã amɛle mi yɛ, be ni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mijie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikɛ amɛ ba ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Miwo amɛ mlai kɛ akpɔi lɛ, ni kɛ gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Asaŋ miŋɔ mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ mihã amɛ, koni nomɛi atsɔ̃ okadi yɛ mi kɛ amɛteŋ, koni amɛkɛle akɛ mi Yehowa, mi ji mɔ ni tsuɔ amɛhe.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: “Shi Israel we lɛ tse mihiɛ atua yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mimlai lɛ anaa, shi moŋ amɛkwa mikpɔi ni kɛ gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ; ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ hu naakpa. No hewɔ lɛ, mito miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mimlila aaaplene amɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ kwrakwra.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ; mɛi ahiɛ ni mi mijie Israel kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Asaŋ mikã amɛ kitã yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ mikɛ amɛ baŋ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã amɛ lɛ nɔ; shikpɔŋ ni hi ni ebaa nii, ni eji shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: “Ejaakɛ amɛkwa mimlai lɛ, ni amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa. Ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ; ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ hã amɛwɔji lɛ.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ mina amɛ mɔbɔ, ni mikpãtãaa amɛhiɛ ni mipleneee amɛ kwrakwra yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: “Mikɛɛ amɛbii yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkabaa nyɛjeŋ yɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ amlai lɛ anaa, ni nyɛkayea amɛkpɔi lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛkɛ amɛwɔji lɛ akabulea nyɛhe.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mi ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ; nyɛbaa nyɛjeŋ yɛ mimlai lɛ moŋ anaa; ni nyɛyea mimlai lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ni nyɛfea mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ koni nomɛi atsɔ̃ okadi yɛ mi kɛ nyɛ teŋ; koni nyɛkɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: “Shi nyɛbii lɛ hu tse mihiɛ atua; amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mlai lɛ anaa, ni amɛyeee mikpɔi lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ; mlai ni kɛji gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ; amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ hu. Kɛkɛ ni mito miyiŋ akɛ mafee amɛ efɔŋ yɛ mimlifu kɛ mimlila naa yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ,

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ; mɛi ahiɛ ni mi, mijie Israelbii lɛ yɛ, kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ, mikã amɛ kitã yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ magbɛ amɛ mashwã jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ, ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ;

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ amɛyeee mikpɔi lɛ anɔ, shi moŋ amɛkwa mimlai lɛ, ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ yakɔ̃ amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ awɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mi hu miwo amɛ mlai ni ehiii, kɛ akpɔi ni haŋ amɛna wala.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: Mibule amɛ kɛtsɔ̃ amɛnikeenii anɔ, no ji amɛkromɔbii ni amɛgbe kɛshã afɔle lɛ, koni mahã amɛhe ajɔ̃ amɛhe. Mifee enɛ, koni amɛkɛna amɛle akɛ, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni mihã amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikã kitã akɛ mikɛaahã amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, gɔŋkpɔ fɛɛ gɔŋkpɔ ni kwɔ, loo tso kusuu fɛɛ tso kusuu ni amɛaana lɛ, amɛyashãa amɛ afɔlei lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni amɛkɛ afɔleshãa nɛɛ wo mimli la; jɛi nɔŋŋ amɛshãa amɛtsofakɛŋmai lɛ yɛ, ni jɛi nɔŋŋ amɛfɔse amɛdãa afɔle lɛ amɛshwie shi yɛ.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Mibi amɛ akɛ, mɛni ji nakai he grɔŋŋ lɛ ni nyɛyaa lɛ? No hewɔ atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ ‘He Grɔŋŋ’ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ.

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Gbii abɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnikeenii yahãa wɔji, ni nyɛgbeɔ nyɛbihii nyɛkɛshãa afɔlei nyɛhãa amɛ lɛ, nyɛmiibule nyɛhe kɛ nɛkɛ nyɛwɔji nɛɛ ajamɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Ao, Israel we, nyɛmiiba ni nyɛbabi mi nii? Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, mihaŋ nyɛbi mi nii! Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Nɔ ni nyɛsusuɔ ni nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, wɔɔtamɔ jeŋmaji kɛ shikpɔji anɔ wekui lɛ, ni wɔsɔmɔ tso kɛ tɛ lɛ, ebaŋ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ.” Nyɔŋmɔ gbalaa toi, ni ekɛfaa

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, mikɛ nineshiwalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ mlila ni naa wa baaye nyɛnɔ maŋtsɛ.

english_verse: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
translation_verse: Mikɛ nineshiwalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ mlila baajie nyɛ kɛaajɛ shikpɔji ni agbɛ nyɛ ashwã amɛnɔ lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Ni mikɛ nyɛaaba majimaji lɛ ateŋ ni mabua nyɛnaa kɛaajɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni jɛi magbala nyɛtoi yɛ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni migbala nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ atoi yɛ Ijipt ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ magbala nyɛ hu nyɛtoi.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: “Maha nyɛtsɔ̃ kplamɔtso lɛ shishi, ni makane nyɛ ekomekome mawo kpãŋmɔ mli.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni majie atuatselɔi lɛ kɛ mɛi ni etɔ̃ minɔ lɛ kɛaaje nyɛteŋ. Majie amɛ kɛaajɛ he ni amɛyato gbɔ yɛ lɛ moŋ nɛ, shi amɛnane yiŋ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No dani nyɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Ao, nyɛ Israel we, nyɛyaa ni nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ayasɔmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewɔji lɛ; shi kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ nyɛabo mi toi kɛ̃, ni migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nyɛkɛ nyɛnikeenii lɛ kɛ nyɛwɔŋjamɔ lɛ babuleŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Shi migɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ji Israel Gɔŋ ni kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jɛi Israel we lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aaasɔmɔ mi yɛ; mana amɛhe tsui yɛ jɛi, ni mabi nyɛfɔlei lɛ kɛ nyɛnikeenii kpakpai lɛ kɛ nyɛkeenii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ fɛɛ shi.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Kɛji mijie nyɛ kɛjɛ majimaji lɛ amli, ni mibua nyɛnaa kɛjɛ shikpɔji ni agbɛ nyɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛba lɛ, mana nyɛhe tsui tamɔ nɔ ko ni jeɔ ŋma, ni majie mikrɔŋkrɔŋ ni mi ji lɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛteŋ ni majimaji aaana.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Kɛji mikɛ nyɛ bashɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mikã he kitã akɛ maŋɔ hã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Ni jɛi nyɛaakai nyɛjeŋba kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni nyɛfee ni nyɛkɛbule nyɛhe lɛ yɛ, ni nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛhe aaafee nyɛ nyaŋemɔ yɛ nifɔɔjianii fɛɛ ni nyɛfee lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, nyɛ Israel we, kɛji mikɛnyɛ ye yɛ migbɛi lɛ hewɔ, shi jeee yɛ nyɛjeŋba gbohii lɛ ahewɔ, loo nyɛnifeemɔnii gbohii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Wuoyigbɛ la lɛ

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛmi wie ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ ohã wuoyigbɛ; wiemɔ oshi Yuda wuoyigbɛ lɛ; gbaa oshi wuoyigbɛ koo lɛ.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ Yuda wuoyigbɛ koo lɛ akɛ, bo Yehowa wiemɔ toi. Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: naa, mawo la yɛ omli, ni eeeshã omli tso ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ tso ŋmɔŋ, kɛ tso gbiŋ fɛɛ tso gbiŋ. La ni tsoɔ grigri lɛ agbeŋ, ni eeeshã he fɛɛ he kɛaajɛ wuoyigbɛ aahu kɛyashi kooyigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Gbɔmɛi fɛɛ baana akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi miwo la lɛ, ni anyɛŋ agbe.”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ akɛ, “Ao, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, amɛkɛɔ yɛ mihe akɛ, ‘Ani jeee abɛbuaŋ sɔŋŋ ewieɔ yɛ?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ miwie ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ oha Yerusalɛm ni oshiɛ oshi hei krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, he ni ajaa yɛ lɛ; gbaa oshi Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ,

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: ni okɛɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikɛ bo ena, ni magbala miklante lɛ kɛaaje ehebo lɛ mli, ni mikɛaagbe jalɔ kɛ mɔfɔŋ fɛɛ yɛ nyɛteŋ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bo, Gbɔmɔ Adesa, hũumɔ kɛ tsui ni ekumɔ, hũumɔ kɛ awerɛho kpele yɛ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛbi bo akɛ, ‘Mɛni hewɔ ohũɔ lɛ?’ Okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Saji ni minu lɛ hewɔ ni. Kɛji eba mli lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baashe gbeyei, ni kɔ̃ɔji fɛɛ baakplɔke, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baatsɔ̃ feetɔ, ni nakutsei fɛɛ tswɛm baakpokpo tamɔ ayawaŋ nu. Naa, be lɛ eshɛ, ni ebaaba mli kɛ̃;’ ” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: Ajɔ naa koni akɛgbe mɔ; asha he ni ekpɛ kaŋkaŋ tamɔ srawa. Aso wɔmli afili wɔ? Mibi, ogbe kpãa kɛ tsɔsemɔ fɛɛ tsɔsemɔ he guɔ.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Gbɔmɔ Adesa, wo yara ni ofo, ejaakɛ afã klante awo miwebii lɛ. Afã klante awo Israel lumɛi fɛɛ. Ajɔɔ amɛ kɛ miwebii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ ahã klante; hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyia nyɛhe ma.

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa miibi, akɛ, ‘Nyɛjwɛŋa he jogbaŋŋ, ani nyɛsusuɔ akɛ kɛ nyɛkwa tsɔsemɔ lɛ toigbalamɔ lɛ baŋ lo?’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, no hewɔ lɛ, gbaa. Tswaa odɛ̃ koni klante lɛ ni baagbe mɛi lɛ abamɔ amɛ nɔtonɔto. No ji klante ni baakpãtã mɛi babaoo ahiɛ lɛ; ni no hewɔ lɛ, gbele ebɔle amɛhe kɛkpe;

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: koni amɛshe gbeyei, ni mɛi babaoo agbeegbee shi hewɔ mitsɔ̃ klante lɛ naa mihã maŋ lɛ agboi lɛ anaa. Mikɛ klante ni kpɛlɛɔ tamɔ srawa lɛ ehã. Ehe miikpɛ tamɔ srawa. Asha he kɛha mɔgbee.

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: Klante, bãa kɛya ninejurɔ ni obã kɛya abɛku, tsɔ̃ ohe ni ofo kɛya he fɛɛ he. Hã enyɔ loo mli.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Mi hu matswa midɛ̃, ni mimlifu lɛ naa aba shi. Mi, Yehowa, miwie.” Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ klante lɛ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kadimɔ gbɛjegbɛi enyɔ nɔ ni Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ eklante lɛ aaanyɛ atsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba lɛ. Gbɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aaanyɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛba. Too gbɛtsɔ̃ɔmɔ okadi oma maŋ lɛ ŋmaŋmasha lɛ.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Okadi lɛ ekome atsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ eklante lɛ atsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba Raba, ni ji Amonbii lɛ amaŋ lɛ mli; okadi kroko lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ gbɛ kɛya Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbote Yerusalɛm ni atswa gbogbo awo ehe lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ damɔ gbɛnta lɛ naa, yɛ he ni gbɛi enyɔ lɛ gbaa akloŋta yɛ lɛ. Ebaahoso gãimlibii kɛkla ni eeebi emãgãi lɛ anii, ni eeekwɛ afɔle kooloo ni agbe lɛ mlɛbo mli fitsofitso.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: Eklamɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ akɛ etsɔ̃ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛya Yerusalɛm, koni ebɔ ta oshe, ni awo naa nɔ abolɔ, ni aŋɔ gbogbokuumɔnii apiŋ agboi lɛ ahe, ni atswa kpokui ni amãmɔ mɔji ni wa.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Eeefee Yerusalɛmbii lɛ akɛ klamɔ ni bɛ mli ni, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ maji ekpãŋ, shi moŋ esa akɛ amɛkai amɛnɔsha lɛ akɛ abaamɔmɔ amɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Akɛni nyɛha ana eshai ni nyɛfee lɛ, ni nyɛnifɔɔjianii eje kpo yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛfeɔ mli, ni mikai nyɛ hewɔ lɛ abaamɔmɔ nyɛ kɛya nomŋɔɔ mli.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Bo Israel lumɔ, yiwalɔ ni he tseee, bo ni obe eshɛ kɛhã onaagbee toigbalamɔ,

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ bo nɛ, Jiemɔ oyifiinɔ lɛ, ni jiemɔ okekre lɛ yɛ oyitso. Nibii ehiŋ shi tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ; nɔ ni eba shi lɛ, awo nɔ; ni nɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ, aba lɛ shi.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Butumɔ! Butumɔ! Butumɔ mabutu maŋ lɛ. Anaŋ he okadi ko kwraa kɛyaashi mɔ gbɛnaa ni ji lɛ aaaba, ni lɛ maŋɔ hã.” Klante lɛ kɛ Amonbii lɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: “Ni bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛɛ Amonbii lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nyɛ yɛ ahora ni amɛbɔɔ Israel lɛ he nɛ; kɛɛmɔ akɛ: ‘Klante, agbala klante kɛhã gbɔmɔgbee; asha he kaŋkaŋ, ni ekpɛ tamɔ srawa.’ ”

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: “Nii ni nyɛnaa lɛ amale ninaa ni, ni nyɛgbalɛi hu amale gbalɛi ni, koni nyɛkɛ sɔ̃ lɛ afɔ̃ lumɛi kɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji ni egboi lɛ anɔ. Amɛ lɛ, amɛnaagbee hiɛkpãtãmɔ be lɛ eshɛ.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Kɛ klante awo ehebo lɛ mli, Makojo bo yɛ he ni abɔ bo yɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ojɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Mimli baawo bo la, ni mimlifu ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tamɔ la lɛ aaaba onɔ; ni majie bo mawo hii dikalɔi yitsoŋwalɔi ni le nifitemɔ he ŋaa lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nyɛbaatsɔ̃ latɛ naa lai; aaashwie nyɛlá shi akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni akaiŋ nyɛ dɔŋŋ; ejaakɛ mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: “Bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ani oookojo, ani oookojo maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ mli lɛ? Belɛ hã ele emusubɔɔnii ni efee lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ emli, asaŋ ni efeɔ amãgãi ni ekɛbuleɔ ehe lɛ; ebe aaashɛ,

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: lá shi ni oshwie kɛ amãgãi ni ofee okɛbule ohe lɛ hewɔ lɛ oye fɔ; ehã ogbii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ; afii ni ato ahã bo lɛ eshɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, miha jeŋmaji lɛ miibɔ bo ahora, ni shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ miiye ohe fɛo.

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Abuuu tsɛ kɛ nyɛ yɛ omli, ayeɔ gbɔ amim yɛ omli; awaa awusa kɛ okulafo yi yɛ omli.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Obuuu minii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, ni obuleɔ mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Mɛi yɛ nyɛteŋ ni yeɔ osheku, bɔ ni afee ni ashwie mɛi alá shi; mɛi komɛi yɛ nyɛteŋ ni amɛyeɔ afɔlei ni ashã ahã amãgãi lɛ, ni mɛi komɛi hu yɛ nyɛteŋ ni bɔɔ nyɛnyɛŋtswi.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Mɛi komɛi kɛ amɛtsɛmɛi aŋamɛi naa bɔlɛ yɛ omli, ni mɛi komɛi tuaa yei ni etee tsuiasɛɛ, ni amɛhe tseee lɛ yɛ omli.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.
translation_verse: Mɔ kɛ enaanyo ŋa naa bɔlɛ; mɔ ko hu kɛ ebinuu ŋa naa bɔlɛ; mɔ ko hu kɛ enyɛmiyoo ni ji etsɛbi naa bɔlɛ yɛ omli.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mɛi heɔ nyɔɔŋnii, koni ashwie lá shi yɛ omli; aheɔ hekpa ni fe nine, ni atswaa nanemɛi ojo. Nyɛhiɛ ekpa minɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mitswa midɛ̃ mishwie onɔ yɛ shishiumɔnii ni ona kɛ lá shi ni oshwie yɛ omli lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Gbi ni mikɛ bo aaaye lɛ, aso ooonyɛ naa odamɔ? Aloo ooonyɛ onine nɔ po owo? Mi, Yehowa, miwie, ni mafee.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: Magbɛ omlibii lɛ mashwã jeŋmaji kɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ, ni mikɛaatsuu ohe muji lɛ mashwie.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Ni ohe guɔ baagbo yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ahiɛ, ni ooona ole akɛ mi ji Yehowa lɛ.” Nyɔŋmɔ niiahetsuumɔ flɔnɔɔ lɛ

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, Israel we lɛ etsɔ̃ tamɔ shika shishi ehã mi. Amɛ fɛɛ kwa lɛ, jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble kɛ sanyaa kɛ dade kɛ sumui ni asere yɛ flɔnɔɔ mli lɛ shishi muji ji amɛ.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Bɔ ni jwiɛtɛi sereɔ yɛ flɔnɔɔ mli lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ aaasere nyɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm; ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi mihuu mimlila lɛ mishwie nyɛnɔ.’ ” Israel Hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ ahe eshai lɛ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ Israel akɛ, bo ji shikpɔŋ ko ni ohe tseee, ni nu hu enɛŋ onɔ yɛ mimlifu be lɛ mli.

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
translation_verse: Emli lumɛi lɛ tamɔ jatai ni huuɔ ni amɛmiitserɛ amɛmilɛ loo mli; amɛkpãtã gbɔmɛi awala ahiɛ; amɛshɔ̃ mɛi ajwetri kɛ nii ni jara wa yɛ amɛdɛŋ; amɛhã yei pii etsɔmɔ okulafoi yɛ Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
translation_verse: Omli osɔfoi lɛ ku mimlai lɛ amli, ni amɛbule minii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ; amɛhãaa ana srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni abule teŋ; asaŋ amɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni he tse kɛ nɔ ni he tseee teŋ, ni amɛbuuu mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, abule mi yɛ amɛteŋ.

english_verse: Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
translation_verse: “Emli lumɛi lɛ tamɔ klãji ni tserɛɔ milɛloo mli, amɛshwieɔ lá shi, amɛkpãtãa mɛi ahiɛ, bɔ ni afee ni amɛwo shishiumɔ ninamɔ.

english_verse: And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me.
translation_verse: Emli gbalɔ lɛ maleɔ ekɛhaa eshai nɛɛ anɔ tamɔ akɛ kaaloo shaa gbogbo he lɛ. Amɛnaa amale ninaa, ni amɛgbaa amale gbalɛi akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ.’ Be mli ni mi, Yehowa miwieko tete.

english_verse: The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niiatsɛmɛi lɛ tswaa ojo, ni amɛjuɔ; amɛwaa ohiafoi kɛ mɛi ni efi amɛ lɛ ayi, ni amɛyeɔ gbɔ amim, ni atooo lɛ najiaŋ.

english_verse: I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one.
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ, mitao akɛ mana mɔ ko kɛjɛ amɛteŋ ni eeetswa gbogbo ni ewule lɛ, ni eeebu folɔ lɛ naa yɛ mihiɛ ehã shikpɔŋ lɛ, koni mikafite lɛ; shi minaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mimli wo amɛ la, ni mikɛ mlifu plenee amɛ, ni miha amɛmusu ebua amɛyiteŋ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, yei enyɔ komɛi, ni ji yoo kome musuŋbii hi shi.

english_verse: The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
translation_verse: Onukpa lɛ gbɛi ji Ohola, ni fioo lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ Oholiba. Mikɛ amɛ hi shi, ni mikɛ amɛ fɔfɔɔ bihii kɛ biyei. Ohola damɔ shi kɛha Samaria, ni Oholiba damɔ shi kɛhã Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers.
translation_verse: Ohola je misɛɛ ni eyabɔ ajwamãŋ, ni ehiɛ yakɔ̃ esuɔlɔi lɛ ni ji Asiriabii lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Tabilɔi ni woɔ afaseo atadei ji amɛ; amraloi kɛ lumɛi kɛ oblahii ni he yɔɔ akɔnɔ kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi sɔŋŋ ji amɛ.

english_verse: She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Asiria hii ni ajegbɛ ahala lɛ fɛɛ lɛ ekɛ amɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ; ni mɛi fɛɛ ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ lɛ, eja amɛwɔji lɛ, ni ekɛbule ehe.

english_verse: Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
translation_verse: Efɔ̃ko ajwamãŋbɔɔ ni ebɔi kɛjɛ Ijipt lɛ, ejaakɛ hii kɛ lɛ wɔ eblayeiaŋ ni amɛmiamia eblayeiaŋ kpokpoai lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ lɛ basabasa tamɔ ajwamãŋ ko.

english_verse: So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mitu lɛ miwo esuɔlɔi lɛ ni ji Asiriabii ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
translation_verse: Amɛ jie eyayaiaŋ kpo amɛmɔmɔ ebihii kɛ ebiyei lɛ; ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ amɛkɛ klante gbe lɛ; ni etsɔ wiemɔ ni yei kɛyeɔ fɛo akɛ akojo lɛ.

english_verse: Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did.
translation_verse: “Oholiba na nɔ ni ba enyɛmi yoo Ohola nɔ lɛ nɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ ehiɛkɔ̃ɔ lɛ naa wa fe Ohola nɔ lɛ, ni ejwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ hu fe enyɛmi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mina akɛ ebule ehe, ni amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛnyiɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english_verse: But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red.
translation_verse: “Shi Oholiba tee nɔ lolo kɛ ejwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ; ena Babilon hii mfonirii ni akɛ atiifɔ tsuru etɛŋ yɛ gbogbo he.

english_verse: They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers.
translation_verse: Ena akɛ amɛkɛ hɛfiinii efimɔ amɛhɛi, ni amɛkɛ yitsofiinii kakadaji efimɔ amɛyitsei; mfoniri nɛɛ mli bii lɛ tamɔ Babilon lumɛi ni afɔ yɛ Kaldea shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her.
translation_verse: Be ni ena amɛfonirii lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ, ni etsu bɔfoi kɛtee lumɛi nɛɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Babilon.

english_verse: Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Babilon hii lɛ ba eŋɔɔ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ bawɔ, ni amɛkɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ bule lɛ. Agbɛnɛ be ni ekɛ amɛ ewo ehe muji egbe naa lɛ amɛje etsine.

english_verse: She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni ebɔ ajwamãŋ faŋŋ lɛ, ni ejie eyayaiaŋ kpo lɛ hã esane je mitsine tamɔ bɔ ni enyɛmi yoo lɛ sane je mitsine lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ etee nɔ ebɔ ejwamaŋ lɛ fe nine, ni ekai eblayeiaŋ bei amli ni eyɔɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔɔ ajwamãŋ lɛ.

english_verse: She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers.
translation_verse: Ehemɛi ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ nɛɛ anuutso tamɔ teji nɔ, ni amɛhenu hu tamɔ okpɔŋɔ he nu.

english_verse: And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body. The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
translation_verse: Bo, Oholiba, nɛkɛ oshwe oblayeiaŋ basabasa nyiɛmɔi ni onyiɛ, be ni Ijiptbii lɛ miamia ofufɔi, ni amɛfite bo lɛ.” Nyɔŋmɔ kojo Oholiba

english_verse: The Lord God said: Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bo Oholiba, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa mibatee osuɔlɔi ni amɛje otsine lɛ shi mawo bo, ni maha amɛte shi amɛwo bo kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he.

english_verse: I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa.
translation_verse: Maha hii ni he yɔɔ akɔnɔ ajɛ Babilon kɛ Kaldea kɛ Pekod kɛ Shoa kɛ Koa kɛ Asiria fɛɛ aba. Mɛnɛɛmɛi fɛɛ lɛ oblahii kɛ amraloi kɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi kɛ lumɛi kɛ gbɛnaahiɛlɔi kɛ tabilɔi ni tara okpɔŋɔi anɔ ji amɛ.

english_verse: Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi pii kɛ ta shwiilii kɛ tsɔnei ni gbalaa nii aaajɛ kooyigbɛ aba; ni amɛaagba amɛwo ohe kɛ tsɛŋi bibii kɛ dade fai, ni maha amɛ hegbɛ ni amɛkojo bo yɛ amɛmlai anaa.

english_verse: I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives.
translation_verse: Mimli aaafu bo koni amɛkɛ bo aye yɛ mlila naa. Amɛaafolɔ ogugɔ kɛ otoii, ni amɛkɛ klante aaagbegbee omɛi ni baashwɛ lɛ. Amɛaaloo obihii kɛ obiyei lɛ kɛaaya, ni omɛi ni aaashwɛ lɛ la aaakpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off.
translation_verse: Amɛaakpɔlɔ otadei lɛ yɛ ohe, ni amɛaajie ojwinei fɛɛfɛji lɛ.

english_verse: I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni mafee ni mikɛku ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ ni obɔi kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa nɛ; no aaahã owoŋ ohiɛ nɔ okwɛ Ijiptbii lɛ, ni okaiŋ amɛ hu dɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, mibatu bo mawo ohenyɛlɔi kɛ mɛi ni eje otsine lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ bo aaaye yɛ yiwalɛ naa. Amɛaaloo nii ni ogbo deŋme yɛ he lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛaashi bo yayai kɛ ohe pasaa: ni amɛaajie ojwamaŋbɔɔ yayaiaŋ kpo. Ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ ba onɔ.

english_verse: have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols.
translation_verse: Aaafee bo enɛɛmɛi ejaakɛ okɛ jeŋmaji lɛ yabɔbɔɔ ajwamãŋ, ni oyanyiɛ amɛwɔji lɛ asɛɛ ni okɛwo ohe muji,

english_verse: You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
translation_verse: Onyiɛ onyɛmi yoo lɛ nanefaamɔi lɛ asɛɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, magbala otoi tamɔ migbala etoi lɛ nɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Ooonu nii kɛaajɛ onyɛmi yoo lɛ kpulu lɛ mli; emli kwɔ, ni eda. Abaaŋmɔ bo, ni abaaye ohe fɛo. Ejaakɛ emli nii lɛ fa.

english_verse: You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin.
translation_verse: Dãa aaatɔ bo, ni owerɛ aaaho ohe. Onyɛmi yoo Samaria toigbalamɔ lɛ gbeyei kɛ fitemɔ kpulu ni.

english_verse: But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Obaanu nii yɛ mli, ni ooolɛmɔ mli. Ooofamɔ oyitsɔi tete, ni oootserɛ ofufɔi ahe; ejaakɛ mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɛ.

english_verse: You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute. The Two Sisters Are Condemned
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, “Akɛni ohiɛ ekpa minɔ, ni oshɛ mi ofɔ osɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, obaana ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ he nɔ.” Nyɔŋmɔ kojo yei enyɔ lɛ

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways!
translation_verse: Yehowa bi mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa ani obaakojo Ohola kɛ Oholiba? Belɛ jajemɔ musubɔɔnii ni amɛfee lɛ otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english_verse: They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛfite gbãlã, ni amɛshwie lá shi; amɛkɛ amɛwɔji lɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ, ni bii ni mikɛ amɛfɔ lɛ, tete amɛkɛ amɛ fee niyenii amɛkɛhã amɛwɔji.

english_verse: They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ gbi ni amɛgbe amɛbii lɛ amɛhã amɛwɔji lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ amɛbabule mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ; ni nakai nɔŋŋ amɛbafee miwe lɛ.

english_verse: They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry.
translation_verse: “Asaŋ, amɛtsu bɔfoi kɛtee majiasɛɛ shɔŋŋ tete po ayaŋɔ hii abaha amɛ; ni kɛ amɛba lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ yei enyɔ nɛɛ juɔ amɛhe, ni amɛdikiɔ amɛhiŋmɛii asɛɛ kɛ adibri, ni amɛwulaa amɛhe kɛ jwinei.

english_verse: They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me.
translation_verse: Amɛtaa saa fɛɛfɛo nɔ, ni aŋmɛɔ okplɔ̃, ni amɛkɛ mitsofakɛŋma kɛ mimu lɛ mamɔɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns,
translation_verse: Anu mɛi babaoo anyamɔ gbee yɛ jɛi, ni ayaŋɔ dãatɔlɔi kɛjɛ ŋa nɔ kɛba ni amɛkɛ nineshigai bawo yei lɛ aniji, ni amɛkɛ akekrei fɛɛfɛji fimɔ amɛyitsei.

english_verse: and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ akɛ, hii ni kɛ yoo nɛɛ wɔɔ lɛ, ani jeee ajwamãŋ amɛbɔɔ lɛ?

english_verse: In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ lɛ yawɔɔ tamɔ akɛ yoo ajwamãŋ wɔɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ amɛkɛ hiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ Ohola kɛ Oholiba ni ji yei nyɛnyɛŋtswii lɛ yawɔ.

english_verse: But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
translation_verse: Shi kojolɔi jalɔi baabu amɛ fɔ akɛ gbãlãfitelɔi kɛ yei láshishwielɔi, ejaakɛ gbãlãfitelɔi kɛ láshishwielɔi ji amɛ.”

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters: I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Mahã asafo yuu abatua amɛ ni awo amɛhe gbeyei ní aha amɛ.

english_verse: They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses.
translation_verse: Asafo lɛ atswia amɛ tɛi, ni amɛkɛ amɛklantei lɛ ashwie amɛ; ni amɛaagbegbee amɛbihii kɛ biyei lɛ, ni amɛaashãshãa amɛshĩai lɛ.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ mafee ni mikɛku ahoshwibɔɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa koni akɛbɔ yei fɛɛ kwa kɔkɔ ni amɛkabɔ ajwamãŋ nɛɛ eko dɔŋŋ tamɔ nyɛfee lɛ.

english_verse: You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ni mawo nyɛ yei enyɔ nɛɛ, nyɛjwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛhe ni nyɛkɛ nyɛwɔji lɛ bule lɛ he nyɔmɔ, ni nyɛna nyɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa.”

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Nomŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ afi ni ji nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ŋmãa ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ ofɔ̃ shi, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ ji gbi krɛdɛɛ nɔ ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ sa Yerusalɛm yi lɛ.

english_verse: Then tell my rebellious people: “Pour water in a cooking pot and set it over a fire. *
translation_verse: Buu weku ni toi egbo lɛ abɛ nɛɛ, ni okɛɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, Okɛ dadesɛŋ ama la nɔ, ni okɛ nu awo mli.

english_verse: Throw in the legs and shoulders of your finest sheep and put in the juicy bones.
translation_verse: Okɛ loo ni afolɔ lɛ kukulii awo mli: hei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ eshuɔ lɛ kɛ ekɔŋ lɛ akɛ wui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afata he ni eyi obɔ̃.

english_verse: Pile wood underneath the pot, and let the meat and bones boil until they are done.”
translation_verse: Ŋɔɔ too ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome, too lai owo latɛŋ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ shishi. Ha ni nu lɛ atswa, hoomɔ, ni wui lɛ tete abe.”

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kpoo hã maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ emli; nakai maŋ lɛ, etamɔ dadesɛŋ ni mli edɔ ŋkanale, ni ŋkanale lɛ yɛ mli lolo. Kɔlɔmɔ loi lɛ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ mli ekomekome, kaahala mli.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mɛi ni agbe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ alá yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lolo. Lá nɛɛ jwere tɛsaa kpataa nɔ, jeee shikpɔŋ nɔ eshwie bɔ ni akɛ su aaanyɛ aha nɔ.

english_verse: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
translation_verse: Mihã mɛi ahiɛ ni akpãtã lɛ alá lɛ shwie tɛsaa kplanaa lɛ nɔ, koni akanyɛ nɔ su aha, bɔ ni afee ni etee mimlifu shi ni ehã matɔ he owele.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, kpoo ha maŋ ni ashwie lá shi yɛ emli lɛ. Mi diɛŋtsɛ hu mato laii pii mawo eshishi.

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Ha lai lɛ afa, shɛremɔ la lɛ, hoomɔ loo lɛ ni ebe jogbaŋŋ, ni otsɔ̃ wonu lɛ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ mli; ha wui lɛ tete aŋala.

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ kɛ dadesɛŋ folo lɛ ama ŋai la lɛ nɔ koni edɔ klakla, ni akɔɔble dadesɛŋ lɛ atsu hɛŋŋ, bɔ ni afee ni emli muji lɛ asere, ni ŋkanale lɛ aje kwraa.

english_verse: I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
translation_verse: Migbo he yaka deŋme, shi kɛ̃lɛ, emli ŋkanale titrii lɛ, lá tete nyɛɛɛ ajie.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ mujinii lɛ no ji ŋkanale lɛ. Akɛni kulɛ mitsuu ohe ni ohe atse shi ohe tseee hewɔ lɛ, hii shi yɛ ohe muji lɛ mli kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni matɔ mihe owele, ni mimii aaashɛ mihe.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Mi, Yehowa, miwie, ni ebaaba mli, ni mafee hu, mifɔŋ, ni minaŋ mɔbɔ, ni mishwaŋ mihe hu; bɔ ni ojeŋba yɔɔ lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni onifeemɔnii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nakai naa makojo bo yɛ; Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.” Gbalɔ lɛ ŋa gbo

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, naa, mibaŋɔ mɔ ni ji ohiŋmɛi mli ajaŋmalaatɛ lɛ trukaa kɛje ohe kɛya. Kɛji eba lɛ nakai lɛ kaawo yara, ni okafo hu, ni ohiŋmɛiŋ akakpala nu tete.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Fo yɛ osɛŋ, kaahã oyaafo je kpo ni anu yɛ onaabu. Kaafee yara ko. Okɛ obɔnduku lɛ afi oyitso, ni owo otokotai lɛ; okɛ mama ko akabala onaabu, ni kaaye yara nɔ niyenii hu.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Mikɛ maŋ lɛ wie leebi mli, ni gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, miŋa lɛ gbo. Hewɔ lɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, mifee bɔ ni afã mi lɛ.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ bi mi akɛ, “Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ? Ani oootsɔ̃ɔ wɔ nɔ ni ofeɔ nɛɛ shishi?”

english_verse: I answered: The Lord God says
translation_verse: Mihã amɛ hetoo akɛ,

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: “Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, Kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, Naa, mibabule mihekrɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ji nyɛhewalɛ ni nyɛkɛwoɔ nyɛhe nɔ lɛ; he krɔŋkrɔŋ ni ji nyɛhiŋmɛiŋ ajaŋmalaatɛ lɛ kɛ nyɛsusumai ashwee lɛ. Nyɛbihii kɛ nyɛbiyei ni nyɛshi yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, akɛ klante baagbe amɛ.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ nyɛbaafee tamɔ bɔ ni mifee mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɛɛ: nyɛkɛ mama eblaŋ nyɛnaabui, ni nyɛyeŋ yara nɔ niyenii hu.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Nyɛbaafimɔ nyɛbɔnduku lɛ, ni nyɛtokotai lɛ aahi nyɛnaji, nyɛwoŋ yara, asaŋ nyɛfoŋ, shi moŋ yɛ nyɛnishaianii ahewɔ lɛ, nyɛaatãrã loo, ni nyɛaakɛ̃mɔ nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ nyɛhe.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Enɛ baaha Ezekiel atsɔ̃ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ahã nyɛ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eeefee lɛ, nakai nyɛaafee. Kɛji enɛ ba mli lɛ, no dani nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ lɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbi nɔ ni mafite amɛSɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni ji amɛmiishɛɛ kɛ amɛhiɛnyam, amɛhiŋmɛiŋ ajaŋmalaatɛ kɛ amɛtsuiŋ nitaomɔnii lɛ, ni makpãtã amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei lɛ hu ahiɛ lɛ

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɔ ko ni lɛ lɛ ehe eje hiɛkpãtãmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aaaba oŋɔɔ abatswa bo adafi.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ aaagbele onaabu, ni okɛ mɔ ni he eje mli lɛ aaawie, ni otɔŋ mu dɔŋŋ; no hewɔ lɛ, oootsɔ̃ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ oha amɛ, ni amɛaana amɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi ekoŋŋ akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ ohã Amonbii lɛ, ni ogba oshi amɛ.

english_verse: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Kɛɛmɔ Amonbii lɛ akɛ, nyɛboa Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa wiemɔ toi, bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, akɛni nyɛnya, ejaakɛ abule miHe Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni afee Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, ni aŋɔ Yuda we lɛ nom lɛ

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, maŋɔ bo maha mɛi ni yɔɔ bokãgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛye onɔ. Amɛbaafee tabilɔi ashitoohei yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛbaato maji amɛhi mli yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; amɛbaaye otsei ayibii lɛ, ni amɛaanu otsina fufɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Maha Rama atsɔ̃ yoomai aniyelihe, ni maha Amonbii amaji wuji lɛ baatsɔ toi atsu. No nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, naa, mite shi miwo bo, ni maŋɔ bo mahã jeŋmaji lɛ ni amɛha onibii. Makpãtã ohiɛ yɛ majimaji fɛɛ ateŋ; ni mafite bo yɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ; makpãtã ohiɛ, ni ooona ole akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Moab he gbalɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, “Akɛni Moab kɛɛ akɛ, naa, Yuda tamɔ shikpɔji krokomɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, mifite Moab anunyam maji wuji ni buɔ ehusu nɔ lɛ. Maji nɛɛ ji Bet-Yeshimot kɛ Baal-Meon kɛ Kiriataim. No baahã Moab he akã aha henyɛlɔi.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: Mikɛ Moab baafata Amonbii lɛ ahe maha bokãgbɛbii lɛ ni amɛŋɔ, ni akaiŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Mibagbala Moabbii atoi, ni amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Edom he Gbalɛ

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni Edom tɔ ehe owele yɛ Yuda we lɛ nɔ, ni yɛ oweletɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ̃ babaoo lɛ,

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mate shi mawo Edom, ni makpãtã emli gbɔmɔ kɛ kooloo fɛɛ hiɛ; ni mafee lɛ amaŋfɔ̃; ni kɛjɛ Teman aahu kɛyashi Dedan lɛ amɛbaanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Mibatsɔ̃ mimaŋ Israelbii anɔ matɔ mihe owele yɛ Edom nɔ. Israelbii kɛ Edom baaye yɛ mimlifu kɛ mimlila naa. Ni amɛaale bɔ ni mitɔɔ owele mihãa.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. Filistia he Gbalɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni Filistibii lɛ to yiŋsha yɛ amɛtsuiŋ ni amɛkɛtɔ mɛi ni ji amɛhenyɛlɔi kɛjɛ teteete lɛ anɔ owele, ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ kwraa kɛmɔ shi

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa mate shi mawo Filistibii lɛ, ni maplene Keretibii lɛ, ni makpãtã mɛi ni baashwɛ yɛ ŋshɔnaagbɛ lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mikɛ mlifu kpele baakã amɛ, ni matɔ mihe owele jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛnɔ, ni no amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, kɛji mitɔ mihe owele yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Be ni wɔyɔɔ wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome lɛ nɔ, nyɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, akɛni Tiro kɛɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm he akɛ, ‘Yiɛ, akumɔ maŋbii agbo lɛ, enaa kã hã mi. Ni akɛni etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ nɛɛ lɛ, mibashwere!’ Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ,

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Amɛbaafite Tiro gbogboi lɛ, ni amɛbaakumɔ emɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amɛshwie shi. Kɛkɛ lɛ mabɛɛ enɔ su tete, ni mafee lɛ tɛsaa kpataa.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni eshikpɔji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ hu akɛ klante baagbe maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ; kɛkɛ lɛ Tirobii aaana ale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, maha Babilon maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar, ni ji maŋtsɛmɛi amaŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi kɛ asraafoi babaoo ajɛ kooyigbɛ abatua Tiro.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Ekɛ klante baakpãtã mɛi ni yɔɔ ohewɔ maji ni jwere ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ, eeetswa ka gbogbo ewo ohe, ni eeetswa kpoku ewo ohe; ni ekɛ tsɛŋi babaoo baaba abatua bo.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baahã akɛ gbogbokuumɔnii lɛ ashimɔ ogbogboi lɛ, ni akɛ lemai aaakumɔ omɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Ekpɔŋɔi ayifalɛ sɔŋŋ naa lɛ, amɛnaneshi mlu kpɔŋŋ lɛ aaatsi onɔ. Kɛji eetsɔ̃ ogboi lɛ amli kɛbote omaŋ lɛ mli tamɔ aboteɔ maŋ ni ajwa egbogbo awo mli lɛ, ekpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ abolɔmɔ kɛ enigbalamɔ shwiilii kɛ eta shwiilii agbɛɛmɔ naawalɛ sɔŋŋ naa lɛ ogbogboi lɛ aaahoso.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ kɛ ekpɔŋɔi lɛ akoklotoi lɛ aaanaanaa oblohuŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ; ekɛ klante aaakpãtã omaŋbii lɛ ahiɛ, ni okulashiŋi ni wa lɛ aaagbeegbee shi.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Ohenyɛlɔi lɛ baaha ojwetrii kɛ oguɔ nii ni oyɔɔ lɛ, amɛbaakumɔ ogbogboi lɛ, ni amɛbaafite oshĩai fɛɛfɛji lɛ; ni tɛi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ sũ lɛ tete amɛbaaloo amɛyawo ŋshɔ mli.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Mahã olalai lɛ agbɛɛmɔ sɛɛ afo, ni anuŋ okpãa saŋkui lɛ agbɛɛmɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: “Mahã otsɔ̃ tɛsaa kpataa, he ni akaa yaa yɛ. Asaŋ bo amaŋ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ mi, Yehowa, miwie.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ Tiro nɛ, ani ŋshɔnaa shikpɔji lɛ ahe kpokpoŋ yɛ oshigbeemɔ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ naa, be ni pilafoi miikɛ̃mɔ, ni aakpãtã omɛi lɛ ahiɛ yɛ omli lɛ?

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ ŋshɔhiɛ lumɛi fɛɛ aaajɛ amɛsɛ̃ii anɔ akpeleke shi, amɛaajie amɛtadei lɛ, amɛaakpɔlɔ amɛheboi wuji ni alo nii awo mli lɛ, amɛaabu hekpokpomɔ tamɔ abuɔ mama, amɛaashwata shikpɔŋ ni amɛhe baakpokpo blibli; be fɛɛ be lɛ amɛhe baajɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ ohewɔ.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Amɛaawo yara yɛ ohewɔ amɛaakɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Bo maŋ ni ogbɛi ehehe, ni okɛ omlibii fɛɛ hiɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ hewalɛ; bo, ni ohe ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni bɔle bo yɛ shikpɔŋ, te aye tɛŋŋ ni osha shi yɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ ahe miikpokpo gbi nɔ ni ogbee shi lɛ. Hɛɛ, ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋ anaa ekpɛ amɛhe yɛ ohiɛkpãtãmɔ lɛ hewɔ.’

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, kɛji mifee omaŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, tamɔ maji ni gbɔmɛi bɛ mli lɛ eko, kɛji mihã ŋshɔŋ bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ baha onɔ, ni nu babaoo tsimɔ onɔ lɛ,

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: no ni manyɛ onɔ koni okɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ ayafata blemabii ni yɔɔ jɛi momo lɛ ahe. Maha bo kɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbohiiaje yɛ naanɔ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli, bɔ ni afee ni mɔ ko akahi omli dɔŋŋ, aloo ona gbɛhe ko yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Maha onaagbee afee gbeyei, ni ohiŋ shi dɔŋŋ; tsɛbelɛ mɛi aaatao bo nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ, anaŋ bo dɔŋŋ kɛaatee naanɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye Tiro ŋkɔmɔ,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: ni okɛɛ Tiro, maŋ ni kã ŋshɔnaa, ni ekɛ ŋshɔnaa majimaji yeɔ guɔ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Ao Tiro, okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mihe yɛ fɛo kɛwula shi.’

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Ohusu yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ. Mɛi ni kpɛ bo akɛ lɛlɛ lɛ kpɛ bo fɛɛfɛo kɛwula shi.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ Hermon Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛsɛotsei sɔŋŋ hɛhɛ bo, ni Lebanon tsenedru akɛfee oshimaatso lɛ.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Bashan tsei wuji akɛgbɔ tablɔi lɛ. Kipro tsei akɛfee odɛke, ni akɛ shuɔ wu ka mli.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Obalaa lɛ Ijipt klala fɛɛfɛo ni alo nii awo mli akɛfee; no nɔŋŋ ji oflaŋaa Onɔhaa buu lɛ, mama bluu kɛ afaseo ni akɛjɛ Kipro ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ akɛfee.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidonbii kɛ Arvadbii ji owirilɔi. Bo diɛŋtsɛ omli ŋaalɔi ji okudɔɔtsɛmɛi.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Gebal onukpai kɛ ŋaalɔi ni yɔɔ omli lɛ ji srɛŋkifoi ni tsimɔɔ omli fɔ̃ji lɛ. Ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛji kɛ amɛsraafoi fɛɛ baa omli amɛbayeɔ bo jara.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “Persiabii kɛ Ludbii kɛ Libiabii yɛ otabilɔi lɛ ateŋ; amɛkɛ tsɛŋ kɛ dade fai tsotsoroɔ shi yɛ otabilɔi ashihilɛhei lɛ amli; amɛ amɛhãa ohiɛ baa nyam.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Arvadhii kɛ Helekhii buɔ yɛ ogbogboi lɛ anɔ kɛkpeɔ, ni Gamad hii buɔ yɛ omɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛkɛ amɛtsɛŋi lɛ tsotsoroɔ ogbogboi lɛ ahe kɛkpeɔ. Amɛ amɛhãa ohe feɔ fɛo kɛwulaa shi.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “Tarshishbii kɛ bo ye jara, ejaakɛ oyɛ guɔ nibii babaoo; amɛkɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ dade kɛ tsɛnsi kɛ sumui baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Helabii kɛ Tubalbii kɛ Meshekbii kɛ bo ye jara. Amɛkɛ gbɔmɛi kɛ akɔɔble nibii baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔyeli nibii lɛ.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Togarmabii kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tawuu okpɔŋɔi kɛ tejiokpɔŋɔi baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Rodobii kɛ bo ye jara. Ŋshɔnaa maji babaoo kɛ bo ye jara krɛdɛɛ ko; amɛ lɛ amɛkɛ shuɔ wu kɛ ebɔnetsei bawoɔ oguɔ nibii ni amɛbaheɔ lɛ nyɔmɔ.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Yuda kɛ Israel kɛ bo ye jara, amɛkɛ ŋmãa kɛ mu kɛ agbãmi kɛ wo kɛ mu kɛ tsofakɛŋma baa, ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damasko kɛ bo ye oguɔ nibii babaoo lɛ he jara. Ekɛ bo ye jara yɛ guɔ nibii srɔtoisrɔtoi babaoo ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Ekɛ wain jɛɔ Helbon, ni akɛ toi ahetsɔi yɛŋ futaa jɛɔ Shar baa.

english_verse: Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices.
translation_verse: Amɛkɛ wain jɛɔ Uzal batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. Akɛ dade nibii kɛ kashia kɛ sinamon batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan kɛ bo ye okpɔŋɔtamɔ sɛi nɔ mama jara.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arabiabii kɛ Kedar lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ ji mɛi ni osumɔ amɛ kɛ gwantɛŋbii kɛ ojwɛnii kɛ abotiai ajarayeli jogbaŋŋ.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Sheba kɛ Rama jarayelɔi kɛ bo ye jara. Amɛkɛ tsofakɛŋmai fɛɛ mli ekpakpai kɛ tɛi ni jara wa fɛɛ kɛ shika baa batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Haran kɛ Kane kɛ Eden kɛ Sheba kɛ Ashur kɛ Kilmad kɛ bo ye jara.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Maji nɛɛ kɛ bo ye atadei kpakpai kɛ mama bluu ni alo nii awo mli atadei, kɛ tsu mli kapɛtii ni hiɛ sui srɔtoi ni akɛ taŋkpee kpãa efimɔ mli kpɛŋŋ jara.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Tarshish lɛji lɛ woɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, otamɔ lɛlɛ ni awo lɛ nii obɔ̃ yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Mɛi ni wiriɔ bo lɛ kɛ bo etee ŋshɔ teŋ tɔ̃ɔ; shi bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ejwra bo yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Be ni okudɔɔtsɛmɛi lɛ bolɔ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ hoso

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: ni wirilɔi lɛ fɛɛ kpeleke shi kɛjɛ lɛlɛ lɛ mli. Asrɛfoi lɛ kɛ kudɔɔtsɛmɛi lɛ badamɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Amɛwo ohe yara ni amɛfo bo waa. Amɛloo mlu amɛwo amɛyiteŋ ni amɛkoklo lamlu mli.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Amɛshɛ amɛyi yɛ ohewɔ, ni amɛbu kpekpe. Amɛwo yara, ni amɛfo bo waa kɛ dɔlɛ naakpa.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Yɛ amɛlelewomɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛwo yaafo lala amɛkɛfo bo akɛ, ‘Namɔ akpãtã ehiɛ pɛŋ yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ tamɔ Tiro?

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Be ni akɛ oguɔ nibii jɛ ŋshɔŋ kɛba lɛ oha mɛi pii tɔrɔ; onii ni ona babaoo kɛ ojarayeli nibii lɛ, oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛmɛi na nii.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, ŋshɔ ejwra bo, ni oshiu kɛtee ŋshɔ shishi; oguɔ nibii kɛ osrafoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ bo eshiu.’

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: “Ŋshɔnaa majiaŋbii fɛɛ ahe ejɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ ohewɔ, ni gbeyei ni naa wa emɔmɔ amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ hu efee amɛ yaa.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Majimaji anɔ jarayelɔi miibo bo ‘tsiaa’, ejaakɛ onaagbee lɛ efee gbeyei, ni olaaje kɛmiiya naanɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa kɛɛmɔ Tiro lumɔ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Owoɔ ohe nɔ ni otsɛɔ ohe nyɔŋmɔ,’ Okɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ji mi, ni mita nyɔŋmɔi lɛ alumɔ sɛi lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋshɔteŋ;’ tsɛbelɛ gbɔmɔ adesa kɛkɛ ji bo, shi jeee nyɔŋmɔ ko. Tsɛbelɛ obuɔ ohe akɛ ole nii tamɔ nɔ ni nyɔŋmɔ ji bo.

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: Efeɔ bo akɛ ole nii fe Daniel, ni teemɔŋ sane ko bɛ ni oleee.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Onilee kɛ oniiashishinumɔ eha ona nii; ona shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi owo ofotroi amli.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Jarayeli he nilee kpele ni oyɔɔ eha onii ni oyɔɔ efa babaoo; ni oninamɔ lɛ eha oowo ohe nɔ.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ: akɛni efeɔ bo akɛ ole nii tamɔ nyɔŋmɔ ko

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: hewɔ lɛ, naa, mahã gbɔi amaji lɛ ateŋ maŋ ni he yɔɔ gbeyei fe fɛɛ, abatua bo; amɛkɛ klante aaabakpãtã nibii fɛɛfɛji ni okɛ onilee na lɛ ahiɛ, amɛaahã onunyam aaaba shi.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Amɛbaanyɛ onɔ amɛwo gbohiiaje bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli, ni obaagbo; obaagbo mɛi ni gboiɔ yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ lɛ agbele lɛ eko.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Be ni oyɔɔ mɛi ni gbeɔ bo lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ani ooonyɛ okɛɛ akɛ ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ko ji mi?’ Be mli ni gbɔmɔ kɛkɛ ji bo, shi ojeee nyɔŋmɔ ko lɛ?

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Obaatsɔ gbɔi anine nɔ ni ogbo foolɔi agbele, ejaakɛ mi, miwie. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.” Tiro Maŋtsɛ lɛ butumɔ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye Tiro maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋkɔmɔ, koni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ: bo lɛ, osɛɛ lɛ mɔ ko bɛ, ole nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ohe yɛ fɛo kɛwula shi.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Ohi Eden, Nyɔŋmɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ tɛ fɛɛ tɛ ni jara wa wula ohe: ojarawatɛi ni ji, rubi kɛ daiamɔnd kɛ topasiɔn kɛ beril kɛ sardio kɛ yaspi kɛ safiro kɛ smaragdo kɛ gaanɛt. Oyɛ fabii kɛ bɛji ni ashwie amɛhe shika. Gbi nɔ ni abɔ bo lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ afee amɛ ahã bo.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Miha mibɔfo ni mifɔ lɛ mu bu ohe; ohi shi yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni onyiɛ tɛi ni tsoɔ tamɔ la ateŋ.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ be ni abɔ bo lɛ shwamɔ ko bɛ ojeŋba he kɛyashi obɔi efɔŋfeemɔ.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Ojarayeli shweremɔ hewɔ lɛ awuiyeli yi bo obɔ̃, ni ofee esha; ni no hewɔ ni mishwie bo kɛje Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni bɔfo ni buɔ ohe lɛ shwie bo kɛje tɛi ni tsoɔ tamɔ la lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Owo ohe ejaakɛ ohe yɛ fɛo. Onilee ha ofee onii tamɔ buulu. Miŋɔ bo mitswa shi; miŋmɛ bo yayai yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ahiɛ koni amɛkwɛ bo.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: Onishaianii lɛ afalɛ yɛ ojarayeli mli anɔkwa ni oyeee lɛ, okɛbule ohei krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ. Mihã la je yɛ omli ni eshã bo wɛɛ, ni mihã otsɔ̃ lamlu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni na bo lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Ni Maji ni le bo fɛɛ she gbeyei, ejaakɛ onaagbee yɛ gbeyei, ni olaaje kɛmiiya naanɔ.” Gbalɛ ni shiɔ Sidon

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ oha Sidon koni ogba oshi lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, bo Sidon, naa mikɛ bo ena, ni mawo mihiɛ nyam yɛ ohewɔ, ni omaŋbii kɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa, kɛji migbala mɛi ni yɔɔ omli lɛ atoi ni mikɛtsɔ̃ɔ bɔ ni miyɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ miha lɛ.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mibaha gbele hela abote omli, ni maha ashwie lá shi yɛ oblohui lɛ amli. Gbohii aaajwere shi yɛ oblohui lɛ amli; mɛi aaanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante ni akɛjɛ okoji anɔ fɛɛ naa. Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.” Aaajɔɔ Israel

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: “Maji ni bɔle Israel we lɛ, ni amɛbɔ lɛ ahora lɛ ateŋ eko eteŋ shi epilaŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmei loo aklati. No amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa.”
