english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ mahã Gog fuuhe ko yɛ Israel, yɛ Gbɛnyiɛlɔi Ajɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ bokãgbɛ lɛ. Gbɛnyiɛlɔi Ajɔɔ nɛɛ mli abaafu Gog kɛ esafo yuu lɛ yɛ, ni gbohii lɛ ayifalɛ baatsi gbɛnyiɛlɔi agbɛ, ni no aaahã awo jɛi gbɛi akɛ Hamon-Gog Jɔɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: Israel we lɛ aaaye nyɔji kpawo sɔŋŋ kɛfu amɛ, bɔ ni afee ni amɛkɛtsuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Israelbii fɛɛ baafata he kɛfu gbohii lɛ, ni no baahã amɛgbɛi ahehe, ejaakɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ majie minunyam lɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ; Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: Nyɔji kpawo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ baafamɔ mɛi krɛdɛɛ koni nakai mɛi lɛ, akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bei fɛɛ koni amɛfu gbohii ni eshwɛ ni jwere shi ni afuko amɛ lɛ koni akɛtsuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛmiikpa shi ni amɛteŋ mɔ ko na gbonyo wu lɛ, eto okadi ko yɛ gbonyo wu lɛ he; okadi lɛ ahi jɛi kɛyashi be ni fulɔi lɛ aaaba abafu wu lɛ yɛ Gog Asafo Yuu Jɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
translation_verse: Maŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Asafo Yuu’ hi shi. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni abaafee atsuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ loofɔji srɔtoi fɛɛ kɛ ŋaŋ kooloi fɛɛ akɛ, nyɛjɛa he fɛɛ he nyɛbaa nyɛbabuaa nyɛhe naa yɛ migbee afɔle kpeteŋkple ni misaa mito mihã nyɛ yɛ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Nyɛbaaye loo ni nyɛbaanu lá.

english_verse: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
translation_verse: Nyɛbaaye kãkãlɔi aloo, ni nyɛbaanu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɛi alá. Nyɛbaaye ojwɛnii kɛ too gwantɛŋbii kɛ too kpakpo kɛ tsinahii, ni ji Bashan kooloi sɔŋŋ ni ewo fɔ lɛ aloo.

english_verse: I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk.
translation_verse: Migbee afɔle ni misaa mito nyɛ nɛɛ lɛ, nyɛbaaye fɔ aahu kɛyaashi nyɛbaatɔrɔ, ni nyɛbaanu lá aahu kɛyaashi ebaatɔ nyɛ tamɔ dãa.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ni yɛ mikpɔlɔ̃ lɛ he lɛ, nyɛbaaye okpɔŋɔi kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtaralɔi kɛ kãkãlɔi kɛ tabilɔi srɔtoi aloo nyɛtɔrɔ. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mi mikɛɛ.” Abaakpale Israel kɛba ekoŋŋ

english_verse: When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory.
translation_verse: “Maha majimaji lɛ fɛɛ ana minunyam lɛ; amɛbaana bɔ ni miye jalɛ sane mihã, kɛ bɔ ni mikɛ minine ŋmɛ amɛnɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ kɛyaa lɛ, Israel we lɛ baale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: Majimaji lɛ hu baale akɛ eshai ni Israel we lɛ fee lɛ hewɔ amɛtee nomŋɔɔ mli lɛ. Akɛni amɛtɔ̃ minɔ lɛ, no hewɔ ni mitsi mihe yɛ amɛhe, ni mitu amɛ miwo amɛhenyɛlɔi adɛŋ ni akɛ klante gbegbee amɛ yɛ ta mli lɛ.

english_verse: Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
translation_verse: Mujinii ni amɛfee lɛ kɛ amɛtɔ̃mɔi lɛ anaa mikɛ amɛ ye yɛ, ni mitsi mihe yɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, agbɛnɛ lɛ makpale Yakob shwiei ni aŋɔ amɛ nom lɛ kɛba ekoŋŋ, ni mana Israel we lɛ fɛɛ mɔbɔ. Maye migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he awuŋã.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Kɛji amɛbahi amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko wooo amɛhe gbeyei lɛ, amɛhiɛ baakpa nɔ akɛ be ni amɛtɔ̃ minɔ lɛ amɛhiɛ shwie shi.

translation_verse: Sɔlemɔ we lɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ shinaatsei lɛ amli lɛɛmɔ kɛ kɛlɛ fɛɛ ye hegbɔ. Tso Afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ Nɔ ko ma shi yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni etamɔ tso afɔleshãa latɛ.

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: Ekwɔlɛ ji ninetalɔi etɛ̃, ni ekɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi enyɔ, kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi enyɔ. Ekoji lɛ kɛ eshishi lɛ kɛ nɔ ni akɛha he lɛ tso akɛfee. Nuu lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Enɛ ji okplɔ̃ ni maa Yehowa hiɛ lɛ.” Shinai lɛ

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: Ni ayeyee kerubii kɛ tɛŋi asamai yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ shinai lɛ ahe, taakɛ aye awo gbogboi lɛ ahe lɛ. Akɛ tso efee agba yɛ koi lɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ.

translation_verse: Ablanaa ko kã piai lɛ ahiɛ, ni ekɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi nyɔŋma, kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi oha. Piai lɛ ashinai lɛ ye kooyigbɛ.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Piai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ srɔdo lɛ mli lɛ daraaa tamɔ nii ni yɔɔ teŋ kɛ shikpɔŋgbɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ ablanaa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ srɔdo lɛ nɔ lɛ lɛɛ fe ablanaa ni yɔɔ teŋ kɛ shishigbɛ srɔdoi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ama tsu lɛ srɔdoi etɛ̃, shi moŋ amɛbɛ akulashiŋi tamɔ bɔ ni tsui krokomɛi ni yɔɔ agbonaagbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ eko lɛ. No hewɔ abɛ ŋwɛigbɛ piai lɛ amli fe piai ni yɔɔ teŋ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them.
translation_verse: Wuoyigbɛ piai lɛ tamɔ kooyigbɛ piai lɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛkɛlɛmɔ kɛ amɛlɛɛmɔ tamɔ ekrokomɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ; amɛnaagbɛi kɛ amɛhe shinai kɛ bɔ ni ato amɛ ahã lɛ hu tamɔ ekrokomɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Gbɛ ko kã wuoyigbɛ piai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ bokãgbɛ he ni atsɔ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ mli lɛ. Gbogbo ko fo wuoyigbɛ piai nɛɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ piai lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nuu lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Piai ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ kɛ piai ni yɔɔ wuoyigbɛ ni amɛhiɛ kwɛɔ kpo lɛ nɔ gbɛ lɛ, nomɛi ji piai krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ. Jɛi osɔfoi ni bɛŋkɛɔ Yehowa lɛ yeɔ afɔle krɔŋkrɔŋi ni fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ. Afɔlei nɛɛ ji niyenii afɔle lɛ kɛ esha afɔle lɛ kɛ sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ, ejaakɛ hei krɔŋkrɔŋi ni.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Kɛji osɔfoi lɛ bote He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, amɛkaje kpo kɛmiiya agbonaa kpo lɛ nɔ, be mli ni amɛ jieko amɛtadei ni amɛwo kɛsɔmɔɔ lɛ amɛshwieko shi, ejaakɛ atadei krɔŋkrɔŋi ni. Amɛkɔlɔ atadei krokomɛi amɛwo dani amɛbɛŋkɛ he ni maŋbii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.” Sɔlemɔ we lɛ dalɛ yɛ ekponɔgbɛ

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni nuu lɛ gbe Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mligbɛ lɛ susumɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ mi je kpo kɛtsɔ agbo ni hiɛ kwɛɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ mli. Eyasusu Sɔlemɔ we lɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ lɛ dalɛ.

english_verse: He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was
translation_verse: Ekɛ susumɔkpãa lɛ susu bokãgbɛ lɛ, ni efee ninetalɔi ohai enumɔ.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: Asaŋ esusu anaigbɛ lɛ ni no hu fee ninetalɔi ohai enumɔ.

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: Esusu ehei ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Atswa gbogbo kɛbɔle he fɛɛ kɛkpe. Gbogbo lɛ kɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi ohai enumɔ, kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu nakai nɔŋŋ. Akɛ gbogbo lɛ fo he ni ji krɔŋkrɔŋ, kɛ he ni bɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ tɛŋ.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Fee sɛɛ lɛ nuu lɛ kɛ mi ba bokãgbɛ agbo lɛ naa,

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: ni naa, Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ anunyam lɛ jɛ bokãgbɛ miiba. Ebaa lɛ jijemɔ ni ekɛba lɛ tamɔ ŋshɔ gbɛɛmɔ; kɛkɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kpɛ kɛ enunyam lɛ.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Ninaa ni mina lɛ tamɔ ninaa ni mina be ni Nyɔŋmɔ ba koni ebafite Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ ninaa nɛɛ etamɔ nɔ ni mina yɛ Kebar Faa lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni miho migbee shi ni mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Yehowa anunyam lɛ tsɔ̃ bokãgbɛ agbo lɛ mli kɛbote Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Mumɔ lɛ wo mi ni ekɛ mi ba mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ; ni naa, Yehowa anunyam lɛ yi Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli obɔ̃ tɔ.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ lɛ, amɛkpa amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ jamɔ, ni amɛ jie amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ agbohii lɛ kɛje mimasɛi, hewɔ lɛ mahi amɛteŋ kɛaatee naanɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, susumɔ bɔ ni Sɔlemɔ we lɛ yɔɔ hã, kɛ esu fɛɛ otsɔ̃ɔ Israel we lɛ koni amɛhiɛ agboi yɛ eshai ni amɛfee lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛhiɛ gboi yɛ nibii fɛɛ ni amɛfee lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, no lɛ ojie Sɔlemɔ we lɛ su lɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ kɛ ehe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛ ekpojeehei lɛ kɛ emlibotemɔhei lɛ kɛ esu lɛ fɛɛ otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ. Ŋmãa yɛ amɛhiɛ ni amɛna, bɔ ni afee ni amɛkwɛ ni amɛye mlai lɛ fɛɛ kɛ akpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ.

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he mla nɛ. No ji akɛ, “Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ema lɛ, kɛ ehewɔ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ ni kã he kɛbɔle lɛ lɛ fɛɛ baafee he ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ. Naa, Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he mla lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: According to the official standards, the altar in the temple had the following measurements: Around the bottom of the altar was a gutter
translation_verse: “Afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ hu dalɛ lɛ nɛ. Susumɔnɔ ni akɛsusu Sɔlemɔ we lɛ no nɔŋŋ akɛsusu afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ. Eshishigbɛ lɛ, awo nɔ ninetalɔ kome, ni elɛɛmɔ hu afee ninetalɔ kome; ni etoi lɛɛmɔ afee dɛ̃ lɛɛmɔ kɛbɔle. Afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ kwɔlɛ afee nɛkɛ.

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Daa gbi lɛ oha too kpakpo kɛ tsina oblanyo kɛ ojwɛni ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe ashã esha he afɔle ahã mi kɛyashi gbii kpawo.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he mlai nɛ: gbi nɔ ni aaama afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni aaashã shãaafɔle ni akɛ lá ashwã nɔ lɛ,

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: ŋɔɔ tsina oblanyo ohã osɔfoi ni ji Levibii ni jɛ Zadok weku lɛ mli lɛ mɛi ni bɛŋkɛɔ mi ni amɛsɔmɔɔ mi lɛ, koni amɛkɛshã esha he afɔle.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Ŋɔɔ elá lɛ eko ni okɛdiki afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he aklontoi ejwɛ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ ahe, kɛ etoi ni bɔle lɛ kpula kɛkpe lɛ he. Bɔ ni ofee; ni okɛtsuu afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he, ni okɛkpãtã hu oha lɛ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ lɛ, ŋɔɔ tsinanuu ni akɛbaashã esha he afɔlei lɛ ni ashã yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ, he ni ato akɛ ashã yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, okɛ too kpakpo hu ni kpa ko bɛ ehe ashã esha he afɔle, ni akɛjie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he esha lɛ tamɔ akɛ tsinanuu lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuu he lɛ.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Kɛji ogbe hetsuumɔ lɛ naa lɛ, okɛ tsinanuu ni kpako bɛ ehe kɛ too ojwɛni ni kpako bɛ ehe ashã afɔle.

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Okɛ amɛ aba mi, Yehowa mihiɛ. Osɔfoi lɛ kɛ ŋoo ashwã amɛnɔ koni ashã akɛ shãa afɔle ahã mi, Yehowa.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ aŋɔ gbii kpawo ni amɛkɛtsuu afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he koni amɛha ehe atse.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kɛji hetsuumɔ gbii lɛ anaa tã lɛ, kɛjɛ gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛyaa lɛ osɔfoi lɛ ashã nyɛshãa afɔlei lɛ kɛ nyɛshidaa afɔlei lɛ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ mana nyɛhe tsui.” Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ.

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Yehowa kɛ mi ku sɛɛ kɛba He krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ shinaa ni yɔɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ naa. Aŋa shinaa lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Shinaa nɛɛ aŋa daa; akagbele, ni mɔ ko akatsɔ̃ jɛi kɛbote mli; ejaakɛ Yehowa, ni ji Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, etsɔ̃ jɛi kɛbote mli, hewɔ lɛ aŋa daa.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Lumɔ lɛ pɛ ji mɔ ni aaanyɛ ayata jɛi eyaye aboloo yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. Lɛ pɛ etsɔ̃ agbo lɛ koishi gbɛ lɛ kɛbote mli ni etsɔ̃ jɛi nɔŋŋ kɛje kpo.” Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mlibotemɔ he mlai

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nuu lɛ kɛ mi tsɔ̃ kooyigbɛ agbo lɛ naa gbɛ kɛba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hiɛ. Mikwɛ, ni naa, Yehowa anunyam lɛ eyi Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ obɔ̃. Kɛkɛ ni miho migbee shi, ni mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ afɔ̃ nɔ, okɛ ohiŋmɛi akwɛ, ni okɛ otoi anu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni makɛɛ bo yɛ Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he akpɔi kɛ mlai lɛ ahe lɛ. Kadimɔ koni ole jogbaŋŋ mɛi ni sa akɛ amɛboteɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli, kɛ mɛi ni esaaa akɛ amɛboteɔ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: “Kɛɛmɔ toigbolɔi lɛ, ni ji Israel we lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, ao Israel we, nyɛmusubɔɔnii lɛ, nyɛkpaa!

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Kɛji nyɛkɛ miniyenii afɔle ni ji fɔ kɛ lá lɛ miiba lɛ, nyɛkaŋmɛa maŋsɛɛbii ni ji tsuiŋ foolɔi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛmiiba miHe Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni amɛbule lɛ. Nyɛmusubɔɔnii fɛɛ lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, nyɛku mikpãŋmɔ lɛ hu mli nyɛfata he.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛtsuuu minibii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ ahe nii yɛ miHe Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ; shi moŋ nyɛto maŋsɛɛbii ni amɛtsu.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Maŋsɛɛbii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Israelbii ateŋ lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko ni ji tsuiŋ foolɔ kɛ helooŋ foolɔ akabote miHe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.” Atse Levibii lɛ kɛje Osɔfoi lɛ ahe

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: “Shi moŋ Levibii ni shi mi kɛtee sɛɛ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyanyiɛ amɛwɔji asɛɛ be ni Israelbii du gbɛ lɛ, abaagbala amɛtoi.

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: Amɛbaasɔ̃mɔ yɛ miHe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, amɛbaabu miSɔlemɔ we lɛ agboi lɛ anaa, ni amɛbaasɔ̃mɔ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli hu. Amɛ amɛbaagbe kooloi ni akɛbaashã shãaafɔlei lɛ, kɛ maŋbii lɛ afɔlei lɛ; ni amɛ nɔŋŋ amɛbaawa maŋbii lɛ ni amɛsɔmɔ amɛ.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Akɛni Levibii lɛ sɔmɔ Israelbii lɛ yɛ amɛwɔji lɛ anaa, ni no hã Israel we lɛ fee esha hewɔ lɛ, mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikã mihe kitã akɛ mibagbala amɛtoi.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Amɛbɛŋkɛŋ mi koni amɛbasɔmɔ mi akɛ osɔfoi; ni amɛbɛŋkɛŋ minibii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ kɛ nibii ni ji krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ ekoeko kwraa he. Shi moŋ, amɛhiɛ baashwie shi yɛ nifɔɔjianii ni amɛfee lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ, mikɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli nitsumɔ baawo amɛdɛŋ koni amɛtsu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni sa ni atsu yɛ mli lɛ.” Osɔfoi lɛ

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Osɔfoi lɛ ni jɛ Levi akutso lɛ mli, ni amɛ ji Zadok shwiei, mɛi ni kã he amɛsɔmɔ mi yɛ miHe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, be mli ni Isrealbii lɛ du gbɛ kɛje mihe lɛ, amɛ amɛbaabɛŋkɛ mi ni amɛsɔmɔ mi. Amɛ amɛbaashã fɔ kɛ lá afɔle lɛ amɛha mi. Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Amɛ amɛbaabote miHe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni amɛ amɛbaabɛŋkɛ mikpɔlɔ̃ lɛ ni amɛsɔmɔ mi; ni amɛ amɛbaatsu minii amɛhã mi.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: Kɛ amɛmiiya Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛwo klala atadei. Amɛkawo kuntu nɔ ko nɔ ko be mli ni amɛsɔmɔɔ yɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ agboi lɛ anaa kɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
translation_verse: “Amɛfi klala bɔnduku, ni amɛwo klala tswakoto. Amɛkafi amɛmli kɛ nɔ ko ni baahã latsa baatsa amɛ.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛmiije kpo kɛya maŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ agbonaagbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛ jie amɛtadei ni amɛwo kɛsɔmɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛkɛshwie He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ piai lɛ amli. Amɛwo atadei krokomɛi koni nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ akatsɛŋe maŋbii lɛ.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ akashɛ amɛyi, ni amɛkato amɛyi hu; shi moŋ amɛshwao nɔ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ko osɔfo ko akanu wain kɛji eeya mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Amɛkaŋɔ yoo okulafo loo yoo ni ashwie lɛ; shi moŋ osɔfo lɛ aŋɔ oblayoo foro ni jɛ Israel we lɛ shwiei lɛ amli, loo okulafo ni ji osɔfo ko ŋa okulafo.

english_verse: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
translation_verse: “Osɔfo lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ mimaŋbii lɛ srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni jeee krɔŋkrɔŋ teŋ. Amɛha amɛle srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni he tseee kɛ nɔ ni he tse teŋ.

english_verse: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Kɛji naataamɔ ko te shi lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ nɔŋŋ afee kojolɔi ni amɛkura sane lɛ yɛ mimlai kɛ akpɔi lɛ anaa. Amɛye mimlai kɛ mikpɔi ni kɔɔ migbii juji ni mito lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ. Amɛfee mihejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: Amɛkaya gbonyo ko he ni amɛkɛbule amɛhe; kɛ̃lɛ yɛ tsɛ loo nyɛ loo binuu loo biyoo, loo nyɛmi nuu loo nyɛmi yoo ni bɛ wu pɛ he amɛaanyɛ amɛbule amɛhe yɛ.

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Gbi nɔ ni eyaa He krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ yɛ mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ koni eyasɔmɔ yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, eyashã ehe esha afɔle. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɛ.

english_verse: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
translation_verse: “Osɔfoi lɛ bɛ gboshinii ko; mi ji amɛgboshinii. Amɛkana gboshinii ko kwraa yɛ Israel. Mi ji amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Nii ni amɛye ji niyenii afɔle lɛ kɛ esha he afɔle lɛ kɛ sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ. Asaŋ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ajɔɔ nɔ yɛ Israel atsɔ̃ amɛnɔ.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Nyɛŋmɔshinii fɛɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni nyɛkɛshãa afɔlei nyɛhãa mi lɛ, osɔfoi lɛ anɔ ni. Asaŋ klɛŋklɛŋ ma aboloo ni nyɛaashã lɛ, akɛhã osɔfoi lɛ, koni mijɔɔmɔ ahi nyɛwe.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Osɔfoi lɛ akaye loofɔlɔ ko aloo kooloo ko ni gbo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edɛŋ gbele, aloo kooloo ko tserɛ lɛ ni egbo.”

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: “Nyɛkɛ ŋsɛnii ni ja kɛ efa ni ja kɛ bat ni ja asusua nii.

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ abaaye Asesei Agbijurɔ lɛ, gbii kpawo lɛ mli gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ, lumɔ lɛ ahã nibii nɛɛ ni akɛshã esha afɔlei kɛ shãa afɔlei kɛ ŋmãa afɔlei kɛ mu lɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ.”

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ Krɔŋkrɔŋ ni afo lɛ, afo emli eko; no kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ, kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋma. Ni jɛi afee He Krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ, no mli Sɔlemɔ we lɛ ama.

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Ao, nyɛ Israel lumɛi, bɔ ni nyɛfee lɛ efa. Nyɛfɔ̃a yiwalɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ nifeemɔi lɛ, ni nyɛyea jalɛ sane koni nyɛfee nɔ ni ja. Nyɛkpaa mimaŋbii lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ji amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: “Efa kɛ bat aye hegbɔ, koni bat lɛ aye homer mlijai nyɔŋma mli ekome, ni efa lɛ hu homer mlijai nyɔŋma mli ekome; homer, afee tɛ ni afo.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Nyɛfea nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ nyɛhã mɔ ni jeee kwa ekwa efee esha, loo mɔ ni leee ni efee esha ko lɛ, koni akɛtsuu Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he.

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: “Afɔle ni nyɛbaashã nɛ: Ŋmãa efa mlijaa ekpaa mli ekome ni ji homer mlijaa nyɔŋmai ekpaa mli ekome. Akoko hu efa mlijaa ekpaa mli ekome, ni ji homer mlijaa nyɔŋmai ekpaa mli ekome.

english_verse: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
translation_verse: Mu he mla nɛ: Mu bat kome mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome, ni ji mu kor mlijaa oha mli ekome.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. translation_verse: Lumɔ lɛ gbɛnaa nitsumɔ ji akɛ, lɛ eha kooloi ni akɛbaashã afɔlei ni ji shãa afɔlei kɛ niyenii afɔlei kɛ dãa afɔlei lɛ yɛ gbii juji kɛ nyɔji hei kɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbii kɛ Israelbii agbii juji krokomɛi ni amɛyeɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Gbijurɔyeli gbii kpawo lɛ mli gbi fɛɛ gbi nɔ lɛ, ehã tsinahii kpawo kɛ ojwɛnii kpawo ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe, ni akɛshã shãa afɔle aha Yehowa. Daa gbi lɛ ehã kpakpo kome hu ni akɛshã esha he afɔle.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ tsina oblanyo ni kpa ko kwraa bɛ ehe, koni okɛtsuu He krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Osɔfo lɛ aŋɔ kooloo ni akɛshã esha he afɔle lɛ lá lɛ eko, koni ekɛdiki Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaatsei lɛ ahe kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ shishitoo koji ejwɛ lɛ ahe; ekɛdiki shinaatsei ni yɔɔ agbo ni kã kɛyaa mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe hu.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: “Asaŋ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛyea Hehoo lɛ. Aye aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã gbii kpawo.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ lumɔ lɛ ahã tsinanuu kome ni akɛshã esha afɔle ahã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni ehã ni akɛshã niyenii afɔle nɛ ŋmãa efa kome afata tsinanuu kome he, ni ŋmãa efa kome afata ojwɛni kome he; ni ŋmãa efa fɛɛ efa lɛ akɛ mu hiŋ kome afata he.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Mligbɛ kpo lɛ nɔ agbo lɛ ni kwɛɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ, aŋa daa nitsumɔ gbii ekpaa lɛ; shi hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ agbele, ni nyɔŋ hee gbi lɛ nɔ hu agbele.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Ni lumɔ lɛ ajɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ etsɔ̃ agbo lɛ koi lɛ shi kɛbote mli, ni eyadamɔ agbo lɛ shinaatso lɛ he. Osɔfoi lɛ ashã eshãa afɔle lɛ kɛ etoiŋjɔlɛ afɔlei lɛ ahã lɛ; ni eja Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa yɛ agbo lɛ shinaa lɛ naa; ni eje kpo. Shi agbo lɛ, akaŋa kwraa kɛyashi gbɛkɛnaashi.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ aba Yehowa hiɛ ni amɛbaja lɛ yɛ agbo lɛ shinaa lɛ naa yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ kɛ nyɔji hei lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Shãa afɔle ni lumɔ lɛ kɛba ebaha Yehowa yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ ji too gwantɛŋbii ekpaa ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe kɛ ojwɛni kome ni kpa ko bɛ ehe.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Niyenii afɔle ni afata ojwɛni kome he ji, ŋmãa efa kome; ni niyenii afɔle ni afata gwantɛŋbii lɛ ahe ji bɔ ni lɛ eeenyɛ. Ekɛ mu hin kome afata ŋmãa efa kome fɛɛ efa kome he.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋ hee gbijurɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ lumɔ lɛ baahã tsina oblanyo kome kɛ too gwantɛŋbii ekpaa kɛ ojwɛni kome ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Niyenii afɔle ni baafata tsinanuu kome he ji ŋmãa efa kome; ni ojwɛni kome hu ŋmãa efa kome; ni gwantɛŋbii lɛ hu ŋmãa bɔ ni lɛ eeenyɛ ehã. Ni ekɛ mu hin kome afata ŋmãa efa kome fɛɛ efa kome he.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Kɛji lumɔ lɛ baabote mli lɛ etsɔ̃ agbo lɛ koi lɛ shi gbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛya mli, ni etsɔ̃ jɛi nɔŋŋ kɛje kpo.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: “Kɛji maŋbii lɛ miiba abaja Yehowa yɛ gbii juji lɛ anɔ lɛ, mɔ ni baatsɔ̃ kooyigbɛ agbo lɛ mli kɛbote mli ni ebaja lɛ, etsɔ̃ wuoyigbɛ agbo lɛ kɛje kpo. Ni mɔ ni aaatsɔ wuoyigbɛ agbo lɛ kɛbote mli lɛ, etsɔ̃ kooyigbɛ agbo lɛ kɛje kpo. Mɔ ko akatsɔ̃ agbo ni etsɔ̃ kɛba mli lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛje kpo. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aya ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛje kpo.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Kɛji maŋbii lɛ miibote mli lɛ, lumɔ lɛ kɛ amɛ abote mli; ni kɛ amɛmiije kpo hu, ekɛ amɛ aje kpo.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Gbijurɔ fɛɛ gbijurɔ nɔ lɛ niyenii afɔle ni afata tsina oblanyo kome he ji ŋmãa efa kome; ni ojwɛni kome hu nɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa efa kome; ni ekɛ ŋmãa bɔ ni eeenyɛ afata gwantɛŋbii lɛ ahe. Ni mu hin kome afata ŋmãa efa kome fɛɛ efa kome he.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: “Kɛji lumɔ lɛ baashã tsuijurɔ naa afɔle ehã Yehowa lɛ, shãa afɔle jio, shidaa afɔle jio, agbele agbo ni kwɛɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ ahã lɛ koni ekɛ eshãa afɔlei lɛ loo shidaa afɔle lɛ ayahã tamɔ efeɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ eje kpo; ni kɛ eje kpo sɛɛ lɛ, aŋa agbo lɛ.” Daa gbi afɔle lɛ

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: “Daa gbi leebi lɛ, ekɛ gwantɛŋbi kome ni eye afi ni kpa ko bɛ ehe ashã shãa afɔle ahã Yehowa. Eshã afɔle nɛɛ daa leebi.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Ekɛ niyenii afɔle afata he daa leebi. Eŋɔ ŋmãa mamu efa mlijaa ekpaa mli ekome, ni ekɛ mu hin mlijaa etɛ̃ mli ekome afata he, ni akɛkpɔtɔ akɛ niyenii afɔle ahã Yehowa. Akpɔ ni akã shi daa ji no.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Kɛji lumɔ lɛ kɛ egbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eko ke ebihii lɛ eko lɛ, no atsɔ̃ ebi lɛ nɔ; egboshinii ni ena ji no.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji lumɔ lɛ fo egbɛfaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko eke etsuji lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi tsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ kɛyashi heyeli afi lɛ nɔ; kɛkɛ lɛ ekɛku sɛɛ ehã lumɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi ebihii lɛ pɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ gboshinii ni akɛke amɛ lɛ akɛ amɛnɔ.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Asaŋ lumɔ lɛ akashɔ̃ maŋbii lɛ agboshinii lɛ eko ni eshwie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi moŋ ekɛ nɔ ni ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ mli eko ahã ebihii lɛ ni etsɔ̃ amɛnɔ, bɔ ni afee ni akashɔ̃ mimaŋbii lɛ eko gboshinii yɛ edɛŋ.” Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli Kpatai lɛ

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nuu lɛ kɛ mi tsɔ̃ gbɛ ko ni kã agbo lɛ masɛi lɛ mli kɛtee kooyigbɛ he ni osɔfoi lɛ atsui krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ni jɛi lɛ mina he ko yɛ tsui lɛ anaigbɛ.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Atswa tɛ gbogbo kɛbɔle kpo fɛɛ kpo he kɛkpe kpula, ni afee latɛi akpɛtɛ gbogbo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni nuu lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Biɛ nɛɛ ji kpatai, he ni Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli suɔlɔi lɛ baahoo loo ni maŋbii kɛbashã afɔlei lɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nuu lɛ kɛ mi ku sɛɛ kɛba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaa lɛ shi ekoŋŋ; ni naa, nu miiho kɛmiijɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ shinaa kpoku lɛ shishi kɛmiiya bokãgbɛ he ni Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hiɛgbɛ kwɛɔ lɛ. Nu lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ wuoyigbɛ yɛ shinaa lɛ kpoku lɛ shishi, yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ wuoyigbɛ.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ mi je kpo kɛtsɔ kooyigbɛ agbo lɛ mli, ni ekpala mi kɛlɔgɔ shi kɛba agbonaagbɛ agbo ni kwɛɔ bokãgbɛ lɛ naa. Ni nu lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ wuoyigbɛ.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ebi mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ona enɛ?” Kɛkɛ ni enyiɛ mihiɛ kɛku sɛɛ kɛba faa lɛ naa ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: Ni be ni miku misɛɛ miba lɛ, mina tsei babaoo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ faa lɛ toi biɛ kɛ biɛ.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ hoɔ kɛyaa bokãgbɛ, ni emaa eyi shi kɛtsɔ̃ɔ Yordan Jɔɔ lɛ mli, ni ekɛ enaa yawoɔ Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu lɛ bote Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehãa Ŋoo Ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu tsɔ̃ɔ nuŋma.”

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Wolɛi aaadamɔ shi kɛjɛ En-Gedi ŋshɔnaa aahu kɛyagbee En-Eglaim ŋshɔnaa tɔ̃ɔ, ni jɛi aaatsɔ yaa kamɔhe. Emli loi srɔtoisrɔtoi aaafa babaoo diɛŋtsɛ tamɔ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ mli loi lɛ.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Shi nu ni yɔɔ emukpoi kɛ ehewɔ ŋmiamɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsɔŋ nuŋma. Nomɛi baanyɔ ŋoo.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Yelitsei srɔtoisrɔtoi fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ faa lɛ toi biɛ kɛ biɛ; ni amɛyibai kplaŋ ni amɛyibii hu kplaŋ shi moŋ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ, amɛbaawo yibii hei, ejaakɛ nuŋma ni jɛɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hãa amɛ nu. Amɛyibii aaatsɔ̃ niyenii, ni amɛyibai lɛ aatsɔ̃ tsabaa.” Shikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: Mikã shikpɔŋ nɛɛ he kitã akɛ mikɛbaahã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ, agbɛnɛ lɛ etsɔ̃ nyɛgbɛfaŋnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛjaa lɛ bɔ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ana pɛpɛɛpɛ tamɔ enyɛmi.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ husu lɛ nɛ: Kooyigbɛ lɛ husu lɛ ajɛ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ naa kɛyatsɔ Hetlon kɛ Lebo-Hamat kɛ Zedad,

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: kɛ Berota kɛ Sibraim ni kã Damasko kɛ Hamat husu lɛ nɔ lɛ. Husu lɛ atsa nɔ aahu kɛyashi Hazer-Hatikon ni kã Hauran husu naa lɛ.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kooyigbɛ husu lɛ ajɛ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ bokãgbɛ kɛya Hazar-Enon ni kã Damasko kɛ Hamat husui lɛ anaa yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ aaatsɔ kooyigbɛ husu lɛ.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: “Bokãgbɛ husu lɛ ajɛ Hazar-Enon ni kã Hauran kɛ Damasko teŋ lɛ. Aŋɔ Yordan Faa lɛ akɛ husu, bɔ ni Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ aye anaigbɛ, ni Gilead shikpɔŋ lɛ hu aye bokãgbɛ. Husu lɛ akã shi aahu kɛyashi Tamar tɔ̃ɔ yɛ bokãgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baatsɔ̃ bokãgbɛ husu.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Wuoyigbɛ husu lɛ nɛ. Kɛjɛ Tamar kɛtsɔ̃ Meribat-Kadesh Faa lɛ he, kɛtsɔ̃ Ijipt nujɔɔ lɛ he kɛyamɔ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsɔ̃ wuoyigbɛ husu.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: “Anaigbɛ husu lɛ ajɛ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ he, ni etsɔ̃ kooyigbɛ aahu kɛyashi he ko yɛ Lebo-Hamat ŋlɛnɔ. Enɛ baatsɔ̃ anaigbɛ husu lɛ.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ nyɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛhaa nyɛhe yɛ Israel akutsei lɛ anaa.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Nyɛfɔ̃a oshiki kɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛhãa nyɛhe, ni etsɔ̃ gboshinii eha nyɛ kɛ mɛi ni ebato gbɔ yɛ nyɛteŋ, ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ nyɛteŋ lɛ. Amɛtsɔmɔ tamɔ Israel fɔmɔbii nɔŋŋ yɛ nyɛteŋ koni amɛ kɛ nyɛ aja shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ akɛ gboshinii hã nyɛ yɛ Israel akutsei lɛ anaa.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Akutso fɛɛ akutso mli ni gbɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ, aha lɛ gboshinii lɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: “Nyɛfoa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ko krɛdɛɛ ni kɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ je husu kɛjɛ bokãgbɛ kɛyashi anaigbɛ nyɛfɔa shi. No lɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ, ni ekɛlɛ atamɔ gbɛfaŋnii lɛ eko nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ bokãgbɛ husu lɛ nɔ kɛyashi anai husu lɛ nɔ. He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ama teŋ.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he krɛdɛɛ ni nyɛbaafo nyɛfɔ̃ shi kɛha Yehowa lɛ kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ, kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni afo lɛ, bɔ ni ajara lɛ nɛ: Asusu ekɛlɛ ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni wuoyigbɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋma yɛ bokãgbɛ ni anaigbɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ. Yehowa Sɔlemɔ we lɛ ama shikpɔŋ nɛɛ teŋ.

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Akɛ nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ahã osɔfoi ni afɔ amɛ mu ni jɛ Zadok shwiei lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛ amɛ ji mɛi ni sɔmɔ mi anɔkwale mli be ni Israelbii kɛ Levibii lɛ du gbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Enɛ afee amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ ni ji krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni afo lɛ mli, ni ebɛŋkɛ Levibii lɛ ahusu lɛ.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Levibii lɛ hu ana amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ osɔfoi lɛ ahusu lɛ ŋlɛnɔ, yɛ wuoyigbɛ. Ekɛlɛ kɛjɛ bokãgbɛ kɛyashi anaigbɛ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ, ni elɛɛmɔ kɛjɛ kooyigbɛ kɛyashi wuoyigbɛ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋma.

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Amɛkahɔ̃ɔ eko, ni amɛkɛkatsake eko hu. Amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ krɛdɛɛ ni akɔ nɛɛ he ko he ko akahã mɔ ko, ejaakɛ eji shikpɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ha Yehowa.

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shwɛɔ, ni elɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi akpei enumɔ kɛ ekɛlɛ hu ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ lɛ akã shi akɛ kwamaŋnɔ, ni akɛfee shihilɛhei kɛ maŋ he shikpɔŋ, ni maŋ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ nɛɛ teŋ.

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛlɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, no ji ninetalɔi akpei ejwɛ kɛ ohai enumɔ kɛjɛ koŋ kome kɛyamɔ koŋ kome.

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ ni shwɛɔ ni kã shi yɛ he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ afee ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋma yɛ bokãgbɛ kɛ anaigbɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ. Akɛ no afee ŋmɔ koni ana niyenii kɛjɛ mli aha nitsulɔi fɛɛ ni tsuɔ maŋ lɛ he nii lɛ.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni jɛ Israel akutsei lɛ amli lɛ, ahu jɛi.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: “Belɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛfo nyɛfɔ̃ shi kɛha he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ fɛɛ lɛ ekɛlɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ afee pɛpɛɛpɛ, no ji ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ.

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: “Agbɛnɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ ni kã Sɔlemɔ we lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛfaŋ nɔ lɛ he biɛ kɛ biɛ, kɛjɛ bokãgbɛ kɛyashi anaigbɛ lɛ, afee lumɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekã shi kɛjɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he kɛtee bokãgbɛ husu lɛ naa, ni anaigbɛ hu ekã kɛjɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ he kɛyamɔ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ. Ekooyigbɛ husu ji he ni Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ kã lɛ, ni ewuoyigbɛ husu ji Benyamin shikpɔŋ lɛ husu naa.” Akutsei krokomɛi lɛ ashikpɔŋ

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛha Gad akutso lɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ husu lɛ ajɛ Tamar kɛnyiɛ wuoyi anaigbɛ kɛyamɔ Meriba-Kadesh Faa lɛ kɛtsɔ Ijipt nujɔɔ lɛ he kɛyamɔ Mediterenia Ŋshɔ lɛ.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nyɛbaaja nyɛha Israel akutsei lɛ; amɛgboshinii kɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnii ji enɛ. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.” Yerusalɛm agboi lɛ

english_verse: The city of Jerusalem will have twelve gates, three on each of the four sides of the city wall. These gates will be named after the twelve tribes of Israel. The gates of Reuben, Judah, and Levi will be in the north; Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan will be in the east; Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun will be in the south; Gad, Asher, and Naphtali will be in the west. Each side of the city wall will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: “Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ hiɛ agboi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ. Kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ gbogbo kome koŋ kɛyashi gbogbo kroko koŋ lɛ kɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi akpei ejwɛ kɛ ohai enumɔ, ni eko fɛɛ eko hiɛ agboi etɛ̃; ni akɛ Israel akutsei lɛ agbɛi ewo agbo fɛɛ agbo. Kooyigbɛ agboi lɛ akɛwo Ruben kɛ Yuda kɛ Levi. Bokãgbɛ agboi lɛ akɛwo Yosef kɛ Benyamin kɛ Dan. Wuoyigbɛ agboi lɛ akɛwo Simeon kɛ Isakar kɛ Zebulon, ni anaigbɛ agboi lɛ akɛwo Gad kɛ Asher kɛ Naftali.

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ gbogbo ni bɔle maŋ lɛ he kpula kɛkpe lɛ ekɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi akpei nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ. Kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔ kɛyaa nɛɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛi ji: ‘Yehowa yɛ jɛi!’ ”

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yuda Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar fã ta kɛba, ni ebasa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ yi.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ lɛ hã eye Maŋtsɛ Yehoiakim nɔ kunim. Kɛkɛ ni emɔ Yehoiakim kɛ nomii komɛi hu, ni eloo Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ mli nibii lɛ ekomɛi, ni ekɛ nomii lɛ kɛ nibii nɛɛ tee Babilon shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ nibii lɛ yawo enyɔŋmɔ lɛ we lɛ mli nitoohe lɛ.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar fã Ashpenaz, epiafonyonukpa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ, akɛ ehala Israelbii nomii lɛ ateŋ maŋtsɛmɛiabii lɛ kɛ abladei ashwiei lɛ ateŋ oblahii komɛi.

english_verse: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
translation_verse: Esa akɛ oblahii nɛɛ ahe yɛ fɛo, kpa ko kpa ko akahi amɛgbɔmɔtsei ahe; amɛyɛ tsɔsemɔ, amɛyɛ jwɛŋmɔ, ni amɛjwɛŋmɔŋ kã shi kɛhã nikasemɔ, koni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛsɔ̃mɔ yɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ mli. Efã hu akɛ atsɔ̃ɔ amɛ Babilonbii awiemɔ lɛ kɛ amɛwoloŋ hu.

english_verse: and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar to akɛ daa gbi lɛ ahã oblahii nɛɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii kɛfɔkɛfɔ ni eyeɔ kɛ wain hu ni enuɔ lɛ eko. Ekɛɛ akɛ atsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nii afii etɛ̃; ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛ oblahii lɛ aba abatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Oblahii ni ahala lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi ji Daniel kɛ Hanania kɛ Mishael kɛ Azaria. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛjɛ Yuda akutso lɛ mli.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Piafonyonukpa fe fɛɛ lɛ wo oblahii ejwɛ nɛɛ gbɛii krokomɛi. Ewo Daniel Belteshazar, ni ewo Hanania Shadrak, ni ewo Mishael Meshak, ni ewo Azaria Abednego.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Shi Daniel tswa efai shi akɛ eyeŋ maŋtsɛ niyenii ni ewo fɔ lɛ, ni enuŋ maŋtsɛ wain lɛ hu koni ekabule ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, ekpa Ashpenaz, piafonyonukpa fe fɛɛ lɛ, fai akɛ eŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ koni ekabule ehe.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ hã Ashpenaz hiɛ sɔ Daniel, ni emusuŋ tsɔ̃ lɛ yɛ ehe.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Shi moŋ ekɛɛ Daniel akɛ, “Miishe gbeyei akɛ aleee nɔ minuŋtsɔ maŋtsɛ, ni eto niyenii kɛ wain ni akɛhã nyɛ lɛ, baana akɛ nyɛgbɔmɔtsei bɛ akɔnɔ tamɔ nyɛtipɛŋfoi oblahii krokomɛi lɛ agbɔmɔtsei. Enɛ aaahã miwala atɔ̃ yɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ.”

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Daniel kɛɛ mɔ ni piafonyonukpa lɛ efã akɛ ekwɛ lɛ Daniel lɛ kɛ Hanania kɛ Mishael kɛ Azaria nɔ lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: “Ofainɛ, hã wɔ tsei ayibii kɛ baibai kɛkɛ koni wɔye kɛ nu folo hu kɛkɛ ni wɔnu kɛyashi biɛ gbii nyɔŋma koni okɛka wɔ, otsuji, okwɛ;

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: koni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ wɔ ato oblahii ni yeɔ maŋtsɛwe lɛ niyenii ni ewo fɔ lɛ ahe. Bɔ ni ooona lɛ odamɔ no nɔ koni ofee wɔ bɔ ni osumɔɔ.”

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Gbii nyɔŋma lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ana akɛ Daniel kɛ enanemɛi lɛ ahiɛ efee fɛo, ni amɛgbɔmɔtsei eshwishwii fe oblahii krokomɛi lɛ ni yeɔ maŋtsɛwe lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai ni ewo fɔ lɛ agbɔmɔtsei.

english_verse: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛlɔ lɛ shi niyenii kɛ wain ni ato akɛ akɛhã amɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni ehã amɛ tsei ayibii kɛ baibai lɛ kɛkɛ, ni amɛye.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ duro nɛkɛ oblahii ejwɛ nɛɛ jwɛŋmɔ, ni amɛnyɛ amɛkase woloŋ kɛ nii fɛɛ ni atsɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ. Yɛ Daniel gbɛfaŋ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hã enu ninaa fɛɛ ninaa kɛ lamɔ fɛɛ lamɔ hu shishi efata he.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Be ni be ni maŋtsɛ lɛ eto lɛ shɛ lɛ, Ashpenaz, piafonyo lɛ, kɛ oblahii lɛ fɛɛ tee Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar hiɛ ekɛ amɛ yatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ amɛ fɛɛ wie, ni Daniel kɛ Hanania kɛ Mishael kɛ Azaria ji mɛi ni maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ sɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ oblahii lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehala amɛ koni amɛsɔ̃mɔ yɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ mli.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Nilee fɛɛ nilee kɛ sane fɛɛ sane ni maŋtsɛ lɛ bi Daniel kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ, ena akɛ amɛle nii shii nyɔŋma toi abɔ fe emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ ninalɔi kɛ ashwãifeelɔi lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_verse: Daniel sɔ̃mɔ yɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi afi nɔ ni Persia Maŋtsɛ Koresh baye Babilon nɔ kunim lɛ.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Nebukadnezar maŋtsɛyeli afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ela lamɔi komɛi. Lamɔi nɛɛ hã etsui bɔ̃i yeli, ni wɔ tserɛ yɛ ehiɛ.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mila lamɔ ko, ni mitsui miiye akɛ male lamɔ lɛ shishi.”

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Amɛto he yɛ Aram wiemɔ mli akɛ, “Nii, oyi ana wala kɛya naanɔ! Jajemɔ lamɔ lɛ otsɔ̃ɔ wɔ, otsuji, ni wɔɔtsɔ̃ɔ bo shishi.”

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni mito miyiŋ akɛ mibabi nyɛ ji akɛ nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛtsɔ̃a mi nɔ lamɔ ni mila lɛ, koni nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi eshishi hu. Kɛji nyɛnyɛɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ mahã atserɛ nyɛmli, ni aaahã nyɛshĩai lɛ atsɔ̃ tamɔ tumo.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛji nyɛnyɛ nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi nɔ lamɔ ni mila lɛ, ni nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ eshishi hu lɛ, no lɛ mibake nyɛ nibii babaoo; asaŋ mibawo nyɛhiɛ nyam hu jogbaŋŋ. Agbɛnɛ nyɛtsɔa mi nɔ lamɔ ni mila lɛ kɛ eshishi hu.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Amɛha hetoo ekoŋŋ amɛkɛɛ akɛ, “Nii atsɔ̃ɔ wɔ lamɔ lɛ, ni wɔɔtsɔ̃ɔ lɛ eshishi.”

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: kɛji nyɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ mi lamɔ lɛ, toigbalamɔ kome kã shi hã nyɛ. Nyɛto nyɛyiŋ akɛ nyɛbaamale, ni nyɛbaashishiu mi kɛyashi beyinɔ ni nibii aaatsake. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛtsɔa mi lamɔ lɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ no baahã male akɛ nyɛbaanyɛ eshishi nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ.”

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Babilonbii lɛ to he amɛhã Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar akɛ, “Nii, mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ je nɛɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ bo osane nɛɛ naa etsɔ̃ɔ. Maŋtsɛ ko kwraa ehiko shi pɛŋ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni eje agbo ehã, ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ hu ehã, ni ekɛ nɛkɛ sane efɔ̃ ashwãifeelɔi loo klamɔfoi loo ŋkunyaayelɔi loo Babilonbii ahiɛ dã.

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Sane ni Maŋtsɛ biɔ nɛɛ mli wa bɔ ni mɔ ko nyɛŋ naa etsɔ̃ɔ akɛ ja wɔnyɔŋmɔi lɛ; ni nyɔŋmɔi nɛɛ hu ashihilɛhe bɛ adesai ateŋ.”

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, awo akpɔ koni agbe nilelɔi lɛ. Atao Daniel kɛ enyɛmimɛi lɛ asɛɛgbɛ koni agbe amɛ hu. Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ Daniel maŋtsɛ lamɔ lɛ shishi

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Daniel kɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛ hiɛshikãmɔ bi maŋtsɛ blafoiatsɛ ni egbɛi ji Ariok, mɔ ni afã lɛ koni egbe Babilon nilelɔi lɛ akɛ,

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: “Mɛni eba hewɔ ni Maŋtsɛ ewo akpɔ ni naa wa nɛkɛ nɛɛ?” Ariok gba Daniel nɔ sane ni eba lɛ.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Daniel tee, ni eyakpa Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar fai akɛ eto lɛ be, ni ebatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ lamɔ ni ela lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Daniel returned home and told his three friends.
translation_verse: Daniel tee ewe lɛ, ni eyabɔ enanemɛi Hanania kɛ Mishael kɛ Azaria amaniɛ;

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: ni ebi amɛ akɛ amɛsɔle amɛkpa Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fai akɛ emusuŋ aaatsɔ̃ lɛ yɛ amɛhe; asaŋ amɛbi lɛ koni egbele teemɔŋ sane lɛ hiɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akagbe amɛ hu afata Babilonbii nilelɔi krokomɛi lɛ ahe.

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Ajie teemɔŋ sane lɛ shishi atsɔ̃ɔ Daniel yɛ ninaa mli nyɔɔŋ, ni Daniel jie Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yi.

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: Daniel wo enaa nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ajie Nyɔŋmɔ, mɔ dɛŋ ni nilee kɛ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ, yi kɛya naanɔi anaanɔ.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Lɛ etsakeɔ bei kɛ yinɔi lɛ; ekpaa maŋtsɛmɛi, ni etoɔ maŋtsɛmɛi. Lɛ eduroɔ jwɛŋmɔ, ni eduroɔ nilelɔi niiashishinumɔ;

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: Mitsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ, miida bo shi, ni miijie oyi, ejaakɛ oduro mi jwɛŋmɔ kɛ hewalɛ; ni otsɔ̃ɔ mi nii ni wɔkpa bo ehe fai lɛ, ejaakɛ oha wɔle maŋtsɛ sane lɛ.” Daniel tsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ lamɔ lɛ kɛ eshishi hu

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Daniel yiŋ etee Ariok, mɔ ni maŋtsɛ efã lɛ akɛ ekpãtã Babilon nilelɔi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kaakpãtã nilelɔi lɛ ahiɛ, shi moŋ okɛ mi aya maŋtsɛ ŋɔɔ, ni matsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ elamɔ lɛ shishi.”

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Ariok nyiɛ Daniel hiɛ kɛtee Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar hiɛ oya, ni Ariok kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ, miyana nuu ko yɛ Yudabii nomii lɛ ateŋ ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ̃ɔ Maŋtsɛ elamɔ lɛ shishi.”

english_verse: The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ bi Daniel ni atsɛɔ lɛ Belteshazar hu lɛ akɛ, “Ani ooonyɛ otsɔ̃ɔ mi lamɔ ni mila lɛ kɛ eshishi hu?”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Daniel here maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ akɛ, “Nii, klamɔfonyo ko klamɔfonyo ko loo ashwãifeelɔ loo ŋulamiiaŋkwɛlɔ ko bɛ ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ̃ɔ teemɔŋ sane ni Nii taoɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: “Be mli ni Maŋtsɛ kã shi ni ewɔɔ lɛ, ela nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ; ni Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni jieɔ teemɔŋ nibii akpo lɛ miihã ole nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Mi lɛ jeee minii ni mile fe adesai fɛɛ hewɔ ni ajie nɛkɛ teemɔŋ sane nɛɛ shi atsɔ̃ɔ mi; shi moŋ bɔ ni afee ni atsɔ̃ɔ Nii, oyitsoŋ saji lɛ kɛ lamɔ ni ola lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: “Nii, olamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ona amãgã kpeteŋkple ko; amãgã nɛɛ da, ni eekpɛ waa, ni ema ohiɛ, ni kɛji ookwɛ lɛ ehe yɛ gbeyei naakpa.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Amãgã nɛɛ yitso lɛ akɛ shika fee, etsitsi kɛ eniji lɛ akɛ jwiɛtɛi fee, emusu kɛ ehɛ lɛ akɛ akɔɔble fee;

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: eshuɔji lɛ akɛ dade fee, ni enaji lɛ fã dade kɛ fã hu su.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: Ohiɛ amãgã nɛɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ ni tɛ ko ni jeee gbɔmɔ adesa nine ta he tse kɛjɛ he ko ni ebatswa amãgã lɛ nane dade fã kɛ su fã lɛ nɔ, ni ejwra naji lɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amãgã lɛ he dade lɛ kɛ su lɛ kɛ akɔɔble lɛ kɛ jwiɛtɛi lɛ kɛ shika lɛ hu fɛɛ tswɛm jwara wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ, ni amɛfuflu, ni amɛtsɔ tamɔ abelenaashaji ni bua gbo abeleshaahe. Kɛkɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo fɛɛ kɛtee, ni eshwɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ ko nɔ ko. Shi tɛ lɛ ni batswa amãgã lɛ da, ni etsɔ̃ gɔŋ kpeteŋkple, ni ekpele jeŋ fɛɛ.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: “Lamɔ lɛ nɛ. Agbɛnɛ wɔɔtsɔ̃ɔ Nii lamɔ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ, bo ji maŋtsɛmɛi amaŋtsɛ. Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ni to bo nakai, ni eduro bo hewalɛ kɛ agbojee kɛ anunyam fɛɛ.

english_verse: over all humans, animals, and birds. You are the head of gold.
translation_verse: Ewo bo hei fɛɛ ni gbɔmɛi adesai kɛ kooloi kɛ loofɔji yɔɔ lɛ nɔyelɔ. Amãgã lɛ shika yitso lɛ bo ni.

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Bo osɛɛ lɛ maŋtsɛyeli kroko aaate shi ni kɛ bo yeee egbɔ; maŋtsɛyeli ko hu ni ji etɛ̃ baaba abaye nɔ. Ekadi ji akɔɔble lɛ; ni eeeye je lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni enine waobii lɛ fã ko dade ni fã ko hu su lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ fã ko he baawa, ni fã ko hu he waŋ.

english_verse: This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni ona dade ni efutu su ni akpɔtɔ mli lɛ, nakai maŋtsɛyeli nɛɛ mli nɔyelɔi lɛ awekui srɔtoi lɛ kɛ amɛhe baabote gbãlãshihilɛ mli moŋ nɛ; shi no tsaŋ amɛ tamɔ bɔ ni dade nyɛɛɛ ekɛ su atsa lɛ.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Bɔ ni ona tɛ ko ni jeee gbɔmɔ adesa nine ni kpɔ lɛ kɛjɛ gɔŋ ko he, ni ebafuflu amãgã ni akɛ dade kɛ akɔɔble kɛ su kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika fee lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ kpeteŋkple lɛ ejie nɔ ni baaba wɔsɛɛ ko lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ bo, Nii. Lamɔ ni migba Nii nɛɛ, eji anɔkwale; ni eshishi ni mitsɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu yɛ mli nyɔŋma shiishi.” Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar juro Daniel

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar kɛ ehiɛ bu shi, ni eja Daniel, ni efã akɛ ashã afɔle kɛ tsofakɛŋma ahã Daniel.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ Daniel akɛ, “Lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ ni fe nyɔŋmɔi fɛɛ kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ anuŋtsɔ lɛ; ni lɛ ejieɔ teemɔŋ saji akpo, ejaakɛ onyɛ ojie nɛkɛ teemɔ sane nɛɛ kpo.”

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar wo Daniel nɔ, ni ehã lɛ gbɛnaa grɔŋŋ, ni ekekee lɛ nibii wuji babaoo hu, ni efee lɛ Babilon kpokpai lɛ anɔkwɛlɔ, asaŋ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ he ŋaawolɔi lɛ fɛɛ anukpa yɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Daniel bi maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔ Shadrak kɛ Meshak kɛ Abednego eto Babilon kpokpai lɛ anɔ nitsumɔi lɛ anɔ; shi Daniel lɛ, lɛ lɛ ehi maŋtsɛwe lɛ.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: Amraloi lɛ kɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛ akutsei anɔkwɛlɔi lɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ajinafoi lɛ bua amɛhe naa koni amɛbakwɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi etɛ̃ nɛɛ. Amɛyiteŋ tsɔi ŋalako lɛ, amɛtadei lɛ he ko eshãko lɛ, lasu tete po ejeee fu yɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar fã akɛ atsu koni atsɛ maŋ nitsulɔi blublu kɛba: amraloi kɛ lumɛi kɛ amraloi asɛɛmɛi kɛ akutsei anɔkwɛlɔi, kɛ maŋtsɛ he ŋaawolɔi kɛ kojolɔi kɛ nitoohei anɔkwɛlɔi, kɛ kpokpai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ nitsulɔi koni amɛbaye amãgã lɛ naagbelemɔ kɛ ekpojiemɔ lɛ he odase.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: sɔ̃ɔlɔ ko bo waa ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Shikpɔji kɛ maji srɔtoi anɔ bii kɛ nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛwieɔ wiemɔi srɔtoi fɛɛ,

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar tsi bɛŋkɛ flɔnɔɔ kɛ emli la grigri lɛ naa. Kɛkɛ ni ewo enaa nɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Shadrak kɛ Meshak kɛ Abednego, Nyɔŋmɔ ŋwɛi flooflonyo lɛ tsuji, nyɛjea kpo yɛ la lɛ mli kɛbaa.” Kɛkɛ ni Shadrak kɛ Meshak kɛ Abednego je kpo yɛ la lɛ mli kɛba.

translation_verse: Nɔ ni gbee lɛ wie lɛ ba mli yɛ Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar nɔ amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ashwie lɛ kɛje gbɔmɛi ateŋ, ni ekpe jwɛi tamɔ tsina. Ŋwɛi bɔ nyɔ egbɔmɔtso nɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni eyi tsɔi tsa kusuu tamɔ okropɔŋ tsɛji, ni ewaobii anaa tsa oookɛɛ loofɔlɔ waobii anaa. Nebukadnezar kafo Nyɔŋmɔ

english_verse: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
translation_verse: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɔmɛi jeee fɛifɛi yɛ ehiɛ, ŋwɛi bɔfoi kɛ adesai fɛɛ yɛ eshishi. Mɔ ko nyɛŋ enine etswa efɔ̃, loo eeebi lɛ akɛ, ‘Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ?’

english_verse: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
translation_verse: “Be ni mihiɛ etserɛ mi sɛɛ lɛ, woo ni awoɔ mi kɛ migbojee kɛ mimaŋtsɛyeli lɛ he anunyam te shi ekoŋŋ. Misɔ̃ɔlɔi kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ tao misɛɛgbɛ, ni amɛhere mi atuu akɛ maŋtsɛ ekoŋŋ. Amɛkɛ maŋtsɛ hewalɛ lɛ wo midɛŋ ekoŋŋ, ni amɛbu mi akɛ lumɔ fe tsutsu lɛ po.

english_verse: That's why I say: “Praise and honor the King who rules from heaven! Everything he does is honest and fair, and he can shatter the power of those who are proud.”
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mi, Nebukadnezar, miijie Ŋwɛi Maŋtsɛ lɛ yi, ni miiwo lɛ, ni miiwo ehiɛ nyam. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efeɔ hi, ni eja hu, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni woɔ ehe nɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ ebaa mɔ lɛ shi.”

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Gbi ko lɛ Maŋtsɛ Belshazar tsɛ enukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi akpe okplɔ̃ kpeteŋkple ko, ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ nu dãa kutuu.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Be mli ni anuɔ dãa lɛ, Belshazar fã akɛ ayahole shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kpuji lɛ ni etsɛ Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar yaloo yɛ Yerusalɛm Sɔlemɔ we lɛ kɛba, koni lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛ enukpai lɛ kɛ eŋãmɛi lɛ kɛ ehemɛi lɛ kɛnu dãa.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛnuɔ dãa lɛ, amɛkafo nyɔŋmɔi ni akɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble kɛ dade kɛ tso kɛ tɛ efee lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛta niyeniiashi lɛ, trukaa lɛ gbɔmɔ nine je kpo, ni ebaŋma nii yɛ asa lɛ gbogbo lɛ he, he ni akɛ kaaloo esha lɛ, yɛ kanetso ni ma shi lɛ ŋlɛnɔ. Maŋtsɛ Belshazar miikwɛ nine lɛ be ni eŋmãa nii lɛ.

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ tsake amrɔ, ni etsui fã, ni eshe gbeyei bɔ sɔŋŋ ni etalɔiaŋ jɔ biɛɛ, ni enakutsei kpokpo.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ bo waa akɛ ayaŋɔ ashwãifeelɔi lɛ kɛ klalɔi lɛ kɛ ŋulamiiaŋkwɛlɔi lɛ abahã lɛ. Be ni Babilon nilelɔi nɛɛ ba lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Mɔ ni baanyɛ gbogbo nɛɛ he niŋmaa nɛɛ ekane, ni asaŋ etsɔ̃ɔ mi eshishi lɛ, abaawula lɛ kɛ lumɔ atade afaseo kɛ shika kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ kuɛnii. Ebaatsɔ̃ nɔyelɔ ni ji etɛ̃ yɛ mimaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli.”

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ nilelɔi lɛ fɛɛ ka niŋmaa lɛ kanemɔ kɛ eshishitsɔ̃ɔmɔ, shi amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kwraa nyɛɛɛ.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: Sane lɛ hao Maŋtsɛ Belshazar naakpa, ni ehã ehiɛ tsake. Ehe onukpai lɛ hu fee yaa.

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Wiemɔ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ enukpai lɛ wieɔ yɛ asa lɛ nɔ lɛ hã jɛi fee hoo. Enɛ hã maŋnyɛ lɛ ba okplɔŋmɛɛ asa lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋnyɛ lɛ wo enaa nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Nii, oyi ana wala kɛya naanɔ! Kaahao, ni kaahã nɔ ko miigba onaa.

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
