translation_verse: Nuu ko yɛ omaŋtsɛyeli nɛɛ mli ni nyɔŋmɔi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ amumɔ yɔɔ emli. Otsɛ yinɔ lɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ jie hiɛshikãmɔ kɛ nilee kɛ jwɛŋmɔ kpo tamɔ nyɔŋmɔi lɛ anilee yɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, otsɛ, Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar, wo lɛ woloŋlelɔi kɛ klamɔfoi kɛ ashwãifeelɔi kɛ ŋulamiiaŋkwɛlɔi fɛɛ anukpa.

english_verse: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
translation_verse: Enilee lɛ naa wa jogbaŋŋ. Ehiɛ kã shi, ni ele nii bɔ ni enyɛɔ lamɔi kɛ ajenui kɛ teemɔŋ saji fɛɛ ashishi etsɔ̃ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, hã ayaŋɔ nuu nɛɛ ni egbɛi ji Daniel, ni otsɛ wo lɛ Belteshazar lɛ, kɛba. Ebaanyɛ etsɔ̃ɔ bo niŋmaa lɛ shishi.” Daniel tsɔ̃ɔ Niŋmaa lɛ shishi

english_verse: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
translation_verse: Ayaŋɔ Daniel oya abahã maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani bo ji Daniel lɛ, Yudabii nomii ni mitsɛ yaŋɔ kɛjɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome lɛ?

english_verse: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
translation_verse: Minu ohe akɛ nyɔŋmɔi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ amumɔ ni yɔɔ omli lɛ naa wa naakpa; anaa akɛ ohiɛ kã shi, ni ole nii, ni oyɛ jwɛŋmɔ hu pam.

english_verse: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
translation_verse: Mikpee nilelɔi kɛ ashwãifeelɔi nɛɛ kɛba biɛ koni amɛbakane nɛkɛ niŋmaa nɛɛ ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔ mi eshishi; shi amɛnyɛɛɛ niŋmaa lɛ shishi amɛtsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
translation_verse: Minu ohe akɛ onyɛɔ onaa teemɔŋ nibii, ni otsɔ̃ɔ shishi. Kɛji ooonyɛ niŋmaa nɛɛ okane koni otsɔ̃ɔ mi eshishi lɛ, abaawula bo kɛ lumɔ atade afaseo kɛ shika kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ kuɛnii, ni obaatsɔ nɔyelɔ ni ji etɛ̃ yɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
translation_verse: Daniel here maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ ekɛɛ, “Nii, nikeenii lɛ ahi shi koni okɛhã mɔ kroko. Shi kɛ̃lɛ mibakane niŋmaa lɛ matsɔ̃ɔ Nii, koni matsɔ̃ɔ Nii eshishi hu.

english_verse: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ lɛ hã otsɛ Nebukadnezar tsɔ̃ maŋtsɛ wulu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ agbojee kɛ anunyam kpeteŋkple;

english_verse: God did such great things for him that people of all nations and races shook with fear. Your father had the power of life or death over everyone, and he could honor or ruin anyone he chose.
translation_verse: ni agbojee ni aduro lɛ naa hewɔ lɛ shikpɔji kɛ asafoi kɛ wiemɔi srɔtoi anɔ bii bluublu sheɔ lɛ gbeyei, ni mɛi ahe kpokpoɔ yɛ ehiɛ. Mɔ ni esumɔɔ akɛ egbe lɛ lɛ, egbeɔ lɛ, ni mɔ ni esumɔɔ akɛ ehi wala mli lɛ, ehãa ehiɔ wala mli. Mɔ ni esumɔɔ akɛ ewo enɔ lɛ, ewoɔ enɔ; ni mɔ hu ni esumɔɔ akɛ eba lɛ shi lɛ, ebaa lɛ shi.

english_verse: But when he became proud and stubborn, his glorious kingdom was taken from him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni ewo ehe nɔ, ni ekpliŋ etsui, ni etsɛ ehe lɛ, akpa lɛ yɛ emaŋtsɛ sɛ̃i lɛ nɔ, ni enunyam lɛ bɔ lɛ.

english_verse: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
translation_verse: Ashwie lɛ kɛje adesai ateŋ; ejwɛŋmɔ tsɔ̃ tamɔ kooloo jwɛŋmɔ, ni eyahi ŋaŋ tejii ateŋ, ni ekpe jwɛi tamɔ tsina. Ŋwɛi bɔ nyɔ egbɔmɔtso nɔ aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni eyoo akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ maŋtsɛyeli nɔ, ni mɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ, lɛ maŋtsɛ ewoɔ.

english_verse: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: “Bo Belshazar, Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar bi lɛ, ole sane nɛɛ fɛɛ, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ obaaa ohe shi;

english_verse: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
translation_verse: shi moŋ owo ohe nɔ yɛ Nuŋtsɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hiɛ. Otee oyaloo kpuji kɛ okpolui ni yɔɔ ewe lɛ kɛba, ni bo kɛ onukpai lɛ kɛ oŋamɛi lɛ kɛ ohemɛi lɛ kɛbanu dãa. Enɛ sɛɛ hu lɛ nyɛjie wɔji srɔtoi ni akɛ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble kɛ dade kɛ tso kɛ tɛ efee lɛ ayi, nibii ni amɛnãaa nii, ni amɛnuuu nii, ni amɛleee nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ yi. Shi Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni lɛ edɛŋ owala kɛ oyaakɛbaa fɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ojieee lɛ moŋ eyi.

english_verse: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
translation_verse: No hewɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ etsu nine nɛɛ, ni ebaŋma nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Belshazar fã amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ, akɛ awula Daniel kɛ lumɔ atade afaseo, kɛ shika kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ kuɛnii hu; asaŋ ashiɛ akɛ Daniel ji nɔyelɔ ni ji etɛ̃ yɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli.

english_verse: That same night, the king was killed.
translation_verse: Shi nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ agbe Babilon Maŋtsɛ Belshazar;

english_verse: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
translation_verse: Eto maŋ onukpai nɔkwɛlɔi wuji etɛ̃ hu koni amraloi lɛ abu amɛ amɛnitsumɔi lɛ ahe akɔntaa, bɔ ni afee ni maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ ko hiɛ akakpãtã. Onukpai etɛ̃ nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ji Daniel.

english_verse: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
translation_verse: Daniel mumɔ kɛ emɔdɛŋbɔɔ naa wa, ni ana akɛ ehe esa fe onukpai krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ to eyiŋ akɛ ebaaŋɔ Daniel eto emaŋtsɛyeli muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni onukpai nɔkwɛlɔi krokomɛi lɛ kɛ amraloi lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ amɛaana tɔ̃mɔ ko yɛ Daniel he lo, koni amɛkɛfolɔ enaa. Shi akɛni Daniel yeɔ anɔkwa hewɔ lɛ amɛnaaa sane ko loo tɔ̃mɔ ko yɛ ehe.

english_verse: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbɔmɛi nɛɛ kɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Wɔnaŋ sane ko sane ko wɔkɛshi nɛkɛ Daniel nɛɛ akɛ ja yɛ eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ jamɔ mla lɛ gbɛfaŋ kɛkɛ wɔɔna eko yɛ.”

english_verse: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, onukpai lɛ kɛ amraloi lɛ bua amɛhe naa kɛba maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Maŋtsɛ Dario yi ana wala kɛya naanɔ!

english_verse: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, Maŋtsɛ, ofainɛ ni owo akpɔ nɛɛ, ni aŋmã awo woloŋ, ni osɔo naa koni etsɔ̃ tamɔ Mediabii kɛ Persiabii amla ni atsakeee hiɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: So King Darius made the law and had it written down.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Dario hã aŋmã akpɔ lɛ awo woloŋ, ni esɔo naa.

english_verse: Daniel heard about the law, but when he returned home, he went upstairs and prayed in front of the window that faced Jerusalem. In the same way that he had always done, he knelt down in prayer three times a day, giving thanks to God.
translation_verse: Be ni Daniel na ele akɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ enine ewo akpɔ ni aŋmã lɛ shishi lɛ, eyiŋ etee ewe. Eŋwɛi pia lɛ he samfɛji lɛ kwɛɔ Yerusalɛm gbɛ kɛji agbele. Ekulaa shi esɔleɔ shii etɛ̃ daa gbi, ni edaa eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ shi. Gbi ko lɛ Daniel yasɔle nakai nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: The men who had spoken to the king watched Daniel and saw him praying to his God for help.
translation_verse: Daniel henyɛlɔi lɛ bua amɛhe naa kɛba, ni amɛbanina Daniel ni eesɔle eekpa eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ fai.

english_verse: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
translation_verse: Amɛhere nɔ, ni amɛkɛɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ akɛ, “Naa, Daniel, Yuda nomii lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome lɛ, ebuuu bo, Nii, kɛ akpɔ ni owo lɛ fɛɛ; ni no hewɔ lɛ, esɔleɔ shii etɛ̃ daa gbi.”

english_verse: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
translation_verse: Edɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ naakpa be ni enu sane nɛɛ, ni esusu he bɔ ni eeefee ehere Daniel yiwala. Esusu sane lɛ he aahu kɛyashi hulushinyɔɔ mli.

english_verse: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni gbɔmɛi lɛ bua amɛhe naa kɛbanina maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni amɛbakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nii, na ole akɛ yɛ Mediabii kɛ Persiabii amla naa lɛ akpɔ loo kitã ni maŋtsɛ ena ewo lɛ atsakeee.”

english_verse: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ fã, ni atee ayaŋɔ Daniel kɛba, ni ashɛ lɛ afɔ̃ jatai abu lɛ mli. Maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛɛ Daniel akɛ, “ONyɔŋmɔ lɛ ni osɔmɔɔ anɔkwale mli lɛ; lɛ eeejie bo.”

english_verse: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
translation_verse: Ayawo tɛ kɛba, ni akɛbatsi jatai abu lɛ naa. Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewolonaasɔomɔ ga lɛ sɔo tɛ lɛ naa; elumɛi lɛ hu sɔosɔoo bu lɛ naa kɛ amɛwolonaasɔomɔ gai lɛ koni akatsake yiŋ ni ato yɛ Daniel he lɛ.

english_verse: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ ku esɛɛ kɛtee emaŋtsɛ we lɛ mli. Ehi ŋmãa nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni ehãaa akɛ hiɛtserɛjiemɔ nɔ ko abɛŋkɛ lɛ. Wɔ tserɛ kwrakwra yɛ ehiŋmɛiaŋ.

english_verse: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
translation_verse: Be ni hiɛ bɔ̃i gbelemɔ lɛ, maŋtsɛ lɛ te shi mra, ni ehe fee oya kɛtee jatai abu lɛ naa.

english_verse: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
translation_verse: Be ni ebɛŋkɛ bu lɛ naa he ni Daniel yɔɔ lɛ, ewo egbee nɔ, ni ekɛ awerɛho gbee bo ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ao! Daniel, Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ tsulɔ, ani oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ni osɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ daa lɛ enyɛ ejie bo yɛ jatai lɛ adɛŋ lo?”

english_verse: Daniel answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Daniel here maŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ao! Nii, oyi ana wala kɛya naanɔ!

english_verse: My God knew that I was innocent, and he sent an angel to keep the lions from eating me. Your Majesty, I have never done anything to hurt you.”
translation_verse: MiNyɔŋmɔ lɛ etsu ebɔfo lɛ kɛba, ni ebaŋamɔ jatai lɛ anaabu, ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeko mi awui ko, ejaakɛ yɛ lɛ ehiɛ lɛ miyeɔ bem, ni bo Nii hu, mitɔ̃ko onɔ.”

english_verse: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ lɛ mii shɛ ehe naakpa, ni efã akɛ ajie Daniel yɛ bu lɛ mli. Ajie Daniel yɛ bu lɛ mli ni apilako ehe ko he ko, ejaakɛ ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ fã, ni ayamɔmɔ mɛi ni yafolɔ Daniel naa hã maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛba, ni ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie jatai abu lɛ mli, amɛ kɛ amɛbii kɛ amɛŋamɛi fɛɛ. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ shɛɛɛ bu lɛ shishi tete ni jatai lɛ mɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛjwara amɛwui amli.

english_verse: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Maŋtsɛ Dario ŋmã wolo ekɛmaje majimaji kɛ asafoi kɛ je lɛ mli wiemɔi srɔtoi ashikpɔji anɔ bii fɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhea omanye!

english_verse: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Miiwo kitã akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ minɔyeli nɛɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ehe akpokpo, ni eshe Daniel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ gbeyei.” “Lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ, mɔ ni yɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ lɛ; anyɛŋ emaŋtsɛyeli hiɛ akpãtã, ni ehewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ efoŋ.

english_verse: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
translation_verse: Jielɔ kɛ herelɔ ji lɛ; etoɔ okadii, ni efeɔ naakpɛɛ nii yɛ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehere Daniel yɛ jatai lɛ adɛŋ.”

english_verse: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
translation_verse: Daniel nɛɛ shwere yɛ Maŋtsɛ Dario yinɔ kɛ Maŋtsɛ Koresh, Persianyo lɛ, hu yinɔ.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
translation_verse: Daniel ŋma akɛ, “Mina yɛ mininaa lɛ mli akɛ nyɔɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ efã kɛjɛ jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ni ehã ŋshɔ fee hamahama.

english_verse: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni kooloi wuji ejwɛ ni soro amɛteŋ eko fɛɛ eko famɔ kpo kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ kooloo lɛ tamɔ jata, shi eyɛ fiji tamɔ okropɔŋ fiji. Mihiɛ kooloo nɛɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ ni akplɔ efiji lɛ yɛ ehe, ni awo enɔ, ni akɛ lɛ damɔ enaji enyɔ nɔ tamɔ gbɔmɔ damɔɔ shi. No sɛɛ lɛ, ahã lɛ gbɔmɔ jwɛŋmɔ.

english_verse: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
translation_verse: Kooloo ni ji enyɔ lɛ tamɔ oshishibrishi. Awo lɛ adamɔ efã kome nɔ; ŋmawutsei etɛ̃ kɔ̃ enaa yɛ enyanyɔji ateŋ. Kɛkɛ ni gbee ko kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Yaa nɔ ni oye loo babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ.”

english_verse: The third beast was like a leopard—except that it had four wings and four heads. It was given authority to rule.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ mihiɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ ni kooloo kroko ko hu fã kpo. Etamɔ kootsɛ; shi eyɛ fiji ejwɛ, ni etamɔ nɔ ko ni aŋɔ nɔyeli hewalɛ kpeteŋkple ahã lɛ.

english_verse: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
translation_verse: Mihiɛ kwɛmɔ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni kooloo ni ji ejwɛ lɛ fã kpo. Ehe yɛ gbeyei kɛ naakpɛɛ fɛɛ; eyɛ hewalɛ naakpa. Eyɛ dade nyanyɔji kpakpatakpakpataa, ni ekɛjwara eniyenii lɛ amli dukuduku ni eye; ni fufuji ni shwɛ lɛ ekɛ enaji naanaa nɔ. Esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni tsɔ̃ hiɛ ba lɛ ateŋ. Lɛ lɛ eyɛ aklontoi nyɔŋma.

english_verse: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Mihiɛ aklontoi lɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ lɛ naa aklonto hee bibioo ko ekwɛ̃ kɛje kpo yɛ amɛteŋ. Aklonto bibioo nɛɛ fãmɔ aklontoi memeji lɛ ateŋ etɛ̃ kɛ amɛshishi fɛɛ eshwie. Aklonto nɛɛ yɛ hiŋmɛii tamɔ gbɔmɔ hiŋmɛii ni eyɛ naabu, ni ekɛmiiwie shwãa wiemɔi agboiagboi. Mɔ ko ni yɛ kɛjɛ blema he ninaa

english_verse: Thrones were set up while I was watching, and the Eternal God took his place. His clothing and his hair were white as snow. His throne was a blazing fire with fiery wheels,
translation_verse: Mihiɛ ninaa lɛ kwɛmɔ aahu kɛyashi beyinɔ ni akɛ maŋtsɛ sɛii bamamɔ shi. Kɛkɛ ni mɔ ko ni onaa akɛ afɔ lɛ etsɛ naakpa baho eta shi. Etade yɛɔ futaa, ni eyiteŋ waŋ hu yɛɔ futaa. Emaŋtsɛ sɛi lɛ miitso kɛ la, ni sɛi lɛ naji ahe kokolonto lɛ hu miitso grigri.

english_verse: and flames were dashing out from all around him. Countless thousands were standing there to serve him. The time of judgment began, and the books were opened.
translation_verse: La miiho yɛ ehiɛ tamɔ faa hoɔ. Gbɔmɛi akpeiakpei akpei abɔ sɔ̃mɔɔ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ, ni mɛi huuhaa abɔ hu damɔ ehiɛ. Kɛkɛ ni kojolɔi lɛ batara shi, ni agbele woji lɛ anaa, ni abɔi kojomɔ.

english_verse: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: Mitee nɔ mikwɛ ninaa lɛ, yɛ wiemɔi agboiagboi ni minuɔ aklonto bibioo lɛ wieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Mihiɛ kwɛmɔ aahu kɛyashi mina akɛ agbe kooloo ni ji ejwɛ lɛ, ni afite egbɔmɔtso lɛ, ni ashɛ lɛ afɔ̃ la lɛ mli koni eshã.

english_verse: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
translation_verse: Kooloi krokomɛi lɛ ni shwɛ lɛ, ashɔ̃ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ; shi akɛ amɛhe ke amɛ kɛyashi be kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa pɔtɛ̃ɛ ko.

english_verse: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
translation_verse: Mina yɛ nyɔɔŋ ninaa lɛ mli nɔ ko ni tamɔ gbɔmɔ adesa. Ekpeleke shi kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni atatu ebɔle ehe kɛba mɔ ni Etsɛ Naakpa lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni ebadamɔ ehiɛ.

english_verse: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
translation_verse: Ahã lɛ nɔyeli kɛ anunyam kɛ maŋtsɛyeli hewalɛ koni majimaji kɛ asafoi srɔtoi kɛ wiemɔi srɔtoi ashikpɔji anɔ bii fɛɛ asɔ̃mɔ lɛ. Emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ naanɔ maŋtsɛyeli ni, ni esɛɛ efoŋ; ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛŋ hiɛ akpãtã. Ninai lɛ ashishitsɔ̃ɔmɔ

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was terrified by these visions, and I didn't know what to think.
translation_verse: Ninai lɛ wo mihe gbeyei, ni mimumɔ hao yɛ mi, Daniel, mimli.

english_verse: But God Most High will give his kingdom to his chosen ones, and it will be theirs forever and ever.”
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ bii hetselɔi lɛ anine baashɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ nɔ, ni eeehi amɛdɛŋ kɛya naanɔi anaanɔ.”

english_verse: I wanted to know more about the fourth beast, because it was so different and much more terrifying than the others. What was the meaning of its iron teeth and bronze claws and of its feet that smashed what the teeth and claws had not ground and crushed?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mitao akɛ male kooloo ni ji ejwɛ lɛ, nɔ ni esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ kooloi krokomɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ he sane. No he yɔɔ gbeyei naakpa kɛ enyanyɔji ni wa tamɔ dade kɛ ewaobii tamɔ akɔɔble ni ekɛjwara kooloi ni ena ebaaye lɛ amli dukuduku lɛ, ni fufuji ni shwɛ lɛ hu ekɛ enaji naanaa nɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
translation_verse: Mitao hu akɛ male aklontoi nyɔŋma ni mamɔ kooloo lɛ yitso he lɛ ahe sane. Mitao hu akɛ male aklonto kome lɛ nɔ ni fã kpo, ni be ni eje kpo lɛ efãmɔ aklontoi lɛ ateŋ etɛ̃ kɛ amɛshishifãi fɛɛ eshwie lɛ hu he sane. Lɛ eyɔɔ hiŋmɛii, ni eyɛ naabu, ni ekɛwieɔ wiemɔi agboiagboi tamɔ nɔ ni efe aklontoi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english_verse: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
translation_verse: Mihiɛ kwɛmɔ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni nɛkɛ aklonto nɛɛ fã ta ewo Nyɔŋmɔ webii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, ni eye amɛnɔ kunim,

english_verse: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
translation_verse: kɛyashi beyinɔ ni mɔ ni Etsɛ Naakpa lɛ ba, ni ebabu Ŋwɛi Flooflonyo lɛ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ bem. Kɛkɛ ni be bashɛ, ni aŋɔ nɔyeli hewalɛ awo mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ adɛŋ.

english_verse: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni kɛ mi wieɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Kooloo ni ji ejwɛ lɛ damɔ shi hã maŋtsɛyeli ni ji ejwɛ ko ni baaba abaye nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaasoro lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛyeli krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ ahe. Ebaafite shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni ebaanaanaa nɔ, ni ebaakpãtã hiɛ.

english_verse: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
translation_verse: Aklontoi nyɔŋma lɛ damɔ shi hã maŋtsɛmɛi nyɔŋma komɛi ni baate shi yɛ maŋtsɛyeli nɛɛ yinɔ. Amɛsɛɛ lɛ maŋtsɛ kome kroko hu ko baate shi. Ebasoro lɛ yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ni tsɔ̃ hiɛ lɛ ahe, ni ebaaba maŋtsɛmɛi etɛ̃ komɛi ãshi.

english_verse: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baawie eshi Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ, ni ebaahã etɔ Ŋwɛi Flooflonyo lɛ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eeeto eyiŋ po akɛ eeetsake Ŋwɛi Flooflonyo lɛ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ ajamɔ mlai lɛ kɛ gbii juji ni amɛyeɔ lɛ fɛɛ, ni ebaaye amɛnɔ kɛyashi afii etɛ̃ kɛ fã.

english_verse: But he will finally be judged, and his kingdom completely destroyed.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋwɛi kojolɔi aaatara shi akojo lɛ, ni abaashɔ̃ nɔyeli hewalɛ lɛ yɛ edɛŋ, ni aaakpãtã ehiɛ butubutu.

english_verse: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ lɛ abaatu shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ maŋtsɛyeli hewalɛ lɛ kɛ egbojee lɛ fɛɛ awo Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ adɛŋ. Amɛmaŋtsɛyeli hewalɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ efoŋ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lumɛi fɛɛ baasɔ̃mɔ amɛ, ni amɛbaabo amɛ toi.”

english_verse: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
translation_verse: Sane lɛ naagbee nɛ. Sane nɛɛ gba, mi Daniel, minaa naakpa, ni ehã migbɔmɔtso tsake; shi mikɛ sane lɛ to minakutsoŋ.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ Belshazar yinɔ afi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ajie ninaa ko ekoŋŋ atsɔ̃ɔ mi, Daniel, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ninaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
translation_verse: Be ni miwo mihiɛ nɔ lɛ, mina gwantɛŋ nuu agbo ko damɔ faa lɛ naa. Eyɛ aklontoi enyɔ; aklontoi nɛɛ kwɔlɔ naakpa, ni ekome kwɔ fe ekome; shi aklontoi lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni kwɔ lɛ no moŋ ji aklonto ni gwantɛŋ nuu lɛ je sɛɛkpee.

english_verse: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
translation_verse: Mina akɛ gwantɛŋ nuu nɛɛ miishi kɛmiiya anaigbɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ kɛ wuoyigbɛ. Kooloo ko kooloo ko kwraa nyɛɛɛ ehiɛ edamɔ; mɔ ko hu nyɛɛɛ nɔ ko ashɔ̃ yɛ edɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, efee nɔ ni lɛ esumɔɔ, ni efee ehe agbo.

english_verse: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
translation_verse: Miisusu ninaa nɛɛ he nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ lɛ naa too kpakpo ko epue kɛjɛ anaigbɛ kɛmiiba. Efo mli kɛ foi waa kɛtsɔ̃ shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni enane diɛŋtsɛ esaaa shikpɔŋ. Aklonto agbo kome ma too kpakpo nɛɛ hiŋmɛii ateŋ.

english_verse: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
translation_verse: Etsɛ̃ kɛbanina gwantɛŋ nuu ni yɔɔ aklontoi enyɔ lɛ ni mina akɛ edamɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ fɛɛ tua lɛ.

english_verse: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
translation_verse: Be ni too kpakpo lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ gwantɛŋ nuu lɛ, emli ewo lɛ la naakpa. Eshi gwantɛŋ nuu lɛ, ni ekumɔ eklontoi enyɔ lɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ. Gwantɛŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ too kpakpo lɛ hiɛ adamɔ. Too kpakpo lɛ tsi gwantɛŋ nuu lɛ etswa shi, ni enaanaa enɔ. Mɔ ko kwraa bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛaashɔ̃ gwantɛŋ nuu lɛ yɛ edɛŋ.

english_verse: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni too kpakpo nɛɛ bɔ̃i ehenɔwomɔ, ejaakɛ esusu akɛ eje agbo. Shi be ni ehe kɛɛ ewaa kwraa lɛ, aku eklonto agbo lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni aklontoi ejwɛ krokomɛi je kpo faŋŋ yɛ aklonto agbo kome lɛ najiaŋ ni amɛmiikwɛ jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
translation_verse: Aklonto bibioo kome ko kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ aklontoi ejwɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome mli. Aklonto nɛɛ bada kpeteŋkple, ni ekpã emli kɛtee wuoyigbɛ kɛ bokãgbɛ kɛ shiwoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: It humiliated heaven's army and dishonored its leader by keeping him from offering the daily sacrifices. In fact, it was so terrible that it even disgraced the temple and wiped out true worship. It also did everything else it wanted to do.
translation_verse: Aŋɔ asafo lɛ ahã lɛ kɛ daa gbi afɔle ni ashãa lɛ hu; ni enɛ lɛ eji tɔ̃mɔ; ashɛ anɔkwale afɔ̃; ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aklonto lɛ fee lɛ shwere.

english_verse: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni minu mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ko gbee miiwie, ni minu ni mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ kroko hu bi mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni wie lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ ninaa nɛɛ baakã he kɛyashi? Mɛɛ be mlatɔ̃mɔ nɛɛ baatsĩ daa gbi afɔleshãa krɔŋŋ lɛ naa kɛyashi? Ni mɛɛ be nɔŋŋ abaanaanaa ŋwɛi asafo lɛ nɔ, ni abaabule He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛyashi.”

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
translation_verse: Be ni mi, Daniel, mina nɛkɛ ninaa nɛɛ, ni miitao eshishi male lɛ, mina mɔ ko tamɔ gbɔmɔ badamɔ mihiɛ.

english_verse: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni minu gbɔmɔ gbee bo kɛjɛ Ulai Faa lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Gabriel ei! Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ mɔnɛ ninaa lɛ shishi.”

english_verse: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
translation_verse: Gabriel tsi eba he ni midamɔ lɛ; shi gbeyei mɔ mi, ni mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi. Kɛkɛ ni Gabriel kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Ao! Gbɔmɔ Adesa bi, na ole akɛ je lɛ naagbee he ninaa nɛ.”

english_verse: While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet
translation_verse: Ekɛ mi hiɛ wiemɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni wɔ ni tsii banyɔ minɔ. Shi Gabriel ta mihe, ni ewo minɔ edamɔ shi,

english_verse: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Naa, mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni baaba yɛ mlifu lɛ naagbee gbii lɛ amli. Je lɛ naagbee be ni ato lɛ he ninaa nɛ.

english_verse: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
translation_verse: “Gwantɛŋ nuu agbo ni ona kɛ eklontoi enyɔ lɛ damɔ shi hã Media kɛ Persia maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ.

english_verse: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
translation_verse: Hela maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he okadi ji too kpakpo lɛ; ni aklonto wulu kome lɛ ni ma ehiŋmɛii ateŋ lɛ ji eklɛŋklɛŋ maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
translation_verse: Bɔ ni aklonto kome nɛɛ kũ, ni aklontoi ejwɛ baye enajiaŋ lɛ, nakai Hela maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli baagbala ejwɛ; shi amɛteŋ eko eko hewalɛ shɛŋ klɛŋklɛŋ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english_verse: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
translation_verse: “Kɛji maŋtsɛyelii ejwɛ nɛɛ anaagbee be lɛ bɛŋkɛ, ni yiwalɛ saji ni amɛyeyee hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ agbala amɛtoi lɛ, maŋtsɛ hiɛwalɔ ko ni le ŋaa fɔŋ baate shi.

english_verse: He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well.
translation_verse: Ebaana hewalɛ kpele; shi ehewalɛ lɛ jɛŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli. Ebaakpãtã nibii ahiɛ butuu, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eeefee lɛ, ebaaye omanye yɛ mli. Ebaakpãtã hewalɔi kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ webii lɛ tete ahiɛ.

english_verse: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
translation_verse: Eŋaalee lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɛtsɔ̃ enɔ lɛ lakamɔ baafa pii, ni ebaawo ehe nɔ. Ebaakpãtã mɛi babaoo ahiɛ, be mli ni amɛleee amɛhe be. Ebaate shi ewo jeŋ fɛɛ Lumɔi alumɔ lɛ; shi abaakpãtã ehiɛ, be mli ni adesa nine etako ehe tete.

english_verse: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
translation_verse: Naa, daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ afɔle ni ashãa lɛ he ninaa ni agbala mli atsɔ̃ɔ bo lɛ, anɔkwale ni. Shi bo lɛ okɛto onakutsoŋ, ejaakɛ be kplaŋŋ baaho aya dani sane nɛɛ baaba mli.”

english_verse: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
translation_verse: Sane nɛɛ hã, mi Daniel, mifee vii; ni mihe ye be saŋŋ; kɛkɛ ni mite shi, ni mitee miyatsa nitsumɔ ni maŋtsɛ kɛwo midɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Mihe jɔ̃ mihe yɛ ninaa nɛɛ hewɔ; ni minuuu shishi.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
translation_verse: Eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli, be ni, mi Daniel, mihiɛ woji amli kwɛmɔ lɛ, mina akɛ afii abɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Gbalɔ Yeremia akɛ Yerusalɛm baakã shi amaŋfɔ̃ kɛyashi lɛ ji afii nyɔŋmai kpawo.

english_verse: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.
translation_verse: Mikpa Yehowa miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ fai, ni mijaje tɔ̃mɔi mikɛɛ, “Ao! Nuŋtsɔ, bo ji Nyɔŋmɔ kpeteŋkple ni he yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ ekpãŋmɔ nɔ, mɔ ni suɔmɔ sɛɛ efooo hã mɛi ni sumɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ ekitãi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But we have sinned terribly by rebelling against you and rejecting your laws and teachings.
translation_verse: “Wɔfee esha, ni wɔtɔ̃; wɔfee yitsoŋwalɛ nibii, ni wɔtse ohiɛ atua, ni wɔyeee okitãi kɛ omlai lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: We have ignored the message your servants the prophets spoke to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and everyone else.
translation_verse: Wɔboko otsuji gbalɔi lɛ ni kɛ wɔmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ wɔlumɛi lɛ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ wɔjaku muu lɛ fɛɛ wie yɛ ogbɛi mli lɛ toi.

english_verse: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
translation_verse: Nuŋtsɔ, wɔNyɔŋmɔ, musuŋtsɔlɔ ji bo, ni okɛ esha faa tsɛbelɛ wɔtse ohiɛ atua,

english_verse: and rejected your teachings that came to us from your servants the prophets.
translation_verse: ni wɔbooo bo Nuŋtsɔ, wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, owiemɔ toi, ni wɔhiii shi bɔ ni otsɔ̃ otsuji gbalɔi lɛ anɔ owo wɔ mla akɛ wɔhi shi lɛ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel has stubbornly refused to obey your laws, and so those curses written by your servant Moses have fallen upon us.
translation_verse: Israel tso muu fɛɛ etɔ̃ omla lɛ, ni amɛyeee omla lɛ nɔ; no hewɔ lɛ, amɛgba afã. Enɛ ehã amɛloo musu ni aŋmã yɛ Mose, otsulɔ lɛ, Mla Wolo lɛ mli lɛ, ejaakɛ wɔfee esha wɔshi bo.

english_verse: You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened.
translation_verse: Ekɛ amanehulu kpeteŋkple ni eba wɔnɔ nɛɛ lɛ ema wiemɔ ni ewie eshi wɔ lɛ nɔ mi. Ogbalako maŋ ko toi nɛkɛ pɛŋ dã, yɛ je nɛɛ mli fɛɛ, tamɔ ogbala Yerusalɛm toi nɛɛ.

english_verse: We have not escaped any of the terrible curses written by Moses, and yet we have refused to beg you for mercy and to remind ourselves of how faithful you have always been.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ efɔŋ nɛɛ eba wɔnɔ tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma yɛ Mose Mla lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ̃lɛ wɔkpako bo Yehowa fai, ni wɔkpaleko kɛjeko wɔnifɔ̃ɔjianii lɛ ahe, ni wɔboko anɔkwale wiemɔ lɛ toi.

english_verse: And when you finally punished us with this horrible disaster, that was also the right thing to do, because we deserved it so much.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Yehowa, wɔNyɔŋmɔ, enɛ hewɔ ni ohã efɔŋ nɛɛ eba wɔnɔ nɛɛ, ejaakɛ bo lɛ jalɔ ji bo yɛ nii fɛɛ ni ofeɔ gbɛfaŋ; shi wɔ lɛ wɔbooo bo toi.

english_verse: Our Lord God, with your own mighty arm you rescued us from Egypt and made yourself famous to this very day, but we have sinned terribly.
translation_verse: “Ao! Nuŋtsɔ, wɔNyɔŋmɔ ni okɛ nineshiwalɛ jie wɔ, omaŋ lɛ, kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni okɛna gbɛi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ, wɔfee esha, ni wɔwa yi.

english_verse: In the past, you treated us with such kindness, that we now beg you to stop being so terribly angry with Jerusalem. After all, it is your chosen city built on your holy mountain, even though it has suffered public disgrace because of our sins and those of our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ao! Nuŋtsɔ, yɛ ojalɛ saneyeli hewɔ lɛ, ofainɛ, foo omli ni efu Yerusalɛm kɛ omli ni ewo lɛ la lɛ sɛɛ. Bo diɛŋtsɛ omaŋ kɛ gɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni. Eshai ni wɔfee kɛ eshai hu ni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ hewɔ lɛ, omaŋ Yerusalɛm kɛ omaŋbii lɛ ahiɛ eshwie shi yɛ majimaji ni bɔle wɔ lɛ ahiɛ.

english_verse: I am your servant, Lord God, and I beg you to answer my prayers and bring honor to yourself by having pity on your temple that lies in ruins.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, wɔNyɔŋmɔ, bo otsulɔ sɔlemɔ kɛ faikpamɔ nɛɛ pɛ toi. Nuŋtsɔ, ohiɛ aba nyam ekoŋŋ yɛ ogbɛi lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: Forgive us! Hurry and do something, not only for your city and your chosen people, but to bring honor to yourself. The Seventy Weeks Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Ao! Yehowa, bo wɔ toi koni ofee he eko ohã wɔ. Ao! MiNyɔŋmɔ, ofainɛ, kaatsɛ kwraa ni ofee he eko ohã wɔ yɛ ogbɛi lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ ogbɛi kpɛtɛ omaŋ lɛ kɛ omaŋbii lɛ ahe.” Gabriel tsɔ̃ɔ gbalɛ lɛ shishi

english_verse: I was still confessing my sins and those of all Israel to the Lord my God, and I was praying for the good of his holy mountain,
translation_verse: Be ni misɔleɔ, ni mijajeɔ mihe eshai lɛ kɛ mimaŋbii, Israelbii lɛ, hu ahe eshai lɛ, ni mikpaa Yehowa, miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, fai yɛ gɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ hewɔ lɛ,

english_verse: when Gabriel suddenly came flying in at the time of the evening sacrifice. This was the same Gabriel I had seen in my vision,
translation_verse: mihiɛ mli miisɔle lolo kɛkɛ lɛ naa bɔfo Gabriel, mɔ ni mina yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ninaa lɛ mli lɛ ni efiliki kɛba mimasɛi trukaa. No mli lɛ eshɛ be mli ni ashãa gbɛkɛnaashi afɔle lɛ.

english_verse: and he explained: Daniel, I am here to help you understand the vision.
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Daniel, miba koni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo gbalɛ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: God thinks highly of you, and at the very moment you started praying, I was sent to give you the answer.
translation_verse: Be ni oje shishi ni obɔi Nyɔŋmɔ faikpamɔ lɛ, afã mi, ni no hewɔ miba koni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo shishi nɛɛ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ sumɔɔ bo naakpa. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛŋmɔ wiemɔ lɛ he koni onu ninaa lɛ shishi.

english_verse: For one week this foreigner will make a firm agreement with many people, and halfway through this week, he will end all sacrifices and offerings. Then the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction will be put there. And it will stay there until the time God has decided to destroy this one who destroys.
translation_verse: Lumɔ nɛɛ kɛ mɛi babaoo baakpãŋ kɛyashi afii kpawo; shi afii etɛ̃ kɛ fã sɛɛ lɛ, lumɔ nɛɛ baagu shãa afɔle kɛ niyenii afɔle shãa kwraa. Abaafee amãgã ni buleɔ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ama he ni yɔɔ grɔŋŋ fe fɛɛ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ mli; ni amãgã nɛɛ baama jɛi kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ eto kɛbaagbala mɔ ni kɛ amãgã lɛ bama jɛi lɛ toi aaashɛ.”

english_verse: In the third year of Cyrus the king of Persia, a message came to Daniel from God, and it was explained in a vision. The message was about a dreadful war, and it was true.
translation_verse: Persia Maŋtsɛ Koresh yinɔ afi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ, ajie ninaa kpo atsɔ̃ɔ Daniel mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Belteshazar hu lɛ. Sane lɛ yɛ mli anɔkwa, ni ekɔɔ haomɔ kpeteŋkple ko he. Atsɔ̃ɔ Daniel, ni enu sane lɛ shishi.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: For three weeks I was in sorrow.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, mi Daniel, mina otsii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ ni miiye ŋkɔmɔ.

english_verse: I ate no fancy food or meat, I drank no wine, and I put no olive oil on my face or hair.
translation_verse: Miyeee niyenii ni ŋɔɔ, miyeee loo lɛ, minuuu wain, ni mikpaaa mu hu kɛyashi otsii etɛ̃ lɛ fɛɛ shɛ.

english_verse: Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ ejwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, midamɔ faa wulu ni gbɛi ji Tigris lɛ naa.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw someone dressed in linen and wearing a solid gold belt.
translation_verse: Miwo mihiɛ nɔ, ni mina nuu ko ni ewo klala atade, ni Ufaz shika kpãa fi emliteŋ.

english_verse: His body was like a precious stone, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming fires, his arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice like the roar of a crowd.
translation_verse: Egbɔmɔtso miikpɛlɛ oookɛɛ ojarawatɛ, ni ehiɛ miikpɛlɛ nyramnyram tamɔ srawa; ehiŋmɛii tamɔ kɔtii ni asu. Eniji kɛ enaji ahe miikpɛlɛ tamɔ akɔɔble ni asha he; ni egbee jije tamɔ asafo yuu gbee.

english_verse: Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid.
translation_verse: Mi Daniel, mi koome mina ninaa lɛ. Hii ni fata mihe yɛ jɛi lɛ enaaa ninaa nɛɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ ŋmiŋmi ni naa wa mɔmɔ amɛ, kɛkɛ ni amɛjojoo foi, ni amɛyateetee amɛhe.

english_verse: and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni minu nuu lɛ gbee ni eewie. Be ni minu ewiemɔ lɛ, ni migbee shi, ni mikɛ mihiɛ bu shi, ni nɔ nyɔ minɔ.

english_verse: and then said, “Daniel, your God thinks highly of you, and he has sent me. So stand up and pay close attention.” I stood trembling, while the angel said:
translation_verse: Bɔfo lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Daniel, Nyɔŋmɔ miisumɔ bo naakpa. Tee shi ni odamɔ shi, koni obo wiemɔi ni mikɛ bo baawie lɛ toi, ejaakɛ atsu mi oŋɔɔ.” Be ni bɔfo lɛ kɛ mi ewie nɛkɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mite shi midamɔ shi kɛ hekpokpomɔ.

english_verse: Daniel, don't be afraid! God has listened to your prayers since the first day you humbly asked for understanding, and he has sent me here.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Daniel, kaashe gbeyei! Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ enu sɔlemɔi ni osɔle kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi nɔ ni okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaaba ohe shi ohã Nyɔŋmɔ. Anu osɔlemɔ lɛ, ni no hewɔ miba nɛɛ.

english_verse: I will tell you what is written in The Book of Truth. But first, you must realize that no one except Michael, the guardian angel of Israel, is on my side.
translation_verse: Shi mibagba bo nɔ ni aŋmã yɛ Anɔkwale Ŋmalɛi lɛ amli lɛ. No ji akɛ mɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni waa mi ni mikɛ mɛnɛɛmɛi wuɔ akɛ ja Mikael, nyɛ Israel lumɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Now I have come here to give you another vision about what will happen to your people in the future.
translation_verse: ni miba koni mibatsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ni baaba omaŋbii lɛ anɔ wɔsɛɛ, ejaakɛ nɔ ni baaba wɔsɛɛ shɔŋŋ he ninaa ona lɛ.”

english_verse: While this angel was speaking to me, I stared at the ground, speechless.
translation_verse: Be ni bɔfo lɛ kɛ mi ewie nɛkɛ egbe naa lɛ, mima mihiɛ shi, ni mitɔ mu.

english_verse: Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni bɔfo lɛ ni esu tamɔ gbɔmɔ adesa lɛ kɛ enine sa minaabu he. Kɛkɛ ni mibɔi wiemɔ, ni mikɛɛ bɔfo ni damɔ mihiɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ninaa lɛ eha mihewojiaŋ fɛɛ miiwa mihe, ni mifee gbedee.

english_verse: I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
translation_verse: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi, minuŋtsɔ tsulɔ, kɛ minuŋtsɔ aaawie hu? Ejaakɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni jio, mumɔŋ nɔ jio, eko fɛɛ eko etã yɛ mimli.”

english_verse: The angel touched me a second time and said, “Don't be frightened! God thinks highly of you, and he intends this for your good, so be brave and strong.” At this, I regained my strength and replied, “Please speak! You have already made me feel much better.”
translation_verse: Ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Ao! Gbɔmɔ ni Naa Nyɔŋmɔ sumɔɔ bo pam, kaashe gbeyei; otsui anyɔ omli, ni ofee ekãa.” Be ni ekɛ mi wie nɛkɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mina ekãa, ni mikɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, wiemɔ, ejaakɛ owo mi hewalɛ.”

english_verse: Then the angel said: Now do you understand why I have come? Soon I must leave to fight against the guardian angel of Persia. Then after I have defeated him, the guardian angel of Greece will attack me.
translation_verse: Bɔfo lɛ to he ni ekɛɛ, “Ole nɔ hewɔ ni miba oŋɔɔ nɛɛ lo? Miiku misɛɛ koni mikɛ bɔfo ni buɔ Persia maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he lɛ ayawu. Kɛji miye enɔ kunim sɛɛ lɛ, Hela maŋtsɛyeli bɔfo lɛ hu baaba koni ekɛ mi abawu.

english_verse: You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king. The Angel's Message to Daniel Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ Dario, Medianyo lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, mi hu midamɔ shi, ni mifi Mikael sɛɛ kɛwo lɛ hewalɛ.

english_verse: What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
translation_verse: Nɔ ni magba bo agbɛnɛ nɛɛ lɛ anɔkwale ni.” Ijipt Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ kɛ Siria Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ Kɛkɛ ni bɔfo lɛ tee nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, maŋtsɛmɛi etɛ̃ krokomɛi baaba abaye Persia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Maŋtsɛ mɔ ni baanyiɛ amɛsɛɛ akɛ maŋtsɛ ni ji ejwɛ lɛ, ebaana nii fe mɛi krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ. Ni kɛji etsɔ̃ enii ni ena lɛ nɔ ena hewalɛ lɛ, ebaawo majimaji ayiŋ, ni abaate shi awo Hela maŋtsɛyeli lɛ.

english_verse: Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases.
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ kãkãlɔ ko baate shi nɛkɛ be mli, ni emaŋtsɛyelihe lɛ baada kpeteŋkple, ni ebaaye etsuinaa sane.

english_verse: But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
translation_verse: Shi be mli ni egbojee lɛ ehe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ ni emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ baagbee shi. Emli baagbala srɔtoi ejwɛ kɛya jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ. Mligbalamɔi nɛɛ anɔyeli baaya ayaje mɛi ni amɛjeee maŋtsɛ nɛɛ shwiei adɛŋ; shi moŋ nɔyelɔi hei nɛɛ ahewalɛ kɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ hewalɛ yeŋ hegbɔ; ni abaashɔ̃ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ mɛi nɛɛ adɛŋ ahã mɛi krokomɛi.

english_verse: The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom.
translation_verse: “Wuoyigbɛ, ni ji Ijipt, maŋtsɛ lɛ he baawa, shi eshishi lumɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome ko baana hewalɛ fe lɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ, ni naagbee mli lɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ baatsɔ̃ shikpɔŋ kpeteŋkple nɔyelɔ.

english_verse: Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed. After this,
translation_verse: Shi afii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ maŋtsɛ, ni ji Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ, baakpãŋ amɛfee ekome, ni Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ ebiyoo baahã Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ gbãlã yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ namɔ hewɔ. Shi ekomefeemɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ etsɛŋ, ni abaamɔ maŋtsɛ biyoo lɛ kɛ etsuji kɛ ebi lɛ kɛ ewu lɛ fɛɛ ni abaagbe amɛ.

english_verse: one of her relatives will become the ruler of the southern kingdom. He will attack the army of the northern kingdom and capture its fortresses.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be mli nɔŋŋ lɛ, maŋtsɛ biyoo lɛ wekunyo ko baate shi, ni ebaaye maŋtsɛ. Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ baafã ta kɛbatua Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ etabilɔi lɛ kɛyabote maŋtsɛ lɛ mɔɔ wulu lɛ mli, ni ebaaye amɛnɔ kunim.

english_verse: Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later
translation_verse: Ebaaloo Siriabii anyɔŋmɔi lɛ kɛ dade amãgãi lɛ kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika nibii ni jara wa lɛ fɛɛ kɛya Ijipt. Ijipt maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baahi shi afii komɛi ni efãaa ta ewooo Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_verse: the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
translation_verse: Shi Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ moŋ ni baafã ta be ko kɛbatua Ijipt; shi abaashwie lɛ, ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛaatee eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom.
translation_verse: “Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ bihii baabua tabilɔi babaoo anaa amɛkɛsaa amɛhe amɛhã ta. Ta ku lɛ eko baafã, ni ebaakpãtã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ egbɛ nɔ hiɛ, tamɔ faa ni eyi kɛteke nɔ. Abaawu ta lɛ aahu kɛyanina Ijipt maŋtsɛ mɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north.
translation_verse: Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ mlila baafã kɛbanina Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ lɛ baawu, ni ebaaye enɔ. Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ ta kpele baaya ta lɛ, shi abaaye enɔ kunim.

english_verse: The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long,
translation_verse: Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ nine baatsɔ̃ Siria tabilɔi akpei nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ anɔ. No baahã maŋtsɛ lɛ awo ehe nɔ akɛ ekpãtã tabilɔi babaoo ahiɛ; shi ekunimyeli nɛɛ sɛɛ etsɛŋ.

english_verse: because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baaya esɛɛ eyabua tabilɔi babaoo fe tsutsubii lɛ anaa, ni afii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ ebaaku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ kɛ ta kpele kɛ tawuu nibii.

english_verse: At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ mɛi babaoo baate shi ashi Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ. Bo diɛŋtsɛ omaŋbii lɛ ateŋ kakawuai komɛi hu aaate shi awo Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ koni ninaa nɛɛ aba mli; shi amɛyeŋ kunim.

english_verse: Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat.
translation_verse: Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baafã ta kɛba, ni ebaaba ebasa maŋ ni atswa gbogbo awo ehe yi. Ebaaye maŋ nɛɛ nɔ kunim, ni ebaaŋɔ maŋ lɛ. Ijipt tabilɔi lɛ nyɛŋ ehiɛ adamɔ. Etabilɔi kakabãŋi lɛ tete naŋ hewalɛ amɛkɛdamɔ shi amɛkɛ lɛ awu.

english_verse: The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land.
translation_verse: Siria maŋtsɛ ni batua shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee Ijipt tabilɔi lɛ bɔ ni lɛ esumɔɔ, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛŋ shi ate awo lɛ. Ebaaba ebahi shiwoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baahi lɛ ehewalɛ shishi.

english_verse: In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
translation_verse: Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baato eyiŋ akɛ ekɛ emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli tabilɔi bluublu baaba abatua Ijipt. Shi ebaatsɔ̃ ŋaa, ni ekɛ Ijipt baakpãŋ, ni ebaaŋɔ ebiyoo ehã Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ gbãlã koni ekɛgbɔjɔ Ijipt maŋtsɛyeli lɛ; shi moŋ eyiŋtoo nɛɛ yeŋ omanye.

english_verse: Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride.
translation_verse: Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baatsɔ̃ ehiɛ ewo ŋshɔnaa shikpɔji lɛ. Ebaaye shikpɔji nɛɛ babaoo anɔ kunim. Shi tatsɛ ko hu baate shi awo lɛ, ni ebaaye enɔ kunim, ni ebaafo Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ henɔwomɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baahã Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ henɔwomɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ hiɛgbele ahã lɛ.

english_verse: He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
translation_verse: Siria maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baaku esɛɛ eyatua mɔji ni yɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; shi abaaye enɔ kunim yɛ jɛi, ni biɛ enaagbee baaba yɛ.

english_verse: The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger. Part Two: The Evil King from the North
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ ko baaba yɛ esɛɛ. Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baawo etsulɔ gbɛ akɛ eyanyɛ maŋbii lɛ anɔ koni etsu amɛ onia pii ewo maŋtsɛ fotro lɛ mli. Shi be kukuoo ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni abaagbe lɛ, jeee yɛ mlifu naa loo ta mli.” Siria Maŋtsɛ fɔŋ lɛ

english_verse: The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery.
translation_verse: Bɔfo lɛ tee ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Mɔ ni baanyiɛ sɛɛ ebaye Siria maŋtsɛ agbɛnɛ lɛ ji gbɔmɔ gbonyo ko ni bɛ hegbɛ akɛ eyeɔ maŋtsɛ; shi be ni aaahɛle shi lɛ etsɔ̃ juukɛfɔ̃ kɛ naadɔkɔmɔ nɔ enine eshɛ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then he will destroy armies and remove God's chosen high priest.
translation_verse: Tabilɔi fɛɛ ni aaate shi awo lɛ lɛ, ebaabɛɛ amɛ eshwie. Nakai nɔŋŋ ebaafee kpãŋmɔ lɛ lumɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_verse: He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers.
translation_verse: Ekɛ majimaji baakpãŋ, shi eyeŋ anɔkwa. Ebaana hewalɛ kpele, tsɛbelɛ emaŋbii ayi faaa.

english_verse: Without warning, he will successfully invade a wealthy province, which is something his ancestors never did. Then he will divide among his followers all of its treasures and property. But none of this will last very long.
translation_verse: Ebaafã ta trukaa kɛya shikpɔŋ ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni ebaaya eyafee nii ni etsɛmɛi kɛ eniimɛi tete efeko eko dã yɛ jɛi. Nii ni ebaaha yɛ jɛi lɛ, ebaajara ehã tabilɔi ni nyiɛ esɛɛ lɛ. Kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ ebaato eyiŋ akɛ ebaafãfãa tai kɛyatua maji tamɔ mɔji; shi eyeŋ omanye.

english_verse: He will gather a large and powerful army, and with great courage he will attack the king of the south. The king of the south will meet him with a much stronger army, but he will lose the battle, because he will be betrayed
translation_verse: “Hewalɛ kɛ ekãa ni yɔɔ emli lɛ baakãnya lɛ koni ebua ta kpele naa koni ekɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ ayawu. Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ hu kɛ ta kpele baaba ekɛ lɛ abawu; shi Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ yeŋ kunim, ejaakɛ abaato eshigbeemɔ he ŋai srɔtoi ashi lɛ.

english_verse: by members of the royal court. He will be ruined, and most of his army will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Mɛi po ni naa edɛŋ niyenii jurɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tete baagbee lɛ shi eko. Etabilɔi lɛ babaoo baanyɔnyɔɔ, ni abaabɛɛ eta lɛ ashwie.

english_verse: The two kings will meet around a table and tell evil lies to each other. But their plans will fail, because God has already decided what will happen.
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛmɛi enyɔ nɛɛ baatara shi yɛ okplɔ̃ kome he amɛye nii, shi amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ yiŋsha yɛ enyɛmi he; ni amɛaalaka amɛhe yɛ niyenii lɛ shishi tete. Amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko yiŋtoo lɛ baŋ mli haŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ be ni ato lɛ shɛko.

english_verse: Then the king of the north will return to his country with great treasures. But on the way, he will attack the religion of God's people and do whatever else he pleases.
translation_verse: Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ nii babaoo ni ena, yɛ taitai ni ewu lɛ amli, lɛ baaku esɛɛ ekɛya eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; shi etsui baasu jamɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaafee nɔ ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esumɔɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ kɛtee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ nɔ.

english_verse: At the time God has decided, the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom again, but this time, things will be different.
translation_verse: “Kɛji be ni ato lɛ shɛ lɛ, ebaaba ebatua Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ; shi nibii ejaŋ haŋ lɛ tamɔ tsuutsu lɛ,

english_verse: Ships from the west will come to attack him, and he will be discouraged. Then he will start back to his own country and take out his anger on the religion of God's faithful people, while showing kindness to those who are unfaithful.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ Romabii kɛ lɛji baaba abatua lɛ, ni ebaashe gbeyei. Ebaagbala ehe shi, ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛ mlila, ni ebaaya ni eyaka akɛ eeefite jamɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Ebaabo mɛi ni ekwa jamɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ moŋ aŋaawoo toi.

english_verse: He will send troops to pollute the temple and the fortress, and he will stop the daily sacrifices. Then he will set up that “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction.
translation_verse: Ebaawo etabilɔi lɛ ekomɛi agbɛ koni amɛyabule Sɔlemɔ we Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ mɔɔ lɛ hu. Amɛbaagu daa gbi afɔlei ni ashãa lɛ, ni amɛkɛ amãgã ni buleɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ baama jɛi.

english_verse: The king will use deceit to win followers from those who are unfaithful to God, but those who remain faithful will do everything possible to oppose him.
translation_verse: Ekɛ naadɔkɔmɔ baalaka mɛi ni ekwa jamɔ lɛ; shi mɛi ni miiye amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ anɔkwa lolo lɛ baadamɔ shi kpɛŋŋ amɛshi lɛ.

english_verse: Wise leaders will instruct many of the people. But for a while, some of these leaders will either be killed with swords or burned alive, or else robbed of their possessions and thrown into prison.
translation_verse: Maŋbii lɛ ateŋ nilelɔi lɛ ekomɛi baatsɔ̃ɔ maŋbii lɛ nii, tsɛbelɛ amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi baanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa, abaashãshãa mɛi komɛi, abaaha amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi anii, ni abaaŋɔ mɛi komɛi nom kɛyashi be ko.

english_verse: They will receive only a little help in their time of trouble, and many of their followers will be treacherous.
translation_verse: Be mli nɔŋŋ ni agbeɔ Nyɔŋmɔ webii lɛ, abaaye abua amɛ fioo ko kɛ̃, ni mɛi pii baaba abafata amɛhe, shi jeee kɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ.

english_verse: Some of those who are wise will suffer, so that God will make them pure and acceptable until the end, which will still come at the time he has decided.
translation_verse: Abaagbe maŋbii lɛ ateŋ nilelɔi lɛ ekomɛi; shi akɛ amɛgbele lɛ baatsuu Nyɔŋmɔ webii lɛ ahe koni amɛyɛ futafuta. Nii nɛɛ baaya nɔ kɛyashi naagbee be lɛ baashɛ, ni ji be ni Nyɔŋmɔ eto lɛ.

english_verse: This king will do as he pleases. He will proudly claim to be greater than any god and will insult the only true God. Indeed, he will be successful until God is no longer angry with his people.
translation_verse: “Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni lɛ etsui taoɔ, ni ebaawo ehe nɔ. Ebaatsɛ ehe agbo fe nyɔŋmɔ fɛɛ nyɔŋmɔ, ni eeewie hepupuumɔ wiemɔ tete eshi nyɔŋmɔi aNyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ. Ebaaya nɔ nɛkɛ aahu kɛyaashi Nyɔŋmɔ emiŋ ŋɔɔ dɔŋŋ, ni agbɛnɛ Nyɔŋmɔ baagbala etoi. Nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ eto akɛ ebaafee lɛ lɛ, ebaana efee lɛ.

english_verse: This king will reject the gods his ancestors worshiped and the god preferred by women. In fact, he will put himself above all gods
translation_verse: Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ ebuŋ nyɔŋmɔ ni etsɛmɛi lɛ ja lɛ tete loo nyɔŋmɔ ni yei sumɔɔ lɛ hu. Ebuŋ nyɔŋmɔ ko nyɔŋmɔ ko, ejaakɛ ebaawo ehe nɔ yɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: and worship only the so-called god of fortresses, who was unknown to his ancestors. And he will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other costly gifts.
translation_verse: Shi moŋ ebaabu nyɔŋmɔ ni buɔ maji ahe. Ebaahiɛ edɛŋ shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ tɛi ni jara wa kɛ nikeenii ni jara wa ekɛyahã nyɔŋmɔ ko ni etsɛmɛi lɛ tete leee koni ekɛwo nakai nyɔŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ nyam.

english_verse: With the help of this foreign god, he will capture the strongest fortresses. Everyone who worships this god will be put in a position of power and rewarded with wealth and land. Part Three: The Time of the End
translation_verse: Nakai ebaafee yɛ mɔji ni wala lɛ amli ehã maŋsɛɛ nyɔŋmɔ ko ni eeekpɛlɛ̃ ehewalɛ nɔ. Mɛi fɛɛ ni buɔ lɛ akɛ amɛnɔyelɔ lɛ, ebaawo amɛhiɛ nyam, ni eeehã amɛye mɛi pii anɔ; ebaajara shikpɔji lɛ amli ehã amɛ akɛ amɛnyɔmɔwoo.

english_verse: At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack the kingdom of the north. But its king will rush out like a storm with war chariots, cavalry, and many ships. Indeed, his forces will flood one country after another,
translation_verse: “Kɛji Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ naagbee be lɛ shɛ lɛ, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ baaya eyatua lɛ. Siria maŋtsɛ lɛ baafã tamɔ ahum ekɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ abakpe kɛ tayaa shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔtalɔi kɛ lɛji babaoo. Ebaatua shikpɔji babaoo, ni ebaatsɔ̃ amɛnɔ kɛho tamɔ faa ni eje ŋa.

english_verse: and when they reach the holy land, tens of thousands will be killed. But the countries of Edom and Moab and the ruler of Ammon will escape.
translation_verse: Ebaatua Shiwoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ tete, ni mɛi akpei nyɔŋmai abɔ baanyɔnyɔɔ; shi hei ni baaje edɛŋ nɛ: Edom kɛ Moab kɛ Amonbii ashikpɔŋ lɛ kpotoo.

english_verse: The king of the north will invade many countries, including Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɛji efã ta nɛɛ ewo nakai shikpɔji lɛ, Ijipt diɛŋtsɛ po yeŋ ehe.

english_verse: and he will take its rich treasures of gold and silver. He will also conquer Libya and Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Ebaaloo Ijipt shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ ejwetri fɛɛ kɛya. Ebaaye Libia kɛ Etiopia hu fɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But he will be alarmed by news from the east and the north, and he will become furious and cause great destruction.
translation_verse: Shi saji ni baajɛ bokãgbɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ aba lɛ baawo ehe gbeyei; ni ekɛ mlila kpele baaya eyakpãtã gbɔmɛi babaoo ahiɛ butuu.

english_verse: After this, he will set up camp between the Mediterranean Sea and Mount Zion. Then he will be destroyed, and no one will be able to save him.
translation_verse: Ebaamamɔ abladei abui ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ kɛ Gɔŋ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ teŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; shi moŋ jɛi enaagbee baaba yɛ, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yeŋ ebuaŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Many of those who lie dead in the ground will rise from death. Some of them will be given eternal life, and others will receive nothing but eternal shame and disgrace.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi ni egboi lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii ahiɛ aaatsɛ̃; mɛi komɛi aaatee naanɔ wala mli; shi mɛi komɛi hu aaatee naanɔ hiɛgbele mli.

english_verse: Everyone who has been wise will shine as bright as the sky above, and everyone who has led others to please God will shine forever like the stars.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi ni le nii lɛ aaakpɛ tamɔ atatu kpɛmɔ, ni mɛi ni etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi pii agbɛ kɛtee jalɛ mli lɛ aaakpɛ tamɔ ŋulamii kɛaatee naanɔ.”

english_verse: Daniel, I now command you to keep the message of this book secret until the end of time, even though many people will go everywhere, searching for the knowledge to be found in it. The End of Time
translation_verse: Shi ekɛɛ mi akɛ, “Bo, Daniel, tsiimɔ wiemɔi nɛɛ anɔ, ni osɔo wolo nɛɛ naa kɛyashi naagbee be lɛ. Ni mɛi pii aaagba amɛhe naa kɛya kɛba kɛtao nɔ ni eba lɛ shishi; ni nilee aaafa.”

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I looked around and saw two other people—one on this side of the river and one on the other side.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni mi, Daniel, mikwɛ ni naa, mɛi krokomɛi enyɔ damɔ shi, mɔ kome yɛ faa lɛ naa biɛ nɛɛ, ni mɔ kome hu yɛ faa lɛ sɛɛ.

english_verse: The angel who had spoken to me was dressed in linen and was standing upstream from them. So one of the two beside the river asked him, “How long before these amazing things happen?”
translation_verse: Ni mɔ kome kɛɛ nuu lɛ ni wo klala ni yɛɔ, mɔ ni yɔɔ faa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ beyinɔ aaagbe nɛkɛ naakpɛɛnii nɛɛ anaa?”

english_verse: The angel then raised both hands toward heaven and said, “In the name of the God who lives forever, I solemnly promise that it will be a time, two times, and half a time. Everything will be over, when the suffering of God's holy people comes to an end.”
translation_verse: Ni nuu ni wo klala ni yɔɔ faa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ wo eninejurɔ kɛ ebɛku nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi, ni ekã mɔ ni hiɛ kã kɛyaa naanɔ lɛ kitã. Minu ni ekɛɛ, “Ebaakã he kɛyashi afii etɛ̃ kɛ fã, beyinɔ ni aaakumɔ hewalɛ ni waa mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ ayi lɛ agbe naa; kɛkɛ lɛ aaagbe enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ naa.”

english_verse: I heard what the angel said, but I didn't understand. So I asked, “Sir, how will it all end?” The angel in my vision then replied:
translation_verse: Minu nɔ ni bɔfo lɛ wie lɛ, shi minuuu shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, mibi akɛ, “Minuŋtsɔ, ofainɛ, te enɛɛmɛi anaagbee lɛ aaatamɔ tɛŋŋ?”

english_verse: Daniel, go about your business, because the meaning of this message will remain secret until the end of time.
translation_verse: Eto he ekɛɛ akɛ, “Daniel, kwɛmɔ ohiɛgbɛ ni oya! Wiemɔi lɛ atsimɔ nɔ, ni asɔo amɛnaa kɛyaashi naagbee be lɛ aaaba.

english_verse: Many people will have their hearts and lives made pure and clean, but those who are evil will keep on being evil and never understand. Only the wise will understand.
translation_verse: Mɛi pii baatsuu amɛhe koni amɛyɛ futafuta ni amɛhe atse. Shi yitsoŋwalɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko nuŋ shishi, ni amɛaaya nɔ amɛye yitsoŋwalɛ sane; shi nilelɔi lɛ, amɛ lɛ, amɛbaanu nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ shishi.

english_verse: So, Daniel, be faithful until the end! You will rest, and at the end of time, you will rise from death to receive your reward.
translation_verse: “Ni bo Daniel, ye anɔkwa kɛyashi naagbee; ni no sɛɛ lɛ obaagbo; shi ooote shi, ni ooona aekoo ni sa bo yɛ naagbee gbi lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me. Hosea's Family
translation_verse: Yehowa wiemɔ ni ekɛ Hosea, ni ji Beeri bi lɛ, wie yɛ Yuda maŋtsɛmɛi Uzia kɛ Yotam kɛ Ahaz kɛ Hezekia ayinɔ lɛ nɛ. No mli lɛ Yeroboam, Yoash bi lɛ, miiye maŋtsɛ yɛ Israel. Hosea ŋa kɛ ebii

english_verse: So I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and we had a son.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Hosea tee ni eyaŋɔ Diblaim biyoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ Gomer lɛ. Gomer na musu ni efɔ binuu.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Hosea, name your son Jezreel, because I will soon punish the descendants of King Jehu of Israel for the murders he committed in Jezreel Valley. I will destroy his kingdom,
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ Hosea akɛ, “Wo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ, ‘Yezreel’, ejaakɛ eshwɛ fioo kɛkɛ ni lá shi ni Yehu shwie yɛ Yezreel maŋ lɛ mli lɛ mibatɔ he owele yɛ eshwiei anɔ, ni mibagu Yehu we lɛ maŋtsɛyeli yɛ Israel.

english_verse: and in Jezreel Valley I will break the power of Israel.”
translation_verse: Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ mibafite Israel tawuu hewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ Yezreel jɔɔ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Later, Gomer had a daughter, and the Lord said, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, because I will no longer have mercy and forgive Israel.
translation_verse: Gomer na musu ekoŋŋ, ni efɔ biyoo. Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Hosea akɛ, “Wo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ, Lo-Ruhama: ‘Mɔbɔnalɛ etã’, ejaakɛ mikaŋ he mihaŋ mimusuŋ atsɔ̃ mi yɛ Israelbii ahe, ni mikɛfaŋ amɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
translation_verse: Shi mimusuŋ aaatsɔ̃ mi yɛ Yuda he, ni mi Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mibahere amɛyiwala; shi moŋ mitsɔ̃ŋ gãi loo klante loo ta loo okpɔŋɔi loo tayaa okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi anɔ mihereŋ amɛyiwala.”

english_verse: After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son.
translation_verse: Be ni Gomer etse ebi Lo-Ruhama fufɔ lɛ, esaa ena musu, ni efɔ binuu ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.” Hope for Israel
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Hosea akɛ, “Wo abifao lɛ gbɛi akɛ, Lo-Ammi ‘Nyɛjeee mimaŋ,’ ejaakɛ Israelbii jeee mimaŋ dɔŋŋ, ni mi hu jeee amɛNyɔŋmɔ ji mi.” Abaatee Israel shi ekoŋŋ

english_verse: Someday it will be impossible to count the people of Israel, because there will be as many of them as there are grains of sand along the seashore. They are now called “Not My People,” but in the future they will be called “Children of the Living God.”
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ Israelbii ayikulɛ aaatamɔ ŋshɔnaa shia ni anyɛŋ asusu aloo akane. Kɛji nakai be lɛ shɛ lɛ, he ni akɛɛ amɛ yɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛjeee mimaŋ lɛ,’ jɛi nɔŋŋ abaakɛɛ amɛ yɛ akɛ, “Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ bii ji nyɛ.”

english_verse: Israel and Judah will unite and choose one leader. Then they will take back their land, and this will be a great day for Jezreel.
translation_verse: No mli Yudabii kɛ Israelbii anaa aaabakpe shi kɛfee ekome, ni amɛaato mɔ koome akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛnyiɛlɔ, ni amɛaashwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ejaakɛ Yezreel gbi lɛ gbi wulu ni.

english_verse: So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.” The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkɛa nyɛnyɛmimɛi hii, Israelbii, lɛ akɛ Ammi, “Mimaŋ ji amɛ” kɛ nyɛmimɛi yei lɛ hu akɛ Ruhama, “Mimusuŋ etsɔ̃ mi yɛ amɛhe.” Gomer yeee anɔkwa lɛ, Israel hu yeee anɔkwa

english_verse: Accuse! Accuse your mother! She is no longer my wife, and now I, the Lord, am not her husband. Beg her to give up prostitution and stop being unfaithful,
translation_verse: “Mibii, nyɛkɛ nyɛnyɛ awiea, ejaakɛ jeee miŋa ji lɛ dɔŋŋ; ni mi hu jeee ewu ji mi. Nyɛkɛ lɛ awiea koni ekpa ejwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ, ni efo egblãfitemɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english_verse: or I will strip her naked like the day she was born. I will make her barren like a desert, and she will die of thirst.
translation_verse: Kɛjeee nakai lɛ maŋmɛ lɛ yayai tamɔ gbi ni afɔ lɛ lɛ; mahã etsɔ̃ tamɔ ŋa nɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi, ni mikɛ kumai baagbe lɛ.

english_verse: You children are the result of her unfaithfulness, and I'll show you no pity.
translation_verse: Asaŋ minaŋ emusuŋbii lɛ hu amɔbɔ, ejaakɛ yoo ajwamãŋ bii ji amɛ.

english_verse: Your mother was unfaithful. She was disgraceful and said, “I'll run after my lovers. Everything comes from them— my food and drink, my linen and wool, my olive oil and wine.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛnyɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ; efee hiɛgbejianii kɛna amɛ musu. Ekɛɛ ehe akɛ, ‘Hã maya mayatiu mishieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ; amɛ amɛhãa mi niyenii kɛ nu kɛ mikuntu kɛ klala lɛ kɛ mimu kɛ dãa.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, will build a fence of thorns to block her path.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ mikɛ ŋmei baafo ehe afabaŋ, ni matswa gbogbo kɛsa eyi koni matsi lɛ gbɛ.

english_verse: She will run after her lovers, but not catch them; she will search, but not find them. Then she will say, “I'll return to my first husband. Life was better then.”
translation_verse: Eeetiu eshieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ asɛɛ nɛ, shi eninaŋ amɛ; ni eeetao amɛ, shi enaŋ amɛ. Kɛ̃lɛ lɛ eeekɛɛ ehe akɛ, ‘Hã makpale kɛya miklɛŋklɛŋ wu lɛ ŋɔɔ; ejaakɛ be ni mikɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ehi hã mi moŋ fe amrɔ nɛɛ.’

english_verse: She didn't know that her grain, wine, and olive oil were gifts from me, as were the gold and silver she used in worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Te eŋɔɔɔ nɔ akɛ mi ji mɔ ni hã lɛ abele kɛ wain kɛ mu kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛjaa jemawɔŋ Baal lɛ.

english_verse: So I'll hold back the harvest of grain and grapes. I'll take back my wool and my linen that cover her body.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, mashɔ̃ mibele lɛ kɛ wain lɛ hu kɛ kuŋtu kɛ klala ni enaa ebuɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Then I'll strip her naked in the sight of her lovers. No one can rescue her.
translation_verse: Maŋmɛ lɛ yayai agbɛnɛ matsɔ̃ɔ eshieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ; ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛŋ lɛ ahere yɛ midɛŋ.

english_verse: I'll stop Israel's celebrations— no more New Moon Festivals, Sabbaths, or other feasts.
translation_verse: Mafo mliflimɔ gbii juji ni eyeɔ lɛ fɛɛ asɛɛ, nyɔji hei kɛ afi gbii juji lɛ, kɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ.

english_verse: She said, “My lovers gave me vineyards and fig trees as payment for sex.” Now I, the Lord, will ruin her vineyards and fig trees; they will become clumps of weeds eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ni maŋala ewaintsei lɛ kɛ agbãmi tsei lɛ ni ekɛɔ akɛ nomɛi ji nɔ ni enaa yɛ eshieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ adɛŋ akɛ enyɔmɔwo lɛ. Mahã fɛɛ atsɔ̃ koo koni ŋaŋ kooloi aye amɛnɔ nii.

english_verse: I'll punish her for the days she worshiped Baal and burned incense to him. I'll punish her for the times she forgot about me and wore jewelry and rings to attract her lovers. I, the Lord, have spoken! The Lord Will Help Israel
translation_verse: Magbala etoi yɛ tsofakɛŋma ni etee eyashã ehã Baal jemawɔji yɛ amɛgbii juji lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ewula kɛ jwinei kɛtee eyanyiɛ eshieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ asɛɛ, ni ehiɛ kpa minɔ.” Nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ. Suɔmɔ ni Yehowa yɔɔ hã ewebii

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord, will lure you into the desert and speak gently to you.
translation_verse: “No hewɔ lɛ, mibagbe eyitso ni mi kɛ lɛ aaatee ŋa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ; mi kɛ lɛ aaayawie naajɔlɛ wiemɔ yɛ jɛi koni eyiŋ atsɔ̃ kɛba shĩa.

english_verse: I will return your vineyards, and then Trouble Valley will become Hopeful Valley. You will say “Yes” to me as you did in your youth, when leaving Egypt.
translation_verse: Makpale ewain tromi lɛ mahã lɛ, ni mahã Amanehulu Jɔɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ Hiɛnɔkãmɔ Agbo ahã lɛ. Eeehere mi nɔ tamɔ efee yɛ eblayeiaŋ lɛ be ni ejɛ Ijipt eba lɛ.

english_verse: I promise from that day on, you will call me your husband instead of your master.
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ ebaatsɛ mi ‘Miwu’ ekoŋŋ, shi jeee ‘MiBaal’ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: I will no longer even let you mention the names of those pagan gods that you called “Master.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mibakɔ jemawɔji Baali lɛ agbɛii yɛ edaaŋ; ni etsiŋ amɛtã tete po dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: And I will agree to let you live in peace—you will no longer be attacked by wild animals and birds or by weapons of war.
translation_verse: “Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, mikɛ ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ loofɔji kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wamɔɔ fɛɛ aaakpãŋ yɛ nyɛhewɔ koni amɛkaye nyɛ awui; ni makumɔ gãi kɛ klante amli, ni mahã tawuu sɛɛ afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni nyɛbaahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english_verse: I will accept you as my wife forever, and instead of a bride price I will give you justice, fairness, love, kindness,
translation_verse: “Israel, mibatsɛ ohe baa akɛ miŋa kɛaatee naanɔ; Maye bo anɔkwa, ni maye bo jalɛ sane, Masumɔ bo, ni mimusuŋ aaatsɔ̃ mi yɛ ohe.

english_verse: and faithfulness. Then you will truly know who I am.
translation_verse: Maye mishiwoo nɔ, ni mafee bo miŋa, ni ooole akɛ mi ji Yehowa.

english_verse: I will command the sky to send rain on the earth,
translation_verse: Nakai be lɛ mahã mimɛi, Israelbii, asɔlemɔ lɛ hetoo.

english_verse: and it will produce grain, grapes, and olives in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Mahã nu anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aba abele kɛ wain kɛ mu ahã Israel.

english_verse: I will scatter the seeds and show mercy to Lo-Ruhamah. I will say to Lo-Ammi, “You are my people,” and they will answer, “You are our God.”
translation_verse: Mahã mimɛi lɛ ahe shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mahã amɛshwere. Mɛi ni atsɛ amɛ akɛ ‘Mɔbɔnalɛ etã’ lɛ, kɛ mɛi hu ni atsɛ amɛ akɛ ‘Nyɛjeee mimɛi’ lɛ, mibana amɛ fɛɛ mɔbɔ. Ni makɛɛ amɛ akɛ, ‘Mimɛi ji nyɛ,’ ni amɛaahere nɔ akɛ ‘bo ji wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Yaa ekoŋŋ ni oyasumɔ yoo ni ewu sumɔɔ lɛ, shi lɛ lɛ ekɛ nuu kroko miifite gbãlã. Osumɔ lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni mi, Yehowa, misumɔɔ mimɛi Israelbii lɛ; tsɛbelɛ amɛ lɛ, amɛkwa mi, ni amɛtee wɔji aŋɔɔ, ni amɛkɛ wain yibii yashãa afɔle amɛhãa amãgãi.”

english_verse: Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
translation_verse: ni mikɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ hii shi kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ ohã mi; okabɔ ajwamãŋ, ni okayagbã nuu ko; ni mi hu mahi shi mahã bo.”

english_verse: It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nakai pɛ Israel baahi shi gbii pii ni amɛbɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ, amɛbɛ lumɛi hu; asaŋ amɛshãaa afɔle; ni amɛbɛ shiu lɛ amɛbɛ efod kɛ terafim hu ni akɛbiɔ nii.

english_verse: But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
translation_verse: Kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ Israelbii baaku amɛsɛɛ, amɛaakpale, ni amɛaabatao Yehowa, amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ, amɛaabatao amɛmaŋtsɛ ni ji David shwie ko hu sɛɛgbɛ. Nakai be lɛ amɛkɛ gbeyeishemɔ aaaba Yehowa ŋɔɔ, ni eeejɔɔ amɛ kɛ nibii kpakpai yɛ naagbee bei lɛ amli.

english_verse: Israel, listen as the Lord accuses everyone in the land! No one is faithful or loyal or truly cares about God.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Israelbii, nyɛboa nɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ toi, ejaakɛ Yehowa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ ena. “Anɔkwayeli kɛ mɔbɔnalɛ etã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni aleee Nyɔŋmɔ hu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: And so your land is a desert. Every living creature is dying— people and wild animals, birds and fish. The Lord Warns the Priests
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi, ni enɔ nibii fɛɛ baagboi. Ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ loofɔji kɛ nuŋ loi tete baagboi.” Yehowa kɛ sane shi Osɔfoi lɛ

english_verse: Don't accuse just anyone! Not everyone is at fault. My case is against you, the priests.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Mɔ ko akashwa mɔ ko, ni mɔ ko akakã mɔ ko hiɛ hu, ejaakɛ nyɛ, Osɔfoi lɛ, nyɛ moŋ ji mɛi ni mikɛyɔɔ sane.

english_verse: You and the prophets will stumble day and night; I'll silence your mothers.
translation_verse: Nyɛ lɛ, nyɛaatɔ̃ shwane, ni gbalɔi lɛ hu kɛ nyɛ baatɔ̃ nyɔɔŋ; no hewɔ lɛ, mibakpãtã Israel, nyɛnyɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: You priests have rejected me, and my people are destroyed by refusing to obey. Now I'll reject you and forget your children, because you have forgotten my Law.
translation_verse: Mimaŋ lɛ hiɛ ekpãtã ejaakɛ amɛleee nii. Akɛni okwa nilee hewɔ lɛ, mi hu miikwa bo akɛ misɔfo; ni akɛni ohiɛ ekpa oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ mla lɛ nɔ hewɔ lɛ, mi hu mihiɛ miikpa obii lɛ anɔ.

english_verse: By adding more of you priests, you multiply the number of people who sin. Now I'll change your pride into shame.
translation_verse: “Bɔ ni amɛ, osɔfoi lɛ, ayi faa lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ amɛfeɔ esha babaoo amɛshiɔ mi; ni no hewɔ lɛ, mibahã amɛhiɛ nyam lɛ atsɔ̃ hiɛgbele.

english_verse: You encourage others to sin, so you can stuff yourselves on their sin offerings.
translation_verse: Amɛtsɔ̃ esha ni mimɛi lɛ feɔ lɛ nɔ amɛna nii, ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛshweɔ akɛ mɛi aya nɔ afee esha.

english_verse: That's why I will punish the people for their deeds, just as I will punish you priests.
translation_verse: Magbala osɔfoi lɛ atoi tamɔ maŋbii lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ amɛjeŋba hewɔ; mawo amɛnishaianii ni amɛfee lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english_verse: Their food won't satisfy, and having sex at pagan shrines won't produce children. My people have rebelled
translation_verse: Amɛbaaye nii nɛ, shi amɛtɔrɔŋ, ni amɛaabɔ ajwamãŋ nɛ, shi amɛshwereŋ kɛ bii, ejaakɛ amɛkwa mi, Yehowa, ni amɛtee wɔji moŋ aŋɔɔ.” Yehowa wie eshi wɔŋjamɔ

english_verse: and have been unfaithful to me, their Lord. God Condemns Israel's Idolatry My people, you are foolish because of too much pleasure and too much wine.
translation_verse: Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Wain momo kɛ wain hee fɛɛ hãa nilee ŋmɛɔ mɔ.

english_verse: You expect wooden idols and other objects of wood to give you advice. Lusting for sex at pagan shrines has made you unfaithful to me, your God.
translation_verse: Mimɛi biɔ tso akɛ egba, ni amɛdɛ̃hiɛmɔtso lɛ gbaa amɛ teemɔŋ saji, ejaakɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ mumɔ ehã amɛkwa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ; ni amɛdu gbɛ, amɛtee wɔji aŋɔɔ.

english_verse: You offer sacrifices on mountaintops and hills, under oak trees, and wherever good shade is found. Your own daughters and daughters-in-law sell themselves for sex.
translation_verse: Amɛshã afɔlei yɛ gɔji lɛ ayiteiaŋ, ni amɛshã tsofakɛŋma yɛ gɔ̃ŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ; amɛshã yɛ odum kɛ onyai kɛ papao tsei ashishi, ejaakɛ tsei lɛ ahɔ̃ɔŋ lɛ mli hi. “Enɛ hewɔ ni nyɛbiyei lɛ bɔɔ ajwamãŋ, ni nyɛbihii aŋamɛi lɛ fiteɔ gbãlã lɛ.

english_verse: But I won't punish them. You men are to blame, because you go to prostitutes and offer sacrifices with them at pagan shrines. Your own foolishness will lead to your ruin.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji nyɛbiyei lɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ lɛ migbalaŋ amɛtoi, ni kɛji nyɛbihii aŋamɛi lɛ hu fite gbãlã lɛ migbalaŋ amɛtoi, ejaakɛ nyɛ, hii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tete lɛ nyɛ kɛ ajwamãŋi ni yɔɔ jamɔhe lɛ yabɔɔ ajwamãŋ, ni nyɛ kɛ amɛ fɛɛ shãa wɔŋjamɔ afɔlei lɛ. Naa, maŋ ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ ehiɛ kpãtãa.

english_verse: Israel, you are unfaithful, but don't lead Judah to sin. Stop worshiping at Gilgal or at sinful Bethel. And quit making promises in my name—the name of the living Lord.
translation_verse: “Kɛji nyɛ, Israelbii, yeee mi anɔkwa yɛ mi jamɔ mli lɛ, nakai su lɛ akabala Yuda hu. Nyɛkayaa Gilgal, ni nyɛkayaa Bet-Aven hu nyɛyajaa; ni nyɛkɛ Yehowa gbɛi lɛ akakãa kitã akɛ ‘Gbii abɔ ni Yehowa ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ nɛɛ!’

english_verse: You are nothing more than a stubborn cow— so stubborn that I, the Lord, cannot feed you like lambs in an open pasture.
translation_verse: Israelbii akuɛŋ ti tamɔ tsina oblayoo. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni Yehowa aaalɛ amɛ tamɔ alɛɔ toobii yɛ ŋa shwaŋŋ nɔ hu?

english_verse: You people of Israel are charmed by idols. Leave those people alone!
translation_verse: Israel ekɔ wɔŋjamɔ efɔ enɔ; nyɛŋmɛa ejeŋ he nyɛhãa lɛ.

english_verse: You get drunk, then sleep with prostitutes; you would rather be vulgar than lead a decent life.
translation_verse: Kɛji amɛnunuu dãi ni amɛtɔrɔ sɛɛ lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ amɛkɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ etsa nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ hiɛgbele moŋ fe hiɛnyam.

english_verse: And so you will be swept away in a whirlwind for sacrificing to idols.
