english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Ni eŋɔ amɛ nakai nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ mli nɔŋŋ, ni efɔ amɛkpãi lɛ anaa ehã amɛ, ni abaptisi lɛ kɛ ewe lɛ mli bii fɛɛ amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ;

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: ni ekɛ amɛ tee ewe lɛ, ni eyaŋmɛ amɛ okplɔ̃, ni emli fili lɛ kɛ ewe lɛ fɛɛ akɛ ehe Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ eye.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Be ni je tsɛre lɛ, asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ tsu asraafoi bakɛɛ, “Ŋmɛɛmɔ gbɔmɛi lɛ ahe ni amɛya.”

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Ni gboklɛfoiakwɛlɔ lɛ jaje nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ etsɔ̃ɔ Paulo akɛ, “Asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ etsu kɛba akɛ aŋmɛɛ nyɛhe, no hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛjea kpo, ni nyɛyabaa jogbaŋŋ.”

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Shi Paulo kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Wɔ ni Romabii ji wɔ ni abuko wɔ fɔ lɛ, amɛyi wɔ yɛ jara nɔ, ni amɛwo wɔ tsuŋ hu; ni kpaako amɛshwieɔ wɔ nigii lo? Dabida, shi moŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛba ni amɛbajie wɔ.”

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Ni asraafoi lɛ yajaje nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ; ni be ni amɛnu akɛ Romabii ji amɛ lɛ, amɛshe gbeyei.

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ni amɛba amɛbakpa amɛ fai, ni be ni amɛ jie amɛ lɛ, amɛtutɔ amɛ akɛ amɛje maŋ lɛ mli.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛje tsu lɛ mli lɛ, amɛtee Lidia we lɛ mli. Amɛna nyɛmimɛi lɛ, ni amɛshɛje amɛmii, ni amɛyiŋ amɛtee.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: Paulo kɛ Sila tsɔ̃ Amfipoli kɛ Apolonia, ni amɛba Tesalonika, he ni Yudafoi akpeehe ko yɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Ni Paulo tee amɛŋɔɔ tamɔ bɔ ni efɔɔ feemɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ amɛ yayiyii yɛ ŋmalɛi lɛ ahe hejɔɔmɔ gbii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ,

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: ni etsɔ̃ɔ mli ni ekɛ ŋmalɛi lɛ amli saji tsɔ̃ɔ naa akɛ ja Kristo lɛ na amanehulu ni ete shi kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ; ni esaa ekɛɛ, “Yesu nɛɛ, mɔ he sane ni mijajeɔ mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ lɛ, lɛ ji Kristo lɛ.”

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Ni amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi he ye, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛ Paulo kɛ Sila he; nakai nɔŋŋ Helabii Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishelɔi lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo kɛ yei hiɛnaanɔbii lɛ hu pii fee.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Shi efee Yudafoi krokomɛi lɛ atãŋ, ni amɛyakpala niiahetswialɔi lɛ ateŋ hii fɔ̃ji komɛi amɛfata amɛhe, ni be ni amɛfee asafo yuu lɛ, amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli hirihiri; ni amɛyatua Yason we lɛ amɛmiitao akɛ amɛkpala Paulo kɛ Sila amɛyahã maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛnaaa amɛ lɛ, amɛkpala Yason kɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi kɛtee maŋ lɛ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ ni amɛbolɔ akɛ, “Mɛnɛɛmɛi ni amɛtsɔ̃ jeŋ hiɛ ebu shi lɛ eba biɛ nɛɛ hu,

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: ni Yason ehere amɛ yɛ eshĩa; ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛkuɔ Kaisare mla lɛ nɔ, ni amɛkɛɔ akɛ maŋtsɛ kroko yɛ ni ji Yesu ko.”

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: Ni amɛhã maŋbii lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ fɛɛ ejijaa kɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛhe sɛɛdaamɔnii yɛ Yason kɛ mɛi krokomɛi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, amɛŋmɛɛ amɛhe. Paulo kɛ Sila yɛ Beroia

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Ni amrɔ̃ lɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ jie Paulo kɛ Sila gbɛ nyɔɔŋ kɛtee Beroia. Ni be ni amɛshɛ jɛi lɛ, amɛyabote Yudafoi lɛ akpeehe lɛ mli.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Shi mɛnɛɛmɛi asu hi fe mɛi ni yɔɔ Tesalonika lɛ, ni amɛ lɛ amɛhere wiemɔ lɛ kɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ, ni daa gbi lɛ amɛkpaa ŋmalɛi lɛ amli amɛkwɛɔ akɛ nibii nɛɛ yɛ mli nakai lo.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi pii he ye, Helayei ni yɔɔ gbɛi kɛ hii hu pii.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Yudafoi ni yɔɔ Tesalonika lɛ nu akɛ Paulo eyajaje Nyɔŋmɔ wiemɔ lɛ yɛ Beroia hu lɛ, amɛba jɛi hu ni amɛbawo mɛi lɛ ayiŋ ni amɛhã amɛ jijaa.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amrɔ lɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ yajie Paulo gbɛ ni eya ŋshɔnaagbɛ; shi Sila kɛ Timoteo hi Beroia.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Mɛi ni yajie Paulo gbɛ lɛ kɛ lɛ tee Atene tɔ̃ɔ; ni be ni eshɛ amɛ akɛ Sila kɛ Timoteo aba eŋɔɔ oya lɛ, amɛyi mli amɛtee. Paulo yɛ Atene

english_verse: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
translation_verse: Be ni Paulo mɛɔ Sila kɛ Timoteo yɛ Atene lɛ, ena akɛ eji maŋ ni eyi obɔ̃ kɛ amãgãi sɔŋŋ, ni ehao lɛ.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ Yudafoi ni yɔɔ kpeehe lɛ kɛ Helafoi Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishelɔi lɛ kɛ mɛi ni kɛ lɛ kpeɔ daa gbi yɛ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ yiyii.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Shi nilelɔi ni ji Epikuromɛi kɛ Stoamɛi lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi kɛ lɛ taa naa ni mɛi komɛi kɛɛ, “Mɛni po naafuutsɛ nɛɛ taoɔ ekɛɛ?” Ni mɛi komɛi hu kɛɛ, “Etamɔ mɔ ni jajeɔ maŋsɛɛ jemawɔji ahe sane etsɔ̃ɔ.” Amɛkɛɛ enɛ ejaakɛ ejaje Yesu kɛ shitee lɛ he Sanekpakpa lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Ni amɛŋɔ lɛ kɛtee Areopago lɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ, “Ani ooohã wɔle nɔ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ hee ni owie he nɛɛ?

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ohã wɔtoii enu maŋsɛɛ saji; hewɔ lɛ wɔmiitao shishi wɔle.”

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Shi Atenebii fɛɛ kɛ gbɔi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ, nɔ ni eshwɛ amɛ pɛ ji sane hee ko gbaa kɛ sane toiboo.

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Ni Paulo yadamɔ Areopago lɛ teŋ ni ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi Atenebii, miyoo yɛ nibii fɛɛ mli akɛ nyɛjaa wɔji pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni mihoɔ ni mikwɛ nii ni nyɛjaa lɛ, mina afɔleshãa latɛ ko hu ni aŋma yɛ nɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ni aleee lɛ nɔŋ.’ No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni nyɛleee lɛ ni kɛ̃ lɛ nyɛjaa lɛ lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ ehe sane mijajeɔ mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ ni bɔ je lɛ kɛ emli nibii fɛɛ lɛ, lɛ ji ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nuŋtsɔ lɛ; ehiii Sɔlemɔtsui ni akɛ niji ma amli,

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: ni asaŋ akɛ gbɔmɛi aniji jaaa lɛ tamɔ mɔ ko ni nɔ ko fiɔ lɛ; lɛ moŋ edɛŋ wala kɛ mumɔ kɛ nii fɛɛ jɛɔ hãa gbɔmɛi fɛɛ;

english_verse: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
translation_verse: ni lá kome ekɛbɔ gbɔmɛi adesai fɛɛ, ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni yinɔi ni eto lɛ kɛ amɛshihilɛhei lɛ ahusui lɛ ekpɛ mli eto momo,

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: koni amɛtao Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ, akɛ aleenɔ, kɛ amɛgbugbuu shi lɛ, amɛaana lɛ lo; tsɛbelɛ ekɛ wɔteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko teŋ jɛkɛɛɛ.

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ, ‘Emli nɔŋŋ wɔhiɛ kãmɔ ni wɔtsiɔ wɔhe ni wɔyɔɔ yɛ;’ tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛlalatsɛmɛi lɛ ekomɛi hu ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, ‘Shi lɛ nɔŋŋ eshwiei ji wɔ hu.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ shwiei ji wɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ wɔsusuɔ akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ su lɛ tamɔ shika loo jwiɛtɛi loo tɛ ko ni gbɔmɔ kɛ eŋaa kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fee.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bei ni aleee lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ eku ehiɛ efɔ̃ nɔ, shi agbɛnɛ lɛ eewo gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he kitã akɛ amɛtsake amɛtsui,

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ eto gbi ko, no nɔ ni ebaatsɔ̃ nuu ni eto lɛ nɔ ekojo jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jalɛ naa; ni ekɛ shi ni etee lɛ kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ lɛ maa enɛ nɔ mi ehãa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛnu gbohiiashitee he lɛ, mɛi komɛi ye ehe fɛo, ni mɛi komɛi hu kɛɛ, “Wɔɔsaa wɔbo owiemɔ nɛɛ toi ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, Paulo shi amɛ.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Shi hii komɛi kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛ ehe ni amɛhe amɛye; amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi ji Dionisio, Areopagonyo lɛ, kɛ yoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Damari lɛ, kɛ mɛi krokomɛi ni fata amɛhe.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Nii nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, Paulo je Atene ni eyiŋ etee Korinto.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Ni eyana Yudafonyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Akwila, ni afɔ lɛ yɛ Ponto, kɛ eŋa Priskila. Akwila jɛ Italia ba etsɛko. Eba ejaakɛ Kaisare Klaudio efã akɛ Yudafoi fɛɛ aje Roma. Ni Paulo tee amɛŋɔɔ;

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: ni akɛni ekɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔ kome hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ amɛ hi shi, ni etsuɔ nii; amɛnitsumɔ nɛɛ ji buufeemɔ.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Shi daa Hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ, Paulo yawieɔ etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi yɛ kpeehe lɛ, ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ etsake Yudafoi kɛ Helabii lɛ.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Sila kɛ Timoteo jɛ Makedonia ba lɛ, Paulo hiɛ dɔ yɛ wiemɔ lɛ he ni eye odase veveeve etsɔ̃ɔ Yudafoi lɛ akɛ Yesu ji Kristo lɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Shi akɛni amɛkuɔ enaa ni amɛwieɔ musubɔɔ wiemɔi hewɔ lɛ, ekpala ehe eshwie amɛnɔ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛlá abua nyɛyiteŋ; mi lɛ sɔ̃ ko wulaaa mi. Kɛjɛ be nɛ nɔ kɛyaa nɛɛ, matee jeŋmajiaŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eje jɛi ni etee Nyɔŋmɔ jalɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Titio Yusto ni eshĩa kpɛtɛ kpeehe lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Shi kpeehe lɛ onukpa lɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Krispo lɛ kɛ ewe muu lɛ fɛɛ he Nuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ amɛye, ni Korintobii lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii hu ni nu wiemɔ lɛ, amɛhe amɛye, ni abaptisi amɛ.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Ni nyɔɔŋ lɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛɛ Paulo yɛ ninaa mli akɛ, “Kaashe gbeyei, shi moŋ wiemɔ, ni okamua onaa,

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ mikɛ bo yɛ, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaŋ ohe ni efeŋ bo efɔŋ ko, ejaakɛ miyɛ mɛi pii yɛ maŋ nɛɛ mli.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Ni ehi jɛi afi kome kɛ nyɔji ekpaa etsɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ wiemɔ lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Shi be ni Galio yeɔ amralo yɛ Akaia lɛ, Yudafoi lɛ kɛ jwɛŋmɔ kome te shi wo Paulo, ni amɛkpala lɛ kɛtee kojomɔ sɛ̃i lɛ hiɛ,

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: amɛkɛɛ, “Nuu nɛɛ woɔ mɛi lɛ ayiŋ ni amɛshi mla lɛ sɛɛ amɛja Nyɔŋmɔ.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Paulo baagbele enaa pɛ lɛ, Galio kɛɛ Yudafoi lɛ akɛ, “Yudafoi, eji juu kɛ fɔ̃ sane ko ni kulɛ, esa akɛ mabo nyɛ toi;

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: shi kɛji wiemɔi loo gbɛii loo nyɛmla lɛ he saji komɛi ni lɛ, no lɛ nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛkwɛa nɔ; ejaakɛ misumɔɔɔ akɛ mikojoɔ nɛkɛ saji.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Ni eshwie amɛ kɛjɛ kojomɔ sɛ̃i lɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Helabii lɛ fɛɛ mɔ kpeehe lɛ onukpa ni atsɛɔ lɛ Sostene lɛ, ni amɛyi lɛ yɛ kojomɔ sɛ̃i lɛ hiɛ; shi Galio ebuuu enɛɛmɛi eko eko. Paulo ku esɛɛ kɛtee Antiokia

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Be ni Paulo ehi jɛi gbii kplaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ye shɛɛ, ni ebote lɛlɛ mli kɛmiiya Siria; ni Priskila kɛ Akwila kɛ lɛ tee ni eyashɛ eyi yɛ Kenkrea, ejaakɛ ewo shi.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Ni amɛba Efeso, ni ekɛ amɛ gbala mli yɛ jɛi. Ni etee kpeehe lɛ, ni ekɛ Yudafoi lɛ yayiyii.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛkpa lɛ fai akɛ etsɛ yɛ amɛŋɔɔ fioo lɛ, ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ;

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: shi moŋ ekɛ amɛ ye shɛɛ ekɛɛ, “Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ miisumɔ lɛ, maku misɛɛ maba nyɛŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ.” Ni efã kɛjɛ Efeso.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Be ni eyakpeleke Kaisarea lɛ, etee Yerusalɛm ni eyaŋa asafo lɛ, ni eyiŋ etee Antiokia.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ni ehi jɛi fioo, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, eyi mli ekoŋŋ ni eyakpa Galatia kɛ Frigia shikpɔji lɛ anɔ ewo kaselɔi lɛ fɛɛ ahewalɛ. Apolo yɛ Efeso kɛ Korinto

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Yudanyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Apolo ni afɔ lɛ yɛ Aleksandria lɛ ba Efeso. Apolo nɛɛ enaa tse ni ele ŋmalɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ hu.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Atsɔ̃ɔ nuu nɛɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ he nii, ni eyɛ ekãa yɛ mumɔ mli ni ewieɔ ni etsɔ̃ɔ Yesu he nii fitsofitso, tsɛ Yohane baptisimɔ lɛ kɛkɛ ele.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Ni ebɔ̃i wiemɔ kɛ ekãa yɛ kpeehe lɛ. Shi be ni Akwila kɛ Priskila nu ehe lɛ, amɛŋɔ lɛ kɛba amɛŋɔɔ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɛ lɛ fitsofitso.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ etao akɛ eya Akaia, hewɔ lɛ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ŋma wolo amɛkɛwo kaselɔi lɛ aŋaa ni amɛhere lɛ atuu. Ni be ni eba jɛi lɛ, ewa mɛi ni etsɔ̃ dromɔ lɛ nɔ ehe eye lɛ babaoo.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ku Yudafoi lɛ anaa yɛ maŋ hiɛ ni ekɛ ŋmalɛi lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ faŋŋ akɛ Yesu ji Kristo lɛ.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Be ni Apolo yɔɔ Korinto lɛ, Paulo yakpa gɔŋ nɔ maji lɛ anɔ kɛbaje Efeso. Ni ebana kaselɔi komɛi,

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Ani be ni nyɛhe nyɛye lɛ nyɛna Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lo?” Ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ ko yɛ he ko jiŋŋ, wɔnuko tete.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Belɛ mɛni mli abaptisi nyɛ awo mɔ?” Ni amɛkɛɛ, “Yohane baptisimɔ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kɛɛ, “Yohane baptisimɔ lɛ, ekɛbaptisi mɛi ni etsake amɛtsui; shi ekɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, amɛhe mɔ ni baa yɛ esɛɛ lɛ moŋ nɔ amɛye; lɛ ji Kristo Yesu lɛ.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛnu enɛ lɛ, abaptisi amɛ awo Nuŋtsɔ Yesu gbɛi mli;

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: ni be ni Paulo kɛ eniji shwie amɛnɔ lɛ, Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ba amɛnɔ, ni amɛwie wiemɔi srɔtoi ni amɛgba.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Shi hii lɛ fɛɛ aaafee nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Ni Paulo tee kpeehe lɛ, ni eyawie kɛ ekãa, ni etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ nii kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ nyɔji etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ ni amɛhe Nyɔŋmɔ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he sane lɛ amɛye.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Shi be ni mɛi komɛi waje amɛtsui ni amɛbooo toi ni amɛwie tsɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ he efɔŋ yɛ mɛi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, eje amɛŋɔɔ ni ejie kaselɔi lɛ hu yɛ amɛteŋ, ni daa gbi lɛ eyawieɔ etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi yɛ mɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Tirano lɛ nikasemɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Ehiɛ nakai feemɔ aahu afii enyɔ sɔŋŋ, ni mɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Asia lɛ, Yudafoi kɛ Helabii lɛ fɛɛ, nu Nuŋtsɔ Yesu wiemɔ lɛ. Skeva bihii lɛ

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Ni Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ Paulo nine nɔ etsu hewalɛ nitsumɔi hu ni nɔ ekaaa,

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: aahu po ni aŋɔɔ eklaladukui kɛ atade hiɛhaanii tete ayahaa helatsɛmɛi anɔ, ni amɛhelai lɛ tãa ni mumɔi fɔ̃ji lɛ hu jeɔ amɛmli.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Shi Yudafoi okɔmfoi ni nyiɛ kpaa shi lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi hu ka ni amɛkɛ Nuŋtsɔ Yesu gbɛi afã mɛi ni mumɔi fɔ̃ji yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ayi akɛ, “Mina Yesu ni Paulo shiɛɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Osɔfonukpa Skeva, Yudanyo lɛ, bihii kpawo ji mɛi ni feɔ nakai nii lɛ.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Shi mumɔ fɔŋ lɛ here nɔ ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Yesu lɛ, mile lɛ, ni Paulo hu, mile lɛ; shi nyɛ lɛ, namɛi ji nyɛ?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Ni gbɔmɔ ni mumɔ fɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ emli lɛ tua amɛ ni enine tsɔ̃ amɛnɔ ni efee amɛ butuu, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe yayai kɛ pilamɔi jo foi kɛjɛ nakai shĩa lɛ.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Ni be ni Yudafoi kɛ Helabii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Efeso lɛ nu enɛ lɛ, gbeyei mɔmɔ amɛ fɛɛ, ni awo Nuŋtsɔ Yesu gbɛi lɛ hiɛ nyam naakpa.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi ni ehe eye lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii hu ba ni amɛbajaje amɛnifeemɔnii lɛ faŋŋ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Ni ŋkunyaayelɔi lɛ hu ateŋ mɛi babaoo ba ni amɛkɛ amɛwoji lɛ babua shi ni amɛshã yɛ mɛi fɛɛ hiɛ; ni be ni abu naa lɛ, efee jwiɛtɛi kukuji akpei nyɔŋmai enumɔ.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ hewalɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ wiemɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ ekɛshwere ni eye kunim. Sakasakafeemɔ ba Efeso

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Nii nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, Paulo to eyiŋ yɛ mumɔ lɛ mli akɛ eeeyatsɔ̃ Makedonia kɛ Akaia kɛya Yerusalɛm, ni ekɛɛ, “Kɛji mishɛ jɛi lɛ, ja miyakwɛ Roma hu.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Shi be ni etsu mɛi ni sɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi enyɔ, Timoteo kɛ Erasto, Makedonia lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ehi Asia be fioo.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Shi nakai be lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ sakasakafeemɔ ko ni bate shi yɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ ejeee shwɛmɔ.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ jwiɛtɛiŋaalɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Demetrio lɛ kɛ jwiɛtɛi feɔ Artemi Sɔlemɔtsui ni hãa ŋaalɔi lɛ naa nitsumɔ pii.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Etsɛ amɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni tsuɔ nakai nii lɛ eko lɛ kɛkpe, ni ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi, nyɛle akɛ nɛkɛ ŋaa nɛɛ wɔkɛnaa wɔnii pii lɛ.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Ni nyɛsaa nyɛmiina ni nyɛmiinu akɛ jeee Efeso nɛɛ kɛkɛ, shi moŋ shwɛ fioo ni Asia fɛɛ lɛ, Paulo nɛɛ ehã mɛi babaoo ayiŋ etsɔ̃, ni ekpale amɛ; ekɛɔ akɛ nii ni akɛ niji fee lɛ jeee nyɔŋmɔi ni.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Miishe gbeyei akɛ, jeee wɔnitsumɔ nɛɛ kɛkɛ he guɔ baagbo, shi moŋ nyɔŋmɔyoo Artemi kekenam lɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ hu abuŋ lɛ ahaŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni enunyam kpeteŋkple lɛ ni Asia kɛ jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu jaa lɛ baabutu.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Be ni ŋaalɔi lɛ nu enɛ lɛ, amɛmli wo la pam, ni amɛbolɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Efesobii Artemi lɛ kekenam ni!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Ni maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ fee sakasaka; ni amɛkɛ jwɛŋmɔ kome tsɛ̃ kɛtee nikwɛmɔhe lɛ, ni amɛyamɔmɔ Gaio kɛ Aristarko ni ji Makedoniabii ni fata Paulo he kɛfã gbɛ lɛ.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Paulo tao akɛ eya mɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, kaselɔi lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ lɛ;

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: ni Asia lumɛi lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi hu ni ji Paulo shieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ tsu eŋɔɔ abawo lɛ ŋaa akɛ ekakwɛ ni etee nikwɛmɔhe lɛ.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni mɛi komɛi bolɔɔ nɛkɛ lɛ, mɛi komɛi hu miibolɔ ekroko; ejaakɛ kpee lɛ efee basabasa ni mɛi kpotoo leee nɔ hewɔ ni amɛbakpe tete.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Akɛni Yudafoi lɛ tsirɛ Aleksandro yisɛɛ kɛba hiɛgbɛ hewɔ lɛ, mɛi pii susu akɛ lɛ ejɛ ni basabasa lɛ ba. Shi Aleksandro fɔ̃ enine eetao akɛ ejieɔ enaa etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi lɛ.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛyoo akɛ Yudanyo ji lɛ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛkɛ gbee kome bolɔ aaafee ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ sɔŋŋ akɛ, “Efesobii Artemi lɛ kekenam ni!”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Ni be ni maŋ woloŋmalɔ lɛ ekpãtã mɛi lɛ, ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi Efesobii, mɛɛ gbɔmɔ po leee akɛ Artemi kekenam lɛ kɛ amãgã ni kpeleke shi kɛjɛ Dio ŋɔɔ lɛ Efesobii amaŋ nɛɛŋ ewulɔmɔ yɔɔ?

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ akɛni enɛ he bɛ ŋwanejee hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ nyɛfeɔ dioo, ni nyɛkafee gidigidi ko.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Nyɛkɛ hii nɛɛ eba biɛ; amɛjeee Sɔlemɔ we nii julɔi lɛ, amɛjeee nyɛnyɔŋmɔyoo lɛ he musubɔlɔi hu.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji Demetrio kɛ enanemɛi ŋaalɔi lɛ kɛ mɔ ko yɛ sane ko lɛ, kojomɔ gbii yɛ, ni amralofoi hu yɛ; nyɛhãa amɛkɛ sane lɛ ayaa amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji saji krokomɛi anaa nyɛtaoɔ lɛ, akwaashɔŋ lɛ aaaye yɛ mla naa.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛ wɔkwɛɛɛ ni ahi lɛ, abaafolɔ wɔnaa yɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ basabasafeemɔ lɛ hewɔ, ni wɔbɛ sane ko ni wɔɔnyɛ wɔkɛjie wɔnaa yɛ hoofeemɔ nɛɛ he.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Ni be ni ekɛɛ enɛ lɛ, ewo asafo lɛ gbɛ.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Be ni gidigidifeemɔ lɛ sɛɛ efo lɛ, Paulo tsu ayatsɛ kaselɔi lɛ kɛba eŋɔɔ ni ewie etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ ni ekɛ amɛ ye shɛɛ, ni eyi mli kɛmiiya Makedonia.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Ni be ni eyatsɔ̃ jɛi niiaŋ ni ekɛ wiemɔi pii wo amɛŋaa lɛ, eba Akaia.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Ni eye nyɔji etɛ̃ yɛ jɛi, ni akɛni Yudafoi lɛ ewo lɛ ka be ni eheɔ efã kɛya Siria hewɔ lɛ, eto eyiŋ akɛ eeeku esɛɛ eyatsɔ̃ Makedonia ekoŋŋ.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Ni Sopatre, Beroianyo lɛ ni ji Pirho bi lɛ, kɛ Aristarko kɛ Sekundo, Tesalonikabii lɛ, kɛ Gaio, Derbenyo lɛ, kɛ Timoteo, kɛ Asiabii ni ji Tihiko kɛ Trofimo lɛ, kɛ lɛ tee Asia.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Mɛnɛɛmɛi tsɔ̃ hiɛ, ni amɛyamɛ wɔ yɛ Troia.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Ni wɔ lɛ wɔfã kɛjɛ Filipi yɛ Akpiti Gbii lɛ asɛɛ, ni gbii enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ wɔyashɛ amɛŋɔɔ yɛ Troia, ni wɔhi jɛi gbii kpawo. Paulo kɛ Troia asafo lɛ ye shɛɛ

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Shi otsi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ be ni wɔbabua wɔhe naa koni amɛye suɔmɔ niyenii lɛ, Paulo wie tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ni ekã wiemɔ lɛ he kɛyashi nyɔɔŋteŋ, ejaakɛ kɛ je tsɛre lɛ ebaayi mli.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Ni asu kanei pii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli he ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ lɛ.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Shi oblanyo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Eutiko lɛ ta samflɛ naa, ni wɔ ni tsii loo lɛ, ejaakɛ Paulo wiemɔ lɛ sɛɛ jɛkɛ, ni wɔ ni emɔ lɛ lɛ sɔŋŋ hã ekpa kɛjɛ sɔɔdoi etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ ebagbee shi, ni ayawo lɛ ni egbo.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kpeleke shi, ni eyabu enɔ, ni efua lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛkafea hoo, ejaakɛ wala yɛ emli.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Ni be ni ekwɔ kɛba ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebakumɔ aboloo lɛ, ni eye eko, ni ekã he ewie aahu kɛyashi jetsɛremɔ wɛlɛŋŋ, kɛkɛ ni eyi mli.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Ni amɛkɛ gbekɛ lɛ tee shĩa ni ehiɛ kã, ni amɛmii shɛ amɛhe naakpa. Paulo jɛ Troia Kɛtee Mileto

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Shi wɔ lɛ wɔtsɔ̃ hiɛ kɛtee lɛlɛ mli, ni wɔfã kɛtee Aso ni wɔyaŋɔ Paulo yɛ jɛi, ejaakɛ Paulo lɛ, lɛ lɛ ebaatsɔ̃ shikpɔŋ hewɔ lɛ bɔ ni eto ji no.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Ni be ni ebanina wɔ yɛ Aso lɛ, wɔwo lɛ ni wɔba Mitilene.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Ni wɔfa yɛ jɛi, ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ wɔbashɛ Kio ŋlɛnɔ. Ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ wɔbashɛ Samo, ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ wɔba Mileto.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Paulo ekpɛ mli akɛ eeeho Efeso he, bɔ ni afee ni ekatsɛ yɛ Asia; ejaakɛ eeye oyai ni kɛ aaaho lɛ, eyashɛ Yerusalɛm Pentekoste gbi lɛ. Paulo kɛ Efeso onukpai lɛ ye shɛɛ

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Ni ejɛ Mileto etsu Efeso ayakpee asafo lɛ mli onukpai lɛ abahã lɛ.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛba eŋɔɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛle bɔ ni mitsɔ̃ mikɛ nyɛ hi shi be muu lɛ fɛɛ, kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi nɔ ni miba Asia nɛɛ,

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: ni mikɛ heshibaa jwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ kɛ yaafonui pii kɛ kai ni ba minɔ yɛ Yudafoi akawoi lɛ amli lɛ sɔmɔ̃ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ;

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: bɔ ni mishiuuu nɔ ko nɔ ko ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ hã nyɛ nɔ, ni mijaje mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ yɛ faŋŋ kɛ shĩa fɛɛ shĩa hu;

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: ni miye odase mitsɔ̃ɔ Yudafoi kɛ Helabii fɛɛ akɛ amɛkpale kɛba Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe wɔNuŋtsɔ Yesu nɔ amɛye.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Ni agbɛnɛ lɛ, naa, efi mi yɛ mumɔ mli hewɔ lɛ miiya Yerusalɛm, ni mileee nɔ ni baaba minɔ yɛ jɛi,

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: akɛ ja nɔ ni Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ yeɔ odase faŋŋ yɛ maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ ekɛɔ akɛ tsuŋwoo kɛ amanehului mɛɔ mi lɛ.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ̃lɛ mibuuu miwala akɛ ejara wa hã mi, bɔ ni afee ni mikɛ miishɛɛ agbe migbɛnyiɛmɔ lɛ kɛ sɔ̃ɔmɔ ni mina yɛ Nuŋtsɔ Yesu dɛŋ akɛ miye Nyɔŋmɔ dromɔ lɛ he Sanekpakpa lɛ he odase faŋŋ lɛ naa.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “Ni agbɛnɛ lɛ naa, mile akɛ, nyɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni minyiɛ nyɛteŋ mishiɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he sane lɛ, nyɛnaŋ mihiɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ miiye odase miitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ, akɛ miyeee nyɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko lá yi sɔ̃;

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ mijaje Nyɔŋmɔ yiŋtoo muu lɛ fɛɛ mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ ni mishiuuu eko nɔ.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛlea nyɛhenɔkwɛmɔ kɛ toiku lɛ fɛɛ ni Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ewo nyɛ amɛnɔkwɛlɔi lɛ, koni nyɛlɛ Nyɔŋmɔ asafo lɛ ni ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ elá he lɛ.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mile akɛ, kɛ mikpa mihe lɛ, klãji fulɔi baabote nyɛteŋ, ni amɛbaŋ toiku lɛ yi.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Ni nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛteŋ hu lɛ, hii ni wieɔ nii ni ejaaa aaate shi, ni amɛaakpala kaselɔi lɛ amɛshwie amɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛsaraa, ni nyɛkaia akɛ afii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ mikɛ yaafonui efɔ̃ɔɔ nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ nyɔɔŋ kɛ shwane lɛ.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Ni agbɛnɛ lɛ, anyɛmimɛi, miitu nyɛ miiwo Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ edromɔ wiemɔ lɛ dɛŋ; lɛ eyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛaahã nyɛnane amɔ shi ni ekɛ gboshinii lɛ ahã nyɛ yɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni atsuu amɛhe lɛ ateŋ.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Mihiɛ ekɔ̃ɔɔ nyɛteŋ mɔ ko jwiɛtɛi loo shika loo atade nɔ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛle akɛ nii ni hiaa mi kɛ mɛi ni kɛ mi yɔɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ niji nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsu he nii.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Mikɛ fɛɛ tsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ akɛ nakai sa akɛ atsu nii ni akɛye abua mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni akai Nuŋtsɔ Yesu wiemɔi ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewie lɛ akɛ, ‘Nɔhãmɔ mli yɛ jɔɔmɔ fe hemɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Be ni ewie nɛkɛ lɛ, ekula shi ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ sɔle.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛfo bloblo naakpa, ni amɛgbeegbee Paulo kuɛ nɔ, ni amɛshwɔshwɔɔ enaa.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Ni nɔ ni dɔ amɛ titri ji wiemɔ ni ewie akɛ amɛnaŋ ehiɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ. Ni amɛyajie lɛ gbɛ yɛ lɛlɛ lɛ mli.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ be ni wɔkɛ amɛ gbala mli lɛ, wɔfã ni wɔnyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛba Ko, ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ wɔkɛba Rodo, ni wɔjɛ jɛi wɔba Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Wɔna lɛlɛ ko yɛ jɛi ni miiya Foinikia ni wɔbote mli ni wɔkɛshwie nɔ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Kipro tua wɔhiɛ lɛ, wɔtswa lɛ wɔfɔ̃ abɛku ni wɔba Siria, ni wɔbakpeleke yɛ Tiro; ejaakɛ jɛi abaajie lɛlɛ lɛ mli nii yɛ.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ni eba mli akɛ, be ni wɔye gbii lɛ tã lɛ, wɔkɛshwie nɔ, ni amɛ kɛ amɛŋamɛi kɛ amɛbii fɛɛ bajie wɔ gbɛ kɛyashi maŋ lɛ klotia; ni wɔkula shi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa, ni wɔsɔle.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Wɔyeyee shɛɛ ni wɔbote lɛlɛ mli; ni amɛ hu amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛtee amɛshĩai.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Shi wɔ lɛ wɔjɛ Tiro wɔba Ptolemai. Ni wɔyaŋa nyɛmimɛi lɛ, ni wɔkɛ amɛ hi shi gbi kome.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ wɔyiŋ kɛtee Kaisarea, ni wɔyabote Sanekpakpashiɛlɔ Filipo ni ji mɛi kpawo lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome lɛ we, ni wɔkɛ lɛ hi shi.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: Ni eyɛ biyei oblayei ejwɛ ni gbaa.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Be ni wɔhi shi gbii kplaŋŋ yɛ jɛi lɛ, gbalɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Agabo lɛ jɛ Yudea ba;

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: ni be ni eba wɔŋɔɔ lɛ, ekɔ Paulo hɛfiinɔ lɛ ni ekɛfi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniji kɛ enaji ekɛɛ, “Bɔ ni Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Nuu mɔ nɔ̃ ni ji hɛfiinɔ nɛɛ, nɛkɛ Yudafoi lɛ baafi lɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni amɛaaŋɔ lɛ amɛwo jeŋmajiaŋbii lɛ adɛŋ.’ ”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be ni wɔnu enɛ lɛ wɔkɛ jɛibii lɛ fɛɛ kpa Paulo fai akɛ ekaya Yerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Shi ehere nɔ ekɛɛ, “Mɛni nyɛfeɔ nɛɛ, nyɛmiifo ni nyɛkɛmiiwo mi awerɛho? Mi lɛ, jeee fii kɛkɛ misaa mihe mito, shi moŋ gbele diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Nuŋtsɔ Yesu gbɛi lɛ hewɔ yɛ Yerusalɛm.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Shi akɛni eŋmɛ̃ɛɛ gbɛ hewɔ lɛ, wɔfee diŋŋ wɔkɛɛ, “Afee bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni nakai gbii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ wɔto wɔnii, ni wɔyiŋ kɛtee Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Ni kaselɔi ni jɛ Kaisarea lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi kɛ wɔ tee, ni amɛhã wɔyato Mnason, Kipronyo ko ni ji kaselɔ kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ lɛ, ŋɔɔ. Paulo yasara Yakobo

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Be ni wɔshɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, nyɛmimɛi lɛ here wɔ atuu.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Paulo kɛ wɔ tee Yakobo ŋɔɔ; ni onukpai lɛ fɛɛ hu yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Eŋa amɛ, ni egba amɛ nibii ni Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ esɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ nɔ etsu yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ lɛ ekomekome.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛnu lɛ, amɛwo Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ nyam, ni amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Anyɛmi, kwɛmɔ Yudafoi akpei abɔ ni ehe eye nɛɛ, ni amɛ fɛɛ lɛ, Mla lɛ he hiɛdɔlɔi ji amɛ.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Shi abatã ohe sane ahã amɛ akɛ otsɔ̃ɔ Yudafoi ni yɔɔ jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ lɛ akɛ amɛkwa Mose, ni okɛɔ akɛ amɛkafolɔ amɛbii aketia, ni asaŋ amɛkanyiɛ amɛkusumi asɛɛ.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ lɛ, te aaafee tɛŋŋ? Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, amɛaanu akɛ oba.

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, feemɔ nɔ ni wɔkɛɔ bo nɛɛ. Wɔyɛ hii ejwɛ ni ewo shi.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ŋɔɔ amɛ ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ ayatsuu nyɛhe, ni owo nɔ ni ahãa lɛ ohã amɛ, koni amɛshɛ amɛyi, ni mɛi lɛ fɛɛ baana akɛ saji ni abagbaa yɛ ohe lɛ eko eko bɛ mli, shi moŋ bo diɛŋtsɛ tete obaa ojeŋ yɛ Mla lɛ naa, ni oyeɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Shi jeŋmajiaŋbii ni ehe eye lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, wɔ diɛŋtsɛ wɔŋma ni wɔkpɛ mli akɛ amɛkaye nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ eko nɔ, shi moŋ amɛhi wɔji afɔlei kɛ lá kɛ kooloi ni ashɔ̃tɔ̃ kɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Paulo ŋɔ hii lɛ, ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ be ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ etsuu amɛhe lɛ, ebote Sɔlemɔ we lɛ ni eyatsɔ̃ɔ beyinɔ ni hetsuumɔ gbii lɛ anaagbee lɛ baashɛ ni abaashã afɔle ahã amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ. Amɔ Paulo yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Shi be ni eshwɛ fioo ni aaagbe gbii kpawo lɛ naa lɛ, Yudafoi ni jɛ Asia lɛ na lɛ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni amɛta asafo lɛ fɛɛ mli, ni amɛbamɔ lɛ;

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: ni amɛbolɔ akɛ, “Ataamɛi Israelbii, nyɛbafataa wɔhe! Naa nuu lɛ ni wieɔ maŋ nɛɛ kɛ Mla lɛ kɛ biɛ nɛɛ he efɔŋ etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi fɛɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ; ni esaa ekɛ Helabii eba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ ekɛbabule He Krɔŋkrɔŋ nɛɛ hu.”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ amɛna lɛ kɛ Trofimo ni jɛ Efeso lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli momo hewɔ lɛ amɛsusu akɛ Paulo kɛ lɛ ba Sɔlemɔ we lɛ.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ni maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ bu, ni maŋbii lɛ sha foi kɛbabua mɛhe naa; ni amɛmɔ Paulo amɛgbala lɛ kɛjɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ kɛje kpo, ni amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ aŋamɔ shinai lɛ.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛheɔ lɛ amɛgbe lɛ, ayatswa asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ adafi akɛ Yerusalɛm fɛɛ efee gidigidi.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Ni amrɔ lɛ eŋɔ asraafoi kɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi ni ekɛ amɛ kpeleke shi kɛ foi kɛbanina amɛ. Be ni amɛna asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ kɛ asraafoi lɛ, amɛfɔ̃ɔ Paulo yii.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ tsi bɛŋkɛ ni emɔ emli, ni efã akɛ awo lɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔi enyɔ, ni ebi mɔ ni ji lɛ kɛ nɔ ni efee.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Shi be ni asafo lɛ mli mɛi komɛi miibolɔ miikɛɛ nɛkɛ lɛ, mɛi komɛi hu miibolɔ miikɛɛ nɔ kroko. Ni akɛni hoofeemɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ena anɔkwale lɛ, efã akɛ akɛ lɛ aya mɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ni be ni eshɛ atrakpoi lɛ anaa lɛ, eba mli akɛ asafo lɛ gidigidifeemɔ hewɔ lɛ asraafoi lɛ wo lɛ,

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: ejaakɛ maŋbii asafo yuu lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ miibolɔ akɛ, “Akɛ lɛ aya!”

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Shi be ni akɛ Paulo baabote mɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebi asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ akɛ, “Ani miyɛ hegbɛ akɛ mikɛ bo wieɔ wiemɔ ko lo?” Ebi lɛ akɛ, “Ole Hela wiemɔ?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Belɛ jeee bo ji Ijiptnyo lɛ ni nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ni ekɛ atuatsemɔ ba ni ekpala hii awuyelɔi akpei ejwɛ eshwie esɛɛ kɛtee ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ?”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kɛɛ, “Mi lɛ Yudanyo ji mi, ni mijɛ Tarso, Kilikia maŋ ko ni yɔɔ gbɛi lɛ mli. Shi miikpa bo fai; ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ ni mikɛ maŋ lɛ awie.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Ni be ni eŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ lɛ, Paulo damɔ atrakpoi lɛ anɔ, ni efɔ̃ maŋ lɛ nine; ni be ni jɛi jɔ koniŋŋ lɛ, ewie yɛ Hebri wiemɔ mli ekɛɛ.

english_verse: “My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!”
translation_verse: “Ataamɛi kɛ anyɛmimɛi, nyɛboa minaa ni mibajie matsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɛɛ toi.”

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛnu akɛ Hebri wiemɔ ekɛ amɛ wieɔ lɛ, amɛfee diŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni ekɛɛ,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Yudanyo ji mi, ni afɔ mi yɛ Tarso yɛ Kilikia moŋ, shi maŋ nɛɛ mli alɛ mi yɛ, ni Gamaliel naji anaa atsɔse mi yɛ, yɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ amla lɛ naa fitsofitso, ni mihiɛ dɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ sane he, tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛ fɛɛ nyɛfeɔ ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ;

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: ni miwaa nɛkɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ nɛɛ yi kɛyashiɔ gbele mli, ni mifimɔ̃ɔ hii kɛ yei fɛɛ mihãa ni ayawoɔ amɛ tsuŋ,

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: bɔ ni osɔfonukpa lɛ tete kɛ onukpai lɛ fɛɛ aaanyɛ aye mi odase. Amɛdɛŋ miŋɔ woji kɛjɛ ni kulɛ mikɛyaahã nyɛmimɛi ni yɔɔ Damasko lɛ, ni miyafimɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ hu kɛba Yerusalɛm koni agbala amɛ toi.

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Shi eba mli akɛ, be ni minyiɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ ni mibabɛŋkɛ Damasko aaafee huludãamɔ mli lɛ, trukaa lɛ la ko ni kpɛmɔ naa wa jɛ ŋwɛi babɔle mi;

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: ni miflɛo migbee shi ni minu gbee ko kɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Saul, Saul, mɛɛba owaa mi yi?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Ni mihere nɔ akɛ, ‘Bo namɔŋ, Nuŋtsɔ?’ Ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Mi Yesu, Nazarenyo lɛ ni owaa lɛ yi lɛ ni.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni kɛ mi nyiɛ lɛ na la lɛ, shi mɔ ni kɛ mi wieɔ lɛ, amɛnuuu egbee.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Ni mikɛɛ, ‘Mɛni mafee, Nuŋtsɔ?’ Ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Tee shi ni oya Damasko, ni jɛi aaatsɔ̃ɔ bo nibii fɛɛ ni ato akɛ ofee lɛ yɛ.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni minaaa nii dɔŋŋ yɛ nakai la lɛ kpɛmɔ hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni kɛ mi nyiɛ lɛ mɔ minine mli amɛyawa mi Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Shi nuu ko yɛ jɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ Anania ni esheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei yɛ Mla lɛ naa, ni Yudafoi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ wieɔ ehe ekpakpa.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Lɛ eba miŋɔɔ, ni ebadamɔ mimasɛi ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Anyɛmi Saul, naa nii!’ Ni nakai ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ mina lɛ faŋŋ.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ, ‘Wɔtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ ehala bo eto, ni ole esuɔmɔnaanii, ni ona Nyɔŋmɔ Jalɔ lɛ, ni onu edaaŋ gbee;

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ obaatsɔ ehe odasefonyo koni oye nii fiaa ni ona ni onu lɛ ahe odase otsɔ̃ɔ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ni agbɛnɛ mɛɛba oshashaoɔ shi? Tee shi ni ohã abaptisi bo, ni afɔ ohe eshai lɛ ashwie ahã bo, ni osɔle otsɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ.

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Ni eba mli akɛ, be ni miku misɛɛ kɛba Yerusalɛm ekoŋŋ ni misɔleɔ yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, efee tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ enyɔ minɔ,

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: ni mina Nuŋtsɔ lɛ ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Feemɔ kpa ni oje Yerusalɛm oya, ejaakɛ amɛboŋ mihe odase ni oyeɔ lɛ toi.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Ni mikɛɛ, ‘Nuŋtsɔ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛle akɛ mi ji mɔ nɔŋŋ ni sa lɛ miwoɔ mɛi ni heɔ onɔ yeɔ lɛ tsuŋ, ni miyiɔ amɛ yɛ kpeehe fɛɛ kpeehe lɛ.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni ashwie Stefano, ohe odaseyelɔ lɛ, lá shi lɛ, mi hu midamɔ jɛi, ni mina egbele lɛ he tsui, ni mibu mɛi ni gbe lɛ lɛ atadei lɛ ahe.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Yaa, ejaakɛ mibatsu bo jeŋmaji lɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ aŋɔɔ.’ ” Paulo, Romanyo lɛ

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ni amɛbo lɛ toi kɛbashi nɛkɛ wiemɔ nɛɛ nɔ, ni amɛwo amɛgbee nɔ amɛkɛɛ, “Akɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ! Ejaakɛ esaaa akɛ ehiɔ jeŋ.”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Shi be ni amɛbolɔɔ ni amɛkpɔlɔɔ amɛhe atadei ni amɛgbɛɔ mlu amɛshwãa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ,

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ fã akɛ akɛ lɛ aya mɔɔ lɛ mli, ni ekɛɛ akɛ akɛ kpelebii atao eyitsoŋ koni ena ele nɔ sane hewɔ ni Yudafoi bolɔɔ amɛwoɔ lɛ nɛkɛ nɛɛ.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Shi be ni afi lɛ ni abaayi lɛ lɛ, Paulo bi asafoiatsɛ ni damɔ shi lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyɛ hegbɛ akɛ nyɛyiɔ Romanyo ko ni abuko lɛ fɔ kɛ kpelebii lo?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Be ni asafoiatsɛ lɛ nu enɛ lɛ, etee asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ ŋɔɔ ni eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni obaafee nɛɛ? Ejaakɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ Romanyo ni.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ ba ni ebabi lɛ akɛ “Kɛɛmɔ mi, ani Romanyo ji bo lo?” Ni ekɛɛ, “Hɛɛ.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ here nɔ akɛ, “Shika pii mikɛhe nɛkɛ maŋnyotsɔmɔ nɛɛ.” Ni Paulo kɛɛ, “Shi mi lɛ, fɔ akɛfɔ mi.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amrɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mɛi ni yaatao eyitsoŋ lɛ je emasɛi ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ hu, akɛni efi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, be ni ena ele akɛ Romanyo ji Paulo lɛ, eshe gbeyei.

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni eetao ele nɔ hewɔ krɛdɛɛ ni Yudafoi lɛ folɔɔ enaa hewɔ lɛ, enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ efɛne lɛ, ni efã akɛ osɔfonukpai lɛ kɛ akwaashɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ aba, ni ekɛ Paulo kpeleke shi, ni ekɛ lɛ yadamɔ amɛhiɛ.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo tɛje ehiɛ ekwɛ akwaashɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛkpe ni ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi kɛ anyɛmimɛi! Mi lɛ, henilee kpakpa sɔŋŋ mikɛba mijeŋ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Shi osɔfonukpa Anania lɛ fã mɛi ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ akɛ agba enaabu ma.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Paulo kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ma kɛ̃ Nyɔŋmɔ aaagba bo, bo gbogbo ni asha he! Ota shi ookojo mi yɛ Mla lɛ naa, ni osaa ojeɔ Mla lɛ sɛɛ ofãa ni agba mi mã?”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Shi mɛi ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ kɛɛ, “Ee! Kwɛɛ! Nyɔŋmɔ osɔfonukpa lɛ ojɛɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kɛɛ, “Anyɛmimɛi, mileee akɛ osɔfonukpa ni ejaakɛ aŋma akɛ, ‘Kaawie omaŋ onukpa he efɔŋ.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Shi be ni Paulo yoo akɛ amɛfã kome lɛ Sadukifoi ni, ni amɛfã kroko lɛ Farisifoi ni lɛ, ebo yɛ akwaashɔŋ lɛ teŋ akɛ, “Anyɛmimɛi, naa, mi lɛ Farisifonyo ji mi kɛ Farisifonyo bi hu. Hiɛnɔkãmɔ kɛ gbohiiashitee lɛ hewɔ akojoɔ mi nɛɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Be ni ewie nɛkɛ lɛ, bei ba Farisifoi lɛ kɛ Sadukifoi lɛ ateŋ, ni asafo lɛ mli gba enyɔ.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Sadukifoi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ gbohiiashitee ko bɛ ni asaŋ ŋwɛi bɔfo loo mumɔ ko hu bɛ; shi Farisifoi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ni blɔmɔ babaoo bate shi, ni mlatsɔɔlɔi lɛ ni yɔɔ Farisifoi lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ te shi ni amɛbe amɛkɛɛ, “Wɔnaaa nɔ ko fɔŋ ko yɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ he; shi kɛji aleenɔ mumɔ ko loo ŋwɛi bɔfo ko kɛ lɛ ewie lɛ, no lɛ ”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Shi be ni bei lɛ mli wa lɛ, asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ she gbeyei akɛ ekolɛ amɛaatserɛ Paulo mli hewɔ lɛ, efã asraafoi lɛ akɛ amɛkpeleke shi ni amɛyashɔ̃ lɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ aba mɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Shi enɔ nyɔɔŋ lɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ badamɔ emasɛi ni ekɛɛ, “Paulo, hã otsui anyɔ omli, ejaakɛ bɔ ni oye mihe odase yɛ Yerusalɛm nɛɛ, ja oyaye odase nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ Roma hu.” Atee Paulo yinɔ apam

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Ni amɛtee osɔfonukpai kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ aŋɔ̃ɔ amɛyakɛɛ, “Wɔkɛ kitãkãmɔ ekpãŋ akɛ wɔsaŋ wɔnaa nɔ ko nɔ ko ja wɔgbe Paulo dã.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛkɛ akwaashɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ayakɛa asafoiatsɛ nukpa lɛ, koni ekɛ lɛ akpeleke shi kɛba nyɛŋɔɔ, tamɔ nɔ ni esane lɛ mli nyɛbaatao fitsofitso, shi wɔ lɛ, dani eeeshɛ nyɛŋɔɔ lɛ, wɔsaa wɔhe ni wɔgbe lɛ.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Shi Paulo nyɛmi yoo bi ko nu amɛkawoo nɛɛ he, ni eyiŋ kɛtee mɔɔ lɛ mli eyatswa Paulo adafi.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo tsɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome kɛba eŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Ŋɔɔ nɛkɛ oblanyo nɛɛ ni okɛ lɛ aya asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ ŋɔɔ, ejaakɛ eyɛ sane ko ni eyaakɛɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni eŋɔ lɛ ni ekɛ lɛ tee asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ ŋɔɔ ni eyakɛɛ lɛ akɛ “Gboklɛfonyo Paulo lɛ tsɛ mi kɛtee eŋɔɔ, ni ekpa mi fai akɛ mikɛ nɛkɛ oblanyo nɛɛ aba oŋɔɔ, ejaakɛ eyɛ sane ko ni ebaakɛɛ bo”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ mɔ enine mli ni ekɛ lɛ tee afã, ni eyabi lɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ sane oyɔɔ ni obaakɛɛ mi?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Ni ekɛɛ, “Yudafoi lɛ efee ekome akɛ amɛbaakpa bo fai, ni wɔ ni okɛ Paulo akpeleke shi kɛba akwaashɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, tamɔ nɔ ni esane lɛ mli amɛbaatao fitsofitso.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni asafoiatsɛnukpa lɛ wo oblanyo lɛ gbɛ, ni ewo lɛ akpɔ akɛ, “Kaakɛɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko akɛ otsi sane nɛɛ tã otsɔ̃ɔ mi.” Akɛ Paulo yahã Amralo Felike

english_verse: The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have
translation_verse: Ni etsɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ ateŋ mɛi enyɔ kɛba eŋɔɔ, ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛsaa asraafoi ohai enyɔ kɛ okpoŋɔiatsɛmɛi nyɔŋmai kpawo kɛ akplɔiatsɛmɛi hu ohai enyɔ ni amɛya Kaisarea gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛ nɛɛhu mli.

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Nyɛsaa kooloi hu nyɛtoa ni ahã Paulo ata nɔ, ni nyɛkɛ lɛ ayahã Amralo Felike shweshweeshwe.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Ni eŋma wolo ni ekɛɛ yɛ mli akɛ,

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Klaudio Lisia miibi amralo jurɔ Felike jogbaŋŋ!

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ nuu nɛɛ, Yudafoi lɛ mɔ lɛ ni kulɛ amɛbaagbe lɛ, shi be ni mina mile akɛ Romanyo ji lɛ lɛ, mikɛ asraafoi lɛ tee miyashɔ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Shi akɛni miitao male nɔ sane hewɔ ni amɛfolɔɔ enaa lɛ, mikɛ lɛ tee amɛkuashɔŋ lɛ hiɛ,

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: ni mina akɛ amɛmla lɛ he ŋwanejee saji komɛi ahewɔ amɛfolɔɔ enaa lɛ, shi sane ko ni sa gbele loo tsuŋwoo bɛ ehe.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Shi be ni abatswa mi adafi akɛ Yudafoi lɛ ewo nuu lɛ ka lɛ, amrɔ lɛ mitsu akɛ akɛ lɛ aba oŋɔ̃ɔ, ni mifã enaaflɔlɔi lɛ hu akɛ amɛba ohiɛ ni amɛbajaje saji ni amɛkɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni asraafoi lɛ ŋɔ Paulo tamɔ bɔ ni afã amɛ lɛ, ni amɛnyiɛ nyɔɔŋ lɛ mli amɛkɛ lɛ ba Antipatri.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Ni je tsɛre lɛ amɛhã okpɔŋɔiatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛ lɛ tee, ni amɛ lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛba mɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛshɛ Kaisarea ni amɛkɛ wolo lɛ yahã amralo lɛ, amɛkɛ Paulo hu badamɔ ehiɛ.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Amralo lɛ kane wolo lɛ, ni ebi lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni ejɛ; ni be ni ena ele akɛ Kilikia ejɛ lɛ,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ekɛɛ, “Kɛ onaafolɔlɔi lɛ hu ba lɛ, no dani mabo bo toi jogbaŋŋ.” Ni efã akɛ akɛ lɛ ato Herode mɔɔ lɛ mli.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: No sɛɛ gbii enumɔ lɛ, osɔfonukpa, Anania kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ekomɛi kɛ mlalelɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Tertulo lɛ ba jɛi, ni amɛbajaje Paulo he sane amɛtsɔ̃ɔ amralo lɛ.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Ayatsɛ Paulo kɛba, ni Tertulo bɔ̃i enaaflɔmɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Lumɔ Felike, oyinɔ nɛɛ wɔtoiŋ ejɔ wɔ babaoo, ni asaŋ oshɔŋŋ ninamɔ naa lɛ, nibii pii eba hiŋmɛi nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Wɔheɔ enɛ fɛɛ kɛ shidaa pii yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Shi bɔ ni afee ni misane sɛɛ akajɛkɛ tuutu ko hewɔ lɛ, miikpa bo fai ni obo wɔ toi fioo yɛ omlihilɛ naa.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Wɔna nuu nɛɛ akɛ mɔ ko ni fiteɔ mɛi ayiŋ ni emuɔ atuatsemɔ mumɔ ewoɔ Yudafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli, ni asaŋ eji Nazaremɛi akuu lɛ naa kpãa.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: ni efã enaaflɔlɔi lɛ akɛ amɛba oŋɔɔ], ni kɛji bo diɛŋtsɛ obi enaa sane lɛ, ooona saji ni wɔfolɔɔ enaa yɛ hewɔ lɛ fɛɛ.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Ni Yudafoi lɛ hu ká mli wao ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ saji nɛɛ yɛ mli nakai. Paulo naajiemɔ

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amralo lɛ fɔ̃ Paulo nine akɛ ewie, ni ewo enaa nɔ ni ekɛɛ, “Akɛni mile akɛ ojɛ oye shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ amralo etsɛ hewɔ lɛ, mina tsuijurɔ ni mikɛaajie minaa.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Kɛ obi mli lɛ, ooona akɛ gbii nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ pɛ nɛ ni mibaho Yerusalɛm akɛ miyaja Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Ni asaŋ amɛnako mi dã akɛ mikɛ mɛi miitaa naa aloo miibú mɛi yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, loo kpeehei lɛ, loo maŋ lɛ mli,

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: ni asaŋ saji ni amɛkɛshwieɔ minɔ nɛɛ, amɛnyɛŋ naa amɛtsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Shi nɔ ni migbaa mli faŋŋ mikɛɔ bo ji enɛ akɛ, tsɔ̃ɔmɔ ni amɛtsɛɔ lɛ akɛ amaletsɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ naa mijaa wɔtsɛmɛi aNyɔŋmɔ lɛ yɛ, miheɔ nibii fɛɛ ni aŋma yɛ Mla lɛ kɛ gbalɔi lɛ amli lɛ miyeɔ,

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: ni miyɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ hiɛnɔkãmɔ ni mɛnɛɛmɛi hu kwɛɔ gbɛ akɛ gbohiiashitee baaba lɛ, ni jalɔi kɛ mɛi ni ejaaa fɛɛ baate shi.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ mikɛ mihe efɔ̃ɔɔ shi lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni mana henilee ni sɔ̃ ko wulaaa lɛ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi ahiɛ yɛ nibii fɛɛ amli.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Shi afii pii asɛɛ lɛ miba ni mikɛ nikeenii abahã mimaŋ lɛ ni mashã afɔle hu.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Enɛ feemɔ mli amɛna mi yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ akɛ mitsuu mihe, shi amɛnaaa mi kɛ asafo ko lɛ, amɛnaaa mi kɛ hoofeemɔ ko hu.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Shi Yudafoi komɛi ni jɛ Asia lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni sa akɛ kulɛ amɛba ohiɛ, ni kɛ amɛyɛ mihe sane ko lɛ ni amɛbajaje.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Aloo mɛnɛɛmɛi diɛŋtsɛ po kɛ amɛna sane ko ni ejaaa yɛ mihe be ni midãmɔ akwaashɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, amɛkɛɛ;

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: akɛ ja nɛkɛ wiemɔ kome ni be ni midamɔ amɛteŋ ni mibo akɛ, ‘Gbohiiashitee hewɔ nyɛkojoɔ mi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ’ lɛ kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Shi akɛni Felike le nɛkɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ nɛɛ he sane pɛpɛɛpɛ hewɔ lɛ, etsi amɛ eto, ni ekɛɛ, “Kɛji asafoiatsɛnukpa Lisia ba lɛ, makwɛ nyɛsane lɛ maye.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Ni efã asafoiatsɛ lɛ akɛ ekɛ Paulo ayato, ni ehã ena hejɔlɛ, ni kɛ ehe gbɔmɛi miiba lɛ sɔ̃ɔmɔ loo saramɔ lɛ ekatsi amɛ gbɛ. Paulo yɛ Felike kɛ Drusila hiɛ

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Gbii kplaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, Felike kɛ eŋa Drusila ni ji Yudayoo lɛ ba, ni ehã ayatsɛ Paulo kɛba, ni ebo Kristo nɔhemɔkɛyeli sane lɛ toi be ni Paulo wieɔ he lɛ.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Shi be ni ewieɔ jalɛ kɛ henɔkwɛmɔ kɛ kojomɔ ni baaba lɛ he lɛ, Felike she gbeyei pam, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ yaa fɛɛ da; shi kɛ mina mihe dekã jiŋŋ, matsɛ bo ekoŋŋ.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Shi asaŋ ehiɛ kã nɔ akɛ Paulo aaahã lɛ shika ni eŋmɛɛ ehe; no hewɔ lɛ, etsɛɔ lɛ kpitiokpitio ni ekɛ lɛ bagbaa sane.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Shi afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Porkio Festo ba baye Felike najiaŋ; ni akɛni Felike miisumɔ akɛ efee nɔ ni sa Yudafoi lɛ ahiɛ hewɔ lɛ, eshi Paulo yɛ tsu lɛ mli.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Be ni Festo baye amralo lɛ, enɔ gbii etɛ̃ pɛ ni ejɛ Kaisarea etee Yerusalɛm.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni osɔfonukpai kɛ Yudafoi lɛ anukpai lɛ bafolɔ Paulo naa amɛhã lɛ, ni amɛkpa lɛ fai akɛ

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
