translation_verse: amɛmiitao ni ekwɛ amɛhiɛ ni etsu ni ayaŋɔ Paulo kɛba Yerusalɛm ejaakɛ amɛwo ka koni amɛgbe lɛ yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Festo here nɔ akɛ Paulo yɛ tsuŋ yɛ Kaisarea, shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu etsɛŋ ni ebaaya jɛi.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ ekɛɛ, “Nyɛhãa nyɛteŋ hiɛnaanɔbii lɛ kɛ mi ayaa jɛi ni kɛ sane fɔŋ ko yɛ nuu lɛ he lɛ, ni amɛkɛɛ.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Ni be ni eye aaafee gbii kpaanyɔ loo nyɔŋma yɛ amɛŋɔ̃ɔ lɛ, eyiŋ etee Kaisarea, ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ eyata kojomɔsɛi lɛ nɔ, ni efã akɛ akɛ Paulo aba.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Be ni eba lɛ, Yudafoi ni jɛ Yerusalɛm ba lɛ babɔle lɛ kɛkpe, ni amɛkɛ naafolɔmɔi pii ni mli wa bashwie enɔ, shi amɛnyɛɛɛ naa amɛtsɔ̃ɔ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Paulo jie enaa ekɛɛ “Mitɔ̃ko Yudafoi amla ko nɔ lɛ, asaŋ mitɔ̃ko Sɔlemɔ we lɛ loo Kaisare nɔ hu.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Shi akɛni Festo miisumɔ akɛ efee nɔ ni sa Yudafoi lɛ ahiɛ hewɔ lɛ, ekɛɛ Paulo akɛ, “Oosumɔ akɛ oya Yerusalɛm ni miyakojo bo yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ nɛkɛ saji nɛɛ ahewɔ lo?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Shi Paulo kɛɛ, “Kaisare kojomɔsɛi lɛ hiɛ midamɔ nɛɛ, he ni sa akɛ akojoɔ mi yɛ lɛ. Yudafoi lɛ, mitɔ̃ko amɛnɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni ole jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ miye sane fɔŋ ko ni mifee nɔ ko ni sa gbele lɛ, mikãmãaa gbele; shi kɛ saji ni mɛnɛɛmɛi folɔɔ minaa yɛ he nɛɛ eko eko bɛ mli lɛ, mɔ ko nyɛŋ ekɛ mi awo amɛdɛŋ. Mikɛ misane lɛ miihã Kaisare yeli.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Festo kɛ ajinafoi lɛ hala mli ni ekɛɛ akɛ, “Ni okɛ osane lɛ ehã Kaisare yeli nɛɛ, Kaisare ŋɔɔ nɔŋŋ oootee.” Akɛ Paulo ba Agripa hiɛ

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Ni gbii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike ba Kaisarea ni amɛbaŋa Festo.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Be ni amɛye gbii kplaŋŋ yɛ jɛi lɛ, Festo jaje Paulo sane lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ ni ekɛɛ, “Nuu ko yɛ biɛ ni Felike shi lɛ yɛ tsuŋ,

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: ni be ni mitee Yerusalɛm lɛ, osɔfonukpai lɛ kɛ Yudafoi anukpai lɛ ba miŋɔɔ kɛ ehe naafolɔmɔ ni amɛkpa mi fai akɛ mibu lɛ fɔ;

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: ni mito he mihã amɛ akɛ ebɛ Romabii amla mli akɛ ajɔɔ mɔ ko nɔ ahãa enaaflɔlɔi, ja mɔ ni afolɔ enaa lɛ kɛ mɛi ni yafolɔ enaa lɛ ekpe hiɛ kɛ hiɛ, ni mɔ lɛ ena hegbɛ ejie enaa yɛ sane ni akɛfɔ enɔ lɛ hewɔ dã.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, be ni amɛnaa bakpe shi yɛ biɛ lɛ, mikɛshashaooo shi, shi enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, miyata kojomɔ sɛi lɛ nɔ, ni mifã akɛ akɛ nuu lɛ aba.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Shi be ni enaaflɔlɔi lɛ badãmɔ shi lɛ, amɛkɛ saji ni misusu lɛ ateŋ ekome flo baaa ebafolɔɔɔ enaa,

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: shi moŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɔŋmɔjamɔ he ŋwanejee saji komɛi kɛ Yesu ko ni egbo ni Paulo mã nɔ mi akɛ ehiɛ kã lɛ he saji amɛhiɛ kɛba.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni mileee bɔ ni mafee matao nɛkɛ saji nɛɛ amli hewɔ lɛ, mibi lɛ akɛ eesumɔ akɛ eya Yerusalɛm ni ayaye nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ yɛ jɛi lo?

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni Paulo bi akɛ akɛ lɛ ato ni Kaisare diɛŋtsɛ ayaye esane lɛ hewɔ lɛ, mifã akɛ akɛ lɛ ato kɛyashi beyinɔ ni mahã akɛ lɛ aya Kaisare ŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni Agripa kɛɛ Festo akɛ, “Kulɛ masumɔ akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ manu gbɔmɔ lɛ daaŋ wiemɔ.” Ni ekɛɛ, “Wɔ lɛ obaanu.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Agripa kɛ Bernike wula kiŋkaŋŋ kɛba ni amɛkɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi nukpai kɛ maŋ lɛ mli gbɔmɛi agboi lɛ babote sanetoiboohe lɛ, ni Festo fã, ni akɛ Paulo ba.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni Festo kɛɛ, “Maŋtsɛ Agripa kɛ nyɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni nyɛkɛ wɔ yɔɔ biɛ, nyɛmiina nuu nɛɛ ni Yudafoi asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ bakpa mi fai yɛ Yerusalɛm kɛ biɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbolɔ akɛ esaaa akɛ ehiɔ jeŋ dɔŋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Shi mi lɛ, mina akɛ efeko nɔ ko ni sa gbele. Ni akɛni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hu etu esane lɛ ewo Kaisare dɛŋ hewɔ lɛ, mikpɛ mli akɛ mahã akɛ lɛ aya.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Shi mibɛ sane krɛdɛɛ ko ni kulɛ maŋma mahã Kaisare; no hewɔ hu ni mikɛ lɛ ba nyɛhiɛ nɛɛ, ni titri lɛ bo Maŋtsɛ Agripa ohiɛ, bɔ ni afee ni kɛji atao sane lɛ mli lɛ, mana nɔ ko maŋma.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ efeɔ mi akɛ ejaaa akɛ akɛ gboklɛfonyo ko majeɔ ni atsɔ̃ɔɔ nɔ ni akɛɛ efee.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Maŋtsɛ Agripa, eji miishɛɛ sane kɛhã mi akɛ mibajie minaa ŋmɛnɛ yɛ ohiɛ, yɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Yudafoi lɛ folɔɔ minaa yɛ he lɛ hewɔ,

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ni kɛji amɛmiisumɔ akɛ amɛaaye he odase lɛ, amɛle mi sa kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ akɛ miba mijeŋ yɛ wɔjamɔ lɛ mli kuu ni yɔɔ veveeve fe fɛɛ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ naa akɛ Farisifonyo.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Ni agbɛnɛ lɛ, shi ni Nyɔŋmɔ ewo wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ hewɔ midãmɔ biɛ ni akojoɔ mi nɛɛ.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: No nɔ wɔkutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ hiɛ kã akɛ amɛnine aaashɛ hewɔ ni amɛhiɛ jamɔ mli waa nyɔɔŋ kɛ shwane lɛ. Maŋtsɛ Agripa, nɛkɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ nɛɛ hewɔ Yudafoi lɛ folɔɔ minãa nɛɛ.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Mɛɛba mɔ ni nyɛbuɔ akɛ ebɛ mli akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ teɔ gbohii ashi lɛ?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: ni mina mifee nakai hu yɛ Yerusalɛm, ni akɛni mina hegbɛ yɛ osɔfonukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, miwo mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ ateŋ mɛi pii atsuŋ, ni kɛ abaagbe amɛ lɛ minaa yɛ mli eko,

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: ni mifɔɔ amɛ yiwaa yɛ kpeehei lɛ fɛɛ, ni minyɛɔ amɛnɔ akɛ amɛwie musubɔɔ wiemɔi, ni miye amɛhe sɛkɛ ko ni wa, ni miwaa amɛyi kɛyaa majiasɛɛ.” Paulo gba etsuitsakemɔ he sane (Bɔfoi

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Enɛ mli mihiɛ ni mifã gbɛ kɛmiiya Damasko yɛ osɔfonukpai lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ gbɛŋmɛɛ naa,

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: ni shwane fintiŋŋ, be ni minyiɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Maŋtsɛ, mina la ko ni kpɛɔ fe hulu jɛ ŋwɛi babɔle mi kɛ mɛi ni kɛ mi nyiɛ lɛ.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Ni be ni wɔ fɛɛ wɔgbeegbee shi lɛ, minu gbee ko kɛ mi wie yɛ Hebri wiemɔ lɛ mli akɛ, ‘Saul, Saul, mɛɛba owaa mi yi? Ewa hã bo akɛ ooofã ntia oshi kooloi akpalamɔ tso lɛ naa dade lɛ.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Ni mikɛɛ, ‘Bo namɔŋ, Nuŋtsɔ?’ Ni nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛɛ, ‘Mi Yesu ni owaa lɛ yi lɛ ni.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Shi tee shi ni odamɔ onaji anɔ; ejaakɛ enɛ hewɔ mijie mihe kpo mitsɔ̃ɔ bo nɛɛ, koni mafee bo sɔ̃ɔlɔ kɛ odasefonyo yɛ nibii ni ona kɛ nii ni mibajie mihe kpo matsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ hewɔ lɛ ahe.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Ni majie bo kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ kɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ni mitsuɔ bo kɛya amɛŋɔɔ nɛɛ adɛŋ,

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: ni oyagbele amɛhiŋmɛii, koni amɛkpale kɛjɛ duŋ mli kɛba la he, kɛjɛ abonsam hewalɛ mli kɛba Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔ̃ɔ, ni amɛna amɛhe eshaifaa kɛ gboshinii yɛ mɛi ni akɛ minɔ hemɔkɛyeli efee amɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ateŋ.’ ” Paulo gba enitsumɔ he sane

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: shi moŋ mijaje mitsɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ Damasko lɛ tsutsu, kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ Yerusalɛm kɛ Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ, kɛ jeŋmaji lɛ hu akɛ amɛtsake amɛtsui ni amɛkpale kɛba Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔɔ ni amɛtsu nii ni sa tsuitsakemɔ.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Enɛɛmɛi ahewɔ ni Yudafoi lɛ mɔ mi yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ ni amɛka mi gbee.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ yelikɛbuamɔ naa mikɛdamɔ shi kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔ, ni miyeɔ odase mitsɔ̃ɔ mɛi bibii kɛ mɛi wuji nɛɛ, ni miwieee wiemɔ ko akɛ ja nii ni gbalɔi lɛ kɛ Mose hu ewie akɛ ebaaba lɛ,

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: bɔ ni Kristo lɛ baana amanehulu, bɔ ni ebaatsɔ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ mɔ yɛ gbohiiashitee lɛ mli ni ebaajaje la lɛ he sane etsɔɔ maŋ lɛ kɛ jeŋmaji lɛ.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Be ni Paulo jie enaa nɛkɛ lɛ, Festo kɛ gbee ni wa kɛɛ, “Paulo, sɛkɛ oyeɔ nɛɛ! Woloŋkasemɔ sɔŋŋ ehã oyeɔ sɛkɛ nɛɛ!”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Shi Paulo kɛɛ, “Miyeko sɛkɛ, Festo, lumɔ jurɔ, shi anɔkwale kɛ hiɛshikãmɔ wiemɔi miwieɔ nɛɛ,

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ lɛ ni miwieɔ kɛ ekãa mitsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ le saji nɛɛ amli; ni mikpaaa shi akɛ nibii nɛɛ eko yɛ ni akɛtee lɛ; ejaakɛ jeee teemɔ he ko afee enɛ yɛ.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Nto oheɔ gbalɔi lɛ oyeɔ, Maŋtsɛ Agripa? Mile akɛ oheɔ oyeɔ.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Shi Agripa kɛɛ Paulo akɛ, “Shwɛ fioo ni ohã matsake mijwɛŋmɔ ni matsɔ̃ Kristofonyo.”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Ni Paulo kɛɛ, “Mina ni kulɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hã ba mli akɛ, shwɛ fioo jio, shwɛ pii jio, jeee bo okome kɛkɛ, shi moŋ mɛi fɛɛ ni boɔ mi toi ŋmɛnɛ nɛɛ hu tsɔ̃ tamɔ mi, shi gboklɛi nɛɛ eko kɛkɛ akawo amɛ!”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ amralo lɛ kɛ Bernike kɛ mɛi ni tara shi lɛ te shi,

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: ni amɛtee afã ni amɛyawie yɛ amɛteŋ akɛ, “Nuu nɛɛ efeko nɔ ko ni sa gbele loo tsuŋwoo.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ni Agripa kɛɛ Festo akɛ, “Eji nuu nɛɛ kɛ esane lɛ hãko Kaisare yeli kulɛ aaanyɛ ehe aŋmɛɛ.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Ni be ni akpɛ mli akɛ wɔbaaya Italia lɛ, amɛŋɔ Paulo kɛ gboklɛfoi krokomɛi hu amɛwo asraafoiohaatsɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Yulio ni jɛ Augusto asafo lɛ mli lɛ dɛŋ.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Shi be ni wɔbote Adramitio lɛlɛ ko ni baafã kɛyatsɔ̃ Asia ŋshɔnaa maji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli lɛ, wɔfã, ni Aristarko, Makedonianyo ni jɛ Tesalonika lɛ fata wɔhe.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ wɔyamã Sidon, ni akɛni Yulio hiɛ Paulo dɔdɔɔdɔ hewɔ lɛ, eŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ akɛ eya eshieŋtsɛmɛi lɛ aŋɔɔ ni eyajɔɔ ehe.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Ni be ni wɔfo Kilikia kɛ Pamfilia ŋshɔ lɛ, wɔbamã Mira yɛ Likia.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Ni asraafoiohaatsɛ lɛ na Aleksandria lɛlɛ ko yɛ jɛi ni miiya Italia, ni ejie wɔ ewo no mli.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Wɔnyiɛ blɛoo gbii pii, ni ekpakpa ko dani wɔshɛ Knido ŋlɛnɔ, ni akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eŋmɛɛɛ wɔ gbɛ hewɔ lɛ, wɔsharã Salmone meo lɛ kɛtsɔ̃ Kreta shishigbɛ;

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: ni ekpakpa ko dani wɔfo mli yɛ jɛi kɛba he ko ni atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ Lɛji adaamɔhe Fɛɛfɛo ni bɛŋkɛ Lasea maŋ lɛ.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ wɔfite be pii, ni akɛni buadayeli be lɛ hu eho momo hewɔ lɛ; ŋshɔhiɛnyiɛmɔ efee gbeyei. Hewɔ lɛ Paulo wo amɛ ŋaa

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi, mina akɛ amanehulu kɛ nilaajemɔ pii baaba gbɛfãa nɛɛ mli, ni jeee lɛlɛ mli nii lɛ kɛ lɛlɛ lɛ kɛkɛ hiɛ baakpãtã, shi moŋ wɔwala diɛŋtsɛ hu.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Shi asraafoiohaatsɛ lɛ heɔ kudɔɔtsɛ lɛ kɛ lɛlɛtsɛ lɛ eyeɔ fe wiemɔi ni Paulo wieɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Ni akɛni Lɛji adaamɔhe Fɛɛfɛo lɛ kãaa shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni aaanyɛ aye fɛ̃ibe lɛ yɛ jɛi hewɔ lɛ, amɛteŋ mɛi pii wo ŋaa akɛ afã yɛ jɛi koni akwɛ akɛ aaanyɛ ashɛ Foinike ni ji Kreta Lɛji adaamɔhe ni kwɛɔ wuoyi-anai kɛ kooyi-anai gbɛ lɛ lo, koni aye fɛ̃ibe lɛ yɛ jɛi. Ahum fã yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Shi be ni wuoyigbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɔ̃i tswaa nyrakee lɛ, efee amɛ akɛ nɔ ni amɛtaoɔ lɛ eba mli, ni amɛfã kɛsharã Kreta he kpaakpa.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Shi etsɛɛɛ kɛkɛ ni ahum ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ kooyi-bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fã kɛbakpee amɛ.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Ni be ni eta lɛlɛ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ekpee lɛ, wɔhã ekpala.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ni be ni wɔkɛ foi sharã ŋshɔkpɔ fioo ni atsɛɔ lɛ Kauda lɛ meo lɛ, ekpakpa ko dani wɔnyɛ bonto lɛ wɔmɔ.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: Amɛwo lɛ, ni amɛkɛ kpãi fimɔ lɛlɛ lɛ, ni akɛni amɛmiishe gbeyei akɛ aleenɔ amɛaagbee shia nɔ hewɔ lɛ, amɛkpa abalaa lɛ, ni amɛkpala kɛkɛ.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni ahum lɛ miitswa wɔ gbeyeigbeyei naakpa hewɔ lɛ, enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, amɛ jie lɛlɛ lɛ mli nii lɛ eko amɛshwie;

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: ni gbi ni ji etɛ̃ nɔ lɛ wɔkɛ wɔ diɛŋtsɛ wɔniji jie lɛlɛ he nibii lɛ wɔshwie.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Wɔnaaa hulu loo ŋulamii gbii pii ni asaŋ jeee ahum fioo tswaa kɛkpeɔ wɔ lɛ, hewɔ lɛ agbɛnɛ wɔhiɛ kãaa wala nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Shi be ni gbii pii eho ni wɔyeko nɔ ko lɛ, Paulo te shi edamɔ amɛteŋ ni ekɛɛ, “Ataamɛi, kulɛ esa akɛ nyɛboɔ mi toi ni akafã yɛ Kreta ni wɔbana amanehulu ni nibii laaje nɛkɛ.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Ni agbɛnɛ hu miiwo nyɛ ŋaa akɛ nyɛna tsui, ejaakɛ nyɛteŋ mɔ ko yiwala tɔŋ, ja lɛlɛ lɛ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ nyɔɔŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ nɔ ni mi ji kɛ mɔ hu ni misɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ bɔfo badamɔ mimasɛi

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: ni ekɛɛ, ‘Kaashe gbeyei, Paulo! Ja akɛ bo yadãmɔ Kaisare hiɛ kɛ̃; ni naa, Nyɔŋmɔ eŋɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni kɛ bo yɔɔ lɛlɛ lɛ mli lɛ eke bo.’

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Hewɔ lɛ nyɛnaa tsui, Ataamɛi, ejaakɛ miheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ miyeɔ akɛ bɔ ni abakɛɛ mi lɛ, nakai baaba mli.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Shi bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, wɔɔyasha ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ kɛ̃.”

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Ni amɛfolɔ sɛkɛi lɛ amɛwo ŋshɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛfɛne kudɔɔ lɛ he kpãi lɛ hu, ni amɛshi hiɛgbɛ abalaa lɛ kɛkpee kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ, ni amɛtsɔ̃ eyi amɛmã shianɔgbɛ.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Shi be ni amlakui lɛ tao foi aje yɛ lɛlɛ lɛ mli ni amɛkwa amɛshi bonto lɛ amɛma ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ tamɔ nɔ ni sɛkɛi amɛyaaŋmɛ yɛ lɛlɛ lɛ yitsogbɛ lɛ,

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛshe gbeyei akɛ aleenɔ wɔɔyagbee tɛsai anɔ, ni amɛŋmɛ sɛkɛi ejwɛ yɛ lɛlɛ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ, ni amɛmiishwe ni je atsɛre.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Paulo kɛɛ asraafoiohaatsɛ lɛ kɛ asraafoi lɛ akɛ “Kɛji mɛnɛɛmɛi ehiii lɛlɛ lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ anyɛŋ nyɛyiwala ahere.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni asraafoi lɛ folɔ bonto lɛ he taŋkpei lɛ, ni amɛhã eyagbee shi.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, miikpa nyɛ fai ni nyɛye nii ejaakɛ no aaahã nyɛyi ana wala, ejaakɛ nyɛteŋ mɔ ko yitsɔi kome ejeŋ eyiteŋ enyɔŋ shi.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Ni be ni ekɛɛ nakai lɛ, ekɔ aboloo, ni eda Nyɔŋmɔ shi yɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛ, ni ekumɔ mli ebɔ̃i yeli.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛna tsui, ni amɛ hu amɛye nii.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛye nii ni amɛtɔrɔ lɛ, amɛshɛrɛ abele ni amɛwo lɛ amɛshwie ŋshɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛhã lɛlɛ lɛ fee huyɛhuyɛ. Lɛlɛ lɛ sha shi

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Ni be ni je tsɛre lɛ amɛna akɛ amɛleee shikpɔŋ lɛ, shi amɛna ble ko kɛ enaa shia, ni amɛto amɛyiŋ akɛ, kɛ amɛaanyɛ lɛ, amɛaahã lɛlɛ lɛ ayasha shi yɛ jɛi.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni amɛyagbee ŋshɔi enyɔ alɛwu nɔ hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ lɛlɛ lɛ yasha shi; ni eyitsogbɛ lɛ yatsɛkɛ shi shiŋŋ, shi esɛɛgbɛ lɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ anaawalɛ lɛ jwara lɛ.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Shi asraafoi lɛ ayiŋtoo ji akɛ amɛaagbe gboklɛfoi lɛ, koni amɛteŋ mɔ ko akasere kɛmiiya ni ejo foi.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni asraafoiohaatsɛ lɛ taoɔ Paulo yiwala ehere hewɔ lɛ, etsi amɛyiŋtoo lɛ naa, ni efã akɛ mɛi ni le seremɔ lɛ tsutsu atu agbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛya shikpɔŋ;

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: shi mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi abumɔ ŋmoŋmolo nɔ, ni mɛi komɛi hu abumɔ lɛlɛ koi lɛ anɔ. Bɔ ni fee ni mɛi lɛ fɛɛ yashɛ shikpɔŋ shweshweeshwe ji no.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Ni be ni wɔje mli sɔŋŋ lɛ, no dani wɔbale akɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ gbɛi ji Malita.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Jɛibii lɛ fee wɔ ejurɔ pii, ejaakɛ amɛshɛre la, ni amɛhere wɔ fɛɛ tswɛm hiɛmɛɛ yɛ nunɛmɔ babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Shi be ni Paulo bua lai ŋmɛŋmlɛbii anaa ni ekɛyawo la lɛ mli lɛ, shinɔ ko jɛ la grigri lɛ mli kpɛtɛ enine he.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Be ni jɛibii lɛ na kooloo lɛ kpɛtɛ enine he lɛ, amɛkɛɛkɛɛ amɛhe akɛ, “Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, nɛkɛ nuu nɛɛ awuyelɔ ni, ni ahere eyiwala kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli moŋ nɛ, shi oweletɔɔ eŋmɛ̃ɛɛ lɛ gbɛ ni eyi ana wala.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Ni ehwanya kooloo lɛ ewo la lɛ mli, ni eyeee lɛ awui ko.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Amɛhiɛ kã nɔ akɛ eeefuufuu loo eeetswa shi egbo trukaa. Shi be ni amɛkwɛ aahu ni amɛna akɛ nɔ ko srɔto ko efeee lɛ lɛ, amɛtsake amɛjwɛŋmɔ ni amɛkɛɛ akɛ nyɔŋmɔ ko ji lɛ.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ onukpa ni atsɛɔ lɛ Publio lɛ yɛ shikpɔji yɛ jɛi niiaŋ; gbɔmɔ nɛɛ here wɔ hiɛmɛɛ ni ekɛ tsuijurɔ fee wɔ gbɔ gbii etɛ̃ sɔŋŋ.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Eba mli akɛ Publio tsɛ kã shi kɛ atridii kɛ fɔ kɛ la wamɔ; ni Paulo tee eŋɔɔ, ni esɔle ekɛ eniji shwie enɔ ni etsa lɛ.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Be ni afee enɛ lɛ, mɛi krokomɛi hu ni he yeɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ba, ni atsa amɛ.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Ni amɛ hu amɛwo wɔhiɛ nyam babaoo, ni be ni wɔfã yɛ jɛi lɛ, amɛhã wɔ nibii ni he hiaa wɔ. Paulo jɛ Malita kɛtee Roma

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Ni nyɔji etɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ wɔyabote Aleksandria lɛlɛ ko ni ekadimɔ ji Dioskurioi ni ebaye fɛ̃ibe lɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli, ni wɔfã kɛtee.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Wɔyadamɔ Sirakusa ni wɔhi jɛi gbii etɛ̃.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Ni wɔjɛ jɛi lɛ, wɔlɔgɔ shi kɛba Regio; ni enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, be ni wuoyigbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔ̃i tswaa lɛ, wɔyi mli, ni gbi ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ wɔshɛ Puteoli.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Jɛi wɔbana nyɛmimɛi komɛi yɛ; ni amɛkpa wɔ fai akɛ wɔkɛ amɛ ahi shi gbii kpawo. Kɛkɛ ni wɔyashɛ Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ nu wɔhe, ni amɛbakpee wɔ yɛ Apio jara nɔ kɛ Gbɔiatoohei Etɛ̃ lɛ; ni be ni Paulo na amɛ lɛ, eda Nyɔŋmɔ shi ni etsui nyɔ emli.

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Ni be ni wɔbashɛ Roma lɛ, aŋmɛ Paulo gbɛ akɛ ekome ehi shi kɛ asraafonyo kome ni miibu ehe. Paulo shiɛ yɛ Roma

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Gbii etɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ Paulo hã atsɛ Yudafoi lɛ anukpai ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛbakpe; ni be ni amɛnaa ebakpe shi lɛ, ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Ataamɛi kɛ anyɛmimɛi, mitɔ̃ko maŋ lɛ loo wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ akusumi lɛ anɔ; kɛ̃lɛ akɛ mi wo Romabii lɛ adɛŋ yɛ Yerusalɛm akɛ gboklɛfonyo.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Be ni amɛtao misane lɛ mli lɛ, amɛsumɔ akɛ amɛŋmɛɛ mihe, ejaakɛ sane ko bɛ mihe kwraa ni sa gbele.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Shi akɛni Yudafoi lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, efi akɛ maŋɔ misane lɛ mahã Kaisare yeli, shi jeee akɛ miyɛ nɔ ko ni mikɛbaafolɔ mimaŋ lɛ naa.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ hewɔ mitsɛ nyɛ kɛba koni mana nyɛ ni mikɛ nyɛ awie ejaakɛ Israel hiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ hewɔ ni awo mi nɛkɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ nɛɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Shi amɛkɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Wɔ lɛ wɔnako woji komɛi kɛjɛko Yudea yɛ ohe, ni asaŋ nyɛmimɛi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko bako biɛ ebagbako ohe sane ko, ni mɔ ko ebawieko ohe wiemɔ fɔŋ ko.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Shi wɔmiisumɔ akɛ wɔle ojwɛŋmɔ, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ kuu nɛɛ wɔle akɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ awieɔ ashiɔ.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Ni be ni amɛto lɛ gbi lɛ, amɛteŋ mɛi pii ba eŋɔɔ yɛ etoohe lɛ, ni kɛjɛ leebi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ, ejaje Nyɔŋmɔ maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he sane etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ni eye he odase faŋŋ, ni ejɛ Mose Mla lɛ kɛ gbalɔi lɛ amli etao ni amɛyiŋ atsɔ̃ kɛba Yesu gbɛfaŋ.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Ni mɛi komɛi he wiemɔi ni ewie lɛ amɛye, shi mɛi komɛi hu heee yeee.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ni akɛni amɛyakpãaa gbee hewɔ lɛ, amɛyiŋ amɛtee be ni Paulo wie wiemɔ nɛɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ ni Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ wie yɛ gbalɔ Yesaia naa

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: akɛ, ‘Yaa maŋ nɛɛ ŋɔɔ ni oyakɛɛ, nu lɛ nyɛbaanu nɛ, shi nyɛnaŋ shishi. Ni na lɛ nyɛbaana nɛ, shi nyɛyoŋ sɛɛ.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ maŋ nɛɛ tsui ekpliŋ, ni amɛtoi wa kɛ ninumɔ, ni amɛmiamia amɛhiŋmɛii, koni amɛkana kɛ amɛhiŋmɛii ni amɛkanu kɛ amɛtoii. Ni amɛtsui hu akana shishi, ni amɛkpale ni mitsa amɛ.’

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Ni be ni ewie wiemɔ nɛɛ lɛ, Yudafoi lɛ yi mli amɛtee, ni amɛjejee ŋwane babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ.]

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Ni Paulo hi shĩa ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyaŋɔ mli afii enyɔ ni ehereɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni baa eŋɔɔ lɛ,

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: ni eshiɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ Maŋtsɛyeli lɛ he sane lɛ, ni ekɛ ekãa fɛɛ jajeɔ Nuŋtsɔ Yesu Kristo he saji lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etsiii lɛ gbɛ.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Wolo nɛɛ jɛ mi Paulo, Yesu Kristo tsulɔ kɛ bɔfo ni atsɛ lɛ ni ajie lɛ ato ahã Nyɔŋmɔ Sanekpakpa lɛ, dɛŋ.

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: Sanekpakpa nɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ewo he shi eto momo yɛ egbalɔi lɛ anaa yɛ Ŋmalɛi Krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ amli,

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: EBi nɛɛ, hetsemɔ Mumɔ lɛ naa lɛ, atsɔ̃ gbohiiashitee lɛ nɔ ajie lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ yɛ hewalɛ mli akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Bi ni ji Yesu Kristo wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: Enɔ mitsɔ̃ mina dromɔ kɛ bɔfo nitsumɔ koni mihã jeŋmaji lɛ fɛɛ abo hemɔkɛyeli lɛ toi, yɛ egbɛi lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Jeŋmaji nɛɛ ateŋ nyɛ Romabii hu nyɛyɔɔ. Nyɛ mɛi ni atsɛ akɛ nyɛbafee Yesu Kristo mɛi lɛ.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: Miiŋma nyɛ mɛi ni Nyɔŋmɔ sumɔɔ ni etsɛ nyɛ ni nyɛ ji mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi ni yɔɔ Roma lɛ fɛɛ, dromɔ kɛ hejɔlɛ ni jɛ wɔTsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ kɛ Nuŋtsɔ Yesu Kristo dɛŋ lɛ ahã nyɛ! Faikpamɔ kɛ shidaa

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, miitsɔ̃ Yesu Kristo nɔ miida miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ shi yɛ nyɛ fɛɛ nyɛhewɔ, akɛ agbaa nyɛhemɔkɛyeli lɛ he sane yɛ je lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ midasefonyo ji Nyɔŋmɔ, mɔ ni misɔmɔɔ yɛ mimumɔ mli yɛ eBi lɛ Sanekpakpa lɛ shiɛmɔ mli lɛ, akɛ mifɔ̃ko nyɛ kaimɔ dã,

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: ni mikpaa fai daa yɛ misɔlemɔi amli, akɛ aleenɔ, Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔ naa lɛ wɔsɛɛ ko lɛ gbɛ aaaja ahã mi ni maba nyɛŋɔɔ lo.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ miishwe akɛ mana nyɛ, koni mikɛ mumɔŋ dromɔ keenii lɛ eko abahã nyɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akɛwaje nyɛ,

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: no ji akɛ, atsɔ̃ nyɛhemɔkɛyeli nɔ ashɛje mimii, ni atsɔ̃ mi hu minɔ lɛ nɔ ashɛje nyɛmii.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Shi anyɛmimɛi, miisumɔ akɛ nyɛle akɛ mifɔɔ miyiŋtoo akɛ maba nyɛŋɔɔ, koni mibana yibii komɛi yɛ nyɛ hu nyɛteŋ, tamɔ mina yɛ jeŋmaji krokomɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, miishwe akɛ nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ Roma lɛ hu, mabajaje Sanekpakpa lɛ matsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ. Sanekpakpa lɛ ji Nyɔŋmɔ hewalɛ

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mihiɛ gbooo Kristo Sanekpakpa lɛ he, ejaakɛ eji Nyɔŋmɔ hewalɛ ni akɛhereɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni heɔ yeɔ lɛ yiwala, Yudanyo lɛ tsutsu kɛ Helanyo hu.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ no mli ajieɔ Nyɔŋmɔ jalɛ kpo yɛ, kɛjɛɔ hemɔkɛyeli mli kɛyaa hemɔkɛyeli mli, tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ akɛ, “Shi jalɔ ni tsɔ̃ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ lɛ yi aaana wala.” Fɔ ni gbɔmɛi eye

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ajieɔ Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛbaa gbɔmɛi ni kɛ nishaianii tsĩɔ anɔkwale lɛ gbɛ lɛ amusubɔɔ kɛ nishaianii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ,

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ he nii ni aaanyɛ ale lɛ yɛ faŋŋ hã amɛ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ejie etsɔ̃ɔ amɛ faŋŋ.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ehenii ni anaaa ni ji enaanɔ hewalɛ kɛ nyɔŋmɔ ni eji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, kɛjɛ jeŋbɔɔ mli beebe lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ enii ni efee lɛ anɔ ayɔseɔ ni anaa faŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɛ naajiemɔ ko;

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ amɛle Nyɔŋmɔ moŋ, shi amɛwooo ehiɛ nyam akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ, ni amɛdaaa lɛ shi hu, shi amɛfee shwɛm yɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔi amli, ni amɛtsui ni kɔɔɔ sane sɛɛ lɛ ewo duŋ.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: Amɛtsɛ amɛhe nilelɔi, shi amɛtsɔ̃mɔ kwashiai,

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: ni Nyɔŋmɔ ni gbooo lɛ anunyam lɛ amɛtsake amɛhã gbɔmɔ ni gboɔ lɛ subaŋ henɔ ko kɛ loofɔji kɛ kooloi naji ejwɛjwɛɛjwɛtsɛmɛi kɛ waamɔnii anɔ.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: No hewɔ hu ni Nyɔŋmɔ ŋmɛɛ amɛhe ehã muji nitsumɔi yɛ amɛtsuiiaŋ akɔnɔi lɛ anaa, bɔ ni afee ni amɛshwie amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ ahiɛ shi yɛ amɛteaŋ.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: Amɛŋɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ anɔkwale lɛ amɛtsakeɔ amale, ni amɛjaa ni amɛsɔ̃mɔɔ bɔɔnɔ lɛ yɛ bɔlɔ lɛ najiaŋ, bɔlɔ ni ajɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa naanɔ lɛ! Amen.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ Nyɔŋmɔ ŋmɛɛ amɛhe ehã hiɛgbejianii ahe hiɛdɔɔ lɛ; ejaakɛ adebɔɔ naanyobɔɔ ni ato lɛ, amɛyei lɛ etsake hiɛ ehã nɔ ni kɛ adebɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo eyaaa;

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: ni nakai nɔŋŋ amɛhii lɛ hu eshi amɛyei lɛ asɛɛ, ni amɛkɛ akɔnɔ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe sɛɛ, ni hii kɛ hii tsuɔ hiɛgbejianii, ni amɛna amɛtɔ̃mɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni sa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni amɛbuuu akɛ esa akɛ amɛleɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ hu ŋmɛɛ amɛhe ehã jwɛŋmɔ ni esaaa koni amɛfee nibii ni esaaa;

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: mɛi ni eyimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ nii ni ejaaa gbɛ fɛɛ, efɔŋfeemɔ, hiɛjoomɔ, nifɔɔjianii; amɛyimɔ tɔ kɛ hetsɛ̃, awuyeli, bei, shishiumɔ, nyɛɛ;

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: amɛyeɔ amɛhe osheku, Nyɔŋmɔnyɛlɔi, mɛi ni hiɛ esɔɔɔ mɔ, hetsɔ̃ɔlɔi, shwãlɔi, nɔfɔŋ he ŋaatsɔlɔi, fɔlɔi anɔtoigbolɔi,

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: mɛi ni bɛ henilee, kpãŋmɔ mli kulɔi, mɛi ni edɔɔɔ mɔ he, mɛi ni enaaa mɔbɔ.

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: Amɛle Nyɔŋmɔ mla lɛ krɛdɛɛ nɛ, akɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nakai nii lɛ sa gbele, shi kɛ̃lɛ jeee feemɔ kɛkɛ amɛfeɔ, shi moŋ amɛnaa mɛi ni tsuɔ nakai nii lɛ ahe miishɛɛ hu.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, bo, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kojoɔ lɛ, obɛ naajiemɔ ko; ejaakɛ be mli ni okojoɔ mɔ kroko lɛ, oobu bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe fɔ; ejaakɛ bo ni okojoɔ lɛ otsuɔ nakai nii lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Shi wɔle akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kojomɔ ni baa mɛi ni tsuɔ nakai nii lɛ anɔ lɛ ja.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Bo gbɔmɔ ni okojoɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ ni ofeɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ, ani osusuɔ akɛ bo lɛ ohe aaaje Nyɔŋmɔ kojomɔ lɛ mli?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Aloo obuuu emlihilɛ kɛ eyishiŋmɛɛ kɛ etsuishitoo babaoo lɛ, ni oleee akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mlihilɛ lɛ gbɛ etsɔ̃ɔ bo kɛya tsuitsakemɔ mli?

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Shi okɛ otsuiwalɛ kɛ ohe ni oshwaaa lɛ miitĩa mlifu naa ohã ohe oto Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu gbi lɛ, nɔ nɔ ni ebaatsɔ̃ ejie ejalɛ kojomɔ lɛ kpo lɛ;

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: lɛ ebaawo mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nyɔ̃mɔ bɔ ni sa enitsumɔi lɛ:

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: mɛi ni kɛ tsuishiŋmɛɛ hiɛɔ ekpakpafeemɔ mli ni amɛtaoɔ anunyam kɛ woo kɛ shihilɛ ni fiteŋ lɛ, eeehã amɛ naanɔ wala;

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: shi mɛi ni sumɔɔ bei ni amɛbooo anɔkwale lɛ toi, shi amɛboɔ nii ni ejaaa moŋ toi lɛ, amɛnɔ ji mlifu kɛ mlila.

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Amanehulu kɛ hejaramɔ aaaba gbɔmɔ fɛɛ gbɔmɔ ni tsuɔ nifɔɔjianii lɛ susuma nɔ, Yudanyo tsutsu kɛ Helanyo hu;

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: shi anunyam kɛ woo kɛ hejɔlɛ aaaba mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni tsuɔ nikpakpai anii lɛ nɔ, Yudanyo tsutsu kɛ Helanyo hu.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kwɛɛɛ gbɔmɛi ahiɛiaŋ.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ mɛi abɔ ni bɛ Mla lɛ ni amɛfee esha lɛ amɛaalaaje akɛ mɛi ni bɛ Mla; ni mɛi abɔ ni yɔɔ Mla lɛ shishi ni amɛfee esha lɛ, Mla lɛ nɔŋŋ akɛaakojo amɛ.

english_verse: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ jeee Mla lɛ nulɔi ji jalɔi yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ, shi moŋ Mla lɛ nɔyelɔi ji mɛi ni aaabu amɛ akɛ jalɔi.

english_verse: Some people naturally obey the Law's commands, even though they don't have the Law.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛ jeŋmajiaŋbii ni bɛ Mla lɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔŋ su lɛ tsuɔ Mla lɛ naanii lɛ, amɛ ni amɛbɛ Mla lɛ amɛ ji mla hã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english_verse: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
translation_verse: Amɛnifeemɔnii tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ aŋma Mla lɛ nitsumɔ lɛ yɛ amɛtsuii amli, ni amɛhenilee hu yeɔ odase, ni amɛjwɛŋmɔ folɔɔ amɛnaa kɛ amɛfee nɔ ni ehiii aloo ejieɔ amɛnaa kɛ amɛfee nɔ ni hi.

english_verse: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
translation_verse: Enɛ baaba mli gbi nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaatsɔ̃ Yesu Kristo nɔ akojo gbɔmɛi ateemɔŋnii lɛ yɛ misanekpakpa lɛ naa lɛ. Yudafoi kɛ Mla lɛ

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji bo lɛ atsɛɔ bo Yudanyo, ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ Mla lɛ nɔ, ni oshwãa ofɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ,

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: ni ole esuɔmɔnaanii lɛ, ni ole nii ni hi, ejaakɛ ajɛ Mla lɛ mli atsɔ̃ɔ bo,

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: ni obuɔ ohe akɛ oji shwilafoi agbɛtsɔ̃ɔlɔ kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ duŋ mli lɛ ala,

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: kɛ mɛi ni leee nii atsɔselɔ kɛ abifabii atsɔ̃ɔlɔ, ejaakɛ oyɛ nilee kɛ anɔkwale he mfoniri kɛjɛ Mla lɛ mli,

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: bo ni otsɔ̃ɔ mɛi krokomɛi anii lɛ, otsɔ̃ɔɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe nii? Oshiɛɔ akɛ akaju, shi ojuɔ;

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: okɛɔ akɛ akafite gbãlã, shi ofiteɔ gbãlã; ohiɔ amãgãi, shi ojuɔ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ nii.

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Bo ni okɛ Mla lɛ shwãa lɛ okɛ Mla lɛ nɔtɔmɔ lɛ gbeɔ Nyɔŋmɔ he guɔ.

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ aŋma akɛ, “Nyɛhewɔ lɛ awieɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbɛi lɛ he musubɔɔ wiemɔi yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ.”

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ oyeɔ Mla lɛ nɔ lɛ, kulɛ ketiafoo he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ; shi kɛ ofee ohe Mla lɛ nɔtɔ̃lɔ lɛ, oketiafoo lɛ etsɔ̃ foo.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji foolɔ lɛ yeɔ Mla lɛ gbɛnai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ani abuŋ efoo lɛ akɛ ketiafoo?

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: Ni heloo gbɛfaŋ foolɔ lɛ ni yeɔ Mla lɛ nɔ lɛ, aaakojo bo ni ohiɛ Mla ni aŋma lɛ ni afo bo ketia hu ni ofee ohe mlatɔ̃lɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ jeee mɔ ni anaa lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ akɛ Yudanyo doo ji Yudanyo, ni asaŋ jeee nɔ ni anaa yɛ kpo nɔ gbɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtso he ji ketiafoo;

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: shi moŋ mɔ ni ji Yudanyo yɛ mligbɛ lɛ ji Yudanyo, ni tsui mli ketiafoo ji nɔ ni atsɔ̃ Mumɔ lɛ nɔ afo, shi jeee Mla lɛ nɔ, ni eyijiemɔ lɛ jɛɛɛ gbɔmɛi aŋɔɔ, shi moŋ Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔɔ ejɛɔ.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: Belɛ agbɛnɛ, mɛni Yudanyo kɛfe mɛi krokomɛi mɔ? Aloo mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ ketiafoo mli?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Efa yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ji akɛ atu Nyɔŋmɔ wiemɔi lɛ awo amɛdɛŋ.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Shi kɛ mɛi komɛi heee yeee lɛ, mɛni? Ani he ni amɛheee amɛyeee lɛ aaahã Nyɔŋmɔ anɔkwayeli lɛ afee yaka?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Dabida! Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛ gbɔmɔ fɛɛ gbɔmɔ fee amalelɔ po, lɛ lɛ ja efee anɔkwafo tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni afee ni ana akɛ osane ja yɛ owiemɔi lɛ amli, ni oye kunim yɛ okojomɔ lɛ mli.”

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Shi kɛji wɔja ni wɔjaaa lɛ hãa Nyɔŋmɔ jalɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, te wɔɔkɛɛ tɛŋŋ? Aso Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ ejaaa kɛji emlifu ba wɔnɔ lɛ? .

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Dabida! Ejaakɛ kɛji nakai ni lɛ, te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaakojo je lɛ?

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ mimalemɔ lɛ hãa Nyɔŋmɔ anɔkwale lɛ faa kɛtekeɔ nɔ hã enunyam lɛ, mɛɛba mɔ ni akã he akojoɔ mi akɛ eshafeelɔ?

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Ani jeee tamɔ bɔ ni afoɔ sane afɔ̃ɔ wɔnɔ ni mɛi komɛi kɛɔ yɛ wɔhe akɛ wɔkɛɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔfea efɔŋ koni ekpakpa aba” lɛ? Nakai mɛi lɛ afɔbuu lɛ ja pɛ. Jalɔ ko bɛ

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: Belɛ mɛni? Ani wɔ Yudafoi wɔhi fe mɛi krokomɛi? Jeee nakai kwraa; ejaakɛ wɔfolɔ Yudafoi kɛ Helabii fɛɛ anaa momo akɛ amɛfɛɛ amɛyɛ esha shishi,

english_verse: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
translation_verse: tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ akɛ, “Jalɔ ko bɛ, mɔ kome folo bɛ;

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: nilelɔ ko bɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni taoɔ Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ.

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Amɛ fɛɛ amɛgba afã, amɛ blublu amɛhiii amɛhãaa nɔ ko; Mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni feɔ ekpakpa, mɔ kome folo bɛ.

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Gbonyobu ni agbele naa ji amɛsɛ̃ lɛ; amɛkɛ amɛlilɛii shishiuɔ mɔ, shikpãi anaa ebɔɔ yɛ amɛnaabu.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: Loomɔ kɛ joomɔ eyi amɛdaaŋ obɔ̃.

english_verse: These people quickly become violent.
translation_verse: Amɛhe yɛ oya kɛ láshishwiemɔ;

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: hiɛkpãtãmɔ kɛ awerɛhoo yɛ amɛgbɛi anɔ.

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: Ni hejɔlɛ gbɛ lɛ amɛleee.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishemɔ ko bɛ amɛhiɛ.”

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ wɔle akɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Mla lɛ kɛɔ lɛ, mɛi ni yɔɔ Mla lɛ shishi lɛ ekɛwieɔ, koni mɔ ko mɔ ko akana naabu, ni jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ aye fɔ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ adamɔŋ Mla lɛ nitsumɔ nɔ abuŋ gbɔmɔ ko gbɔmɔ ko bem yɛ ehiɛ; ejaakɛ Mla nɔ atsɔ̃ɔ aleɔ nɔ ni ji esha. Jalɛ ni jɛ hemɔkɛyeli mli lɛ

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ lɛ ashi Mla lɛ sɛɛ ajie Nyɔŋmɔ jalɛ lɛ kpo faŋŋ, ni no he odase Mla lɛ kɛ gbalɔi lɛ yeɔ;

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: no ji Nyɔŋmɔ jalɛ ni atsɔ̃ɔ Yesu Kristo nɔ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ akɛhãa mɛi fɛɛ ni heɔ yeɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ srɔto ko bɛ;

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ mɛi fɛɛ efee esha, ni Nyɔŋmɔ anunyam lɛ ebɔ amɛ,

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: ni akɛ edromɔ lɛ buɔ amɛ bem yaka kɛtsɔ̃ɔ kpɔ̃mɔ ni yɔɔ Kristo Yesu mli lɛ nɔ.

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ mɛni nɔ wɔshwãa wɔfɔ̃ɔ? Nɔ ko bɛ. Mɛɛ Mla nɔ atsɔ̃? Nitsumɔi anɔ lɛ nɔ lo? Dabi, shi hemɔkɛyeli mla lɛ nɔ moŋ atsɔ̃.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, wɔbuɔ akɛ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ atsɔ̃ɔ abuɔ gbɔmɔ bem, shi jeee Mla nitsumɔi anɔ.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Aloo Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Yudafoi kɛkɛ aNyɔŋmɔ ni? Ani jeee jeŋmaji lɛ hu aNyɔŋmɔ ni? Hɛɛ, jeŋmaji lɛ hu aNyɔŋmɔ

english_verse: There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith.
translation_verse: akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kome ni, ni hemɔkɛyeli naa ebuɔ ketiafoo bem, ni esaa edamɔɔ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ ebuɔ foo bem lɛ.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Belɛ wɔmiitsɔ̃ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ wɔhã Mla lɛ afee yaka lo? Dabida, shi wɔkɛmiima Mla lɛ nɔ mi moŋ.

english_verse: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
translation_verse: Belɛ mɛni wɔɔkɛɛ akɛ Abraham ni ji wɔtsɛ yɛ heloo gbɛfaŋ lɛ na mɔ?

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: Kɛ nitsumɔi anɔ adamɔ abu lɛ bem lɛ, kulɛ eyɛ shwãa nɔ, shi belɛ jeee yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.

english_verse: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ te ŋmalɛ lɛ kɛɔ tɛŋŋ? “Ni Abraham he Nyɔŋmɔ eye, ni abu no jalɛ ahã lɛ.”

english_verse: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
translation_verse: Mɔ ni tsuɔ nii lɛ, abuuu enyɔmɔwoo lɛ akɛ dromɔ nɔ ko, shi moŋ akɛ egbɛnaa nɔ ko.

english_verse: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
translation_verse: Shi mɔ ni jeee nii etsuɔ, shi eheɔ mɔ ni buɔ eshafeelɔ bem lɛ nɔ eyeɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ buɔ ehemɔkɛyeli lɛ akɛ jalɛ ehãa lɛ.

english_verse: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
translation_verse: Tamɔ bɔ ni David hu kɛɔ akɛ ajɔɔ gbɔmɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ shiɔ nitsumɔi asɛɛ ebuɔ lɛ jalɔ lɛ,

english_verse: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
translation_verse: Ajɔɔ nuu ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ ebuuu ehe esha lɛ ehãaa lɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ nɛkɛ jɔɔmɔ nɛɛ, mɛi ni afo amɛ ketia kɛkɛ anɔ ni, aloo foolɔi lɛ hu anɔ̃ŋ? Ejaakɛ wɔkɛɔ akɛ abu hemɔkɛyeli lɛ akɛ jalɛ ahã Abraham.

english_verse: But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ te abu lɛ jalɛ ahã lɛ tɛŋŋ? Be ni afo lɛ ketia lɛ aloo be mli ni afoko lɛ ketia lɛ? Jeee be mli ni afo lɛ ketia, shi moŋ be ni eji foolɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Ni enine shɛ ketiafoo okadi lɛ nɔ akɛ jalɛ naasɔomɔnɔ ni akɛsɔo ehemɔkɛyeli ni ena be mli ni eji foolɔ beebe lɛ naa, ni efee mɛi fɛɛ ni heɔ yeɔ be ni amɛ ji foolɔi lɛ atsɛ, ni abu hemɔkɛyeli ahã amɛ hu akɛ jalɛ;

english_verse: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
translation_verse: ni asaŋ efee ketiafolɔi atsɛ hu ehã mɛi ni amɛjeee ketiafolɔi kɛkɛ, shi moŋ amɛkɔ wɔtsɛ Abraham, mɔ ni he ye be mli ni eji foolɔ beebe lɛ, nane. Nyɔŋmɔ shiwoo ni anaa kɛtsɔ̃ɔ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ

english_verse: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ jeee Mla nɔ ni Abraham ye hewɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ wo lɛ loo eshwiei ashi akɛ je lɛ aaatsɔ̃ enɔ lɛ, shi moŋ akɛni ehe eye ni Nyɔŋmɔ bu lɛ akɛ jalɔ lɛ hewɔŋ.

english_verse: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛ Mla shishibii lɛ ji niyelɔi lɛ, belɛ hemɔkɛyeli lɛ efee yaka, ni shiwoo lɛ hu he bɛ sɛɛnamɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
translation_verse: Mla lɛ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu baa, shi he ni mla bɛ lɛ, mlatɔ̃mɔ hu bɛ.

english_verse: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
translation_verse: Enɛ hewɔ ejɛ hemɔkɛyeli mli lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni shiwoo lɛ afee dromɔ sane, ni ama shi shiŋŋ ahã eshwiei lɛ fɛɛ, ni jeee Mla shishibii lɛ kɛkɛ, shi moŋ mɛi ni jɛ Abraham, ni ji wɔ fɛɛ wɔtsɛ lɛ, hemɔkɛyeli lɛ mli lɛ hu;

english_verse: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
translation_verse: tamɔ bɔ ni aŋma lɛ akɛ, “Mikɛ bo efee jeŋmaji pii atsɛ” yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ni ehe eye lɛ hiɛ, mɔ hu ni tsiɛ̃ɔ gbohii ahiɛ, ni etsɛɔ nibii ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ momo lɛ.

english_verse: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
translation_verse: Ni he ni kulɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ ko bɛ lɛ, ena hiɛnɔkãmɔ kɛ he ni ehe eye, mɔ ni etsɔ̃ jeŋmaji pii atsɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni akɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nakai oshwiei lɛ aaatamɔ.”

english_verse: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
translation_verse: ni eyiŋ efeee lɛ kɔshikɔshi yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ shiwoo lɛ he tamɔ akɛ eheee eyeee, shi moŋ ena hewalɛ yɛ hemɔkɛyeli mli, ni ewo Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ nyam,

english_verse: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
translation_verse: ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ akɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ ewo he shi lɛ, eeenyɛ efee hu.

english_verse: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
translation_verse: Shi jeee lɛ kɛkɛ ehewɔ aŋma akɛ “abu no jalɛ ahã lɛ” lɛ,

english_verse: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
translation_verse: shi moŋ wɔ mɛi ni abaabu ahã wɔ lɛ hu hewɔ, wɔ mɛi ni wɔheɔ mɔ ni tee wɔNuŋtsɔ Yesu shi kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ lɛ nɔ wɔyeɔ lɛ;

english_verse: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_verse: shi akɛ lɛ hã yɛ wɔtɔ̃mɔi lɛ ahewɔ, ni atee lɛ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ wɔbembuu hewɔ.

english_verse: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ akɛni adamɔ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ abu wɔ bem hewɔ lɛ, wɔ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ teŋ yɛ hejɔlɛ kɛtsɔ̃ wɔNuŋtsɔ Yesu Kristo nɔ.

english_verse: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
translation_verse: Lɛ enɔ wɔtsɔ̃ ni wɔkɛ hemɔkɛyeli lɛ ena gbɛ hu kɛba dromɔ ni wɔyɔɔ mli nɛɛ mli, ni wɔnyaa yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ anunyam lɛ ni wɔhiɛ kã nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english_verse: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
translation_verse: Shi jeee enɛ kɛkɛ, shi moŋ wɔnyaa yɛ amanehului amli hu, ejaakɛ wɔle akɛ amanehulu lɛ tsɛɔ hiɛmiamɔ kɛbaa,

english_verse: And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope
translation_verse: ni hiɛmiamɔ tsɛɔ su ni sa Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ kɛbaa; ni su nɛɛ tsɛɔ hiɛnɔkãmɔ kɛbaa;

english_verse: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
translation_verse: ni hiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ efeee efolo; ejaakɛ atsɔ̃ Mumɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ ni akɛhã wɔ lɛ nɔ afɔse Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔ awo wɔtsuii amli.

english_verse: Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be mli ni wɔhe waaa lɛ beebe Kristo bagbo yɛ be ni sa mli ehã mɛi ni efeee Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔnaa nii lɛ.

english_verse: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ekpakpa ko dani mɔ ko aaagbo ahã jalɔ ko; ni mɔ kpakpa ko hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ mɔ ko aaashi etsitsi akɛ eeegbo.

english_verse: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ jieɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esuɔmɔ ni ekɛsumɔ wɔ lɛ shi etsɔ̃ɔ, akɛ be mli ni wɔji eshafeelɔi lɛ beebe ni Kristo bagbo yɛ wɔnajiaŋ.

english_verse: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ ni abu wɔ bem yɛ elá lɛ hewɔ lɛ, aaatsɔ̃ enɔ ahere wɔyiwala kɛjɛ mlifu lɛ mli aahu.

english_verse: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛ be mli ni wɔji henyɛlɔi lɛ ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Bi lɛ gbele lɛ bakpãtã wɔ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ teŋ lɛ, agbɛnɛ ni akpãtã wɔteŋ nɛɛ, aaahere wɔyiwala yɛ ewala lɛ mli aahu.

english_verse: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
translation_verse: Shi jeee no kɛkɛ, shi asaŋ wɔshwãa wɔfɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ hu yɛ wɔNuŋtsɔ Yesu Kristo, mɔ nɔ ni tsɔ̃ ni agbɛnɛ wɔna kpãtãmɔ lɛ hewɔ. Adam kɛ Kristo

english_verse: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
translation_verse: Agbɛnɛ, gbɔmɔ kome nɔ esha tsɔ̃ kɛba je lɛ mli, ni gbele tsɔ̃ esha nɔ kɛba. Bɔ ni fee nɛ ni gbele lɛ tsɛŋe gbɔmɛi fɛɛ, ejaakɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee esha lɛ.

english_verse: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
translation_verse: Esha yɛ jeŋ dani ahã Mla lɛ; shi akɛni mla bɛ hewɔ lɛ, abuuu esha lɛ he akɔntaa.

english_verse: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
translation_verse: Kɛ̃lɛ gbele lɛ ye maŋtsɛ kɛjɛ Adam yinɔ kɛbashi Mose yinɔ yɛ mɛi po ni efeko esha ni tamɔ Adam nɔtɔmɔ lɛ anɔ, Adam ni ji mɔ ni baaba lɛ mfoniri lɛ.

english_verse: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
translation_verse: Shi Nyɔŋmɔ dromɔ nɔkeenɔ lɛ tamɔɔɔ shigbeemɔnɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ, kɛ mɔ kome lɛ shigbeemɔ lɛ hewɔ ni mɛi pii lɛ gboi lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ dromɔ lɛ kɛ nɔkeenɔ ni tsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ kome ni ji Yesu Kristo lɛ dromɔ nɔ ba lɛ fa kɛteke nɔ hã mɛi pii lɛ aahu.

english_verse: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
translation_verse: Ni srɔto yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔkeenɔ lɛ kɛ esha ni tsɔ̃ mɔ kome nɔ kɛba lɛ mli; ejaakɛ mɔ kome he esha ni akojo lɛ, ehebuamɔ lɛ fee fɔbuu; shi dromɔ ni jɛ mɛi pii anɔtɔ̃mɔ mli lɛ tsɔ̃ bembuu.

english_verse: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛ mɔ kome shigbeemɔ lɛ hewɔ jɛ ni gbele tsɔ̃ nakai mɔ kome lɛ nɔ ye maŋtsɛ lɛ, belɛ mɛi ni ena dromɔ kɛ jalɛ nɔkeenɔ ni fa kɛteke nɔ lɛ aaatsɔ̃ mɔ kome ni ji Yesu Kristo lɛ nɔ aye maŋtsɛ yɛ wala mli aahu.

english_verse: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔ̃ mɔ kome shigbeemɔ nɔ abu gbɔmɛi fɛɛ fɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ atsɔ̃ mɔ kome jalɛ nɔ abu gbɔmɛi fɛɛ awala bem.

english_verse: Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ kome lɛ toigbele lɛ nɔ ahã mɛi pii tsɔ̃mɔ eshafeelɔi lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ aaatsɔ̃ mɔ kome lɛ toiboo lɛ nɔ ahã mɛi pii hu atsɔ̃mɔ jalɔi.

english_verse: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
translation_verse: Shi Mla lɛ babote mli koni nɔtɔmɔ lɛ afa kɛteke nɔ. Shi he ni esha fa yɛ lɛ, dromɔ lɛ fa kɛteke nɔ yɛ jɛi,

english_verse: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_verse: koni bɔ nɔŋŋ ni esha lɛ ye maŋtsɛ yɛ gbele mli lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ dromɔ lɛ atsɔ̃ jalɛ nɔ aye maŋtsɛ kɛya naanɔ wala mli yɛ Yesu Kristo, wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ, hewɔ.

english_verse: What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better?
translation_verse: Belɛ te wɔɔkɛɛ tɛŋŋ? Aso wɔkã he wɔhi esha lɛ mli, koni dromɔ lɛ afa?

english_verse: No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning?
translation_verse: Dabida! Wɔ ni esha gbɛfaŋ lɛ wɔtamɔ mɛi ni egboi lɛ, te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni wɔhiɛ aaakãmɔ yɛ emli loloŋ?

english_verse: Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death?
translation_verse: Aloo nyɛleee akɛ wɔteŋ mɛi abɔ ni abaptisi wɔ awo Kristo Yesu mli lɛ, egbele lɛ mli abaptisi wɔ awo?

english_verse: When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ baptisimɔ ni abaptisi wɔ awo egbele lɛ mli lɛ efu wɔ kɛ lɛ fɛɛ, koni tamɔ bɔ ni atee Kristo shi kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ yɛ Tsɛ lɛ anunyam naa lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ wɔ hu wɔɔnyiɛ yɛ wala hee mli.

english_verse: If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ kɛji wɔ kɛ lɛ efee ekome yɛ egbele lɛ henɔ lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ wɔ kɛ lɛ aaafee ekome yɛ eshitee lɛ nɔ lɛ mli hu;

english_verse: We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ wɔle enɛ akɛ asɛŋ wɔgbɔmɔ momo lɛ kɛ lɛ, koni esha gbɔmɔtso lɛ hiɛ akpãtã ni wɔkasɔ̃mɔ esha lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ gbɔmɔ ni egbo lɛ, eye ehe yɛ esha dɛŋ.

english_verse: As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
translation_verse: Shi kɛ wɔ kɛ Kristo gbo lɛ, wɔheɔ wɔyeɔ akɛ wɔ kɛ lɛ aaana wala hu,

english_verse: We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die.
translation_verse: ejaakɛ wɔle akɛ ni atee Kristo shi kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ nɛɛ, egboŋ dɔŋŋ; gbele naŋ enɔ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ ni egbo lɛ, esha hewɔ egbo, shi kome pɛ; shi ni ehiɛ kã nɛɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ ehiɛ kã ehã.

english_verse: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
translation_verse: Nakai nyɛ hu nyɛbua nyɛhe akɛ mɛi ni egboi yɛ esha gbɛfaŋ ni amɛhiɛ kãmɔ hã Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ Yesu Kristo, wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ, mli.

english_verse: Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkahãa esha miiyea nyɛgbɔmɔtso ni baagbo lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛ, ni nyɛbo lɛ toi yɛ ekɔnɔi lɛ amli;

english_verse: or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God.
translation_verse: ni asaŋ nyɛkɛ nyɛhenii lɛ akahãa esha akɛ esha lɛ tawuunii; shi moŋ nyɛkɛ nyɛhe ahãa Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ mɛi ni hiɛ etsɛ̃ kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ, ni nyɛkɛ nyɛhenii lɛ afea jalɛ tawuunii nyɛhãa Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law. Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ esha naŋ nyɛnɔ hewalɛ, ejaakɛ jeee Mla shishi nyɛyɔɔ, shi moŋ dromɔ shishi nyɛyɔɔ. Jalɛ tsuji ji wɔ

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not!
translation_verse: Belɛ mɛni? Aso wɔfee esha akɛni wɔbɛ mla shishi shi dromɔ moŋ shishi wɔyɔɔ lɛ? Dabida!

english_verse: Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him.
translation_verse: Ani nyɛleee akɛ, mɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛhe feɔ tsuji nyɛhãa ni nyɛboɔ lɛ toi lɛ, nakai gbɔmɔ lɛ ni nyɛboɔ lɛ toi lɛ tsuji ji nyɛ; esha ni kɛ mɔ yaa gbele mli lɛ tsuji jio, aloo toiboo ni kɛ mɔ yaa jalɛ mli lɛ tsuji jio?

english_verse: You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received.
translation_verse: Shi shidaa ahã Nyɔŋmɔ, akɛ kulɛ sa lɛ esha tsuji ji nyɛ, shi agbɛnɛ nyɛjɛ nyɛtsui fiaa mli nyɛbo nɛkɛ tsɔ̃ɔmɔ ni akɛ nyɛ ewo mli nɛɛ toi.

english_verse: Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
translation_verse: Ni akɛni akpɔ̃ nyɛ yɛ esha dɛŋ lɛ, nyɛtsɔ̃mɔ jalɛ tsuji.

english_verse: I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
translation_verse: Miiwie akɛ gbɔmɔ yɛ nyɛgbedemɔ ni jɛ gbɔmɔfɔmɔ su mli lɛ hewɔ. Tamɔ bɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛhenii lɛ fee tsuji nyɛhã nyaŋemɔ nii kɛ mlatɔ̃mɔ koni nyɛkɛtɔ̃ Mla lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ agbɛnɛ nyɛkɛ nyɛhenii lɛ afea jalɛ tsuji ahãa krɔŋkrɔŋfeemɔ.

english_verse: When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God.
translation_verse: Be ni nyɛ ji esha tsuji lɛ, nyɛye nyɛhe kɛjɛ jalɛ dɛŋ.

english_verse: But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death.
translation_verse: Ni mɛni nyɛna kɛjɛ mli yɛ nakai be lɛ mli? Yibii ni nyɛhiɛ egboi yɛ he agbɛnɛ, ejaakɛ nomɛi anaagbee ji gbele.

english_verse: Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life.
translation_verse: Shi agbɛnɛ lɛ, ni akpɔ̃ nyɛ yɛ esha dɛŋ ni nyɛtsɔ̃mɔ Nyɔŋmɔ tsuji nɛɛ, nɔ ni nyɛnaa kɛjɛɔ mli ji krɔŋkrɔŋfeemɔ, ni enaagbee ji naanɔ wala.

english_verse: Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ esha dɛŋ nyɔmɔwoo lɛ gbele ni; shi Nyɔŋmɔ dromɔ keenɔ lɛ naanɔ walaŋ yɛ Yesu Kristo, wɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ, mli.

english_verse: My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive.
translation_verse: Aloo nyɛleee, anyɛmimɛi, mɛi ni le Mla mikɛwieɔ nɛɛ, akɛ Mla lɛ yeɔ gbɔmɔ nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wala mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english_verse: For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free
translation_verse: Tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ yɛ yoo ni yɔɔ wu gbɛfaŋ lɛ, gbii abɔ fɛɛ ni ewu lɛ hiɛ kã lɛ, mla efi lɛ ekpɛtɛ ewu lɛ; shi kɛji ewu lɛ gbo lɛ, ekɛ ewu mla lɛ bɛ sane ko dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
translation_verse: No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɛji ewu lɛ yɛ jeŋ lolo ni eyagbã mɔ kroko lɛ, atsɛɔ lɛ gbãlãfitelɔ; shi kɛji ewu lɛ gbo lɛ, eye ehe kɛjɛ mla lɛ dɛŋ, ni kɛ eyagbã nuu kroko lɛ, ejeee gbãlãfitelɔ dɔŋŋ.

english_verse: That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God.
translation_verse: Minyɛmimɛi, nakai nɔŋŋ nyɛ hu atsɔ̃ Kristo gbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ ahã nyɛgboi yɛ Mla lɛ gbɛfaŋ, ni nyɛtsɔ̃mɔ mɔ kroko ni ji mɔ ni atee lɛ shi kɛjɛ gbohii ateŋ lɛ nii, koni wɔwo yibii wɔhã Nyɔŋmɔ.

english_verse: When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die.
translation_verse: Ejaakɛ be ni wɔhi shi yɛ wɔgbɔmɔfɔmɔ su lɛ naa lɛ, eshai ahe akɔnɔi lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ Mla lɛ nɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ wɔhenii lɛ amli ni wɔkɛwo yibii wɔhã gbele.

english_verse: But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law. The Battle with Sin
